FILE: SECURITY.md

# Security

This is an experimental kernel and graphics driver that runs with relaxed macOS security (SIP and AMFI settings). Do not
install it on a machine that holds data you cannot lose or that others rely on.

If you find a security problem in the code of this repository (for example a kernel memory bug reachable from an
unprivileged process through IntelXe.kext's user client), please report it privately through GitHub's
"Report a vulnerability" button on the Security tab instead of opening a public issue.

# IntelXe Manager

A macOS app for what otherwise takes Terminal: see the state of the machine and the driver, and install, repair, undo, uninstall and
update it, and do stages 2 and 4 of the install guide in the OpenCore EFI. It is a front end: `install.sh` and `efi.sh` from the package
do the work, so a change made here and one made in Terminal are the same change.

Released from 0.1.2 on (`IntelXe-Manager-VERSION.zip` on the release page; the install guide's step 3.1). The Driver page's
install was used on the test machine (the test builds before 0.1.2); the EFI page made stage 4 there on the EFI of its SSD. Not
used yet: *Undo* on a real EFI, *Use an EFI folder...* on a USB stick that then booted, and a whole install from a
fresh macOS.

**Setup assistant** (opens by itself until it has finished once; the Overview page opens it again): 1. OpenCore's
settings (stage 2), with *Also prepare Safari on the GPU* to turn Apple Secure Boot off in the same change
(`efi.sh --settings-safari-apply`); 2. the driver package; 3. `IntelXe.kext` and SSDT-ARCOFF in the EFI (stage 4, with
HybridPM.kext on a hybrid CPU); 4. a GPU test; 5. done, with extras: Safari on the GPU, Zink for Java games, HiDPI
sizes, the menu bar item and the check at login. When OpenCore recorded no boot path it lists the EFI partitions to
choose from.

| Page | What |
|---|---|
| Overview | a status header with the one action that matters now, the setup steps, this Mac's requirements (macOS, processor, card, SIP, AMFI boot-arg, `IntelXe.kext`, Metal device, boot guard); start-up warnings with fixes; *macOS updates*: the update guard (below) |
| Monitor | five-minute charts of the GPU clock, temperatures, the card's power (with the package's and the power limit) and frames; the optional menu bar item |
| Driver | choose a package (download the latest release, or a folder you unpacked); check, install, repair, undo, uninstall; *Safari and WebKit*: the system-volume copy of the Metal driver (`ssv-install.sh`) |
| EFI (OpenCore) | the EFI OpenCore booted from: mount it; `IntelXe.kext` and `SSDT-ARCOFF.aml` with their `config.plist` entries, and `HybridPM.kext` where the CPU needs it (stage 4); SIP, boot-args and quirks (stage 2, separate); `SecureBootModel` for Safari; undo the last change |
| OpenGL (Zink) | the same for the optional Zink package; on or off for every LWJGL application |
| Display | HiDPI modes (display scaling) on or off through `hidpi.sh` (the package's, or the app's copy); needs IntelXeFB from 0.1.3, takes effect after a restart; Variable refresh |
| Power and app | GPU power profile and clock range (the default's label, e.g. "Default (1200-2850 MHz)", from the range `debug.intelxe.sensors` reports), *Fast GPU response for apps* (the GuC low-latency hint, off by default), *Game mode* (below), open at login, the check at login |
| Tests | the GPU test (Metal features, OpenGL, OpenCL, video decoding bit for bit, encoding quality, compute rate, bandwidth, smoothness) and a long test (about two minutes: video memory, a minute under load). The expected compute rate and bandwidth are the card's `gpu_test` entry in `data/platforms.json` (`Sources/SupportedDevices.swift`, generated by `tools/parity/devices.py --write-swift`), found by PCI device ID: the B580's are measured, the B570's come from Intel's specification; another GPU gets no verdict |
| Report | the diagnostics report (`tools/report/collect-macos.sh`), optionally in administrator mode (the OpenCore config, root-only counters), with ACPI tables (greyed out on macOS 26, which no longer publishes them) or staged-probe results; a progress bar (step N of TOTAL) while it runs; what it found, and the issue forms with the report ID filled in |
| Staged probe | XeProbe ([`docs/PROBE-MODE.md`](../docs/PROBE-MODE.md)), for an Intel GPU the driver does not support yet: the Intel GPUs of this Mac (IOKit, by PCI class), the boot-arg `xeprobe=0xDEVICE` set in or taken out of the EFI's `config.plist` (`efi.sh --xeprobe-plan` / `--xeprobe-off-plan`, shown and confirmed as on the EFI page), XeProbe's state this start (`debug.xeprobe.info`: attached, family, whether the GuC image stage 3 needs is in the kext), each stage with what it does and what it risks, run one at a time as root (`sysctl debug.xeprobe.stage=N` through the password dialog; stages 3 and 4 ask first), the NVRAM breadcrumb switch, the results, the log and the previous start's breadcrumb. Each run goes into `xeprobe-history.txt` in the app's folder, with the results after it; a stage the Mac never came back from is recorded at the next start. *Create a report with the results* runs the collector with `--probe` and that record (`XE_PROBE_HISTORY`) |
| Log | what the scripts print, while they run |

The About window (app menu) has the version, the licences and the credits.

**macOS update guard** ([`docs/design/DESIGN-os-update-guard.md`](../docs/design/DESIGN-os-update-guard.md)): the
Overview page lists the macOS updates Software Update offers (its record in `/Library/Preferences`, or *Check now*)
with whether the installed release supports each (`install.sh --supports-macos`). For one it does not, it warns (also
in a banner and in the check at login): there would be no desktop on the Arc afterwards. For one it does, *Prepare*
runs `Resources/osupdate-guard.sh --prepare` as root: a root-owned copy of the installed release's package and a
one-shot LaunchDaemon. At the first start of the new macOS that daemon checks the kexts, the Metal driver, the
system-volume copy and the boot guard, runs the kept package's `install.sh --apply` when something is missing and the
release supports the new macOS, restarts once, and removes itself (three tries at most, 14 days of waiting at most);
the page shows its result, the Report collects its log. Nothing is parked before the update (the design note says
why). Without a preparation the page still notices a new macOS build at the next start and shows what is missing.

**Game mode** ([`docs/design/DESIGN-game-mode.md`](../docs/design/DESIGN-game-mode.md)), off unless turned on, and
off again at every start of the app: while a game (an app in the games category, or one added from the menu bar
item) is in front, the GPU's lowest clock goes up (2400 MHz by default, through `debug.intelxe.slpc_min` and step
17), and optionally a running Time Machine backup is stopped. A root helper started once through the password
dialog does it and puts it back when the game leaves the front, when game mode is turned off, when the app ends or on
a signal. The menu bar item shows the state and turns it on and off.

After an install the app compares the EFI's `IntelXe.kext` with the package's (executable and `Info.plist`, byte for byte). It
warns only when they differ, the kext or its `Kernel > Add` entry is missing or off, or the EFI could not be read (then it says
"could not be checked", not "update it").

### The EFI page

`efi.sh` decides what changes; the app shows it. **Which EFI:** OpenCore's NVRAM variable
`4D1FDA02-38C7-4A6A-9CC6-4BCCA8B30102:boot-path` names the partition it booted from, which `diskutil` resolves by its
partition UUID; disk numbers are never used, they change between boots. OpenCore writes that variable only when
`Misc > Security > ExposeSensitiveData` includes 1 (`efi/sample-z790` has 6, without it): then the page lists the EFI
partitions with their disk's name and size to choose from, remembers the choice by UUID, and the stage-4 change adds 1
to `ExposeSensitiveData` so that the next boot records it.
**Use an EFI folder...** works on a folder you pick instead (a USB stick's `EFI` folder, or the folder holding it):
`efi.sh --efi`, with backups under `efi-backups/folder-<hash of the path>/`; on Windows, `windows/IntelXe-EFI.ps1` does the same.

**Every write** shows the disk (name, internal or external, size, device, partition UUID) and efi.sh's plan, line by
line, then asks; the password dialog follows. The app passes the plan's SHA-256 with the command, and efi.sh writes
nothing if the EFI no longer gives that plan. Before a change efi.sh copies the whole EFI folder to
`/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver/efi-backups/<partition UUID>/<NNN-date>/`; **Undo** puts back,
from the newest backup, only the files that change touched (`config.plist`, `IntelXe.kext`, `SSDT-ARCOFF.aml`,
`HybridPM.kext`), and
each undo goes one change further back.

- **Stage 4:** copies `IntelXe.kext` when it is missing or differs, adds or enables its `Kernel > Add` entry (and turns
  off an earlier `B580.kext` entry), copies `SSDT-ARCOFF.aml` and adds or enables its `ACPI > Add` entry. The table
  must name the card's upstream port as `ioreg` shows it (`\_SB.PC00.PEG1.PEGP` for the shipped one); with another path
  efi.sh writes that path into a copy of the table ("adapted to this card's port"). An `SSDT-ARCOFF.aml` of your own
  that names the port is kept. On a 12th-14th gen hybrid Intel CPU it also copies `HybridPM.kext` with an entry right
  below `Lilu.kext`'s; without Lilu in the EFI it leaves HybridPM out with a note.
- **Stage 2 (separate button):** `csr-active-config` with at least `0x803` (a wider value stays), `amfi_get_out_of_my_way=0x1`
  and `intelxe_surfvram=2` added to the boot-args (the rest kept), `csr-active-config` and `boot-args` in
  `NVRAM > Delete`, `ResizeAppleGpuBars = 10`, `DisableIoMapper = true`, `ReconnectGraphicsOnConnect = false`.
- `config.plist` is edited with `plutil` on a copy, written back as XML and checked with `plutil -lint` before it
  replaces the EFI's. The values are kept; dictionary keys come out in plutil's (alphabetical) order.
- Nothing for stage 1: installing macOS needs another machine or the USB installer.

Changes go through the macOS administrator password dialog (`osascript ... with administrator privileges`); there is no helper tool and
nothing stays running, but game mode's helper while game mode is on and the update guard's one-shot daemon after a
*Prepare*. A download is compared with the `.sha256` file of the same GitHub release. That finds a damaged file, it does
not prove who made the release. Files go to `~/Library/Application Support/IntelXe Manager`. It contacts only GitHub, and sends no data
(the Report page only opens the issue form in the browser).

English and Turkish, following the system language (`Resources/`).

## Building

`app/build.sh OUTDIR` needs the Command Line Tools and gives a universal, ad-hoc signed `IntelXe Manager.app`. `@State` is avoided, because
on the macOS 27 SDK it is a macro and the Command Line Tools have no SwiftUI macro plugin.

## Testing without the card

- `IntelXeManager --selftest [PACKAGE] [--snapshot FOLDER]`: version comparison, hash list, quoting, a release as GitHub sends it, the facts
  read from this machine, the package's `--status` and `--check`, and a PNG of each page.
- `release/test-install-flow.sh PACKAGE`: `install.sh` through install, damage, repair, undo and uninstall, in a throwaway root, with `kmutil`
  and the root checks stubbed. It does not test the real kernel collection step.
- `release/test-efi-flow.sh [PACKAGE]`: `efi.sh` against a fake EFI folder made from `efi/sample-z790/config.plist` as stage 1 leaves it:
  status, plans, apply, settings, undo, the plan hash, the ACPI path check, the boot-path and `ioreg` parsing. No root, no partition.
- With a package, `--selftest` also runs efi.sh through the app's own functions against a fake EFI (plan, hash, apply, the notice after
  an install, undo), and `--snapshot` adds the EFI page. Not tested without the real machine: OpenCore's `boot-path` on a real boot,
  mounting a real EFI partition, the password dialog, and `ioreg` with a real card.
- `app/tests/test-osupdate-guard.sh`: the update guard through preparation and the starts after minor and major
  updates (repair, restart, bounded tries, expiry, the boot guard, a damaged package) against a throwaway root, with a
  package made from `release/templates/install.sh` and `kmutil`, `nvram` and `shutdown` stubbed.
- `app/tests/test-gamemode-helper.sh`: game mode's helper against a throwaway root with `sysctl` and `tmutil` stubbed.
- `--selftest` also reads XeProbe's results lines, and with a package sets and removes the XeProbe boot-arg on the
  fake EFI through the plan's hash; `--snapshot` adds the Probe page as on a Lunar Lake laptop after a failed stage 3.
  Not tested without the hardware: the stage runs (`sysctl` as root), IOKit's GPU list on an Intel machine, the record
  of a stage the Mac never came back from.
- `IntelXeManager --gputest` / `--longtest` run the Tests page's GPU tests in Terminal (they need the card).

FILE: app/build.sh
================================================
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build.sh OUTDIR: "OUTDIR/IntelXe Manager.app", universal (x86_64 for the machines it serves, arm64 for working on it), ad-hoc signed.
set -euo pipefail
D=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd); O=$1; A="$O/IntelXe Manager.app"
VER=$(cat "$D/../VERSION")
mkdir -p "$O/obj" "$A/Contents/MacOS" "$A/Contents/Resources"
for arch in x86_64 arm64; do
    swiftc -O -swift-version 5 -target $arch-apple-macos15.0 "$D"/Sources/*.swift -module-name IntelXeManager -o "$O/obj/IntelXeManager-$arch"
done
lipo -create "$O/obj/IntelXeManager-x86_64" "$O/obj/IntelXeManager-arm64" -output "$A/Contents/MacOS/IntelXeManager"
sed "s/@VER@/$VER/g" "$D/Info.plist" > "$A/Contents/Info.plist"
ditto "$D/Resources" "$A/Contents/Resources"
install -m 755 "$D/../release/templates/efi.sh" "$A/Contents/Resources/efi.sh"   # for packages made before efi.sh
install -m 644 "$D/../release/templates/efi-rules.json" "$A/Contents/Resources/efi-rules.json"   # its rules, beside it
install -m 755 "$D/../release/templates/hidpi.sh" "$A/Contents/Resources/hidpi.sh"   # for packages made before hidpi.sh
install -m 755 "$D/../tools/report/collect-macos.sh" "$A/Contents/Resources/collect-macos.sh"   # the diagnostics report
codesign -f -s - --deep "$A" 2>/dev/null
echo "$A"

FILE: app/Resources/gamemode-helper.sh
================================================
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# gamemode-helper.sh: IntelXe Manager's game mode, for one session of the app (docs/design/DESIGN-game-mode.md).
#
#   sudo gamemode-helper.sh --run APP_PID OWNER_UID FLOOR_MHZ STOP_BACKUPS
#                          the app starts it once, in the background, when game mode is turned on. It reads one word
#                          per line from a pipe only OWNER_UID can write: "game" raises the GPU's lowest clock to
#                          FLOOR_MHZ (debug.intelxe.slpc_min, sent to the GuC with debug.intelxe.step=17) and, with
#                          STOP_BACKUPS=1, stops Time Machine backups that run while the game stays in front;
#                          "desktop" puts the lowest clock back as it was; "quit" ends it. It ends too when APP_PID
#                          ends or on a signal, and puts the clock back first. Nothing is written to disk but its pipe
#                          and state in /var/run/intelxe-gamemode (gone at the next start of macOS, as the clock is).
#   gamemode-helper.sh --status    the state a helper holds, "key=value" (no root)
#   sudo gamemode-helper.sh --restore
#                          put back the lowest clock a helper that was killed left raised (from its state)
set -uo pipefail

# Tests (app/tests/test-gamemode-helper.sh) run it as a normal user against a throwaway root, with sysctl and tmutil
# stubbed: GM_ROOT is honoured only then, never when the script runs as root.
R="" STUB=""
if [ -n "${GM_ROOT:-}" ] && [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then R=$GM_ROOT; STUB=$R/stub/; fi
SYSCTL=${STUB:-/usr/sbin/}sysctl
TMUTIL=${STUB:-/usr/bin/}tmutil
D="$R/var/run/intelxe-gamemode"
CTL="$D/ctl" STATE="$D/state"

say() { printf '%s gamemode: %s\n' "$(date '+%H:%M:%S')" "$*"; }
need_root() { [ -n "$R" ] || [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "$1 needs root"; exit 1; }; }
kv() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$STATE" 2>/dev/null | head -1; }
num() { case "$1" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1;; esac; }
alive() { num "$1" && kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null; }

# set_min MHZ: the GuC's lowest GT clock, now (until the next start of macOS or the next change)
set_min() {
    "$SYSCTL" -w "debug.intelxe.slpc_min=$1" >/dev/null && "$SYSCTL" -w debug.intelxe.step=17 >/dev/null
}

write_state() {
    printf 'pid=%s\napp=%s\norig_min=%s\nfloor=%s\nphase=%s\nstop_backups=%s\n' "$$" "$APP" "$ORIG" "$FLOOR" "$PHASE" "$TM" > "$STATE.new" \
        && chmod 644 "$STATE.new" && mv -f "$STATE.new" "$STATE"
}

# a helper that was killed (kill -9, a crash) cannot put the clock back itself: its state still says "game"
restore_stale() {
    local pid orig
    [ -f "$STATE" ] || return 0
    pid=$(kv pid); orig=$(kv orig_min)
    alive "$pid" && return 0
    if [ "$(kv phase)" = game ] && num "$orig"; then
        set_min "$orig" && say "put back the lowest GPU clock a stopped helper left raised: $orig MHz"
    fi
    rm -f "$STATE" "$CTL"
}

tm_stop() {
    "$TMUTIL" status 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'Running = 1' || return 0
    "$TMUTIL" stopbackup >/dev/null 2>&1 && say "stopped a Time Machine backup (the next scheduled one runs as usual)"
}

game() {
    [ "$PHASE" = game ] && return 0
    PHASE=game; write_state
    if [ "$FLOOR" -gt "$ORIG" ]; then set_min "$FLOOR" && say "a game is in front: lowest GPU clock $FLOOR MHz (was $ORIG)"
    else say "a game is in front: the lowest GPU clock is already $ORIG MHz"; fi
    [ "$TM" = 1 ] && tm_stop
}

desktop() {
    [ "$PHASE" = game ] || return 0
    PHASE=desktop; write_state
    [ "$FLOOR" -gt "$ORIG" ] && set_min "$ORIG" && say "no game in front: lowest GPU clock back to $ORIG MHz"
}

cleanup() {
    desktop
    rm -f "$CTL" "$STATE"
    say "ended: everything is as it was"
}

run() {
    need_root --run
    APP=${1:-} OWNER=${2:-} FLOOR=${3:-} TM=${4:-0} PHASE=desktop
    alive "$APP" || { echo "no such app process: $APP"; exit 2; }
    num "$OWNER" || { echo "not a user id: $OWNER"; exit 2; }
    num "$FLOOR" && [ "$FLOOR" -ge 300 ] && [ "$FLOOR" -le 3000 ] || { echo "the clock must be 300-3000 MHz: $FLOOR"; exit 2; }
    case "$TM" in 0|1) ;; *) echo "STOP_BACKUPS is 0 or 1: $TM"; exit 2;; esac
    mkdir -p "$D"; chmod 755 "$D"
    if [ -f "$STATE" ] && alive "$(kv pid)"; then echo "game mode already runs (pid $(kv pid))"; exit 1; fi
    restore_stale
    ORIG=$("$SYSCTL" -n debug.intelxe.slpc_min 2>/dev/null)
    num "$ORIG" || { echo "IntelXe.kext does not answer (debug.intelxe.slpc_min): game mode needs the driver"; exit 3; }
    # never above the highest clock the user chose (the Quiet setting's 1800 MHz, intelxe-gpu-max-mhz)
    local max; max=$("$SYSCTL" -n debug.intelxe.slpc_max 2>/dev/null)
    if num "$max" && [ "$max" -gt 0 ] && [ "$FLOOR" -gt "$max" ]; then FLOOR=$max; fi
    rm -f "$CTL"; mkfifo -m 600 "$CTL" || { echo "could not make $CTL"; exit 1; }
    [ -n "$R" ] || chown "$OWNER" "$CTL"
    write_state
    trap cleanup EXIT
    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT
    trap '' HUP
    exec 3<>"$CTL"
    say "on for app $APP: lowest GPU clock $FLOOR MHz while a game is in front (now $ORIG MHz)$([ "$TM" = 1 ] && echo ", Time Machine backups stopped then")"
    local line n=0
    while alive "$APP"; do
        if read -r -t 2 -u 3 line; then
            case "$line" in
                game) game;;
                desktop) desktop;;
                quit) break;;
            esac
        fi
        n=$((n + 1))
        [ "$PHASE" = game ] && [ "$TM" = 1 ] && [ $((n % 5)) = 1 ] && tm_stop
    done
    exit 0
}

case "${1:-}" in
    --run) shift; run "$@" ;;
    --status)
        if [ -f "$STATE" ]; then cat "$STATE"; alive "$(kv pid)" && echo "running=yes" || echo "running=no"; else echo "running=no"; fi ;;
    --restore) need_root --restore; restore_stale ;;
    *) sed -n '3,15p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
esac



================================================
FILE: app/Resources/osupdate-guard.sh
================================================
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# osupdate-guard.sh: IntelXe Manager's macOS update guard (docs/design/DESIGN-os-update-guard.md).
#
#   osupdate-guard.sh --check            the stack as it is now, one "key=value" per line. No root, changes nothing.
#   osupdate-guard.sh --status           the preparation and the last result, "key=value". No root, changes nothing.
#   sudo osupdate-guard.sh --prepare PACKAGE [TARGET] [--no-restart]
#                                        before a macOS update: record what is installed, keep a root-owned copy of
#                                        PACKAGE (the installed release's package) and install a one-shot LaunchDaemon
#                                        that runs --finish at each start until the update has happened
#   sudo osupdate-guard.sh --finish      the LaunchDaemon's run. Same build as recorded: wait (for 14 days at most).
#                                        A new build: check the kexts, the Metal driver, the system-volume copy and the
#                                        boot guard; when the package supports the new macOS and something is missing,
#                                        install the kept package again (install.sh --apply) and restart once; at most
#                                        three tries. A boot guard the update's restarts set is cleared once. Then it
#                                        removes itself. It never touches the EFI.
#   sudo osupdate-guard.sh --cancel      remove the LaunchDaemon, the record and the kept package (log and result stay)
#
# Everything goes to /Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver/osupdate/: state (the record), result (the
# last outcome), osupdate.log (the diagnostics report collects it), package/ (the kept copy), tries.
set -uo pipefail

# Tests (app/tests/test-osupdate-guard.sh) run it as a normal user against a throwaway root: OSG_ROOT is honoured only
# then, never when the script runs as root, so a root run always works on the real system with the real tools.
R="" STUB=""
if [ -n "${OSG_ROOT:-}" ] && [ "$(id -u)" != 0 ]; then R=$OSG_ROOT; STUB=$R/stub/; fi
KMUTIL=${STUB:-/usr/bin/}kmutil
NVRAM=${STUB:-/usr/sbin/}nvram
SHUTDOWN=${STUB:-/sbin/}shutdown
WAIT=${OSG_WAIT:-90}; [ -n "$R" ] || WAIT=90   # seconds the kexts get to appear after a start

BK="$R/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver"
G="$BK/osupdate"
STATE="$G/state" RESULT="$G/result" LOG="$G/osupdate.log" TRIES="$G/tries" PKG="$G/package"
LABEL=io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.osupdate
PLIST="$R/Library/LaunchDaemons/$LABEL.plist"
SV="$R/System/Library/CoreServices/SystemVersion.plist"
EXT="$R/Library/Extensions" GB="$R/Library/GPUBundles"
SSV="$R/System/Library/Extensions/NVMTLDriver.bundle"
AUXKC="$R/Library/KernelCollections/AuxiliaryKernelExtensions.kc"
MAX_TRIES=3 EXPIRE_DAYS=14
# the /Library kexts install.sh puts in the Auxiliary Kernel Collection, as "file bundle-id"; IntelXe.kext comes from the EFI
KEXTS="IntelXeFB:io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB NMXAccel:com.nullmoth.NMXAccel NMXAGDC:com.nullmoth.NMXAGDC"

say() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
need_root() { [ -n "$R" ] || [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "$1 needs root: sudo $0 $1"; exit 1; }; }
own() { [ -n "$R" ] || chown "$@"; }
plist_get() { /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :$2" "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
os_version() { plist_get "$SV" ProductVersion; }
os_build() { plist_get "$SV" ProductBuildVersion; }
kv() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" "$2" 2>/dev/null | head -1; }   # kv KEY FILE

# the kexts' state, one word each: loaded, installed (the file is there, the kernel did not load it) or absent
kext_states() {
    local loaded k f id
    loaded=$("$KMUTIL" showloaded --list-only 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ "$loaded" == *"io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXe ("* ]]; then echo "kext_IntelXe=loaded"; else echo "kext_IntelXe=absent"; fi
    for k in $KEXTS; do
        f=${k%%:*} id=${k#*:}
        if [[ "$loaded" == *"$id ("* ]]; then echo "kext_$f=loaded"
        elif [ -d "$EXT/$f.kext" ]; then echo "kext_$f=installed"
        else echo "kext_$f=absent"; fi
    done
}

# the boot guard as IntelXeFB left it: ok, armed:<stage> (a boot that has not run its desktop for a minute yet) or held:<why>
guard_state() {
    local off g
    off=$("$NVRAM" intelxe-accel-off 2>/dev/null | cut -f2- || true)
    g=$("$NVRAM" intelxe-guard 2>/dev/null | cut -f2- || true)
    if [ -n "$off" ] && [ "$off" != ok ]; then echo "held:$off"
    elif [ -n "$g" ] && [ "$g" != ok ]; then echo "armed:$g"
    else echo ok; fi
}

check() {
    local ks
    ks=$(kext_states)
    echo "macos_version=$(os_version)"
    echo "macos_build=$(os_build)"
    echo "$ks"
    echo "installed_version=$(cat "$BK/installed-version" 2>/dev/null || echo none)"
    if [ ! -f "$AUXKC" ]; then echo "aux_kc=missing"
    elif grep -aq io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB "$AUXKC" 2>/dev/null; then echo "aux_kc=ours"
    else echo "aux_kc=without-ours"; fi
    [ -d "$GB/NVMTLDriverLib.bundle" ] && [ -d "$GB/nvmtl" ] && echo "plugin=present" || echo "plugin=missing"
    [ -f "$SSV/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver" ] && echo "ssv=present" || echo "ssv=absent"
    [ -f "$GB/nvmtl/ssv-component.plist" ] && echo "ssv_record=yes" || echo "ssv_record=no"
    echo "boot_guard=$(guard_state)"
    # kexts that are installed and not loaded: the collection was not rebuilt for this macOS, or not approved
    echo "not_loaded=$(echo "$ks" | sed -n 's/^kext_\(.*\)=installed$/\1/p' | tr '\n' ',' | sed 's/,$//')"
}

# support VERSION PACKAGE_DIR: ok, untested or no. The package's install.sh says (--supports-macos, from 0.1.5); an
# earlier package is for its own major version only (install.sh --status: package_macos)
support() {
    local v=$1 p=$2 major
    if grep -q -- '--supports-macos)' "$p/install.sh" 2>/dev/null; then "$p/install.sh" --supports-macos "$v"; return; fi
    major=$("$p/install.sh" --status 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^package_macos=//p')
    [ -n "$major" ] && [ "${v%%.*}" = "$major" ] && echo ok || echo no
}

package_ok() { (cd "$1" && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS >/dev/null 2>&1); }

remove_daemon() { rm -f "$PLIST"; }

# write_result RESULT MESSAGE: the outcome for the Manager (its Overview page and the check at login); EXTRA holds more
# "key=value" lines
EXTRA=""
write_result() {
    {
        echo "result=$1"
        echo "when=$(date +%s)"
        echo "from=$(kv from_version "$STATE") ($(kv from_build "$STATE"))"
        echo "to=$(os_version) ($(os_build))"
        echo "tries=$(cat "$TRIES" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        echo "package=$(kv package_version "$STATE")"
        [ -n "$EXTRA" ] && printf '%s\n' "$EXTRA"
        echo "message=$2"
    } > "$RESULT.new" && mv -f "$RESULT.new" "$RESULT"
    chmod 644 "$RESULT"
    say "result: $1: $2"
}

# finish_with RESULT MESSAGE: the outcome, then the daemon, the record and the kept package go; nothing stays to run again
finish_with() {
    write_result "$1" "$2"
    remove_daemon
    rm -rf "$PKG" "$STATE" "$TRIES"
    say "removed $PLIST and the kept package"
}

prepare() {
    local src=${1:-} target="" restart=yes a
    shift || true
    for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in --no-restart) restart=no;; *) target=$a;; esac; done
    [ -n "$src" ] && [ -x "$src/install.sh" ] && [ -f "$src/SHA256SUMS" ] || { echo "not a package (no install.sh and SHA256SUMS): ${src:-none given}"; exit 1; }
    src=$(cd "$src" && pwd)
    package_ok "$src" || { echo "the package's files differ from its SHA256SUMS: nothing prepared"; exit 1; }
    local st pv pm iv
    st=$("$src/install.sh" --status 2>/dev/null)
    pv=$(echo "$st" | sed -n 's/^package_version=//p'); pm=$(echo "$st" | sed -n 's/^package_macos=//p')
    iv=$(cat "$BK/installed-version" 2>/dev/null || echo none)
    [ "$iv" != none ] || { echo "the driver is not installed (no installed-version): nothing to guard"; exit 1; }
    [ "$iv" = "$pv" ] || { echo "the installed driver is $iv, the package is $pv: choose the installed release's package"; exit 1; }
    mkdir -p "$R/Library/LaunchDaemons"
    say "== preparing for a macOS update (from $(os_version) $(os_build)${target:+ to $target})"
    rm -rf "$PKG.new"
    ditto "$src" "$PKG.new" || { rm -rf "$PKG.new"; say "could not copy the package: nothing prepared"; exit 1; }
    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$PKG.new" 2>/dev/null || true
    own -R root:wheel "$PKG.new"; chmod -R go-w "$PKG.new"
    rm -rf "$PKG"; mv "$PKG.new" "$PKG"
    package_ok "$PKG" || { rm -rf "$PKG"; say "the kept copy differs from SHA256SUMS: nothing prepared"; exit 1; }
    # the copy that runs: a root-owned one, not the app bundle's (the app may move, or be replaced by a user)
    install -m 755 "$0" "$G/osupdate-guard.sh.new" 2>/dev/null || { cp "$0" "$G/osupdate-guard.sh.new"; chmod 755 "$G/osupdate-guard.sh.new"; }
    own root:wheel "$G/osupdate-guard.sh.new"; mv -f "$G/osupdate-guard.sh.new" "$G/osupdate-guard.sh"
    {
        echo "prepared_at=$(date +%s)"
        echo "from_version=$(os_version)"
        echo "from_build=$(os_build)"
        echo "target=$target"
        echo "package_version=$pv"
        echo "package_macos=$pm"
        echo "restart=$restart"
        check | sed 's/^/before_/'
    } > "$STATE.new" && mv -f "$STATE.new" "$STATE"
    rm -f "$TRIES" "$RESULT"
    cat > "$PLIST.new" <<PL
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key><string>$LABEL</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key><array><string>/bin/bash</string><string>$G/osupdate-guard.sh</string><string>--finish</string></array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key><true/>
</dict>
</plist>
PL
    # a file launchd cannot read would never run: then nothing is prepared
    plutil -lint "$PLIST.new" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f "$PLIST.new" "$STATE"; rm -rf "$PKG"; say "the LaunchDaemon file is not valid: nothing prepared"; exit 1; }
    own root:wheel "$PLIST.new"; chmod 644 "$PLIST.new"; mv -f "$PLIST.new" "$PLIST"
    say "kept $pv's package in $PKG; $PLIST runs the check at the first start of the new macOS"
    case "$(support "${target:-$(os_version)}" "$PKG")" in
        no) say "note: $pv does not support macOS ${target:-$(os_version)}: after that update the guard only reports, it installs nothing";;
        untested) say "note: $pv was not tested on macOS ${target:-$(os_version)}; the guard installs it again if needed";;
    esac
    echo "== prepared"
}

finish() {
    [ -f "$STATE" ] || { remove_daemon; say "nothing prepared: removed the LaunchDaemon"; exit 0; }
    local fb nb now age tries
    fb=$(kv from_build "$STATE"); nb=$(os_build); now=$(date +%s)
    if [ "$nb" = "$fb" ]; then
        age=$(( (now - $(kv prepared_at "$STATE")) / 86400 ))
        if [ "$age" -ge "$EXPIRE_DAYS" ]; then
            finish_with expired "prepared $age days ago and still on $(os_version) ($nb): the preparation is removed; prepare again before the next update"
        else say "still on $(os_version) ($nb): waiting for the update (prepared $age day(s) ago)"; fi
        exit 0
    fi
    tries=$(( $(cat "$TRIES" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) + 1 )); echo "$tries" > "$TRIES"
    say "== macOS was updated: $(kv from_version "$STATE") ($fb) -> $(os_version) ($nb), check $tries of $MAX_TRIES"
    # the kexts of the Auxiliary Kernel Collection load a little after the daemons start
    local c i=0
    while :; do
        c=$(check)
        echo "$c" | grep -q '^not_loaded=$' && break
        [ "$i" -ge "$WAIT" ] && break
        sleep 5; i=$((i + 5))
    done
    echo "$c" | sed 's/^/  /' | tee -a "$LOG" >/dev/null
    local sup notl plugin ssv guard ssvnote efi
    sup=$(support "$(os_version)" "$PKG"); notl=$(echo "$c" | sed -n 's/^not_loaded=//p')
    plugin=$(echo "$c" | sed -n 's/^plugin=//p'); ssv=$(echo "$c" | sed -n 's/^ssv=//p'); guard=$(echo "$c" | sed -n 's/^boot_guard=//p')
    efi=$(echo "$c" | sed -n 's/^kext_IntelXe=//p')
    # the system-volume copy: an update replaces the system volume, and the copy with it; putting it back needs the
    # user (Apple Secure Boot off, a new snapshot): the Manager offers it
    if [ "$(kv before_ssv "$STATE")" = present ] && [ "$ssv" != present ]; then ssvnote=gone; else ssvnote=$ssv; fi
    EXTRA=$(printf 'support=%s\nssv=%s\nboot_guard=%s\nefi_kext=%s\nnot_loaded=%s\nplugin=%s' "$sup" "$ssvnote" "$guard" "$efi" "$notl" "$plugin")
    local from; from=$(kv from_version "$STATE")
    if [ "$sup" = no ]; then
        finish_with unsupported "release $(kv package_version "$STATE") does not support macOS $(os_version): nothing was installed. Install a release that supports it, or go back to macOS $from (Time Machine)."
        exit 0
    fi
    # IntelXe.kext comes from OpenCore, not from /Library: without it the /Library kexts have nothing to attach to, and
    # installing them again would not help
    if [ "$efi" != loaded ]; then
        finish_with efi-kext "IntelXe.kext from the EFI did not load on macOS $(os_version): check the EFI (its Kernel > Add entry, MinKernel and MaxKernel); nothing was installed"
        exit 0
    fi
    # the boot guard holding acceleration off after the update, when it was clear before and no kernel panic was recorded
    # since the preparation: the update's own restarts inside the first minute of a boot count as failed boots. Cleared
    # once (the first check after the update); a panic report, or a second time, leaves it to the user
    local clear=no panics
    panics=$(find "$R/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports" -name '*.panic' -newer "$STATE" 2>/dev/null | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')
    case "$guard" in held:*)
        if [ "$(kv before_boot_guard "$STATE")" = ok ] && [ -z "$panics" ] && [ "$tries" = 1 ]; then clear=yes
        else say "the boot guard holds acceleration off (${guard#held:})${panics:+; panic reports since the preparation: $panics}: left to you (the Manager's Clear the boot guard, or Reset NVRAM)"; fi;;
    esac
    local inst repaired=no
    inst=$("$PKG/install.sh" --status 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^installed_state=//p')
    if [ -n "$notl" ] || [ "$plugin" != present ] || [ "$inst" != same ]; then
        say "to repair: ${notl:+not loaded: $notl; }Metal driver $plugin; installed files: ${inst:-unknown}"
        if [ "$tries" -gt "$MAX_TRIES" ]; then
            finish_with gave-up "$MAX_TRIES tries did not bring the driver back on macOS $(os_version): see this log; install the package again from the Driver page"
            exit 0
        fi
        if ! package_ok "$PKG"; then
            finish_with refused "the kept package's files differ from its SHA256SUMS: nothing was installed"
            exit 0
        fi
        say "installing release $(kv package_version "$STATE") again: install.sh --apply"
        if "$PKG/install.sh" --apply >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then
            repaired=yes
        elif [ "$tries" -ge "$MAX_TRIES" ]; then
            finish_with gave-up "install.sh --apply failed $tries times on macOS $(os_version): see this log"
            exit 0
        else
            write_result retrying "install.sh --apply failed (try $tries of $MAX_TRIES); the next start tries again"
            exit 0
        fi
    fi
    if [ "$clear" = yes ]; then
        # both values: a held boot on the firmware framebuffer leaves the count to intelxe-accel-off (intelxe-guard=ok), but
        # only in the kernel's copy until a clean restart (IntelXe.kext's bootGuardDecide)
        "$NVRAM" intelxe-accel-off=ok intelxe-guard=ok && say "cleared the boot guard (intelxe-accel-off=ok, intelxe-guard=ok): it was clear before the update and no panic was recorded since"
    fi
    if [ "$repaired" = no ] && [ "$clear" = no ]; then
        local note=""
        [ "$ssvnote" = gone ] && note="; the system-volume copy (Safari on the GPU) is gone: install it again from the Driver page"
        case "$guard" in held:*) note="$note; the boot guard holds acceleration off: clear it on the Overview page once you know why";; esac
        finish_with ok "the driver works on macOS $(os_version)$note"
        exit 0
    fi
    # something changed: the next start checks it (the daemon stays); restart once by itself when that was allowed
    if [ "$repaired" = yes ]; then
        write_result repaired "installed release $(kv package_version "$STATE") again for macOS $(os_version)$([ "$clear" = yes ] && echo " and cleared the boot guard"); the next start checks that it loads"
    else
        write_result guard-cleared "cleared the boot guard, which the update's restarts had set; the next start checks the desktop"
    fi
    if [ "$tries" = 1 ] && [ "$(kv restart "$STATE")" = yes ]; then
        say "restarting once by itself, in one minute"
        "$SHUTDOWN" -r +1 >> "$LOG" 2>&1 || say "could not restart: restart by hand"
    fi
}

status() {
    if [ -f "$STATE" ]; then echo "prepared=yes"; sed 's/^/state_/' "$STATE"; else echo "prepared=no"; fi
    [ -f "$PLIST" ] && echo "daemon=yes" || echo "daemon=no"
    echo "tries=$(cat "$TRIES" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [ -f "$RESULT" ] && sed 's/^/last_/' "$RESULT"
    echo "log=$LOG"
}

cancel() {
    remove_daemon
    rm -rf "$PKG" "$STATE" "$TRIES"
    say "preparation cancelled: removed $PLIST and the kept package"
}

# the guard's folder, and its log kept short (the last 2000 lines); only for the runs that write
start() {
    need_root "$1"
    mkdir -p "$G"; chmod 755 "$G"
    if [ -f "$LOG" ] && [ "$(wc -l < "$LOG")" -gt 4000 ]; then tail -n 2000 "$LOG" > "$LOG.new" && mv -f "$LOG.new" "$LOG"; fi
}
case "${1:-}" in
    --check) check ;;
    --status) status ;;
    --prepare) start --prepare; shift; prepare "$@" ;;
    --finish) start --finish; finish ;;
    --cancel) start --cancel; cancel ;;
    *) sed -n '3,20p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
esac

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The Display page: HiDPI modes ("Larger Text ... More Space") for the monitor on the card, through hidpi.sh.
// hidpi.sh decides what is written (an NVRAM flag, a display override with the HiDPI sizes, WindowServer's
// DisplayResolutionEnabled) and takes back only what it wrote; the app shows its status and runs --on / --off as root.
import Foundation
import SwiftUI

/// hidpi.sh --status.
struct HiDPIStatus {
    var values: [String: String] = [:]
    init() {}
    init(text: String) {
        for line in text.split(separator: "\n") {
            let pair = line.split(separator: "=", maxSplits: 1, omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
            if pair.count == 2 { values[pair[0]] = pair[1] }
        }
    }
    subscript(key: String) -> String { values[key] ?? "" }
    var known: Bool { !values.isEmpty }
    /// The installed IntelXeFB offers scaled modes (0.1.3 on).
    var supported: Bool { self["hidpi_supported"] == "1" }
    /// --on has run: the NVRAM flag and this script's override.
    var on: Bool { self["hidpi_nvram"] == "1" && self["hidpi_override"] == "ours" }
    /// An override for this monitor that hidpi.sh did not write (another HiDPI tool's): hidpi.sh leaves it alone.
    var foreignOverride: Bool { self["hidpi_override"] == "other" }
    /// The framebuffer offers the scaled modes this boot.
    var active: Bool { self["hidpi_active"] == "1" }
    /// --on or --off ran but the machine has not restarted since.
    var pending: Bool { on != active }
}

/// The package's hidpi.sh, or the copy in this app (the same file) for packages made before it.
func hidpiScript(for package: Package?) -> URL? {
    if let own = package?.directory.appendingPathComponent("hidpi.sh"), FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: own.path) { return own }
    return Bundle.main.url(forResource: "hidpi", withExtension: "sh")
}

func hidpiStatus(script: URL) -> HiDPIStatus {
    HiDPIStatus(text: commandOutput("/bin/bash", [script.path, "--status"], seconds: 30) ?? "")
}

enum HiDPIAction: String, Identifiable {
    case on, off
    var id: String { rawValue }
    var argument: String { self == .on ? "--on" : "--off" }
    var title: String {
        switch self {
        case .on: return String(localized: "Turn HiDPI modes on")
        case .off: return String(localized: "Turn HiDPI modes off")
        }
    }
}

extension Manager {
    func refreshHiDPI() async {
        let (wanted, active) = await Task.detached { () -> (Bool, Bool) in
            // IntelXeFB: unset = on; a value whose first character is not '1' = off (read once, at start)
            let nv = commandOutput("/usr/sbin/nvram", ["intelxefb-vrr-modes"]) ?? ""
            let value = nv.split(separator: "\t").dropFirst().first.map { String($0).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) }
            let reg = commandOutput("/usr/sbin/ioreg", ["-r", "-c", "IntelXeFramebuffer", "-l", "-w0"]) ?? ""
            return (value.map { $0.hasPrefix("1") } ?? true, reg.contains("IOFBTimingRange"))
        }.value
        vrrWanted = wanted; vrrActive = active
        guard let script = hidpiScript(for: package) else { hidpi = HiDPIStatus(); return }
        hidpi = await Task.detached { hidpiStatus(script: script) }.value
    }

    func setVRR(_ on: Bool) {
        perform(title: on ? String(localized: "Turn Variable refresh on") : String(localized: "Turn Variable refresh off"),
                command: "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxefb-vrr-modes=\(on ? 1 : 0)", needsRoot: true, then: { result in
            if result.cancelled { self.lastResult = String(localized: "Cancelled. Nothing changed.") }
            else if result.succeeded { self.lastResult = String(localized: "Finished. Restart to use the change."); self.rebootNeeded = true }
            else { self.lastResult = String(localized: "It did not finish. See the log.") }
        })
    }

    func performHiDPI(_ action: HiDPIAction) {
        guard let script = hidpiScript(for: package) else { return }
        perform(title: action.title, command: "/bin/bash \(shellQuoted(script.path)) \(action.argument)", needsRoot: true, then: { result in
            if result.cancelled {
                self.lastResult = String(localized: "Cancelled. Nothing changed.")
            } else if result.succeeded {
                self.lastResult = String(localized: "Finished. Restart to use the change.")
                self.rebootNeeded = true
            } else {
                self.lastResult = String(localized: "It did not finish. See the log.")
            }
        })
    }
}

struct DisplayView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var manager: Manager
    var body: some View {
        let status = manager.hidpi
        Form {
            Section2(title: "HiDPI modes", symbol: "display") {
                Caption("Optional: sharp \"looks like\" sizes in System Settings > Displays, at the full refresh rate.",
                        detail: "Optional. Like display scaling on Windows: System Settings > Displays offers \"looks like\" sizes (Larger Text ... More Space) that draw text and windows sharp at a larger size, at the monitor's full refresh rate. They are scaled on the GPU.")
                if status.known {
                    LabeledContent("Monitor") { Text(monitorText(status)).textSelection(.enabled) }
                    LabeledContent("HiDPI modes") { Text(stateText(status)) }
                } else {
                    Text("Reading the display settings…").foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                if status.known {
                    if !status.supported {
                        Label("The installed driver has no HiDPI modes yet. Install release 0.1.3 or later first.", systemImage: "exclamationmark.triangle")
                    } else if status.foreignOverride {
                        Label("This monitor already has a display override from another tool (one-key-hidpi or similar). It is left as it is: remove it first to use this one.", systemImage: "exclamationmark.triangle")
                    }
                    if status.on {
                        Button(HiDPIAction.off.title, role: .destructive) { manager.performHiDPI(.off) }
                    } else {
                        Button(HiDPIAction.on.title) { manager.performHiDPI(.on) }.disabled(!status.supported || status.foreignOverride)
                    }
                    Caption("It takes effect after a restart.",
                            detail: "It takes effect after a restart. Then choose a size in System Settings > Displays. Turning them off takes back only what was written here, and a chosen HiDPI size goes back to the monitor's own.")
                }
            }
            Section2(title: "Variable refresh (Adaptive-Sync)", symbol: "speedometer") {
                Caption("For Adaptive-Sync monitors: no tearing or stutter below the maximum rate.",
                        detail: "System Settings > Displays lists a Variable refresh rate for monitors that support Adaptive-Sync: the monitor then waits for each new frame, so games and video run without tearing or stutter below the maximum rate. On by default; turn it off if the monitor flickers in Variable mode.")
                LabeledContent("Variable modes") {
                    Text(manager.vrrWanted == manager.vrrActive ? (manager.vrrActive ? String(localized: "On") : String(localized: "Off"))
                         : (manager.vrrWanted ? String(localized: "On after a restart") : String(localized: "Off after a restart")))
                }
                if manager.vrrWanted {
                    Button("Turn Variable refresh off", role: .destructive) { manager.setVRR(false) }
                } else {
                    Button("Turn Variable refresh on") { manager.setVRR(true) }
                }
            }
            DisplayTroubleshootingView()
        }
        .formStyle(.grouped)
    }

    func monitorText(_ status: HiDPIStatus) -> String {
        let parts = [status["display"], status["native"]].filter { !$0.isEmpty }
        return parts.isEmpty ? String(localized: "Not found") : parts.joined(separator: "  ")
    }

    func stateText(_ status: HiDPIStatus) -> String {
        switch (status.on, status.active) {
        case (true, true): return String(localized: "On")
        case (true, false): return String(localized: "On after a restart")
        case (false, true): return String(localized: "Off after a restart")
        default: return String(localized: "Off")
        }
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The EFI page's facts and commands. efi.sh decides what changes in the EFI (the package's copy, or the one inside this app
// for packages made before it): the app shows its plan, asks, and runs it with the plan's SHA-256, so that efi.sh writes
// nothing unless the EFI is still in the state the plan was made from.
import CryptoKit
import Foundation

/// Which EFI efi.sh works on: the one OpenCore recorded in NVRAM, a partition chosen by its UUID, or a folder that holds
/// EFI/OC (one the user chose, such as a USB stick's; the tests' fake EFI).
enum EFITarget: Hashable {
    case recorded
    case partition(String)
    case folder(String)
    var arguments: [String] {
        switch self {
        case .recorded: return []
        case .partition(let uuid): return ["--part", uuid]
        case .folder(let path): return ["--efi", path]
        }
    }
}

/// The folder to give efi.sh --efi for a folder the user picked: the picked folder when it holds EFI/OC (a USB stick, a
/// mounted partition), its parent when it is the EFI folder itself (it holds OC); nil for anything else.
func efiFolderRoot(for picked: URL) -> String? {
    let fm = FileManager.default
    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
    func dir(_ url: URL) -> Bool { fm.fileExists(atPath: url.path, isDirectory: &isDir) && isDir.boolValue }
    let url = picked.standardizedFileURL
    if dir(url.appendingPathComponent("EFI/OC")) { return url.path }
    let parent = url.deletingLastPathComponent()
    if dir(url.appendingPathComponent("OC")) && dir(parent.appendingPathComponent("EFI/OC")) { return parent.path }
    return nil
}

/// An EFI partition efi.sh found: "candidate=UUID|device|disk|size|mount point|OpenCore".
struct EFICandidate: Hashable, Identifiable {
    let uuid: String
    let device: String
    let disk: String
    let size: String
    let mountPoint: String
    let openCore: String
    var id: String { uuid }
    init?(_ text: String) {
        let fields = text.split(separator: "|", omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
        guard fields.count >= 6, !fields[0].isEmpty else { return nil }
        (uuid, device, disk, size, mountPoint, openCore) = (fields[0], fields[1], fields[2], fields[3], fields[4], fields[5])
    }
    var label: String { "\(disk.isEmpty ? "?" : disk), \(size) (\(device))" }
}

/// efi.sh --status.
struct EFIStatus {
    var values: [String: String] = [:]
    var candidates: [EFICandidate] = []
    init() {}
    init(text: String) {
        for line in text.split(separator: "\n") {
            let pair = line.split(separator: "=", maxSplits: 1, omittingEmptySubsequences: false).map(String.init)
            guard pair.count == 2 else { continue }
            if pair[0] == "candidate" {
                if let candidate = EFICandidate(pair[1]) { candidates.append(candidate) }
            } else {
                values[pair[0]] = pair[1]
            }
        }
    }
    subscript(key: String) -> String { values[key] ?? "" }
    var known: Bool { !values.isEmpty }
    var found: Bool { !["", "none"].contains(self["efi_source"]) }
    var mounted: Bool { self["efi_mounted"] == "yes" }
    var readable: Bool { self["efi_readable"] == "yes" }
    var isOpenCore: Bool { self["opencore"] == "yes" }
    var fileChanges: Int { Int(self["plan_changes"]) ?? 0 }
    var settingsChanges: Int { Int(self["settings_changes"]) ?? 0 }
    var backup: String? { ["", "none"].contains(self["backup"]) ? nil : self["backup"] }
    /// boot logging: on, off, partial, missing (no Misc > Debug), or "" (not read)
    var bootLogging: String { self["boot_logging"] }
    /// HybridPM.kext's rows on the EFI page: for a CPU that needs it, or when the EFI has it
    var showsHybridPM: Bool { self["hybridpm_needed"] == "yes" || ["same", "different"].contains(self["hybridpm_file"]) }
}

/// A cheap fingerprint of what efi.sh reads in an EFI (EFI/OC/config.plist, ACPI, Kexts with their contents, Drivers):
/// paths, sizes and modification times, no file contents. The EFI page compares it to notice changes made outside the
/// app (another tool, a text editor, a second copy of the app) and reads the EFI again. nil when it cannot be read.
func efiFingerprint(root: String) -> String? {
    guard !root.isEmpty else { return nil }
    let oc = URL(fileURLWithPath: root).appendingPathComponent("EFI/OC")
    let fm = FileManager.default
    func stamp(_ url: URL) -> String? {
        guard let a = try? fm.attributesOfItem(atPath: url.path) else { return nil }
        let size = (a[.size] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value ?? -1
        let time = (a[.modificationDate] as? Date)?.timeIntervalSince1970 ?? 0
        return "\(url.path.dropFirst(oc.path.count))=\(size)@\(time)"
    }
    guard let config = stamp(oc.appendingPathComponent("config.plist")) else { return nil }
    var parts = [config]
    for sub in ["ACPI", "Kexts", "Drivers"] {
        let dir = oc.appendingPathComponent(sub)
        guard let walk = fm.enumerator(at: dir, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil) else { continue }
        var entries: [String] = []
        for case let url as URL in walk { if let s = stamp(url) { entries.append(s) } }
        parts += entries.sorted()
    }
    return parts.joined(separator: "\n")
}

/// A plan as efi.sh prints it. Its hash goes back to efi.sh with the command.
struct EFIPlan: Hashable {
    let text: String
    var hash: String { SHA256.hash(data: Data(text.utf8)).map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined() }
    var lines: [String] { text.split(separator: "\n").map(String.init) }
    var changes: Bool { lines.dropFirst().contains { !$0.hasPrefix("note ") && $0 != "nothing to change" } }
}

enum EFIAction: String, Identifiable {
    case mount, apply, settings, safari, settingsSafari, bootLog, bootLogOff, xeprobe, xeprobeOff, undo
    var id: String { rawValue }
    var argument: String {
        switch self {
        case .mount: return "--mount"
        case .apply: return "--apply"
        case .settings: return "--settings-apply"
        case .safari: return "--safari-apply"
        case .settingsSafari: return "--settings-safari-apply"
        case .bootLog: return "--bootlog-apply"
        case .bootLogOff: return "--bootlog-off-apply"
        case .xeprobe: return "--xeprobe-apply"
        case .xeprobeOff: return "--xeprobe-off-apply"
        case .undo: return "--undo"
        }
    }
    /// what the action's efi.sh command takes besides its argument: the GPU's device id for the XeProbe boot-arg
    func extraArguments(probeDevice: String?) -> [String] {
        self == .xeprobe ? ["--probe-device", probeDevice ?? ""] : []
    }
    var planArgument: String? {
        switch self {
        case .mount: return nil
        case .apply: return "--plan"
        case .settings: return "--settings-plan"
        case .safari: return "--safari-plan"
        case .settingsSafari: return "--settings-safari-plan"
        case .bootLog: return "--bootlog-plan"
        case .bootLogOff: return "--bootlog-off-plan"
        case .xeprobe: return "--xeprobe-plan"
        case .xeprobeOff: return "--xeprobe-off-plan"
        case .undo: return "--undo-plan"
        }
    }
}

/// The package's efi.sh, or the copy in this app when the package's is older than it (made before efi.sh, or before
/// the XeProbe boot-arg change and its probe_boot_arg status): the files still come from the package (--package), only the steps
/// are the newer script's. Each efi.sh reads the efi-rules.json beside it (the package's, or the one in this app's
/// Resources), never the other one's.
func efiScript(for package: Package) -> URL? {
    let own = package.directory.appendingPathComponent("efi.sh")
    if let text = try? String(contentsOf: own, encoding: .utf8), text.contains("--xeprobe-off-plan"), text.contains("probe_boot_arg=") { return own }
    return Bundle.main.url(forResource: "efi", withExtension: "sh") ?? (FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: own.path) ? own : nil)
}

/// efi.sh's command line, as words.
func efiWords(script: URL, package: Package, target: EFITarget, _ argument: String) -> [String] {
    ["/bin/bash", script.path, argument, "--package", package.directory.path] + target.arguments
}

func efiStatus(script: URL, package: Package, target: EFITarget) -> EFIStatus {
    let words = efiWords(script: script, package: package, target: target, "--status")
    return EFIStatus(text: commandOutput(words[0], Array(words.dropFirst()), seconds: 90) ?? "")
}

/// A plan, or nil when efi.sh could not make one (the EFI is not mounted, not OpenCore, ...). `extra`: more arguments
/// (--probe-device for the XeProbe boot-arg).
func efiPlan(script: URL, package: Package, target: EFITarget, _ argument: String, extra: [String] = []) -> EFIPlan? {
    let words = efiWords(script: script, package: package, target: target, argument) + extra
    guard let text = commandOutput(words[0], Array(words.dropFirst()), seconds: 90), text.hasPrefix("EFI: ") else { return nil }
    return EFIPlan(text: text)
}

/// What to say about the EFI after a driver action. Only when the EFI's IntelXe.kext is not this package's, or not on,
/// or could not be read.
enum EFINotice: Equatable {
    case kextDiffers, kextMissing, unchecked, removeKext

    static func after(_ action: DriverAction, status: EFIStatus) -> EFINotice? {
        switch action {
        case .install, .repair:
            switch status["kext_file"] {
            case "same": return ["enabled", "unknown", ""].contains(status["kext_entry"]) ? nil : .kextMissing
            case "different": return .kextDiffers
            case "absent": return .kextMissing
            default: return .unchecked
            }
        case .uninstall:
            return status["kext_entry"] == "enabled" || status["kext_entry"] == "unknown" || !status.known ? .removeKext : nil
        case .check, .undo:
            return nil
        }
    }
}

FILE: app/Sources/GPUTest.swift

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// A quick check of the GPU through Metal (about 15 s): does it compute and draw correctly, and are its compute rate,
// memory bandwidth, upload rate and round-trip latency where this card should be? A number far below says which part
// to look at (a low compute rate: the GPU or CPU clock; low uploads: the PCIe link or Resizable BAR). Then which video
// codecs macOS sees in hardware, with a short hardware-encode rate. Read only: nothing is installed or changed.
import CoreMedia
import CoreVideo
import Foundation
import IOKit
import Metal
import VideoToolbox

struct TestResult: Identifiable, Hashable {
    enum State { case good, warning, bad, info }
    let id = UUID()
    let title: String
    let value: String
    let state: State
    var help: String = ""
}

/// What the GPU test expects of one card (SupportedDevices.swift, generated from data/platforms.json "supported"): about
/// what it reaches, and the results at or above which the verdict is good, or fair (below: bad). measured: false when
/// the figures come from the card's specification, not from a run on one.
struct GPUTestExpectation {
    let name: String
    let measured: Bool
    let tflops, tflopsGood, tflopsFair: Double
    let memoryGBs, memoryGood, memoryFair: Double
}

/// "13", "11.5": a figure as the help texts give it.
private func figure(_ v: Double) -> String { v == v.rounded() ? String(format: "%.0f", v) : String(format: "%.1f", v) }

/// The PCI device id ("e20b") of the Intel card behind a registry entry: the IOPCIDevice at it or above it. nil when
/// there is none, or it is not Intel's.
func intelPCIDeviceID(registryID: UInt64) -> String? {
    guard registryID != 0 else { return nil }
    func id(_ e: io_registry_entry_t, _ key: String) -> String? {
        guard let d = IORegistryEntryCreateCFProperty(e, key as CFString, kCFAllocatorDefault, 0)?.takeRetainedValue() as? Data,
              d.count >= 2 else { return nil }
        return String(format: "%04x", UInt16(d[0]) | UInt16(d[1]) << 8)   // little-endian, as ioreg shows it
    }
    var entry = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IORegistryEntryIDMatching(registryID))
    for _ in 0..<8 where entry != 0 {
        if IOObjectConformsTo(entry, "IOPCIDevice") != 0 {
            let device = id(entry, "vendor-id") == "8086" ? id(entry, "device-id") : nil
            IOObjectRelease(entry)
            return device
        }
        var parent: io_registry_entry_t = 0
        let r = IORegistryEntryGetParentEntry(entry, kIOServicePlane, &parent)
        IOObjectRelease(entry)
        entry = r == KERN_SUCCESS ? parent : 0
    }
    if entry != 0 { IOObjectRelease(entry) }
    return nil
}

/// The expected rates for the card behind this Metal device, by its PCI device id: the PCI device above the device's
/// registry entry, or else the supported card the app found on the bus (supportedCardOnBus) when the Metal device
/// carries that card's name. nil (another GPU, or a card without figures): the numbers are shown without a verdict.
func gpuTestExpectation(for d: MTLDevice) -> GPUTestExpectation? {
    if let id = intelPCIDeviceID(registryID: d.registryID) { return gpuTestExpectations[id] }
    if let card = supportedCardOnBus(), d.name.contains(card.name) { return gpuTestExpectations[card.id] }
    return nil
}

private let kernels = """
#include <metal_stdlib>
using namespace metal;
kernel void vadd(device const float *a [[buffer(0)]], device const float *b [[buffer(1)]], device float *c [[buffer(2)]], uint i [[thread_position_in_grid]]) { c[i] = a[i] + b[i]; }
kernel void fma16(device float *o [[buffer(0)]], constant float &a [[buffer(1)]], uint g [[thread_position_in_grid]]) {
    float x0 = g, x1 = g + 1, x2 = g + 2, x3 = g + 3, x4 = g + 4, x5 = g + 5, x6 = g + 6, x7 = g + 7;
    float y0 = -x0, y1 = -x1, y2 = -x2, y3 = -x3, y4 = -x4, y5 = -x5, y6 = -x6, y7 = -x7;
    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++) {
        x0 = fma(x0, a, 0.001f); x1 = fma(x1, a, 0.001f); x2 = fma(x2, a, 0.001f); x3 = fma(x3, a, 0.001f);
        x4 = fma(x4, a, 0.001f); x5 = fma(x5, a, 0.001f); x6 = fma(x6, a, 0.001f); x7 = fma(x7, a, 0.001f);
        y0 = fma(y0, a, 0.001f); y1 = fma(y1, a, 0.001f); y2 = fma(y2, a, 0.001f); y3 = fma(y3, a, 0.001f);
        y4 = fma(y4, a, 0.001f); y5 = fma(y5, a, 0.001f); y6 = fma(y6, a, 0.001f); y7 = fma(y7, a, 0.001f); }
    o[g] = x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + y0 + y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6 + y7; }
kernel void copy4(device const float4 *a [[buffer(0)]], device float4 *b [[buffer(1)]], uint i [[thread_position_in_grid]]) { b[i] = a[i]; }
kernel void tiny(device uint *o [[buffer(0)]], uint i [[thread_position_in_grid]]) { if (i == 0) o[0] += 1; }
struct VOut { float4 p [[position]]; float4 c; };
vertex VOut tri(uint v [[vertex_id]]) { const float2 p[3] = { float2(-1, -1), float2(3, -1), float2(-1, 3) }; VOut o; o.p = float4(p[v], 0, 1); o.c = float4(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1); return o; }
fragment float4 col(VOut i [[stage_in]]) { return i.c; }
"""

/// GPU time of `body`'s command buffers, the best of `runs` after one warm-up.
private func gpuTime(_ q: MTLCommandQueue, runs: Int = 4, _ body: (MTLCommandBuffer) -> Void) -> Double {
    var best = Double.infinity
    for i in 0...runs {
        guard let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer() else { return .nan }
        body(cb); cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
        if i > 0, cb.status == .completed { best = min(best, cb.gpuEndTime - cb.gpuStartTime) }
    }
    return best
}

func runGPUTest(progress: @escaping (String) -> Void) -> [TestResult] {
    var out: [TestResult] = []
    guard let d = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice(), let q = d.makeCommandQueue() else {
        return [TestResult(title: String(localized: "Metal"), value: String(localized: "No Metal device"), state: .bad,
                           help: String(localized: "macOS runs without graphics acceleration. The System page and a diagnostics report say why."))]
    }
    out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Metal device"), value: d.name, state: .info))
    // the card's expected rates (SupportedDevices.swift); on another GPU the numbers are shown without a verdict
    let expect = gpuTestExpectation(for: d)
    func judged(_ r: TestResult) -> TestResult { expect != nil ? r : TestResult(title: r.title, value: r.value, state: .info) }
    let lib: MTLLibrary
    do { lib = try d.makeLibrary(source: kernels, options: nil) } catch {
        return out + [TestResult(title: String(localized: "Shader compiler"), value: String(localized: "Failed"), state: .bad, help: error.localizedDescription)]
    }
    func pso(_ n: String) -> MTLComputePipelineState? { lib.makeFunction(name: n).flatMap { try? d.makeComputePipelineState(function: $0) } }

    // 1. compute is correct
    progress(String(localized: "Compute…"))
    if let p = pso("vadd") {
        let n = 1 << 20
        let a = d.makeBuffer(length: n * 4, options: .storageModeShared)!, b = d.makeBuffer(length: n * 4, options: .storageModeShared)!
        let c = d.makeBuffer(length: n * 4, options: .storageModeShared)!
        let pa = a.contents().bindMemory(to: Float.self, capacity: n), pb = b.contents().bindMemory(to: Float.self, capacity: n)
        for i in 0..<n { pa[i] = Float(i); pb[i] = Float(i % 7) * 0.5 }
        let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer()!, e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder()!
        e.setComputePipelineState(p); e.setBuffer(a, offset: 0, index: 0); e.setBuffer(b, offset: 0, index: 1); e.setBuffer(c, offset: 0, index: 2)
        e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: n, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
        cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
        let pc = c.contents().bindMemory(to: Float.self, capacity: n)
        var bad = 0; for i in 0..<n where pc[i] != pa[i] + pb[i] { bad += 1 }
        out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Compute results"), value: bad == 0 ? String(localized: "Correct") : String(localized: "\(bad) of \(n) wrong"),
                              state: bad == 0 ? .good : .bad))
    }
    // 2. drawing is correct
    progress(String(localized: "Drawing…"))
    if let vf = lib.makeFunction(name: "tri"), let ff = lib.makeFunction(name: "col") {
        let rd = MTLRenderPipelineDescriptor(); rd.vertexFunction = vf; rd.fragmentFunction = ff; rd.colorAttachments[0].pixelFormat = .rgba8Unorm
        let td = MTLTextureDescriptor.texture2DDescriptor(pixelFormat: .rgba8Unorm, width: 256, height: 256, mipmapped: false)
        td.usage = [.renderTarget, .shaderRead]; td.storageMode = .managed
        if let rp = try? d.makeRenderPipelineState(descriptor: rd), let tex = d.makeTexture(descriptor: td) {
            let pass = MTLRenderPassDescriptor(); pass.colorAttachments[0].texture = tex; pass.colorAttachments[0].loadAction = .clear
            pass.colorAttachments[0].storeAction = .store; pass.colorAttachments[0].clearColor = MTLClearColor(red: 0, green: 0, blue: 0, alpha: 0)
            let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer()!, e = cb.makeRenderCommandEncoder(descriptor: pass)!
            e.setRenderPipelineState(rp); e.drawPrimitives(type: .triangle, vertexStart: 0, vertexCount: 3); e.endEncoding()
            let bl = cb.makeBlitCommandEncoder()!; bl.synchronize(resource: tex); bl.endEncoding()
            cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
            var px = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: 256 * 256 * 4)
            tex.getBytes(&px, bytesPerRow: 256 * 4, from: MTLRegionMake2D(0, 0, 256, 256), mipmapLevel: 0)
            var bad = 0
            for i in stride(from: 0, to: px.count, by: 4) where abs(Int(px[i]) - 64) > 2 || abs(Int(px[i + 1]) - 128) > 2 || abs(Int(px[i + 2]) - 191) > 2 || px[i + 3] != 255 { bad += 1 }
            out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Drawing results"), value: bad == 0 ? String(localized: "Correct") : String(localized: "\(bad) of 65536 pixels wrong"),
                                  state: bad == 0 ? .good : .bad))
        }
    }
    // the Metal features apps and games use, OpenGL, OpenCL, Vulkan (APITests.swift)
    out.append(contentsOf: runAPITests(progress: progress))
    // 3. compute rate (16 independent FMA chains per thread)
    progress(String(localized: "Compute rate…"))
    if let p = pso("fma16") {
        let n = 160 * 1024 * 16
        let o = d.makeBuffer(length: n * 4, options: .storageModePrivate)!
        var a: Float = 0.999
        // the GT clock rises from its 1200 MHz floor only under a steady load: half a second of it first
        let warm = Date().addingTimeInterval(0.5)
        while Date() < warm {
            guard let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer(), let e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder() else { break }
            e.setComputePipelineState(p); e.setBuffer(o, offset: 0, index: 0); e.setBytes(&a, length: 4, index: 1)
            e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: n, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
            cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
        }
        let t = gpuTime(q) { cb in
            let e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder()!; e.setComputePipelineState(p); e.setBuffer(o, offset: 0, index: 0); e.setBytes(&a, length: 4, index: 1)
            e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: n, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
        }
        let tf = Double(n) * 16 * 256 * 2 / t / 1e12
        if let e = expect {
            let help = e.measured
                ? String(localized: "An Arc \(e.name) reaches about \(figure(e.tflops)) TFLOP/s. Far less: the GPU clock is held low (power settings) or the CPU starves it (HybridPM).")
                : String(localized: "By its specification an Arc \(e.name) reaches about \(figure(e.tflops)) TFLOP/s (not measured on one yet). Far less: the GPU clock is held low (power settings) or the CPU starves it (HybridPM).")
            out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Compute rate (FP32)"), value: String(format: "%.1f TFLOP/s", tf),
                                  state: tf >= e.tflopsGood ? .good : tf >= e.tflopsFair ? .warning : .bad, help: tf >= e.tflopsGood ? "" : help))
        } else { out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Compute rate (FP32)"), value: String(format: "%.1f TFLOP/s", tf), state: .info)) }
    }
    // 4. memory bandwidth (VRAM to VRAM)
    progress(String(localized: "Memory bandwidth…"))
    if let p = pso("copy4") {
        let bytes = 256 << 20
        let a = d.makeBuffer(length: bytes, options: .storageModePrivate)!, b = d.makeBuffer(length: bytes, options: .storageModePrivate)!
        let t = gpuTime(q) { cb in
            let e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder()!; e.setComputePipelineState(p); e.setBuffer(a, offset: 0, index: 0); e.setBuffer(b, offset: 0, index: 1)
            e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: bytes / 16, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
        }
        let gbs = 2 * Double(bytes) / t / 1e9
        if let e = expect {
            let help = e.measured
                ? String(localized: "An Arc \(e.name)'s memory gives about \(figure(e.memoryGBs)) GB/s. Far less: the memory or GPU clock is held low.")
                : String(localized: "By its specification an Arc \(e.name)'s memory gives at most \(figure(e.memoryGBs)) GB/s (not measured on one yet). Far less: the memory or GPU clock is held low.")
            out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Memory bandwidth"), value: String(format: "%.0f GB/s", gbs),
                                  state: gbs >= e.memoryGood ? .good : gbs >= e.memoryFair ? .warning : .bad, help: gbs >= e.memoryGood ? "" : help))
        } else { out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Memory bandwidth"), value: String(format: "%.0f GB/s", gbs), state: .info)) }
    }
    // 5. upload (system memory to VRAM over PCIe)
    progress(String(localized: "Upload rate…"))
    do {
        let bytes = 256 << 20
        let s = d.makeBuffer(length: bytes, options: .storageModeShared)!, v = d.makeBuffer(length: bytes, options: .storageModePrivate)!
        let t = gpuTime(q) { cb in let bl = cb.makeBlitCommandEncoder()!; bl.copy(from: s, sourceOffset: 0, to: v, destinationOffset: 0, size: bytes); bl.endEncoding() }
        let gbs = Double(bytes) / t / 1e9
        out.append(judged(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Upload (PCIe)"), value: String(format: "%.1f GB/s", gbs), state: gbs >= 8 ? .good : gbs >= 3 ? .warning : .bad,
                              help: gbs >= 8 ? "" : String(localized: "The card's PCIe 4.0 x8 link moves about 12-14 GB/s. Far less: the link trained slower (slot, riser, BIOS PCIe setting)."))))
    }
    // 6. round trip: one tiny command buffer, committed and waited for
    progress(String(localized: "Latency…"))
    if let p = pso("tiny") {
        let o = d.makeBuffer(length: 64, options: .storageModePrivate)!
        var ts: [Double] = []
        for _ in 0..<64 {
            let t0 = CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent()
            let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer()!, e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder()!
            e.setComputePipelineState(p); e.setBuffer(o, offset: 0, index: 0)
            e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: 64, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 64, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
            cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
            ts.append((CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() - t0) * 1e6)
        }
        let med = ts.sorted()[ts.count / 2]
        out.append(judged(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Round trip"), value: String(format: "%.0f µs", med), state: med <= 200 ? .good : med <= 600 ? .warning : .bad,
                              help: med <= 200 ? "" : String(localized: "One small job, sent and waited for, takes about 60 µs on the test machine. Much more: the GPU idles at a low clock between jobs."))))
    }
    progress(String(localized: "Video…"))
    out.append(contentsOf: videoCheck().map(judged))
    out.append(contentsOf: runVideoTests(progress: progress).map(judged))   // VideoTest.swift
    return out
}

// MARK: - video

private func videoCheck() -> [TestResult] {
    var out: [TestResult] = []
    let codecs: [(String, CMVideoCodecType)] = [("H.264", kCMVideoCodecType_H264), ("HEVC", kCMVideoCodecType_HEVC),
                                                ("AV1", kCMVideoCodecType_AV1), ("VP9", kCMVideoCodecType_VP9)]
    var decode: [String] = []
    for (name, c) in codecs where VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(c) { decode.append(name) }
    out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Hardware video decode"), value: decode.isEmpty ? String(localized: "None") : decode.joined(separator: ", "),
                          state: decode.count >= 3 ? .good : decode.isEmpty ? .bad : .warning,
                          help: decode.count >= 3 ? "" : String(localized: "The driver decodes H.264, HEVC, AV1 and VP9 on the card. Missing ones: the VideoToolbox components are not installed or did not load.")))
    var encoders: [String] = []
    var list: CFArray?
    if VTCopyVideoEncoderList(nil, &list) == noErr, let items = list as? [[String: Any]] {
        for item in items where (item[kVTVideoEncoderList_IsHardwareAccelerated as String] as? Bool) == true {
            // the main codecs only, by codec type (Apple Silicon lists ProRes, depth and alpha variants too)
            let type = (item[kVTVideoEncoderList_CodecType as String] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? 0
            let names: [CMVideoCodecType: String] = [kCMVideoCodecType_H264: "H.264", kCMVideoCodecType_HEVC: "HEVC", kCMVideoCodecType_AV1: "AV1"]
            if let n = names[type], !encoders.contains(n) { encoders.append(n) }
        }
    }
    out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Hardware video encoders"), value: encoders.isEmpty ? String(localized: "None") : encoders.joined(separator: ", "),
                          state: encoders.isEmpty ? .warning : .good))
    return out
}
