// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Problems the app can see by itself at start, the same ones the diagnostics report warns about (collect-macos.sh's
// codes): a kernel panic since the last look, the boot guard holding acceleration off, a system-volume copy of the Metal
// plugin out of step with /Library, a half-done HiDPI switch, a kext loaded at another version than its file, a hybrid
// Intel CPU without HybridPM, HybridPM loaded but off. Each shows as a banner with what to do; a dismissed one stays quiet until it changes.
import Foundation

struct HealthIssue: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let code: String
    let text: String
    /// what changes when the issue is a new one (a panic file's name, a version): a dismissal holds for this key only
    let key: String
    var id: String { code }
}

private func sha256Prefix(_ path: String) -> String? {
    guard let out = commandOutput("/usr/bin/shasum", ["-a", "256", path]) else { return nil }
    let s = out.split(separator: " ").first.map(String.init) ?? ""
    return s.count >= 16 ? String(s.prefix(16)) : nil
}

private func plistValue(_ path: String, _ key: String) -> String? {
    guard let d = NSDictionary(contentsOfFile: path) else { return nil }
    return d[key] as? String
}

/// 12th-14th gen Core with efficiency cores, by the CPU's name (machdep.cpu.model is what OpenCore's Cpuid1Data makes it):
/// i3/i5/i7/i9-12xxx..14xxx, without Core Ultra (HybridPM leaves it alone) and the desktop models with P-cores only. The
/// same list as efi.sh and the diagnostics report.
func hybridCPU(_ brand: String) -> Bool {
    brand.range(of: #"\bi[3579]-1[2-4]([0-9]{3}|[0-9]{2}[UP])"#, options: .regularExpression) != nil
        && brand.range(of: #"Ultra|i3-1[234]100|i3-12300|i5-12400|i5-12490|i5-12500(?!H)|i5-12600(?![KH])"#, options: .regularExpression) == nil
}

func healthIssues(_ facts: SystemFacts) -> [HealthIssue] {
    var list: [HealthIssue] = []
    let fm = FileManager.default
    // a kernel panic report from the boot before this one (macOS writes it during the boot after the panic)
    let dr = "/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports"
    var newest: (String, Date)? = nil
    for dir in [dr, dr + "/Retired"] {
        for name in (try? fm.contentsOfDirectory(atPath: dir)) ?? [] where name.hasSuffix(".panic") && !name.hasPrefix(".") {
            let p = dir + "/" + name
            if let m = (try? fm.attributesOfItem(atPath: p))?[.modificationDate] as? Date, m > (newest?.1 ?? .distantPast) { newest = (name, m) }
        }
    }
    // only a report written during this boot is about the boot before it: an older one (still on disk for days) would
    // otherwise be reported after every normal restart (14 Nov 2026: a panic at 01:00 shown after every restart that day)
    if let (name, date) = newest, let boot = bootTime(), date >= boot.addingTimeInterval(-5) {
        let f = DateFormatter(); f.dateStyle = .medium; f.timeStyle = .short
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "panics", text: String(localized: "macOS restarted after a kernel panic (\(f.string(from: date))). A diagnostics report holds its text."), key: name))
    }
    if facts.bootGuardOff {
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "accel-off", text: facts.bootGuard.firmwareDisplay
            ? String(localized: "The boot guard holds acceleration off: earlier boots did not reach a healthy desktop, and this one runs on the firmware framebuffer. Clear it once you know why.")
            : String(localized: "The boot guard holds acceleration off: earlier boots did not reach a healthy desktop. Clear it once you know why."), key: "on"))
    }
    let ssv = "/System/Library/Extensions/NVMTLDriver.bundle", mark = "/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/ssv-component.plist"
    let ssvMesa = sha256Prefix(ssv + "/Contents/Frameworks/nvmtl/libvulkan_intel.dylib")
    let libMesa = sha256Prefix("/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libvulkan_intel.dylib")
    // this package's copy waits in a new boot snapshot (ssv-install.sh --apply records its Mesa): the restart is all
    let pendingMesa = plistValue(mark, "mesa").map { String($0.prefix(16)) }
    let ssvPending = pendingMesa != nil && pendingMesa == libMesa && pendingMesa != ssvMesa
    if fm.fileExists(atPath: ssv) && fm.fileExists(atPath: useLibraryFlag) && ssvMesa != nil && ssvMesa == libMesa {
        // the copy is the /Library part's, but NMXAccel is told to load the /Library copy: Safari draws in software
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "ssv-use-library", text: useLibraryMadeByInstall() == true
            ? String(localized: "The system-volume copy of the Metal driver is this release's, but NVMTLDriver.use-library, which install.sh made for an older copy, still makes every process use the /Library copy, and Safari draws in software. Use the system-volume copy on the Driver page, then restart.")
            : String(localized: "The system-volume copy of the Metal driver is this release's, but /Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.use-library makes every process use the /Library copy, and Safari draws in software. Remove it on the Driver page (Use the system-volume copy) if you did not make it on purpose."), key: ssvMesa ?? "use"))
    } else if ssvPending {
        // nothing to do but restart (the app's restart banner says so after its own install)
    } else if fm.fileExists(atPath: ssv) && !fm.fileExists(atPath: useLibraryFlag) {
        if let a = ssvMesa, let b = libMesa, a != b {
            list.append(HealthIssue(code: "ssv-mesa", text: String(localized: "The system-volume copy of the Metal driver is older than the rest of the install, and WindowServer uses it. Install the package's system-volume copy too (system-volume/ssv-install.sh --apply) and restart."), key: a + b))
        }
    } else if !fm.fileExists(atPath: ssv) && fm.fileExists(atPath: mark) {
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "ssv-gone", text: String(localized: "The system-volume copy of the Metal driver is gone (a macOS update replaces the system volume). Install it again, or use the /Library copy."), key: plistValue(mark, "build") ?? "gone"))
    }
    let nv = commandOutput("/usr/sbin/nvram", ["intelxefb-hidpi"]) ?? ""
    let hidpiOn = nv.contains("\t1")
    let ws = (CFPreferencesCopyValue("DisplayResolutionEnabled" as CFString, "/Library/Preferences/com.apple.windowserver" as CFString,
                                     kCFPreferencesAnyUser, kCFPreferencesCurrentHost) as? Bool) ?? ((NSDictionary(contentsOfFile: "/Library/Preferences/com.apple.windowserver.plist")?["DisplayResolutionEnabled"] as? Bool) ?? false)
    var ours = 0
    if let e = fm.enumerator(atPath: "/Library/Displays/Contents/Resources/Overrides") {
        for case let rel as String in e {
            let p = "/Library/Displays/Contents/Resources/Overrides/" + rel
            if NSDictionary(contentsOfFile: p)?["IntelXeHiDPI"] != nil { ours += 1 }
        }
    }
    if hidpiOn && (ours == 0 || !ws) {
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "hidpi-half", text: String(localized: "The HiDPI switch is only half on. Turn it on again on the Display page, then restart."), key: "\(ours)\(ws)"))
    } else if !hidpiOn && ours > 0 {
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "hidpi-stale", text: String(localized: "A HiDPI display override is left without the framebuffer's HiDPI modes. Turn HiDPI off or on again on the Display page."), key: "\(ours)"))
    }
    let loaded = commandOutput("/usr/bin/kmutil", ["showloaded", "--list-only"], seconds: 30) ?? ""
    for (kext, id) in [("IntelXeFB", "io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB"), ("NMXAccel", "com.nullmoth.NMXAccel"), ("NMXAGDC", "com.nullmoth.NMXAGDC")] {
        guard let line = loaded.split(separator: "\n").first(where: { $0.contains(id + " ") }),
              let open = line.firstIndex(of: "("), let close = line[open...].firstIndex(of: ")") else { continue }
        let lv = String(line[line.index(after: open)..<close])
        if let fv = plistValue("/Library/Extensions/\(kext).kext/Contents/Info.plist", "CFBundleShortVersionString"), fv != lv {
            list.append(HealthIssue(code: "kext-version", text: String(localized: "\(kext).kext \(lv) is loaded, but \(fv) is installed. Restart; if it stays, run Install this package again."), key: lv + fv))
            break
        }
    }
    // installed in /Library but not loaded while IntelXe.kext (from the EFI) is: the Auxiliary Kernel Collection was not
    // rebuilt for this macOS (an update), or the restart after an install has not happened yet
    if facts.kextLoaded && fm.fileExists(atPath: "/Library/Extensions/IntelXeFB.kext") && !loaded.contains("io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB ") {
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "kexts-not-loaded", text: String(localized: "IntelXeFB.kext is installed but not loaded. After a macOS update the Auxiliary Kernel Collection needs rebuilding: install this package again on the Driver page, then restart. Right after an install, just restart."), key: sysctlString("kern.osversion") ?? "on"))
    }
    list += osUpdateIssues(facts)
    let brand = commandOutput("/usr/sbin/sysctl", ["-n", "machdep.cpu.brand_string"]) ?? ""
    if !loaded.lowercased().contains("hybridpm") {
        if hybridCPU(brand) {
            list.append(HealthIssue(code: "cpu-hybridpm", text: String(localized: "This CPU has performance and efficiency cores (12th-14th gen Core) and HybridPM.kext is not loaded: macOS can hold the cores at low clocks, which makes the GPU look slow too. Add HybridPM.kext from the -efi.zip below Lilu in your EFI (the EFI page does it; install guide: Hybrid Intel CPUs)."), key: "on"))
        }
    } else if commandOutput("/usr/sbin/sysctl", ["-n", "debug.hybridpm.enabled"])?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) == "0" {
        // loaded but not converting: an unsupported CPU, or a macOS whose XCPM routine it does not find (before 20 s after
        // boot it is still waiting, which the reason says)
        let why = commandOutput("/usr/sbin/sysctl", ["-n", "debug.hybridpm.why"])?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
        if !why.contains("waiting") && !why.contains("routed: on 20 s") {
            list.append(HealthIssue(code: "hybridpm-off", text: String(localized: "HybridPM.kext is loaded but does nothing: \(why.isEmpty ? "–" : why)."), key: why))
        }
    }
    return list
}

/// The macOS update guard's warnings (OSUpdate.swift): a macOS update on offer that the installed driver does not support
/// (its macOS major version differs), and a result of the guard's check after an update that needs the user.
func osUpdateIssues(_ facts: SystemFacts) -> [HealthIssue] {
    guard facts.installedVersion != nil else { return [] }
    var list: [HealthIssue] = []
    let record = NSDictionary(contentsOfFile: softwareUpdatePlist) as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
    if let other = offeredMacOSUpdates(record).first(where: { supportByMajor($0.version, packageMajor: facts.macOSMajor) == .no }) {
        list.append(HealthIssue(code: "osupdate-unsupported", text: String(localized: "\(other.title) is offered, and the installed driver does not support it: after that update the Arc card would show no desktop. Wait for a release that supports it."), key: other.version))
    }
    if let text = try? String(contentsOfFile: osUpdateDirectory + "/result", encoding: .utf8) {
        var v = keyValues(text)
        let result = v["result"] ?? ""
        if ["unsupported", "efi-kext", "gave-up", "refused", "retrying"].contains(result) {
            for (k, value) in v { v["last_" + k] = value }
            list.append(HealthIssue(code: "osupdate-result", text: osUpdateResultText(result, v), key: v["when"] ?? result))
        }
    }
    return list
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Runs the package's own scripts. The app decides nothing about what is copied where: install.sh does, so a change made in
// Terminal and one made here are the same change. EFI files are never touched.
import Foundation

/// A shell word: the whole text, quoted for /bin/sh.
func shellQuoted(_ text: String) -> String { "'" + text.replacingOccurrences(of: "'", with: "'\\''") + "'" }

/// Text for a double-quoted AppleScript string.
func appleScriptQuoted(_ text: String) -> String {
    text.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\", with: "\\\\").replacingOccurrences(of: "\"", with: "\\\"")
}

/// The AppleScript that runs this command as root with its output in a log file: macOS asks for the password.
func privilegedScript(command: String, log: String, prompt: String) -> String {
    let shell = "/bin/bash -c \(shellQuoted(command)) >> \(shellQuoted(log)) 2>&1"
    return "do shell script \"\(appleScriptQuoted(shell))\" with prompt \"\(appleScriptQuoted(prompt))\" with administrator privileges"
}

struct RunResult {
    let succeeded: Bool
    let cancelled: Bool
    let message: String
}

/// `needsRoot`: through the macOS password dialog. Blocks: call it off the main thread.
func run(command: String, needsRoot: Bool, log: URL, prompt: String) -> RunResult {
    FileManager.default.createFile(atPath: log.path, contents: nil)
    let process = Process()
    let errors = Pipe()
    process.standardError = errors
    process.standardOutput = Pipe()
    if needsRoot && ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["INTELXE_MANAGER_TEST_NO_ROOT"] == nil {
        process.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/bin/osascript")
        process.arguments = ["-e", privilegedScript(command: command, log: log.path, prompt: prompt)]
    } else {
        process.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "/bin/bash")
        process.arguments = ["-c", "(\(command)) >> \(shellQuoted(log.path)) 2>&1"]
    }
    do { try process.run() } catch { return RunResult(succeeded: false, cancelled: false, message: error.localizedDescription) }
    let data = errors.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()
    process.waitUntilExit()
    let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
    return RunResult(succeeded: process.terminationStatus == 0, cancelled: text.contains("-128"), message: text)
}

enum DriverAction: String, CaseIterable, Identifiable {
    case check, install, repair, undo, uninstall
    var id: String { rawValue }
    var argument: String {
        switch self {
        case .check: return "--check"
        case .install: return "--apply"
        case .repair: return "--repair"
        case .undo: return "--undo"
        case .uninstall: return "--uninstall"
        }
    }
    var needsRoot: Bool { self != .check }
    var needsReboot: Bool { self != .check }
}

/// Which package a download or a chosen folder is for.
enum PackageKind { case driver, zink, vulkan }

/// vulkan/install.sh: the optional Vulkan provider for games (experimental).
enum VulkanAction: String, Identifiable {
    case install, undo, test
    var id: String { rawValue }
    var arguments: String {
        switch self {
        case .install: return ""
        case .undo: return "--undo"
        case .test: return "--test"
        }
    }
    var needsRoot: Bool { self != .test }
}

enum ZinkAction: String, Identifiable {
    case install, undo, globalOn, globalOff, glOn, glOff, test
    var id: String { rawValue }
    var arguments: String {
        switch self {
        case .install: return ""
        case .undo: return "--undo"
        case .globalOn: return "--global on"
        case .globalOff: return "--global off"
        case .glOn: return "--global-gl on"
        case .glOff: return "--global-gl off"
        case .test: return "--test"
        }
    }
    var needsRoot: Bool { self != .test }
}

/// zink-gl/install.sh --global-gl off without the package: the LaunchAgent goes, and the logged-in user's session stops
/// inserting the boot library into applications started from now on.
func cglzinkGlobalOffCommand() -> String {
    "rm -f \(shellQuoted(cglzinkGlobalAgent)); u=$(stat -f %Su /dev/console); if [ -n \"$u\" ] && [ \"$u\" != root ]; then "
        + "case \"$(launchctl asuser \"$(id -u \"$u\")\" launchctl getenv DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES)\" in *libcglzink-boot*) "
        + "launchctl asuser \"$(id -u \"$u\")\" launchctl unsetenv DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES ;; esac; fi; echo off"
}

/// zink-gl/install.sh --global on|off without the package (it is only needed to install): the same LaunchAgent, which
/// sets JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS at every login, and the same variable for the user logged in now.
func zinkGlobalCommand(on: Bool) -> String {
    let gl = "/Library/IntelXe/GL"
    let options = "-Dorg.lwjgl.glfw.libname=\(gl)/libglfw.3.dylib -Dorg.lwjgl.opengl.libname=\(gl)/libGLzink.dylib"
    let agent = shellQuoted(zinkAgent), domain = shellQuoted(String(zinkAgent.dropLast(6)))
    let user = "u=$(stat -f %Su /dev/console); "
    if !on {
        return "rm -f \(agent); " + user + "if [ -n \"$u\" ] && [ \"$u\" != root ]; then launchctl asuser \"$(id -u \"$u\")\" launchctl unsetenv JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS; fi; echo off"
    }
    return "set -e; [ -d \(gl) ] || { echo 'Zink is not installed'; exit 1; }; rm -f \(agent); "
        + "defaults write \(domain) Label -string io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.zink-gl; "
        + "defaults write \(domain) ProgramArguments -array /bin/launchctl setenv JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS \(shellQuoted(options)); "
        + "defaults write \(domain) RunAtLoad -bool true; chown root:wheel \(agent); chmod 644 \(agent); plutil -convert xml1 \(agent); "
        + user + "if [ -n \"$u\" ] && [ \"$u\" != root ]; then launchctl asuser \"$(id -u \"$u\")\" launchctl setenv JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS \(shellQuoted(options)); fi; echo on"
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The steps of an install.sh run (install, repair, undo, uninstall), read from what install.sh prints as it works:
// each step begins at a line install.sh writes (its "== ..." headings and "ok" lines), so the list follows the script
// and nothing here guesses at timing. The full output stays one click away.
import SwiftUI

struct DriverRun: Equatable {
    let action: DriverAction
    /// where this run's output begins in Manager.log
    let logStart: Int
    let start = Date()
    var end: Date?
    var finished = false
    var succeeded = false
    var cancelled = false
    var dismissed = false
}

struct InstallStep {
    let title: String
    /// output that shows the step has begun; empty = begun from the start
    let marker: String
}

extension DriverAction {
    /// install.sh's steps for this action, in order (none for the check, which takes seconds)
    var steps: [InstallStep] {
        let rootPrompt = InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Administrator password"), marker: "")
        let checks = InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Check the system and the package"), marker: "== intel-gpu-macos-driver")
        let rebuild = InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Rebuild the Auxiliary Kernel Collection (a few minutes)"), marker: "== rebuilding the Auxiliary Kernel Collection")
        switch self {
        case .check: return []
        case .install:
            return [rootPrompt, checks,
                    InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Back up what it replaces"), marker: "== 0 problem(s)"),
                    InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Copy the kexts into /Library/Extensions"), marker: "== backup:"),
                    InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Copy the Metal driver into /Library/GPUBundles"), marker: "GPUBundles/NVMTLDriverLib.bundle"),
                    rebuild]
        case .repair:
            return [rootPrompt, checks, InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Put back the files that differ"), marker: "== 0 problem(s)"), rebuild]
        case .undo:
            return [rootPrompt, InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Restore the last backup"), marker: "== restoring"), rebuild]
        case .uninstall:
            return [rootPrompt, InstallStep(title: String(localized: "Remove the driver's files"), marker: "ok    removed"), rebuild]
        }
    }
}

enum StepState { case pending, running, done, skipped, failed }

/// Each step's state from the run's output so far: the last step that has begun is the one running (or the one that
/// failed); earlier ones are done, or skipped when their line never came (a repair without kexts rebuilds nothing).
func stepStates(_ steps: [InstallStep], output: String, run: DriverRun) -> [StepState] {
    let begun = steps.map { $0.marker.isEmpty || output.contains($0.marker) }
    let last = begun.lastIndex(of: true) ?? 0
    return steps.indices.map { i in
        if run.finished && run.succeeded { return begun[i] ? .done : .skipped }
        if i < last { return begun[i] ? .done : .skipped }
        if i == last { return run.finished ? .failed : .running }
        return run.finished ? .skipped : .pending
    }
}

/// The step list with checkmarks, the elapsed time, how it ended, and the run's whole output in a disclosure group.
struct DriverRunView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var manager: Manager
    let run: DriverRun
    var closable = false
    @StateObject private var showLog = Flag()

    var body: some View {
        let output = String(manager.log.dropFirst(run.logStart))
        let steps = run.action.steps
        let states = stepStates(steps, output: output, run: run)
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
            HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline) {
                Text(run.action.title).font(.headline)
                Spacer()
                TimelineView(.periodic(from: run.start, by: 1)) { context in
                    Text(elapsed(to: run.end ?? context.date)).font(.callout.monospacedDigit()).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
                if closable && run.finished {
                    Button { manager.driverRun?.dismissed = true } label: { Image(systemName: "xmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.secondary) }
                        .buttonStyle(.borderless).help(Text("Close")).accessibilityLabel(Text("Close"))
                }
            }
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
                ForEach(steps.indices, id: \.self) { i in
                    HStack(spacing: 8) {
                        icon(states[i]).frame(width: 18, height: 16)
                        Text(steps[i].title)
                            .foregroundStyle(states[i] == .pending || states[i] == .skipped ? .secondary : .primary)
                            .fontWeight(states[i] == .running ? .semibold : .regular)
                    }
                    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.25), value: states[i])
                }
            }
            if run.finished {
                Label(resultText, systemImage: run.succeeded ? "checkmark.seal.fill" : run.cancelled ? "xmark.circle" : "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
                    .foregroundStyle(run.succeeded ? Color.green : run.cancelled ? Color.secondary : Color.red)
            }
            DisclosureGroup(isExpanded: $showLog.on) {
                ScrollView {
                    Text(output.isEmpty ? String(localized: "Nothing yet.") : output)
                        .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
                        .textSelection(.enabled)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                        .padding(6)
                }
                .frame(height: 150)
                .defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom)
                .background(Color.primary.opacity(0.05), in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6))
            } label: {
                Text("Full log").font(.callout)
            }
        }
    }

    var resultText: String {
        if run.cancelled { return String(localized: "Cancelled. Nothing changed.") }
        if !run.succeeded { return String(localized: "It did not finish. See the log.") }
        return run.action.needsReboot ? String(localized: "Finished. Restart to use the change.") : String(localized: "Finished.")
    }

    @ViewBuilder func icon(_ state: StepState) -> some View {
        switch state {
        case .pending: Image(systemName: "circle").foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
        case .running: ProgressView().controlSize(.small).scaleEffect(0.8)
        case .done: Image(systemName: "checkmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.green)
        case .skipped: Image(systemName: "minus.circle").foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
        case .failed: Image(systemName: "xmark.circle.fill").foregroundStyle(.red)
        }
    }

    func elapsed(to date: Date) -> String {
        let s = max(0, Int(date.timeIntervalSince(run.start)))
        return String(format: "%d:%02d", s / 60, s % 60)
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The check at login: a LaunchAgent in the user's own ~/Library/LaunchAgents starts this app with --login-check once per
// login. It looks for what the start-up warnings look for (healthIssues: a system-volume copy that a macOS update
// removed, the boot guard holding acceleration off, a kext at another version, a recent panic...) and, only when there
// is something, shows one dialog; then it quits. Nothing runs as root and nothing is changed: fixing is the app's job,
// which the dialog opens. Off unless turned on (Power and app page, or the Driver page's Safari section).
import AppKit
import Foundation

let loginCheckLabel = "io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeManager.login-check"
var loginCheckAgent: URL {
    FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent("Library/LaunchAgents/\(loginCheckLabel).plist")
}

func loginCheckEnabled() -> Bool { FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: loginCheckAgent.path) }

/// Writes or removes the agent. It takes effect at the next login (nothing is started now).
func setLoginCheck(_ on: Bool) {
    if !on { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: loginCheckAgent); return }
    guard let binary = Bundle.main.executablePath else { return }
    let plist: [String: Any] = [
        "Label": loginCheckLabel,
        "ProgramArguments": [binary, "--login-check"],
        "RunAtLoad": true,
        "LimitLoadToSessionType": "Aqua",
        "ProcessType": "Interactive",
    ]
    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: loginCheckAgent.deletingLastPathComponent(), withIntermediateDirectories: true)
    if let data = try? PropertyListSerialization.data(fromPropertyList: plist, format: .xml, options: 0) { try? data.write(to: loginCheckAgent) }
}

/// The app was moved or updated in another place: point the agent at this copy.
func refreshLoginCheckPath() {
    guard loginCheckEnabled(), let binary = Bundle.main.executablePath,
          let d = NSDictionary(contentsOf: loginCheckAgent), let args = d["ProgramArguments"] as? [String], args.first != binary else { return }
    setLoginCheck(true)
}

/// --login-check: runs without a window. Waits for the desktop to settle, checks, shows at most one dialog.
func runLoginCheck() {
    Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 20)
    let facts = SystemFacts.probe()
    let dismissed = UserDefaults.standard.dictionary(forKey: "healthDismissed") as? [String: String] ?? [:]
    let issues = healthIssues(facts).filter { dismissed[$0.code] != $0.key }
    guard !issues.isEmpty else { return }
    let app = NSApplication.shared
    app.setActivationPolicy(.accessory)
    app.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true)
    let alert = NSAlert()
    alert.messageText = issues.count == 1 ? String(localized: "IntelXe Manager: one thing needs attention")
                                          : String(localized: "IntelXe Manager: \(issues.count) things need attention")
    alert.informativeText = issues.map { "• " + $0.text }.joined(separator: "\n\n")
    alert.addButton(withTitle: String(localized: "Open IntelXe Manager"))
    alert.addButton(withTitle: String(localized: "Later"))
    alert.addButton(withTitle: String(localized: "Don't remind me of these"))
    switch alert.runModal() {
    case .alertFirstButtonReturn:
        let config = NSWorkspace.OpenConfiguration()
        config.createsNewApplicationInstance = true
        config.arguments = ["--section", issues.contains { $0.code.hasPrefix("ssv") || $0.code.hasPrefix("kext") } ? "driver" : "system"]
        let done = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
        NSWorkspace.shared.openApplication(at: Bundle.main.bundleURL, configuration: config) { _, _ in done.signal() }
        _ = done.wait(timeout: .now() + 10)
    case .alertThirdButtonReturn:
        var d = dismissed
        for i in issues { d[i.code] = i.key }
        UserDefaults.standard.set(d, forKey: "healthDismissed")
    default: break
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The long GPU test (about two minutes). Video memory: most of it in 512 MB buffers is filled by the GPU with a pattern
// made from each word's address, checked by the GPU, then filled with the inverse and checked again (a bad memory cell,
// a wrong mapping or a write that lands elsewhere shows as mismatches). Stability: a minute of full compute load while
// the GT clock and temperatures are sampled (debug.intelxe.sensors), watching for failed command buffers (a GPU reset)
// and for the clock falling under load (thermal or power throttling).
import Foundation
import Metal

private let memShaders = """
#include <metal_stdlib>
using namespace metal;
static inline uint pat(uint i, uint seed) { uint x = i * 2654435761u ^ seed; x ^= x >> 13; x *= 0x5bd1e995u; return x ^ (x >> 15); }
kernel void fillp(device uint *b [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &seed [[buffer(1)]], uint i [[thread_position_in_grid]]) { b[i] = pat(i, seed); }
kernel void checkp(device const uint *b [[buffer(0)]], constant uint &seed [[buffer(1)]], device atomic_uint *bad [[buffer(2)]],
                   uint i [[thread_position_in_grid]], uint lane [[thread_index_in_simdgroup]]) {
    const uint m = b[i] != pat(i, seed) ? 1u : 0u; const uint s = simd_sum(m);
    if (lane == 0 && s) atomic_fetch_add_explicit(bad, s, memory_order_relaxed);
}
kernel void burn(device float *o [[buffer(0)]], uint g [[thread_position_in_grid]]) {
    float a = g, b = g + 1, c = g + 2, d = g + 3;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4096; i++) { a = fma(a, 0.9999f, 0.001f); b = fma(b, 0.9999f, 0.001f); c = fma(c, 0.9999f, 0.001f); d = fma(d, 0.9999f, 0.001f); }
    o[g] = a + b + c + d;
}
"""

func runLongTest(progress: @escaping (String) -> Void) -> [TestResult] {
    var out: [TestResult] = []
    guard let d = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice(), let q = d.makeCommandQueue(), let lib = try? d.makeLibrary(source: memShaders, options: nil) else {
        return [TestResult(title: "Metal", value: String(localized: "No Metal device"), state: .bad)]
    }
    func cps(_ n: String) -> MTLComputePipelineState? { lib.makeFunction(name: n).flatMap { try? d.makeComputePipelineState(function: $0) } }
    guard let fill = cps("fillp"), let check = cps("checkp"), let burn = cps("burn") else { return out }

    // 1. video memory
    let chunk = 512 << 20, words = chunk / 4
    // XE_LONGTEST_GB / XE_LONGTEST_SECONDS: a shorter run (for checking the test itself)
    let env = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
    let budget = env["XE_LONGTEST_GB"].flatMap(Int.init).map { $0 << 30 } ?? min(Int(Double(d.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize) * 0.8), 10 << 30)
    let seconds = env["XE_LONGTEST_SECONDS"].flatMap(Double.init) ?? 60
    var bufs: [MTLBuffer] = []
    while bufs.count * chunk + chunk <= budget, let b = d.makeBuffer(length: chunk, options: .storageModePrivate) { bufs.append(b) }
    let bad = d.makeBuffer(length: 4, options: .storageModeShared)!
    bad.contents().storeBytes(of: UInt32(0), as: UInt32.self)
    var failed = false
    let seeds: [UInt32] = [0x1234_5678, ~UInt32(0x1234_5678)]
    for (pass, seed) in seeds.enumerated() {
        progress(String(localized: "Video memory, pass \(pass + 1) of 2…"))
        for (k, b) in bufs.enumerated() {
            var s = seed &+ UInt32(k)
            guard let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer(), let e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder() else { failed = true; break }
            e.setComputePipelineState(fill); e.setBuffer(b, offset: 0, index: 0); e.setBytes(&s, length: 4, index: 1)
            e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: words, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
            cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted(); if cb.status != .completed { failed = true }
        }
        for (k, b) in bufs.enumerated() {
            var s = seed &+ UInt32(k)
            guard let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer(), let e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder() else { failed = true; break }
            e.setComputePipelineState(check); e.setBuffer(b, offset: 0, index: 0); e.setBytes(&s, length: 4, index: 1); e.setBuffer(bad, offset: 0, index: 2)
            e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: words, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
            cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted(); if cb.status != .completed { failed = true }
        }
    }
    let errors = bad.contents().load(as: UInt32.self)
    let gb = Double(bufs.count * chunk) / Double(1 << 30)
    out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Video memory"),
                          value: failed ? String(localized: "The GPU stopped during the test") : errors == 0 ? String(format: String(localized: "%.1f GB tested twice, no errors"), gb)
                                 : String(format: String(localized: "%.1f GB tested, %u words wrong"), gb, errors),
                          state: failed || errors > 0 ? .bad : .good,
                          help: failed || errors > 0 ? String(localized: "Wrong words in video memory point at the card (memory, overclock, heat) or at how the driver maps it; a report helps tell them apart.") : ""))
    bufs = []

    // 2. a minute of full load
    let o = d.makeBuffer(length: 160 * 1024 * 16 * 4, options: .storageModePrivate)!
    var clocks: [Int] = [], temps: [Int] = [], errorsLoad = 0
    let t0 = Date(); var lastSample = Date.distantPast
    while Date().timeIntervalSince(t0) < seconds {
        if Date().timeIntervalSince(lastSample) >= 1 {
            lastSample = Date()
            progress(String(localized: "Load, \(Int(Date().timeIntervalSince(t0))) of \(Int(seconds)) s…"))
            if let s = sysctlString("debug.intelxe.sensors"), s.hasPrefix("act") {
                let parts = s.split(separator: " ")
                if let i = parts.firstIndex(of: "act"), i + 1 < parts.count, let v = Int(parts[i + 1]) { clocks.append(v) }
                if let i = parts.firstIndex(of: "package"), i + 1 < parts.count, let v = Int(parts[i + 1]) { temps.append(v) }
            }
        }
        guard let cb = q.makeCommandBuffer(), let e = cb.makeComputeCommandEncoder() else { errorsLoad += 1; break }
        e.setComputePipelineState(burn); e.setBuffer(o, offset: 0, index: 0)
        e.dispatchThreads(MTLSize(width: 160 * 1024 * 16, height: 1, depth: 1), threadsPerThreadgroup: MTLSize(width: 256, height: 1, depth: 1)); e.endEncoding()
        cb.commit(); cb.waitUntilCompleted()
        if cb.status != .completed { errorsLoad += 1 }
    }
    out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "A minute of full load"), value: errorsLoad == 0 ? String(localized: "No GPU errors") : String(localized: "\(errorsLoad) failed GPU jobs"),
                          state: errorsLoad == 0 ? .good : .bad,
                          help: errorsLoad == 0 ? "" : String(localized: "Jobs failing under load mean GPU resets or hangs: make a diagnostics report right after this.")))
    if clocks.count >= 10 {
        let busy = clocks.filter { $0 > 0 }
        let first = busy.prefix(busy.count / 2), second = busy.suffix(busy.count / 2)
        let a = first.isEmpty ? 0 : first.reduce(0, +) / first.count, b = second.isEmpty ? 0 : second.reduce(0, +) / second.count
        let drop = a > 0 ? Double(a - b) / Double(a) : 0
        out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "GPU clock under load"), value: "\(a) → \(b) MHz", state: drop > 0.15 ? .warning : .good,
                              help: drop > 0.15 ? String(localized: "The clock fell during the minute: the card gets too hot or reaches its power limit (airflow, fan curve, power cable).") : ""))
    }
    if let hot = temps.max() {
        out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Highest GPU temperature"), value: "\(hot) °C", state: hot >= 90 ? .bad : hot >= 82 ? .warning : .good,
                              help: hot >= 82 ? String(localized: "Above about 85 °C the card lowers its clock; check the airflow in the case.") : ""))
    } else {
        out.append(TestResult(title: String(localized: "Clock and temperature"), value: String(localized: "Not read (needs IntelXe.kext 0.1.4 or later)"), state: .info))
    }
    return out
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The menu bar item (opt-in, from the Monitor page): frames, GPU clock and temperature at a glance, the main display's
// "looks like" sizes at the current refresh rate (the HiDPI ones included) to switch with one click, game mode
// (GameMode.swift: on or off, and the app in front counted as a game), and the app.
import AppKit
import CoreGraphics
import SwiftUI

/// The main display's sizes at the refresh rate in use, one per "looks like" size (the HiDPI variant when there is one).
struct DisplaySize: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let mode: CGDisplayMode
    var id: String { "\(mode.width)x\(mode.height)-\(mode.pixelWidth)" }
    var title: String { "\(mode.width) × \(mode.height)" + (mode.pixelWidth > mode.width ? "  HiDPI" : "") }
    static func == (a: DisplaySize, b: DisplaySize) -> Bool { a.id == b.id }
    func hash(into h: inout Hasher) { h.combine(id) }
}

func displaySizes() -> (sizes: [DisplaySize], current: String) {
    let id = CGMainDisplayID()
    guard let cur = CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode(id) else { return ([], "") }
    let opts = [kCGDisplayShowDuplicateLowResolutionModes as String: true] as CFDictionary
    let all = (CGDisplayCopyAllDisplayModes(id, opts) as? [CGDisplayMode]) ?? []
    var best: [String: CGDisplayMode] = [:]
    for m in all where m.isUsableForDesktopGUI() && abs(m.refreshRate - cur.refreshRate) < 0.5 {
        let key = "\(m.width)x\(m.height)"
        if let b = best[key], b.pixelWidth >= m.pixelWidth { continue }   // prefer the HiDPI one of a size
        best[key] = m
    }
    let sizes = best.values.map { DisplaySize(mode: $0) }.sorted { $0.mode.width > $1.mode.width }
    return (sizes, DisplaySize(mode: cur).id)
}

struct MenuBarContent: View {
    @ObservedObject var model: MonitorModel
    @Environment(\.openWindow) var openWindow
    var body: some View {
        let s = model.now
        Text(s.fps.map { String(format: "%.0f ", $0) + String(localized: "frames/s") } ?? "–")
        if let c = s.actMHz { Text(c == 0 ? String(localized: "GPU idle") : String(localized: "GPU \(c) MHz")) }
        if let t = s.packageC { Text(String(localized: "GPU \(t) °C")) }
        Divider()
        let (sizes, current) = displaySizes()
        Menu(String(localized: "Display size")) {
            ForEach(sizes) { size in
                Button((size.id == current ? "✓ " : "    ") + size.title) {
                    var cfg: CGDisplayConfigRef?
                    if CGBeginDisplayConfiguration(&cfg) == .success {
                        CGConfigureDisplayWithDisplayMode(cfg, CGMainDisplayID(), size.mode, nil)
                        CGCompleteDisplayConfiguration(cfg, .permanently)
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Divider()
        GameModeMenu()
        Divider()
        Button(String(localized: "Open IntelXe Manager")) { NSApp.activate(ignoringOtherApps: true); openWindow(id: "main") }
        Button(String(localized: "Quit")) { NSApp.terminate(nil) }
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The Monitor page: what the card does right now, once a second, with the last five minutes drawn. Read only and cheap:
// sysctls anyone may read (NMXAccel's presented frames, IntelXe's VRAM use and, from 0.1.4, debug.intelxe.sensors with
// the GT clock, temperatures, the card's and the package's power and the power limits) and the main display's mode from
// CoreGraphics.
import Charts
import CoreGraphics
import Foundation
import SwiftUI

func sysctlString(_ name: String) -> String? {
    var size = 0
    guard sysctlbyname(name, nil, &size, nil, 0) == 0, size > 0 else { return nil }
    var buf = [CChar](repeating: 0, count: size + 1)
    guard sysctlbyname(name, &buf, &size, nil, 0) == 0 else { return nil }
    return String(cString: buf)
}
func sysctlInt(_ name: String) -> Int64? {
    var v: Int64 = 0, size = MemoryLayout<Int64>.size
    if sysctlbyname(name, &v, &size, nil, 0) == 0 { return size == 4 ? Int64(Int32(truncatingIfNeeded: v)) : v }
    var v32: Int32 = 0; size = 4
    return sysctlbyname(name, &v32, &size, nil, 0) == 0 ? Int64(v32) : nil
}
private func firstInt(_ text: String, after label: String) -> Int? {
    guard let r = text.range(of: label) else { return nil }
    let digits = text[r.upperBound...].drop(while: { $0 == " " }).prefix(while: { $0.isNumber })
    return Int(digits)
}
/// "card power 36.98 W" -> 36.98; nil for "n/a" (the kext refused that window) or without the label (before 0.1.4)
private func firstWatts(_ text: String, after label: String) -> Double? {
    guard let r = text.range(of: label) else { return nil }
    let number = text[r.upperBound...].drop(while: { $0 == " " }).prefix(while: { $0.isNumber || $0 == "." })
    guard !number.isEmpty, text[r.upperBound...].drop(while: { $0 == " " }).dropFirst(number.count).hasPrefix(" W") else { return nil }
    return Double(number)
}
/// "card PL2 190 W (on)" -> 190 when that limit is on
private func enabledLimit(_ text: String, _ label: String) -> Double? {
    guard let r = text.range(of: label) else { return nil }
    let rest = text[r.upperBound...].drop(while: { $0 == " " })
    let number = rest.prefix(while: { $0.isNumber || $0 == "." })
    guard !number.isEmpty, rest.dropFirst(number.count).hasPrefix(" W (on)") else { return nil }
    return Double(number)
}

/// The GT clock's hardware range as IntelXe reads it (debug.intelxe.sensors, from 0.1.4): RP0, the most the GPU runs at,
/// and RPn, the least. nil without the sysctl or while the GPU sleeps.
func gtClockLimits() -> (rp0: Int, rpn: Int)? {
    guard let text = sysctlString("debug.intelxe.sensors"), text.hasPrefix("act"),
          let rp0 = firstInt(text, after: "RP0"), let rpn = firstInt(text, after: "RPn"), rp0 > 0 else { return nil }
    return (rp0, rpn)
}

/// The GT clock range of the default setting: IntelXe's SLPC floor of 1200 MHz (Wa_14022085890) up to RP0, both kept
/// within RPn...RP0 as the kernel keeps them (xe_core.cpp slpcParams). The B580: 1200-2850 MHz.
func defaultClockRange(rp0: Int, rpn: Int) -> (min: Int, max: Int) { (min(max(1200, rpn), rp0), rp0) }

struct MonitorSample {
    var fps: Double?
    var actMHz: Int?, reqMHz: Int?, maxMHz: Int?
    var packageC: Int?, vramC: Int?
    var vramUsedMB: Int?
    /// the CPU-visible part of VRAM (the 1 GB BAR window macOS can map, ResizeAppleGpuBars = 10): its size, what is in it,
    /// and how often the kernel had to say no (refusals) or put a buffer in system memory instead (spills) since boot
    var windowMB: Int?, windowUsedMB: Int?, windowRefusals: Int?, windowSpills: Int?
    /// average power over the last reading's window (debug.intelxe.sensors from the PMT kext of 0.1.4)
    var cardW: Double?, packageW: Double?
    /// the card's sustained (PL1) or burst (PL2) limit, whichever is on, PL1 first
    var cardLimitW: Double?
    var mode = ""
}

/// One reading for the Monitor page's charts.
struct MonitorPoint: Identifiable {
    let t: Date
    let v: Double
    var id: Date { t }
}

final class MonitorModel: ObservableObject {
    @Published var now = MonitorSample()
    /// the last five minutes, one point a second
    @Published var fpsHistory: [MonitorPoint] = []
    @Published var clockHistory: [MonitorPoint] = []
    @Published var tempHistory: [MonitorPoint] = []
    @Published var powerHistory: [MonitorPoint] = []
    @Published var sensorsMissing = false
    /// the last RP0 read: the clock chart's top while the GPU sleeps
    var lastMaxMHz: Int?
    static let window: TimeInterval = 300
    /// false: keep the values set from outside (the snapshots)
    var live = true
    private var timer: Timer?
    private var lastFrames: Int64?
    private var lastTime = Date()

    func start() {
        guard live, timer == nil else { return }
        sample()
        timer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] _ in self?.sample() }
    }
    func stop() { timer?.invalidate(); timer = nil; lastFrames = nil }

    private func sample() {
        var s = MonitorSample()
        let t = Date()
        if let frames = sysctlInt("debug.nmxaccel_async_frames") {
            if let last = lastFrames { s.fps = Double(frames - last) / max(0.1, t.timeIntervalSince(lastTime)) }
            lastFrames = frames
        }
        lastTime = t
        if let text = sysctlString("debug.intelxe.sensors"), text.hasPrefix("act") {
            s.actMHz = firstInt(text, after: "act"); s.reqMHz = firstInt(text, after: "req"); s.maxMHz = firstInt(text, after: "RP0")
            s.packageC = firstInt(text, after: "package"); s.vramC = firstInt(text, after: "VRAM")
            s.cardW = firstWatts(text, after: "card power"); s.packageW = firstWatts(text, after: "package power")
            s.cardLimitW = enabledLimit(text, "card PL1") ?? enabledLimit(text, "card PL2")
            if let m = s.maxMHz, m > 0 { lastMaxMHz = m }
            sensorsMissing = false
        } else { sensorsMissing = sysctlString("debug.intelxe.state") != nil }
        if let v = sysctlString("debug.intelxe.vram") {
            if let a = firstInt(v, after: "): used"), let b = firstInt(v, after: "the window: used") { s.vramUsedMB = a + b }
            if v.hasPrefix("window ") {
                s.windowMB = firstInt(v, after: "window "); s.windowUsedMB = firstInt(v, after: "): used")
                s.windowRefusals = firstInt(v, after: "window refusals"); s.windowSpills = firstInt(v, after: "spilled to system memory:")
            }
        }
        let id = CGMainDisplayID()
        if let m = CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode(id) {
            let hz = m.refreshRate
            s.mode = "\(m.width)x\(m.height)" + (m.pixelWidth != m.width ? " (\(m.pixelWidth)x\(m.pixelHeight) " + String(localized: "pixels") + ")" : "")
                + (hz > 0 ? String(format: ", %.0f Hz", hz) : "")
        }
        now = s
        let oldest = t.addingTimeInterval(-Self.window)
        func add(_ value: Double?, to list: inout [MonitorPoint]) {
            if let value { list.append(MonitorPoint(t: t, v: value)) }
            if let i = list.firstIndex(where: { $0.t >= oldest }), i > 0 { list.removeFirst(i) }
        }
        add(s.fps, to: &fpsHistory)
        add(s.actMHz.map(Double.init), to: &clockHistory)
        add(s.packageC.map(Double.init), to: &tempHistory)
        add(s.cardW, to: &powerHistory)
    }
}

/// The last five minutes of one reading: a line over a light wash, its scale on the right.
struct MetricChart: View {
    let points: [MonitorPoint]
    let color: Color
    let top: Double
    var body: some View {
        let end = points.last?.t ?? Date()
        Chart(points) { p in
            AreaMark(x: .value("Time", p.t), y: .value("Value", min(p.v, top)))
                .foregroundStyle(LinearGradient(colors: [color.opacity(0.28), color.opacity(0.02)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
                .interpolationMethod(.monotone)
            LineMark(x: .value("Time", p.t), y: .value("Value", min(p.v, top)))
                .foregroundStyle(color)
                .lineStyle(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 1.6))
                .interpolationMethod(.monotone)
        }
        .chartXScale(domain: end.addingTimeInterval(-MonitorModel.window)...end)
        .chartYScale(domain: 0...top)
        .chartXAxis(.hidden)
        .chartYAxis {
            AxisMarks(position: .trailing, values: .automatic(desiredCount: 3)) { _ in
                AxisGridLine().foregroundStyle(Color.secondary.opacity(0.25))
                AxisValueLabel().font(.caption2)
            }
        }
        .overlay {
            if points.count < 2 { Text("No readings yet").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary) }
        }
        .frame(width: 230, height: 58)
        .accessibilityLabel(Text("The last five minutes"))
    }
}

/// A reading as a number with a line under it, and its chart beside it.
struct MetricRow: View {
    let title: LocalizedStringKey
    let symbol: String
    let value: String
    var detail: String = ""
    let points: [MonitorPoint]
    let color: Color
    let top: Double
    var body: some View {
        HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 12) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 3) {
                Label(title, systemImage: symbol).font(.subheadline).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                Text(value).font(.title3.weight(.semibold).monospacedDigit()).contentTransition(.numericText())
                    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: value)
                if !detail.isEmpty { Text(detail).font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary) }
            }
            Spacer(minLength: 8)
            MetricChart(points: points, color: color, top: top)
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 2)
    }
}

struct MonitorView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var manager: Manager
    @StateObject var model: MonitorModel
    @AppStorage("menuBarItem") var menuBarItem = false
    init(model: MonitorModel = MonitorModel()) { _model = StateObject(wrappedValue: model) }
    var body: some View {
        let s = model.now
        Form {
            Section2(title: "GPU", symbol: "gauge.medium") {
                if model.sensorsMissing {
                    Label("The GPU clock and temperatures need IntelXe.kext 0.1.4 or later in your EFI.", systemImage: "info.circle").foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                } else {
                    MetricRow(title: "Clock", symbol: "speedometer",
                              value: s.actMHz.map { $0 == 0 ? String(localized: "idle (power saving)") : "\($0) MHz" } ?? "–",
                              detail: s.maxMHz.map { String(localized: "max") + " \($0) MHz" } ?? "",
                              points: model.clockHistory, color: .accentColor,
                              top: Double(s.maxMHz ?? model.lastMaxMHz ?? max(1000, Int(model.clockHistory.map(\.v).max() ?? 0))))
                    MetricRow(title: "Temperature", symbol: "thermometer.medium",
                              value: s.packageC.map { String(localized: "GPU \($0) °C") } ?? "–",
                              detail: s.vramC.map { String(localized: "memory \($0) °C") } ?? "",
                              points: model.tempHistory, color: .orange, top: max(100, model.tempHistory.map(\.v).max() ?? 0))
                    if s.cardW != nil || !model.powerHistory.isEmpty {
                        MetricRow(title: "Power", symbol: "bolt",
                                  value: s.cardW.map { String(format: "%.1f W ", $0) + String(localized: "card") } ?? "–",
                                  detail: [s.packageW.map { String(localized: "GPU package") + String(format: " %.1f W", $0) },
                                           s.cardLimitW.map { String(localized: "limit") + String(format: " %.0f W", $0) }]
                                      .compactMap { $0 }.joined(separator: " · "),
                                  points: model.powerHistory, color: .pink,
                                  top: max(60, (model.powerHistory.map(\.v).max() ?? 0) * 1.2))
                    }
                }
                LabeledContent("Video memory in use") { Text(s.vramUsedMB.map { String(format: "%.1f GB", Double($0) / 1024) } ?? "–") }
                if let total = s.windowMB, let used = s.windowUsedMB, total > 0 { WindowGauge(total: total, used: used, sample: s) }
            }
            Section2(title: "Display", symbol: "display") {
                MetricRow(title: "Frames presented", symbol: "film.stack",
                          value: s.fps.map { String(format: "%.0f ", $0) + String(localized: "frames/s") } ?? "–",
                          detail: String(localized: "Rises with motion on screen, a few when nothing moves."),
                          points: model.fpsHistory, color: .green, top: max(60, model.fpsHistory.map(\.v).max() ?? 60))
                LabeledContent("Mode") { Text(s.mode.isEmpty ? "–" : s.mode) }
                LabeledContent("Variable refresh") { Text(manager.vrrActive ? String(localized: "Offered") : String(localized: "Off")) }
            }
            Section2(title: "Menu bar", symbol: "menubar.rectangle") {
                CaptionedToggle(title: "Show in the menu bar", caption: "Frames, GPU clock and temperature, and the display sizes (HiDPI ones too) to switch with one click.", isOn: $menuBarItem)
            }
        }
        .formStyle(.grouped)
        .onAppear { model.start() }
        .onDisappear { model.stop() }
    }
}

/// The CPU-visible window of the card's memory: how full it is, and a warning when it is nearly full or the kernel has
/// already had to refuse a buffer or put one in system memory (programs then run slower or fail to start).
struct WindowGauge: View {
    let total: Int, used: Int
    let sample: MonitorSample
    var body: some View {
        let fill = min(1, Double(used) / Double(total))
        let pressed = (sample.windowRefusals ?? 0) > 0 || (sample.windowSpills ?? 0) > 0
        let level: Color = fill >= 0.9 || pressed ? .orange : fill >= 0.75 ? .yellow : .accentColor
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 5) {
            HStack(spacing: 6) {
                Label("CPU-visible video memory", systemImage: "rectangle.split.3x1").foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                InfoButton("macOS can map only a 1 GB window of the card's 12 GB (ResizeAppleGpuBars = 10). Buffers the CPU writes go there; the rest of the memory is only for the GPU. The driver keeps the window for programs that need it and puts background programs' buffers in system memory, but many open GPU-heavy programs can still fill it: then new buffers are refused or moved to system memory, and programs slow down or fail to start. Quitting a few helps.")
                Spacer()
                Text("\(used) / \(total) MB").monospacedDigit().foregroundStyle(level == .accentColor ? Color.primary : level)
            }
            ProgressView(value: fill).tint(level).accessibilityLabel(Text("CPU-visible video memory"))
            if pressed {
                Text("The window ran out since the last restart: \(sample.windowRefusals ?? 0) buffers refused, \(sample.windowSpills ?? 0) moved to system memory.")
                    .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.orange)
            } else if fill >= 0.9 {
                Text("Nearly full: quitting GPU-heavy programs frees it.").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.orange)
            }
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 2)
    }
}

extension String { func ifEmpty(_ other: String) -> String { isEmpty ? other : self } }

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The Report page: tools/report/collect-macos.sh, carried in the app, makes the diagnostics archive (on the Desktop) and
// prints what it recognised as wrong ("Warning <code>: <text>"); the page lists those with a way to fix each one the
// app can fix, and opens the issue forms with the report ID filled in. The script only reads; administrator mode runs
// it as root (the OpenCore config from the EFI partitions, the driver's root-only counters, the CPU clock), and the
// user's own name is still removed from the archive (XE_REPORT_USER).
import AppKit
import Foundation
import SwiftUI

struct ReportWarning: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let id = UUID()
    let code: String
    let text: String
}

/// Issue forms; GitHub fills a form field from a query parameter named after the field's id.
func issueFormURL(template: String, field: String, value: String?) -> URL {
    var c = URLComponents(string: "https://github.com/\(repository)/issues/new")!
    c.queryItems = [URLQueryItem(name: "template", value: template)]
    if let value { c.queryItems?.append(URLQueryItem(name: field, value: value)) }
    return c.url!
}

let reportTitle = String(localized: "Create a diagnostics report")

/// The report's progress: collect-macos.sh prints "== step N/TOTAL: NAME" as each section starts; the bar follows the
/// last one in the run's output (the log, read every half second while it runs).
struct ReportProgress: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var manager: Manager
    static func names(_ key: String) -> String {
        switch key {
        case "system": return String(localized: "This Mac")
        case "pci": return String(localized: "PCI devices")
        case "display": return String(localized: "Displays")
        case "driver": return String(localized: "The driver")
        case "stack": return String(localized: "The graphics stack")
        case "logs": return String(localized: "Logs and panics")
        case "opencore": return String(localized: "OpenCore")
        case "probe": return String(localized: "Staged probe")
        case "acpi": return String(localized: "ACPI tables")
        case "tests": return String(localized: "Self-tests")
        case "summary": return String(localized: "Summary")
        case "redaction": return String(localized: "Removing private details")
        default: return key
        }
    }
    var body: some View {
        let output = manager.log.dropFirst(manager.runLogStart)
        let last = output.split(separator: "\n").last { $0.hasPrefix("== step ") }
        let parts = last.map { $0.dropFirst(8).split(separator: ":", maxSplits: 1) } ?? []
        let nums = parts.first?.split(separator: "/").compactMap { Int($0) } ?? []
        let n = nums.count == 2 ? nums[0] : 0, total = nums.count == 2 ? max(nums[1], 1) : 1
        let name = parts.count == 2 ? Self.names(parts[1].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)) : String(localized: "Starting")
        TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 1)) { ctx in
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
                ProgressView(value: Double(max(n - 1, 0)) + 0.5, total: Double(total))
                    .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.3), value: n)
                HStack {
                    Text(n > 0 ? String(localized: "Step \(n) of \(total): \(name)") : name).font(.callout)
                    Spacer()
                    Text(String(localized: "\(Int(ctx.date.timeIntervalSince(manager.runStartedAt))) s")).font(.callout.monospacedDigit()).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

extension Manager {
    func createReport(acpi: Bool, probe: Bool, admin: Bool, bootLogs: Bool = false) {
        guard let script = Bundle.main.url(forResource: "collect-macos", withExtension: "sh") else { return }
        let desktop = FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent("Desktop")
        var args = ["--out", desktop.path]
        if acpi { args.append("--acpi") }
        if probe { args.append("--probe") }
        if bootLogs { args.append("--boot-logs") }
        var command = "/bin/sh \(shellQuoted(script.path)) " + args.map(shellQuoted).joined(separator: " ")
        if admin { command = "XE_REPORT_USER=\(shellQuoted(NSUserName())) " + command }
        // the Probe page's record of its stage runs, earlier boots included (collect-macos.sh copies it into probe/)
        if probe && FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: probeHistoryFile.path) {
            command = "XE_PROBE_HISTORY=\(shellQuoted(probeHistoryFile.path)) " + command
        }
        let start = log.count
        reportWarnings = []
        perform(title: reportTitle, command: command, needsRoot: admin, then: { result in
            let lines = String(self.log.dropFirst(start)).split(separator: "\n").map(String.init)
            let field = { (name: String) in lines.first { $0.hasPrefix(name) }.map { String($0.dropFirst(name.count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) } }
            self.reportWarnings = lines.compactMap { line in
                guard line.hasPrefix("Warning "), let colon = line.firstIndex(of: ":") else { return nil }
                let code = String(line[line.index(line.startIndex, offsetBy: 8)..<colon])
                return ReportWarning(code: code, text: String(line[line.index(after: colon)...]).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces))
            }
            if result.cancelled {
                self.lastResult = String(localized: "Cancelled. No report was written.")
            } else if result.succeeded, let id = field("Report ID:"), let file = field("File:") {
                self.reportID = id; self.reportFile = file
                self.lastResult = String(localized: "Report \(id) is on the Desktop. Attach it to a new issue and put the ID in the form.")
                NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([URL(fileURLWithPath: file)])
            } else {
                self.lastResult = String(localized: "No report was written. See the log.")
            }
        })
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The Settings page: the driver's settings that IntelXe and IntelXeFB read from NVRAM at start (written through the
// password dialog; the display ones are applied at once too, through their sysctls), and the app's own.
import Foundation
import ServiceManagement
import SwiftUI

/// NVRAM value of a key, nil when unset (or "ok", which the kexts read as unset).
/// The Metal driver reads it at start: present = the GuC low-latency hint for apps (nvmtl_guc_hint_env); off by default
/// since 0.1.4. The flag of 0.1.4's first builds (NVMTLDriver.no-low-latency, present = off) is removed on any change.
let lowLatencyFlag = "/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.low-latency"
let oldNoLowLatencyFlag = "/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.no-low-latency"

func nvramValue(_ key: String) -> String? {
    guard let out = commandOutput("/usr/sbin/nvram", [key]), let tab = out.firstIndex(of: "\t") else { return nil }
    let v = out[out.index(after: tab)...].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
    return v.isEmpty || v == "ok" ? nil : v
}

struct DriverSettings: Equatable {
    var profile = 0          // intelxe-gpu-profile: 0 balanced, 1 power saving
    var clocks = 0           // 0 default, 1 quiet (max 1800 MHz), 2 performance (min 2400 MHz)
    var hwCursor = true      // intelxefb-hwcursor
    var dpms = false         // intelxefb-dpms
    var lfc = true           // intelxefb-vrr-lfc
    var vrrFloor = 0         // intelxefb-vrr-floor (Hz, 0 = the panel's)
    var gpuTiming = false    // /tmp/nvmtl-gputime (test builds of the Metal driver)
    var fastResponse = false  // the GuC low-latency hint for apps; on = /Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.low-latency

    static func read() -> DriverSettings {
        var s = DriverSettings()
        s.profile = Int(nvramValue("intelxe-gpu-profile") ?? "") ?? 0
        let mn = Int(nvramValue("intelxe-gpu-min-mhz") ?? "") ?? 0, mx = Int(nvramValue("intelxe-gpu-max-mhz") ?? "") ?? 0
        s.clocks = mx > 0 && mx <= 1800 ? 1 : mn >= 2400 ? 2 : 0
        s.hwCursor = (nvramValue("intelxefb-hwcursor") ?? "1") != "0"
        s.dpms = (nvramValue("intelxefb-dpms") ?? "0") == "1"
        s.lfc = (nvramValue("intelxefb-vrr-lfc") ?? "1") != "0"
        s.vrrFloor = Int(nvramValue("intelxefb-vrr-floor") ?? "") ?? 0
        s.gpuTiming = FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: "/tmp/nvmtl-gputime")
        s.fastResponse = FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: lowLatencyFlag)
        return s
    }

    /// The shell commands that make `self` so (NVRAM for the next start; the display sysctls at once).
    func commands() -> String {
        let (mn, mx) = clocks == 1 ? (0, 1800) : clocks == 2 ? (2400, 0) : (0, 0)
        var c = [
            "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxe-gpu-profile=\(profile)",
            "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxe-gpu-min-mhz=\(mn)", "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxe-gpu-max-mhz=\(mx)",
            "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxefb-hwcursor=\(hwCursor ? 1 : 0)", "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxefb-dpms=\(dpms ? 1 : 0)",
            "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxefb-vrr-lfc=\(lfc ? 1 : 0)", "/usr/sbin/nvram intelxefb-vrr-floor=\(vrrFloor)",
            "/usr/sbin/sysctl -q debug.intelxefb_hwcursor=\(hwCursor ? 1 : 0) debug.intelxefb_dpms=\(dpms ? 1 : 0) debug.intelxefb_vrr_lfc=\(lfc ? 1 : 0) debug.intelxefb_vrr_floor_hz=\(vrrFloor) || true",
        ]
        c.append(gpuTiming ? "/usr/bin/touch /tmp/nvmtl-gputime && /bin/chmod 644 /tmp/nvmtl-gputime" : "/bin/rm -f /tmp/nvmtl-gputime")
        c.append("/bin/rm -f \(shellQuoted(oldNoLowLatencyFlag))")
        c.append(fastResponse ? "/usr/bin/touch \(shellQuoted(lowLatencyFlag)) && /bin/chmod 644 \(shellQuoted(lowLatencyFlag))" : "/bin/rm -f \(shellQuoted(lowLatencyFlag))")
        return c.joined(separator: " && ")
    }
}

extension Manager {
    func applySettings(_ s: DriverSettings) {
        perform(title: String(localized: "Save the driver settings"), command: s.commands(), needsRoot: true, then: { result in
            if result.cancelled { self.lastResult = String(localized: "Cancelled. Nothing changed.") }
            else if result.succeeded { self.lastResult = String(localized: "Saved. The display settings apply now; the power settings at the next start."); self.rebootNeeded = true }
            else { self.lastResult = String(localized: "It did not finish. See the log.") }
        })
    }
}

// Plain observable state (no SwiftUI macros: the app builds with the command line tools alone)
final class SettingsState: ObservableObject {
    @Published var saved = DriverSettings()
    @Published var edit = DriverSettings()
    @Published var loaded = false
    /// the default setting's GT clock range on this card (defaultClockRange); nil when IntelXe does not report RP0 and RPn
    @Published var clockRange: (min: Int, max: Int)?
    @Published var loginItem = SMAppService.mainApp.status == .enabled
    @Published var loginCheck = loginCheckEnabled()
}

struct SettingsView: View {
    @EnvironmentObject var manager: Manager
    @StateObject var st = SettingsState()
    @AppStorage("autoUpdateCheck") var autoUpdateCheck = true

    var body: some View {
        Form {
            Section2(title: "Power", symbol: "bolt") {
                Picker("GPU power profile", selection: $st.edit.profile) {
                    Text("Balanced").tag(0); Text("Power saving").tag(1)
                }
                Picker("GPU clock", selection: $st.edit.clocks) {
                    Text(st.clockRange.map { String(localized: "Default (\(String($0.min))–\(String($0.max)) MHz)") } ?? String(localized: "Default")).tag(0)
                    Text("Quiet (up to 1800 MHz: less heat and fan noise)").tag(1)
                    Text("Performance (at least 2400 MHz: lowest latency, more power)").tag(2)
                }
                Text("Applied at the next start.").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                CaptionedToggle(title: "Fast GPU response for apps", caption: "Keeps the GPU clock up while an app's GPU work runs.",
                                detail: "Keeps the GPU clock up while an app's GPU work runs, instead of letting short bursts run at the lowest clock: games, Metal and OpenCL apps and benchmarks respond faster (Geekbench 4-6 percent higher). The desktop itself is not affected; an idle GPU sleeps either way. Applies to apps started afterwards. Off by default: in tests the first heavy run after a long idle was sometimes followed by a GPU fault with it on.", isOn: $st.edit.fastResponse)
            }
            Section2(title: "Diagnostics", symbol: "stethoscope") {
                CaptionedToggle(title: "GPU timing in the driver's log", caption: "For performance reports; test builds of the Metal driver only.", isOn: $st.edit.gpuTiming)
                HStack {
                    Text("Power and diagnostics are saved together; the power settings apply at the next start.").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    Spacer()
                    Button("Revert") { st.edit = st.saved }.disabled(st.edit == st.saved)
                    Button("Save") { manager.applySettings(st.edit); st.saved = st.edit }.disabled(st.edit == st.saved).keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)
                }
            }
            GameModeSection()
            Section2(title: "This app", symbol: "gearshape") {
                CaptionedToggle(title: "Open at login", caption: "Keeps the menu bar item there. Applies at once.", isOn: Binding(get: { st.loginItem }, set: { on in
                    do { if on { try SMAppService.mainApp.register() } else { try SMAppService.mainApp.unregister() } } catch {}
                    st.loginItem = SMAppService.mainApp.status == .enabled
                }))
                CaptionedToggle(title: "Check the driver at login", caption: "After each login, a dialog only when something needs attention.",
                                detail: "Without opening the app: after each login, a dialog only when something needs attention, such as a macOS update that removed the system-volume copy. Applies from the next login.", isOn: Binding(get: { st.loginCheck }, set: { setLoginCheck($0); st.loginCheck = loginCheckEnabled() }))
                CaptionedToggle(title: "Check for a new release at start", caption: "Asks GitHub for the latest release when the app opens.", isOn: $autoUpdateCheck)
            }
        }
        .formStyle(.grouped)
        .task {
            if !st.loaded {
                let s = await Task.detached { DriverSettings.read() }.value; st.saved = s; st.edit = s; st.loaded = true
                st.clockRange = gtClockLimits().map { defaultClockRange(rp0: $0.rp0, rpn: $0.rpn) }
            }
        }
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Release signatures: a release's list of hashes (VERSION.sha256) is signed with the project's Ed25519 key
// (release/signing.swift, VERSION.sha256.sig beside it). The app installs a downloaded package only when that list is
// signed by a key below and the zip's hash is in it, so a release that only came from the same GitHub page (an account
// taken over, an asset replaced) is refused.
import CryptoKit
import Foundation

/// Ed25519 public keys whose signatures the app accepts (base64 of the raw 32 bytes). A new key goes here in an app
/// release signed with an old one before the old one is retired (docs/RELEASE-KEYS.md): release/release-keys.sh adds
/// and retires keys here and in the Windows app's list (ReleaseSigning.cs) together; keep this on one line, as it reads it.
let releaseSigningKeys = ["PZGslAxn39LtMGgkWHbn9MzK8nc+IeM2TrvJpbifZXA="]

/// Whether `signature` holds a signature of `list` by one of releaseSigningKeys: the .sig file's text (base64, one line)
/// or the .sigs file's (one signature per line, one line per key during a key change: docs/RELEASE-KEYS.md). `keys` is
/// for tests (release/test-signing.sh: throwaway keys).
func releaseSignatureValid(list: Data, signature: String, keys: [String] = releaseSigningKeys) -> Bool {
    let lines = signature.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).map { $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces) }.filter { !$0.isEmpty }
    return lines.contains { line in
        guard let sig = Data(base64Encoded: line) else { return false }
        return keys.contains { key in
            guard let raw = Data(base64Encoded: key), let publicKey = try? Curve25519.Signing.PublicKey(rawRepresentation: raw) else { return false }
            return publicKey.isValidSignature(sig, for: list)
        }
    }
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The smoothness test: a window on the main display draws a moving bar at the display's full rate for five seconds,
// and each frame's on-screen time (MTLDrawable presentedTime) is recorded. From the gaps: the rate reached, frames
// that came a refresh or more late (a visible stutter), and how even the pacing was.
import AppKit
import Metal
import QuartzCore

private final class SmoothRunner: NSObject {
    let window: NSWindow
    let layer = CAMetalLayer()
    let device: MTLDevice
    let queue: MTLCommandQueue
    var presented: [CFTimeInterval] = []
    var link: CVDisplayLink?
    var frame = 0
    let lock = NSLock()

    init?(device: MTLDevice) {
        guard let q = device.makeCommandQueue(), let screen = NSScreen.main else { return nil }
        self.device = device; queue = q
        let size = NSSize(width: 640, height: 360)
        window = NSWindow(contentRect: NSRect(x: screen.frame.midX - size.width / 2, y: screen.frame.midY - size.height / 2, width: size.width, height: size.height),
                          styleMask: [.titled], backing: .buffered, defer: false, screen: screen)
        super.init()
        window.title = String(localized: "Smoothness test")
        let view = NSView(frame: NSRect(origin: .zero, size: size)); view.wantsLayer = true
        layer.device = device; layer.pixelFormat = .bgra8Unorm; layer.framebufferOnly = true
        layer.drawableSize = CGSize(width: size.width * screen.backingScaleFactor, height: size.height * screen.backingScaleFactor)
        layer.displaySyncEnabled = true; layer.maximumDrawableCount = 3
        view.layer = layer; window.contentView = view
    }

    func snapshot() -> [CFTimeInterval] { lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }; return presented.sorted() }

    /// One frame: clear to a colour whose bar position moves, present, note when it reached the screen.
    func draw() {
        guard let d = layer.nextDrawable(), let cb = queue.makeCommandBuffer() else { return }
        let rp = MTLRenderPassDescriptor(); rp.colorAttachments[0].texture = d.texture; rp.colorAttachments[0].loadAction = .clear
        let t = Double(frame % 120) / 120; frame += 1
        rp.colorAttachments[0].clearColor = MTLClearColor(red: t, green: 0.3, blue: 1 - t, alpha: 1); rp.colorAttachments[0].storeAction = .store
        cb.makeRenderCommandEncoder(descriptor: rp)?.endEncoding()
        d.addPresentedHandler { [weak self] dr in
            guard let self, dr.presentedTime > 0 else { return }
            self.lock.lock(); self.presented.append(dr.presentedTime); self.lock.unlock()
        }
        cb.present(d); cb.commit()
    }
}

/// Runs on the main thread for about six seconds (the window must be on screen); returns the results.
@MainActor func runSmoothTest() async -> [TestResult] {
    guard let d = MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice(), let r = SmoothRunner(device: d) else { return [] }
    r.window.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
    let hz = Double(NSScreen.main?.maximumFramesPerSecond ?? 60)
    let end = Date().addingTimeInterval(5.5)
    try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 400_000_000)   // let the window settle
    while Date() < end {
        r.draw()
        try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(1e9 / hz / 2))   // twice per refresh: the drawable queue paces it
    }
    try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 300_000_000)
    r.window.orderOut(nil)
    let times = r.snapshot()
    guard times.count > 30 else {
        return [TestResult(title: String(localized: "Smoothness"), value: String(localized: "Too few frames reached the screen (\(times.count))"), state: .bad)]
    }
    let gaps = zip(times.dropFirst(), times).map { $0 - $1 }
    let span = times.last! - times.first!, fps = Double(gaps.count) / span
    let period = 1 / hz
    let late = gaps.filter { $0 > period * 1.5 }.count
    let mean = gaps.reduce(0, +) / Double(gaps.count)
    let sd = (gaps.map { ($0 - mean) * ($0 - mean) }.reduce(0, +) / Double(gaps.count)).squareRoot()
    let okRate = fps >= hz * 0.95, okLate = Double(late) <= Double(gaps.count) * 0.01
    return [
        TestResult(title: String(localized: "Frame rate in a window"), value: String(format: "%.0f fps (", fps) + String(localized: "display") + String(format: " %.0f Hz)", hz),
                   state: okRate ? .good : fps >= hz * 0.75 ? .warning : .bad,
                   help: okRate ? "" : String(localized: "The display's full rate was not reached: in a scaled (HiDPI) size the compositor does more work; in the monitor's own size this points at the driver.")),
        TestResult(title: String(localized: "Late frames"), value: String(localized: "\(late) of \(gaps.count)") + String(format: ", ± %.2f ms", sd * 1000),
                   state: okLate ? .good : .warning,
                   help: okLate ? "" : String(localized: "Frames shown a refresh or more late are visible as stutter."))
    ]
}
