#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build-neo.sh [STEP...]: Intel's compute runtime (NEO) for macOS x86_64 over IntelXe.kext: the Level Zero driver
# libze_intel_gpu.1.dylib (and, with OCL=1, the OpenCL ICD libigdrcl.dylib), with gmmlib and the Level Zero loader.
# Runs on the build Mac (Apple silicon or Intel) and cross-compiles to x86_64. See compute/README.md.
#   STEP: fetch patch gmmlib loader igc-headers icd neo stage (default: all, in that order; icd only with OCL=1)
#   L0_WORK   work directory (default $HOME/intelxe-l0): src/ (pinned upstream checkouts, patched on branch intelxe),
#             build/, prefix/ (gmmlib, loader, IGC headers), stage/ (what goes to the test machine)
#   OCL=1     also build the OpenCL ICD (libigdrcl), the Khronos ICD loader (libOpenCL.1.dylib) and cl_hello
#   IGC_PREFIX the IGC install of compute/build-igc.sh (libigc, libigdfcl, libopencl-clang and IGC's headers). With it:
#             NEO compiles against that IGC, the built-in kernels are compiled at build time and embedded (no builtins/
#             directory needed), ocloc is built, and stage/ gets the compiler, ocloc and kernels/ compiled with it.
#             Without it: IGC's headers only (igc-headers), no compiler on the Mac (compute/ocloc-docker.sh).
#   JOBS      ninja -j (default: all cores)
# Needs git, cmake >= 3.21, ninja on PATH, the Xcode command line tools. ~1.5 GB of sources and builds; the NEO build
# is ~5 minutes on 8 Apple silicon cores (more with IGC_PREFIX: the built-in kernels are compiled by ocloc).
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
W=${L0_WORK:-$HOME/intelxe-l0}
SRC=$W/src
BLD=$W/build
PREFIX=$W/prefix
STAGE=${OUT:-$W/stage}
J=${JOBS:-$(/usr/sbin/sysctl -n hw.ncpu)}
IGCP=${IGC_PREFIX:-}
[ -z "$IGCP" ] || [ -e "$IGCP/lib/pkgconfig/igc-opencl.pc" ] || { echo "IGC_PREFIX=$IGCP: no IGC install there" >&2; exit 1; }

# Pins: NEO at the commit docs/parity reads (2026-10-30), and the gmmlib, loader and IGC revisions its
# manifests/manifest.yml names for that commit (IGC: headers only).
NEO_URL=https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime.git
NEO_REV=248eb54f84415da3498d9f4070ba09cc55efab94
GMM_URL=https://github.com/intel/gmmlib.git
GMM_TAG=intel-gmmlib-22.10.2
GMM_REV=733c91a19baa65c40f4b1cf95a3991cc8c84d866
LOADER_URL=https://github.com/oneapi-src/level-zero.git
LOADER_TAG=v1.35.0
LOADER_REV=9e1a8b2c07ed6ce1f00b0a195fa5efa0db8e3650
IGC_URL=https://github.com/intel/intel-graphics-compiler.git
IGC_REV=0f18b8dc2e5d75fa86ba9f1960eab87b5a89a4c6
# OpenCL only: macOS's OpenCL.framework loads no ICDs, so the Khronos loader (builds unchanged) and its headers
ICD_URL=https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCL-ICD-Loader.git
ICD_TAG=v2025.07.22
ICD_REV=ad770a1b64c6b8d5f2ed4e153f22e4f45939f27f
CLH_URL=https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCL-Headers.git
CLH_TAG=v2025.07.22
CLH_REV=8a97ebc88daa3495d6f57ec10bb515224400186f

X86=(-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0)
command -v ninja >/dev/null || { echo "ninja is not on PATH (pip install ninja, or brew install ninja)" >&2; exit 1; }

fetch() {
	mkdir -p "$SRC"
	[ -d "$SRC/neo/.git" ] || git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "$NEO_URL" "$SRC/neo"
	[ -d "$SRC/gmmlib/.git" ] || git clone -q --depth 1 -b "$GMM_TAG" "$GMM_URL" "$SRC/gmmlib"
	[ -d "$SRC/level-zero/.git" ] || git clone -q --depth 1 -b "$LOADER_TAG" "$LOADER_URL" "$SRC/level-zero"
	if [ ! -d "$SRC/igc/.git" ]; then
		# the headers NEO compiles against (the igc-opencl-devel layout), not the compiler
		git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --sparse "$IGC_URL" "$SRC/igc"
		git -C "$SRC/igc" sparse-checkout set IGC/AdaptorOCL IGC/common visa/include visa/iga/IGALibrary/api \
			IGC/ZEBinWriter/zebin/source
	fi
	if [ "${OCL:-0}" = 1 ]; then
		[ -d "$SRC/ocl-icd-loader/.git" ] || git clone -q --depth 1 -b "$ICD_TAG" "$ICD_URL" "$SRC/ocl-icd-loader"
		[ -d "$SRC/ocl-headers/.git" ] || git clone -q --depth 1 -b "$CLH_TAG" "$CLH_URL" "$SRC/ocl-headers"
		[ "$(git -C "$SRC/ocl-icd-loader" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$ICD_REV" ] && [ "$(git -C "$SRC/ocl-headers" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$CLH_REV" ] ||
			{ echo "OpenCL loader/headers are not at the pinned revisions" >&2; exit 1; }
	fi
	git -C "$SRC/neo" fetch -q --filter=blob:none origin "$NEO_REV" 2>/dev/null || true
	git -C "$SRC/igc" checkout -q "$IGC_REV"
}

# component dir, pinned revision, patch directory: branch intelxe = the pin + our series (git am)
apply_series() {
	local dir=$1 rev=$2 pdir=$3
	[ "$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse "$rev^{commit}")" = "$rev" ] || { echo "$dir: $rev missing" >&2; exit 1; }
	git -C "$dir" checkout -q -f -B intelxe "$rev"
	local p
	while read -r p; do
		[ -n "$p" ] || continue
		git -C "$dir" -c user.name=intelxe-build -c user.email=build@localhost am -q --keep-cr "$pdir/$p"
	done < "$pdir/series"
}

patch() {
	apply_series "$SRC/neo" "$NEO_REV" "$HERE/patches/compute-runtime"
	apply_series "$SRC/gmmlib" "$GMM_REV" "$HERE/patches/gmmlib"
	apply_series "$SRC/level-zero" "$LOADER_REV" "$HERE/patches/level-zero"
}

gmmlib() {
	cmake -S "$SRC/gmmlib" -B "$BLD/gmmlib" -G Ninja "${X86[@]}" -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$PREFIX" -DRUN_TEST_SUITE=OFF \
		-Wno-dev >/dev/null
	ninja -C "$BLD/gmmlib" -j "$J" install >/dev/null
}

loader() {
	cmake -S "$SRC/level-zero" -B "$BLD/level-zero" -G Ninja "${X86[@]}" -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$PREFIX" >/dev/null
	ninja -C "$BLD/level-zero" -j "$J" install >/dev/null
}

icd() {
	[ "${OCL:-0}" = 1 ] || return 0
	mkdir -p "$PREFIX/include"
	cp -R "$SRC/ocl-headers/CL" "$PREFIX/include/"
	cmake -S "$SRC/ocl-icd-loader" -B "$BLD/ocl-icd" -G Ninja "${X86[@]}" -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$PREFIX" \
		-DOPENCL_ICD_LOADER_HEADERS_DIR="$SRC/ocl-headers" -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF >/dev/null
	ninja -C "$BLD/ocl-icd" -j "$J" install >/dev/null
}

# IGC's igc-opencl-devel package layout, from the source: what NEO's find_igc.cmake (pkg-config igc-opencl) wants.
igc_headers() {
	if [ -n "$IGCP" ]; then
		echo "IGC: $IGCP (compute/build-igc.sh)"
		return 0
	fi
	local I=$SRC/igc P=$PREFIX/igc
	rm -rf "$P"
	mkdir -p "$P/include/igc/common" "$P/include/igc/zebin" "$P/include/visa" "$P/include/iga" "$P/lib/pkgconfig"
	cp -R "$I/IGC/AdaptorOCL/ocl_igc_shared" "$I/IGC/AdaptorOCL/ocl_igc_interface" "$I/IGC/AdaptorOCL/OCLAPI" \
		"$I/IGC/AdaptorOCL/cif" "$P/include/igc/"
	cp "$I/IGC/common/StateSaveAreaHeader.h" "$P/include/igc/common/"
	cp "$I/visa/include/RelocationInfo.h" "$P/include/visa/"
	(cd "$I/visa/iga/IGALibrary/api" && find . -name '*.h*' -exec cp {} "$P/include/iga/" \;)
	cp "$I/IGC/ZEBinWriter/zebin/source/ZEELF.h" "$P/include/igc/zebin/"
	sed "s|#cmakedefine IGC_REVISION \"\${IGC_REVISION}\"|#define IGC_REVISION \"$IGC_REV\"|" \
		"$I/IGC/AdaptorOCL/ocl_igc_interface/impl/version_in.h" > "$P/include/igc/ocl_igc_interface/impl/version.h"
	local maj min pat
	maj=$(sed -n 's/^  set(IGC_API_MAJOR_VERSION \([0-9]*\))/\1/p' "$I/IGC/CMakeLists.txt")
	min=$(sed -n 's/^  set(IGC_API_MINOR_VERSION \([0-9]*\))/\1/p' "$I/IGC/CMakeLists.txt")
	pat=$(sed -n 's/^  set(IGC_API_PATCH_VERSION \([0-9]*\))/\1/p' "$I/IGC/CMakeLists.txt")
	# igc.opencl.h.in has no Mach-O branch: the names NEO dlopen()s for the compiler (absent until IGC is ported)
	cat > "$P/include/igc/igc.opencl.h" <<EOF
// Generated by compute/build-neo.sh: IGC's library names on macOS.
#ifndef IGC_OPENCL_H
#define IGC_OPENCL_H
#define IGC_LIBRARY_NAME "libigc.$maj.dylib"
#define FCL_LIBRARY_NAME "libigdfcl.$maj.dylib"
#endif // IGC_OPENCL_H
EOF
	cat > "$P/lib/pkgconfig/igc-opencl.pc" <<EOF
prefix=$P
exec_prefix=\${prefix}
includedir=\${prefix}/include/igc
libdir=\${exec_prefix}/lib

Name: igc-opencl
Description: Intel(R) Graphics Compiler for OpenCL(TM), headers only (intel-gpu-macos-driver compute/build-neo.sh)
Version: $maj.$min.$pat
Cflags: -I\${includedir} -I\${includedir}/cif -I\${includedir}/ocl_igc_shared/executable_format -I\${includedir}/ocl_igc_shared/device_enqueue
Libs:
EOF
}

neo() {
	local ocl=FALSE targets=(ze_intel_gpu) igcdir=$PREFIX/igc builtins=(-DCOMPILE_BUILT_INS=FALSE
		-DNEO_DISABLE_BUILTINS_COMPILATION=TRUE)
	[ "${OCL:-0}" = 1 ] && ocl=TRUE && targets+=(igdrcl_dll)
	if [ -n "$IGCP" ]; then
		# with the compiler: ocloc, and the built-in kernels compiled by it (through the x86_64 IGC: Rosetta on Apple
		# silicon) and embedded in the drivers
		igcdir=$IGCP
		targets+=(ocloc ocloc_lib)
		builtins=(-DCOMPILE_BUILT_INS=TRUE -DNEO_DISABLE_BUILTINS_COMPILATION=FALSE)
	fi
	# Battlemage and Lunar Lake (Xe2) only; no ULTs; without IGC the built-in kernels come as files from ocloc-docker.sh,
	# Intel's prebuilt kernels_bin repository not being public; long-running VM probe, small BAR, no ULLS: 0006, 0009.
	cmake -S "$SRC/neo" -B "$BLD/neo" -G Ninja "${X86[@]}" -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=Darwin -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=x86_64 \
		-DNEO_XEMAC_DIR="$REPO/user/xemac" -DIGC_DIR="$igcdir" -DGMM_DIR="$PREFIX" -DLEVEL_ZERO_ROOT="$PREFIX" \
		-DNEO_SKIP_UNIT_TESTS=1 -DNEO_SKIP_AUB_TESTS=1 "${builtins[@]}" \
		-DNEO_BUILD_WITH_OCL=$ocl -DBUILD_WITH_L0=TRUE -DDISABLE_WDDM_LINUX=TRUE -DNEO_DISABLE_LTO=TRUE \
		-DNEO_DISABLE_LD_GOLD=1 -DNEO_DISABLE_LD_LLD=1 \
		-DSUPPORT_GEN12LP=0 -DSUPPORT_XE_HPG_CORE=0 -DSUPPORT_XE_HPC_CORE=0 -DSUPPORT_XE3_CORE=0 -DSUPPORT_XE3P_CORE=0 \
		-DSUPPORT_XE2_HPG_CORE=1 -DSUPPORT_BMG=1 -DSUPPORT_LNL=1 -Wno-dev >/dev/null
	ninja -C "$BLD/neo" -j "$J" "${targets[@]}"
}

# The test machine's layout: bin/ze_hello and zes_info, lib/ with the driver, gmmlib and the loader, and kernels/ and
# builtins/ when ocloc-docker.sh has filled $L0_WORK/kernels and $L0_WORK/builtins. Every image finds the others
# through @rpath (@executable_path/../lib, @loader_path); ad-hoc signed; SHA256SUMS over everything.
stage() {
	rm -rf "$STAGE"
	mkdir -p "$STAGE/bin" "$STAGE/lib"
	[ -d "$W/kernels" ] && cp -R "$W/kernels" "$STAGE/"
	[ -d "$W/builtins" ] && cp -R "$W/builtins" "$STAGE/"
	cp -a "$PREFIX"/lib/libze_loader*.dylib "$PREFIX"/lib/libigdgmm*.dylib "$BLD"/neo/bin/libze_intel_gpu*.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
	[ -e "$BLD/neo/bin/libigdrcl.dylib" ] && cp -a "$BLD"/neo/bin/libigdrcl*.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
	if [ -n "$IGCP" ]; then
		# the compiler next to NEO (patch 0010 finds it there), and ocloc
		cp -a "$IGCP"/lib/libigc*.dylib "$IGCP"/lib/libigdfcl*.dylib "$IGCP"/lib/libopencl-clang*.dylib \
			"$IGCP"/lib/libiga64*.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
		cp "$BLD"/neo/bin/libocloc.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
		cp "$BLD"/neo/bin/ocloc-[0-9]* "$STAGE/bin/ocloc"
		# kernels/ with the staged ocloc (what ocloc-docker.sh does in a Linux container otherwise): the source (for
		# cl_hello source), its SPIR-V (ze_hello spirv) and the Battlemage binary (kernel)
		mkdir -p "$STAGE/kernels"
		local cl
		for cl in "$REPO"/user/tests/compute/kernels/*.cl; do
			cp "$cl" "$STAGE/kernels/"
			"$STAGE/bin/ocloc" compile -q -file "$cl" -device bmg -output "$(basename "$cl" .cl)" \
				-out_dir "$STAGE/kernels" >/dev/null
		done
		rm -f "$STAGE"/kernels/*.gen
	fi
	local f
	for f in "$STAGE"/lib/libze_intel_gpu.1.*.dylib "$STAGE"/lib/libigdrcl.dylib; do
		[ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] && install_name_tool -add_rpath @loader_path "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
	done
	clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=14.0 -O1 -Wall -I"$PREFIX/include" -o "$STAGE/bin/ze_hello" \
		"$REPO/user/tests/compute/ze_hello.c" -L"$PREFIX/lib" -lze_loader -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/../lib
	clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=14.0 -O1 -Wall -I"$PREFIX/include" -o "$STAGE/bin/zes_info" \
		"$REPO/user/tests/compute/zes_info.c" -L"$PREFIX/lib" -lze_loader -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/../lib
	if [ "${OCL:-0}" = 1 ] && [ -e "$PREFIX/lib/libOpenCL.1.dylib" ]; then
		cp -a "$PREFIX"/lib/libOpenCL*.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
		clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=14.0 -O1 -Wall -I"$PREFIX/include" -o "$STAGE/bin/cl_hello" \
			"$REPO/user/tests/compute/cl_hello.c" -L"$PREFIX/lib" -lOpenCL -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/../lib
	fi
	for f in "$STAGE"/bin/* "$STAGE"/lib/*.dylib; do
		[ -L "$f" ] || codesign -s - -f "$f" 2>/dev/null
	done
	(cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sort | xargs shasum -a 256 > SHA256SUMS) # not itself
	echo "staged in $STAGE:"
	(cd "$STAGE" && ls -l bin lib && ls | grep -E '^(kernels|builtins)$' | xargs -I{} sh -c 'echo "{}: $(ls {} | wc -l) files"')
}

steps=("$@")
[ ${#steps[@]} -gt 0 ] || steps=(fetch patch gmmlib loader igc-headers icd neo stage)
for s in "${steps[@]}"; do
	echo "== $s"
	case $s in
	fetch | patch | gmmlib | loader | icd | neo | stage) "$s" ;;
	igc-headers) igc_headers ;;
	*) echo "unknown step $s" >&2; exit 2 ;;
	esac
done

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build-sycl.sh [STEP...]: SYCL on macOS x86_64 over our Level Zero: Intel's DPC++ (intel/llvm) - the SYCL runtime
# libsycl, the Unified Runtime loader and its Level Zero adapters, UMF, and the clang -fsycl compiler with its tools and
# device libraries - built from one LLVM tree for x86_64 on the build Mac (Apple silicon: the build tools and the
# compiler run under Rosetta, as in build-igc.sh). See docs/design/DESIGN-sycl.md.
#   STEP: fetch patch configure compiler runtime stage (default: all, in that order); onednn (optional: fetch, patch
#         and build oneDNN's SYCL GPU library with the built compiler, into $SYCL_WORK/onednn-build; stage then takes
#         it when it is there)
#   SYCL_WORK  work directory (default $HOME/intelxe-sycl): src/intel-llvm, deps/ (pinned upstream checkouts; patched
#              on branch intelxe), build/, stage/ (what goes to the test machine)
#   L0_WORK    compute/build-neo.sh's work directory (default $HOME/intelxe-l0): the Level Zero loader and headers it
#              installed in prefix/, NEO's ze_intel_gpu.h, and (OCL=1) the OpenCL headers and ICD loader sources
#   IGC_PREFIX optional: compute/build-igc.sh's install. Its ocloc (staged by build-neo.sh in $L0_WORK/stage/bin) lets
#              the test program carry a Battlemage binary next to its SPIR-V (ahead-of-time, spir64_gen)
#   JOBS       ninja -j (default: all cores)
# Needs git, cmake >= 3.21, ninja and python3 on PATH, the Xcode command line tools, Rosetta on Apple silicon.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
W=${SYCL_WORK:-$HOME/intelxe-sycl}
L0W=${L0_WORK:-$HOME/intelxe-l0}
SRC=$W/src/intel-llvm
DEPS=$W/deps
BLD=$W/build
STAGE=${OUT:-$W/stage}
J=${JOBS:-$(/usr/sbin/sysctl -n hw.ncpu)}

# Pins. intel/llvm at the DPC++ v7.2.0 tag; the dependencies its CMake would fetch, at the revisions it names there
# (FetchContent is run disconnected: nothing is downloaded during the build). TREE = SHA-256 of `git ls-tree -r <rev>`
# (every path, mode and blob id of the revision: the checkouts are partial clones, so this is what can be hashed
# without fetching every blob).
DPCPP_URL=https://github.com/intel/llvm.git
DPCPP_TAG=v7.2.0
DPCPP_REV=71767974d44acf0464ebf4b26c2059781eb7d6ee
DPCPP_TREE=08d6ade04888c35b48fa93c52d71365967fa91aee1d2d5c4b58b2009d95f1eb3
UMF_URL=https://github.com/oneapi-src/unified-memory-framework.git
UMF_TAG=v1.2.0
UMF_REV=d8763834d68f9545db30bea5d092edd78ad3d748
UMF_TREE=8c058107871176aca133e9fd0258271ef7f03fd5aa99577b7ebb89626c667754
EMHASH_URL=https://github.com/ktprime/emhash.git
EMHASH_REV=5e131ba09a5290823fe71099d9c35eb5df5345b6
EMHASH_TREE=ca8e7447efc4c0f9f1422f8886e1f0ab30dc7335b004069049b098cb1f0151ef
SPVH_URL=https://github.com/KhronosGroup/SPIRV-Headers.git
SPVH_REV=5c50cbd25a40f8b60e44a2ccc2f1ba3c9e0d0299
SPVH_TREE=96ec83a58480759f36e39667a2b593b27d5e8cc2e0f9e4af6155f6a1a771a53a
VCI_URL=https://github.com/intel/vc-intrinsics.git
VCI_REV=4fc83e12979096db72c129bd432238d5ca397e4d
VCI_TREE=7add8f3a5f54bed11ea8e5b262b5b8c5405575f3380994152ca9d4d0a29dd263
# the XPTI framework's hash map (xptifw/src/CMakeLists.txt names this commit, version 1.3.12)
PHMAP_URL=https://github.com/greg7mdp/parallel-hashmap.git
PHMAP_REV=8a889d3699b3c09ade435641fb034427f3fd12b6
PHMAP_TREE=130db94cb553e4340b1981ba94b4bcfd8e943088a8f7eb534cd5940de804ce37
# oneDPL (oneAPI's parallel STL over SYCL; header-only), release tag oneDPL-release-2022.14.0
ONEDPL_URL=https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDPL.git
ONEDPL_TAG=oneDPL-release-2022.14.0
ONEDPL_REV=66efa97efe014565b2f8dd9e579efd76dd8cd9ec
ONEDPL_TREE=72b4f8f925897021ec14706ff79879a4bc092762412211ceec1ecd21d49006dd
# oneDNN (oneAPI's deep-learning primitives), release tag v3.14.2: built by the optional step `onednn` only
ONEDNN_URL=https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN.git
ONEDNN_TAG=v3.14.2
ONEDNN_REV=4db284662a37cf46401655b5ee99391d9de52c00
ONEDNN_TREE=14290b4ad45880d036959f78ef9a3ecf4bfd49b80e290027d8dc98823e004c63
# the parts of intel/llvm the build reads (sparse checkout)
DPCPP_PATHS=(buildbot clang cmake libc libclc libdevice llvm llvm-spirv opencl sycl sycl-jit third-party unified-runtime xpti
	xptifw)

command -v ninja >/dev/null || { echo "ninja is not on PATH (pip install ninja, or brew install ninja)" >&2; exit 1; }

tree_sum() { git -C "$1" ls-tree -r "$2" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-64; }

# dir url rev tree-sha256 [sparse paths...]
get() {
	local dir=$1 url=$2 rev=$3 sum=$4
	shift 4
	if [ ! -d "$dir/.git" ]; then
		mkdir -p "$dir"
		git -C "$dir" init -q
		git -C "$dir" remote add origin "$url"
		[ $# -eq 0 ] || git -C "$dir" sparse-checkout set "$@"
		git -C "$dir" fetch -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none origin "$rev"
		git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
	fi
	[ "$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse "$rev^{commit}")" = "$rev" ] || { echo "$dir: $rev missing" >&2; exit 1; }
	local got
	got=$(tree_sum "$dir" "$rev")
	[ "$got" = "$sum" ] || { echo "$dir: tree SHA-256 $got, pinned $sum" >&2; exit 1; }
	echo "$(basename "$dir") $rev ok"
}

fetch() {
	get "$SRC" "$DPCPP_URL" "$DPCPP_REV" "$DPCPP_TREE" "${DPCPP_PATHS[@]}"
	get "$DEPS/umf" "$UMF_URL" "$UMF_REV" "$UMF_TREE"
	get "$DEPS/emhash" "$EMHASH_URL" "$EMHASH_REV" "$EMHASH_TREE"
	get "$DEPS/spirv-headers" "$SPVH_URL" "$SPVH_REV" "$SPVH_TREE"
	get "$DEPS/vc-intrinsics" "$VCI_URL" "$VCI_REV" "$VCI_TREE"
	get "$DEPS/parallel-hashmap" "$PHMAP_URL" "$PHMAP_REV" "$PHMAP_TREE"
	get "$DEPS/onedpl" "$ONEDPL_URL" "$ONEDPL_REV" "$ONEDPL_TREE" include LICENSE.txt
}

# component dir, pinned revision, patch directory: branch intelxe = the pin + our series (git am)
apply_series() {
	local dir=$1 rev=$2 pdir=$3
	git -C "$dir" checkout -q -f -B intelxe "$rev"
	local p
	while read -r p; do
		[ -n "$p" ] || continue
		git -C "$dir" -c user.name=intelxe-build -c user.email=build@localhost am -q --keep-cr "$pdir/$p"
	done < "$pdir/series"
}

patch() {
	apply_series "$SRC" "$DPCPP_REV" "$HERE/patches/intel-llvm"
	apply_series "$DEPS/umf" "$UMF_REV" "$HERE/patches/umf"
}

configure() {
	local L0P=$L0W/prefix
	[ -e "$L0P/lib/libze_loader.dylib" ] || { echo "no Level Zero loader in $L0P (compute/build-neo.sh loader)" >&2; exit 1; }
	[ -e "$L0W/src/neo/level_zero/include/level_zero/ze_intel_gpu.h" ] || { echo "no NEO source in $L0W/src/neo" >&2; exit 1; }
	[ -d "$L0W/src/ocl-headers/CL" ] && [ -d "$L0W/src/ocl-icd-loader" ] ||
		{ echo "no OpenCL headers/ICD loader in $L0W/src (OCL=1 compute/build-neo.sh fetch)" >&2; exit 1; }
	# the adapters include <level_zero/ze_api.h> (the loader's) and <level_zero/ze_intel_gpu.h> (NEO's): one directory
	# with both, the loader's headers from build-neo.sh's prefix and NEO's from the pinned NEO source
	rm -rf "$W/l0-include"
	mkdir -p "$W/l0-include/level_zero"
	cp -R "$L0P/include/level_zero/." "$L0W/src/neo/level_zero/include/level_zero/." "$W/l0-include/level_zero/"
	# x86_64 on any build Mac: LLVM_HOST_TRIPLE and no CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME, so the build's own tools (tablegen, the
	# just-built clang compiling libdevice) are x86_64 and run under Rosetta (compute/build-igc.sh does the same).
	# DEFAULT_SYSROOT: the built clang finds the macOS SDK (libc++, libSystem) without -isysroot, for libdevice's host
	# objects and for SYCL programs.
	# Level Zero only (the OpenCL adapter is not built), no tests. XPTI tracing (libsycl's and the UR loader's trace
	# points, the xptifw dispatcher, sycl-trace/sycl-prof and their collectors) and sycl-jit (kernel_compiler's
	# in-process compilation of SYCL source; upstream's configure.py leaves both it and libdevice out on Darwin).
	PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$L0P/lib/pkgconfig cmake -S "$SRC/llvm" -B "$BLD" -G Ninja \
		-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
		-DLLVM_HOST_TRIPLE=x86_64-apple-darwin -DLLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD="X86;SPIRV" \
		-DDEFAULT_SYSROOT="$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)" \
		-DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_ZSTD=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_LIBXML2=OFF -DLLVM_ENABLE_LIBEDIT=OFF \
		-DLLVM_INCLUDE_TESTS=OFF -DLLVM_INCLUDE_BENCHMARKS=OFF -DLLVM_INCLUDE_EXAMPLES=OFF -DLLVM_INCLUDE_DOCS=OFF \
		-DCLANG_ENABLE_STATIC_ANALYZER=OFF -DCLANG_ENABLE_ARCMT=OFF \
		-DLLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS="clang;sycl;llvm-spirv;opencl;xpti;xptifw;libdevice;sycl-jit" \
		-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_PROJECTS="sycl;llvm-spirv;opencl;xpti;xptifw;libdevice;sycl-jit" \
		-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_SYCL_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/sycl" -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_LLVM_SPIRV_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/llvm-spirv" \
		-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_XPTI_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/xpti" -DXPTI_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/xpti" \
		-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_XPTIFW_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/xptifw" -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_SYCL_JIT_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/sycl-jit" \
		-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_LIBDEVICE_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/libdevice" -DLLVM_EXTERNAL_OPENCL_SOURCE_DIR="$SRC/opencl" \
		-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_SPIRV_HEADERS_SOURCE_DIR="$DEPS/spirv-headers" \
		-DSYCL_ENABLE_BACKENDS="level_zero;level_zero_v2" -DSYCL_ENABLE_XPTI_TRACING=ON \
		-DSYCL_ENABLE_EXTENSION_JIT=ON -DSYCL_JIT_ENABLE_WERROR=OFF -DSYCL_INCLUDE_TESTS=OFF \
		-DSYCL_ENABLE_MAJOR_RELEASE_PREVIEW_LIB=OFF \
		-DSYCL_ENABLE_WERROR=OFF -DXPTI_ENABLE_WERROR=OFF -DXPTI_ENABLE_TESTS=OFF -DSYCL_UR_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
		-DUR_ENABLE_TRACING=ON -DUR_ENABLE_SANITIZER=OFF -DUR_ENABLE_SYMBOLIZER=OFF -DUR_USE_EXTERNAL_UMF=OFF \
		-DUMF_HWLOC_STANDIN=ON -DUMF_BUILD_CUDA_PROVIDER=OFF -DUMF_BUILD_LIBUMF_POOL_JEMALLOC=OFF \
		-DL0_COMPUTE_RUNTIME_HEADERS="$W/l0-include" \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED=ON \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_UNIFIED-MEMORY-FRAMEWORK="$DEPS/umf" \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_EMHASH="$DEPS/emhash" \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_VC-INTRINSICS="$DEPS/vc-intrinsics" \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_PARALLEL-HASHMAP="$DEPS/parallel-hashmap" \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_OCL-HEADERS="$L0W/src/ocl-headers" \
		-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_OCL-ICD="$L0W/src/ocl-icd-loader" \
		-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$W/prefix"
}

# the compiler: clang (-fsycl), the offload tools the driver runs (sycl-post-link, llvm-spirv, clang-offload-wrapper,
# ...), and libdevice (the device libraries, compiled by the just-built clang)
compiler() {
	ninja -C "$BLD" -j "$J" sycl-compiler libsycldevice
}

# the runtime: libsycl (with the UR loader linked in), both Level Zero adapters, UMF, sycl-ls; sycl-jit (in-process
# SYCL compiler for kernel_compiler); XPTI: the xptifw dispatcher, sycl-trace and sycl-prof with their collectors
runtime() {
	ninja -C "$BLD" -j "$J" sycl-runtime-libraries ur_adapter_level_zero ur_adapter_level_zero_v2 umf sycl-ls \
		sycl-jit xptifw sycl-trace sycl-prof
}

# $1 output, $2 source, $3... extra flags: a test program with the built compiler for macOS 15 x86_64. The linker is
# named by path: /usr/bin/ld is a shim that loads libxcrun, which has no x86_64 slice, and the x86_64 clang runs it
# from a Rosetta process on an Apple-silicon build Mac.
sycl_cc() {
	local out=$1 src=$2
	shift 2
	"$BLD/bin/clang++" -fsycl "$@" -O2 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 --ld-path="$(xcrun -f ld)" \
		-o "$out" "$src" -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/../lib
}

# $1 output, $2 source, $3... extra flags: with a Battlemage binary next to the SPIR-V when an ocloc is there
# (compute/build-neo.sh with IGC_PREFIX stages one): the driver runs `ocloc` from PATH; the runtime takes the native
# image on a matching device and the SPIR-V elsewhere
sycl_cc_aot() {
	local out=$1 src=$2 oc=${OCLOC:-$L0W/stage/bin/ocloc}
	shift 2
	if [ -x "$oc" ]; then
		PATH=$(dirname "$oc"):$PATH sycl_cc "$out" "$src" -fsycl-targets=spir64_gen,spir64 \
			-Xsycl-target-backend=spir64_gen "-device bmg" "$@"
	else
		echo "no ocloc ($oc): $(basename "$out") carries SPIR-V only"
		sycl_cc "$out" "$src" -fsycl-targets=spir64 "$@"
	fi
}

# The host headers sycl_libs' run-time SYCL compilation reads (libc++ and the C library's, from the build Mac's SDK),
# copied into $1 with the SDK's layout: sycl-jit compiles SYCL source as the driver's device-only compile does, with
# the program's host target as the auxiliary triple, so it needs the platform's C++ headers; the test machine has no
# SDK. The list is what a device-only compile of the same source includes from the SDK.
rtc_sysroot() {
	local dst=$1 sdk tmp
	sdk=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)
	tmp=$(mktemp -d)
	awk '/R"SYCL\(/{p=1; next} /\)SYCL"/{p=0} p' "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/sycl_libs.cpp" > "$tmp/rtc.cpp"
	"$BLD/bin/clang++" -fsycl -fsycl-device-only -fsyntax-only -isysroot "$sdk" -MD -MF "$tmp/rtc.d" \
		-o /dev/null "$tmp/rtc.cpp"
	mkdir -p "$dst"
	tr ' \\' '\n\n' < "$tmp/rtc.d" | grep "^$sdk/" | sort -u | while read -r f; do
		mkdir -p "$dst/$(dirname "${f#"$sdk"/}")"
		cp "$f" "$dst/${f#"$sdk"/}"
	done
	cp "$sdk/SDKSettings.json" "$dst/"
	rm -rf "$tmp"
	echo "rtc-sysroot: $(find "$dst" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files from $sdk"
}

# The test machine's layout: bin/ sycl_hello (SPIR-V and, with ocloc, a Battlemage binary), sycl_hello_jit (SPIR-V
# only), sycl_libs (oneDPL and the kernel compiler; SPIR-V + Battlemage), sycl-ls, sycl-trace, sycl-prof; lib/ libsycl,
# the UR loader and adapters, UMF, sycl-jit, the XPTI dispatcher and the trace collectors (the Level Zero loader and
# driver come from the L0 stage); share/rtc_kernels.spv; rtc-sysroot/ (the SDK headers the run-time SYCL compile
# reads); night-sycl.sh; ad-hoc signed; SHA256SUMS over everything.
stage() {
	rm -rf "$STAGE"
	mkdir -p "$STAGE/bin" "$STAGE/lib" "$STAGE/share"
	cp -a "$BLD"/lib/libsycl.*dylib "$BLD"/lib/libur_adapter_level_zero*.dylib "$BLD"/lib/libumf.*dylib \
		"$BLD"/lib/libsycl-jit*.dylib "$BLD"/lib/libxptifw*.dylib "$BLD"/lib/libsycl_ur_trace_collector.dylib \
		"$BLD"/lib/libze_trace_collector.dylib "$BLD"/lib/libsycl_profiler_collector.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
	cp "$BLD/bin/sycl-ls" "$BLD/bin/sycl-trace" "$BLD/bin/sycl-prof" "$STAGE/bin/"
	# the build Mac's library directories as rpaths: @loader_path instead (UMF, xptifw beside them; the Level Zero
	# loader from DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, the L0 stage's lib/)
	local f r
	for f in "$STAGE"/lib/*.dylib; do
		[ -L "$f" ] && continue
		for r in $(otool -l "$f" | awk '/cmd LC_RPATH/{getline; getline; print $2}'); do
			case $r in /*) install_name_tool -delete_rpath "$r" "$f" ;; esac
		done
		otool -l "$f" | grep -q "path @loader_path " || install_name_tool -add_rpath @loader_path "$f"
	done
	sycl_cc_aot "$STAGE/bin/sycl_hello" "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/sycl_hello.cpp"
	sycl_cc "$STAGE/bin/sycl_hello_jit" "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/sycl_hello.cpp" -fsycl-targets=spir64
	sycl_cc_aot "$STAGE/bin/sycl_libs" "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/sycl_libs.cpp" -I"$DEPS/onedpl/include"
	# the SPIR-V kernel sycl_libs loads: OpenCL C through this clang and the SPIR-V translator
	"$BLD/bin/clang" --target=spir64 -cl-std=CL2.0 -Xclang -finclude-default-header -O2 -c -emit-llvm \
		-o "$STAGE/share/rtc_kernels.bc" "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/kernels/rtc_kernels.cl"
	"$BLD/bin/llvm-spirv" "$STAGE/share/rtc_kernels.bc" -o "$STAGE/share/rtc_kernels.spv"
	rm "$STAGE/share/rtc_kernels.bc"
	rtc_sysroot "$STAGE/rtc-sysroot"
	# oneDNN, when the onednn step was run: lib/libdnnl and bin/onednn_hello (SPIR-V only: oneDNN's own kernels are
	# compiled at run time, so it runs over the IGC stage anyway)
	local ob=$W/onednn-build
	if [ -e "$ob/src/libdnnl.dylib" ]; then
		cp -a "$ob"/src/libdnnl*.dylib "$STAGE/lib/"
		for r in $(otool -l "$STAGE"/lib/libdnnl.3.*.dylib | awk '/cmd LC_RPATH/{getline; getline; print $2}'); do
			case $r in /*) install_name_tool -delete_rpath "$r" "$STAGE"/lib/libdnnl.3.*.dylib ;; esac
		done
		otool -l "$STAGE"/lib/libdnnl.3.*.dylib | grep -q "path @loader_path " ||
			install_name_tool -add_rpath @loader_path "$STAGE"/lib/libdnnl.3.*.dylib
		sycl_cc "$STAGE/bin/onednn_hello" "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/onednn_hello.cpp" -fsycl-targets=spir64 \
			-I"$DEPS/onednn/include" -I"$ob/include" -L"$ob/src" -ldnnl
	else
		echo "no oneDNN ($ob): run the onednn step for lib/libdnnl and bin/onednn_hello"
	fi
	cp "$REPO/user/tests/sycl/night-sycl.sh" "$STAGE/"
	for f in "$STAGE"/bin/* "$STAGE"/lib/*.dylib; do
		[ -L "$f" ] || codesign -s - -f "$f" 2>/dev/null
	done
	(cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sort | xargs shasum -a 256 > SHA256SUMS)
	echo "staged in $STAGE ($(du -sh "$STAGE" | cut -f1)):"
	(cd "$STAGE" && ls -l bin lib)
}

# oneDNN for Intel GPUs through SYCL (Level Zero), no CPU engine, Xe2 kernels only (the B580), no graph API, tests or
# examples; compiled by the built clang (-fsycl objects need intel-llvm 0009 on Mach-O, and every link of them -fsycl:
# such an object is a bundler container, not a Mach-O file, so ld64 alone cannot read it). Patches onednn/: the Level
# Zero and OpenCL loaders by their macOS names, size_t != uint64_t. nGEN generates most kernels as Xe2 binaries; the
# OpenCL C ones are compiled at run time through the OpenCL device with the same UUID (NEO's OpenCL ICD), so a run
# needs the IGC stage and OCL_ICD_FILENAMES (oneDNN's other route, through kernel_compiler and ocloc, is its
# experimental ONEDNN_EXPERIMENTAL_SYCL_KERNEL_COMPILER, not used).
onednn() {
	local ob=$W/onednn-build ld
	get "$DEPS/onednn" "$ONEDNN_URL" "$ONEDNN_REV" "$ONEDNN_TREE"
	apply_series "$DEPS/onednn" "$ONEDNN_REV" "$HERE/patches/onednn"
	ld=$(xcrun -f ld)
	# a link-only -fsycl command ignores -mmacosx-version-min (the result would require the build Mac's macOS); the
	# environment variable is honoured (DESIGN-sycl.md section 7.3)
	export MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0
	cmake -S "$DEPS/onednn" -B "$ob" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
		-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER="$BLD/bin/clang" -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER="$BLD/bin/clang++" \
		-DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64 -DCMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR=x86_64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
		-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-fsycl --ld-path=$ld" -DCMAKE_SHARED_LINKER_FLAGS="-fsycl --ld-path=$ld" \
		-DDNNL_TARGET_ARCH=X64 -DDNNL_CPU_RUNTIME=NONE -DDNNL_GPU_RUNTIME=SYCL -DDNNL_GPU_VENDOR=INTEL \
		-DONEDNN_ENABLE_PRIMITIVE_GPU_ISA=XE2 -DONEDNN_BUILD_GRAPH=OFF -DDNNL_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
		-DDNNL_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DONEDNN_WERROR=OFF
	ninja -C "$ob" -j "$J" dnnl
}

steps=("$@")
[ ${#steps[@]} -gt 0 ] || steps=(fetch patch configure compiler runtime stage)
for s in "${steps[@]}"; do
	echo "== $s"
	case $s in
	fetch | patch | configure | compiler | runtime | stage | onednn) "$s" ;;
	*) echo "unknown step $s" >&2; exit 2 ;;
	esac
done

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# ocloc-docker.sh: Intel's offline compiler (ocloc, with IGC) in a Linux x86_64 container, for a build Mac without
# the macOS IGC build (compute/build-igc.sh), and as the reference compiler to compare the macOS one against
# (docs/design/DESIGN-level-zero.md, 4.3). The output is native Battlemage code (zebin), which the macOS Level Zero
# driver loads without a compiler.
#   compute/ocloc-docker.sh kernel FILE.cl OUTDIR      OUTDIR/<name>_bmg.bin, for zeModuleCreate(ZE_MODULE_FORMAT_NATIVE)
#   compute/ocloc-docker.sh builtins NEO_SRC OUTDIR    NEO's buffer built-in kernels (fill, copy, copy rect, kernel
#                                                      timestamps) for Battlemage in its four addressing modes, named as
#                                                      the driver's FileStorage looks them up in the working directory:
#                                                      20_1_0_<mode>_<kernel>.builtin_kernel.bin (IP= overrides 20_1_0)
#   compute/ocloc-docker.sh shell                      a shell in the container
# Needs docker that runs linux/amd64 images (OrbStack, or Docker Desktop with Rosetta). The packages are the compute-
# runtime 26.40.40196.8 release (ocloc) and IGC v2.42.6, checked against the sha256 sums the releases publish; they are
# kept in $L0_WORK/ocloc-debs and baked into the image intelxe-ocloc:26.40.40196.8 once.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
W=${L0_WORK:-$HOME/intelxe-l0}
DEBS=$W/ocloc-debs
IMAGE=intelxe-ocloc:26.40.40196.8
CR=https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/releases/download/26.40.40196.8
IGC=https://github.com/intel/intel-graphics-compiler/releases/download/v2.42.6
PKGS=(
	"$CR/intel-ocloc_26.40.40196.8-0_amd64.deb b2868d6d7958cc5ca28fa9b48a7d39961760ee39ef07673d5b58894dd53d6b4e"
	"$CR/libigdgmm12_22.10.2_amd64.deb 053fceadb84a1d2f9a30a0d1bc9b16424b3f1a90cc49900fcd80aadcf25c8a4d"
	"$IGC/intel-igc-core-2_2.42.6+23070_amd64.deb e20539632f2d99875d8f8b225d5da58b31f98baa54bb47c6328aa98ec473ab9d"
	"$IGC/intel-igc-opencl-2_2.42.6+23070_amd64.deb 7f5593cf828503ffb8450967768bde9209e22753bc576296e846b5a751011fa3"
)

image() {
	docker image inspect "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return
	mkdir -p "$DEBS"
	local p url sum f
	for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do
		url=${p% *} sum=${p#* } f=$DEBS/$(basename "$url")
		[ -f "$f" ] || curl -sSfL -o "$f" "$url"
		echo "$sum  $f" | shasum -a 256 -c - >/dev/null || { echo "checksum mismatch: $f" >&2; rm -f "$f"; exit 1; }
	done
	local ctx
	ctx=$(mktemp -d)
	cp "$DEBS"/*.deb "$ctx/"
	cat > "$ctx/Dockerfile" <<'EOF'
FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ubuntu:24.04
COPY *.deb /tmp/debs/
RUN apt-get -qq update && apt-get -qq install -y --no-install-recommends /tmp/debs/*.deb && rm -rf /tmp/debs /var/lib/apt/lists/*
EOF
	docker build -q --platform linux/amd64 -t "$IMAGE" "$ctx" >/dev/null
	rm -rf "$ctx"
}

run() { docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 "$@"; }

kernel() {
	local src out name
	src=$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)/$(basename "$1")
	mkdir -p "$2"
	out=$(cd "$2" && pwd)
	name=$(basename "$src" .cl)
	run -v "$(dirname "$src")":/in:ro -v "$out":/out -w /out "$IMAGE" \
		ocloc compile -q -file "/in/$(basename "$src")" -device bmg -output "$name"
	rm -f "$out/${name}_bmg.spv"
	ls -l "$out/${name}_bmg.bin"
}

# The options are those of shared/source/built_ins/kernels/CMakeLists.txt for Battlemage (XE2_HPG_CORE's builtin
# addressing modes in cmake/setup_platform_flags.cmake, the 20.1.0 release), source first to SPIR-V, then to the binary.
builtins() {
	local neo out
	neo=$(cd "$1" && pwd)
	mkdir -p "$2"
	out=$(cd "$2" && pwd)
	run -v "$neo/shared/source/built_ins/kernels":/in:ro -v "$out":/out -w /out -e IP="${IP:-20_1_0}" "$IMAGE" bash -c '
set -e
types="-Didx_t=uint -Dcoord2_t=uint2 -Dcoord4_t=uint4 -Doffset_t=uint"
wide="-Didx_t=ulong -Dcoord2_t=ulong2 -Dcoord4_t=ulong4 -Doffset_t=ulong"
lsc="-DLSC_STCC_DEFAULT=0 -DLSC_STCC_L1UC_L3UC=1 -DLSC_STCC_L1UC_L3WB=2 -DLSC_STCC_L1WT_L3UC=3 -DLSC_STCC_L1WT_L3WB=4 -DLSC_STCC_L1S_L3UC=5 -DLSC_STCC_L1S_L3WB=6 -DLSC_STCC_L1WB_L3WB=7 -DUSE_LSC_INTRINSICS_WB"
mkdir -p /tmp/w
for mode in bindful_image_stateless_buffer bindful_image_stateless_buffer_wide bindless_image_stateless_buffer bindless_image_stateless_buffer_wide; do
  t=$types; case $mode in *_wide) t=$wide;; esac
  addr=bindful; internal=()
  case $mode in bindless_*) addr=bindless; internal=(-internal_options "-cl-intel-use-bindless-mode -cl-intel-use-bindless-advanced-mode");; esac
  for k in copy_buffer_rect copy_buffer_to_buffer copy_kernel_timestamps fill_buffer; do
    ocloc -q -file /in/$k.builtin_kernel -spv_only -device bmg -heapless_mode disable -cl-intel-greater-than-4GB-buffer-required -64 \
      -output ${mode}_$k -out_dir /tmp/w "${internal[@]}" -options "$t $lsc -cl-kernel-arg-info"
    ocloc -q -file /tmp/w/${mode}_${k}_bmg.spv -spirv_input -device 20.1.0 -heapless_mode disable -cl-intel-greater-than-4GB-buffer-required \
      -64 -stateful_address_mode $addr -output ${IP}_${mode}_$k.builtin_kernel -output_no_suffix -out_dir /out "${internal[@]}" \
      -options "$t $lsc -cl-kernel-arg-info"
  done
done
rm -f /out/*.spv'
	ls "$out" | wc -l | xargs echo "built-in binaries in $out:"
}

case ${1:-} in
kernel) image; kernel "${2:?FILE.cl}" "${3:?OUTDIR}" ;;
builtins) image; builtins "${2:?NEO_SRC}" "${3:?OUTDIR}" ;;
shell) image; run -it "$IMAGE" bash ;;
*) sed -n '3,15p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
esac

From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:40:50 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 1/9] Portability fixes for macOS (Apple clang, libc++,
 libSystem)

- size_t is unsigned long and uint64_t unsigned long long on macOS:
  Math::nextPowerOfTwo/prevPowerOfTwo/log2 get size_t overloads (a size_t
  argument was ambiguous), Event's start timestamps are uint64_t as
  getGlobalTimestamps() writes them, and the mutable command list passes
  getPeerAllocation() the uintptr_t it takes
- libc++ defines std::mutex in an inline namespace (std::__1): include
  <mutex> instead of forward-declaring std::mutex
- the Annex K stand-ins (memcpy_s, strcpy_s, fopen_s, ...) are built on
  macOS as on Linux: <sys/cdefs.h> sets __STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__ and the
  libc reports __STDC_LIB_EXT1__ for memset_s alone
- gmmlib takes its Linux GMM_INIT_IN_ARGS (FileDescriptor) on macOS too
- RTLD_DEEPBIND is glibc's; macOS's two-level namespace already binds a
  library's references to its own images
- sysman's PMU readers: no perf_event_open on macOS, and syscall 298 is
  another call there, so perfEventOpen fails with ENOSYS

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

FILE: compute/patches/compute-runtime/0003-macOS-NEO-s-system-calls-over-xemac-the-user-side-of.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:41:00 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 3/9] macOS: NEO's system calls over xemac, the user side of
 IntelXe.kext

The Linux DRM/xe backend is built unchanged: every call it makes to the
kernel goes through NEO::SysCalls, and sys_calls_macos.cpp replaces
sys_calls_linux.cpp. The render node is IntelXe.kext's xe interface
(Linux's xe uAPI behind an IOUserClient), reached through xemac:

- open("/dev/dri/renderD128") is xemac_open(); /dev/dri/by-path does
  not exist, so Drm::discoverDevices tries the renderD nodes in turn and
  finds the one device. XEMAC_FAKE=1 gives xemac's canned Battlemage.
- ioctl, mmap, munmap and close of that fd go to xemac. The request
  numbers are those drm.h/xe_drm.h encode on a BSD system
  (<sys/ioccom.h>), which the kext decodes.
- /sys/dev/char/226:128 -> ../../devices/.../0000:bb:dd.f/drm/renderD128
  is synthesized from the kext's PCI identity, so getPciPath() works;
  readlink("/proc/self/exe") is answered with proc_pidpath() (AIL).
- prctl, pidfd_open and pidfd_getfd fail with ENOSYS; dlinfo
  (RTLD_DI_LINKMAP) walks dyld's image list; mremap(MREMAP_FIXED) and
  MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE are Mach VM calls; SOCK_CLOEXEC is FD_CLOEXEC.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

diff --git a/shared/source/os_interface/macos/sys_calls_macos.cpp b/shared/source/os_interface/macos/sys_calls_macos.cpp

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+// NEO's system calls on macOS. The Linux DRM/xe backend (shared/source/os_interface/linux) is built unchanged: every
+// call it makes to the kernel goes through NEO::SysCalls, and here the render node is IntelXe.kext's xe interface,
+// reached through xemac (xemac.h: xemac_open/xemac_ioctl/xemac_mmap in place of open/ioctl/mmap of a DRM node):
+//  - open("/dev/dri/renderD128") opens the kext's xe client (xemac_open; XEMAC_FAKE=1 gives a canned Battlemage
+//    without the kext). There is one device; /dev/dri/by-path does not exist, so Drm::discoverDevices tries the
+//    renderD nodes in turn.
+//  - ioctl, mmap, munmap and close of that fd go to xemac. The ioctl numbers are those NEO's drm.h/xe_drm.h encode on a
+//    BSD system (<sys/ioccom.h>), which is what the kext decodes.
+//  - The PCI address NEO reads from /sys/dev/char/<major>:<minor> -> ../../devices/.../0000:bb:dd.f/drm/renderD128 is
+//    synthesized from the kext's PCI identity (xemac_pci_info), so getPciPath() and the BDF-based code work.
+//  - Linux-only calls without a macOS counterpart (prctl, pidfd_open, pidfd_getfd) fail with ENOSYS, which their
+//    callers already handle (IPC handles by pidfd are a Linux >= 5.6 feature that NEO probes for).
+//  - dlinfo(RTLD_DI_LINKMAP) is answered from dyld's image list (see link.h in macos/include), readlink of
+//    /proc/self/exe from proc_pidpath().
+//  - mremap/MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE are done with the Mach VM calls.
+
+#include "shared/source/os_interface/linux/sys_calls.h"
+
+#include "xemac.h"
+
+#include <cerrno>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <cstring>
+#include <dirent.h>
+#include <dlfcn.h>
+#include <fcntl.h>
+#include <link.h>
+#include <mach-o/dyld.h>
+#include <mach/mach.h>
+#include <mach/mach_vm.h>
+#include <mutex>
+#include <poll.h>
+#include <string>
+#include <string_view>
+#include <sys/file.h>
+#include <sys/ioctl.h>
+#include <sys/resource.h>
+#include <sys/socket.h>
+#include <sys/stat.h>
+#include <sys/types.h>
+#include <sys/un.h>
+#include <unistd.h>
+#include <vector>
+
+#include <libproc.h>
+
+extern char **environ;
+
+namespace NEO {
+
+namespace SysCalls {
+
+namespace {
+// The one render node. NEO tries /dev/dri/renderD128 + i for i < 64; only the first answers.
+constexpr const char *renderNode = "/dev/dri/renderD128";
+// What getDevicePath() answers for the xemac fd; access() and readlink() recognise it.
+constexpr const char *devicePathOfRenderNode = "/sys/dev/char/226:128";
+
+bool isRenderNode(const char *file) {
+    return file && std::strcmp(file, renderNode) == 0;
+}
+
+bool isSyntheticDevicePath(const char *path) {
+    return path && std::strcmp(path, devicePathOfRenderNode) == 0;
+}
+
+int openRenderNode() {
+    int fd = xemac_open();
+    if (fd < 0 && errno == 0) {
+        errno = ENOENT;
+    }
+    return fd;
+}
+
+// The xemac fd of the process (one device), for readlink() of the synthetic device path.
+int anyXemacFd = -1;
+} // namespace
+
+char **getEnviron() {
+    return environ;
+}
+
+void exit(int code) {
+    std::exit(code);
+}
+
+unsigned int getProcessId() {
+    static unsigned int pid = ::getpid();
+    return pid;
+}
+
+unsigned int getCurrentProcessId() {
+    return ::getpid();
+}
+
+std::string getProcessName() {
+    char path[PROC_PIDPATHINFO_MAXSIZE] = {0};
+    if (proc_pidpath(::getpid(), path, sizeof(path)) <= 0) {
+        return "";
+    }
+    std::string executablePath(path);
+    auto lastSeparator = executablePath.find_last_of('/');
+    if (lastSeparator != std::string::npos) {
+        return executablePath.substr(lastSeparator + 1u);
+    }
+    return executablePath;
+}
+
+unsigned long getNumThreads() {
+    thread_act_array_t threads = nullptr;
+    mach_msg_type_number_t count = 0;
+    if (task_threads(mach_task_self(), &threads, &count) != KERN_SUCCESS) {
+        return 0;
+    }
+    for (mach_msg_type_number_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+        mach_port_deallocate(mach_task_self(), threads[i]);
+    }
+    vm_deallocate(mach_task_self(), reinterpret_cast<vm_address_t>(threads), count * sizeof(thread_act_t));
+    return count;
+}
+
+bool isShutdownInProgress() {
+    return false;
+}
+
+int mkdir(const std::string &path) {
+    return ::mkdir(path.c_str(), S_IRWXU | S_IRWXG | S_IROTH | S_IXOTH);
+}
+
+int rmdir(const std::string &path) {
+    return ::rmdir(path.c_str());
+}
+
+int close(int fd) {
+    if (xemac_is_fd(fd)) {
+        if (fd == anyXemacFd) {
+            anyXemacFd = -1;
+        }
+        return xemac_close(fd);
+    }
+    return ::close(fd);
+}
+
+int open(const char *file, int flags) {
+    if (isRenderNode(file)) {
+        int fd = openRenderNode();
+        if (fd >= 0) {
+            anyXemacFd = fd;
+        }
+        return fd;
+    }
+    if (file && std::strncmp(file, "/dev/dri/", 9) == 0) {
+        errno = ENOENT; // other render and card nodes: no such device
+        return -1;
+    }
+    return ::open(file, flags);
+}
+
+int openWithMode(const char *file, int flags, int mode) {
+    if (isRenderNode(file)) {
+        return open(file, flags);
+    }
+    return ::open(file, flags, mode);
+}

+void sync() {
+    ::sync();
+}

+int fsync(int fd) {
+    return ::fsync(fd);

+int ioctl(int fileDescriptor, unsigned long int request, void *arg) {
+    if (xemac_is_fd(fileDescriptor)) {
+        return xemac_ioctl(fileDescriptor, request, arg);
+    }
+    return ::ioctl(fileDescriptor, request, arg);

+void *dlopen(const char *filename, int flag) {
+    return ::dlopen(filename, flag);
+}
+
+// dlinfo(RTLD_DI_LINKMAP): the loaded images as a link_map list. For the handle of a library, its own entry (the
+// image whose RTLD_NOLOAD open gives the same handle); for dlopen(nullptr), the whole list from the main executable on.
+int dlinfo(void *handle, int request, void *info) {
+    if (request != RTLD_DI_LINKMAP || !handle || !info) {
+        errno = EINVAL;
+        return -1;
+    }
+    struct Images {
+        std::vector<std::string> names;
+        std::vector<link_map> maps;
+    };
+    static thread_local Images images;
+    images.names.clear();
+    images.maps.clear();
+
+    const uint32_t count = _dyld_image_count();
+    void *self = ::dlopen(nullptr, RTLD_LAZY | RTLD_NOLOAD);
+    const bool wholeProcess = (self == handle);
+    if (self) {
+        ::dlclose(self);
+    }
+    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+        const char *name = _dyld_get_image_name(i);
+        if (!name) {
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (!wholeProcess) {
+            void *h = ::dlopen(name, RTLD_LAZY | RTLD_NOLOAD);
+            if (h) {
+                ::dlclose(h);
+            }
+            if (h != handle) {
+                continue;
+            }
+        }
+        images.names.emplace_back(name);
+        if (!wholeProcess) {
+            break;
+        }
+    }
+    if (images.names.empty()) {
+        errno = ENOENT;
+        return -1;
+    }
+    images.maps.resize(images.names.size());
+    for (size_t i = 0; i < images.maps.size(); i++) {
+        images.maps[i] = {};
+        images.maps[i].l_name = images.names[i].data();
+        images.maps[i].l_next = i + 1 < images.maps.size() ? &images.maps[i + 1] : nullptr;
+        images.maps[i].l_prev = i > 0 ? &images.maps[i - 1] : nullptr;
+    }
+    *static_cast<link_map **>(info) = images.maps.data();
+    return 0;
+}
+
+int access(const std::string &pathName, int mode) {
+    if (isSyntheticDevicePath(pathName.c_str())) {
+        return anyXemacFd >= 0 ? 0 : (errno = ENOENT, -1);
+    }
+    return ::access(pathName.c_str(), mode);
+}

+int readlink(const char *path, char *buf, size_t bufsize) {
+    if (path && std::strcmp(path, "/proc/self/exe") == 0) {
+        // the executable's path, which AIL (application-specific settings) and the compiler cache key on
+        char exe[PROC_PIDPATHINFO_MAXSIZE] = {0};
+        int len = proc_pidpath(::getpid(), exe, sizeof(exe));
+        if (len <= 0) {
+            errno = ENOENT;
+            return -1;
+        }
+        size_t n = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(len), bufsize);
+        std::memcpy(buf, exe, n);
+        return static_cast<int>(n);
+    }
+    if (isSyntheticDevicePath(path)) {
+        // /sys/dev/char/226:128 -> ../../devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:01.0/0000:bb:dd.f/drm/renderD128, as on Linux for
+        // a discrete GPU behind a root port. getPciPath() takes the 12 characters before /drm/render.
+        struct xemac_pci_info pci = {};
+        if (anyXemacFd < 0 || xemac_pci_info(anyXemacFd, &pci) != 0) {
+            errno = ENOENT;
+            return -1;
+        }
+        char link[256];
+        int len = snprintf(link, sizeof(link), "../../devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:01.0/0000:%02x:%02x.%x/drm/renderD128",
+                           pci.bus, pci.dev, pci.func);
+        if (len < 0) {
+            errno = EINVAL;
+            return -1;
+        }
+        size_t n = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(len), bufsize);
+        std::memcpy(buf, link, n);
+        return static_cast<int>(n);
+    }
+    return static_cast<int>(::readlink(path, buf, bufsize));
+}
+
+int getDevicePath(int deviceFd, char *buf, size_t &bufSize) {
+    if (xemac_is_fd(deviceFd)) {
+        snprintf(buf, bufSize, "%s", devicePathOfRenderNode);
+        return 0;
+    }
+    struct stat st;
+    if (::fstat(deviceFd, &st)) {
+        return -1;
+    }
+    snprintf(buf, bufSize, "/sys/dev/char/%d:%d", major(st.st_rdev), minor(st.st_rdev));
+    return 0;
+}

+}
+
+// mremap(MREMAP_MAYMOVE | MREMAP_FIXED): the pages of [oldAddress, +size) move to newAddress, replacing what was there,
+// and the old range is unmapped.
+void *mremapFixed(void *oldAddress, size_t size, void *newAddress) noexcept {
+    mach_vm_address_t target = reinterpret_cast<mach_vm_address_t>(newAddress);
+    vm_prot_t cur = VM_PROT_NONE, max = VM_PROT_NONE;
+    kern_return_t kr = mach_vm_remap(mach_task_self(), &target, size, 0, VM_FLAGS_FIXED | VM_FLAGS_OVERWRITE,
+                                     mach_task_self(), reinterpret_cast<mach_vm_address_t>(oldAddress), false, &cur, &max,
+                                     VM_INHERIT_COPY);
+    if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) {
+        errno = (kr == KERN_NO_SPACE || kr == KERN_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE) ? ENOMEM : EINVAL;
+        return MAP_FAILED;
+    }
+    mach_vm_deallocate(mach_task_self(), reinterpret_cast<mach_vm_address_t>(oldAddress), size);
+    return reinterpret_cast<void *>(target);
+}
+
+// mmap(MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE | MAP_NORESERVE, PROT_NONE): reserve exactly [address, +size) unless something is there.
+void *mmapFixedNoReplace(void *address, size_t size) noexcept {
+    mach_vm_address_t at = reinterpret_cast<mach_vm_address_t>(address);
+    kern_return_t kr = mach_vm_allocate(mach_task_self(), &at, size, VM_FLAGS_FIXED);
+    if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS) {
+        errno = (kr == KERN_NO_SPACE) ? EEXIST : ENOMEM;
+        return MAP_FAILED;
+    }
+    mach_vm_protect(mach_task_self(), at, size, false, VM_PROT_NONE);
+    return reinterpret_cast<void *>(at);
+}

Subject: [PATCH 4/9] cmake: build on macOS (x86_64) against xemac

- NEO_XEMAC_DIR (required on macOS) names the xemac directory of
  intel-gpu-macos-driver (user/xemac); its xemac.c and our
  sys_calls_macos.cpp replace sys_calls_linux.cpp in the Level Zero and
  OpenCL libraries, linked with IOKit and CoreFoundation. xemac.c's
  "drm-uapi/*.h" resolve to the kext's own uAPI copies (NEO_XEMAC_UAPI_DIR,
  by default <xemac>/../uapi).
- the macOS stand-in headers come before the system ones
- Apple clang is "AppleClang": take the clang branches (MATCHES Clang),
  so GCC-only warning flags are not passed to it; libc++ deprecations
  stay warnings
- no forced Ninja response files: Apple's ar takes no @file
- no librt; dl and pthread are libSystem
- ld64 has no version scripts: the global: patterns become an exported
  symbols list (neo_apple_export_symbols); -Bsymbolic has no Mach-O
  counterpart and needs none

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+    endforeach()
+    set(_file "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${target}.exported_symbols")

+  endfunction()

 macOS

- IoctlHelperXe created every VM with DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE.
  A kernel that implements the xe uAPI without long-running mode
  (IntelXe.kext before its lrmode branch) refuses it, and device
  creation failed. The flag is now probed once with a scratch VM; a
  kernel that accepts it (IntelXe.kext since lrmode: no job timeout,
  user-fence out-syncs only, preemption for moves and frees) gets LR
  VMs as on Linux; without it NEO runs in dma-fence mode VMs: the same
  exec and bind ioctls with user fences, but a job is subject to the
  kernel's job timeout.
- isSmallBarConfigAllowed() is true on macOS: the B580's CPU-visible
  window is 1 GB of its 12 GB there, and the kext maps a VRAM BO into the
  window when it is mapped and moves it to system memory when it cannot
  enter (as xe's fault handler does). Linux NEO refuses such a device on
  xe ("Resizable BAR not detected").

+// A kernel that implements the xe uAPI without long-running VMs (IntelXe.kext on macOS before its lrmode branch)
+// refuses DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE. NEO then runs in dma-fence mode VMs: the same exec and bind ioctls with user

+bool IoctlHelperXe::isLongRunningVmSupported() {
+    if (longRunningVmSupport < 0) {
+        struct drm_xe_vm_create vmCreate = {};
+        vmCreate.flags = DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE;
+        longRunningVmSupport = 0;
+        if (IoctlHelper::ioctl(DrmIoctl::gemVmCreate, &vmCreate) == 0) {
+            struct drm_xe_vm_destroy vmDestroy = {};
+            vmDestroy.vm_id = vmCreate.vm_id;
+            IoctlHelper::ioctl(DrmIoctl::gemVmDestroy, &vmDestroy);
+            longRunningVmSupport = 1;
+        }
+        XELOG(" -> IoctlHelperXe::%s %d\n", NEO_FUNCTION_NAME, longRunningVmSupport);
+    }
+    return longRunningVmSupport == 1;

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:57:06 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 8/9] device: thread-group preemption when there is no compiler

Mid-thread preemption saves the threads' state with the SIP kernel,
which NEO gets from the compiler (IGC). Without a compiler library
Device::isStateSipRequired() is false, but PreemptionHelper's state SIP
programming asks for the SIP kernel when the mode is MidThread and
aborts (built_ins.cpp: no compiler interface) at the first launch on a
compute queue. A device whose default is MidThread now preempts at
thread-group boundaries when no compiler interface can be created: the
macOS port until IGC is ported. ForcePreemptionMode still overrides.

FILE: compute/patches/compute-runtime/0009-xe-no-direct-submission-without-long-running-VMs.patch

From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:03:03 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 9/9] xe: no direct submission without long-running VMs

Direct submission (ULLS) starts one batch that runs on the engine for
good, spinning on a semaphore while the driver appends work to its
ring. Xe2 enables it by default. In a dma-fence-mode VM, which NEO now
falls back to when the kernel refuses DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE,
that batch meets the job timeout and the queue is reset and banned.
IoctlHelper::isDirectSubmissionAllowedByKmd() lets the xe helper veto
it when long-running VMs are not available; EnableDirectSubmission
still overrides. A kernel that accepts LR VMs (IntelXe.kext since its
lrmode branch: their jobs have no timeout) passes the probe of patch 6,
and ULLS is on as on Linux.

FILE: compute/patches/compute-runtime/0010-macOS-find-the-compiler-libraries-next-to-NEO.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:46:49 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 10/12] macOS: find the compiler libraries next to NEO

NEO loads IGC by leaf name (IGC_LIBRARY_NAME, FCL_LIBRARY_NAME from
igc.opencl.h: libigc.2.dylib, libigdfcl.2.dylib). On macOS dlopen() of
a leaf name searches LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH and the fallback
paths (/usr/local/lib, /usr/lib) only, not the directory of the image
that calls it, so a staged lib/ directory worked only with
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH set. SysCalls::dlopen now retries a leaf name that was
not found in the directory of the image it is in (libze_intel_gpu,
libigdrcl or libocloc), where Linux packages put the compiler too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

 .../os_interface/macos/sys_calls_macos.cpp    | 20 ++++++++++++++++++-

+// A leaf name (the compiler: libigc.2.dylib, libigdfcl.2.dylib) that dlopen() does not find on DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH or
+// the fallback paths is looked for next to this library, as Linux finds it in the same lib directory as NEO.
 void *dlopen(const char *filename, int flag) {
-    return ::dlopen(filename, flag);
+    void *handle = ::dlopen(filename, flag);
+    if (handle || !filename || std::strchr(filename, '/')) {
+        return handle;
+    }
+    static const char anchor = 0;
+    Dl_info info = {};
+    if (!dladdr(&anchor, &info) || !info.dli_fname) {
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    std::string path(info.dli_fname);
+    const auto slash = path.rfind('/');
+    if (slash == std::string::npos) {
+        return nullptr;
+    }
+    path.resize(slash + 1);
+    path += filename;
+    return ::dlopen(path.c_str(), flag);
 }

FILE: compute/patches/compute-runtime/0011-ocloc-build-on-macOS.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:54:39 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 11/12] ocloc: build on macOS

The offline compiler (ocloc, libocloc) is NEO's command-line front end
to IGC; on macOS it compiles OpenCL C and SPIR-V to Battlemage binaries
on the build Mac, and NEO's build can use it for the built-in kernels.

- libocloc takes the macOS system calls (sys_calls_macos.cpp and xemac,
  NEO_SYS_CALLS_SOURCES/LIBS as the drivers do) instead of
  sys_calls_linux.cpp, and an exported-symbols list made from
  ocloc.exports (neo_apple_export_symbols) instead of the version script
- ocloc has rpaths @executable_path and @executable_path/../lib (NEO
  builds with CMAKE_SKIP_RPATH): libocloc next to it in the build tree,
  in ../lib in a staged one
- the build-time ocloc command (built-in kernels) sets DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH,
  which dyld reads, instead of LD_LIBRARY_PATH
- IGA (ocloc disasm/asm) is dlopen()ed as libiga64.2.dylib, the Mach-O
  name, not libiga64.dylib.2
- ocloc_supported_devices_helper_linux.cpp: the former-ocloc output
  lengths are uint64_t as the API declares them (size_t is unsigned long,
  uint64_t unsigned long long on macOS)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

FILE: compute/patches/compute-runtime/0012-buffer-pools-the-pool-buffer-is-still-the-pool-s-whi.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:13:17 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 12/12] buffer pools: the pool buffer is still the pool's while
 it is destroyed

clReleaseContext aborted on macOS (reference_tracked_object.h:137,
"current < 0") as soon as the context had a small-buffers pool: the
context destroys its pools, a pool destroys its buffer (mainStorage, a
unique_ptr), and MemObj::~MemObj asks the context whether the buffer is
a pool buffer (Context::isPoolBuffer compares mainStorage.get()) to
know whether it holds a context reference to drop. libstdc++ deletes
the object and then clears the pointer; libc++ clears the pointer
first, so with libc++ the answer was "no", the buffer dropped a
reference it never took and the count went below zero.
AbstractBuffersPool now deletes its buffer before it clears the
pointer, which gives the same answer with either library.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
---
 shared/source/utilities/buffer_pool_allocator.h | 10 +++++++++-
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/shared/source/utilities/buffer_pool_allocator.h b/shared/source/utilities/buffer_pool_allocator.h
index a76aab8ccb..5dac59a3ac 100644
--- a/shared/source/utilities/buffer_pool_allocator.h
+++ b/shared/source/utilities/buffer_pool_allocator.h
@@ -46,7 +46,15 @@ struct AbstractBuffersPool : public NonCopyableClass {
     AbstractBuffersPool(MemoryManager *memoryManager, OnChunkFreeCallback onChunkFreeCallback, const SmallBuffersParams &params);
     AbstractBuffersPool(AbstractBuffersPool &&bufferPool) noexcept = default;
     AbstractBuffersPool &operator=(AbstractBuffersPool &&other) noexcept = delete;
-    virtual ~AbstractBuffersPool() = default;
+    virtual ~AbstractBuffersPool() {
+        // The buffer must still be the pool's while it is destroyed: MemObj::~MemObj asks the context whether it is a
+        // pool buffer (Context::isPoolBuffer: mainStorage.get() == buffer) to know whether it holds a context
+        // reference. libc++'s unique_ptr clears its pointer before it deletes the object (libstdc++'s after), so the
+        // answer was "no" with libc++ (macOS), the context's internal reference count went below zero and
+        // clReleaseContext aborted. Delete first, clear afterwards, with either library.
+        delete mainStorage.get();
+        static_cast<void>(mainStorage.release());
+    }
 
     void tryFreeFromPoolBuffer(BufferParentType *possiblePoolBuffer, size_t offset, size_t size);
     bool isPoolBuffer(const BufferParentType *buffer) const;

From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:01:08 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 1/5] cmake: build libigc and libigdfcl on macOS (Mach-O, ld64)

IGC's CMake knows Windows, Linux and Android. macOS is built as Linux
(the same POSIX user-mode code: dlopen, pthreads, the LINUX/ICBE_LINUX
definitions, LLVM_ON_UNIX), with the ELF/GNU-linker specifics replaced:

- architecture detection: Darwin is a "Linux" OS; the processor comes
  from CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES when set (an x86_64 build on an arm64
  Mac), and the host is the target (a Mac runs what it builds, natively
  or under Rosetta), so no cross-compilation is set up
- ld64 has no --whole-archive/--start-group: the archives whose members
  are only reached at run time (the BiF resources of libigc, the OpenCL
  C header resource of libigdfcl, found by dlsym) are linked with
  -force_load (igc_link_whole_archive); ld64 resolves archives over the
  whole link line without groups
- the GNU/ELF-only options are removed from the compile and link flags:
  -Bsymbolic (a two-level-namespace dylib binds its own references
  already), -z relro/now/noexecstack (dyld's defaults), --no-undefined
  (ld64's default; -undefined dynamic_lookup, which the clang branch
  adds, would turn it off) and --gc-sections (-dead_strip instead);
  no --exclude-libs
- the version script that keeps LLVM's symbols out of libigc's exports
  becomes an exported-symbols list made by
  Scripts/igc_create_exports_list_macos.sh: the same selection (IGC's
  default-visibility definitions and the BiF resources) read with nm -m

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+# macOS counterpart of igc_create_linker_script.sh: ld64 has no version scripts, so the symbols libigc exports are
+# given as an -exported_symbols_list. Same selection as the Linux script: the non-hidden (default visibility)
+# definitions of IGC's own objects and of the libraries it names (the BiF resources: data, found by dlsym);
+# everything else, LLVM included, stays local to the dylib.
+#   $1 output file, $2 BiF library or "null", $3 DX10, $4 DXIL, $5 Vulkan FE library or "null", then objects.
+
+readonly OUT=$1
+readonly BIF_LIBRARY=$2
+readonly VULKAN_FE_LIBRARY=$5
+shift 5
+
+exported() {
+    # nm -m: "external" = default visibility, "private external" = hidden
+    nm -m -g -U "$@" 2>/dev/null | grep ' external ' | grep -v 'private external' | awk '{print $NF}'
+}
+
+{
+    [[ "$BIF_LIBRARY" != "null" ]] && exported "$BIF_LIBRARY"
+    [[ "$VULKAN_FE_LIBRARY" != "null" ]] && exported "$VULKAN_FE_LIBRARY"
+    objs=()
+    for f in "$@"; do
+        [[ $f == *.o ]] && objs+=("$f")
+    done
+    [[ ${#objs[@]} -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s\0' "${objs[@]}" | xargs -0 nm -m -g -U 2>/dev/null | grep ' external ' |
+        grep -v 'private external' | awk '{print $NF}'
+} | grep -v ':$' | sort -u > "$OUT.tmp"
+mv "$OUT.tmp" "$OUT"

+  elseif(ANDROID OR (CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME MATCHES "Linux|Darwin"))

From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:01:08 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 2/5] macOS: the Linux headers and code paths in IGC's sources

- LoadBuffer.cpp (libigdfcl's resources): no <link.h> (ELF) or
  <linux/limits.h> on macOS; <limits.h> has PATH_MAX. The resources are
  found by dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, name) as on Linux: Mach-O exports them
  with a leading underscore, which dlsym adds
- igax.hpp: macOS has no <malloc.h>; malloc and free are in <stdlib.h>
- the __linux__ branches that are POSIX or compiler rather than Linux
  are taken on macOS too: iStdLib's bit scans (__builtin_clz/ffs instead
  of loops), atomic reference counts (__sync builtins; the Windows
  Interlocked* calls otherwise), GetModuleFileName (an #error
  otherwise), the GCC diagnostic pragmas around LLVM headers, the
  default visibility of GenISA getDeclaration, the dump directories
  (/tmp/IntelIGC) and the IGC_* environment variables
  (IGC_DEBUG_VARIABLES, LINUX_RELEASE_MODE)
- SysUtils::GetProcessName: getprogname() instead of /proc/<pid>/cmdline

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Subject: [PATCH 4/5] cmake: Apple's ar and libSystem; LLVM 22's deprecations
 stay warnings

- RenderSurfaceStateIRBG and RTStackReflectionIRBG are static libraries
  whose sources are all headers (HEADER_FILE_ONLY): GNU ar makes an
  empty archive, Apple's ar(1) refuses ("no archive members"); on
  macOS each gets one empty object

  librt, clock_gettime is in libSystem
- Apple clang reports the deprecations of LLVM 22 that vc-intrinsics
  v0.25.0 still uses (PointerType::get with a pointee type,
  InsertPosition): -Wno-error=deprecated-declarations on macOS, so they
  are warnings as in the GCC builds

From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:01:15 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 5/5] macOS: size_t is not uint64_t

On x86_64 Linux size_t and uint64_t are both unsigned long; on macOS
uint64_t is unsigned long long, a distinct type of the same width.
Code that relies on them being one type does not compile there:

- MDFrameWork: the metadata of size_t fields (allocSize, ...) found no
  CreateNode/readNode overload (int, unsigned, uint64_t are ambiguous
  for unsigned long): size_t overloads that forward to uint64_t
- OCLRuntimeInfoPrinter (VC): LLVM's YAML traits have no unsigned long:
  one that forwards to uint64_t's
- EstimateFunctionSize: ScaledNumber<uint64_t>::toInt<size_t> compares
  ambiguously; toInt<uint64_t>
- Stats: %ju/%jd/%#jx for uint64_t (uintmax_t is unsigned long on both,
  so it matched on Linux only): PRIu64/PRId64/PRIx64

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

FILE: compute/patches/intel-llvm/0001-clang-offload-wrapper-no-ELF-section-names-on-Mach-O.patch

From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: intelxe-build <build@localhost>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:07:12 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 1/5] clang-offload-wrapper: no ELF section names on Mach-O

The device images went to __CLANG_OFFLOAD_BUNDLE__<kind>-<triple>, the
registration constructors to .text.startup and the image info to .tgtimg.
None is a valid Mach-O section specifier (segment,section), so the wrapper
module does not compile for a Darwin host. On Mach-O they stay in their
default sections: the runtime gets the images from the descriptor the
constructor registers, not from the sections.

+// The SYCL runtime for -fsycl links, as Linux::addOffloadRTLibs does on Linux:
+// libsycl and, when it was built, the host part of the device libraries.
+void AppleMachO::addOffloadRTLibs(unsigned ActiveKinds, const ArgList &Args,
+                                  ArgStringList &CmdArgs) const {
+  if (!(ActiveKinds & Action::OFK_SYCL) ||
+      !Args.hasFlag(options::OPT_offloadlib, options::OPT_no_offloadlib,
+                    true) ||
+      Args.hasArg(options::OPT_nostdlib) || Args.hasArg(options::OPT_nolibsycl) ||
+      Args.hasArg(options::OPT_r))
+    return;
+  SmallString<128> Path(SYCLInstallation->getSYCLRTLibPath());
+  llvm::sys::path::remove_dots(Path, true);
+  if (Args.hasFlag(options::OPT_frtlib_add_rpath,
+                   options::OPT_fno_rtlib_add_rpath, false))
+    CmdArgs.append({"-rpath", Args.MakeArgString(Path)});
+  CmdArgs.push_back(Args.MakeArgString("-L" + Path));
+  CmdArgs.push_back(Args.hasArg(options::OPT_fpreview_breaking_changes)
+                        ? "-lsycl-preview"
+                        : "-lsycl");
+  SmallString<128> DevLibHost(Path);
+  llvm::sys::path::append(DevLibHost, "libsycl-devicelib-host.a");
+  if (getVFS().exists(DevLibHost))
+    CmdArgs.push_back(Args.MakeArgString(DevLibHost));
+}

FILE: compute/patches/intel-llvm/0003-clang-SPIR-V-builtins-take-int64_t-not-the-first-64-.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: intelxe-build <build@localhost>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:07:13 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 3/5] clang: SPIR-V builtins take int64_t, not the first 64-bit
 type

The SPIR-V builtin declarations used getIntTypeForBitwidth(64), the first
64-bit integer type: long. The SYCL headers convert 64-bit arguments to
[u]int64_t, which a SYCL device target takes from the host. On Linux both
are long, on Windows both long long; on a Darwin host int64_t is long long
while long is also 64-bit, so every 64-bit builtin call was ambiguous
(__spirv_ocl_nan, __spirv_GroupIAdd, ...). The 64-bit types are now the
target's Int64Type, so Linux and Windows are unchanged.
---
 clang/lib/Sema/SPIRVBuiltins.td | 8 ++++++--
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/clang/lib/Sema/SPIRVBuiltins.td b/clang/lib/Sema/SPIRVBuiltins.td
index e5019b520..1630e76cf 100644
--- a/clang/lib/Sema/SPIRVBuiltins.td
+++ b/clang/lib/Sema/SPIRVBuiltins.td
@@ -328,8 +328,12 @@ def Short     : IntType<"short",     QualType<"Context.ShortTy", 0, 1>, 16>;
 def UShort    : UIntType<"ushort",    QualType<"Context.UnsignedShortTy">, 16>;
 def Int       : IntType<"int",       QualType<"Context.IntTy", 0, 1>, 32>;
 def UInt      : UIntType<"uint",      QualType<"Context.UnsignedIntTy">, 32>;
-def Long      : IntType<"long",      QualType<"Context.getIntTypeForBitwidth(64, true)", 0, 1>, 64>;
-def ULong     : UIntType<"ulong",     QualType<"Context.getIntTypeForBitwidth(64, false)">, 64>;
+// The 64-bit integers are the target's int64_t/uint64_t (Int64Type, which a
+// SYCL device target takes from the host): the SYCL headers pass
+// [u]int64_t. The first 64-bit type would be long on a Darwin host, where
+// int64_t is long long, and every 64-bit call would be ambiguous.
+def Long      : IntType<"long",      QualType<"(Context.getTargetInfo().getInt64Type() == TargetInfo::SignedLongLong ? Context.LongLongTy : Context.LongTy)", 0, 1>, 64>;
+def ULong     : UIntType<"ulong",     QualType<"(Context.getTargetInfo().getInt64Type() == TargetInfo::SignedLongLong ? Context.UnsignedLongLongTy : Context.UnsignedLongTy)">, 64>;
 def Float     : FPType<"float",     QualType<"Context.FloatTy">, 32>;
 def Double    : FPType<"double",    QualType<"Context.DoubleTy">, 64>;
 def Half      : FPType<"half",      QualTypeFromFunction<"GetFloat16Type">, 16>;

FILE: compute/patches/intel-llvm/0006-clang-pass-C-records-in-registers-by-Apple-s-rule-on.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: intelxe-build <build@localhost>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 17:23:42 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 6/7] clang: pass C++ records in registers by Apple's rule on
 Darwin

Apple's clang, which builds libc++ and the other C++ libraries of the
platform (and libsycl, the UR adapters and UMF here: their CMake uses the
system compiler), decides whether a C++ record is passed in registers by
the Clang 4 rule on Darwin: a trivial copy constructor and a trivial
destructor, the move constructor not considered. This clang used the
C++11 rule, which also wants one copy or move constructor that is not
deleted. For a record whose copy and move constructors are all deleted
the two disagree: Apple's clang passes it in registers, this clang by
address.

sycl::detail::type_erased_cgfo_ty is such a record (two pointers, every
copy and move deleted) and is passed by value to libsycl's
HandlerAccess::preProcess and postProcess. A program built by this
clang passed its address in %rsi; libsycl, built by Apple's clang, read
the object pointer from %rsi and the invoker from %rdx and called
whatever %rdx held: a call through a null pointer in the first
sycl::reduction on a discrete GPU (getGroupsCounterAccDiscrete).

getCallingConvKind now gives the Clang 4 rule on Darwin targets, so this
clang and Apple's agree on every record (checked over a set of copy,
move and destructor combinations on x86_64 and arm64).
---
 clang/lib/Basic/TargetInfo.cpp | 8 +++++++-
 1 file changed, 7 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/clang/lib/Basic/TargetInfo.cpp b/clang/lib/Basic/TargetInfo.cpp
index 46b5bdecb..df8817e92 100644
--- a/clang/lib/Basic/TargetInfo.cpp
+++ b/clang/lib/Basic/TargetInfo.cpp
@@ -627,8 +627,14 @@ ParsedTargetAttr TargetInfo::parseTargetAttr(StringRef Features) const {
 
 TargetInfo::CallingConvKind
 TargetInfo::getCallingConvKind(bool ClangABICompat4) const {
+  // Darwin: Apple's clang, which builds the system's C++ libraries (libc++) and
+  // every other C++ library on the platform, passes C++ records by the Clang 4
+  // rule too: in registers when the copy constructor and the destructor are
+  // trivial, whatever the move constructor is. A record whose copy and move
+  // constructors are all deleted therefore goes in registers there, and
+  // indirectly by the C++11 rule; the two sides of a call then disagree.
   if (getCXXABI() != TargetCXXABI::Microsoft &&
-      (ClangABICompat4 || getTriple().isPS4()))
+      (ClangABICompat4 || getTriple().isPS4() || getTriple().isOSDarwin()))
     return CCK_ClangABI4OrPS4;
   return CCK_Default;
 }

FILE: compute/patches/intel-llvm/0008-sycl-Mach-O-names-for-sycl-jit-and-the-XPTI-tools.patch

From: intelxe-build <build@localhost>

Subject: [PATCH] sycl: Mach-O names for sycl-jit and the XPTI tools

The runtime loads the kernel compiler's in-process JIT (sycl-jit, used
by kernel_compiler for source_language::sycl) as libsycl-jit.so by leaf
name, which on Linux finds it through libsycl's RUNPATH. On Darwin a
leaf-name dlopen does not search the caller's rpaths: take
libsycl-jit.dylib from libsycl's own directory, as on Windows.

sycl-jit hides LLVM's symbols with a linker version script outside
Windows and Apple; ld64 has none, so the library exported all of LLVM,
weak definitions included, which dyld coalesces with another LLVM's in
the same process (IGC's frontend library exports LLVM symbols). The
same six entry points through -exported_symbols_list on Apple.

sycl-prof and sycl-sanitize name the XPTI dispatcher and their
collectors libxptifw.so and lib*_collector.so; .dylib on Apple, as
sycl-trace already does.

sycl-trace's UR/SYCL collector loads its Level Zero and CUDA printers as
lib*_trace_collector.so from its own directory: .dylib on Apple.

`clang -fsycl -c` makes a fat object: the host object with the device
code added as sections __CLANG_OFFLOAD_BUNDLE__<kind>-<triple>, flagged
"exclude", through llvm-objcopy. Mach-O has neither: section names are
"segment,section" of at most 16 characters, and llvm-objcopy's Mach-O
back end refuses --set-section-flags ("option is not supported for
MachO"), so every separate compile step (CMake, make) failed on macOS;
only a compile-and-link in one step worked.

For a Mach-O host object the bundler now writes its own binary bundle
format, as for PCH and AST files: the "object" is a bundler container
that the driver unbundles at the -fsycl link (the host part goes to
ld64, the device parts to the SYCL device link), and that the unbundler
already accepted (a file that is not a known object reads through the
binary handler). A plain Mach-O object without bundles reads as the
host bundle, the unbundler's "no bundles found" case, as before.

types: std::min of a size_t and a size_t - int64_t difference does not

FILE: compute/patches/opencl-clang/0001-Build-and-find-the-PCH-resources-on-macOS.patch
================================================
From 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?=
 <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:36:46 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] Build and find the PCH resources on macOS

opencl-clang links its Linux shared object with a version script and
-Bsymbolic, and asks the linker for --no-undefined; ld64 has none of
them. On Apple the same exports are given as an exported-symbols list
(opencl_clang_macos.exports, from opencl_clang.map: Compile,
CheckCompileOptions and the PCM_* resource symbols, wildcards included;
not Link, CheckLinkOptions and GetKernelArgInfo, which the version
script lists but this version does not define: GNU ld ignores such
names, ld64 fails on them). Two-level namespace already binds the
dylib's own references, and ld64 rejects undefined symbols by default.

The resources (OpenCL C headers and precompiled modules) are found with
dlopen(<own install name>) + dlsym. On macOS dlopen() of a leaf name
searches DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH and the fallback paths, not the directory
the library was loaded from, so the library opens itself by the path
dladdr() gives (RTLD_NOLOAD), and falls back to the name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -175,7 +175,19 @@ bool ResourceManager::GetResourceUnix(const char *id, const char *pszType,
                                       const char *lib, bool relocate,
                                       const char *&res, size_t &size) {
 
+#ifdef __APPLE__
+  // macOS: dlopen() of a leaf name (the library's install name) searches DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH and the fallback paths,
+  // not the directory this library was loaded from. The resources are in this image: open it by its own path.
+  static const char anchor = 0;
+  Dl_info info;
+  void *handle = nullptr;
+  if (dladdr(&anchor, &info) && info.dli_fname)
+    handle = dlopen(info.dli_fname, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_NOLOAD);
+  if (!handle)
+    handle = dlopen(lib, RTLD_NOW);
+#else
   void *handle = dlopen(lib, RTLD_NOW);
+#endif
   if (!handle) {
     return false;
   }
