/*
 * USB wake virtual device for USBWakeFixup.kext (osy, v1.0).
 * macOS only turns a USB (keyboard/mouse) wake into a full wake when the ACPI node on the wake GPE
 * carries a top-level acpi-wake-type; OpenCore DeviceProperties only reach the PCI device. The kext
 * matches this PNP0D10 device and sets it. It shares XHCI's _PRW (GPE 0x6D); SSDT-PCHWAKE leaves
 * XHCI as the only S3 wake source on that GPE, so nothing else gains display wake.
 */
DefinitionBlock ("", "SSDT", 2, "WEX", "USBW", 0x00001000)
{
    External (_SB_.PC00.XHCI._PRW, MethodObj)    // 0 Arguments

    If ((CondRefOf (\_OSI, Local0) && _OSI ("Darwin")))
    {
        If (CondRefOf (\_SB.PC00.XHCI._PRW))
        {
            Device (\_SB.USBW)
            {
                Name (_HID, "PNP0D10")  // _HID: Hardware ID
                Name (_UID, "WAKE")  // _UID: Persistent Unique ID
                Method (_PRW, 0, NotSerialized)  // _PRW: Power Resources for Wake
                {
                    Return (\_SB.PC00.XHCI._PRW ())
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

FILE: firmware/README.md
================================================
# Firmware

IntelXe.kext builds two of Intel's firmware images into its binary:

| File | Version | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| `bmg_guc_70.bin` | GuC 70.72.1 | `de81c75f46a127c33cd59f604d800e9ffc7ed3495967ba0d8767cd6985ab398b` |
| `bmg_huc.bin` | HuC 8.2.10 (GSC CPD layout) | `747452aa8c4ed7760c68a80f3d913eafde9304d6f4db481e3f2aebb0a818bf15` |

Both come from [linux-firmware](https://gitlab.com/kernel-firmware/linux-firmware) (`xe/`). They are redistributable under `LICENSE.xe`, which is copied here unmodified from linux-firmware's `LICENSES/LICENSE.xe`.

The blobs themselves are **not committed**. To get them, run:

```sh
firmware/fetch.sh                          # from linux-firmware main
LINUX_FIRMWARE_REF=<tag> firmware/fetch.sh # from a specific tag or commit
```

The script checks the sha256 values above, and `kernel/IntelXe/build.py` checks them again. If linux-firmware has moved to newer firmware, the check fails on purpose. Fetch from an older tag, or bring the kext up on the new version first.

The B580 has no GSC for HuC. The media GuC authenticates the HuC: HUC_KERNEL_LOAD_INFO reads `0x00500001` (running) after `AUTHENTICATE_HUC`.

## XeProbe's GuC images

XeProbe ([docs/PROBE-MODE.md](../docs/PROBE-MODE.md)) loads a GuC in stage 3 on Intel GPUs that IntelXe does not drive
yet. `build.py` builds in every `<stem>_guc_70.bin` it finds next to the Battlemage files. `probe-guc.sha256` pins one
image per family to linux-firmware tag `20261019`:

| File | linux-firmware | GuC | Families |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tgl_guc_70.bin` | `i915/` | 70.49.4 | TGL, RKL, ADL-S, RPL-S, ADL-N |
| `adlp_guc_70.bin` | `i915/` | 70.49.4 | ADL-P, RPL-U, RPL-P |
| `dg1_guc_70.bin` | `i915/` | 70.49.4 | DG1 |
| `dg2_guc_70.bin` | `i915/` | 70.53.0 | DG2, ATS-M (Arc Alchemist) |
| `mtl_guc_70.bin` | `i915/` | 70.53.0 | MTL, ARL |
| `lnl_guc_70.bin` | `xe/` | 70.72.1 | LNL |
| `ptl_guc_70.bin` | `xe/` | 70.72.1 | PTL, WCL |

```sh
firmware/fetch.sh --probe        # all seven (about 2.4 MB, all of it ends up in IntelXe.kext)
firmware/fetch.sh --probe lnl    # only Lunar Lake's
```

`build.py` prints for each image whether it is the pinned one. It builds in another release's image too: stage 3
prints the version it loads, and `sysctl debug.xeprobe.info` lists every image built in.
`kernel/IntelXe/tests/probe_css_test.cpp` checks the header of each pinned image when given the directory.

FILE: firmware/fetch.sh
================================================
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# fetch.sh: download the Battlemage GuC and HuC firmware from linux-firmware into this directory and check them.
#
#   firmware/fetch.sh            fetch bmg_guc_70.bin and bmg_huc.bin (skips files that are already present and good)
#   LINUX_FIRMWARE_REF=<tag> firmware/fetch.sh    fetch from a linux-firmware tag or commit instead of main
#   firmware/fetch.sh --probe [STEM...]   also the GuC images XeProbe builds in for stage 3 on other Intel GPUs
#                                (probe-guc.sha256: tgl adlp dg1 dg2 mtl lnl ptl, or only the stems named, e.g. lnl),
#                                from the linux-firmware tag that file pins (LINUX_FIRMWARE_PROBE_REF overrides it)
#
# The blobs are Intel's redistributable binaries under LICENSE.xe (linux-firmware LICENSES/LICENSE.xe, copied here).
# They are not committed to this repository. kernel/IntelXe/build.py builds them into IntelXe.kext and checks the same
# sha256 values; a newer linux-firmware may carry newer firmware, in which case the check fails on purpose: the kext
# was brought up and tested with exactly these versions (GuC 70.72.1, HuC 8.2.10).
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REF=${LINUX_FIRMWARE_REF:-main}
PROBE=0 STEMS=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
	case $1 in
		--probe) PROBE=1;;
		-*) sed -n '3,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2;;
		*) [ $PROBE = 1 ] || { sed -n '3,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2; }; STEMS="$STEMS $1";;
	esac
	shift
done
PINS=$HERE/probe-guc.sha256
for s in $STEMS; do
	grep -qE "^[0-9a-f]{64}  [a-z0-9]+/${s}_guc_70\.bin " "$PINS" || { echo "no GuC image for '$s' in $PINS" >&2; exit 2; }
done

sha() { shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }

fetch() { # name sha256 [path in linux-firmware [ref]]
	name=$1; want=$2; path=${3:-xe/$1}; ref=${4:-$REF}; dst=$HERE/$name
	if [ -f "$dst" ] && [ "$(sha "$dst")" = "$want" ]; then echo "ok      $name"; return 0; fi
	for base in "https://gitlab.com/kernel-firmware/linux-firmware/-/raw/$ref" \
		"https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/firmware/linux-firmware.git/plain"; do
		url=$base/$path
		[ "$base" = "${base#https://git.kernel.org}" ] || url=$url?h=$ref
		if curl -fsSL -o "$dst.part" "$url"; then
			got=$(sha "$dst.part")
			if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then mv "$dst.part" "$dst"; echo "fetched $name ($url)"; return 0; fi
			echo "sha256 mismatch for $name from $url: $got" >&2
		fi
		rm -f "$dst.part"
	done
	echo "could not fetch $name with sha256 $want" >&2
	return 1
}

# Values from the files the driver was tested with.
fetch bmg_guc_70.bin de81c75f46a127c33cd59f604d800e9ffc7ed3495967ba0d8767cd6985ab398b   # GuC 70.72.1
fetch bmg_huc.bin    747452aa8c4ed7760c68a80f3d913eafde9304d6f4db481e3f2aebb0a818bf15   # HuC 8.2.10

# XeProbe's GuC images (--probe): the list, the paths and the pinned tag are in probe-guc.sha256
[ $PROBE = 1 ] || exit 0
PREF=${LINUX_FIRMWARE_PROBE_REF:-$(sed -nE 's/.*linux-firmware tag ([0-9A-Za-z._-]+).*/\1/p' "$PINS" | head -1)}
[ -n "$PREF" ] || { echo "$PINS names no linux-firmware tag" >&2; exit 1; }
bad=0
while read -r want path ver; do
	case $want in ''|'#'*) continue;; esac
	name=${path##*/}
	if [ -n "$STEMS" ]; then
		case " $STEMS " in *" ${name%_guc_70.bin} "*) ;; *) continue;; esac
	fi
	fetch "$name" "$want" "$path" "$PREF" || bad=1
	[ -f "$HERE/$name" ] && echo "        $name: GuC $ver, for XeProbe stage 3 (linux-firmware $PREF $path)"
done < "$PINS"
exit $bad

# Kernel extensions

## IntelXe/ — GPU core (`io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXe`, IntelXe.kext)

A plain IOKit kext, without Lilu, for the Arc B580 (Battlemage BMG-G21, `8086:e20b`), since 0.1.4 the Arc B570
(the same chip with fewer Xe-cores, `8086:e20c`) and since 2026-11-13 the Arc Pro B60 and Pro B50 (the G21 workstation
cards, `8086:e211`, `8086:e212`); the last three are untested on hardware. BMG-G31 (Arc Pro B70, `8086:e220`-`e223`) is
matched in a personality of its own and refused at start unless the tester boot-arg `-intelxe_allow_g31` is set. It
follows Linux `drivers/gpu/drm/xe` closely.

- **Platforms:** `xe_platform.h`/`xe_platform.cpp` hold one descriptor per device-ID list, as Linux `xe_pci.c` does (IP
  versions, flags, engine mask, WOPCM, PAT entries, MOCS index, firmware names). Start looks the device up once and
  logs it (`IntelXe: 8086:e20b: BMG-G21, graphics 20.01, media 13.01, discrete`); only BMG-G21 is supported, every
  other entry stops start with one log line. The Battlemage constants of the code read the descriptor. Design and what
  the other families need: [DESIGN-platforms.md](../docs/design/DESIGN-platforms.md).

- **Bring-up:**
  - pcode init status, forcewake;
  - PAT/MOCS tables (xe2), GT and engine workarounds and tunings;
  - GuC 70.72.1 load with ADS, CT, SLPC and GuC RC;
  - golden contexts per engine class;
  - MSI interrupts;
  - media GT (VCS0/VCS2, VECS) with its own GuC, HuC 8.2.10 authentication and media SLPC.
- **Memory:**
  - VRAM buddy allocator (drm_buddy style) and GGTT range allocator;
  - 5-level PPGTT with 64 KB and 2 MB/1 GB leaves;
  - a CPU-visible BAR2 window, with buffers spilling to system memory when it is full;
  - userptr, including read-only imports.
- **uAPI:** the xe uAPI that Mesa's ANV uses (`uapi/xe_drm.h`), over an IOUserClient (`IOAccelIntelXeClient`):
  - queries, GEM create/mmap (the `GEM_CREATE` extension chain checked as `xe_bo.c` does, in `xe_uapi_args.cpp`),
    VM bind (async), exec queues on GuC submission;
  - DRM syncobjs (binary and timeline);
  - user fences: `DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_USER_FENCE` on exec (written by the ring after the batch) and VM_BIND (written once
    the bind's fence signals), and `DRM_IOCTL_XE_WAIT_USER_FENCE`, as Intel's compute runtime uses them.
  - `uapi/intelxe_drm.h` adds IOSurface implicit fences (the dma-resv model) and scan-out pinning for the display side.
- **Robustness:** job watchdog / TDR, GT reset, shutdown quiesce, sleep/wake (`intelxePowerEvent`); an engine and
  fault-register dump in the G2H log when the GuC resets a context or a job never starts, with the BO moves, TLB
  invalidations and the faulting VM's last unbind/remap/bind.
- **Direct submission** (`debug.intelxe.direct`; 0.1.4: opt-in, default 0; in this tree since 12 Nov: on once the device is
  up, `-intelxe_nodirect` keeps it off): an application's render or compute queue keeps an
  armed slot on its ring, so a job starts without a GuC round trip ([design](../docs/design/DESIGN-direct-submission.md)).
- **Settings and readings:** the GPU power profile and clock range from NVRAM (`intelxe-gpu-profile`,
  `intelxe-gpu-min-mhz`, `intelxe-gpu-max-mhz`, written by the app); `debug.intelxe.sensors` (GT clock, temperatures,
  and on BMG the card and package energy and average power from PMT telemetry as Linux xe_hwmon reads them, with
  implausible power windows refused and counted, then the card and package PL1/PL2 and the card's I1 read through the
  pcode mailbox as xe_hwmon reads them, read only; readable by anyone); `debug.intelxe.sensors_raw` (the same sample as
  `struct intelxe_sensors`, `uapi/intelxe_sensors.h`: MHz, degrees, microjoules, milliwatts, a timestamp; version 2
  adds per-engine busy and total ticks from the GuC's engine activity statistics, `xe_engact.h`; what Level Zero
  sysman reads through xemac; both sysctls sample under `gDevLock` and write telemetry/mailbox registers only on a GPU
  that is up); `debug.intelxe.slpc_min` / `slpc_max` (root: the GT clock floor and ceiling, live: sent to the GuC at
  once, clamped to RPn..RP0, kept for every SLPC start; Level Zero's `zesFrequencySetRange`); `debug.intelxe.jobtime` (each job's stages in GPU timestamps, off by default).
- **Display boost** (`debug.intelxe.disp_boost`, on by default; `-intelxe_nodispboost` keeps it off): the first frame
  NMXAccel presents after 250 ms of a quiet display (`debug.nmxaccel_idle_boost_ms`) asks for a lease on the GT's minimum
  clock (`debug.intelxe.disp_boost_idle_ms`, 400 ms), so a window started after idle does not wait for SLPC's ramp. The
  miss trigger (a lease while frames are still running at the vblank they were due at, as i915 boosts after a missed
  vblank) is off by default (`debug.intelxe.disp_boost_misses` 0; it cost 8-10 W in 4K60 video); counters in
  `debug.intelxe.disp_boost_stats` ([design](../docs/design/DESIGN-display-boost.md)).
- **PCIe ASPM (experimental, untested, off unless written):** `xe_aspm.cpp`, the checks in `xe_aspm.h`.
  - `sysctl debug.intelxe.aspm` (anyone): every link between the GPU function and its root port (on the B580: the
    card's switch downstream port <-> GPU, and root port <-> the card's switch upstream port), each end's Link
    Capabilities (ASPM support, L0s/L1 exit latency), Link Control (ASPM, Common Clock, CLKREQ#), Link Status (speed,
    width, slot clock), Device Capabilities (acceptable latencies, RBER) and L1 PM Substates, whether L1 passes the
    checks, the endpoints below the path, and the last change made.
  - `sudo sysctl debug.intelxe.aspm_l1=1`: ASPM L1 on every link of the path, only if every link passes Linux
    `drivers/pci/pcie/aspm.c`'s rules (L1 in both ends' Link Capabilities, no pre-1.1 function, Common Clock configured
    where the slot clock is shared, each endpoint's acceptable L1 latency against the link's exit latency plus 1 us per
    link); otherwise nothing changes and the reason is in the report and the log. `=0`: ASPM off on the path. `=-1`
    (default): leave the links alone (what was changed stays until a reboot). Changes go through
    `IOPCIDevice::setASPMState`, upstream end first to enable and downstream end first to disable, the root port's
    link first to enable and the GPU's link first to disable; L1 substates are not enabled (IOPCIFamily clears their
    control registers on a link it changes). After a system wake the last 0 or 1 is applied again where the links lost
    it.

**Version:** since 0.1.2 the kext carries the number of the release that last rebuilt it (0.1.4 here). 0.1.0 to 0.1.3
shipped `rb7u` (renamed to IntelXe; tested on macOS 26.7.1); 0.1.4 adds the B570's ID, the NVRAM settings, the sensors and job-timing sysctls, the engine dump and direct submission (the 9 Nov test build), and since 10 Nov in this tree the platform descriptors, user fences, the wider CAT-fault dump, the card and package power in `debug.intelxe.sensors` and the experimental, untested ASPM sysctls. `rb7u` is
`rb7t` (VRAM-shared IOSurfaces fixed at boot, purgeable BOs, shared BOs, external fds behind `debug.intelxe.fds`)
plus `rb7u` (macOS 26 starts drivers while the card is still leaving its reset: wait for config space, read the VRAM
size again). The earlier steps, each a separate patch in the development tree:

| Step | What |
|---|---|
| `ph` | `pi` + IODMACommand-based DMA (VT-d ready) + `intelxePowerEvent` for IntelXeFB's sleep/wake save/restore |
| `pv` | **BAR window under pressure.** 32 MB of the 1 GB CPU-visible window is kept for page tables (a full window had made every VM_BIND fail with ENOMEM); one memory descriptor per CPU map (GEM_MMAP_OFFSET returns a cookie), so `IOConnectUnmapMemory64` finds and removes VRAM mappings (it never did); cheap eviction scans; `debug.intelxe.vram` (window, VRAM and system BOs per process) and window counters in `debug.intelxe.stats` |
| `pv2` | EXEC waits behind the VM's kernel fences (BO clears), as `xe_exec` waits on the VM resv KERNEL slot |
| `pv3` | a CPU map of a BO beyond a full window moves it to system memory (`boMoveSys`, xe's fault migrate to TT) instead of failing with ENOSPC |
| `sv1`-`sv7` | VRAM-shared IOSurfaces (`uapi/intelxe_surfvram_kabi.h`, the registry NMXAccel and the plugin use; on at boot with `intelxe_surfvram=2`, as the install guide sets it, otherwise off until `debug.intelxe.surfvram` is set) |

What is not done yet for the window: a BO the CPU has mapped never leaves it (an IOKit user mapping of a physical range
cannot be pointed elsewhere), so the window is first come, first served, with spills to system memory.

## IntelXeFB/ — display (`io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB`, IntelXeFB.kext, class `IntelXeFramebuffer`)

An IOFramebuffer for the card's DisplayPort outputs (display IP 14.01, C20 PHYs).

- **Mode setup:**
  - takes over the mode the GOP lit;
  - reads EDID over DP AUX;
  - scaled modes through the pipe scaler;
  - the modes and refresh rates the monitor's EDID offers (all blocks, Linux's drm_edid parsing; 120 modes on the test
    monitor, the same rates as Windows);
  - Adaptive-Sync (VRR) with an LFC pacer.
- **Link:** retraining and a full modeset with C20 PLL programming (`IntelXeLink.cpp`).
- **Cursor:** hardware cursor.
- **Pipe gamma:** for IOPresentment.
- **Flips:** real flips from scan-out buffers pinned in VRAM.
- **Power:** sleep save/restore.
- **Boot-time arming:** at boot it matches from the AuxKC and arms acceleration in the kernel together with NMXAccel ("boot1"), with an NVRAM panic-loop guard (`intelxe-guard`).
- **Second display pipe (in this tree, implemented behind `-intelxefb_pipeb` / NVRAM `intelxefb-pipeb=1`, default off,
  untested: needs a second monitor):** connector scan over every port's AUX channel, pipe B lit for a DP sink
  (`IntelXeLink` `kEnableNew`, the arithmetic in `IntelXeDisplayPlan.h` with a host test in `tests/plan_test.cpp`), a second
  framebuffer `IntelXeFramebufferPipe` as head 1, published at IntelXeFB's start disconnected (`IntelXeFBConnected`) and
  connected when a sink lights pipe B, so a monitor is a connection change without a WindowServer restart (with
  `NVRMTiming` for NMXAGDC; NMXAccel's boot arm gives it a display pipe with `nmxheads=1`:
  [`DESIGN-multihead-accel.md`](../docs/design/DESIGN-multihead-accel.md)). `debug.intelxefb_pipeb` (knob
  only): 1 scan + light, 0 off, 2 scan.
  The dry run `sudo sysctl -n debug.intelxefb_pipeb_plan` is always there and only reads registers; the mode it plans
  for is `debug.intelxefb_pipeb_mode` (empty = pipe A's timing, `1920x1080@60`, `1920x1080@60n`, `edid`, with
  `:tc1`..`:tc4`/`:a` for the port). Design: [`docs/design/DESIGN-second-pipe.md`](../docs/design/DESIGN-second-pipe.md).

**Version:** the number of the release that last rebuilt it (0.1.4 here). 0.1.0 to 0.1.2 shipped v10m: boot1 + v9 + v10b (`intelxefbRunGated`: NMXAccel's pipe registration inside IOGraphics' gate order; detailed timings answered with their mode size) + v10c (boot-guard fix) + the later steps up to v10m (modes from the EDID). 0.1.3 added refresh rates above the firmware's mode, Adaptive-Sync modes on by default and the opt-in HiDPI modes (`intelxefb-hidpi`); 0.1.4 reads the user settings from NVRAM (`intelxefb-hwcursor`, `intelxefb-dpms`, `intelxefb-vrr-lfc`, `intelxefb-vrr-floor`).

Boot guard (`intelxe-guard` in NVRAM): after two accelerated boots in a row that end inside their first minute the next boots arm with
NMXAccel's safest settings (`IntelXeFBAccelSafe`); four in a row turn acceleration off for the next boots (`intelxe-accel-off`, until
`sudo nvram intelxe-accel-off=ok intelxe-guard=ok`; `nvram -d` leaves it in place on macOS 26). On macOS 26 WindowServer uses no display
without the accelerator's pipe, so IntelXeFB alone left the Apple logo on screen; from 0.1.5 IntelXe.kext reads the same values first
(`uapi/intelxe_bootguard.h`, shared with IntelXeFB and `IntelXe/tests/bootguard_test.cpp`) and on a held boot (also `-intelxe_noaccel`,
safe mode) gives the display to Apple's IONDRVFramebuffer on the firmware's surface before IntelXeFB and NMXAccel are offered the GPU, so a
held boot has an unaccelerated desktop to repair from (`sysctl debug.intelxe.bootguard`; NVRAM `intelxe-held-display=fb` or the boot-arg
`intelxe_helddisplay=1` keeps IntelXeFB instead; [`DESIGN-boot-guard-held-display.md`](../docs/design/DESIGN-boot-guard-held-display.md)). One such boot only makes
the next one try again: it may have been a power cut. On x86 macOS the kernel's NVRAM writes after boot stay in memory until a clean
shutdown (AppleEFINVRAM ignores the SYNCNOW keys, and calling `IODTNVRAM::sync()` from IntelXeFB's start hung the boot), so `install.sh`
adds a LaunchDaemon that writes the cleared guard with `nvram` once per boot; tested on the B580 with a power cut (5 Nov). Since v10c "healthy" needs WindowServer itself: its
IOFramebuffer server connection (opened by the process named WindowServer, the last time 45 s ago or more), steady VBL
clients, and for the accelerated stage at least 120 NMXAccel frame calls. Before, VBL clients and one frame call were
enough, and NMXAccel's display pipe provides both on its own: at a boot where WindowServer deadlocked before it started
the guard still cleared.

Scripts (`scripts/`):
- `intelxe-accel.sh`: arms WindowServer acceleration by hand, used by builds before boot1.
- `intelxefb-load.sh` + `io.github.yusufklncc.intelxefb.plist`: the LaunchDaemon loader for builds before boot1; a no-op with boot1.
- `install-boot1.sh` / `rollback-boot1.sh`: switch the installed kexts to boot1 and back. Paths inside them are those of the development machine.

Licence: `IntelXeFB.cpp` is derived from nullmoth's NMIntelFB/NVRMFB and is therefore PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. `IntelXeLink.*`, `IntelXeEdid.*`, `IntelXeDisplayPlan.h` and `tests/` are MIT. See `IntelXeFB/LICENSE`.

Host test of the second-pipe arithmetic: `cd kernel/IntelXeFB/tests && c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o plan_test plan_test.cpp ../IntelXeEdid.cpp && ./plan_test`.

## HybridPM/ — CPU clocks for hybrid Intel CPUs (`io.github.yusufklncc.HybridPM`, HybridPM.kext)

A Lilu plugin, separate from the GPU driver, for Alder Lake / Raptor Lake CPUs (12th to 14th generation Core with P- and
E-cores). macOS's XCPM writes the P-cores' HWP request in 100 MHz units where they count 78.741 MHz, and pins busy cores
to low clocks; HybridPM converts the request and lets the hardware pick each core's clock. On the test machine's
i7-14700K one thread went from ~55 to 128 M iterations/s and Geekbench's GPU scores rose about a third (the driver's
CPU work per command buffer runs faster). `efi.sh` and the app add it below Lilu at stage 4 when the CPU needs it.
Details, controls and `hpmstat`: [HybridPM/README.md](HybridPM/README.md).
Built by `kernel/HybridPM/build.py` (MacKernelSDK and Lilu's headers).

## Building

```sh
firmware/fetch.sh                                   # GuC/HuC blobs (not in git)
git clone https://github.com/acidanthera/MacKernelSDK external/MacKernelSDK   # or MACKERNELSDK=/path
python3 kernel/IntelXe/build.py                        # -> build/IntelXe.kext, build/IntelXeFB.kext
python3 kernel/IntelXe/build.py --debug                # -O0, INTELXE_DEBUG=1 (destructive bring-up steps, batch dumps)
python3 kernel/IntelXe/build.py --only IntelXe --output /tmp/k
python3 kernel/HybridPM/build.py --lilu /path/to/Lilu.kext   # -> build/HybridPM/HybridPM.kext, hpmstat
```

Built on an Apple Silicon Mac with the Command Line Tools (x86_64 kext target).

Host tests (no GPU, any Mac), from `kernel/IntelXe/tests/`:

```sh
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o platform_test platform_test.cpp ../xe_platform.cpp && ./platform_test
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o uapi_test uapi_test.cpp ../xe_uapi_args.cpp && ./uapi_test
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o pmt_test pmt_test.cpp ../xe_platform.cpp && ./pmt_test
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o aspm_test aspm_test.cpp && ./aspm_test
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o pcode_test pcode_test.cpp ../xe_platform.cpp && ./pcode_test
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o sensors_test sensors_test.cpp && ./sensors_test
c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o dispboost_test dispboost_test.cpp && ./dispboost_test
```

`platform_test` checks the descriptor table against the constants the code used, XeProbe's former family table and
Linux's BMG id lists; `uapi_test` checks the sync, user-fence wait and `GEM_CREATE` extension argument handling against
Linux xe; `pmt_test` checks the BMG energy path (PMT offsets, GUID decode, field extraction, unit scaling, wrap
accumulation, average power, the power-window sanity guard); `pcode_test` checks the pcode mailbox protocol against a
fake pcode (write order, busy mailbox, timeout, error codes as Linux `xe_pcode.c`) and the power-limit units and report
text; `sensors_test` checks `debug.intelxe.sensors_raw`'s struct layout (`uapi/intelxe_sensors.h`), the sample built
from the registers, the energy meter and the limits, and that `debug.intelxe.sensors`' text made from that sample is
byte for byte the text before it existed (against a copy of the old code, every buffer length); `engact_test` checks the
GuC engine activity arithmetic (`xe_engact.h`) against a transcription of Linux `xe_guc_engine_activity.c`; `slpcboost_test`
checks the `slpc_boost` lease and the live `slpc_min`/`slpc_max` rules; `dispboost_test` checks the display boost lease
(`debug.intelxe.disp_boost`, [DESIGN-display-boost.md](../docs/design/DESIGN-display-boost.md): the miss streak, the floor,
renewal and expiry, the rate limit, the gates, sleep and switch-off); `aspm_test` checks the ASPM path logic (latency decoding against Linux aspm.c, which links may take L1, the call
order for enabling and disabling, the report text). The GPU test for user fences is `user/tests/kernel/ufence.c`.



================================================
FILE: kernel/HybridPM/README.md
================================================
# HybridPM: CPU clocks for hybrid Intel CPUs (`io.github.yusufklncc.HybridPM`, HybridPM.kext)

A small [Lilu](https://github.com/acidanthera/Lilu) plugin for 12th to 14th generation Intel Core desktop and laptop
CPUs (Alder Lake and Raptor Lake, with performance and efficiency cores) and Core Ultra 200S desktop CPUs (Arrow Lake). It is not part of the GPU driver, but without
it macOS runs these CPUs well below their clocks, and the GPU driver spends a lot of CPU time per command buffer, so the
GPU looks slow too.

## Why

macOS's CPU power management (XCPM) predates hybrid CPUs and gets two things wrong on them:

- **Units.** XCPM writes `IA32_HWP_REQUEST` (MSR 0x774) in 100 MHz ratio units. Hybrid P-cores count HWP performance in
  units of 78.741 MHz (Linux `intel_pstate`, `HYBRID_SCALING_FACTOR_ADL`). The turbo ratio 56 of an i7-14700K
  (5.6 GHz) becomes 56 x 78.741 MHz = 4.41 GHz on the P-cores: one thread never goes above 4.4 GHz.
- **Pinned clocks.** XCPM also writes its own per-CPU pick into the request's *desired* field, which pins a core to that
  clock. With CpuTopologyRebuild's grouping it left fully busy cores at 800 MHz while others ran at 3.3 GHz under the
  same load.

HybridPM finds the XCPM routine that builds and writes the request (by its byte pattern, searched forward from the
exported `_xcpm_enable_pstate_ctrs`; at +0x1140 on macOS 15.8.1, +0x1190 on 26.7.1), routes it, and after Apple's write
converts the request on the P-cores: *max* becomes the core's HWP *highest* (the turbo ratio table still applies) and
*desired* is converted to HWP units. By default it then sets *desired* to 0 (autonomous: the hardware picks each
core's clock from its own load and EPP, as Linux does), EPP 0, and turns energy-efficient turbo off (MSR_POWER_CTL
bit 19). The unit mismatch was first found by NootedGreen's XE-PM
(JulioNectar/Hackintosh-XPS13Plus-IrisXe-Tahoe).

Everything takes effect 20 s after boot: the HWP MSRs fault until XCPM sets `IA32_PM_ENABLE`.

## Measured

On the test machine (i7-14700K, Z790, macOS 26.7.1 and 15.8.1), a perl loop in million iterations per second, PL2
253 W either way:

| Load | Without | With HybridPM |
|---|---|---|
| 1 thread | ~55 | 128 (5.39 GHz) |
| 8 threads | ~400 | ~1010 |
| 28 threads | 920-1365 | ~1500 |

Idle package power stayed about 10 W for every EPP. Geekbench's GPU scores (Metal, OpenCL) on the Arc B580 were about a
third higher with it, because the driver's per-command-buffer CPU work runs at the higher clock. A user with an
i5-13400F (also Alder Lake / Raptor Lake hybrid) and no HybridPM got GPU scores about 30 % lower than the test machine.

## Which CPUs

It acts only on Intel family 6 CPUs that are hybrid (CPUID leaf 7 EDX bit 15), have HWP, and are one of the models whose
HWP unit is known: the models whose P-cores use the 78.741 MHz unit (the models Linux `intel_pstate` gives
`HYBRID_SCALING_FACTOR_ADL`; their E-cores count in 100 MHz units and are left alone), and Arrow Lake desktop, whose
P-cores and E-cores both count in smaller units:

| Model | Linux name | CPUs |
|---|---|---|
| 0x97 | `ALDERLAKE` | 12th gen desktop (and some 13th/14th gen i5, e.g. i5-13400F stepping C0) |
| 0x9A | `ALDERLAKE_L` | 12th gen laptop (H, P, U) |
| 0xB7 | `RAPTORLAKE` | 13th and 14th gen desktop (e.g. i7-14700K, i5-13400F stepping B0) |
| 0xBA | `RAPTORLAKE_P` | 13th gen laptop (H, P, U) |
| 0xBF | `RAPTORLAKE_S` | some 13th/14th gen desktop i3/i5 models |
| 0xC6 | `ARROWLAKE` | Core Ultra 200S desktop (e.g. Core Ultra 7 265K/KF): P-cores 62.5 MHz, E-cores ~70.8 MHz per unit, measured from Linux CPPC on a 265KF; both core types are converted |

`0xBE` (`ALDERLAKE_N`, N100 and the like) is listed as well but has efficiency cores only, so the hybrid check already
leaves it alone. Other Core Ultra models (Meteor Lake 0xAA/0xAC, Arrow Lake H/U 0xC5/0xB5, Lunar Lake 0xBD, Panther Lake 0xCC)
use other or unmeasured units (Linux: 80 MHz for Meteor Lake, 86.957 MHz for Lunar Lake) and is left alone, as is any model not
listed, any CPU that is not hybrid (an i5-12400 with P-cores only, every CPU before 12th gen) and any non-Intel CPU.
On those the plugin does nothing: it routes nothing, reads and writes no MSR, logs one line (`HybridPM hpm: off: ...`)
and shows the reason:

```sh
sysctl debug.hybridpm.enabled debug.hybridpm.why
# debug.hybridpm.enabled: 0
# debug.hybridpm.why: unsupported model 0xAA (Core Ultra: another HWP scale)
```

The model comes from the CPUID instruction itself, so OpenCore's `Cpuid1Data` (which changes what the kernel records)
does not hide it.

## Installing

It ships in the release's `-efi.zip` and macOS package (`EFI/OC/Kexts/HybridPM.kext`, with `hpmstat`). On macOS,
stage 4 of the install guide adds it: `efi.sh` and IntelXe Manager's EFI page copy it and put its `Kernel > Add` entry
right below `Lilu.kext`'s when the CPU's name is one of these models, and leave it out with a note when the EFI does
not load Lilu (Lilu is required and not shipped here). The Windows EFI tool (`IntelXe-EFI.ps1`) does the same, by the
name of the CPU of the PC it runs on (checked on macOS against `efi.sh`, not yet run on Windows). By hand, see the
install guide's *Hybrid Intel CPUs* section.

## Controls

Live, as root (`sudo sysctl ...`):

| sysctl | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `debug.hybridpm.hwp` | 1 | convert XCPM's ratios to HWP units on the P-cores (on Arrow Lake the E-cores too) |
| `debug.hybridpm.autonomous` | 1 | 1 = desired 0, the hardware picks the clock; 0 = XCPM's pick (converted) |
| `debug.hybridpm.epp` | 0 | EPP override 0 (performance) .. 255 (power saving); -1 keeps XCPM's |
| `debug.hybridpm.eet_off` | 1 | 1 = energy-efficient turbo off |

Read-only, any user:

| sysctl | What |
|---|---|
| `debug.hybridpm.enabled` | 1 once the conversion is active (20 s after boot) |
| `debug.hybridpm.why` | `on (model 0xB7)` when active; otherwise why not: `not hybrid (model 0x..)`, `unsupported model 0x..`, `not an Intel CPU`, `route 3: XCPM request writer not found`, ... |
| `debug.hybridpm.route` | 0 not tried (unsupported CPU); 1 routed; 2 a kernel symbol is missing; 3 the XCPM routine was not found (exactly one match is required); 4 routing failed |
| `debug.hybridpm.state` | (supported CPUs only) a binary sample for `hpmstat`: per-CPU APERF/MPERF, HWP capabilities and request, core type and temperature; package RAPL energy, power limits (MSR 0x610 and the MCHBAR copy, the lower one applies), perf-limit reasons, turbo ratio limits |

Boot-args: `-hpmoff` (Lilu: the plugin does not start, and `debug.hybridpm` does not exist), `hpmhwp=0`, `hpmauto=0`, `hpmepp=N` (-1..255), `hpmeet=0`;
`-hpmdbg` shows the debug lines of a `--debug` build, `-hpmbeta` lets it start on a macOS newer than 26.

`hpmstat [interval-ms [count]]` (no root) diffs two samples and prints each CPU's effective clock, busy share, HWP
request and capabilities and temperature, plus package power, power limits, perf-limit reasons and EET:

```sh
./hpmstat 1000 5
```

## Limits

- Tested on one machine, an i7-14700K (Raptor Lake S), on macOS 26.7.1 and 15.8.1, with CpuTopologyRebuild
  (`ctrsmt=off`). Lilu allows it from Big Sur to Tahoe; only those two releases were tried.
- The routine is found by byte pattern. A macOS update that changes it leaves `route` at 3 and the plugin inactive
  (XCPM's behaviour, nothing worse).
- It needs Lilu (any recent release; the test machine runs 1.7.2), which most OpenCore EFIs already have for
  VirtualSMC. Lilu is not shipped here.
- Package-level HWP control (request bit 42) is left alone; XCPM does not use it on these CPUs.
- Power limits (PL1/PL2) are not changed; `hpmstat` only shows them.

## Building

```sh
python3 kernel/HybridPM/build.py --sdk /path/to/MacKernelSDK --lilu /path/to/Lilu.kext
#   -> build/HybridPM/HybridPM.kext, build/HybridPM/hpmstat
```

`--lilu` takes a DEBUG `Lilu.kext` (its `Contents/Resources` has the headers and `plugin_start.cpp`), that folder, or a
Lilu source checkout. `--debug` builds -O0 with Lilu's debug logging. Lilu's `plugin_start.cpp` is compiled into the kext,
so its BSD-3-Clause notice (`LICENSE.Lilu`) goes into the bundle's `Contents/Resources`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Build HybridPM.kext (kernel/HybridPM, a Lilu plugin) and hpmstat, its user-space reader.

Usage: build.py [--debug] [--output DIR] [--sdk DIR] [--lilu DIR]   (default output: <repo>/build/HybridPM)

The kext is built -O2 -g (symbols stripped) by default, the release build; --debug builds it -O0 with DEBUG=1, which
turns on Lilu's DBGLOG lines (shown with the boot-arg -hpmdbg and a DEBUG Lilu). hpmstat is signed ad hoc.

Build dependencies, not vendored:
- MacKernelSDK (https://github.com/acidanthera/MacKernelSDK, APSL-2.0): --sdk, $MACKERNELSDK or <repo>/external/MacKernelSDK.
- Lilu (https://github.com/acidanthera/Lilu, BSD-3-Clause): its headers and Library/plugin_start.cpp, which is compiled
  into the kext. --lilu takes a Lilu.kext (DEBUG build, whose Contents/Resources holds Headers/ and Library/), that
  Contents/Resources folder, or a Lilu source checkout; $LILU or <repo>/external/Lilu.kext. Lilu's licence text is
  kept in LICENSE.Lilu and copied into the bundle's Resources.
"""

def run(cmd): subprocess.run([str(x) for x in cmd],check=True,cwd=HERE)
def lilu_dir(p):
 for d in (p/'Contents/Resources',p,p/'Lilu'):
  if (d/'Headers/kern_api.hpp').is_file() and (d/'Library/plugin_start.cpp').is_file(): return d
 sys.exit(f'Lilu headers not found under {p}: pass --lilu with a Lilu.kext (DEBUG build), its Contents/Resources or a Lilu checkout')
def main():
 p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
 p.add_argument('--debug',action='store_true',help='-O0 with DEBUG=1 (DBGLOG lines)')
 p.add_argument('--release',action='store_true',help='no effect: the release build is the default')
 p.add_argument('--output',type=Path,default=REPO/'build/HybridPM')
 p.add_argument('--sdk',type=Path,default=Path(os.environ.get('MACKERNELSDK',REPO/'external/MacKernelSDK')),
  help='MacKernelSDK checkout (default: $MACKERNELSDK or <repo>/external/MacKernelSDK)')
 p.add_argument('--lilu',type=Path,default=Path(os.environ.get('LILU',REPO/'external/Lilu.kext')),
  help='Lilu.kext, its Contents/Resources, or a Lilu checkout (default: $LILU or <repo>/external/Lilu.kext)')
 a=p.parse_args();out=a.output.resolve()
 sdk=a.sdk.resolve()
 if not (sdk/'Headers').is_dir() or not (sdk/'Library/x86_64/libkmod.a').is_file():
  sys.exit(f'MacKernelSDK not found at {sdk}: pass --sdk, set MACKERNELSDK, or clone it to {REPO/"external/MacKernelSDK"}')
 lilu=lilu_dir(a.lilu.resolve())
 kext=out/'HybridPM.kext'

 bundle=kext/'Contents';(bundle/'MacOS').mkdir(parents=True);(bundle/'Resources').mkdir()
 objdir=out/'obj';objdir.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
 # The kernel C++ flags of kernel/IntelXe/build.py (the WEG/Lilu kext ABI, 10.6 deployment target), plus Lilu's headers
 # as system headers (-isystem): kern_util.hpp raises -Wsign-conversion and -Wshadow warnings that are not ours.
 base=['xcrun','clang++','-arch','x86_64','-std=c++17',('-O0' if a.debug else '-O2'),'-g','-fapple-kext','-fno-exceptions','-fno-rtti',
  '-fno-stack-protector','-fno-builtin','-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables','-mno-red-zone','-nostdinc','-DKERNEL','-DKERNEL_PRIVATE',
  '-D__APPLE__','-D__MACH__','-I'+str(sdk/'Headers'),'-isystem',str(lilu),'-mmacosx-version-min=10.6','-DAPPLE_KEXT_ASSERTIONS=1',
  '-DDRIVER_PRIVATE','-DAPPLE','-DNeXT','-fno-common','-Wall','-Wextra','-Wno-unused-parameter','-Wno-deprecated-declarations',
  '-DPRODUCT_NAME=HybridPM',f'-DMODULE_VERSION={VER}','-fdebug-compilation-dir=.']
 if a.debug: base+=['-DDEBUG=1']
 objects=[]
 for src in [HERE/'HybridPM.cpp',lilu/'Library/plugin_start.cpp']:
  obj=objdir/(src.stem+'.o');run(base+['-c',src,'-o',obj]);objects.append(obj)

 run(['xcrun','strip','-S',exe])

 libs['com.apple.iokit.IOPCIFamily']='1.1';libs['as.vit9696.Lilu']='1.2.0'

  CFBundleShortVersionString=VER,OSBundleCompatibleVersion='0.1.0',OSBundleRequired='Root',OSBundleLibraries=libs,

 (bundle/'Info.plist').write_bytes(plistlib.dumps(info))
 shutil.copyfile(HERE/'LICENSE.Lilu',bundle/'Resources/LICENSE-Lilu.txt')   # plugin_start.cpp is in the binary
 syms=subprocess.check_output(['xcrun','nm','-u',str(exe)],text=True)

FILE: kernel/HybridPM/hpmstat.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/*
 * hpmstat: diff two HybridPM samples (sysctl debug.hybridpm.state) and print per-CPU effective clock, busy share,
 * HWP request/capabilities and temperature, plus package power from RAPL, the MSR and MCHBAR power limits,
 * perf-limit reasons and EET. No root needed.
 *
 *   hpmstat [interval-ms [count]]     default 1000 ms, 1 sample
 *
 * kernel/HybridPM/build.py builds it next to the kext; by hand: clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -o hpmstat hpmstat.c
 */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define MAX_CPUS 64
struct HpmCpu { uint64_t aperf, mperf, hwpReq, hwpCap; uint8_t type, temp, pad[6]; };
struct HpmState {
	uint32_t version, ncpu, tjmax, pkgTemp;
	uint64_t tsc, pkgEnergy, iaEnergy, gtEnergy, raplUnit, pkgPowerLimit, mchPowerLimit, perfLimitReasons, powerCtl,
	         turboRatio, turboRatioCores, platformInfo;
	struct HpmCpu cpu[MAX_CPUS];
};

static int sample(struct HpmState *s)
{
	size_t len = sizeof(*s);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.hybridpm.state", s, &len, NULL, 0) || len != sizeof(*s) || s->version != 1) {
		perror("debug.hybridpm.state");
		return -1;
	}
	return 0;
}

static void limit(const char *name, uint64_t v, double unit)
{
	printf("%s PL1 %.1f W%s tw %u/%u, PL2 %.1f W%s%s", name, (v & 0x7fff) * unit, (v >> 15) & 1 ? "" : " (off)",
	       (unsigned)(v >> 17) & 0x1f, (unsigned)(v >> 22) & 3, ((v >> 32) & 0x7fff) * unit, (v >> 47) & 1 ? "" : " (off)",
	       (v >> 63) & 1 ? ", locked" : "");
}

static const char *reasons[16] = {"PROCHOT", "THERMAL", NULL, NULL, "RSR", "RATL", "VR_THERMAL", "VR_TDC", "OTHER",
	NULL, "PL1", "PL2", "MAX_TURBO", "TURBO_ATTEN", NULL, NULL};

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int ms = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 1000, count = argc > 2 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 1;
	static struct HpmState a, b;
	if (sample(&a))
		return 1;
	const double base = ((a.platformInfo >> 8) & 0xff) * 100.0;
	const double punit = 1.0 / (1 << (a.raplUnit & 0xf)), eunit = 1.0 / (1 << ((a.raplUnit >> 8) & 0x1f));
	for (int n = 0; n < count; n++) {
		usleep(ms * 1000);
		if (sample(&b))
			return 1;
		const double dt = (double)(b.tsc - a.tsc) / (base * 1e6);
		printf("pkg %.1f W (IA %.1f W, GT %.1f W), %u C (TjMax %u), base %.0f MHz, EET %s, ",
		       (double)((uint32_t)(b.pkgEnergy - a.pkgEnergy)) * eunit / dt, (double)((uint32_t)(b.iaEnergy - a.iaEnergy)) * eunit / dt,
		       (double)((uint32_t)(b.gtEnergy - a.gtEnergy)) * eunit / dt, b.pkgTemp, b.tjmax, base,
		       (b.powerCtl >> 19) & 1 ? "off" : "on");
		printf("limits now:");
		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
			if (reasons[i] && ((b.perfLimitReasons >> i) & 1))
				printf(" %s", reasons[i]);
		printf(", logged:");
		for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
			if (reasons[i] && ((b.perfLimitReasons >> (16 + i)) & 1))
				printf(" %s", reasons[i]);
		printf("\n");
		limit("MSR", b.pkgPowerLimit, punit);
		printf("; ");
		limit("MCHBAR", b.mchPowerLimit, punit);
		printf("\nturbo ratios %016llx cores %016llx\n", (unsigned long long)b.turboRatio, (unsigned long long)b.turboRatioCores);
		printf("cpu type   MHz busy%%  hwp hi/gu/eff/lo  req min/max/des/epp  temp\n");
		for (int c = 0; c < MAX_CPUS; c++) {
			const struct HpmCpu *x = &a.cpu[c], *y = &b.cpu[c];
			if (!y->type)
				continue;
			const double dm = (double)(y->mperf - x->mperf), da = (double)(y->aperf - x->aperf);
			const double busy = dm / (b.tsc - a.tsc) * 100.0, mhz = dm > 0 ? da / dm * base : 0;
			printf("%3d  %s  %5.0f %5.1f   %3u/%3u/%3u/%3u     %3u/%3u/%3u/%3u     %3u\n", c, y->type == 0x40 ? "P" : y->type == 0x20 ? "E" : "?",
			       mhz, busy, (unsigned)(y->hwpCap & 0xff), (unsigned)(y->hwpCap >> 8) & 0xff, (unsigned)(y->hwpCap >> 16) & 0xff,
			       (unsigned)(y->hwpCap >> 24) & 0xff, (unsigned)(y->hwpReq & 0xff), (unsigned)(y->hwpReq >> 8) & 0xff,
			       (unsigned)(y->hwpReq >> 16) & 0xff, (unsigned)(y->hwpReq >> 24) & 0xff, y->temp);
		}
		a = b;
	}
	return 0;
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Build IntelXe.kext (kernel/IntelXe) and IntelXeFB.kext (kernel/IntelXeFB): plain IOKit kexts, no Lilu, with the MacKernelSDK.

Usage: build.py [--debug] [--release] [--output DIR] [--sdk DIR] [--firmware DIR] [--only IntelXe|IntelXeFB]
       (default output: <repo>/build)

IntelXe.kext is built -O2 -g by default; --debug builds it -O0 with INTELXE_DEBUG=1 (the destructive bring-up steps and the
batch dump sysctls). IntelXeFB.kext is -O2 -g as well (-O0 with --debug); --release is kept for old command lines.

XeProbe (xe_probe.cpp, docs/PROBE-MODE.md) is a second personality of IntelXe.kext: it attaches only to the device the
boot-arg xeprobe=0xDEVICE names. GuC images for the families it can probe are built in when present in the firmware
directory as <stem>_guc_70.bin (stems tgl, adlp, dg1, dg2, mtl, lnl, ptl; linux-firmware i915/ and xe/;
firmware/fetch.sh --probe fetches the ones firmware/probe-guc.sha256 pins, about 2.4 MB in all); Battlemage uses the
image below. A missing image only makes stage 3 report it.

MacKernelSDK (https://github.com/acidanthera/MacKernelSDK, APSL-2.0) is a build dependency and is not vendored: pass
--sdk, set MACKERNELSDK, or clone it to <repo>/external/MacKernelSDK.

The GuC firmware is built in from bmg_guc_70.bin (linux-firmware xe/bmg_guc_70.bin) and the HuC firmware from
bmg_huc.bin (xe/bmg_huc.bin, HuC 8.2.10, GSC CPD layout), both checked by sha256. They are Intel's redistributable
binaries under LICENSE.xe and are not in git: run firmware/fetch.sh first (or pass --firmware DIR).
"""
import argparse,hashlib,os,plistlib,subprocess,sys
from pathlib import Path
HERE=Path(__file__).resolve().parent          # kernel/IntelXe
REPO=HERE.parent.parent
FBDIR=HERE.parent/'IntelXeFB'                    # kernel/IntelXeFB
VER=(REPO/'VERSION').read_text().strip()       # the release that last rebuilt the kext
GUC='bmg_guc_70.bin'
GUC_SHA='de81c75f46a127c33cd59f604d800e9ffc7ed3495967ba0d8767cd6985ab398b'  # GuC 70.72.1
HUC='bmg_huc.bin'
HUC_SHA='747452aa8c4ed7760c68a80f3d913eafde9304d6f4db481e3f2aebb0a818bf15'  # HuC 8.2.10
# BMG-G31 (Arc Pro B70; xe_platform.cpp kIdsBMGG31): not supported, so not in the IOPCIMatch of the supported cards. Both
# kexts match it in a personality of its own ("<kext>-G31"); IntelXe::start refuses it unless the tester boot-arg
# -intelxe_allow_g31 is set (the entry's testerBootArg), and IntelXeFB attaches only after IntelXe brought the card up
# (IntelXeReady). tools/parity/devices.py checks these ids against the kernel's G31 entry.
G31_TESTER_MATCH='0xe2208086 0xe2218086 0xe2228086 0xe2238086'
def run(cmd): subprocess.run([str(x) for x in cmd],check=True,cwd=HERE)
def main():
 p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
 p.add_argument('--release',action='store_true',help='no effect: both kexts are -O2 unless --debug')
 p.add_argument('--no-probe-guc',action='store_true',help='with --release: build without the XeProbe GuC images of other families (firmware/fetch.sh --probe)')
 p.add_argument('--debug',action='store_true',help='IntelXe at -O0 with INTELXE_DEBUG=1, IntelXeFB at -O0')
 p.add_argument('--output',type=Path,default=REPO/'build')
 p.add_argument('--sdk',type=Path,default=Path(os.environ.get('MACKERNELSDK',REPO/'external/MacKernelSDK')),
  help='MacKernelSDK checkout (default: $MACKERNELSDK or <repo>/external/MacKernelSDK)')
 p.add_argument('--firmware',type=Path,default=REPO/'firmware',help='directory with bmg_guc_70.bin and bmg_huc.bin')
 p.add_argument('--only',choices=['IntelXe','IntelXeFB'],help='build one kext only')
 p.add_argument('--surfvram',type=int,choices=range(0,4),help='IntelXeSurfVramDefault in the personality: debug.intelxe.surfvram at boot (boot-arg intelxe_surfvram=N wins)')
 a=p.parse_args();out=a.output.resolve()
 sdk=a.sdk.resolve()
 if not (sdk/'Headers').is_dir() or not (sdk/'Library/x86_64/libkmod.a').is_file():
  sys.exit(f'MacKernelSDK not found at {sdk}: pass --sdk, set MACKERNELSDK, or clone it to {REPO/"external/MacKernelSDK"}')
 objdir=out/'obj';objdir.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
 # Same kernel C++ flags as HybridPM.
 base=['xcrun','clang++','-arch','x86_64','-std=c++17','-g','-fapple-kext','-fno-exceptions','-fno-rtti',
  '-fno-stack-protector','-fno-builtin','-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables','-mno-red-zone','-nostdinc','-DKERNEL','-DKERNEL_PRIVATE',
  '-D__APPLE__','-D__MACH__','-I'+str(sdk/'Headers'),'-mmacosx-version-min=10.6','-DAPPLE_KEXT_ASSERTIONS=1',
  '-DDRIVER_PRIVATE','-DAPPLE','-DNeXT','-fno-common','-Wall','-Wextra','-Wno-unused-parameter','-Wno-deprecated-declarations',
  '-fdebug-compilation-dir=.']
 if a.only in (None,'IntelXe'):
  for fwname,sha,name,inc in ((GUC,GUC_SHA,'kGucFw','guc_fw.inc'),(HUC,HUC_SHA,'kHucFw','huc_fw.inc')):
   src=a.firmware.resolve()/fwname
   if not src.is_file(): sys.exit(f'{src} is missing: run firmware/fetch.sh first')
   fw=src.read_bytes()
   assert hashlib.sha256(fw).hexdigest()==sha, f'{src}: unexpected sha256'
   (objdir/inc).write_text(f'static const uint8_t {name}[] __attribute__((aligned(16))) = {{\n'+
    '\n'.join(','.join(str(b) for b in fw[i:i+64])+',' for i in range(0,len(fw),64))+f'\n}};\nstatic const uint32_t {name}Size = {len(fw)};\n'+
    f'static const char {name}Name[] = "{fwname}";\n')   # IntelXe::start: the platform descriptor must name this file
  # XeProbe: whatever other GuC images are in the firmware directory. firmware/probe-guc.sha256 pins one per family
  # (firmware/fetch.sh --probe fetches them); another linux-firmware release's image is built in too, and said so:
  # stage 3 prints the version it loads, and debug.xeprobe.info lists every image built in.
  pins={}
  for line in (REPO/'firmware/probe-guc.sha256').read_text().splitlines():
   w=line.split()
   if len(w)==3 and not line.startswith('#'): pins[Path(w[1]).name]=(w[0],w[2])
  probe=[]
  for stem in ('tgl','adlp','dg1','dg2','mtl','lnl','ptl'):
   f=a.firmware.resolve()/f'{stem}_guc_70.bin'
   if f.exists():
    fw=f.read_bytes();probe.append((stem,fw));h=hashlib.sha256(fw).hexdigest();pin=pins.get(f.name)
    how=f'the pinned GuC {pin[1]}' if pin and pin[0]==h else f'NOT the pinned image (sha256 {h})' if pin else f'sha256 {h}'
    print(f'XeProbe GuC image {f.name}: {len(fw)} bytes, {how}')
  missing=[s for s in ('tgl','adlp','dg1','dg2','mtl','lnl','ptl') if s not in dict(probe)]
  if missing: print(f'XeProbe: no GuC image for {", ".join(missing)} (stage 3 says so there; firmware/fetch.sh --probe)')
  if missing and a.release and not a.no_probe_guc:
   sys.exit(f'--release: XeProbe GuC image(s) missing for {", ".join(missing)}: run firmware/fetch.sh --probe (into the --firmware directory), or pass --no-probe-guc')
  probe_stems=' '.join(s for s,_ in probe)
  inc='struct XpFw { const char *name; const uint8_t *data; uint32_t size; };\n'
  for stem,fw in probe:
   inc+=f'static const uint8_t kXpFw_{stem}[] __attribute__((aligned(16))) = {{\n'+'\n'.join(','.join(str(b) for b in fw[i:i+64])+',' for i in range(0,len(fw),64))+'\n};\n'
  inc+='static const XpFw kXpFw[] = {'+''.join(f'{{"{s}", kXpFw_{s}, {len(fw)}}},' for s,fw in probe)+'{nullptr, nullptr, 0}};\n'
  inc+=f'static const uint32_t kXpFwCount = {len(probe)};\n'
  (objdir/'xe_probe_fw.inc').write_text(inc)
 base.append('-I'+str(objdir))
 def kext(name,ident,srcs,libs,personality,extra={},ioclass=None,opt=[],more={}):
  # kmod_info: what Xcode generates for a kext (KMOD_EXPLICIT_DECL plus the C++ runtime hooks libkmod.a calls).
  bundle=out/f'{name}.kext/Contents';(bundle/'MacOS').mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
  info_c=objdir/f'{name}_kmod_info.c'
  info_c.write_text('#include <mach/kmod.h>\n'
   'extern kern_return_t _start(kmod_info_t *, void *);\nextern kern_return_t _stop(kmod_info_t *, void *);\n'
   f'extern kern_return_t {name}_start(kmod_info_t *, void *);\nextern kern_return_t {name}_stop(kmod_info_t *, void *);\n'
   f'__attribute__((visibility("default"))) KMOD_EXPLICIT_DECL({ident}, "{VER}", _start, _stop)\n'
   f'__private_extern__ kmod_start_func_t *_realmain = {name}_start;\n__private_extern__ kmod_stop_func_t *_antimain = {name}_stop;\n'
   '__private_extern__ int _kext_apple_cc = __APPLE_CC__;\n')
  objects=[]
  for src in srcs:
   objects.append(objdir/(Path(src).stem+'.o'));run(base+opt+['-c',HERE/src,'-o',objects[-1]])
  objects.append(objdir/f'{name}_kmod_info.o');run(cflags+opt+['-c',info_c,'-o',objects[-1]])
  exe=bundle/f'MacOS/{name}'
  run(['xcrun','ld','-arch','x86_64','-kext','-undefined','dynamic_lookup','-no_fixup_chains','-macos_version_min','10.6','-o',exe,*objects,sdk/'Library/x86_64/libkmod.a'])
  run(['xcrun','strip','-S',exe])
  info=dict(CFBundleIdentifier=ident,CFBundleExecutable=name,CFBundleName=name,CFBundlePackageType='KEXT',CFBundleVersion=VER,
   CFBundleShortVersionString=VER,OSBundleCompatibleVersion='0.1.0',OSBundleLibraries=libs,
   IOKitPersonalities={name:dict(CFBundleIdentifier=ident,IOClass=ioclass or name,IOProviderClass='IOPCIDevice',IOPCIMatch='0xe20b8086 0xe20c8086 0xe2118086 0xe2128086',**personality),
    f'{name}-G31':dict(CFBundleIdentifier=ident,IOClass=ioclass or name,IOProviderClass='IOPCIDevice',IOPCIMatch=G31_TESTER_MATCH,**personality),
    **{k:dict(CFBundleIdentifier=ident,**v) for k,v in more.items()}},**extra)
  (bundle/'Info.plist').write_bytes(plistlib.dumps(info))
  syms=subprocess.check_output(['xcrun','nm','-u',str(exe)],text=True)
  assert not any(x in syms for x in ['chkstk_darwin','___memcpy_chk']), 'userspace ABI imported'
  print(out/f'{name}.kext')
 cflags=['xcrun','clang','-std=c11']+[x for x in base[2:] if x not in('-std=c++17','-fapple-kext','-fno-rtti','-fno-exceptions')]
 libs={x:'10.0.0' for x in ['com.apple.kpi.bsd','com.apple.kpi.iokit','com.apple.kpi.libkern','com.apple.kpi.mach','com.apple.kpi.unsupported']}
 libs['com.apple.iokit.IOPCIFamily']='1.1'
 intelxeopt=['-O0','-DINTELXE_DEBUG=1'] if a.debug else ['-O2','-DINTELXE_DEBUG=0','-Wframe-larger-than=3072']
 if a.only in (None,'IntelXe'):
  intelxepers=dict(IOProbeScore=5000)
  if a.surfvram is not None: intelxepers['IntelXeSurfVramDefault']=a.surfvram
  # XeProbe: offered every Intel PCI device, in its own match category (beside any other driver); XeProbe::probe declines
  # all but the display function the boot-arg xeprobe=0xDEVICE names, so without that boot-arg it attaches nowhere.
  xeprobe=dict(IOClass='XeProbe',IOProviderClass='IOPCIDevice',IOPCIMatch='0x00008086&0x0000ffff',IOMatchCategory='XeProbe',IOProbeScore=0,
   XeProbeGuC=probe_stems)   # the families whose GuC image is built in (release/package.sh checks all seven)
  kext('IntelXe','io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXe',['IntelXe.cpp','xe_core.cpp','xe_vram.cpp','IntelXeClient.cpp','xe_probe.cpp','xe_fd.cpp',
   'xe_platform.cpp','xe_uapi_args.cpp','xe_aspm.cpp'],libs,intelxepers,
   dict(OSBundleRequired='Root'),opt=intelxeopt,more={'XeProbe':xeprobe})
 # IntelXeFB links IOGraphicsFamily, so it goes into the AuxKC (/Library/Extensions + kmutil), not OpenCore.
 # IOMatchCategory IOFramebuffer lets it sit on the GPU beside IntelXe and NMXAccel. It matches at boot from the AuxKC
 # (2026-10-29, "boot1": no more IOPropertyMatch intelxe-fb-armed / LaunchDaemon load); off with -intelxe_nofb or in safe mode.
 fblibs={x:'10.0.0' for x in ['com.apple.kpi.bsd','com.apple.kpi.iokit','com.apple.kpi.libkern','com.apple.kpi.mach']}
 fblibs.update({'com.apple.iokit.IOPCIFamily':'1.1','com.apple.iokit.IOGraphicsFamily':'1.0.0'})
 if a.only in (None,'IntelXeFB'):
  # IOPropertyMatch IntelXeReady: on macOS 26 the card can drop off the bus in the first seconds of boot; IntelXe.kext sets
  # IntelXeReady on the PCI device and re-registers it once bring-up succeeded, so the framebuffer matches only then.
  kext('IntelXeFB','io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB',[FBDIR/'IntelXeFB.cpp',FBDIR/'IntelXeLink.cpp',FBDIR/'IntelXeEdid.cpp'],fblibs,
   dict(IOProbeScore=60000,IOMatchCategory='IOFramebuffer',IOPropertyMatch=dict(IntelXeReady=True)),ioclass='IntelXeFramebuffer',
   opt=['-O0'] if a.debug else ['-O2','-Wframe-larger-than=3072'])
  # /Library/Extensions: install.sh refuses an unsigned binary, so the kext is signed ad hoc here (IntelXe.kext stays
  # unsigned: OpenCore injects it)
  run(['codesign','-f','-s','-',out/'IntelXeFB.kext'])
if __name__=='__main__':main()

// GuC ABI pieces for the minimal ADS, copied from Linux v7.2 drivers/gpu/drm/xe (MIT, Copyright Intel Corporation):
// xe_guc_fwif.h (guc_policies, guc_gt_system_info, guc_ads, guc_engine_usage*, guc_um_*, GUC_CTL_*),
// abi/guc_capture_abi.h (guc_mmio_reg_set), abi/guc_scheduler_abi.h (class/instance limits),
// abi/uc_fw_abi.h (uc_css_header), xe_guc_ads.c (__guc_ads_blob).
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

#define GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES 16
#define GUC_MAX_INSTANCES_PER_CLASS 32
#define GUC_GENERIC_GT_SYSINFO_MAX 16
#define GUC_CAPTURE_LIST_INDEX_MAX 2
#define GUC_UM_HW_QUEUE_MAX 3

#define GLOBAL_POLICY_MAX_NUM_WI 15
#define GLOBAL_POLICY_DEFAULT_DPC_PROMOTE_TIME_US 500000

#define GUC_CTL_LOG_PARAMS 0
#define GUC_CTL_WA 1
#define GUC_CTL_FEATURE 2
#define GUC_CTL_DEBUG 3
#define   GUC_LOG_DISABLED (1u << 6)
#define GUC_CTL_ADS 4             // GUC_ADS_ADDR 21:1 = GGTT address >> 12
#define GUC_CTL_DEVID 5
#define GUC_CTL_MAX_DWORDS 14

struct guc_mmio_reg_set {
	uint32_t address;
	uint16_t count;
	uint16_t reserved;
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_policies {
	uint32_t submission_queue_depth[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES];
	uint32_t dpc_promote_time;
	uint32_t is_valid;
	uint32_t max_num_work_items;
	uint32_t global_flags;
	uint32_t reserved[4];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_gt_system_info {
	uint8_t mapping_table[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES][GUC_MAX_INSTANCES_PER_CLASS];
	uint32_t engine_enabled_masks[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES];
	uint32_t generic_gt_sysinfo[GUC_GENERIC_GT_SYSINFO_MAX];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_ads {
	struct guc_mmio_reg_set reg_state_list[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES][GUC_MAX_INSTANCES_PER_CLASS];
	uint32_t reserved0;
	uint32_t scheduler_policies;
	uint32_t gt_system_info;
	uint32_t reserved1;
	uint32_t control_data;
	uint32_t golden_context_lrca[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES];
	uint32_t eng_state_size[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES];
	uint32_t private_data;
	uint32_t um_init_data;
	uint32_t capture_instance[GUC_CAPTURE_LIST_INDEX_MAX][GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES];
	uint32_t capture_class[GUC_CAPTURE_LIST_INDEX_MAX][GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES];
	uint32_t capture_global[GUC_CAPTURE_LIST_INDEX_MAX];
	uint32_t wa_klv_addr_lo;
	uint32_t wa_klv_addr_hi;
	uint32_t wa_klv_size;
	uint32_t reserved[11];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_engine_usage_record {
	uint32_t current_context_index;
	uint32_t last_switch_in_stamp;
	uint32_t reserved0;
	uint32_t total_runtime;
	uint32_t reserved1[4];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_engine_usage {
	struct guc_engine_usage_record engines[GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES][GUC_MAX_INSTANCES_PER_CLASS];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_um_queue_params {
	uint64_t base_dpa;
	uint32_t base_ggtt_address;
	uint32_t size_in_bytes;
	uint32_t rsvd[4];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_um_init_params {
	uint64_t page_response_timeout_in_us;
	uint32_t rsvd[6];
	struct guc_um_queue_params queue_params[GUC_UM_HW_QUEUE_MAX];
} __attribute__((packed));

struct guc_ads_blob {
	struct guc_ads ads;
	struct guc_policies policies;
	struct guc_gt_system_info system_info;
	struct guc_engine_usage engine_usage;
	struct guc_um_init_params um_init_params;
} __attribute__((packed));

struct uc_css_header {
	uint32_t module_type;
	uint32_t header_size_dw;
	uint32_t header_version;
	uint32_t reserved0;
	uint32_t module_vendor;
	uint32_t date;
	uint32_t size_dw;
	uint32_t key_size_dw, modulus_size_dw, exponent_size_dw;
	uint32_t time;
	uint32_t reserved_g0[5];
	uint32_t sw_version;
	uint32_t submission_version;
	uint32_t reserved_g1[11];
	uint32_t header_info;
	uint32_t private_data_size;
	uint32_t ukernel_info;
} __attribute__((packed));
static_assert(sizeof(struct uc_css_header) == 128, "CSS header");

// Logical ring context (LRC) image for the Xe2 copy engine, from Linux v7.2 drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_lrc.c (MIT,
// Copyright Intel Corporation): set_offsets(), XE2_CTX_COMMON, xe2_bcs_offsets, set_context_control(), and the
// layout of regs/xe_lrc_layout.h. Graphics 20.01 has no indirect ring state (graphics_xe2), so the ring registers
// live in the context image.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

#define LRC_NOP(x) (0x80 | (x))
#define LRC_LRI(count, flags) ((flags) << 6 | (count))
#define LRC_POSTED 1
#define LRC_REG(x) ((x) >> 2)
#define LRC_REG16(x) (((x) >> 9) | 0x80), (((x) >> 2) & 0x7f)

#define XE2_CTX_COMMON \
	LRC_NOP(1), \
	LRC_LRI(15, LRC_POSTED), \
	LRC_REG16(0x244), LRC_REG(0x034), LRC_REG(0x030), LRC_REG(0x038), LRC_REG(0x03c), LRC_REG(0x168), LRC_REG(0x140), \
	LRC_REG(0x110), LRC_REG(0x1c0), LRC_REG(0x1c4), LRC_REG(0x1c8), LRC_REG(0x180), LRC_REG16(0x2b4), LRC_REG(0x120), \
	LRC_REG(0x124), \
	LRC_NOP(1), \
	LRC_LRI(9, LRC_POSTED), \
	LRC_REG16(0x3a8), LRC_REG16(0x3ac), LRC_REG(0x108), LRC_REG16(0x284), LRC_REG16(0x280), LRC_REG16(0x27c), \
	LRC_REG16(0x278), LRC_REG16(0x274), LRC_REG16(0x270)

static const uint8_t xe2_rcs_offsets[] = {
	XE2_CTX_COMMON,
	LRC_NOP(2),
	LRC_LRI(2, LRC_POSTED),
	LRC_REG16(0x5a8), LRC_REG16(0x5ac),
	LRC_NOP(6),
	LRC_LRI(1, 0),
	LRC_REG(0x0c8),
	0
};

static const uint8_t xe2_xcs_offsets[] = {
	XE2_CTX_COMMON,
	0
};

static const uint8_t xe2_bcs_offsets[] = {
	LRC_NOP(1),
	LRC_LRI(15, LRC_POSTED),
	LRC_REG16(0x244), LRC_REG(0x034), LRC_REG(0x030), LRC_REG(0x038), LRC_REG(0x03c), LRC_REG(0x168), LRC_REG(0x140),
	LRC_REG(0x110), LRC_REG(0x1c0), LRC_REG(0x1c4), LRC_REG(0x1c8), LRC_REG(0x180), LRC_REG16(0x2b4), LRC_REG(0x120),
	LRC_REG(0x124),
	LRC_NOP(1),
	LRC_LRI(9, LRC_POSTED),
	LRC_REG16(0x3a8), LRC_REG16(0x3ac), LRC_REG(0x108), LRC_REG16(0x284), LRC_REG16(0x280), LRC_REG16(0x27c),
	LRC_REG16(0x278), LRC_REG16(0x274), LRC_REG16(0x270),
	LRC_NOP(4 + 8 + 1),
	LRC_LRI(2, LRC_POSTED),
	LRC_REG16(0x200), LRC_REG16(0x204),
	0
};

// MI commands (instructions/xe_mi_commands.h, xe_instr_defs.h)
#define MI_INSTR(op) ((uint32_t)(op) << 23)
#define MI_NOOP MI_INSTR(0x0)
#define MI_ARB_ON_OFF MI_INSTR(0x8)
#define   MI_ARB_ENABLE 1u
#define MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END MI_INSTR(0xa)
#define MI_STORE_DATA_IMM MI_INSTR(0x20)
#define   MI_SDI_GGTT (1u << 22)
#define   MI_SDI_NUM_DW(x) ((x) + 3 - 2)
#define   MI_SDI_NUM_QW(x) ((2 * (x) + 3 - 2) | 1u << 21)   // bit 21: the store is a qword
#define MI_LOAD_REGISTER_IMM MI_INSTR(0x22)
#define   MI_LRI_LRM_CS_MMIO (1u << 19)
#define   MI_LRI_FORCE_POSTED (1u << 12)
#define   MI_LRI_NUM_REGS(x) (2 * (x) + 1 - 2)

// Context image dword indices (regs/xe_lrc_layout.h)
#define CTX_CONTEXT_CONTROL (0x02 + 1)
#define CTX_RING_HEAD (0x04 + 1)
#define CTX_RING_TAIL (0x06 + 1)
#define CTX_RING_START (0x08 + 1)
#define CTX_RING_CTL (0x0a + 1)
#define CTX_TIMESTAMP (0x22 + 1)
#define CTX_ASID (0x2e + 1)
#define CTX_PDP0_UDW (0x30 + 1)
#define CTX_PDP0_LDW (0x32 + 1)

static inline void lrcSetOffsets(uint32_t *regs, const uint8_t *data, uint32_t base) {
	while (*data) {
		if (*data & 0x80) {
			regs += *data++ & 0x7f;
			continue;
		}
		uint8_t count = *data & 0x3f, flags = *data >> 6;
		data++;
		*regs = MI_LOAD_REGISTER_IMM | MI_LRI_NUM_REGS(count) | MI_LRI_LRM_CS_MMIO;
		if (flags & LRC_POSTED) *regs |= MI_LRI_FORCE_POSTED;
		regs++;
		do {
			uint32_t offset = 0;
			uint8_t v;
			do {
				v = *data++;
				offset = offset << 7 | (v & 0x7f);
			} while (v & 0x80);
			regs[0] = base + (offset << 2);
			regs += 2;
		} while (--count);
	}
	*regs = MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END | 1;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_aspm.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// PCIe ASPM on the GPU's path to the CPU (experimental, off unless asked for; untested on hardware).
//
//   sysctl debug.intelxe.aspm          (anyone) every link between the GPU function and its root port: Link Capabilities,
//                                      Link Control, Link Status, Device Capabilities, L1 PM Substates, the L1 checks
//                                      and the last change made
//   sudo sysctl debug.intelxe.aspm_l1=1   L1 on every link of the path, if every check passes (else nothing changes)
//   sudo sysctl debug.intelxe.aspm_l1=0   ASPM (L0s and L1) off on every link of the path
//   sudo sysctl debug.intelxe.aspm_l1=-1  (default) leave the links alone from now on (what was changed stays until a
//                                      reboot, or until 0 is written)
// After a system wake the last 0 or 1 written is applied again where the links no longer match it.
//
// The path: the B580 sits behind a switch on the card (upstream port 8086:e2ff, a downstream port 8086:e2f0 per
// function group) under a CPU or PCH root port, so it has two links: downstream port <-> GPU and root port <-> upstream
// port. In the service plane every IOPCIDevice's provider is the bridge driver (IOPCI2PCIBridge) of the port above it,
// whose provider is that port's IOPCIDevice; the walk stops at the host bridge, which is no IOPCIDevice.
//
// Changes go only through IOPCIDevice::setASPMState(client, state), called on each function of the downstream end of a
// link: IOPCIDevice.cpp passes it to its parent IOPCI2PCIBridge::setDeviceASPMState (IOPCIBridge.cpp), which writes the
// Link Control ASPM bits of both ends of exactly that link (the device and the bridge's own IOPCIDevice, fBridgeDevice),
// enable upstream first and disable downstream first, masked with what both ends advertise, and records the value in
// both ends' "pci-aspm-default". IOPCIFamily keeps Link Control in the config space it saves at sleep and restores at
// wake, so it holds without us; the wake path here only checks it. No direct Link Control write is needed: both links
// have an IOPCI2PCIBridge above their downstream end. Side effect of that call on function 0: the L1 PM Substates
// Control 1/2 registers of both ends are rewritten, to 0 unless the device tree gives "pci-l1ss-enable" or
// "pci-l1pm-control" (setDeviceL1PMBits), so L1 substates the firmware had enabled on a link we change are switched off.
// Links already in the requested state are not touched (xeAspmPlan).
#include "IntelXe.h"
#include "xe_aspm.h"
#include <IOKit/IORegistryEntry.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>

extern IntelXe *gDev;
IOLock *gAspmLock;     // allocated with the kext's other locks (IntelXe_start)
int gAspmL1 = -1;      // debug.intelxe.aspm_l1
static char gAspmLast[1024] = "none";

namespace {

struct AspmPath {
	XeAspmLink links[XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS];
	IOPCIDevice *upDev[XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS];
	IOPCIDevice *downDev[XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS][XE_ASPM_MAX_FN];
	char bridgeClass[XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS][48];   // the driver above each link's downstream end (setASPMState needs IOPCI2PCIBridge)
	uint32_t nLinks;
	XeAspmEndpoint eps[XE_ASPM_MAX_EPS];
	uint32_t nEps;
	bool tooMany;
	char err[128];
};

void readFn(IOPCIDevice *d, XeAspmFn *f) {
	bzero(f, sizeof *f);
	f->vendor = d->configRead16((UInt8)kIOPCIConfigVendorID);
	f->device = d->configRead16((UInt8)kIOPCIConfigDeviceID);
	f->bus = d->getBusNumber();
	f->dev = d->getDeviceNumber();
	f->fn = d->getFunctionNumber();
	if (f->vendor == 0xffff) return;
	UInt8 off = 0;
	if (!d->findPCICapability(kIOPCIPCIExpressCapability, &off) || !off) return;
	f->pcie = true;
	f->type = (uint8_t)(d->configRead16((UInt8)(off + XE_PCIE_FLAGS)) >> 4 & 0xf);
	f->devCap = d->configRead32((UInt8)(off + XE_PCIE_DEVCAP));
	f->lnkCap = d->configRead32((UInt8)(off + XE_PCIE_LNKCAP));
	f->lnkCtl = d->configRead16((UInt8)(off + XE_PCIE_LNKCTL));
	f->lnkSta = d->configRead16((UInt8)(off + XE_PCIE_LNKSTA));
	IOByteCount x = 0;
	if (d->extendedFindPCICapability((UInt32)-(int32_t)XE_PCIE_EXT_CAP_L1SS, &x) && x) {
		f->l1ss = true;
		f->l1ssCap = d->extendedConfigRead32(x + XE_L1SS_CAP);
		f->l1ssCtl1 = d->extendedConfigRead32(x + XE_L1SS_CTL1);
		f->l1ssCtl2 = d->extendedConfigRead32(x + XE_L1SS_CTL2);
	}
}

uint8_t pcieType(IOPCIDevice *d) {
	UInt8 off = 0;
	if (!d->findPCICapability(kIOPCIPCIExpressCapability, &off) || !off) return 0xff;
	return (uint8_t)(d->configRead16((UInt8)(off + XE_PCIE_FLAGS)) >> 4 & 0xf);
}

// The port above `d` (nullptr at the host bridge), and the bridge driver in between
IOPCIDevice *pciUp(IOPCIDevice *d, IORegistryEntry **bridge = nullptr) {
	IORegistryEntry *b = d->getParentEntry(gIOServicePlane);
	if (!b || OSDynamicCast(IOPCIDevice, b)) return nullptr;
	if (bridge) *bridge = b;
	return OSDynamicCast(IOPCIDevice, b->getParentEntry(gIOServicePlane));
}

// Every function of `d`'s device on its bus (the bridge's children with d's device number), function 0 first.
uint32_t siblingFunctions(IORegistryEntry *bridge, IOPCIDevice *d, IOPCIDevice **out, bool *tooMany) {
	uint32_t n = 0;
	if (OSIterator *it = bridge->getChildIterator(gIOServicePlane)) {
		while (OSObject *o = it->getNextObject()) {
			IOPCIDevice *c = OSDynamicCast(IOPCIDevice, o);
			if (!c || c->getBusNumber() != d->getBusNumber() || c->getDeviceNumber() != d->getDeviceNumber()) continue;
			if (n == XE_ASPM_MAX_FN) { *tooMany = true; break; }
			out[n++] = c;
		}
		it->release();
	}
	if (!n) out[n++] = d;
	for (uint32_t i = 1; i < n; i++)   // by function number
		for (uint32_t j = i; j > 0 && out[j]->getFunctionNumber() < out[j - 1]->getFunctionNumber(); j--) {
			IOPCIDevice *t = out[j];
			out[j] = out[j - 1];
			out[j - 1] = t;
		}
	return n;
}

// The lowest path link above endpoint `e` and the links between them; false if its path does not reach one.
bool endpointPlace(const AspmPath &p, IOPCIDevice *e, uint32_t *link, uint32_t *hops) {
	IOPCIDevice *d = e;
	uint32_t h = 0;
	for (int depth = 0; depth < 8; depth++) {
		IOPCIDevice *u = pciUp(d);
		if (!u) return false;
		const uint8_t ut = pcieType(u), dt = pcieType(d);
		if (xeAspmIsLink(ut, dt)) {
			for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p.nLinks; k++)
				if (p.upDev[k] == u) {
					*link = k;
					*hops = h;
					return true;
				}
			h++;
		}
		d = u;
	}
	return false;
}

void addEndpoint(AspmPath &p, IOPCIDevice *e) {
	XeAspmFn f;
	readFn(e, &f);
	if (!f.pcie || !xeAspmIsEndpoint(f.type)) return;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < p.nEps; i++)
		if (p.eps[i].bus == f.bus && p.eps[i].dev == f.dev && p.eps[i].fn == f.fn) return;
	uint32_t link = 0, hops = 0;
	if (!endpointPlace(p, e, &link, &hops)) return;
	if (p.nEps == XE_ASPM_MAX_EPS) {
		p.tooMany = true;
		return;
	}
	p.eps[p.nEps++] = XeAspmEndpoint{f.vendor, f.device, f.bus, f.dev, f.fn, f.devCap, link, hops};
}

// The links from `gpu` to its root port (link 0 = the GPU's own), and every endpoint below the top link. false (with
// p.err) when there is no link at all.
bool buildPath(IOPCIDevice *gpu, AspmPath &p) {
	bzero(&p, sizeof p);
	IOPCIDevice *d = gpu;
	for (int depth = 0; depth < 8 && p.nLinks < XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS; depth++) {
		IORegistryEntry *bridge = nullptr;
		IOPCIDevice *u = pciUp(d, &bridge);
		if (!u) break;
		if (xeAspmIsLink(pcieType(u), pcieType(d))) {
			const uint32_t k = p.nLinks++;
			p.upDev[k] = u;
			readFn(u, &p.links[k].up);
			strlcpy(p.bridgeClass[k], bridge->getMetaClass()->getClassName(), sizeof p.bridgeClass[k]);
			p.links[k].nDown = siblingFunctions(bridge, d, p.downDev[k], &p.tooMany);
			for (uint32_t i = 0; i < p.links[k].nDown; i++) readFn(p.downDev[k][i], &p.links[k].down[i]);
			if (pcieType(u) == XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT) break;
		}
		d = u;
	}
	if (!p.nLinks) {
		snprintf(p.err, sizeof p.err, "no PCIe link found above the GPU");
		return false;
	}
	// Endpoints: each function of the top link's downstream end and everything below it (the GPU among them)
	const uint32_t top = p.nLinks - 1;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < p.links[top].nDown; i++) {
		IOPCIDevice *t = p.downDev[top][i];
		addEndpoint(p, t);
		if (IORegistryIterator *it = IORegistryIterator::iterateOver(t, gIOServicePlane, kIORegistryIterateRecursively)) {
			while (IORegistryEntry *o = it->getNextObject())
				if (IOPCIDevice *e = OSDynamicCast(IOPCIDevice, o)) addEndpoint(p, e);
			it->release();
		}
	}
	return true;
}

void rereadPath(AspmPath &p) {
	for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p.nLinks; k++) {
		readFn(p.upDev[k], &p.links[k].up);
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < p.links[k].nDown; i++) readFn(p.downDev[k][i], &p.links[k].down[i]);
	}
}

void lastf(size_t *n, const char *fmt, ...) __printflike(2, 3);
void lastf(size_t *n, const char *fmt, ...) {
	if (*n >= sizeof gAspmLast - 1) return;
	va_list ap;
	va_start(ap, fmt);
	const int k = vsnprintf(gAspmLast + *n, sizeof gAspmLast - *n, fmt, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (k > 0) *n = *n + (size_t)k < sizeof gAspmLast - 1 ? *n + (size_t)k : sizeof gAspmLast - 1;
}

// Take the path to `target` (0 or 1). gAspmLock held. 0 or an errno; what happened goes to gAspmLast and the log.
int aspmApply(int target, const char *why) {
	size_t n = 0;
	gAspmLast[0] = 0;
	if (!gDev || !gDev->pciDevice()) return ENODEV;
	if (gDev->pwrSuspendSent || gDev->suspended) {
		lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=%d not applied: the device is asleep\n", why, target);
		return EBUSY;
	}
	AspmPath *p = static_cast<AspmPath *>(IOMalloc(sizeof(AspmPath)));
	if (!p) return ENOMEM;
	int err = 0;
	if (!buildPath(gDev->pciDevice(), *p)) {
		lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=%d refused: %s\n", why, target, p->err);
		LOG("ASPM: aspm_l1=%d refused: %s", target, p->err);
		err = ENODEV;
		goto out;
	}
	for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p->nLinks; k++)
		if (strncmp(p->bridgeClass[k], "IOPCI2PCIBridge", sizeof p->bridgeClass[k])) {
			// IOPCIDevice::setASPMState answers kIOReturnUnsupported unless the parent is an IOPCI2PCIBridge (subclasses
			// keep its setDeviceASPMState); report the class so a different driver shows up here, then let the call decide.
			lastf(&n, "%s: note: link %u's bridge driver is %s\n", why, k, p->bridgeClass[k]);
		}
	if (target == 1) {
		if (p->tooMany) {
			lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=1 refused: %s\n", why, xeAspmWhyName(XE_ASPM_TOO_MANY));
			LOG("ASPM: aspm_l1=1 refused: %s", xeAspmWhyName(XE_ASPM_TOO_MANY));
			err = EPERM;
			goto out;
		}
		for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p->nLinks; k++) {
			const XeAspmVerdict v = xeAspmL1Check(p->links, p->nLinks, k, p->eps, p->nEps);
			if (v.why != XE_ASPM_OK) {
				const XeAspmLink &l = p->links[k];
				lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=1 refused, nothing changed: link %u (%04x:%04x <-> %04x:%04x): %s", why, k,
					l.up.vendor, l.up.device, l.down[0].vendor, l.down[0].device, xeAspmWhyName(v.why));
				if (v.why == XE_ASPM_LATENCY)
					lastf(&n, " (%04x:%04x accepts %u ns, the link gives %u ns)", p->eps[v.index].vendor,
						p->eps[v.index].device, v.acceptableNs, v.latencyNs);
				lastf(&n, "\n");
				LOG("ASPM: aspm_l1=1 refused: link %u (%04x:%04x <-> %04x:%04x): %s", k, l.up.vendor, l.up.device,
					l.down[0].vendor, l.down[0].device, xeAspmWhyName(v.why));
				err = EPERM;
				goto out;
			}
		}
	}
	{
		XeAspmStep steps[XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS * XE_ASPM_MAX_FN * 2];
		const uint32_t ns = xeAspmPlan(p->links, p->nLinks, target, steps, sizeof steps / sizeof steps[0]);
		uint16_t before[XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS][2];
		for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p->nLinks; k++) before[k][0] = p->links[k].up.lnkCtl, before[k][1] = p->links[k].down[0].lnkCtl;
		if (!ns) {
			lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=%d: every link already %s, nothing written\n", why, target, target ? "has L1" : "has ASPM off");
			goto out;
		}
		for (uint32_t s = 0; s < ns; s++) {
			IOPCIDevice *d = p->downDev[steps[s].link][steps[s].fn];
			const IOReturn r = d->setASPMState(gDev, steps[s].state);
			LOG("ASPM: link %u: setASPMState(%02x:%02x.%x, %s) = 0x%x", steps[s].link, d->getBusNumber(),
				d->getDeviceNumber(), d->getFunctionNumber(), xeAspmCtlName(steps[s].state), r);
			if (r != kIOReturnSuccess) {
				lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=%d stopped: setASPMState on %02x:%02x.%x (link %u, %s) returned 0x%x after %u of %u calls\n",
					why, target, d->getBusNumber(), d->getDeviceNumber(), d->getFunctionNumber(), steps[s].link,
					xeAspmCtlName(steps[s].state), r, s, ns);
				err = EIO;
				break;
			}
		}
		rereadPath(*p);
		if (!err) lastf(&n, "%s: aspm_l1=%d: %u setASPMState call(s)\n", why, target, ns);
		for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p->nLinks; k++) {
			const XeAspmLink &l = p->links[k];
			const int st = xeAspmLinkState(l);
			const bool ok = target == 1 ? st >= 0 && (st & XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1) : st == 0;
			lastf(&n, "  link %u: up LnkCtl 0x%04x -> 0x%04x, down LnkCtl 0x%04x -> 0x%04x: %s%s\n", k, before[k][0],
				l.up.lnkCtl, before[k][1], l.down[0].lnkCtl, st >= 0 ? xeAspmCtlName((uint32_t)st) : "ends differ",
				ok ? "" : " (NOT as asked)");
			LOG("ASPM: link %u: LnkCtl up 0x%04x -> 0x%04x, down 0x%04x -> 0x%04x%s", k, before[k][0], l.up.lnkCtl,
				before[k][1], l.down[0].lnkCtl, ok ? "" : " (not as asked)");
			if (!ok && !err) err = EIO;
		}
	}
out:
	IOFree(p, sizeof(AspmPath));
	return err;
}

}   // namespace

// debug.intelxe.aspm_l1 write
int xeAspmSet(int v) {
	if (v < -1 || v > 1) return EINVAL;
	if (!gAspmLock) return ENODEV;
	IOLockLock(gAspmLock);
	int err = 0;
	if (v == -1) {
		size_t n = 0;
		gAspmLast[0] = 0;
		lastf(&n, "sysctl: aspm_l1=-1: the links are left as they are now (a reboot gives the firmware's settings back)\n");
		gAspmL1 = -1;
	} else if (!(err = aspmApply(v, "sysctl"))) {
		gAspmL1 = v;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gAspmLock);
	return err;
}

// After a system wake (IntelXe::setPowerState): the last 0 or 1 again where IOPCIFamily's restore did not keep it.
void xeAspmWake() {
	if (!gAspmLock) return;
	IOLockLock(gAspmLock);
	if (gAspmL1 >= 0) {
		const int err = aspmApply(gAspmL1, "wake");
		if (err) LOG("ASPM: aspm_l1=%d after wake: %d", gAspmL1, err);
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gAspmLock);
}

// debug.intelxe.aspm
int xeAspmReport(char *b, size_t len) {
	size_t n = 0;
	char t[256];
	if (!gDev || !gDev->pciDevice()) return snprintf(b, len, "no device\n");
	if (gDev->pwrSuspendSent || gDev->suspended) return snprintf(b, len, "unavailable (asleep)\n");
	AspmPath *p = static_cast<AspmPath *>(IOMalloc(sizeof(AspmPath)));
	if (!p) return snprintf(b, len, "no memory\n");
	IOLockLock(gAspmLock);
	snprintf(t, sizeof t, "aspm_l1 = %d (%s); experimental, untested\n", gAspmL1,
		gAspmL1 < 0 ? "leave as the firmware set it" : gAspmL1 ? "L1 on the path" : "ASPM off on the path");
	xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, t);
	if (!buildPath(gDev->pciDevice(), *p)) {
		snprintf(t, sizeof t, "%s\n", p->err);
		xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, t);
	} else {
		for (uint32_t k = 0; k < p->nLinks; k++) {
			const XeAspmLink &l = p->links[k];
			const int st = xeAspmLinkState(l);
			snprintf(t, sizeof t, "link %u: %s <-> %s, ASPM %s, via %s\n", k, xeAspmTypeName(l.up.type),
				xeAspmTypeName(l.down[0].type), st >= 0 ? xeAspmCtlName((uint32_t)st) : "differs between the ends",
				p->bridgeClass[k]);
			xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, t);
			xeAspmFormatFn(b, len, &n, "up  ", l.up);
			for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++) xeAspmFormatFn(b, len, &n, "down", l.down[i]);
			const XeAspmVerdict v = xeAspmL1Check(p->links, p->nLinks, k, p->eps, p->nEps);
			xeAspmFormatVerdict(b, len, &n, v, l, p->eps);
		}
		xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, "endpoints below the path (L1 acceptable latency, link above, links between):\n");
		for (uint32_t e = 0; e < p->nEps; e++) {
			char a[16];
			xeAspmNs(a, sizeof a, xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(p->eps[e].devCap), true);
			snprintf(t, sizeof t, "  %02x:%02x.%x %04x:%04x: %s, link %u, %u\n", p->eps[e].bus, p->eps[e].dev, p->eps[e].fn,
				p->eps[e].vendor, p->eps[e].device, a, p->eps[e].link, p->eps[e].hops);
			xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, t);
		}
		if (p->tooMany) xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, "  (more functions or endpoints than the tables hold: aspm_l1=1 refuses)\n");
	}
	xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, "last change:\n");
	xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, gAspmLast);
	if (n && b[n - 1] != '\n') xeAspmPut(b, len, &n, "\n");
	IOLockUnlock(gAspmLock);
	IOFree(p, sizeof(AspmPath));
	return (int)n;
}

static int aspmHandler SYSCTL_HANDLER_ARGS {
	constexpr size_t kLen = 8192;
	char *b = static_cast<char *>(IOMalloc(kLen));
	if (!b) return ENOMEM;
	const int n = xeAspmReport(b, kLen);
	const int err = SYSCTL_OUT(req, b, (size_t)(n > 0 ? (n < (int)kLen - 1 ? n : (int)kLen - 1) : 0) + 1);
	IOFree(b, kLen);
	return err;
}
static int aspmL1Handler SYSCTL_HANDLER_ARGS {
	int v = gAspmL1, err = sysctl_handle_int(oidp, &v, 0, req);
	if (err || !req->newptr) return err;
	return xeAspmSet(v);
}
SYSCTL_DECL(_debug_intelxe);
SYSCTL_PROC(_debug_intelxe, OID_AUTO, aspm, CTLTYPE_STRING | CTLFLAG_RD | CTLFLAG_ANYBODY, nullptr, 0, aspmHandler, "A",
	"experimental: PCIe ASPM state of every link between the GPU and its root port, the L1 checks, the last change");
SYSCTL_PROC(_debug_intelxe, OID_AUTO, aspm_l1, CTLTYPE_INT | CTLFLAG_RW, nullptr, 0, aspmL1Handler, "I",
	"experimental: 1 = ASPM L1 on the GPU's path if every check passes, 0 = ASPM off there, -1 = leave it (default)");
void xeAspmRegister(bool on) {
	if (on) {
		sysctl_register_oid(&sysctl__debug_intelxe_aspm);
		sysctl_register_oid(&sysctl__debug_intelxe_aspm_l1);
	} else {
		sysctl_unregister_oid(&sysctl__debug_intelxe_aspm_l1);
		sysctl_unregister_oid(&sysctl__debug_intelxe_aspm);
	}
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_aspm.h
