// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// PCIe ASPM on the links between the GPU and the CPU's root port (debug.intelxe.aspm, debug.intelxe.aspm_l1): the pure
// parts, so that tests/aspm_test.cpp builds them on the host. The register layout is the PCIe Base Specification's as
// Linux include/uapi/linux/pci_regs.h names it; the rules are Linux drivers/pci/pcie/aspm.c (tree abf8c33, v7.4 merge
// window):
//   - L1 only where both ends of the link advertise it in Link Capabilities (pcie_aspm_cap_init, aspm.c:994);
//   - no ASPM on a link with a pre-1.1 function (no Role-Based Error Reporting, pcie_aspm_sanity_check, aspm.c:1129-1161)
//     or with a function that is not PCIe;
//   - the L1 exit latency of each link, plus 1 us for every link between it and the endpoint, must not exceed the L1
//     acceptable latency of every endpoint below it (pcie_aspm_check_latency, aspm.c:608-675); the exit latencies are
//     the Link Capabilities' as read now, which depend on the Common Clock configuration (aspm.c:961-965);
//   - Linux sets Common Clock Configuration on a link whose two ends report Slot Clock Configuration and retrains it
//     before it looks at the latencies (pcie_aspm_configure_common_clock, aspm.c:409-475). No retraining here: a link
//     that would need it (shared reference clock, CCC clear or inconsistent) is refused instead;
//   - order (PCIe r6.2 sec 7.5.3.7, aspm.c:1084-1096): L1 is enabled in the upstream component before the downstream
//     one and disabled in the downstream component first; every function of a multi-function device gets the same value.
// The kext reads the registers through IOPCIDevice and changes them only through IOPCIDevice::setASPMState (xe_aspm.cpp).
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#if defined(KERNEL)
#include <libkern/libkern.h>   // snprintf
#else
#include <stdio.h>
#endif

// pci_regs.h: offsets in the PCI Express capability, and in the L1 PM Substates extended capability (ID 0x1e)
static constexpr uint32_t XE_PCIE_FLAGS = 0x02, XE_PCIE_DEVCAP = 0x04, XE_PCIE_LNKCAP = 0x0c, XE_PCIE_LNKCTL = 0x10,
	XE_PCIE_LNKSTA = 0x12, XE_PCIE_DEVCTL = 0x08;
static constexpr uint32_t XE_L1SS_CAP = 0x04, XE_L1SS_CTL1 = 0x08, XE_L1SS_CTL2 = 0x0c;
static constexpr uint32_t XE_PCIE_EXT_CAP_L1SS = 0x1e;
// PCI_EXP_FLAGS_TYPE values
enum : uint8_t { XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT = 0, XE_PCIE_LEG_END = 1, XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT = 4, XE_PCIE_UPSTREAM = 5, XE_PCIE_DOWNSTREAM = 6 };
static constexpr uint32_t XE_DEVCAP_EXT_TAG = 0x20;   // PCI_EXP_DEVCAP_EXT_TAG
static constexpr uint16_t XE_DEVCTL_EXT_TAG = 0x100;   // PCI_EXP_DEVCTL_EXT_TAG
static constexpr uint32_t XE_DEVCAP_L0S_ACC = 0x1c0, XE_DEVCAP_L1_ACC = 0xe00, XE_DEVCAP_RBER = 0x8000;
static constexpr uint32_t XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L0S = 0x400, XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L1 = 0x800, XE_LNKCAP_L0SEL = 0x7000,
	XE_LNKCAP_L1EL = 0x38000, XE_LNKCAP_CLKPM = 0x40000;
static constexpr uint16_t XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L0S = 0x1, XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1 = 0x2, XE_LNKCTL_ASPMC = 0x3, XE_LNKCTL_CCC = 0x40,
	XE_LNKCTL_CLKREQ_EN = 0x100;
static constexpr uint16_t XE_LNKSTA_CLS = 0xf, XE_LNKSTA_NLW = 0x3f0, XE_LNKSTA_SLC = 0x1000, XE_LNKSTA_DLLLA = 0x2000;
// L1SS capability / control 1: PCI-PM L1.2, PCI-PM L1.1, ASPM L1.2, ASPM L1.1 in bits 0-3 of both
static constexpr uint32_t XE_L1SS_BITS = 0xf, XE_L1SS_CAP_SS = 0x10;

static constexpr uint32_t XE_ASPM_MAX_FN = 8, XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS = 4, XE_ASPM_MAX_EPS = 16;

// One PCIe function's registers, as read from config space. pcie false: no PCI Express capability, or the function did
// not answer (vendor 0xffff).
struct XeAspmFn {
	uint16_t vendor, device;
	uint8_t bus, dev, fn;
	bool pcie;
	uint8_t type;               // PCI_EXP_FLAGS_TYPE
	uint32_t devCap, lnkCap;
	uint16_t lnkCtl, lnkSta;
	bool l1ss;                  // the L1 PM Substates capability is present
	uint32_t l1ssCap, l1ssCtl1, l1ssCtl2;
};

// A link: the upstream component (a root port or a switch downstream port) and the functions of the downstream
// component (all on the port's secondary bus, function 0 first).
struct XeAspmLink {
	XeAspmFn up;
	XeAspmFn down[XE_ASPM_MAX_FN];
	uint32_t nDown;
};

// An endpoint below the path: its Device Capabilities, the lowest path link above it (index into the links, 0 = the
// GPU's own link) and the number of links between it and that one (0: it sits on it; an endpoint behind another
// downstream port of the card's switch is 1 link below the root port's link).
struct XeAspmEndpoint {
	uint16_t vendor, device;
	uint8_t bus, dev, fn;
	uint32_t devCap;
	uint32_t link, hops;
};

// aspm.c:478-512: exit latencies from Link Capabilities and acceptable latencies from Device Capabilities, in ns
static inline uint32_t xeAspmL0sExitNs(uint32_t lnkCap) {
	const uint32_t e = (lnkCap & XE_LNKCAP_L0SEL) >> 12;
	return e == 7 ? 5000 : 64u << e;
}
static inline uint32_t xeAspmL1ExitNs(uint32_t lnkCap) {
	const uint32_t e = (lnkCap & XE_LNKCAP_L1EL) >> 15;
	return e == 7 ? 65000 : 1000u << e;
}
static inline uint32_t xeAspmL0sAcceptableNs(uint32_t devCap) {
	const uint32_t e = (devCap & XE_DEVCAP_L0S_ACC) >> 6;
	return e == 7 ? UINT32_MAX : 64u << e;
}
static inline uint32_t xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(uint32_t devCap) {
	const uint32_t e = (devCap & XE_DEVCAP_L1_ACC) >> 9;
	return e == 7 ? UINT32_MAX : 1000u << e;
}
static inline bool xeAspmIsEndpoint(uint8_t type) { return type == XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT || type == XE_PCIE_LEG_END; }
// A pair (parent port, child function) forms a link when the parent faces downstream and the child is what sits at the
// other end of a link: an endpoint or a switch upstream port. A switch's downstream port under its upstream port is
// inside the switch, not a link.
static inline bool xeAspmIsLink(uint8_t parentType, uint8_t childType) {
	return (parentType == XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT || parentType == XE_PCIE_DOWNSTREAM) &&
		(xeAspmIsEndpoint(childType) || childType == XE_PCIE_UPSTREAM);
}

enum XeAspmWhy : uint32_t {
	XE_ASPM_OK,
	XE_ASPM_NO_FN,             // the link has no downstream function
	XE_ASPM_NOT_PCIE,          // a function without a PCIe capability or not answering
	XE_ASPM_PRE_1_1,           // a downstream function without RBER (pre-1.1)
	XE_ASPM_NO_L1_UP,          // the upstream port does not advertise L1
	XE_ASPM_NO_L1_DOWN,        // a downstream function does not advertise L1
	XE_ASPM_CCC_INCONSISTENT,  // Common Clock Configuration differs between the ends or functions
	XE_ASPM_CCC_NOT_SET,       // both ends share the slot clock but CCC is clear (Linux would set it and retrain)
	XE_ASPM_LATENCY,           // an endpoint below does not accept the L1 exit latency
	XE_ASPM_TOO_MANY,          // more functions or endpoints than the tables hold
};
static inline const char *xeAspmWhyName(XeAspmWhy w) {
	switch (w) {
		case XE_ASPM_OK: return "ok";
		case XE_ASPM_NO_FN: return "no downstream function";
		case XE_ASPM_NOT_PCIE: return "a function has no PCIe capability or does not answer";
		case XE_ASPM_PRE_1_1: return "a downstream function is pre-1.1 (no RBER; Linux pcie_aspm_sanity_check)";
		case XE_ASPM_NO_L1_UP: return "the upstream port does not support ASPM L1 (Link Capabilities bit 11)";
		case XE_ASPM_NO_L1_DOWN: return "a downstream function does not support ASPM L1 (Link Capabilities bit 11)";
		case XE_ASPM_CCC_INCONSISTENT: return "Common Clock Configuration differs between the link's functions";
		case XE_ASPM_CCC_NOT_SET:
			return "both ends use the slot clock but Common Clock Configuration is clear (Linux sets it and retrains the "
				"link first; not done here)";
		case XE_ASPM_LATENCY: return "an endpoint does not accept the L1 exit latency (Device Capabilities 11:9)";
		case XE_ASPM_TOO_MANY: return "more functions or endpoints than the tables hold";
	}
	return "?";
}

struct XeAspmVerdict {
	XeAspmWhy why;
	uint32_t index;          // the function (down[] index, or endpoint index for XE_ASPM_LATENCY) the check failed on
	uint32_t latencyNs;      // XE_ASPM_LATENCY: the link's exit latency plus the switch latency for that endpoint,
	uint32_t acceptableNs;   //   and what the endpoint accepts
};

// May link `li` of `links` take ASPM L1? Every endpoint whose path goes through it (e.link <= li) must accept the
// larger of the two ends' L1 exit latencies plus 1 us per link between the endpoint and this one (aspm.c:651-668).
static inline XeAspmVerdict xeAspmL1Check(const XeAspmLink *links, uint32_t nLinks, uint32_t li,
	const XeAspmEndpoint *eps, uint32_t nEps) {
	XeAspmVerdict v = {XE_ASPM_OK, 0, 0, 0};
	if (li >= nLinks) { v.why = XE_ASPM_NO_FN; return v; }
	const XeAspmLink &l = links[li];
	if (!l.nDown) { v.why = XE_ASPM_NO_FN; return v; }
	if (l.nDown > XE_ASPM_MAX_FN || nEps > XE_ASPM_MAX_EPS) { v.why = XE_ASPM_TOO_MANY; return v; }
	if (!l.up.pcie) { v.why = XE_ASPM_NOT_PCIE; return v; }
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++)
		if (!l.down[i].pcie) { v.why = XE_ASPM_NOT_PCIE; v.index = i; return v; }
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++)
		if (!(l.down[i].devCap & XE_DEVCAP_RBER)) { v.why = XE_ASPM_PRE_1_1; v.index = i; return v; }
	if (!(l.up.lnkCap & XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L1)) { v.why = XE_ASPM_NO_L1_UP; return v; }
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++)
		if (!(l.down[i].lnkCap & XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L1)) { v.why = XE_ASPM_NO_L1_DOWN; v.index = i; return v; }
	const bool ccUp = l.up.lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_CCC;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++)
		if (((l.down[i].lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_CCC) != 0) != ccUp) { v.why = XE_ASPM_CCC_INCONSISTENT; v.index = i; return v; }
	// aspm.c:422-430: the slot clock is shared when both ends report Slot Clock Configuration (function 0 below)
	if ((l.up.lnkSta & XE_LNKSTA_SLC) && (l.down[0].lnkSta & XE_LNKSTA_SLC) && !ccUp) { v.why = XE_ASPM_CCC_NOT_SET; return v; }
	// aspm.c:625-629: the downstream exit latency is function 0's
	const uint32_t up = xeAspmL1ExitNs(l.up.lnkCap), dw = xeAspmL1ExitNs(l.down[0].lnkCap);
	const uint32_t exit = up > dw ? up : dw;
	for (uint32_t e = 0; e < nEps; e++) {
		if (eps[e].link > li) continue;   // its path does not go through this link
		const uint64_t lat = (uint64_t)exit + 1000ull * (eps[e].hops + (li - eps[e].link));
		const uint32_t acc = xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(eps[e].devCap);
		if (lat > acc) {
			v.why = XE_ASPM_LATENCY;
			v.index = e;
			v.latencyNs = lat > UINT32_MAX ? UINT32_MAX : (uint32_t)lat;
			v.acceptableNs = acc;
			return v;
		}
	}
	return v;
}

// The ASPM Control value every end of the link has now, or -1 when they differ.
static inline int xeAspmLinkState(const XeAspmLink &l) {
	const int s = l.up.lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_ASPMC;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++)
		if ((l.down[i].lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_ASPMC) != s) return -1;
	return s;
}

// One IOPCIDevice::setASPMState call: on function `fn` of link `link`'s downstream component, with ASPM Control `state`
// (0, or the L0s/L1 enable bits). IOPCI2PCIBridge::setDeviceASPMState (IOPCIFamily IOPCIBridge.cpp) then writes both
// ends of that link: to enable, the bridge (upstream) first and the device second, to disable (state 0) the device
// first and the bridge second; it keeps only the bits both ends support (aspmCaps from Link Capabilities 11:10).
struct XeAspmStep {
	uint8_t link, fn;
	uint8_t state;
};

// The calls that take the path to `target` (1: L1 on every link, 0: ASPM off on every link), in the Linux order.
// Enable: links from the root port down (the upstream link first), and on each link L1 only once the link holds no L1
// enable that a direct enable call would clear in the wrong order: IOPCIFamily's enable path first clears L1 in the
// bridge and then in the device, so a link with any ASPM bit set is first disabled (device before bridge), then
// enabled. L0s stays on where every end of the link has it on now and drops elsewhere. Disable: links from the GPU up
// (the downstream link first). Within a link the functions go from the highest to function 0 for a disable and from
// function 0 up for an enable: for a multi-function device only the states enabled in every function are enabled
// (PCIe r6.2 sec 7.5.3.7), so the first disabled function already disables the component before the bridge, and the
// last enabled one enables it after the bridge. Links already in the target state get no call. Returns the number of
// steps (at most `max`; 0 also when there is nothing to do).
static inline uint32_t xeAspmPlan(const XeAspmLink *links, uint32_t nLinks, int target, XeAspmStep *steps, uint32_t max) {
	uint32_t n = 0;
	auto add = [&](uint32_t li, uint32_t fn, uint8_t st) {
		if (n < max) steps[n++] = XeAspmStep{(uint8_t)li, (uint8_t)fn, st};
	};
	if (nLinks > XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS) return 0;
	if (target == 1) {
		for (uint32_t k = nLinks; k-- > 0;) {
			const XeAspmLink &l = links[k];
			const int now = xeAspmLinkState(l);
			const uint8_t want = (uint8_t)(XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1 | (now >= 0 ? (now & XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L0S) : 0));
			if (now == want) continue;
			bool any = l.up.lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_ASPMC;
			for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++) any = any || (l.down[i].lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_ASPMC);
			if (any)
				for (uint32_t i = l.nDown; i-- > 0;) add(k, i, 0);
			for (uint32_t i = 0; i < l.nDown; i++) add(k, i, want);
		}
	} else if (target == 0) {
		for (uint32_t k = 0; k < nLinks; k++) {
			const XeAspmLink &l = links[k];
			if (xeAspmLinkState(l) == 0) continue;
			for (uint32_t i = l.nDown; i-- > 0;) add(k, i, 0);
		}
	}
	return n;
}

// Report text
static inline const char *xeAspmTypeName(uint8_t t) {
	switch (t) {
		case XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT: return "endpoint";
		case XE_PCIE_LEG_END: return "legacy endpoint";
		case XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT: return "root port";
		case XE_PCIE_UPSTREAM: return "switch upstream port";
		case XE_PCIE_DOWNSTREAM: return "switch downstream port";
		default: return "other";
	}
}
static inline const char *xeAspmCtlName(uint32_t c) {
	static const char *const k[] = {"off", "L0s", "L1", "L0s L1"};
	return k[c & 3];
}
static inline void xeAspmPut(char *b, size_t len, size_t *n, const char *s) {
	if (*n >= len) return;
	const int k = snprintf(b + *n, len - *n, "%s", s);
	if (k > 0) *n = *n + (size_t)k < len ? *n + (size_t)k : len - 1;
}
// "1 us", "64 ns", ">64 us", "any"
static inline void xeAspmNs(char *o, size_t len, uint32_t ns, bool acceptable) {
	if (ns == UINT32_MAX) snprintf(o, len, "any");
	else if (!acceptable && ns == 65000) snprintf(o, len, ">64 us");
	else if (!acceptable && ns == 5000) snprintf(o, len, ">4 us");
	else if (ns >= 1000) snprintf(o, len, "%u us", ns / 1000);
	else snprintf(o, len, "%u ns", ns);
}
// One function, two lines: "<role> bb:dd.f vvvv:dddd <type>" and its link registers decoded.
static inline void xeAspmFormatFn(char *b, size_t len, size_t *n, const char *role, const XeAspmFn &f) {
	char t[256];
	snprintf(t, sizeof t, "  %s %02x:%02x.%x %04x:%04x", role, f.bus, f.dev, f.fn, f.vendor, f.device);
	xeAspmPut(b, len, n, t);
	if (!f.pcie) {
		xeAspmPut(b, len, n, ": no PCIe capability or no answer\n");
		return;
	}
	char l0s[16], l1[16], a0[16], a1[16];
	xeAspmNs(l0s, sizeof l0s, xeAspmL0sExitNs(f.lnkCap), false);
	xeAspmNs(l1, sizeof l1, xeAspmL1ExitNs(f.lnkCap), false);
	xeAspmNs(a0, sizeof a0, xeAspmL0sAcceptableNs(f.devCap), true);
	xeAspmNs(a1, sizeof a1, xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(f.devCap), true);
	snprintf(t, sizeof t, " %s\n    LnkCap 0x%08x: ASPM support %s, exit L0s %s L1 %s, ClkPM %u, port %u\n",
		xeAspmTypeName(f.type), f.lnkCap, xeAspmCtlName(f.lnkCap >> 10), l0s, l1, (f.lnkCap & XE_LNKCAP_CLKPM) ? 1 : 0,
		f.lnkCap >> 24);
	xeAspmPut(b, len, n, t);
	snprintf(t, sizeof t, "    LnkCtl 0x%04x: ASPM %s, CommonClk %u, ClkReq %u; LnkSta 0x%04x: gen %u x%u, SlotClk %u, DLActive %u\n",
		f.lnkCtl, xeAspmCtlName(f.lnkCtl), (f.lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_CCC) ? 1 : 0, (f.lnkCtl & XE_LNKCTL_CLKREQ_EN) ? 1 : 0,
		f.lnkSta, f.lnkSta & XE_LNKSTA_CLS, (f.lnkSta & XE_LNKSTA_NLW) >> 4, (f.lnkSta & XE_LNKSTA_SLC) ? 1 : 0,
		(f.lnkSta & XE_LNKSTA_DLLLA) ? 1 : 0);
	xeAspmPut(b, len, n, t);
	snprintf(t, sizeof t, "    DevCap 0x%08x: acceptable L0s %s L1 %s, RBER %u\n", f.devCap, a0, a1,
		(f.devCap & XE_DEVCAP_RBER) ? 1 : 0);
	xeAspmPut(b, len, n, t);
	if (!f.l1ss) {
		xeAspmPut(b, len, n, "    L1 PM Substates: no capability\n");
		return;
	}
	auto ss = [](char *o, size_t ol, uint32_t v) {
		snprintf(o, ol, "%s%s%s%s", (v & 8) ? " ASPM-L1.1" : "", (v & 4) ? " ASPM-L1.2" : "", (v & 2) ? " PCIPM-L1.1" : "",
			(v & 1) ? " PCIPM-L1.2" : "");
		if (!(v & XE_L1SS_BITS)) snprintf(o, ol, " none");
	};
	char sc[64], sl[64];
	ss(sc, sizeof sc, f.l1ssCap);
	ss(sl, sizeof sl, f.l1ssCtl1);
	snprintf(t, sizeof t, "    L1 PM Substates: cap 0x%08x (%s), ctl1 0x%08x (enabled%s), ctl2 0x%08x\n", f.l1ssCap,
		sc + 1, f.l1ssCtl1, sl, f.l1ssCtl2);
	xeAspmPut(b, len, n, t);
}
// A link's verdict for L1: "L1 allowed" or "L1 refused: <reason>".
static inline void xeAspmFormatVerdict(char *b, size_t len, size_t *n, const XeAspmVerdict &v, const XeAspmLink &l,
	const XeAspmEndpoint *eps) {
	char t[384];
	if (v.why == XE_ASPM_OK) snprintf(t, sizeof t, "  L1 check: allowed\n");
	else if (v.why == XE_ASPM_LATENCY)
		snprintf(t, sizeof t, "  L1 check: refused: %s: %04x:%04x at %02x:%02x.%x needs %u ns or less, the link gives %u ns\n",
			xeAspmWhyName(v.why), eps[v.index].vendor, eps[v.index].device, eps[v.index].bus, eps[v.index].dev,
			eps[v.index].fn, v.acceptableNs, v.latencyNs);
	else if (v.index < l.nDown && (v.why == XE_ASPM_NOT_PCIE || v.why == XE_ASPM_PRE_1_1 || v.why == XE_ASPM_NO_L1_DOWN ||
		v.why == XE_ASPM_CCC_INCONSISTENT))
		snprintf(t, sizeof t, "  L1 check: refused: %s (%04x:%04x)\n", xeAspmWhyName(v.why), l.down[v.index].vendor,
			l.down[v.index].device);
	else snprintf(t, sizeof t, "  L1 check: refused: %s\n", xeAspmWhyName(v.why));
	xeAspmPut(b, len, n, t);
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// BAR-window revocation (debug.intelxe.bar_revoke, default 0): the pure parts, so that tests/barrevoke_test.cpp builds
// them on the host. Design: docs/design/DESIGN-rebar-window.md section 8.
//
// A BO the CPU has mapped used to stay in the 1 GB BAR window for good: an IOKit user mapping of a physical range has no
// fault handler a driver can hook (Linux's TTM zaps the mmap and lets the next CPU fault find the BO wherever it is now).
// With bar_revoke 1, a cold, idle, CPU-mapped window BO can move to system memory while its user mapping stays valid:
//  1. the mapping is blocked (IOMemoryMap::redirect(NULL): a UPL_BLOCK_ACCESS UPL on its device-pager VM object, the
//     user PTEs removed, so every CPU access waits in vm_fault),
//  2. the copy engine copies the VRAM into new, physically contiguous system pages,
//  3. the GPU PTEs of every binding are rewritten to the new pages (the BO's VMs are idle and held),
//  4. the mapping is redirected (IOMemoryMap::redirect(new backing)): xnu transposes the user's VM object with the VM
//     object of a kernel mapping of the new pages (upl_transpose / vm_object_transpose, the "Virtual VRAM" path
//     vm_fault knows), which unblocks it,
//  5. the result is checked (a kernel mapping of the object the user now maps must resolve to the new pages) before
//     the old VRAM is given back.
// What can go wrong at each step, and what is kept or undone, is the state machine below; which BOs are taken, and in
// which order (least recently touched first), is the policy.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

// ─── candidates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// What the kernel knows about one window BO, under its client's lock.
struct XeRevokeFacts {
	uint64_t size;
	uint64_t touchNs;        // last CPU touch through the uAPI (GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, a map) or EXEC on a VM binding it
	bool inWindow;           // VRAM inside the BAR window
	bool mapped;             // the CPU was given a mapping (XeBo::mapped)
	bool contig;             // one physical run (a phys_contiguous device-pager object; the only shape redirected)
	bool pinned;             // a scan-out pin or DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_SCANOUT: the display reads its DPA
	bool shared;             // another client has a handle, a GEM name or a PRIME export of it
	bool compressed;         // bound with a compressed PAT once (system memory has no CCS)
	bool moving;             // a move is in progress, or its binding records do not describe its PTEs (noMove)
	bool clearPending;       // its fresh-VRAM clear has not landed
	bool vmBusy;             // a VM that binds it has work outstanding (in-flight jobs pin it)
	bool purgeable;          // not WILLNEED: the purge path frees it instead
	uint32_t liveMaps;       // CPU maps with a mapping (all its maps)
	uint32_t unusedMaps;     // GEM_MMAP_OFFSET cookies not mapped yet (a map in flight)
	uint32_t otherMaps;      // maps owned by another client, by handle (old user space) or detached from a closed handle
	bool descBusy;           // its map's descriptor is held by more than the map entry and the mapping (IOKit is mapping
	                         // or unmapping it right now)
	bool refsUnaccounted;    // a reference other than its handles, bindings and the one map (a deferred free, a pending
	                         // user-fence store, a lingering map)
};

enum XeRevokeWhy : uint8_t {
	kRvOk,
	kRvNotWindow,     // not in the window (nothing to revoke)
	kRvUnmapped,      // never CPU-mapped: the ordinary eviction (boMove) takes it
	kRvPinned,
	kRvShared,
	kRvCompressed,
	kRvNotContig,
	kRvTooBig,        // above debug.intelxe.bar_revoke_max_mb (contiguous system pages are hard to get)
	kRvMoving,
	kRvClear,
	kRvBusy,          // in-flight jobs
	kRvPurgeable,
	kRvMaps,          // not exactly one live map, or maps the redirect would not reach
	kRvInFlight,      // a map being made or removed
	kRvRefs,
	kRvHot,           // touched within the hot window (not for the forced path)
	kRvWhyCount
};
static inline const char *xeRevokeWhyName(XeRevokeWhy w) {
	static const char *const n[kRvWhyCount] = {"ok", "not in window", "unmapped", "pinned", "shared", "compressed",
		"not contiguous", "too big", "moving", "clear pending", "busy", "purgeable", "maps", "map in flight", "references",
		"hot"};
	return w < kRvWhyCount ? n[w] : "?";
}

// Whether a BO may be revoked now. maxBytes: the size limit; hotNs: a BO touched less than this long ago stays (0: no
// such rule, the forced path).
static inline XeRevokeWhy xeRevokeCheck(const XeRevokeFacts &f, uint64_t maxBytes, uint64_t now, uint64_t hotNs) {
	if (!f.inWindow) return kRvNotWindow;
	if (!f.mapped && !f.liveMaps && !f.unusedMaps) return kRvUnmapped;
	if (f.pinned) return kRvPinned;
	if (f.shared) return kRvShared;
	if (f.purgeable) return kRvPurgeable;
	if (f.compressed) return kRvCompressed;
	if (!f.contig) return kRvNotContig;
	if (!f.size || f.size > maxBytes || (f.size & 0xfff)) return kRvTooBig;
	if (f.moving) return kRvMoving;
	if (f.unusedMaps || f.descBusy) return kRvInFlight;
	if (f.liveMaps != 1 || f.otherMaps) return kRvMaps;
	if (f.refsUnaccounted) return kRvRefs;
	if (f.clearPending) return kRvClear;
	if (f.vmBusy) return kRvBusy;
	if (hotNs && now >= f.touchNs && now - f.touchNs < hotNs) return kRvHot;
	if (hotNs && now < f.touchNs) return kRvHot;   // touched after `now` was read
	return kRvOk;
}

// ─── least recently touched first ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
struct XeRevokeCand {
	uint64_t size, touchNs;
	uint32_t id;
};
// Sorts c[0..n) by touch time, oldest first (ties: larger first, then id: deterministic), and returns how many from the
// front are needed to cover `need` bytes (n if all of them do not).
static inline uint32_t xeRevokePick(XeRevokeCand *c, uint32_t n, uint64_t need) {
	for (uint32_t i = 1; i < n; i++) {   // insertion sort: n is small (one scan's candidates, capped by the caller)
		const XeRevokeCand x = c[i];
		uint32_t j = i;
		for (; j > 0; j--) {
			const XeRevokeCand &p = c[j - 1];
			const bool before = x.touchNs < p.touchNs || (x.touchNs == p.touchNs &&
				(x.size > p.size || (x.size == p.size && x.id < p.id)));
			if (!before) break;
			c[j] = c[j - 1];
		}
		c[j] = x;
	}
	uint64_t got = 0;
	uint32_t k = 0;
	while (k < n && got < need) got += c[k++].size;
	return k;
}
// The cut-off of a revocation pass over several clients: the touch time of the last candidate xeRevokePick takes for
// `need`. Each client then revokes its candidates touched at or before it, oldest first, without holding two client
// locks at once. 0: nothing to take.
static inline uint64_t xeRevokeCutoff(XeRevokeCand *c, uint32_t n, uint64_t need) {
	const uint32_t k = xeRevokePick(c, n, need);
	return k ? c[k - 1].touchNs : 0;
}

// ─── one revocation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// States: where the BO's data and its two views (the CPU's mapping, the GPU's PTEs) are.
enum XeRevokeState : uint8_t {
	kRsStart,        // VRAM; nothing done (the new pages and descriptors may exist)
	kRsBlocked,      // the CPU mapping blocked (redirect(NULL)), VRAM still the BO's
	kRsCopied,       // the new pages hold a copy, the CPU still blocked
	kRsGpuMoved,     // the GPU PTEs point at the new pages, the CPU still blocked
	kRsRedirected,   // redirect(new backing) returned: the CPU is unblocked, on the new pages if it worked
	kRsDone,         // verified: the BO lives in system memory, the old VRAM may go
	kRsRolledBack,   // the BO is in VRAM as before, both views on it
	kRsBroken,       // a step reported success and the result was not there: everything kept, the feature off
	kRsUndecided,    // the check itself could not run (no memory for its mapping): the BO stays in system memory as the
	                 // redirect reported, the VRAM is kept too (never freed), the feature off
};
enum XeRevokeEvent : uint8_t {
	kReBlockOk,
	kReBlockFail,       // no live mapping found, or the redirect(NULL) failed
	kReCopyOk,
	kReCopyFail,        // the copy failed and has completed (or never ran)
	kReCopyLate,        // the copy did not complete in time: it may still write the new pages
	kReRemapOk,
	kReRemapFail,       // a page-table page could not be allocated
	kReRedirectOk,      // redirect(new backing) returned success and the map now names the new descriptor
	kReRedirectRefused, // it failed before the transpose: the map still names the old descriptor (unblocked, on VRAM)
	kReVerifyOk,
	kReVerifyFail,      // the map names the new descriptor but its object does not resolve to the new pages
	kReVerifyUnknown,   // no kernel mapping could be made to check it
};
// What the mechanism must do on a transition (bits).
enum : uint16_t {
	kRaUnblock = 1u << 0,    // redirect the blocked map to its own descriptor again (commits the blocking UPL)
	kRaGpuBack = 1u << 1,    // rewrite the GPU PTEs back to the VRAM
	kRaFreeVram = 1u << 2,   // the old VRAM goes (after the TLB invalidation)
	kRaFreeSys = 1u << 3,    // the new pages go (nothing maps them)
	kRaKeepSys = 1u << 4,    // the new pages are never freed (something may still reach them)
	kRaKeepVram = 1u << 5,   // the VRAM is held (a late copy job still reads it)
	kRaAdopt = 1u << 6,      // the BO now lives in the new pages; its map takes the new descriptor
	kRaLatchOff = 1u << 7,   // the mechanism misbehaved: no more revocations until the knob is written again
	kRaAdoptDesc = 1u << 8,  // the map takes the descriptor IOKit now has for it (the redirect re-parented the mapping)
	kRaKeepPagers = 1u << 9, // the old descriptor and the new pages' physical descriptor live as long as the BO (below)
};

// ─── who must stay alive after the redirect (barwin2, B580 14 Nov) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
// Every CPU fault on a device-pager VM object, phys_contiguous or not, asks the pager first (vm_fault_page:
// MUST_ASK_PAGER is true for a pager that is not the compressor; memory_object_data_request -> device_pager_data_request
// -> device_data_action), and device_data_action answers KERN_ABORTED - a SIGBUS in the faulting thread - once the
// descriptor that made the pager is freed (IOGeneralMemoryDescriptor::free clears reserved->dp.memory). The transpose
// moves the pagers with the objects: after it the user's object faults through the pager of the physical descriptor of
// the new pages (`phys`), and if the transpose failed, still through the old descriptor's (`old`). barwin released
// both right after the redirect: the check passed (its fault came first), then every later user fault on a revoked BO
// was a SIGBUS (barrevoke now: exit 138; the natural run passed because the BOs it revoked were other processes', which
// had not touched them yet). The descriptor whose pager the user's object may have must live as long as the mapping,
// that is as long as the BO (the map holds the BO until its mapping is gone).
enum : uint8_t {
	kRdBridge = 1u << 0,   // the bridge (when the map did not take it)
	kRdKmap = 1u << 1,     // the kernel mapping of the new pages
	kRdPhys = 1u << 2,     // the new pages' physical descriptor
	kRdOld = 1u << 3,      // the map's old descriptor (when the map took the bridge)
};
// Descriptors the mechanism may release when it is done, from the actions taken. The rest are kept with the BO (or
// still the map's).
static inline uint8_t xeRevokeReleasable(uint16_t acts) {
	uint8_t r = kRdKmap;   // the kernel mapping: nothing faults through it after the commit
	if (!(acts & kRaAdoptDesc)) r |= kRdBridge;   // the map did not take it
	if (!(acts & kRaKeepPagers)) r |= kRdPhys;
	if ((acts & kRaAdoptDesc) && !(acts & kRaKeepPagers)) r |= kRdOld;
	return r;
}
// The descriptors whose pager the user's object may fault through in final state s (after the actions acts): old only
// while no transpose can have happened, phys after a verified one, either when it is not known.
static inline uint8_t xeRevokePagerOwners(XeRevokeState s, uint16_t acts) {
	if (!(acts & kRaAdoptDesc)) return kRdOld;   // makeMapping never ran or failed before the transpose
	if (s == kRsDone) return kRdPhys;
	return kRdPhys | kRdOld;                     // Broken (transpose failed silently) or Undecided
}
struct XeRevokeStep {
	XeRevokeState next;
	uint16_t actions;
	bool valid;   // false: the event cannot happen in that state (a bug in the caller)
};
static inline XeRevokeStep xeRevokeNext(XeRevokeState s, XeRevokeEvent e) {
	switch (s) {
	case kRsStart:
		if (e == kReBlockOk) return {kRsBlocked, 0, true};
		if (e == kReBlockFail) return {kRsRolledBack, kRaFreeSys, true};
		break;
	case kRsBlocked:
		if (e == kReCopyOk) return {kRsCopied, 0, true};
		if (e == kReCopyFail) return {kRsRolledBack, kRaUnblock | kRaFreeSys, true};
		if (e == kReCopyLate) return {kRsRolledBack, kRaUnblock | kRaKeepSys | kRaKeepVram, true};
		break;
	case kRsCopied:
		if (e == kReRemapOk) return {kRsGpuMoved, 0, true};
		if (e == kReRemapFail) return {kRsRolledBack, kRaGpuBack | kRaUnblock | kRaFreeSys, true};
		break;
	case kRsGpuMoved:
		if (e == kReRedirectOk) return {kRsRedirected, 0, true};
		// unblocked by redirect() itself and still on the VRAM: the GPU goes back. The pages are kept: whatever made
		// makeMapping fail may have left a descriptor that names them, and this is the first sign the mechanism does
		// not work on this kernel
		if (e == kReRedirectRefused) return {kRsRolledBack, kRaGpuBack | kRaKeepSys | kRaLatchOff, true};
		break;
	case kRsRedirected:
		if (e == kReVerifyOk) return {kRsDone, kRaFreeVram | kRaAdopt | kRaAdoptDesc | kRaKeepPagers, true};
		// the transpose failed silently (xnu logs upl_transpose and carries on): the CPU is on the VRAM, the memory
		// references were swapped all the same, so the new pages may be named by the old descriptor: keep them
		if (e == kReVerifyFail) return {kRsBroken, kRaGpuBack | kRaKeepSys | kRaLatchOff | kRaAdoptDesc | kRaKeepPagers, true};
		// most likely it worked (the map names the new descriptor): the GPU stays with the CPU's probable view, and
		// neither memory is freed, so whichever the CPU reaches is still allocated
		if (e == kReVerifyUnknown)
			return {kRsUndecided, kRaKeepVram | kRaAdopt | kRaLatchOff | kRaAdoptDesc | kRaKeepPagers, true};
		break;
	default:
		break;
	}
	return {s, 0, false};
}
// Whether the CPU mapping is blocked in state s (every path must leave it unblocked).
static inline bool xeRevokeCpuBlocked(XeRevokeState s) { return s == kRsBlocked || s == kRsCopied || s == kRsGpuMoved; }
// Whether the GPU PTEs point at the new pages in state s.
static inline bool xeRevokeGpuOnSys(XeRevokeState s) {
	return s == kRsGpuMoved || s == kRsRedirected || s == kRsDone || s == kRsUndecided;
}
// Terminal states.
static inline bool xeRevokeFinal(XeRevokeState s) {
	return s == kRsDone || s == kRsRolledBack || s == kRsBroken || s == kRsUndecided;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// rb8f: the pure parts of asynchronous binds and of bind user fences, so that tests/bindq_test.cpp builds them on the
// host (no GPU, no IOKit):
//  - which way a VM_BIND goes (xeBindPath): Linux applies a bind's page-table update on the CPU at once only when it has
//    no unsignaled in-fence and its bind queue is idle (xe_pt.c xe_pt_vm_dependencies: "if (!job &&
//    !no_in_syncs(...)) return -ETIME; if (!job && !xe_exec_queue_is_idle(q)) return -ETIME"; xe_migrate.c
//    xe_migrate_update_pgtables: -ETIME from the CPU path means "a job is needed", __xe_migrate_update_pgtables then
//    builds a migrate job that the scheduler runs once its dependencies have signaled). Here the "job" is the bind call
//    itself, queued on its bind queue and applied (CPU page-table writes, as before) by a worker when its in-fences
//    have signaled and every earlier call of the same bind queue has been applied;
//  - the out-fence of a queued call (kXeBindSlot): one record per queued call in a ring of kXeBjMax (xeBjAlloc), whose
//    fence has signaled once the call was applied and the bind fence it then produced (clears, invalidation:
//    XeBindFence, rb8d) has signaled. A record is reused only after that, so a fence whose record holds another serial
//    is an old one that signaled;
//  - the order the worker applies queued calls in (xeBindPick): per bind queue in submission order (a drm_sched entity
//    runs its jobs in order; each bind job also depends on the queue's last fence, xe_sched_job_last_fence_add_dep),
//    calls of different bind queues in whatever order their in-fences allow (Linux orders them only where their
//    page-table updates overlap, the VM's range fences; here every apply is one critical section under the client lock);
//  - xe_vm.c check_ufence: an op that removes or splits a VMA (UNMAP, the unmapping half of a REMAP, which a MAP over
//    existing VMAs makes as well; op_lock_and_prep) answers EBUSY while the user fence of the bind that made the VMA
//    (vma_add_ufence) has not signaled; xeUfBusy;
//  - what becomes of a bind user fence still pending when its client closes (xeUfOrphanAction): Linux's
//    user_fence_worker writes it as long as the process's address space has users (mmget_not_zero), else drops it.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include "xe_tlbinval.h"

// ─── which way a VM_BIND goes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
enum XeBindPathKind : uint8_t {
	kXeBindNow,    // applied in the ioctl (no in-fence pending, the bind queue idle)
	kXeBindQueue,  // queued on its bind queue, applied when its in-fences have signaled
	kXeBindWait,   // the pre-rb8f way: the ioctl waits for the in-fences (and the queue's earlier calls), then applies
};
// asyncOn: debug.intelxe.bind_async. inPending: an in-fence has not signaled. queuePending: calls of this bind queue are
// queued and not applied yet. room: a record and the memory for a queued call are there. A call behind queued calls of
// its queue is queued as well whatever the switch says (it may have been turned off while some were queued), so that
// the queue's order holds; without room it waits in the ioctl.
static inline XeBindPathKind xeBindPath(bool asyncOn, bool inPending, uint32_t queuePending, bool room) {
	if (!inPending && !queuePending) return kXeBindNow;
	if (room && (asyncOn || queuePending)) return kXeBindQueue;
	return kXeBindWait;
}

// ─── out-fence records of queued calls ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// XeFence {0, kXeBindSlot, tl, serial}: tl names the bind queue (its own id, never 0), so two fences of one queue
// compare like the seqnos of one exec queue (fenceMerge, surfAdd keep the later one: a later call's bind fence folds in
// the earlier calls', xeBindFenceNext), and fences of two queues are kept apart.
static constexpr uint32_t kXeBjMax = 1024;   // queued calls at most (a power of two: serial % kXeBjMax survives the wrap)
struct XeBjRec {
	volatile uint32_t serial;    // the call that owns it, 0 never used
	volatile uint8_t applied;    // its ops are in the page tables (or it was dropped): res is valid
	XeBindFence res;             // the bind fence the apply produced (the queue's last fence after it)
};
static inline XeFence xeBindJobFence(uint32_t tl, uint32_t serial) { return XeFence{0, kXeBindSlot, tl, serial}; }
template <typename Sig>
static inline bool xeBjSignaled(const XeBjRec *tab, const XeFence &f, Sig sig) {
	const XeBjRec &r = tab[f.seqno % kXeBjMax];
	if (r.serial != f.seqno) return true;   // reused: only after the call it held had signaled
	if (!__atomic_load_n(&r.applied, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) return false;
	return sig(r.res.clear) && sig(r.res.tlb);
}
template <typename Sig>
static inline bool xeBjFree(const XeBjRec &r, Sig sig) {
	return !r.serial || (__atomic_load_n(&r.applied, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE) && sig(r.res.clear) && sig(r.res.tlb));
}
// A record for a new queued call: its serial, or 0 when the ring is full (the record kXeBjMax calls back has not
// signaled yet). *next: the serial counter (0 is skipped).
template <typename Sig>
static inline uint32_t xeBjAlloc(XeBjRec *tab, uint32_t *next, Sig sig) {
	uint32_t s = *next ? *next : 1;
	XeBjRec &r = tab[s % kXeBjMax];
	if (!xeBjFree(r, sig)) return 0;
	__atomic_store_n(&r.applied, 0, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
	__atomic_store_n(&r.serial, s, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
	*next = s + 1;
	return s;
}
// The call was applied (or dropped): its bind fence, then the flag readers test first.
static inline void xeBjPublish(XeBjRec *tab, uint32_t serial, const XeBindFence &res) {
	XeBjRec &r = tab[serial % kXeBjMax];
	r.res = res;
	__atomic_store_n(&r.applied, 1, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);
}

// ─── the order queued calls are applied in ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The first call, in submission order, that is the oldest of its bind queue and whose in-fences have all signaled.
// N: a list node with `next`; key(n): its bind queue; ready(n): its in-fences have signaled. nullptr: none.
template <typename N, typename Key, typename Ready>
static inline N *xeBindPick(N *head, Key key, Ready ready) {
	for (N *j = head; j; j = j->next) {
		bool oldest = true;
		for (N *k = head; k != j && oldest; k = k->next) oldest = key(k) != key(j);
		if (oldest && ready(j)) return j;
	}
	return nullptr;
}

// Calls of two bind queues of one VM whose ranges overlap are applied in the order they were made: Linux's CPU path
// returns -ETIME while an overlapping update of the VM is pending (xe_pt_vm_dependencies: the VM's range-fence tree,
// rftree, "GPU is busy updating"), and the job it makes instead depends on that update's fence. A queued call is
// therefore an in-fence of a later call of another queue that overlaps it (xeBindSpanOverlap); an UNMAP_ALL (a BO's
// VMAs, wherever they are) and a call's span are compared as the whole address space.
struct XeBindSpan { uint64_t lo, hi; };   // [lo, hi), hi 0: empty
static inline XeBindSpan xeBindOpSpan(bool unmapAll, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	if (unmapAll) return XeBindSpan{0, ~0ull};
	return XeBindSpan{addr, range ? addr + range : addr};
}
static inline bool xeBindSpanOverlap(const XeBindSpan &a, const XeBindSpan &b) {
	return a.hi > a.lo && b.hi > b.lo && a.lo < b.hi && b.lo < a.hi;
}

// ─── user fences of VMAs (xe_vm.c check_ufence) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// [a, a + alen) and [b, b + blen) share a byte.
static inline bool xeRangeOverlap(uint64_t a, uint64_t alen, uint64_t b, uint64_t blen) {
	return alen && blen && a < b + blen && b < a + alen;
}
// An op over [addr, addr + range) meets a VMA over [vaddr, vaddr + vrange) whose user fence is pending (ufPending):
// the call answers EBUSY. removes: the op removes or splits what it overlaps (MAP, MAP_USERPTR, UNMAP, UNMAP_ALL;
// PREFETCH does not). byHandle: an UNMAP_ALL, which meets the VMAs of its object (sameObject) whatever their range.
static inline bool xeUfBusy(bool removes, bool byHandle, bool sameObject, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range, uint64_t vaddr,
	uint64_t vrange, bool ufPending) {
	if (!ufPending || !removes) return false;
	return byHandle ? sameObject : xeRangeOverlap(addr, range, vaddr, vrange);
}

// ─── a bind user fence whose client closed ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// xe_sync.c user_fence_worker: mmget_not_zero(ufence->mm) ? copy_to_user : "ufence wasn't signaled". The mm reference
// (mmgrab at parse) keeps the address space struct, and the write happens while the process still has it. Here the
// page stays wired and mapped into the kernel (or the BO it lies in stays held) until the write; it is written once the
// bind fence has signaled if the process still exists, dropped as soon as the process is gone, and dropped after
// limitNs pending so that a fence that never signals cannot keep a page wired for good.
enum XeUfOrphanKind : uint8_t { kXeUfKeep, kXeUfWrite, kXeUfDropGone, kXeUfDropLate };
static inline XeUfOrphanKind xeUfOrphanAction(bool ready, bool procAlive, uint64_t now, uint64_t orphanNs, uint64_t limitNs) {
	if (!procAlive) return kXeUfDropGone;
	if (ready) return kXeUfWrite;
	return now - orphanNs >= limitNs ? kXeUfDropLate : kXeUfKeep;
}
// The bound: a started job's limit (DRM_XE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX, 10 s) plus the TLB fence timeout (xeTlbTimeoutNs, 2.25 s
// with the 4 KB H2G ring), rounded up: every bind fence has signaled or been forced by then.
static constexpr uint64_t kXeUfOrphanNs = 15000000000ull;

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_direct.h
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// rb8e: the pure part of direct submission's user fences (xe_core.cpp "direct submission"), so that tests/direct_test.cpp
// builds it on the host.
//
// The armed ring slot (dsSlot) is written when the queue arms, before the job that will run in it is known; what it
// runs comes from memory written at submit time (dsSubmit) before the mailbox releases the slot: the job's stub (jobPre
// and the jump to its batch) and, after the batch and the cache flush, its post-stub, which the slot calls with a
// first-level MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START (GGTT) where the normal ring path stores the user fence (jobPost). The post-stub is
// the job's user fence or nothing, as xe_ring_ops.c emits it: render and compute store it right after the flush
// (__emit_job_gen12_render_compute), copy and video after a plain MI_FLUSH_DW (__emit_job_gen12_simple / _video:
// emit_flush_dw), both with emit_store_imm_ppgtt_posted (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM | MI_SDI_NUM_QW(1), the qword at a PPGTT
// address); then MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END back to the slot, which stores the seqno and raises the interrupt, so a waiter
// woken by it reads the value. WAS: a job with a user fence made the armed queue leave direct submission (queueExec),
// since the slot had no store for it.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

static constexpr uint32_t kXeDsPostBytes = 64;   // one post-stub (at most 11 dwords used)

// The post-stub of a job into dw (kXeDsPostBytes / 4 dwords at most); returns the dword count. rc: render or compute.
static inline uint32_t xeDsPostStub(uint32_t *dw, bool rc, bool hasUf, uint64_t addr, uint64_t value) {
	uint32_t n = 0;
	if (hasUf) {
		if (!rc) {   // emit_flush_dw: MI_FLUSH_DW | MI_FLUSH_IMM_DW, no post-sync
			dw[n++] = 0x26u << 23 | 2;
			dw[n++] = 0;
			dw[n++] = 0;
			dw[n++] = 0;
		}
		dw[n++] = 0x20u << 23 | 1u << 21 | (2 * 1 + 3 - 2);   // MI_STORE_DATA_IMM | MI_SDI_NUM_QW(1), PPGTT
		dw[n++] = (uint32_t)addr;
		dw[n++] = (uint32_t)(addr >> 32);
		dw[n++] = (uint32_t)value;
		dw[n++] = (uint32_t)(value >> 32);
	}
	dw[n++] = 0xau << 23;   // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END
	return n;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// engact: per-engine busy time from the GuC's engine activity statistics, for Level Zero sysman's zesEngineGetActivity
// (debug.intelxe.sensors_raw version 2, uapi/intelxe_sensors.h). The pure parts, so that tests/engact_test.cpp builds
// them on the host; the buffers, the H2G and the register reads are in xe_core.cpp (engActEnable, xeEngActSample).
//
// Linux (v7.4-rc3 drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_guc_engine_activity.c, read 13 Nov 2026; the PMU events engine-active-ticks and
// engine-total-ticks of xe_pmu.c): when the GuC's submission interface is 1.14.1 or newer (BMG's 70.72.1 firmware has
// 1.38.1), xe_guc_engine_activity_enable_stats sends XE_GUC_ACTION_SET_DEVICE_ENGINE_ACTIVITY_BUFFER (0x550C) with the
// GGTT addresses of a metadata page (struct guc_engine_activity_metadata) and an activity buffer (struct
// guc_engine_activity_data: one 16-byte struct guc_engine_activity per [GuC class][logical instance], 16 x 32), after
// pc_start and rc_enable on every GuC load. The GuC then keeps, per engine, the ticks it was active and the tick it went
// active at (0 when idle), with a change number per record and a global one in the metadata. Reading:
//  - active ticks (get_engine_active_ticks): when the global change number moved and the engine's own did, the active
//    ticks since the last read are added to a running total; while the engine runs, the time since it went active
//    (the GPM timestamp, MISC_STATUS_0 >> (3 - RPM_CONFIG0 CTC shift), low 32 bits, minus last_update_tick) is added on top;
//  - total ticks (get_engine_total_ticks): the CPU time since the statistics were enabled, scaled by the engine's
//    quanta_ratio / 0x8000 (its share under SR-IOV; the whole in native mode), in GuC timestamp ticks
//    (guc_tsc_frequency_hz from the metadata).
// The same arithmetic here, with two differences, both because the kext reloads the GuC at every GT reset and wake and
// clears the buffers before it hands them over again: at each enable the records' snapshot is re-based to zero (Linux
// keeps it, and a GuC whose counters restarted would make active go backwards by the old count) while the running
// totals stay, so both counters only grow; and a GPM timestamp that reads 0 or all ones (a GT that went down between
// the record and the register) does not move the running engine's part.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaClasses = 16;        // GUC_MAX_ENGINE_CLASSES
static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaInstances = 32;      // GUC_MAX_INSTANCES_PER_CLASS
static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaTotalQuanta = 0x8000;   // TOTAL_QUANTA
static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaActionSetDeviceBuffer = 0x550C;   // XE_GUC_ACTION_SET_DEVICE_ENGINE_ACTIVITY_BUFFER
static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaRequiredSubmitVer = 1u << 16 | 14u << 8 | 1u;   // 1.14.1, as sw_version (major 23:16)
static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaMetaOff = 0, kXeEaDataOff = 0x1000;   // in the kext's one 12 KB buffer per GuC
static constexpr uint32_t kXeEaBytes = 0x3000;

// xe_guc_fwif.h struct guc_engine_activity (packed)
struct XeEaRecord {
	uint16_t changeNum;
	uint16_t quantaRatio;
	uint32_t lastUpdateTick;
	uint64_t activeTicks;
} __attribute__((packed));
static_assert(sizeof(XeEaRecord) == 16, "guc_engine_activity");
// struct guc_engine_activity_metadata
struct XeEaMeta {
	uint32_t gucTscHz;
	uint32_t lagLatencyUs;
	uint32_t globalChangeNum;
	uint32_t reserved;
} __attribute__((packed));
static_assert(sizeof(XeEaMeta) == 16, "guc_engine_activity_metadata");
static_assert(kXeEaDataOff + kXeEaClasses * kXeEaInstances * sizeof(XeEaRecord) <= kXeEaBytes, "activity data fits");

// The record's offset in the activity data: engine_activity[guc_class][guc_logical_instance].
static inline uint32_t xeEaRecordOffset(uint32_t gucClass, uint32_t logical) {
	return (gucClass * kXeEaInstances + logical) * (uint32_t)sizeof(XeEaRecord);
}

// The engine activity statistics exist from GuC submission interface 1.14.1 (is_engine_activity_supported).
static inline bool xeEaSupported(uint32_t submissionVersion) {
	return (submissionVersion & 0xffffff) >= kXeEaRequiredSubmitVer;
}

// 3 - RPM_CONFIG0's CTC shift parameter (bits 2:1): how far MISC_STATUS_0 is shifted to get GPM ticks.
static inline uint32_t xeEaGpmShift(uint32_t rpmConfig0) { return 3 - ((rpmConfig0 >> 1) & 3); }

// MISC_STATUS_0 as xe_mmio_read64_2x32 reads it, shifted: the low 32 bits are what is compared with last_update_tick.
// 0 or all ones (no answer) is not a timestamp.
static inline bool xeEaGpmLow(uint32_t lo, uint32_t hi, uint32_t shift, uint32_t *out) {
	if ((lo == 0 && hi == 0) || (lo == 0xffffffffu && hi == 0xffffffffu)) return false;
	*out = (uint32_t)((((uint64_t)hi << 32) | lo) >> shift);
	return true;
}

// Linux struct engine_activity, one per engine
struct XeEaEngine {
	uint64_t active;          // the running part (ticks since the engine went active), 0 when idle
	uint64_t lastCpuNs;       // CPU time of the previous total-ticks read
	uint64_t quanta, quantaNs, quantaRemNs;
	uint64_t total;           // active ticks summed from the records
	bool running;
	uint32_t globalChange;    // cached metadata.global_change_num
	uint32_t tscHz;           // cached metadata.guc_tsc_frequency_hz (re-read while 0)
	XeEaRecord cached;        // the record as last taken
};

// engine_activity_set_cpu_ts at an enable, and the re-base described above (the totals stay).
static inline void xeEaEnable(XeEaEngine &e, uint64_t nowNs) {
	e.lastCpuNs = nowNs;
	e.running = false;
	e.active = 0;
	e.globalChange = 0;
	e.cached = XeEaRecord{};
}

// get_engine_active_ticks, first half: take the record if it changed. Returns whether the engine runs (the caller then
// reads the GPM timestamp and calls xeEaActiveRunning).
static inline bool xeEaActiveUpdate(XeEaEngine &e, uint32_t globalChange, const XeEaRecord &rec) {
	if (globalChange && globalChange != e.globalChange) {
		e.globalChange = globalChange;
		if (rec.changeNum && rec.changeNum != e.cached.changeNum) {
			e.running = rec.lastUpdateTick != 0;
			e.total += rec.activeTicks - e.cached.activeTicks;
			e.active = 0;
			e.cached.changeNum = rec.changeNum;
			e.cached.lastUpdateTick = rec.lastUpdateTick;
			e.cached.activeTicks = rec.activeTicks;
		}
	}
	return e.running;
}

// Second half: the running part from the GPM timestamp (gpmOk false: no timestamp, the part stays as it was).
static inline void xeEaActiveRunning(XeEaEngine &e, bool gpmOk, uint32_t gpmLow) {
	if (e.running && gpmOk) e.active = (uint32_t)(gpmLow - e.cached.lastUpdateTick);
}

static inline uint64_t xeEaActiveTicks(const XeEaEngine &e) { return e.total + e.active; }

// mul_u64_u32_div(a, b, c) without a 128-bit division: a = q c + r, so a b / c = q b + r b / c (r b < 2^64 for c <= 2^32).
static inline uint64_t xeEaMulDiv(uint64_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t c) {
	return (a / c) * b + (a % c) * b / c;
}

// get_engine_total_ticks: the CPU time since the last read, scaled by the quanta ratio, in GuC ticks. quantaRatio is the
// record's (read every time; the cached one when the GuC is down), tscHz the metadata's.
static inline uint64_t xeEaTotalTicks(XeEaEngine &e, uint16_t quantaRatio, uint32_t tscHz, uint64_t nowNs) {
	if (!e.tscHz) e.tscHz = tscHz;
	e.cached.quantaRatio = quantaRatio;
	const uint64_t delta = nowNs > e.lastCpuNs ? nowNs - e.lastCpuNs : 0;
	e.lastCpuNs = nowNs;
	const uint64_t numerator = (e.quantaRemNs + delta) * e.cached.quantaRatio;
	e.quantaNs += numerator / kXeEaTotalQuanta;
	e.quantaRemNs = numerator % kXeEaTotalQuanta;
	e.quanta = xeEaMulDiv(e.quantaNs, e.tscHz, 1000000000u);
	return e.quanta;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_fd.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// rb7t: the clone device behind object file descriptors (fd sharing stages 1-2; docs/reports/b580-fd-sharing-20261103.md
// §5 "A", b580-fd-sharing-stage0-20261104.md §5). Linux makes a file for a syncobj (anon_inode "syncobj_file"), a
// sync_file and a dma-buf and installs it in the caller's fd table; a kext cannot (falloc/fdalloc are not KPI). Here the
// caller (xemac) opens INTELXE_OBJ_DEVICE itself and passes that fd IN the export ioctl, and the kext binds the object to the
// open's minor:
//  - /dev/intelxeobj is a devfs clone node (devfs_make_node_clone, 0666 as a render node): every lookup takes a new minor
//    from a 24-bit counter that skips the minors open now. stat() makes a lookup too, so nothing is recorded for a minor
//    until d_open; a minor that is open already (a second open through a mknod alias) answers EBUSY.
//  - one record per open minor {kind, object, pid}; d_close is that minor's last close (dup, fork, SCM_RIGHTS and XPC
//    carry the same open file, so it comes when the last holder anywhere has closed it, or exited) and releases the
//    object, as drm_syncobj_file_release / dma_buf_release / sync_file_release do.
//  - an fd is resolved in the CALLER's fd table (file_vnode_withvid, com.apple.kpi.bsd: the IOUserClient's
//    externalMethod runs on the calling thread), so a number names nothing in another process: the fd itself is the
//    capability. While that holds the fileproc, the minor cannot reach its last close (close() waits for the I/O count),
//    so the record is stable for the duration; the record table itself is gFdLock's. (file_vnode, which the design
//    named, is in com.apple.kpi.private only, which a third-party kext may not link.)
//  - nothing is offered on the object fd itself: read/write/mmap ENODEV, ioctl ENOTTY (SYNC_IOC_FILE_INFO,
//    DMA_BUF_IOCTL_*_SYNC_FILE: WSI takes ENOTTY as "no implicit sync"), poll/select is stage 4 (kqueue needs
//    cdevsw_setkqueueok, not in the SDK's headers). DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_OBJ_INFO on the device answers what an fd holds.
// The device exists only once debug.intelxe.fds was set to 1 (or boot-arg intelxe_fds=1): until then nothing of this is visible.
// Unload: refused (IntelXe::terminate, IntelXe_stop) while a minor is open, as NMDRM refuses with descriptors open.
// Locks: gFdLock is a leaf (taken under client locks and gClientsLock; only atomic reference increments and allocation
// inside); gFdEnLock serialises the one-time registration (devfs calls back into objClone under its own lock, which then
// takes gFdLock: gFdLock is never held while calling devfs).
#include "IntelXe.h"
#include "xe_fd.h"
#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>
#include <libkern/OSAtomic.h>
#include <sys/conf.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include <sys/file.h>
#include <sys/proc.h>
#include <sys/vnode.h>
#include <miscfs/devfs/devfs.h>

int gFds = 0;
int gFdsBoot = 0;
static IOLock *gFdLock, *gFdEnLock;
static int gMajor = -1;
static void *gNode;
static volatile UInt32 gNextMinor;

struct FdRec {
	FdRec *next;
	uint32_t minor, kind;
	void *obj;
	int pid;
};
static constexpr uint32_t kBuckets = 256;
static FdRec *gRecs[kBuckets];
// debug.intelxe.fd_stats (gFdLock): minors open now (in total and by kind), and since load: opens, opens refused (fds 0 /
// minor open already), last closes, binds and imports by kind, resolutions refused
static struct {
	uint32_t open, byKind[4], opens, offOpens, busyOpens, closes, binds[4], takes[4], badFd, notOurs, bound;
} gFdSt;

// dev_t is an int: major bits 31:24, minor 23:0 (sys/types.h makedev), without the macros' sign conversions
static uint32_t devMinor(dev_t d) { return (uint32_t)d & 0xffffffu; }
static int devMajor(dev_t d) { return (int)((uint32_t)d >> 24); }

static FdRec **slot(uint32_t minor) {
	FdRec **pp = &gRecs[minor % kBuckets];
	while (*pp && (*pp)->minor != minor) pp = &(*pp)->next;
	return pp;
}

// DEVFS_CLONE_ALLOC: a minor for a new vnode (an open or a stat). DEVFS_CLONE_FREE is not relied on (ptmx_clone ignores
// it too): nothing is kept per allocation, and a minor is only skipped while a record holds it.
static int objClone(dev_t, int action) {
	if (action != DEVFS_CLONE_ALLOC) return -1;
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	uint32_t m = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 0x1000000u; i++) {
		m = (uint32_t)OSIncrementAtomic(reinterpret_cast<volatile SInt32 *>(&gNextMinor)) & 0xffffffu;
		if (m && !*slot(m)) break;
		m = 0;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	return m ? (int)m : -1;
}

static int objOpen(dev_t dev, int, int, proc_t p) {
	auto *r = static_cast<FdRec *>(IOMallocZero(sizeof(FdRec)));
	if (!r) return ENOMEM;
	r->minor = devMinor(dev);
	r->pid = p ? proc_pid(p) : 0;
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	int err = 0;
	if (!gFds) err = ENODEV, gFdSt.offOpens++;              // switched off: nothing new (bound minors stay valid)
	else if (*slot(r->minor)) err = EBUSY, gFdSt.busyOpens++;   // open already (a second node for the same minor)
	else {
		r->next = gRecs[r->minor % kBuckets];
		gRecs[r->minor % kBuckets] = r;
		gFdSt.open++;
		gFdSt.byKind[kFdNone]++;
		gFdSt.opens++;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	if (err) IOFree(r, sizeof(*r));
	return err;
}

static int objClose(dev_t dev, int, int, proc_t) {
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	FdRec **pp = slot(devMinor(dev)), *r = *pp;
	if (r) {
		*pp = r->next;
		gFdSt.open--;
		gFdSt.byKind[r->kind & 3]--;
		gFdSt.closes++;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	if (!r) return 0;
	if (r->obj) xeFdObjRelease(r->kind, r->obj);
	IOFree(r, sizeof(*r));
	return 0;
}

static int objIoctl(dev_t, u_long, caddr_t, int, proc_t) { return ENOTTY; }
// what eno_rdwrt / eno_stop / eno_reset / eno_select are (enodev), typed: read, write ENODEV; select answers nonzero
// (ENODEV), which spec_select reports as ready, as for any device without select; poll() gets POLLNVAL (no kqueue)
static int objRw(dev_t, struct uio *, int) { return ENODEV; }
static int objStop(struct tty *, int) { return ENODEV; }
static int objReset(int) { return ENODEV; }
static int objSelect(dev_t, int, void *, proc_t) { return ENODEV; }

static struct cdevsw gSw = {objOpen, objClose, objRw, objRw, objIoctl, objStop, objReset, nullptr, objSelect, eno_mmap,
	eno_strat, eno_getc, eno_putc, 0};

bool xeFdInit() {
	gFdLock = IOLockAlloc();
	gFdEnLock = IOLockAlloc();
	return gFdLock && gFdEnLock;
}

int xeFdEnable() {
	if (!gFdEnLock) return ENXIO;
	IOLockLock(gFdEnLock);
	int err = 0;
	if (gMajor < 0) {
		const int maj = cdevsw_add(-1, &gSw);
		if (maj < 0) err = EBUSY;
		else if (!(gNode = devfs_make_node_clone((dev_t)((uint32_t)maj << 24), DEVFS_CHAR, UID_ROOT, GID_WHEEL, 0666, objClone, "intelxeobj"))) {
			cdevsw_remove(maj, &gSw);
			err = ENOMEM;
		} else {
			gMajor = maj;
		}
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gFdEnLock);
	return err;
}

uint32_t xeFdOpenCount() {
	if (!gFdLock) return 0;
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	const uint32_t n = gFdSt.open;
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	return n;
}

bool xeFdFini() {
	if (xeFdOpenCount()) return false;
	if (gFdEnLock) IOLockLock(gFdEnLock);
	if (gMajor >= 0) {
		devfs_remove(gNode);
		cdevsw_remove(gMajor, &gSw);
		gNode = nullptr;
		gMajor = -1;
	}
	if (gFdEnLock) IOLockUnlock(gFdEnLock);
	if (gFdLock) IOLockFree(gFdLock);
	if (gFdEnLock) IOLockFree(gFdEnLock);
	gFdLock = gFdEnLock = nullptr;
	return true;
}

// The record behind the caller's fd: 0 with gFdLock held (the caller unlocks, then file_drop(fd)), or EBADF (not an
// open fd: fp_lookup) / EINVAL (a socket, pipe or kqueue: not a vnode; another file; one of ours never opened). On an
// error nothing is held.
static int fdRecord(int fd, FdRec **out) {
	vnode_t vp = nullptr;
	if (gMajor < 0) return fd < 0 ? EBADF : EINVAL;   // (not reached: the ioctls need fds on, which made the device)
	uint32_t vid = 0;   // file_vnode_withvid: com.apple.kpi.bsd (file_vnode itself is only in com.apple.kpi.private)
	int err = file_vnode_withvid(fd, &vp, &vid);
	if (err) {
		IOLockLock(gFdLock);
		if (err == EBADF) gFdSt.badFd++;
		else gFdSt.notOurs++;
		IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
		return err == EBADF ? EBADF : EINVAL;
	}
	const dev_t rdev = vp && vnode_ischr(vp) ? vnode_specrdev(vp) : NODEV;
	const bool ours = rdev != NODEV && devMajor(rdev) == gMajor;
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	FdRec *r = ours ? *slot(devMinor(rdev)) : nullptr;
	if (!r) {
		gFdSt.notOurs++;
		IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
		file_drop(fd);
		return EINVAL;
	}
	*out = r;
	return 0;
}

int xeFdBind(int fd, uint32_t kind, void *obj) {
	FdRec *r;
	int err = fdRecord(fd, &r);
	if (err) return err;
	if (r->kind != kFdNone) {
		err = EBUSY;   // bound already: xemac opens a new minor for every export
	} else {
		r->kind = kind;
		r->obj = obj;
		gFdSt.byKind[kFdNone]--;
		gFdSt.byKind[kind & 3]++;
		gFdSt.binds[kind & 3]++;
	}
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	file_drop(fd);
	return err;
}

int xeFdTake(int fd, uint32_t *kind, void **obj) {
	FdRec *r;
	int err = fdRecord(fd, &r);
	if (err) return err;
	*kind = r->kind;
	*obj = r->obj;
	if (r->obj) xeFdObjGet(r->kind, r->obj);
	gFdSt.takes[r->kind & 3]++;
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	file_drop(fd);
	return 0;
}

void xeFdForEach(uint32_t kind, void (*fn)(void *obj, void *ctx), void *ctx) {
	if (!gFdLock) return;
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	for (uint32_t b = 0; b < kBuckets; b++)
		for (FdRec *r = gRecs[b]; r; r = r->next)
			if (r->kind == kind && r->obj) fn(r->obj, ctx);
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
}

int xeFdStatsString(char *out, size_t len) {
	if (!gFdLock) return snprintf(out, len, "object fds: not initialised\n");
	IOLockLock(gFdLock);
	const auto s = gFdSt;
	IOLockUnlock(gFdLock);
	return snprintf(out, len,
		"fds %d, device /dev/intelxeobj %s (major %d)\n"
		"minors open %u: unbound %u, BO %u, syncobj %u, sync file %u\n"
		"opens %u (refused: fds off %u, minor open already %u), last closes %u\n"
		"binds: BO %u, syncobj %u, sync file %u; lookups: none %u, BO %u, syncobj %u, sync file %u; refused: not an open fd "
		"%u, not an object fd %u\n",
		gFds, gMajor >= 0 ? "present" : "absent", gMajor, s.open, s.byKind[0], s.byKind[1], s.byKind[2], s.byKind[3], s.opens,
		s.offOpens, s.busyOpens, s.closes, s.binds[1], s.binds[2], s.binds[3], s.takes[0], s.takes[1], s.takes[2],
		s.takes[3], s.badFd, s.notOurs);
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_fd.h

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// rb7t: object file descriptors (fd sharing stages 1-2, uapi/intelxe_drm.h INTELXE_OBJ_DEVICE): the clone device /dev/intelxeobj,
// one record per open minor, and the resolution of a caller's fd to its record. What the records hold (BOs, syncobjs,
// sync files) and the ioctls are xe_core.cpp's; this file only keeps a typed pointer per minor and hands references
// out through the callbacks xeFdObj* (xe_core.cpp).
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

enum : uint32_t { kFdNone = 0, kFdBo = 1, kFdSyncobj = 2, kFdSyncFile = 3 };   // = INTELXE_OBJ_KIND_*

extern int gFds;   // debug.intelxe.fds: 1 = object fds offered (INTELXE_CAP_FD_OBJECTS, DRM_CAP_PRIME, the four ioctls)
extern int gFdsBoot;   // boot-arg intelxe_fds=1: switch gFds on with the first client (devfs is up by then)

bool xeFdInit();                 // module start: the lock only (the device appears with xeFdEnable)
bool xeFdFini();                 // module stop: false (refuse) while a minor is open; else the node and cdevsw go
int xeFdEnable();                // the clone device, made once (debug.intelxe.fds 1, boot-arg intelxe_fds=1)
uint32_t xeFdOpenCount();        // minors open now (IntelXe::terminate refuses while there are any)
// Bind obj (a reference the record takes over on success) to the unbound minor behind the caller's fd: EBADF (not an
// open fd), EINVAL (not an open of INTELXE_OBJ_DEVICE), EBUSY (bound already).
int xeFdBind(int fd, uint32_t kind, void *obj);
// The object behind the caller's fd, with a new reference (xeFdObjGet) the caller drops with xeFdObjPut: EBADF / EINVAL
// as above; an unbound minor gives kFdNone and nullptr.
int xeFdTake(int fd, uint32_t *kind, void **obj);
// fn on every bound record of a kind, under the record lock (fn takes no lock but leaves and may allocate).
void xeFdForEach(uint32_t kind, void (*fn)(void *obj, void *ctx), void *ctx);
int xeFdStatsString(char *out, size_t len);   // debug.intelxe.fd_stats

// xe_core.cpp: a new reference to obj (called under the record lock: atomic increments only), its drop, and the
// release of the record's own reference after the minor's last close (no lock held).
void xeFdObjGet(uint32_t kind, void *obj);
void xeFdObjPut(uint32_t kind, void *obj);
void xeFdObjRelease(uint32_t kind, void *obj);

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Long-running (LR) VMs, DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE without FAULT_MODE (docs/design/DESIGN-lr-mode.md): the pure
// part, so that tests/lr_test.cpp builds it on the host. The rest is in xe_core.cpp ("long-running VMs").
//
// Linux (drivers/gpu/drm/xe, dl/linux-xe): xe_vm_in_preempt_fence_mode(vm) = LR and not fault mode. Such a VM's exec
// queues have no job timeout (xe_guc_submit.c guc_exec_queue_init: MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT for q->vm in LR mode), its
// execs take only user fences as out-syncs (xe_exec.c xe_exec_ioctl -> xe_sync.c xe_sync_entry_parse with
// SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_LR_MODE: a syncobj signal is EOPNOTSUPP; VM_BIND passes the same flag, xe_vm.c xe_vm_bind_ioctl), and
// its memory is protected by preempt fences instead of job fences: every exec queue of the VM has one in the dma-resv
// of the VM and of its external BOs (xe_vm.c xe_vm_add_compute_exec_queue, BOOKKEEP), so whatever waits for the BOs to
// be idle (a move, an eviction, a free) enables the fence, which suspends the queue (xe_preempt_fence.c
// preempt_fence_enable_signaling -> q->ops->suspend: xe_guc_submit.c __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_suspend, a GuC
// schedule disable after the queue ran min_run_period_lr_ms since its last resume, xe_device.c: 5 ms) and signals once
// the GuC confirms (guc_exec_queue_suspend_wait, 5 s, then guc_exec_queue_suspend_timeout_ban). The rebind worker then
// rebinds what moved, waits for those rebinds, and resumes the queues (xe_vm.c preempt_rebind_work_func ->
// resume_and_reinstall_preempt_fences -> q->ops->resume: __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_resume, a schedule enable).
// Here a move holds the VM's queues off itself (it rewrites the PTEs on the CPU, so "rebind" is the move's own remap
// plus its TLB invalidation, waited for before the resume), and a deferred free of an LR VM waits for one preemption
// cycle of the VM's queues instead of their jobs (which may never end).
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

// xe_device.c: xe->min_run_period_lr_ms = 5 (vm->preempt.min_run_period_ms of an LR VM without fault mode)
static constexpr uint64_t kXeLrMinRunNs = 5000000ull;
// guc_exec_queue_wait_suspend_done: HZ * 5
static constexpr uint64_t kXeLrConfirmNs = 5000000000ull;

// What one exec queue of an LR VM being preempted needs next.
//   counts:     the queue's context may still run (not banned; a closed queue or one the TDR path is taking off still
//               counts until its own disable is confirmed or its ring is idle)
//   foreign:    closed or being taken off (queueKickOff): its teardown or the watchdog sends the disable, not this
//   stuck:      this preemption's disable was not confirmed in time and the queue was banned: it counts until the GT
//               reset that request brought has stopped the engines (or the disable is confirmed after all)
//   sent:       this preemption sent its schedule disable (sentNs: when)
//   offByOther: a schedule disable sent by someone else (teardown, the TDR path) is in flight or done
//   confirmed:  SCHED_CONTEXT_MODE_DONE (disable) arrived for the queue
//   ringIdle:   every job written to its ring has completed (the hold keeps new ones out of the ring)
//   gucDown:    the queue's GuC cannot take H2G now (GT reset in progress, system sleep)
//   onNs:       when the preemption last resumed it (0: never preempted)
enum XeLrStep : uint8_t {
	kXeLrIsOff,            // nothing of it can run: preempted (confirmed), idle, or not counted
	kXeLrWaitConfirm,      // the disable is out, its confirmation is not in yet
	kXeLrWaitMinRun,       // resumed less than kXeLrMinRunNs ago: the disable waits (xe: xe_sleep_relaxed_ms(wait_ms))
	kXeLrWaitGuc,          // the GuC is not reachable now; tried again later
	kXeLrSendDisable,      // send the schedule disable now
	kXeLrConfirmTimeout,   // not confirmed within kXeLrConfirmNs: ban (guc_exec_queue_suspend_timeout_ban), GT reset
};
struct XeLrQueueState {
	bool counts, foreign, stuck, sent, offByOther, confirmed, ringIdle, gucDown;
	uint64_t sentNs, onNs;
};
static inline XeLrStep xeLrQueueStep(const XeLrQueueState &s, uint64_t now, uint64_t minRunNs = kXeLrMinRunNs,
	uint64_t confirmNs = kXeLrConfirmNs) {
	if (s.stuck) return s.confirmed ? kXeLrIsOff : kXeLrWaitConfirm;   // banned, the engines not stopped yet
	if (!s.counts) return kXeLrIsOff;
	if (s.sent || s.offByOther) {
		if (s.confirmed) return kXeLrIsOff;
		return s.sent && now - s.sentNs > confirmNs ? kXeLrConfirmTimeout : kXeLrWaitConfirm;
	}
	// __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_suspend only disables an enabled context; one with nothing in its ring and nothing
	// allowed into it (the hold) touches no memory, so it needs no round trip to the GuC
	if (s.ringIdle) return kXeLrIsOff;
	if (s.foreign) return kXeLrWaitConfirm;   // its own disable is on the way (teardown, queueKickOff)
	if (s.gucDown) return kXeLrWaitGuc;
	if (s.onNs && now - s.onNs < minRunNs) return kXeLrWaitMinRun;
	return kXeLrSendDisable;
}

// A deferred free sealed when the VM had asked for cycle `to` may go once the VM completed cycle `done` (wrapping
// counters: xe's preempt fences of one exec queue share a dma_fence context whose seqnos only grow, q->lr.seqno).
static inline bool xeLrCycleCovers(uint32_t done, uint32_t to) { return (int32_t)(done - to) >= 0; }

// The resume of a preempted queue (resume_and_reinstall_preempt_fences -> __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_resume): a
// schedule enable only for a queue whose disable this preemption sent and that can still run; never while another
// hold or a requested cycle is still on the VM (xe: suspend_count, the last resume enables).
static inline bool xeLrResumeNow(uint32_t holds, uint32_t req, uint32_t done) { return !holds && req == done; }
static inline bool xeLrSendEnable(bool sent, bool counts, bool gucDown) { return sent && counts && !gucDown; }

// xe_exec.c xe_exec_ioctl on an LR VM: an exec without batch buffers does nothing at all (no in-fence wait, no
// out-sync: `if (!xe_vm_in_lr_mode(vm))` around xe_sync_in_fence_get / xe_sync_entry_signal), and the job timeout does
// not apply to the queue (xe_exec_queue_is_lr: q->vm in LR mode and not a VM bind queue).
static inline bool xeLrExecNoop(bool lr, uint32_t numBatch) { return lr && !numBatch; }
static inline bool xeLrJobTimeoutApplies(bool lr) { return !lr; }

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Memory regions: where a GPU object's memory comes from, as Linux xe decides it (its TTM placements XE_PL_TT,
// XE_PL_VRAM0 and XE_PL_STOLEN), keyed by the platform descriptor. The first step towards an integrated memory path
// (Lunar Lake: no VRAM, BOs in system memory, the stolen DSM behind BAR2). Today only BMG is started, and for it every
// answer here is the VRAM-or-system choice the code always made. Plain C++ without IOKit types, header only:
// tests/platform_test.cpp checks it on the host. Design: docs/design/DESIGN-lunar-lake.md.
//
// Linux references are to drivers/gpu/drm/xe in dl/linux-xe (abf8c33), checked against v6.18 where the note says so.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include "xe_platform.h"

// xe_bo.h XE_PL_*: the region a BO's backing lives in.
enum XeMemRegion : uint8_t {
	XE_MEM_SYSTEM = 0,   // XE_PL_TT: system pages; uAPI DRM_XE_MEM_REGION_CLASS_SYSMEM, instance 0, placement bit 0
	XE_MEM_VRAM0 = 1,    // XE_PL_VRAM0: tile 0's VRAM; uAPI DRM_XE_MEM_REGION_CLASS_VRAM, instance 1, placement bit 1
	XE_MEM_STOLEN = 2,   // XE_PL_STOLEN: the DSM; kernel objects only, never in the uAPI
};

// ─── user BOs (DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The region a user BO is made in first, from its placement bits (already checked against xePlatformMemRegionMask):
// tile 0's VRAM if the placement names it, else system memory. xe_bo.c __xe_bo_placement_for_flags lists the VRAM
// placement before the system one, and TTM validates into the first with room; a full VRAM falls back to system memory
// when the placement allows it (here: GEM_CREATE's spill). On an integrated part the mask has no VRAM bit, so this is
// always system memory.
static inline XeMemRegion xeMemUserRegion(const XePlatformDesc *d, uint32_t placement) {
	return (placement & xePlatformMemRegionMask(d) & (1u << XE_MEM_VRAM0)) ? XE_MEM_VRAM0 : XE_MEM_SYSTEM;
}
// xe_query.c query_mem_regions: system memory (instance 0), then one VRAM region per tile that has one (instance 1).
static inline uint32_t xeMemQueryRegions(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return xePlatformHasVram(d) ? 2u : 1u; }

// ─── the driver's own objects ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// The kernel objects this driver keeps in VRAM on BMG, and the region Linux gives each. On a discrete part all of them
// are VRAM; on an integrated one they are system memory, except the firmware's initial framebuffer, which is stolen.
enum XeKernelObject : uint8_t {
	XE_KOBJ_PAGETABLE,    // xe_pt.c xe_pt_create: XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM_IF_DGFX (here: ptPageAlloc)
	XE_KOBJ_LRC,          // xe_lrc.c xe_lrc_init: XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM_IF_DGFX (here: lrcAlloc, debug.intelxe.lrc_vram)
	XE_KOBJ_GUC_UM,       // xe_guc_ads.c guc_um_init_params' queues: XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM_IF_DGFX (here: gUmDpa)
	XE_KOBJ_DISPLAY,      // display/xe_fb_pin.c, xe_display_bo.c, xe_dsb_buffer.c: XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM_IF_DGFX
	                      // (here: xeDispVramAlloc for IntelXeFB)
	XE_KOBJ_INITIAL_FB,   // display/xe_initial_plane.c initial_plane_bo: the firmware's framebuffer, XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM0
	                      // on a discrete part, XE_BO_FLAG_STOLEN on an integrated one
};
static inline XeMemRegion xeMemKernelRegion(const XePlatformDesc *d, XeKernelObject o) {
	if (xePlatformHasVram(d)) return XE_MEM_VRAM0;
	return o == XE_KOBJ_INITIAL_FB ? XE_MEM_STOLEN : XE_MEM_SYSTEM;
}

// ─── stolen memory of an integrated part from graphics 12.70 (xe_ttm_stolen_mgr.c detect_lmembar_integrated) ─────
// BAR2 (the LMEMBAR) holds the GSM (the GGTT's 8 MB of entries) and then the DSM. stolen_base is 8 MB: from 12.70 a
// GGTT PTE with the DM bit takes the offset from GSMBASE as its address. Inputs are register values, so the decode is
// testable without the GPU:
//   ggc            GGC (0x108040; MMIO, not config space): GGMS 7:6 must be 3 (8 MB of GSM); GMS 15:8 the DSM size
//   stolenReserved STOLEN_RESERVED (0x1082c0, 64 bits as two dwords): WOPCM_SIZE 9:7 (get_wopcm_size)
//   bar2Start/Len  BAR2's physical address and length (pci_resource_start/len(pdev, 2))
//   gscpsmiBase    GSCPSMI_BASE (0x880c on the media GT: 0x38880c) when Wa_14019821291 applies (MEDIA_VERSION_RANGE
//                  (1300, 2000): MTL/ARL and LNL; the BIOS applies it, the driver keeps out of what it reserved), else 0
struct XeStolenIgfx {
	uint64_t size;        // usable DSM bytes; 0 = no stolen memory (why says which check failed)
	uint64_t gpuBase;     // mgr->stolen_base: 8 MB (GSM + 8 MB)
	uint64_t ioBase;      // mgr->io_base: BAR2 + 8 MB, where the CPU reaches it
	uint64_t gmsBytes;    // GGC.GMS decoded
	uint32_t wopcmBytes;  // the WOPCM at the top of the DSM, carved out
	uint64_t psmiBytes;   // Wa_14019821291: bytes below the WOPCM the BIOS reserved for GSC PSMI, carved out
	const char *why;      // nullptr when size > 0
};

// xe_ttm_stolen_mgr.c get_wopcm_size: STOLEN_RESERVED WOPCM_SIZE (9:7) 0-3: 1 << val MB, 5-6: 1 << (val - 1) MB, the
// rest (4, 7) unknown: 0 ("Missing case wopcm_size").
static inline uint32_t xeStolenWopcmBytes(uint64_t stolenReserved) {
	const uint32_t v = (uint32_t)(stolenReserved >> 7) & 7;
	if (v <= 3) return (1u << v) << 20;
	if (v == 5 || v == 6) return (1u << (v - 1)) << 20;
	return 0;
}
// detect_lmembar_integrated's GMS switch: 0x00-0x04 x 32 MB, 0xf0-0xfe (n - 0xf0 + 1) x 4 MB, else invalid (~0).
static inline uint64_t xeStolenGmsBytes(uint32_t ggc) {
	const uint32_t gms = (ggc >> 8) & 0xff;
	if (gms <= 0x04) return (uint64_t)gms * (32ull << 20);
	if (gms >= 0xf0 && gms <= 0xfe) return (uint64_t)(gms - 0xf0 + 1) * (4ull << 20);
	return ~0ull;
}

static inline XeStolenIgfx xeStolenDecodeIgfx(uint32_t ggc, uint64_t stolenReserved, uint64_t bar2Start, uint64_t bar2Len,
		uint64_t gscpsmiBase) {
	XeStolenIgfx s = {};
	s.gpuBase = 8ull << 20;
	s.ioBase = bar2Start + s.gpuBase;
	if (((ggc >> 6) & 3) != 3) {
		s.why = "GGC.GGMS is not 3 (8 MB of GSM)";
		return s;
	}
	s.gmsBytes = xeStolenGmsBytes(ggc);
	if (s.gmsBytes == ~0ull) {
		s.gmsBytes = 0;
		s.why = "GGC.GMS is not a valid size";
		return s;
	}
	s.wopcmBytes = xeStolenWopcmBytes(stolenReserved);
	if (!s.wopcmBytes) {
		s.why = "STOLEN_RESERVED.WOPCM_SIZE is not a known size";
		return s;
	}
	// Linux subtracts in u32 and lets the BAR2 check below catch an underflow (GMS 0, or a DSM smaller than the WOPCM)
	if (s.gmsBytes <= s.wopcmBytes) {
		s.why = "the DSM is no larger than the WOPCM";
		return s;
	}
	uint64_t size = s.gmsBytes - s.wopcmBytes;
	// Wa_14019821291: a GSCPSMI_BASE inside the DSM (bits 5:0 masked) marks the part from there up as reserved
	const uint64_t psmi = gscpsmiBase & ~0x3full;
	if (psmi >= s.ioBase && psmi < s.ioBase + size) {
		s.psmiBytes = s.ioBase + size - psmi;
		size = psmi - s.ioBase;
	}
	if (size + s.gpuBase > bar2Len) {
		s.why = "GSM + DSM do not fit in BAR2";
		return s;
	}
	if (!size) {
		s.why = "nothing left after the reservations";
		return s;
	}
	s.size = size;
	return s;
}
