// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The pcode mailbox as Linux drivers/gpu/drm/xe drives it, and the power-limit words xe_hwmon reads through it on
// platforms with has_mbx_power_limits (BMG, xe_pci.c:421). From Linux tree abf8c33 (v7.4 merge window): xe_pcode_api.h,
// xe_pcode.h, xe_pcode.c, xe_mmio.c __xe_mmio_wait32, regs/xe_mchbar_regs.h, xe_hwmon.c. Only the pure parts live here
// (register layout, the mailbox protocol over an MMIO accessor, error decoding, unit scaling, the report text) so that
// tests/pcode_test.cpp builds them on the host against a fake pcode; the lock, the MMIO and the reads are
// IntelXe::pcodeRead and IntelXe::powerLimitsRead. Read only: nothing here writes a power limit.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#ifdef KERNEL
#include <libkern/libkern.h>   // snprintf
#else
#include <stdio.h>
#endif

// xe_pcode_api.h:13-29
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_MAILBOX = 0x138124;
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_READY = 1u << 31;
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_ERROR_MASK = 0xff;   // the error field shares bits 7:0 with PCODE_MB_COMMAND
enum : uint32_t {
	PCODE_SUCCESS = 0x0, PCODE_ILLEGAL_CMD = 0x1, PCODE_TIMEOUT = 0x2, PCODE_ILLEGAL_DATA = 0x3,
	PCODE_ILLEGAL_SUBCOMMAND = 0x4, PCODE_LOCKED = 0x6, PCODE_GT_RATIO_OUT_OF_RANGE = 0x10, PCODE_REJECTED = 0x11,
};
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_DATA0 = 0x138128;
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_DATA1 = 0x13812c;
// xe_pcode_api.h:37-39
static constexpr uint32_t DGFX_PCODE_STATUS = 0x7e, DGFX_GET_INIT_STATUS = 0, DGFX_INIT_STATUS_COMPLETE = 1;
// xe_pcode_api.h:42-47, 49-55
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_POWER_SETUP = 0x7c;
static constexpr uint32_t POWER_SETUP_SUBCOMMAND_READ_I1 = 0x4;
static constexpr uint32_t POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS = 1u << 31, POWER_SETUP_I1_SHIFT = 6, POWER_SETUP_I1_DATA_MASK = 0xffff;
static constexpr uint32_t READ_PSYSGPU_POWER_LIMIT = 0x6, READ_PACKAGE_POWER_LIMIT = 0x8;
static constexpr uint32_t READ_PL_FROM_PCODE = 0x0, READ_PL_FROM_FW = 0x1, READ_PL_ACCEPTED = 0x2;
// xe_pcode.h:21: xe_pcode_read's timeout
static constexpr uint32_t PCODE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10;

// regs/xe_mchbar_regs.h:41-46: a power-limit word (PCU_CR_PACKAGE_RAPL_LIMIT layout; the mailbox returns PL1 in DATA0
// and PL2 in DATA1 in the same layout, xe_hwmon.c:211-214)
static constexpr uint32_t PWR_LIM_VAL = 0x7fff;   // 14:0
static constexpr uint32_t PWR_LIM_EN = 1u << 15;
static constexpr uint32_t PWR_LIM_TIME_X_SHIFT = 22, PWR_LIM_TIME_X_MASK = 0x3;    // 23:22
static constexpr uint32_t PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_SHIFT = 17, PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_MASK = 0x1f;   // 21:17
// xe_hwmon.c:79-85: the units of mailbox-power-limit platforms (PKG_POWER_SKU_UNIT does not exist there), as right
// shifts: power 1/8 W, time 1/1024 s (energy: XE_ENERGY_UNIT_MBX in xe_pmt.h). Set at :1526-1528.
static constexpr uint8_t XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX = 0x3, XE_TIME_UNIT_MBX = 0xa;

// xe_pcode.h:41-44 PCODE_MBOX: command 7:0, param1 15:8, param2 23:16 (xe_pcode_api.h:15-17)
static constexpr uint32_t xePcodeMbox(uint32_t cmd, uint32_t param1, uint32_t param2) {
	return (cmd & 0xff) | (param1 & 0xff) << 8 | (param2 & 0xff) << 16;
}

// xe_pcode.c:38-71 pcode_mailbox_status: the mailbox's error field as an errno (positive here), 0 on success
static inline int xePcodeStatusErrno(uint32_t mailbox) {
	switch (mailbox & PCODE_ERROR_MASK) {
	case PCODE_SUCCESS: return 0;
	case PCODE_ILLEGAL_CMD: return ENXIO;
	case PCODE_TIMEOUT: return ETIMEDOUT;
	case PCODE_ILLEGAL_DATA: return EINVAL;
	case PCODE_ILLEGAL_SUBCOMMAND: return ENXIO;
	case PCODE_LOCKED: return EBUSY;
	case PCODE_GT_RATIO_OUT_OF_RANGE: return EOVERFLOW;
	case PCODE_REJECTED: return EACCES;
	default: return EPROTO;
	}
}

// xe_pcode.c:73-102 __pcode_mailbox_rw, with xe_mmio.c:325-370 __xe_mmio_wait32 for the wait on READY. Io supplies
// uint32_t rd(uint32_t off), void wr(uint32_t off, uint32_t v) and void delayUs(uint32_t us). The caller holds the
// pcode lock (tile->pcode.lock, xe_pcode.c:111). EAGAIN when the mailbox is still busy (a device that does not answer
// reads all ones, READY included), ETIMEDOUT when pcode does not clear READY within timeoutUs, otherwise the decoded
// error field. With returnData, DATA0 (and DATA1 when data1 is given) are read back as xe_pcode_read does.
template <class Io>
static int xePcodeMailboxRw(Io &io, uint32_t mbox, uint32_t *data0, uint32_t *data1, uint32_t timeoutUs, bool returnData) {
	if (io.rd(PCODE_MAILBOX) & PCODE_READY) return EAGAIN;
	io.wr(PCODE_DATA0, *data0);
	io.wr(PCODE_DATA1, data1 ? *data1 : 0);
	io.wr(PCODE_MAILBOX, PCODE_READY | mbox);
	// __xe_mmio_wait32: poll with a wait that doubles from 10 us, never past the deadline, then one last read
	bool done = false;
	for (uint32_t waited = 0, wait = 10;;) {
		if (!(io.rd(PCODE_MAILBOX) & PCODE_READY)) {
			done = true;
			break;
		}
		if (waited >= timeoutUs) break;
		if (wait > timeoutUs - waited) wait = timeoutUs - waited;
		io.delayUs(wait);
		waited += wait;
		wait = wait < 50000 ? wait << 1 : wait;
	}
	if (!done && (io.rd(PCODE_MAILBOX) & PCODE_READY)) return ETIMEDOUT;
	if (returnData) {
		*data0 = io.rd(PCODE_DATA0);
		if (data1) *data1 = io.rd(PCODE_DATA1);
	}
	return xePcodeStatusErrno(io.rd(PCODE_MAILBOX));
}

// xe_hwmon.c:361-362: a power-limit word's value, REG_FIELD_GET(PWR_LIM_VAL) * SF_POWER >> scl_shift_power, here in
// milliwatts (SF_POWER / 1000; exact for the 1/8 W unit)
static inline uint32_t xePowerLimitMw(uint32_t word, uint8_t shift) {
	return (uint32_t)((uint64_t)(word & PWR_LIM_VAL) * 1000000u >> shift) / 1000u;
}
// xe_hwmon.c:585-601: the limit's time window in ms, tau = (1 + x/4) * 2^y units: (4 | x) << y, >> (time shift + 2)
static inline uint64_t xePowerLimitTauMs(uint32_t word, uint8_t timeShift) {
	const uint32_t x = word >> PWR_LIM_TIME_X_SHIFT & PWR_LIM_TIME_X_MASK, y = word >> PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_SHIFT & PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_MASK;
	return ((uint64_t)(4 | x) << y) * 1000u >> (timeShift + 2);
}
// xe_hwmon.c:891-908 with :1176 (power_crit, SF_POWER) or curr_crit (SF_CURR): I1 in U10.6, watts when bit 31 is set
// (xe_hwmon.c:855, 1133-1136), amperes otherwise; here milliwatts or milliamperes
static inline uint32_t xePowerI1Milli(uint32_t i1) {
	return (uint32_t)((uint64_t)(i1 & POWER_SETUP_I1_DATA_MASK) * 1000u >> POWER_SETUP_I1_SHIFT);
}

// The four power limits as xe_hwmon_get_preregistration_info reads them (xe_hwmon.c:1499-1508): PL1 and PL2 of the
// card (READ_PSYSGPU_POWER_LIMIT) and of the package (READ_PACKAGE_POWER_LIMIT). The read asks for READ_PL_FROM_FW, the
// param2 xe uses until it has written the limits back (prepare_power_limit_param2, xe_hwmon.c:178-188, with
// boot_power_limit_read false); this driver never writes them, so that stays the request. Plus I1 (power1_crit /
// curr1_crit). xe exposes no rated (TDP) value on these platforms (xe_hwmon.c:1124-1126 hides power_rated_max) and reads
// no PKG_POWER_SKU there, so there is none here either.
enum : uint32_t { XE_PL_CARD = 0, XE_PL_PKG = 1, XE_PL_CHANNELS = 2 };
struct XePowerLimits {
	int err {ENODATA};                    // 0, or the errno of the first failed limit read
	uint32_t word[XE_PL_CHANNELS][2] {};  // [card/package][PL1 = DATA0, PL2 = DATA1]
	int i1Err {ENODATA};
	uint32_t i1 {0};
};
// The report text: ", card PL1 X W (on|off), card PL2 ..., package PL1 ..., package PL2 ..." and, when I1 was read,
// ", card crit Z W" (or A). Units: XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX. Returns the length written (always < len; text that does not fit
// is cut).
static inline size_t xePowerLimitsText(char *buf, size_t len, const XePowerLimits &pl) {
	size_t n = 0;
	auto add = [&](int k) { if (k > 0) n = n + (size_t)k < len ? n + (size_t)k : (len ? len - 1 : 0); };
	if (!len) return 0;
	if (pl.err) {
		add(snprintf(buf, len, ", power limits unavailable (pcode error %d)", pl.err));
		return n;
	}
	static const char *const kCh[XE_PL_CHANNELS] = {"card", "package"};
	for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_PL_CHANNELS; c++)
		for (uint32_t l = 0; l < 2; l++) {
			const uint32_t w = pl.word[c][l], mw = xePowerLimitMw(w, XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX);
			const char *on = w & PWR_LIM_EN ? "on" : "off";
			if (mw % 1000)
				add(snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", %s PL%u %u.%03u W (%s)", kCh[c], l + 1, mw / 1000, mw % 1000, on));
			else
				add(snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", %s PL%u %u W (%s)", kCh[c], l + 1, mw / 1000, on));
		}
	if (!pl.i1Err) {
		const uint32_t m = xePowerI1Milli(pl.i1);
		add(snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card crit %u.%03u %s", m / 1000, m % 1000, pl.i1 & POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS ? "W" : "A"));
	}
	return n;
}

// The platform descriptor table (xe_platform.h). Values from Linux drivers/gpu/drm/xe (MIT, torvalds/master as in

// GMD_ID platforms); xe_uc_fw.c XE_GUC/HUC/GSC_FIRMWARE_DEFS; xe_wopcm.c xe_wopcm_size; xe_pat.c xe_pat_init_early;
// xe_mocs.c get_mocs_settings. DMC paths: i915/display/intel_dmc.c dmc_firmware_default (not in dl/linux-xe; read
// from torvalds/master 2026-11-10). Built like Linux's tables: a device desc per platform, the graphics/media IP
// features folded in by the functions below, then one entry per pciids.h id list. Constant-initialized (constexpr):
// no static constructor in the kext.
#include "xe_platform.h"

namespace {

constexpr uint64_t bits(uint32_t first, uint32_t n) { return ((1ull << n) - 1) << first; }
constexpr uint64_t kVcs = bits(XE_HW_ENGINE_VCS0, 8), kVecs = bits(XE_HW_ENGINE_VECS0, 4), kCcs = bits(XE_HW_ENGINE_CCS0, 4);
constexpr uint64_t kRcs0 = 1ull << XE_HW_ENGINE_RCS0, kBcs0 = 1ull << XE_HW_ENGINE_BCS0, kBcs8 = 1ull << XE_HW_ENGINE_BCS8;
constexpr uint64_t kCcs0 = 1ull << XE_HW_ENGINE_CCS0, kGsccs0 = 1ull << XE_HW_ENGINE_GSCCS0;

// ─── graphics IPs (xe_pci.c xe_graphics_desc) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
constexpr XePlatformDesc graphicsXelp(XePlatformDesc d) {   // graphics_xelp (12.00, 12.10)
	d.engineMask |= kRcs0 | kBcs0;
	return d;
}
constexpr XePlatformDesc graphicsXehpg(XePlatformDesc d) {   // graphics_xehpg (12.55)
	d.engineMask |= kRcs0 | kBcs0 | kCcs;
	d.hasRangeTlbInval = true;
	return d;
}
constexpr XePlatformDesc graphicsXelpg(XePlatformDesc d) {   // graphics_xelpg (12.70, 12.71, 12.74)
	d.engineMask |= kRcs0 | kBcs0 | kCcs0;
	d.hasRangeTlbInval = true;
	return d;
}
constexpr XePlatformDesc graphicsXe2(XePlatformDesc d) {   // graphics_xe2 (20.01, 20.02, 20.04, 30.00-30.05): XE2_GFX_FEATURES
	d.hasAccessCounter = d.hasAsid = d.hasAtomicPteBit = d.hasRangeTlbInval = d.hasUsm = d.has64bitTimestamp = true;
	d.engineMask |= kRcs0 | kBcs8 | kBcs0 | kCcs;
	return d;
}
// ─── media IPs (xe_media_desc) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
constexpr XePlatformDesc mediaXem(XePlatformDesc d) { d.engineMask |= kVcs | kVecs; return d; }                // 12.00, 12.55
constexpr XePlatformDesc mediaXelpmp(XePlatformDesc d) { d.engineMask |= kVcs | kVecs | kGsccs0; return d; }   // 13.00+

// ─── device descs (xe_pci.c), with the per-platform values xe picks elsewhere ───────────────────────────────────
constexpr XePlatformDesc gen12Integrated(XePlatform p) {   // tgl_desc, rkl_desc, adl_s_desc, adl_p_desc, adl_n_desc
	XePlatformDesc d;
	d.platform = p;
	d.preGmdidGraphics = d.graphicsVerx100 = 1200;   // graphics_ip_xelp
	d.preGmdidMedia = d.mediaVerx100 = 1200;         // media_ip_xem
	d.dmaMaskBits = 39;
	d.hasCachedPt = d.hasDisplay = d.hasLlc = true;
	d.hasSriov = p != XE_ROCKETLAKE;
	d.maxGtPerTile = 1;
	d.vaBits = 48;
	d.vmMaxLevel = 3;
	d.wopcmBytes = 2u << 20;   // WOPCM_SIZE
	d.patEntries = 4;          // xelp_pat_table (GRAPHICS_VERx100 <= 1210)
	d.mocsUcIndex = 3;         // gen12_mocs_desc
	d.gucMajor = 70;
	d.gucMinor = 44;
	d.hucFw = p == XE_ALDERLAKE_N ? nullptr : "i915/tgl_huc.bin";   // no ALDERLAKE_N line in XE_HUC_FIRMWARE_DEFS
	d.gucFw = p == XE_ALDERLAKE_P ? "i915/adlp_guc_70.bin" : "i915/tgl_guc_70.bin";
	d.gucStem = p == XE_ALDERLAKE_P ? "adlp" : "tgl";
	// display: tigerlake, rocketlake, alderlake_s, alderlake_p (ADL-N is its subplatform alderlake_n)
	d.dmcFw = p == XE_TIGERLAKE ? "i915/tgl_dmc_ver2_12.bin" : p == XE_ROCKETLAKE ? "i915/rkl_dmc_ver2_03.bin" :
		p == XE_ALDERLAKE_S ? "i915/adls_dmc_ver2_01.bin" : "i915/adlp_dmc.bin";
	d.missing = "Xe_LP integrated (12.00): no VRAM, so no integrated memory path (system memory BOs, stolen DSM, GGTT "
		"in GSM), Gen12 LRC/PAT/MOCS/workaround tables, xelp_irq_handler, i915 GuC 70.44";
	return mediaXem(graphicsXelp(d));
}

constexpr XePlatformDesc entry(const char *name, const char *sub, const uint16_t *ids, uint32_t n, XePlatformDesc d) {
	d.name = name;
	if (sub) d.subplatform = sub;
	d.ids = ids;
	d.nIds = n;
	return d;
}
#define XP_IDS(a) a, sizeof(a) / sizeof(a[0])

// BMG ids by subplatform (pciids.h INTEL_BMG_G21_IDS; the rest of INTEL_BMG_IDS has none). kIdsBMG holds both.
const uint16_t kIdsBMGG21[] = {0xe202, 0xe209, 0xe20b, 0xe20c, 0xe20d, 0xe210, 0xe211, 0xe212, 0xe216};
const uint16_t kIdsBMGG31[] = {0xe220, 0xe221, 0xe222, 0xe223};

}   // namespace

// In XeProbe's former order (xe_pci.c pciidlist order, by family): a name lookup finds the same entry as before.
constexpr XePlatformDesc kXePlatforms[] = {
	entry("TGL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsTGL), gen12Integrated(XE_TIGERLAKE)),
	entry("RKL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsRKL), gen12Integrated(XE_ROCKETLAKE)),
	entry("ADL-S", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsADLS), gen12Integrated(XE_ALDERLAKE_S)),
	entry("RPL-S", "RPLS", XP_IDS(kIdsRPLS), gen12Integrated(XE_ALDERLAKE_S)),
	entry("ADL-P", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsADLP), gen12Integrated(XE_ALDERLAKE_P)),
	entry("RPL-U", "RPLU", XP_IDS(kIdsRPLU), gen12Integrated(XE_ALDERLAKE_P)),
	entry("RPL-P", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsRPLP), gen12Integrated(XE_ALDERLAKE_P)),
	entry("ADL-N", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsADLN), gen12Integrated(XE_ALDERLAKE_N)),
	entry("DG1", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsDG1), dg1()),
	entry("DG2", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsDG2), dg2(false)),
	entry("ATS-M", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsATSM), dg2(true)),
	entry("MTL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsMTL), mtl(1270)),
	entry("ARL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsARL), mtl(0)),        // mtl_desc; graphics 12.70 or 12.74 by SKU (GMD_ID)
	entry("LNL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsLNL), lnl()),
	entry("BMG", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsBMGG21), bmg(true)),
	entry("BMG", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsBMGG31), bmg(false)),
	entry("PTL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsPTL), ptl(3000, "i915/xe3lpd_dmc.bin")),        // display 30.00
	entry("WCL", nullptr, XP_IDS(kIdsWCL), ptl(0, "i915/xe3lpd_3002_dmc.bin")),      // ptl_desc; display 30.02
};
const uint32_t kXePlatformCount = sizeof(kXePlatforms) / sizeof(kXePlatforms[0]);
static_assert(sizeof(kIdsBMG) == sizeof(kIdsBMGG21) + sizeof(kIdsBMGG31), "kIdsBMG = G21 + G31 (tests/platform_test.cpp)");

const XePlatformDesc *xePlatformFind(uint16_t devId) {
	for (uint32_t p = 0; p < kXePlatformCount; p++)
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kXePlatforms[p].nIds; i++)
			if (kXePlatforms[p].ids[i] == devId) return &kXePlatforms[p];
	return nullptr;
}

const XePlatformDesc *xePlatformByName(const char *name) {
	for (uint32_t p = 0; p < kXePlatformCount; p++) {
		const char *a = kXePlatforms[p].name, *b = name;
		while (*a && *a == *b) a++, b++;
		if (*a == *b) return &kXePlatforms[p];
	}
	return nullptr;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Platform descriptors: what Linux xe_pci.c keeps per device (struct xe_device_desc, with the xe_graphics_desc and
// xe_media_desc of the IP the platform ships) plus the per-platform values xe picks elsewhere (xe_uc_fw.c firmware,
// xe_wopcm.c, xe_pat.c n_entries, xe_mocs.c uc_index, i915 intel_dmc.c). One entry per device-id list of
// xe_probe_ids.inc (Linux include/drm/intel/pciids.h). Looked up once by PCI device id: IntelXe::start, which starts
// only on an entry marked supported, and XeProbe, which takes any. Plain C++ without IOKit types, so
// tests/platform_test.cpp builds it on the host. Design and the roadmap per family: docs/design/DESIGN-platforms.md.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

// xe_platform_types.h enum xe_platform, same order (graphics version, then chronological)
enum XePlatform : uint8_t {
	XE_PLATFORM_UNINITIALIZED = 0,
	XE_TIGERLAKE,
	XE_ROCKETLAKE,
	XE_ALDERLAKE_S,
	XE_ALDERLAKE_P,
	XE_ALDERLAKE_N,
	XE_DG1,
	XE_DG2,
	XE_PVC,
	XE_METEORLAKE,
	XE_LUNARLAKE,
	XE_BATTLEMAGE,
	XE_PANTHERLAKE,
};

// Where the GPU's energy counters are (Linux xe_hwmon.c xe_hwmon_energy_get, :500-539). Only BMG is implemented here;
// the register path the other dGPUs take (REG_PKG_ENERGY_STATUS: PCU_CR_PACKAGE_ENERGY_STATUS, PVC/CRI registers, unit
// from PKG_POWER_SKU_UNIT) would be a second value.
enum XeEnergySource : uint8_t {
	XE_ENERGY_NONE = 0,   // not read (debug.intelxe.sensors prints no energy)
	XE_ENERGY_PMT,        // XE_BATTLEMAGE: the PUNIT PMT telemetry word (xe_pmt.h), card and package
};

// xe_hw_engine_types.h enum xe_hw_engine_id: bit positions of XePlatformDesc::engineMask
enum : uint32_t {
	XE_HW_ENGINE_RCS0 = 0,
	XE_HW_ENGINE_BCS0 = 1, XE_HW_ENGINE_BCS8 = 9,
	XE_HW_ENGINE_VCS0 = 10,    // VCS0-7: 10-17
	XE_HW_ENGINE_VECS0 = 18,   // VECS0-3: 18-21
	XE_HW_ENGINE_CCS0 = 22,    // CCS0-3: 22-25
	XE_HW_ENGINE_GSCCS0 = 26,
};

struct XePlatformDesc {
	const char *name {nullptr};          // family as XeProbe names it (debug.xeprobe.family): "BMG", "ADL-P", ...
	const char *subplatform {nullptr};   // xe_subplatform_desc name ("G21"), nullptr = none
	XePlatform platform {XE_PLATFORM_UNINITIALIZED};
	const uint16_t *ids {nullptr};       // PCI device ids (vendor 8086)
	uint32_t nIds {0};
	// IP versions (verx100). preGmdid*: xe_device_desc pre_gmdid_*_ip, 0 on platforms with GMD_ID (graphics >= 12.70).
	// graphics/mediaVerx100: the IP this entry describes: pre_gmdid_* where set, else the GMD_ID value Linux's
	// tests/xe_pci.c GMDID_CASE gives the platform (0 = not listed there; read GMD_ID).
	uint16_t preGmdidGraphics {0}, preGmdidMedia {0};
	uint16_t graphicsVerx100 {0}, mediaVerx100 {0};
	// xe_device_desc
	uint8_t dmaMaskBits {0};     // dma_mask_size
	uint8_t vaBits {0};          // va_bits
	uint8_t vmMaxLevel {0};      // vm_max_level (root page-table level)
	uint8_t maxGtPerTile {0};    // 2 = standalone media GT at MEDIA_GT_GSI_OFFSET (media >= 13.00)
	bool isDgfx {false}, hasFlatCcs {false}, hasLlc {false}, hasDisplay {false}, hasSriov {false}, hasPxp {false};
	bool hasCachedPt {false}, hasHeciGscfi {false}, hasHeciCscfi {false}, hasGscNvm {false}, hasFanControl {false};
	bool hasMbxThermalInfo {false}, hasMbxPowerLimits {false}, needsScratch {false}, need64kVram {false};
	bool hasSocRemapperTelem {false};   // has_soc_remapper_telem: the telemetry window's region set via SG_REMAP_INDEX1
	// xe_graphics_desc of the graphics IP
	bool hasUsm {false}, hasAsid {false}, hasAccessCounter {false}, hasAtomicPteBit {false}, hasRangeTlbInval {false};
	bool has64bitTimestamp {false};
	uint64_t engineMask {0};     // graphics hw_engine_mask | media hw_engine_mask (XE_HW_ENGINE_* bits)
	// elsewhere in xe
	uint32_t wopcmBytes {0};     // xe_wopcm.c xe_wopcm_size
	uint8_t patEntries {0};      // xe_pat.c xe_pat_init_early n_entries (valid pat_index values)
	uint8_t mocsUcIndex {0};     // xe_mocs.c get_mocs_settings uc_index (GuC shim MOCS, MEM_SET MOCS)
	XeEnergySource energySource {XE_ENERGY_NONE};   // xe_hwmon.c xe_hwmon_energy_get: platform == XE_BATTLEMAGE -> PMT
	uint8_t energyShift {0};     // xe_hwmon scl_shift_energy: ENERGY_UNIT (14) on mailbox-power-limit platforms
	// linux-firmware paths: xe_uc_fw.c XE_GUC/HUC/GSC_FIRMWARE_DEFS, i915 intel_dmc.c dmc_firmware_default. nullptr: Linux
	// loads none for the platform. gucStem: the <stem> of <stem>_guc_70.bin (XeProbe's firmware directory names).
	const char *gucFw {nullptr}, *gucStem {nullptr}, *hucFw {nullptr}, *gscFw {nullptr}, *dmcFw {nullptr};
	uint16_t gucMajor {0}, gucMinor {0};   // the GuC release XE_GUC_FIRMWARE_DEFS wants (major, minimum minor)
	// The GSC compatibility version XE_GSC_FIRMWARE_DEFS wants (xe_gsc.c query_compatibility_version: project major,
	// compatibility major; "cv104.1.0" on LNL). The file is named by the compatibility major (fw_filename_gsc:
	// xe/lnl_gsc_1.bin), not by the project.
	uint16_t gscMajor {0}, gscMinor {0};
	// Device workarounds (xe_device_wa_oob.rules), where this driver applies them per platform.
	// Wa_14022085890: SUBPLATFORM(BATTLEMAGE, G21). xe_guc_pc.c pc_needs_min_freq_change raises the SLPC minimum to
	// BMG_MIN_FREQ (1200 MHz) on the primary GT of every BMG (platform == XE_BATTLEMAGE), and with this workaround on the
	// media GT too (IntelXe::mediaPcStart). xePlatformSlpcMin* below.
	bool wa14022085890 {false};
	// Wa_15015404425: PLATFORM(LUNARLAKE), PLATFORM(PANTHERLAKE) (PTL: off again from media B0, 15015404425_disable).
	// xe_mmio.c mmio_flush_pending_writes: four dummy writes to 0x130030 before every MMIO read. XeProbe does them.
	bool wa15015404425 {false};
	// this driver
	bool supported {false};        // IntelXe starts on it; every other entry is refused at start with `missing`
	const char *missing {nullptr}; // what the family still needs (the start refusal's log line)
	// An entry that is not supported but that a tester may start anyway: the boot-arg (a flag, without its leading '-')
	// that lets IntelXe start on it, with a warning in the log. nullptr: refused, whatever the boot-args.
	const char *testerBootArg {nullptr};
};

extern const XePlatformDesc kXePlatforms[];
extern const uint32_t kXePlatformCount;

// The entry listing devId, or nullptr (xe_pci.c pciidlist / pci_match_id).
const XePlatformDesc *xePlatformFind(uint16_t devId);
// The first entry of that family name (debug.xeprobe.family), or nullptr.
const XePlatformDesc *xePlatformByName(const char *name);

// Derived values, as xe computes them from the descriptor.
static inline uint64_t xePlatformVmSize(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return 1ull << d->vaBits; }   // xe_vm_create vm->size
static inline uint64_t xePlatformDmaLimit(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return 1ull << d->dmaMaskBits; }
// IOBufferMemoryDescriptor physical mask for memory the GPU reads by device address: dma_mask_size bits, pages
static inline uint64_t xePlatformPhysMask(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return (xePlatformDmaLimit(d) - 1) & ~0xfffull; }
// xe_guc_pc.c pc_needs_min_freq_change: whether pc_adjust_freq_bounds raises the GT's SLPC minimum to BMG_MIN_FREQ.
// Primary GT: Wa_14022085890, or platform BATTLEMAGE (CRESCENTISLAND has no entry here). Media GT: Wa_14022085890 only.
static inline bool xePlatformSlpcMinPrimary(const XePlatformDesc *d) {
	return d->wa14022085890 || d->platform == XE_BATTLEMAGE;
}
static inline bool xePlatformSlpcMinMedia(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->wa14022085890; }
// The enabled-engine bits of a class from engineMask (first: XE_HW_ENGINE_* of instance 0, n instances)
static inline uint32_t xePlatformEngines(const XePlatformDesc *d, uint32_t first, uint32_t n) {
	return (uint32_t)(d->engineMask >> first) & ((1u << n) - 1);
}

// ─── memory model: what xe derives from is_dgfx (and has_llc, has_cached_pt, the graphics version) ───────────────
// For the code that differs on an integrated part (Lunar Lake and the other !isDgfx entries). None of those is
// supported yet, so on BMG every answer is the discrete one the code has always assumed. docs/design/DESIGN-lunar-lake.md.

// The lowest graphics version the entry can have: graphicsVerx100, or the family's first for an entry whose IP is read
// from GMD_ID per SKU (ARL: 12.70/12.74, WCL: 30.xx; graphicsVerx100 0). For xe's GRAPHICS_VERx100(xe) >= N checks.
static inline uint16_t xePlatformGraphicsMin(const XePlatformDesc *d) {
	if (d->graphicsVerx100) return d->graphicsVerx100;
	return d->platform == XE_METEORLAKE ? 1270 : d->platform == XE_PANTHERLAKE ? 3000 : 0;
}
// No device memory: every BO is in system memory (xe_tile.c xe_tile_alloc_vram and xe_device.c xe_device_vram_alloc
// make a VRAM region only when IS_DGFX).
static inline bool xePlatformIntegrated(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return !d->isDgfx; }
static inline bool xePlatformHasVram(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx; }
// has_llc: the GPU shares the CPU's last-level cache (Gen12 integrated). Lunar Lake does not (lnl_desc sets no has_llc):
// CPU-cached memory is coherent only through the PAT index's coherency mode (xe_pat.c coh_mode, XE_COH_1WAY/2WAY).
static inline bool xePlatformHasLlc(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->hasLlc; }
// xe->info.mem_region_mask: bit 0 system memory (always: xe_device.c xe_device_probe), bit 1 tile 0's VRAM (xe_tile.c
// xe_tile_init_noalloc, IS_DGFX only). The uAPI's placement bits and the instances of QUERY_MEM_REGIONS.
static inline uint32_t xePlatformMemRegionMask(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return 1u | (d->isDgfx ? 2u : 0u); }
// xe_query.c query_gt_list: near_mem_regions 0x1 (system memory) on an integrated part, tile 0's VRAM bit otherwise;
// far_mem_regions = mem_region_mask ^ near.
static inline uint32_t xePlatformNearMemRegions(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx ? 2u : 1u; }
static inline uint32_t xePlatformFarMemRegions(const XePlatformDesc *d) {
	return xePlatformMemRegionMask(d) ^ xePlatformNearMemRegions(d);
}
// Stolen memory (DSM): the detect function xe_ttm_stolen_mgr.c xe_ttm_stolen_mgr_init picks.
enum XeStolenModel : uint8_t {
	XE_STOLEN_LMEMBAR_DGFX = 1,   // detect_lmembar_dgfx: DSMBASE in VRAM, through BAR2, up to the tile's end minus WOPCM
	XE_STOLEN_LMEMBAR_IGFX,       // detect_lmembar_integrated (graphics >= 12.70): BAR2 (LMEMBAR) holds GSM (8 MB), then
	                              // DSM; stolen_base 8 MB, size from GGC.GMS minus WOPCM (xe_stolen.h)
	XE_STOLEN_BIOS,               // detect_stolen: intel_graphics_stolen_res (BDSM, reserved by the x86 early quirks)
};
static inline XeStolenModel xePlatformStolen(const XePlatformDesc *d) {
	if (d->isDgfx) return XE_STOLEN_LMEMBAR_DGFX;
	return xePlatformGraphicsMin(d) >= 1270 ? XE_STOLEN_LMEMBAR_IGFX : XE_STOLEN_BIOS;
}
// xe_ttm_stolen_cpu_access_needs_ggtt: before 12.70, the CPU reaches an integrated part's stolen memory only through
// the GGTT aperture (BAR2 is GMADR there), not directly.
static inline bool xePlatformStolenCpuViaGgtt(const XePlatformDesc *d) {
	return xePlatformGraphicsMin(d) < 1270 && !d->isDgfx;
}
// What BAR2 is. On a discrete part it is VRAM (LMEM_BAR, regs/xe_bars.h). On an integrated part from 12.70 it is the
// LMEMBAR, which holds GSM and DSM (detect_lmembar_integrated: DSM at BAR2 + 8 MB); before 12.70 it is the GGTT
// aperture. Code that maps BAR2 as VRAM must check this first.
static inline bool xePlatformBar2IsVram(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx; }
// xe_ggtt.c xe_ggtt_init_early: the GSM (GGTT page table) size. From graphics 12.50 it is 8 MB, so a 4 GiB GGTT. Before
// that it comes from the GGMS field of the GMCH control word (probe_gsm_size); 0 here means "read GGC".
static inline uint32_t xePlatformGsmBytes(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return xePlatformGraphicsMin(d) >= 1250 ? 8u << 20 : 0; }
// System memory and the CPU caches.
// - Discrete: the GPU's system-memory accesses always snoop (xe_bo.c xe_ttm_tt_create: "DGFX GPU system memory accesses
//   are always coherent with the CPU", every TT page WB).
// - Integrated: only through a coherent PAT index (xe_vm.c refuses a userptr bind with a non-coherent one).
static inline bool xePlatformSysAlwaysCoherent(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx; }
// xe_ttm_tt_create: on an integrated part without has_cached_pt the GPU's page-table walks do not snoop, so page-table
// BOs are CPU write-combined (Xe_LPG and later: MTL, LNL, PTL).
static inline bool xePlatformPtWriteCombined(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return !d->isDgfx && !d->hasCachedPt; }
// Flat CCS of system-memory BOs (xe_bo.c xe_bo_needs_ccs_pages, xe_migrate.c): kept in extra pages after the BO's own
// (CCS bytes = size / 512), cleared, copied and saved by the migrate engine. This applies to integrated Xe2 and later
// with flat CCS, if the BIOS left it on (xe_device.c probe_has_flat_ccs reads XE2_FLAT_CCS_ENABLE). A discrete Xe2
// part keeps flat CCS in VRAM only.
static inline bool xePlatformSysCcs(const XePlatformDesc *d) {
	return !d->isDgfx && d->hasFlatCcs && xePlatformGraphicsMin(d) >= 2000;
}
// xe_pat.c xe_pat_init_early (graphics 20 and 30): the page-table-access PAT entry (PAT_PTA) is programmed on discrete
// parts only; xe2_pat_ats on both.
static inline bool xePlatformPatPta(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx; }
// Discrete-only steps of xe: the VF_CAP_REG write after wmb() in xe_device_wmb; the DGFX_PCODE_STATUS and LMEM_INIT
// waits at probe (xe_pcode.c xe_pcode_ready, xe_device.c assert_lmem_ready).
static inline bool xePlatformWmbMmio(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx; }
static inline bool xePlatformLmemInitWait(const XePlatformDesc *d) { return d->isDgfx; }

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// GPU energy from the PMT telemetry region, as Linux xe_hwmon reads it on Battlemage. The register layout comes from
// Linux drivers/gpu/drm/xe (tree abf8c33, v7.4 merge window): regs/xe_pmt.h, regs/xe_regs.h SOC_BASE,
// regs/xe_soc_remapper_regs.h, xe_vsec.c xe_guid_decode / xe_pmt_telem_read, xe_hwmon.c xe_hwmon_energy_get. Only the
// pure parts live here (offsets, GUID decode, field extraction, unit scaling, wrap accumulation, average power) so that
// tests/pmt_test.cpp builds them on the host; the MMIO reads are IntelXe::pmtTelemRead and IntelXe::energySample.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

// regs/xe_regs.h:12
static constexpr uint32_t SOC_BASE = 0x280000;
// regs/xe_pmt.h:10-21. The discovery table (the VSEC telemetry header's .offset, xe_vsec.c:32) holds the PUNIT GUID;
// the telemetry window itself starts at BMG_TELEMETRY_OFFSET, both in BAR0 (tbir 0, xe_vsec.c:31).
static constexpr uint32_t BMG_PMT_BASE_OFFSET = 0xdb000;
static constexpr uint32_t BMG_DISCOVERY_OFFSET = SOC_BASE + BMG_PMT_BASE_OFFSET;
static constexpr uint32_t PUNIT_TELEMETRY_GUID = BMG_DISCOVERY_OFFSET + 0x4;
static constexpr uint32_t BMG_ENERGY_STATUS_PMT_OFFSET = 0x30;   // ENERGY_PKG 31:0, ENERGY_CARD 63:32
static constexpr uint32_t BMG_TELEMETRY_BASE_OFFSET = 0xe0000;
static constexpr uint32_t BMG_TELEMETRY_OFFSET = SOC_BASE + BMG_TELEMETRY_BASE_OFFSET;
// regs/xe_soc_remapper_regs.h:10-11: the SoC re-mapper picks which telemetry memory region the window shows
// (xe_soc_remapper.c:18-22 xe_soc_remapper_set_telem_region, an rmw of bits 31:24).
static constexpr uint32_t SG_REMAP_INDEX1 = SOC_BASE + 0x08;
static constexpr uint32_t SG_REMAP_TELEM_SHIFT = 24, SG_REMAP_TELEM_MASK = 0xffu << SG_REMAP_TELEM_SHIFT;

// xe_vsec.c:23 (a PMT GUID field, not a PCI id), 73-80 (GUID layout and the PUNIT telemetry offset), 82-93 (enums)
static constexpr uint32_t BMG_PMT_GUID_DEVICE_ID = 0xe2f8;
static constexpr uint32_t PUNIT_TELEMETRY_OFFSET = 0x0200, PUNIT_WATCHER_OFFSET = 0x14a0;
static constexpr uint32_t OOBMSM_0_WATCHER_OFFSET = 0x18d8, OOBMSM_1_TELEMETRY_OFFSET = 0x1000;
enum : uint32_t { XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT, XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_0, XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_1 };
enum : uint32_t { XE_PMT_CAP_CRASHLOG, XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY, XE_PMT_CAP_WATCHER };

// xe_hwmon.c:84 ENERGY_UNIT: the energy unit of platforms whose power limits go through the pcode mailbox (BMG), as a
// right shift: one count is 2^-14 J (61 uJ). xe_hwmon_get_preregistration_info sets scl_shift_energy from it (:1527).
static constexpr uint8_t XE_ENERGY_UNIT_MBX = 14;

// xe_vsec.c:97-139 xe_guid_decode: the telemetry memory region (re-mapper index) and the offset inside the window that
// a GUID names. 0 or a negative errno-style value (-19 ENODEV: not a BMG GUID, -22 EINVAL: no such capability/record).
static inline int xePmtGuidDecode(uint32_t guid, uint32_t *index, uint32_t *offset) {
	const uint32_t recordId = guid >> 30 & 0x3, capType = guid >> 28 & 0x3, deviceId = guid >> 12 & 0xffff;
	if (deviceId != BMG_PMT_GUID_DEVICE_ID) return -19;
	if (capType > XE_PMT_CAP_WATCHER) return -22;
	*offset = 0;
	if (capType == XE_PMT_CAP_CRASHLOG) {
		*index = recordId == XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT ? 2 : 4;
		return 0;
	}
	switch (recordId) {
	case XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT:
		*index = 0;
		*offset = capType == XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY ? PUNIT_TELEMETRY_OFFSET : PUNIT_WATCHER_OFFSET;
		break;
	case XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_0:
		*index = 1;
		if (capType == XE_PMT_CAP_WATCHER) *offset = OOBMSM_0_WATCHER_OFFSET;
		break;
	case XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_1:
		*index = 1;
		if (capType == XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY) *offset = OOBMSM_1_TELEMETRY_OFFSET;
		break;
	default:
		return -22;
	}
	return 0;
}
// xe_vsec.c:147, 156: the BAR0 offset xe_pmt_telem_read copies from: the telemetry window, the GUID's offset in it, then
// the caller's offset (BMG_ENERGY_STATUS_PMT_OFFSET for energy).
static inline uint32_t xePmtTelemOffset(uint32_t guidOffset, uint32_t userOffset) {
	return BMG_TELEMETRY_OFFSET + guidOffset + userOffset;
}
// xe_soc_remapper.c:15, 20-21: SG_REMAP_INDEX1 with the telemetry field set to the region (xe_mmio_rmw32).
static inline uint32_t xePmtRemapValue(uint32_t old, uint32_t index) {
	return (old & ~SG_REMAP_TELEM_MASK) | (index << SG_REMAP_TELEM_SHIFT & SG_REMAP_TELEM_MASK);
}

// regs/xe_pmt.h:15-16 ENERGY_PKG / ENERGY_CARD of the 64-bit energy word (xe_hwmon.c:525-528 REG_FIELD_GET64).
static inline uint32_t xePmtEnergyPkg(uint64_t v) { return (uint32_t)v; }
static inline uint32_t xePmtEnergyCard(uint64_t v) { return (uint32_t)(v >> 32); }

// xe_hwmon.c:111-118 struct xe_hwmon_energy_info and :534-535: the 32-bit counter wraps (after 2^32 >> 14 J = 262144 J,
// about 22 minutes at 200 W), so each read adds the difference modulo 2^32 to a 64-bit sum. The first read adds the
// counter itself (reg_val_prev starts at 0), so the sum counts from the counter's own start, as Linux's does.
struct XeEnergyAccum {
	uint32_t prev {0};
	uint64_t accum {0};
	void add(uint32_t reg) {
		accum += (uint32_t)(reg - prev);
		prev = reg;
	}
};
// xe_hwmon.c:537-538 mul_u64_u32_shr(accum, SF_ENERGY, shift): microjoules, with the product split so that it cannot
// overflow 64 bits ((q << s + r) * 1e6 >> s = q * 1e6 + (r * 1e6 >> s) exactly).
static inline uint64_t xeEnergyMicrojoules(uint64_t accum, uint8_t shift) {
	const uint64_t q = accum >> shift, r = accum & ((1ull << shift) - 1);
	return q * 1000000ull + (r * 1000000ull >> shift);
}

// The two hwmon channels (xe_hwmon.c:45-46 CHANNEL_CARD, CHANNEL_PKG) plus an average power per channel. Linux leaves the
// power average to user space (energyN_input over time); debug.intelxe.sensors has no history of its own, so the meter
// keeps the energy and time of the last reading at least minWindowNs old and reports the average since then. Readers
// closer together than that (sysctl reads twice: size, then text; two apps polling) get the last average again rather
// than one over a few microseconds.
enum : uint32_t { XE_ENERGY_CARD = 0, XE_ENERGY_PKG = 1, XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS = 2 };
// Sanity limits of one power window (this driver's, not Linux's: xe_hwmon hands out the energy sums only). On the B580
// right after a boot two windows read package 85 W and then 152 W against a card 37 W, which cannot be: the package is
// part of the card (xe_hwmon.c:1464-1472 labels the channels "card" and "pkg"). Later windows were consistent. Nothing
// in the read path explains it (the two counters are separate 32-bit words, each read whole under gPmtLock right
// after the re-mapper write, as xe_pmt_telem_read does), so it is taken as the firmware's counters running apart for a
// while (one updated later or filtered more than the other). Such a window is not reported: its averages are dropped
// (n/a), the base moves on to this reading, and the meter counts it. Rejected: either channel above
// XE_POWER_CEILING_MW (no Battlemage card draws that much; a counter that stepped back reads as ~262144 J), or the
// package above the card by more than a quarter of the card plus XE_POWER_PKG_SLACK_MW (the two counters are not
// sampled at the same instant, so a short window can see some of one without the other).
static constexpr uint64_t XE_POWER_CEILING_MW = 600000, XE_POWER_PKG_SLACK_MW = 10000;
static inline bool xePowerWindowSane(uint64_t cardMw, uint64_t pkgMw) {
	if (cardMw > XE_POWER_CEILING_MW || pkgMw > XE_POWER_CEILING_MW) return false;
	return pkgMw <= cardMw + cardMw / 4 + XE_POWER_PKG_SLACK_MW;
}
struct XeEnergyMeter {
	XeEnergyAccum ch[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS];
	uint64_t baseUj[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS] {}, baseNs {0};
	uint32_t mw[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS] {};   // average power of the last full window, milliwatts
	bool haveBase {false}, havePower {false};
	bool pkgValid {false};   // the package average of the last window passed xePowerWindowSane (card power still shown)
	bool resync {false};   // set at suspend: the counter may have restarted, so the next read only re-bases
	uint32_t rejected {0};   // windows xePowerWindowSane refused (reported n/a, re-based)
	uint8_t shift {XE_ENERGY_UNIT_MBX};
	uint64_t uj(uint32_t c) const { return xeEnergyMicrojoules(ch[c].accum, shift); }
	void update(uint64_t pmtVal, uint64_t nowNs, uint64_t minWindowNs) {
		const uint32_t reg[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS] = {xePmtEnergyCard(pmtVal), xePmtEnergyPkg(pmtVal)};
		if (resync) {
			// Sleep may have powered the card off and restarted the counters: a smaller value would read as a wrap of
			// 262144 J. Take the new values as the reference, keep the sum, and start a new power window.
			for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS; c++) ch[c].prev = reg[c];
			resync = haveBase = havePower = pkgValid = false;
		} else {
			for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS; c++) ch[c].add(reg[c]);
		}
		if (!haveBase || nowNs - baseNs >= minWindowNs) {
			if (haveBase) {
				const uint64_t dtUs = (nowNs - baseNs) / 1000 ? (nowNs - baseNs) / 1000 : 1;
				uint64_t mwide[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS];
				for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS; c++)
					mwide[c] = (uj(c) - baseUj[c]) * 1000 / dtUs;   // uJ / us = W; * 1000 = mW
				// Per channel: the card counter is the one that stays consistent (on the B580 the package counter ran at
				// 60-200 W against a 36 W card for the first 15+ minutes after boot), so a refused package window keeps
				// the card's average and reports only the package as n/a.
				havePower = mwide[XE_ENERGY_CARD] <= XE_POWER_CEILING_MW;
				pkgValid = havePower && xePowerWindowSane(mwide[XE_ENERGY_CARD], mwide[XE_ENERGY_PKG]);
				if (havePower) mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] = (uint32_t)mwide[XE_ENERGY_CARD];
				if (pkgValid) mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] = (uint32_t)mwide[XE_ENERGY_PKG];
				if (!pkgValid) rejected++;
			}
			for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS; c++) baseUj[c] = uj(c);
			baseNs = nowNs;
			haveBase = true;
		}
	}
};

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// xe_probe_css.h: the CSS header check XeProbe makes on a GuC image before stage 3 uploads it, and the version it
// carries (Linux xe_uc_fw.c parse_css_header / uc_fw_parse). Kept apart from xe_probe.cpp so that the host test
// (tests/probe_css_test.cpp) checks it against the linux-firmware images firmware/fetch.sh --probe pins.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include "guc_abi.h"

struct XpCss {
	uint32_t upload;   // bytes the DMA copies: the CSS header and the ucode
	uint32_t rsa;      // bytes of the RSA signature after them
	uint32_t ver;      // sw_version: major 23:16, minor 15:8, patch 7:0
	uint32_t priv;     // private_data_size: the GuC's private area after the ADS (8-9 MB in linux-firmware 20261019)
};
static constexpr uint32_t kXpCssMaxPriv = 64u << 20;   // more is not a GuC image the probe should map memory for

// false when the image is too short for its header, the header's sizes do not add up, the image is shorter than
// header + ucode + RSA, or the private data size is past kXpCssMaxPriv. Every size is checked before it is used, so a
// truncated or foreign file cannot make the probe read past the image.
static inline bool xpCssCheck(const uint8_t *image, uint32_t size, XpCss *out) {
	if (!image || size < sizeof(uc_css_header)) return false;
	const uc_css_header *css = reinterpret_cast<const uc_css_header *>(image);
	const uint64_t keys = (uint64_t)css->key_size_dw + css->modulus_size_dw + css->exponent_size_dw;
	if (css->header_size_dw < keys || (css->header_size_dw - keys) * 4 != sizeof(uc_css_header)) return false;
	if (css->size_dw < css->header_size_dw) return false;
	const uint64_t ucode = ((uint64_t)css->size_dw - css->header_size_dw) * 4, rsa = (uint64_t)css->key_size_dw * 4;
	const uint64_t upload = sizeof(uc_css_header) + ucode;
	if (ucode == 0 || upload + rsa > size || css->private_data_size > kXpCssMaxPriv) return false;
	if (out) {
		out->upload = (uint32_t)upload;
		out->rsa = (uint32_t)rsa;
		out->ver = css->sw_version;
		out->priv = css->private_data_size;
	}
	return true;
}

static inline uint32_t xpVerMajor(uint32_t v) { return (v >> 16) & 0xff; }
static inline uint32_t xpVerMinor(uint32_t v) { return (v >> 8) & 0xff; }
static inline uint32_t xpVerPatch(uint32_t v) { return v & 0xff; }

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Context image register layouts (set_offsets tables) copied from Linux drivers/gpu/drm/xe/xe_lrc.c
// (MIT, Copyright Intel Corporation; torvalds/master as of 2026-10-30): gen12/dg2 xcs, gen12/xehp/dg2/mtl/xe2 rcs,
// xe2 bcs/xcs. Encoding as in set_offsets(): NOP(n) skips n dwords, LRI(count, flags) starts a register list,
// REG/REG16 give offsets from the engine base. Used only by xe_probe.cpp.

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_recovery.h

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// rb8d: the pure parts of the job watchdog's recovery after the GuC resets a context (xe_core.cpp watchRun), so that
// tests/recovery_test.cpp builds them on the host.
//
// Linux (v7.1 xe_guc_submit.c): a CONTEXT_RESET_NOTIFICATION or NOTIFY_MEMORY_CAT_ERROR
// (xe_guc_exec_queue_reset_handler, xe_guc_exec_queue_memory_cat_error_handler: "Treat the same as engine reset") runs
// the queue's TDR at once (xe_guc_exec_queue_reset_trigger_cleanup): banned, scheduling disabled with the minimum
// preemption timeout, a GT reset if the GuC does not confirm within 5 s; ENGINE_FAILURE_NOTIFICATION (the GuC could not
// reset the engine) is a GT reset (xe_guc_exec_queue_reset_failure_handler). Every other queue goes on as before, and
// one whose job the GuC never starts is caught by its own TDR after job_timeout_ms, 5 s by default (xe_hw_engine.c
// hw_engine_init_early), which resets the GT for a job that never started (timeout_needs_gt_reset), twice per job
// (xe_sched_invalidate_job(job, 2)), and bans the queue after that.
//
// IntelXe's watchdog used one limit, debug.intelxe.job_timeout_ms (10 s, Linux's DRM_XE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX, since a
// started job's run time is checked on top), for a never-started job too, so the queue after a CAT fault waited 10 s
// (12 Nov: "seqno 3543 never started in 10020 ms: GT reset"). Now:
//  - a job that never started gets Linux's 5 s (xeNotStartedLimitMs: job_timeout_ms if lower), as Linux's TDR fires at
//    job_timeout_ms and does not wait for a run time a job that never started cannot have;
//  - for a while after the GuC reset a context of a reset domain (xeResetDomain: render and compute are one), a job of
//    that domain that has not started 2 s after both the reset and its own submission
//    (xeStuckAfterReset) means the engine kept the reset context (the 12 Nov dump: RING_CURRENT_LRCA unchanged, ACTHD 0)
//    and the GT is reset then rather than after the timeout. This is IntelXe's own shortcut (bounded, logged and counted:
//    debug.intelxe.stats "recovery"), taken under the same twice-per-job rule.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

static constexpr uint64_t kXeNotStartedMs = 5000;            // xe_hw_engine.c: job_timeout_ms = 5 * 1000
static constexpr uint64_t kXeStuckAfterResetNs = 2000000000ull;
static constexpr uint64_t kXeResetWindowNs = 30000000000ull;   // how long after a GuC context reset the shortcut applies

// The watchdog's limit for a job that never started, in ms (0: the watchdog is off).
static inline uint64_t xeNotStartedLimitMs(uint64_t jobTimeoutMs) {
	return jobTimeoutMs && jobTimeoutMs < kXeNotStartedMs ? jobTimeoutMs : jobTimeoutMs ? kXeNotStartedMs : 0;
}

// The reset domain of a primary-GT engine class (DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_*): render (0) and compute (4) share one
// (xe_gt.c xe_gt_any_hw_engine_by_reset_domain; the GuC's engine-reset save list carries RCU_MODE / CCS_MODE once for
// that domain, xe_guc_ads.c guc_mmio_regset_write), every other class is its own (domain = class + 8). -1: unknown.
static inline int xeResetDomain(uint16_t drmClass) {
	if (drmClass == 0 || drmClass == 4) return 0;
	return drmClass < 8 ? 8 + drmClass : -1;
}

// A job of a queue in the domain of a GuC context reset that happened at resetNs (0: none): outstanding since sinceNs
// (the watchdog's first sight of it), started or not. True: stuck behind the reset context.
static inline bool xeStuckAfterReset(uint64_t now, uint64_t resetNs, uint64_t sinceNs, bool started) {
	if (started || !resetNs || !sinceNs || now < resetNs || now - resetNs > kXeResetWindowNs) return false;
	const uint64_t from = sinceNs > resetNs ? sinceNs : resetNs;
	return now >= from && now - from >= kXeStuckAfterResetNs;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_sensors.h

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// debug.intelxe.sensors (text) and debug.intelxe.sensors_raw (uapi/intelxe_sensors.h, binary) from one sample. The
// pure parts live here so that tests/sensors_test.cpp builds them on the host: the sample filled from the register
// values, the energy meter and the power limits, and the text made from the sample, which is the text
// IntelXe::sensorsString printed before the binary form existed (IntelXe Manager and tools/regress parse it: the first
// "act", "req", "RP0", "RPn", "package", "VRAM", "card power" and "package power"; new fields only at the end). The
// register reads, the locks and the sysctls are in IntelXe.cpp.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include "uapi/intelxe_sensors.h"
#include "xe_pcode.h"
#include "xe_pmt.h"

struct XeSensorsSample {
	intelxe_sensors s {};
	bool energyKnown {false};   // the platform reads energy from PMT telemetry (BMG): the text has the energy fields
	int pmtErr {0};             // the telemetry read's errno (energy unavailable), with the GUID it used
	uint32_t guid {0};
	uint32_t rejected {0};      // power windows the meter refused (xePowerWindowSane)
	bool limitsKnown {false};   // has_mbx_power_limits (BMG): the text has the power limits
	XePowerLimits pl {};
};

// GT frequency fields are in units of 50/3 MHz (xe_guc_pc.c decode_freq)
static inline uint32_t xeSensorsMhz(uint32_t raw) { return (raw * 50 + 1) / 3; }

static inline void xeSensorsBegin(XeSensorsSample &x, uint32_t state, uint64_t nowNs) {
	x.s.version = INTELXE_SENSORS_VERSION;
	x.s.size = (uint32_t)sizeof(intelxe_sensors);
	x.s.state = state;
	x.s.timestamp_ns = nowNs;
}

// MTL_MIRROR_TARGET_WP1 (CAGF in 8:0), the request register (23+8:23), MTL_RP_STATE_CAP (RP0 8:0, RPn 24:16), the BMG
// package and VRAM temperature registers (degrees in 7:0). A device that reads all ones in WP1 and the cap does not
// answer: nothing is valid.
static inline void xeSensorsSetRegs(XeSensorsSample &x, uint32_t wp1, uint32_t req, uint32_t cap, uint32_t pkg, uint32_t vram) {
	if (wp1 == 0xffffffffu && cap == 0xffffffffu) {
		x.s.state = INTELXE_SENSORS_NO_ANSWER;
		return;
	}
	x.s.act_mhz = xeSensorsMhz(wp1 & 0x1ff);
	x.s.req_mhz = xeSensorsMhz(req >> 23 & 0x1ff);
	x.s.rp0_mhz = xeSensorsMhz(cap & 0x1ff);
	x.s.rpn_mhz = xeSensorsMhz(cap >> 16 & 0x1ff);
	x.s.pkg_temp_c = (int32_t)(pkg & 0xff);
	x.s.vram_temp_c = (int32_t)(vram & 0xff);
	x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_FREQ | INTELXE_SENSORS_TEMP;
}

// SLPC's efficient frequency and the range it runs with; 0 for max while SLPC has not started (no range then).
static inline void xeSensorsSetRange(XeSensorsSample &x, uint32_t rpe, uint32_t min, uint32_t max) {
	if (!max) return;
	x.s.rpe_mhz = rpe;
	x.s.min_mhz = min;
	x.s.max_mhz = max;
	x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_RANGE;
}

// After the meter took the telemetry word (err 0), or the read's error.
static inline void xeSensorsSetEnergy(XeSensorsSample &x, int err, uint32_t guid, const XeEnergyMeter &m) {
	x.energyKnown = true;
	x.pmtErr = err;
	x.guid = guid;
	if (err) return;
	x.rejected = m.rejected;
	for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS; c++) x.s.energy_uj[c] = m.uj(c);
	x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_ENERGY;
	if (m.havePower) {
		x.s.power_mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] = m.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD];
		x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_CARD;
	}
	if (m.pkgValid) {
		x.s.power_mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] = m.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG];
		x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_PKG;
	}
}

static inline void xeSensorsSetLimits(XeSensorsSample &x, const XePowerLimits &pl) {
	x.limitsKnown = true;
	x.pl = pl;
	if (pl.err) return;
	for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_PL_CHANNELS; c++)
		for (uint32_t l = 0; l < 2; l++) {
			x.s.limit_mw[c][l] = xePowerLimitMw(pl.word[c][l], XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX);
			if (pl.word[c][l] & PWR_LIM_EN) x.s.limit_on |= 1u << (c * 2 + l);
		}
	x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_LIMITS;
	if (!pl.i1Err) {
		x.s.crit_milli = xePowerI1Milli(pl.i1);
		x.s.crit_is_watts = (pl.i1 & POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS) ? 1 : 0;
		x.s.valid |= INTELXE_SENSORS_CRIT;
	}
}

// The debug.intelxe.sensors text. Returns what snprintf would (the length of the whole text, which may exceed len; the
// handler cuts it).
static inline int xeSensorsText(char *buf, size_t len, const XeSensorsSample &x) {
	const intelxe_sensors &s = x.s;
	switch (s.state) {
	case INTELXE_SENSORS_ASLEEP: return snprintf(buf, len, "unavailable (asleep)\n");
	case INTELXE_SENSORS_NOT_MAPPED: return snprintf(buf, len, "unavailable (not mapped)\n");
	case INTELXE_SENSORS_NO_ANSWER: return snprintf(buf, len, "unavailable (the device does not answer)\n");
	case INTELXE_SENSORS_NO_DEVICE: return snprintf(buf, len, "no device\n");
	default: break;
	}
	size_t n = (size_t)snprintf(buf, len, "act %u MHz, req %u MHz, RP0 %u MHz, RPn %u MHz, package %u C, VRAM %u C",
		s.act_mhz, s.req_mhz, s.rp0_mhz, s.rpn_mhz, (uint32_t)s.pkg_temp_c, (uint32_t)s.vram_temp_c);
	if (x.energyKnown) {
		if (x.pmtErr && n < len) {
			n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", energy unavailable (PMT error %d, GUID 0x%08x)", x.pmtErr, x.guid);
		} else if (n < len) {
			const uint64_t card = s.energy_uj[XE_ENERGY_CARD], pkg = s.energy_uj[XE_ENERGY_PKG];
			n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card energy %llu.%03llu J, package energy %llu.%03llu J",
				(unsigned long long)(card / 1000000), (unsigned long long)(card % 1000000 / 1000),
				(unsigned long long)(pkg / 1000000), (unsigned long long)(pkg % 1000000 / 1000));
			const uint32_t cmw = s.power_mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD], pmw = s.power_mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG];
			if (n < len && (s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_CARD))
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card power %u.%02u W", cmw / 1000, cmw % 1000 / 10);
			else if (n < len)
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card power n/a");
			if (n < len && (s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_PKG))
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", package power %u.%02u W", pmw / 1000, pmw % 1000 / 10);
			else if (n < len)
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", package power n/a");
			if (n < len) n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", power windows rejected %u", x.rejected);
		}
	}
	if (x.limitsKnown && n < len) n += xePowerLimitsText(buf + n, len - n, x.pl);
	if (n < len) n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, "\n");
	return (int)n;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/xe_slpcboost.h

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// slpcboost: debug.intelxe.slpc_boost, a ten-second lease on the GT's lowest clock that any user may ask for
// (docs/design/DESIGN-game-mode.md, section 2), and since 14 Nov the kernel's own short display lease on the same floor
// (dispboost, XeDispLease below; docs/design/DESIGN-display-boost.md). The pure parts, so that tests/slpcboost_test.cpp builds them on the host;
// the glue (the sysctl, the timer, the H2G) is in xe_core.cpp next to slpcParams.
//
// Linux (v7.2 xe_guc_pc.c) has one minimum: xe_guc_pc_set_min_freq (sysfs freq0/min_freq, root) checks RPn..RP0,
// returns -EAGAIN while the PC is not ready ("might be in the middle of a gt reset"), and pc_set_min_freq sends
// SLPC_PARAM_IGNORE_EFFICIENT_FREQUENCY (min < RPe) and then SLPC_PARAM_GLOBAL_MIN_GT_UNSLICE_FREQ_MHZ. The lease uses
// the same two parameters; what it adds is who may ask and for how long:
//  - a write of N MHz asks for a floor of N for kXeBoostLeaseNs after the write; a write before the end renews it (and
//    may change N); 0 ends it. One lease for the whole GPU, not one per requester: the latest write wins. Two users
//    share it: B's write replaces A's floor and end, and a release by either ends it for both (the other's next
//    renewal, every few seconds in the app, takes a new one). No user can hold the clock above the administrator's
//    ceiling or for longer than 10 s after the last write, so sharing costs at most power, never a lower floor;
//  - the floor is clamped to [RPn, the ceiling], the ceiling being debug.intelxe.slpc_max (0 = RP0) clamped to RPn..RP0
//    as slpcParams clamps it, so the lease never lifts the clock above what the administrator allowed. The minimum the
//    GuC is given while a lease runs is the higher of the lease's floor and the administrator's own (slpc_min): a lease
//    never lowers the floor;
//  - at most kXeBoostRateMax requests (N > 0) per kXeBoostRateWindowNs, whoever makes them (EBUSY beyond): a renewal
//    every few seconds needs one. Releases (0) are always taken and not counted;
//  - nothing while the GT is suspended, in a reset, wedged or without SLPC (EAGAIN, as Linux), except a release;
//  - system sleep ends the lease (the GuC is reset; the resume sends the administrator's floor).
//
// Live range (sysman2, 13 Nov): debug.intelxe.slpc_min and slpc_max are the administrator's floor and ceiling, root
// only, as Linux's freq0/min_freq and max_freq (xe_gt_freq.c min_freq_store / max_freq_store, mode 0644): a write is
// sent to the GuC at once while SLPC runs (xeSlpcKnobWrite: MAX = the new ceiling, then the minimum the lease rules
// give with it), and kept for every later SLPC start (bring-up, GT reset, wake: slpcParams), as Linux keeps
// user_requested_min/max and re-sends them from pc_adjust_requested_freq. Where Linux answers a value outside RPn..RP0
// with EINVAL, the knob takes it clamped to RPn..RP0 (xeSlpcKnobValue; 0 = the default: 1200 MHz floor, RP0
// ceiling); a negative value is EINVAL. Linux sends min > max as asked ("min becomes a fixed request"); so does this.
// With the lease: a lease still never goes above the ceiling (lowering slpc_max below a running lease lowers the
// minimum the GuC has at once) and never lowers the floor (raising slpc_min above a lease's floor raises the minimum);
// only who may write differs: slpc_boost any user for 10 s, slpc_min/max root until changed.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

static constexpr uint64_t kXeBoostLeaseNs = 10000000000ull;      // 10 s
static constexpr uint64_t kXeBoostRateWindowNs = 1000000000ull;  // 1 s
static constexpr uint32_t kXeBoostRateMax = 10;                  // writes per window
static constexpr uint64_t kXeBoostRetryNs = 100000000ull;        // a send the GT was not ready for: again in 100 ms
static constexpr uint32_t kXeSlpcDefaultMinMhz = 1200;           // BMG_MIN_FREQ (primary GT, every BMG), slpcParams' default

// The GT's frequency limits (from RP_STATE_CAP, MHz) and the administrator's knobs as the sysctls hold them.
struct XeSlpcBounds {
	uint32_t rpn, rp0;
	int userMin;   // debug.intelxe.slpc_min (<= 0: the default floor)
	int userMax;   // debug.intelxe.slpc_max (<= 0: RP0)
};

// slpcParams' ceiling: slpc_max or RP0, within RPn..RP0.
static inline uint32_t xeSlpcCeiling(const XeSlpcBounds &b) {
	uint32_t max = b.userMax > 0 ? (uint32_t)b.userMax : b.rp0;
	if (max > b.rp0) max = b.rp0;
	if (max < b.rpn) max = b.rpn;
	return max;
}

// slpcParams' floor without a lease: slpc_min or 1200, within RPn..RP0.
static inline uint32_t xeSlpcUserFloor(const XeSlpcBounds &b) {
	uint32_t min = b.userMin > 0 ? (uint32_t)b.userMin : kXeSlpcDefaultMinMhz;
	if (min < b.rpn) min = b.rpn;
	if (min > b.rp0) min = b.rp0;
	return min;
}

// A requested floor clamped to [RPn, the ceiling].
static inline uint32_t xeBoostClamp(uint32_t mhz, const XeSlpcBounds &b) {
	const uint32_t ceil = xeSlpcCeiling(b);
	if (mhz > ceil) mhz = ceil;
	if (mhz < b.rpn) mhz = b.rpn;
	return mhz;
}

// dispboost (docs/design/DESIGN-display-boost.md): the kernel's own short lease on the same floor, taken when a frame's GPU
// work was not done at the vblank it was due (NMXAccel's present worker tells IntelXe, "intelxeDispBoost"), the
// counterpart of i915's intel_display_rps_boost_after_vblank -> intel_rps_boost -> slpc_boost_work (min = boost_freq,
// RP0 by default). Rules:
//  - a miss while a display lease runs renews it (until = miss + lease length): it lasts only while misses keep coming;
//  - with no lease, a miss counts towards a streak (misses less than one lease length apart); the lease starts at the
//    streak's misses-th miss (debug.intelxe.disp_boost_misses; 1 = every miss, as i915), so one late frame of an
//    otherwise idle desktop does not lift the clock;
//  - at most kXeDispGrantMax new leases per kXeDispGrantWindowNs (renewals are not counted: they send nothing);
//  - the floor is debug.intelxe.disp_boost_mhz (0 = the ceiling: i915's boost_freq is RP0), clamped to [RPn, the
//    ceiling] like slpc_boost's, so never above slpc_max; it only ever raises the minimum the GuC gets;
//  - nothing while switched off, while the clock is under manual control (freq_manual), with the power-saving SLPC
//    profile (i915 does no waitboost there either), or while the GT cannot take a new minimum; each counted;
//  - system sleep and switching it off end the lease at once.
static constexpr uint32_t kXeDispCeiling = 0xffffffffu;           // disp.mhz meaning "the ceiling" (clamped where used)
static constexpr uint32_t kXeDispGrantMax = 5;                     // new display leases per window
static constexpr uint64_t kXeDispGrantWindowNs = 1000000000ull;    // 1 s

// Why a miss may not boost now (the glue decides; the pure part counts).
enum XeDispGate { kXeDispGateOk, kXeDispGateOff, kXeDispGateManual, kXeDispGatePowerSaving, kXeDispGateNotReady };
enum XeDispVerdict { kXeDispGranted, kXeDispRenewed, kXeDispStreak, kXeDispRateLimited, kXeDispIgnored };

struct XeDispLease {
	uint32_t mhz;          // the floor asked while the lease runs (0 = no lease; kXeDispCeiling = the ceiling)
	uint64_t untilNs;      // when it ends unless a miss renews it
	uint64_t startNs;      // when it began (the time boosted is counted when it ends)
	uint32_t streak;       // misses towards a new lease, each less than a lease length after the one before
	uint64_t lastMissNs;
	uint64_t windowNs;     // the grant rate limit's current window
	uint32_t windowGrants;
	// counters (debug.intelxe.disp_boost_stats)
	uint64_t misses;       // misses taken (whatever came of them)
	uint64_t grants, renewals, streakMisses, rateLimited, off, manual, powerSaving, notReady;
	uint64_t expiries, sleepEnds, knobEnds;
	uint64_t boostedNs;    // time with a display lease, the running one not included
};

struct XeSlpcBoost {
	uint32_t askedMhz;     // the active lease's request as written (0 = no lease); clamped where it is used
	uint64_t untilNs;      // when it ends
	uint32_t sentMhz;      // the minimum the GuC was last given (slpcParams or the lease); 0 = unknown, nothing to restore
	uint32_t sentMaxMhz;   // the maximum the GuC was last given (slpcParams or a slpc_max write); 0 = unknown
	uint64_t windowNs;     // the rate limit's current window
	uint32_t windowWrites;
	// counters (debug.intelxe.stats "slpc boost")
	uint32_t grants, renewals, releases, expiries, sleepEnds, rateLimited, notReady, clamped, sends;
	uint32_t rangeWrites, maxSends;   // slpc_min/slpc_max writes, MAX sends they made
	XeDispLease disp;      // dispboost: the display lease (its own counters)
};

enum XeBoostVerdict { kXeBoostGranted, kXeBoostRenewed, kXeBoostReleased, kXeBoostNoLease, kXeBoostRateLimited, kXeBoostNotReady };

static inline bool xeBoostActive(const XeSlpcBoost &s, uint64_t now) { return s.askedMhz && now < s.untilNs; }

// The lease's floor now (0 = none), clamped to the current bounds (slpc_max may have changed since the write).
static inline uint32_t xeBoostFloor(const XeSlpcBoost &s, const XeSlpcBounds &b, uint64_t now) {
	return xeBoostActive(s, now) ? xeBoostClamp(s.askedMhz, b) : 0;
}

static inline bool xeDispActive(const XeDispLease &d, uint64_t now) { return d.mhz && now < d.untilNs; }

// The display lease's floor now (0 = none), clamped to the current bounds.
static inline uint32_t xeDispFloor(const XeDispLease &d, const XeSlpcBounds &b, uint64_t now) {
	return xeDispActive(d, now) ? xeBoostClamp(d.mhz, b) : 0;
}

// The minimum the GuC should have now: the administrator's floor, raised to the leases' (slpc_boost's, the display's).
static inline uint32_t xeBoostEffectiveMin(const XeSlpcBoost &s, const XeSlpcBounds &b, uint64_t now) {
	const uint32_t user = xeSlpcUserFloor(b), lease = xeBoostFloor(s, b, now), disp = xeDispFloor(s.disp, b, now);
	const uint32_t m = lease > user ? lease : user;
	return disp > m ? disp : m;
}

// ms left on the lease (0 = none).
static inline uint64_t xeBoostLeftMs(const XeSlpcBoost &s, uint64_t now) {
	return xeBoostActive(s, now) ? (s.untilNs - now + 999999) / 1000000 : 0;
}

// A write of mhz (0 = release) at now. ready: the GT can take a new minimum (up, not suspended, not in reset, SLPC running).
// A release (0) is taken before the rate limit and does not count against it: it can only lower the clock back to the
// administrator's floor, and a client that hit EBUSY must still be able to end its lease (night of 13 Nov: eleven writes
// in a second, then the release was refused and the lease ran its 10 s).
static inline XeBoostVerdict xeBoostWrite(XeSlpcBoost &s, uint64_t now, uint32_t mhz, const XeSlpcBounds &b, bool ready) {
	const bool active = xeBoostActive(s, now);
	if (!mhz) {
		if (!active) {
			s.askedMhz = 0;
			return kXeBoostNoLease;
		}
		s.askedMhz = 0;
		s.untilNs = 0;
		s.releases++;
		return kXeBoostReleased;
	}
	if (!s.windowNs || now - s.windowNs >= kXeBoostRateWindowNs || now < s.windowNs) {
		s.windowNs = now ? now : 1;
		s.windowWrites = 0;
	}
	if (s.windowWrites >= kXeBoostRateMax) {
		s.rateLimited++;
		return kXeBoostRateLimited;
	}
	s.windowWrites++;
	if (!ready) {
		s.notReady++;
		return kXeBoostNotReady;
	}
	if (xeBoostClamp(mhz, b) != mhz) s.clamped++;
	s.askedMhz = mhz;
	s.untilNs = now + kXeBoostLeaseNs;
	if (active) s.renewals++;
	else s.grants++;
	return active ? kXeBoostRenewed : kXeBoostGranted;
}

// Ends the display lease at now (or at its own end, if that came first), adding its time to boostedNs. False: none ran.
static inline bool xeDispEnd(XeDispLease &d, uint64_t now) {
	if (!d.mhz) return false;
	const uint64_t end = now < d.untilNs ? now : d.untilNs;
	if (end > d.startNs) d.boostedNs += end - d.startNs;
	d.mhz = 0;
	d.untilNs = 0;
	d.streak = 0;
	return true;
}

// The time boosted so far, the running lease's part included.
static inline uint64_t xeDispBoostedNs(const XeDispLease &d, uint64_t now) {
	if (!d.mhz) return d.boostedNs;
	const uint64_t end = now < d.untilNs ? now : d.untilNs;
	return d.boostedNs + (end > d.startNs ? end - d.startNs : 0);
}

// The timer: a lease past its end is over. True when one ended now (slpc_boost's or the display's).
static inline bool xeBoostExpire(XeSlpcBoost &s, uint64_t now) {
	bool ended = false;
	if (s.disp.mhz && now >= s.disp.untilNs) {
		xeDispEnd(s.disp, now);
		s.disp.expiries++;
		ended = true;
	}
	if (!s.askedMhz || now < s.untilNs) return ended;
	s.askedMhz = 0;
	s.untilNs = 0;
	s.expiries++;
	return true;
}

// System sleep: the leases end, and the GuC forgets what it was given (the resume's slpcParams sends the administrator's
// floor and sets sentMhz again). now: for the display lease's time boosted (0: counted to its end).
static inline void xeBoostSleep(XeSlpcBoost &s, uint64_t now = 0) {
	if (s.askedMhz) s.sleepEnds++;
	s.askedMhz = 0;
	s.untilNs = 0;
	if (xeDispEnd(s.disp, now ? now : s.disp.untilNs)) s.disp.sleepEnds++;
	s.disp.streak = 0;
	s.sentMhz = 0;
	s.sentMaxMhz = 0;
}

// A missed vblank at now (dispboost). leaseNs: the lease length (debug.intelxe.disp_boost_ms); misses: the streak that
// starts a lease (>= 1); mhz: the floor to ask (0 = the ceiling). The glue then sends what is owed (xeBoostToSend).
static inline XeDispVerdict xeDispMiss(XeDispLease &d, uint64_t now, uint64_t leaseNs, uint32_t misses, uint32_t mhz,
                                       XeDispGate gate) {
	d.misses++;
	switch (gate) {
	case kXeDispGateOk: break;
	case kXeDispGateOff: d.off++; return kXeDispIgnored;
	case kXeDispGateManual: d.manual++; return kXeDispIgnored;
	case kXeDispGatePowerSaving: d.powerSaving++; return kXeDispIgnored;
	case kXeDispGateNotReady: d.notReady++; return kXeDispIgnored;
	}
	if (!misses) misses = 1;
	if (xeDispActive(d, now)) {   // still late with the floor raised: keep it while the misses go on
		if (now + leaseNs > d.untilNs) d.untilNs = now + leaseNs;   // never shortens a longer (idle-exit) lease
		d.lastMissNs = now;
		d.renewals++;
		return kXeDispRenewed;
	}
	if (d.mhz && xeDispEnd(d, now)) d.expiries++;   // ended, the timer not run yet: its time counted to its end
	if (d.streak && d.lastMissNs && now >= d.lastMissNs && now - d.lastMissNs < leaseNs) d.streak++;
	else d.streak = 1;
	d.lastMissNs = now;
	if (d.streak < misses) {
		d.streakMisses++;
		return kXeDispStreak;
	}
	if (!d.windowNs || now < d.windowNs || now - d.windowNs >= kXeDispGrantWindowNs) {
		d.windowNs = now ? now : 1;
		d.windowGrants = 0;
	}
	if (d.windowGrants >= kXeDispGrantMax) {
		d.rateLimited++;
		return kXeDispRateLimited;   // the streak stays: the next miss past the window starts the lease
	}
	d.windowGrants++;
	d.mhz = mhz ? mhz : kXeDispCeiling;
	d.startNs = now;
	d.untilNs = now + leaseNs;
	d.streak = 0;
	d.grants++;
	return kXeDispGranted;
}

// debug.intelxe.disp_boost written 0: the lease ends now. True when one ran.
static inline bool xeDispSwitchOff(XeDispLease &d, uint64_t now) {
	d.streak = 0;
	if (!xeDispEnd(d, now)) return false;
	d.knobEnds++;
	return true;
}

// What to send now: the effective minimum when it differs from what the GuC has (0: nothing). Nothing while sentMhz is
// unknown (before SLPC started, during sleep): slpcParams sends the whole set then.
static inline uint32_t xeBoostToSend(const XeSlpcBoost &s, const XeSlpcBounds &b, uint64_t now) {
	if (!s.sentMhz) return 0;
	const uint32_t want = xeBoostEffectiveMin(s, b, now);
	return want != s.sentMhz ? want : 0;
}

// When the timer should run next (0 = not needed): the end of the lease that ends first, or soon when a send is still
// owed.
static inline uint64_t xeBoostNextNs(const XeSlpcBoost &s, const XeSlpcBounds &b, uint64_t now) {
	if (xeBoostToSend(s, b, now)) return now + kXeBoostRetryNs;
	uint64_t next = s.askedMhz ? s.untilNs : 0;
	if (s.disp.mhz && (!next || s.disp.untilNs < next)) next = s.disp.untilNs;
	return next;
}

// A slpc_min / slpc_max write: false (EINVAL) for a negative value; else what the knob keeps: 0 (the default) as is, a
// value clamped to [RPn, RP0] once the GT's limits are known (rp0 != 0; before SLPC's first start slpcParams clamps).
static inline bool xeSlpcKnobValue(int mhz, uint32_t rpn, uint32_t rp0, int *out) {
	if (mhz < 0) return false;
	uint32_t v = (uint32_t)mhz;
	if (v && rp0) {
		if (v > rp0) v = rp0;
		if (v < rpn) v = rpn;
	}
	*out = (int)v;
	return true;
}

// The ceiling to send after a knob write (0: the GuC has it already, or what it has is not known).
static inline uint32_t xeSlpcMaxToSend(const XeSlpcBoost &s, const XeSlpcBounds &b) {
	if (!s.sentMaxMhz) return 0;
	const uint32_t want = xeSlpcCeiling(b);
	return want != s.sentMaxMhz ? want : 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// tlbinring: an EXEC whose only pending in-fences are TLB invalidations (a bind's out-fence since rb8d) waits for them on
// the GPU, at the head of its job, instead of in the FIFO; the pure parts, so that tests/tlbinring_test.cpp builds them
// on the host. docs/design/DESIGN-rb8-cost.md, "tlbinring".
//
// Linux (v6.18): xe_pt.c xe_pt_update_ops_run makes an unbind's fence the TLB invalidation job's fence ("tlb
// invalidation must be done before signaling unbind/rebind"; xe_tlb_inval_job.c xe_tlb_inval_job_push, run by its
// dep scheduler once the page-table update has signaled); vm_bind_ioctl_ops_fini signals it into the out-syncs. An exec
// that names the bind's syncobj gets it as a drm_sched dependency (xe_exec.c xe_exec_ioctl -> xe_sync.c
// xe_sync_entry_add_deps -> drm_sched_job_add_dependency), so the job's run_job (the ring write) happens only after
// xe_tlb_inval.c xe_tlb_inval_done_handler (or xe_tlb_inval_fence_timeout) signaled it. The job's own ring then
// invalidates the engine's TLB before the batch when the VM's tlb_flush_seqno moved (xe_sched_job.c xe_sched_job_arm,
// xe_ring_ops.c emit_pipe_invalidate(..., ring_ops_flush_tlb)).
//
// Here: the same order, kept on the GPU. The job goes to the ring (an armed direct-submission slot, or with
// debug.intelxe.tlb_inring 2 the normal ring path) with an MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT at its head, in the preparser-disabled
// part before the invalidating PIPE_CONTROL: poll the TLB word (a GGTT dword that the CPU sets to the invalidation
// done seqno whenever it moves: TLB_INVALIDATION_DONE, the fence timeout, a GT reset or resume) until it is >= the
// newest invalidation among the in-fences. Nothing of the job (the in-ring TLB flush, the batch, the user fence, the
// seqno) runs before every invalidation it depends on has completed on every GuC it went to, which is what Linux's
// dependency gives; only the place of the wait moves from the CPU to the command streamer. Freed memory is not
// involved: deferred frees wait for the CPU-side done seqno and the VM's jobs (xeDeferReady), as before.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include "xe_tlbinval.h"

// The value the TLB word gets: done on every GuC an invalidation goes to (the primary, and the media GuC while it is
// up), i.e. the one behind. tlbSeqDone(s) == xeSeqDone(xeTlbDoneBoth(...), s).
static inline uint32_t xeTlbDoneBoth(uint32_t primary, uint32_t media, bool mediaOn) {
	return !mediaOn || xeSeqDone(media, primary) ? primary : media;
}

// Whether the word moves from cur to v: forward in seqno order only (racing publishers, a late one with an older value,
// never move it back; the word is always a value that was done).
static inline bool xeTlbWordAdvances(uint32_t cur, uint32_t v) { return (int32_t)(v - cur) > 0; }

// MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT compares unsigned (COMPARE_OP_SAD_GTE_SDD: word >= target), the seqnos wrap at 2^32. A target is
// taken only when the unsigned order of word and target is their seqno order (word below it, or past it without a wrap
// in between: the wait then passes at once) and the target is nonzero and below kXeTlbWordGuard, so the word reaches
// it before it can wrap: stepping from below the target past 0xffffffff in one publish would need 2^20 invalidations
// issued and unanswered, while tlbStallCheck counts every invalidation done 2.25 s after its issue and each one is a
// VM_BIND, a queue create/destroy or a migrate window. Targets from the guard to the wrap (one in 4096 seqnos) take the
// old path. A job stranded anyway (beyond that bound) waits in the ring, not started, until the job watchdog's
// never-started rule resets the GT (twice, then bans the queue): it never runs early.
static constexpr uint32_t kXeTlbWordGuard = 0xfff00000u;

// What an EXEC's pending in-fences allow (deps: the unsignaled ones, its own queue's left out).
enum XeTlbInring : uint32_t {
	kXeTlbInringNone,    // no TLB-invalidation fence among them (nothing for this path)
	kXeTlbInringWait,    // only TLB-invalidation fences: *target, the newest, is what the job waits for in the ring
	kXeTlbInringOther,   // a TLB-invalidation fence and another kind (a job, a clear, a queued bind): the FIFO
	kXeTlbInringWrap,    // only TLB fences, but the target is not usable with an unsigned compare against word
};
static inline XeTlbInring xeTlbInringPlan(const XeFence *f, uint32_t n, uint32_t word, uint32_t *target) {
	bool tlb = false, other = false;
	uint32_t t = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		if (f[i].slot != kXeTlbSlot) {
			other = true;
			continue;
		}
		if (!tlb || !xeSeqDone(t, f[i].seqno)) t = f[i].seqno;   // invalidations complete in order: the newest covers all
		tlb = true;
	}
	*target = t;
	if (!tlb) return kXeTlbInringNone;
	if (other) return kXeTlbInringOther;
	if (!t || t >= kXeTlbWordGuard || (word <= t) != ((int32_t)(t - word) >= 0)) return kXeTlbInringWrap;
	return kXeTlbInringWait;
}

// Where such an EXEC goes. knob: debug.intelxe.tlb_inring (0 off, 1 armed queues, 2 any queue); haveWord: the TLB word
// is mapped (the direct-submission page exists); armed: the queue is in direct submission; free: nothing else holds
// the job back (FIFO empty, no TDR, no LR hold, no GT reset or sleep), the conditions under which an EXEC without
// in-fences goes to the ring at once.
enum XeTlbPath : uint32_t {
	kXeTlbPathOld,      // as before: the FIFO and the submit worker (an armed queue leaves direct submission first)
	kXeTlbPathDirect,   // the armed slot, the wait in the job's stub: the queue stays armed
	kXeTlbPathRing,     // the normal ring path, the wait in the ring (knob 2)
};
static inline XeTlbPath xeTlbInringPath(int knob, XeTlbInring plan, bool haveWord, bool armed, bool free) {
	if (knob <= 0 || plan != kXeTlbInringWait || !haveWord || !free) return kXeTlbPathOld;
	if (armed) return kXeTlbPathDirect;
	return knob >= 2 ? kXeTlbPathRing : kXeTlbPathOld;
}

// The wait itself, 5 dwords (xe_mi_commands.h MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT, XE_INSTR_NUM_DW(5)): MI_SEMW_GGTT, MI_SEMW_POLL,
// COMPARE_OP_SAD_GTE_SDD; data, address low, high, token. The armed direct-submission slot polls its mailbox the same way.
static inline uint32_t xeSemWaitGte(uint32_t *dw, uint32_t n, uint32_t ggtt, uint32_t value) {
	dw[n++] = 0x1cu << 23 | 1u << 22 | 1u << 15 | 1u << 12 | 3;
	dw[n++] = value;
	dw[n++] = ggtt;
	dw[n++] = 0;
	dw[n++] = 0;
	return n;
}
