// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The pure parts of the PPGTT TLB invalidation policy (rb8c), so that tests/tlbinval_test.cpp builds them on the host:
//  - the interval one VM_BIND's page-table changes must invalidate (XeInvalInterval, was BindCtx::touch), and the span a
//    page-table entry at a level stands for (xePtSpan): a change of an entry invalidates the whole span the entry maps,
//    as xe_pt.c xe_pt_update_ops_rfence_interval aligns an update's range to the span of the highest-level entry it
//    wrote. Splitting a live huge leaf (2 MB at level 1, 1 GB at level 2) is such a change of the parent entry;
//  - the range a PAGE_SELECTIVE invalidation is widened to (xe_guc_tlb_inval.c send_tlb_inval_ppgtt: a power of two,
//    aligned to itself, at least 4 KB, and at least 16 MB from 2 MB up: "Minimum invalidation size for a 2MB page that
//    the hardware expects is 16MB");
//  - when a deferred free may go: its TLB invalidation has completed AND every job the VM's queues had been handed
//    when the unbind was sealed has completed. xe frees page-table BOs and VM-private BO memory through TTM, whose
//    ttm_bo_release defers the release until every fence of the (VM-shared) dma-resv has signaled, BOOKKEEP included:
//    the exec jobs (xe_exec.c drm_gpuvm_resv_add_fence(..., DMA_RESV_USAGE_BOOKKEEP)) and the bind and TLB invalidation
//    fences (xe_pt.c xe_pt_update_ops_run). Before rb8c only the invalidation was waited for.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

// Bytes one entry of a level-`level` table maps (xe_pt_shift: 12 + 9 * level).
static inline uint64_t xePtSpan(int level) { return 1ull << (12 + 9 * level); }

// The VA interval one bind call's page-table changes cover (unions every touched range).
struct XeInvalInterval {
	bool any;
	uint64_t lo, hi;
	void touch(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
		if (!any) {
			any = true;
			lo = a;
			hi = b;
			return;
		}
		if (a < lo) lo = a;
		if (b > hi) hi = b;
	}
};

// send_tlb_inval_ppgtt's range for [start, end): false = a full invalidation instead (the length is beyond what a
// range invalidation encodes); else *outStart and *outLog2 (log2 of the length, >= 12).
static inline bool xeTlbInvalRange(uint64_t start, uint64_t end, uint64_t *outStart, uint32_t *outLog2) {
	if (end <= start || end - start > (1ull << 46)) return false;
	const uint64_t orig = start;
	uint64_t len = end - start < 0x1000 ? 0x1000 : end - start;
	uint64_t align = len <= 1 ? 1 : 1ull << (64 - __builtin_clzll(len - 1));   // roundup_pow_of_two
	start &= ~(align - 1);
	end = (end + align - 1) & ~(align - 1);
	len = align;
	while (start + len < end) {
		len <<= 1;
		start = orig & ~(len - 1);
	}
	if (len >= (2ull << 20)) {
		if (len < (16ull << 20)) len = 16ull << 20;
		start = orig & ~(len - 1);
	}
	*outStart = start;
	*outLog2 = (uint32_t)(63 - __builtin_clzll(len));
	return true;
}

// A deferred free's state: sealed (its bind call issued the invalidation it waits for), that invalidation done, the
// VM's jobs of that moment done. Only then may the memory be reused.
static inline bool xeDeferReady(bool sealed, bool tlbDone, bool jobsDone) { return sealed && tlbDone && jobsDone; }

// ─── rb8d: fences, and a VM_BIND's out-fence ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// A fence is one seqno on one in-order timeline: an exec queue's seqno slot (slot, generation), or the TLB invalidation
// sequence (slot kXeTlbSlot, seqno = the GuC TLB_INVALIDATION seqno: done once every GuC it went to has answered
// TLB_INVALIDATION_DONE up to it, which they do in order, as xe_tlb_inval_done_handler completes xe_tlb_inval fences in
// seqno order). slot kXeFenceDone: signaled. point: its timeline point while it sits in a timeline syncobj.
struct XeFence { uint64_t point; uint32_t slot, gen, seqno; };
// rb8f: kXeBindSlot, a queued VM_BIND's out-fence (xe_bindq.h: seqno = the call's serial, gen = its bind queue)
static constexpr uint32_t kXeFenceDone = ~0u, kXeTlbSlot = ~1u, kXeBindSlot = ~2u;
static inline XeFence xeTlbFence(uint32_t seq) { return XeFence{0, kXeTlbSlot, 0, seq}; }
static inline bool xeSeqDone(uint32_t done, uint32_t seq) { return (int32_t)(done - seq) >= 0; }

// What a VM_BIND's out-fences stand for: the copy-engine clears of the BOs it bound, and the TLB invalidation of what it
// unbound. xe_pt.c xe_pt_update_ops_run: "tlb invalidation must be done before signaling unbind/rebind": when an update
// needs an invalidation the fence it returns (and xe_vm.c vm_bind_ioctl_ops_fini signals into every out-sync and makes
// the bind queue's last fence) is the invalidation job's fence, which runs after the update job (xe_tlb_inval_job_push
// with the update's fence as dependency); the update job itself waits for the BOs' kernel fences (their clears). Before
// rb8d an unbind's out-fence here was the clear alone and signaled while the GPU could still translate through the
// entries the unbind removed. The fences of one bind queue signal in order (each bind job depends on the queue's last
// fence, xe_sched_job_last_fence_add_dep), so a bind's fence also covers the binds before it: next() folds the
// previous out-fence of the same bind queue in. rb8e: that is the queue the call names (exec_queue_id of a
// DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_VM_BIND queue), else the VM's default bind queue (xe_vm.c to_wait_exec_queue: q ?: vm->q[0];
// xe_exec_queue.c xe_exec_queue_last_fence_get / _set keep one last fence per exec queue): xeBindLast. WAS the VM's
// for every call, so a bind on one queue waited for another queue's invalidation.
struct XeBindFence { XeFence clear, tlb; };
// sig(fence): signaled now. clear: the latest clear among the BOs this call bound; unbound: the call removed or replaced
// entries and issued invalidation tlbSeq after its page-table writes. The clears all run on the kernel's migrate queue
// (one timeline, XeVm::kern), so the later of two stands for both; invalidation seqnos only grow.
template <typename Sig>
static inline XeBindFence xeBindFenceNext(const XeBindFence &prev, const XeFence &clear, bool unbound, uint32_t tlbSeq, Sig sig) {
	const XeFence done = {0, kXeFenceDone, 0, 0};
	XeBindFence n;
	const bool pc = sig(prev.clear), cc = sig(clear);
	if (cc) n.clear = pc ? done : prev.clear;
	else if (pc || prev.clear.slot != clear.slot || prev.clear.gen != clear.gen) n.clear = clear;
	else n.clear = xeSeqDone(clear.seqno, prev.clear.seqno) ? clear : prev.clear;
	if (unbound) n.tlb = xeTlbFence(tlbSeq);
	else n.tlb = sig(prev.tlb) ? done : prev.tlb;
	return n;
}
// debug.intelxe.bind_tlb_fence (rb8cost, DESIGN-rb8-cost.md): 1 (the default) keeps the invalidation in the out-fence
// above; 0 drops it (rb8b) and is honoured only when the kext was booted with -intelxe_unsafe_bindfence. Measured on the
// B580 (night of 13 Nov, Geekbench 6 OpenCL import, 3 runs each way): no speed difference, and its first run with 0 had
// 3 GuC context resets and a GT reset, so a plain root write must not be able to turn it off. Only 0 and 1 are taken.
enum XeKnobWrite : uint32_t { kXeKnobTaken, kXeKnobRange, kXeKnobLocked };
static inline XeKnobWrite xeBindTlbFenceWrite(int v, bool unlocked) {
	if (v != 0 && v != 1) return kXeKnobRange;
	if (!v && !unlocked) return kXeKnobLocked;
	return kXeKnobTaken;
}

// The fences an out-sync of the bind gets: the parts not signaled yet (a binary syncobj holds both, as a sync file's
// several; a timeline point gets both at the same point, reached when both are), or one signaled fence.
template <typename Sig>
static inline uint32_t xeBindFenceParts(const XeBindFence &f, XeFence out[2], Sig sig) {
	uint32_t n = 0;
	if (!sig(f.clear)) out[n++] = f.clear;
	if (!sig(f.tlb)) out[n++] = f.tlb;
	if (!n) out[n++] = XeFence{0, kXeFenceDone, 0, 0};
	return n;
}

// The invalidations the TLB fence watchdog completes without an answer (xe_tlb_inval.c xe_tlb_inval_fence_timeout: a
// fence pending longer than the timeout is signaled with -ETIME, and the done seqno moves past it): every seqno from
// the oldest pending (done + 1) up to issued whose issue time (a ring of the last 64, older ones read as the newest
// that overwrote them, which only delays) is at least timeoutNs old. Returns the new done value (done: none).
static inline uint32_t xeTlbTimedOut(uint32_t done, uint32_t issued, const uint64_t issueNs[64], uint64_t now, uint64_t timeoutNs) {
	uint32_t s = done;
	while (s != issued && (int64_t)(now - issueNs[(s + 1) & 63]) >= (int64_t)timeoutNs) s++;
	return s;
}

// rb8e: the TLB invalidation fence timeout. xe_guc_tlb_inval.c tlb_inval_timeout_delay: hw_tlb_timeout = HZ / 4 ("what
// HW/GuC needs to process TLB inv request") plus twice xe_guc_ct_queue_proc_time_jiffies ("the actual delay caused by
// the CTB transport"), which xe_guc_ct.c computes as (CTB_H2G_BUFFER_SIZE / SZ_4K) * HZ: one second per 4 KB of H2G
// ring ("a 4KiB buffer full of commands takes a little over a second to process"). xe_tlb_inval.c
// xe_tlb_inval_fence_timeout signals a fence once msecs_to_jiffies(now - inval_time) >= that delay. With Linux's 4 KB
// H2G ring (IntelXe's is the same size) 250 ms + 2 s = 2.25 s. WAS a fixed 1 s.
static constexpr uint64_t xeTlbTimeoutNs(uint32_t h2gBytes) {
	return 250000000ull + 2ull * (h2gBytes / 4096u) * 1000000000ull;
}

// rb8e: the bind queue whose last fence a VM_BIND folds in and replaces (xe_vm.c to_wait_exec_queue): the named bind
// queue's, or with exec_queue_id 0 the VM's default queue's.
static inline XeBindFence *xeBindLast(XeBindFence *namedQueue, XeBindFence *vmDefault) {
	return namedQueue ? namedQueue : vmDefault;
}

// rb8d: the operation dword of a GuC TLB_INVALIDATION action (xe_guc_tlb_inval.c MAKE_INVAL_OP: the type at
// XE_GUC_TLB_INVAL_TYPE_SHIFT 0, XE_GUC_TLB_INVAL_MODE_HEAVY (0) at XE_GUC_TLB_INVAL_MODE_SHIFT 8, and
// XE_GUC_TLB_INVAL_FLUSH_CACHE, bit 31). Types (abi/guc_actions_abi.h): FULL 0, PAGE_SELECTIVE 1, GUC 3 (the GGTT,
// send_tlb_inval_ggtt).
enum : uint32_t { kXeTlbInvalFull = 0, kXeTlbInvalPageSelective = 1, kXeTlbInvalGuc = 3 };
static inline uint32_t xeTlbInvalOp(uint32_t type) { return type << 0 | 0u << 8 | 1u << 31; }

// rb8d: a timeline syncobj's value (drm_syncobj_timeline: the highest point reached, i.e. it and every point before it
// have signaled), from its entries in the order they were added. A point that holds several fences (a bind's clear and
// invalidation, a transferred point of several queues) is reached once all of them are: the signaled entries at the
// point of the first unsignaled one do not count. WAS the last signaled entry before the first unsignaled one, which
// reported a two-fence point reached as soon as its first fence had signaled. *counted: how many leading entries
// count (signaled history; the caller keeps the last of them, carrying the value, and may drop the rest).
template <typename Sig>
static inline uint64_t xeTimelineValue(const XeFence *f, uint32_t n, Sig sig, uint32_t *counted) {
	uint32_t i = 0;
	while (i < n && sig(f[i])) i++;
	uint32_t last = i;
	while (last && i < n && f[last - 1].point >= f[i].point) last--;
	uint64_t v = 0;
	for (uint32_t k = 0; k < last; k++)
		if (f[k].point > v) v = f[k].point;
	*counted = last;
	return v;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// xe uAPI argument checks (xe_uapi_args.h), function by function after Linux drivers/gpu/drm/xe (MIT, dl/linux-xe):
// xe_bo.c, xe_sync.c, xe_vm.c, xe_wait_user_fence.c.
#include "xe_uapi_args.h"
#include <sys/errno.h>

// xe_bo.c MAX_USER_EXTENSIONS
static constexpr uint32_t kMaxUserExtensions = 16;

// gem_create_set_pxp_type: NONE is the default; HWDRM needs xe_pxp_key_assign, which is ENODEV with PXP off (xe->pxp
// NULL on every platform without has_pxp)
static int gemCreateSetPxpType(uint64_t value) {
	if (value == DRM_XE_PXP_TYPE_NONE) return 0;
	if (value != DRM_XE_PXP_TYPE_HWDRM) return EINVAL;
	return ENODEV;
}

// gem_create_user_ext_set_property: gem_create_set_property_funcs has the one entry PXP_TYPE (index 0)
static int gemCreateUserExtSetProperty(uint64_t extension, XeUserRead rd, void *ctx) {
	drm_xe_ext_set_property ext;
	if (rd(ctx, extension, &ext, sizeof(ext))) return EFAULT;
	// xe's three tests: below ARRAY_SIZE(gem_create_set_property_funcs), pad 0, and equal to the extension's name
	if (ext.property >= 1 || ext.pad || ext.property != DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_EXTENSION_SET_PROPERTY) return EINVAL;
	return gemCreateSetPxpType(ext.value);   // gem_create_set_property_funcs[DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_SET_PROPERTY_PXP_TYPE]
}

// gem_create_user_extensions: recursive in xe (ext_number + 1 per link), a loop here
int xeGemCreateExtensions(uint64_t ext, XeUserRead rd, void *ctx) {
	for (uint32_t n = 0; ext; n++) {
		if (n >= kMaxUserExtensions) return E2BIG;
		drm_xe_user_extension u;
		if (rd(ctx, ext, &u, sizeof(u))) return EFAULT;
		if (u.pad || u.name >= 1) return EINVAL;   // gem_create_user_extension_funcs has one entry, SET_PROPERTY (0)
		if (int err = gemCreateUserExtSetProperty(ext, rd, ctx)) return err;
		ext = u.next_extension;
	}
	return 0;
}

// xe_gem_create_ioctl up to xe_vm_lookup. The VRAM placement is bit 1 (tile 0's VRAM: XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM_MASK after the
// shift by ffs(XE_BO_FLAG_SYSTEM) - 1).
int xeGemCreateCheck(const drm_xe_gem_create &g, uint32_t memRegionMask, uint16_t graphicsVerx100) {
	constexpr uint32_t kFlags = DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_DEFER_BACKING | DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_SCANOUT |
		DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM | DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NO_COMPRESSION;
	if (g.pad[0] || g.pad[1] || g.pad[2] || g.reserved[0] || g.reserved[1]) return EINVAL;
	if ((g.placement & ~memRegionMask) || !g.placement) return EINVAL;   // at least one valid placement
	if (g.flags & ~kFlags) return EINVAL;
	if (g.handle) return EINVAL;
	if (!g.size) return EINVAL;
	if (g.size & 0xfff) return EINVAL;   // ~PAGE_MASK (size > SIZE_MAX cannot happen with a 64-bit size_t)
	if ((g.flags & DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NO_COMPRESSION) && graphicsVerx100 < 2000) return EOPNOTSUPP;
	const bool vram = g.placement & 2;   // bo_flags & XE_BO_FLAG_VRAM_MASK
	if ((g.flags & DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM) && !vram) return EINVAL;
	if (!g.cpu_caching || g.cpu_caching > DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC) return EINVAL;
	if (vram && g.cpu_caching != DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC) return EINVAL;
	if ((g.flags & DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_SCANOUT) && g.cpu_caching == DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB)
		return EINVAL;   // XE_BO_FLAG_FORCE_WC: display scan-out is never CPU-cache coherent
	return 0;
}

// xe_sync_entry_parse, up to the object lookups
int xeSyncEntryCheck(const drm_xe_sync &s, uint32_t flags) {
	if ((s.flags & ~(uint32_t)DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL) || s.reserved[0] || s.reserved[1]) return EINVAL;
	const bool signal = s.flags & DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL;
	switch (s.type) {
		case DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ:
			if ((flags & kXeSyncParseLrMode) && signal) return EOPNOTSUPP;
			if (s.addr >> 32) return EINVAL;   // upper_32_bits(sync_in.addr): the handle shares a union with addr
			return 0;
		case DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_TIMELINE_SYNCOBJ:
			if ((flags & kXeSyncParseLrMode) && signal) return EOPNOTSUPP;
			if (s.addr >> 32) return EINVAL;
			if (!s.timeline_value) return EINVAL;
			return 0;
		case DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_USER_FENCE:
			if (flags & kXeSyncParseDisallowUfence) return EOPNOTSUPP;
			if (!signal) return EOPNOTSUPP;
			if (s.addr & 0x7) return EINVAL;
			return 0;
		default:
			return EINVAL;
	}
}

// xe_vm_create_ioctl up to xe_vm_create: every check answers EINVAL, so their order does not matter
int xeVmCreateCheck(const drm_xe_vm_create &v, bool *lr) {
	constexpr uint32_t kAll = DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_SCRATCH_PAGE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE |
		DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT;   // ALL_DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAGS
	*lr = false;
	if (v.extensions || v.reserved[0] || v.reserved[1] || (v.flags & ~kAll)) return EINVAL;
	if ((v.flags & DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE) && !(v.flags & DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE)) return EINVAL;
	if ((v.flags & DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT) && !(v.flags & DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE)) return EINVAL;
	if (v.flags & DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE) return EINVAL;   // FAULT_MODE && !xe->info.has_usm
	*lr = (v.flags & DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE) != 0;
	return 0;
}

// xe_wait_user_fence_ioctl: VALID_FLAGS = ABSTIME, MAX_OP = LTE
int xeUfenceArgsCheck(const drm_xe_wait_user_fence &a) {
	if (a.extensions || a.pad || a.pad2 || a.reserved[0] || a.reserved[1]) return EINVAL;
	if (a.flags & ~(uint16_t)DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_FLAG_ABSTIME) return EINVAL;
	if (a.op > DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_LTE) return EINVAL;
	if (a.addr & 0x7) return EINVAL;
	return 0;
}

// do_compare after copy_from_user
int xeUfenceCompare(uint64_t rvalue, uint64_t value, uint64_t mask, uint16_t op) {
	bool passed;
	switch (op) {
		case DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_EQ: passed = (rvalue & mask) == (value & mask); break;
		case DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_NEQ: passed = (rvalue & mask) != (value & mask); break;
		case DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_GT: passed = (rvalue & mask) > (value & mask); break;
		case DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_GTE: passed = (rvalue & mask) >= (value & mask); break;
		case DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_LT: passed = (rvalue & mask) < (value & mask); break;
		case DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_OP_LTE: passed = (rvalue & mask) <= (value & mask); break;
		default: return EINVAL;   // XE_WARN_ON("Not possible"): the ioctl checked op
	}
	return passed ? 0 : 1;
}

// to_jiffies_timeout: negative = forever (and the field becomes MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT); 0 = no wait; else relative or
// absolute. xe never waits less than one jiffy for a nonzero timeout (`return timeout ?: 1`): a deadline already passed
// still gets one more look (now + 1).
int64_t xeUfenceDeadline(drm_xe_wait_user_fence &a, uint64_t now) {
	if (a.timeout < 0) {
		a.timeout = INT64_MAX;
		return INT64_MAX;
	}
	if (a.timeout == 0) return 0;
	const uint64_t n = now > (uint64_t)INT64_MAX - 2 ? (uint64_t)INT64_MAX - 2 : now;
	if (a.flags & DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_FLAG_ABSTIME) return (uint64_t)a.timeout <= n ? (int64_t)(n + 1) : a.timeout;
	// beyond MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT is "very long", not forever (MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT - 1)
	if ((uint64_t)a.timeout >= (uint64_t)INT64_MAX - n) return INT64_MAX - 1;
	return (int64_t)(n + (uint64_t)a.timeout);
}

// the tail of xe_wait_user_fence_ioctl
void xeUfenceTimeoutLeft(drm_xe_wait_user_fence &a, uint64_t start, uint64_t now) {
	if (a.flags & DRM_XE_UFENCE_WAIT_FLAG_ABSTIME) return;
	const uint64_t spent = now > start ? now - start : 0;
	a.timeout = spent >= (uint64_t)a.timeout ? 0 : a.timeout - (int64_t)spent;
}

bool xeSyncWaitEntryDone(uint64_t point, bool hasFence, bool fenceDone, uint64_t lastSubmitted, uint64_t value, bool avail) {
	if (!point) return hasFence && (avail || fenceDone);
	return value >= point || (avail && lastSubmitted >= point);
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The parts of the xe uAPI that are argument checks and arithmetic only: no device, no locks, no IOKit types, so
// tests/uapi_test.cpp builds them on the host (as xe_platform.cpp). Each function names the Linux function it follows
// (drivers/gpu/drm/xe, dl/linux-xe); xe_core.cpp calls them from the ioctls.
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include "uapi/xe_drm.h"

// Reads len bytes of the caller's memory at addr into dst: 0, or EFAULT (copyin in the kext, a fake memory in the test).
typedef int (*XeUserRead)(void *ctx, uint64_t addr, void *dst, size_t len);

// xe_bo.c gem_create_user_extensions -> gem_create_user_ext_set_property -> gem_create_set_pxp_type, on a device without
// PXP (Battlemage: bmg_desc has no has_pxp; xe_pxp_key_assign answers ENODEV). At most MAX_USER_EXTENSIONS (16) in the
// chain (E2BIG), each read once (EFAULT), base.pad 0 and name SET_PROPERTY (EINVAL), the property PXP_TYPE with pad 0
// (EINVAL); PXP_TYPE_NONE accepted, HWDRM ENODEV, any other type EINVAL.
int xeGemCreateExtensions(uint64_t ext, XeUserRead rd, void *ctx);

// xe_bo.c xe_gem_create_ioctl, its argument checks in its order, up to the VM lookup (the caller: ENOENT) and the
// extension chain (xeGemCreateExtensions). All EINVAL except NO_COMPRESSION below graphics 20 (EOPNOTSUPP): pad and
// reserved 0; a placement that is nonzero and within memRegionMask (xe->info.mem_region_mask: xePlatformMemRegionMask,
// 3 on a discrete part, 1 on an integrated one); only the four known flags; no handle; a nonzero size of whole pages;
// NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM only with a VRAM placement; cpu_caching WB or WC, WC for anything that may live in VRAM, not WB for
// a scan-out (XE_BO_FLAG_FORCE_WC).
int xeGemCreateCheck(const drm_xe_gem_create &g, uint32_t memRegionMask, uint16_t graphicsVerx100);

// xe_sync.c xe_sync_entry_parse, the checks that need no object: flags only SIGNAL and reserved 0 (EINVAL); syncobj
// types: no signal in LR mode (EOPNOTSUPP), a 32-bit handle (EINVAL), a nonzero timeline point (EINVAL); USER_FENCE:
// refused where the caller disallows it (EOPNOTSUPP: a VM_BIND without binds), never a wait (EOPNOTSUPP), 8-byte aligned
// (EINVAL). Other types EINVAL. The caller then looks the syncobj up (ENOENT) or, for a bind's user fence, reads the
// address once (user_fence_create's get_user: EFAULT).
enum : uint32_t {
	kXeSyncParseExec = 1u << 0,             // SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_EXEC
	kXeSyncParseLrMode = 1u << 1,           // SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_LR_MODE
	kXeSyncParseDisallowUfence = 1u << 2,   // SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_DISALLOW_USER_FENCE
};
int xeSyncEntryCheck(const drm_xe_sync &s, uint32_t flags);

// xe_vm.c xe_vm_create_ioctl, its argument checks: extensions and reserved zero, only ALL_DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAGS,
// FAULT_MODE only with LR_MODE, NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT only with FAULT_MODE (all EINVAL). FAULT_MODE is refused as xe refuses
// it on a device without has_usm (EINVAL): there is no GPU page-fault service here. LR_MODE without it is accepted
// (lrmode: xe_lr.h). *lr: the VM is long-running.
int xeVmCreateCheck(const drm_xe_vm_create &v, bool *lr);

// xe_wait_user_fence.c xe_wait_user_fence_ioctl, its argument checks in its order: extensions, pad, pad2 and reserved
// 0; only the ABSTIME flag; op at most LTE; addr 8-byte aligned. All EINVAL.
int xeUfenceArgsCheck(const drm_xe_wait_user_fence &a);

// xe_wait_user_fence.c do_compare once the value is read: 0 when (rvalue & mask) OP (value & mask) holds, 1 when it does
// not, EINVAL for an unknown op.
int xeUfenceCompare(uint64_t rvalue, uint64_t value, uint64_t mask, uint16_t op);

// xe_wait_user_fence.c to_jiffies_timeout in nanoseconds of the caller's clock (now): the deadline, INT64_MAX = forever,
// 0 = compare once. A negative timeout waits forever and is set to INT64_MAX in a (MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT), so the time
// left written back stays huge; ABSTIME is a deadline on that clock (xemac converts CLOCK_MONOTONIC to it).
int64_t xeUfenceDeadline(drm_xe_wait_user_fence &a, uint64_t now);

// After the wait (any outcome): a relative timeout loses the time waited, never below 0; an absolute one stays.
void xeUfenceTimeoutLeft(drm_xe_wait_user_fence &a, uint64_t start, uint64_t now);

// One entry of DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT / SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE_WAIT (drm_syncobj.c drm_syncobj_array_wait_timeout): point 0 (every
// binary wait, and a timeline wait for point 0) means the syncobj's current fence: available (WAIT_AVAILABLE) once it has
// one, done once that one has signaled. A timeline point above 0 is available once it was submitted, done once the
// timeline reached it. WAS: a point-0 entry of a TIMELINE_WAIT counted as available and done at once, so Mesa's
// WAIT_PENDING (always a TIMELINE_WAIT, point 0 for binaries) returned before the signalling submit reached the kernel
// and its SYNCOBJ_TRANSFER found no fence (EINVAL: a present answered VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN once the queue had a submit
// thread, 13 Nov).
bool xeSyncWaitEntryDone(uint64_t point, bool hasFence, bool fenceDone, uint64_t lastSubmitted, uint64_t value, bool avail);

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// VRAM and GGTT range allocators of IntelXe.kext (phase 2).
//
// VramBuddy follows drivers/gpu/drm/drm_buddy.c as xe_ttm_vram_mgr.c uses it: power-of-two blocks of a minimum chunk
// (64 KB, XE_VRAM_FLAGS_NEED64K / the 64K PTE granule), roots that are the largest naturally aligned blocks of the
// region (so a 2 MB or 1 GB block is aligned in device physical address space and can back a huge PTE), split on
// allocation and merged with their buddy on free; DRM_BUDDY_TOPDOWN_ALLOCATION (highest addresses first) for BOs the
// CPU never maps, best fit from the bottom otherwise; DRM_BUDDY_CONTIGUOUS_ALLOCATION as one power-of-two block whose
// unused tail is trimmed back (drm_buddy_block_trim). A BO's VRAM is a list of blocks (XeBo::blocks, linked by `link`).
// Callers hold gResLock.
//
// GgttRanges hands out GGTT address ranges to IntelXeFB (scan-out slots, cursor) instead of fixed addresses; IntelXe's own
// GGTT layout (IntelXe.h) stays below kGgttDispStart.
#include "IntelXe.h"
#include "xe_vram.h"
#include <sys/errno.h>

static VBlock *gNodeCache;

static VBlock *nodeNew(uint64_t off, uint8_t order, VBlock *parent) {
	VBlock *n = gNodeCache;
	if (n) gNodeCache = n->next;
	else n = static_cast<VBlock *>(IOMalloc(sizeof(VBlock)));
	if (!n) return nullptr;
	bzero(n, sizeof(*n));
	n->off = off;
	n->order = order;
	n->parent = parent;
	return n;
}

static void nodeDel(VBlock *n) {
	n->next = gNodeCache;
	gNodeCache = n;
}

static void listAdd(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *n) {
	n->state = kVFree;
	n->prev = nullptr;
	n->next = b->lists[n->order];
	if (n->next) n->next->prev = n;
	b->lists[n->order] = n;
	b->freeBytes += vblockSize(n);
}

static void listDel(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *n) {
	if (n->prev) n->prev->next = n->next;
	else b->lists[n->order] = n->next;
	if (n->next) n->next->prev = n->prev;
	n->prev = n->next = nullptr;
	b->freeBytes -= vblockSize(n);
}

bool buddyInit(VramBuddy *b, uint64_t start, uint64_t end) {
	bzero(b, sizeof(*b));
	start = (start + kVChunk - 1) & ~(kVChunk - 1);
	end &= ~(kVChunk - 1);
	b->start = start;
	b->end = end;
	for (uint64_t off = start; off < end;) {
		int o = kVMaxOrder;
		while (o > 0 && ((off & ((kVChunk << o) - 1)) || off + (kVChunk << o) > end)) o--;
		if (b->nRoots == sizeof(b->roots) / sizeof(b->roots[0])) return false;
		VBlock *r = nodeNew(off, (uint8_t)o, nullptr);
		if (!r) return false;
		b->roots[b->nRoots++] = r;
		listAdd(b, r);
		off += kVChunk << o;
	}
	b->size = b->freeBytes;
	return true;
}

static bool split(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *n) {
	const uint64_t half = vblockSize(n) / 2;
	VBlock *l = nodeNew(n->off, (uint8_t)(n->order - 1), n), *r = nodeNew(n->off + half, (uint8_t)(n->order - 1), n);
	if (!l || !r) {
		if (l) nodeDel(l);
		if (r) nodeDel(r);
		return false;
	}
	n->left = l;
	n->right = r;
	n->state = kVSplit;
	return true;
}

// Free block n (not on a list), merging with free buddies upwards.
static void freeBlock(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *n) {
	while (n->parent) {
		VBlock *p = n->parent, *bud = p->left == n ? p->right : p->left;
		if (bud->state != kVFree) break;
		listDel(b, bud);
		nodeDel(bud);
		nodeDel(n);
		p->left = p->right = nullptr;
		n = p;
	}
	listAdd(b, n);
}

// One block of `order`: across every free list of that order and above, the highest (topdown) or lowest address,
// split down to `order` keeping the half on that side.
static VBlock *allocOrder(VramBuddy *b, int order, bool topdown) {
	VBlock *best = nullptr;
	for (int o = order; o <= kVMaxOrder; o++)
		for (VBlock *n = b->lists[o]; n; n = n->next)
			if (!best || (topdown ? n->off > best->off : n->off < best->off)) best = n;
	if (!best) return nullptr;
	listDel(b, best);
	while (best->order > order) {
		if (!split(b, best)) {
			freeBlock(b, best);
			return nullptr;
		}
		VBlock *keep = topdown ? best->right : best->left, *other = topdown ? best->left : best->right;
		listAdd(b, other);
		best = keep;
	}
	best->state = kVAlloc;
	return best;
}

// drm_buddy_block_trim: keep the first `keep` bytes of allocated block n, give the rest back. Returns the kept blocks
// (address order, linked by `link`).
static VBlock *trim(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *n, uint64_t keep) {
	if (keep >= vblockSize(n) || !n->order) return n;
	if (!split(b, n)) return n;   // keep the whole block rather than fail
	const uint64_t half = vblockSize(n) / 2;
	VBlock *l = n->left, *r = n->right;
	l->state = kVAlloc;
	if (keep <= half) {
		freeBlock(b, r);
		return trim(b, l, keep);
	}
	r->state = kVAlloc;
	l->link = trim(b, r, keep - half);
	return l;
}

static int log2Floor(uint64_t v) { return 63 - __builtin_clzll(v); }

VBlock *buddyAlloc(VramBuddy *b, uint64_t size, bool topdown, bool contiguous) {
	size = (size + kVChunk - 1) & ~(kVChunk - 1);
	if (!size || size > b->freeBytes) return nullptr;
	const uint64_t chunks = size / kVChunk;
	if (contiguous) {
		int order = log2Floor(chunks);
		if ((1ull << order) < chunks) order++;
		if (order > kVMaxOrder) return nullptr;
		VBlock *n = allocOrder(b, order, topdown);
		return n ? trim(b, n, size) : nullptr;
	}
	// Largest blocks first (2 MB and up wherever the request and free space allow, for huge PTEs), smaller ones only
	// when the larger orders have nothing left.
	VBlock *head = nullptr, **tail = &head;
	uint64_t left = size;
	int cap = kVMaxOrder;
	while (left) {
		int o = log2Floor(left / kVChunk);
		if (o > cap) o = cap;
		VBlock *n = nullptr;
		for (; o >= 0 && !(n = allocOrder(b, o, topdown)); o--) {}
		if (!n) {
			buddyFree(b, head);
			return nullptr;
		}
		cap = o;   // nothing larger is free any more
		*tail = n;
		tail = &n->link;
		left -= vblockSize(n);
	}
	return head;
}

void buddyFree(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *list) {
	while (list) {
		VBlock *nx = list->link;
		list->link = nullptr;
		freeBlock(b, list);
		list = nx;
	}
}

// ─── GGTT ranges for IntelXeFB ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
static GgttRange gGgtt[64];
static uint32_t gGgttN;

int ggttRangeAlloc(uint64_t size, uint64_t align, bool fixed, uint32_t *addr) {
	size = (size + 0xfff) & ~0xfffull;
	if (!align || (align & (align - 1))) align = 0x1000;
	if (!size || gGgttN == sizeof(gGgtt) / sizeof(gGgtt[0])) return ENOSPC;
	uint64_t at = fixed ? *addr : kGgttDispStart;
	if (fixed && ((at & 0xfff) || at < kGgttDispStart || at + size > kGgttDispEnd)) return EINVAL;
	for (;;) {
		at = (at + align - 1) & ~(align - 1);
		if (at + size > kGgttDispEnd) return ENOSPC;
		uint32_t i = 0;
		while (i < gGgttN && (gGgtt[i].start + gGgtt[i].size <= at || gGgtt[i].start >= at + size)) i++;
		if (i == gGgttN) break;
		if (fixed) return EBUSY;
		at = gGgtt[i].start + gGgtt[i].size;
	}
	gGgtt[gGgttN++] = {(uint32_t)at, (uint32_t)size};
	*addr = (uint32_t)at;
	return 0;
}

void ggttRangeStats(uint32_t *n, uint64_t *bytes) {   // gResLock
	uint64_t b = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < gGgttN; i++) b += gGgtt[i].size;
	*n = gGgttN;
	*bytes = b;
}

int ggttRangeFree(uint32_t addr) {
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < gGgttN; i++)
		if (gGgtt[i].start == addr) {
			gGgtt[i] = gGgtt[--gGgttN];
			return 0;
		}
	return ENOENT;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// VRAM buddy allocator and GGTT range manager (xe_vram.cpp). Callers hold gResLock.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

static constexpr uint64_t kVChunk = 64ull << 10;   // minimum block: 64 KB
static constexpr int kVMaxOrder = 14;               // 64 KB << 14 = 1 GB
enum : uint8_t { kVFree = 1, kVAlloc = 2, kVSplit = 3 };

struct VBlock {
	uint64_t off;            // device physical address (DPA)
	uint8_t order, state;
	VBlock *parent, *left, *right;
	VBlock *prev, *next;     // free list of its order
	VBlock *link;            // the owning BO's block list
};
static inline uint64_t vblockSize(const VBlock *b) { return kVChunk << b->order; }

struct VramBuddy {
	uint64_t start, end, size, freeBytes;
	VBlock *lists[kVMaxOrder + 1];
	VBlock *roots[64];
	uint32_t nRoots;
};

bool buddyInit(VramBuddy *b, uint64_t start, uint64_t end);
VBlock *buddyAlloc(VramBuddy *b, uint64_t size, bool topdown, bool contiguous);
void buddyFree(VramBuddy *b, VBlock *list);

// GGTT addresses IntelXeFB may be given: above IntelXe's own objects (everything IntelXe.h places ends below 0x10000000).
static constexpr uint64_t kGgttDispStart = 0x10000000, kGgttDispEnd = 0xff000000;
struct GgttRange { uint32_t start, size; };
int ggttRangeAlloc(uint64_t size, uint64_t align, bool fixed, uint32_t *addr);
int ggttRangeFree(uint32_t addr);
void ggttRangeStats(uint32_t *n, uint64_t *bytes);   // IntelXeFB ranges in use (of 64) and their bytes

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// aspm_test: offline check of the ASPM path logic (xe_aspm.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. latency decoding equals Linux aspm.c calc_l0s_latency / calc_l1_latency / calc_l*_acceptable
//   2. link detection: root/downstream port above an endpoint or upstream port is a link; DSP under USP is not
//   3. the L1 checks: support on both ends (every function), pre-1.1, PCIe present, common clock, endpoint latency
//      with 1 us per link (pcie_aspm_check_latency), endpoints of other links
//   4. the plan: enable from the root port down, disable from the GPU up, disable-first when an ASPM bit is set,
//      L0s kept only where every end has it, multi-function order, nothing for links already in the target state
//   5. the report text decodes the registers
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o aspm_test aspm_test.cpp && ./aspm_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_aspm.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// A PCIe function: L1EL encoding l1e (1 us << e), L0s and L1 support, CCC/SLC, acceptable L1 encoding acc1
static XeAspmFn fn(uint16_t dev, uint8_t type, uint32_t l1e = 2, bool l1 = true, bool l0s = true, bool ccc = true,
	bool slc = true, uint32_t acc1 = 7, uint16_t aspm = 0, uint8_t func = 0) {
	XeAspmFn f = {};
	f.vendor = 0x8086;
	f.device = dev;
	f.fn = func;
	f.pcie = true;
	f.type = type;
	f.devCap = XE_DEVCAP_RBER | acc1 << 9 | 7u << 6;
	f.lnkCap = (l0s ? XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L0S : 0) | (l1 ? XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L1 : 0) | 3u << 12 | l1e << 15;
	f.lnkCtl = (uint16_t)((ccc ? XE_LNKCTL_CCC : 0) | aspm);
	f.lnkSta = (uint16_t)((slc ? XE_LNKSTA_SLC : 0) | 4 | 16 << 4);
	return f;
}

// The B580 path: link 0 = DSP e2f0 <-> GPU e20b, link 1 = root port <-> USP e2ff
static void b580(XeAspmLink *l, XeAspmEndpoint *eps, uint32_t *nEps, uint32_t gpuAcc = 6) {
	memset(l, 0, 2 * sizeof *l);
	l[0].up = fn(0xe2f0, XE_PCIE_DOWNSTREAM);
	l[0].down[0] = fn(0xe20b, XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT, 2, true, true, true, true, gpuAcc);
	l[0].nDown = 1;
	l[1].up = fn(0xa70d, XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT, 4);
	l[1].down[0] = fn(0xe2ff, XE_PCIE_UPSTREAM, 3);
	l[1].nDown = 1;
	eps[0] = XeAspmEndpoint{0x8086, 0xe20b, 3, 0, 0, l[0].down[0].devCap, 0, 0};
	*nEps = 1;
}

int main() {
	// 1. aspm.c:478-512
	CHECK(xeAspmL0sExitNs(0) == 64 && xeAspmL0sExitNs(6u << 12) == 4096 && xeAspmL0sExitNs(7u << 12) == 5000, "L0s exit");
	CHECK(xeAspmL1ExitNs(0) == 1000 && xeAspmL1ExitNs(6u << 15) == 64000 && xeAspmL1ExitNs(7u << 15) == 65000, "L1 exit");
	CHECK(xeAspmL0sAcceptableNs(0) == 64 && xeAspmL0sAcceptableNs(5u << 6) == 2048 && xeAspmL0sAcceptableNs(7u << 6) == UINT32_MAX,
		"L0s acceptable");
	CHECK(xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(0) == 1000 && xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(6u << 9) == 64000 && xeAspmL1AcceptableNs(7u << 9) == UINT32_MAX,
		"L1 acceptable");

	// 2. links
	CHECK(xeAspmIsLink(XE_PCIE_DOWNSTREAM, XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT), "DSP-endpoint");
	CHECK(xeAspmIsLink(XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT, XE_PCIE_UPSTREAM), "RP-USP");
	CHECK(xeAspmIsLink(XE_PCIE_ROOT_PORT, XE_PCIE_LEG_END), "RP-legacy endpoint");
	CHECK(!xeAspmIsLink(XE_PCIE_UPSTREAM, XE_PCIE_DOWNSTREAM), "USP-DSP is inside the switch");
	CHECK(!xeAspmIsLink(XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT, XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT), "endpoint-endpoint");

	// 3. checks
	XeAspmLink l[2];
	XeAspmEndpoint eps[XE_ASPM_MAX_EPS];
	uint32_t ne = 0;
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "B580 link 0: %u", xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why);
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 1, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "B580 link 1: %u", xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 1, eps, ne).why);
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 2, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_NO_FN, "link index past the path");

	// latency: link 1 exit = max(RP 16 us, USP 8 us) + 1 us for the link below = 17 us
	b580(l, eps, &ne, 4);   // GPU accepts 16 us
	XeAspmVerdict v = xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 1, eps, ne);
	CHECK(v.why == XE_ASPM_LATENCY && v.latencyNs == 17000 && v.acceptableNs == 16000, "link 1 latency: %u %u %u", v.why,
		v.latencyNs, v.acceptableNs);
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "link 0: 4 us within 16 us");
	b580(l, eps, &ne, 5);   // 32 us: both fine
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 1, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "link 1 within 32 us");
	b580(l, eps, &ne, 1);   // 2 us: link 0's own 4 us fails
	v = xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne);
	CHECK(v.why == XE_ASPM_LATENCY && v.latencyNs == 4000 && v.acceptableNs == 2000, "link 0 latency %u", v.latencyNs);
	// an endpoint behind another downstream port (audio): only link 1, 1 link below it
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	eps[ne++] = XeAspmEndpoint{0x8086, 0xe2f7, 5, 0, 0, XE_DEVCAP_RBER | 4u << 9, 1, 1};
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "audio does not constrain the GPU's link");
	v = xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 1, eps, ne);
	CHECK(v.why == XE_ASPM_LATENCY && v.index == 1 && v.latencyNs == 17000, "audio constrains link 1: %u %u", v.why, v.latencyNs);

	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[1].up.lnkCap &= ~XE_LNKCAP_ASPM_L1;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 1, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_NO_L1_UP, "root port without L1");
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "the other link unaffected");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[1] = fn(0xe2f7, XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT, 2, false, true, true, true, 7, 0, 1);
	l[0].nDown = 2;
	v = xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne);
	CHECK(v.why == XE_ASPM_NO_L1_DOWN && v.index == 1, "function 1 without L1");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[0].devCap &= ~XE_DEVCAP_RBER;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_PRE_1_1, "pre-1.1");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[0].pcie = false;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_NOT_PCIE, "not PCIe");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[0].lnkCtl &= (uint16_t)~XE_LNKCTL_CCC;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_CCC_INCONSISTENT, "CCC on one end only");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].up.lnkCtl &= (uint16_t)~XE_LNKCTL_CCC;
	l[0].down[0].lnkCtl &= (uint16_t)~XE_LNKCTL_CCC;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_CCC_NOT_SET, "shared clock, CCC clear");
	l[0].down[0].lnkSta &= (uint16_t)~XE_LNKSTA_SLC;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_OK, "separate clocks, CCC clear: allowed");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].nDown = 0;
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, ne).why == XE_ASPM_NO_FN, "no function");
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	CHECK(xeAspmL1Check(l, 2, 0, eps, XE_ASPM_MAX_EPS + 1).why == XE_ASPM_TOO_MANY, "too many endpoints");

	// 4. plan
	XeAspmStep st[64];
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	uint32_t n = xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 1, st, 64);
	CHECK(n == 2 && st[0].link == 1 && st[0].state == XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1 && st[1].link == 0 && st[1].state == XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1,
		"enable from the root port down: n %u [%u %u] [%u %u]", n, st[0].link, st[0].state, st[1].link, st[1].state);
	CHECK(xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 0, st, 64) == 0, "disable with ASPM already off: nothing");
	CHECK(xeAspmPlan(l, 2, -1, st, 64) == 0, "-1: nothing");
	// L1 already on both links: nothing to do; disable goes from the GPU up
	l[0].up.lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1, l[0].down[0].lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1;
	l[1].up.lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1, l[1].down[0].lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1;
	CHECK(xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 1, st, 64) == 0, "L1 already on");
	n = xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 0, st, 64);
	CHECK(n == 2 && st[0].link == 0 && st[0].state == 0 && st[1].link == 1 && st[1].state == 0, "disable from the GPU up");
	// L0s on both ends of link 1 stays; L1 on one end only of link 0: disabled first, then enabled
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[1].up.lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L0S, l[1].down[0].lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L0S;
	l[0].up.lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1;
	n = xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 1, st, 64);
	CHECK(n == 4, "steps %u", n);
	CHECK(st[0].link == 1 && st[0].state == 0 && st[1].link == 1 && st[1].state == (XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1 | XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L0S),
		"link 1: off, then L0s+L1 (%u %u)", st[0].state, st[1].state);
	CHECK(st[2].link == 0 && st[2].state == 0 && st[3].link == 0 && st[3].state == XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1,
		"link 0: off, then L1 (L0s dropped)");
	// L0s on one end only: dropped
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[0].lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L0S;
	n = xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 1, st, 64);
	CHECK(n == 3 && st[0].link == 1 && st[1].link == 0 && st[1].state == 0 && st[2].state == XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1, "L0s one end");
	// multi-function: enable function 0 first, disable the highest first
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[1] = fn(0xe2f7, XE_PCIE_ENDPOINT, 2, true, true, true, true, 7, 0, 1);
	l[0].nDown = 2;
	n = xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 1, st, 64);
	CHECK(n == 3 && st[1].link == 0 && st[1].fn == 0 && st[2].fn == 1, "enable: fn 0 then fn 1");
	l[0].up.lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1, l[0].down[0].lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1, l[0].down[1].lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1;
	n = xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 0, st, 64);
	CHECK(n == 2 && st[0].fn == 1 && st[1].fn == 0, "disable: fn 1 then fn 0");
	CHECK(xeAspmPlan(l, 2, 0, st, 1) == 1, "max respected");
	CHECK(xeAspmPlan(l, XE_ASPM_MAX_LINKS + 1, 1, st, 64) == 0, "too many links");
	// link state
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	CHECK(xeAspmLinkState(l[0]) == 0, "state off");
	l[0].up.lnkCtl |= XE_LNKCTL_ASPM_L1;
	CHECK(xeAspmLinkState(l[0]) == -1, "state differs");

	// 5. report
	char b[2048];
	size_t m = 0;
	b580(l, eps, &ne);
	l[0].down[0].l1ss = true;
	l[0].down[0].l1ssCap = 0x1f;
	l[0].down[0].l1ssCtl1 = 0;
	xeAspmFormatFn(b, sizeof b, &m, "down", l[0].down[0]);
	CHECK(strstr(b, "8086:e20b endpoint") && strstr(b, "ASPM support L0s L1") && strstr(b, "L1 4 us") &&
		strstr(b, "acceptable L0s any L1 64 us") && strstr(b, "ASPM-L1.1 ASPM-L1.2 PCIPM-L1.1 PCIPM-L1.2") &&
		strstr(b, "(enabled none)") && strstr(b, "gen 4 x16"), "report:\n%s", b);
	m = 0;
	v = XeAspmVerdict{XE_ASPM_LATENCY, 0, 17000, 16000};
	xeAspmFormatVerdict(b, sizeof b, &m, v, l[1], eps);
	CHECK(strstr(b, "needs 16000 ns or less, the link gives 17000 ns") != nullptr, "verdict: %s", b);
	m = 0;
	char small[16];
	xeAspmFormatFn(small, sizeof small, &m, "down", l[0].down[0]);
	CHECK(m < sizeof small && strlen(small) == m, "truncation: %zu", m);

	printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", checks, fails);
	return fails != 0;
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/barrevoke_test.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// barrevoke_test: offline check of the BAR-window revocation policy and state machine (xe_barrevoke.h,
// debug.intelxe.bar_revoke; docs/design/DESIGN-rebar-window.md section 8).
//   1. xeRevokeCheck: every reason a window BO is not taken, in its order, and the hot window (forced path: none)
//   2. xeRevokePick / xeRevokeCutoff: least recently touched first, ties larger first then by id; just enough to cover
//      the need; the cut-off of a pass over several clients takes the same BOs as one global pick
//   3. xeRevokeNext: every path through the state machine, enumerated, keeps the safety rules:
//      - the old VRAM is freed only after the verification, and never while the GPU is sent back to it;
//      - the CPU mapping never stays blocked: every path that blocked it unblocks it (Unblock or the redirect);
//      - the GPU PTEs are back on the VRAM in every final state but Done;
//      - the new pages are freed only where nothing can name them, never after a redirect that touched the mapping;
//      - a step that reported success without its effect latches the feature off;
//      - a verification that cannot run (no memory for its mapping) frees neither memory and latches off;
//      - barwin2: the descriptor whose pager the user's VM object faults through (the new pages' physical descriptor
//        after a transpose, the old one before or after a failed one) is never released while the BO lives;
//   4. the release rules alone (xeRevokeReleasable / xeRevokePagerOwners), the barwin release reproduced as a failure
//      - every (state, event) pair the caller can produce is valid, and no other is
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o barrevoke_test barrevoke_test.cpp && ./barrevoke_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_barrevoke.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static XeRevokeFacts good() {
	XeRevokeFacts f = {};
	f.size = 2ull << 20;
	f.touchNs = 1000000000ull;
	f.inWindow = f.mapped = f.contig = true;
	f.liveMaps = 1;
	return f;
}

// The path walker: applies events from s and checks the rules on the way. Returns the number of final states reached.
struct Walk {
	XeRevokeState s;
	bool blocked, gpuSys, vramFreed, vramKept, sysFreed, sysKept, latched, redirected, unblocked;
	uint16_t acts;
	char path[160];
};
static int finals;
static void walk(Walk w) {
	if (xeRevokeFinal(w.s)) {
		finals++;
		CHECK(!w.blocked, "%s: final with the CPU blocked", w.path);
		const bool onSys = w.s == kRsDone || w.s == kRsUndecided;
		CHECK(onSys ? w.gpuSys : !w.gpuSys, "%s: GPU on %s in final state %d", w.path, w.gpuSys ? "sys" : "VRAM", w.s);
		CHECK(w.vramFreed == (w.s == kRsDone), "%s: VRAM %s in state %d", w.path, w.vramFreed ? "freed" : "kept", w.s);
		CHECK(w.s != kRsUndecided || (w.vramKept && w.latched && !w.sysFreed), "%s: undecided must keep both", w.path);
		CHECK(!(w.sysFreed && w.sysKept), "%s: pages freed and kept", w.path);
		CHECK(!(w.sysFreed && w.redirected), "%s: pages freed after a redirect", w.path);
		CHECK(w.s != kRsDone || (!w.sysFreed && !w.sysKept), "%s: Done must keep the pages as the BO's", w.path);
		CHECK(w.s != kRsBroken || (w.latched && w.sysKept), "%s: Broken must latch off and keep the pages", w.path);
		CHECK(w.s != kRsRolledBack || w.sysFreed || w.sysKept, "%s: rolled back without deciding about the pages", w.path);
		// barwin2: the descriptor whose pager the user's object faults through is never released while the BO lives
		// (B580 14 Nov: released after the check, every later fault on a revoked BO was a SIGBUS)
		const uint8_t owners = xeRevokePagerOwners(w.s, w.acts), rel = xeRevokeReleasable(w.acts);
		CHECK(!(owners & rel), "%s: pager owner(s) %#x released (%#x)", w.path, owners, rel);
		CHECK(!(rel & kRdOld) || !(owners & kRdOld), "%s: old descriptor released while it may own the pager", w.path);
		CHECK((rel & kRdKmap) != 0, "%s: the kernel mapping must go", w.path);
		CHECK(!(w.acts & kRaAdoptDesc) || !(rel & kRdBridge), "%s: the map's bridge released", w.path);
		CHECK((w.acts & kRaAdoptDesc) || (rel & (kRdBridge | kRdPhys)) == (kRdBridge | kRdPhys),
			"%s: no redirect reached the map, but descriptors are kept", w.path);
		return;
	}
	for (int e = kReBlockOk; e <= kReVerifyUnknown; e++) {
		const XeRevokeStep st = xeRevokeNext(w.s, (XeRevokeEvent)e);
		if (!st.valid) {
			CHECK(st.next == w.s && !st.actions, "invalid step changes state or acts");
			continue;
		}
		Walk n = w;
		snprintf(n.path + strlen(n.path), sizeof(n.path) - strlen(n.path), ">%d", e);
		const uint16_t a = st.actions;
		if (e == kReBlockOk) n.blocked = true;
		if (e == kReRedirectOk || e == kReRedirectRefused) {
			CHECK(w.blocked, "%s: redirect while not blocked", n.path);
			n.blocked = false, n.redirected = true;
		}
		if (a & kRaUnblock) {
			CHECK(w.blocked, "%s: unblock while not blocked", n.path);
			n.blocked = false, n.unblocked = true;
		}
		if (e == kReRemapOk) n.gpuSys = true;
		if (a & kRaGpuBack) n.gpuSys = false;
		if (a & kRaFreeVram) {
			CHECK(!(a & kRaGpuBack), "%s: VRAM freed while the GPU goes back to it", n.path);
			CHECK(w.s == kRsRedirected && e == kReVerifyOk, "%s: VRAM freed before the verification", n.path);
			CHECK(!(a & kRaKeepVram), "%s: VRAM freed and kept", n.path);
			n.vramFreed = true;
		}
		if (a & kRaFreeSys) n.sysFreed = true;
		if (a & kRaKeepSys) n.sysKept = true;
		if (a & kRaKeepVram) n.vramKept = true;
		if (a & kRaLatchOff) n.latched = true;
		if (a & kRaAdopt) CHECK(st.next == kRsDone || st.next == kRsUndecided, "%s: adopted outside Done", n.path);
		if (a & kRaAdoptDesc) CHECK(w.s == kRsRedirected, "%s: descriptor adopted without a redirect", n.path);
		if (a & kRaAdoptDesc) CHECK(a & kRaKeepPagers, "%s: a redirect that reached the map must keep the pagers", n.path);
		// the GPU must still be on the VRAM while the CPU is blocked and the copy is not done
		if (xeRevokeCpuBlocked(st.next) && st.next != kRsGpuMoved) CHECK(!n.gpuSys, "%s: GPU on sys before the copy", n.path);
		CHECK(xeRevokeCpuBlocked(st.next) == n.blocked, "%s: blocked state %d vs walker %d", n.path, st.next, n.blocked);
		CHECK(xeRevokeGpuOnSys(st.next) == n.gpuSys || st.next == kRsRolledBack || st.next == kRsBroken,
			"%s: GPU state %d vs walker", n.path, st.next);
		n.s = st.next;
		n.acts |= a;
		walk(n);
	}
}

int main() {
	// 1.
	const uint64_t now = 10000000000ull, hot = 1000000000ull, max = 16ull << 20;
	{
		XeRevokeFacts f = good();
		CHECK(xeRevokeCheck(f, max, now, hot) == kRvOk, "good BO: %s", xeRevokeWhyName(xeRevokeCheck(f, max, now, hot)));
		struct { void (*set)(XeRevokeFacts &); XeRevokeWhy want; } cases[] = {
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.inWindow = false; }, kRvNotWindow},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.mapped = false; x.liveMaps = 0; }, kRvUnmapped},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.pinned = true; }, kRvPinned},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.shared = true; }, kRvShared},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.purgeable = true; }, kRvPurgeable},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.compressed = true; }, kRvCompressed},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.contig = false; }, kRvNotContig},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.size = 32ull << 20; }, kRvTooBig},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.size = (2ull << 20) + 1; }, kRvTooBig},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.size = 0; }, kRvTooBig},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.moving = true; }, kRvMoving},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.unusedMaps = 1; }, kRvInFlight},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.descBusy = true; }, kRvInFlight},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.liveMaps = 2; }, kRvMaps},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.liveMaps = 0; }, kRvMaps},   // mapped (sticky) but its mapping is gone
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.otherMaps = 1; }, kRvMaps},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.refsUnaccounted = true; }, kRvRefs},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.clearPending = true; }, kRvClear},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.vmBusy = true; }, kRvBusy},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.touchNs = now - hot / 2; }, kRvHot},
			{[](XeRevokeFacts &x) { x.touchNs = now + 5; }, kRvHot},
		};
		for (auto &cs : cases) {
			XeRevokeFacts x = good();
			cs.set(x);
			const XeRevokeWhy w = xeRevokeCheck(x, max, now, hot);
			CHECK(w == cs.want, "want %s, got %s", xeRevokeWhyName(cs.want), xeRevokeWhyName(w));
		}
		XeRevokeFacts x = good();
		x.touchNs = now - hot / 2;
		CHECK(xeRevokeCheck(x, max, now, 0) == kRvOk, "forced path ignores the hot window");
		x.touchNs = now - hot;
		CHECK(xeRevokeCheck(x, max, now, hot) == kRvOk, "exactly hotNs ago is cold");
		// order: a pinned BO that is also busy reports pinned (the cheaper, permanent reason first)
		x = good();
		x.pinned = x.vmBusy = true;
		CHECK(xeRevokeCheck(x, max, now, hot) == kRvPinned, "first reason wins");
		CHECK(!strcmp(xeRevokeWhyName(kRvHot), "hot") && !strcmp(xeRevokeWhyName((XeRevokeWhy)99), "?"), "names");
	}

	// 2.
	{
		XeRevokeCand c[6] = {{1 << 20, 500, 1}, {4 << 20, 100, 2}, {2 << 20, 300, 3}, {2 << 20, 100, 4}, {8 << 20, 900, 5},
			{4 << 20, 100, 6}};
		const uint32_t k = xeRevokePick(c, 6, 9 << 20);
		// order: t=100 (4 MB id 2, 4 MB id 6, 2 MB id 4), t=300, t=500, t=900
		CHECK(c[0].id == 2 && c[1].id == 6 && c[2].id == 4 && c[3].id == 3 && c[4].id == 1 && c[5].id == 5, "order %u %u %u %u %u %u",
			c[0].id, c[1].id, c[2].id, c[3].id, c[4].id, c[5].id);
		CHECK(k == 3, "9 MB needs the first three (4+4+2): %u", k);
		CHECK(xeRevokePick(c, 6, 0) == 0, "nothing needed");
		CHECK(xeRevokePick(c, 6, 100ull << 20) == 6, "more than all: all");
		CHECK(xeRevokePick(c, 0, 1) == 0, "none");
		CHECK(xeRevokePick(c, 6, 1) == 1, "one byte: one BO");
		// the cut-off over two clients equals a global pick
		XeRevokeCand a[3] = {{2 << 20, 50, 1}, {2 << 20, 700, 2}, {2 << 20, 200, 3}};   // client A
		XeRevokeCand b[3] = {{2 << 20, 100, 4}, {2 << 20, 800, 5}, {2 << 20, 150, 6}};  // client B
		XeRevokeCand all[6];
		memcpy(all, a, sizeof(a));
		memcpy(all + 3, b, sizeof(b));
		const uint64_t cut = xeRevokeCutoff(all, 6, 7 << 20);   // four BOs: 50, 100, 150, 200
		CHECK(cut == 200, "cut-off %llu", (unsigned long long)cut);
		uint32_t taken = 0;
		for (auto &x : a) taken += x.touchNs <= cut;
		for (auto &x : b) taken += x.touchNs <= cut;
		CHECK(taken == 4, "per-client pass at the cut-off takes %u", taken);
		CHECK(xeRevokeCutoff(all, 6, 0) == 0, "no need, no cut-off");
	}

	// 3.
	{
		Walk w = {};
		w.s = kRsStart;
		walk(w);
		CHECK(finals == 8, "paths to a final state: %d", finals);   // BlockFail, CopyFail, CopyLate, RemapFail, Refused,
		                                                              // VerifyFail, VerifyUnknown, Done
		// the expected outcomes, path by path
		struct { XeRevokeEvent ev[6]; int n; XeRevokeState end; uint16_t must, mustNot; } paths[] = {
			{{kReBlockFail}, 1, kRsRolledBack, kRaFreeSys, kRaUnblock | kRaFreeVram},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyFail}, 2, kRsRolledBack, kRaUnblock | kRaFreeSys, kRaFreeVram | kRaGpuBack},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyLate}, 2, kRsRolledBack, kRaUnblock | kRaKeepSys | kRaKeepVram, kRaFreeSys | kRaFreeVram},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyOk, kReRemapFail}, 3, kRsRolledBack, kRaUnblock | kRaGpuBack | kRaFreeSys, kRaFreeVram},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyOk, kReRemapOk, kReRedirectRefused}, 4, kRsRolledBack, kRaGpuBack | kRaKeepSys | kRaLatchOff,
				kRaUnblock | kRaFreeSys | kRaFreeVram},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyOk, kReRemapOk, kReRedirectOk, kReVerifyFail}, 5, kRsBroken,
				kRaGpuBack | kRaKeepSys | kRaLatchOff | kRaAdoptDesc, kRaFreeVram | kRaFreeSys | kRaUnblock},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyOk, kReRemapOk, kReRedirectOk, kReVerifyUnknown}, 5, kRsUndecided,
				kRaKeepVram | kRaLatchOff | kRaAdoptDesc | kRaKeepPagers, kRaFreeVram | kRaFreeSys | kRaGpuBack | kRaUnblock},
			{{kReBlockOk, kReCopyOk, kReRemapOk, kReRedirectOk, kReVerifyOk}, 5, kRsDone,
				kRaFreeVram | kRaAdopt | kRaAdoptDesc | kRaKeepPagers,
				kRaGpuBack | kRaFreeSys | kRaKeepSys | kRaLatchOff},
		};
		for (auto &p : paths) {
			XeRevokeState s = kRsStart;
			uint16_t acts = 0;
			bool ok = true;
			for (int i = 0; i < p.n; i++) {
				const XeRevokeStep st = xeRevokeNext(s, p.ev[i]);
				ok &= st.valid;
				acts |= st.actions;
				s = st.next;
			}
			CHECK(ok && s == p.end, "path of %d events ends in %d (want %d)", p.n, s, p.end);
			CHECK((acts & p.must) == p.must, "path of %d events: actions %#x lack %#x", p.n, acts, p.must);
			CHECK(!(acts & p.mustNot), "path of %d events: actions %#x include %#x", p.n, acts, acts & p.mustNot);
		}
		// events out of order are refused
		CHECK(!xeRevokeNext(kRsStart, kReVerifyOk).valid, "verify before anything");
		CHECK(!xeRevokeNext(kRsBlocked, kReRedirectOk).valid, "redirect before the copy");
		CHECK(!xeRevokeNext(kRsCopied, kReRedirectOk).valid, "redirect before the GPU moved");
		CHECK(!xeRevokeNext(kRsDone, kReBlockOk).valid, "nothing after Done");
		CHECK(!xeRevokeNext(kRsRolledBack, kReBlockOk).valid, "nothing after a rollback");
	}

	// 4.
	{
		const uint16_t done = kRaFreeVram | kRaAdopt | kRaAdoptDesc | kRaKeepPagers;
		CHECK(xeRevokeReleasable(done) == kRdKmap, "Done releases only the kernel mapping: %#x", xeRevokeReleasable(done));
		CHECK(xeRevokePagerOwners(kRsDone, done) == kRdPhys, "Done: the user's object faults through phys's pager");
		// barwin's release (bridge to the map, old descriptor and phys dropped): phys owned the pager -> SIGBUS
		const uint16_t barwin = kRaFreeVram | kRaAdopt | kRaAdoptDesc;
		CHECK(xeRevokeReleasable(barwin) & xeRevokePagerOwners(kRsDone, barwin) & kRdPhys,
			"the barwin rule released the pager owner (the B580 SIGBUS), so this check must see it");
		CHECK(xeRevokeReleasable(kRaUnblock | kRaFreeSys) == (kRdKmap | kRdBridge | kRdPhys), "copy failure releases all set-up");
		CHECK(xeRevokePagerOwners(kRsRolledBack, kRaGpuBack | kRaKeepSys | kRaLatchOff) == kRdOld, "refused: old owns it");
	}

	printf("%s: %d of %d checks failed\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails, checks);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/bindq_test.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// bindq_test: offline check of rb8f's pure parts (xe_bindq.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. xeBindPath: applied at once only with no in-fence pending and an idle bind queue (xe_pt.c
//      xe_pt_vm_dependencies: no_in_syncs and xe_exec_queue_is_idle, else a job); queued with the switch on, or behind
//      queued calls of the same queue whatever the switch; the old wait without room
//   2. the out-fence records (xeBjAlloc / xeBjPublish / xeBjSignaled): pending until applied and the bind fence the
//      apply produced has signaled; a full ring refuses; a record is reused only once its fence has signaled, and the
//      old fence then still reads signaled; the serial skips 0 across the wrap
//   3. xeBindPick: the oldest call of each bind queue only, in submission order; a ready call behind a blocked one of
//      its queue waits, a ready call of another queue does not
//   4. a model of the worker: random calls on three bind queues, with in-fences on exec-queue seqnos and on earlier
//      queued calls (other queues' and its own), random completions of execs, clears and invalidations: every call is
//      applied once, after its in-fences, each queue's calls in submission order; once a call's out-fence reads
//      signaled so do the earlier calls of its queue (so fenceMerge / surfAdd may keep the later of two fences of one
//      queue), and its own clear and invalidation have completed; everything is applied in the end
//   5. xeUfBusy (xe_vm.c check_ufence): EBUSY only for an op that removes or splits a VMA it meets whose user fence is
//      pending; UNMAP_ALL meets its object's VMAs; PREFETCH never
//   6. xeBindOpSpan / xeBindSpanOverlap: calls of two bind queues are ordered where their ranges overlap
//      (xe_pt_vm_dependencies, the VM's range fences); UNMAP_ALL meets everything, an empty range nothing
//   7. xeUfOrphanAction (xe_sync.c user_fence_worker, mmget_not_zero): written once ready while the process lives,
//      dropped once it is gone, dropped after the bound while pending
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o bindq_test bindq_test.cpp && ./bindq_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <vector>
#include "xe_bindq.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// ─── the fence world of the model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
static XeBjRec gTab[kXeBjMax];
static uint32_t gExecDone[4], gClearDone, gTlbDone;
static const uint32_t kClearSlot = 3;   // the migrate queue: clears, in order
static bool sig(const XeFence &f) {
	if (f.slot == kXeFenceDone) return true;
	if (f.slot == kXeTlbSlot) return xeSeqDone(gTlbDone, f.seqno);
	if (f.slot == kXeBindSlot) return xeBjSignaled(gTab, f, sig);
	return xeSeqDone(gExecDone[f.slot], f.seqno);
}
static const XeFence kDone = {0, kXeFenceDone, 0, 0};

static void testPath() {
	for (int a = 0; a < 2; a++)
		for (int in = 0; in < 2; in++)
			for (uint32_t qp = 0; qp < 2; qp++)
				for (int room = 0; room < 2; room++) {
					const XeBindPathKind k = xeBindPath(a, in, qp, room);
					XeBindPathKind want;
					if (!in && !qp) want = kXeBindNow;
					else if (room && (a || qp)) want = kXeBindQueue;
					else want = kXeBindWait;
					CHECK(k == want, "path async %d in %d queued %u room %d: %d, want %d", a, in, qp, room, k, want);
				}
	CHECK(xeBindPath(true, false, 0, false) == kXeBindNow, "nothing to wait for: applied at once");
	CHECK(xeBindPath(false, false, 3, true) == kXeBindQueue, "behind queued calls with the switch off: queued");
	CHECK(xeBindPath(false, true, 0, true) == kXeBindWait, "switch off, in-fence pending: the old wait");
}

static void testRecords() {
	memset(gTab, 0, sizeof gTab);
	memset(gExecDone, 0, sizeof gExecDone);
	gClearDone = gTlbDone = 0;
	uint32_t next = 1;
	std::vector<uint32_t> s;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kXeBjMax; i++) {
		const uint32_t v = xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig);
		CHECK(v == i + 1, "alloc %u: %u", i, v);
		s.push_back(v);
	}
	CHECK(xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig) == 0, "a full ring refuses");
	const XeFence f0 = xeBindJobFence(7, s[0]);
	CHECK(!sig(f0), "pending before its apply");
	// applied with a bind fence still pending (an invalidation)
	xeBjPublish(gTab, s[0], XeBindFence{kDone, xeTlbFence(5)});
	CHECK(!sig(f0), "applied, invalidation pending: not signaled");
	CHECK(xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig) == 0, "its record is not free while its fence is pending");
	gTlbDone = 5;
	CHECK(sig(f0), "applied, invalidation done: signaled");
	const uint32_t r = xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig);
	CHECK(r == kXeBjMax + 1 && r % kXeBjMax == s[0] % kXeBjMax, "reuse of the first record: %u", r);
	CHECK(sig(f0), "the old fence still reads signaled after its record was reused");
	CHECK(!sig(xeBindJobFence(7, r)), "the new call is pending");
	// wrap: serial 0 is never handed out
	memset(gTab, 0, sizeof gTab);
	next = 0xffffffffu;
	const uint32_t w1 = xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig), w2 = xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig);
	CHECK(w1 == 0xffffffffu && w2 == 1, "across the wrap: %u then %u", w1, w2);
	// a dropped call (published with signaled parts) signals at once
	xeBjPublish(gTab, w1, XeBindFence{kDone, kDone});
	CHECK(sig(xeBindJobFence(1, w1)), "dropped: signaled");
}

struct PNode { PNode *next; int q; bool ready; };
static void testPick() {
	PNode n[5] = {};
	const int qs[5] = {0, 1, 0, 2, 1};
	for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
		n[i].q = qs[i];
		n[i].next = i < 4 ? &n[i + 1] : nullptr;
	}
	auto key = [](PNode *p) { return p->q; };
	auto ready = [](PNode *p) { return p->ready; };
	CHECK(!xeBindPick(&n[0], key, ready), "nothing ready: none");
	n[2].ready = true;   // queue 0's second, behind its blocked first
	CHECK(!xeBindPick(&n[0], key, ready), "a ready call behind a blocked one of its queue waits");
	n[3].ready = true;   // queue 2's first
	CHECK(xeBindPick(&n[0], key, ready) == &n[3], "another queue's ready call goes");
	n[0].ready = true;
	CHECK(xeBindPick(&n[0], key, ready) == &n[0], "submission order among the ready oldest");
	n[4].ready = true;   // queue 1's second: its first (n[1]) is not ready
	n[0].ready = n[3].ready = false;
	CHECK(!xeBindPick(&n[0], key, ready), "queue 1's second waits for its first; queue 0's second for its first");
}

// ─── 4. the worker model ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
struct Job {
	Job *next;
	int q, idx;
	uint32_t serial;
	std::vector<XeFence> deps;
	bool clear, unbind;
};
static void testModel(unsigned seed) {
	srand(seed);
	memset(gTab, 0, sizeof gTab);
	memset(gExecDone, 0, sizeof gExecDone);
	gClearDone = gTlbDone = 0;
	uint32_t next = 1, execSeq[3] = {0, 0, 0}, clearSeq = 0, tlbSeq = 0;
	XeBindFence last[3] = {{kDone, kDone}, {kDone, kDone}, {kDone, kDone}};
	Job *head = nullptr, **tail = &head;
	std::vector<Job *> all;
	std::vector<std::vector<int>> applied(3);
	std::vector<int> made(3, 0);
	std::vector<XeFence> outs;   // every call's out-fence, in submission order
	std::vector<int> outQ, prevSame;   // the queue of each call, and the call before it on that queue (-1 none)
	int lastIdx[3] = {-1, -1, -1};
	int nApplied = 0, badDeps = 0, badOrder = 0, badMono = 0, badOwn = 0;
	auto step = [&]() {   // random completions
		for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++)
			if (rand() % 3 == 0 && gExecDone[k] != execSeq[k]) gExecDone[k]++;
		if (rand() % 3 == 0 && gClearDone != clearSeq) gClearDone++;
		gExecDone[kClearSlot] = gClearDone;
		if (rand() % 3 == 0 && gTlbDone != tlbSeq) gTlbDone++;
	};
	auto worker = [&]() {
		for (;;) {
			Job *j = xeBindPick(head, [](Job *p) { return p->q; }, [](Job *p) {
				for (const XeFence &d : p->deps)
					if (!sig(d)) return false;
				return true;
			});
			if (!j) return;
			for (const XeFence &d : j->deps) badDeps += !sig(d);
			if (!applied[j->q].empty() && applied[j->q].back() + 1 != j->idx) badOrder++;
			if (applied[j->q].empty() && j->idx != 0) badOrder++;
			applied[j->q].push_back(j->idx);
			XeFence clr = kDone;
			if (j->clear) clr = XeFence{0, kClearSlot, 0, ++clearSeq};
			if (j->unbind) ++tlbSeq;
			const XeBindFence out = xeBindFenceNext(last[j->q], clr, j->unbind, tlbSeq, sig);
			last[j->q] = out;
			xeBjPublish(gTab, j->serial, out);
			for (Job **pp = &head; *pp; pp = &(*pp)->next)
				if (*pp == j) {
					*pp = j->next;
					if (tail == &j->next) tail = pp;
					break;
				}
			nApplied++;
		}
	};
	const int kCalls = 3000;
	for (int i = 0; i < kCalls; i++) {
		const int q = rand() % 3;
		Job *j = new Job();
		j->q = q;
		j->idx = made[q]++;
		j->clear = rand() % 2;
		j->unbind = rand() % 2;
		// in-fences: an exec seqno handed out (maybe not done), an earlier call's out-fence (any queue)
		if (rand() % 2) {
			const int k = rand() % 3;
			j->deps.push_back(XeFence{0, (uint32_t)k, 0, ++execSeq[k]});
		}
		if (!outs.empty() && rand() % 2) j->deps.push_back(outs[(size_t)rand() % outs.size()]);
		j->serial = xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig);
		while (!j->serial) {   // ring full: the ioctl would wait; here completions run until a record is free
			step();
			worker();
			j->serial = xeBjAlloc(gTab, &next, sig);
		}
		*tail = j;
		tail = &j->next;
		all.push_back(j);
		outs.push_back(xeBindJobFence((uint32_t)q + 1, j->serial));
		outQ.push_back(q);
		prevSame.push_back(lastIdx[q]);
		lastIdx[q] = (int)outs.size() - 1;
		step();
		worker();
		// monotonic per queue (each sampled call against the one before it on its queue: transitively all of them),
		// and a signaled call's own parts complete
		for (int t = 0; t < 8; t++) {
			const size_t a = (size_t)rand() % outs.size();
			if (!sig(outs[a])) continue;
			if (prevSame[a] >= 0 && !sig(outs[(size_t)prevSame[a]])) badMono++;
			const XeBjRec &r = gTab[outs[a].seqno % kXeBjMax];
			if (r.serial == outs[a].seqno && !(sig(r.res.clear) && sig(r.res.tlb))) badOwn++;
		}
	}
	for (int guard = 0; head && guard < 100000; guard++) {   // everything completes in the end
		for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) gExecDone[k] = execSeq[k];
		gClearDone = clearSeq;
		gExecDone[kClearSlot] = gClearDone;
		gTlbDone = tlbSeq;
		worker();
	}
	gClearDone = clearSeq;
	gExecDone[kClearSlot] = gClearDone;
	gTlbDone = tlbSeq;
	int unsignaled = 0;
	for (const XeFence &f : outs) unsignaled += !sig(f);
	CHECK(!head && nApplied == kCalls, "seed %u: applied %d of %d", seed, nApplied, kCalls);
	CHECK(!badDeps, "seed %u: %d calls applied before an in-fence had signaled", seed, badDeps);
	CHECK(!badOrder, "seed %u: %d calls applied out of their queue's order", seed, badOrder);
	CHECK(!badMono, "seed %u: %d out-fences signaled before an earlier one of their queue", seed, badMono);
	CHECK(!badOwn, "seed %u: %d out-fences signaled with their own clear or invalidation pending", seed, badOwn);
	CHECK(!unsignaled, "seed %u: %d out-fences unsignaled once everything completed", seed, unsignaled);
	for (Job *j : all) delete j;
}

static void testUfBusy() {
	// removes/splits: MAP, UNMAP over a pending VMA
	CHECK(xeUfBusy(true, false, false, 0x10000, 0x10000, 0x18000, 0x1000, true), "UNMAP over part of a pending VMA: EBUSY");
	CHECK(!xeUfBusy(true, false, false, 0x10000, 0x10000, 0x20000, 0x1000, true), "adjacent, not overlapping: no");
	CHECK(!xeUfBusy(true, false, false, 0x10000, 0x10000, 0x18000, 0x1000, false), "signaled user fence: no");
	CHECK(!xeUfBusy(false, false, false, 0x10000, 0x10000, 0x18000, 0x1000, true), "PREFETCH: never");
	CHECK(xeUfBusy(true, true, true, 0, 0, 0x18000, 0x1000, true), "UNMAP_ALL of the VMA's object: EBUSY");
	CHECK(!xeUfBusy(true, true, false, 0, 0, 0x18000, 0x1000, true), "UNMAP_ALL of another object: no");
	CHECK(!xeRangeOverlap(0, 0, 0, 0x1000), "an empty range overlaps nothing");
	CHECK(xeRangeOverlap(0xfffff000ull, 0x2000, 0x100000000ull, 0x1000), "overlap across 4 GB");
}

static void testSpan() {
	const XeBindSpan a = xeBindOpSpan(false, 0x10000, 0x10000), b = xeBindOpSpan(false, 0x1f000, 0x1000),
		c = xeBindOpSpan(false, 0x20000, 0x1000), all = xeBindOpSpan(true, 0, 0), none = xeBindOpSpan(false, 0x10000, 0);
	CHECK(xeBindSpanOverlap(a, b) && xeBindSpanOverlap(b, a), "overlapping ranges of two queues: ordered");
	CHECK(!xeBindSpanOverlap(a, c), "adjacent ranges: not ordered");
	CHECK(xeBindSpanOverlap(all, c) && xeBindSpanOverlap(a, all), "UNMAP_ALL meets every range");
	CHECK(!xeBindSpanOverlap(none, a) && !xeBindSpanOverlap(all, none), "an empty range meets nothing");
	const XeBindSpan top = xeBindOpSpan(false, 0xffffffffe000ull, 0x2000);
	CHECK(xeBindSpanOverlap(top, all) && top.hi == 0x1000000000000ull, "the top of the 48-bit space");
}

static void testOrphan() {
	const uint64_t lim = kXeUfOrphanNs;
	CHECK(xeUfOrphanAction(true, true, 100, 0, lim) == kXeUfWrite, "ready, process alive: written");
	CHECK(xeUfOrphanAction(true, false, 100, 0, lim) == kXeUfDropGone, "ready, process gone: dropped");
	CHECK(xeUfOrphanAction(false, false, 100, 0, lim) == kXeUfDropGone, "pending, process gone: dropped");
	CHECK(xeUfOrphanAction(false, true, lim - 1, 0, lim) == kXeUfKeep, "pending within the bound: kept");
	CHECK(xeUfOrphanAction(false, true, 5 + lim, 5, lim) == kXeUfDropLate, "pending at the bound: dropped");
	CHECK(xeUfOrphanAction(true, true, 5 + 2 * lim, 5, lim) == kXeUfWrite, "ready late, process alive: written");
	CHECK(lim >= 10000000000ull + xeTlbTimeoutNs(4096), "the bound covers a started job's limit and the TLB fence timeout");
}

int main() {
	testPath();
	testRecords();
	testPick();
	for (unsigned s = 1; s <= 20; s++) testModel(s);
	testUfBusy();
	testSpan();
	testOrphan();
	printf("bindq_test: %d checks, %d failures\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/bootguard_test.cpp
