// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// bootguard_test: offline check of the boot guard's rules (uapi/intelxe_bootguard.h), which IntelXe.kext (bootGuardDecide,
// the firmware framebuffer on a held boot) and IntelXeFB.kext (guardBegin) share.
//   1. parsing intelxe-guard and the "ok means absent" rule
//   2. decide() against the rules IntelXeFB's guardBegin had before the shared header (written out below as
//      oldGuardBegin), over every combination of the guard, intelxe-accel-off and the two boot-args; and against
//      NMXAccel's nmxGuardHolds (nvrm-accel.cpp), which reads the same values
//   3. what a held boot shows (intelxe-held-display, boot-arg intelxe_helddisplay)
//   4. the state machine over several boots: crashes to safe and held, a held boot on the firmware framebuffer and what
//      it writes, clearing from that boot, a power cut that loses the kernel's writes, the old one-variable clear
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o bootguard_test bootguard_test.cpp && ./bootguard_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <string>
#include "uapi/intelxe_bootguard.h"

using namespace intelxeguard;

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// IntelXeFB guardBegin before intelxe_bootguard.h (0.1.4), with one deliberate change: an empty intelxe-accel-off counts
// as absent, as NMXAccel always read it (guardBegin read "" as set, nmxGuardHolds as clear: the two kexts disagreed).
struct Old { bool allowed, safePublished, wroteOff; unsigned accelFails, fbFails; int heldBy; };
static Old oldGuardBegin(const char *prev, const char *offIn, bool noaccel, bool safeMode)
{
	Old o = {};
	const bool had = prev && strcmp(prev, "ok") && prev[0];
	bool accelOff = offIn && offIn[0] && strcmp(offIn, "ok");
	bool byCount = false, fAccelSafe = false;
	if (had && !strncmp(prev, "accel", 5)) {
		unsigned n = 0;
		for (const char *c = prev + 5; *c >= '0' && *c <= '9' && n < 1000; c++) n = n * 10 + (unsigned)(*c - '0');
		o.accelFails = n ? n : 1;
		if (o.accelFails >= 4) { o.wroteOff = true; byCount = !accelOff; accelOff = true; }
		else if (o.accelFails >= 2) fAccelSafe = true;
	}
	if (had && prev[0] == 'f' && prev[1] == 'b') {
		unsigned f = 0;
		for (const char *c = prev + 2; *c >= '0' && *c <= '9' && f < 1000; c++) f = f * 10 + (unsigned)(*c - '0');
		o.fbFails = f ? f : 1;
	}
	o.heldBy = noaccel ? kHeldByBootArg : safeMode ? kHeldBySafeMode : accelOff ? (byCount ? kHeldByCount : kHeldByAccelOff) : kNotHeld;
	o.allowed = o.heldBy == kNotHeld;
	o.safePublished = o.allowed && fAccelSafe;
	return o;
}

// nvrm-accel.cpp nmxGuardHolds: what NMXAccel reads at its start
static bool nmxGuardHolds(const char *off, const char *guard)
{
	if (off && off[0] && strcmp(off, "ok")) return true;
	if (guard && !strncmp(guard, "accel", 5)) {
		unsigned n = 0;
		for (const char *c = guard + 5; *c >= '0' && *c <= '9' && n < 1000; c++) n = n * 10 + (unsigned)(*c - '0');
		if (n >= 4) return true;
	}
	return false;
}

static void testParse()
{
	CHECK(!isSet(nullptr) && !isSet("") && !isSet("ok") && isSet("o") && isSet("okay") && isSet("test") && isSet("accel1"), "isSet");
	struct { const char *v; char kind; unsigned n; } t[] = {
		{"", 0, 0}, {"ok", 0, 0}, {"accel", 'a', 1}, {"accel1", 'a', 1}, {"accel3", 'a', 3}, {"accel12", 'a', 12},
		{"accel0", 'a', 1}, {"fb", 'f', 1}, {"fb2", 'f', 2}, {"junk", '?', 0}, {"f", '?', 0},
	};
	for (const auto &c : t) {
		const Prev p = parsePrev(c.v);
		CHECK(p.kind == c.kind && p.n == c.n, "parsePrev(\"%s\") = %c%u, want %c%u", c.v, p.kind ? p.kind : '0', p.n, c.kind ? c.kind : '0', c.n);
	}
	CHECK(digitsAfter("99999") >= 1000 && digitsAfter("99999") < 100000, "digits are bounded");
}

static void testAgainstOld()
{
	const char *guards[] = {"", "ok", "accel", "accel1", "accel2", "accel3", "accel4", "accel5", "accel6", "accel10", "fb", "fb1", "fb3", "junk"};
	const char *offs[] = {"", "ok", "test", "4 accelerated boots in a row ended inside their first minute"};
	int n = 0;
	for (const char *g : guards)
		for (const char *o : offs)
			for (int na = 0; na < 2; na++)
				for (int sm = 0; sm < 2; sm++) {
					const Decision d = decide(g, o, na, sm);
					const Old r = oldGuardBegin(g, o, na, sm);
					n++;
					CHECK(d.accelAllowed == r.allowed && (d.accelAllowed && d.safe) == r.safePublished && d.writeAccelOff == r.wroteOff
					      && d.accelFails == r.accelFails && d.fbFails == r.fbFails && d.heldBy == r.heldBy,
					      "guard \"%s\" off \"%s\" noaccel %d -x %d: allowed %d/%d safe %d/%d write %d/%d accel %u/%u fb %u/%u heldBy %d/%d",
					      g, o, na, sm, d.accelAllowed, r.allowed, d.accelAllowed && d.safe, r.safePublished, d.writeAccelOff, r.wroteOff,
					      d.accelFails, r.accelFails, d.fbFails, r.fbFails, d.heldBy, r.heldBy);
					// the state follows from the rest
					const int want = !d.accelAllowed ? kHeld : d.safe ? kSafe : d.accelFails ? kRetry : kNormal;
					CHECK(d.state == want, "state %d, want %d", d.state, want);
					// NMXAccel holds exactly when the guard does by its NVRAM values (boot-args are its own checks)
					if (!na && !sm) CHECK(nmxGuardHolds(o, g) == !d.accelAllowed, "NMXAccel and the guard disagree on \"%s\" / \"%s\"", g, o);
				}
	CHECK(n == 14 * 4 * 4, "%d combinations", n);
	// the named cases
	CHECK(decide("accel1", "", false, false).state == kRetry, "one crash: try again");
	CHECK(decide("accel2", "", false, false).state == kSafe && decide("accel3", "ok", false, false).state == kSafe, "two or three: safe settings");
	CHECK(decide("accel4", "", false, false).state == kHeld && decide("accel4", "", false, false).heldBy == kHeldByCount, "four: held by the count");
	CHECK(decide("ok", "anything", false, false).heldBy == kHeldByAccelOff, "intelxe-accel-off holds");
	CHECK(decide("accel2", "", true, false).heldBy == kHeldByBootArg && !decide("accel2", "", true, false).safe, "a boot-arg hold has no safe settings");
}

static void testHeldDisplay()
{
	CHECK(heldDisplay(nullptr, -1) == kDisplayFirmware && heldDisplay("", -1) == kDisplayFirmware && heldDisplay("ok", -1) == kDisplayFirmware,
	      "default: the firmware framebuffer");
	CHECK(heldDisplay("fw", -1) == kDisplayFirmware && heldDisplay("firmware", -1) == kDisplayFirmware && heldDisplay("x", -1) == kDisplayFirmware,
	      "fw, firmware, anything unknown: firmware");
	CHECK(heldDisplay("fb", -1) == kDisplayFramebuffer && heldDisplay("framebuffer", -1) == kDisplayFramebuffer && heldDisplay("1", -1) == kDisplayFramebuffer,
	      "fb, framebuffer, 1: IntelXeFB");
	CHECK(heldDisplay("fb", 0) == kDisplayFirmware && heldDisplay("", 1) == kDisplayFramebuffer && heldDisplay("fw", 1) == kDisplayFramebuffer,
	      "the boot-arg wins");
	CHECK(heldDisplay("", 7) == kDisplayFirmware, "a boot-arg value other than 0/1 is ignored");
}

// ---- several boots ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// flash: what survives a power cut; mem: the running boot's NVRAM (kernel writes land here, reach flash at a clean
// shutdown); userspace nvram(8) writes both.
struct Nvram { std::string guard, off, display; };
enum Outcome { kHealthy, kPowerCut };   // a clean shutdown at the end, or the power gone (also how a panic is modelled)
struct Boot { int state, heldBy; bool firmware, safe; };

static Boot boot(Nvram &flash, Outcome how, bool noaccel = false, bool safeMode = false, bool clearFromDesktop = false,
                 bool clearOffOnly = false)
{
	Nvram mem = flash;
	const Decision d = decide(mem.guard.c_str(), mem.off.c_str(), noaccel, safeMode);
	const bool firmware = d.state == kHeld && heldDisplay(mem.display.c_str(), -1) == kDisplayFirmware;
	if (firmware) {   // IntelXe::bootGuardDecide; IntelXeFB does not start
		if (d.writeAccelOff) mem.off = "4 accelerated boots in a row ended inside their first minute";
		if (const char *g = guardAfterFirmwareHold(mem.guard.c_str(), d)) mem.guard = g;
	} else {          // IntelXeFB guardBegin, then the accelerated stage when allowed
		if (d.writeAccelOff) mem.off = "4 accelerated boots in a row ended inside their first minute";
		mem.guard = "fb" + std::to_string(d.fbFails + 1);
		if (d.accelAllowed) mem.guard = "accel" + std::to_string(d.accelFails + 1);
		if (how == kHealthy) mem.guard = "ok";   // healthy minute; guard-clear.sh writes it to flash at once
		if (how == kHealthy) flash.guard = "ok";
	}
	// the IntelXe Manager's "Clear the boot guard" from this boot's desktop (userspace: memory and flash)
	if (clearFromDesktop) { mem.off = "ok"; flash.off = "ok"; if (!clearOffOnly) { mem.guard = "ok"; flash.guard = "ok"; } }
	if (how == kHealthy) flash = mem;   // a clean shutdown flushes the kernel's writes
	return {d.state, d.heldBy, firmware, d.safe};
}

static void testBoots()
{
	Nvram nv;
	// a crash in the accelerated minute: the boot's other writes are lost, but the accel<n> IntelXeFB wrote at the arm is
	// what the next boot reads (the count went up over panics and held power buttons in the 5-6 Nov tests). Model: the
	// arm's value reaches flash, nothing else.
	auto crash = [&](bool noaccel = false) {
		const Decision d = decide(nv.guard.c_str(), nv.off.c_str(), noaccel, false);
		const Boot b = boot(nv, kPowerCut, noaccel);
		if (d.accelAllowed) nv.guard = "accel" + std::to_string(d.accelFails + 1);
		return b;
	};
	Boot b = crash();
	CHECK(b.state == kNormal && nv.guard == "accel1", "boot 1 normal, crashed: %s", nv.guard.c_str());
	b = crash();
	CHECK(b.state == kRetry && nv.guard == "accel2", "boot 2 retries: %s", nv.guard.c_str());
	b = crash();
	CHECK(b.state == kSafe && b.safe && nv.guard == "accel3", "boot 3 safe settings: %s", nv.guard.c_str());
	b = crash();
	CHECK(b.state == kSafe && nv.guard == "accel4", "boot 4 safe settings: %s", nv.guard.c_str());
	// boot 5: held by the count, the firmware framebuffer shows the desktop; a clean restart without clearing
	b = boot(nv, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld && b.heldBy == kHeldByCount && b.firmware, "boot 5 held on the firmware framebuffer");
	CHECK(nv.guard == "ok" && isSet(nv.off.c_str()), "boot 5 recorded the hold in intelxe-accel-off and cleared the count: %s / %s",
	      nv.guard.c_str(), nv.off.c_str());
	b = boot(nv, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld && b.heldBy == kHeldByAccelOff && b.firmware, "boot 6 still held (intelxe-accel-off)");
	// boot 7: the user clears from the held desktop (both variables), restarts
	b = boot(nv, kHealthy, false, false, true);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld, "boot 7 held, cleared from its desktop");
	b = boot(nv, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kNormal && nv.guard == "ok" && !isSet(nv.off.c_str()), "boot 8 normal and healthy");

	// a held boot whose kernel writes are lost (power cut): accel4 is still there, so the next boot is held the same way
	Nvram p; p.guard = "accel4";
	b = boot(p, kPowerCut);
	CHECK(b.firmware && p.guard == "accel4" && !isSet(p.off.c_str()), "power cut in a held boot: nothing changed in flash");
	b = boot(p, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld && b.heldBy == kHeldByCount && b.firmware, "and the next boot is held again");
	// the old instruction (intelxe-accel-off=ok only) from a held boot after its writes were flushed: enough
	b = boot(p, kHealthy, false, false, true, true);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld, "held, intelxe-accel-off=ok from its desktop");
	b = boot(p, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kNormal, "intelxe-accel-off=ok alone clears it once the held boot's own writes reached flash");
	// ... but not when those writes were lost: the Manager therefore clears both
	Nvram q; q.guard = "accel4";
	b = boot(q, kPowerCut, false, false, true, true);
	b = boot(q, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld, "intelxe-accel-off=ok alone after a power cut in the held boot: held again (clear both)");
	Nvram r; r.guard = "accel4";
	b = boot(r, kPowerCut, false, false, true, false);
	b = boot(r, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kNormal, "both cleared from the held desktop survive a power cut");

	// -intelxe_noaccel and safe mode: held on the firmware framebuffer, the count below the hold left for later
	Nvram s; s.guard = "accel2";
	b = boot(s, kHealthy, true);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld && b.heldBy == kHeldByBootArg && b.firmware && s.guard == "accel2", "boot-arg hold keeps accel2: %s", s.guard.c_str());
	b = boot(s, kHealthy, false, true);
	CHECK(b.heldBy == kHeldBySafeMode && b.firmware && s.guard == "accel2", "safe mode the same");
	b = boot(s, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kSafe && s.guard == "ok", "without them: the safe settings, then healthy");

	// intelxe-held-display=fb: IntelXeFB unaccelerated as before (it writes fb<n>, the hold stays in intelxe-accel-off)
	Nvram f; f.guard = "accel4"; f.display = "fb";
	b = boot(f, kHealthy);
	CHECK(b.state == kHeld && !b.firmware && isSet(f.off.c_str()) && f.guard == "ok", "fb: IntelXeFB held as before (%s)", f.guard.c_str());

	CHECK(guardAfterFirmwareHold("accel4", decide("accel4", "", false, false)) && !strcmp(guardAfterFirmwareHold("accel4", decide("accel4", "", false, false)), "ok"),
	      "a count that made the hold is cleared");
	CHECK(!guardAfterFirmwareHold("accel2", decide("accel2", "", true, false)) && !guardAfterFirmwareHold("fb2", decide("fb2", "x", false, false))
	      && !guardAfterFirmwareHold("accel4", decide("accel4", "", true, false).state == kHeld ? Decision{kNormal, 0, 4, 0, true, false, true} : Decision{}),
	      "anything else is left alone (a boot that is not held, a count below the hold, fb<n>)");
	CHECK(!strcmp(stateName(kHeld), "held") && !strcmp(stateName(kSafe), "safe") && !strcmp(heldByName(kHeldByCount), "count"), "names");
}

int main()
{
	testParse();
	testAgainstOld();
	testHeldDisplay();
	testBoots();
	printf("%s: %d checks, %d failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "ok", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/direct_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// direct_test: offline check of xe_direct.h (rb8e), no GPU needed. The post-stub direct submission calls between a
// job's cache flush and its seqno store holds what xe_ring_ops.c (v6.18) emits there for a job with a user fence:
//   - render / compute: emit_store_imm_ppgtt_posted (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM | MI_SDI_NUM_QW(1) = 0x10200003, address and
//     value as two dwords each, PPGTT: no MI_SDI_GGTT bit), then MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END
//   - copy / video: emit_flush_dw first (MI_FLUSH_DW | MI_FLUSH_IMM_DW = 0x13000002 and three zero dwords)
//   - no user fence: MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END alone
// and always fits the post-stub's kXeDsPostBytes.
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o direct_test direct_test.cpp && ./direct_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "xe_direct.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// xe_mi_commands.h (v6.18)
static constexpr uint32_t MI_INSTR(uint32_t op) { return op << 23; }
static constexpr uint32_t MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END = MI_INSTR(0xA), MI_STORE_DATA_IMM = MI_INSTR(0x20), MI_SDI_GGTT = 1u << 22,
	MI_FLUSH_DW = MI_INSTR(0x26), MI_FLUSH_IMM_DW = 4 - 2;
static constexpr uint32_t MI_SDI_NUM_QW(uint32_t x) { return (2 * x + 3 - 2) | 1u << 21; }

int main() {
	uint32_t dw[kXeDsPostBytes / 4 + 8];
	srandom(1);
	for (int r = 0; r < 20000; r++) {
		const bool rc = random() % 2, uf = random() % 4 != 0;
		const uint64_t addr = ((uint64_t)random() << 21 | (uint64_t)random() << 3) & 0xfffffffffff8ull,
			value = (uint64_t)random() << 33 ^ (uint64_t)random();
		for (uint32_t &d : dw) d = 0xdeadbeef;
		const uint32_t n = xeDsPostStub(dw, rc, uf, addr, value);
		CHECK(n * 4 <= kXeDsPostBytes && dw[kXeDsPostBytes / 4] == 0xdeadbeef, "%u dwords: beyond the post-stub", n);
		CHECK(dw[n - 1] == MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END, "round %d: does not end with MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END", r);
		if (!uf) {
			CHECK(n == 1, "no user fence: %u dwords", n);
			continue;
		}
		uint32_t i = 0;
		if (!rc) {
			CHECK(dw[0] == (MI_FLUSH_DW | MI_FLUSH_IMM_DW) && !dw[1] && !dw[2] && !dw[3], "copy/video: emit_flush_dw first");
			i = 4;
		}
		CHECK(dw[i] == (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM | MI_SDI_NUM_QW(1)) && dw[i] == 0x10200003u && !(dw[i] & MI_SDI_GGTT),
			"store header 0x%08x", dw[i]);
		CHECK(dw[i + 1] == (uint32_t)addr && dw[i + 2] == (uint32_t)(addr >> 32), "address");
		CHECK(dw[i + 3] == (uint32_t)value && dw[i + 4] == (uint32_t)(value >> 32), "value");
		CHECK(n == i + 6, "length %u", n);
	}
	printf("direct_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails != 0;
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/dispboost_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// dispboost_test: offline check of the display boost lease (xe_slpcboost.h, XeDispLease; docs/design/DESIGN-display-boost.md).
//   1. the streak: one late frame does not boost; the second within a lease length does; misses far apart never do;
//      disp_boost_misses 1 boosts on the first (i915's rule)
//   2. the floor: the ceiling (RP0, or slpc_max) or disp_boost_mhz clamped to it; never below slpc_min; the higher of the
//      display lease and slpc_boost's; the GuC told once, and back to the administrator's floor at the end
//   3. renewal: misses during the lease move its end; it ends a lease length after the last miss; the time boosted
//   4. rate limit: 5 new leases a second, renewals not counted; a new second takes them again
//   5. gates: off, freq_manual, the power-saving profile, a GT that cannot take it: counted, nothing changes
//   6. sleep and switching off end the lease at once (time counted to then); sleep leaves nothing to send
//   7. slpc_max lowered during a lease: the floor follows it at once
//   8. the timer late: a miss after the lease's end but before its timer ran starts a new streak, the old lease's time
//      counted to its end; xeBoostNextNs names the earlier of the two leases' ends
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o dispboost_test dispboost_test.cpp && ./dispboost_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include "xe_slpcboost.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static constexpr uint64_t s = 1000000000ull, ms = 1000000ull;
static constexpr uint64_t L = 50 * ms;   // debug.intelxe.disp_boost_ms default

// xe_core.cpp boostSync as far as the GuC is concerned: send what is owed.
static uint32_t sync(XeSlpcBoost &b, const XeSlpcBounds &bd, uint64_t now) {
	const uint32_t m = xeBoostToSend(b, bd, now);
	if (m) {
		b.sentMhz = m;
		b.sends++;
	}
	return m;
}
// A booted GT: slpcParams sent the administrator's floor.
static XeSlpcBoost fresh(const XeSlpcBounds &bd) {
	XeSlpcBoost b = {};
	b.sentMhz = xeSlpcUserFloor(bd);
	b.sentMaxMhz = xeSlpcCeiling(bd);
	return b;
}
static XeDispVerdict miss(XeSlpcBoost &b, uint64_t now, uint32_t misses = 2, uint32_t mhz = 0, XeDispGate g = kXeDispGateOk) {
	xeBoostExpire(b, now);   // the glue (dispRun) runs the timer's work first
	return xeDispMiss(b.disp, now, L, misses, mhz, g);
}

int main() {
	const XeSlpcBounds def = {400, 2850, 0, 0};   // the B580: RPn 400, RP0 2850; slpc_min/max at their defaults
	const uint64_t t = 7 * s;

	// 1.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		CHECK(miss(b, t) == kXeDispStreak && !xeDispActive(b.disp, t) && sync(b, def, t) == 0, "one late frame: nothing");
		CHECK(miss(b, t + 11 * ms) == kXeDispGranted && xeDispActive(b.disp, t + 11 * ms), "the second, 11 ms later: lease");
		CHECK(b.disp.grants == 1 && b.disp.streakMisses == 1 && b.disp.misses == 2, "counted");
		XeSlpcBoost f = fresh(def);
		for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) CHECK(miss(f, t + (uint64_t)i * 200 * ms) == kXeDispStreak, "misses 200 ms apart (%d)", i);
		CHECK(!f.disp.grants && f.disp.streakMisses == 10, "never a lease");
		CHECK(miss(f, t + 1800 * ms + L - 1) == kXeDispGranted, "but one within a lease length of the last: lease");
		XeSlpcBoost one = fresh(def);
		CHECK(miss(one, t, 1) == kXeDispGranted, "disp_boost_misses 1: the first miss boosts");
		XeSlpcBoost three = fresh(def);
		CHECK(miss(three, t, 3) == kXeDispStreak && miss(three, t + 5 * ms, 3) == kXeDispStreak &&
			miss(three, t + 10 * ms, 3) == kXeDispGranted, "disp_boost_misses 3: the third");
	}
	// 2.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		miss(b, t);
		miss(b, t + 5 * ms);
		CHECK(xeDispFloor(b.disp, def, t + 5 * ms) == 2850 && xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, def, t + 5 * ms) == 2850, "floor RP0");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t + 5 * ms) == 2850 && sync(b, def, t + 6 * ms) == 0, "the GuC told once");
		const uint64_t end = t + 5 * ms + L;
		CHECK(xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t + 6 * ms) == end, "the timer at the lease's end");
		CHECK(xeBoostExpire(b, end) && b.disp.expiries == 1 && !b.disp.mhz, "expired");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, end) == 1200 && xeBoostNextNs(b, def, end) == 0, "back to the default floor, nothing more");

		const XeSlpcBounds capped = {400, 2850, 0, 2400};   // slpc_max 2400
		XeSlpcBoost c = fresh(capped);
		miss(c, t, 1);
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(c, capped, t) == 2400, "never above slpc_max");
		XeSlpcBoost m = fresh(def);
		miss(m, t, 1, 2000);
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(m, def, t) == 2000, "disp_boost_mhz 2000");
		XeSlpcBoost m2 = fresh(capped);
		miss(m2, t, 1, 2600);
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(m2, capped, t) == 2400, "disp_boost_mhz above slpc_max: slpc_max");
		const XeSlpcBounds high = {400, 2850, 2600, 0};   // slpc_min 2600
		XeSlpcBoost h = fresh(high);
		miss(h, t, 1, 2000);
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(h, high, t) == 2600 && sync(h, high, t) == 0, "never below slpc_min, nothing to send");
		XeSlpcBoost u = fresh(def);   // slpc_boost's lease of 2000 for 10 s and a display lease
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(u, t, 2000, def, true) == kXeBoostGranted && sync(u, def, t) == 2000, "slpc_boost 2000");
		miss(u, t + 1 * ms, 1);
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(u, def, t + 1 * ms) == 2850 && sync(u, def, t + 1 * ms) == 2850, "the higher: display");
		CHECK(xeBoostNextNs(u, def, t + 2 * ms) == t + 1 * ms + L, "the timer at the display lease's end (the earlier)");
		xeBoostExpire(u, t + 1 * ms + L);
		CHECK(sync(u, def, t + 1 * ms + L) == 2000 && xeBoostNextNs(u, def, t + 1 * ms + L) == t + 10 * s,
			"back to slpc_boost's floor, then its end");
		CHECK(u.expiries == 0 && u.disp.expiries == 1, "only the display lease expired");
	}
	// 3.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		miss(b, t, 1);
		uint64_t last = t;
		for (int i = 1; i <= 20; i++) {   // late frames every 11 ms (90 Hz) for 220 ms
			last = t + (uint64_t)i * 11 * ms;
			CHECK(miss(b, last, 1) == kXeDispRenewed, "renewed (%d)", i);
		}
		CHECK(b.disp.grants == 1 && b.disp.renewals == 20 && sync(b, def, last) == 2850 && b.sends == 1, "one lease, one send");
		CHECK(xeDispActive(b.disp, last + L - 1) && !xeDispActive(b.disp, last + L), "ends a lease length after the last");
		CHECK(xeDispBoostedNs(b.disp, last) == 220 * ms, "boosted 220 ms so far");
		xeBoostExpire(b, last + L + 3 * ms);   // the timer a little late
		CHECK(b.disp.boostedNs == 220 * ms + L, "boosted until its end, not until the timer ran (%llu)",
			(unsigned long long)b.disp.boostedNs);
	}
	// 4.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		uint64_t now = t;
		for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {   // five leases, each ended by its timer before the next miss
			CHECK(miss(b, now, 1) == kXeDispGranted, "lease %d", i);
			CHECK(miss(b, now + 10 * ms, 1) == kXeDispRenewed, "renewal %d (not counted)", i);
			now += 10 * ms + L + 1 * ms;
			xeBoostExpire(b, now);
		}
		CHECK(now < t + s && miss(b, now, 1) == kXeDispRateLimited && b.disp.rateLimited == 1 && !xeDispActive(b.disp, now),
			"the sixth in that second refused");
		CHECK(miss(b, t + s, 1) == kXeDispGranted, "a new second");
	}
	// 5.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		CHECK(miss(b, t, 1, 0, kXeDispGateOff) == kXeDispIgnored && b.disp.off == 1, "off");
		CHECK(miss(b, t, 1, 0, kXeDispGateManual) == kXeDispIgnored && b.disp.manual == 1, "freq_manual");
		CHECK(miss(b, t, 1, 0, kXeDispGatePowerSaving) == kXeDispIgnored && b.disp.powerSaving == 1, "power saving");
		CHECK(miss(b, t, 1, 0, kXeDispGateNotReady) == kXeDispIgnored && b.disp.notReady == 1, "not ready");
		CHECK(b.disp.misses == 4 && !b.disp.grants && !b.disp.mhz && sync(b, def, t) == 0, "nothing changed");
		CHECK(miss(b, t + 1 * ms, 2) == kXeDispStreak, "a gated miss is no part of a streak");
	}
	// 6.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		miss(b, t, 1);
		sync(b, def, t);
		xeBoostSleep(b, t + 20 * ms);
		CHECK(b.disp.sleepEnds == 1 && !b.disp.mhz && b.disp.boostedNs == 20 * ms, "sleep ends it, 20 ms boosted");
		CHECK(xeBoostToSend(b, def, t + 21 * ms) == 0 && xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t + 21 * ms) == 0, "nothing to send after sleep");
		XeSlpcBoost o = fresh(def);
		miss(o, t, 1);
		sync(o, def, t);
		CHECK(xeDispSwitchOff(o.disp, t + 30 * ms) && o.disp.knobEnds == 1 && o.disp.boostedNs == 30 * ms, "switched off");
		CHECK(sync(o, def, t + 30 * ms) == 1200, "the floor back at once");
		CHECK(!xeDispSwitchOff(o.disp, t + 31 * ms) && o.disp.knobEnds == 1, "again: nothing");
		XeSlpcBoost z = fresh(def);
		xeBoostSleep(z);
		CHECK(!z.disp.sleepEnds, "sleep without a lease");
	}
	// 7.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		miss(b, t, 1);
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t) == 2850, "RP0");
		const XeSlpcBounds lowered = {400, 2850, 0, 2000};
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, lowered, t + 1 * ms) == 2000 && sync(b, lowered, t + 1 * ms) == 2000,
			"slpc_max 2000 during it: 2000 at once");
	}
	// 8.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = fresh(def);
		miss(b, t, 1);
		const uint64_t late = t + L + 5 * ms;   // past the end, the timer has not run
		CHECK(xeDispMiss(b.disp, late, L, 2, 0, kXeDispGateOk) == kXeDispStreak && !b.disp.mhz && b.disp.boostedNs == L,
			"a new streak; the old lease counted to its end");
		CHECK(b.disp.expiries == 1, "counted as expired (grants = expiries + sleep ends + switch-offs + the running one)");
		CHECK(xeDispMiss(b.disp, late + 4 * ms, L, 2, 0, kXeDispGateOk) == kXeDispGranted, "and the next starts a lease");
	}

	printf("dispboost_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/dupimport.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// dupimport: rb7l regression test for two imports of one VRAM-shared IOSurface backing in one process (what WindowServer
// does when it makes a new wrapper for an app's window surface before it frees the old one). Mesa ANV releases a BO with
// DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_UNMAP_ALL of its handle (xe_vm_unbind_bo); the kernel must then drop only the bindings made through
// that handle, not those of the other import of the same backing. Before rb7l it dropped every binding of the BO, the
// second import's VA fell back to the scratch page and the window read zeros (Minecraft's black flicker, 2026-10-31).
// Needs debug.intelxe.surfvram >= 1 (sudo sysctl -w debug.intelxe.surfvram=1). Only when no game/benchmark runs. Steps:
//   1. a 2560x1440 BGRA IOSurface; SURFACE_VRAM CREATE -> handle h1; SURFACE_VRAM again (no CREATE) -> handle h2, same gen
//   2. a scratch VM (as Mesa makes it): h1 at VA1, h2 at VA2; the copy engine writes pattern A through VA1
//   3. reading through VA2 gives pattern A (both imports map the same VRAM)
//   4. UNMAP_ALL of h1, GEM_CLOSE h1 (Mesa's release of the first import)
//   5. reading through VA2 still gives pattern A. rb7k and before: all zeros (scratch) -> FAIL
//   6. UNMAP_ALL of h2 + GEM_CLOSE: VA2 now reads zeros (the unmap itself still works)
//   7. rb7m: an import with INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE returns the client's existing handle; without it, a new one
// clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o dupimport dupimport.c -framework IOKit -framework IOSurface -framework CoreFoundation
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurface.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"
#include "intelxe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) { errno = ENXIO; return -1; }
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } \
	else { printf("PASS "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } } while (0)

enum { W = 2560, H = 1440, ROW = W * 4 };
static const uint64_t kBytes = (uint64_t)ROW * H;
static const uint64_t kBatch = 0x100000, kSys = 0x10000000, kVa1 = 0x40000000, kVa2 = 0x80000000;

static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int vmBind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t op, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range, uint16_t pat) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = op; b.bind.pat_index = pat;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b) ? errno : 0;
}
static uint32_t syncobj(void) {
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) { fprintf(stderr, "syncobj %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return sc.handle;
}
static int waitBin(uint32_t h, uint64_t timeoutNs) {
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + timeoutNs)};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w) ? errno : 0;
}
static void pattern(uint32_t *p, uint32_t seed) { for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kBytes / 4; i++) p[i] = (i * 2654435761u) ^ seed; }
static long mismatches(const uint32_t *p, uint32_t seed, long *zeros) {
	long bad = 0, z = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kBytes / 4; i++) { if (p[i] != ((i * 2654435761u) ^ seed)) bad++; if (!p[i]) z++; }
	if (zeros) *zeros = z;
	return bad;
}

static struct { uint32_t vm, q, batch, sys; uint32_t *bp, *sp; } g;
// MEM_COPY (page mode, 4 MB per command) of kBytes from src to dst on the copy engine; waits for it. 0 = done.
static int gpuCopy(uint64_t src, uint64_t dst) {
	uint32_t k = 0;
	for (uint64_t off = 0; off < kBytes; off += 4u << 20) {
		const uint64_t chunk = kBytes - off < (4u << 20) ? kBytes - off : (4u << 20);
		const uint64_t s = src + off, d = dst + off;
		g.bp[k++] = (2u << 29 | 0x5au << 22) | 1u << 19 | (10 - 2);
		g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(chunk / 256) - 1; g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(chunk / 0x1000) - 1; g.bp[k++] = 0xfff; g.bp[k++] = 0xfff;
		g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)s; g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(s >> 32); g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)d; g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(d >> 32);
		g.bp[k++] = 3u << 28 | 3u << 3;
	}
	g.bp[k++] = 0xa << 23; g.bp[k++] = 0;
	__sync_synchronize();
	const uint32_t so = syncobj();
	struct drm_xe_sync sy = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = so};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = g.q, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&sy, .address = kBatch, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	int r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x) ? errno : waitBin(so, 2000000000ull);
	struct drm_syncobj_destroy dd = {.handle = so};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_DESTROY, &dd);
	return r;
}

int main(void) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_get_cap cap = {.capability = INTELXE_CAP_SURFACE_VRAM};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap) || !cap.value) {
		fprintf(stderr, "debug.intelxe.surfvram is 0: sudo sysctl -w debug.intelxe.surfvram=1\n");
		return 2;
	}
	CFNumberRef w = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){W}), h = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){H}),
	            bpe = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){4}), bpr = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){ROW}),
	            pf = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){0x42475241});
	const void *k[] = {kIOSurfaceWidth, kIOSurfaceHeight, kIOSurfaceBytesPerElement, kIOSurfaceBytesPerRow, kIOSurfacePixelFormat};
	const void *v[] = {w, h, bpe, bpr, pf};
	CFDictionaryRef props = CFDictionaryCreate(NULL, k, v, 5, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	IOSurfaceRef sf = IOSurfaceCreate(props);
	if (!sf) { fprintf(stderr, "IOSurfaceCreate\n"); return 1; }
	const uint32_t sid = IOSurfaceGetID(sf), seed = 0xa0000000u ^ (uint32_t)(ns() & 0xffffff);
	// 1
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v1 = {.surface_id = sid, .size = kBytes, .flags = INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_CREATE};
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v2 = {.surface_id = sid, .size = kBytes};
	int r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM, &v1) ? errno : 0;
	CHECK(!r && v1.handle, "CREATE -> handle %u, %llu bytes, gen %u (err %d)", v1.handle, (unsigned long long)v1.size_out, v1.gen, r);
	if (r) return 1;
	r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM, &v2) ? errno : 0;
	CHECK(!r && v2.handle && v2.handle != v1.handle && v2.gen == v1.gen, "second import -> handle %u (gen %u, err %d)", v2.handle, v2.gen, r);
	if (r) return 1;
	// 2
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {.flags = DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_SCRATCH_PAGE};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	g.vm = vc.vm_id;
	const uint64_t sysSize = (kBytes + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull;
	g.batch = gem(0x10000, 1); g.sys = gem(sysSize, 1);
	g.bp = map(g.batch, 0x10000); g.sp = map(g.sys, sysSize);
	r = (!g.bp || !g.sp) ? ENOMEM : vmBind(g.vm, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP, g.batch, kBatch, 0x10000, 2);
	if (!r) r = vmBind(g.vm, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP, g.sys, kSys, sysSize, 2);
	if (!r) r = vmBind(g.vm, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP, v1.handle, kVa1, v1.size_out, 0);
	if (!r) r = vmBind(g.vm, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP, v2.handle, kVa2, v2.size_out, 0);
	CHECK(!r, "VM with scratch: system BO, h1 at 0x%llx, h2 at 0x%llx (err %d)", (unsigned long long)kVa1, (unsigned long long)kVa2, r);
	if (r) return 1;
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create q = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = g.vm, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &q)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	g.q = q.exec_queue_id;
	pattern(g.sp, seed);
	CHECK(!gpuCopy(kSys, kVa1), "copy engine writes pattern A through h1");
	// 3
	long z = 0, bad;
	memset(g.sp, 0, kBytes);
	r = gpuCopy(kVa2, kSys);
	bad = mismatches(g.sp, seed, &z);
	CHECK(!r && !bad, "read through h2: pattern A (%ld dwords differ, %ld zero)", bad, z);
	// 4
	r = vmBind(g.vm, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_UNMAP_ALL, v1.handle, 0, 0, 0);
	struct drm_gem_close c1 = {.handle = v1.handle};
	CHECK(!r && !xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &c1), "UNMAP_ALL h1 + GEM_CLOSE h1 (Mesa releasing the first import; err %d)", r);
	// 5
	memset(g.sp, 0, kBytes);
	r = gpuCopy(kVa2, kSys);
	bad = mismatches(g.sp, seed, &z);
	CHECK(!r && !bad, "read through h2 after h1 went: still pattern A (%ld dwords differ, %ld zero%s)", bad, z,
	      z == (long)(kBytes / 4) ? ": h2's mapping is gone, the scratch page answered - the rb7k bug" : "");
	// 6
	r = vmBind(g.vm, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_UNMAP_ALL, v2.handle, 0, 0, 0);
	struct drm_gem_close c2 = {.handle = v2.handle};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &c2);
	memset(g.sp, 0xff, kBytes);
	const int r2 = gpuCopy(kVa2, kSys);
	mismatches(g.sp, seed, &z);
	CHECK(!r && !r2 && z == (long)(kBytes / 4), "UNMAP_ALL h2: VA2 reads the scratch page's zeros (%ld of %llu dwords zero; err %d/%d)", z,
	      (unsigned long long)(kBytes / 4), r, r2);
	// 7 (rb7m): INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE gives back the handle this client already holds for the backing
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v3 = {.surface_id = sid, .size = kBytes};
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v4 = {.surface_id = sid, .size = kBytes, .flags = INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE};
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v5 = {.surface_id = sid, .size = kBytes};
	r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM, &v3) ? errno : 0;
	const int r4 = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM, &v4) ? errno : 0;
	const int r5 = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM, &v5) ? errno : 0;
	if (r4 == EINVAL)
		printf("INFO SAME_HANDLE: EINVAL (a kernel before rb7m)\n");
	else
		CHECK(!r && !r4 && v4.handle == v3.handle && v4.gen == v3.gen, "SAME_HANDLE import -> the existing handle %u (got %u, err %d/%d)", v3.handle, v4.handle, r, r4);
	CHECK(!r5 && v5.handle != v3.handle, "import without SAME_HANDLE -> a handle of its own (%u, err %d)", v5.handle, r5);
	struct drm_gem_close c3 = {.handle = v3.handle}, c5 = {.handle = v5.handle};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &c3); xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &c5);
	struct drm_xe_vm_destroy vd = {.vm_id = g.vm};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_DESTROY, &vd);
	CFRelease(sf);
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/engact_test.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// engact_test: offline check of the GuC engine activity arithmetic (xe_engact.h) against Linux's
// xe_guc_engine_activity.c (v7.4-rc3), no GPU needed.
//   1. the ABI: record and metadata sizes, the record offset per [GuC class][logical instance], the 12 KB buffer, the
//      supported-version rule (1.14.1; BMG's 70.72.1 image has 1.38.1), the GPM shift from RPM_CONFIG0
//   2. active ticks, record by record, against a direct transcription of get_engine_active_ticks: nothing before the
//      GuC's first update, the idle delta summed, a running engine's part from the GPM timestamp (u32 wrap), unchanged
//      global or engine change numbers ignoring the record, change_num 0 ignored
//   3. total ticks against get_engine_total_ticks: the CPU time scaled by quanta_ratio / 0x8000 with its remainder,
//      in GuC ticks (mul_u64_u32_div without 128-bit division, checked against a 128-bit reference)
//   4. the kext's two departures: a re-enable after a GuC reload re-bases the records (counters restart in the GuC, the
//      totals here only grow); a GPM timestamp of 0 or all ones leaves the running part as it was
//   5. 2000 pseudo-random sequences: active never decreases across updates without a reload when the GuC's counters
//      only grow, total never decreases, both match the reference transcription
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o engact_test engact_test.cpp && ./engact_test
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_engact.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// get_engine_active_ticks / get_engine_total_ticks transcribed with Linux's names and types (u16/u32/u64), reading
// from a record and metadata instead of the iosys_map.
struct LxActivity { uint16_t change_num, quanta_ratio; uint32_t last_update_tick; uint64_t active_ticks; };
struct LxMeta { uint32_t guc_tsc_frequency_hz, lag_latency_usec, global_change_num, reserved; };
struct LxEa { uint64_t active, last_cpu_ts, quanta, quanta_ns, quanta_remainder_ns, total; bool running; LxMeta metadata;
	LxActivity activity; };
static uint64_t lxActive(LxEa *ea, const LxMeta &meta, const LxActivity &rec, uint64_t misc_status_0, uint32_t shift) {
	LxActivity *cached_activity = &ea->activity;
	LxMeta *cached_metadata = &ea->metadata;
	uint32_t last_update_tick, global_change_num;
	uint64_t active_ticks, gpm_ts;
	uint16_t change_num;
	global_change_num = meta.global_change_num;
	if (!global_change_num) goto update;
	if (global_change_num == cached_metadata->global_change_num) goto update;
	cached_metadata->global_change_num = global_change_num;
	change_num = rec.change_num;
	if (!change_num || change_num == cached_activity->change_num) goto update;
	last_update_tick = rec.last_update_tick;
	active_ticks = rec.active_ticks;
	ea->running = !!last_update_tick;
	ea->total += active_ticks - cached_activity->active_ticks;
	ea->active = 0;
	cached_activity->change_num = change_num;
	cached_activity->last_update_tick = last_update_tick;
	cached_activity->active_ticks = active_ticks;
update:
	if (ea->running) {
		gpm_ts = misc_status_0 >> shift;
		ea->active = (uint32_t)gpm_ts - cached_activity->last_update_tick;
	}
	return ea->total + ea->active;
}
static uint64_t lxTotal(LxEa *ea, const LxMeta &meta, const LxActivity &rec, uint64_t now) {
	if (!ea->metadata.guc_tsc_frequency_hz) ea->metadata.guc_tsc_frequency_hz = meta.guc_tsc_frequency_hz;
	ea->activity.quanta_ratio = rec.quanta_ratio;
	const uint64_t cpu_delta = now - ea->last_cpu_ts;
	ea->last_cpu_ts = now;
	const uint64_t numerator = (ea->quanta_remainder_ns + cpu_delta) * ea->activity.quanta_ratio;
	ea->quanta_ns += numerator / 0x8000;
	ea->quanta_remainder_ns = numerator % 0x8000;
	ea->quanta = (uint64_t)((unsigned __int128)ea->quanta_ns * ea->metadata.guc_tsc_frequency_hz / 1000000000u);
	return ea->quanta;
}

static uint64_t rng = 0x243f6a8885a308d3ull;
static uint32_t rnd() {
	rng ^= rng << 13, rng ^= rng >> 7, rng ^= rng << 17;
	return (uint32_t)(rng >> 16);
}

// The kernel's read (engActSample) for one engine: update, then the GPM part when it runs, then the total.
static uint64_t kActive(XeEaEngine &e, uint32_t gcn, const XeEaRecord &r, uint64_t misc, uint32_t shift) {
	if (xeEaActiveUpdate(e, gcn, r)) {
		uint32_t g = 0;
		const bool ok = xeEaGpmLow((uint32_t)misc, (uint32_t)(misc >> 32), shift, &g);
		xeEaActiveRunning(e, ok, g);
	}
	return xeEaActiveTicks(e);
}

int main() {
	// 1.
	CHECK(sizeof(XeEaRecord) == 16 && sizeof(XeEaMeta) == 16, "sizes");
	CHECK(offsetof(XeEaRecord, quantaRatio) == 2 && offsetof(XeEaRecord, lastUpdateTick) == 4 &&
		offsetof(XeEaRecord, activeTicks) == 8, "record offsets");
	CHECK(offsetof(XeEaMeta, globalChangeNum) == 8, "metadata offsets");
	CHECK(xeEaRecordOffset(0, 0) == 0 && xeEaRecordOffset(0, 1) == 16 && xeEaRecordOffset(1, 0) == 512 &&
		xeEaRecordOffset(4, 3) == (4 * 32 + 3) * 16, "record offset");
	CHECK(kXeEaDataOff + xeEaRecordOffset(15, 31) + 16 == kXeEaBytes, "the last record ends the buffer");
	CHECK(kXeEaActionSetDeviceBuffer == 0x550C, "action");
	CHECK(xeEaSupported(1u << 16 | 38u << 8 | 1u), "1.38.1 (BMG 70.72.1)");
	CHECK(xeEaSupported(1u << 16 | 14u << 8 | 1u) && !xeEaSupported(1u << 16 | 14u << 8 | 0u) &&
		!xeEaSupported(1u << 16 | 13u << 8 | 9u) && xeEaSupported(2u << 16), "1.14.1 boundary");
	CHECK(!xeEaSupported(0), "no version");
	CHECK(xeEaGpmShift(0) == 3 && xeEaGpmShift(1u << 1) == 2 && xeEaGpmShift(3u << 1) == 0 && xeEaGpmShift(0xfffffff9u) == 3,
		"shift");
	{
		uint32_t g = 7;
		CHECK(!xeEaGpmLow(0, 0, 0, &g) && !xeEaGpmLow(0xffffffffu, 0xffffffffu, 0, &g) && g == 7, "no timestamp");
		CHECK(xeEaGpmLow(0x80000000u, 0x5u, 1, &g) && g == 0xc0000000u, "shifted across dwords: 0x%x", g);
	}

	// 2. fixed sequence, against the transcription
	{
		XeEaEngine e = {};
		LxEa lx = {};
		xeEaEnable(e, 1000);
		lx.last_cpu_ts = 1000;
		XeEaMeta m = {};
		XeEaRecord r = {};
		auto step = [&](uint64_t misc, const char *what) {
			const LxMeta lm = {m.gucTscHz, m.lagLatencyUs, m.globalChangeNum, 0};
			const LxActivity la = {r.changeNum, r.quantaRatio, r.lastUpdateTick, r.activeTicks};
			const uint64_t want = lxActive(&lx, lm, la, misc, 3);
			const uint64_t got = kActive(e, m.globalChangeNum, r, misc, 3);
			CHECK(got == want, "%s: active %llu, Linux %llu", what, (unsigned long long)got, (unsigned long long)want);
			return got;
		};
		CHECK(step(0, "before the GuC's first update") == 0, "zero");
		m.globalChangeNum = 1;
		r = {1, 0x8000, 0, 500};
		CHECK(step(0, "idle, 500 ticks done") == 500, "500");
		m.globalChangeNum = 2;
		r = {2, 0x8000, 1000, 500};   // went active at tick 1000
		CHECK(step(1200ull << 3, "running since 1000, now 1200") == 700, "500 + 200");
		CHECK(step(1500ull << 3, "same record, now 1500") == 1000, "500 + 500");
		m.globalChangeNum = 3;   // another engine changed: this record did not
		CHECK(step(1600ull << 3, "global moved, record not") == 1100, "500 + 600");
		m.globalChangeNum = 4;
		r = {3, 0x8000, 0, 1300};   // idle again after 800 more
		CHECK(step(1700ull << 3, "idle at 1300") == 1300, "1300");
		m.globalChangeNum = 5;
		r = {0, 0x8000, 0, 9999};   // change_num 0: ignored
		CHECK(step(0, "change_num 0") == 1300, "ignored");
		m.globalChangeNum = 6;
		r = {4, 0x8000, 0xfffffff0u, 1300};   // running, its start tick about to wrap
		CHECK(step((uint64_t)0x10u << 3, "u32 wrap") == 1300 + 0x20, "wrap");
	}

	// 3. total ticks: 19.2 MHz GuC TSC, ratio 1.0 then 0.5, remainders
	{
		XeEaEngine e = {};
		LxEa lx = {};
		xeEaEnable(e, 0);
		const LxMeta lm = {19200000, 0, 1, 0};
		LxActivity la = {1, 0x8000, 0, 0};
		uint64_t t = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
			t += 1000000000ull / 3;
			const uint64_t want = lxTotal(&lx, lm, la, t);
			const uint64_t got = xeEaTotalTicks(e, la.quanta_ratio, lm.guc_tsc_frequency_hz, t);
			CHECK(got == want, "total %llu, Linux %llu", (unsigned long long)got, (unsigned long long)want);
		}
		CHECK(e.quanta >= 31999990 && e.quanta <= 32000000, "5/3 s at 19.2 MHz: %llu", (unsigned long long)e.quanta);
		la.quanta_ratio = 0x4000;
		const uint64_t before = e.quanta;
		t += 1000000000ull;
		const uint64_t want = lxTotal(&lx, lm, la, t);
		const uint64_t got = xeEaTotalTicks(e, la.quanta_ratio, lm.guc_tsc_frequency_hz, t);
		CHECK(got == want && got - before == 9600000, "half share: +%llu", (unsigned long long)(got - before));
		XeEaEngine z = {};
		CHECK(xeEaTotalTicks(z, 0, 19200000, 5000000000ull) == 0, "ratio 0 (no record yet): 0");
		for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
			const uint64_t a = (uint64_t)rnd() << 30 | rnd();
			const uint32_t b = rnd() | 1;
			CHECK(xeEaMulDiv(a, b, 1000000000u) == (uint64_t)((unsigned __int128)a * b / 1000000000u), "muldiv %llu %u",
				(unsigned long long)a, b);
		}
	}

	// 4. re-enable after a reload: the GuC's counters restart at 0, the totals continue
	{
		XeEaEngine e = {};
		xeEaEnable(e, 0);
		kActive(e, 1, XeEaRecord{1, 0x8000, 0, 5000}, 0, 3);
		CHECK(xeEaActiveTicks(e) == 5000, "before the reload");
		xeEaTotalTicks(e, 0x8000, 1000000000u, 1000);
		const uint64_t tot = e.quanta;
		xeEaEnable(e, 2000);   // GT reset: buffer cleared, handed over again
		CHECK(xeEaActiveTicks(e) == 5000 && !e.running, "kept across the enable");
		kActive(e, 1, XeEaRecord{1, 0x8000, 0, 300}, 0, 3);   // the new GuC's first update: change numbers from 1 again
		CHECK(xeEaActiveTicks(e) == 5300, "continues: %llu", (unsigned long long)xeEaActiveTicks(e));
		xeEaTotalTicks(e, 0x8000, 1000000000u, 2500);
		CHECK(e.quanta == tot + 500, "total continues from the enable, the gap left out: %llu", (unsigned long long)e.quanta);
		// a running engine and a GPM read of 0 (GT down): the running part stays
		kActive(e, 2, XeEaRecord{2, 0x8000, 100, 300}, 150ull << 3, 3);
		CHECK(xeEaActiveTicks(e) == 5350, "running 50: %llu", (unsigned long long)xeEaActiveTicks(e));
		kActive(e, 2, XeEaRecord{2, 0x8000, 100, 300}, 0, 3);
		CHECK(xeEaActiveTicks(e) == 5350, "GPM 0: unchanged %llu", (unsigned long long)xeEaActiveTicks(e));
		kActive(e, 2, XeEaRecord{2, 0x8000, 100, 300}, ~0ull, 3);
		CHECK(xeEaActiveTicks(e) == 5350, "GPM all ones: unchanged");
	}

	// 5. random sequences: a GuC whose active_ticks grow and whose last_update_tick follows its timestamp
	for (int seq = 0; seq < 2000; seq++) {
		XeEaEngine e = {};
		LxEa lx = {};
		xeEaEnable(e, 0);
		uint32_t gcn = 0;
		uint16_t cn = 0;
		uint64_t act = 0, now = 0, ts = 1000, prevA = 0, prevT = 0;
		uint32_t start = 0;
		bool running = false;
		const uint32_t shift = rnd() % 4;
		for (int k = 0; k < 40; k++) {
			const uint32_t dt = 1 + rnd() % 100000;
			ts += dt;
			now += dt * 52;   // ~19.2 MHz
			if (running) act += dt;
			const uint32_t what = rnd() % 4;
			if (what == 0) {   // the engine changes state, the GuC updates its record
				running = !running;
				start = running ? (uint32_t)ts : 0;
				gcn++;
				if (!++cn) cn = 1;
			} else if (what == 1) {
				gcn++;   // another engine's update
			}
			const XeEaRecord r = {cn, 0x8000, start, act};
			const uint64_t misc = ts << shift;
			const LxMeta lm = {19200000, 0, gcn, 0};
			const LxActivity la = {r.changeNum, r.quantaRatio, r.lastUpdateTick, r.activeTicks};
			const uint64_t want = lxActive(&lx, lm, la, misc, shift);
			const uint64_t got = kActive(e, gcn, r, misc, shift);
			CHECK(got == want, "seq %d step %d: %llu vs %llu", seq, k, (unsigned long long)got, (unsigned long long)want);
			CHECK(got >= prevA, "seq %d step %d: active went back", seq, k);
			const uint64_t tw = lxTotal(&lx, lm, la, now), tg = xeEaTotalTicks(e, 0x8000, 19200000, now);
			CHECK(tg == tw && tg >= prevT, "seq %d step %d: total %llu vs %llu", seq, k, (unsigned long long)tg,
				(unsigned long long)tw);
			prevA = got;
			prevT = tg;
		}
	}

	printf("%s: %d of %d checks failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails, checks);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/lr_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// lr_test: offline check of long-running VMs' pure logic (xe_lr.h, xeVmCreateCheck in xe_uapi_args.cpp), no GPU needed.
//   1. DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE flags (xe_vm.c xe_vm_create_ioctl): LR_MODE accepted, FAULT_MODE refused (no fault
//      service: xe's !has_usm answer), the FAULT/LR and NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT/FAULT dependencies, unknown bits, reserved
//   2. the syncs an exec and a bind on an LR VM may carry (xe_sync.c xe_sync_entry_parse, SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_LR_MODE)
//   3. one queue's preemption step (xeLrQueueStep: __guc_exec_queue_process_msg_suspend, min_run_period_lr_ms,
//      guc_exec_queue_wait_suspend_done's 5 s; closed queues and ones banned for an unconfirmed disable count until
//      they are really off), driven through a whole preemption of a few queues
//   4. cycles (preempt fences' seqnos), resume rules, exec without batch, the job timeout exemption
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o lr_test lr_test.cpp ../xe_uapi_args.cpp && ./lr_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/errno.h>
#include "xe_lr.h"
#include "xe_uapi_args.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static void vmCreate() {
	auto chk = [](uint32_t flags, bool *lr) {
		drm_xe_vm_create v = {};
		v.flags = flags;
		return xeVmCreateCheck(v, lr);
	};
	bool lr = true;
	CHECK(chk(0, &lr) == 0 && !lr, "plain VM");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_SCRATCH_PAGE, &lr) == 0 && !lr, "scratch VM");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE, &lr) == 0 && lr, "LR VM accepted");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_SCRATCH_PAGE, &lr) == 0 && lr, "LR scratch VM");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE, &lr) == EINVAL && !lr,
		"fault mode refused (no GPU fault service)");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE, &lr) == EINVAL, "fault mode without LR");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT, &lr) == EINVAL,
		"NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT without fault mode");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_FAULT_MODE | DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT,
		&lr) == EINVAL, "NO_VM_OVERCOMMIT with fault mode: still fault mode");
	CHECK(chk(1u << 4, &lr) == EINVAL, "unknown flag");
	CHECK(chk(DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE | 1u << 31, &lr) == EINVAL && !lr, "unknown flag with LR");
	drm_xe_vm_create v = {};
	v.flags = DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE;
	v.reserved[1] = 1;
	CHECK(xeVmCreateCheck(v, &lr) == EINVAL && !lr, "reserved");
	v = {};
	v.extensions = 0x1000;
	CHECK(xeVmCreateCheck(v, &lr) == EINVAL, "extensions");
}

static void syncs() {
	auto mk = [](uint32_t type, uint32_t flags, uint64_t addr, uint64_t point) {
		drm_xe_sync e = {};
		e.type = type;
		e.flags = flags;
		e.addr = addr;
		e.timeline_value = point;
		return e;
	};
	const uint32_t SIG = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, EXEC = kXeSyncParseExec, LR = kXeSyncParseLrMode;
	// exec on an LR VM: what xe_exec_ioctl passes (SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_EXEC | SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_LR_MODE)
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, SIG, 3, 0), EXEC | LR) == EOPNOTSUPP, "exec: syncobj out");
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_TIMELINE_SYNCOBJ, SIG, 3, 4), EXEC | LR) == EOPNOTSUPP,
		"exec: timeline out");
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, 0, 3, 0), EXEC | LR) == 0, "exec: syncobj in");
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_TIMELINE_SYNCOBJ, 0, 3, 4), EXEC | LR) == 0, "exec: timeline in");
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_USER_FENCE, SIG, 0x2000, 1), EXEC | LR) == 0, "exec: user fence");
	// VM_BIND on an LR VM: xe_vm_bind_ioctl passes SYNC_PARSE_FLAG_LR_MODE too
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, SIG, 3, 0), LR) == EOPNOTSUPP, "bind: syncobj out");
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_USER_FENCE, SIG, 0x2000, 1), LR) == 0, "bind: user fence");
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_USER_FENCE, SIG, 0x2000, 1), LR | kXeSyncParseDisallowUfence) ==
		EOPNOTSUPP, "bind without ops: no user fence");
	// the same entries on a dma-fence VM are fine
	CHECK(xeSyncEntryCheck(mk(DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, SIG, 3, 0), EXEC) == 0, "dma-fence VM: syncobj out");
}

static XeLrQueueState q0() {
	XeLrQueueState s = {};
	s.counts = true;
	return s;
}

static void step() {
	const uint64_t T = 10000000000ull;   // "now"
	XeLrQueueState s = q0();
	s.ringIdle = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "idle ring: off without a disable");
	s = q0();
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrSendDisable, "busy, never preempted: disable now");
	s.onNs = T - 1000000;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitMinRun, "resumed 1 ms ago: waits for the 5 ms run period");
	s.onNs = T - kXeLrMinRunNs;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrSendDisable, "resumed 5 ms ago: disable");
	s = q0();
	s.gucDown = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitGuc, "GuC down: nothing sent");
	s.ringIdle = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "GuC down but idle: off");
	s = q0();
	s.sent = true;
	s.sentNs = T - 1000;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "disable out: waits for the confirmation");
	s.ringIdle = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "a disable sent is waited for even if the ring went idle");
	s.confirmed = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "confirmed: off");
	s = q0();
	s.sent = true;
	s.sentNs = T - kXeLrConfirmNs - 1;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrConfirmTimeout, "not confirmed in 5 s: ban");
	s.sentNs = T - kXeLrConfirmNs;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "exactly 5 s: still waits");
	s = q0();
	s.offByOther = true;
	s.sentNs = 0;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "teardown's disable: waited, never timed out here");
	s.confirmed = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "teardown's disable confirmed: off");
	s = q0();
	s.counts = false;
	s.sent = true;
	s.sentNs = 0;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "banned: does not count");
	s = q0();
	s.foreign = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "closed, ring busy: waits for its teardown's disable, sends none");
	s.ringIdle = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "closed, ring idle: off");
	s = q0();
	s.foreign = true;
	s.offByOther = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "closed, its disable out: waits");
	s.confirmed = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "closed, its disable confirmed: off");
	s = q0();
	s.counts = false;   // banned for the unconfirmed disable
	s.stuck = true;
	s.ringIdle = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrWaitConfirm, "banned for an unconfirmed disable: not off until the GT reset");
	s.confirmed = true;
	CHECK(xeLrQueueStep(s, T) == kXeLrIsOff, "stuck but confirmed after all: off");

	// a whole preemption of three queues: busy, idle, busy and resumed 2 ms ago; the GuC confirms one per tick
	struct Q { XeLrQueueState s; bool confirmAt; uint64_t sentAt; };
	Q qs[3] = {{q0(), false, 0}, {q0(), false, 0}, {q0(), false, 0}};
	qs[1].s.ringIdle = true;
	qs[2].s.onNs = T - 2000000;
	uint32_t disables = 0, ticks = 0;
	bool allOff = false;
	for (uint64_t now = T; ticks < 20 && !allOff; now += 1000000, ticks++) {   // a 1 ms tick
		allOff = true;
		for (Q &q : qs) {
			if (q.s.sent && now - q.sentAt >= 2000000) q.s.confirmed = true;   // the GuC answers in 2 ms
			const XeLrStep st = xeLrQueueStep(q.s, now);
			if (st == kXeLrSendDisable) {
				q.s.sent = true;
				q.s.sentNs = q.sentAt = now;
				disables++;
			}
			allOff = (st == kXeLrIsOff) && allOff;
		}
	}
	CHECK(allOff, "the preemption completes");
	CHECK(disables == 2, "two disables (the idle queue needs none): %u", disables);
	CHECK(ticks == 6, "done after the third queue's run period (3 ms) and its confirmation (2 ms): %u ticks", ticks);
}

static void cycles() {
	CHECK(xeLrCycleCovers(5, 5) && xeLrCycleCovers(6, 5) && !xeLrCycleCovers(4, 5), "cycle order");
	CHECK(xeLrCycleCovers(2, 0xfffffffeu) && !xeLrCycleCovers(0xfffffffeu, 2), "cycle counters wrap");
	CHECK(xeLrResumeNow(0, 7, 7), "no hold, no cycle pending: resume");
	CHECK(!xeLrResumeNow(1, 7, 7), "a move still holds the VM");
	CHECK(!xeLrResumeNow(0, 8, 7), "a cycle asked for meanwhile");
	CHECK(xeLrSendEnable(true, true, false), "this preemption's disable: enable");
	CHECK(!xeLrSendEnable(false, true, false), "never disabled (idle): no enable");
	CHECK(!xeLrSendEnable(true, false, false), "banned meanwhile: stays off");
	CHECK(!xeLrSendEnable(true, true, true), "GuC down: the registration enables it");
	CHECK(xeLrExecNoop(true, 0) && !xeLrExecNoop(true, 1) && !xeLrExecNoop(false, 0), "LR exec without batch: nothing");
	CHECK(!xeLrJobTimeoutApplies(true) && xeLrJobTimeoutApplies(false), "no job timeout on LR queues");
}

int main() {
	vmCreate();
	syncs();
	step();
	cycles();
	printf("%d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# night phase barrevoke (sourced by the night scripts, or run with bash on its own: tmo, say and $O are defined here when
# the night driver has not). Needs the barwin kext (debug.intelxe.bar_revoke) and user/tests/kernel/barrevoke built next
# to this script (or BARREVOKE_BIN). docs/design/DESIGN-rebar-window.md section 8: CPU-mapped BOs leave the BAR window
# with their mappings redirected to system memory.
#  1. forced, knob 0: barrevoke now 4 (sudo: writes debug.intelxe.bar_revoke_now) -> $O/barrevoke-now4.log
#  2. knob 1: barrevoke natural 4 (GEM_CREATE's eviction revokes the oldest) -> $O/barrevoke-natural4.log
#  3. knob 1: barrevoke now 16 (the size limit's edge) -> $O/barrevoke-now16.log
#  4. checks after each: WindowServer pid unchanged, no new GuC / GT resets, no CAT error; the bar_revoke line of
#     debug.intelxe.vram before and after -> $O/barrevoke-vram.txt; on a latched or broken result the g2h log is saved
# The knob goes back to 0 at the end. Every binary runs under tmo (a bash timer: no perl / env / sh wrapper).
# Do not run while a game or benchmark runs: the test takes the whole window for a few seconds.
BARREVOKE_DIR=${BARREVOKE_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)}
BARREVOKE_BIN=${BARREVOKE_BIN:-$BARREVOKE_DIR/barrevoke}
O=${O:-$HOME/b580/barrevoke/$(date +%m%d-%H%M)}
mkdir -p "$O"
if ! declare -F tmo >/dev/null; then
tmo() {   # tmo <seconds> <command...>: run it, kill it after <seconds>; its exit code (137 = killed)
	local s=$1; shift
	"$@" & local p=$!
	( trap 'kill $sp 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM; sleep "$s" & sp=$!; wait $sp; kill -9 $p 2>/dev/null ) > /dev/null 2>&1 &
	local w=$!
	wait $p; local r=$?
	kill $w 2>/dev/null; wait $w 2>/dev/null
	return $r
}
fi
declare -F say >/dev/null || say() { echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) $*" | tee -a "$O/say.txt"; }
declare -F resets >/dev/null || resets() {
	sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*GuC context resets ([0-9]+); GT resets ([0-9]+).*/\1 \2/p'
}
barrevoke_line() { sysctl -n debug.intelxe.vram 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 '^bar_revoke '; }
barrevoke_set() { sudo -n sysctl debug.intelxe.bar_revoke="$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
barrevoke_run() {   # tag args...
	local tag=$1 ws0 ws1 r0 r1 c0 c1 rc; shift
	ws0=$(pgrep -x WindowServer); r0=$(resets)
	c0=$(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'CAT errors [0-9]+' | head -1)
	{ echo "== $tag before (bar_revoke $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.bar_revoke))"; barrevoke_line; } >> "$O/barrevoke-vram.txt"
	if [ "${1:-}" = now ]; then tmo 120 sudo -n "$BARREVOKE_BIN" "$@" > "$O/barrevoke-$tag.log" 2>&1
	else tmo 120 "$BARREVOKE_BIN" "$@" > "$O/barrevoke-$tag.log" 2>&1; fi
	rc=$?
	{ echo "== $tag after (exit $rc)"; barrevoke_line; } >> "$O/barrevoke-vram.txt"
	ws1=$(pgrep -x WindowServer); r1=$(resets)
	c1=$(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'CAT errors [0-9]+' | head -1)
	local ok=PASS
	grep -q '^PASSED' "$O/barrevoke-$tag.log" || ok=FAIL
	grep -q '^SKIP' "$O/barrevoke-$tag.log" && ok=SKIP
	[ "$ws0" = "$ws1" ] && [ "$r0" = "$r1" ] && [ "$c0" = "$c1" ] || ok="$ok+SYSTEM"
	say "BARREVOKE $tag $ok (exit $rc): $(grep -E '^(revoked|FAIL|SKIP|PASSED|FAILED)' "$O/barrevoke-$tag.log" | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')" \
		"| WindowServer $ws0->$ws1, resets $r0->$r1, $c0->$c1"
	if sysctl -n debug.intelxe.vram | grep -qE 'LATCHED OFF|broken [1-9]|undecided [1-9]'; then
		sudo -n sysctl -n debug.intelxe.g2h 2>/dev/null | tail -80 > "$O/g2h-barrevoke-$tag.txt"
		say "BARREVOKE $tag: latched / broken, g2h saved"
	fi
}
phase_barrevoke() {
	if ! sysctl -n debug.intelxe.bar_revoke >/dev/null 2>&1; then say "BARREVOKE: kext without debug.intelxe.bar_revoke, skipped"; return 0; fi
	[ -x "$BARREVOKE_BIN" ] || { say "BARREVOKE: no binary at $BARREVOKE_BIN, skipped"; return 0; }
	if [ -x "$HOME/b580/wsitest/gpu_busy.sh" ] && b=$("$HOME/b580/wsitest/gpu_busy.sh"); then say "BARREVOKE: GPU busy ($b), skipped"; return 0; fi
	say "BARREVOKE start: window $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.vram | head -1 | cut -c1-120); resets $(resets)"
	barrevoke_set 0
	barrevoke_run now4 now 4
	barrevoke_set 1
	barrevoke_run natural4 natural 4
	barrevoke_run now16 now 16
	barrevoke_set 0
	say "BARREVOKE end: bar_revoke $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.bar_revoke); $(barrevoke_line | head -1 | cut -c1-200)"
}
# run on its own: bash night-barrevoke.sh
if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then set -o pipefail; phase_barrevoke; fi

# night phase rb8cost (sourced by the night scripts after night-kernel.sh, which defines gbrun; tmo, say and $O come from
# the night driver). Needs the rb8cost kext installed. Per knob (docs/design/DESIGN-rb8-cost.md): Geekbench 6 OpenCL
# import x3 with the knob 0 vs 1, alternating, then all of them off vs on; the "rb8 cost" stats line before and after each
# run goes to $O/rb8cost-counters.txt, scores to $O/gb-results.txt (gbrun) and $O/rb8cost.txt.
# bind_tlb_fence is left out since 13 Nov: its 0 reset the GPU on the B580 (3 GuC context resets, 1 GT reset) for no
# gain, and the kext now takes 0 only with the boot-arg -intelxe_unsafe_bindfence (without it the "off" runs would
# silently run with 1). Set RB8COST_KNOBS to choose the knobs (e.g. RB8COST_KNOBS=defer_jobs).
RB8COST_KNOBS="${RB8COST_KNOBS:-exec_tlb_dep defer_jobs ggtt_inval_wait}"
rb8cost_set() { for k in $1; do sudo -n sysctl debug.intelxe.$k=$2 >/dev/null 2>&1; done; }
rb8cost_line() { sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -o 'rb8 cost.*'; sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -oE 'direct submission[^;]*;[^\n]*' | cut -c1-220; }
rb8cost_one() {   # knobs value tag
  rb8cost_set "$1" "$2"
  { echo "== $3 ($1=$2) before"; rb8cost_line; } >> "$O/rb8cost-counters.txt"
  gbrun OpenCL import "$3"
  { echo "== $3 after"; rb8cost_line; } >> "$O/rb8cost-counters.txt"
  echo "$3 $(tail -1 "$O/gb-results.txt" | awk '{print $3}') [$1]=$2" >> "$O/rb8cost.txt"   # tag score knobs
}
phase_rb8cost() {
  if ! sysctl -n debug.intelxe.bind_tlb_fence >/dev/null 2>&1; then say "RB8COST: kext without the knobs, skipped"; return 0; fi
  rb8cost_set "$RB8COST_KNOBS" 1
  say "RB8COST start: $(rb8cost_line | head -1 | cut -c1-300)"
  for k in $RB8COST_KNOBS; do
    for i in 1 2 3; do rb8cost_one "$k" 0 "rb8cost-$k-off$i"; rb8cost_one "$k" 1 "rb8cost-$k-on$i"; done
    say "RB8COST $k: off $(grep -E "^rb8cost-$k-off" "$O/rb8cost.txt" | awk '{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ') on $(grep -E "^rb8cost-$k-on" "$O/rb8cost.txt" | awk '{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  done
  for i in 1 2 3; do rb8cost_one "$RB8COST_KNOBS" 0 "rb8cost-all-off$i"; rb8cost_one "$RB8COST_KNOBS" 1 "rb8cost-all-on$i"; done
  rb8cost_set "$RB8COST_KNOBS" 1
  say "RB8COST all: off $(grep -E '^rb8cost-all-off' "$O/rb8cost.txt" | awk '{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ') on $(grep -E '^rb8cost-all-on' "$O/rb8cost.txt" | awk '{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  say "RB8COST end: $(rb8cost_line | head -1 | cut -c1-300); resets $(resets)"
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/night-tlbinring.sh
