# night phase tlbinring (sourced by the night scripts after night-kernel.sh, which defines gbrun and resets; tmo, say and
# $O come from the night driver). Needs the tlbinring kext (branch tlbinring: debug.intelxe.tlb_inring) installed.
# docs/design/DESIGN-rb8-cost.md "tlbinring": with tlb_inring 1 an EXEC whose only pending in-fences are TLB
# invalidations waits for them in the ring (MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT on the TLB word) and an armed queue stays in direct
# submission; 0 (default) is the rb8f behaviour (FIFO, dsExit).
#  1. Geekbench 6 OpenCL import x3, knob 0 vs 1 alternating (0 first, then 1 first, then 0 first); the "rb8 cost" and
#     "direct submission" stats lines before and after each run -> $O/tlbinring-counters.txt, scores -> $O/tlbinring.txt
#  2. cl_gbmicro (chain, churn, import, mixed; the plugin's unaligned import on) x3, knob 0 vs 1 alternating ->
#     $O/tlbinring-gbcl/<knob>-<run>.log, RESULT lines in $O/tlbinring-gbcl/results.txt
#  3. CAT stress with the knob on: bindstress 10 min, all four queue kinds, EXECs waiting on the bind timeline as Mesa's
#     (bindfence; the binary next to this script, built from branch tlbinring, since ~/b580/cat/bindstress has no
#     bindfence and its EXECs have no in-fences, so they would never take the new path) -> $O/bs-tlbinring.log
# The knob goes back to 0 at the end. TLBINRING_ON=2 runs the "on" side with the normal-ring path as well.
TLBINRING_DIR=${TLBINRING_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)}
TLBINRING_ON=${TLBINRING_ON:-1}
tlbinring_set() { sudo -n sysctl debug.intelxe.tlb_inring=$1 >/dev/null 2>&1; }
tlbinring_line() {
  local s; s=$(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats)
  echo "$s" | grep -o 'rb8 cost.*'
  echo "$s" | grep -o 'direct submission.*' | head -1
  echo "$s" | grep -oE 'jobs: direct [0-9]+, via worker [0-9]+'
}
# the tlbinring counters in one short line: armed slot, normal ring, word already there; fallbacks
tlbinring_short() {
  sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -o 'rb8 cost.*' | sed -nE 's/.*(tlb_inring [0-9]+).*(EXEC in-fences on an invalidation [0-9]+).*(EXECs to the worker for in-fences [0-9]+ \(left direct mode [0-9]+\)).*(armed slot [0-9]+, normal ring [0-9]+ \(word already there [0-9]+\)); old path: ([^;]*);.*/\1; \2; \3; \4; fallback \5/p'
}
tlbinring_gb() {   # knob tag
  tlbinring_set "$1"
  { echo "== $2 (tlb_inring=$1) before"; tlbinring_line; } >> "$O/tlbinring-counters.txt"
  gbrun OpenCL import "$2"
  { echo "== $2 after"; tlbinring_line; } >> "$O/tlbinring-counters.txt"
  echo "$2 $(tail -1 "$O/gb-results.txt" | awk '{print $3}') tlb_inring=$1" >> "$O/tlbinring.txt"
  say "TLBINRING $2: $(tlbinring_short)"
}
tlbinring_gbcl() {   # knob run
  local d="$O/tlbinring-gbcl" g="$TLBINRING_DIR/cl_gbmicro" tag="k$1-$2" r0 r1 g0 t0 g1 t1
  [ -x "$g" ] || { say "TLBINRING gbcl: no binary at $g"; return 0; }
  mkdir -p "$d"; tlbinring_set "$1"; r0=$(resets)
  ( export NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 NVMTL_ENABLE=1 NVMTL_IMPORT_UNALIGNED=1
    tmo $((15 * 4 * 3 + 60)) "$g" -q -t 15 -m chain,churn,import,mixed ) > "$d/$tag.log" 2>&1
  r1=$(resets); read -r g0 t0 <<< "${r0:-0 0}"; read -r g1 t1 <<< "${r1:-0 0}"
  sed -n "s/^RESULT /RESULT knob=$1 run=$2 /p" "$d/$tag.log" >> "$d/results.txt"
  grep -qE '^(CHECK|FAIL)' "$d/$tag.log" && say "TLBINRING gbcl $tag: $(grep -E '^(CHECK|FAIL)' "$d/$tag.log" | head -2 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [ $((g1 - g0 + t1 - t0)) -gt 0 ] && say "TLBINRING gbcl $tag: guc+$((g1 - g0)) gt+$((t1 - t0))"
  say "TLBINRING gbcl $tag: $(grep '^RESULT' "$d/$tag.log" | sed -nE 's/RESULT mode=([a-z]+) .*ops_s=([0-9.]+) p50_us=([0-9.]+).*/\1 \2\/s p50 \3/p' | tr '\n' ' ')"
}
phase_tlbinring() {
  if ! sysctl -n debug.intelxe.tlb_inring >/dev/null 2>&1; then say "TLBINRING: kext without debug.intelxe.tlb_inring, skipped"; return 0; fi
  say "TLBINRING start: exec_tlb_dep $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.exec_tlb_dep 2>&1) (want 1), direct $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.direct), on = $TLBINRING_ON; resets $(resets)"
  sudo -n sysctl debug.intelxe.exec_tlb_dep=1 >/dev/null 2>&1
  : > "$O/tlbinring.txt"
  # 1. Geekbench OpenCL import, alternating which side goes first
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    if [ $((i % 2)) = 1 ]; then tlbinring_gb 0 "tlbinring-off$i"; tlbinring_gb "$TLBINRING_ON" "tlbinring-on$i"
    else tlbinring_gb "$TLBINRING_ON" "tlbinring-on$i"; tlbinring_gb 0 "tlbinring-off$i"; fi
  done
  say "TLBINRING GB OpenCL import: off $(grep -E '^tlbinring-off' "$O/tlbinring.txt" | awk '{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ')on $(grep -E '^tlbinring-on' "$O/tlbinring.txt" | awk '{print $2}' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  # 2. cl_gbmicro
  mkdir -p "$O/tlbinring-gbcl"; : > "$O/tlbinring-gbcl/results.txt"
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    if [ $((i % 2)) = 1 ]; then tlbinring_gbcl 0 "$i"; tlbinring_gbcl "$TLBINRING_ON" "$i"
    else tlbinring_gbcl "$TLBINRING_ON" "$i"; tlbinring_gbcl 0 "$i"; fi
  done
  # 3. CAT stress, knob on
  local bs="$TLBINRING_DIR/bindstress-tlb" mode=bindfence
  [ -x "$bs" ] || { bs=~/b580/cat/bindstress; mode=""; say "TLBINRING bindstress: no bindstress-tlb next to this script, ~/b580/cat/bindstress without bindfence (the new path is not exercised)"; }
  tlbinring_set "$TLBINRING_ON"
  { echo "== bindstress (tlb_inring=$TLBINRING_ON) before"; tlbinring_line; } >> "$O/tlbinring-counters.txt"
  ( cd ~/b580/cat && tmo 800 "$bs" 10 r,rl,c,cl $mode > "$O/bs-tlbinring.log" 2>&1 )
  { echo "== bindstress after"; tlbinring_line; } >> "$O/tlbinring-counters.txt"
  say "TLBINRING bindstress 10 min $mode tlb_inring=$TLBINRING_ON: $(tail -1 "$O/bs-tlbinring.log"); $(grep -m1 '^kext deltas' "$O/bs-tlbinring.log" | cut -c1-160)"
  say "TLBINRING bindstress counters: $(tlbinring_short)"
  grep -q 'RESULT: PASS' "$O/bs-tlbinring.log" || sudo -n sysctl -n debug.intelxe.g2h | tail -60 > "$O/g2h-tlbinring-bs.txt" 2>&1
  tlbinring_set 0
  say "TLBINRING end: tlb_inring $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.tlb_inring); resets $(resets)"
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/pcode_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// pcode_test: offline check of the pcode mailbox and power-limit path's pure parts (xe_pcode.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. registers, commands and fields equal Linux xe_pcode_api.h, xe_pcode.h and regs/xe_mchbar_regs.h
//   2. pcode_mailbox_status's error decoding (xe_pcode.c:38-71)
//   3. __pcode_mailbox_rw (xe_pcode.c:73-102) against a fake pcode: write order, read-back, busy mailbox, an absent
//      device, the timeout and its total wait, __xe_mmio_wait32's last read (xe_mmio.c:361-370), error replies
//   4. unit scaling of the limit words (xe_hwmon.c:361-362, :585-601, :903-904) and the report text
//   5. the descriptor: BMG (G21 and G31) has mailbox power limits (xe_pci.c:421); no other family here does
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o pcode_test pcode_test.cpp ../xe_platform.cpp && ./pcode_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <vector>
#include "xe_platform.h"
#include "xe_pcode.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// A pcode behind PCODE_MAILBOX/DATA0/DATA1: a command written with READY stays busy for `busyReads` mailbox reads, then
// READY clears, the error field holds `error` and DATA0/DATA1 hold the reply.
struct FakePcode {
	uint32_t mailbox {0}, data0 {0}, data1 {0};
	uint32_t busyReads {2}, error {PCODE_SUCCESS}, reply0 {0}, reply1 {0};
	bool absent {false};        // the device does not answer: every read is all ones
	bool neverDone {false};     // READY never clears
	uint32_t busyLeft {0};
	uint64_t waitedUs {0};
	std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, uint32_t>> writes;
	uint32_t rd(uint32_t off) {
		if (absent) return 0xffffffffu;
		if (off == PCODE_MAILBOX) {
			if ((mailbox & PCODE_READY) && !neverDone) {
				if (busyLeft) busyLeft--;
				else {
					mailbox = error;   // READY clear, error code in 7:0
					data0 = reply0;
					data1 = reply1;
				}
			}
			return mailbox;
		}
		return off == PCODE_DATA0 ? data0 : off == PCODE_DATA1 ? data1 : 0xdeadbeefu;
	}
	void wr(uint32_t off, uint32_t v) {
		writes.push_back({off, v});
		if (off == PCODE_MAILBOX) mailbox = v, busyLeft = busyReads;
		else if (off == PCODE_DATA0) data0 = v;
		else if (off == PCODE_DATA1) data1 = v;
	}
	void delayUs(uint32_t us) { waitedUs += us; }
};

int main() {
	// 1. constants
	CHECK(PCODE_MAILBOX == 0x138124 && PCODE_DATA0 == 0x138128 && PCODE_DATA1 == 0x13812c, "mailbox registers");
	CHECK(PCODE_READY == 0x80000000u && PCODE_ERROR_MASK == 0xff, "READY bit 31, error 7:0");
	CHECK(PCODE_POWER_SETUP == 0x7c && POWER_SETUP_SUBCOMMAND_READ_I1 == 4, "PCODE_POWER_SETUP, READ_I1");
	CHECK(READ_PSYSGPU_POWER_LIMIT == 6 && READ_PACKAGE_POWER_LIMIT == 8, "card / package power-limit subcommands");
	CHECK(READ_PL_FROM_PCODE == 0 && READ_PL_FROM_FW == 1 && READ_PL_ACCEPTED == 2, "param2 of the limit reads");
	CHECK(DGFX_PCODE_STATUS == 0x7e && DGFX_GET_INIT_STATUS == 0 && DGFX_INIT_STATUS_COMPLETE == 1, "init status");
	CHECK(PCODE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS == 10, "xe_pcode_read timeout");
	CHECK(PWR_LIM_VAL == 0x7fff && PWR_LIM_EN == 0x8000, "PWR_LIM_VAL 14:0, PWR_LIM_EN 15");
	CHECK(XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX == 3 && XE_TIME_UNIT_MBX == 10, "PWR_UNIT 0x3, TIME_UNIT 0xa");
	CHECK(POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS == 0x80000000u && POWER_SETUP_I1_SHIFT == 6 && POWER_SETUP_I1_DATA_MASK == 0xffff, "I1");
	CHECK(xePcodeMbox(PCODE_POWER_SETUP, READ_PSYSGPU_POWER_LIMIT, READ_PL_FROM_FW) == 0x01067c, "PCODE_MBOX 0x%06x",
		xePcodeMbox(PCODE_POWER_SETUP, READ_PSYSGPU_POWER_LIMIT, READ_PL_FROM_FW));
	CHECK(xePcodeMbox(PCODE_POWER_SETUP, READ_PACKAGE_POWER_LIMIT, READ_PL_FROM_PCODE) == 0x00087c, "package, from pcode");
	CHECK(xePcodeMbox(0x1ff, 0x1ff, 0x1ff) == 0xffffff, "fields masked to 8 bits");

	// 2. status
	struct { uint32_t code; int err; } st[] = {{PCODE_SUCCESS, 0}, {PCODE_ILLEGAL_CMD, ENXIO}, {PCODE_TIMEOUT, ETIMEDOUT},
		{PCODE_ILLEGAL_DATA, EINVAL}, {PCODE_ILLEGAL_SUBCOMMAND, ENXIO}, {PCODE_LOCKED, EBUSY},
		{PCODE_GT_RATIO_OUT_OF_RANGE, EOVERFLOW}, {PCODE_REJECTED, EACCES}, {0x5, EPROTO}, {0xff, EPROTO}};
	for (auto &t : st) CHECK(xePcodeStatusErrno(0x7c00u | t.code) == t.err, "status 0x%x -> %d", t.code, t.err);
	CHECK(xePcodeStatusErrno(0x01067c00u) == 0, "only bits 7:0 are the error");

	// 3. the mailbox protocol
	{
		FakePcode p;
		p.reply0 = 0x00038cf0u;
		p.reply1 = 0x00008708u;
		uint32_t d0 = 0, d1 = 0;
		const uint32_t mbox = xePcodeMbox(PCODE_POWER_SETUP, READ_PSYSGPU_POWER_LIMIT, READ_PL_FROM_FW);
		const int err = xePcodeMailboxRw(p, mbox, &d0, &d1, PCODE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS * 1000, true);
		CHECK(err == 0 && d0 == 0x00038cf0u && d1 == 0x00008708u, "read: err %d data 0x%08x 0x%08x", err, d0, d1);
		CHECK(p.writes.size() == 3 && p.writes[0] == std::make_pair(PCODE_DATA0, 0u) && p.writes[1] == std::make_pair(PCODE_DATA1, 0u) &&
			p.writes[2] == std::make_pair(PCODE_MAILBOX, PCODE_READY | mbox), "DATA0, DATA1, then MAILBOX = READY | mbox");
		CHECK(p.waitedUs == 10 + 20, "waits double from 10 us: %llu us", (unsigned long long)p.waitedUs);
	}
	{
		FakePcode p;   // the request goes in DATA0 (pcode_try_request); no DATA1 given: 0 is written
		uint32_t d0 = 0x12345678;
		xePcodeMailboxRw(p, DGFX_PCODE_STATUS, &d0, nullptr, 1000, true);
		CHECK(p.writes.size() == 3 && p.writes[0].second == 0x12345678 && p.writes[1].second == 0, "DATA0 request, DATA1 0");
	}
	{
		FakePcode p;   // busy before the request: -EAGAIN, nothing written
		p.mailbox = PCODE_READY | 0x7c;
		p.neverDone = true;
		uint32_t d0 = 0, d1 = 0;
		CHECK(xePcodeMailboxRw(p, 0x7c, &d0, &d1, 10000, true) == EAGAIN && p.writes.empty(), "busy mailbox: EAGAIN, no write");
	}
	{
		FakePcode p;   // a device that reads all ones
		p.absent = true;
		uint32_t d0 = 0;
		CHECK(xePcodeMailboxRw(p, 0x7c, &d0, nullptr, 10000, true) == EAGAIN && p.writes.empty(), "absent device: EAGAIN");
	}
	{
		FakePcode p;   // pcode never answers: ETIMEDOUT after exactly the timeout, data untouched
		p.neverDone = true;
		uint32_t d0 = 0xaaaa, d1 = 0xbbbb;
		const int err = xePcodeMailboxRw(p, 0x7c, &d0, &d1, PCODE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS * 1000, true);
		CHECK(err == ETIMEDOUT && p.waitedUs == 10000 && d0 == 0xaaaa && d1 == 0xbbbb, "timeout: err %d after %llu us", err,
			(unsigned long long)p.waitedUs);
	}
	{
		// the answer comes with the read after the deadline: success (xe_mmio.c:361-370). 10 ms in doubling waits from
		// 10 us is 10 waits (10+20+...+2560 = 5110, then 4890 to the deadline): 11 polls, then the last read.
		FakePcode p;
		p.busyReads = 11;
		p.reply0 = 7;
		uint32_t d0 = 0;
		const int err = xePcodeMailboxRw(p, 0x7c, &d0, nullptr, 10000, true);
		CHECK(err == 0 && d0 == 7 && p.waitedUs == 10000, "answer at the last read: err %d, waited %llu us", err,
			(unsigned long long)p.waitedUs);
	}
	{
		FakePcode p;   // an error reply: the data is read back, the error decoded
		p.error = PCODE_ILLEGAL_SUBCOMMAND;
		p.reply0 = 0x55;
		uint32_t d0 = 0;
		CHECK(xePcodeMailboxRw(p, 0x7c, &d0, nullptr, 10000, true) == ENXIO && d0 == 0x55, "illegal subcommand: ENXIO");
		FakePcode q;
		q.error = PCODE_LOCKED;
		uint32_t e0 = 0;
		CHECK(xePcodeMailboxRw(q, 0x7c, &e0, nullptr, 10000, false) == EBUSY && e0 == 0, "locked: EBUSY; no read-back asked");
	}

	// 4. units and text
	CHECK(xePowerLimitMw(PWR_LIM_EN | 190 * 8, XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX) == 190000, "190 W");
	CHECK(xePowerLimitMw(1, XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX) == 125, "one count = 1/8 W");
	CHECK(xePowerLimitMw(0xffffffffu, XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX) == 4095875, "only bits 14:0 count: %u mW",
		xePowerLimitMw(0xffffffffu, XE_PWR_UNIT_MBX));
	CHECK(xePowerLimitTauMs(10u << PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_SHIFT, XE_TIME_UNIT_MBX) == 1000, "x 0, y 10: 1 s");
	CHECK(xePowerLimitTauMs(3u << PWR_LIM_TIME_X_SHIFT | 12u << PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_SHIFT, XE_TIME_UNIT_MBX) == 7000,
		"x 3, y 12: 1.75 * 4 s");
	CHECK(xePowerLimitTauMs(0, XE_TIME_UNIT_MBX) == 0, "x 0, y 0: 4 / 4096 s rounds to 0 ms");
	CHECK(xePowerI1Milli(POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS | 300u << 6) == 300000, "I1 300 W");
	CHECK(xePowerI1Milli(1) == 15, "I1 1/64: %u", xePowerI1Milli(1));

	XePowerLimits pl;
	char buf[512];
	size_t n = xePowerLimitsText(buf, sizeof buf, pl);
	CHECK(!strcmp(buf, ", power limits unavailable (pcode error 96)") && n == strlen(buf), "not read: %s", buf);
	pl.err = 0;
	pl.word[XE_PL_CARD][0] = PWR_LIM_EN | 190 * 8 | 10u << PWR_LIM_TIME_Y_SHIFT;
	pl.word[XE_PL_CARD][1] = 2 * 8 + 1;   // 2.125 W, off
	pl.word[XE_PL_PKG][0] = PWR_LIM_EN | (150 * 8 + 4);
	pl.word[XE_PL_PKG][1] = PWR_LIM_EN | 300 * 8;
	n = xePowerLimitsText(buf, sizeof buf, pl);
	CHECK(!strcmp(buf, ", card PL1 190 W (on), card PL2 2.125 W (off), package PL1 150.500 W (on), package PL2 300 W (on)"),
		"limits: %s", buf);
	pl.i1Err = 0;
	pl.i1 = POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS | (400u << 6 | 32);
	n = xePowerLimitsText(buf, sizeof buf, pl);
	CHECK(n == strlen(buf) && strstr(buf, "package PL2 300 W (on), card crit 400.500 W") && buf[n - 1] == 'W', "I1 W: %s", buf);
	pl.i1 = 50u << 6;
	xePowerLimitsText(buf, sizeof buf, pl);
	CHECK(strstr(buf, ", card crit 50.000 A") != nullptr, "I1 without bit 31 is amperes: %s", buf);
	char small[24];
	memset(small, 'x', sizeof small);
	n = xePowerLimitsText(small, sizeof small, pl);
	CHECK(n == sizeof small - 1 && small[n] == 0 && !strncmp(small, ", card PL1 190 W (on), c", n), "cut to the buffer: %zu '%s'",
		n, small);
	CHECK(xePowerLimitsText(small, 0, pl) == 0, "no room: nothing");
	// the text must not look like the fields tools/regress and the app take the first match of
	pl.word[XE_PL_CARD][0] = PWR_LIM_EN | 190 * 8;
	xePowerLimitsText(buf, sizeof buf, pl);
	CHECK(!strstr(buf, "card power") && !strstr(buf, "package power") && !strstr(buf, " C,") && !strstr(buf, "MHz"),
		"no field names of the earlier text: %s", buf);

	// 5. descriptor
	for (uint32_t p = 0; p < kXePlatformCount; p++)
		CHECK(kXePlatforms[p].hasMbxPowerLimits == (kXePlatforms[p].platform == XE_BATTLEMAGE), "%s%s: has_mbx_power_limits",
			kXePlatforms[p].name, kXePlatforms[p].subplatform ? kXePlatforms[p].subplatform : "");
	CHECK(xePlatformFind(0xe20b)->hasMbxPowerLimits && xePlatformFind(0xe212)->hasMbxPowerLimits &&
		xePlatformFind(0xe223)->hasMbxPowerLimits, "B580, Pro B50, G31");

	printf("%s: %d checks, %d failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/pmt_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// pmt_test: offline check of the BMG energy path's pure parts (xe_pmt.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. the BAR0 offsets equal Linux regs/xe_pmt.h, regs/xe_regs.h and regs/xe_soc_remapper_regs.h
//   2. xe_guid_decode (xe_vsec.c:97-139) for every record/capability, and refusals of foreign GUIDs
//   3. the re-mapper rmw keeps the other bits; ENERGY_PKG / ENERGY_CARD field extraction
//   4. unit scaling (mul_u64_u32_shr(accum, SF_ENERGY, 14)) against 128-bit arithmetic
//   5. 32-bit wrap accumulation (xe_hwmon.c:534-535), the meter's power windows and the resync after suspend
//   6. the descriptor: BMG (G21 and G31) reads energy from PMT with unit shift 14; no other family reads energy
//   7. the power-window sanity guard: the B580's post-boot readings (package 85 W, then 152 W, card 37 W) are refused,
//      re-based and counted; the boundary of the margin; the 600 W ceiling; a counter that steps back
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o pmt_test pmt_test.cpp ../xe_platform.cpp && ./pmt_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include "xe_platform.h"
#include "xe_pmt.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// A GUID with the xe_vsec.c:73-78 layout
static uint32_t guid(uint32_t record, uint32_t cap, uint32_t device = BMG_PMT_GUID_DEVICE_ID, uint32_t low = 0) {
	return record << 30 | cap << 28 | (device & 0xffff) << 12 | (low & 0xfff);
}

int main() {
	// 1. offsets
	CHECK(PUNIT_TELEMETRY_GUID == 0x35b004, "PUNIT_TELEMETRY_GUID 0x%x", PUNIT_TELEMETRY_GUID);
	CHECK(BMG_DISCOVERY_OFFSET == 0x35b000, "BMG_DISCOVERY_OFFSET 0x%x", BMG_DISCOVERY_OFFSET);
	CHECK(BMG_TELEMETRY_OFFSET == 0x360000, "BMG_TELEMETRY_OFFSET 0x%x", BMG_TELEMETRY_OFFSET);
	CHECK(SG_REMAP_INDEX1 == 0x280008, "SG_REMAP_INDEX1 0x%x", SG_REMAP_INDEX1);
	CHECK(SG_REMAP_TELEM_MASK == 0xff000000u, "SG_REMAP_TELEM_MASK 0x%x", SG_REMAP_TELEM_MASK);
	CHECK(BMG_ENERGY_STATUS_PMT_OFFSET == 0x30, "energy offset");

	// 2. GUID decode
	uint32_t idx = 99, off = 99;
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT, XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY, BMG_PMT_GUID_DEVICE_ID, 0xabc), &idx, &off) == 0 &&
		idx == 0 && off == 0x200, "PUNIT telemetry: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtTelemOffset(off, BMG_ENERGY_STATUS_PMT_OFFSET) == 0x360230, "energy word at BAR0 0x%x",
		xePmtTelemOffset(off, BMG_ENERGY_STATUS_PMT_OFFSET));
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT, XE_PMT_CAP_WATCHER), &idx, &off) == 0 && idx == 0 && off == 0x14a0,
		"PUNIT watcher: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT, XE_PMT_CAP_CRASHLOG), &idx, &off) == 0 && idx == 2 && off == 0,
		"PUNIT crashlog: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_0, XE_PMT_CAP_CRASHLOG), &idx, &off) == 0 && idx == 4 && off == 0,
		"OOBMSM crashlog: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_0, XE_PMT_CAP_WATCHER), &idx, &off) == 0 && idx == 1 && off == 0x18d8,
		"OOBMSM_0 watcher: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_0, XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY), &idx, &off) == 0 && idx == 1 && off == 0,
		"OOBMSM_0 telemetry: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_OOBMSM_1, XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY), &idx, &off) == 0 && idx == 1 && off == 0x1000,
		"OOBMSM_1 telemetry: index %u offset 0x%x", idx, off);
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(3, XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY), &idx, &off) == -22, "record 3: -EINVAL");
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT, 3), &idx, &off) == -22, "capability 3: -EINVAL");
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(guid(XE_PMT_RECORD_PUNIT, XE_PMT_CAP_TELEMETRY, 0xe2f9), &idx, &off) == -19, "other device: -ENODEV");
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(0xffffffffu, &idx, &off) == -19, "device gone (all ones): -ENODEV");
	CHECK(xePmtGuidDecode(0, &idx, &off) == -19, "zero GUID: -ENODEV");

	// 3. re-mapper and fields
	CHECK(xePmtRemapValue(0xabcdef12u, 0) == 0x00cdef12u, "remap index 0: 0x%08x", xePmtRemapValue(0xabcdef12u, 0));
	CHECK(xePmtRemapValue(0x00cdef12u, 4) == 0x04cdef12u, "remap index 4: 0x%08x", xePmtRemapValue(0x00cdef12u, 4));
	CHECK(xePmtEnergyPkg(0x1122334455667788ull) == 0x55667788u, "ENERGY_PKG is bits 31:0");
	CHECK(xePmtEnergyCard(0x1122334455667788ull) == 0x11223344u, "ENERGY_CARD is bits 63:32");

	// 4. scaling: 2^-14 J per count
	CHECK(xeEnergyMicrojoules(1ull << 14, 14) == 1000000, "one joule");
	CHECK(xeEnergyMicrojoules(1, 14) == 61, "one count = %llu uJ", (unsigned long long)xeEnergyMicrojoules(1, 14));
	CHECK(xeEnergyMicrojoules(3ull << 14 | 8192, 14) == 3500000, "3.5 J");
	uint64_t x = 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ull;
	for (int i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
		x ^= x << 13, x ^= x >> 7, x ^= x << 17;
		const uint64_t a = x >> 20;   // up to 2^44 counts (about a gigajoule): far beyond any uptime
		const uint64_t want = (uint64_t)((unsigned __int128)a * 1000000u >> 14);
		if (xeEnergyMicrojoules(a, 14) != want) {
			CHECK(false, "scaling of %llu: %llu, want %llu", (unsigned long long)a,
				(unsigned long long)xeEnergyMicrojoules(a, 14), (unsigned long long)want);
			break;
		}
	}
	checks++;

	// 5. accumulation
	XeEnergyAccum ea;
	ea.add(0x1000);
	CHECK(ea.accum == 0x1000, "the first read adds the counter itself (reg_val_prev 0)");
	ea.add(0xfffffff0u);
	ea.add(0x10);
	CHECK(ea.accum == 0x1000 + (0xfffffff0ull - 0x1000) + 0x20, "wrap: +0x20 across 2^32, accum 0x%llx",
		(unsigned long long)ea.accum);
	ea.add(0x10);
	CHECK(ea.accum == 0x100000010ull, "no change, no add");

	const uint64_t J = 1ull << 14, s = 1000000000ull, win = s / 2;
	auto word = [](uint64_t card, uint64_t pkg) { return (uint64_t)(uint32_t)card << 32 | (uint32_t)pkg; };
	XeEnergyMeter m;
	uint64_t card = 100 * J, pkg = 40 * J;
	m.update(word(card, pkg), 10 * s, win);
	CHECK(!m.havePower && m.uj(XE_ENERGY_CARD) == 100000000 && m.uj(XE_ENERGY_PKG) == 40000000, "first read: energy, no power");
	card += J / 50, pkg += J / 100;   // 1 ms later (sysctl's size call, then the text): no window yet
	m.update(word(card, pkg), 10 * s + s / 1000, win);
	CHECK(!m.havePower, "a window shorter than 0.5 s gives no power");
	card += 20 * J - J / 50, pkg += 12 * J - J / 100;   // 20 W card, 12 W package over the second
	m.update(word(card, pkg), 11 * s, win);
	CHECK(m.havePower && m.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 20000 && m.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] == 12000, "1 s: card %u mW, package %u mW",
		m.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD], m.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG]);
	card += J;   // a second reader 0.1 s later: same averages, window kept
	m.update(word(card, pkg), 11 * s + s / 10, win);
	CHECK(m.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 20000 && m.baseNs == 11 * s, "short read keeps the last average and the base");
	card += 17 * J;   // 18 J card since the base at 11 s; package idle
	m.update(word(card, pkg), 12 * s, win);
	CHECK(m.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 18000 && m.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] == 0, "18 J over the 1 s since the base: card %u mW",
		m.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD]);
	// the counter wraps inside a window: 2^32 counts = 262144 J; 250 W for 2 s across the wrap
	card = 0x100000000ull - 3 * J;
	XeEnergyMeter w;
	w.update(word(card, pkg), 0, win);
	card += 500 * J;
	w.update(word(card, pkg), 2 * s, win);
	CHECK(w.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 250000, "wrap within the window: %u mW", w.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD]);
	CHECK(w.uj(XE_ENERGY_CARD) == (0x100000000ull + 497 * J) * 1000000 >> 14, "sum continues past 2^32 counts");
	// suspend: the counter restarts lower; the sum must not jump by a wrap
	const uint64_t before = w.uj(XE_ENERGY_CARD);
	w.resync = true;
	w.update(word(5 * J, 2 * J), 100 * s, win);
	CHECK(w.uj(XE_ENERGY_CARD) == before && !w.havePower && !w.resync, "resync: sum kept (%llu uJ), no power",
		(unsigned long long)w.uj(XE_ENERGY_CARD));
	w.update(word(5 * J + 15 * J, 2 * J + 5 * J), 101 * s, win);
	CHECK(w.havePower && w.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 15000 && w.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] == 5000 &&
		w.uj(XE_ENERGY_CARD) == before + 15000000, "after resync: 15 W / 5 W, card %u mW", w.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD]);

	// 7. sanity guard
	CHECK(xePowerWindowSane(37000, 19600) && xePowerWindowSane(0, 0) && xePowerWindowSane(190000, 150000), "normal windows");
	CHECK(!xePowerWindowSane(37000, 85000) && !xePowerWindowSane(37000, 152000), "package 85 / 152 W over card 37 W");
	CHECK(xePowerWindowSane(40000, 40000 + 10000 + 10000) && !xePowerWindowSane(40000, 60001),
		"margin: a quarter of the card plus 10 W");
	CHECK(xePowerWindowSane(0, 10000) && !xePowerWindowSane(0, 10001), "card 0: package up to 10 W");
	CHECK(xePowerWindowSane(600000, 600000) && !xePowerWindowSane(600001, 1000) && !xePowerWindowSane(600000, 600001),
		"600 W ceiling on either channel");
	{
		// after boot: windows of 1 s each. card 37 W throughout; package 85 W, then 152 W, then 19.5 W.
		XeEnergyMeter g;
		uint64_t c = 1000 * J, p = 600 * J;
		g.update(word(c, p), 5 * s, win);
		c += 37 * J, p += 85 * J;
		g.update(word(c, p), 6 * s, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && !g.pkgValid && g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 37000 && g.rejected == 1 && g.baseNs == 6 * s,
			"package 85 W > card 37 W: package n/a (card kept), re-based, counted");
		c += J / 10;   // a reader 0.1 s later: still n/a, the base kept
		g.update(word(c, p), 6 * s + s / 10, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && !g.pkgValid && g.rejected == 1 && g.baseNs == 6 * s, "inside the window after a refusal: package n/a, base kept");
		c += 37 * J - J / 10, p += 152 * J;
		g.update(word(c, p), 7 * s, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && !g.pkgValid && g.rejected == 2, "package 152 W: refused too (%u)", g.rejected);
		c += 37 * J, p += 19 * J + J / 2;   // 19.5 W (the idle reading was 19.6 W)
		g.update(word(c, p), 8 * s, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && g.pkgValid && g.rejected == 2 && g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 37000 && g.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] == 19500,
			"consistent window: card %u mW, package %u mW", g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD], g.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG]);
		CHECK(g.uj(XE_ENERGY_PKG) == (600 * J + 85 * J + 152 * J + 19 * J + J / 2) * 1000000 >> 14,
			"the energy sums are not touched by the guard");
		// a counter that steps back by one count reads as a 2^32 wrap: ~262144 J in 1 s, above the ceiling
		g.update(word(c, p - 1), 9 * s, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && !g.pkgValid && g.rejected == 3, "package counter stepped back: package refused (%u)", g.rejected);
		c += 30 * J, p += 1 + 15 * J;
		g.update(word(c, p), 10 * s, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && g.pkgValid && g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 30000 && g.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] == 15000, "next window after it: %u / %u mW",
			g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD], g.mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG]);
		// the card counter stepping back is above the ceiling for the card itself: no power at all for that window
		g.update(word(c - 1, p + 15 * J), 11 * s, win);
		CHECK(!g.havePower && !g.pkgValid && g.rejected == 4, "card counter stepped back: both n/a (%u)", g.rejected);
		c += 30 * J, p += 15 * J;
		g.update(word(c - 1, p + 15 * J), 12 * s, win);
		CHECK(g.havePower && g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] == 30000, "card back to normal: %u mW", g.mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD]);
		// a refusal keeps the resync path's behaviour: the first read after resume still only re-bases
		g.resync = true;
		g.update(word(3 * J, J), 50 * s, win);
		CHECK(!g.havePower && !g.pkgValid && g.rejected == 4, "resync is not a refusal");
	}

	// 6. descriptor
	const XePlatformDesc *g21 = xePlatformFind(0xe20b), *g31 = xePlatformFind(0xe221);
	CHECK(g21 && g21->energySource == XE_ENERGY_PMT && g21->energyShift == 14 && g21->hasSocRemapperTelem, "BMG-G21");
	CHECK(g31 && g31->energySource == XE_ENERGY_PMT && g31->energyShift == 14 && g31->hasSocRemapperTelem, "BMG-G31");
	for (uint32_t p = 0; p < kXePlatformCount; p++)
		if (kXePlatforms[p].platform != XE_BATTLEMAGE)
			CHECK(kXePlatforms[p].energySource == XE_ENERGY_NONE && !kXePlatforms[p].hasSocRemapperTelem,
				"%s: no energy source yet", kXePlatforms[p].name);

	printf("%s: %d checks, %d failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/probe_css_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// probe_css_test: offline check of XeProbe's GuC image header check (xe_probe_css.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. well-formed headers (RSA 2048 as tgl/adlp/dg1, RSA 3072 as dg2/mtl/lnl/ptl/bmg) pass, with the upload size,
//      the RSA size, the version and the private data size Linux xe_uc_fw.c parse_css_header computes
//   2. every malformed header is refused before a size is used: shorter than the header, key sizes that do not add up
//      to the 128-byte header, size_dw under header_size_dw (the old code wrapped around), no ucode, an image shorter
//      than header + ucode + RSA, a private data size past the cap
//   3. with a directory argument: every <stem>_guc_70.bin of firmware/probe-guc.sha256 found there passes, and carries
//      the version that file lists (run after firmware/fetch.sh --probe)
// from kernel/IntelXe: c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I. -o /tmp/probe_css_test tests/probe_css_test.cpp &&
//   /tmp/probe_css_test [FIRMWARE_DIR [PINS (default ../../firmware/probe-guc.sha256)]]
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <string>
#include <vector>
#include "xe_probe_css.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// An image as linux-firmware lays it out: the CSS header, ucode, the RSA signature (key_size_dw dwords).
static std::vector<uint8_t> image(uint32_t keyDw, uint32_t ucodeBytes, uint32_t ver, uint32_t priv = 8392704) {
	uc_css_header h = {};
	h.module_type = 0x6;
	h.key_size_dw = keyDw;
	h.modulus_size_dw = keyDw;
	h.exponent_size_dw = 1;
	h.header_size_dw = 32 + 2 * keyDw + 1;
	h.size_dw = h.header_size_dw + ucodeBytes / 4;
	h.sw_version = ver;
	h.private_data_size = priv;
	std::vector<uint8_t> b(sizeof(h) + ucodeBytes + keyDw * 4, 0xa5);
	memcpy(b.data(), &h, sizeof(h));
	return b;
}
static uc_css_header *hdr(std::vector<uint8_t> &b) { return reinterpret_cast<uc_css_header *>(b.data()); }
static bool check(const std::vector<uint8_t> &b, XpCss *c = nullptr) { return xpCssCheck(b.data(), (uint32_t)b.size(), c); }

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	// 1. well-formed
	for (uint32_t keyDw : {64u, 96u}) {
		auto b = image(keyDw, 0x40000, 70u << 16 | 72u << 8 | 1u);
		XpCss c = {};
		CHECK(check(b, &c), "RSA %u bits refused", keyDw * 32);
		CHECK(c.upload == 128 + 0x40000, "upload %u", c.upload);
		CHECK(c.rsa == keyDw * 4, "rsa %u", c.rsa);
		CHECK(xpVerMajor(c.ver) == 70 && xpVerMinor(c.ver) == 72 && xpVerPatch(c.ver) == 1, "version %08x", c.ver);
		CHECK(c.priv == 8392704, "priv %u", c.priv);
		CHECK(xpCssCheck(b.data(), (uint32_t)b.size(), nullptr), "no out pointer");
		// trailing bytes after the signature are allowed (Linux takes the sizes from the header)
		b.resize(b.size() + 4096, 0);
		CHECK(check(b), "trailing bytes refused");
	}

	// 2. malformed
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0);
		CHECK(!xpCssCheck(b.data(), 127, nullptr), "shorter than the header accepted");
		CHECK(!xpCssCheck(nullptr, 4096, nullptr), "null image accepted");
	}
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0);
		hdr(b)->modulus_size_dw = 95;   // header no longer 128 bytes after the keys
		CHECK(!check(b), "key sizes that do not add up accepted");
	}
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0);
		hdr(b)->key_size_dw = 0xffffffffu;   // keys past header_size_dw: the old subtraction wrapped around
		CHECK(!check(b), "keys larger than the header accepted");
	}
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0);
		hdr(b)->size_dw = hdr(b)->header_size_dw - 1;   // the old (size_dw - header_size_dw) * 4 wrapped to ~16 GB
		CHECK(!check(b), "size_dw under header_size_dw accepted");
	}
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0);
		hdr(b)->size_dw = hdr(b)->header_size_dw;
		CHECK(!check(b), "an image without ucode accepted");
	}
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0);
		b.resize(b.size() - 1);   // the RSA signature one byte short
		CHECK(!check(b), "truncated image accepted");
		b.resize(128 + 0x800);
		CHECK(!check(b), "image cut in the ucode accepted");
	}
	{
		auto b = image(96, 0x1000, 0, kXpCssMaxPriv + 1);
		CHECK(!check(b), "private data size past the cap accepted");
		auto ok = image(96, 0x1000, 0, kXpCssMaxPriv);
		CHECK(check(ok), "private data size at the cap refused");
	}

	// 3. the pinned linux-firmware images, when given
	if (argc > 1) {
		const std::string dir = argv[1], pins = argc > 2 ? argv[2] : "../../firmware/probe-guc.sha256";
		FILE *pf = fopen(pins.c_str(), "r");
		CHECK(pf, "cannot read %s", pins.c_str());
		char line[512];
		int found = 0;
		while (pf && fgets(line, sizeof(line), pf)) {
			char sha[80], path[128], ver[32];
			if (line[0] == '#' || sscanf(line, "%79s %127s %31s", sha, path, ver) != 3) continue;
			const char *name = strrchr(path, '/') ? strrchr(path, '/') + 1 : path;
			FILE *f = fopen((dir + "/" + name).c_str(), "rb");
			if (!f) continue;
			std::vector<uint8_t> b;
			uint8_t chunk[65536];
			for (size_t k; (k = fread(chunk, 1, sizeof(chunk), f)) > 0;) b.insert(b.end(), chunk, chunk + k);
			fclose(f);
			XpCss c = {};
			CHECK(check(b, &c), "%s refused", name);
			char got[32];
			snprintf(got, sizeof(got), "%u.%u.%u", xpVerMajor(c.ver), xpVerMinor(c.ver), xpVerPatch(c.ver));
			CHECK(!strcmp(got, ver), "%s carries %s, %s lists %s", name, got, pins.c_str(), ver);
			found++;
		}
		if (pf) fclose(pf);
		printf("%d pinned image(s) found in %s\n", found, dir.c_str());
	}

	printf("%d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// recovery_test: offline check of the job watchdog's recovery rules after a GuC context reset (xe_recovery.h, rb8d).
//   1. xeNotStartedLimitMs: Linux's 5 s TDR (xe_hw_engine.c job_timeout_ms) for a job that never started, the
//      configured timeout when it is lower, off when the watchdog is off
//   2. xeResetDomain: render and compute share a reset domain, copy and video do not
//   3. xeStuckAfterReset: a never-started job is stuck only 2 s after both the reset and its own submission, within
//      the 30 s window; a started job never is; and through a model of the 12 Nov fault (CAT reset at t, the next
//      queue's job submitted 1 ms later, watchdog every 500 ms) the GT reset comes 2-2.5 s after the fault, not 10 s
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o recovery_test recovery_test.cpp && ./recovery_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include "xe_recovery.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

int main() {
	// 1.
	CHECK(xeNotStartedLimitMs(10000) == 5000, "10 s timeout: %llu", (unsigned long long)xeNotStartedLimitMs(10000));
	CHECK(xeNotStartedLimitMs(2000) == 2000, "lower timeout kept");
	CHECK(xeNotStartedLimitMs(0) == 0, "watchdog off");
	CHECK(xeNotStartedLimitMs(5000) == 5000, "equal");

	// 2.
	CHECK(xeResetDomain(0) == xeResetDomain(4) && xeResetDomain(0) >= 0, "render and compute");
	CHECK(xeResetDomain(1) != xeResetDomain(0) && xeResetDomain(2) != xeResetDomain(3) && xeResetDomain(3) != xeResetDomain(0),
		"copy, video decode, video enhance: their own");
	CHECK(xeResetDomain(9) == -1, "unknown class");

	// 3.
	const uint64_t s = 1000000000ull, t = 100 * s;
	CHECK(!xeStuckAfterReset(t + 3 * s, 0, t, false), "no reset");
	CHECK(!xeStuckAfterReset(t + 3 * s, t, t, true), "started");
	CHECK(!xeStuckAfterReset(t + s, t, t - 5 * s, false), "1 s after the reset");
	CHECK(xeStuckAfterReset(t + 2 * s, t, t - 5 * s, false), "2 s after the reset, outstanding from before");
	CHECK(!xeStuckAfterReset(t + 3 * s, t, t + 2 * s, false), "submitted 1 s ago");
	CHECK(xeStuckAfterReset(t + 4 * s, t, t + 2 * s, false), "submitted 2 s ago");
	CHECK(!xeStuckAfterReset(t + 31 * s, t, t + 28 * s, false), "outside the window");
	CHECK(!xeStuckAfterReset(t - s, t, t - 5 * s, false), "reset in the future (clock read before it)");
	// the 12 Nov sequence: CAT at t, the next job submitted at t + 1 ms; the watchdog first sees it at its next run
	// (every 500 ms) and checks again every 500 ms; a GT reset at the first check that finds it stuck
	{
		const uint64_t submit = t + 1000000, phase = 137000000;   // the watchdog's runs are at phase + k * 500 ms
		uint64_t since = 0, resetAt = 0;
		for (uint64_t now = t - s + phase; now < t + 15 * s && !resetAt; now += 500000000ull) {
			if (now < submit) continue;
			if (!since) {
				since = now;
				continue;
			}
			if (xeStuckAfterReset(now, t, since, false)) resetAt = now;
			else if (now - since >= xeNotStartedLimitMs(10000) * 1000000ull) resetAt = now;   // the plain not-started limit
		}
		CHECK(resetAt && resetAt - t >= 2 * s && resetAt - t <= 3 * s, "GT reset %.2f s after the fault",
			resetAt ? (double)(resetAt - t) / s : -1.0);
	}

	printf("recovery_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/sensors_test.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// sensors_test: offline check of debug.intelxe.sensors and sensors_raw's pure parts (xe_sensors.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. struct intelxe_sensors' layout (uapi/intelxe_sensors.h: xemac and NEO's sysman read it; offsets fixed; version
//      2 appends the engine counters after version 1's 120 bytes)
//   2. the sample from register values: the 50/3 MHz decoding, the temperature fields, an absent device
//   3. the energy meter and the power limits into the struct (microjoules, milliwatts, enable bits, I1)
//   4. the text: identical to what IntelXe::sensorsString printed before the binary form (a copy of that code below,
//      compared over fixed and pseudo-random samples and every buffer length up to the whole text)
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o sensors_test sensors_test.cpp && ./sensors_test
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_sensors.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

// IntelXe::sensorsString before sensors_raw (kernel/IntelXe/IntelXe.cpp at 6adbb5b), with the register reads, the
// telemetry read and the limits read as inputs. `energyKnown` = PMT platform with its lock, `limitsKnown` = mailbox
// limits with their lock.
struct Legacy {
	uint32_t wp1, req, cap, pkg, vram;
	bool energyKnown;
	int err;
	uint32_t guid;
	XeEnergyMeter energy;
	bool limitsKnown;
	XePowerLimits pl;
};
static int legacyText(char *buf, size_t len, const Legacy &in) {
	auto mhz = [](uint32_t raw) { return (raw * 50 + 1) / 3; };
	const uint32_t wp1 = in.wp1, req = in.req, cap = in.cap, pkg = in.pkg, vram = in.vram;
	if (wp1 == 0xffffffffu && cap == 0xffffffffu) return snprintf(buf, len, "unavailable (the device does not answer)\n");
	size_t n = (size_t)snprintf(buf, len, "act %u MHz, req %u MHz, RP0 %u MHz, RPn %u MHz, package %u C, VRAM %u C",
		mhz(wp1 & 0x1ff), mhz(req >> 23 & 0x1ff), mhz(cap & 0x1ff), mhz(cap >> 16 & 0x1ff), pkg & 0xff, vram & 0xff);
	if (in.energyKnown) {
		uint64_t uj[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS] = {};
		uint32_t mw[XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS] = {}, rejected = 0;
		bool power = false, pkgPower = false;
		const int err = in.err;
		if (!err) {
			for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_ENERGY_CHANNELS; c++) uj[c] = in.energy.uj(c), mw[c] = in.energy.mw[c];
			power = in.energy.havePower;
			pkgPower = in.energy.pkgValid;
			rejected = in.energy.rejected;
		}
		if (err && n < len) {
			n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", energy unavailable (PMT error %d, GUID 0x%08x)", err, in.guid);
		} else if (n < len) {
			n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card energy %llu.%03llu J, package energy %llu.%03llu J",
				(unsigned long long)(uj[XE_ENERGY_CARD] / 1000000), (unsigned long long)(uj[XE_ENERGY_CARD] % 1000000 / 1000),
				(unsigned long long)(uj[XE_ENERGY_PKG] / 1000000), (unsigned long long)(uj[XE_ENERGY_PKG] % 1000000 / 1000));
			if (n < len && power)
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card power %u.%02u W", mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] / 1000,
					mw[XE_ENERGY_CARD] % 1000 / 10);
			else if (n < len)
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", card power n/a");
			if (n < len && pkgPower)
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", package power %u.%02u W", mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] / 1000,
					mw[XE_ENERGY_PKG] % 1000 / 10);
			else if (n < len)
				n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", package power n/a");
			if (n < len) n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, ", power windows rejected %u", rejected);
		}
	}
	if (in.limitsKnown && n < len) n += xePowerLimitsText(buf + n, len - n, in.pl);
	if (n < len) n += (size_t)snprintf(buf + n, len - n, "\n");
	return (int)n;
}

static XeSensorsSample sampleOf(const Legacy &in) {
	XeSensorsSample x;
	xeSensorsBegin(x, INTELXE_SENSORS_OK, 123);
	xeSensorsSetRegs(x, in.wp1, in.req, in.cap, in.pkg, in.vram);
	if (x.s.state != INTELXE_SENSORS_OK) return x;
	if (in.energyKnown) xeSensorsSetEnergy(x, in.err, in.guid, in.energy);
	if (in.limitsKnown) xeSensorsSetLimits(x, in.pl);
	return x;
}

// Every buffer length from 0 to the whole text + 2: same return value, same bytes (snprintf's cut included).
static void compareText(const Legacy &in, const char *what) {
	const XeSensorsSample x = sampleOf(in);
	char a[1024], b[1024];
	const int full = legacyText(a, sizeof a, in);
	CHECK(full > 0 && full < (int)sizeof a, "%s: legacy text length %d", what, full);
	for (size_t len = 0; len <= (size_t)full + 2; len++) {
		memset(a, 0x5a, sizeof a);
		memset(b, 0x5a, sizeof b);
		const int ra = legacyText(a, len, in), rb = xeSensorsText(b, len, x);
		if (ra != rb || memcmp(a, b, sizeof a)) {
			CHECK(false, "%s, len %zu: legacy %d \"%.*s\", new %d \"%.*s\"", what, len, ra, (int)(len ? len - 1 : 0), a,
				rb, (int)(len ? len - 1 : 0), b);
			return;
		}
	}
	checks++;
}

static uint64_t rng = 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ull;
static uint32_t rnd() {
	rng ^= rng << 13, rng ^= rng >> 7, rng ^= rng << 17;
	return (uint32_t)(rng >> 16);
}

int main() {
	// 1. layout
	// version 1 ends at 120 (reserved1 at 116); version 2 appends the engine counters there and changes nothing before
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, reserved1) == 116, "reserved1 at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, reserved1));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, engine_count) == 120, "engine_count at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, engine_count));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, engine_tick_hz) == 128, "engine_tick_hz at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, engine_tick_hz));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, engines) == 136, "engines at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, engines));
	CHECK(sizeof(intelxe_sensors_engine) == 32, "engine entry %zu", sizeof(intelxe_sensors_engine));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors_engine, active_ticks) == 16 && offsetof(intelxe_sensors_engine, total_ticks) == 24,
		"engine entry offsets");
	CHECK(sizeof(intelxe_sensors) == 136 + 32 * INTELXE_SENSORS_MAX_ENGINES, "sizeof %zu", sizeof(intelxe_sensors));
	CHECK(INTELXE_SENSORS_VERSION == 2, "version");
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, timestamp_ns) == 16, "timestamp_ns at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, timestamp_ns));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, act_mhz) == 24, "act_mhz at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, act_mhz));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, rpe_mhz) == 40, "rpe_mhz at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, rpe_mhz));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, pkg_temp_c) == 52, "pkg_temp_c at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, pkg_temp_c));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, energy_uj) == 64, "energy_uj at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, energy_uj));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, power_mw) == 80, "power_mw at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, power_mw));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, limit_mw) == 88, "limit_mw at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, limit_mw));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, limit_on) == 104, "limit_on at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, limit_on));
	CHECK(offsetof(intelxe_sensors, crit_milli) == 108, "crit_milli at %zu", offsetof(intelxe_sensors, crit_milli));
	CHECK(INTELXE_SENSORS_CARD == XE_ENERGY_CARD && INTELXE_SENSORS_PKG == XE_ENERGY_PKG &&
		INTELXE_SENSORS_CARD == XE_PL_CARD && INTELXE_SENSORS_PKG == XE_PL_PKG, "channel indices");

	// 2. registers: CAGF 126 = 2100 MHz, request 144 = 2400 MHz, RP0 171 = 2850 MHz, RPn 24 = 400 MHz, 47 C, 52 C (the
	// bits above the temperature field ignored)
	Legacy b580 = {};
	b580.wp1 = 0x0000007e;
	b580.req = 144u << 23 | 0x1234;
	b580.cap = 24u << 16 | 171u;
	b580.pkg = 0xab00 | 47;
	b580.vram = 0xcd00 | 52;
	XeSensorsSample x = sampleOf(b580);
	CHECK(x.s.version == INTELXE_SENSORS_VERSION && x.s.size == sizeof(intelxe_sensors) && x.s.timestamp_ns == 123,
		"header %u %u %llu", x.s.version, x.s.size, (unsigned long long)x.s.timestamp_ns);
	CHECK(x.s.state == INTELXE_SENSORS_OK && x.s.valid == (INTELXE_SENSORS_FREQ | INTELXE_SENSORS_TEMP), "valid 0x%x",
		x.s.valid);
	CHECK(x.s.act_mhz == 2100 && x.s.req_mhz == 2400 && x.s.rp0_mhz == 2850 && x.s.rpn_mhz == 400, "MHz %u %u %u %u",
		x.s.act_mhz, x.s.req_mhz, x.s.rp0_mhz, x.s.rpn_mhz);
	CHECK(x.s.pkg_temp_c == 47 && x.s.vram_temp_c == 52, "temperatures %d %d", x.s.pkg_temp_c, x.s.vram_temp_c);
	char t[1024];
	xeSensorsText(t, sizeof t, x);
	CHECK(!strcmp(t, "act 2100 MHz, req 2400 MHz, RP0 2850 MHz, RPn 400 MHz, package 47 C, VRAM 52 C\n"), "text %s", t);
	compareText(b580, "registers only");
	xeSensorsSetRange(x, 0, 0, 0);
	CHECK(!(x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_RANGE), "no range before SLPC");
	xeSensorsSetRange(x, 1800, 1200, 2850);
	CHECK((x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_RANGE) && x.s.rpe_mhz == 1800 && x.s.min_mhz == 1200 && x.s.max_mhz == 2850,
		"range %u %u %u", x.s.rpe_mhz, x.s.min_mhz, x.s.max_mhz);
	xeSensorsText(t, sizeof t, x);
	CHECK(!strcmp(t, "act 2100 MHz, req 2400 MHz, RP0 2850 MHz, RPn 400 MHz, package 47 C, VRAM 52 C\n"),
		"the range is not in the text: %s", t);

	Legacy gone = b580;
	gone.wp1 = gone.cap = 0xffffffffu;
	x = sampleOf(gone);
	CHECK(x.s.state == INTELXE_SENSORS_NO_ANSWER && x.s.valid == 0 && x.s.act_mhz == 0, "absent device: state %u valid 0x%x",
		x.s.state, x.s.valid);
	compareText(gone, "absent device");
	XeSensorsSample asleep;
	xeSensorsBegin(asleep, INTELXE_SENSORS_ASLEEP, 5);
	xeSensorsText(t, sizeof t, asleep);
	CHECK(!strcmp(t, "unavailable (asleep)\n") && asleep.s.valid == 0, "asleep: %s", t);
	xeSensorsBegin(asleep, INTELXE_SENSORS_NOT_MAPPED, 5);
	xeSensorsText(t, sizeof t, asleep);
	CHECK(!strcmp(t, "unavailable (not mapped)\n"), "not mapped: %s", t);

	// 3. energy: two telemetry words 1 s apart (card in 63:32, package in 31:0, units of 2^-14 J): card +36 J, package
	// +20 J
	Legacy e = b580;
	e.energyKnown = true;
	e.energy.update((uint64_t)1000000u << 32 | 500000u, 1000000000ull, 500000000ull);
	e.energy.update((uint64_t)(1000000u + 36u * 16384u) << 32 | (500000u + 20u * 16384u), 2000000000ull, 500000000ull);
	x = sampleOf(e);
	const uint64_t card = xeEnergyMicrojoules(1000000ull + 36ull * 16384, 14), pkg = xeEnergyMicrojoules(500000ull + 20ull * 16384, 14);
	CHECK(x.s.energy_uj[INTELXE_SENSORS_CARD] == card && x.s.energy_uj[INTELXE_SENSORS_PKG] == pkg, "energy %llu %llu",
		(unsigned long long)x.s.energy_uj[0], (unsigned long long)x.s.energy_uj[1]);
	CHECK((x.s.valid & (INTELXE_SENSORS_ENERGY | INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_CARD | INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_PKG)) ==
		(INTELXE_SENSORS_ENERGY | INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_CARD | INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_PKG), "valid 0x%x", x.s.valid);
	CHECK(x.s.power_mw[INTELXE_SENSORS_CARD] == 36000 && x.s.power_mw[INTELXE_SENSORS_PKG] == 20000, "power %u %u",
		x.s.power_mw[0], x.s.power_mw[1]);
	compareText(e, "energy and power");
	Legacy first = b580;   // one reading: energy, no power window yet
	first.energyKnown = true;
	first.energy.update((uint64_t)7u << 32 | 9u, 1, 500000000ull);
	x = sampleOf(first);
	CHECK((x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_ENERGY) && !(x.s.valid & (INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_CARD | INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_PKG)),
		"first reading valid 0x%x", x.s.valid);
	compareText(first, "energy, no window");
	Legacy refused = b580;   // package above the card: the package window is refused, the card's kept
	refused.energyKnown = true;
	refused.energy.update(0, 1000000000ull, 500000000ull);
	refused.energy.update((uint64_t)(37u * 16384u) << 32 | (152u * 16384u), 2000000000ull, 500000000ull);
	x = sampleOf(refused);
	CHECK((x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_CARD) && !(x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_POWER_PKG) &&
		x.s.power_mw[INTELXE_SENSORS_PKG] == 0 && x.rejected == 1, "refused window: valid 0x%x pkg %u rejected %u",
		x.s.valid, x.s.power_mw[1], x.rejected);
	compareText(refused, "refused package window");
	Legacy pmtErr = b580;
	pmtErr.energyKnown = true;
	pmtErr.err = 61;   // ENODATA
	pmtErr.guid = 0x1e2f8200;
	x = sampleOf(pmtErr);
	CHECK(!(x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_ENERGY) && x.s.energy_uj[0] == 0, "PMT error: valid 0x%x", x.s.valid);
	compareText(pmtErr, "PMT error");

	// power limits: card PL1 190 W on, PL2 250 W off, package PL1 120 W on, PL2 0; I1 = 300 W
	Legacy l = e;
	l.limitsKnown = true;
	l.pl.err = 0;
	l.pl.word[XE_PL_CARD][0] = PWR_LIM_EN | 190 * 8;
	l.pl.word[XE_PL_CARD][1] = 250 * 8;
	l.pl.word[XE_PL_PKG][0] = PWR_LIM_EN | 120 * 8 + 1;
	l.pl.word[XE_PL_PKG][1] = 0;
	l.pl.i1Err = 0;
	l.pl.i1 = POWER_SETUP_I1_WATTS | 300u << POWER_SETUP_I1_SHIFT;
	x = sampleOf(l);
	CHECK(x.s.limit_mw[0][0] == 190000 && x.s.limit_mw[0][1] == 250000 && x.s.limit_mw[1][0] == 120125 &&
		x.s.limit_mw[1][1] == 0, "limits %u %u %u %u", x.s.limit_mw[0][0], x.s.limit_mw[0][1], x.s.limit_mw[1][0],
		x.s.limit_mw[1][1]);
	CHECK(x.s.limit_on == (1u << 0 | 1u << 2), "limit_on 0x%x", x.s.limit_on);
	CHECK((x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_CRIT) && x.s.crit_milli == 300000 && x.s.crit_is_watts == 1, "crit %u %u",
		x.s.crit_milli, x.s.crit_is_watts);
	compareText(l, "limits");
	Legacy amps = l;
	amps.pl.i1 = 50u << POWER_SETUP_I1_SHIFT;
	x = sampleOf(amps);
	CHECK(x.s.crit_milli == 50000 && x.s.crit_is_watts == 0, "crit in amperes %u %u", x.s.crit_milli, x.s.crit_is_watts);
	compareText(amps, "crit in amperes");
	Legacy noI1 = l;
	noI1.pl.i1Err = 5;
	x = sampleOf(noI1);
	CHECK((x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_LIMITS) && !(x.s.valid & INTELXE_SENSORS_CRIT) && x.s.crit_milli == 0, "no I1 0x%x",
		x.s.valid);
	compareText(noI1, "no I1");
	Legacy plErr = l;
	plErr.pl.err = 61;
	x = sampleOf(plErr);
	CHECK(!(x.s.valid & (INTELXE_SENSORS_LIMITS | INTELXE_SENSORS_CRIT)) && x.s.limit_mw[0][0] == 0, "limits error 0x%x",
		x.s.valid);
	compareText(plErr, "limits error");

	// 4. pseudo-random samples (any register values, meters after random readings, both lock/platform choices)
	for (int i = 0; i < 300; i++) {
		Legacy r = {};
		r.wp1 = rnd();
		r.req = rnd();
		r.cap = (i % 37 == 0) ? 0xffffffffu : rnd();
		if (i % 37 == 0) r.wp1 = 0xffffffffu;
		r.pkg = rnd();
		r.vram = rnd();
		r.energyKnown = rnd() & 1;
		r.err = (rnd() % 4 == 0) ? (int)(rnd() % 100) : 0;
		r.guid = rnd();
		uint64_t ns = 0;
		for (uint32_t k = rnd() % 4; k; k--) {
			ns += 1 + rnd() % 2000000000u;
			r.energy.update((uint64_t)rnd() << 32 | rnd(), ns, 500000000ull);
		}
		r.limitsKnown = rnd() & 1;
		r.pl.err = (rnd() % 4 == 0) ? 61 : 0;
		for (uint32_t c = 0; c < XE_PL_CHANNELS; c++)
			for (uint32_t k = 0; k < 2; k++) r.pl.word[c][k] = rnd();
		r.pl.i1Err = (rnd() % 3 == 0) ? 5 : 0;
		r.pl.i1 = rnd();
		char what[32];
		snprintf(what, sizeof what, "random %d", i);
		compareText(r, what);
	}

	printf("%s: %d of %d checks failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails, checks);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}



================================================
FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/slpcboost_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// slpcboost_test: offline check of debug.intelxe.slpc_boost's lease (xe_slpcboost.h).
//   1. bounds: slpcParams' ceiling and floor, the request clamped to [RPn, min(RP0, slpc_max)]
//   2. a lease: granted, the effective minimum raised (never lowered below slpc_min), the GuC told once
//   3. renew: a write before the end moves the end and may change the floor (the latest write wins); expiry after 10 s
//      without a write, the administrator's floor owed to the GuC again
//   4. release: 0 ends it at once; 0 without a lease changes nothing
//   5. rate limit: 10 requests a second whoever makes them, the 11th refused and not counted, a new second takes writes;
//      a release always taken and never counted (also right after EBUSY); two users share the one lease
//   6. GT not ready (reset, sleep): a request refused, a release taken; the owed send retried, nothing owed while unknown
//   7. sleep: the lease ends, nothing is sent until slpcParams runs again
//   8. a lease clamped again when slpc_max is lowered during it
//   9. live range: slpc_min/max writes clamped to RPn..RP0 (0 the default, negative refused), MAX and MIN owed after a
//      write, the lease capped by the new ceiling at once, min above max sent as asked, sleep and the resume's floor
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o slpcboost_test slpcboost_test.cpp && ./slpcboost_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include "xe_slpcboost.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static constexpr uint64_t s = 1000000000ull, ms = 1000000ull;

// The kernel's glue (xe_core.cpp boostSync) as far as the GuC is concerned: send what is owed when ready.
static uint32_t sync(XeSlpcBoost &b, const XeSlpcBounds &bd, uint64_t now, bool ready) {
	const uint32_t m = xeBoostToSend(b, bd, now);
	if (m && ready) {
		b.sentMhz = m;
		b.sends++;
		return m;
	}
	return 0;
}

int main() {
	// the B580: RPn 400, RP0 2850; slpcParams' defaults
	const XeSlpcBounds def = {400, 2850, 1200, 0};

	// 1.
	CHECK(xeSlpcCeiling(def) == 2850, "ceiling RP0: %u", xeSlpcCeiling(def));
	CHECK(xeSlpcCeiling({400, 2850, 1200, 1800}) == 1800, "ceiling slpc_max");
	CHECK(xeSlpcCeiling({400, 2850, 1200, 5000}) == 2850 && xeSlpcCeiling({400, 2850, 1200, 100}) == 400, "ceiling clamped");
	CHECK(xeSlpcUserFloor(def) == 1200 && xeSlpcUserFloor({400, 2850, 0, 0}) == 1200, "floor default");
	CHECK(xeSlpcUserFloor({400, 2850, 100, 0}) == 400 && xeSlpcUserFloor({400, 2850, 9000, 0}) == 2850, "floor clamped");
	CHECK(xeBoostClamp(2400, def) == 2400, "in range");
	CHECK(xeBoostClamp(3000, def) == 2850, "above RP0: %u", xeBoostClamp(3000, def));
	CHECK(xeBoostClamp(3000, {400, 2850, 1200, 1800}) == 1800, "never above slpc_max");
	CHECK(xeBoostClamp(100, def) == 400, "below RPn");
	CHECK(xeBoostClamp(0xffffffffu, def) == 2850, "huge");

	// 2.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 100 * s;
		CHECK(xeBoostToSend(b, def, t) == 0, "nothing sent before SLPC ran (sentMhz unknown)");
		b.sentMhz = xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, def, t);   // slpcParams at bring-up
		CHECK(b.sentMhz == 1200, "bring-up floor %u", b.sentMhz);
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostGranted && b.grants == 1, "granted");
		CHECK(xeBoostFloor(b, def, t) == 2400 && xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, def, t) == 2400, "floor 2400");
		CHECK(xeBoostLeftMs(b, t) == 10000, "10 s left: %llu", (unsigned long long)xeBoostLeftMs(b, t));
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t, true) == 2400, "sent 2400");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t + ms, true) == 0, "sent once");
		CHECK(xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t) == t + kXeBoostLeaseNs, "timer at the end");
		// a lease below the administrator's floor does not lower it
		XeSlpcBoost l = {};
		l.sentMhz = 2000;
		const XeSlpcBounds high = {400, 2850, 2000, 0};
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(l, t, 800, high, true) == kXeBoostGranted && xeBoostEffectiveMin(l, high, t) == 2000 &&
			xeBoostToSend(l, high, t) == 0, "a lower lease changes nothing");
	}

	// 3.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 50 * s;
		b.sentMhz = 1200;
		xeBoostWrite(b, t, 2400, def, true);
		sync(b, def, t, true);
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + 5 * s, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostRenewed && b.renewals == 1, "renewed");
		CHECK(xeBoostLeftMs(b, t + 5 * s) == 10000 && sync(b, def, t + 5 * s, true) == 0, "renewal: new end, nothing sent");
		CHECK(!xeBoostExpire(b, t + 12 * s) && xeBoostActive(b, t + 12 * s), "still on at 12 s (renewed at 5 s)");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + 13 * s, 2000, def, true) == kXeBoostRenewed && sync(b, def, t + 13 * s, true) == 2000,
			"the latest write wins: 2000 sent");
		const uint64_t end = t + 23 * s;
		CHECK(xeBoostFloor(b, def, end - 1) == 2000 && xeBoostFloor(b, def, end) == 0, "ends 10 s after the last write");
		CHECK(xeBoostExpire(b, end) && b.expiries == 1 && b.askedMhz == 0, "expired");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, end, true) == 1200, "the administrator's floor back");
		CHECK(xeBoostNextNs(b, def, end) == 0 && !xeBoostExpire(b, end + s), "nothing more to do");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, end + s, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostGranted && b.grants == 2, "a new lease after the end");
		// the app's pattern: a write every 5 s keeps it; a client that stops leaves it for at most 10 s
		XeSlpcBoost a = {};
		a.sentMhz = 1200;
		uint64_t now = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++, now += 5 * s) {
			xeBoostExpire(a, now);
			xeBoostWrite(a, now, 2400, def, true);
			sync(a, def, now, true);
		}
		CHECK(a.grants == 1 && a.renewals == 19 && a.sends == 1 && a.sentMhz == 2400, "renewed every 5 s: one grant, one send");
		CHECK(xeBoostActive(a, now + 4 * s) && !xeBoostActive(a, now + 5 * s), "the client stopped: ends 10 s after its last write");
	}

	// 4.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 10 * s;
		b.sentMhz = 1200;
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t, 0, def, true) == kXeBoostNoLease && b.releases == 0 && sync(b, def, t, true) == 0,
			"release without a lease");
		xeBoostWrite(b, t, 2850, def, true);
		sync(b, def, t, true);
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + s, 0, def, true) == kXeBoostReleased && b.releases == 1 && !xeBoostActive(b, t + s), "released");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t + s, true) == 1200 && xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t + s) == 0, "floor back at once, no timer");
	}

	// 5.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 7 * s + 300 * ms;
		b.sentMhz = 1200;
		int ok = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) ok += xeBoostWrite(b, t + i * ms, 2400, def, true) != kXeBoostRateLimited;
		CHECK(ok == 10, "10 writes in a second: %d", ok);
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + 500 * ms, 2000, def, true) == kXeBoostRateLimited && b.rateLimited == 1 && b.askedMhz == 2400 &&
			xeBoostActive(b, t + 500 * ms), "the 11th request refused, the lease unchanged");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + 999 * ms, 2000, def, true) == kXeBoostRateLimited && b.rateLimited == 2 && b.askedMhz == 2400,
			"still refused in the same second");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + s, 2000, def, true) == kXeBoostRenewed && b.askedMhz == 2000, "a new second");
		// the night of 13 Nov: 11 writes in a second, then a release in the same second must end the lease at once
		XeSlpcBoost r = {};
		r.sentMhz = 1200;
		for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) xeBoostWrite(r, t + i * ms, 2400, def, true);
		sync(r, def, t, true);
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(r, t + 11 * ms, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostRateLimited, "the 11th request refused");
		const uint32_t limited = r.rateLimited, used = r.windowWrites;
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(r, t + 12 * ms, 0, def, true) == kXeBoostReleased && r.releases == 1 && !xeBoostActive(r, t + 12 * ms),
			"a release after EBUSY is taken");
		CHECK(r.rateLimited == limited && r.windowWrites == used, "the release not counted against the limit");
		CHECK(sync(r, def, t + 12 * ms, true) == 1200 && xeBoostNextNs(r, def, t + 12 * ms) == 0, "floor back at once, no timer");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(r, t + 13 * ms, 0, def, true) == kXeBoostNoLease && r.rateLimited == limited, "a second release: no lease");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(r, t + 14 * ms, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostRateLimited, "a request in that second still refused");
		// releases never use up the window: 10 releases, then 10 requests all taken
		XeSlpcBoost q = {};
		q.sentMhz = 1200;
		const uint64_t u = 60 * s;
		for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) CHECK(xeBoostWrite(q, u + i * ms, 0, def, true) == kXeBoostNoLease, "release %d", i);
		int taken = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) taken += xeBoostWrite(q, u + (100 + i) * ms, 2400, def, true) != kXeBoostRateLimited;
		CHECK(taken == 10 && q.rateLimited == 0, "50 releases then 10 requests in one second: %d taken", taken);
		// a release in a reset after the limit: taken too
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(q, u + 200 * ms, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostRateLimited &&
			xeBoostWrite(q, u + 201 * ms, 0, def, false) == kXeBoostReleased, "a release while limited and not ready");
		// two users share one lease: B's write replaces A's floor and end, B's release ends it for A too
		XeSlpcBoost two = {};
		two.sentMhz = 1200;
		const uint64_t v = 90 * s;
		xeBoostWrite(two, v, 2400, def, true);                                       // A
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(two, v + 3 * s, 1800, def, true) == kXeBoostRenewed &&   // B
			xeBoostFloor(two, def, v + 3 * s) == 1800 && xeBoostLeftMs(two, v + 3 * s) == 10000, "the latest write wins");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(two, v + 4 * s, 0, def, true) == kXeBoostReleased && !xeBoostActive(two, v + 4 * s),
			"a release by B ends the lease A asked for");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(two, v + 5 * s, 2400, def, true) == kXeBoostGranted, "A's next renewal takes a new lease");
		// a flood: at most 10 a second get through
		XeSlpcBoost f = {};
		f.sentMhz = 1200;
		int through = 0;
		for (uint64_t now = 0; now < 3 * s; now += ms) through += xeBoostWrite(f, now + s, 2400, def, true) != kXeBoostRateLimited;
		CHECK(through <= 31 && through >= 30, "a 1 kHz flood for 3 s: %d through", through);
	}

	// 6.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 20 * s;
		b.sentMhz = 1200;
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t, 2400, def, false) == kXeBoostNotReady && b.notReady == 1 && !xeBoostActive(b, t),
			"refused in a reset");
		xeBoostWrite(b, t + s, 2400, def, true);
		sync(b, def, t + s, true);
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t + 2 * s, 0, def, false) == kXeBoostReleased, "a release is taken during a reset");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t + 2 * s, false) == 0 && xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t + 2 * s) == t + 2 * s + kXeBoostRetryNs,
			"not sent during the reset: retried in 100 ms");
		CHECK(sync(b, def, t + 2 * s + kXeBoostRetryNs, true) == 1200 && xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t + 3 * s) == 0,
			"sent once the GT is back");
	}

	// 7.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 30 * s;
		b.sentMhz = 1200;
		xeBoostWrite(b, t, 2400, def, true);
		sync(b, def, t, true);
		xeBoostSleep(b);
		CHECK(b.sleepEnds == 1 && !xeBoostActive(b, t + s) && b.sentMhz == 0, "sleep ends the lease");
		CHECK(xeBoostToSend(b, def, t + s) == 0 && xeBoostNextNs(b, def, t + s) == 0, "nothing sent while asleep, no timer");
		b.sentMhz = xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, def, t + 60 * s);   // the resume's slpcParams
		CHECK(b.sentMhz == 1200, "the resume sends the administrator's floor");
		xeBoostSleep(b);
		CHECK(b.sleepEnds == 1, "a sleep without a lease is not counted");
	}

	// 8.
	{
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		const uint64_t t = 40 * s;
		b.sentMhz = 1200;
		xeBoostWrite(b, t, 3000, def, true);
		CHECK(b.clamped == 1 && sync(b, def, t, true) == 2850, "3000 clamped to RP0");
		const XeSlpcBounds quiet = {400, 2850, 1200, 1800};   // the administrator lowers slpc_max during the lease
		CHECK(xeBoostFloor(b, quiet, t + s) == 1800 && sync(b, quiet, t + s, true) == 1800, "clamped again to the new ceiling");
	}

	// 9. live range (slpc_min / slpc_max writes, xeSlpcKnobWrite's pure part)
	{
		int v = -1;
		CHECK(!xeSlpcKnobValue(-1, 400, 2850, &v) && v == -1, "negative: EINVAL, nothing stored");
		CHECK(xeSlpcKnobValue(0, 400, 2850, &v) && v == 0, "0 = the default, kept as 0");
		CHECK(xeSlpcKnobValue(1500, 400, 2850, &v) && v == 1500, "in range");
		CHECK(xeSlpcKnobValue(9999, 400, 2850, &v) && v == 2850, "above RP0: clamped %d", v);
		CHECK(xeSlpcKnobValue(100, 400, 2850, &v) && v == 400, "below RPn: clamped %d", v);
		CHECK(xeSlpcKnobValue(9999, 0, 0, &v) && v == 9999, "limits not known yet: kept (slpcParams clamps at the start)");
		XeSlpcBoost b = {};
		XeSlpcBounds bd = def;
		const uint64_t t = 50 * s;
		CHECK(xeSlpcMaxToSend(b, bd) == 0, "nothing before SLPC ran (sentMaxMhz unknown)");
		b.sentMhz = xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, bd, t);   // slpcParams
		b.sentMaxMhz = xeSlpcCeiling(bd);
		CHECK(xeSlpcMaxToSend(b, bd) == 0 && xeBoostToSend(b, bd, t) == 0, "nothing owed after slpcParams");
		bd.userMax = 2000;   // zesFrequencySetRange(1500, 2000): max first is not needed (1500 < current max)
		bd.userMin = 1500;
		CHECK(xeSlpcMaxToSend(b, bd) == 2000, "max 2000 owed");
		b.sentMaxMhz = 2000;
		CHECK(sync(b, bd, t, true) == 1500, "min 1500 owed");
		CHECK(xeBoostWrite(b, t, 2400, bd, true) == kXeBoostGranted, "a lease under the new range");
		CHECK(sync(b, bd, t, true) == 2000, "the lease's floor capped by slpc_max 2000");
		bd.userMax = 1800;   // root lowers the ceiling during the lease: the GuC's min follows at once
		CHECK(xeSlpcMaxToSend(b, bd) == 1800, "max 1800 owed");
		b.sentMaxMhz = 1800;
		CHECK(sync(b, bd, t + s, true) == 1800, "min lowered with the ceiling");
		bd.userMin = 2500;   // a floor above the ceiling is sent as asked (Linux: min becomes a fixed request)
		xeBoostWrite(b, t + s, 0, bd, true);
		CHECK(sync(b, bd, t + s, true) == 2500, "min above max: %u", b.sentMhz);
		bd.userMin = 0;   // back to the defaults
		bd.userMax = 0;
		CHECK(xeSlpcMaxToSend(b, bd) == 2850 && (b.sentMaxMhz = 2850) && sync(b, bd, t + s, true) == 1200, "defaults");
		xeBoostSleep(b);
		CHECK(b.sentMaxMhz == 0 && xeSlpcMaxToSend(b, bd) == 0, "sleep: the GuC's max unknown until slpcParams");
		bd.userMin = 1600;   // written while asleep: kept, sent by the resume's slpcParams
		CHECK(xeBoostToSend(b, bd, t + 2 * s) == 0, "nothing sent while asleep");
		CHECK(xeBoostEffectiveMin(b, bd, t + 3 * s) == 1600, "the resume's floor is the new slpc_min");
	}

	printf("slpcboost_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

FILE: kernel/IntelXe/tests/tlbinring_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// tlbinring_test: offline check of the in-ring TLB wait's pure parts (xe_tlbinring.h), no GPU needed.
//   1. xeTlbInringPlan: which pending in-fences an EXEC may wait for in the ring (TLB invalidations only), the target
//      (the newest, across the seqno wrap), and the targets an unsigned compare cannot take (0, the guard below the wrap,
//      a word on the other side of the wrap)
//   2. xeTlbInringPath: when the job goes to the armed slot (the queue stays in direct submission), to the normal ring
//      (knob 2) or the old way (FIFO, leaving direct submission), against a brute-force statement of the rules
//   3. a model of the GPU's MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT (unsigned word >= target) and the TLB word (xeTlbWordAdvances from racing,
//      stale publishers), around the 2^32 wrap: for every accepted job and every word value the GPU can read while
//      the job is pending, the semaphore passes exactly when its invalidations are done in seqno order (never early,
//      never stranded); the word never moves back and is never ahead of the done seqno; with a jump past the documented
//      bound (2^20 unanswered invalidations) the wait can strand a job but still never releases it early
//   4. xeTlbDoneBoth (the word's value) is done for seqno s exactly when tlbSeqDone is (primary and, while it is up,
//      the media GuC)
//   5. what the free/reuse paths still wait for: an unbind's deferred free (xeDeferReady) stays held until the CPU-side
//      done seqno passes its invalidation and the VM's jobs of that moment complete, whatever the EXECs that wait for
//      that invalidation in the ring do; and those EXECs' batches never start before the same invalidation is done
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o tlbinring_test tlbinring_test.cpp && ./tlbinring_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <vector>
#include "xe_tlbinring.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static XeFence tlb(uint32_t s) { return xeTlbFence(s); }
static XeFence job(uint32_t slot, uint32_t s) { return XeFence{0, slot, 1, s}; }
static bool semPass(uint32_t word, uint32_t target) { return word >= target; }   // COMPARE_OP_SAD_GTE_SDD, unsigned
static int gAccepted, gRefused;

int main() {
	srandom(12);
	// 1. the plan
	{
		uint32_t t = 7;
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(nullptr, 0, 0, &t) == kXeTlbInringNone, "no in-fences");
		XeFence j1[] = {job(3, 10), XeFence{0, kXeBindSlot, 2, 4}};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(j1, 2, 0, &t) == kXeTlbInringNone, "jobs and a queued bind only: nothing for this path");
		XeFence m[] = {tlb(100), job(3, 10)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(m, 2, 90, &t) == kXeTlbInringOther && t == 100, "a TLB fence and a job: the FIFO");
		XeFence m2[] = {job(3, 10), tlb(100)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(m2, 2, 90, &t) == kXeTlbInringOther, "order does not matter");
		XeFence a[] = {tlb(100), tlb(105), tlb(103)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(a, 3, 99, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait && t == 105, "newest of several: %u", t);
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(a, 3, 105, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait, "word at the target: passes at once");
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(a, 3, 200, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait, "word past the target, no wrap between");
		XeFence g[] = {tlb(kXeTlbWordGuard - 1)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(g, 1, kXeTlbWordGuard - 10, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait, "just below the guard");
		XeFence g2[] = {tlb(kXeTlbWordGuard)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(g2, 1, kXeTlbWordGuard - 10, &t) == kXeTlbInringWrap, "at the guard");
		XeFence g3[] = {tlb(0xfffffffeu)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(g3, 1, 0xfffffff0u, &t) == kXeTlbInringWrap, "just before the wrap");
		XeFence z[] = {tlb(0)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(z, 1, 0xfffffff0u, &t) == kXeTlbInringWrap, "target 0 (no wait encoded as 0)");
		XeFence w[] = {tlb(5)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(w, 1, 0xfffffff0u, &t) == kXeTlbInringWrap, "word before the wrap, target after it");
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(w, 1, 2, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait && t == 5, "both after the wrap");
		XeFence wr[] = {tlb(0xfffffff8u), tlb(3)};   // 3 is newer (wrap-aware)
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(wr, 2, 1, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait && t == 3, "newest across the wrap: %u", t);
		XeFence far[] = {tlb(0x10)};   // word 0x80000020: seqno order says the word is behind, unsigned says ahead
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(far, 1, 0x80000020u, &t) == kXeTlbInringWrap, "orders disagree");
	}
	// 2. the path, against the rules written out
	for (int knob = -1; knob <= 3; knob++)
		for (uint32_t plan = 0; plan < 4; plan++)
			for (int bits = 0; bits < 8; bits++) {
				const bool word = bits & 1, armed = bits & 2, free = bits & 4;
				const XeTlbPath p = xeTlbInringPath(knob, (XeTlbInring)plan, word, armed, free);
				XeTlbPath want = kXeTlbPathOld;
				if (knob >= 1 && plan == kXeTlbInringWait && word && free) {
					if (armed) want = kXeTlbPathDirect;            // knob 1 and 2: the armed queue stays armed
					else if (knob >= 2) want = kXeTlbPathRing;     // knob 2: the normal ring path too
				}
				CHECK(p == want, "knob %d plan %u word %d armed %d free %d: %u, want %u", knob, plan, word, armed, free, p, want);
			}
	// 3. the GPU model around the wrap
	auto model = [](uint32_t base, uint32_t maxJump, int steps, bool expectExact) {
		uint32_t issued = base, done = base, word = base;   // seqnos: issued, CPU-side done, the TLB word
		struct Job { uint32_t target; bool passed; };
		std::vector<Job> jobs;
		std::vector<uint32_t> stale;   // values publishers computed earlier and may still store (racing)
		int strandedSeen = 0, early = 0, accepted = 0, refused = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < steps; i++) {
			const int op = (int)(random() % 4);
			if (op == 0) {   // VM_BINDs issue invalidations
				issued += 1 + (uint32_t)(random() % 8);
			} else if (op == 1 && done != issued) {   // TLB_INVALIDATION_DONE (in order, may cover several)
				uint32_t step = 1 + (uint32_t)(random() % maxJump);
				if (step > issued - done) step = issued - done;
				done += step;
				stale.push_back(done);
			} else if (op == 2) {   // a publisher stores what it computed (maybe long ago): only forward
				if (!stale.empty()) {
					const size_t k = (size_t)random() % stale.size();
					const uint32_t v = stale[k];
					if (xeTlbWordAdvances(word, v)) word = v;
					stale.erase(stale.begin() + (long)k);
				}
			} else if (done != issued) {   // an EXEC on the newest pending invalidation (or an older one)
				const uint32_t s = issued - (uint32_t)(random() % (issued - done));
				XeFence f[] = {tlb(s)};
				uint32_t t;
				if (xeTlbInringPlan(f, 1, word, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait) {
					jobs.push_back({t, false});
					accepted++;
				} else {
					refused++;
				}
			}
			CHECK(xeSeqDone(done, word), "the word %u is ahead of done %u", word, done);
			for (Job &j : jobs) {   // the GPU polls: every value the word takes is read
				const bool pass = semPass(word, j.target), isDone = xeSeqDone(word, j.target);
				if (pass && !xeSeqDone(done, j.target)) early++;
				if (isDone && !pass) strandedSeen++;
				if (pass) j.passed = true;
			}
			std::vector<Job> keep;
			for (const Job &j : jobs) if (!j.passed) keep.push_back(j);
			jobs.swap(keep);
		}
		// drain: everything answered and published
		done = issued;
		if (xeTlbWordAdvances(word, done)) word = done;
		for (const Job &j : jobs) if (!semPass(word, j.target)) strandedSeen++;
		CHECK(early == 0, "base 0x%x: %d waits passed before their invalidation was done", base, early);
		if (expectExact) CHECK(strandedSeen == 0, "base 0x%x: %d waits stranded", base, strandedSeen);
		gAccepted += accepted;
		gRefused += refused;
		return strandedSeen;
	};
	int stranded = 0;
	for (int r = 0; r < 60; r++) {   // across the wrap, across the guard, anywhere
		const uint32_t base = r < 20 ? 0xffffffffu - (uint32_t)(random() % 200000) :
			r < 40 ? kXeTlbWordGuard - (uint32_t)(random() % 30000) : (uint32_t)random();
		model(base, 1000, 60000, true);   // completions of up to 1000 at once: far below the bound
	}
	printf("model: %d EXECs waited in the ring, %d refused (wrap guard)\n", gAccepted, gRefused);
	CHECK(gAccepted > 100000 && gRefused > 0, "the model exercised both");
	// past the bound: one completion of more than 2^20 can strand a waiter whose target was just below the guard;
	// never an early release
	{
		uint32_t word = kXeTlbWordGuard - 0x100, t;
		XeFence f[] = {tlb(kXeTlbWordGuard - 1)};
		CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(f, 1, word, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait, "accepted below the guard");
		const uint32_t v = t + (1u << 20) + 5;   // wraps past 0 in one step
		CHECK(xeTlbWordAdvances(word, v), "forward in seqno order");
		word = v;
		stranded = !semPass(word, t);
		CHECK(stranded, "documented limit: a jump of 2^20 strands it (the watchdog's GT reset, never an early start)");
		CHECK(!semPass(kXeTlbWordGuard - 2, t), "never early");
	}
	// 4. xeTlbDoneBoth against tlbSeqDone's rule
	for (int i = 0; i < 200000; i++) {
		const uint32_t p = (uint32_t)random() ^ (uint32_t)random() << 16, m = p + (uint32_t)(random() % 2001) - 1000;
		const uint32_t s = p + (uint32_t)(random() % 4001) - 2000;
		const bool media = random() & 1;
		const bool want = xeSeqDone(p, s) && (!media || xeSeqDone(m, s));
		CHECK(xeSeqDone(xeTlbDoneBoth(p, m, media), s) == want, "p %u m %u media %d s %u", p, m, media, s);
	}
	// 5. the free/reuse paths: an unbind seals its free with invalidation S and the VM's jobs of that moment (q0 up to
	// seqno 50); two EXECs after it wait for S in the ring; nothing of what the EXECs do changes when the free may go
	{
		const uint32_t S = 1000;
		uint32_t tlbDone = 998, q0Done = 40, word = 998;
		const uint32_t snapQ0 = 50;
		std::vector<uint32_t> execTargets;
		for (int e = 0; e < 2; e++) {
			XeFence f[] = {tlb(S)};
			uint32_t t;
			CHECK(xeTlbInringPlan(f, 1, word, &t) == kXeTlbInringWait && t == S, "exec %d waits in the ring", e);
			execTargets.push_back(t);
		}
		auto ready = [&] { return xeDeferReady(true, xeSeqDone(tlbDone, S), xeSeqDone(q0Done, snapQ0)); };
		auto batchMayRun = [&](uint32_t t) { return semPass(word, t); };
		CHECK(!ready(), "free held: invalidation and jobs pending");
		for (uint32_t t : execTargets) CHECK(!batchMayRun(t), "EXEC batch held by the semaphore");
		q0Done = 50;   // the VM's jobs of the unbind's moment complete
		CHECK(!ready(), "free still held: the invalidation is pending (the EXECs being in the ring changes nothing)");
		tlbDone = 1000;   // TLB_INVALIDATION_DONE; the publish has not happened yet
		CHECK(ready(), "free goes once the CPU-side done passes S and the snapshot's jobs are done");
		for (uint32_t t : execTargets) CHECK(!batchMayRun(t), "the word lags: the batch still waits (late, never early)");
		word = tlbDone;   // xeTlbWordPublish
		for (uint32_t t : execTargets) CHECK(batchMayRun(t), "after the publish the batches run");
		q0Done = 40;
		CHECK(!ready(), "and the other way round: invalidation done, jobs pending: held");
	}
	printf("tlbinring_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}
