FILE: kernel/IntelXeFB/tests/plan_test.cpp
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// plan_test: offline check of IntelXeDisplayPlan.h (the second display pipe's arithmetic), no GPU needed. The expected
// values are worked out by hand from the Linux v6.18 functions each helper names (skl_watermark.c, intel_display.c,
// intel_dp.c, intel_pmdemand.c, intel_bw.c); the comments show the working.
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -I.. -o plan_test plan_test.cpp ../IntelXeEdid.cpp && ./plan_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "IntelXeDisplayPlan.h"
#include "IntelXeEdid.h"

using namespace intelxeplan;

static int fails, checks;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); \
	printf("\n"); } } while (0)
#define EQ(a, b) CHECK((uint64_t)(a) == (uint64_t)(b), "%s = %llu (0x%llx), want %llu (0x%llx)", #a, \
	(unsigned long long)(a), (unsigned long long)(a), (unsigned long long)(b), (unsigned long long)(b))

// CEA 1920x1080@60 (VIC 16): 148.5 MHz, 2200 x 1125
static const Timing k1080 = { 148500, 1920, 2008, 2052, 2200, 1080, 1084, 1089, 1125, true, true };
// 2560x1440 at about 180 Hz with reduced blanking (the panel's kind of mode): 706250 kHz, 2720 x 1443 (made up but sane)
static const Timing k1440 = { 706250, 2560, 2608, 2640, 2720, 1440, 1443, 1448, 1443 + 0, false, true };

static void testPorts()
{
	Port p = {};
	CHECK(portInfo(4, &p), "TC2");
	EQ(p.phy, 6); EQ(p.aux, 0x16F410); EQ(p.hpd, 1u << 25); EQ(p.ddiSel, 5); EQ(p.clkSel, 0x70000000u);   // display-plan.md facts
	CHECK(!strcmp(p.name, "TC2"), "name %s", p.name);
	CHECK(portInfo(0, &p), "A");
	EQ(p.phy, 0); EQ(p.aux, 0x64010); EQ(p.hpd, 1u << 16); EQ(p.ddiSel, 1); EQ(p.clkSel, 1u << 28);
	CHECK(portInfo(6, &p), "TC4");
	EQ(p.phy, 8); EQ(p.aux, 0x16F810); EQ(p.hpd, 1u << 27); EQ(p.clkSel, 9u << 28);
	CHECK(!portInfo(1, &p) && !portInfo(2, &p) && !portInfo(7, &p) && !portInfo(-1, &p), "B, C, 7, -1 are not BMG ports");
	EQ(portFromName("tc1"), 3); EQ(portFromName("TC4"), 6); EQ(portFromName("a"), 0);
	EQ(portFromName("tc5"), -1); EQ(portFromName("b"), -1); EQ(portFromName(""), -1);
	EQ(pipePowerWell(1), 6); EQ(pwReq(6), 1u << 13); EQ(pwState(6), 1u << 12); EQ(pwFuse(6), 1u << 20);
}

static void testDbuf()
{
	EQ(mbusJoined(1), 1); EQ(mbusJoined(2), 1); EQ(mbusJoined(3), 0); EQ(mbusJoined(5), 0);
	EQ(dbufSlices(0, 1, true), 0xF); EQ(dbufSlices(0, 1, false), 0x3);
	EQ(dbufSlices(0, 3, false), 0x3); EQ(dbufSlices(1, 3, false), 0xC); EQ(dbufSlices(1, 3, true), 0);   // no joined A+B entry
	EQ(enabledSlices(1, true), 0xF); EQ(enabledSlices(3, false), 0xF); EQ(enabledSlices(1, false), 0x3);
	EQ(mbusDdbOffset(0x3), 0); EQ(mbusDdbOffset(0xC), 2048); EQ(mbusDdbOffset(0xF), 0);
	uint32_t w[4] = { 2560, 1920, 0, 0 }, off = 99;
	Ddb d = pipeDdb(0, 1, true, w, &off);
	EQ(d.start, 0); EQ(d.end, 4096); EQ(off, 0);
	d = pipeDdb(0, 3, false, w, &off);
	EQ(d.start, 0); EQ(d.end, 2048); EQ(off, 0);
	d = pipeDdb(1, 3, false, w, &off);
	EQ(d.start, 0); EQ(d.end, 2048); EQ(off, 2048);   // relative to the S3/S4 bank
	// B + C share S3/S4: weights 1920 / 3840 -> B 0..682, C 682..2048 (2048 x 1920 / 5760 = 682.67)
	uint32_t w2[4] = { 0, 1920, 3840, 0 };
	d = pipeDdb(1, 6, false, w2, &off); EQ(d.start, 0); EQ(d.end, 682); EQ(off, 2048);
	d = pipeDdb(2, 6, false, w2, &off); EQ(d.start, 682); EQ(d.end, 2048);
	d = pipeDdb(3, 3, false, w, &off); EQ(d.size(), 0);   // not active
	// pipe_mbus_dbox_ctl, display 14.01: I 2 << 5, B2B max 16 << 20, delay 1 << 17, regulate 1 << 16, B 0xA << 8, A 12 / 8
	EQ(mbusDboxCtl(true), 0x01030A4Cu); EQ(mbusDboxCtl(false), 0x01030A48u);
	EQ(mbusCtlBits(true, 0), 0xC0000000u); EQ(mbusCtlBits(false, 0), 0u); EQ(mbusCtlBits(false, -1), 7u << 26);
	EQ(dbufMinTracker(true), 3); EQ(dbufMinTracker(false), 1);
	EQ(DBUF_CTL_S(0), 0x45008); EQ(DBUF_CTL_S(1), 0x44FE8); EQ(DBUF_CTL_S(2), 0x44300); EQ(DBUF_CTL_S(3), 0x44304);
	EQ(ddbReg(Ddb{ 0, 2048 }), 0x07FF0000u); EQ(ddbReg(Ddb{ 2040, 2048 }), 0x07FF07F8u); EQ(ddbReg(Ddb{ 0, 0 }), 0);
	d = ddbFromReg(0x03E70000u); EQ(d.start, 0); EQ(d.end, 0x3E8);
}

static void testLink()
{
	Link l = {};
	// 1080p60: 148500 x 24 / 8 = 445500 kB/s; RBR x1 162000, x2 324000, x4 648000 -> RBR x4
	CHECK(linkConfig(148500, 24, 810000, 4, &l), "1080p60");
	EQ(l.rate, 162000); EQ(l.lanes, 4);
	// 3840x2160@60 CVT-RB (533250 kHz): 1599750 kB/s -> HBR2 x4 (HBR x4 = 1080000, HBR2 x2 = 1080000 too small)
	CHECK(linkConfig(533250, 24, 810000, 4, &l), "4k60");
	EQ(l.rate, 540000); EQ(l.lanes, 4);
	CHECK(!linkConfig(533250, 24, 270000, 4, &l), "4k60 on an HBR sink");
	CHECK(linkConfig(533250, 24, 810000, 2, &l), "4k60 on 2 lanes"); EQ(l.rate, 810000); EQ(l.lanes, 2);
	EQ(maxDataRate(810000, 4), 3240000); EQ(rateFromBwCode(0x1E), 810000);
	// intel_link_compute_m_n: data 445500 / 648000 = 0.6875 -> M 0x580000 / N 0x800000 after four halvings of
	// 0x8000000; link 148500 x 0x80000 / 162000 = 480597.33 -> 480597 / 0x80000
	const MN m = linkMN(24, 4, 148500, 162000);
	EQ(m.tu, 64); EQ(m.dataM, 0x580000); EQ(m.dataN, 0x800000); EQ(m.linkM, 480597); EQ(m.linkN, 0x80000);
	EQ(dataMReg(m), 0x7E580000u);
	// 706250 kHz on HBR2 x4: data 2118750 / 2160000 x 2^23 = 8228352 (0x7D8E00 after 4 halvings: 0x8000000 -> 0x800000)
	const MN m2 = linkMN(24, 4, 706250, 540000);
	EQ(m2.dataN, 0x800000); EQ(m2.dataM, (uint32_t)((uint64_t)2118750 * 0x8000000 / 2160000 >> 4));
	EQ(m2.linkM, (uint32_t)((uint64_t)706250 * 0x80000 / 540000)); EQ(m2.linkN, 0x80000);
	// hsw_linetime_wm: 2200 x 8000 / 148500 = 118.52 -> 119
	EQ(linetimeWm(2200, 148500), 119); EQ(linetimeWm(65535, 20000), 0x1FF);
	EQ(minCdclk(1305600), 652800); EQ(minCdclk(1305601), 652801);
	const TimingRegs r = timingRegs(k1080);
	EQ(r.htotal, (2200u - 1) << 16 | (1920 - 1)); EQ(r.hblank, (2200u - 1) << 16 | (1920 - 1));
	EQ(r.hsync, (2052u - 1) << 16 | (2008 - 1)); EQ(r.vtotal, (1125u - 1) << 16 | (1080 - 1));
	EQ(r.vblank, (1125u - 1) << 16); EQ(r.vsync, (1089u - 1) << 16 | (1084 - 1)); EQ(r.scl, 0);
	EQ(r.pipesrc, (1920u - 1) << 16 | (1080 - 1)); EQ(r.funcSync, 3u << 16);
	const Timing back = timingFromRegs(r.htotal, r.hsync, r.vtotal, r.vsync, r.funcSync, 148500);
	CHECK(!memcmp(&back, &k1080, sizeof back), "timing round trip");
	EQ(refreshMilliHz(k1080), 60000);
}

static void testWm()
{
	// latencies: LP0 0 (-> + 6 read latency on the valid levels), LP1 4, LP2 8, LP3 10, LP4 0 (levels 4-7 off)
	const Latency lat = latencyFromRegs(0x00040000, 0x000A0008, 0, 20);
	const uint16_t want[8] = { 6, 10, 14, 16, 0, 0, 0, 0 };
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) EQ(lat.us[i], want[i]);
	EQ(lat.sagvUs, 20);
	const Latency lat2 = latencyFromRegs(0x00050002, 0x00000007, 0x00090008, 0);   // LP3 0: levels 4-5 zeroed, no + 6
	const uint16_t want2[8] = { 2, 5, 7, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 };
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) EQ(lat2.us[i], want2[i]);
	// 1920 wide, 148.5 MHz, htotal 2200: 7680 bytes/line -> 15 blocks + 1 = 16; line time 14.81 -> 15 us
	const WmParams p = wmParams(1920, 4, 148500, 2200);
	EQ(p.blocksPerLine.val, 16u << 16); EQ(p.linetimeUs, 15);
	// 6 us: method1 = 6 x 148500 x 4 / 512000 + 1 = 7.96 (6 < 15 us line time: method1); blocks 8 + 1 = 9 -> at least
	// one line (16); lines ceil(7.96 / 16) = 1; min_ddb = 16 + 2 = 18, + 1 = 19
	WmLevel w = planeWm(p, 6);
	EQ(w.enable, 1); EQ(w.blocks, 16); EQ(w.lines, 1); EQ(w.minDdb, 19);
	// 50 us: method2 = ceil(50 x 148500 / 2200000) = 4 lines x 16 = 64 (50 >= 15 us); blocks 65, lines 4, min 65 + 7 + 1
	w = planeWm(p, 50);
	EQ(w.blocks, 65); EQ(w.lines, 4); EQ(w.minDdb, 73);
	w = planeWm(p, 0);
	EQ(w.enable, 0); EQ(w.minDdb, kRejected);
	// transition: (16 - 1) + 4 + 10 + 1 = 30 blocks, min max(19, 31)
	const WmLevel t = transWm(planeWm(p, 6));
	EQ(t.blocks, 30); EQ(t.minDdb, 31); EQ(t.enable, 1);
	// a rejected SAGV WM0 makes a transition WM that never fits (u16 arithmetic as Linux)
	const WmLevel tr = transWm(planeWm(p, 0));
	EQ(tr.minDdb, kRejected);
	EQ(wmReg(WmLevel{ true, 16, 1, 19 }), 0x80004010u);
	// cursor: 256 x 4 = 1024 bytes -> 2 + 1 = 3 blocks/line; its last usable level (3, 16 us >= 15 us: method2 =
	// ceil(16 x 148500 / 2200000) = 2 lines x 3 = 6) needs 6 + 1 = 7 blocks, min 7 + 1 + 1 = 9; with one pipe at least 32
	EQ(cursorAlloc(148500, 2200, lat, 2), 9); EQ(cursorAlloc(148500, 2200, lat, 1), 32);
	PipeWm pw = {};
	CHECK(pipeWm(k1080, 1920, lat, Ddb{ 0, 2048 }, 2, &pw), "1080p pipe in 2048 blocks");
	EQ(pw.vblankMaxLevel, 3); EQ(pw.ddbLevel, 3);
	EQ(pw.cursor.start, 2039); EQ(pw.cursor.end, 2048); EQ(pw.plane.start, 0); EQ(pw.plane.end, 2039);
	EQ(pw.regBufCfg, 0x07F60000u); EQ(pw.regCurBufCfg, 0x07FF07F7u);
	EQ(pw.useSagv, 1);   // SAGV WM0 (latency 26) fits
	EQ(pw.regWm[0], wmReg(pw.sagv0)); EQ(pw.regTrans, wmReg(pw.sagvTrans));
	CHECK(pw.wm[1].enable && pw.wm[3].enable && !pw.wm[4].enable, "levels 1-3 on, 4 off");
	EQ(pw.regWm[4], wmReg(WmLevel{ false, pw.wm[3].blocks, pw.wm[3].lines, 0 }));   // the copy WA keeps 3's values, disabled
	// a 20-block DDB: 9 for the cursor, 11 left; level 0 needs 19 -> refused
	CHECK(!pipeWm(k1080, 1920, lat, Ddb{ 0, 20 }, 2, &pw) && pw.ddbLevel < 0, "20 blocks: no level fits");
	// a vblank of 2 lines: level 0 with latency 0 needs 1 + 0 + 1 line <= 2; level 1 (10 us: 1 line) does not fit
	Timing tight = k1080; tight.vtotal = 1082;
	CHECK(pipeWm(tight, 1920, lat, Ddb{ 0, 2048 }, 2, &pw), "tight vblank");
	EQ(pw.vblankMaxLevel, 0); CHECK(!pw.wm[1].enable, "level 1 off by the vblank");
	EQ(pw.useSagv, 0);   // SAGV latency 26 us does not fit the vblank either
	Timing none = k1080; none.vtotal = 1081;   // 1 line of vblank: nothing fits
	CHECK(!pipeWm(none, 1920, lat, Ddb{ 0, 2048 }, 2, &pw) && pw.vblankMaxLevel < 0, "1-line vblank refused");
}

static void testPmdemand()
{
	const uint32_t r0 = 0xFFFF0000u | 2u << 12 | 0u << 8 | 1u << 6 | 3u << 4 | 1u, r1 = 653u << 20 | 810u << 8 | 7u << 4 | 2u;
	const PmDemand p = pmdemandFromRegs(r0, r1);
	EQ(p.qclkBw, 0xFFFF); EQ(p.voltage, 2); EQ(p.pipes, 1); EQ(p.dbufs, 3); EQ(p.phys, 1);
	EQ(p.cdclkMhz, 653); EQ(p.ddiclkMhz, 810); EQ(p.scalers, 7); EQ(p.plls, 2);
	uint32_t a = r0 | 1u << 3, b = r1 | PMDEMAND_REQ;   // bits outside the fields stay, REQ is cleared
	pmdemandToRegs(p, &a, &b);
	EQ(a, r0 | 1u << 3); EQ(b, r1);
	const PmDemand n = pmdemandFor(p, 2, 0xF, 2, 540000);
	EQ(n.pipes, 2); EQ(n.dbufs, 3); EQ(n.phys, 2); EQ(n.plls, 3); EQ(n.ddiclkMhz, 540); EQ(n.scalers, 7);
	EQ(n.cdclkMhz, 653); EQ(n.voltage, 2); EQ(n.qclkBw, 0xFFFF);
	const PmDemand m = pmdemandMax(p, n);
	EQ(m.ddiclkMhz, 810); EQ(m.pipes, 2); EQ(m.phys, 2); EQ(m.plls, 3);
	// bandwidth: 6 channels, 2 QGV points, GDDR (type 8); dclk field 900 -> 15000 MHz -> 360000 MB/s, capped at 53000
	const uint32_t qgv[8] = { 900, 450 };
	EQ(deratedBwMBps(2u << 8 | 6u << 4 | 8u, qgv, 8), 53000);
	const uint32_t slow[8] = { 30, 15 };   // 500 MHz: 12000 MB/s x 70 % = 8400
	EQ(deratedBwMBps(2u << 8 | 6u << 4 | 8u, slow, 8), 8400);
	EQ(deratedBwMBps(2u << 8 | 6u << 4 | 9u, slow, 8), 6600);   // ECC: 45 %
	EQ(deratedBwMBps(0, slow, 8), 0);
}

// pipe A as the GOP left it on the B580 (2560x1440 on TC2, HBR2 x4, MBUS joined) and a 1080p sink on TC1
static LiveState liveA()
{
	LiveState s = {};
	s.pipeA = 0;
	const TimingRegs r = timingRegs(k1440);
	s.htotal = r.htotal; s.hblank = r.hblank; s.hsync = r.hsync; s.vtotal = r.vtotal; s.vblank = r.vblank; s.vsync = r.vsync;
	s.funcCtl = 1u << 31 | 5u << 27 | 2u << 24 | 3u << 1 | r.funcSync;   // TC2, SST, x4
	s.valfreq = 540000;
	const MN mn = linkMN(24, 4, k1440.clock, 540000);
	s.dataM = dataMReg(mn); s.dataN = mn.dataN; s.linkM = mn.linkM; s.linkN = mn.linkN;
	s.planeBufCfg = ddbReg(Ddb{ 0, 900 }); s.curBufCfg = ddbReg(Ddb{ 900, 932 });   // the GOP's plane + IntelXeFB's cursor
	s.mbusCtl = MBUS_JOIN | MBUS_HASHING_1x4;
	s.dbufCtl[0] = DBUF_POWER_REQUEST | DBUF_POWER_STATE | 3u << 16;
	s.pmd0 = 0xFFFFu << 16 | 1u << 6 | 1u << 4 | 1u; s.pmd1 = 653u << 20 | 540u << 8 | 2u;
	s.lat01 = 0x00040000; s.lat23 = 0x000A0008; s.latSagv = 20;
	s.memGlobal = 2u << 8 | 6u << 4 | 8u; s.qgvLow[0] = 900; s.qgvLow[1] = 450;
	return s;
}

static void testPlan()
{
	LiveState s = liveA();
	Request q = { 1, 3, k1080, 810000, 4 };
	Plan pl = {};
	EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kOk);
	CHECK(!strcmp(pl.portA.name, "TC2") && !strcmp(pl.portB.name, "TC1"), "ports %s %s", pl.portA.name, pl.portB.name);
	// pipe A recomputed from its own registers gives its registers back
	EQ(pl.a.t.clock, k1440.clock); EQ(dataMReg(pl.a.mn), s.dataM); EQ(pl.a.mn.linkM, s.linkM); EQ(pl.a.link.lanes, 4);
	EQ(pl.a.ddb.end, 4096); EQ(pl.a.dbox, mbusDboxCtl(true));
	EQ(pl.joinedNow, 1); EQ(pl.joinedAfter, 0);
	EQ(pl.a2.ddb.end, 2048); EQ(pl.aKeepsDdb, 1);
	EQ(pl.b.link.rate, 162000); EQ(pl.b.link.lanes, 4); EQ(pl.b.ddb.start, 0); EQ(pl.b.ddb.end, 2048); EQ(pl.b.mbusOffset, 2048);
	EQ(pl.b.slices, 0xC); EQ(pl.slicesNow, 0x1); EQ(pl.slicesAfter, 0xF);
	EQ(pl.mbusCtlAfter, 0u); EQ(pl.trackerNow, 3); EQ(pl.trackerAfter, 1); EQ(pl.b.dbox, 0x01030A48u);
	EQ(pl.pwIdx, 6);
	EQ(pl.pmdPost.pipes, 2); EQ(pl.pmdPost.phys, 2); EQ(pl.pmdPost.plls, 3); EQ(pl.pmdPost.dbufs, 3); EQ(pl.pmdPost.ddiclkMhz, 540);
	EQ(pl.pmdPre.ddiclkMhz, 540); EQ(pl.pmd0Post >> 16, 0xFFFF); EQ((pl.pmd0Post >> 6) & 3, 2); EQ(pl.pmd1Post & 7, 3);
	EQ(pl.bwMBps, 53000); EQ(pl.needMBps, (706250u * 4 + 148500u * 4 + 999) / 1000);
	CHECK(pl.b.wmOk && pl.b.wm.useSagv, "pipe B watermarks");
	// refusals
	q.port = 4; EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kPortInUse);
	q.port = 1; EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kBadPort);
	q.port = 3; s.transconfB = 1u << 31; EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kPipeInUse);
	s = liveA(); s.planeBufCfg = ddbReg(Ddb{ 0, 3000 }); EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kDdbA);
	// the panel on pipe B and the second output on pipe A: B's bank would move from offset 0 (joined) to 2048
	s = liveA(); s.pipeA = 1; q.pipe = 0; EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kDdbA); EQ(pl.a.mbusOffset, 0); EQ(pl.a2.mbusOffset, 2048);
	q.pipe = 1;
	s = liveA(); q.sinkMaxRate = 162000; q.sinkMaxLanes = 2; EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kNoLink);
	q = { 1, 3, k1080, 810000, 4 }; q.mode.clock = 1400000; q.mode.htotal = 9000; q.mode.vtotal = 2000;
	q.sinkMaxRate = 810000; EQ(computePlan(s, q, &pl), kNoLink);   // 4.2 GB/s: more than HBR3 x4
	s = liveA(); s.funcCtl = 0; EQ(computePlan(s, Request{ 1, 3, k1080, 810000, 4 }, &pl), kPipeA);
	s = liveA(); s.qgvLow[0] = 30; s.qgvLow[1] = 15; s.memGlobal = 2u << 8 | 1u << 4 | 8u;   // 2000 x 0.7 = 1400 MB/s
	EQ(computePlan(s, Request{ 1, 3, k1080, 810000, 4 }, &pl), kBandwidth);
}

// the dry run's "WxH@Hz" modes are drm_cvt_mode timings (intelxeedid::cvt): the VESA CVT 1.2 rasters; the clock is
// Linux's, which never takes off the 0.25 MHz step (it subtracts clock % 250 before setting the clock), so 138.611 MHz
// instead of the reference 138.5 for 1080p60 RB
static void testCvt()
{
	intelxeedid::Mode m = {};
	CHECK(intelxeedid::cvt(1920, 1080, 60, true, &m), "1080p60 RB");
	EQ(m.clock, 138611); EQ(m.htotal, 2080); EQ(m.hsync_start, 1968); EQ(m.hsync_end, 2000); EQ(m.vtotal, 1111);
	CHECK(intelxeedid::cvt(1920, 1080, 60, false, &m), "1080p60");
	EQ(m.clock, 173106); EQ(m.htotal, 2576); EQ(m.vtotal, 1120);
	CHECK(intelxeedid::cvt(3840, 2160, 60, true, &m), "4k60 RB");
	EQ(m.clock, 533120); EQ(m.htotal, 4000); EQ(m.vtotal, 2222);
}

// the second framebuffer while disconnected: the placeholder timing NMXAGDC answers for it, its mode, when IOGraphics hears
static void testSecondFb()
{
	const Timing t = offlineTiming();
	CHECK(timingSane(t), "the placeholder timing is sane");
	EQ(t.hdisplay, k1080.hdisplay); EQ(t.htotal, k1080.htotal); EQ(t.vtotal, k1080.vtotal); EQ(t.clock, k1080.clock);
	EQ(refreshMilliHz(t), 60000);   // 148.5 MHz / (2200 x 1125)
	// nvk5_timing_bad's rules (NMXAGDC refuses 0x921/0x711 otherwise): visible <= sync start < sync end <= total
	CHECK(t.hdisplay <= t.hsyncStart && t.hsyncStart < t.hsyncEnd && t.hsyncEnd <= t.htotal && t.htotal != t.hdisplay, "h");
	CHECK(t.vdisplay <= t.vsyncStart && t.vsyncStart < t.vsyncEnd && t.vsyncEnd <= t.vtotal && t.vtotal != t.vdisplay, "v");
	EQ(secondFbMode(true), kSecondModeSink); EQ(secondFbMode(false), kSecondModeOffline);
	CHECK(kSecondModeSink != kSecondModeOffline && kSecondModeSink > 0 && kSecondModeOffline > 0, "two distinct positive mode IDs");
	CHECK(secondFbModeValid(1) && secondFbModeValid(2) && !secondFbModeValid(0) && !secondFbModeValid(3), "mode IDs");
	// the connect interrupt: only for a real change
	CHECK(!secondFbReport(false, false, false), "disconnected stays disconnected (start, stop with nothing plugged)");
	CHECK(!secondFbReport(false, false, true), "a sink seen while staying disconnected is not reported");
	CHECK(secondFbReport(false, true, false) && secondFbReport(false, true, true), "plug");
	CHECK(secondFbReport(true, false, false) && secondFbReport(true, false, true), "unplug");
	CHECK(!secondFbReport(true, true, false), "the same monitor after a wake");
	CHECK(secondFbReport(true, true, true), "another monitor after a wake");
	CHECK(sameTiming(t, k1080) && !sameTiming(t, k1440), "sameTiming");
	Timing u = t; u.pvsync = false;
	CHECK(!sameTiming(t, u), "sameTiming sees the sync polarity");
}

int main()
{
	testSecondFb();
	testCvt();
	testPorts();
	testDbuf();
	testLink();
	testWm();
	testPmdemand();
	testPlan();
	printf("plan_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# apply.sh <mesa-checkout>: turn an upstream Mesa checkout at f01e9b07a91 into the exact source of the released
# libvulkan_intel.dylib: prod9 (installed as a7021b7e) with the B580 -> IntelXe rename of patches/0101. intelxe.diff is
# the whole difference; patches/ and xe2-venc/ hold the same changes split into reviewable steps.
#   git clone https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa.git && git -C mesa checkout f01e9b07a91f7e7ab730edfbb383b083f146067b
#   mesa/apply.sh mesa
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "${1:?usage: apply.sh <mesa-checkout at f01e9b07a91>}"
[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" = f01e9b07a91f7e7ab730edfbb383b083f146067b ] || { echo "the checkout is not at f01e9b07a91" >&2; exit 1; }
patch -p1 -s < "$HERE/intelxe.diff"
# an empty generated header the diff cannot carry
mkdir -p src/intel/blorp/stub && : > src/intel/blorp/stub/blorp_shaders.h
echo "patched: now run $HERE/configure.sh with MESA_SRC=$(pwd)"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# configure.sh: meson setup for the B580 ANV driver on macOS, with the options of the installed build (prod9).
#   MESA_SRC=<patched mesa> mesa/configure.sh && ninja -C $MESA_SRC/build src/intel/vulkan/libvulkan_intel.dylib
# Needs: meson + ninja, python3 with mako/packaging/pyyaml, and mesa_clc + vtn_bindgen2 for the system CLC
# (-Dmesa-clc=system: a host build of Mesa's clc tools, which need LLVM/Clang with SPIR-V support).
# MESA_GIT_SHA1_OVERRIDE keeps the version string of the released build ("Mesa 27.0.0-devel (git-a3ad934832)").
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)
: "${MESA_SRC:?set MESA_SRC to the patched Mesa source tree (mesa/apply.sh)}"
cd "$MESA_SRC"
export MESA_GIT_SHA1_OVERRIDE=${MESA_GIT_SHA1_OVERRIDE:-a3ad934832}
exec meson setup "${BUILD:-build}" --cross-file "$HERE/darwin-x86_64.ini" \
	-Dbuildtype=release -Db_ndebug=true '-Dc_args=-Xclang -fno-split-cold-code' '-Dcpp_args=-Xclang -fno-split-cold-code' \
	-Dplatforms=macos -Dvulkan-drivers=intel -Dgallium-drivers= -Dvulkan-layers= -Dtools= \
	-Dopengl=false -Dgles1=disabled -Dgles2=disabled -Dglx=disabled -Degl=disabled -Dgbm=disabled \
	-Dllvm=disabled -Dintel-rt=enabled -Dintel-elk=false \
	-Dvideo-codecs=h264dec,h265dec,av1dec,vp9dec,h264enc,h265enc,av1enc \
	-Dzstd=disabled -Dvalgrind=disabled -Dlibunwind=disabled -Dlmsensors=disabled \
	-Dperfetto=false -Dbuild-tests=false -Dxmlconfig=disabled -Dexpat=disabled -Dspirv-tools=disabled \
	-Dmesa-clc=system -Dxemac="$REPO/user/xemac" \
	"$@"

Subject: [PATCH 1/6] util/futex: implement futexes on macOS with
 os_sync_wait_on_address

macOS 14.4 added os_sync_wait_on_address() and os_sync_wake_by_address_*(),
which have futex semantics. Use them when the deployment target allows,
so code that needs futex_wait()/futex_wake() (anv's block pool, for one)
builds on macOS. Absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC timeouts are turned into the
relative timeout os_sync_wait_on_address_with_timeout() takes.

Generated-by: LLM
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+#elif defined(__APPLE__)
+
+#include <assert.h>
+#include <errno.h>
+#include <limits.h>
+#include <time.h>
+#include <os/clock.h>
+#include <os/os_sync_wait_on_address.h>
+
+int futex_wake(uint32_t *addr, int32_t count)
+{
+   assert(count == 1 || count == INT32_MAX);
+   /* Fails with ENOENT when nobody waits, which is not an error here. */
+   if (count == 1)
+      os_sync_wake_by_address_any(addr, sizeof(*addr), OS_SYNC_WAKE_BY_ADDRESS_NONE);
+   else
+      os_sync_wake_by_address_all(addr, sizeof(*addr), OS_SYNC_WAKE_BY_ADDRESS_NONE);
+   return 0;
+}
+
+int futex_wait(uint32_t *addr, int32_t value, const struct timespec *timeout)
+{
+   int ret;
+
+   if (timeout == NULL) {
+      ret = os_sync_wait_on_address(addr, (uint32_t)value, sizeof(*addr),
+                                    OS_SYNC_WAIT_ON_ADDRESS_NONE);
+   } else {
+      /* The timeout is absolute on CLOCK_MONOTONIC, like FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET. */
+      struct timespec now;
+      clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &now);
+      int64_t ns = (int64_t)(timeout->tv_sec - now.tv_sec) * 1000000000 +
+                   (timeout->tv_nsec - now.tv_nsec);
+      if (ns <= 0) {
+         errno = ETIMEDOUT;
+         return -1;
+      }
+      ret = os_sync_wait_on_address_with_timeout(addr, (uint32_t)value,
+                                                 sizeof(*addr),
+                                                 OS_SYNC_WAIT_ON_ADDRESS_NONE,
+                                                 OS_CLOCK_MACH_ABSOLUTE_TIME,
+                                                 ns);
+   }
+   return ret < 0 ? -1 : 0;
+}

From 5d25e3d2d5ffe98a82a21661aff040516a2d352a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?= <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 05:25:05 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 4/6] intel: add -Dintel-internal-shaders=stub to build anv
 without mesa-clc and glslang

anv's internal shaders (indirect draw generation, query copies, DGC, the
resinfo helpers, blorp's indirect copies) are OpenCL C compiled by
mesa-clc, which needs LLVM, and the fp64 library, BVH builders and ASTC
decoder are GLSL compiled by glslang. Neither is available on every
host (macOS without Homebrew), which makes it impossible to bring anv
up there at all.

With intel-internal-shaders=stub the intel Vulkan driver no longer pulls
in mesa-clc or glslang: ray tracing is off, the generated NIR builders are
replaced by stubs that log and abort when used, blorp keeps a hand-written
blorp_check_in_bounds(), and ASTC emulation and the runtime's BVH helpers
are compiled out. Meant for bring-up only; the default stays 'enabled'.

Generated-by: LLM
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+/* Copyright © 2026 Intel Corporation
+ * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+ */
+
+/* Stand-in for the blorp_shaders.h that vtn_bindgen2 generates from
+ * blorp_shaders.cl, used with -Dintel-internal-shaders=stub (no mesa-clc).
+ * blorp_check_in_bounds() is small enough to build by hand; the indirect
+ * copy shaders abort.
+ */
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <stdlib.h>
+#include "compiler/nir/nir_builder.h"
+#include "util/log.h"
+
+static inline nir_def *
+blorp_check_in_bounds(nir_builder *b, nir_def *bounds_rect, nir_def *pos)
+{
+   nir_def *x = nir_channel(b, pos, 0), *y = nir_channel(b, pos, 1);
+
+   return nir_iand(b,
+                   nir_iand(b, nir_uge(b, x, nir_channel(b, bounds_rect, 0)),
+                               nir_ult(b, x, nir_channel(b, bounds_rect, 1))),
+                   nir_iand(b, nir_uge(b, y, nir_channel(b, bounds_rect, 2)),
+                               nir_ult(b, y, nir_channel(b, bounds_rect, 3))));
+}
+
+static inline void
+blorp_shaders_missing(const char *name)
+{
+   mesa_loge("blorp was built without internal shaders (%s)", name);
+   abort();
+}
+
+#define blorp_copy_memory_indirect_shader(b, ...) \
+   blorp_shaders_missing("blorp_copy_memory_indirect_shader")
+#define blorp_copy_memory_to_image_indirect_shader(b, ...) \
+   blorp_shaders_missing("blorp_copy_memory_to_image_indirect_shader")

From 9b84189307c12d88198a3c6ed7b730b4748c01a1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 05:25:05 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 5/6] anv: link with dynamic lookup on macOS

The entrypoints anv does not implement are weak references that are
never defined; ld64 rejects them unless undefined symbols may be looked
up at run time, as kosmickrisp already does.

Generated-by: LLM
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+  # ld64 only accepts with dynamic lookup (same as kosmickrisp).

FILE: mesa/patches/0006-anv-run-on-macOS-over-xemac-a-kernel-extension-speak.patch
================================================
From 62a3813717721f43500ae574082064cf560d33c2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?= <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 05:25:46 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 6/6] anv: run on macOS over xemac, a kernel extension speaking
 the xe uAPI

-Dxemac=<dir> points at the user-space side of a macOS kernel extension
that implements Linux's xe uAPI (DRM core syncobj ioctls plus DRM_XE_*)
behind an IOUserClient: xemac.h/xemac.c and a libdrm stand-in
(libdrm/xf86drm.h, xemac_drm.c) that implements the libdrm calls Mesa
makes on top of xemac_ioctl(). With it:

- dep_libdrm is the stand-in, so HAVE_LIBDRM code (vk_drm_syncobj,
  u_sync_provider, vk_instance's DRM enumeration, intel_kmd,
  intel_device_info) builds and runs unchanged;
- intel_ioctl() goes to xemac_ioctl(), like intel_virtio_ioctl() for
  virtio;
- anv opens and closes its device through anv_kmd_open()/anv_kmd_close()
  (xemac_open()/xemac_close()), and xe BO maps go through xemac_mmap()/
  xemac_munmap(), since IOKit mappings must be torn down by the kernel
  extension;
- dma-buf/sync_file/opaque fd sharing and VK_EXT_physical_device_drm are
  not advertised.

Generated-by: LLM
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

diff --git a/src/intel/vulkan/anv_nvmtl_surface.c b/src/intel/vulkan/anv_nvmtl_surface.c
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..6f39c64e6af
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/intel/vulkan/anv_nvmtl_surface.c
@@ -0,0 +1,128 @@
+/*
+ * Implicit IOSurface synchronization for the nullmoth Metal plugin on B580.kext (macOS, xemac).
+ *
+ * B580.kext keeps, per IOSurface ID, the fences of the jobs that last wrote and read the surface (uapi/b580_drm.h, the
+ * dma-resv model). These entry points let the plugin, which only sees Vulkan objects, attach a submission's fence to a
+ * surface and import a surface's fences into a timeline semaphore it then waits on in vkQueueSubmit, so a consumer in
+ * another process (WindowServer compositing a game's frame) waits on the GPU instead of the producer waiting on the CPU.
+ * They are looked up with dlsym; a plugin that does not find them, or a kernel without B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES, keeps
+ * the CPU-side ordering.
+ */
+#include "anv_private.h"
+
+#include "vk_drm_syncobj.h"
+#include "vk_fence.h"
+#include "vk_semaphore.h"
+
+#include "drm-uapi/drm.h"
+#include "../../../../b580/uapi/b580_drm.h"
+
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_cap_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t *supported);
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_attach_v1(VkDevice _device, VkFence fence, VkSemaphore sem, uint64_t value,
+                                            uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags);
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_import_v1(VkDevice _device, VkSemaphore sem, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags,
+                                            uint64_t *wait_value, uint32_t *count);
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_wait_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags, int64_t timeout_abs_ns);
+
+/* intel_ioctl restarts on EAGAIN, which ATTACH returns for a point that has no fence yet: retry on EINTR only */
+static int
+nvmtl_ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, void *arg)
+{
+   int ret;
+   do {
+#ifdef HAVE_XEMAC
+      ret = xemac_ioctl(fd, request, arg);
+#else
+      ret = ioctl(fd, request, arg);
+#endif
+   } while (ret == -1 && errno == EINTR);
+   return ret;
+}
+
+static struct vk_drm_syncobj *
+nvmtl_syncobj_of(VkFence _fence, VkSemaphore _sem)
+{
+   struct vk_sync *sync = NULL;
+   if (_fence) {
+      VK_FROM_HANDLE(vk_fence, fence, _fence);
+      sync = vk_fence_get_active_sync(fence);
+   } else if (_sem) {
+      VK_FROM_HANDLE(vk_semaphore, sem, _sem);
+      sync = vk_semaphore_get_active_sync(sem);
+   }
+   return sync ? vk_sync_as_drm_syncobj(sync) : NULL;
+}
+
+static VkResult
+nvmtl_errno_result(int err)
+{
+   switch (err) {
+   case 0: return VK_SUCCESS;
+   case EAGAIN: return VK_NOT_READY;
+   case ETIME: case ETIMEDOUT: return VK_TIMEOUT;
+   case ENOSPC: case ENOMEM: return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY;
+   case ENOENT: case EINVAL: return VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN;
+   default: return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   }
+}
+
+/* *supported = 1 when the kernel has the surface-fence ioctls (B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES). */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_cap_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t *supported)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct drm_get_cap cap = { .capability = B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES };
+   *supported = 0;
+   if (intel_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap))
+      return VK_SUCCESS;
+   *supported = cap.value == 1;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Attach the fence of `fence` (a binary syncobj), or of timeline semaphore `sem` at `value`, to surface `surface_id`
+ * as a B580_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE or _READ user. VK_NOT_READY: not submitted yet (EAGAIN). */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_attach_v1(VkDevice _device, VkFence fence, VkSemaphore sem, uint64_t value, uint32_t surface_id,
+                            uint32_t flags)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct vk_drm_syncobj *s = nvmtl_syncobj_of(fence, sem);
+   if (!s)
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_attach a = {
+      .surface_id = surface_id, .syncobj = s->syncobj, .point = fence ? 0 : value, .flags = flags,
+   };
+   return nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_ATTACH, &a) ? nvmtl_errno_result(errno) : VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Add the fences of surface `surface_id` that a B580_SURFACE_FENCE_READER or _WRITER must wait for as new points of
+ * timeline semaphore `sem` (one used for nothing else). *wait_value: the point to wait on, 0 when there is nothing. */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_import_v1(VkDevice _device, VkSemaphore sem, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags,
+                            uint64_t *wait_value, uint32_t *count)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   *wait_value = 0;
+   if (count)
+      *count = 0;
+   struct vk_drm_syncobj *s = nvmtl_syncobj_of(VK_NULL_HANDLE, sem);
+   if (!s || !(s->base.flags & VK_SYNC_IS_TIMELINE))
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_import m = { .surface_id = surface_id, .syncobj = s->syncobj, .flags = flags };
+   if (nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_IMPORT, &m))
+      return nvmtl_errno_result(errno);
+   *wait_value = m.count_out ? m.point_out : 0;
+   if (count)
+      *count = m.count_out;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Wait on the CPU until the fences of surface `surface_id` that `flags` names have signaled, or until
+ * `timeout_abs_ns` (CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW; 0 polls). VK_TIMEOUT when it ran out. */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_wait_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags, int64_t timeout_abs_ns)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_wait w = { .surface_id = surface_id, .flags = flags, .timeout_ns = timeout_abs_ns };
+   return nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT, &w) ? nvmtl_errno_result(errno) : VK_SUCCESS;
+}

FILE: mesa/patches/0009-util-anon_file-create-anonymous-files-in-the-per-user-temp-dir-on-macOS.patch
================================================
From: =?UTF-8?q?Yusuf=20=C4=B0hsan=20KILIN=C3=87?= <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 12:45:00 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] util/anon_file: create anonymous files in the per-user temp
 dir on macOS

macOS has neither memfd_create() nor SHM_ANON, so os_create_anonymous_file()
falls back to a file in get_or_create_user_temp_dir(), which without
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (never set on macOS) is /tmp/xdg-runtime-mesa-<uid>. A
sandboxed process may not create files there: in QuickTime Player (App
Sandbox) and VTDecoderXPCService (VTDecoderSandboxProfile, which allows
writes only under /private/var/folders) anv_state_table_init() got -1, so
vkCreateDevice() returned VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED and Vulkan Video
(the B580 AV1 VideoToolbox decoder) and Metal could not come up there.
POSIX shm is no way out: sandboxed apps may only use their application
group's shm names.

The platform's counterpart of XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is the per-user temporary
directory, confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR): owned by the user, mode 0700,
emptied at boot, and redirected by the App Sandbox into the app's container.
Unless XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is set, create the file there first; the file is
still unlinked right after mkostemp(), and its only use stays the same
(ftruncate() + MAP_SHARED mappings of the one fd in this process). When the
file cannot be created there (a process whose effective uid differs from
the uid the directory belongs to, such as WindowServer, uid 0 / euid 88),
the /tmp fallback is tried as before.

+/*
+ * macOS has neither memfd nor SHM_ANON, and a sandboxed process may create
+ * neither files in /tmp nor POSIX shm objects outside its application group.
+ * The per-user temporary directory, confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR), is the
+ * platform's counterpart of XDG_RUNTIME_DIR: owned by the user, mode 0700,
+ * emptied at boot, and inside an App Sandbox redirected to a directory of the
+ * app's own, so it is where a sandboxed process (QuickTime Player,
+ * VTDecoderXPCService, ...) may create a temporary file.
+ * Returns a pointer to the path buffer, which the caller must free(), or NULL.
+ */
+static char*
+get_darwin_user_temp_dir(void)
+{
+   size_t n = confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR, NULL, 0);
+   char *buf = n ? malloc(n) : NULL;
+
+   if (!buf)
+      return NULL;
+   if (confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR, buf, n) == 0 || buf[0] == '\0') {
+      free(buf);
+      return NULL;
+   }

+   n = strlen(buf);
+   while (n > 1 && buf[n - 1] == '/')
+      buf[--n] = '\0';

FILE: mesa/patches/0011-anv-xemac-keep-video-session-memory-in-CPU-visible-VRAM.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:40:00 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 11] anv: xemac: keep video session memory in CPU-visible VRAM

The xemac port offers only host-visible memory types for video session
memory (the driver CPU-maps it and the kernel cannot migrate a VRAM BO
into the BAR window on a CPU fault). On a dGPU the first host-visible
type is system memory, and that is what applications (FFmpeg's
ff_vk_alloc_mem, any "first matching type" allocator) pick, so the MFX/
VDEnc/HCP row-store, MV and statistics buffers were in system RAM and
every per-macroblock / per-CTU access crossed PCIe.

Offer only the CPU-visible VRAM types when there are any; system memory
stays the fallback (and the kernel still places a BO in system memory
when the CPU-visible window is full).

Arc B580, 1080p, 600 frames, CQP: H.264 encode 3.21 s -> 0.95 s
(187 -> 630 fps), HEVC encode 0.90 s -> 0.52 s (660 -> 1150 fps);
H.264 and AV1 decode output unchanged (framemd5 identical).

Applies on top of 0010 (src/mesa-venc) and on src/mesa-video.

FILE: mesa/patches/0013-anv-index-mutable-descriptor-type-lists-by-pBindings.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 15:20:00 +0300
Subject: [PATCH 13] anv: index the mutable descriptor type lists by pBindings
 index, not binding number

VkMutableDescriptorTypeCreateInfoEXT::pMutableDescriptorTypeLists[i]
describes pBindings[i] of the VkDescriptorSetLayoutCreateInfo it chains
to (radv and nvk index it so, and so does anv's own
GetDescriptorSetLayoutSupport). anv_CreateDescriptorSetLayout walks the
bindings sorted by binding number and looked the list up with that
number b instead of the pBindings index (info_idx). With sparse or
unordered binding numbers a mutable binding got another binding's list,
or none when b >= mutableDescriptorTypeListCount, which sizes it for
every descriptor type: a sampler state in the sampler heap and the
largest surface size.

Seen with a layout whose mutable storage-image band sits at binding
numbers 480-607 with 321 lists: every set took 160 sampler states instead
of 32, so a descriptor pool sized from the same lists (which pools index
correctly, by pPoolSizes index) held a fifth of its maxSets
(VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_POOL_MEMORY at 51 of 256 sets).

+/* nvmtl (gpuperf): anv_device_import_bo for a GEM handle the kernel already gave this client (B580.kext's
+ * DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_VRAM: an IOSurface's VRAM backing, shared with other processes) and its size. The handle is
+ * this import's: a second import of the same surface gets its own handle (and its own anv_bo); on failure it is closed. */
+VkResult
+anv_device_import_bo_handle(struct anv_device *device, uint32_t gem_handle, uint64_t size,
+                            enum anv_bo_alloc_flags alloc_flags, uint64_t client_address,
+                            struct anv_bo **bo_out)
+{
+   assert(alloc_flags & ANV_BO_ALLOC_EXTERNAL);
+   struct anv_bo_cache *cache = &device->bo_cache;
+   simple_mtx_lock(&cache->mutex);
+   struct anv_bo *bo = anv_device_lookup_bo(device, gem_handle);
+   struct anv_bo new_bo = {
+      .name = "nvmtl-surface-vram",
+      .gem_handle = gem_handle,
+      .refcount = 1,
+      .offset = -1,
+      .alloc_flags = alloc_flags | ANV_BO_ALLOC_IMPORTED,
+      .size = size,
+      .actual_size = size,
+   };
+   if (!bo || bo->refcount > 0 || !size) {
+      device->kmd_backend->gem_close(device, &new_bo);
+      simple_mtx_unlock(&cache->mutex);
+      return vk_error(device, VK_ERROR_INVALID_EXTERNAL_HANDLE);
+   }
+   uint32_t bo_flags;
+   VkResult result = anv_gem_import_bo_alloc_flags_to_bo_flags(device, bo, new_bo.alloc_flags, &bo_flags);
+   if (result != VK_SUCCESS) {
+      device->kmd_backend->gem_close(device, &new_bo);
+      simple_mtx_unlock(&cache->mutex);
+      return result;
+   }
+   uint32_t alignment = anv_bo_vma_calc_alignment_requirement(device, new_bo.alloc_flags, size);
+   result = anv_bo_vma_alloc_or_close(device, &new_bo, new_bo.alloc_flags, client_address, alignment);
+   if (result != VK_SUCCESS) {
+      simple_mtx_unlock(&cache->mutex);
+      return result;
+   }
+   result = device->kmd_backend->vm_bind_bo(device, &new_bo);
+   if (result != VK_SUCCESS) {
+      anv_bo_vma_free(device, &new_bo);
+      device->kmd_backend->gem_close(device, &new_bo);
+      simple_mtx_unlock(&cache->mutex);
+      return result;
+   }
+   *bo = new_bo;
+   ANV_RMV(bo_allocate, device, bo);
+   bo->flags = bo_flags;
+   simple_mtx_unlock(&cache->mutex);
+   *bo_out = bo;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+

 anv_device_export_bo(struct anv_device *device,

+bool
+anv_nvmtl_surface_vram_staged(struct anv_device *device, uint64_t need, enum anv_bo_alloc_flags alloc_flags,
+                              uint64_t client_address, struct anv_bo **bo, VkResult *result)
+{
+   struct nvmtl_anv_surface_vram_req *req = nvmtl_staged_vram;
+   if (!req)
+      return false;
+   nvmtl_staged_vram = NULL;   /* one import per stage */
+   struct drm_b580_surface_vram v = {
+      .surface_id = req->surface_id, .plane = req->plane,
+      .size = req->size > need ? req->size : need, .flags = req->flags & B580_SURFACE_VRAM_CREATE,
+   };
+   if (nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_VRAM, &v)) {
+      req->err = errno;
+      *result = vk_errorf(device, VK_ERROR_INVALID_EXTERNAL_HANDLE, "surface %u VRAM: errno %d", req->surface_id, req->err);
+      return true;
+   }
+   req->err = 0;
+   req->size_out = v.size_out;
+   req->gen = v.gen;
+   if (v.size_out < need) {
+      struct anv_bo tmp = { .gem_handle = v.handle };
+      device->kmd_backend->gem_close(device, &tmp);
+      req->err = ENOSPC;
+      *result = vk_error(device, VK_ERROR_INVALID_EXTERNAL_HANDLE);
+      return true;
+   }
+   *result = anv_device_import_bo_handle(device, v.handle, v.size_out, alloc_flags | ANV_BO_ALLOC_EXTERNAL,
+                                         client_address, bo);
+   if (*result != VK_SUCCESS)
+      req->err = EIO;
+   return true;
+}

================================================
anv: AV1 BRC loop filter back-annotation on Xe2 (on top of 0015)

Under CBR/VBR the HuC update kernel now also picks the loop filter levels for the base_q_idx it chooses
(UPD_EnableLFUpdate, as media-driver always does; off for intra block copy frames). The frame header then
carries loop_filter_level[2..3] only when the chosen luma levels are not both zero, so its length is known
only on the GPU: the padding OBU and tile group header are recorded for both lengths in second level batches,
and the one matching the kernel's AVP_INLOOP_FILTER_STATE levels runs (MI_CONDITIONAL_BATCH_BUFFER_END); the
tile group obu_size store after PAK picks its address the same way.
vk_video: the header layout's size_in_bits now ends after trailing_one_bit (the HuC rewrites over that many
bits and only zero-pads: without the one bit the header has no trailing_one_bit, byte aligned it grows a byte).
CDEF stays as the application set it (ffmpeg's sequence header has enable_cdef = 0).

+/* After the update kernel ran: keep the luma loop filter levels it put in the output AVP_INLOOP_FILTER_STATE
+ * (DW1 bits 5:0 and 11:6, media-driver readBRCMetaDataFromSLBB) with a 0xfff compare mask behind them. */
+static void
+anv_av1_brc_capture_lf_levels(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd, const struct anv_av1_brc_frame *brc)
+{
+   struct anv_video_session *vid = cmd->video.vid;
+   struct anv_address dst = anv_av1_brc_scratch_addr(vid, ANV_AV1_BRC_SCRATCH_LF_LEVELS);
+   struct mi_builder b;
+
+   mi_builder_init(&b, cmd->device->info, &cmd->batch);
+   mi_builder_set_mocs(&b, anv_mocs_for_address(cmd->device, &dst));
+   mi_store(&b, mi_mem32(dst), mi_mem32(anv_av1_brc_slb_out_addr(vid, brc->layout.inloop_filter_offset + 4)));
+   mi_store(&b, mi_mem32(anv_address_add(dst, 4)), mi_imm(0xfff));
+}
+
+/* First command of a second level batch that only applies when the kernel's luma loop filter levels are both
+ * zero (@with_chroma_levels false) or not (true): loop_filter_level[2..3] are coded only in the latter case. */
+static void
+anv_av1_brc_emit_lf_variant_check(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd, bool with_chroma_levels)
+{
+   anv_batch_emit(&cmd->batch, GENX(MI_CONDITIONAL_BATCH_BUFFER_END), cbbe) {
+      /* the batch ends unless (levels & mask) <op> 0 holds */
+      cbbe.CompareOperation = with_chroma_levels ? MADGreaterThanIDD : MADEqualIDD;
+      cbbe.EndCurrentBatchBufferLevel = true;
+      cbbe.CompareSemaphore = 1;
+      cbbe.CompareMaskMode = CompareMaskModeEnabled;
+      cbbe.CompareDataDword = 0;
+      cbbe.CompareAddress = anv_av1_brc_scratch_addr(cmd->video.vid, ANV_AV1_BRC_SCRATCH_LF_LEVELS);
+   }
+}

FILE: mesa/patches/0017-anv-H.264-HuC-BRC-single-PAK-pass.patch
================================================
anv: run the H.264 HuC BRC as single PAK pass (on top of 0010..0016)

The encode runs one PAK pass per frame but told the AVC BRC kernels there were two (UPD_MaxNumPass 2,
INIT_SinglePassOnly 0) and compensated with a second BRC update right after the encode, which accounts each
frame twice (once there, once in the next frame's update). Use media-driver's single pass VDEnc BRC
(AvcEncodeBRC::EnableVdencSinglePass): INIT_SinglePassOnly 1, UPD_MaxNumPass 1, no post-encode update.
1080p60 CBR 6 Mbit/s, 300 frames: 7.04 -> 6.32 Mbit/s (600 frames: 6.63 -> 6.16); the remainder is the
initial buffer (ffmpeg leaves virtualBufferSizeInMs 0, the driver then uses 2 s / 1 s initial).

FILE: mesa/patches/0018-anv-AV1-encode-quarter-pel-motion-search.patch
================================================
anv: AV1 encode on Xe2: quarter-pel motion search and media-driver's reference id defaults (on top of 0017)

VDENC_CMD2 SubPelMode was never programmed, so the VDEnc searched integer motion vectors only. media-driver's
VDENC_CMD2 parameters default to subPelMode 3 (quarter pel) and no AV1 feature changes it. 1080p60 BBB, CQP
q index 120: 18.2 -> 7.2 Mbit/s with 36.3 -> 38.3 dB; VBR 2/4/8 Mbit/s: +2.1/+2.9/+4.0 dB (now -0.6/-0.4/+0.2 dB
against HEVC at the same rate). Applies to the gen12.5 path too, which had the same omission.
The AV1 reference ids of unused list entries keep media-driver's default (LAST) instead of 0.

FILE: mesa/patches/0020-util-os_misc-macOS-per-process-options-file.patch
================================================
util/os_misc: macOS per-process options file as a fallback to getenv() (like Android's properties)

Processes started by a launcher (Minecraft from TLauncher: java) or system daemons get no environment we can set, so
INTEL_MEASURE, INTEL_DEBUG, ANV_DEBUG, MESA_VK_WSI_* could not be used on them. os_get_option() now falls back, on
macOS and for non-secure lookups only, to /tmp/mesa-options-<getprogname()>: NAME=VALUE lines, '#' comments, read once
at the first lookup, and only when the file is a regular file owned by the process's effective user and not writable by
group or others (nobody can set options for another user's processes or the window server's). Example:
  printf 'INTEL_MEASURE=rt,file=/tmp/mc.csv,start=3000,count=300\nMESA_VK_WSI_FPS_LOG=/tmp/mc-fps.log\n' > /tmp/mesa-options-java

@@ -216,6 +216,79 @@ os_get_android_option(const char *name)
 }
 #endif
 
+#if DETECT_OS_APPLE
+#  include <stdlib.h>
+#  include <sys/stat.h>
+#  include <fcntl.h>
+#  include <unistd.h>
+
+/**
+ * macOS: options for processes whose environment cannot be set (a game
+ * started by a launcher, a system daemon), as a fallback to getenv(), the
+ * way Android falls back to its property system.
+ *
+ * The file /tmp/mesa-options-<program name> (getprogname(), e.g. "java")
+ * holds NAME=VALUE lines ('#' starts a comment).  It is read once, when the
+ * first option is looked up, and only if it is a regular file owned by the
+ * process's effective user and not writable by group or others, so nobody
+ * can set options for another user's processes (or the window server's).
+ */
+#define MESA_APPLE_OPTIONS_MAX 64
+static struct { char *name, *value; } apple_options[MESA_APPLE_OPTIONS_MAX];
+static unsigned apple_option_count;
+
+static void
+os_load_apple_options(void)
+{
+   char path[256];
+   snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "/tmp/mesa-options-%s", getprogname());
+
+   int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC);
+   if (fd < 0)
+      return;
+   struct stat st;
+   FILE *f = NULL;
+   if (fstat(fd, &st) == 0 && S_ISREG(st.st_mode) && st.st_uid == geteuid() &&
+       !(st.st_mode & (S_IWGRP | S_IWOTH)))
+      f = fdopen(fd, "r");
+   if (!f) {
+      close(fd);
+      return;
+   }
+
+   char line[1024];
+   while (apple_option_count < MESA_APPLE_OPTIONS_MAX &&
+          fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
+      char *p = line;
+      while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t')
+         p++;
+      if (*p == '#' || *p == '\0')
+         continue;
+      p[strcspn(p, "\r\n")] = '\0';
+      char *eq = strchr(p, '=');
+      if (!eq || eq == p)
+         continue;
+      *eq = '\0';
+      apple_options[apple_option_count].name = strdup(p);
+      apple_options[apple_option_count].value = strdup(eq + 1);
+      apple_option_count++;
+   }
+   fclose(f);
+}
+
+static const char *
+os_get_apple_option(const char *name)
+{
+   static util_once_flag once = UTIL_ONCE_FLAG_INIT;
+   util_call_once(&once, os_load_apple_options);
+   for (unsigned i = 0; i < apple_option_count; i++) {
+      if (!strcmp(apple_options[i].name, name))
+         return apple_options[i].value;
+   }
+   return NULL;
+}
+#endif
+
 #if DETECT_OS_WINDOWS

@@ -249,6 +322,11 @@ os_get_option_internal(const char *name, bool use_secure_getenv)

    }
+#endif

+      opt = os_get_apple_option(name);
+   }
 #endif

FILE: mesa/patches/0022-anv-measure-initialize-the-batch-list-link-in-anv_measure_init.patch

anv/measure: initialize the batch's list link in anv_measure_init()

anv_measure_reset() calls anv_measure_init() for a command buffer that has no measure batch yet (capture was off when it
was allocated, e.g. INTEL_MEASURE=...,start=N) and returns right away, so the batch keeps the zeroed link vk_alloc +
memset left. Its first submission with snapshots then dereferences measure->base.link.next (NULL) in
_anv_measure_submit()'s "reused command buffer without reset" check (0eed818588a): Minecraft 26.3 (Vulkan) died with
SIGSEGV in _anv_measure_submit+0x50 from xe_queue_exec_locked the moment capture started at frame 20000. Platform
independent; upstream main has the same code. Also leave cmd_buffer->measure NULL when the allocation fails instead of
writing through a NULL pointer.

+      cmd_buffer->measure = NULL;
+      return;

FILE: mesa/patches/0023-anv-keep-push-descriptor-data-in-host-memory.patch
================================================
anv: keep push descriptor data in host memory, never read it back from write-combined memory

anv_push_descriptor_set_init() keeps the previous descriptors on a new push with the same layout by copying the old
descriptor memory into the new allocation (the "TODO: keep a copy of the old data on the host" there). That memory
comes from the surface/dynamic/indirect-push state pools, which on a discrete GPU are write-combined VRAM: every push
reads it back over PCIe uncached. Minecraft 26.3 (Vulkan) spent 17% of its render thread in that memmove (646 of
3872 samples at ~950 fps, anv_push_descriptor_set_init+563 / +815).

The command buffer's push sets now keep a host copy (push_set->host_shadow): descriptor writes go to host memory
(set->desc_{surface,sampler}_mem.map points at it), the copy keeps the previous descriptors without any read, and
anv_push_descriptor_set_upload() streams the whole set into the GPU allocation after each push's writes (write-only,
which write-combined memory does at full speed). The GPU addresses, sizes and the re-allocation rule
(set_used_on_gpu) are unchanged. Other users of anv_push_descriptor_set_init (ASTC emulation) keep the old path.

--- a/src/intel/vulkan/anv_descriptor_set.c
+++ b/src/intel/vulkan/anv_descriptor_set.c
@@ -1812,6 +1812,49 @@
    }
 
    return VK_SUCCESS;
+}

+/* The host copy of a push set's descriptor data, grown to `size` (keeping
+ * its contents: a push with the same layout keeps the previous descriptors).
+ */
+static bool
+anv_push_descriptor_shadow_grow(struct anv_push_descriptor_set *push_set,
+                                void **shadow, uint32_t *shadow_size,
+                                uint32_t size)
+{
+   if (*shadow_size >= size)
+      return true;
+   void *grown = vk_zalloc(push_set->shadow_alloc, size, 64,
+                           VK_SYSTEM_ALLOCATION_SCOPE_OBJECT);
+   if (grown == NULL)
+      return false;
+   if (*shadow) {
+      memcpy(grown, *shadow, *shadow_size);
+      vk_free(push_set->shadow_alloc, *shadow);
+   }
+   *shadow = grown;
+   *shadow_size = size;
+   return true;
+}
+
+/* After a push's descriptor writes: stream the host copies into the GPU
+ * memory the set points at (write-only, so write-combined memory is fine).
+ */
+void
+anv_push_descriptor_set_upload(struct anv_push_descriptor_set *push_set)
+{
+   if (!push_set->host_shadow)
+      return;
+   if (push_set->surface_gpu.map && push_set->surface_shadow) {
+      memcpy(push_set->surface_gpu.map, push_set->surface_shadow,
+             MIN2(push_set->surface_gpu.alloc_size,
+                  push_set->surface_shadow_size));
+   }
+   if (push_set->sampler_gpu.map && push_set->sampler_shadow) {
+      memcpy(push_set->sampler_gpu.map, push_set->sampler_shadow,
+             MIN2(push_set->sampler_gpu.alloc_size,
+                  push_set->sampler_shadow_size));
+   }
 }

FILE: mesa/patches/0024-wsi-metal-IOSurface-swapchains-one-CA-commit-per-refresh.patch
================================================
wsi/metal: IOSurface swapchains: at most two Core Animation commits per refresh, kernel calls only for shown frames

Minecraft 26.3 at ~950 fps (IMMEDIATE) spent 8.7% of its render thread in vkQueuePresentKHR, 6.4% of it in
CA::Transaction::commit, plus the IOSurface write-fence ioctls of every present and the acquire's GPU-idle wait.
The window server composites once per display refresh, so frames beyond that are never shown.

- IMMEDIATE still shows a frame at present when the last one went out at least half a refresh ago; a frame
  presented sooner is held, and the refresh thread shows the newest held one (latest-wins, without waiting for its
  rendering: implicit sync). At most two commits per refresh instead of one per frame.
- IMMEDIATE never makes acquire wait for that: an acquire that finds no free image shows the held frame at once, and
  IMMEDIATE swapchains, like MAILBOX ones, get at least four images (the shown one, the one the window server is
  letting go of, the held one, one to render into; more images than minImageCount is allowed). Images the window
  server still holds are polled every 50 us instead of 200 us.
- A frame's write fence is attached to its IOSurface (and the VRAM copy marked newer, the VRAM tag bumped) when it is
  shown, not when it is presented: a frame replaced before it was shown costs no kernel calls.
- Acquire waits for the window server's GPU reads only of an image that was shown since the application last had it.

wsitest 1280x720, IMMEDIATE, 3 images asked: 13914 fps, acquire 0.002 ms, 466 shown/s (wsi2: 4591 fps, acquire
0.100 ms, every frame committed); 2560x1302: 5726 fps (wsi2: 4779). MAILBOX 6313 fps; all VERIFY PASS.

+uint64_t
+wsi_metal_display_refresh_ns(void)
+{
+   uint64_t ns = 1000000000ull / 60;
+   CVDisplayLinkRef link;
+   if (CVDisplayLinkCreateWithActiveCGDisplays(&link) == kCVReturnSuccess) {
+      CVDisplayLinkSetCurrentCGDisplay(link, CGMainDisplayID());
+      const CVTime t = CVDisplayLinkGetNominalOutputVideoRefreshPeriod(link);
+      if (!(t.flags & kCVTimeIsIndefinite) && t.timeValue > 0 && t.timeScale > 0)
+         ns = (uint64_t)((double)t.timeValue * 1e9 / (double)t.timeScale);
+      CVDisplayLinkRelease(link);
+   }
+   return ns;

FILE: mesa/patches/0025-intel-drop-the-internal-shaders-stub-again.patch
================================================
intel: drop -Dintel-internal-shaders=stub again (reverts "intel: add -Dintel-internal-shaders=stub to build anv without
mesa-clc and glslang", 0004)

The stub was for bringing ANV up on macOS without mesa-clc and glslang. With them built for the host (LLVM/clang 23.1.2,
SPIRV-LLVM-Translator 23.1.2: a native mesa_clc and vtn_bindgen2, found with -Dmesa-clc=system), ANV's internal shaders
are built as upstream builds them, and what aborted under the stub works: query copies on the GPU (libanv_query_copy,
heavily used by DXVK), blorp's indirect memory-to-image copies, image size queries on indirect descriptors (resinfo,
robustness2), indirect draw generation, the fp64 library and ASTC emulation. The Vulkan CTS hit 22+25+ SIGABRTs on those
(dEQP-VK.renderpasses.dynamic_rendering...random, api.copy_and_blit, robustness2 sampled images).

FILE: mesa/patches/0026-anv-xemac-unmap-with-RESERVE-without-a-hole.patch
================================================
anv/xemac: VK_MEMORY_UNMAP_RESERVE_BIT_EXT leaves the range reserved without a hole in between

anv_device_unmap_bo(replace = true) took the BO mapping down (xemac_munmap) and then mmap(MAP_FIXED, PROT_NONE) over
the range it had left unmapped. On macOS 15 an mmap(MAP_FIXED) over an unmapped gap kills the process: EXC_GUARD,
GUARD_TYPE_VIRT_MEMORY, DEALLOC_GAP at the placed address (vkplaced, in anv_UnmapMemory2). With replace, xemac now does
both in one step (xemac_munmap_reserve: the placed view is overwritten in place with a PROT_NONE reservation, so the
range is never a hole). Needs the xemac of xemac-placed-map-mach_vm_remap.patch (second version).

 #ifdef HAVE_XEMAC

+   /* BO mappings are the kernel extension's; it takes them down. With
+    * replace, it leaves the range reserved itself: unmapping first and then
+    * mmap(MAP_FIXED) over the hole is killed with EXC_GUARD (DEALLOC_GAP) on
+    * macOS 15.
+    */

+      if (xemac_munmap_reserve(map, map_size) != 0) {

+                          "Failed to map over original mapping");

+   }
    xemac_munmap(map, map_size);
 #endif
    if (replace) {

FILE: mesa/patches/0040-anv-H.264-encode-B-frames-as-media-driver-random-access-rounding-CMD3.patch
================================================
anv: H.264 encode B frames as media-driver programs them (Xe2 VDEnc)

media-driver (AvcBasicFeature, AvcEncodeRounding, EncodeAvcVdencConstSettings) differs from what ANV programmed
for B-frame GOPs in four places, all now as media-driver does:
- VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT IsRandomAccess for B pictures (randomAccess = CodingType == B_TYPE; Xe2);
- VDENC_CMD3 cost row of P pictures by GOP structure: 1 in a B GOP, 2 in an IP GOP (isIPGOP = GopRefDist == 1),
  from VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlInfoKHR::consecutiveBFrameCount (was always 2, the old TODO);
- inter rounding enabled in MFX_AVC_SLICE_STATE and VDENC_AVC_SLICE_STATE with the static BRC values
  (P 3, non-reference B 0, reference B 2; was disabled);
- reference B from StdVideoEncodeH264PictureInfo::flags.is_reference, not from pSetupReferenceSlot (FFmpeg passes a
  setup slot for non-reference B frames too): CMD3 row 3/4, CollocMVWREn and the Xe2 IMG_STATE ref row.
1080p60 VBR 3/6/12 Mbit/s, GOP 120, 2 B frames, Netflix Aerial: BD-rate against x264 medium +34.2% -> +18.9%
(PSNR-Y), +43.7% -> +25.4% (VMAF).

FILE: mesa/patches/0041-anv-AV1-encode-two-reference-P-pictures-are-P-not-GPB.patch
================================================
anv: AV1 encode: two-reference P pictures are P, with their own reference names (Xe2 VDEnc)

FFmpeg's P pictures with two references are UNIDIRECTIONAL_COMPOUND with LAST + GOLDEN. ANV typed every
unidirectional compound picture as GPB and gave the VDEnc the GPB default reference ids (L0 LAST, LAST2; L1 BWDREF,
ALTREF2) while binding the LAST and GOLDEN pictures: the VDEnc searched the GOLDEN picture for blocks it labelled
LAST2, which the frame header (and so the PAK) maps to the LAST picture. media-driver (Av1ReferenceFrames) makes such
a low delay picture a P picture (m_PFrame: only forward group names, VAAPI ref_frame_ctrl_l0 LAST + GOLDEN) whose
reference ids are the names; GPB stays for pictures that also use the backward group (BWDREF, ALTREF2, ALTREF).
1080p60 VBR 3/6/12 Mbit/s, GOP 120, Netflix Aerial: BD-rate against SVT-AV1 preset 8 +304% -> +162% (PSNR-Y),
+220% -> +90% (VMAF); bitrate 3.51/6.73/12.67 -> 3.27/6.33/12.43 Mbit/s.

anv: AV1 encode BRC picks the CDEF parameters (Xe2)

With CDEF enabled in the sequence header (FFmpeg 0001: under rate control, as with VAAPI), media-driver lets the
HuC BRC update kernel choose the CDEF parameters (Av1Brc: UPD_EnableCDEFUpdate when enable_cdef and not intra block
copy) and reads them back from the output AVP_INLOOP_FILTER_STATE (DW5: cdef_bits 29:28). cdef_params() is
4 + 12 << cdef_bits bits (5.9.19), so with the kernel's choice the frame header has one of 4 lengths per loop filter
variant of 0016: pack all (up to 8), capture DW5 next to the loop filter levels, and run the padding / tile group
header / leb128 sub-batch whose loop filter and cdef_bits checks (MI_CONDITIONAL_BATCH_BUFFER_END) both hold.

+/* HEVC_VP9_RDOQ_STATE (Xe2: 154 dwords): the RDOQ lambdas for the picture's slice type and bit depth, two 16-bit
+ * values per dword (media-driver HevcBasicFeature MHW_SETPAR HEVC_VP9_RDOQ_STATE, mhw_vdbox_hcp_impl.h) */
+static void
+anv_h265_emit_rdoq_state(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd, const VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR *enc_info,
+                         const StdVideoH265SequenceParameterSet *sps)
+{
+   const struct VkVideoEncodeH265PictureInfoKHR *frame_info =
+      vk_find_struct_const(enc_info->pNext, VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_PICTURE_INFO_KHR);
+   const unsigned st = frame_info->pStdPictureInfo->pic_type == STD_VIDEO_H265_PICTURE_TYPE_I ||
+                       frame_info->pStdPictureInfo->pic_type == STD_VIDEO_H265_PICTURE_TYPE_IDR ? 0 : 1;
+   const bool ten = sps->bit_depth_luma_minus8 == 2;
+   uint32_t *dw = anv_batch_emit_dwords(&cmd->batch, 154);
+   if (!dw)
+      return;
+   memset(dw, 0, 154 * 4);
+   dw[0] = 0x73880098;   /* HEVC_VP9_RDOQ_STATE, DWord length 152 */
+   for (unsigned blk = 0; blk < 4; blk++) {   /* intra luma, intra chroma, inter luma, inter chroma */

+         if (ten) {

+            b = anv_hevc_rdoq_lambda_10bit[st][blk >> 1][blk & 1][2 * i + 1];

+            b = anv_hevc_rdoq_lambda_8bit[st][blk >> 1][blk & 1][2 * i + 1];
+         }
+         dw[2 + blk * 32 + i] = a | b << 16;
+      }
+   }

FILE: mesa/patches/0045-anv-H.264-HuC-BRC-patches-the-slice-states-in-the-SLBB.patch
================================================
anv: H.264 HuC BRC patches the slice states too (SLBB layout as media-driver, gen125+)

media-driver puts the slice states behind the image-state group in the BRC second level batch (AvcHucBrcUpdatePkt::
ConstructImageStateReadBuffer: image group + BBE, cache line aligned, then per slice MFX_AVC_SLICE_STATE +
VDENC_AVC_SLICE_STATE + BBE; UPD_SLBB_Size = aligned image group, UPD_NumSlicesForRounding = slices) and runs each
slice's group from the kernel's output (AvcVdencPkt::SendSlice), so the HuC applies its QP dependent rounding to the
slices. ANV kept the slice states in the primary batch. The output slice groups are seeded with the driver's own
first, so the PAK always runs complete states.
1080p60 VBR 3/6/12 Mbit/s against x264 medium: Netflix Aerial BD-rate +10.5% -> +9.2% (PSNR-Y), +17.7% -> +16.3%
(VMAF); DrivingPOV +30.6% -> +29.9%, +12.7% -> +12.3%.

--- a/src/intel/vulkan/genX_cmd_video_enc.c
+++ b/src/intel/vulkan/genX_cmd_video_enc.c
@@ -1660,9 +1660,12 @@

 anv_h264_emit_mfx_avc_slice_state(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd,
+                                  struct anv_batch *batch,
                                   const VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR *enc_info,
                                   uint32_t slice_id)
 {
+   if (!batch)

FILE: mesa/patches/0046-anv-AV1-HuC-BRC-GOP-model-with-B-frames-as-media-driver.patch
================================================
anv: AV1 HuC BRC models a GOP with one B frame between the anchors, as media-driver

media-driver (Av1Brc::SetDmemForInit / SetDmemForUpdate) gives the BRC kernel a GOP of GopRefDist > 1 as
INIT_GopP/GopB/GopB1/GopB2, UPD_MaxBRCLevel from GopRefDist and types random access inter frames as B when the
application sends no hierarchy level. ANV described every GOP as all P frames. With Vulkan's flat reference pattern
only GopRefDist 2 has a consistent split (P = B = intra period / 2); 3 gives media-driver a negative GopB2 and 4 or 8
count B1/B2 frames that a flat GOP does not have, so those keep the all-P model.
Goes with 0047 (two PAK passes, which bring the overshoot of this model from 27/19/9% to 18/14/9%) and an encoder
that asks for one B frame. 1080p60 VBR 3/6/12 Mbit/s, 1 B frame, with 0047, BD-rate against SVT-AV1 (PSNR-Y / VMAF):
Netflix Aerial +156.7% / +84.4% (all-P model) -> +135.7% / +68.6%, DrivingPOV +133.9% / +79.8% -> +108.0% / +61.9%.

FILE: mesa/patches/0047-anv-AV1-HuC-BRC-two-PAK-passes-as-media-driver.patch
================================================
anv: AV1 HuC BRC runs two PAK passes, as media-driver

media-driver gives every BRC frame two passes (EncodeAv1VdencFeatureManager::SetPassNum): the second BRC update
(UPD_PAKPassNum 1) sees the first pass's size and asks for a re-encode with HUC_STATUS bit 31, and the second PAK
pass runs only then (AddCondBBEndFor2ndPass). The pass is a second-level batch behind the conditional end, so
only it is skipped; its calls into the kernel's batches and the header variant batches nest one level deeper
(measured on Xe2: a second-level call from a second-level batch returns, and a conditional end there ends only
that level). The loop filter / CDEF variants of the re-encode are captured inside the pass, so the obu_size patch
after the passes matches the bitstream either way.
First test, Netflix Aerial 1080p60 VBR 3 Mbit/s, 600 frames: 1 B frame 3813 -> 3529 kbit/s (key frames 161 -> 122 kB),
2 B frames 3266 -> 3150 kbit/s; all frames decode with dav1d.

FILE: mesa/patches/0050-anv-nvmtl-GPU-reset-recovery-replace-a-banned-exec-queue-on-the-same-VM.patch
================================================
anv/nvmtl: GPU reset recovery - replace a banned exec queue on the same VM

nvmtl_anv_device_recover_v1(VkDevice, flags, info), looked up with dlsym by the nullmoth Metal plugin: each banned exec
queue (and companion RCS queue) of the device is replaced by a fresh one on device->vm_id, the new context gets anv's
initial queue state again (genX(init_queue_state), split out of genX(init_device_state)), the old queues are destroyed
and the queue and device lost flags are cleared. This is what Linux userspace does after an xe context ban (iris replaces
its exec queue); the VM, BOs and GPU addresses survive, so every Vulkan handle the plugin holds stays valid. flags:
FORCE (replace every queue, waiting for it to go idle: tests), QUERY (report only). The caller serializes submissions
and fence waits around it. Base: Mesa "tile4v" = tile4 + 0040-0043 (51b37d76, mesa-wsi build-cpu3); touches no file of 0040-0043.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+/* The initial state of one queue's hardware contexts (its exec queue and, for compute and copy queues, the companion
+ * RCS one). Also used by nvmtl_anv_device_recover_v1 (anv_nvmtl_recover.c) when a banned exec queue is replaced by a
+ * fresh one on the same VM: a new context starts from the kernel's default image and needs this state again.
+ */
+VkResult
+genX(init_queue_state)(struct anv_queue *queue)
+{
+   struct anv_device *device = queue->device;
+   VkResult res;
+
+   switch (queue->family->engine_class) {
+   case INTEL_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER:
+      res = init_render_queue_state(queue, false /* is_companion_rcs_batch */);
+      break;
+   case INTEL_ENGINE_CLASS_COMPUTE: {
+      res = init_compute_queue_state(queue);
+      if (res != VK_SUCCESS)
+         return res;
+
+      /**
+       * Execute RCS init batch by default on the companion RCS command buffer in
+       * order to support MSAA copy/clear operations on compute queue.
+       */
+      res = init_render_queue_state(queue, true /* is_companion_rcs_batch */);
+      break;
+   }
+   case INTEL_ENGINE_CLASS_VIDEO:
+      res = init_copy_video_queue_state(queue);
+      break;
+   case INTEL_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY:
+      res = init_copy_video_queue_state(queue);
+      if (res != VK_SUCCESS)
+         return res;
+
+      /**
+       * Execute RCS init batch by default on the companion RCS command buffer in
+       * order to support MSAA copy/clear operations on copy queue.
+       */
+      res = init_render_queue_state(queue, true /* is_companion_rcs_batch */);
+      break;
+   default:
+      res = vk_error(device, VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED);
+      break;
+   }
+   return res;
 }

+/*
+ * GPU-reset recovery for the nullmoth Metal plugin on B580.kext (macOS, xemac): a fresh exec queue on the same VM.
+ *
+ * On xe a hang is per context: the GuC resets the guilty context (CONTEXT_RESET_NOTIFICATION), the kernel bans that
+ * exec queue and signals every fence it handed out; a GT reset bans the queues whose work had started and replays the
+ * rest. The VM, its BOs and every GPU address stay valid, and Linux userspace goes on with a new exec queue on the same
+ * VM (iris_xe_replace_batch). anv instead reports VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, which is final for a VkDevice. That is right
+ * for a Vulkan application, but the Metal plugin cannot make a new VkDevice behind an MTLDevice: a new device is a new
+ * VM (no dma-buf on macOS), and Metal applications hold GPU addresses (gpuAddress, argument buffers) and CPU pointers
+ * (contents) into the old one. WindowServer must keep its MTLDevice through a GPU restart the way it does on Apple's
+ * drivers (in-flight command buffers end with an error, new work runs).
+ *
+ * nvmtl_anv_device_recover_v1 does what Linux userspace does after a ban: each banned exec queue (and its companion RCS
+ * queue) is replaced by a new one on device->vm_id, the new context gets anv's initial queue state again
+ * (genX(init_queue_state)), the old queue is destroyed, and the queue and device lost flags are cleared. Nothing else of
+ * the device changes: every VkBuffer, VkImage, VkDeviceMemory, pipeline, descriptor set and command pool stays valid.
+ * What the cancelled work was writing is undefined, as after a GPU restart on Apple's drivers.
+ *
+ * The caller must make sure no other thread submits to, or waits on, this device's queues while it runs (the plugin
+ * holds its submit lock and drains its fence waiters). It is looked up with dlsym; a plugin that does not find it keeps
+ * the old behaviour (a lost device stays lost).
+ */
+#include "anv_private.h"
+
+#include "common/xe/intel_queue.h"
+#include "drm-uapi/xe_drm.h"
+
+#include "xe/anv_queue.h"
+
+#define NVMTL_ANV_RECOVER_FORCE (1u << 0)      /* replace every queue, banned or not (tests); waits for each to idle */
+#define NVMTL_ANV_RECOVER_QUERY (1u << 1)      /* only report bans and the lost state, change nothing */
+
+struct nvmtl_anv_recover_info {
+   uint32_t size;              /* in: sizeof(struct nvmtl_anv_recover_info) */
+   uint32_t was_lost;          /* out: the device was marked lost */
+   uint32_t queues_banned;     /* out: exec queues (main or companion) the kernel reports banned */
+   uint32_t queues_replaced;   /* out: anv queues that got new exec queues */
+   int32_t  error;             /* out: errno of the step that failed, 0 */
+   uint32_t failed_step;       /* out: 0 none, 1 ban query, 2 create, 3 init state, 4 not xe */
+};
+
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_device_recover_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t flags, struct nvmtl_anv_recover_info *info);
+
+/* 1 banned, 0 not, -errno: the query failed (an id the kernel does not know: treated as gone) */
+static int
+nvmtl_exec_queue_banned(struct anv_device *device, uint32_t exec_queue_id)
+{
+   if (!exec_queue_id)
+      return 0;
+   struct drm_xe_exec_queue_get_property p = {
+      .exec_queue_id = exec_queue_id,
+      .property = DRM_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_GET_PROPERTY_BAN,
+   };
+   if (intel_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_GET_PROPERTY, &p))
+      return -errno;
+   return p.value ? 1 : 0;
+}
+
+static void
+nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(struct anv_device *device, uint32_t exec_queue_id, bool wait_idle)
+{
+   if (!exec_queue_id)
+      return;
+   /* A queue that was not banned (NVMTL_ANV_RECOVER_FORCE) may still run work the caller waits for: destroying it
+    * would kill that work. A banned one has nothing left (the kernel dropped and signalled its jobs). */
+   if (wait_idle)
+      anv_xe_wait_exec_queue_idle(device, exec_queue_id);
+   struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d = { .exec_queue_id = exec_queue_id };
+   intel_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d);
+}
+
+/* The initial-state batch of the old context: done (its fence completes with the ban) or abandoned after 2 s. */
+static void
+nvmtl_drop_init_submit(struct anv_device *device, struct anv_async_submit **submit)
+{
+   if (!*submit)
+      return;
+   VkResult r = vk_sync_wait(&device->vk, (*submit)->signal.sync, (*submit)->signal.signal_value,
+                             VK_SYNC_WAIT_COMPLETE, os_time_get_absolute_timeout(2000000000ull));
+   if (r == VK_SUCCESS)
+      anv_async_submit_destroy(*submit);   /* else leaked: its BOs may still be in use */
+   *submit = NULL;
+}
+
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_device_recover_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t flags, struct nvmtl_anv_recover_info *info)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct nvmtl_anv_recover_info local = { .size = sizeof(local) };
+   if (!info || info->size < sizeof(*info))
+      info = &local;
+   const uint32_t size = info->size;
+   memset(info, 0, sizeof(*info));
+   info->size = size;
+
+   if (device->info->kmd_type != INTEL_KMD_TYPE_XE) {
+      info->failed_step = 4;
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   }
+
+   info->was_lost = vk_device_is_lost_no_report(&device->vk) ? 1 : 0;
+
+   /* Which queues are banned. A failed query (EINVAL: the kernel no longer knows the id) counts as banned: the queue is
+    * unusable either way. */
+   bool replace[ANV_MAX_QUEUE_FAMILIES * 8] = { false };
+   const uint32_t nq = MIN2(device->queue_count, ARRAY_SIZE(replace));
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq; i++) {
+      struct anv_queue *queue = &device->queues[i];
+      const int b0 = nvmtl_exec_queue_banned(device, queue->exec_queue_id);
+      const int b1 = nvmtl_exec_queue_banned(device, queue->companion_rcs_id);
+      if (b0 != 0) info->queues_banned++;
+      if (b1 != 0) info->queues_banned++;
+      if (b0 < 0 || b1 < 0) info->error = -(b0 < 0 ? b0 : b1);
+      replace[i] = b0 != 0 || b1 != 0 || (flags & NVMTL_ANV_RECOVER_FORCE) ||
+                   /* lost without a ban (an exec ioctl failed): a fresh context, as iris does for any reset */
+                   (info->was_lost && vk_queue_is_lost(&queue->vk));
+   }
+   /* lost, but no queue says why (a device-level loss such as a query timeout): every queue gets a fresh context */
+   if (info->was_lost && !info->queues_banned) {
+      bool any = false;
+      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq; i++) any |= replace[i];
+      if (!any)
+         for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq; i++) replace[i] = true;
+   }
+   if (flags & NVMTL_ANV_RECOVER_QUERY)
+      return VK_SUCCESS;
+
+   bool nothing = true;
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq; i++) nothing &= !replace[i];
+   if (nothing)
+      return info->was_lost ? VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST : VK_SUCCESS;
+
+   VkResult result = VK_SUCCESS;
+   simple_mtx_lock(&device->mutex);   /* anv_queue_submit's lock: no submission sees half a swap */
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq && result == VK_SUCCESS; i++) {
+      if (!replace[i])
+         continue;
+      struct anv_queue *queue = &device->queues[i];
+      const bool idle = (flags & NVMTL_ANV_RECOVER_FORCE) && !info->was_lost &&
+                        !nvmtl_exec_queue_banned(device, queue->exec_queue_id);
+
+      /* the new exec queues first, into a copy: anv_xe_create_engine only reads the family and writes the ids */
+      const VkDeviceQueueCreateInfo qci = {
+         .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INFO,
+         .flags = queue->vk.flags,
+         .queueFamilyIndex = queue->vk.queue_family_index,
+         .queueCount = 1,   /* no VkDeviceQueueGlobalPriorityCreateInfo: MEDIUM, what the plugin creates its queue with */
+      };
+      struct anv_queue fresh = *queue;
+      fresh.exec_queue_id = 0;
+      fresh.companion_rcs_id = 0;
+      fresh.bind_queue_id = 0;
+      result = anv_xe_create_engine(device, &fresh, &qci);
+      if (result != VK_SUCCESS) {
+         info->failed_step = 2;
+         info->error = errno;
+         nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(device, fresh.exec_queue_id, false);
+         nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(device, fresh.companion_rcs_id, false);
+         nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(device, fresh.bind_queue_id, false);
+         break;
+      }
+
+      const uint32_t old_exec = queue->exec_queue_id, old_comp = queue->companion_rcs_id,
+                     old_bind = queue->bind_queue_id;
+      nvmtl_drop_init_submit(device, &queue->init_submit);
+      nvmtl_drop_init_submit(device, &queue->init_companion_submit);
+      if (idle) {   /* FORCE on a live queue: the old one finishes its work before the new one takes over */
+         anv_xe_wait_exec_queue_idle(device, old_exec);
+         if (old_comp)
+            anv_xe_wait_exec_queue_idle(device, old_comp);
+      }
+      p_atomic_set(&queue->exec_queue_id, fresh.exec_queue_id);
+      p_atomic_set(&queue->companion_rcs_id, fresh.companion_rcs_id);
+      p_atomic_set(&queue->bind_queue_id, fresh.bind_queue_id);
+      queue->vk._lost.lost = 0;
+
+      /* the new context starts from the kernel's default image: anv's initial state again, as at vkCreateDevice */
+      result = anv_genX(device->info, init_queue_state)(queue);
+      if (result != VK_SUCCESS) {
+         info->failed_step = 3;
+         info->error = errno;
+      }
+
+      nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(device, old_exec, false);
+      nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(device, old_comp, false);
+      nvmtl_exec_queue_destroy(device, old_bind, false);
+      if (result == VK_SUCCESS)
+         info->queues_replaced++;
+   }
+   if (result == VK_SUCCESS) {
+      /* every queue that needed it has a fresh context: the device is usable again */
+      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq; i++)
+         device->queues[i].vk._lost.lost = 0;
+      p_atomic_set(&device->vk._lost.lost, 0);
+      device->vk._lost.reported = false;
+   } else {
+      vk_device_set_lost(&device->vk, "nvmtl: exec queue replacement failed (step %u, errno %d)",
+                         info->failed_step, info->error);
+   }
+   simple_mtx_unlock(&device->mutex);
+   return result;
+}

FILE: mesa/patches/0051-blorp-compute-clear-bounds-after-RGB-widening-and-tile-offsets.patch
================================================
blorp: a compute clear's bounds rectangle is the one the walker covers (after the RGB-as-red widening and tile offsets)

blorp_clear() wrote params.wm_inputs.clear.bounds_rect from the caller's rectangle before the slice's tile offsets were
added to params.x0..y1 and before a 24/48/96-bpb format's x range was multiplied by 3 (clear_rgb_as_red). The walker
(blorp_exec_compute) covers params.x0..x1 x y0..y1 and the BLORP-gpgpu-clear kernel discards invocations outside
bounds_rect, so on a compute queue an RGB clear wrote only the first third of each row (and a slice with a tile offset
lost its last tile_x/tile_y columns/rows). The rectangle is now set after both adjustments (and per piece of a clear wider than 16K). Render-engine clears do not
use bounds_rect and are unchanged.
