FILE: mesa/patches/0075-anv-HEVC-and-AV1-HuC-BRC-model-a-dyadic-B-pyramid-per-level.patch
================================================
anv: HEVC and AV1 HuC BRC model a dyadic B pyramid per level, as media-driver

media-driver's VDEnc BRC models a B pyramid (HierarchicalFlag) per level: BRC init splits the GOP into P, B, B1, B2
frames and turns BRCPyramidEnable on (HEVC: media_softlet/agnostic/common/codec/hal/enc/hevc/packet/
encode_huc_brc_init_packet.cpp, GopRefDist != 3; AV1: features/encode_av1_brc.cpp SetDmemForInit), and each picture is
typed by its level (HierarchLevelPlus1 1/2/3/4 -> P_OR_LB/B/B1/B2: encode_huc_brc_update_packet.cpp, encode_av1_brc.cpp
SetDmemForUpdate, UPD_MaxBRCLevel 3/2/1 for GopRefDist 8/4/2). anv modelled every B frame alike (HEVC: GopB1/GopB2 0,
BRCPyramidEnable 0; AV1: only one B frame between the anchors).
Vulkan has no per-picture level; the app signals the dyadic pattern (VK_VIDEO_ENCODE_{H265,AV1}_RATE_CONTROL_REFERENCE_
PATTERN_DYADIC_BIT_KHR) and anv derives HierarchLevelPlus1 from the order distance between a picture's nearest past and
future references (GopRefDist at level 2, halved per level below), which is what a dyadic split gives (FFmpeg's
hw_base_encode_set_b_pictures). Flat GOPs are unchanged (byte-identical output).
B580, 1080p60 VBR 3/6/12 Mbit/s, HEVC with 7 B frames in 3 levels (Intel's default GopRefDist 8 pyramid at TU4):
BD-rate against the same pyramid without the per-level model -7.0% PSNR-Y / -5.1% VMAF on Netflix Aerial; against Intel
QSV defaults (hevc_qsv, GopRefDist 8 pyramid) +0.3% / -0.4%. AV1: the same model, active only with a dyadic pattern,
which FFmpeg's Vulkan AV1 encoder cannot produce yet (one hidden frame per temporal unit, vulkan_encode.c prev_buf_ref).

+/* media-driver's HierarchLevelPlus1 of the picture in a dyadic B pyramid (1 = P / low-delay B, 2 = the B between
+ * the anchors, 3 and 4 the levels below), which VA-API gets from the app and Vulkan does not carry: the level of a B
+ * picture follows from the distance between its nearest past and future references, gop_ref_dist at level 2 and
+ * halved at each level below. 0 when it cannot be told (no references). */
+static uint32_t
+anv_h265_hier_level_plus1(const VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR *enc_info,
+                          StdVideoEncodeH265ReferenceListsInfo *ref_lists,
+                          uint32_t gop_ref_dist)
+{
+   const struct VkVideoEncodeH265PictureInfoKHR *frame_info = anv_h265_frame_info(enc_info);
+   const int32_t poc = frame_info->pStdPictureInfo->PicOrderCntVal;
+   int32_t past = INT32_MIN, future = INT32_MAX;
+
+   if (!ref_lists)
+      return 0;
+
+   for (unsigned list = 0; list < 2; list++) {
+      const uint8_t *ref_pic_list = list == 0 ? ref_lists->RefPicList0 : ref_lists->RefPicList1;
+      unsigned ref_cnt = (list == 0 ? ref_lists->num_ref_idx_l0_active_minus1 :
+                                      ref_lists->num_ref_idx_l1_active_minus1) + 1;
+
+      for (unsigned i = 0; i < ref_cnt; i++) {
+         if (ref_pic_list[i] == STD_VIDEO_H265_NO_REFERENCE_PICTURE)
+            continue;
+         const VkVideoReferenceSlotInfoKHR *slot = anv_h265_find_ref_slot(enc_info, ref_pic_list[i]);
+         const VkVideoEncodeH265DpbSlotInfoKHR *dpb =
+            slot ? vk_find_struct_const(slot->pNext, VIDEO_ENCODE_H265_DPB_SLOT_INFO_KHR) : NULL;
+         if (!dpb)
+            continue;
+         const int32_t rpoc = dpb->pStdReferenceInfo->PicOrderCntVal;
+         if (rpoc < poc && rpoc > past)
+            past = rpoc;
+         if (rpoc > poc && rpoc < future)
+            future = rpoc;
+      }
+   }
+
+   if (past == INT32_MIN)
+      return 0;
+   if (future == INT32_MAX)
+      return 1;   /* only past references: P or low-delay B */
+
+   const uint32_t span = (uint32_t)(future - past);
+   uint32_t level = 2;
+   for (uint32_t d = gop_ref_dist; d > span && d > 1 && level < 4; d /= 2)
+      level++;
+   return level;
+}

FILE: mesa/patches/0076-vulkan-video-H.264-encode-slice-headers-carry-ref-list-modifications-and-MMCOs.patch
================================================
vulkan/video: H.264 encode slice headers carry the reference list modifications and MMCOs

vk_video_encode_h264_slice_header() wrote ref_pic_list_modification_flag_l0/l1 from the application but no
modification operations after it (assert(0) TODO, and no terminating modification_of_pic_nums_idc 3), and always wrote
adaptive_ref_pic_marking_mode_flag 0. With B frames used as references (B pyramid) FFmpeg reorders the lists and
unmarks the pictures that left its DPB with MMCO 1, so every such slice header was corrupt: libavcodec reports
"illegal reordering_of_pic_nums_idc" / "reference count overflow", and the decoder's sliding window keeps other
references than the encoder (PSNR ~18 dB, drift). Write ref_pic_list_modification() and dec_ref_pic_marking() per
H.264 7.3.3.1 / 7.3.3.3 (as radv_video_enc.c does), closing each list with its end code whether or not the
application passed it, and the IDR flags from the picture info.
B580 (anv), FFmpeg h264_vulkan with Intel's AVC default GOP (GopRefDist 4, B pyramid): streams decode without errors
and bit-exact on libavcodec and the B580 VideoToolbox decoder; mediakit BD-rate vs the flat 2-B GOP -1.5..-4.1% PSNR-Y.

+/* ref_pic_list_modification() for one list (H.264 7.3.3.1). The operations come from the application;
+ * the list is closed with modification_of_pic_nums_idc == 3 whether or not the application passed the
+ * end entry itself.
+ */
+static void
+h264_encode_ref_list_mods(struct vl_bitstream_encoder *enc,
+                          const StdVideoEncodeH264RefListModEntry *ops,
+                          unsigned count)
+{
+   for (unsigned i = 0; ops && i < count; i++) {
+      const StdVideoEncodeH264RefListModEntry *op = &ops[i];
+      if (op->modification_of_pic_nums_idc == STD_VIDEO_H264_MODIFICATION_OF_PIC_NUMS_IDC_END)
+         break;
+      vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->modification_of_pic_nums_idc);
+      if (op->modification_of_pic_nums_idc == STD_VIDEO_H264_MODIFICATION_OF_PIC_NUMS_IDC_SHORT_TERM_SUBTRACT ||
+          op->modification_of_pic_nums_idc == STD_VIDEO_H264_MODIFICATION_OF_PIC_NUMS_IDC_SHORT_TERM_ADD)
+         vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->abs_diff_pic_num_minus1);
+      else if (op->modification_of_pic_nums_idc == STD_VIDEO_H264_MODIFICATION_OF_PIC_NUMS_IDC_LONG_TERM)
+         vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->long_term_pic_num);
+   }
+   vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, STD_VIDEO_H264_MODIFICATION_OF_PIC_NUMS_IDC_END);
+}
+
+/* dec_ref_pic_marking() memory management control operations (H.264 7.3.3.3), closed with
+ * memory_management_control_operation == 0 whether or not the application passed the end entry.
+ */
+static void
+h264_encode_mmcos(struct vl_bitstream_encoder *enc,
+                  const StdVideoEncodeH264RefPicMarkingEntry *ops,
+                  unsigned count)
+{
+   for (unsigned i = 0; ops && i < count; i++) {
+      const StdVideoEncodeH264RefPicMarkingEntry *op = &ops[i];
+      const StdVideoH264MemMgmtControlOp mmco = op->memory_management_control_operation;
+      if (mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_END)
+         break;
+      vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, mmco);
+      if (mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_UNMARK_SHORT_TERM ||
+          mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_MARK_LONG_TERM)
+         vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->difference_of_pic_nums_minus1);
+      if (mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_UNMARK_LONG_TERM)
+         vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->long_term_pic_num);
+      if (mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_MARK_LONG_TERM ||
+          mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_MARK_CURRENT_AS_LONG_TERM)
+         vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->long_term_frame_idx);
+      if (mmco == STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_SET_MAX_LONG_TERM_INDEX)
+         vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, op->max_long_term_frame_idx_plus1);
+   }
+   vl_bitstream_exp_golomb_ue(enc, STD_VIDEO_H264_MEM_MGMT_CONTROL_OP_END);
+}

FILE: mesa/patches/0077-anv-HEVC-encode-turns-P-slices-into-generalized-P-B-before-the-BRC-batch-writes-the-slice-header.patch
================================================
anv: HEVC encode turns P slices into generalized P/B before the BRC batch writes the slice header

VDEnc codes HEVC P pictures as low delay B with L1 = L0. anv made that conversion (slice type B, L1 copied from L0,
num_ref_idx_active_override_flag when the counts differ from the PPS) piecemeal: L1 in the VDENC_CMD2 emission and the
override in the per-slice loop, both after the HuC BRC second level batch had already written the slice headers
(anv_h265_brc_compute_slb_layout / the SLB build). With one L0 reference nothing differs from the PPS defaults, but
with two (Intel's P frames at TU4 use two, hevcehw caps) the header said one active reference while VDEnc coded
ref_idx for two: CABAC desync, "cu_qp_delta outside the valid range" from libavcodec. Normalize the reference lists and
slice headers once at the start of anv_h265_encode_video, before anything is derived from them.
B580, FFmpeg hevc_vulkan with 2 P references: streams decode without errors and bit-exact on libavcodec and the B580
VideoToolbox decoder (were PSNR 8-13 dB).

+
+   /* VDEnc encodes P pictures as generalized P/B (low delay B with L1 = L0). Turn the
+    * application's P slices into that form before anything is derived from them: the HuC BRC
+    * second level batch writes the slice headers before the per-slice loop below runs, and with
+    * more than one L0 reference the header has to carry num_ref_idx_active_override_flag and

+      ref_lists->num_ref_idx_l1_active_minus1 = ref_lists->num_ref_idx_l0_active_minus1;
+      for (int i = 0; i < STD_VIDEO_H265_MAX_NUM_LIST_REF; i++) {
+         ref_lists->RefPicList1[i] = ref_lists->RefPicList0[i];
+         ref_lists->list_entry_l1[i] = ref_lists->list_entry_l0[i];

+          (pps->num_ref_idx_l0_default_active_minus1 != ref_lists->num_ref_idx_l0_active_minus1 ||

+         slice_header->flags.num_ref_idx_active_override_flag = true;

FILE: mesa/patches/0078-anv-macOS-resolve-the-optional-entrypoints-to-NULL-at-link-time-instead-of-dynamic-lookup.patch
================================================
anv (macOS): resolve the optional entrypoints to NULL at link time instead of by dynamic lookup

vk_entrypoints_gen.py --weak declares every entrypoint a driver may implement as weak, so the entrypoint tables hold
NULL for the ones it does not: ELF resolves weak undefined symbols to 0, MSVC points them at vk_entrypoint_stub with
/alternatename (and vk_dispatch_table_gen.py skips the stub). ld64 has no weak undefined symbols outside of dylib
imports and accepts them only with -undefined dynamic_lookup (as kosmickrisp and lavapipe link on darwin). Each of
them then becomes a flat-namespace lookup that dyld resolves by searching every loaded image when the driver is
loaded: 10986 for anv (anv/gfx*/vk_common/wsi/... tables), ~390 ms per dlopen of libvulkan_intel.dylib, paid by every
process that creates a Metal device or a VideoToolbox session on the B580.

Link the driver twice on darwin: once as before (libvulkan_intel_unresolved, not installed), then
vk_entrypoints_null_macho.py lists the symbols that link left to dynamic lookup and writes an assembly file defining
each weak one as an absolute 0 with private extern visibility, and the real driver is linked with that file and
without -undefined dynamic_lookup. Every table entry for an entrypoint the driver lacks is NULL at link time, as on
ELF; nothing is looked up at load time any more. A non-weak symbol left to dynamic lookup is a real missing
dependency and fails the build: there was one, NSNumber from wsi_common_metal_layer.m, so the macOS WSI dependency
now lists Foundation (it was only found because some other image had loaded Foundation).

B580 hackintosh (x86_64 macOS): dlopen of libvulkan_intel.dylib 390 ms -> 3.4 ms (cold after purge
673 -> 217 ms; with AppKit/Metal/VideoToolbox/AVFoundation already loaded 406 -> 1.1 ms); MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice
411 -> 22 ms; a vtdecq process 0.72 -> 0.33 s. vkGetInstanceProcAddr/vkGetDeviceProcAddr resolve the same 865
commands identically (all 15 instance and 210 device extensions enabled); Metal compute/render, VideoToolbox decode
(per-frame md5) and H.264/HEVC/AV1 encode (byte-identical streams) unchanged.

new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..d75073decc1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/vulkan/util/vk_entrypoints_null_macho.py
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+"""Resolve the optional (weak) entrypoints of a Mach-O Vulkan driver to NULL at link time.
+
+vk_entrypoints_gen.py --weak declares every entrypoint a driver may implement as a weak symbol, so that the
+entrypoint tables hold NULL for the ones it does not (ELF weak undefined symbols resolve to 0; MSVC points them at
+vk_entrypoint_stub through /alternatename instead). ld64 has no weak undefined symbols outside of dylib imports: it only accepts them with
+-undefined dynamic_lookup, which turns each one into a flat-namespace lookup that dyld searches every loaded image
+for when the driver is loaded (about 11000 for anv, ~0.3 s per dlopen).
+
+This script takes a link of the driver made with -undefined dynamic_lookup, lists the symbols left to dynamic lookup,
+and writes an assembly file that defines each weak one as an absolute 0 with hidden (private extern) visibility.
+Linking the driver again with that file resolves every reference at link time to NULL, exactly what ELF does, with
+no lookups left and no -undefined dynamic_lookup. A non-weak symbol left to dynamic lookup is a real missing
+dependency and fails the build.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument('--nm', required=True, help='nm program')
+    parser.add_argument('--lib', required=True, help='driver linked with -undefined dynamic_lookup')
+    parser.add_argument('--out', required=True, help='assembly file to write')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    out = subprocess.run([args.nm, '-m', '-u', args.lib], check=True,
+                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+
+    weak, missing = [], []
+    for line in out.splitlines():
+        if '(dynamically looked up)' not in line:
+            continue
+        fields = line.split()
+        sym = fields[fields.index('(dynamically') - 1]
+        (weak if 'weak' in fields else missing).append(sym)
+
+    if missing:
+        sys.exit('undefined symbols that are not optional entrypoints:\n  ' + '\n  '.join(missing))
+
+    with open(args.out, 'w') as f:
+        f.write('/* Generated by vk_entrypoints_null_macho.py from %s, do not edit. */\n' % args.lib.split('/')[-1])
+        f.write('/* Optional entrypoints this driver does not implement: NULL, resolved at link time. */\n')
+        for sym in sorted(set(weak)):
+            f.write('\t.globl %s\n\t.private_extern %s\n%s = 0\n' % (sym, sym, sym))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

FILE: mesa/patches/0079-anv-VP9-decode-alternates-two-motion-vector-buffers-instead-of-copying.patch
================================================
anv: VP9 decode alternates two motion vector buffers instead of copying one into the other

The MVs a VP9 inter frame may read (use_prev_frame_mvs) are those of the frame decoded last, or none after a key or
intra-only frame. anv wrote each frame's MVs to ANV_VID_MEM_VP9_MV_CUR and then copied them, with a HuC stream copy,
into ANV_VID_MEM_VP9_MV_PREV (ANV_VID_MEM_VP9_MV_ZERO after key/intra-only frames): 1.2 MB per 4K frame, 5 MB per 8K
frame, which was most of a frame's decode time on the B580 (4K 8-bit 30 Mbit/s: 248 fps decode-only, 582 fps with the
copy left out). media-driver alternates between two MV temporal buffers instead (media_softlet decode_vp9_basic_feature:
m_curMvTempBufIdx / m_colMvTempBufIdx, "CurrentMVTemporalBuffer" / "CollocatedMVTemporalBuffer[0]" of
HCP_PIPE_BUF_ADDR_STATE). anv does the same with MV_CUR and MV_PREV, keeping the addresses in the VP9 execution state
so that the alternation follows execution order, like LastFrameType (ea055452687): an inter frame's
HCP_PIPE_BUF_ADDR_STATE goes into a second-level batch whose MV addresses (DW31-32, DW66-67 on gfx12 to xe3p) are
copied in from the execution state when it runs, and after the frame the state advances on the GPU (PREV = CUR,
CUR <-> OTHER; PREV = ZERO after a key or intra-only frame) with a few MI_COPY_MEM_MEMs.
B580: libvpx VP9 decodes bit-exact (per-frame md5 against libavcodec) as before, 8/10-bit 1080p/4K/8K, the libvpx
conformance vectors for intra-only frames, tiles, loop filter deltas, odd sizes and inter-frame reference scaling
(resize_inter 1:2 and 3:4); decode-only 4K 8-bit 248 -> ~550 fps (see the report for every clip).

FILE: mesa/patches/0082-anv-nvmtl-one-handle-per-IOSurface-backing-shares-one-anv_bo-as-PRIME-imports-do.patch

From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Subject: [PATCH 0082] anv/nvmtl: one handle per IOSurface backing: imports share one anv_bo, as PRIME imports do

Linux gives a file one GEM handle per object: drm_gem_prime_fd_to_handle returns the existing handle for a dma-buf the
file imported before, and anv_device_import_bo then finds the anv_bo in its cache and takes a reference, so every import
of a buffer shares one anv_bo, one VA and one binding, and the last release unbinds it (xe_vm_unbind_bo: UNMAP_ALL of the
handle). B580.kext's SURFACE_VRAM gave each import of a shared IOSurface backing a new handle, and
anv_device_import_bo_handle refused a handle it already knew, so the window server's second import of an app's window
backing was a second anv_bo; releasing the first unbound the second's VA (the black flicker of 2026-10-31, fixed in the
kernel by rb7l's per-handle UNMAP_ALL).

With B580.kext rb7m the import asks for the client's existing handle (B580_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE) and
anv_device_import_bo_handle_locked refcounts the anv_bo the cache already holds, with anv_device_import_bo's checks. The
ioctl and the cache lookup run under the BO cache mutex, as anv_device_import_bo does fd-to-handle, so a release of the
same handle cannot come between them. A handle the import does not keep is closed only when no anv_bo owns it. An older
kernel answers EINVAL to the flag: the import retries without it and behaves as before.

Applies to src/intel/vulkan of a3ad934832b and of the newest stack on it (0074-0081).

+/* One handle per backing per device, as PRIME gives Linux (drm_gem_prime_fd_to_handle): with it, the BO cache shares one
+ * anv_bo, one VA and one binding between the imports of a backing (anv_device_import_bo's refcount), and releasing one
+ * import cannot unbind another's VA. Without it (a kernel before rb7m), each import is a handle and an anv_bo of its own,
+ * as before. Called with the BO cache mutex held, like anv_device_import_bo's anv_gem_fd_to_handle, so a release of the
+ * same handle cannot come between the ioctl and the cache lookup. */
+static bool nvmtl_same_handle_refused;
+static int
+nvmtl_surface_vram_ioctl(struct anv_device *device, unsigned long request, void *arg, uint32_t *flags)
+{
+   if (!nvmtl_same_handle_refused)
+      *flags |= B580_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE;
+   int r = nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, request, arg);
+   if (r && errno == EINVAL && (*flags & B580_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE)) {
+      *flags &= ~B580_SURFACE_VRAM_SAME_HANDLE;
+      r = nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, request, arg);
+      if (r == 0)
+         nvmtl_same_handle_refused = true;   /* the flag was what it refused: a kernel before rb7m */
+   }
+   return r;
+}
+/* A handle we got but will not use: closed unless an anv_bo already owns it (SAME_HANDLE gave back a live import's). The
+ * BO cache mutex is held. */
+static void
+nvmtl_handle_drop(struct anv_device *device, uint32_t handle)
+{
+   struct anv_bo *owner = anv_device_lookup_bo(device, handle);
+   if (owner && owner->refcount > 0)
+      return;
+   struct anv_bo tmp = { .gem_handle = handle };
+   device->kmd_backend->gem_close(device, &tmp);
+}

FILE: mesa/patches/0083-anv-nvmtl-a-creator-may-ask-for-a-Tile4-IOSurface-backing-when-the-window-server-reads-layouts.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ <78423442+yusufklncc@users.noreply.github.com>
Subject: [PATCH 0083] anv/nvmtl: a creator may ask for a Tile4 IOSurface backing when the window server reads layouts

On Linux a client picks a tiled modifier from the compositor's dmabuf feedback (iris ranks LINEAR lowest and 4_TILED /
4_TILED_BMG_CCS highest, iris_resource.c modifier_priority), so the compositor samples the client's buffer tiled. The
Metal plugin's IOSurface backings were always linear (the creator recorded DRM_FORMAT_MOD_LINEAR), and the window server
sampled them linear. A staged request may now carry NVMTL_ANV_SURFACE_VRAM_WANT_TILE4 with width, height, cpp (4) and the
IOSurface's bytesPerRow: when B580_CAP_SURFACE_VRAM_LAYOUT is 1 (the window server imports with SURFACE_VRAM2) the backing
is created I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED with the row rounded up to 128 B (uncompressed, as every backing), sized for whole tiles;
the kernel's CPU-lock page-off detiles it. Refused as Tile4 (a backing that exists with another layout, a size the
kernel will not take): linear, as before. Without the flag nothing changes. For the plugin's /tmp/nvmtl-svtile4 prototype.
Applies on top of 0082.

+ * with another layout: EBUSY) or without the capability. A Mesa before 0083 ignores the flag: linear. */

FILE: mesa/patches/0084-anv-Xe2-H.264-encode-quality-levels-are-VDEnc-target-usage-7-4-1-as-media-driver.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0084] anv: Xe2 H.264 encode quality levels are VDEnc target usage 7/4/1, as media-driver

On top of the installed Mesa 935ef655 (src/mesa-onehandle working tree). Built and tested from a copy
(src/mesa-videotu, build-vt): libvulkan_intel.dylib sha256 8dc4146d..., NOT installed.

H.264 encode had one quality level, target usage 4, so every preset encoded the same (macOS kit 2 Nov:
veryfast/medium/veryslow 556.5/556.3/556.5 fps, byte-identical streams). HEVC (7/4/1) and AV1 (7/4/2)
already map their levels. Now H.264 on Xe2 does too, with what media-driver's Xe2_HPM AVC VDEnc encoder
changes per target usage (EncodeAvcVdencFeatureManagerXe2_Hpm::MapTargetUsage keeps 1, 2, 4, 7):

- maxQualityLevels 3 for H.264 on Xe2 (ANV_H264_ENCODE_QUALITY_LEVELS); level 0/1/2 = TU 7/4/1.
- VDENC_AVC_IMG_STATE: the Xe2_HPM tables (encode_avc_vdenc_const_settings_xe2_hpm_open.h dw2/dw4/dw5/dw12/
  dw13/dw14/dw25, already in h264_vdenc_tables.h for all 8 TUs) indexed by the session's TU instead of 4.
- Trellis quantization (AvcEncodeTrellis, DDI default trellisInternal): on for TU 1 and 2 with CABAC
  (m_trellisQuantizationEnable { 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 }, rounding 3): VDENC_AVC_IMG_STATE TrellisQuantEn,
  MFX_AVC_IMG_STATE TrellisQuantizationEnable / Rounding (chroma TQ stays disabled).
- VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT (AvcBasicFeature MHW_SETPAR): reference prefetch verticalShift32Minus1 0,
  hzShift32Minus1 15, numVerticalReqMinus1 5, numHzReqMinus1 0, top prefetch mode 0 (the other DW2 fields at
  the MHW_PAR defaults), DW5 bit 17 (VdencPipeModeSelectPar0) = 1, DW5 bit 8 (VdencPipeModeSelectPar1) =
  { 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 }[TU - 1].
- Not taken over: perf mode (perfModeEnabled for TU 6/7) - m_perfModeSupported is never set in media-driver;
  INIT_SinglePassOnly for TU 7 - ANV's BRC is single pass at every TU already.

Measured on the B580 (vtencq, 1080p60 Aerial 600 frames, 6 Mbit/s VBR, page cache warm), level 0/1/2:
755.2 / 556.7 / 191.2 fps; 6213 / 6186 / 6306 kbit/s; PSNR-Y 34.78 / 34.80 / 35.02 dB. Level 1 (TU 4, the
default) is byte-identical to the installed driver (7732670 bytes both). Windows QSV (1 Nov, adapter not pinned)
veryfast/medium/veryslow: 562.9 / 541.0 / 195.0 fps.

FILE: mesa/patches/0087-anv-Xe2-HEVC-encode-VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT-reference-prefetch-and-DW5-as-media-driver.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0087] anv: Xe2 HEVC encode VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT reference prefetch and DW5 as media-driver

On top of 0084 (installed Mesa 935ef655 = src/mesa-onehandle + 0084 = src/mesa-videotu). Built from a file copy
(src/mesa-hevctu, build-hevctu; same meson options as build-vt, release, x86_64). NOT installed.

Xe2 only (Gen12/12.5 unchanged). ANV's HEVC encoder programmed VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT DW2/DW3 with the genxml
defaults (top prefetch mode 1, numVerticalReqMinus1 11, source TLB prefetch on with offset 4: what media-driver
programs for Xe3, encode_hevc_basic_feature_xe3_lpm_base.cpp) and left DW5 bit 17 clear. media-driver's
Xe2_HPM HEVC VDEnc path:
- DW2: no HEVC override (HevcBasicFeature / HevcVdencPkt MHW_SETPAR(VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT)), so the
  MHW_PAR_T(VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT) defaults (mhw_vdbox_vdenc_cmdpar.h): HME region prefetch 1, top prefetch
  mode 0, left prefetch at wrap around 1, verticalShift32Minus1 2, hzShift32Minus1 3, numVerticalReqMinus1 6,
  numHzReqMinus1 2, prefetch offset 0. ANV's Xe2 AV1 encoder already uses exactly these.
- DW3: VDENC_PIPE_MODE_SELECT_CMD constructor zeros (mhw_vdbox_vdenc_hwcmd_xe2_hpm.h), not set by HEVC.
- DW5 bit 17 = VdencPipeModeSelectPar0 = 1 (encode_hevc_vdenc_packet.cpp, unless WaEnableOnlyASteppingFeatures).
  No DW5 bit 8 for HEVC (AVC only).
Prefetch fields only change memory access timing; DW5 bit 17 is undocumented in the open source, so the
level 1 (TU 4) bitstream must be compared against 0084 before use (see docs/reports/b580-hevc-tu1-20261103.md).
This is a faithfulness fix found while analysing HEVC veryslow (TU 1) 4K/8K at ~50% of Windows QSV; it is not
expected to close that gap (the report attributes it to Windows' two-VDBOX HEVC encode at 4K and above).

FILE: mesa/patches/0090-wsi-native-images-without-dma-buf-export-on-devices-that-have-none.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0090] wsi: native images without dma-buf export on devices that have none

On top of 0089 (src/mesa-cts1, build-cts1, same meson options as build-prod8). NOT installed.

A headless swapchain (VK_EXT_headless_surface) of a hardware device uses native DRM images
(wsi_configure_native_image / wsi_create_native_image_mem): the image is created with
VkExternalMemoryImageCreateInfo(DMA_BUF), its memory allocated exportable as DMA_BUF and exported at once
(wsi_init_image_dmabuf_fd -> vkGetMemoryFdKHR). With xemac (macOS: no dma-bufs, no
VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf) the export fails in ANV (anv_device_export_bo: anv_gem_handle_to_fd < 0 ->
VK_ERROR_TOO_MANY_OBJECTS), so every headless vkCreateSwapchainKHR failed:
dEQP-VK.image.swapchain_mutable.headless.* (90 fails) and dEQP-VK.api.array.oversized_array.wsi.headless.* (5).

wsi_device now records VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf support (has_export_memory_dma_buf). Without it a native
image is created and allocated without the DMA_BUF external handle type and not exported: image->dma_buf_fd
stays -1, which the acquire/present paths already treat as "no dma-buf implicit sync" (as when the kernel
lacks sync-file import/export). Headless never reads its images outside the device, so it works unchanged,
with the same tiled, modifier-selected, blit-free images as on Linux. The window systems that do share
images (X11, Wayland, display) are not built without dma-bufs, and every Linux driver using this path exposes
VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf, so nothing changes there.

Not chosen: CPU images for such devices (WSI_IMAGE_TYPE_CPU, what MESA_VK_WSI_DEBUG=sw does). It also creates
the swapchains, but adds an image-to-buffer blit per present and records command buffers during
vkCreateSwapchainKHR, which crashes dEQP-VK.wsi.headless.swapchain.simulate_oom.* (SIGSEGV in ANV's
mi_builder/blorp writing into the NULL dwords of a batch whose allocation failed; reproducible on prod8 with
MESA_VK_WSI_DEBUG=sw).

================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0091] anv: clear the whole sampler state before packing it

On top of 0090 (src/mesa-cts1, build-cts1). NOT installed.

genX(emit_sampler_state) packs SAMPLER_STATE (4 dwords on Gfx12/Xe2) into slots of ANV_SAMPLER_STATE_DWORDS (8)
and never wrote the other 4. anv_WriteSamplerDescriptorsEXT (VK_EXT_descriptor_heap) packs into an
uninitialized stack struct anv_sampler_state and copies ANV_SAMPLER_STATE_SIZE (32) bytes, the reported sampler
descriptor size, so the upper 16 bytes of every sampler descriptor were stack garbage.

sampler made from different call histories: "Descriptor data is not invariant" (2 fails; the invariance.*
variant passes only because its writes come from one tight loop with identical stack contents).
anv_nir_lower_descriptor_heap had the same garbage in embedded_key.sampler, which is hashed and compared for
embedded samplers. vkCreateSampler was not affected (its state is in zeroed object memory).

Subject: [PATCH 0095] anv: Xe2 HEVC encode: target usage 1 takes TU 4's VDENC_CMD2 DW54

On top of prod8 (935ef655 + 0084-0087; NOT on 0088, which is a diagnostic patch that rewrites the same line).
Built as one object with build-prod8's compile command (x86_64, Xe2 variant libanv_per_hw_ver200): no warnings.

ANV takes its Xe2 HEVC VDENC_CMD2 values from media-driver's Xe2_HPM tables; TU 1 and TU 4 differ only in seven
dwords (8, 9, 12, 51-54). Measured on an Arc B580 (hackintosh, 3 Nov 2026, 4K 300 frames, VBR 25 Mbit/s, 0088
switches; docs/reports/b580-hevc-tu1-ab-20261103.md section 7 in the development repository):

- DW54 alone from TU 4: 23.2 -> 9.9 ms per frame (DW51 alone 16.8, DW53 18.2, DW52 22.4, DW8/9/12 no change);
  Intel's Windows driver on the same card: 12.34 ms per frame at TU 1, one VDBOX;
- quality with DW54 from TU 4 (1080p 3/6/12 + 4K 12/25/50 Mbit/s, two clips, BD-rate PSNR-Y): -8.3/-13.0 (1080p)
  and -4.5/-7.3 (4K) against Windows QSV at TU 1; +0.7..+1.9% against our TU 1 with media-driver's DW54.

So TU 1 keeps every other TU 1 setting and takes TU 4's DW54. This is a deliberate departure from media-driver's
open table (Intel's Windows driver uses closed tables). ANV_HEVC_TU1_MEDIA_DRIVER_DW54=true restores it.

FILE: mesa/patches/0096-meson-dead-strip-on-darwin-as-the-ld64-form-of-gc-sections.patch
================================================
meson: -dead_strip on darwin as the ld64 form of --gc-sections

ld_args_gc_sections is how every driver drops the shared code it does not use ("particularly relevant for Vulkan
drivers"); it only probes for --gc-sections, which ld64 does not have, so darwin builds keep everything. ld64's
equivalent is -dead_strip; Mach-O objects are already split per symbol (MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS), so no
-ffunction-sections/-fdata-sections is needed.

libvulkan_intel.dylib (x86_64, prod8 objects; the meson build is byte-identical to relinking build-prod8's objects
with -Wl,-dead_strip): 31.7 -> 26.9 MB, __TEXT 27.8 -> 23.6 MiB, __DATA_CONST 624 -> 512 KiB, rebases 11526 -> 8950
(pages with fixups 152 -> 125), binds 349 -> 330, the optional entrypoints resolved to NULL 10954 -> 9195. Same
175 exports, same 9 initializers, same ObjC sections; the 22 entrypoint tables anv uses are identical slot by slot
(9702 NULL); the 7 dropped are the Android and vk_cmd_enqueue tables nothing references. All 865 commands resolve
the same through vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr. dlopen time is unchanged within noise (3.20 -> 3.18 ms median under
Rosetta); the gain is size and ~27 fewer dirty pages per process.

     ld_args_gc_sections += '-Wl,--gc-sections'
     _trial_c += ['-ffunction-sections', '-fdata-sections']
     _trial_cpp += ['-ffunction-sections', '-fdata-sections']
+  elif host_machine.system() == 'darwin' and \
+       cc.links('static char unused() { return 5; } int main() { return 0; }',
+                args : '-Wl,-dead_strip', name : 'dead_strip')
+    # ld64's equivalent of --gc-sections. Mach-O objects are already split per symbol
+    # (MH_SUBSECTIONS_VIA_SYMBOLS), so no -ffunction-sections/-fdata-sections needed.

FILE: mesa/patches/0098-anv-xemac-fd-handle-types-from-what-the-kernel-offers-at-runtime.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0098] anv: xemac fd handle types from what the kernel offers, at runtime

On top of mesa-prod9 (prod8 + 0089-0092 + 0095 + 0096). Built in a copy (src/mesa-fd1, build-fd1.sh, same meson
options as build-prod9, -Dxemac=src/xemac-fd1/user); NOT installed. Stage 0 of fd sharing
(docs/reports/b580-fd-sharing-20261103.md, report b580-fd-sharing-stage0-20261104.md). Needs the xemac of
patches/xemac/fd1-object-fds-syncobj-sync-file-prime-and-fake-device.patch (xemac_fd_sharing, xemac_obj_size).

With xemac (macOS, B580.kext) the fd extensions were off at compile time (ANV_FD_SHARING false): no syncobj fds,
sync files or dma-bufs existed. B580.kext now gets object fds (opens of the clone device /dev/b580obj, one kernel
object per fd; uapi/b580_drm.h B580_CAP_FD_OBJECTS), so the device is asked at physical device creation
(xemac_fd_sharing(): B580_CAP_FD_OBJECTS = 1, and DRM_CAP_PRIME = IMPORT|EXPORT for BO fds):
 - VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd and VK_KHR_external_fence_fd with syncobj fds and sync files (OPAQUE_FD and
   SYNC_FD come together: vk_semaphore/vk_fence derive both from the drm_syncobj sync type, and a shared binary
   semaphore's move goes through a sync file),
 - VK_KHR_external_memory_fd with PRIME fds.
An older kernel (or XEMAC_FDS=0) reports neither and the device is exactly as before. VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf
(stage 3) and VK_EXT_physical_device_drm stay off under xemac; Linux is unchanged (all true).

An imported BO's size came from lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END) on the dma-buf. An object fd here is an open of a character
device, whose SEEK_END is 0 (checked on macOS), so under xemac the kernel answers it: xemac_obj_size()
(DRM_IOCTL_B580_OBJ_INFO through the device's IOUserClient, never an ioctl on the object fd).

Validation on the build Mac (x86_64 deqp-vk under Rosetta, XEMAC_FAKE=1, the fake device's object fds):
dEQP-VK.api.external.* 550 cases: prod9 61 Pass / 489 NotSupported -> 144 Pass / 406 NotSupported, 0 Fail
(+83: semaphore opaque_fd 20, sync_fd 8, fence opaque_fd 22, sync_fd 9, memory opaque_fd 24; the remaining fd
NotSupported are the dup/dup2/dup3/send_over_socket cases CTS compiles only for Linux/Android). With
XEMAC_FAKE_FDS=0 (a kernel without object fds) all 550 results are identical to prod9.

FILE: mesa/patches/0099-anv-OPAQUE_FD-is-not-DMA_BUF-compatible-on-a-device-without-dma-buf.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0099] anv: OPAQUE_FD is not DMA_BUF-compatible on a device without dma-buf

On top of 0098 (src/mesa-fd1, build-fd1). NOT installed.

vkGetPhysicalDeviceExternalBufferProperties(OPAQUE_FD) and the image query with an explicit layout (linear or a DRM
format modifier) returned opaque_fd_dma_buf_props: compatibleHandleTypes and exportFromImportedHandleTypes include
DMA_BUF. On Linux the device always has VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf; with xemac after 0098 it has
VK_KHR_external_memory_fd but not (yet) dma-buf, and promising DMA_BUF there is the 0089 bug again (the handle
type of an extension the device does not expose). Without the dma-buf extension they now
return opaque_fd_only_props (OPAQUE_FD only), as the implicit-layout image case always did. Nothing changes on
Linux.

Validation: as 0098 (api.external.* 144 Pass, 0 Fail on the fake device; prod9 behaviour with XEMAC_FAKE_FDS=0).

FILE: mesa/patches/0100-anv-AV1-video-sessions-hand-out-their-internal-buffers-in-a-few-memory-bindings.patch
================================================
From: Yusuf İhsan KILINÇ
Subject: [PATCH 0100] anv: AV1 video sessions hand out their internal buffers in a few memory bindings

On top of 0099 (src/mesa-vb1 = mesa-fd2 + this, build-vb1). NOT installed.

vkGetVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR reported one binding per internal buffer: an Xe2 AV1 encode session with HuC
BRC had 57, an Xe2 AV1 film-grain decode session 41 (upstream ANV reports the same 41 on Xe2: its enum has 41 AV1
entries and none is skipped there). The Vulkan Video samples, and the CTS AV1 encoder built on them, read the
requirements into a fixed array of 40 (VulkanVideoSession.cpp, MAX_BOUND_MEMORY): every AV1 encode case overflowed
the stack (SIGSEGV / __stack_chk_fail), the CTS decode path refused film grain with InternalError.

AV1 sessions now group their buffers into memory bindings (memoryBindIndex 0..n-1): the AVP line/tile buffers, the
default CDF tables (CPU-written), DBD + tile size/bitstream streamout, the Xe2 VDEnc row stores + statistics, and the
HuC BRC buffers. Decode: 3 bindings, encode: 5 (4 without BRC). Inside a binding each buffer sits at its own
alignment (4096) in enum order, with its old size; the binding's memoryTypeBits are the buffers' (all identical, the
xemac CPU-visible VRAM selection of 0011 included) and its alignment their maximum. vkBindVideoSessionMemoryKHR fans
a binding out into vid->vid_mem[type] (memory, memoryOffset + sub-offset, size), so command emission, CPU
initialisation and queries keep addressing vid_mem[type] unchanged. One layout function answers both entry points.
H.264, H.265 and VP9 keep one binding per buffer with the same memoryBindIndex values and sizes as before.
The requirements query now returns VK_INCOMPLETE when the array is short (spec; it returned VK_SUCCESS).

Validation (Mac, fake device with VCS/VECS + HuC, scratch instrumented builds of fd2 and this):
- bindings AV1 decode 39/41 -> 3, AV1 encode 57 -> 5 (176x144 ... 7680x4320, 8/10-bit, film grain up to 16K);
  H.264/H.265/VP9 identical; every internal buffer keeps its size, lies 4K-aligned inside its binding, no overlap;
  bytes: at most the per-buffer 4K page rounding the separate bindings had (AV1 encode 9,448,320 vs 9,457,664).
- AV1 encode batches of 13 configurations (CQP/CBR/VBR, quality 0/1/2, 8/10-bit, up to 8K multi-tile): every
  differing dword is an address resolving to the same internal buffer + offset (or same app BO + offset); with the
  session memory in one allocation the batches are byte-identical.
- CTS AV1/H.264/H.265/VP9 decode and H.264/H.265 encode cases: same results; non-AV1 batches byte-identical, AV1
  equal modulo addresses. gv00-gv04 case by case identical; gv07 film grain InternalError 6 -> 0; gv13 AV1 encode
  CRASH 56 -> 0 (the encoder now runs; the fake device writes no bitstream).

+ * more than applications expect a session to have: the Vulkan Video samples (and the CTS encoder built on them) read
+ * the requirements into a fixed array of 40. The AV1 buffers are therefore handed out in a few memory bindings, each
+ * holding a group of them back to back at their own alignment. Only where a buffer lives changes: every buffer keeps
+ * its size, its alignment and its memory types, and the command emission still finds it in vid->vid_mem[type].
+ */
+static uint32_t
+av1_video_mem_group(uint32_t type)
+{
+   if (type < ANV_VID_MEM_AV1_CDF_DEFAULTS_0)
+      return 0;   /* AVP line, tile line and tile column buffers */
+   if (type <= ANV_VID_MEM_AV1_CDF_DEFAULTS_3)
+      return 1;   /* the default CDF tables, written by the CPU */
+   if (type <= ANV_VID_MEM_AV1_ENCODE_TILE_BITSTREAM_ACCUM)
+      return 2;   /* DBD, tile size and tile bitstream streamout */
+   if (type <= ANV_VID_MEM_AV1_ENCODE_PAK_TILE_STATS)
+      return 3;   /* Xe2 VDEnc row stores and VDEnc / PAK statistics */
+   return 4;      /* HuC BRC: the AV1 CDF, data and SLB buffers and the shared BRC buffers */
+}
+
+struct anv_video_mem_slot {
+   uint32_t type;          /* ANV_VID_MEM_*, index in vid_mem[] */
+   uint32_t binding;       /* index in anv_video_mem_layout::bindings[] */
+   VkDeviceSize offset;    /* from the start of the binding */
+   VkDeviceSize size;
+};
+
+struct anv_video_mem_layout {
+   uint32_t slot_count;
+   uint32_t binding_count;
+   struct anv_video_mem_slot slots[ANV_VID_MEM_BRC_MAX];
+   uint32_t group[ANV_VID_MEM_BRC_MAX];
+   VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR bindings[ANV_VID_MEM_BRC_MAX];
+};
+
+/* Where each internal buffer of the session lives: the same answer for vkGetVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR and
+ * vkBindVideoSessionMemoryKHR, as it only depends on the session's creation parameters. Codecs other than AV1 keep
+ * one binding per buffer, with the buffer's type as memoryBindIndex, exactly as before.
+ */
+static void
+get_video_session_mem_layout(struct anv_device *device,
+                             struct anv_video_session *vid,
+                             struct anv_video_mem_layout *layout)
+{
+   VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR reqs[ANV_VID_MEM_BRC_MAX];
+   uint32_t count = ARRAY_SIZE(reqs);
+
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++)
+      reqs[i] = (VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR) {
+         .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_VIDEO_SESSION_MEMORY_REQUIREMENTS_KHR,
+      };
+   get_video_session_buffer_reqs(device, vid, reqs, &count);
+   assert(count <= ARRAY_SIZE(reqs));
+
+   const bool grouped = vid->vk.op & (VK_VIDEO_CODEC_OPERATION_DECODE_AV1_BIT_KHR |
+                                      VK_VIDEO_CODEC_OPERATION_ENCODE_AV1_BIT_KHR);
+
+   layout->slot_count = count;
+   layout->binding_count = 0;
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+      const uint32_t type = reqs[i].memoryBindIndex;
+      const VkMemoryRequirements *req = &reqs[i].memoryRequirements;
+      const uint32_t group = grouped ? av1_video_mem_group(type) : type;
+
+      uint32_t b = 0;
+      while (b < layout->binding_count &&
+             !(grouped && layout->group[b] == group &&
+               layout->bindings[b].memoryRequirements.memoryTypeBits == req->memoryTypeBits))
+         b++;
+
+      if (b == layout->binding_count) {
+         layout->binding_count++;
+         layout->group[b] = group;
+         layout->bindings[b] = (VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR) {
+            .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_VIDEO_SESSION_MEMORY_REQUIREMENTS_KHR,
+            .memoryBindIndex = grouped ? b : type,
+            .memoryRequirements = {
+               .size = 0,
+               .alignment = req->alignment,
+               .memoryTypeBits = req->memoryTypeBits,
+            },
+         };
+      }
+
+      VkMemoryRequirements *bind_req = &layout->bindings[b].memoryRequirements;
+      const VkDeviceSize offset = align64(bind_req->size, req->alignment);
+
+      bind_req->alignment = MAX2(bind_req->alignment, req->alignment);
+      bind_req->size = offset + req->size;
+      layout->slots[i] = (struct anv_video_mem_slot) {
+         .type = type,
+         .binding = b,
+         .offset = offset,
+         .size = req->size,
+      };
+   }
+}
+
+VkResult
+anv_GetVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR(VkDevice _device,
+                                         VkVideoSessionKHR videoSession,
+                                         uint32_t *pVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsCount,
+                                         VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR *mem_reqs)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_video_session, vid, videoSession);
+   VK_OUTARRAY_MAKE_TYPED(VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR,
+                          out,
+                          mem_reqs,
+                          pVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsCount);
+   struct anv_video_mem_layout layout;
+
+   get_video_session_mem_layout(device, vid, &layout);
+
+   for (uint32_t b = 0; b < layout.binding_count; b++) {
+      vk_outarray_append_typed(VkVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR, &out, p) {
+         p->memoryBindIndex = layout.bindings[b].memoryBindIndex;
+         p->memoryRequirements = layout.bindings[b].memoryRequirements;
+      }
+   }
+
+   return vk_outarray_status(&out);
 }

FILE: mesa/patches/0102-util-disk_cache-keep-the-cache-for-processes-whose-real-user-is-root-on-macOS.patch
================================================
From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: util/disk_cache: keep the shader cache on macOS when the real user is root

Mesa turns its disk cache off when the effective and real ids differ (__normal_user), because the environment that
chooses the cache directory belongs to the real user. macOS runs its own system processes that way with a real uid of
0: WindowServer (real 0, effective _windowserver) and loginwindow after login (real 0, effective the user). The cache
was therefore off in exactly the compositor, which compiled every pipeline again after each boot and login (the
stutter in the first seconds of a session). A real user of root is no less privileged than any effective user, so on
macOS the cache stays on in that case; a setuid program started by another user still gets none.

Measured on the B580 with a root process that drops its effective ids like loginwindow (24 render pipelines): with
the released build no cache entries were written and every run took ~100 ms; with this patch 74 entries were written
and warm runs took 53 ms (cold 145 ms).

At login on the B580 (WindowServer, same mode, the user idle for 60 s after logging in), with the cache emptied (the
behaviour before this patch) and then warm: WindowServer CPU time from boot to login 27.1 s -> 14.8 s, in the first 30 s
after login 17.6 s -> 9.2 s, shader compiles in those 30 s 265 -> 6. The login window's transition also stopped timing
out: WindowServer compiled while loginwindow waited for the display reconfiguration (8 s once), and when the
transition gave up before a scaled HiDPI mode was set, the login screen stayed in a corner of the panel.

Applies on top of intelxe.diff (or patches/0101). In 0.1.3.
---

FILE: mesa/patches/0103-anv-VK_EXT_memory_priority-as-a-recorded-hint.patch
================================================
From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: anv: VK_EXT_memory_priority as a recorded hint

DXVK and vkd3d-proton pass VkMemoryPriorityAllocateInfoEXT whenever the device offers VK_EXT_memory_priority
(user/tests/vulkan/vkcaps.c listed it as the one extension they use that ANV lacked on the B580). Upstream ANV does not
offer it on either kernel driver: as of Mesa main 2026-10-29 (bd583379bc8) only RADV (amdgpu BO-list priorities) and
lavapipe (records it) expose it. Neither i915 nor xe has a BO priority or residency hint in its uAPI
(drm_xe_gem_create carries placement and flags only; DRM_IOCTL_XE_MADVISE has a preferred location for SVM ranges and
a purgeable state, no priority), and IntelXe.kext does not page VRAM out at all (it moves BOs out of the 1 GB BAR
window, which is about CPU visibility, not priority). So there is nothing to map the priority to.

The extension is a hint an implementation may ignore, so ANV now accepts it, as lavapipe does: the feature is on, the
priority is parsed in vkAllocateMemory and recorded in anv_device_memory::priority (0.5 when absent), and it changes
nothing else. Not exposed: VK_EXT_pageable_device_local_memory, which invites those layers to allocate past the heap
budget and leave the paging to the kernel, ordered by priority; nothing here can order it.

Platform independent (i915 and xe, Linux and macOS). Applies on intelxe.diff + patches/0102.

From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: anv: descriptor buffers: no per-set surface state on LSC platforms

In EXT_descriptor_buffer mode, genX(flush_binding_mode) calls update_descriptor_set_surface_state() for every bound
set whenever a stage's offsets are dirty, and each new set address allocates a 64-byte RENDER_SURFACE_STATE from the
command buffer's surface state stream and fills it (isl_buffer_fill_state).

That surface state is only read by emit_binding_table() for a binding table entry of type
ANV_DESCRIPTOR_SET_DESCRIPTORS, and build_packed_binding_table() only creates such an entry when
!devinfo->has_lsc ("Only add a binding table entry on platform that cannot use LSC_ADDR_SURFTYPE_SS");
emit_binding_table() asserts !has_lsc for it. On LSC platforms (DG2, MTL, Xe2, Xe3) shaders read descriptor buffer
memory through device->descriptor_buffer_view_state (BRW_SHADER_RELOC_DESCRIPTORS_BUFFERS_VIEW_HANDLE), so the
per-set state is never read.

The Metal plugin's descriptor-buffer model points sets 0/1 at a new region for almost every dispatch (0.97 new
regions per bind in Geekbench), so this is an allocation and a surface-state pack per set per dispatch, plus 64 bytes
of surface state stream each time, for nothing. CPU only: no GPU command changes.

Upstream main (2026-11-13) still has the same code. Not built or measured here.

FILE: mesa/patches/0106-anv-video-decode-DPB-slot-indices-never-corrupt-the-stack-or-stop-the-client.patch
================================================
From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: anv: video decode: DPB slot indices never corrupt the stack or stop the client

vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR's decode paths indexed arrays by slotIndex with only an assert: anv_h265_decode_video's
dpb_idx[16] (written for every reference slot, read through the RefPicSet* entries of StdVideoDecodeH265PictureInfo,
handed to the HuC S2L parameters) and anv_h264_decode_video's dpb_slots[17]; the AV1 path's prev_refs[9] is guarded.
By the reference number they index 16-entry arrays and the HuC S2L parameters' PicOrderCntValList[15] and
RefIdxMapping[15], and H.265 writes ReferencePictureAddress[hcp_ref_idx] with up to 16 active references into 8
entries. A slotIndex at or above the session's maxDpbSlots is invalid usage, but FFmpeg's H.264/H.265 Vulkan
hwaccels up to 9.0.2 number slots by their own DPB array index: 16 on the JCT-VC streams RPS_B_qualcomm_5,
RPS_C_ericsson_5, RPS_E_qualcomm_5 (a 16-picture DPB), 19 on the JVT streams HCBP2_HHI_A / HCMP1_HHI_A. On an Arc B580
the H.265 ones aborted the decoding process in __stack_chk_fail under anv_h265_decode_video <- gfx20_CmdDecodeVideoKHR.

Refusing such a decode is not an answer either: a first version of this patch left it unrecorded and set
VK_ERROR_INVALID_VIDEO_STD_PARAMETERS_KHR on the command buffer; FFmpeg 9.0.2 then never submitted, its execution's
fence stayed reset, and the decoder hung at the next use of that execution context (B580: all five streams).

For H.264 and H.265 the slot index is only a key (each reference is addressed through its picture resource; the
index ties pReferenceSlots to the RefPicSet* entries, and becomes H.264's 16-bit PictureID). dpb_idx and dpb_slots
are now tables of ANV_VIDEO_DECODE_SLOT_KEYS (256) entries: any uint8_t RefPicSet* entry is a valid read, any index
below 256 a valid write, and those streams decode as the client meant. CmdDecodeVideoKHR first makes a sanitized copy
of the decode info: a reference whose index is beyond the codec's table (256; AV1 9) or past the references the codec
path holds (H.264 16, H.265 15: the HuC parameters' size, which a 16-picture DPB never exceeds) is left out and decodes
as a missing reference; a VP9 inter frame whose reference names are not all in pReferenceSlots (anv_vp9_get_ref_idx
returned 0xff and the decode read pReferenceSlots[255]) is not recorded. H.265 keeps at most 8 active references.
Each case logs once (mesa_logw_once). No error is set: the command buffer ends with VK_SUCCESS, the submission
happens and signals the client's semaphores and fence. Negative indices are skipped as before. Encode is unchanged.

Platform independent. Applies on upstream f01e9b07a91 (with offsets) and on intelxe.diff (+ 0102-0105).

+/* A decode must never be able to corrupt the driver or stop a client: the
+ * codec paths below index arrays by slotIndex (H.265 dpb_idx, H.264
+ * dpb_slots, AV1 prev_refs) and by the reference number, and look VP9
+ * reference names up among the reference slots. A slotIndex at or above the
+ * session's maxDpbSlots is invalid usage, but clients do it: FFmpeg's H.264
+ * and H.265 hwaccels up to 9.0 number slots by their own DPB array index (16
+ * on H.265 streams with a 16-picture DPB, 19 on some H.264 streams), and
+ * with asserts off ANV wrote past its stack arrays (__stack_chk_fail).
+ * Refusing such a decode (an error on the command buffer) is no better: the
+ * client's submission never happens, and FFmpeg 9.0.2 then waits forever on
+ * the execution's fence it had already reset.
+ *
+ * H.264 and H.265 use slot indices only as keys (pictures are addressed
+ * through each reference's picture resource), so their key tables take any
+ * index below ANV_VIDEO_DECODE_SLOT_KEYS and such a stream decodes as the
+ * client meant. What still cannot be honoured is recorded without it: a
+ * reference whose index is beyond the codec's table, or past the number of
+ * references the codec path holds, is left out (decoded as a missing
+ * reference); a VP9 inter frame whose reference names are not all bound is
+ * not decoded. Either way the command buffer ends with VK_SUCCESS and the
+ * submission signals its semaphores and fence.
+ */
+#define ANV_VIDEO_DECODE_MAX_REFS 32
+
+static bool
+anv_video_decode_sanitize(const struct anv_video_session *vid,
+                          const VkVideoDecodeInfoKHR *in,
+                          VkVideoDecodeInfoKHR *out,
+                          VkVideoReferenceSlotInfoKHR *refs)
+{
+   uint32_t keys = UINT32_MAX, max_refs = ANV_VIDEO_DECODE_MAX_REFS;
+
+   switch (vid->vk.op) {
+   case VK_VIDEO_CODEC_OPERATION_DECODE_H264_BIT_KHR:
+      keys = ANV_VIDEO_DECODE_SLOT_KEYS;
+      max_refs = ANV_VIDEO_H264_MAX_NUM_REF_FRAME;
+      break;
+   case VK_VIDEO_CODEC_OPERATION_DECODE_H265_BIT_KHR:
+      keys = ANV_VIDEO_DECODE_SLOT_KEYS;
+      /* the HuC S2L parameters hold 15 (PicOrderCntValList): a 16-picture
+       * DPB has at most 15 references beside the current picture */
+      max_refs = ANV_VIDEO_H265_MAX_NUM_REF_FRAME - 1;
+      break;
+   case VK_VIDEO_CODEC_OPERATION_DECODE_AV1_BIT_KHR:
+      keys = ANV_VIDEO_AV1_MAX_DPB_SLOTS;
+      break;
+   default:
+      break;
+   }
+
+   *out = *in;
+   uint32_t n = 0;
+   bool dropped = false, over = false;
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < in->referenceSlotCount; i++) {
+      const int32_t slot = in->pReferenceSlots[i].slotIndex;
+      if (slot >= 0 && (uint32_t)slot >= vid->vk.max_dpb_slots)
+         over = true;
+      if ((slot >= 0 && (uint32_t)slot >= keys) || n == max_refs) {
+         dropped = true;
+         continue;
+      }
+      refs[n++] = in->pReferenceSlots[i];
+   }
+   out->referenceSlotCount = n;
+   out->pReferenceSlots = n ? refs : NULL;
+
+   if (over || dropped ||
+       (in->pSetupReferenceSlot &&
+        in->pSetupReferenceSlot->slotIndex >= (int32_t)vid->vk.max_dpb_slots)) {
+      mesa_logw_once("anv: vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR: a DPB slot index at or above the "
+                     "session's maxDpbSlots (%u)%s", vid->vk.max_dpb_slots,
+                     dropped ? "; references the decoder cannot hold left out" :
+                               "; used as a key");
+   }
+
+   /* VP9 looks each reference name up among the reference slots; a name that
+    * is not there gave index 0xff and a read past pReferenceSlots.
+    */
+   if (vid->vk.op == VK_VIDEO_CODEC_OPERATION_DECODE_VP9_BIT_KHR) {
+      const struct VkVideoDecodeVP9PictureInfoKHR *vp9_pic_info =
+         vk_find_struct_const(out->pNext, VIDEO_DECODE_VP9_PICTURE_INFO_KHR);
+      const StdVideoDecodeVP9PictureInfo *std_pic = vp9_pic_info->pStdPictureInfo;
+
+      if (!std_pic->flags.intra_only &&
+          std_pic->frame_type != STD_VIDEO_VP9_FRAME_TYPE_KEY) {
+         for (unsigned i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
+            if (anv_vp9_get_ref_idx(out, vp9_pic_info->referenceNameSlotIndices[i]) == 0xff) {
+               mesa_logw_once("anv: vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR: a VP9 reference name "
+                              "without a reference slot; frame not decoded");
+               return false;
+            }
+         }
+      }
+   }
+
+   return true;
+}
+

FILE: mesa/patches/0107-zink-ZINK_BAR_BUFFERS-map-buffers-directly-on-a-small-BAR-opt-in.patch
================================================
From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: zink: ZINK_BAR_BUFFERS, map buffers directly on a small BAR (opt-in)

Without a resizable BAR, zink flags every buffer of 8 KiB or more
PIPE_RESOURCE_FLAG_DONT_MAP_DIRECTLY, so each glBufferSubData, orphaning
glBufferData and INVALIDATE map becomes a staging buffer plus a GPU copy
(on Intel Xe2 a blorp 3D draw with its flushes, often ending the render
pass). That keeps VRAM buffers out of the CPU window, but it also applies
to buffers placed in host memory, where it only adds GPU work.

ZINK_BAR_BUFFERS=sysmem maps those host-memory buffers directly;
ZINK_BAR_BUFFERS=all maps every buffer as on a resizable-BAR device.
EXT_host_image_copy stays off on a small BAR either way. Unset, nothing
changes.

FILE: mesa/patches/0108-anv-state-cache-perf-fix-for-zink.patch
================================================
From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: anv: BTP+BTI state cache keying (anv_state_cache_perf_fix) for zink

Without anv_state_cache_perf_fix, a render target binding table entry that points to a new surface state needs a
render target cache flush with a stall at scoreboard (ANV_PIPE_RT_BTI_CHANGE): at every vkCmdBeginRendering and around
every blorp operation. The bit also keeps Xe2 from using RESOURCE_BARRIER for the barrier in the same pending bits, so
a render-to-texture boundary becomes a full drain (end-of-pipe sync). Zink ends and begins render passes often (every
FBO switch of a GL deferred renderer, every glGenerateMipmap level, every buffer copy blorp runs as a draw).

With the option, the kernel programs COMMON_SLICE_CHICKEN3 bit 13 for the render queue
(DRM_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_SET_DISABLE_STATE_CACHE_PERF_FIX; i915: the register in the queue's init batch): the render cache's
state cache is tagged by binding table pointer plus index, so a new binding table cannot hit a stale surface state and
the flush is not needed. That is a property of the hardware tag, not of the API, so it holds for GL through zink as for
D3D12. Upstream (af2d51eafa9, "anv: enable BTP+BTI RCC keying for some workloads") turns it on only for vkd3d because
of performance, not correctness: with the option ANV keeps only render targets in the binding table, everything else
goes bindless, and DXVK's D3D11 shaders lost to the extra registers for descriptor set base offsets. Zink on ANV
already uses descriptor buffers (bindless), so that cost does not arise; platforms without LSC never get the keying
(platform_supports_btp_bit_rcc).

Measured on the Arc B580 (zgbench, zink-gl/bench, 1920x1080 window, 2 rounds, images identical by hash, 0 GPU resets):
GPU time per frame -10.7% for a shader-pack-like frame (8 passes, a mip chain, 2 MiB of uploads), -36.3% for passes and
barriers only. Opt out with anv_state_cache_perf_fix=false in the environment or, on macOS, in
/tmp/mesa-options-<process> (patches/0020); either wins over this entry.

Platform independent; applies on upstream f01e9b07a91 and on intelxe.diff (+ 0102-0106).

Generated-by: LLM
---
--- a/src/intel/vulkan/00-anv-defaults.conf
+++ b/src/intel/vulkan/00-anv-defaults.conf
@@ -246,6 +246,15 @@
         -->
         <engine engine_name_match="mesa zink">
             <option name="no_16bit" value="true" />
+            <!--
+            BTP+BTI keying of the render cache's state cache, so render
+            target changes need no RT flush and stall. Zink binds every
+            non-render-target resource bindlessly already (descriptor
+            buffers), so the DX11 register-pressure regression that keeps
+            this vkd3d-only does not apply. Opt out with the environment
+            (or options file) anv_state_cache_perf_fix=false.
+            -->
+            <option name="anv_state_cache_perf_fix" value="true" />

FILE: mesa/patches/0109-anv-descriptor-buffers-reload-set-offsets-a-layout-without-the-stage-left.patch
================================================
From: IntelXe (Claude Opus 5.5)
Subject: anv: descriptor buffers: reload a set's offset for stages an earlier set layout did not have

anv_cmd_buffer_set_descriptor_buffer_offsets() stores a set's new (buffer index, offset) in the bind state and flags
only the stages of the set layout it is given (descriptors_dirty, descriptor_buffers.offsets_dirty).
genX(flush_binding_mode) recomputes push_constants.buffer.sets[] (the per-set surface/sampler offsets the shaders
read from push constants) only when an active stage is in offsets_dirty, and re-emits the push constants of the
flagged stages only. A set layout without bindings has shader_stages == 0: its new offset is stored and nothing is
flagged. When a later call with a set layout that has stages gives the same offset, the comparison with the bind
state says "no change", so buffer.sets[] keeps the offset from before the empty layout's call and the stages read
the set at an older offset. The same holds for any stage that the layout given with a change did not have.

Hit by the Metal plugin's descriptor-buffer model (issue #9): a stage plan without bindings is an empty set layout
whose region offset is the page cursor, and the next real region starts at that cursor. Replaying the per-draw
capture of RenderBox drawing Safari's icon (iconservicesagent, 168 draws, 63 pipelines) through this logic: with
table-pc converting both stages, 3 draws read set 0 or 1 at a stale offset (e.g. P3 set 0 pushed at 0x0 while bound
at 0x40 after P30's empty set 0 at 0x40); fragment-only conversion: 0 (the vertex stage's table set changes every
draw, which reloads buffer.sets[] for everything). Pushing on every draw does not help: it copies the stale
buffer.sets[].

Remember per set which stages of the bind point were not flagged when its offset last changed, and flag the ones a
later layout has even when the offset is the same. A changed offset still flags only the layout's stages (the
per-stage re-emission the plugin's table sets rely on is kept).

Reproduction: user/tests/vulkan/vk_dbuf_empty_set.c (compute; result[1] is 111 instead of 222 without this patch).
Platform independent; upstream main (2026-11-15) has the same code. Applies on upstream f01e9b07a91 and on
intelxe.diff (+ 0102-0108). Compiled (anv_cmd_buffer.c, -fsyntax-only), not run on the B580.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/intel/vulkan/anv_nvmtl_surface.c

+/*
+ * Implicit IOSurface synchronization for the nullmoth Metal plugin on B580.kext (macOS, xemac).
+ *
+ * B580.kext keeps, per IOSurface ID, the fences of the jobs that last wrote and read the surface (uapi/b580_drm.h, the
+ * dma-resv model). These entry points let the plugin, which only sees Vulkan objects, attach a submission's fence to a
+ * surface and import a surface's fences into a timeline semaphore it then waits on in vkQueueSubmit, so a consumer in
+ * another process (WindowServer compositing a game's frame) waits on the GPU instead of the producer waiting on the CPU.
+ * They are looked up with dlsym; a plugin that does not find them, or a kernel without B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES, keeps
+ * the CPU-side ordering.
+ */
+#include "anv_private.h"
+
+#include "vk_drm_syncobj.h"
+#include "vk_fence.h"
+#include "vk_semaphore.h"
+
+#include "drm-uapi/drm.h"
+#include "../../../../b580/uapi/b580_drm.h"
+
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_cap_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t *supported);
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_attach_v1(VkDevice _device, VkFence fence, VkSemaphore sem, uint64_t value,
+                                            uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags);
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_import_v1(VkDevice _device, VkSemaphore sem, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags,
+                                            uint64_t *wait_value, uint32_t *count);
+PUBLIC VkResult nvmtl_anv_surface_wait_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags, int64_t timeout_abs_ns);
+
+/* intel_ioctl restarts on EAGAIN, which ATTACH returns for a point that has no fence yet: retry on EINTR only */
+static int
+nvmtl_ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, void *arg)
+{
+   int ret;
+   do {
+#ifdef HAVE_XEMAC
+      ret = xemac_ioctl(fd, request, arg);
+#else
+      ret = ioctl(fd, request, arg);
+#endif
+   } while (ret == -1 && errno == EINTR);
+   return ret;
+}
+
+static struct vk_drm_syncobj *
+nvmtl_syncobj_of(VkFence _fence, VkSemaphore _sem)
+{
+   struct vk_sync *sync = NULL;
+   if (_fence) {
+      VK_FROM_HANDLE(vk_fence, fence, _fence);
+      sync = vk_fence_get_active_sync(fence);
+   } else if (_sem) {
+      VK_FROM_HANDLE(vk_semaphore, sem, _sem);
+      sync = vk_semaphore_get_active_sync(sem);
+   }
+   return sync ? vk_sync_as_drm_syncobj(sync) : NULL;
+}
+
+static VkResult
+nvmtl_errno_result(int err)
+{
+   switch (err) {
+   case 0: return VK_SUCCESS;
+   case EAGAIN: return VK_NOT_READY;
+   case ETIME: case ETIMEDOUT: return VK_TIMEOUT;
+   case ENOSPC: case ENOMEM: return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY;
+   case ENOENT: case EINVAL: return VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN;
+   default: return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   }
+}
+
+/* *supported = 1 when the kernel has the surface-fence ioctls (B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES). */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_cap_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t *supported)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct drm_get_cap cap = { .capability = B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES };
+   *supported = 0;
+   if (intel_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap))
+      return VK_SUCCESS;
+   *supported = cap.value == 1;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Attach the fence of `fence` (a binary syncobj), or of timeline semaphore `sem` at `value`, to surface `surface_id`
+ * as a B580_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE or _READ user. VK_NOT_READY: not submitted yet (EAGAIN). */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_attach_v1(VkDevice _device, VkFence fence, VkSemaphore sem, uint64_t value, uint32_t surface_id,
+                            uint32_t flags)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct vk_drm_syncobj *s = nvmtl_syncobj_of(fence, sem);
+   if (!s)
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_attach a = {
+      .surface_id = surface_id, .syncobj = s->syncobj, .point = fence ? 0 : value, .flags = flags,
+   };
+   return nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_ATTACH, &a) ? nvmtl_errno_result(errno) : VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Add the fences of surface `surface_id` that a B580_SURFACE_FENCE_READER or _WRITER must wait for as new points of
+ * timeline semaphore `sem` (one used for nothing else). *wait_value: the point to wait on, 0 when there is nothing. */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_import_v1(VkDevice _device, VkSemaphore sem, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags,
+                            uint64_t *wait_value, uint32_t *count)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   *wait_value = 0;
+   if (count)
+      *count = 0;
+   struct vk_drm_syncobj *s = nvmtl_syncobj_of(VK_NULL_HANDLE, sem);
+   if (!s || !(s->base.flags & VK_SYNC_IS_TIMELINE))
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_import m = { .surface_id = surface_id, .syncobj = s->syncobj, .flags = flags };
+   if (nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_IMPORT, &m))
+      return nvmtl_errno_result(errno);
+   *wait_value = m.count_out ? m.point_out : 0;
+   if (count)
+      *count = m.count_out;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Wait on the CPU until the fences of surface `surface_id` that `flags` names have signaled, or until
+ * `timeout_abs_ns` (CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW; 0 polls). VK_TIMEOUT when it ran out. */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_wait_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags, int64_t timeout_abs_ns)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_wait w = { .surface_id = surface_id, .flags = flags, .timeout_ns = timeout_abs_ns };
+   return nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT, &w) ? nvmtl_errno_result(errno) : VK_SUCCESS;
+}

+}
+
+static struct vk_drm_syncobj *
+nvmtl_syncobj_of(VkFence _fence, VkSemaphore _sem)
+{
+   struct vk_sync *sync = NULL;
+   if (_fence) {
+      VK_FROM_HANDLE(vk_fence, fence, _fence);
+      sync = vk_fence_get_active_sync(fence);
+   } else if (_sem) {
+      VK_FROM_HANDLE(vk_semaphore, sem, _sem);
+      sync = vk_semaphore_get_active_sync(sem);
+   }
+   return sync ? vk_sync_as_drm_syncobj(sync) : NULL;
+}
+
+static VkResult
+nvmtl_errno_result(int err)
+{
+   switch (err) {
+   case 0: return VK_SUCCESS;
+   case EAGAIN: return VK_NOT_READY;
+   case ETIME: case ETIMEDOUT: return VK_TIMEOUT;
+   case ENOSPC: case ENOMEM: return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY;
+   case ENOENT: case EINVAL: return VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN;
+   default: return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   }
+}
+
+/* *supported = 1 when the kernel has the surface-fence ioctls (B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES). */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_cap_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t *supported)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct drm_get_cap cap = { .capability = B580_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES };
+   *supported = 0;
+   if (intel_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap))
+      return VK_SUCCESS;
+   *supported = cap.value == 1;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Attach the fence of `fence` (a binary syncobj), or of timeline semaphore `sem` at `value`, to surface `surface_id`
+ * as a B580_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE or _READ user. VK_NOT_READY: not submitted yet (EAGAIN). */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_attach_v1(VkDevice _device, VkFence fence, VkSemaphore sem, uint64_t value, uint32_t surface_id,
+                            uint32_t flags)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct vk_drm_syncobj *s = nvmtl_syncobj_of(fence, sem);
+   if (!s)
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_attach a = {
+      .surface_id = surface_id, .syncobj = s->syncobj, .point = fence ? 0 : value, .flags = flags,
+   };
+   return nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_ATTACH, &a) ? nvmtl_errno_result(errno) : VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Add the fences of surface `surface_id` that a B580_SURFACE_FENCE_READER or _WRITER must wait for as new points of
+ * timeline semaphore `sem` (one used for nothing else). *wait_value: the point to wait on, 0 when there is nothing. */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_import_v1(VkDevice _device, VkSemaphore sem, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags,
+                            uint64_t *wait_value, uint32_t *count)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   *wait_value = 0;
+   if (count)
+      *count = 0;
+   struct vk_drm_syncobj *s = nvmtl_syncobj_of(VK_NULL_HANDLE, sem);
+   if (!s || !(s->base.flags & VK_SYNC_IS_TIMELINE))
+      return VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT;
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_import m = { .surface_id = surface_id, .syncobj = s->syncobj, .flags = flags };
+   if (nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_IMPORT, &m))
+      return nvmtl_errno_result(errno);
+   *wait_value = m.count_out ? m.point_out : 0;
+   if (count)
+      *count = m.count_out;
+   return VK_SUCCESS;
+}
+
+/* Wait on the CPU until the fences of surface `surface_id` that `flags` names have signaled, or until
+ * `timeout_abs_ns` (CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW; 0 polls). VK_TIMEOUT when it ran out. */
+PUBLIC VkResult
+nvmtl_anv_surface_wait_v1(VkDevice _device, uint32_t surface_id, uint32_t flags, int64_t timeout_abs_ns)
+{
+   ANV_FROM_HANDLE(anv_device, device, _device);
+   struct drm_b580_surface_fence_wait w = { .surface_id = surface_id, .flags = flags, .timeout_ns = timeout_abs_ns };
+   return nvmtl_ioctl(device->fd, DRM_IOCTL_B580_SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT, &w) ? nvmtl_errno_result(errno) : VK_SUCCESS;
+}

+static void
+anv_h265_frame_size_in_ctb(const StdVideoH265SequenceParameterSet *sps,
+                           uint32_t *ctb_w, uint32_t *ctb_h)
+{
+   uint32_t width_in_pix, height_in_pix;
+   anv_h265_frame_size(sps, &width_in_pix, &height_in_pix);
+   uint32_t ctb_size = 1 << (sps->log2_diff_max_min_luma_coding_block_size +
+                             sps->log2_min_luma_coding_block_size_minus3 + 3);
+
+   *ctb_w = DIV_ROUND_UP(width_in_pix, ctb_size);
+   *ctb_h = DIV_ROUND_UP(height_in_pix, ctb_size);
+}
+
+/* CTB address the slice segment starts at, or the CTB count of the picture
+ * for slice_id == naluSliceSegmentEntryCount.
+ *
+ * Slice segments are row aligned and placed by the application through
+ * slice_segment_address. Some applications leave the addresses at 0 though,
+ * in which case the picture is split into evenly sized groups of CTB rows.
+ */
+static uint32_t
+anv_h265_slice_start_ctb(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd,
+                         const VkVideoEncodeInfoKHR *enc_info,
+                         uint32_t slice_id)
+{
+   const struct VkVideoEncodeH265PictureInfoKHR *frame_info = anv_h265_frame_info(enc_info);
+   const StdVideoH265SequenceParameterSet *sps = anv_h265_sps(cmd, enc_info);
+   const uint32_t num_slices = frame_info->naluSliceSegmentEntryCount;
+   uint32_t ctb_w, ctb_h;
+   anv_h265_frame_size_in_ctb(sps, &ctb_w, &ctb_h);
+
+   if (slice_id >= num_slices)
+      return ctb_w * ctb_h;
+
+   bool app_placed = true;
+   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < num_slices && app_placed; i++) {
+      uint32_t addr =
+         frame_info->pNaluSliceSegmentEntries[i].pStdSliceSegmentHeader->slice_segment_address;
+      uint32_t prev = i == 0 ? 0 :
+         frame_info->pNaluSliceSegmentEntries[i - 1].pStdSliceSegmentHeader->slice_segment_address;
+
+      app_placed = (i == 0 ? addr == 0 : addr > prev) &&
+                   addr < ctb_w * ctb_h && addr % ctb_w == 0;
+   }
+
+   if (app_placed)
+      return frame_info->pNaluSliceSegmentEntries[slice_id].pStdSliceSegmentHeader->slice_segment_address;
+
+   return (slice_id * ctb_h / num_slices) * ctb_w;
+}
+

+/* Redirects cmd->batch into a second-level batch so that a
+ * MI_CONDITIONAL_BATCH_BUFFER_END in it only skips the commands recorded
+ * until anv_video_end_sub_batch().
+ */
+struct anv_video_sub_batch {
+   struct anv_batch parent;
+};
+
+static bool
+anv_video_begin_sub_batch(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd, uint32_t size,
+                          struct anv_video_sub_batch *sub)
+{
+   struct anv_state state = anv_cmd_buffer_alloc_temporary_state(cmd, size, 64);
+   if (state.map == NULL)
+      return false;
+
+   sub->parent = cmd->batch;
+   anv_batch_set_storage(&cmd->batch,
+                         anv_cmd_buffer_temporary_state_address(cmd, state),
+                         state.map, state.alloc_size);
+   cmd->batch.extend_cb = NULL;
+   cmd->batch.user_data = NULL;
+   return true;
+}
+
+static void
+anv_video_end_sub_batch(struct anv_cmd_buffer *cmd,
+                        struct anv_video_sub_batch *sub)
+{
+   anv_batch_emit(&cmd->batch, GENX(MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END), bbe);
+
+   struct anv_address sub_addr = cmd->batch.start_addr;
+   VkResult status = cmd->batch.status;
+
+   cmd->batch = sub->parent;
+   if (status != VK_SUCCESS) {
+      anv_batch_set_error(&cmd->batch, status);
+      return;
+   }
+
+   anv_batch_emit(&cmd->batch, GENX(MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START), bbs) {
+      bbs.SecondLevelBatchBuffer = Secondlevelbatch;
+      bbs.AddressSpaceIndicator = ASI_PPGTT;
+      bbs.BatchBufferStartAddress = sub_addr;
+   }
+}
+

FILE: mesa/xe2-venc/0012-anv-re-init-the-HuC-BRC-when-rate-control-parameters.patch
================================================
From 25e396887b34b7925cb8f15ffdf3933016923934 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Emil J. Tywoniak" <emil@tywoniak.eu>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 01:41:26 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 12/18] anv: re-init the HuC BRC when rate control parameters
 change

The HuC BRC only reads the rate control parameters in its init pass,
which runs when the session's frame_counter is 0. frame_counter was only
reset when VK_VIDEO_CODING_CONTROL_RESET_BIT_KHR and
ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL_BIT_KHR came together, but apps change the bitrate
mid-stream with an ENCODE_RATE_CONTROL update on its own. The new
values were stored in the session but never reached the HuC, so the
encoder kept the bitrate it was first initialised with.

SteamVR's vrlink starts low and raises the bitrate as the link allows.
Without stream resets the output stayed pinned at ~10 Mbit/s; with this
change it follows the requested bitrate (~110 Mbit/s observed).

Restart the BRC whenever any rate control parameter actually changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014zf3d6ZuUHNvTB81JRfHds

          rc->rc_flags = h264_rc->flags;
       }

FILE: mesa/xe2-venc/0014-anv-map-HEVC-encode-quality-levels-to-VDEnc-target-u.patch
================================================
From 572154b530bf41ecae7f2641092976a8247bd85c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Emil J. Tywoniak" <emil@tywoniak.eu>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 02:28:00 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 14/18] anv: map HEVC encode quality levels to VDEnc target
 usage

The target usage was fixed to 4. Expose three encode quality levels for
HEVC and pick the target usage from the level the application sets
with vkCmdControlVideoCodingKHR, fastest first like RADV does:

  level 0: target usage 7 (speed)
  level 1: target usage 4 (balanced, the previous fixed value)
  level 2: target usage 1 (quality)

On a B580 at 1152x4608, target usage 7 takes about half the video
engine time of 4 per frame for about 0.3 dB of PSNR, which matters for
low latency streaming.

FILE: mesa/xe2-venc/0015-anv-single-pass-HEVC-BRC-for-the-low-latency-tunings.patch
================================================
From b205fd1ede839a0d2e660f2f943e19fdc1717ad4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Emil J. Tywoniak" <emil@tywoniak.eu>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 02:32:38 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 15/18] anv: single pass HEVC BRC for the low latency tunings

With the HuC BRC every frame gets a second, conditional PAK pass that
re-encodes the frame when the BRC update asks for it. With a tight
virtual buffer that re-encode triggers often and costs a whole PAK
pass plus its latency, which is what the low latency tunings are
asking to avoid. Run a single pass for LOW_LATENCY and
ULTRA_LOW_LATENCY.

B580, 1152x4608, CBR 110 Mbit/s, one frame of virtual buffer:

               video engine/frame   bitrate
  two passes   4.2 - 5.2 ms         87 - 99 Mbit/s
  single pass  3.5 - 3.7 ms         98 - 99.5 Mbit/s

The iHD media driver lands at 3.7 ms and 99 Mbit/s for the same input.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014zf3d6ZuUHNvTB81JRfHds

FILE: mesa/xe2-venc/0016-anv-bound-HEVC-encode-bitstream-writes-to-the-destin.patch
================================================
From 80809902254f58ab391455fff2c2aa12b190d18c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Emil J. Tywoniak" <emil@tywoniak.eu>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 02:35:11 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 16/18] anv: bound HEVC encode bitstream writes to the
 destination range

HCP_IND_OBJ_BASE_ADDR_STATE never programmed the PAK-BSE access upper
bound, so a frame larger than dstBufferRange was written past the end
of the range the application handed in. Program the bound to the end
of the range, rounded down to a page.

Checked by forcing a 64 KiB bound with frames of over 1 MiB: the PAK
stops at the bound and the engine keeps going, without a hang.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014zf3d6ZuUHNvTB81JRfHds

FILE: mesa/xe2-venc/0017-anv-program-the-full-HEVC-LCU-max-bit-size-on-Gfx12..patch
