From 9c0e289b4696904c854e65f3d4971fda6c1d9c3d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Emil J. Tywoniak" <emil@tywoniak.eu>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 02:39:25 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 17/18] anv: program the full HEVC LCU max bit size on Gfx12.5+

lcu_max_bits_size_allowed() needs up to 18 bits (81920 for 8 bit 4:2:0
with 64x64 CTBs) but was masked to 16, so the PAK got 16384. From
Gfx12.5 on HCP_PIC_STATE carries the two MSBs in DW6 bits 18:17, like
the media driver programs them (LcuMaxBitSizeAllowedMsb2its in the
Xe_HPM and Xe2 HCP definitions). Add the field to the Gfx12.5 genxml and
program it.

No visible change in output with the LCU max size report disabled, but
the value is no longer bogus if that is turned on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014zf3d6ZuUHNvTB81JRfHds

FILE: mesa/xe2-venc/0018-anv-use-the-P010-variant-format-for-HEVC-encode-refe.patch
================================================
From 2663375102e864a55764f50d14743c1a38730d93 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Emil J. Tywoniak" <emil@tywoniak.eu>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 02:46:17 +0200
Subject: [PATCH 18/18] anv: use the P010 variant format for HEVC encode
 references

For 10 bit HEVC encode the reconstructed and reference pictures have to
be described as P010 variant, both in HCP_SURFACE_STATE and in
VDENC_REF_SURFACE_STATE; only the raw source is plain P010. This is what
the media driver programs (HevcBasicFeature HCP_SURFACE_STATE and
MosFormatToVdencSurfaceReconFormat). Plain P010 everywhere made the
motion search miss, so every P frame came out about the size of an
IDR frame.

Add the P010 variant value to the VDEnc surface format list (it shares
3 with the old Y8_UNORM name) and program it.

B580, 1152x4608 Big Buck Bunny, 10 bit:

                     before                 after             iHD
  CQP 26             326 Mbit/s  42.2 dB    33 Mbit/s 42.0 dB  35 Mbit/s 41.9 dB
  VBR 80 Mbit/s      102 Mbit/s  31.0 dB    75 Mbit/s 45.3 dB  81 Mbit/s 45.2 dB

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014zf3d6ZuUHNvTB81JRfHds

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/nvrm_off.h

// The driver stays off when the boot picker's "1401: Remove NVIDIA driver" tool asked for it.
// The tool writes -nvoff to boot-args and sets the NVRAM flag nullmoth-remove. OpenCore rewrites boot-args at every
// start (the install lists it under NVRAM Delete), so -nvoff only reached macOS when the user picked macOS in the same
// picker session; anyone who restarted instead got the driver back and the same failed start. The flag is not rewritten
// and stays set until the recover daemon has removed the driver, so it is read too.
//
// Boot guard: a driver that cannot bring its display up must not leave the Mac on a black screen until someone types
// -nvoff. NVRM counts each start in the NVRAM variable nullmoth-nv-starts; NVRMFB clears it the moment the display path
// is up (its first head is lit, or there is no display on this card to light). Two starts in a row that never got that
// far turn the driver off on the next start, exactly like -nvoff: the firmware's framebuffer gives a desktop, and the
// install's recovery puts the previous driver back. Every check is a read, so all parts of the driver agree within a
// boot; only NVRM's start counts. A variable that cannot be written (NVRAM not native) only means the guard never trips.
#pragma once
#include <IOKit/IORegistryEntry.h>
#include <IOKit/IODeviceTreeSupport.h>
#include <IOKit/IOLib.h>
#include <libkern/c++/OSData.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>

#define NVRM_GUARD_VAR "nullmoth-nv-starts"
#define NVRM_GUARD_OK_VAR "nullmoth-nv-ok"
#define NVRM_GUARD_LIMIT 2

static inline unsigned nvrm_guard_starts(IORegistryEntry *options)
{
    OSObject *o = options->copyProperty(NVRM_GUARD_VAR);
    OSData *d = OSDynamicCast(OSData, o);
    unsigned n = (d && d->getLength() >= 1) ? *(const unsigned char *)d->getBytesNoCopy() : 0;
    if (o) o->release();
    return n;
}

static inline bool nvrm_driver_off(void)
{
    char arg[8];
    if (PE_parse_boot_argn("-nvoff", arg, sizeof arg))
        return true;
    IORegistryEntry *options = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/options", gIODTPlane);
    if (!options)
        return false;  // NVRAM not published yet: the boot-arg alone decides, as before
    OSObject *flag = options->copyProperty("nullmoth-remove");
    const bool guard = nvrm_guard_starts(options) >= NVRM_GUARD_LIMIT;
    options->release();
    if (flag) { flag->release(); return true; }
    return guard;
}

// What this boot did to the counter, so the wait exemption below only ever undoes its own increment: true once the
// increment was written (not merely attempted), and the pause state moves 0 -> 1 -> 2 exactly once per boot even with
// one auto-go worker per NVRM instance.
static bool gNvrmGuardCounted;
static volatile SInt32 gNvrmGuardPause;   // 0 not paused, 1 paused (counter taken back), 2 resumed or given up
static thread_t gNvrmGuardPauseOwner;     // the worker that claimed the pause: only it may resume it

// NVRM's start, once per boot: one more start that has not reached its display yet.
static inline void nvrm_guard_count_start(void)
{
    static bool counted;
    if (counted) return;
    counted = true;
    IORegistryEntry *options = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/options", gIODTPlane);
    if (!options) return;
    unsigned char n = (unsigned char)(nvrm_guard_starts(options) + 1);
    if (OSData *d = OSData::withBytes(&n, 1)) { gNvrmGuardCounted = options->setProperty(NVRM_GUARD_VAR, d); d->release(); }
    options->release();
    if (gNvrmGuardCounted)
        IOLog("NVRM: boot guard: start %u without a display so far (the driver turns itself off after %u)\n", n, NVRM_GUARD_LIMIT);
}

// A start that is waiting on purpose (the 10 s Turing settle, the 100 s small-BAR1 wait) must not count as a failed
// start if the Mac is reset meanwhile: the screen shows the boot logo for that long, two resets switched the driver off
// (-nvoff for the next boot) on machines where it works, and the first login then reported the driver as not loaded.
// The count is taken back for the wait and taken again just before the display is armed, so a start that hangs before
// the wait (RM never came up) or after it (the head never lit) still counts. Only this boot's own written increment is
// taken back; a counter nobody wrote this boot, or one that could not be written back, is left alone.
static inline void nvrm_guard_pause_for_wait(unsigned ms)
{
    if (!gNvrmGuardCounted) return;
    if (!OSCompareAndSwap(0, 1, &gNvrmGuardPause)) return;
    gNvrmGuardPauseOwner = current_thread();
    IORegistryEntry *options = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/options", gIODTPlane);
    if (!options) { gNvrmGuardPause = 2; return; }
    const unsigned n = nvrm_guard_starts(options);
    bool written = false;
    if (n >= 1) {
        unsigned char m = (unsigned char)(n - 1);
        if (m == 0) { options->removeProperty(NVRM_GUARD_VAR); written = nvrm_guard_starts(options) == 0; }
        else if (OSData *d = OSData::withBytes(&m, 1)) { written = options->setProperty(NVRM_GUARD_VAR, d); d->release(); }
    }
    options->release();
    if (!written) { gNvrmGuardPause = 2; return; }
    IOLog("NVRM: boot guard: start %u not counted during the %u s wait (a reset now is not a failed start)\n", n, ms / 1000);
}
// Only the worker that took the count back puts it back (a second card's worker, or one whose pause never happened,
// must not resume a pause that is still being written). `guardCleared` is the framebuffer's boot-wide word
// (debug.nvrmfb_guard_cleared) that it already cleared the guard this boot: a display was lit, or the card had none to
// light, after a hand-run go during the wait; counting again then would leave a strike behind a working boot.
static inline void nvrm_guard_resume_after_wait(bool guardCleared)
{
    if (gNvrmGuardPauseOwner != current_thread()) return;
    if (!OSCompareAndSwap(1, 2, &gNvrmGuardPause)) return;
    if (guardCleared) return;
    IORegistryEntry *options = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/options", gIODTPlane);
    if (!options) return;
    unsigned char n = (unsigned char)(nvrm_guard_starts(options) + 1);
    bool written = false;
    if (OSData *d = OSData::withBytes(&n, 1)) { written = options->setProperty(NVRM_GUARD_VAR, d); d->release(); }
    options->release();
    if (written)
        IOLog("NVRM: boot guard: start %u counted again, arming the display (the driver turns itself off after %u)\n", n, NVRM_GUARD_LIMIT);
}

// NVRMFB, once the display path is up: this start counts as good, and the install's trial is over.
static inline void nvrm_guard_display_up(const char *why)
{
    static bool cleared;
    if (cleared) return;
    cleared = true;
    IORegistryEntry *options = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/options", gIODTPlane);
    if (!options) return;
    options->removeProperty(NVRM_GUARD_VAR);
    OSObject *ok = options->copyProperty(NVRM_GUARD_OK_VAR);
    if (ok) ok->release();
    else if (OSData *d = OSData::withBytes("1", 1)) { options->setProperty(NVRM_GUARD_OK_VAR, d); d->release(); }
    options->release();
    IOLog("NVRM: boot guard cleared: %s\n", why);
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gen_stubs.py — one vendor subclass per family base; every pure virtual still open along the base chain becomes a logging stub.
v1 missed the family's own overrides because its regex did not accept `APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE` before the `;`, so it also
   stubbed methods the family implements (getOwningTask → nullptr …). A stub over a real implementation is a silent lie."""
import re
spec = [("NVResource",["IOAccelResource2"]),("NVSysMemory",["IOAccelSysMemory","IOAccelMemory"]),("NVVidMemory",["IOAccelVidMemory","IOAccelMemory"]),
        ("NVSurface",["IOAccelLegacySurface","IOAccelSurface"]),("NVDisplayPipe",["IOAccelLegacyDisplayPipe","IOAccelDisplayPipe"]),
        ("NVGLContext",["IOAccelGLContext2","IOAccelContext2","IOAccelSubmitter2"]),("NV2DContext",["IOAccel2DContext2","IOAccelContext2","IOAccelSubmitter2"]),
        ("NVCLContext",["IOAccelCLContext2","IOAccelContext2","IOAccelSubmitter2"]),("NVVideoContext",["IOAccelVideoContext2","IOAccelContext2","IOAccelSubmitter2"])]
def decls(hdr):
    out=[]
    for l in open("iofam/%s.h"%hdr):
        m=re.match(r"\s*virtual\s+(.+?)\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\((.*?)\)(\s*const)?\s*(= 0)?\s*(APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE)?\s*;", l)
        if m: out.append((m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2), m.group(3).strip(), m.group(4) or "", bool(m.group(5))))
    return out
code=["// GENERATED by gen_stubs.py: one vendor subclass per family base; every pure virtual left open along the base chain is a logging stub.", "#pragma once"]
code+=['#include "%s.h"'%c[0] for _,c in spec]
n_st=0; per={}
for cls, chain in spec:
    implemented=set(); pending=[]
    for hdr in chain:                       # most-derived first: a non-pure redeclaration closes a base's pure
        for t,n,a,c,p in decls(hdr):
            key=(n,re.sub(r"\s+","",a))
            if not p: implemented.add(key)
            elif key not in implemented and key not in [(x[1],re.sub(r"\s+","",x[2])) for x in pending]: pending.append((t,n,a,c))
    code.append("class %s : public %s {\n    OSDeclareDefaultStructors(%s)\n    NM_TAHOE_FWD(%s)\npublic:" % (cls, chain[0], cls, cls))
    for t,n,a,c in pending:
        args=[x.strip() for x in a.split(",")] if a.strip() else []
        named=", ".join("%s a%d"%(x,i) for i,x in enumerate(args))
        ret = "" if t=="void" else (" return true;" if (t=="bool" and n.startswith(("commit","update"))) else " return false;" if t=="bool" else " return nullptr;" if "*" in t else " return 0;")
        code.append("    %s %s(%s)%s APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE { ALOG(\"%s::%s\");%s }" % (t, n, named, c, cls, n, ret)); n_st+=1
    per[cls]=len(pending)
    code.append("};\nOSDefineMetaClassAndStructors(%s, %s)" % (cls, chain[0]))
open("nvaccel_stubs.h","w").write("\n".join(code)+"\n"); print("stubs:", n_st, per)

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/gen_tahoe_fwd.py
================================================
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gen_tahoe_fwd.py NVACCEL_BINARY MISSING_SYMBOLS — writes tahoe_fwd.h for the macOS 26 build.

Tahoe (26) made 27 IOAcceleratorFamily2 methods private and retyped 7 more (unsigned int -> enum), so a kext can no longer
link to them by name. NVAccel never calls them: they only fill vtable slots our classes inherit. The vtable layout itself
is unchanged (every base vtable has the same slot count and order as on macOS 15; checked with tools/vtdump.py against the
26.7.1 KDK), and Apple still exports every base vtable. So for the 26 build each such slot gets an override that jumps
through the base class's exported vtable, which reaches Apple's implementation without naming it."""
import re, subprocess, sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', '..', '..', 'tools'))
from vtdump import vtables
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
BASES = {'NVResource': 'IOAccelResource2', 'NVSysMemory': 'IOAccelSysMemory', 'NVVidMemory': 'IOAccelVidMemory',
         'NVSurface': 'IOAccelLegacySurface', 'NVDisplayPipe': 'IOAccelLegacyDisplayPipe', 'NVGLContext': 'IOAccelGLContext2',
         'NV2DContext': 'IOAccel2DContext2', 'NVCLContext': 'IOAccelCLContext2', 'NVVideoContext': 'IOAccelVideoContext2',
         'NVEventMachine': 'IOAccelEventMachineFast2', 'NVDisplayMachine': 'IOAccelLegacyDisplayMachine', 'NVTask': 'IOAccelTask',
         'NVMemoryMap': 'IOAccelMemoryMap', 'NVAccel': 'IOGraphicsAccelerator2'}
def decls():
    out = {}
    for sub in ('iofam', 're'):
      for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(HERE, sub)):
        if not f.endswith('.h'): continue
        cls = f[:-2]
        for l in open(os.path.join(HERE, sub, f)):
            m = re.match(r'\s*virtual\s+(.+?)\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\((.*?)\)(\s*const)?\s*(= 0)?\s*(APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE)?\s*;', l)
            if m:
                args = [a.strip() for a in m.group(3).split(',')] if m.group(3).strip() else []
                out.setdefault((cls, m.group(2), len(args), bool(m.group(4))), (m.group(1).strip(), args))
    return out
def main(binary, missfile):
    miss = {l.strip() for l in open(missfile) if l.strip()}
    vt = vtables(binary); d = decls()
    dem = lambda xs: subprocess.run(['c++filt'], input='\n'.join(xs), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split('\n')
    h = ['// GENERATED by gen_tahoe_fwd.py for the macOS 26 (Tahoe) build. Do not edit.', '#pragma once', '#ifdef NM_TAHOE']
    defs = []; used = set(); n = 0
    for cls, base in BASES.items():
        slots = vt['%d%s' % (len(cls), cls)]
        decl_lines = []
        for idx, (sym, dn) in enumerate(zip(slots, dem(slots))):
            if sym not in miss: continue
            m = re.match(r'(\w+)::(\w+)\((.*)\)( const)?$', dn)
            owner, name, const = m.group(1), m.group(2), bool(m.group(4))
            arity = 0 if not m.group(3).strip() else m.group(3).count(',') + 1
            ret, args = d[(owner, name, arity, const)]
            params = ', '.join('%s a%d' % (a, i) for i, a in enumerate(args))
            types = ''.join(', ' + a for a in args); call = ''.join(', a%d' % i for i in range(arity))
            c = ' const' if const else ''
            decl_lines.append('    %s %s(%s)%s override;' % (ret, name, params, c))
            # The vtable address is loaded through the GOT: ld -kext leaves a RIP-relative lea to an undefined symbol with no
            # relocation at all (measured: it pointed at 0), while GOT entries get UNSIGNED relocations the kernel linker fills.
            # A naked tail jump through the base vtable slot: every argument and return register passes through untouched,
            # so the reconstructed headers' return types (several are only known as void) cannot truncate a result.
            defs.append('__attribute__((naked)) %s %s::%s(%s)%s { __asm__("movq __ZTV%d%s@GOTPCREL(%%rip), %%r11\\n\\tjmpq *%d(%%r11)"); }'
                        % (ret, cls, name, params, c, len(base), base, 8 * (2 + idx)))
            used.add(base); n += 1
        h.append('#define NM_TAHOE_FWD_%s \\\n%s' % (cls, ' \\\n'.join(decl_lines) if decl_lines else ''))
    h.append('#define NM_TAHOE_FWD(cls) NM_TAHOE_FWD_##cls')
    h += ['#define NM_TAHOE_FWD_DEFS \\'] + ['%s \\' % x for x in defs] + ['/* %d forwarded slots */' % n]
    h += ['#else', '#define NM_TAHOE_FWD(cls)', '#define NM_TAHOE_FWD_DEFS', '#endif']
    open(os.path.join(HERE, 'tahoe_fwd.h'), 'w').write('\n'.join(h) + '\n')
    print('tahoe_fwd.h: %d forwarded slots over %d base vtables' % (n, len(used)))
if __name__ == '__main__': main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])

// NMXAccel: class names for the accelerator built with -DNMX_ACCEL.
//
// Upstream includes this header from nvrm-accel.cpp but does not ship it. This reconstruction renames every
// OSMetaClass the file defines, so NMXAccel can be loaded next to NVAccel without a metaclass name clash. The names
// are the ones in the released NMXAccel.kext (nullmoth-nvidia-2.1.0, Library/NullMoth/kexts/15): its vtables are
// __ZTV8NMXAccel, __ZTV7NMXTask, __ZTV17IOAccelNMXCarrier, ... and the service names it looks up ("NVRM",

// (plugin/nvmtl_vk.c).

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/nmx_heads.h
================================================
/*
 * NMXAccel (kexts/NVRM/accel, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 with the rest of this directory): what the accelerator does
 * about each IntelXeFB head, as a pure function of what it knows, so the same rule drives the late-head arm and the
 * diagnostic sysctl debug.nmxaccel_heads, and can be checked off the machine (tests/nmx_heads_test.cpp).
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 *
 * Design: docs/design/DESIGN-multihead-accel.md.
 */
#pragma once

enum NmxHeadVerdict {
    kNmxHeadAbsent = 0,        // nothing has published at this index
    kNmxHeadPiped,             // handed to the display machine, and a display pipe drives this very framebuffer
    kNmxHeadRegisteredNoPipe,  // handed to the display machine, but no pipe of its own was found (see the log)
    kNmxHeadBootArm,           // the boot-time arm is still pending: it registers every published head with head 0
    kNmxHeadLateArm,           // published after the arm, multi-head knob on: registered now (through IOGraphics' gate)
    kNmxHeadNotReady,          // as kNmxHeadLateArm, but its scan-out does not describe itself yet: retried
    kNmxHeadManual,            // published after the arm, knob off: only `sysctl debug.nvaccelfb=3` registers it (as before)
    kNmxHeadNotArmed,          // the accelerator is not armed (held, failed, -intelxe_noaccel): nothing registers any head
    kNmxHeadBlocked,           // a lower index has not published: the registration walk stops before this one
    kNmxHeadTerminated,        // its framebuffer went away (IntelXeFB stopped); the slot is free for a new one
    kNmxHeadPipedOffline,      // as kNmxHeadPiped, but its framebuffer reports no display: the pipe idles (no resource,
                               // no frames) until a monitor arrives as a connection change
    kNmxHeadVerdictCount
};

struct NmxHeadIn {
    bool published;    // slotted from the IntelXeFramebuffer publish notification
    bool registered;   // found_framebuffer was called for it
    bool piped;        // a display pipe drives it (pipe+0x98 read back)
    bool scanoutOk;    // nvScanoutInfo answered with a CPU mapping and a size
    bool terminated;   // its framebuffer terminated after it was slotted
    bool pipeFB;       // an IntelXeFramebufferPipe (kNmxCapPipeFB): IntelXeFB's second pipe, published at its start
    bool disconnected; // its framebuffer publishes IntelXeFBConnected = false (no monitor); absent = connected
};
struct NmxAccelIn {
    bool knob;               // nmxheads=1 / NVRAM nmx-heads=1 / debug.nmxaccel_heads_auto
    bool armed;              // debug.nvaccelfb reads 1 for real (gNvAccelArmed)
    bool armPending;         // the boot-time arm is waiting or running
    unsigned publishedMask;  // bit i = head i published (gNvHeadsPublished)
};

static inline int nmxHeadVerdict(unsigned idx, const NmxHeadIn &h, const NmxAccelIn &a)
{
    if (h.terminated && !h.published) return kNmxHeadTerminated;
    if (!h.published) return kNmxHeadAbsent;
    if (h.registered) return !h.piped ? kNmxHeadRegisteredNoPipe : h.disconnected ? kNmxHeadPipedOffline : kNmxHeadPiped;
    // registerPendingLocked walks 0, 1, 2, ... and stops at the first index that has not published
    for (unsigned j = 0; j < idx && j < 32; j++)
        if (!((a.publishedMask >> j) & 1u)) return kNmxHeadBlocked;
    // IntelXeFB publishes its second framebuffer at its start (with -intelxefb_pipeb), so it is there for the boot arm.
    // With the knob off the boot walk stops before it, as a head published after the arm waits: only
    // `sysctl debug.nvaccelfb=3` registers it (the knob-off behaviour of the late-publish days)
    if (a.armPending) return (idx != 0 && h.pipeFB && !a.knob) ? kNmxHeadManual : kNmxHeadBootArm;
    if (!a.armed) return kNmxHeadNotArmed;
    if (idx == 0) return kNmxHeadManual;   // head 0 is only ever the boot arm's (or the sysctl's)
    if (!a.knob) return kNmxHeadManual;
    // a head with no monitor is registered as it is (Apple's model: a pipe for every framebuffer; it gets its framebuffer
    // resource at its first mode change); a connected one once its scan-out describes itself
    if (h.disconnected) return kNmxHeadLateArm;
    return h.scanoutOk ? kNmxHeadLateArm : kNmxHeadNotReady;
}
// the boot walk (registerPendingLocked from the boot arm) stops at this head: the second pipe's framebuffer, knob off
static inline bool nmxHeadBootSkips(unsigned idx, bool pipeFB, bool knob)
{
    return idx != 0 && pipeFB && !knob;
}

static inline const char *nmxHeadVerdictName(int v)
{
    switch (v) {
    case kNmxHeadAbsent:           return "absent";
    case kNmxHeadPiped:            return "armed (own display pipe)";
    case kNmxHeadRegisteredNoPipe: return "registered, NO pipe of its own";
    case kNmxHeadBootArm:          return "would be armed by the pending boot arm";
    case kNmxHeadLateArm:          return "would be armed now (multi-head knob)";
    case kNmxHeadNotReady:         return "would be armed once its scan-out describes itself";
    case kNmxHeadManual:           return "waits for `sysctl debug.nvaccelfb=3` (multi-head knob off)";
    case kNmxHeadNotArmed:         return "not armed: the accelerator itself is not armed";
    case kNmxHeadBlocked:          return "blocked: a lower head has not published";
    case kNmxHeadTerminated:       return "terminated (slot free)";
    case kNmxHeadPipedOffline:     return "armed (own display pipe), no monitor: idle until one is connected";
    default:                       return "?";
    }
}

// Per-head capabilities, read from the framebuffer's properties when it publishes. Head 0 (IntelXeFramebuffer) has all of
// them; the second pipe's framebuffer (IntelXeFramebufferPipe) has none: no flips (no nmxScanout), no pipe gamma, no
// hardware cursor, no adaptive sync. With the knob on, a head without a capability is never asked for it.
enum {
    kNmxCapFlip   = 1u << 0,   // IntelXeFBScanoutVersion: nmxScanout map/flip/home
    kNmxCapGamma  = 1u << 1,   // IntelXeFBPipeGammaSize: nmxPipeGamma
    kNmxCapTiming = 1u << 2,   // NVRMTiming: NMXAGDC can answer IOPresentment's link and plane-scaler queries
    kNmxCapPipeFB = 1u << 3,   // an IntelXeFramebufferPipe (the second pipe's framebuffer)
};
// true when the knob is on and head (not 0) lacks cap: the caller skips the call it would make
static inline bool nmxHeadLacks(bool knob, unsigned head, unsigned caps, unsigned cap)
{
    return knob && head != 0 && !(caps & cap);
}

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/nmx_vbldue.h
================================================
/*
 * NMXAccel (kexts/NVRM/accel, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 with the rest of this directory): when a frame the present
 * worker is about to show was due on the panel, as a pure function of what it knows, so it can be checked off the
 * machine (tests/nmx_vbldue_test.cpp).
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 *
 * Design: docs/design/DESIGN-display-boost.md. The present worker waits for the frame's GPU work (nvSurfWaitReady); a
 * frame whose work is still running at the start of vblank it was due at missed that vblank, and the worker tells IntelXe
 * then (i915's intel_display_rps_boost_after_vblank: a wait on the crtc's vblank queue that boosts when the flip's fence
 * has not signalled by the vblank). The frame is due at the first start of vblank after t0, the time the worker took it
 * (its present, or the landing of the frame it waited behind).
 */
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>

// The frame length from the framebuffer's NVRMFlipWaitUs (5/4 of a frame, in us; IntelXeFB publishFlipWait). 0 =
// unknown: no property (nvAccelFlipWaitUs answers 50000 then) or a value that is no refresh rate (24 Hz and up).
static inline uint64_t nmxFrameNsFromFlipWait(uint64_t us)
{
    if (!us || us >= 50000) return 0;
    return us * 1000 * 4 / 5;
}

// The first start of vblank after t0Ns. lastVblNs: a start of vblank the framebuffer saw (0 = no phase known); frameNs:
// the frame length (0 = unknown). Without a phase: one frame after t0 (any interval of a frame holds one start of vblank,
// so a frame not done by then certainly missed one). 0 = unknown (no frame length).
static inline uint64_t nmxVblDueNs(uint64_t t0Ns, uint64_t lastVblNs, uint64_t frameNs)
{
    if (!frameNs) return 0;
    if (!lastVblNs) return t0Ns + frameNs;
    if (lastVblNs > t0Ns) {   // vblanks at lastVbl - j * frame: the earliest that is still after t0
        const uint64_t j = (lastVblNs - t0Ns - 1) / frameNs;
        return lastVblNs - j * frameNs;
    }
    return lastVblNs + ((t0Ns - lastVblNs) / frameNs + 1) * frameNs;
}

// The phase from IntelXeFB's op 4 query (NMXScanout version 4): agoNs since the pipe's last start of vblank at queryNs.
// 0 = no phase (the framebuffer answered ~0: its timestamps do not look live, or it is older).
static inline uint64_t nmxLastVblNs(uint64_t queryNs, uint64_t agoNs, uint64_t frameNs)
{
    if (agoNs == ~0ull || !frameNs || agoNs > 2 * frameNs || agoNs > queryNs) return 0;
    return queryNs - agoNs;
}

        }

    }

            *a2 = (int)(pitch >> ((a1 >= base) ? (unsigned)(a1 - base) : 0u));
        }

    }

    // family's own CPU page-on/off must never run on it; both go to B580's copy engine instead (nmxSVCopy).
    void pageon(IOAccelEvent *, bool) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;

    IOMemoryDescriptor *fApDesc = nullptr;
    // Set by the plugin's surface-dirty escape: the allocation cookie of the VRAM the GPU wrote for this resource. The
    // family's own "VRAM newest" bit can be set on a VRAM copy nothing ever rendered into (freshly allocated,
    // zero-filled); a zero-copy flip of that copy, or a page-off from it, puts a black frame on the panel while the real
    // pixels sit in the surface's system memory. The display pipe compares this with the current allocation's cookie
    // before trusting the family bit, so VRAM re-allocated under the same resource counts as unwritten again (a parked
    // allocation that comes back keeps its cookie, and so its record). 0 = never written.
    unsigned long long fPluginWroteCookie = 0;

    void submitSwapCopy(IOAccelEvent* a0, IOAccelResource2* a1, IOAccelResource2* a2) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE {
        (void)a0;
        nvAccelSwapProbe(a1, a2);
        IOAccelResource2 *src = nvAccelResHasContent(a2) ? a2
                              : nvAccelResHasContent(a1) ? a1 : nullptr;
        if (src && !nvAccelFlipTo(src)) nvAccelCopyToScanout(src);
    }
    void shapeSurface(unsigned int a0, unsigned short a1, unsigned short a2) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE {
        const unsigned w = a1, h = a2;
        uint32_t smode = *(const volatile uint32_t *)((const uint8_t *)this + 0x11B0);
        unsigned bpp = ((smode >> 16) & 0xf) + 1;
        if (bpp < 4 || bpp > 16) bpp = 4;
        unsigned pitch = (unsigned)((w * bpp + 255u) & ~255u);
        unsigned size  = pitch * h;
        IOAccelResource2 **bufs = (IOAccelResource2 **)((uint8_t *)this + 0x11C0);
        unsigned present = 0, shaped = 0;

            if (!(a0 & (1u << i))) continue;
            IOAccelResource2 *r = OSDynamicCast(IOAccelResource2, bufs[i]);
            if (!r) continue;
            present++;
            if (r->initSurfaceBuffer(this, w, h, size, pitch, 0)) shaped++;
        }
        ALOG("NVSurface::shapeSurface(mode 0x%x, %u x %u) smode 0x%x bpp %u pitch %u size %u -> %u present, %u shaped",
             a0, w, h, smode, bpp, pitch, size, present, shaped);

        if (gShapeDumps < 4) { gShapeDumps++;
            const volatile unsigned long long *qq = (const volatile unsigned long long *)((const unsigned char *)this + 0x1160);
            for (unsigned o = 0; o < 0x60; o += 16)
                ALOG("   surf+0x%04x: %016llx %016llx", 0x1160 + o, qq[o / 8], qq[o / 8 + 1]);
        }
    }
    uint32_t getDirtyBufferBitsFromPrivateModeBits(unsigned long long a0) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE { ALOG("NVSurface::getDirtyBufferBitsFromPrivateModeBits(0x%llx)", (unsigned long long)a0); return 0; }
#ifdef NMX_ACCEL
    // Page-flip copy-forward: WindowServer carries the unchanged parts of the last frame into the buffer it is about to
    // draw. The family's own answer is Unsupported, and WindowServer then dropped every frame before its swap
    // ("copy_forward_region: copy forward failed (0xe00002c7) ... disabling", no swap ever reached submitSwapCopy).
    // IOAccelLegacySurface::copy_forward passes the surface's buffer 0 (the one it then prepares for drawing) first.
    IOReturn submitCopyForward(IOAccelEvent *ev, unsigned int flags, IOAccelResource2 *dst, IOAccelResource2 *src,
                               IOAccelBounds const *rects, unsigned int count) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE {
        (void)ev; (void)flags;
        return nvAccelCopyRects(dst, src, rects, count) ? kIOReturnSuccess : kIOReturnUnsupported;
    }
    // B580: the family refuses most WindowServer shapes with "Bad frame buffer index" (the index must be below the
    // display machine's framebuffer count). Log what WindowServer asks for before the family decides.
    IOReturn set_shape_backing_length_ext(eIOAccelSurfaceShapeBits bits, unsigned int fbIndex, unsigned long long addr,
                                          unsigned int rowBytes, unsigned long long length, IOAccelDeviceRegion *rgn,
                                          unsigned long long rgnSize) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE {
#ifdef NM_TAHOE   // macOS 26: IOAccelSurface::set_shape_backing_length_ext is private (and retyped); reach it via the base vtable
        IOReturn r = nmx_super_IOAccelLegacySurface_set_shape_backing_length_ext_7(IOReturn, this, bits, fbIndex, addr, rowBytes, length, rgn, rgnSize);
#else
        IOReturn r = IOAccelLegacySurface::set_shape_backing_length_ext(bits, fbIndex, addr, rowBytes, length, rgn, rgnSize);
#endif
        static volatile SInt32 n = 0, bad = 0;
        SInt32 k = OSIncrementAtomic(&n);
        SInt32 b = r ? OSIncrementAtomic(&bad) : -1;
        if (k < 6 || (b >= 0 && (b < 30 || (b % 1000) == 0)))
            ALOG("NVSurface::set_shape_backing_length_ext #%d: bits 0x%x fbIndex %u addr 0x%llx rowBytes %u length %llu rgnSize %llu -> 0x%x",
                 (int)k, (unsigned)bits, fbIndex, addr, rowBytes, length, rgnSize, (unsigned)r);
        return r;
    }
#endif
};

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/re/IOAccelDevice2.h
================================================
/*
 * IOAccelDevice2 — reconstructed from IOAcceleratorFamily2 (macOS Sequoia, x86_64).
 *
 * Apple ships no header for this class. Everything below was read out of the
 * binary with ../re/vtable.py, not inferred from documentation or guessed:
 *
 *   superclass    __ZN14IOAccelDevice210superClassE relocates against
 *                 IOUserClient::gMetaClass                        -> IOUserClient
 *   class size    OSMetaClass ctor immediate in
 *                 __ZN14IOAccelDevice29MetaClassC2Ev: movl $0x188 -> 392 bytes
 *   vtable        __ZTV14IOAccelDevice2 @ 0x6f100, 311 slots
 *   dispatch      __ZN14IOAccelDevice214sDeviceMethodsE @ 0x6fbb0,
 *                 legacy IOExternalMethod[10], 48-byte stride
 *
 * THE TWO THINGS THAT MUST NOT DRIFT
 *
 * 1. VTABLE ORDER. The three new virtuals occupy slots 302/303/304 and the six
 *    reserved slots follow at 305..310. Declaring them in any other order, or
 *    omitting a reserved slot, moves every later entry. A virtual call then
 *    lands on the wrong function — a panic at runtime, silence at compile time.
 *
 * 2. CLASS SIZE. A subclass's own members start at offset 392. If this header
 *    computes a smaller size, those members overlap IOAccelDevice2's private
 *    ivars and corrupt them. Nothing warns. The static_assert below is the
 *    guard; if it ever fires, re-read the metaclass ctor rather than adjusting
 *    the number to make it pass.
 */

#ifndef _IOACCELDEVICE2_H
#define _IOACCELDEVICE2_H

#include <IOKit/IOUserClient.h>
#include <IOKit/IOService.h>

/*
 * Payload structs. The dispatch table gives their exact SIZES; it does not give
 * their field layouts. They are therefore declared opaque and size-checked —
 * inventing plausible fields would be a guess wearing the costume of a fact.
 * Fill them in only as each one is actually decoded.
 */
#define IOACCEL_OPAQUE(name, bytes)                                            \
    struct name { uint8_t opaque[bytes]; };                                    \
    static_assert(sizeof(struct name) == (bytes), #name " wrong size")

IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceConfigData,        64);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceEventMachineData, 600);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceSurfaceData,       24);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceGlobalObjectIDData, 8);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceTraceFilterData,    8);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceInfoReturnData,    24);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceGIDGroupData,      16);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceAPIProperty,       16);

/* get_name() writes into a caller-supplied buffer of exactly this size. */
enum { kIOAccelDeviceNameSize = 64 };

/* Total object size from the metaclass constructor. */
enum { kIOAccelDevice2Size = 0x188 };

class IOAccelDevice2 : public IOUserClient
{
    OSDeclareDefaultStructors(IOAccelDevice2);

public:
    /* --- OSObject ------------------------------------------------ slot 20 */
    virtual void free() APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;

    /* --- IOService -------------------------------- slots 129,131,186,187 */
    virtual bool requestTerminate(IOService *provider, IOOptionBits options)
        APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
    virtual bool didTerminate(IOService *provider, IOOptionBits options,
                              bool *defer) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
    virtual bool start(IOService *provider) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
    virtual void stop(IOService *provider) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;

    /* --- IOUserClient ----------------------------- slots 268,288,298 */
    virtual IOReturn externalMethod(uint32_t selector,
                                    IOExternalMethodArguments *args,
                                    IOExternalMethodDispatch *dispatch,
                                    OSObject *target,
                                    void *reference) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
    virtual IOReturn clientClose() APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;
    virtual IOExternalMethod *getTargetAndMethodForIndex(IOService **targetP,
                                                         UInt32 index)
        APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;

    /*
     * --- IOAccelDevice2's own virtuals -------------- slots 302,303,304
     * ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Do not reorder, do not insert.
     */
    virtual bool deviceStart();                       /* slot 302 */
    virtual void deviceStop();                        /* slot 303 */
    virtual void orphanClientMappings(OSSet *set);    /* slot 304 */

    /*
     * Reserved padding, slots 305..310. Six, exactly.
     *
     * The argument is "IOAccelDevice", NOT "IOAccelDevice2". The macro pastes
     * className ## index, and the shipping binary exports
     * __ZN14IOAccelDevice223_RESERVEDIOAccelDevice0Ev — i.e. the method is
     * named _RESERVEDIOAccelDevice0. Passing the class's own name yields
     * _RESERVEDIOAccelDevice20, a symbol that exists nowhere, and the kext
     * fails to link with "could not find a kext which exports this symbol".
     * The vtable ORDER is identical either way, so nothing catches this except
     * comparing the emitted names against the binary.
     */
    OSMetaClassDeclareReservedUnused(IOAccelDevice, 0);
    OSMetaClassDeclareReservedUnused(IOAccelDevice, 1);
    OSMetaClassDeclareReservedUnused(IOAccelDevice, 2);
    OSMetaClassDeclareReservedUnused(IOAccelDevice, 3);
    OSMetaClassDeclareReservedUnused(IOAccelDevice, 4);
    OSMetaClassDeclareReservedUnused(IOAccelDevice, 5);

public:
    /*
     * Non-virtual members. These are absent from the vtable, so their order is
     * irrelevant to binary compatibility; they are the targets of the ten
     * entries in sDeviceMethods, reached via getTargetAndMethodForIndex.
     */
    bool init(OSDictionary *properties, task_t owningTask);

    IOReturn get_config(IOAccelDeviceConfigData *out);              /* sel 0 */
    IOReturn get_name(char *out);                                   /* sel 1 */
    IOReturn get_event_machine(IOAccelDeviceEventMachineData *out); /* sel 2 */
    IOReturn get_surface_info(uint32_t id,
                              IOAccelDeviceSurfaceData *out);       /* sel 3 */
    IOReturn set_stereo(uint32_t a, uint32_t b);                    /* sel 4 */
    IOReturn get_next_global_object_id(
                 IOAccelDeviceGlobalObjectIDData *out);             /* sel 5 */
    IOReturn get_current_trace_filter(
                 IOAccelDeviceTraceFilterData *out);                /* sel 6 */
    IOReturn get_device_info(IOAccelDeviceInfoReturnData *out);     /* sel 7 */
    IOReturn get_next_gid_group(IOAccelDeviceGIDGroupData *out);    /* sel 8 */
    IOReturn set_api_property(IOAccelDeviceAPIProperty *inout);     /* sel 9 */

    void stopLocked();
    void detach_device();
    void add_orphaned_mappings(OSSet *set);

    static IOExternalMethod sDeviceMethods[10];

private:
    /*
     * IOAccelDevice2's private ivars, whose layout is not recovered. Their
     * total extent is fixed by the metaclass size; the compiler supplies
     * sizeof(IOUserClient) so this stays correct across OS revisions where the
     * base class changes but 0x188 does not.
     */
    uint8_t _opaque[kIOAccelDevice2Size - sizeof(IOUserClient)];

/*
 * IOAccelerator — reconstructed from IOGraphicsFamily (macOS Sequoia, x86_64).
 *
 * The base of IOGraphicsAccelerator2, which is the class our driver must BE.
 * Apple ships no header.
 *
 * THIS CLASS DOES NOT LIVE IN IOAcceleratorFamily2. It is UNDEFINED there
 * (`nm` shows `U __ZN13IOAccelerator10gMetaClassE`). It lives in
 * IOGraphicsFamily, which Sequoia ships ONLY inside SystemKernelExtensions.kc —
 * there is no standalone binary on disk. Read it with:
 *   vtable.py <kc> --entry com.apple.iokit.IOGraphicsFamily --class IOAccelerator
 *
 * WHERE EACH FACT CAME FROM
 *   size        136 bytes — from the KERNEL'S OWN OSMetaClass registry, read by
 *               the inspector in bench/AccelDevice. NOT from disassembly: inside
 *               a collection the metaclass ctor is awkward to reach, and the
 *               registry is the authority our header must agree with anyway.
 *   superclass  IOService — same source (full chain:
 *               IOService -> IORegistryEntry -> OSObject).
 *   vtable      __ZTV13IOAccelerator, 270 slots, of which only the destructors
 *               and getMetaClass() are its own.
 *
 * WHY THIS ONE IS SAFE DESPITE COMING FROM A COLLECTION
 * A .kc-sourced class normally gets WEAKER verification: prelinked slots are
 * chained pointers whose cacheLevel-0 targets (the kernel's own methods) resolve
 * to nothing, so inherited slots read blank and verify_class.py can only compare
 * what Apple's side resolved. Here that does not matter, because the class adds
 * NO VIRTUALS AT ALL, and that was measured rather than assumed:
 *
 *     Apple's IOAccelerator vtable   270 slots   (vtable.py, --entry)
 *     clang's IOService vtable       269 entries (-fdump-vtable-layouts)
 *
 * vtable.py's count runs exactly one above clang's on every class checked
 * (IOAccelDevice2: 313 vs 312), so these are the SAME LENGTH. A subclass that
 * adds a virtual makes its vtable longer; this one does not. There is therefore
 * no slot ordering to get wrong — only the size, which the kernel confirms.
 */

#ifndef _IOACCELERATOR_H
#define _IOACCELERATOR_H

#include <IOKit/IOService.h>

/* From the kernel's OSMetaClass registry, not from disassembly. */
enum { kIOAcceleratorSize = 136 };

class IOAccelerator : public IOService
{
    OSDeclareDefaultStructors(IOAccelerator);

public:
    /*
     * The only three methods this class adds. NONE of them are virtual — they
     * are absent from the vtable — so their presence here cannot disturb slot
     * ordering. Parameter types are recovered from the mangled names:
     *
     *   __ZN13IOAccelerator13createAccelIDEjPi   (unsigned int, int *)
     *   __ZN13IOAccelerator13retainAccelIDEji    (unsigned int, int)
     *   __ZN13IOAccelerator14releaseAccelIDEji   (unsigned int, int)
     *
     * NOTE: the Itanium ABI mangles static and non-static member functions
     * identically, so the binary cannot tell us which these are. They are
     * declared static here to match the historical IOGraphics headers. This is
     * the one unverified detail in this file — and it is inert, because
     * declaring them generates no symbol reference unless they are CALLED.
     * If you ever call one, confirm the linkage first.
     */
    static IOReturn createAccelID(IOOptionBits options, int32_t *identifier);
    static IOReturn retainAccelID(IOOptionBits options, int32_t identifier);
    static IOReturn releaseAccelID(IOOptionBits options, int32_t identifier);

private:
    /*
     * Layout not recovered; total extent fixed by the registry size. The
     * compiler supplies sizeof(IOService) so this stays correct even if the
     * base changes between SDKs, and the static_assert catches it if not.
     */
    uint8_t _opaque[kIOAcceleratorSize - sizeof(IOService)];
};

static_assert(sizeof(IOAccelerator) == kIOAcceleratorSize,
              "IOAccelerator must be exactly 136 bytes — IOGraphicsAccelerator2 "
              "and every other subclass starts its own members at that offset "
              "and will corrupt the parent's ivars if this is wrong");

#endif /* _IOACCELERATOR_H */

/*
 * IOAccelSharedUserClient2 — reconstructed from IOAcceleratorFamily2
 * (macOS Sequoia, x86_64). Apple ships no header.
 *
 * This is the RESOURCE plane of the Metal driver: allocating GPU memory,
 * shared memory, fences and MTLEvents. Everything a Metal app does that isn't
 * command submission arrives through the 21 selectors below.
 *
 * All of it was READ OUT OF THE BINARY with ../re/vtable.py:
 *
 *   superclass   __ZN24IOAccelSharedUserClient210superClassE relocates against
 *                IOUserClient::gMetaClass                     -> IOUserClient
 *   class size   movl $0x168, %ecx in the metaclass ctor       -> 360 bytes
 *   vtable       __ZTV24IOAccelSharedUserClient2, 310 slots
 *   dispatch     __ZN24IOAccelSharedUserClient214sSharedMethodsE @ 0x77cb0,
 *                IOExternalMethod[21] — length proved by the next defined
 *                symbol landing at exactly table + 21*48.
 *
 * VTABLE ORDER DIFFERS FROM IOAccelDevice2. Here the six reserved slots come
 * FIRST (302..307) and the two new virtuals come AFTER them (308, 309). In
 * IOAccelDevice2 the new virtuals come first and the reserved slots trail. Do
 * not assume a house style — read each class's vtable. Getting this backwards
 * puts sharedStart() where a reserved slot belongs, which is a panic at
 * runtime and silence at build time.
 *
 * Verify any change with:  python3 re/verify_class.py IOAccelSharedUserClient2
 */

#ifndef _IOACCELSHAREDUSERCLIENT2_H
#define _IOACCELSHAREDUSERCLIENT2_H

#include <IOKit/IOUserClient.h>
#include <IOKit/IOService.h>

/*
 * Payload structs. The dispatch table gives exact SIZES but not field layouts,
 * so these are opaque and size-checked. Filling in invented fields would be a
 * guess dressed as a fact; decode them one at a time as they are needed.
 */
#ifndef IOACCEL_OPAQUE
#define IOACCEL_OPAQUE(name, bytes)                                            \
    struct name { uint8_t opaque[bytes]; };                                    \
    static_assert(sizeof(struct name) == (bytes), #name " wrong size")
#endif

IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelSharedPageoffResourceArgs,             8);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelDeviceShmemData,                      16);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelSharedGetInfoReturnData,              16);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelSharedSetupDirtyRingReturnData,       24);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelCreateMTLEventResult,                 24);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelMemoryData,                           48);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelAllocatedSize,                         8);
IOACCEL_OPAQUE(IOAccelResourceSetResourceOwnerIdentityData, 16);

/*
 * IOGraphicsAccelerator2 — reconstructed from IOAcceleratorFamily2
 * (macOS Sequoia, x86_64). Apple ships no header.
 *
 * THIS IS THE CLASS OUR DRIVER MUST *BE*. Everything else in the stack hangs
 * off an instance of this: macOS finds a graphics accelerator by finding an
 * IOGraphicsAccelerator2 attached to a PCI GPU.
 *
 * IT IS AN ABSTRACT CLASS. 17 of its vtable slots are `___cxa_pure_virtual`,
 * and those 17 methods are the ENTIRE required vendor interface — see
 * re/DRIVER-CONTRACT.md. The other 67 new virtuals have working defaults we
 * inherit for free and override only where NVIDIA differs from Apple's model.
 *
 * WHERE EACH FACT CAME FROM
 *   size        3544 bytes — the KERNEL'S OWN OSMetaClass registry (read by the
 *               inspector in bench/AccelDevice), cross-checked against the
 *               `movl $0xdd8, %ecx` immediate in the metaclass constructor.
 *               Two independent sources agreeing.
 *   superclass  IOAccelerator (full chain: IOAccelerator -> IOService ->
 *               IORegistryEntry -> OSObject), from the same registry.
 *   vtable      __ZTV22IOGraphicsAccelerator2 — 84 new virtual slots, 268..351.
 *
 * THE 84 NEW VIRTUALS BELOW ARE MACHINE-GENERATED, IN VTABLE ORDER.
 * Regenerate, never hand-edit:
 *
 *   python3 re/gen_virtuals.py re/x86/IOAcceleratorFamily2 IOGraphicsAccelerator2 268 \
 *     --names re/x86/AMDRadeonX4000:AMDRadeonX4000_AMDGraphicsAccelerator \
 *     --names re/x86/AMDRadeonX4000:AMDRadeonX4000_AMDEllesmereGraphicsAccelerator
 *
 * RETURN TYPES ARE INFERRED, NOT RECOVERED. The Itanium ABI does not encode
 * return types for non-template functions, so they are guessed from naming
 * convention and marked. This is INERT for vtable layout, and on x86_64 every
 * method here returns a pointer or an integer — same ABI register. It would
 * only matter for a struct returned by value or a float return, neither of
 * which appears here. Confirm the return type of any method you IMPLEMENT; the
 * 67 we inherit are unaffected.
 *
 * THE INHERITED OVERRIDES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED. IOGraphicsAccelerator2
 * overrides 14 IOService/OSObject methods (free, start, stop, terminate,
 * finalize, message, newUserClient, getWorkLoop, setProperties, requestProbe,
 * requestTerminate, didTerminate, configureReport, updateReport). Re-declaring
 * them here would be pure risk: they occupy slots that already exist, so
 * declaring them cannot help, while getting ONE signature subtly wrong would
 * create a NEW virtual slot and shift all 84 below it. A subclass can still
 * override any of them directly — they are inherited normally.
 */

#ifndef _IOGRAPHICSACCELERATOR2_H
#define _IOGRAPHICSACCELERATOR2_H

#include "IOAccelerator.h"

/* Referenced across the interface; layouts not needed to subclass. */
class IOAccelAllocationInfo;
class IOAccelClientSharedRO;
class IOAccelClientSharedRW;
class IOAccelCommandDescriptor;
class IOAccelConfig;
class IOAccelEvent;
class IOAccelMemory;
class IOAccelMemoryMap;
class IOAccelResource2;
class IOAccelShared2;
class IOAccelSurface;
class IOAccelSysMemory;
class IOAccelTask;
class IOAccelVidMemory;
class IOFramebuffer;
class IOMemoryDescriptor;
class IOPCIDevice;
class IOSurface;

/* From the kernel's registry, cross-checked against the metaclass constructor. */
enum { kIOGraphicsAccelerator2Size = 0xdd8 };   /* 3544 */

class IOGraphicsAccelerator2 : public IOAccelerator
{
    OSDeclareDefaultStructors(IOGraphicsAccelerator2);

public:
    // NOT PART OF THE GENERATED LIST BELOW. newUserClient is an IOService virtual, so its
    //   vtable slot already exists: declaring it here adds no slot and moves nothing. It is here
    //   because the family DOES override it -- IOAcceleratorFamily2 exports
    //   IOGraphicsAccelerator2::newUserClient(task*, void*, unsigned int, IOUserClient**) at 0x3e34a
    //   -- and this header did not say so. Without it, a subclass override calling
    //   super::newUserClient would resolve all the way up to IOService's default and SILENTLY BYPASS
    //   the family's own user clients: every IOAccelerationUserClient, IOAccelSharedUserClient2 and
    //   IOAccelDisplayPipeUserClient2 the compositor opens to drive us at all.
    virtual IOReturn newUserClient(task_t owningTask, void *securityID, UInt32 type,
                                   IOUserClient **handler) APPLE_KEXT_OVERRIDE;

    /* ---- IOGraphicsAccelerator2's own virtuals, slots 268..351 (84 of them) ----
     * ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND MACHINE-GENERATED. Do not reorder, do not
     * insert, do not delete. Regenerate with re/gen_virtuals.py.
     * Return types are INFERRED — see the note in that script. */
    virtual void acceleratorDidLock(char const*, int);   /* slot 268 */
    virtual void acceleratorWillUnlock(char const*, int);   /* slot 269 */
    virtual uint64_t tmpTotalVRAM();   /* slot 270 */
    virtual uint64_t totalTextureMemory();   /* slot 271 */
    virtual bool isIdle();   /* slot 272 */
    virtual uint64_t getStampMemory(unsigned int*) = 0;   /* slot 273 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual OSObject * createEventMachine();   /* slot 274 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * newEventMachine() = 0;   /* slot 275 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual OSObject * newClientSharedRO();   /* slot 276 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * newClientSharedRW();   /* slot 277 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual void deleteClientSharedRO(IOAccelClientSharedRO*);   /* slot 278 */
    virtual void deleteClientSharedRW(IOAccelClientSharedRW*);   /* slot 279 */
    virtual OSObject * createShared(task*);   /* slot 280 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createSysMemory();   /* slot 281 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createVidMemory(IOAccelShared2*, IOAccelResource2*, unsigned long long, void*);   /* slot 282 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createMemoryMap(IOAccelTask*, IOAccelMemory*, unsigned int);   /* slot 283 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createResource(IOAccelShared2*, unsigned int);   /* slot 284 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createCommandDescriptor();   /* slot 285 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual void deleteCommandDescriptor(IOAccelCommandDescriptor*);   /* slot 286 */
    virtual OSObject * newBlockFence();   /* slot 287 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual void scrubEvents();   /* slot 288 */
    virtual OSObject * createDrawable(IOAccelSurface*, IOAccelShared2*, bool);   /* slot 289 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual void resourceTypeForIOSurface(IOSurface*);   /* slot 290 */
    virtual OSObject * createDisplayPipe(IOFramebuffer*, unsigned int);   /* slot 291 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createMemoryDescriptorWithAddressRange(unsigned long long, unsigned long long, unsigned int, task*);   /* slot 292 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createMemoryDescriptorWithPersistentMemoryDescriptor(IOMemoryDescriptor*);   /* slot 293 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createBufferMemoryDescriptorWithOptions(unsigned int, unsigned long, unsigned long);   /* slot 294 — factory — returns a pointer */
    virtual OSObject * createBufferMemoryDescriptorInTaskWithOptions(task*, unsigned int, unsigned long, unsigned long);   /* slot 295 — factory — returns a pointer */

    virtual void freeWaitToPrepareVidMemory(IOAccelVidMemory*, bool, bool);   /* slot 297 */
    virtual void freeWaitToPrepareVidMap(IOAccelMemoryMap*, bool, bool);   /* slot 298 */

    virtual void acceleratorFinalize();   /* slot 310 */
    virtual void submitSwapCopy(IOAccelEvent*, IOAccelResource2*, IOAccelResource2*);   /* slot 311 */
    /* NON-VIRTUAL (a direct callq in the family, so it takes NO vtable slot and adding it here shifts
       nothing). Measured 2026-09-15: `IOAccelSharedUserClient2::new_resource` calls
       `IOGraphicsAccelerator2::acceleratorWaitEnabled()`, which SLEEPS until bit 0x2 of the flags dword at
       ivar 0xc78 is set — and the only thing that sets it is `enableAccelerator()`, which the family calls
       from `IOAccel[Legacy]DisplayMachine::display_mode_did_change(uint32_t)`. Its whole body is: bail if
       ivar 0xc92 & 8, start the event machine's hardware-progress timer, OR in 0x2. Every allocation on our
       accelerator hung here, in the kernel, for as long as this bit stayed clear. */
    void enableAccelerator();
    void disableAccelerator();
    virtual void populateAccelConfig(IOAccelConfig*) = 0;   /* slot 312 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual uint64_t calcMaxGPUPhysicalMemoryBytes(unsigned long long);   /* slot 313 */
    virtual bool configureDevice(IOPCIDevice*) = 0;   /* slot 314 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual void teardownDevice(IOPCIDevice*) = 0;   /* slot 315 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual OSObject * createKernelGPUTask() = 0;   /* slot 316 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual void systemWillSleep();   /* slot 317 */

    virtual void systemWillChangeSpeed();   /* slot 319 */

    virtual bool configIsHeadless();   /* slot 321 */
    virtual OSObject * newDisplayMachine() = 0;   /* slot 322 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */

    virtual OSObject * new2DContext() = 0;   /* slot 329 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */

    virtual OSObject * newSysMemory() = 0;   /* slot 334 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual OSObject * newVidMemory() = 0;   /* slot 335 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */
    virtual OSObject * newResource() = 0;   /* slot 336 — PURE VIRTUAL, WE MUST IMPLEMENT */

    virtual OSObject * newStatistics();   /* slot 338 — factory — returns a pointer */

    virtual OSObject * createRemoteMemory(IOAccelShared2*, unsigned long long, unsigned int, unsigned int);   /* slot 342 — factory — returns a pointer */

    /* Layout not recovered; extent fixed by the registry size. */

// SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
// nmx_heads_test: offline check of nmx_heads.h (which IntelXeFB heads NMXAccel arms, and when), no GPU needed.
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o nmx_heads_test nmx_heads_test.cpp && ./nmx_heads_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include "nmx_heads.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define EQ(a, b) do { checks++; if ((a) != (b)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: %s = %s, want %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #a, \
	nmxHeadVerdictName(a), nmxHeadVerdictName(b)); } } while (0)
#define TRUE(c) do { checks++; if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #c); } } while (0)

int main()
{
	// fields: published, registered, piped, scanoutOk, terminated, pipeFB, disconnected
	const NmxHeadIn none = {}, pub = { true, false, false, true, false, false, false }, pubNoScan = { true, false, false, false, false, false, false };
	const NmxHeadIn piped = { true, true, true, true, false, false, false }, regNoPipe = { true, true, false, true, false, false, false };
	const NmxHeadIn gone = { false, false, false, false, true, false, false };

	// one monitor, knob off, armed at boot: head 0 piped, nothing else; the knob changes nothing about it
	NmxAccelIn a = { false, true, false, 0x1 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(0, piped, a), kNmxHeadPiped);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, none, a), kNmxHeadAbsent);
	a.knob = true;
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(0, piped, a), kNmxHeadPiped);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, none, a), kNmxHeadAbsent);

	// head 1 published after the arm: knob off = today's manual step; knob on = registered now (or once it scans out)
	a = { false, true, false, 0x3 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, pub, a), kNmxHeadManual);
	a.knob = true;
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, pub, a), kNmxHeadLateArm);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, pubNoScan, a), kNmxHeadNotReady);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, piped, a), kNmxHeadPiped);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, regNoPipe, a), kNmxHeadRegisteredNoPipe);

	// the boot arm is pending (waiting for IntelXeFB, or arming): it takes every published head, knob or not
	a = { true, false, true, 0x3 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(0, pub, a), kNmxHeadBootArm);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, pub, a), kNmxHeadBootArm);
	a.armed = true;   // levels 1/3 written, the arm not finished yet: still the boot arm's
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, pub, a), kNmxHeadBootArm);

	// not armed at all (held by IntelXeFB's guard, -intelxe_noaccel, arm failed): nothing registers a head on its own
	a = { true, false, false, 0x3 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, pub, a), kNmxHeadNotArmed);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(0, pub, a), kNmxHeadNotArmed);

	// head 0 is never the late arm's, even with the knob (a manual or boot registration only)
	a = { true, true, false, 0x1 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(0, pub, a), kNmxHeadManual);

	// a hole: head 2 without head 1 is never reached by the registration walk
	a = { true, true, false, 0x5 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(2, pub, a), kNmxHeadBlocked);
	a.publishedMask = 0x7;
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(2, pub, a), kNmxHeadLateArm);

	// a terminated head frees its slot; a new framebuffer there is a new publish
	a = { true, true, false, 0x1 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, gone, a), kNmxHeadTerminated);
	const NmxHeadIn back = { true, false, false, true, true, false, false };
	a.publishedMask = 0x3;
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, back, a), kNmxHeadLateArm);

	// capabilities: never skipped on head 0, nor with the knob off; head 1 without a capability is skipped with the knob
	TRUE(!nmxHeadLacks(true, 0, 0, kNmxCapFlip));
	TRUE(!nmxHeadLacks(false, 1, 0, kNmxCapFlip));
	TRUE(nmxHeadLacks(true, 1, kNmxCapPipeFB | kNmxCapTiming, kNmxCapFlip));
	TRUE(nmxHeadLacks(true, 1, kNmxCapPipeFB | kNmxCapTiming, kNmxCapGamma));
	TRUE(!nmxHeadLacks(true, 1, kNmxCapFlip | kNmxCapGamma, kNmxCapGamma));

	// IntelXeFB's second framebuffer published at its start, disconnected (no monitor): fields published, registered,
	// piped, scanoutOk, terminated, pipeFB, disconnected
	const NmxHeadIn off = { true, false, false, false, false, true, true };
	const NmxHeadIn offPiped = { true, true, true, false, false, true, true };
	const NmxHeadIn onPiped = { true, true, true, true, false, true, false };
	const NmxHeadIn onNoScan = { true, false, false, false, false, true, false };
	// the boot arm pending: knob on takes it (pipe without a resource), knob off leaves it for debug.nvaccelfb=3
	a = { true, false, true, 0x3 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, off, a), kNmxHeadBootArm);
	a.knob = false;
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, off, a), kNmxHeadManual);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(0, pub, a), kNmxHeadBootArm);   // head 0 always the boot arm's
	TRUE(nmxHeadBootSkips(1, true, false));
	TRUE(!nmxHeadBootSkips(1, true, true));
	TRUE(!nmxHeadBootSkips(0, true, false));
	TRUE(!nmxHeadBootSkips(1, false, false));         // any other head: the walk as before
	// registered: idle while disconnected, armed once a monitor is there
	a = { true, true, false, 0x3 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, offPiped, a), kNmxHeadPipedOffline);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, onPiped, a), kNmxHeadPiped);
	// after the arm, knob on: a disconnected head needs no scan-out to be registered; a connected one still does
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, off, a), kNmxHeadLateArm);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, onNoScan, a), kNmxHeadNotReady);
	a.knob = false;
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, off, a), kNmxHeadManual);
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, offPiped, a), kNmxHeadPipedOffline);   // registered by hand: shown as it is
	// not armed: nothing, connected or not
	a = { true, false, false, 0x3 };
	EQ(nmxHeadVerdict(1, off, a), kNmxHeadNotArmed);

	for (int v = 0; v < kNmxHeadVerdictCount; v++) TRUE(nmxHeadVerdictName(v)[0] != '?');
	printf("%s: %d checks, %d failed\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "ok", checks, fails);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;
}

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/tests/nmx_vbldue_test.cpp

// SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
// nmx_vbldue_test: offline check of nmx_vbldue.h (when a frame the present worker shows was due on the panel), no GPU.
// c++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -I.. -o nmx_vbldue_test nmx_vbldue_test.cpp && ./nmx_vbldue_test
#include <stdio.h>
#include "nmx_vbldue.h"

static int fails, checks;
#define EQ(a, b) do { checks++; const unsigned long long x_ = (a), y_ = (b); if (x_ != y_) { fails++; \
	printf("FAIL %s:%d: %s = %llu, want %llu\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #a, x_, y_); } } while (0)

int main()
{
	const uint64_t f180 = 5555555;   // 180 Hz
	// NVRMFlipWaitUs is 5/4 of a frame: 180 Hz publishes 6944 us; no property (50000) and 0 are unknown
	EQ(nmxFrameNsFromFlipWait(6944), 5555200ull);
	EQ(nmxFrameNsFromFlipWait(50000), 0);
	EQ(nmxFrameNsFromFlipWait(0), 0);
	EQ(nmxFrameNsFromFlipWait(20833), 16666400ull);   // 60 Hz

	// no frame length: unknown; no phase: one frame after t0
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(1000000, 0, 0), 0);
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(1000000, 0, f180), 1000000 + f180);

	// the phase known, the last vblank before t0: the next one after t0
	const uint64_t v = 100000000;   // a start of vblank at 100 ms
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v + 1000000, v, f180), v + f180);            // presented 1 ms after it
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v + f180 - 1, v, f180), v + f180);           // just before the next
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v, v, f180), v + f180);                      // exactly at a vblank: due at the next one
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v + f180, v, f180), v + 2 * f180);
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v + 10 * f180 + 7, v, f180), v + 11 * f180); // the phase from 10 frames back
	// the last vblank after t0 (the query ran after the frame was taken): the earliest vblank after t0
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v - 1000000, v, f180), v);
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v - f180 - 1, v, f180), v - f180);
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v - f180, v, f180), v);                      // t0 on a vblank: the one after it
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(v - 3 * f180 + 5, v, f180), v - 2 * f180);

	// op 4's answer: ~0 (not live), longer ago than two frames, or before the clock's start = no phase
	EQ(nmxLastVblNs(v, 2000000, f180), v - 2000000);
	EQ(nmxLastVblNs(v, ~0ull, f180), 0);
	EQ(nmxLastVblNs(v, 2 * f180 + 1, f180), 0);
	EQ(nmxLastVblNs(1000, 2000, f180), 0);
	EQ(nmxLastVblNs(v, 1000, 0), 0);

	// end to end: the worker took a frame 3 ms after a vblank; the query 1 ms later said 4 ms ago: due 2.56 ms later
	const uint64_t t0 = v + 3000000, q = t0 + 1000000;
	EQ(nmxVblDueNs(t0, nmxLastVblNs(q, 4000000, f180), f180), v + f180);

	printf("nmx_vbldue_test: %d checks, %d failed\n", checks, fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

/*
 * NullMoth NVIDIA driver for macOS
 * Copyright (c) 2026 NullMoth Systems.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 */

#ifndef NVRM_AGDC_K5_H
#define NVRM_AGDC_K5_H
#include <stdint.h>

#define NVK5_CMD_LINKCONFIG   0x921u
#define NVK5_CMD_FBCAPEX      0x711u
#define NVK5_CAP_PLANESCALER  0x10u
// kAGDCFBGetExtendedCapability types IOPresentment asks after the plane scaler (__GatherAGDCDisplayPipelineCapabilities):
// 0x08 pipe scaler, 0x04 linearization, 0x02 gamma, 0x01 CSC. Only the gamma one is answered (NMX, stage 4).
#define NVK5_CAP_GAMMA        0x02u
// One gamma capability entry (same 0x32c record as the plane scaler's; offsets read from IOPresentment's
// IOPresentmentCapabilitiesDisplayPipe::IOPresentmentCreateGammaDictionary): +0 flags, +4 plane mask (u64), +0xc
// NonAtomicApplicationPeriod (float), +0x10 type, +0x14 fixed format, +0x18 configuration ID (u64), +0x20 minimum
// (float), +0x24 maximum (float), +0x28 maximum size (u64, the table length CoreDisplay resamples to).
//   flags 0x4: the entry is applied atomically with the frame (CoreDisplay's EOTF/regamma check requires it unless
//              ignoreEOTFAtomicity is set: IOPCapabilities::SupportsEOTF via DisplayPipe::IsEOTFSupportedInHW)
//   type 0x80: a 3-channel table of 10-bit precision (CoreDisplay's GammaChannelTableEntryCountAndType ranks 0x200 16,
//              0x100 12, 0x80 10, 0x40/0x10 8 bits; 0x3d0 are the 3-channel types). IOPresentment sends tables of the
//              types 0x8/0x10-0x2000 through IOAccelDisplayPipeTransactionSetPipePostGammaTable.
#define NVK5_GAMMA_FLAGS      0x4u
#define NVK5_GAMMA_TYPE       0x80u
#define NVK5_TIMING_TAG       0x4b350001u
#define NVK5_TIMING_WORDS     13

enum { NVK5_T_TAG, NVK5_T_PCLK, NVK5_T_HVIS, NVK5_T_HSS, NVK5_T_HSE, NVK5_T_HTOT, NVK5_T_VVIS, NVK5_T_VSS, NVK5_T_VSE, NVK5_T_VTOT,
       NVK5_T_REFRESH_MHZ, NVK5_T_HSYNCPOS, NVK5_T_VSYNCPOS };

#pragma pack(push, 1)
struct NVAGDCTiming {
    uint32_t hScaledInset, vScaledInset, scalerFlags, hScaled, vScaled, signalConfig, signalLevels;
    uint64_t pixelClock, minPixelClock, maxPixelClock;
    uint32_t hActive, hBlanking, hSyncOffset, hSyncPulseWidth;
    uint32_t vActive, vBlanking, vSyncOffset, vSyncPulseWidth;
    uint32_t hBorderLeft, hBorderRight, vBorderTop, vBorderBottom;
    uint32_t hSyncConfig, hSyncLevel, vSyncConfig, vSyncLevel;
    uint32_t numLinks, vBlankingExtension;
    uint16_t pixelEncoding, bitsPerColorComponent, colorimetry, dynamicRange;
    uint16_t dscBitsPerPixel, dscSliceHeight, dscSliceWidth, field8a;
    uint8_t  tail[8];
};
struct NVAGDCLinkConfig {
    int32_t  id;
    int32_t  groupID;
    uint64_t flags;
    struct NVAGDCTiming timing;
    uint32_t port, stream;
    uint32_t state;
};
struct NVAGDCFBExtCap {
    uint32_t fbIndex, type, count;
    uint8_t  entry[8][0x32c];
};
#pragma pack(pop)
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct NVAGDCTiming) == 0x94, "AGDC timing is 0x94");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct NVAGDCLinkConfig) == 0xb0, "AGDCLinkConfig_t is 0xb0");
_Static_assert(__builtin_offsetof(struct NVAGDCLinkConfig, port) == 0xa4, "stream address at +0xa4");
_Static_assert(sizeof(struct NVAGDCFBExtCap) == 0x196c, "AGDCFBGetExtendedCapability_t is 0x196c");

static inline void nvk5_zero(void *p, unsigned long n) { uint8_t *b = (uint8_t *)p; while (n--) *b++ = 0; }
static inline void nvk5_put32(uint8_t *e, unsigned off, uint32_t v) { e[off] = (uint8_t)v; e[off+1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); e[off+2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16); e[off+3] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); }

static inline int nvk5_timing_bad(const uint32_t *t, unsigned long bytes)
{
    if (!t || bytes != NVK5_TIMING_WORDS * sizeof(uint32_t)) return 1;
    if (t[NVK5_T_TAG] != NVK5_TIMING_TAG) return 2;
    if (!t[NVK5_T_PCLK] || !t[NVK5_T_HVIS] || !t[NVK5_T_VVIS]) return 3;
    if (!(t[NVK5_T_HVIS] <= t[NVK5_T_HSS] && t[NVK5_T_HSS] < t[NVK5_T_HSE] && t[NVK5_T_HSE] <= t[NVK5_T_HTOT])) return 4;
    if (!(t[NVK5_T_VVIS] <= t[NVK5_T_VSS] && t[NVK5_T_VSS] < t[NVK5_T_VSE] && t[NVK5_T_VSE] <= t[NVK5_T_VTOT])) return 5;
    if (t[NVK5_T_HTOT] == t[NVK5_T_HVIS] || t[NVK5_T_VTOT] == t[NVK5_T_VVIS]) return 6;
    return 0;
}

static inline void nvk5_fill_link(struct NVAGDCLinkConfig *l, const uint32_t *t)
{
    int32_t id = l->id; nvk5_zero(l, sizeof *l); l->id = id;
    l->groupID = -1;
    l->flags = 0x8 | 0x1 | 0x2;
    struct NVAGDCTiming *g = &l->timing;
    g->pixelClock = g->minPixelClock = g->maxPixelClock = t[NVK5_T_PCLK];
    g->hActive = t[NVK5_T_HVIS]; g->hBlanking = t[NVK5_T_HTOT] - t[NVK5_T_HVIS];
    g->hSyncOffset = t[NVK5_T_HSS] - t[NVK5_T_HVIS]; g->hSyncPulseWidth = t[NVK5_T_HSE] - t[NVK5_T_HSS];
    g->vActive = t[NVK5_T_VVIS]; g->vBlanking = t[NVK5_T_VTOT] - t[NVK5_T_VVIS];
    g->vSyncOffset = t[NVK5_T_VSS] - t[NVK5_T_VVIS]; g->vSyncPulseWidth = t[NVK5_T_VSE] - t[NVK5_T_VSS];
    g->hSyncConfig = t[NVK5_T_HSYNCPOS] ? 1 : 0; g->vSyncConfig = t[NVK5_T_VSYNCPOS] ? 1 : 0;
    g->numLinks = 1;
    g->pixelEncoding = 0x0001;
    g->bitsPerColorComponent = 0x0002;
    g->colorimetry = 0x0001;
    g->dynamicRange = 0x0001;
    l->port = 1; l->stream = 0;
    l->state = 1;
}
static inline void nvk5_fill_link_port(struct NVAGDCLinkConfig *l, const uint32_t *t, uint32_t port)
{
    nvk5_fill_link(l, t); l->port = port;
}

// The plane-scaler capability: the panel's size, and scale factors 1:1 (0x10001; WAS 0x70007, up to 7x). Nothing in
// this stack implements a plane scaler for IOPresentment, and with 7x it left the scaling of a scaled (HiDPI) mode to
// the pipe before login: the login window was drawn at the scaled size's ratio into a corner of the panel (IntelXeFB
// HiDPI, 0.1.3). With 1:1 WindowServer scales on the GPU there too, as it does after login.
static inline void nvk5_fill_planescaler(struct NVAGDCFBExtCap *c, const uint32_t *t)
{
    uint32_t idx = c->fbIndex, type = c->type; nvk5_zero(c, sizeof *c); c->fbIndex = idx; c->type = type;
    c->count = 1;
    uint8_t *e = c->entry[0]; uint32_t w = t[NVK5_T_HVIS], h = t[NVK5_T_VVIS];
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x000, 0x80004);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x004, 0);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x01c, 1);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x024, h); nvk5_put32(e, 0x028, w); nvk5_put32(e, 0x02c, h); nvk5_put32(e, 0x030, w);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x034, 0x10001);   // scale factors 1:1 (see below)
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x038, 0);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x1a4, 1);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x1ac, h); nvk5_put32(e, 0x1b0, w); nvk5_put32(e, 0x1b4, h); nvk5_put32(e, 0x1b8, w);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x1bc, 0x10001);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x1c0, 0);
}

// gammaSize: the pipe gamma table length the framebuffer can program (0 = none: the gamma query stays unanswered)
static inline void nvk5_fill_gamma(struct NVAGDCFBExtCap *c, uint32_t gammaSize)
{
    uint32_t idx = c->fbIndex, type = c->type; nvk5_zero(c, sizeof *c); c->fbIndex = idx; c->type = type;
    c->count = 1;
    uint8_t *e = c->entry[0];
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x00, NVK5_GAMMA_FLAGS);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x04, 1);                 // plane mask: plane 0, the only plane the plane-scaler answer lists
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x08, 0);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x0c, 0);                 // NonAtomicApplicationPeriod 0.0f
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x10, NVK5_GAMMA_TYPE);
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x14, 0);                 // no fixed format
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x20, 0);                 // minimum 0.0f
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x24, 0x3f800000u);       // maximum 1.0f
    nvk5_put32(e, 0x28, gammaSize);         // maximum size (u64, high word 0)
}

#define NVK5_R_UNSUPPORTED  0
#define NVK5_R_LINK         1
#define NVK5_R_CAPS         2
#define NVK5_R_GAMMA        3
#define NVK5_R_BADARG     (-1)
#define NVK5_R_NOTFOUND   (-2)
struct nvk5_head { const uint32_t *t; unsigned long tBytes; uint32_t gammaSize; };
static inline int nvk5_answer_heads(unsigned cmd, const void *in, unsigned long inSize, void *out, unsigned long outSize,
                                    const struct nvk5_head *h, unsigned nh, int *why, int32_t *idxOut)
{
    *idxOut = -1;
    if (cmd != NVK5_CMD_LINKCONFIG && cmd != NVK5_CMD_FBCAPEX) return NVK5_R_UNSUPPORTED;
    const int link = cmd == NVK5_CMD_LINKCONFIG;
    const unsigned long want = link ? sizeof(struct NVAGDCLinkConfig) : sizeof(struct NVAGDCFBExtCap);
    if (!out || outSize != want) { *why = link ? 0x10 : 0x20; return NVK5_R_BADARG; }
    if (!in || inSize != want) { *why = link ? 0x12 : 0x22; return NVK5_R_BADARG; }
    if (in != out) {
        const uint8_t *s = (const uint8_t *)in; uint8_t *d = (uint8_t *)out; unsigned long n = want;
        if (d < s) while (n--) *d++ = *s++; else while (n--) d[n] = s[n];
    }
    uint32_t idx = link ? (uint32_t)((struct NVAGDCLinkConfig *)out)->id : ((struct NVAGDCFBExtCap *)out)->fbIndex;
    *idxOut = (int32_t)idx;
    const uint32_t ctype = link ? 0 : ((struct NVAGDCFBExtCap *)out)->type;
    if (!link && ctype != NVK5_CAP_PLANESCALER && ctype != NVK5_CAP_GAMMA) return NVK5_R_UNSUPPORTED;
    if (!link && ctype == NVK5_CAP_GAMMA && (idx >= nh || !h[idx].gammaSize)) return NVK5_R_UNSUPPORTED;
    if (idx >= nh) { *why = link ? 0x11 : 0x21; return NVK5_R_BADARG; }
    const uint32_t *t = h[idx].t;
    int bad = t ? nvk5_timing_bad(t, h[idx].tBytes) : 0x31;
    if (bad) { *why = bad; return NVK5_R_NOTFOUND; }
    if (link) { nvk5_fill_link_port((struct NVAGDCLinkConfig *)out, t, 1u + idx); return NVK5_R_LINK; }
    if (ctype == NVK5_CAP_GAMMA) { nvk5_fill_gamma((struct NVAGDCFBExtCap *)out, h[idx].gammaSize); return NVK5_R_GAMMA; }
    nvk5_fill_planescaler((struct NVAGDCFBExtCap *)out, t); return NVK5_R_CAPS;
}
static inline int nvk5_answer(unsigned cmd, const void *in, unsigned long inSize, void *out, unsigned long outSize,
                              const uint32_t *t, unsigned long tBytes, int *why)
{
    struct nvk5_head h0 = { t, tBytes, 0 }; int32_t idx;
    return nvk5_answer_heads(cmd, in, inSize, out, outSize, &h0, 1, why, &idx);
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/kexts/NVRMAGDC/nvrm_off.h

// The driver stays off when the boot picker's "1401: Remove NVIDIA driver" tool asked for it.
// The tool writes -nvoff to boot-args and sets the NVRAM flag nullmoth-remove. OpenCore rewrites boot-args at every
// start (the install lists it under NVRAM Delete), so -nvoff only reached macOS when the user picked macOS in the same
// picker session; anyone who restarted instead got the driver back and the same failed start. The flag is not rewritten
// and stays set until the recover daemon has removed the driver, so it is read too.
#pragma once
#include <IOKit/IORegistryEntry.h>
#include <IOKit/IODeviceTreeSupport.h>
#include <pexpert/pexpert.h>

static inline bool nvrm_driver_off(void)
{
    char arg[8];
    if (PE_parse_boot_argn("-nvoff", arg, sizeof arg))
        return true;
    IORegistryEntry *options = IORegistryEntry::fromPath("/options", gIODTPlane);
    if (!options)
        return false;  // NVRAM not published yet: the boot-arg alone decides, as before
    OSObject *flag = options->copyProperty("nullmoth-remove");
    options->release();
    if (!flag)
        return false;
    flag->release();
    return true;
}

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/air_dis.c

/* nvmtl-air-dis -S <in.air> -o <out.ll>: print a Metal AIR bitcode module as LLVM assembly.
 *
 * The plugin decodes AIR in process with the LLVM library it ships (air-runtime/libLLVM.dylib, upstream LLVM). When that
 * is not possible (a library over the in-process size cap, or a reader the plugin could not load), it runs this tool, so
 * a malformed module costs a failed translation instead of the app. It uses the same upstream library, found next to
 * this executable, and therefore prints exactly what the in-process path prints. Arguments are the ones the plugin
 * passes; anything else is refused. Exit 0 on success, 1 on a parse or write failure, 2 on bad arguments or setup. */
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <limits.h>
#include <mach-o/dyld.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

/* Out of process the size cap is only a memory bound, far above any shader library a real app ships. */
#define AIR_DIS_MAX_BYTES (1024L * 1024L * 1024L)

static int g_error;
static int (*p_severity)(void *);
static void on_diagnostic(void *d, void *ctx) { (void)ctx; if (p_severity && p_severity(d) == 0) g_error = 1; }

static int library_path(char *out, size_t cap) {
    char exe[PATH_MAX], real[PATH_MAX];
    uint32_t n = sizeof exe;
    if (_NSGetExecutablePath(exe, &n) != 0 || !realpath(exe, real)) return -1;
    char *slash = strrchr(real, '/');
    if (!slash) return -1;
    *slash = 0;
    return snprintf(out, cap, "%s/air-runtime/libLLVM.dylib", real) < (int)cap ? 0 : -1;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc != 5 || strcmp(argv[1], "-S") || strcmp(argv[3], "-o")) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: nvmtl-air-dis -S <in.air> -o <out.ll>\n");
        return 2;
    }
    const char *in = argv[2], *out = argv[4];
    char lib[PATH_MAX];
    if (library_path(lib, sizeof lib)) { fprintf(stderr, "cannot locate air-runtime\n"); return 2; }
    void *h = dlopen(lib, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
    if (!h) { fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", dlerror()); return 2; }
    void *(*ctx_create)(void) = dlsym(h, "LLVMContextCreate");
    void (*ctx_dispose)(void *) = dlsym(h, "LLVMContextDispose");
    void (*set_handler)(void *, void (*)(void *, void *), void *) = dlsym(h, "LLVMContextSetDiagnosticHandler");
    void *(*buf_copy)(const char *, size_t, const char *, int) = dlsym(h, "LLVMCreateMemoryBufferWithMemoryRangeCopy");
    void (*buf_dispose)(void *) = dlsym(h, "LLVMDisposeMemoryBuffer");
    int (*parse)(void *, void *, void **) = dlsym(h, "LLVMParseBitcodeInContext2");
    int (*print)(void *, const char *, char **) = dlsym(h, "LLVMPrintModuleToFile");
    void (*mod_dispose)(void *) = dlsym(h, "LLVMDisposeModule");
    void (*msg_dispose)(char *) = dlsym(h, "LLVMDisposeMessage");
    p_severity = dlsym(h, "LLVMGetDiagInfoSeverity");
    if (!ctx_create || !ctx_dispose || !set_handler || !buf_copy || !buf_dispose || !parse || !print || !mod_dispose || !msg_dispose) {
        fprintf(stderr, "air-runtime lacks a required LLVM entry point\n");
        return 2;
    }
    FILE *f = fopen(in, "rb");
    struct stat st;
    if (!f || fstat(fileno(f), &st) || !S_ISREG(st.st_mode) || st.st_size < 4 || st.st_size > AIR_DIS_MAX_BYTES) {
        fprintf(stderr, "cannot read %s as a bitcode file\n", in);
        if (f) fclose(f);
        return 1;
    }
    char *bytes = malloc((size_t)st.st_size);
    size_t got = bytes ? fread(bytes, 1, (size_t)st.st_size, f) : 0;
    fclose(f);
    if (got != (size_t)st.st_size) { fprintf(stderr, "short read on %s\n", in); free(bytes); return 1; }

    void *ctx = ctx_create();
    set_handler(ctx, on_diagnostic, NULL);
    void *buf = buf_copy(bytes, got, "nvmtl-air", 0), *module = NULL;
    free(bytes);
    int rc = 1;
    g_error = 0;
    if (buf && !parse(ctx, buf, &module) && module && !g_error) {
        char *msg = NULL;
        if (print(module, out, &msg) == 0) rc = 0;
        else fprintf(stderr, "cannot write %s: %s\n", out, msg ? msg : "?");
        if (msg) msg_dispose(msg);
    } else {
        fprintf(stderr, "%s is not a bitcode module this LLVM can read\n", in);
    }
    if (module) mod_dispose(module);
    if (buf) buf_dispose(buf);   /* LLVMParseBitcodeInContext2 copies what it needs; the buffer stays ours */
    ctx_dispose(ctx);
    if (rc) remove(out);
    return rc;
}

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvconv.metal
