/*
 * NullMoth NVIDIA driver for macOS
 * Copyright (c) 2026 NullMoth Systems.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 */

#include <metal_stdlib>
using namespace metal;

constant uint BK = 16;

template <uint BM, uint BN, uint TM, uint TN>
static inline void nvconv_body(device const float *src ,
                         device const float *wts ,
                         device float *dst , device const float *bias, device const float *res, uint epi,
                         constant uint *kp ,
                         constant uint *cp ,
                         uint3 tgp, uint lid, threadgroup float (*As)[BM + 4], threadgroup float (*Bs)[BN + 4])
{
    const uint cin = cp[32], cout = cp[33], kw = cp[34], kh = cp[35], batch = cp[37];
    const uint sw = cp[38], sh = cp[39], dw = cp[40], dh = cp[41];
    const int offx = as_type<int>(cp[44]), offy = as_type<int>(cp[45]);
    const uint strx = cp[46], stry = cp[47], dilx = cp[48], dily = cp[49];
    const uint sC = kp[8], sW = kp[9], sH = kp[10], sN = kp[11];
    const uint wCo = kp[28], wCi = kp[29], wKw = kp[30], wKh = kp[31];
    const uint ob0 = res ? 80u : bias ? 60u : 40u;
    const uint oC = kp[ob0 + 8], oW = kp[ob0 + 9], oH = kp[ob0 + 10], oN = kp[ob0 + 11];

    const uint M = batch * dh * dw, N = cout, K = kh * kw * cin;
    const uint m0 = tgp.x * BM, n0 = tgp.y * BN;
    const bool fast = (cin % BK) == 0;

    const uint ACNT = BK * BM / 256, akk = lid % BK, amm0 = lid / BK;
    uint am_n[ACNT]; int am_bx[ACNT], am_by[ACNT]; bool am_ok[ACNT];
    for (uint i = 0; i < ACNT; i++) {
        const uint am = m0 + amm0 + 16 * i;
        am_ok[i] = am < M;
        const uint aox = am % dw, at2 = am / dw, aoy = at2 % dh;
        am_n[i] = at2 / dh; am_bx[i] = int(aox * strx) + offx; am_by[i] = int(aoy * stry) + offy;
    }
    const uint BCNT = BK * BN / 256, bkk = lid / (BN / BCNT), bnn = (lid % (BN / BCNT)) * BCNT;

    const uint tx = lid % 16, ty = lid / 16;
    float acc[TM][TN] = {{0}};

    for (uint k0 = 0; k0 < K; k0 += BK) {
        uint tci0 = 0, tix = 0, tiy = 0;
        if (fast) { tci0 = k0 % cin; const uint t = k0 / cin; tix = t % kw; tiy = t / kw; }
        {
            const uint k = k0 + akk;
            uint ci = 0, ix = 0, iy = 0;
            const bool kok = k < K;
            if (kok) {
                if (fast) { ci = tci0 + akk; ix = tix; iy = tiy; }
                else { ci = k % cin; const uint t = k / cin; ix = t % kw; iy = t / kw; }
            }
            for (uint i = 0; i < ACNT; i++) {
                float v = 0.0f;
                if (kok && am_ok[i]) {
                    const int x = am_bx[i] + int(ix * dilx), y = am_by[i] + int(iy * dily);
                    if (x >= 0 && y >= 0 && uint(x) < sw && uint(y) < sh) v = src[ci * sC + uint(x) * sW + uint(y) * sH + am_n[i] * sN];
                }
                As[akk][amm0 + 16 * i] = v;
            }
        }
        {
            const uint k = k0 + bkk;
            float v[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
            if (k < K) {
                uint ci, ix, iy;
                if (fast) { ci = tci0 + bkk; ix = tix; iy = tiy; }
                else { ci = k % cin; const uint t = k / cin; ix = t % kw; iy = t / kw; }
                const uint base = ci * wCi + ix * wKw + iy * wKh;
                for (uint j = 0; j < BCNT; j++) { const uint co = n0 + bnn + j; v[j] = co < N ? wts[co * wCo + base] : 0.0f; }
            }
            for (uint j = 0; j < BCNT; j++) Bs[bkk][bnn + j] = v[j];
        }
        threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
        for (uint kk = 0; kk < BK; kk++) {
            float a[TM], b[TN];
            for (uint i = 0; i < TM; i++) a[i] = As[kk][ty * TM + i];
            for (uint j = 0; j < TN; j++) b[j] = Bs[kk][tx * TN + j];
            for (uint i = 0; i < TM; i++) for (uint j = 0; j < TN; j++) acc[i][j] = fma(a[i], b[j], acc[i][j]);
        }
        threadgroup_barrier(mem_flags::mem_threadgroup);
    }
    for (uint i = 0; i < TM; i++) {
        const uint m = m0 + ty * TM + i;
        if (m >= M) continue;
        const uint ox = m % dw, t2 = m / dw, oy = t2 % dh, n = t2 / dh;
        const uint ob = ox * oW + oy * oH + n * oN;
        for (uint j = 0; j < TN; j++) {
            const uint co = n0 + tx * TN + j;
            if (co >= N) continue;
            float v = acc[i][j];
            if (epi == 4) { v = v > 0.0f ? v : v * (bias ? bias[co] : 0.0f); }
            else {
                v += bias ? bias[co] : 0.0f;
                if (epi == 1) v = max(v, 0.0f); else if (epi == 2) v = clamp(v, 0.0f, 6.0f); else if (epi == 3) v = 1.0f / (1.0f + exp(-v));
            }
            if (res) v += res[co * oC + ob];
            dst[co * oC + ob] = v;
        }
    }
}

kernel void nvconv3_b(device const float *src [[buffer(0)]], device const float *wts [[buffer(1)]], device float *dst [[buffer(2)]],
                      constant uint *kp [[buffer(23)]], constant uint *cp [[buffer(29)]], constant uint &epi [[buffer(30)]],
                      uint3 tgp [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]], uint lid [[thread_index_in_threadgroup]])
{ threadgroup float As[BK][128 + 4]; threadgroup float Bs[BK][64 + 4]; nvconv_body<128, 64, 8, 4>(src, wts, dst, nullptr, nullptr, epi, kp, cp, tgp, lid, As, Bs); }
kernel void nvconv3_s(device const float *src [[buffer(0)]], device const float *wts [[buffer(1)]], device float *dst [[buffer(2)]],
                      constant uint *kp [[buffer(23)]], constant uint *cp [[buffer(29)]], constant uint &epi [[buffer(30)]],
                      uint3 tgp [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]], uint lid [[thread_index_in_threadgroup]])
{ threadgroup float As[BK][64 + 4]; threadgroup float Bs[BK][32 + 4]; nvconv_body<64, 32, 4, 2>(src, wts, dst, nullptr, nullptr, epi, kp, cp, tgp, lid, As, Bs); }
kernel void nvconv4_b(device const float *src [[buffer(0)]], device const float *wts [[buffer(1)]], device const float *bias [[buffer(2)]],
                      device float *dst [[buffer(3)]], constant uint *kp [[buffer(23)]], constant uint *cp [[buffer(29)]], constant uint &epi [[buffer(30)]],
                      uint3 tgp [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]], uint lid [[thread_index_in_threadgroup]])
{ threadgroup float As[BK][128 + 4]; threadgroup float Bs[BK][64 + 4]; nvconv_body<128, 64, 8, 4>(src, wts, dst, bias, nullptr, epi, kp, cp, tgp, lid, As, Bs); }
kernel void nvconv4_s(device const float *src [[buffer(0)]], device const float *wts [[buffer(1)]], device const float *bias [[buffer(2)]],
                      device float *dst [[buffer(3)]], constant uint *kp [[buffer(23)]], constant uint *cp [[buffer(29)]], constant uint &epi [[buffer(30)]],
                      uint3 tgp [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]], uint lid [[thread_index_in_threadgroup]])
{ threadgroup float As[BK][64 + 4]; threadgroup float Bs[BK][32 + 4]; nvconv_body<64, 32, 4, 2>(src, wts, dst, bias, nullptr, epi, kp, cp, tgp, lid, As, Bs); }
kernel void nvconv5_b(device const float *src [[buffer(0)]], device const float *wts [[buffer(1)]], device const float *bias [[buffer(2)]],
                      device const float *res [[buffer(3)]], device float *dst [[buffer(4)]], constant uint *kp [[buffer(23)]], constant uint *cp [[buffer(29)]],
                      constant uint &epi [[buffer(30)]], uint3 tgp [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]], uint lid [[thread_index_in_threadgroup]])
{ threadgroup float As[BK][128 + 4]; threadgroup float Bs[BK][64 + 4]; nvconv_body<128, 64, 8, 4>(src, wts, dst, bias, res, epi, kp, cp, tgp, lid, As, Bs); }
kernel void nvconv5_s(device const float *src [[buffer(0)]], device const float *wts [[buffer(1)]], device const float *bias [[buffer(2)]],
                      device const float *res [[buffer(3)]], device float *dst [[buffer(4)]], constant uint *kp [[buffer(23)]], constant uint *cp [[buffer(29)]],
                      constant uint &epi [[buffer(30)]], uint3 tgp [[threadgroup_position_in_grid]], uint lid [[thread_index_in_threadgroup]])
{ threadgroup float As[BK][64 + 4]; threadgroup float Bs[BK][32 + 4]; nvconv_body<64, 32, 4, 2>(src, wts, dst, bias, res, epi, kp, cp, tgp, lid, As, Bs); }
kernel void nvconv_cmp(device const float *a [[buffer(5)]], device const float *b [[buffer(6)]], device atomic_uint *bad [[buffer(7)]],
                       constant uint &n [[buffer(8)]], device float *sample [[buffer(9)]], uint gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])
{
    if (gid >= n) return;
    const float x = a[gid], y = b[gid];
    if (gid < 6) { sample[gid * 2] = x; sample[gid * 2 + 1] = y; }
    if (!(fabs(x - y) <= 1e-3f * fabs(x) + 1e-4f)) atomic_fetch_add_explicit(bad, 1u, memory_order_relaxed);
}

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_cache_file.h

/* nvmtl_cache_file.h - shader-cache files that prove they are whole.
   A cache entry is read back by a later process and trusted: a shader that is short, torn or from a half-finished write
   is a wrong shader, not a missing one. Every entry is written as <payload><footer>, where the footer holds a magic,
   the payload length and a 64-bit hash of the payload. A reader accepts the file only when all three agree and otherwise
   deletes it, so the next lookup translates again. The write goes to a temporary file in the same folder and only then is
   renamed over the final name, so no process ever sees a partial file under the final name.
   IntelXe (nm29): the temporary file is NOT flushed (fsync / F_FULLFSYNC) before the rename. Safari's WebKit GPU process
   sandbox (macOS 26) refuses fsync, F_FULLFSYNC and renamex_np, and a store that needs them is a store that never
   happens (NVMTLLibraryLoad.m, nvmtl_store_file). The footer is what proves an entry whole: a renamed file whose data did
   not reach the disk before a crash fails its length or hash check, is removed, and is translated again.
   An entry without a footer (written by an older driver) is not trusted: it reads as missing and is removed.
   Pure C over file descriptors, so tools/test_cache_file.c proves it without the plugin. */
/* From nullmoth 2.9 (52a62bf, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0), changed for IntelXe as noted below. */
#ifndef NVMTL_CACHE_FILE_H
#define NVMTL_CACHE_FILE_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#define NVMTL_CF_FOOTER 16u
#define NVMTL_CF_MAGIC 0x31464356u   /* "VCF1" little-endian */

static inline uint64_t nvmtl_cf_hash(const uint8_t *p, size_t n)
{
    uint64_t h = 1469598103934665603ull;   /* FNV-1a, 64-bit */
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) { h ^= p[i]; h *= 1099511628211ull; }
    return h;
}

/* Why a file was refused, for the log. */
typedef enum { NVMTL_CF_OK = 0, NVMTL_CF_MISSING, NVMTL_CF_SHORT, NVMTL_CF_NO_FOOTER, NVMTL_CF_LENGTH, NVMTL_CF_HASH } nvmtl_cf_status;
static inline const char *nvmtl_cf_why(nvmtl_cf_status s)
{
    switch (s) { case NVMTL_CF_OK: return "ok"; case NVMTL_CF_MISSING: return "missing"; case NVMTL_CF_SHORT: return "shorter than a footer";
                 case NVMTL_CF_NO_FOOTER: return "no footer (written by an older driver, or cut short)";
                 case NVMTL_CF_LENGTH: return "payload length does not match the file"; default: return "payload hash does not match"; }
}

/* Checks a file image; on NVMTL_CF_OK *payload_len is the payload's length (the payload is the file's first bytes). */
static inline nvmtl_cf_status nvmtl_cf_check(const uint8_t *file, size_t size, size_t *payload_len)
{
    if (size < NVMTL_CF_FOOTER) return NVMTL_CF_SHORT;
    const uint8_t *f = file + size - NVMTL_CF_FOOTER;
    uint32_t magic, len; uint64_t hash;
    memcpy(&magic, f, 4); memcpy(&len, f + 4, 4); memcpy(&hash, f + 8, 8);
    if (magic != NVMTL_CF_MAGIC) return NVMTL_CF_NO_FOOTER;
    if ((size_t)len != size - NVMTL_CF_FOOTER) return NVMTL_CF_LENGTH;
    if (nvmtl_cf_hash(file, len) != hash) return NVMTL_CF_HASH;
    if (payload_len) *payload_len = len;
    return NVMTL_CF_OK;
}

/* Reads and verifies `path`. Returns a malloc'd payload (caller frees) or NULL with *status set. A file that fails the
   check is removed so the next lookup translates it again; a file that simply is not there is left alone. */
static inline uint8_t *nvmtl_cf_read(const char *path, size_t *payload_len, nvmtl_cf_status *status)
{
    nvmtl_cf_status st = NVMTL_CF_MISSING; uint8_t *buf = NULL; size_t len = 0;
    int fd = open(path, O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC);
    if (fd < 0) { if (status) *status = NVMTL_CF_MISSING; return NULL; }
    struct stat sb;
    if (!fstat(fd, &sb) && sb.st_size >= 0) {
        len = (size_t)sb.st_size; buf = malloc(len ? len : 1);
        size_t got = 0;
        while (buf && got < len) { ssize_t r = read(fd, buf + got, len - got); if (r > 0) got += (size_t)r; else if (r < 0 && errno == EINTR) continue; else break; }
        if (buf && got == len) st = nvmtl_cf_check(buf, len, payload_len);
        else st = NVMTL_CF_SHORT;
    }
    close(fd);
    if (st != NVMTL_CF_OK) { free(buf); buf = NULL; unlink(path); }
    if (status) *status = st;
    return buf;
}

/* Writes payload+footer to a temporary file beside `path` and renames it into place. Returns 0, or an errno. */
static inline int nvmtl_cf_write(const char *path, const void *payload, size_t n)
{
    if (n > 0xffffffffu) return EFBIG;
    char tmp[1100];
    static unsigned seq;
    int k = snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s.tmp-%d-%u", path, (int)getpid(), __atomic_fetch_add(&seq, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED));
    if (k <= 0 || (size_t)k >= sizeof tmp) return ENAMETOOLONG;
    int fd = open(tmp, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_CLOEXEC, 0644);
    if (fd < 0) return errno;
    uint8_t foot[NVMTL_CF_FOOTER]; uint32_t magic = NVMTL_CF_MAGIC, len = (uint32_t)n; uint64_t h = nvmtl_cf_hash(payload, n);
    memcpy(foot, &magic, 4); memcpy(foot + 4, &len, 4); memcpy(foot + 8, &h, 8);
    int err = 0;
    const uint8_t *parts[2] = { payload, foot }; const size_t sizes[2] = { n, NVMTL_CF_FOOTER };
    for (int p = 0; p < 2 && !err; p++)
        for (size_t off = 0; off < sizes[p];) {
            ssize_t w = write(fd, parts[p] + off, sizes[p] - off);
            if (w > 0) off += (size_t)w; else if (w < 0 && errno == EINTR) continue; else { err = errno ? errno : EIO; break; }
        }
    /* no fsync / F_FULLFSYNC: see the note at the top (the footer, not a flush, proves the entry whole) */
    if (close(fd) != 0 && !err) err = errno;
    if (!err && rename(tmp, path) != 0) err = errno;
    if (err) unlink(tmp);
    return err;
}
#endif

/*

/* nvmtl_caps_query.h - MTLDevice capability answers decided from the Vulkan bits the device reported, never fixed.
 * Each function takes the raw bits (VkFormatFeatureFlags, VkSampleCountFlags, a feature boolean) so tools/test_caps_query.c can
 * prove that a device without the bit answers NO. */
#ifndef NVMTL_CAPS_QUERY_H
#define NVMTL_CAPS_QUERY_H
#include <stdint.h>

#define NVMTL_FF_SAMPLED_FILTER_LINEAR 0x00001000u   /* VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_SAMPLED_IMAGE_FILTER_LINEAR_BIT */
#define NVMTL_FF_COLOR_ATTACHMENT      0x00000080u   /* VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT */
#define NVMTL_SC_4                     0x00000004u   /* VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_4_BIT */

/* the three 32-bit float formats Metal's query covers: R32Float, RG32Float, RGBA32Float */
typedef struct { uint32_t r32, rg32, rgba32; } nvmtl_format_bits;

/* supports32BitFloatFiltering: every one of the three filters linearly when sampled */
static inline int nvmtl_cap_float32_filtering(const nvmtl_format_bits *optimal_features)
{
    return optimal_features && (optimal_features->r32 & optimal_features->rg32 & optimal_features->rgba32 & NVMTL_FF_SAMPLED_FILTER_LINEAR) != 0;
}
/* supports32BitMSAA: each is a colour attachment and the device offers 4 samples for it (the smallest count Metal's query is about) */
static inline int nvmtl_cap_float32_msaa(const nvmtl_format_bits *features, const nvmtl_format_bits *sample_counts)
{
    if (!features || !sample_counts) return 0;
    const uint32_t f = features->r32 & features->rg32 & features->rgba32;
    const uint32_t s = sample_counts->r32 & sample_counts->rg32 & sample_counts->rgba32;
    return (f & NVMTL_FF_COLOR_ATTACHMENT) != 0 && (s & NVMTL_SC_4) != 0;
}
/* supportsPullModelInterpolation: SPIR-V's InterpolationFunction capability (interpolateAtOffset / Sample / Centroid) needs sampleRateShading */
static inline int nvmtl_cap_pull_model_interpolation(int sample_rate_shading) { return sample_rate_shading != 0; }
/* supportsQueryTextureLOD: OpImageQueryLod is core Vulkan with no feature bit; it needs a working device and the translator's lowering */
static inline int nvmtl_cap_query_texture_lod(int vulkan_up, int translator_lowers_lod_query) { return vulkan_up && translator_lowers_lod_query; }
/* supportsVertexAmplificationCount: the multiview view count the device reported with the feature on (0 = off or absent) */
static inline int nvmtl_cap_vertex_amplification(uint32_t count, uint32_t device_views) { return count <= 1 || (device_views >= 2 && count <= device_views); }
#endif

// nvmtl_claims.h - what the Metal device claims to apps, decided from what the Vulkan device can back.
//
// Each claim is tied to the Vulkan capability that implements it, so a GPU without the capability does not advertise
// the Metal feature (an app that trusts the claim and uses the feature would get a pipeline the driver cannot build).
//
//   ray tracing        VK_KHR_ray_query + VK_KHR_acceleration_structure (+ deferred host operations)
//   barycentrics       VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric: the translator emits BaryCoordKHR / BaryCoordNoPerspKHR
//   Metal 3 family     always: mesh and object shaders are lowered to compute plus vertex work in the plugin
//                      (NVMTLLibraryLoad.m, xlate_lower_mesh2), so they do not depend on VK_EXT_mesh_shader
//
// NVIDIA: every card the driver supports (Turing and newer) has both extensions in NVK, so its claims are unchanged.
// tools/test_claims.c checks that, and checks that a GCN-class device without the barycentric extension does not
// claim it; built with -DNVMTL_CLAIMS_UNGATED (the old, unconditional claims) that second part must fail.
#ifndef NVMTL_CLAIMS_H
#define NVMTL_CLAIMS_H

struct nvmtl_caps {
    int barycentric;    // VK_KHR_fragment_shader_barycentric advertised with fragmentShaderBarycentric
    int raytracing;     // the ray-query set the device enables (nvmtl_vk_rt_available)
};

static inline int nvmtl_claim_barycentrics(const struct nvmtl_caps *c)
{
#ifdef NVMTL_CLAIMS_UNGATED
    (void)c;
    return 1;
#else
    return c->barycentric != 0;
#endif
}

static inline int nvmtl_claim_metal3(const struct nvmtl_caps *c)
{
    (void)c;
    return 1;   // mesh shaders are emulated through compute: backed on every device
}

static inline int nvmtl_claim_raytracing(const struct nvmtl_caps *c)
{
    return c->raytracing != 0;
}

#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_cmd_refusal.h

/*
 * NullMoth NVIDIA driver for macOS
 * Copyright (c) 2026 NullMoth Systems.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 */
#ifndef NVMTL_CMD_REFUSAL_H
#define NVMTL_CMD_REFUSAL_H
/*
 * A refused command buffer: why it was refused.
 *
 * -[MTLCommandQueue commandBuffer] returns nil when the Vulkan side cannot begin a command buffer. WindowServer
 * does not tolerate that: CoreDisplay asserts "Failed to get a MTLCommandBuffer" and the session restarts. The cause
 * is usually an earlier failure that disabled the backend for the rest of the process, so the line that names the
 * refusal says which case it is. The texts are macros so that each cause is logged from its own call site: nvlog
 * throttles by format string, and one shared format would let a flood of one cause hide the first line of another.
 */
typedef enum {
    NVMTL_REFUSE_NONE = 0,
    NVMTL_REFUSE_BACKEND_DOWN,   /* the backend is not running in this process */
    NVMTL_REFUSE_POOL,           /* vkCreateCommandPool failed */
    NVMTL_REFUSE_ALLOC,          /* vkAllocateCommandBuffers failed */
    NVMTL_REFUSE_BEGIN           /* vkBeginCommandBuffer failed */
} nvmtl_refusal;

#define NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_BACKEND_DOWN \
    "the Vulkan backend is not running in this process: it failed to start, or a submit, a fence wait or the " \
    "completion check disabled it (look for 'disabling backend' or a start-up failure above)"
#define NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_POOL  "vkCreateCommandPool failed"
#define NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_ALLOC "vkAllocateCommandBuffers failed"
#define NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_BEGIN "vkBeginCommandBuffer failed"

static inline const char *nvmtl_refusal_text(nvmtl_refusal why)
{
    switch (why) {
    case NVMTL_REFUSE_BACKEND_DOWN: return NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_BACKEND_DOWN;
    case NVMTL_REFUSE_POOL:         return NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_POOL;
    case NVMTL_REFUSE_ALLOC:        return NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_ALLOC;
    case NVMTL_REFUSE_BEGIN:        return NVMTL_REFUSE_TEXT_BEGIN;
    default:                        return "no refusal";
    }
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_copy_compat.h

/* nvmtl_copy_compat.h - which two Vulkan formats one image-to-image copy may join.
   vkCmdCopyImage copies bits, and it accepts two different single-plane colour formats when they are size-compatible:
   the same texel size for uncompressed formats, the same compatibility class for block-compressed ones. Depth and stencil
   formats must match exactly. The texture copy used to demand an identical VkFormat, so a copy Metal performs (an sRGB
   texture and its linear twin, a texture and a view that reads it in another format, the BGRA/RGBA twins) was dropped with
   one log line and the destination kept whatever the memory held before - in a recycled heap placement, the previous
   resource's texels. tools/test_copy_compat.c checks the table. Values are VkFormat numbers from the Vulkan core table. */
#ifndef NVMTL_COPY_COMPAT_H
#define NVMTL_COPY_COMPAT_H
#include <stdint.h>
/* The compatibility class of a colour format: uncompressed formats are keyed by texel bytes (1..32), block-compressed BC
   formats by 100 + their class, anything else (depth, stencil, ETC, ASTC, multi-planar, unknown) by 0 = exact match only. */
static inline uint32_t nvmtl_copy_class(uint32_t f)
{
    if (f == 1) return 1;                           /* R4G4_UNORM_PACK8 */
    if (f >= 2 && f <= 8) return 2;                 /* 4444, 565, 5551 packings */
    if (f >= 9 && f <= 15) return 1;                /* R8 */
    if (f >= 16 && f <= 22) return 2;               /* R8G8 */
    if (f >= 23 && f <= 36) return 3;               /* R8G8B8, B8G8R8 */
    if (f >= 37 && f <= 69) return 4;               /* RGBA8, BGRA8, ABGR8 packed, A2R10G10B10, A2B10G10R10 */
    if (f >= 70 && f <= 76) return 2;               /* R16 */
    if (f >= 77 && f <= 83) return 4;               /* R16G16 */
    if (f >= 84 && f <= 90) return 6;               /* R16G16B16 */
    if (f >= 91 && f <= 97) return 8;               /* R16G16B16A16 */
    if (f >= 98 && f <= 100) return 4;              /* R32 */
    if (f >= 101 && f <= 103) return 8;             /* R32G32 */
    if (f >= 104 && f <= 106) return 12;            /* R32G32B32 */
    if (f >= 107 && f <= 109) return 16;            /* R32G32B32A32 */
    if (f >= 110 && f <= 112) return 8;             /* R64 */
    if (f >= 113 && f <= 115) return 16;            /* R64G64 */
    if (f >= 116 && f <= 118) return 24;            /* R64G64B64 */
    if (f >= 119 && f <= 121) return 32;            /* R64G64B64A64 */
    if (f == 122 || f == 123) return 4;             /* B10G11R11_UFLOAT, E5B9G9R9_UFLOAT */
    /* 124-130 are depth/stencil: exact match only */
    if (f >= 131 && f <= 146) return 100 + (f - 131) / 2;   /* BC1 RGB, BC1 RGBA, BC2, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H, BC7 - each a UNORM/SRGB or UNORM/SNORM pair */
    return 0;
}
/* 1 when one vkCmdCopyImage may copy from a src-format image into a dst-format image. */
static inline int nvmtl_copy_formats_ok(uint32_t src, uint32_t dst)
{
    if (src == dst) return 1;
    const uint32_t a = nvmtl_copy_class(src), b = nvmtl_copy_class(dst);
    return a && a == b;
}
#endif

/*
 * NullMoth NVIDIA driver for macOS
 * Copyright (c) 2026 NullMoth Systems.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 */

/* nvmtl_counter_heap.h - Metal 4 counter heaps over Vulkan timestamp queries.
 * A timestamp heap entry is one 64-bit value (MTL4TimestampHeapEntry). The device counts in units of timestampPeriod nanoseconds,
 * so the frequency Metal asks for is 1e9 / period; a device that reports no usable period or no timestamp bits has no counters
 * and answers 0, and a heap is then refused. */
#ifndef NVMTL_COUNTER_HEAP_H
#define NVMTL_COUNTER_HEAP_H
#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#define NVMTL_HEAP_TYPE_INVALID   0
#define NVMTL_HEAP_TYPE_TIMESTAMP 1
#define NVMTL_HEAP_MAX_ENTRIES    32768u   /* the legacy sample buffer's limit, which backs the heap */

static inline uint64_t nvmtl_ts_frequency(double period_ns, uint32_t valid_bits)
{
    if (!valid_bits || !isfinite(period_ns) || period_ns <= 0.0) return 0;
    const double hz = 1e9 / period_ns;
    return hz < 1.0 || hz > 1.8e19 ? 0 : (uint64_t)(hz + 0.5);
}
static inline uint64_t nvmtl_heap_entry_size(int type) { return type == NVMTL_HEAP_TYPE_TIMESTAMP ? 8u : 0u; }
/* NULL when a heap of this type and count can be made, else why not */
static inline const char *nvmtl_heap_refusal(int type, uint64_t count, uint64_t frequency)
{
    if (type != NVMTL_HEAP_TYPE_TIMESTAMP) return "only timestamp heaps exist";
    if (!count || count > NVMTL_HEAP_MAX_ENTRIES) return "an entry count outside 1..32768";
    if (!frequency) return "this device has no usable GPU timestamps";
    return 0;
}
/* a resolve of `range` entries into a destination of `dest_bytes` bytes at `dest_off`: does it fit */
static inline int nvmtl_heap_resolve_fits(uint64_t entries, uint64_t dest_off, uint64_t dest_bytes)
{ return entries && dest_off <= dest_bytes && entries <= (dest_bytes - dest_off) / 8u; }
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_cs_hazard.h
================================================
/* compute2: what a compute module needs from the barrier before its dispatch. Pure C (offline-checkable: tools/b580/cs_offline.m).
 *
 * nvmtl_cs_access(): the Vulkan access types the kernel can read GPU-written memory through, for the narrow serial
 * barrier (NVMTL_CS_BAR). Storage buffers (physical/BDA and descriptor), storage images and texel buffers are read and
 * written through the dataport: VK_ACCESS_2_SHADER_STORAGE_READ/WRITE. A sampled image or uniform texel buffer goes
 * through the sampler: + SHADER_SAMPLED_READ. A Uniform block other than the address table (binding 640, written by the
 * CPU before the submit) would be read through the constant cache: + UNIFORM_READ.
 *
 * nvmtl_cs_reach(): NVMTL_CS_HAZARD (opt-in). 1 when every memory address the kernel can touch is derived from the
 * address-table qwords it received as push constants (compute table-pc applied): no descriptor-bound buffer, image,
 * sampler or acceleration structure; every OpConvertUToPtr takes a value whose provenance is a table qword (P) plus
 * integer arithmetic; no pointer or address is loaded from memory, passed as a function parameter or merged with a
 * non-P value. Then the buffers a dispatch can reach are exactly the bound buffers of its table entries (Metal makes an
 * access outside the bound buffer undefined), and two serial dispatches whose reachable buffers do not overlap (or only
 * share buffers both read) need no barrier. *wr = 1 when the kernel stores or performs an atomic on physical memory.
 * Any doubt answers 0: the barrier stays.
 */
#ifndef NVMTL_CS_HAZARD_H
#define NVMTL_CS_HAZARD_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define NVMTL_CS_ACC_SAMPLED 1u
#define NVMTL_CS_ACC_UNIFORM 2u
static uint32_t nvmtl_cs_access(const void *bytes, size_t nbytes)
{
    const uint32_t *w = bytes; const size_t nw = nbytes / 4;
    if (!w || nw < 5 || w[0] != 0x07230203u) return NVMTL_CS_ACC_SAMPLED | NVMTL_CS_ACC_UNIFORM;
    const uint32_t bound = w[3];
    if (!bound || bound > (1u << 22)) return NVMTL_CS_ACC_SAMPLED | NVMTL_CS_ACC_UNIFORM;
    uint32_t r = 0, table = 0;
    for (size_t at = 5; at < nw;) {
        const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16, op = i[0] & 0xffffu;
        if (!wc || at + wc > nw) return NVMTL_CS_ACC_SAMPLED | NVMTL_CS_ACC_UNIFORM;
        if (op == 71 && wc == 4 && i[2] == 33 && i[3] == 640) table = i[1];
        if (op == 25 && wc >= 9 && i[7] != 2) r |= NVMTL_CS_ACC_SAMPLED;   /* OpTypeImage, Sampled 0 (unknown) or 1 */
        if (op == 27) r |= NVMTL_CS_ACC_SAMPLED;                          /* OpTypeSampledImage */
        at += wc;
    }
    for (size_t at = 5; at < nw;) {
        const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16, op = i[0] & 0xffffu;
        if (op == 59 && wc >= 4 && i[3] == 2 && i[2] != table) r |= NVMTL_CS_ACC_UNIFORM;
        at += wc;
    }
    return r;
}

static int nvmtl_cs_reach(const void *bytes, size_t nbytes, int *wr)
{
    const uint32_t *w = bytes; const size_t nw = nbytes / 4;
    *wr = 1;
    if (!w || nw < 5 || w[0] != 0x07230203u) return 0;
    const uint32_t bound = w[3];
    if (!bound || bound > (1u << 22)) return 0;
    /* per id: 1 = the type is a PhysicalStorageBuffer pointer, 2 = P (address derived from a table qword),
       4 = PushConstant pointer into a table member (>= first table member), 8 = defined as a constant/clean value */
    uint8_t *k = calloc(bound, 1); uint32_t *ty = calloc(bound, 4), *ptrsc = calloc(bound, 4);
    uint32_t pushvar = 0, first_member = ~0u; int ok = 0, writes = 0;
    if (!k || !ty || !ptrsc) goto out;
    for (size_t at = 5; at < nw;) {
        const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16, op = i[0] & 0xffffu;
        if (!wc || at + wc > nw) goto out;
        if (op == 32 && wc == 4 && i[1] < bound) { ptrsc[i[1]] = i[2] + 1; if (i[2] == 5349) k[i[1]] |= 1; }
        if (op == 59 && wc >= 4) {
            switch (i[3]) {
            case 1: case 4: case 6: case 7: break;               /* Input, Workgroup, Private, Function */
            case 9: if (pushvar) goto out; pushvar = i[2]; break; /* the one push block */
            default: goto out;                                    /* descriptors, images, ... */
            }
        }
        if (op == 4472 || op == 5341 || op == 25 || op == 26 || op == 27) goto out;   /* ray query, AS, image, sampler */
        at += wc;
    }
    if (!pushvar) goto out;
    {   /* the push block's member at offset 48 is the first table qword (nvmtl_spirv_table_pc_ex, NVMTL_PC_TABLE_CS_OFFSET) */
        uint32_t ptype = 0, block = 0;
        for (size_t at = 5; at < nw && !ptype;) { const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16;
            if ((i[0] & 0xffffu) == 59 && wc >= 4 && i[2] == pushvar) ptype = i[1]; at += wc; }
        for (size_t at = 5; at < nw && ptype && !block;) { const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16;
            if ((i[0] & 0xffffu) == 32 && wc == 4 && i[1] == ptype) block = i[3]; at += wc; }
        for (size_t at = 5; at < nw && block;) { const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16;
            if ((i[0] & 0xffffu) == 72 && wc == 5 && i[1] == block && i[3] == 35 && i[4] == 48) first_member = i[2]; at += wc; }
    }
    if (first_member == ~0u) goto out;
    /* forward data flow, iterated to a fixed point for phis (back edges) */
    for (int pass = 0; pass < 8; pass++) {
        int changed = 0;
        for (size_t at = 5; at < nw;) {
            const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16, op = i[0] & 0xffffu;
            const uint32_t rt = wc >= 3 ? i[1] : 0, id = wc >= 3 ? i[2] : 0;
            uint8_t add = 0;
#define NVK_P(x) ((x) < bound && (k[(x)] & 2))
            switch (op) {
            case 65: case 66: case 67: case 70:   /* access chains: the base's provenance; a push-table member pointer */
                if (wc >= 4 && id < bound) {
                    if (i[3] == pushvar && wc >= 5) {
                        /* OpAccessChain %ptr %push %member: a member >= first_member is a table qword */
                        uint32_t mv = ~0u;
                        for (size_t j = 5; j < nw;) { const uint32_t *c = w + j, cw = c[0] >> 16;
                            if ((c[0] & 0xffffu) == 43 && cw >= 4 && c[2] == i[4]) { mv = c[3]; break; } j += cw; }
                        if (mv != ~0u && mv >= first_member) add = 4;
                    } else if (NVK_P(i[3])) add = 2;
                    else if (i[3] < bound && (k[i[3]] & 4)) add = 4;
                }
                break;
            case 61:   /* OpLoad: from a table member -> P; a pointer or address loaded from memory is never P */
                if (wc >= 4 && i[3] < bound && (k[i[3]] & 4)) add = 2;
                break;
            case 128: case 130: case 113: case 114: case 124: case 83:   /* IAdd ISub UConvert SConvert Bitcast CopyObject */
            case 199: case 197: case 198: case 194: case 196:            /* And Or Xor ShiftRightLogical ShiftLeftLogical */
            case 81: case 80: case 117: case 120:                        /* CompositeExtract/Construct, PtrToU, UToPtr */
                for (uint32_t a = 3; a < wc; a++) if (NVK_P(i[a])) { add = 2; break; }   /* base + any index stays P */
                break;
            case 169: {   /* OpSelect: both values */
                if (wc == 6 && NVK_P(i[4]) && NVK_P(i[5])) add = 2;
                break; }
            case 245: {   /* OpPhi: every incoming value */
                int all = wc >= 5;
                for (uint32_t a = 3; a + 1 < wc; a += 2) if (!NVK_P(i[a])) { all = 0; break; }
                if (all) add = 2;
                break; }
            default: break;
            }
#undef NVK_P
            if (wc >= 3 && id < bound && rt < bound && (op == 61 || op == 65 || op == 66 || op == 67 || op == 70 || op == 120 ||
                                         op == 169 || op == 245 || op == 83 || op == 55 || op == 57 || op == 124)) ty[id] = rt;
            if (add && id < bound && (k[id] & add) != add) { k[id] |= add; changed = 1; }
            at += wc;
        }
        if (!changed) break;
    }
    /* every physical pointer made, and every physical access, must be P */
    for (size_t at = 5; at < nw;) {
        const uint32_t *i = w + at, wc = i[0] >> 16, op = i[0] & 0xffffu;
#define NVK_PP(x) ((x) < bound && ty[(x)] < bound && (k[ty[(x)]] & 1))   /* x has a physical pointer type */
#define NVK_OK(x) ((x) < bound && (k[(x)] & 2))
        if (op == 120 && wc == 4 && !NVK_OK(i[3])) goto out;                     /* ConvertUToPtr of a non-P value */
        if ((op == 61 || op == 55) && wc >= 3 && i[1] < bound && (k[i[1]] & 1)) goto out;   /* pointer loaded / passed in */
        if (op == 61 && wc >= 4 && NVK_PP(i[3]) && !NVK_OK(i[3])) goto out;      /* physical load through a non-P pointer */
        if (op == 62 && wc >= 3) {                                               /* OpStore */
            if (NVK_PP(i[1])) { if (!NVK_OK(i[1])) goto out; writes = 1; }
            if (NVK_OK(i[2])) goto out;                                          /* an address stored to memory escapes */
        }
        if (op == 63 && wc >= 3) {                                               /* OpCopyMemory */
            if (NVK_PP(i[1])) { if (!NVK_OK(i[1])) goto out; writes = 1; }
            if (NVK_PP(i[2]) && !NVK_OK(i[2])) goto out;
        }
        if (op == 228 && wc >= 2 && NVK_PP(i[1])) { if (!NVK_OK(i[1])) goto out; writes = 1; }   /* OpAtomicStore */
        if (((op >= 227 && op <= 242 && op != 228) || op == 5614 || op == 5615 || op == 6035) && wc >= 4 && NVK_PP(i[3])) {
            if (!NVK_OK(i[3])) goto out; writes = 1; }
        if (op == 57) for (uint32_t a = 4; a < wc; a++) if (NVK_OK(i[a]) || NVK_PP(i[a])) goto out;   /* passed to a function */
#undef NVK_PP
#undef NVK_OK
        at += wc;
    }
    ok = 1;
out:
    free(k); free(ty); free(ptrsc);
    if (ok) *wr = writes;
    return ok;
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_dbuf_reuse.h

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* nvmtl_dbuf_reuse.h: when the descriptor-buffer model (nvmtl_dbuf.c) may point a stage at a region of descriptor memory
   it already wrote, and which slot descriptors it has to make again. Pure functions over the stage's bookkeeping, so a
   host program runs the plugin's own decisions without Vulkan or a GPU (user/tests/metal/dbuf_model.c).

   Per command buffer and stage (`which`) the model keeps
     cur      the region the stage points at now: the stage layout (plan) it was written for, where it is (offset in the
              page of generation gen), the stage epoch it is valid at, and the address-table entries it holds (need);
     mru      the last NVMTL_DB_MRU regions written, so a pipeline switch back and forth (A, B, A ...) finds its region;
     epoch    bumped whenever a slot changed or an object was destroyed: a region is reused only at the epoch it was
              noted at;
     valid    the slots whose shadow descriptor (made by vkGetDescriptorEXT) still describes what the slot names;
     objgen   the object generation (nvmtl_objgen) the valid shadows were made at: a destroyed view or sampler may have
              left its pointer to a new object, so every shadow is made again after one.
   2026-11-12 ("keep"): a change that touches nothing the current region holds (no slot of its plan, none of its address
   table's entries) leaves that region valid. Before, any slot change made the next draw write a new region, so a
   pipeline that reads its buffers from pushed table entries (table-pc) still got a fresh region, and ANV a new surface
   state, for every setVertexBytes. NVMTL_DB_KEEP=0 restores that.
   2026-11-13 ("table set"): a stage whose address table has a set of its own (compute's set 1, graphics sets 4 and 5:
   nvmtl_db_table_plan) keeps its table apart from its region (tab): a new table is a new one-descriptor region in that
   set and a new offset, while the stage region (textures, samplers, buffer descriptors) stays where it is. Before, the
   table's descriptor was in the stage region, so every setBuffer offset a table-reading kernel saw wrote a new region.
   2026-11-13 ("bufoff", branch dbufgeek): a kernel's storage buffers whose offsets it takes from push constants
   (nvmtl_bufoff_pc.h) have descriptors that hold the buffer from its offset's 256-byte window (wmask); such a slot's
   descriptor changes only with its wide change (wchg: the buffer, its size, or the offset mod 256), so a new offset alone
   keeps the region. Before, every setBuffer offset of a Geekbench chain changed the descriptor its region held: a new
   region per dispatch whatever the keep rule (13 Nov night, D2b: 1.00).

   2026-11-13 night (branch dbufgb, nvmtl_dbr_objgen_bufkeep): an object destroyed elsewhere drops only the shadows and
   regions that hold an object (textures, samplers, texel views, a table's texture entries); buffer descriptors and
   buffer-only tables survive it. nvmtl_dbr_find_keys: a recent region (no table) made from exactly what the slots hold
   now serves again, though a change in between made it stale by epoch.

   The including file defines NVMTL_NBUF, NVMTL_NTEX and NVMTL_CHG_WORDS. */
#ifndef NVMTL_DBUF_REUSE_H
#define NVMTL_DBUF_REUSE_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#if !defined(NVMTL_NBUF) || !defined(NVMTL_NTEX) || !defined(NVMTL_CHG_WORDS)
#error "nvmtl_dbuf_reuse.h needs NVMTL_NBUF, NVMTL_NTEX and NVMTL_CHG_WORDS"
#endif

#define NVMTL_DB_MRU 8   /* dbufgb: 4 before; a chain of four kernels over two buffer pairs (content reuse) needs 8 */
typedef struct {
    const void *plan;                /* the stage layout the region was written for; NULL = none */
    const uint64_t *smask;           /* NVMTL_CHG_WORDS words: the slots whose descriptors the region holds (the plan's) */
    uint64_t wmask;                  /* buffer slots (word 0) it holds at their offset's window: touched by wchg only */
    uint32_t off, gen, epoch, need;  /* offset in the page of generation gen; the stage epoch it is valid at; its table's
                                        entries (NVMTL_TABNEED form, 0 = the whole table) */
    uint8_t table;                   /* the region holds an address table */
} nvmtl_dbr_region;
/* the table a stage with a table set points at: the table plan it was written for, where it is (offset in the page of
   generation gen) and the entries it holds (NVMTL_TABNEED form, 0 = the whole table). live: no change touched them since. */
typedef struct {
    const void *plan;
    uint32_t off, gen, need;
    uint8_t live;
} nvmtl_dbr_tab;
/* dbufgb: what a region without a table was made from, slot by slot in its plan's order (nvmtl_db_keys in nvmtl_dbuf.c):
   a buffer slot's device address, offset (or its window) and size, an object slot's handle. n 0xff: no key (a region
   with a table, or more slots than NVMTL_DBR_KEYMAX); objs: a slot names an object (a texture, sampler or texel view),
   so the key holds only while the object generation is og */
#define NVMTL_DBR_KEYMAX 12
typedef struct { uint64_t a, b, c; } nvmtl_dbr_key;
typedef struct { uint8_t n, objs; uint64_t og; nvmtl_dbr_key k[NVMTL_DBR_KEYMAX]; } nvmtl_dbr_keys;
typedef struct {
    nvmtl_dbr_region cur, mru[NVMTL_DB_MRU];
    nvmtl_dbr_keys mkey[NVMTL_DB_MRU];   /* the key of mru[m] (dbufgb) */
    nvmtl_dbr_tab tab;
    uint32_t epoch, mru_next;
    uint64_t objgen;
    uint64_t valid[NVMTL_CHG_WORDS];
    uint64_t wvalid;                 /* buffer slots whose window shadow (NVMTL_DBT_SSBOW) still holds: cleared by wchg */
} nvmtl_dbr_stage;

/* a table holding entries `have` serves a stage that reads `need` (0 = the whole table), as nvmtl_tabneed_covers */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_covers(uint32_t have, uint32_t need)
{
    if (!have) return 1;
    if (!need) return 0;
    return (have & 0xffu) >= (need & 0xffu) && ((have >> 8) & 0xffu) >= ((need >> 8) & 0xffu);
}
/* the bits of [lo, hi) that fall in word k */
static inline uint64_t nvmtl_dbr_range_word(uint32_t lo, uint32_t hi, uint32_t k)
{
    const uint32_t b0 = k * 64, b1 = b0 + 64;
    if (hi <= b0 || lo >= b1 || lo >= hi) return 0;
    const uint32_t a = lo > b0 ? lo - b0 : 0, z = hi < b1 ? hi - b0 : 64;
    const uint64_t upto = z >= 64 ? ~0ull : (1ull << z) - 1;
    return upto & ~((1ull << a) - 1);
}
/* word k of the slots a table holding entries `need` is made from: the buffer addresses (slots 0..) and texture sizes
   (slots NVMTL_NBUF..) */
static inline uint64_t nvmtl_dbr_tab_word(uint32_t need, uint32_t k)
{
    const uint32_t nb = need ? (need & 0xffu) : NVMTL_NBUF, nt = need ? ((need >> 8) & 0xffu) : NVMTL_NTEX;
    return nvmtl_dbr_range_word(0, nb, k) | nvmtl_dbr_range_word(NVMTL_NBUF, NVMTL_NBUF + nt, k);
}
/* does a change of the slots in chg (wide changes in wchg) alter what region r holds? Its descriptors (smask; the
   window descriptors of wmask by wchg), and, with a table, the entries its table was written with */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_touches(const nvmtl_dbr_region *r, const uint64_t *chg, uint64_t wchg)
{
    if (wchg & r->wmask) return 1;
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) {
        uint64_t m = r->smask ? r->smask[k] : ~0ull;
        if (r->table) m |= nvmtl_dbr_tab_word(r->need, k);
        if (chg[k] & m) return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}
/* does a change of the slots in chg alter a table holding entries `need`? */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_tab_touches(uint32_t need, const uint64_t *chg)
{
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) if (chg[k] & nvmtl_dbr_tab_word(need, k)) return 1;
    return 0;
}
/* slots in chg changed. Their shadows are made again when a plan next reads them; regions noted before are stale
   (epoch), except, with keep on, those the change touches nothing of. 1 = the current region was kept. A region is kept
   only while it is in the bound page (gen_now): reuse never crosses a page.
   keep_on 1 (NVMTL_DB_KEEP=cur, the rule of 2026-11-12): only the current region is looked at.
   keep_on 2 (default, 2026-11-13): every recent region valid until now is looked at. A compute chain A, B, C, A ... with
   a setBuffer or setBytes between the dispatches killed the regions of B and C on every change even when none of them
   read the changed slot (a pushed entry: cs-table-pc), so every dispatch wrote a new region (Geekbench 6 Metal: 0.97
   regions per bind).
   The stage's own table (table set) dies when the change touches an entry it holds; with keep off, on any change. */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_changed(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const uint64_t *chg, uint64_t wchg, uint32_t gen_now, int keep_on)
{
    const uint32_t was = st->epoch;
    if (st->tab.live && (!keep_on || nvmtl_dbr_tab_touches(st->tab.need, chg))) st->tab.live = 0;
    const int keep = keep_on && st->cur.plan && st->cur.gen == gen_now && st->cur.epoch == was && !nvmtl_dbr_touches(&st->cur, chg, wchg);
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) st->valid[k] &= ~chg[k];
    st->wvalid &= ~wchg;
    st->epoch++;
    if (!keep_on) return 0;
    for (uint32_t m = 0; m < NVMTL_DB_MRU; m++) {
        nvmtl_dbr_region *r = &st->mru[m];
        if (!r->plan || r->gen != gen_now || r->epoch != was) continue;
        const int same = keep && r->plan == st->cur.plan && r->off == st->cur.off;
        if (same || (keep_on >= 2 && !nvmtl_dbr_touches(r, chg, wchg))) r->epoch = st->epoch;
    }
    if (!keep) return 0;
    st->cur.epoch = st->epoch;
    return 1;
}
/* a view, sampler or heap slot was given up since the shadows were made: none of them is trusted, no region either */
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_objgen(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, uint64_t gen)
{
    if (st->objgen == gen) return;
    memset(st->valid, 0, sizeof st->valid); st->wvalid = 0; st->objgen = gen; st->epoch++; st->tab.live = 0;
}
/* 2026-11-13 night (branch dbufgb): does what a region holds depend on an object pointer (a texture, sampler or texel
   view slot, or a table's texture entries)? Buffer slots (indices < NVMTL_NBUF) are compared by device address, size and
   offset as well as by handle (nvmtl_vk_bind_buffer marks a buffer made again at the same handle as changed), so their
   descriptors, window descriptors and table entries say the same whatever the object generation. */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_tab_objects(uint32_t need) { return !need || ((need >> 8) & 0xffu) != 0; }
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_region_objects(const nvmtl_dbr_region *r)
{
    if (!r->smask) return 1;
    if (NVMTL_NBUF < 64 && (r->smask[0] >> (NVMTL_NBUF & 63))) return 1;
    for (uint32_t k = 1; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) if (r->smask[k]) return 1;
    return r->table && nvmtl_dbr_tab_objects(r->need);
}
/* nvmtl_dbr_objgen for the buffer model since dbufgb: only what can name a destroyed object goes - the shadows of slots
   from NVMTL_NBUF on, the regions that hold one of those or texture entries of a table, and a table set's table with
   texture entries. Regions of buffer descriptors (a kernel's storage buffers, bufoff's windows) and buffer-only tables
   stay valid. Geekbench destroys textures and views all the time (MPS temporary images; 13 Nov night: 32,772 resources
   freed in one Metal run), and every one of them made every stage write a new region and make every descriptor again
   (323,620 made for 140,387 regions). *dropped / *kept: the regions (current and recent) this call dropped and kept. */
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_objgen_bufkeep(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, uint64_t gen, uint32_t *dropped, uint32_t *kept)
{
    *dropped = *kept = 0;
    if (st->objgen == gen) return;
    st->valid[0] &= NVMTL_NBUF >= 64 ? ~0ull : (1ull << NVMTL_NBUF) - 1;
    for (uint32_t k = 1; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) st->valid[k] = 0;
    st->objgen = gen;
    if (st->tab.live && nvmtl_dbr_tab_objects(st->tab.need)) st->tab.live = 0;
    if (st->cur.plan) { if (nvmtl_dbr_region_objects(&st->cur)) { st->cur.plan = NULL; (*dropped)++; } else (*kept)++; }
    for (uint32_t m = 0; m < NVMTL_DB_MRU; m++) {
        nvmtl_dbr_region *r = &st->mru[m];
        if (r->plan && r->epoch == st->epoch && nvmtl_dbr_region_objects(r)) { r->plan = NULL; (*dropped)++; }
    }
}
/* a region written for plan in page gen that serves a stage reading table entries need: the current one or one of the
   last few. 1 = found (st->cur is it). */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_find(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const void *plan, uint32_t gen, uint32_t need)
{
    if (st->cur.plan == plan && st->cur.gen == gen && st->cur.epoch == st->epoch && nvmtl_dbr_covers(st->cur.need, need)) return 1;
    for (uint32_t m = 0; m < NVMTL_DB_MRU; m++) {
        const nvmtl_dbr_region *r = &st->mru[m];
        if (r->plan == plan && r->gen == gen && r->epoch == st->epoch && nvmtl_dbr_covers(r->need, need)) { st->cur = *r; return 1; }
    }
    return 0;
}
/* a new region was written; k: what it was made from (NULL or n 0xff: no key) */
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_note(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const void *plan, const uint64_t *smask, uint64_t wmask, int table, uint32_t off,
                                  uint32_t gen, uint32_t need)
{
    st->cur = (nvmtl_dbr_region){ plan, smask, wmask, off, gen, st->epoch, need, (uint8_t)(table != 0) };
    st->mkey[st->mru_next % NVMTL_DB_MRU].n = 0xff;
    st->mru[st->mru_next++ % NVMTL_DB_MRU] = st->cur;
}
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_note_keys(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const nvmtl_dbr_keys *k)
{
    nvmtl_dbr_keys *d = &st->mkey[(st->mru_next + NVMTL_DB_MRU - 1) % NVMTL_DB_MRU];
    if (!k || k->n > NVMTL_DBR_KEYMAX) { d->n = 0xff; return; }
    d->n = k->n; d->objs = k->objs; d->og = k->og;
    memcpy(d->k, k->k, k->n * sizeof k->k[0]);
}
/* dbufgb ("content reuse"): a recent region of plan in page gen, without a table, made from exactly what the slots hold
   now (k) - and, when it holds an object, at the object generation og. Its bytes are then the ones a new region would
   get, whatever changed in between: a chain that alternates buffers (A, B, then B, A: a ping-pong solver, a blur pass
   to a temporary and back) found its regions stale by epoch and wrote a new one per dispatch. 1 = found (st->cur is it,
   valid at the stage's epoch again). */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_find_keys(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const void *plan, uint32_t gen, const nvmtl_dbr_keys *k, uint64_t og)
{
    if (!k || k->n > NVMTL_DBR_KEYMAX) return 0;
    for (uint32_t m = 0; m < NVMTL_DB_MRU; m++) {
        nvmtl_dbr_region *r = &st->mru[m]; const nvmtl_dbr_keys *mk = &st->mkey[m];
        if (r->plan != plan || r->gen != gen || r->table || mk->n != k->n || (mk->objs && mk->og != og)) continue;
        if (k->n && memcmp(mk->k, k->k, k->n * sizeof k->k[0])) continue;
        r->epoch = st->epoch; st->cur = *r;
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}
/* the stage's table serves a stage with table plan `plan` reading entries `need` in page gen: 1 = point the set at
   st->tab.off again */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_tab_find(const nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const void *plan, uint32_t gen, uint32_t need)
{
    return st->tab.live && st->tab.plan == plan && st->tab.gen == gen && nvmtl_dbr_covers(st->tab.need, need);
}
/* a new table was written (its descriptor at off, in a region of table plan `plan`) */
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_tab_note(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, const void *plan, uint32_t off, uint32_t gen, uint32_t need)
{
    st->tab = (nvmtl_dbr_tab){ plan, off, gen, need, 1 };
}
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_valid(const nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, uint32_t i) { return (int)((st->valid[i >> 6] >> (i & 63)) & 1); }
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_set_valid(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, uint32_t i) { st->valid[i >> 6] |= 1ull << (i & 63); }
/* the shadow of slot i (< 64) made as a window descriptor: wide (1) or exact (0). A window shadow stays good across
   offset-only changes, an exact one does not */
static inline int nvmtl_dbr_shadow_ok(const nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, uint32_t i, int wide)
{
    return wide ? (int)((st->wvalid >> i) & 1) : nvmtl_dbr_valid(st, i);
}
static inline void nvmtl_dbr_shadow_made(nvmtl_dbr_stage *st, uint32_t i, int wide)
{
    if (wide) st->wvalid |= 1ull << i; else nvmtl_dbr_set_valid(st, i);
}
#endif

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/* nvmtl_desc_bufs.h: which buffer indices a lowered module still reads through descriptors (NVMTL_ICB_DGC=1, the plan's
   offer of buffers a shader may set; docs/design/DESIGN-icb-dgc.md section 10). Header-only: nvmtl_vk.c and the host
   check user/tests/metal/icb_lower_check.m use the same scan. */
#ifndef NVMTL_DESC_BUFS_H
#define NVMTL_DESC_BUFS_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

/* NVMTL_ICB_DGC=1: the buffer indices m (< 32) a module reads through a buffer descriptor of its own (a StorageBuffer or
   Uniform variable at binding m outside the heap set 2 and the framebuffer-fetch set 3): the address lowering kept them
   (an index from loaded data, wrapper buffer_addresses kept_roots) or refused the whole module. A DGC sequence cannot set
   a descriptor, so a buffer a shader sets by address never reaches such an index: the plan does not offer it
   (nvmtl_dgc_takes) and a shader's set_*_buffer to it refuses the slot instead of the kernel writing the CPU's buffer
   (mtl_gpu_icb2 C0..C2 before 13 Nov). A malformed module gives 0xffffffff (nothing offered). */
static inline uint32_t nvmtl_spirv_desc_bufs(const void *p, size_t n)
{
    const uint32_t *w = (const uint32_t *)p; size_t nw = n / 4;
    if (!p || nw < 5 || w[0] != 0x07230203u) return 0xffffffffu;
    const uint32_t bound = w[3];
    if (!bound || bound > (1u << 24)) return 0xffffffffu;
    uint8_t *sc = (uint8_t *)calloc(bound, 1);   // 1 = a StorageBuffer/Uniform variable
    uint32_t *bind = (uint32_t *)malloc(bound * sizeof *bind), *set = (uint32_t *)calloc(bound, sizeof *set);
    uint32_t mask = 0;
    if (!sc || !bind || !set) { free(sc); free(bind); free(set); return 0xffffffffu; }
    memset(bind, 0xff, bound * sizeof *bind);
    for (size_t i = 5; i < nw; ) {
        const uint32_t wc = w[i] >> 16, op = w[i] & 0xffffu;
        if (!wc || i + wc > nw) { mask = 0xffffffffu; goto out; }
        if (op == 71 && wc == 4 && w[i + 1] < bound) {
            if (w[i + 2] == 33) bind[w[i + 1]] = w[i + 3];
            else if (w[i + 2] == 34) set[w[i + 1]] = w[i + 3];
        } else if (op == 59 && wc >= 4 && w[i + 2] < bound && (w[i + 3] == 12 || w[i + 3] == 2)) sc[w[i + 2]] = 1;
        i += wc;
    }
    for (uint32_t v = 0; v < bound; v++)
        if (sc[v] && bind[v] < 32 && set[v] != 2 && set[v] != 3) mask |= 1u << bind[v];
out:
    free(sc); free(bind); free(set);
    return mask;
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_desc_stats.h

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* nvmtl_desc_stats.h: NVMTL_DESC_STATS=1, what the descriptor work of each model costs (DESCRIPTOR-MODEL.md section 13).
   The same counters in both models, so a night run can compare them per draw: how many draws and dispatches were bound,
   the host time spent binding them (nvmtl_vk_cmd_bind_set and the compute binds: descriptor sets or descriptor-buffer
   regions, the address table, the pushed table entries, and the Vulkan calls they make), and what that work consisted of.

   Off (the default), every site is one test of a cached int. On, a counter is a plain add to this thread's block: no
   locked instruction, so the counting itself does not pay the write-combining drain an atomic pays after a draw
   (DESCRIPTOR-MODEL.md section 12). The blocks of all threads are summed when a line is written: "DESCSTAT" every
   5 s of command-buffer completions (the window since the last line) and "DESCSTAT-TOTAL" when the process exits.
   The format (nvmtl_dstat_format) is pure, so the host model (user/tests/metal/dbuf_model.c) checks it. */
#ifndef NVMTL_DESC_STATS_H
#define NVMTL_DESC_STATS_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

enum {
    NVMTL_DS_DRAW,       /* graphics binds (one per draw that reached nvmtl_vk_cmd_bind_set) */
    NVMTL_DS_DISP,       /* compute binds (one per dispatch, any path) */
    NVMTL_DS_TICKS,      /* host time in those binds, mach_absolute_time ticks */
    NVMTL_DS_NOBIND,     /* binds that failed: their draw or dispatch was not recorded */
    /* classic model */
    NVMTL_DS_SETNEW,     /* descriptor sets built */
    NVMTL_DS_SETREUSE,   /* the last set bound again (also with a new table offset) */
    NVMTL_DS_UPDATES,    /* vkUpdateDescriptorSets calls */
    NVMTL_DS_WRITES,     /* their descriptor writes */
    NVMTL_DS_COPIES,     /* and copies */
    NVMTL_DS_ALLOCS,     /* vkAllocateDescriptorSets calls */
    NVMTL_DS_BINDSETS,   /* vkCmdBindDescriptorSets calls */
    /* descriptor-buffer model */
    NVMTL_DS_REGION,     /* stage regions written */
    NVMTL_DS_REGREUSE,   /* a stage pointed at a region written before (current or recent) */
    NVMTL_DS_KEEP,       /* slot changes that left the current region valid (nvmtl_dbuf_reuse.h "keep") */
    NVMTL_DS_MADE,       /* slot descriptors made (vkGetDescriptorEXT) */
    NVMTL_DS_BYTES,      /* descriptor bytes written into regions */
    NVMTL_DS_OFFSETS,    /* vkCmdSetDescriptorBufferOffsetsEXT calls */
    NVMTL_DS_BUFBINDS,   /* vkCmdBindDescriptorBuffersEXT calls with a changed page address (13 Nov) */
    NVMTL_DS_SETMOVE,    /* sets those offset calls moved (another buffer index or offset than the bind point's last
                            call gave that set): ANV's per-set work at the next draw or dispatch (a surface state for the
                            new address, the stage's push constants again) and descriptors at an address the GPU's state
                            cache has not seen (13 Nov evening) */
    /* both */
    NVMTL_DS_TABLES,     /* address-table snapshots */
    NVMTL_DS_PUSHES,     /* vkCmdPushConstants calls (table-pc entries, dispatch values, sample positions) */
    NVMTL_DS_LEGACY,     /* classic-set calls made while the buffer model is on (each one an ANV binding-mode switch) */
    /* buffer model, 13 Nov night (branch dbufgb) */
    NVMTL_DS_OBJDROP,    /* stage regions (current and recent) dropped because a view, sampler or heap slot was given up */
    NVMTL_DS_OBJKEEP,    /* current regions that survived such a destroy (they hold buffer descriptors only) */
    NVMTL_DS_BODISP,     /* compute binds of kernels whose storage-buffer offsets are pushed (bufoff) */
    NVMTL_DS_PCDISP,     /* compute binds of kernels that read address-table entries from push constants (cs-table-pc) */
    NVMTL_DS_REGKEY,     /* of the regions reused, those found by what they were made from (nvmtl_dbr_find_keys) */
    NVMTL_DS_N
};
typedef struct { uint64_t v[NVMTL_DS_N]; } nvmtl_dstat;

/* d = a - b, counter by counter */
static inline void nvmtl_dstat_sub(nvmtl_dstat *d, const nvmtl_dstat *a, const nvmtl_dstat *b)
{
    for (int k = 0; k < NVMTL_DS_N; k++) d->v[k] = a->v[k] - b->v[k];
}
/* one line: model "classic" or "buffer", what (e.g. "5.0 s" or "total 12.3 s"), d the counts, tick_ns the length of
   one tick in ns. Returns the length written (snprintf). */
static inline int nvmtl_dstat_format(char *b, size_t n, const char *model, const char *what, const nvmtl_dstat *d, double tick_ns)
{
    const uint64_t *v = d->v;
    const uint64_t binds = v[NVMTL_DS_DRAW] + v[NVMTL_DS_DISP];
    const double ns = (double)v[NVMTL_DS_TICKS] * tick_ns;
    const double per = binds ? ns / (double)binds : 0.0;
    const double pd = binds ? 1.0 / (double)binds : 0.0;
    return snprintf(b, n,
        "%s %s: %llu draws + %llu dispatches bound, %.0f ns each (%.1f ms); "
        "sets %llu new + %llu reused, %llu updates (%llu writes, %llu copies), %llu allocs, %llu binds; "
        "regions %llu new + %llu reused + %llu kept, %llu descriptors made, %.1f KB, %llu offset calls (%llu sets moved), %llu buffer binds; "
        "%llu tables, %llu pushes, %llu legacy calls, %llu not recorded; per bind: %.2f sets, %.2f regions, %.2f tables, %.0f B, "
        "%.2f sets moved; objects destroyed: %llu regions dropped, %llu kept; dispatches: %llu bufoff, %llu table-pc; "
        "%llu regions reused by content",
        model, what, (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_DRAW], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_DISP], per, ns / 1e6,
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_SETNEW], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_SETREUSE], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_UPDATES],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_WRITES], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_COPIES], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_ALLOCS],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_BINDSETS],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_REGION], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_REGREUSE], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_KEEP],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_MADE], (double)v[NVMTL_DS_BYTES] / 1024.0, (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_OFFSETS],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_SETMOVE], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_BUFBINDS],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_TABLES], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_PUSHES], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_LEGACY],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_NOBIND],
        (double)v[NVMTL_DS_SETNEW] * pd, (double)v[NVMTL_DS_REGION] * pd, (double)v[NVMTL_DS_TABLES] * pd, (double)v[NVMTL_DS_BYTES] * pd,
        (double)v[NVMTL_DS_SETMOVE] * pd, (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_OBJDROP], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_OBJKEEP],
        (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_BODISP], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_PCDISP], (unsigned long long)v[NVMTL_DS_REGKEY]);
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_dirty.h

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* nvmtl_dirty.h: the dirty-only binding decisions of nvmtl_snapshot_set_c (nvmtl_vk.c), as pure functions over bit masks so
   a host program can check them (user/tests/metal/dirty_model.c) without Vulkan or a GPU.

   Per stage (`which`) the binding table keeps the last descriptor set built in this command buffer (t->last) with
     lastw    the bindings (indices < 256) that set holds valid descriptors for,
     last_hi  how many storage-texture bindings it holds,
     chg      the bindings whose slot changed since it was built (one bit per index, NVMTL_CHG_WORDS words),
     dirty    chg is not empty,
     gen      the object generation (nvmtl_vk_objgen) read when it was built.
   A draw then either binds that set again (reuse), binds it with a newer address table on the same page (was: only
   buffers changed and the pipeline reads them all through the table), or builds a new set; with dirty-only on, the new
   set copies the descriptors of the last one that did not change instead of writing them again.

   A slot is compared by handle (kind, VkImageView/VkSampler/VkBuffer pointer, offset). The same pointer can name another
   object once the first is destroyed (the allocator hands the address out again), so a descriptor the last set holds is
   trusted only while no image view, buffer view or sampler was destroyed since that set was built (same_gen); otherwise
   the set is not reused and nothing is copied from it. 2026-11-10: Safari's six-canvas WebGPU page drew white blocks and
   a stale rectangle of wallpaper with dirty-only on, and was right with NVMTL_NO_DIRTYONLY=1.

   The including file defines NVMTL_NBUF, NVMTL_STEX_BASE, NVMTL_NSTEX and NVMTL_CHG_WORDS. */
#ifndef NVMTL_DIRTY_H
#define NVMTL_DIRTY_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#if !defined(NVMTL_NBUF) || !defined(NVMTL_STEX_BASE) || !defined(NVMTL_NSTEX) || !defined(NVMTL_CHG_WORDS)
#error "nvmtl_dirty.h needs NVMTL_NBUF, NVMTL_STEX_BASE, NVMTL_NSTEX and NVMTL_CHG_WORDS"
#endif

typedef struct {
    const uint64_t *pm;      /* 4 words: the bindings this pipeline's stage reads (indices < 256) */
    const uint64_t *lastw;   /* 4 words: the bindings the last set holds */
    const uint64_t *chg;     /* NVMTL_CHG_WORDS words */
    uint32_t hi, last_hi;    /* storage textures this pipeline reads / the last set holds */
    int have_last;           /* a last set exists, is this command buffer's and was built for the same texel-buffer mask */
    int dirty;
    int tabok;               /* the last set's address table holds the entries this stage reads */
    int same_gen;            /* no view or sampler was destroyed since the last set was built */
    int dirty_only;          /* NVMTL_NO_DIRTYONLY unset */
} nvmtl_ds_in;

/* every binding the pipeline reads is one the last set holds */
static inline int nvmtl_ds_covered(const uint64_t *pm, const uint64_t *lastw)
{
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) if (pm[k] & ~lastw[k]) return 0;
    return 1;
}
/* nothing changed since the last set was built, and its descriptors can still be trusted */
static inline int nvmtl_ds_live(const nvmtl_ds_in *in) { return in->have_last && !in->dirty && in->same_gen; }

/* the last set serves this draw as it is */
static inline int nvmtl_ds_reuse(const nvmtl_ds_in *in)
{
    return nvmtl_ds_live(in) && in->tabok && in->hi <= in->last_hi && nvmtl_ds_covered(in->pm, in->lastw);
}

/* only buffer slots (indices 0..31) changed, or nothing did and only the table is short: the last set serves with a new
   address table on the same page (table_ubo), provided the pipeline reads no buffer descriptor that changed. The caller
   still checks the page and makes the table. */
static inline int nvmtl_ds_was(const nvmtl_ds_in *in, int table_ubo)
{
    if (!table_ubo || !in->have_last || !in->same_gen || !(in->dirty || !in->tabok) || in->hi > in->last_hi) return 0;
    if (in->dirty && (in->pm[0] & 0xffffffffull)) return 0;
    if (in->chg[0] >> 32) return 0;
    for (int k = 1; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) if (in->chg[k]) return 0;
    return nvmtl_ds_covered(in->pm, in->lastw);
}
/* The was path taken: the set's buffer descriptors of the changed slots are stale from now on, so they leave lastw
   (a later pipeline that reads one of them as a descriptor gets a new set). WAS: lastw kept them, chg was cleared, and
   the next pipeline that read such a buffer descriptor bound the set again with the old buffer in it. */
static inline void nvmtl_ds_was_taken(uint64_t *lastw, uint64_t *chg)
{
    lastw[0] &= ~(chg[0] & 0xffffffffull);
    memset(chg, 0, NVMTL_CHG_WORDS * sizeof *chg);
}

/* A new set. m: the bindings it is written for (the pipeline's, plus the last set's while that one is live, so a later
   pipeline that reads them can reuse it). *hi grows to last_hi likewise. Returns 1 when unchanged descriptors are copied
   from the last set; cm (NVMTL_CHG_WORDS words, every binding index including storage textures 63..127 at 256..320) then
   has a bit for each binding to copy. WAS: cm was 4 words and nvmtl_snapshot_set_md read cm[4] and cm[5] past it for
   storage textures 63 and up. */
static inline int nvmtl_ds_new(const nvmtl_ds_in *in, uint64_t m[4], uint32_t *hi, uint64_t cm[NVMTL_CHG_WORDS])
{
    const int live = nvmtl_ds_live(in);
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) m[k] = in->pm[k] | (live ? in->lastw[k] : 0);
    if (live && in->last_hi > *hi) *hi = in->last_hi;
    memset(cm, 0, NVMTL_CHG_WORDS * sizeof *cm);
    if (!live || !in->dirty_only) return 0;
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) cm[k] = in->lastw[k];
    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < NVMTL_NSTEX; j++) {
        const uint32_t i = NVMTL_STEX_BASE + j;
        if (j < in->last_hi) cm[i >> 6] |= 1ull << (i & 63); else cm[i >> 6] &= ~(1ull << (i & 63));
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < NVMTL_CHG_WORDS; k++) cm[k] &= ~in->chg[k];
    return 1;
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_env_knobs.h

/* nvmtl_env_knobs.h - the driver knobs a release plugin forgets when it loads.
   A release plugin drops the NVMTL_/NVK_/NAK_/NVRM_ variables it inherits from the environment: a variable left behind
   in a shell by an earlier experiment must not change how every Metal app launched from that shell draws, and the
   supported route for a setting is the conf file read right after this. Three per-process switches were always kept.
   NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 keeps every knob for this one process: a launcher that sets knobs for one application on purpose
   opts in with that single line, and a process that does not set it behaves exactly as before. The rule is pure over
   the vector it is given, so tools/test_env_knobs.c proves it without loading the plugin. */
#ifndef NVMTL_ENV_KNOBS_H
#define NVMTL_ENV_KNOBS_H
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

/* a driver knob: one of our prefixes, including the translator's (METAL2VULKAN_) and the Mesa / RADV / ACO / NIR
   switches the bundled Vulkan drivers read. Several of them name files that get written or libraries that get
   loaded, so none may reach a process that did not set them for itself. */
static inline int nvmtl_env_knob_prefixed(const char *kv)
{
    return !strncmp(kv, "NVMTL_", 6) || !strncmp(kv, "NVK_", 4) || !strncmp(kv, "NAK_", 4) || !strncmp(kv, "NVRM_", 5)
        || !strncmp(kv, "METAL2VULKAN_", 13) || !strncmp(kv, "MESA_", 5) || !strncmp(kv, "NIR_", 4)
        || !strncmp(kv, "RADV_", 5) || !strncmp(kv, "ACO_", 4)
        /* Intel's ANV and our stack: INTEL_MEASURE names a file to write, the codecs and xemac read their own */
        || !strncmp(kv, "INTEL_", 6) || !strncmp(kv, "ANV_", 4) || !strncmp(kv, "INTELXE", 7) || !strncmp(kv, "XEMAC_", 6);
}

/* A process with more privilege than whoever set its environment: setuid/setgid (issetugid), or running as root.
   dyld drops DYLD_* for the first case; the knobs include library paths (NVMTL_ICD_LIB, NVMTL_NVK_DYLIB, the vendor
   plugin path) and file paths that get written, so the plugin must not reopen that door. Such a process keeps no
   knob, opt-in or not. */
static inline int nvmtl_env_privileged(void)
{
    return issetugid() || geteuid() == 0;
}

/* 1 when this process asked to keep its own knobs (the exact value 1; anything else is an ordinary knob and is forgotten) */
static inline int nvmtl_env_knobs_kept(char **envp)
{
    if (nvmtl_env_privileged()) return 0;
    for (char **e = envp; e && *e; e++) if (!strcmp(*e, "NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1")) return 1;
    return 0;
}

/* 1 for a variable the release plugin keeps even without the opt-in */
static inline int nvmtl_env_knob_always_kept(const char *kv)
{
    if (nvmtl_env_privileged()) return 0;
    return !strncmp(kv, "NVMTL_UNIFORM_CBUF=", 19)          /* the GL uniform path's per-process override */
        || !strncmp(kv, "NVMTL_UNIFORM_CBUF_STATS=", 25)    /* and its diagnostics */
        || !strncmp(kv, "NVMTL_PRESENT_INLINE=", 21);       /* the switch that restores inline presents */
}

/* The cached answer for this process: 1 when it set NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1. Besides keeping the knobs, a release plugin then
   writes its log (nvmtl_log_path) and its fps census for this process, which it never does otherwise. */
static inline int nvmtl_process_env_on(void)
{
    static int on = -1;
    if (on < 0) { const char *e = getenv("NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV"); on = e && !strcmp(e, "1") && !nvmtl_env_privileged(); }
    return on;
}

/* A library path that came from a knob or the conf file. A release plugin loads it only when it is a root-owned regular
   file, not a link, in a root-owned folder nobody else can write: the plugin runs inside every Metal app, so a path to
   a user-writable file would hand each of them, WindowServer included, to whoever can write that file. */
static inline int nvmtl_code_path_allowed(const char *path)
{
#if defined(NVMTL_RELEASE) && NVMTL_RELEASE   /* the build passes NVMTL_RELEASE=1 or nothing; elsewhere it is tested with #if */
    struct stat st, ds; char dir[1024];
    if (!path || strlen(path) >= sizeof dir || path[0] != '/') return 0;
    if (lstat(path, &st) != 0 || !S_ISREG(st.st_mode) || st.st_uid != 0 || (st.st_mode & (S_IWGRP | S_IWOTH))) return 0;
    strcpy(dir, path); *strrchr(dir, '/') = 0;
    if (lstat(dir[0] ? dir : "/", &ds) != 0 || !S_ISDIR(ds.st_mode)) return 0;
    return ds.st_uid == 0 && !(ds.st_mode & (S_IWGRP | S_IWOTH));
#else
    (void)path; return 1;   /* development builds load from build folders */
#endif
}

/* Unsets every driver knob in envp that is not kept and returns how many it forgot. envp is the process environment,
   which unsetenv edits, so the names are collected first and removed after. At most 256 are forgotten, as before. */
static inline unsigned nvmtl_release_forget_env(char **envp)
{
    if (nvmtl_env_knobs_kept(envp)) return 0;
    char *names[256]; unsigned n = 0;
    for (char **e = envp; e && *e && n < 256; e++) {
        if (!nvmtl_env_knob_prefixed(*e) || nvmtl_env_knob_always_kept(*e)) continue;
        const char *eq = strchr(*e, '='); if (!eq) continue;
        names[n] = strndup(*e, (size_t)(eq - *e)); if (names[n]) n++;
    }
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; i++) { unsetenv(names[i]); free(names[i]); }
    return n;
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_fd_token.h

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 */
#ifndef NVMTL_FD_TOKEN_H
#define NVMTL_FD_TOKEN_H
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

/* The RM bridge uses a read-only null descriptor as an owned handle number.
 * If the host sandbox forbids that path, an anonymous pipe at EOF has the
 * same read-only behavior. No inherited descriptor or filesystem access is
 * borrowed. Other paths, access modes and failures retain normal semantics. */
static int nvmtl_icd_open(const char *path, int flags, ...)
{
    mode_t mode = 0;
    if (flags & O_CREAT) {
        va_list args; va_start(args, flags); mode = (mode_t)va_arg(args, int); va_end(args);
    }
    int fd = open(path, flags, mode);
    if (fd >= 0 || !path || strcmp(path, "/dev/null") ||
        (flags & ~O_CLOEXEC) != O_RDONLY ||
        (errno != EACCES && errno != EPERM)) return fd;
    int ends[2];
    if (pipe(ends)) return -1;
    close(ends[1]);
    if ((flags & O_CLOEXEC) && fcntl(ends[0], F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) < 0) {
        int error = errno; close(ends[0]); errno = error; return -1;
    }
    return ends[0];
}
#endif

/* nvmtl_format_twin.h - colour formats that differ only in channel order.
   Metal draws through the attachment's format, so a pipeline declared in one format renders correctly into an attachment of
   its twin (red stays red). The pairs are the 8-bit RGBA/BGRA ones, with and without sRGB, and the two 10-bit packings.
   Vulkan formats and Metal pixel formats are both given, so tools/test_format_twin.c can check they describe the same pairs. */
#ifndef NVMTL_FORMAT_TWIN_H
#define NVMTL_FORMAT_TWIN_H
#include <stdint.h>
typedef struct { uint32_t mtl, vk; } nvmtl_format_pair;
/* MTLPixelFormat / VkFormat: RGBA8Unorm 70 / R8G8B8A8_UNORM 37, BGRA8Unorm 80 / B8G8R8A8_UNORM 44, the sRGB pair 71 / 43 and
   81 / 50, RGB10A2Unorm 90 / A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32 64, BGR10A2Unorm 94 / A2R10G10B10_UNORM_PACK32 58. */
static const nvmtl_format_pair nvmtl_format_twins[][2] = {
    { { 70, 37 }, { 80, 44 } }, { { 71, 43 }, { 81, 50 } }, { { 90, 64 }, { 94, 58 } },
};
static inline uint32_t nvmtl_format_twin_vk(uint32_t f)
{
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof nvmtl_format_twins / sizeof nvmtl_format_twins[0]; i++)
        for (int s = 0; s < 2; s++) if (nvmtl_format_twins[i][s].vk == f) return nvmtl_format_twins[i][1 - s].vk;
    return 0;
}
static inline uint32_t nvmtl_format_twin_mtl(uint32_t f)
{
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < sizeof nvmtl_format_twins / sizeof nvmtl_format_twins[0]; i++)
        for (int s = 0; s < 2; s++) if (nvmtl_format_twins[i][s].mtl == f) return nvmtl_format_twins[i][1 - s].mtl;
    return 0;
}
#endif

// glcpu4: the Apple OpenGL CPU pieces, each switchable on its own in the same binary (default on).
//
//   NVMTL_GLCPU4=0            every speed piece below off (the prod7 path), unless a piece's own variable says otherwise;
//                             prod8: not NVMTL_UNCOMMITTED_HANDLERS
//   NVMTL_HANDLER_ARENA=0|1   glcpu3: helper-free completed handlers copied into the command buffer's arena (nvmtl_handler_arena.h)
//   NVMTL_VB_ADDR=0|1         vertex buffers bound by device address (vkCmdBindVertexBuffers3KHR, VK_KHR_device_address_commands)
//   NVMTL_RESREF_BORROW=0|1   resource-set membership and residency counts without transient ARC retain/release pairs
//   NVMTL_VRAM_TAG_ASYNC=0|1  the per-frame IOSurface VRAM generation tag written off the committing thread
//   NVMTL_UNCOMMITTED_HANDLERS=0|1  a command buffer released without being committed runs its scheduled and completed
//                             handlers at release, as Apple's driver does (a contract fix, not a speed piece)
//
// A piece reads its variable once per process (first use) and logs its state. Unset: a speed piece follows NVMTL_GLCPU4
// (unset = on).
// prod8: the contract fix (NVMTL_UNCOMMITTED_HANDLERS, NVMTL_G4_FIX) no longer follows NVMTL_GLCPU4: it is on unless its own
// variable is 0, so NVMTL_GLCPU4=0 is "the four speed pieces off" and an A/B of them keeps Apple's handler contract on
// both sides.
#include <stdlib.h>
void nvlog(const char *fmt, ...);
static int nvmtl_g4_read_ex(const char *env, const char *what, int follows_master) {
    const char *e = getenv(env), *m = getenv("NVMTL_GLCPU4");
    const int on = (e && *e) ? e[0] != '0' : !(follows_master && m && m[0] == '0');
    nvlog("glcpu4: %s %s (%s=%s, NVMTL_GLCPU4=%s%s)", what, on ? "ON" : "off", env, e ? e : "unset", m ? m : "unset",
          follows_master ? "" : ", not followed: contract fix");
    return on;
}
static int nvmtl_g4_read(const char *env, const char *what) { return nvmtl_g4_read_ex(env, what, 1); }
#define NVMTL_G4_SWITCH(fn, env, what) \
    static int fn(void) { static int v = -1; if (__builtin_expect(v < 0, 0)) v = nvmtl_g4_read(env, what); return v; }
#define NVMTL_G4_FIX(fn, env, what) \
    static int fn(void) { static int v = -1; if (__builtin_expect(v < 0, 0)) v = nvmtl_g4_read_ex(env, what, 0); return v; }
