FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_sass_params.h
================================================
#ifndef NVMTL_SASS_PARAMS_H
#define NVMTL_SASS_PARAMS_H
/*
 * nvmtl_sass_params.h — the parameter block a raw-SASS compute kernel reads.
 *
 * The compiled kernel takes everything it needs through NVIDIA's constant bank 0: buffer addresses,
 * the dispatch grid, bindless texture and sampler handles, the byte offset of each threadgroup
 * allocation inside the shared window, and any constant table the compiler lifted into the block.
 * The compiler records WHERE each of those goes (`launchrec.py`, read out of the cubin itself) and
 * this packs the values the driver resolved into exactly those places.
 *
 * Every offset here comes from the cubin, never from a prediction: the assembler places a
 *    by-value table or an inline-sampler word where it likes, and predicting those disagreed with it
 *    in a fifth of real kernels. A parameter the optimised code never reads is
 *    absent from the cubin; writing it anyway is harmless, leaving a gap in the block is not.
 *
 * Overlap is refused rather than resolved. Two parameters claiming the same byte means the record
 *    and the cubin disagree, and a kernel launched on a half-written bank reads another resource's
 *    descriptor — which the hardware cannot report and no pixel would reveal.
 */
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <string.h>

enum nvmtl_sass_param_kind {
    NVMTL_SASS_BUFFER        = 1,  /* index into `addresses`: a Metal buffer's GPU address */
    NVMTL_SASS_GRID_X        = 2,  /* the dispatch size, in threads, per axis */
    NVMTL_SASS_GRID_Y        = 3,
    NVMTL_SASS_GRID_Z        = 4,
    NVMTL_SASS_TEXTURE       = 5,  /* index into `handles`: an NVK image descriptor index */
    NVMTL_SASS_SAMPLER       = 6,  /* index into `handles`: an NVK sampler descriptor index */
    NVMTL_SASS_TG_OFFSET     = 7,  /* index into `tg_offsets`: bytes into the shared window */
    NVMTL_SASS_CONST_TABLE   = 8,  /* bytes from `tables`, copied in by value */
    NVMTL_SASS_INLINE_SAMPLER = 9, /* index into `handles`: a constexpr sampler's descriptor index */
    /* an `array_ref<void>` argument: `addresses[index]` holds the address of a table THIS driver
     *    built, one 8-byte entry per Metal buffer index, because Metal materialises that array
     *    rather than the app passing it (MPS's ndArrayConvolution2D does this). */
    NVMTL_SASS_ADDRESS_TABLE = 10,
};

#define NVMTL_SASS_MAX_PARAM_BYTES 1024
#define NVMTL_SASS_MAX_PARAMS      64
#define NVMTL_SASS_MAX_TABLES      8

struct nvmtl_sass_param {
    uint32_t offset;   /* from the cubin */
    uint32_t size;     /* from the cubin */
    uint32_t kind;
    uint32_t index;    /* which buffer / handle / threadgroup index / table this is */
    uint32_t unused;   /* the shader never reads it; still written, so the block has no holes */
};

struct nvmtl_sass_table {
    const uint8_t *bytes;
    uint32_t       size;
};

/*
 * Pack one kernel's parameter block.
 *
 * `out` receives `*out_bytes` bytes to copy to constant bank 0 at the kernel's parameter offset.
 * Returns 0, or a negative number naming which precondition failed:
 *   -1 arguments      -2 a parameter lies outside the block      -3 two parameters overlap
 *   -4 a buffer index or address is unusable                     -5 a grid axis is zero or repeated
 *   -6 an unknown kind                                           -7 a handle index is unusable
 *   -8 a threadgroup offset is unusable                          -9 a table is missing or mis-sized
 */
static inline int nvmtl_sass_pack(
    const struct nvmtl_sass_param *params, uint32_t count,
    const uint64_t *addresses, uint32_t address_count,
    const uint64_t *handles, uint32_t handle_count,
    const uint32_t *tg_offsets, uint32_t tg_count,
    const struct nvmtl_sass_table *tables, uint32_t table_count,
    const uint32_t threads[3],
    uint8_t *out, uint32_t out_capacity, uint32_t *out_bytes)
{
    uint8_t claimed[NVMTL_SASS_MAX_PARAM_BYTES];
    uint32_t end = 0, seen_grid = 0;

    if (!params || !count || count > NVMTL_SASS_MAX_PARAMS || !out || !out_bytes || !threads)
        return -1;
    if (out_capacity > NVMTL_SASS_MAX_PARAM_BYTES)
        out_capacity = NVMTL_SASS_MAX_PARAM_BYTES;
    memset(claimed, 0, sizeof claimed);
    memset(out, 0, out_capacity);
    *out_bytes = 0;

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const struct nvmtl_sass_param *p = &params[i];
        if (!p->size || p->offset >= out_capacity || p->size > out_capacity - p->offset)
            return -2;
        for (uint32_t b = p->offset; b < p->offset + p->size; b++) {
            if (claimed[b])
                return -3;
            claimed[b] = 1;
        }
        uint8_t *dst = out + p->offset;

        switch (p->kind) {
        case NVMTL_SASS_ADDRESS_TABLE:
        case NVMTL_SASS_BUFFER: {
            if (p->size != 8 || (p->offset & 7) || !addresses || p->index >= address_count)
                return -4;
            uint64_t v = addresses[p->index];
            if (!v && !p->unused)
                return -4;                      /* a bound buffer at address 0 is never valid */
            memcpy(dst, &v, 8);
            break;
        }
        case NVMTL_SASS_GRID_X:
        case NVMTL_SASS_GRID_Y:
        case NVMTL_SASS_GRID_Z: {
            uint32_t axis = p->kind - NVMTL_SASS_GRID_X;
            if (p->size != 4 || (p->offset & 3) || !threads[axis] || (seen_grid & (1u << axis)))
                return -5;
            seen_grid |= 1u << axis;
            memcpy(dst, &threads[axis], 4);
            break;
        }
        case NVMTL_SASS_TEXTURE:
        case NVMTL_SASS_SAMPLER:
        case NVMTL_SASS_INLINE_SAMPLER: {
            /* the handle word the shader reads: NVK's descriptor index, already packed by
             * nvmtl_nvk_sass_*_handle_v1 on the side that owns the descriptor tables */
            if (p->size != 8 || (p->offset & 7) || !handles || p->index >= handle_count)
                return -7;
            uint64_t v = handles[p->index];
            memcpy(dst, &v, 8);
            break;
        }
        case NVMTL_SASS_TG_OFFSET: {
            if (p->size != 4 || (p->offset & 3) || !tg_offsets || p->index >= tg_count)
                return -8;
            memcpy(dst, &tg_offsets[p->index], 4);
            break;
        }
        case NVMTL_SASS_CONST_TABLE: {
            if (!tables || p->index >= table_count || p->index >= NVMTL_SASS_MAX_TABLES)
                return -9;
            const struct nvmtl_sass_table *t = &tables[p->index];
            if (!t->bytes || t->size != p->size)
                return -9;
            memcpy(dst, t->bytes, t->size);
            break;
        }
        default:
            return -6;
        }
        if (p->offset + p->size > end)
            end = p->offset + p->size;
    }

    /* every axis of the grid must be present: a kernel whose guard reads an unwritten axis would
     * run the wrong number of threads and still complete */
    if (seen_grid != 7)
        return -5;

    *out_bytes = (end + 7) & ~7u;              /* the bank is filled in 8-byte words */
    return 0;
}

/*
 * The shared window: Metal gives a length per threadgroup index, the kernel reads one window with a
 * byte offset per index. Returns the window size, or 0 if it does not fit `limit`.
 */
static inline uint32_t nvmtl_sass_threadgroup_window(
    const uint32_t *lengths, uint32_t count, uint32_t align, uint32_t limit,
    uint32_t *offsets_out)
{
    uint32_t cursor = 0;
    if (!lengths || !offsets_out || !align || (align & (align - 1)))
        return 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        cursor = (cursor + align - 1) & ~(align - 1);
        offsets_out[i] = cursor;
        if (lengths[i] > limit - cursor)
            return 0;                          /* refuse rather than overlap two allocations */
        cursor += lengths[i];
    }
    return cursor;
}

#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_scanout_p4.h
================================================
/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 * gpuperf phase 4: what happens to a WindowServer composite that has a scan-out (or readback) binding, decided per
 * frame. Pure C, no plugin state: NVMTLObjects.m / NVMTLEventSync.m use it, user/tests/plugin/scanout_p4_unit.c tests it
 * on the host.
 *
 * A bound composite's frame is always copied into its scan-out buffer (VRAM to VRAM). Its IOSurface's system-memory pages
 * (what a CPU reader of the surface sees) are then handled by the readback mode:
 *   p4    (default) phase 4: no copy into the pages. At publication the plugin marks the binding newer (NMXAccel selector
 *         2); the family's valid bits then say the device copy is current, so a CPU lock of the surface (a screenshot,
 *         a capture), a frame the kernel copies instead of flipping, and an unbind page the frame off from the scan-out
 *         buffer on the copy engine (nmxScanPageoff). A mark the kernel refuses reads that frame back after all.
 *   full  every frame is also read back into the pages over PCIe (before 2026-11-14 the default; 12.8 ms of GPU per
 *         frame on a B580 at 3440x1440, ~2.2 ms at 2560x1440). NVMTL_SCANOUT_READBACK=1, or the root-owned diag flag
 *         /tmp/nvmtl-scanout-readback-full.
 *   off   no copy into the pages and no mark: CPU readers of the composite see whatever frame the pages last got. A
 *         measurement mode only (td016's default). NVMTL_SCANOUT_READBACK=0, or /tmp/nvmtl-no-scanout-readback.
 * Phase 4 needs the pages to have the scan-out buffer's layout, since the kernel's page-off copies the buffer 1:1 from
 * offset 0: the same row pitch, the plane at the start of the allocation, and an allocation that holds the frame rounded
 * up to whole pages (the page-off copies whole pages and stops at the allocation's last whole page). A frame that does not
 * qualify is read back, and the reason is logged once per binding.
 *
 * WAS (until 2026-11-14): phase 4 also required debug.intelxe.surfvram >= 2 (the VRAM-shared IOSurface switch, 0 in the
 * kext unless the boot-arg intelxe_surfvram=2 is set) and the readback switch on. Phase 4 uses nothing of the VRAM-shared
 * surfaces, so on a machine without that boot-arg it never engaged and every frame was read back; with the readback
 * switched off (td016) it could not engage anywhere. */
#ifndef NVMTL_SCANOUT_P4_H
#define NVMTL_SCANOUT_P4_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef enum { NVMTL_SORB_P4 = 0, NVMTL_SORB_FULL = 1, NVMTL_SORB_OFF = 2 } nvmtl_sorb_mode;

static inline const char *nvmtl_sorb_name(nvmtl_sorb_mode m)
{
    return m == NVMTL_SORB_FULL ? "full readback" : m == NVMTL_SORB_OFF ? "readback OFF, no marks (CPU readers may see an older frame)"
                                                                        : "phase 4 (no readback; CPU locks page the frame off)";
}
/* NVMTL_SCANOUT_READBACK: unset, empty, "p4", "4" or "auto" = p4; "1", "full", "on" = full; "0", "off" = off. Anything
   else is p4 (the safe default that does not cost a readback). */
static inline nvmtl_sorb_mode nvmtl_sorb_parse(const char *e)
{
    if (!e || !*e) return NVMTL_SORB_P4;
    if (!strcmp(e, "1") || !strcmp(e, "full") || !strcmp(e, "on")) return NVMTL_SORB_FULL;
    if (!strcmp(e, "0") || !strcmp(e, "off")) return NVMTL_SORB_OFF;
    return NVMTL_SORB_P4;
}
/* The run-time diag flags override the environment: off wins over full (a measurement switch is never made safer by
   accident: both set means the measurer asked for the cheapest). */
static inline nvmtl_sorb_mode nvmtl_sorb_effective(nvmtl_sorb_mode env, int flag_full, int flag_off)
{
    return flag_off ? NVMTL_SORB_OFF : flag_full ? NVMTL_SORB_FULL : env;
}

/* Why a bound composite's frame is (or is not) handled by phase 4. 0 is "not decided yet" (a binding's first frame). */
enum {
    NVMTL_P4_YES = 1,        /* phase 4: scan-out buffer only, the binding marked newer at publication */
    NVMTL_P4_UNBOUND,        /* no binding: read back (the only copy of the frame for other processes) */
    NVMTL_P4_MODE_FULL,      /* readback mode full */
    NVMTL_P4_MODE_OFF,       /* readback mode off: scan-out buffer only, no mark */
    NVMTL_P4_PITCH,          /* the pages' row pitch differs from the scan-out buffer's */
    NVMTL_P4_PLANE_OFFSET,   /* the plane does not start at the allocation's start */
    NVMTL_P4_ALLOC_SHORT,    /* the allocation is shorter than the frame rounded up to pages */
    NVMTL_P4_REFUSED,        /* the kernel refused a recent mark for this binding (held off for a while) */
    NVMTL_P4_NWHY
};
static inline const char *nvmtl_p4_why_name(int w)
{
    switch (w) {
    case NVMTL_P4_YES: return "engaged";
    case NVMTL_P4_UNBOUND: return "not bound";
    case NVMTL_P4_MODE_FULL: return "readback mode full";
    case NVMTL_P4_MODE_OFF: return "readback mode off";
    case NVMTL_P4_PITCH: return "row pitch differs from the scan-out buffer's";
    case NVMTL_P4_PLANE_OFFSET: return "plane not at the start of the allocation";
    case NVMTL_P4_ALLOC_SHORT: return "allocation shorter than the page-rounded frame";
    case NVMTL_P4_REFUSED: return "kernel refused a recent mark";
    default: return "?";
    }
}
typedef struct {
    int p4;        /* skip the readback and mark the binding newer at publication */
    int readback;  /* copy the frame into the IOSurface's pages */
    int why;       /* NVMTL_P4_* */
} nvmtl_p4_decision;

static inline uint64_t nvmtl_p4_frame_pages_bytes(uint32_t pitch, uint32_t h)
{
    return ((uint64_t)pitch * h + 0xfffull) & ~0xfffull;
}
/* bound: the surface has a scan-out or readback binding (its frame goes into that buffer). pitch, h: the binding's.
   row: the plane's bytes per row; plane_off: the plane's offset from IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress; alloc: IOSurfaceGetAllocSize.
   refused: the kernel refused a mark for this binding recently. */
static inline nvmtl_p4_decision nvmtl_p4_decide(nvmtl_sorb_mode mode, int bound, uint32_t pitch, uint32_t h, size_t row,
                                                size_t plane_off, size_t alloc, int refused)
{
    nvmtl_p4_decision d = { 0, 1, NVMTL_P4_UNBOUND };
    if (!bound) return d;
    if (mode == NVMTL_SORB_FULL) { d.why = NVMTL_P4_MODE_FULL; return d; }
    if (mode == NVMTL_SORB_OFF) { d.readback = 0; d.why = NVMTL_P4_MODE_OFF; return d; }
    if (!pitch || (size_t)pitch != row) { d.why = NVMTL_P4_PITCH; return d; }
    if (plane_off) { d.why = NVMTL_P4_PLANE_OFFSET; return d; }
    if ((uint64_t)alloc < nvmtl_p4_frame_pages_bytes(pitch, h)) { d.why = NVMTL_P4_ALLOC_SHORT; return d; }
    if (refused) { d.why = NVMTL_P4_REFUSED; return d; }
    d.p4 = 1; d.readback = 0; d.why = NVMTL_P4_YES;
    return d;
}
/* What the selector-2 answer means (NMXAccel kNmxSc*; -1: no present client or an NMXAccel without selector 2). */
static inline const char *nvmtl_p4_mark_status_name(int st)
{
    switch (st) {
    case 0: return "marked";
    case 4: return "busy";
    case 7: return "not bound by this client";
    case 8: return "no family resource (a CPU lock would not page it off)";
    case 9: return "caller is not WindowServer";
    case -1: return "no present client / NMXAccel without phase 4";
    default: return "refused";
    }
}
#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_sparse.h

/* nvmtl_sparse.h - Metal sparse textures (tier 1) over Vulkan sparse image residency, behind NVMTL_SPARSE_TEXTURES=1.
   The Vulkan side is nvmtl_sparse_vk.c (included at the end of nvmtl_vk.c, so it shares its device and queue), the Metal
   side NVMTLSparse.m; docs/design/DESIGN-sparse-textures.md says what maps to what and in which order.
   Off (the default) nothing here is reached: no feature is enabled, no answer changes, no submission waits. */
#ifndef NVMTL_SPARSE_H
#define NVMTL_SPARSE_H
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stddef.h>

/* (Placement sparse buffers - Metal 4's MTLBufferSparseTier1 - ride the same knob, the same batches and the same
   ordering; they need sparseResidencyBuffer too.) */
/* NVMTL_SPARSE_TEXTURES=1 in this process (a release plugin keeps it with NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 or the conf file) */
int nvmtl_sparse_knob(void);
/* the knob is on and the device was created with sparseBinding + sparseResidencyImage2D + shaderResourceResidency on a
   queue that binds sparse memory, with timeline semaphores: every sparse answer of the plugin follows this */
int nvmtl_vk_sparse_tex(void);
/* nvmtl_vk.c's device creation: enables the features (from what the device supports) when the knob asks for them.
   supported/enabled are VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures. Returns 1 when sparse textures are on. */
int nvmtl_sparse_tex_enable(const void *supported, void *enabled, int queue_sparse, int timeline);

/* The tile shape (texels) of a sparse image of this format and shape (Vulkan's sparse image format granularity),
   0 when the format cannot be sparse. is3d: a 3D image; samples: 1 for every texture here. */
int nvmtl_vk_sparse_tile_shape(uint32_t vkfmt, int is3d, uint32_t samples, uint32_t *tw, uint32_t *th, uint32_t *td);
/* The bytes of one tile (the sparse block size: VkMemoryRequirements.alignment of a sparse image; 64 KiB on ANV), 0 off */
uint32_t nvmtl_vk_sparse_tile_bytes(void);

/* A sparse image's layout: tile shape, and its mip tail (Vulkan: imageMipTailFirstLod and the tail's opaque range). */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t tw, th, td;          /* tile shape in texels */
    uint32_t tile_bytes;
    uint32_t tail_first;          /* first mip level of the tail (== mips: no tail) */
    uint32_t single_tail;         /* one tail for every layer (VK_SPARSE_IMAGE_FORMAT_SINGLE_MIPTAIL_BIT) */
    uint64_t tail_size, tail_offset, tail_stride;   /* bytes; offset/stride in the image's opaque range */
    uint32_t mem_bits;            /* memory types the image may be bound to */
} nvmtl_sparse_layout;

/* A colour image with SPARSE_BINDING | SPARSE_RESIDENCY and nothing bound (every tile reads zero), its base view, and
   its layout. Arguments as nvmtl_vk_image_create_typed. out->placed is 1 (no memory of its own). -1 when the format or
   shape cannot be sparse here. */
int nvmtl_vk_image_create_sparse(uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t vkfmt, uint32_t bpp, int a8, uint32_t mips, int storage,
                                 uint32_t mtl_type, uint32_t layers, void *nvk_image_out, nvmtl_sparse_layout *lay);
/* Sparse textures are on and the device binds sparse residency buffers (placement sparse buffers) */
int nvmtl_vk_sparse_buf(void);
/* A VkBuffer with SPARSE_BINDING | SPARSE_RESIDENCY (+ SPARSE_ALIASED where offered) of `size` bytes rounded up to
   `page_bytes` (which the buffer block size must divide), nothing bound: every byte reads zero, writes vanish.
   out->placed is 1 (no memory of its own); *mem_bits the memory types its tiles may come from. -1 when refused. */
int nvmtl_vk_buffer_create_sparse_residency(size_t size, uint32_t page_bytes, void *nvk_buffer_out, uint32_t *mem_bits);
/* Destroys a sparse buffer at once (no grace deferral), which unbinds its range */
void nvmtl_vk_sparse_buffer_destroy(void *nvk_buffer);
/* The tile pool of a sparse MTLHeap: one VkDeviceMemory of `bytes` (whole tiles) of a type sparse images can bind. */
int nvmtl_vk_sparse_pool_create(size_t bytes, void **mem_out);
void nvmtl_vk_sparse_pool_free(void *mem, size_t bytes);
/* 1 when a placement heap's memory type (nvk_heap.memtype) can back tiles of an image of layout `lay` */
int nvmtl_vk_sparse_memtype_ok(const nvmtl_sparse_layout *lay, uint32_t memtype);

/* A batch of binds that runs when the submission it rides is submitted (nvk_cmdbuf.sparse), before that submission's
   commands and after everything submitted before it (nvmtl_vk_submit_begin_at). mem NULL unbinds. */
typedef struct nvmtl_sparse_batch nvmtl_sparse_batch;
nvmtl_sparse_batch *nvmtl_sparse_batch_of(void *nvk_cmdbuf_c);   /* the batch of a recording, made on first use */
int nvmtl_sparse_batch_tile(nvmtl_sparse_batch *b, void *img, uint32_t mip, uint32_t layer, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t z,
                            uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t d, void *mem, uint64_t mem_off);
int nvmtl_sparse_batch_opaque(nvmtl_sparse_batch *b, void *img, uint64_t res_off, uint64_t size, void *mem, uint64_t mem_off);
/* A range of a sparse buffer bound to `mem` at mem_off (NULL: unbound); merged with the previous range when contiguous */
int nvmtl_sparse_batch_buffer(nvmtl_sparse_batch *b, void *buf, uint64_t res_off, uint64_t size, void *mem, uint64_t mem_off);
/* run(b, ctx) once the work submitted before the batch has COMPLETED (a CPU wait), then drop(ctx): for binds whose
   arguments the GPU writes (updateTextureMapping:indirectBuffer:). drop alone when the batch is never run. */
int nvmtl_sparse_batch_defer(nvmtl_sparse_batch *b, void (*run)(nvmtl_sparse_batch *, void *), void *ctx, void (*drop)(void *));
void nvmtl_sparse_batch_free(nvmtl_sparse_batch *b);
/* nvmtl_vk_submit_begin_at, submit mutex held: queues c's batch (if any) and returns the timeline point c must wait for
   on *sem (0: none). */
uint64_t nvmtl_sparse_before_submit(void *nvk_cmdbuf_c, void **sem);
/* ---- tier 2: per-tile access counters (NVMTL_SPARSE_TIER2=1 with NVMTL_SPARSE_TEXTURES=1; DESIGN-sparse-textures.md
   "Tier 2"). Vulkan and Xe2 have none: the translator (src/sparse_counters.rs, caps bit 4) makes every texel read of a
   heap texture add to its tile's counter. Heap slot NVMTL_SC_SLOT holds the directory (binding 3, RGBA32UI, one element
   per heap slot) and the counters (binding 4, R32UI); a texture's counters are a header of NVMTL_SC_HEADER words (where
   each level's counters start; word 15: how many) and then level by level, slice, z, y, x. Off, nothing here is reached
   and the heap hands out every slot as before. */
#define NVMTL_SC_SLOT 32767u        /* the translator's sparse_counters::COUNTER_HEAP_SLOT: the heap's last slot */
#define NVMTL_SC_HEADER 16u
#define NVMTL_SC_LEVELS 15u
/* NVMTL_SPARSE_TIER2=1 and NVMTL_SPARSE_TEXTURES=1 in this process */
int nvmtl_sparse_tier2_knob(void);
/* the knob, sparse textures on, and the counters made (the heap has its texel bindings, the slot is kept) */
int nvmtl_vk_sparse_tier2(void);
/* A texture's counters: the record its heap slots' directory elements get, and where each level starts */
typedef struct {
    uint32_t rec[4];                      /* directory element: header word, w | h << 16, d | slices << 16, levels | log2 tile */
    uint32_t start[NVMTL_SC_LEVELS];      /* level m's first counter, from the end of the header */
    uint32_t gx[NVMTL_SC_LEVELS], gy[NVMTL_SC_LEVELS], gz[NVMTL_SC_LEVELS];   /* tiles per level */
    uint32_t levels, slices, count;       /* counted levels, slices (layers; 1 for 3D), counters after the header */
} nvmtl_sc_layout;
/* Counters for a new sparse texture of level-0 size w x h x d (d 1 unless 3D), `slices` layers, `mips` levels and tile
   shape tw x th x td; views[0..1] (NULL allowed) are the image views its heap slots will hold. Zeroed on the GPU before
   this returns. 0 on success; -1 (logged): the texture stays tier 1. */
int nvmtl_sparse_counters_make(void *const views[2], uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t d, uint32_t slices, uint32_t mips,
                               uint32_t tw, uint32_t th, uint32_t td, nvmtl_sc_layout *out);
/* the texture is gone: its slots stop counting at once, its counters go back */
void nvmtl_sparse_counters_free(const nvmtl_sc_layout *l);
/* nvmtl_vk.c's heap: a slot now holds `view` / the slot was given up. No-ops unless the counters are on. */
void nvmtl_sparse_counters_slot(uint32_t slot, const void *view);
void nvmtl_sparse_counters_slot_gone(uint32_t slot);
/* Records into c (an nvk_cmdbuf), ordered as a blit: the counters of tiles [x, x + w) x [y, y + h) x [z, z + d) of `level`
   and `slice` copied into dst (an nvk_buffer) at dst_off, one uint32 per tile, x fastest, then y, then z (reset: then
   cleared); or only cleared (dst NULL). Tiles outside the level are skipped. Returns -1 when nothing could be recorded. */
int nvmtl_sparse_counters_get(void *c, const nvmtl_sc_layout *l, uint32_t level, uint32_t slice, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t z,
                              uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t d, void *dst, size_t dst_off, int reset);
#ifdef __OBJC__

int nvmtl_sparse_heap_init(id heap, MTLHeapDescriptor *d);       /* MTLHeapTypeSparse: 1 a tile pool, 0 not ours, -1 failed */

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_spec_fc.h

// Function-constant values into a module whose function constants are specialization constants
// (nvmtl_translate_fc_spec, translator wrapper spec_fc.rs). The values become the specialization constants' defaults,
// which is exactly what VkSpecializationInfo would do: the driver folds them before it compiles. The SpecIds are read
// from the module's decorations:
//   0x00800000 | (index << 3) | lane    value of function constant `index`, lane `lane`
//   0x01000000 | index                  1 when function constant `index` has a value (is_function_constant_defined)
// (other specialization constants, such as a kernel's workgroup size at SpecId 0-3, are not touched)
// Values are little-endian bytes as Metal holds them (MTLFunctionConstantValues), lane after lane.
#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#define NVMTL_SPEC_DEFINED 0x01000000u
#define NVMTL_SPEC_VALUE 0x00800000u

// Returns a malloc'ed copy of the module with the values applied (*out_words words), or NULL on a malformed module.
// *applied counts the specialization constants that took a supplied value (definedness included).
// freeze: the specialization constants become plain constants (OpSpecConstant* -> OpConstant*, SpecId decorations
// dropped), the module then is exactly a module translated with the values; otherwise they stay specialization
// constants whose defaults are the values.
static uint32_t *nvmtl_spec_fc_apply_ex(const uint32_t *w, size_t n, const uint32_t *idx, const uint32_t *sz,
                                        const uint8_t *const *pay, size_t count, size_t *out_words, unsigned *applied, int freeze);
static uint32_t *nvmtl_spec_fc_apply(const uint32_t *w, size_t n, const uint32_t *idx, const uint32_t *sz,
                                     const uint8_t *const *pay, size_t count, size_t *out_words, unsigned *applied)
{
    return nvmtl_spec_fc_apply_ex(w, n, idx, sz, pay, count, out_words, applied, 0);
}
static uint32_t *nvmtl_spec_fc_apply_ex(const uint32_t *w, size_t n, const uint32_t *idx, const uint32_t *sz,
                                        const uint8_t *const *pay, size_t count, size_t *out_words, unsigned *applied, int freeze)
{
    if (applied) *applied = 0;
    if (n < 5 || w[0] != 0x07230203u) return NULL;
    const uint32_t bound = w[3];
    if (!bound || bound > (1u << 26)) return NULL;
    uint32_t *spec = calloc(bound, sizeof *spec);      // id -> SpecId + 1 (0: none)
    uint32_t *tinfo = calloc(bound, sizeof *tinfo);    // type id -> bits | signed << 8 | float << 9 (0: not a scalar)
    uint32_t *out = malloc(n * sizeof *out);
    if (!spec || !tinfo || !out) { free(spec); free(tinfo); free(out); return NULL; }
    memcpy(out, w, n * sizeof *out);
    for (size_t i = 5; i < n;) {
        const uint32_t op = w[i] & 0xffffu, wc = w[i] >> 16;
        if (!wc || i + wc > n) { free(spec); free(tinfo); free(out); return NULL; }
        if (op == 71 && wc == 4 && w[i + 2] == 1 && w[i + 1] < bound) spec[w[i + 1]] = w[i + 3] + 1;      // OpDecorate SpecId
        else if (op == 21 && wc == 4 && w[i + 1] < bound) tinfo[w[i + 1]] = (w[i + 2] & 0xff) | (w[i + 3] ? 1u << 8 : 0); // OpTypeInt
        else if (op == 22 && wc >= 3 && w[i + 1] < bound) tinfo[w[i + 1]] = (w[i + 2] & 0xff) | 1u << 9;          // OpTypeFloat
        else if (op == 54) break;                                                                               // OpFunction: no more
        i += wc;
    }
    for (size_t i = 5; i < n;) {
        const uint32_t op = w[i] & 0xffffu, wc = w[i] >> 16;
        if (op == 54) break;
        // OpSpecConstantTrue / OpSpecConstantFalse / OpSpecConstant
        if ((op == 48 || op == 49 || op == 50) && wc >= 3 && w[i + 2] < bound && spec[w[i + 2]]) {
            const uint32_t sid = spec[w[i + 2]] - 1;
            if (!(sid & (NVMTL_SPEC_DEFINED | NVMTL_SPEC_VALUE))) { spec[w[i + 2]] = 0; i += wc; continue; }   // not ours
            const uint32_t index = (sid & NVMTL_SPEC_DEFINED) ? (sid & ~NVMTL_SPEC_DEFINED) : (sid & ~NVMTL_SPEC_VALUE) >> 3, lane = sid & 7;
            const uint8_t *v = NULL; uint32_t vlen = 0;
            for (size_t k = 0; k < count; k++) if (idx[k] == index) { v = pay[k]; vlen = sz[k]; break; }
            if (sid & NVMTL_SPEC_DEFINED) {
                if (op != 50) { out[i] = (wc << 16) | (v ? 48u : 49u); if (v && applied) (*applied)++; }
            } else if (v && op != 50) {                                  // a bool-typed constant: one byte per lane
                if (lane < vlen) { out[i] = (wc << 16) | (v[lane] ? 48u : 49u); if (applied) (*applied)++; }
            } else if (v && op == 50 && w[i + 1] < bound && tinfo[w[i + 1]]) {
                const uint32_t ti = tinfo[w[i + 1]], bits = ti & 0xff, bytes = bits / 8;
                if (bytes && (lane + 1) * bytes <= vlen && ((bits <= 32 && wc == 4) || (bits == 64 && wc == 5))) {
                    uint64_t x = 0;
                    memcpy(&x, v + lane * bytes, bytes);
                    if (bits < 32 && (ti & (1u << 8)) && (x >> (bits - 1)) & 1) x |= ~0ull << bits;   // signed: sign-extend
                    out[i + 3] = (uint32_t)x;
                    if (bits == 64) out[i + 4] = (uint32_t)(x >> 32);
                    if (applied) (*applied)++;
                }
            }
        }
        i += wc;
    }
    if (freeze) {   // after the values are in: plain constants, and the SpecId decorations go
        // spec[id] is nonzero only for ours now; a composite is frozen when all its constituents are
        size_t o = 5;
        for (size_t i = 5; i < n;) {
            const uint32_t op = out[i] & 0xffffu, wc = out[i] >> 16;
            if (op == 71 && wc == 4 && out[i + 2] == 1 && out[i + 1] < bound && spec[out[i + 1]]) { i += wc; continue; }   // our SpecId
            uint32_t nop = op;
            if ((op == 48 || op == 49 || op == 50) && wc >= 3 && out[i + 2] < bound && spec[out[i + 2]])
                nop = op == 48 ? 41u : op == 49 ? 42u : 43u;                                       // Spec* -> Constant*
            else if (op == 51 && wc >= 3 && out[i + 2] < bound) {
                int all = 1; for (uint32_t k = 3; k < wc; k++) if (out[i + k] >= bound || !spec[out[i + k]]) all = 0;
                if (all) { nop = 44u; spec[out[i + 2]] = 1; }                                      // OpConstantComposite
            }
            memmove(out + o, out + i, wc * sizeof *out);
            out[o] = (wc << 16) | nop;
            o += wc; i += wc;
        }
        n = o;
    }
    free(spec); free(tinfo);
    *out_words = n;
    return out;
}

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT */
/* nvmtl_spv_literal.h: which operand words of a SPIR-V instruction are literals, for the plugin's module passes that look
   for every use of an id (cs-table-pc in nvmtl_table_pc.h, bufoff in nvmtl_bufoff_pc.h). Pure C, no Vulkan or ObjC.

   Those passes refuse a module when any word of an instruction equals the id they want to move or rewrite, because a
   word they cannot classify might be a use. A literal that merely equals the id then refuses the module for nothing,
   and small ids are common: the translator declares the compute dispatch block early (ids 3 to 30), so
   `OpVariable %p StorageBuffer` (storage class 12), `OpVariable %p Function` (7), `OpExtInst %t %r %glsl Sqrt` (31) or
   `OpTypeVector %v %f 3` refused it. On the Geekbench 7 kernels 14 of 115 kernels lost cs-table-pc that way (B580
   night of 13 Nov, DESCRIPTOR-MODEL.md section 16).

   nvmtl_spv_word_is_literal(i, k) answers 1 only for operand positions the SPIR-V grammar fixes as literals (or as
   label ids, which can never be another kind of id) in the instructions where they occur; every other word is still
   treated as a possible id, so an instruction this table does not know keeps the old, conservative answer. */
#ifndef NVMTL_SPV_LITERAL_H
#define NVMTL_SPV_LITERAL_H
#include <stdint.h>

/* i: the instruction's first word; k: the word index (1 = the first operand). wc must be the instruction's word count. */
static int nvmtl_spv_word_is_literal(const uint32_t *i, uint32_t k)
{
    const uint32_t op = i[0] & 0xffffu, wc = i[0] >> 16;
    if (!k || k >= wc) return 0;
    switch (op) {
    case 12:  return k == 4;                       /* OpExtInst: type, result, set, the instruction number, operands */
    case 23: case 24: return k == 3;               /* OpTypeVector / OpTypeMatrix: the component or column count */
    case 25:  return k >= 3;                       /* OpTypeImage: dim, depth, arrayed, MS, sampled, format, access */
    case 32: case 39: return k == 2;               /* OpTypePointer / OpTypeForwardPointer: the storage class */
    case 43: case 50: return k >= 3;               /* OpConstant / OpSpecConstant: the value */
    case 52:  return k == 3;                       /* OpSpecConstantOp: the opcode (its own literals stay counted) */
    case 54:  return k == 3;                       /* OpFunction: the function control mask */
    case 59:  return k == 3;                       /* OpVariable: the storage class */
    case 61:  return k >= 4;                       /* OpLoad: memory operands */
    case 62:  return k >= 3;                       /* OpStore: memory operands */
    case 63:  return k >= 3;                       /* OpCopyMemory: memory operands */
    case 64:  return k >= 4;                       /* OpCopyMemorySized: memory operands */
    case 79:  return k >= 5;                       /* OpVectorShuffle: the components */
    case 81:  return k >= 4;                       /* OpCompositeExtract: the indices */
    case 82:  return k >= 5;                       /* OpCompositeInsert: the indices */
    case 246: return k >= 3;                       /* OpLoopMerge: loop control and its literals (k 1, 2: labels) */
    case 247: return k >= 2;                       /* OpSelectionMerge: selection control */
    case 250: return k >= 4;                       /* OpBranchConditional: branch weights */
    case 251: return k >= 3;                       /* OpSwitch: case literals and their labels (labels are never other ids) */
    case 342: case 349: case 350: case 351: case 352: case 353: case 354: case 355: case 356: case 357: case 358:
    case 359: case 360: case 361: case 362:
              return k == 4;                       /* OpGroupNonUniformBallotBitCount, IAdd .. LogicalXor: the group operation */
    case 264: case 265: case 266: case 267: case 268: case 269: case 270:
              return k == 4;                       /* OpGroupIAdd .. OpGroupSMax: the group operation */
    case 87: case 88: case 91: case 92: case 95: case 98:
              return k == 5;                       /* image sample / fetch / read: the image operands mask */
    case 89: case 90: case 93: case 94: case 96: case 97:
              return k == 6;                       /* the Dref and gather forms: the image operands mask */
    case 99:  return k == 4;                       /* OpImageWrite: the image operands mask */
    default:  return 0;
    }
}
#endif

/* nvmtl_spvcache_name.h - which shader-cache entries the stale sweep keeps. Entry names are
   <digest>.<stage>.<build tag><mode suffixes>.c3.spv, where the build tag names the translator and the suffixes
   (-u2, -p5, -as1, ...) name the modes the process translated in. Pure, so tools/test_app_profile.c proves it. */
#ifndef NVMTL_SPVCACHE_NAME_H
#define NVMTL_SPVCACHE_NAME_H
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
/* Room for the build tag (sha256-<64 hex>) and every mode suffix, with space to spare. */
#define NVMTL_SPVCACHE_TAG_MAX 160
/* Writes the cache tag for translator build `build` in the given modes. Returns 1, or 0 when the whole tag does not fit
   in `cap` (a cut tag would let two modes share entries); on 0 the caller must not cache. */
static inline int nvmtl_spvcache_mode_tag(char *tag, size_t cap, const char *build, int unroll, int canonical,
                                          int argbuf_samplers, int no_ptr_phi_load, int no_pixel_hw_filter)
{
    if (!tag || !cap || !build) return 0;
    const int k = snprintf(tag, cap, "%s%s%s%s%s%s", build, unroll ? "-u2" : "", canonical ? "-p5" : "",
                           argbuf_samplers ? "-as1" : "", no_ptr_phi_load ? "-np" : "", no_pixel_hw_filter ? "-nf" : "");
    return k > 0 && (size_t)k < cap;
}
/* 1 when `name` is an entry of translator build `build` (any mode); 0 for another build's entry or a foreign file. */
static inline int nvmtl_spvcache_same_build(const char *name, const char *build)
{
    const size_t n = strlen(name), bn = strlen(build);
    if (!bn || n < 7 || strcmp(name + n - 7, ".c3.spv")) return 0;
    for (const char *at = strstr(name, build); at; at = strstr(at + 1, build))
        if (at > name && at[-1] == '.' && (at[bn] == '-' || at[bn] == '.')) return 1;
    return 0;
}
#endif

// nvmtl_tex_upload.h: ordering and lifetime decisions for asynchronous texture uploads.
//
// replaceRegion and IOSurface uploads currently submit a copy and wait for the GPU before returning
// (nvmtl_vk_image_write*), so a GL app that uploads many textures per frame stalls once per upload. An
// earlier attempt (community PR #96) deferred the wait but was reverted: nvmtl_vk_image_destroy frees the
// image and its memory at once, and IOSurface-backed textures are uploaded then destroyed, so a deferred
// copy could land in freed GPU memory.
//
// This is the decision logic for doing it safely, gated by NVMTL_ASYNC_TEX_UPLOAD. One async upload may be
// in flight per image; its in-flight handle is recorded on the image. Before anything that would overwrite,
// read back, CPU-map or free that image's memory, the pending upload is finished (fence waited) first. Pure,
// so the invariants are unit-tested without a GPU; the plugin supplies the fence primitives.
//
// Invariants (each an arm of test_tex_upload.c):
//   - synchronous path (flag off): a new upload submits-and-waits; nothing is ever left pending, so the
//     destroy/readback guard finds nothing to finish and is a no-op (this is what keeps the current path
//     byte-for-byte the same);
//   - a second upload to the same image finishes the first (it would otherwise overwrite a texture, or reuse
//     staging bytes, while the GPU is still copying);
//   - destroy, readback, CPU map and surface-out finish a pending upload first (no use-after-free: this is
//     the #96 regression this guard exists to prevent);
//   - a draw that merely SAMPLES the image needs no CPU finish: the upload's command buffer was submitted, so
//     queue order plus the image's TRANSFER->SHADER_READ barrier already order the copy before the sample.

#ifndef NVMTL_TEX_UPLOAD_H
#define NVMTL_TEX_UPLOAD_H

#include <stdint.h>

// Per-image async-upload bookkeeping. `infl` is an opaque handle to the in-flight submission (the plugin
// stores an nvmtl_inflight pointer, cast to uint64_t); 0 means no async upload is in flight for this image.
typedef struct { uint64_t infl; } nvmtl_up_state;

typedef enum {
    NVMTL_UP_SUBMIT_WAIT  = 0,   // submit the copy and wait now (the synchronous default)
    NVMTL_UP_SUBMIT_ASYNC = 1,   // submit without waiting; the caller records the handle with nvmtl_up_set
} nvmtl_up_submit;

// Decide how to submit a new upload to an image. If a previous async upload to THIS image is still in
// flight, it must be finished first: its handle is returned through *finish_first (0 means none). The submit
// mode is async only when the flag is on.
static inline nvmtl_up_submit nvmtl_up_before_upload(const nvmtl_up_state *s, int async_flag,
                                                     uint64_t *finish_first)
{
    *finish_first = s ? s->infl : 0;
    return async_flag ? NVMTL_UP_SUBMIT_ASYNC : NVMTL_UP_SUBMIT_WAIT;
}

// What a consumer (destroy, readback, CPU map, surface-out) must finish before touching the image's memory:
// the pending in-flight handle, or 0 for nothing. On the synchronous path `infl` is never set, so this
// returns 0 and the consumer proceeds exactly as it does today.
static inline uint64_t nvmtl_up_before_consume(const nvmtl_up_state *s)
{
    return s ? s->infl : 0;
}

// Record the in-flight handle after an async submit; clear it after the upload has been finished (waited).
static inline void nvmtl_up_set(nvmtl_up_state *s, uint64_t infl) { if (s) s->infl = infl; }
static inline void nvmtl_up_clear(nvmtl_up_state *s) { if (s) s->infl = 0; }

#endif

FILE: nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_ts_convert.comp

#version 460
// Metal GPU timestamps: the raw Vulkan timestamp ticks a resolveCounters: copied into Metal's destination become
// nanoseconds on the host's CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW scale (the scale -sampleTimestamps:gpuTimestamp: answers in), in place.
// ns = ref_ns +/- |tick - ref_tick| (signed, modulo the queue's timestampValidBits) * period, with period split into
// its integer nanoseconds and a 32-bit binary fraction. MTLCounterErrorValue (~0: a sample never written) is left as
// it is. One invocation per sample (nvmtl_vk_cmd_ts_resolve).
//   glslangValidator -V --target-env vulkan1.2 nvmtl_ts_convert.comp -o nvmtl_ts_convert.spv
#extension GL_EXT_buffer_reference : require
#extension GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types_int64 : require
layout(local_size_x = 64) in;
layout(buffer_reference, std430, buffer_reference_align = 8) buffer Stamps { uint64_t t[]; };
layout(push_constant) uniform Args {
    uint64_t dst;        // the first resolved sample (8-aligned)
    uint64_t ref_tick;   // a GPU tick ...
    uint64_t ref_ns;     // ... and the host nanosecond it was read at
    uint64_t mask;       // (1 << timestampValidBits) - 1
    uint count;
    uint period_int;     // timestampPeriod = period_int + period_frac / 2^32 ns per tick
    uint period_frac;
    uint pad;
} a;

void main()
{
    const uint i = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x;
    if (i >= a.count) return;
    Stamps s = Stamps(a.dst);
    const uint64_t v = s.t[i];
    if (v == ~0ul) return;
    const uint64_t d = (v - a.ref_tick) & a.mask;
    const bool before = (d & ((a.mask >> 1) + 1ul)) != 0ul;
    const uint64_t mag = before ? ((~d + 1ul) & a.mask) : d;
    const uint64_t hi = mag >> 32, lo = mag & 0xfffffffful;
    const uint64_t ns = mag * uint64_t(a.period_int) + hi * uint64_t(a.period_frac) + ((lo * uint64_t(a.period_frac)) >> 32);
    s.t[i] = before ? a.ref_ns - ns : a.ref_ns + ns;
}

    if (!a0) {

        if (!z) { nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: NULL pointer, %lu bytes: no buffer to stand in -> nil", (unsigned long)a1); return nil; }
        void *zc = [z contents];
        if (zc) { memset(zc, 0, a1); if (z->_shadow.map) [z didModifyRange:NSMakeRange(0, a1)]; }
        if (a3) { void (^user)(void *, NSUInteger) = [a3 copy]; const NSUInteger n = a1;
                  z->_hostDealloc = ^(void *p, NSUInteger l) { (void)p; (void)l; user(NULL, n); }; }
        { static int said; if (!said++) nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: NULL pointer, %lu bytes -> a zero-filled buffer of our own; its deallocator gets (NULL, %lu)", (unsigned long)a1, (unsigned long)a1); }
        return z;
    }
    NVMTLBuffer *b = [NVMTLBuffer new];
    b->_storage = sm;
    b->_ropt = a2 & ((MTLResourceOptions)0xF | ((MTLResourceOptions)0x3 << MTLResourceHazardTrackingModeShift));
    b->_hostDealloc = a3 ? [a3 copy] : nil;
    // Managed on a discrete GPU means the GPU works on its own copy, synchronized by didModifyRange (CPU -> GPU) and
    // synchronizeResource (GPU -> CPU). Apple's OpenCL wraps every cl_mem this way; importing the pages zero-copy put
    // every kernel access across PCIe instead (a 5600x4200 byte-image rotate: 6.6 s per dispatch, Geekbench 6 OpenCL
    // Horizon Detection hit the 60 s GPU watchdog). The caller's pages become the managed shadow, so contents is still
    // the caller's pointer, and the GPU side lives in VRAM (every size: see mirror_min below).
    // Every size since fix13: small ones too. WAS 1 MiB and up ("the transfer outweighs the win"), but a small cl_mem is
    // where OpenCL keeps its counters and histograms, and atomics on the caller's pages crossed PCIe one at a time:
    // Geekbench's find_min_and_max took 205-511 ms per dispatch and build_histograms 122 ms, 52% of its GPU time; with
    // the VRAM copy the same shapes take 1.9 ms and 0.4 ms (clatom). NVMTL_MANAGED_MIRROR_MIN=<bytes>: the old floor.
    static long long mirror_min = -1;
    if (mirror_min < 0) { const char *e = getenv("NVMTL_MANAGED_MIRROR_MIN"); mirror_min = (e && *e) ? atoll(e) : 0; }
    if (sm == MTLStorageModeManaged && (long long)a1 >= mirror_min && nvmtl_vk_buffer_import_host(a0, a1, &b->_shadow) == 0) {
        if (nvmtl_vk_buffer_create(a1, 0, &b->_b) == 0) {
            [b didModifyRange:NSMakeRange(0, a1)];
            { static int said; if (!said++) nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: managed %lu bytes -> VRAM copy, caller's pages are the shadow", (unsigned long)a1); }
            return b;
        }
        nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: managed %lu bytes: VRAM refused - the GPU reads the caller's pages directly", (unsigned long)a1);
        b->_b = b->_shadow; memset(&b->_shadow, 0, sizeof b->_shadow);
        return b;
    }
    if (nvmtl_vk_buffer_import_host(a0, a1, &b->_b) == 0) {
        static int said; if (!said++) nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: IMPORTED the caller's pages (%lu bytes at %p) \u2014 zero copy", (unsigned long)a1, a0);
        return b;
    }
    if (nvmtl_vk_buffer_create(a1, 1, &b->_b) || !b->_b.map) {
        nvmtl_alloc_failed("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy");
        nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: could neither import nor allocate %lu bytes -> nil", (unsigned long)a1);
        return nil;
    }
    memcpy(b->_b.map, a0, a1);
    b->_hostPtr = a0; b->_hostLen = (size_t)a1;
    { static int said; if (!said++) nvlog("newBufferWithBytesNoCopy: COPIED %lu bytes at %p (import alignment %zu) \u2014 resynced at every submission",
                                          (unsigned long)a1, a0, nvmtl_vk_host_import_align()); }
    return b;
}
- (id)newBufferWithDescriptor:(id)a0 { nvlog("newBufferWithDescriptor: -> nil (not built yet)"); return nil; }
- (id)newBufferWithIOSurface:(IOSurfaceRef)a0 { nvlog("newBufferWithIOSurface: -> nil (not built yet)"); return nil; }
- (id)newIndirectCommandBufferWithDescriptor:(id)a0 maxCount:(NSUInteger)a1 options:(NSUInteger)a2 { nvlog("newIndirectCommandBufferWithDescriptor:maxCount:options: -> nil (not built yet)"); return nil; }

/*
 * NullMoth NVIDIA driver for macOS
 * Copyright (c) 2026 NullMoth Systems.
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0
 */

#include <unistd.h>

#import <objc/runtime.h>
#import <objc/message.h>
#import <os/lock.h>

static os_unfair_lock  gFwdLock = OS_UNFAIR_LOCK_INIT;
static CFMutableDictionaryRef gEncCache;
static CFMutableDictionaryRef gSeen;
static int gIndexBuilt = 0;

typedef NSMethodSignature *(*nvfwd_msfs_fn)(id, SEL, SEL);
static struct { __unsafe_unretained Class cls; nvfwd_msfs_fn orig; } gOrig[32];
static int gNOrig = 0;

static nvfwd_msfs_fn nvfwd_original_for(Class c)
{
    for (Class k = c; k; k = class_getSuperclass(k))
        for (int i = 0; i < gNOrig; i++)
            if (gOrig[i].cls == k) return gOrig[i].orig;
    return NULL;
}

static const char *const kNVCounterpart[][2] = {
    {"NVMTLDevice",                 "MTLIOAccelDevice"},
    {"NVMTLCommandQueue",           "MTLIOAccelCommandQueue"},
    {"NVMTLCommandBuffer",          "MTLIOAccelCommandBuffer"},
    {"NVMTLBuffer",                 "MTLIOAccelBuffer"},
    {"NVMTLTexture",                "MTLIOAccelTexture"},
    {"NVMTLRenderCommandEncoder",   "MTLIOAccelRenderCommandEncoder"},
    {"NVMTLBlitCommandEncoder",     "MTLIOAccelBlitCommandEncoder"},
    {"NVMTLAccelerationStructureCommandEncoder", "_MTLAccelerationStructureCommandEncoder"},
    {"NVMTLAccelerationStructure",  "MTLIOAccelAccelerationStructure"},
    {"NVMTLComputeCommandEncoder",  "MTLIOAccelComputeCommandEncoder"},
    {"NVMTLHeap",                   "MTLIOAccelHeap"},
    {"NVMTLFence",                  "MTLIOAccelFence"},
    {"NVMTLSamplerState",           "MTLIOAccelSamplerState"},
    {"NVMTLDepthStencilState",      "MTLIOAccelDepthStencilState"},
    {"NVMTLLibrary",                "MTLLibrary"},
    {"NVMTLFunction",               "MTLFunction"},
    {"NVMTLArgumentEncoder",        "MTLArgumentEncoder"},
    {"NVMTLRenderPipelineState",    "MTLRenderPipelineState"},
    {"NVMTLComputePipelineState",   "MTLComputePipelineState"},
    {"NVMTLIndirectCommandBuffer",  "MTLIndirectCommandBuffer"},
    {NULL, NULL}
};

static const char *nvfwd_counterpart_encoding(Class c, SEL sel)
{
    const char *cn = class_getName(c);
    if (!cn) return NULL;
    for (int i = 0; kNVCounterpart[i][0]; i++) {
        if (strcmp(cn, kNVCounterpart[i][0])) continue;
        const char *an = kNVCounterpart[i][1];
        Class ac = objc_getClass(an);
        if (ac) {
            Method m = class_getInstanceMethod(ac, sel);
            if (m) return method_getTypeEncoding(m);
        }
        Protocol *p = objc_getProtocol(an);
        if (p) {
            for (int req = 0; req < 2; req++)
                for (int inst = 0; inst < 1; inst++) {
                    struct objc_method_description d =
                        protocol_getMethodDescription(p, sel, req == 0, YES);
                    if (d.name && d.types) return d.types;
                }
        }
        return NULL;
    }
    return NULL;
}

static void nvfwd_index_class(Class c)
{
    unsigned mc = 0;
    Method *ms = class_copyMethodList(c, &mc);
    for (unsigned j = 0; j < mc; j++) {
        const char *sn = sel_getName(method_getName(ms[j]));
        const char *te = method_getTypeEncoding(ms[j]);
        if (!sn || !te) continue;
        CFStringRef k = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, sn, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
        if (k) {
            if (!CFDictionaryContainsKey(gEncCache, k)) {
                CFStringRef v = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, te, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
                if (v) { CFDictionarySetValue(gEncCache, k, v); CFRelease(v); }
            }
            CFRelease(k);
        }
    }
    free(ms);
}

static void nvfwd_build_index(void)
{
    if (gIndexBuilt) return;
    gIndexBuilt = 1;
    int nclass = 0, nproto = 0;

    unsigned n = 0;
    Class *all = objc_copyClassList(&n);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const char *cn = class_getName(all[i]);
        if (!cn) continue;
        if (strncmp(cn, "MTL", 3) && strncmp(cn, "AGX", 3) && strncmp(cn, "AMD", 3) &&
            strncmp(cn, "IOAccel", 7) && strncmp(cn, "CA", 2) && strncmp(cn, "Apple", 5)) continue;
        nvfwd_index_class(all[i]);
        nclass++;
    }
    free(all);

    unsigned np = 0;
    Protocol *__unsafe_unretained *ps = objc_copyProtocolList(&np);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < np; i++) {
        const char *pn = protocol_getName(ps[i]);
        if (!pn || strncmp(pn, "MTL", 3)) continue;
        nproto++;
        for (int req = 0; req < 2; req++) {
            unsigned dc = 0;
            struct objc_method_description *ds =
                protocol_copyMethodDescriptionList(ps[i], req == 0, YES, &dc);
            for (unsigned j = 0; j < dc; j++) {
                const char *sn = ds[j].name ? sel_getName(ds[j].name) : NULL;
                const char *te = ds[j].types;
                if (!sn || !te) continue;
                CFStringRef k = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, sn, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
                if (k) {
                    if (!CFDictionaryContainsKey(gEncCache, k)) {
                        CFStringRef v = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, te, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
                        if (v) { CFDictionarySetValue(gEncCache, k, v); CFRelease(v); }
                    }
                    CFRelease(k);
                }
            }
            free(ds);
        }
    }
    free(ps);

    nvlog("NVMTLForward: encoding index built from %d classes + %d protocols, %ld selectors",
          nclass, nproto, (long)CFDictionaryGetCount(gEncCache));
}

static NSMethodSignature *nvfwd_synthesize(SEL sel)
{
    const char *sn = sel_getName(sel);
    int colons = 0;
    for (const char *p = sn; *p; p++) if (*p == ':') colons++;
    char enc[80];
    if (colons > 60) return nil;
    int o = 0;
    enc[o++] = '@'; enc[o++] = '@'; enc[o++] = ':';
    for (int i = 0; i < colons; i++) enc[o++] = '@';
    enc[o] = 0;
    nvlog("NVMTLForward: SYNTHESIZED signature \"%s\" for %s — no class or protocol declares it", enc, sn);
    return [NSMethodSignature signatureWithObjCTypes:enc];
}

static NSMethodSignature *nvfwd_msfs(id self, SEL _cmd, SEL sel)
{
    nvfwd_msfs_fn orig = nvfwd_original_for(object_getClass(self));
    if (orig) {
        NSMethodSignature *s = orig(self, _cmd, sel);
        if (s) return s;
    }

    const char *cte = nvfwd_counterpart_encoding(object_getClass(self), sel);
    if (cte) return [NSMethodSignature signatureWithObjCTypes:cte];

    const char *sn = sel_getName(sel);
    CFStringRef key = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, sn, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
    if (!key) return nil;

    os_unfair_lock_lock(&gFwdLock);
    nvfwd_build_index();
    CFStringRef enc = (CFStringRef)CFDictionaryGetValue(gEncCache, key);
    os_unfair_lock_unlock(&gFwdLock);
    CFRelease(key);

    if (enc) {
        char buf[512];
        if (CFStringGetCString(enc, buf, sizeof buf, kCFStringEncodingUTF8))
            return [NSMethodSignature signatureWithObjCTypes:buf];
    }
    return nvfwd_synthesize(sel);
}

static void nvfwd_forward(id self, SEL _cmd, NSInvocation *inv)
{
    SEL sel = [inv selector];
    const char *cn = class_getName(object_getClass(self));
    const char *sn = sel_getName(sel);

    char key[320];
    snprintf(key, sizeof key, "%s %s", cn, sn);
    long count = 0;
    CFStringRef k = CFStringCreateWithCString(NULL, key, kCFStringEncodingUTF8);
    if (k) {
        os_unfair_lock_lock(&gFwdLock);
        if (!gSeen) gSeen = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, NULL);
        count = (long)(intptr_t)CFDictionaryGetValue(gSeen, k) + 1;
        CFDictionarySetValue(gSeen, k, (const void *)(intptr_t)count);
        os_unfair_lock_unlock(&gFwdLock);
        CFRelease(k);
    }
    if (count <= 3 || (count % 1000) == 0) {
        extern const char *nvmtl_log_path(void);
        FILE *lf = fopen(nvmtl_log_path(), "a");
        const char *rt_ = [[inv methodSignature] methodReturnType];
        static const char *const kApple_[] = { "_MTLFunctionInternal", "_MTLFunction", "_MTLLibrary",
                                               "_MTLDevice", "_MTLCommandQueue", "_MTLCommandBuffer", NULL };
        for (int ci_ = 0; kApple_[ci_]; ci_++) {
            Class ac_ = objc_getClass(kApple_[ci_]);
            Method am_ = ac_ ? class_getInstanceMethod(ac_, [inv selector]) : NULL;
            const char *te_ = am_ ? method_getTypeEncoding(am_) : NULL;
            if (te_) { rt_ = te_; break; }
        }
        int deref_ = rt_ && (rt_[0] == '^' || (rt_[0] == 'r' && rt_[1] == '^'));
        if (lf) { fprintf(lf, "pid %d NVMTL: SPI-STUB -[%s %s]  (call #%ld, zero-returned — NOT IMPLEMENTED)%s\n", getpid(), cn, sn, count,
                          deref_ ? "  POINTER RETURN — a caller that dereferences this NULL will crash" : ""); fclose(lf); }
    }

    NSUInteger len = [[inv methodSignature] methodReturnLength];
    if (len) {
        void *z = calloc(1, len);
        if (z) { [inv setReturnValue:z]; free(z); }
    }
}

static const char *const kNVFwdClasses[] = {
    "NVMTLDevice", "NVMTLCommandQueue", "NVMTLCommandBuffer", "NVMTLBuffer", "NVMTLTexture",
    "NVMTLLibrary", "NVMTLFunction", "NVMTLArgumentEncoder", "NVMTLRenderPipelineState",
    "NVMTLRenderCommandEncoder", "NVMTLBlitCommandEncoder", "NVMTLComputeCommandEncoder",
    "NVMTLAccelerationStructureCommandEncoder", "NVMTLAccelerationStructure",
    "NVMTLComputePipelineState", "NVMTLDepthStencilState", "NVMTLSamplerState", "NVMTLFence",
    "NVMTLHeap", "NVMTLIndirectCommand", "NVMTLIndirectCommandBuffer",
    "NVMTLParallelRenderCommandEncoder", "NVMTLRenderPipelineReflection", "NVMTLComputePipelineReflection", "NVMTLArgument",
    "NVMTLStructType", "NVMTLStructMember", "NVMTLPointerType", "NVMTLTextureReferenceType", "NVMTLVertexAttribute",
    NULL
};

@interface NVMTLForwardInstaller : NSObject @end
@implementation NVMTLForwardInstaller
+ (void)load
{
    gEncCache = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks,
                                                   &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
    int installed = 0;
    for (int i = 0; kNVFwdClasses[i]; i++) {
        Class c = objc_getClass(kNVFwdClasses[i]);
        if (!c) { nvlog("NVMTLForward: class %s not found — NOT protected", kNVFwdClasses[i]); continue; }

        if (gNOrig < (int)(sizeof gOrig / sizeof gOrig[0])) {
            nvfwd_msfs_fn prev = (nvfwd_msfs_fn)class_getMethodImplementation(
                                     c, @selector(methodSignatureForSelector:));
            if (prev == (nvfwd_msfs_fn)nvfwd_msfs) prev = NULL;
            gOrig[gNOrig].cls  = c;
            gOrig[gNOrig].orig = prev;
            gNOrig++;
        }
        class_replaceMethod(c, @selector(methodSignatureForSelector:), (IMP)nvfwd_msfs,    "@@::");
        class_replaceMethod(c, @selector(forwardInvocation:),          (IMP)nvfwd_forward, "v@:@");
        installed++;
    }
    nvlog("NVMTLForward: forwarding net installed on %d classes (was: log-then-abort on 20)", installed);
}
@end

// An OpenGL app with vsync on keeps the display's refresh rate after a late frame, in every process this plugin loads
// into.
//
// AppKit hands an OpenGL frame to the window server in NSCGLSurfaceFlush. With vsync on, it first calls -[NSCGLSurface
// synchronize]. While the window server has not yet taken the previous frame, that waits for the first time after now
// in the surface's image queue's VBL info. The window server fills that info (CoreAnimation's CAShmemImageQueueUpdate)
// with its last vblank plus one to four refresh periods, taking the period from the timestamp of its update. Its window
// updates pass none, and CoreAnimation then spaces the times 1/60 s apart. On a faster display, one frame that misses
// the window server's update makes the next wait up to four refreshes. That wait ends on the window server's vblank, so
// the frame after it reaches the window server just after its update, and the next waits again: the app runs at two to
// three refreshes a frame until a frame happens to come early.
// Here synchronize waits for the display's next vblank by the display's own refresh period, as the info says when it
// has the period: a late frame costs one refresh, and the next frame is back in time.
//
// NVMTL_NO_GL_VBLANK_FIX in a process's environment leaves AppKit's own synchronize. Another image in the process that
// makes the same correction adds the same marker method to NSCGLSurface (NVGLVBL_MARKER), and only the first installs.

#include <CoreGraphics/CoreGraphics.h>
#include <mach-o/dyld.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <objc/runtime.h>
#include <os/lock.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>

int  nvmtl_hitch_ms(void);                  // nvmtl_vk.c: NVMTL_HITCH_MS
void nvmtl_hitch_frame(const char *source);

// QuartzCore's image queue calls synchronize makes, and a VBL info entry as CAImageQueueGetVBLInfo copies it out: the
// vblank's host time, the same time in seconds, and a rate (1)
typedef struct _CAImageQueue *NVGLVBLQueueRef;
struct nvglvbl_info { uint64_t host_time; double seconds; float rate; };
enum { NVGLVBL_ENTRIES = 4 };   // as many as synchronize asks for (and the window server writes)
#define NVGLVBL_MARKER "correctsVBlankWaitByDisplayPeriod"
#define NVGLVBL_WINDOW_RECHECK_S 1.0   // a window's display is looked up again after this (it may have moved)
enum { NVGLVBL_WINDOW_CACHE = 8 };      // windows whose display's period is remembered

static struct {
    size_t (*unconsumed)(NVGLVBLQueueRef queue, uint64_t, uint32_t);
    uint32_t (*vbl_info)(NVGLVBLQueueRef queue, struct nvglvbl_info *info, size_t count);
    // CoreGraphics, for the refresh rate of a window's display: looked up rather than linked (AppKit, which this needs,
    // brings it), so the plugin loads nothing more into the processes it is in
    __typeof__(&CGWindowListCreateDescriptionFromArray) window_descriptions;
    __typeof__(&CGRectMakeWithDictionaryRepresentation) rect_from_dictionary;
    __typeof__(&CGGetDisplaysWithRect) displays_with_rect;
    __typeof__(&CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode) copy_display_mode;
    __typeof__(&CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate) refresh_rate;
    __typeof__(&CGDisplayModeRelease) release_display_mode;
    const CFStringRef *window_bounds_key;
    IMP synchronize;                    // AppKit's own
    ptrdiff_t queue_ivar, window_ivar;  // -[NSCGLSurface] _imageQueue and _windowID
    atomic_bool installed;
} gGLVBL;

static uint64_t nvglvbl_mach_from_seconds(double s)
{
    static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
    if (!tb.denom) mach_timebase_info(&tb);
    return (uint64_t)(s * 1e9 * tb.denom / tb.numer);
}

// the refresh period (mach time) of the display window is on, 0 when unknown
static uint64_t nvglvbl_window_period(uint32_t window)
{
    static os_unfair_lock lock = OS_UNFAIR_LOCK_INIT;
    static struct { uint32_t window; uint64_t period, checked; } cache[NVGLVBL_WINDOW_CACHE];
    static unsigned next;
    const uint64_t now = mach_absolute_time(), recheck = nvglvbl_mach_from_seconds(NVGLVBL_WINDOW_RECHECK_S);
    os_unfair_lock_lock(&lock);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < NVGLVBL_WINDOW_CACHE; i++)
        if (cache[i].checked && cache[i].window == window && now - cache[i].checked < recheck) {
            const uint64_t period = cache[i].period;
            os_unfair_lock_unlock(&lock);
            return period;
        }
    os_unfair_lock_unlock(&lock);

    double hz = 0;
    const void *wid = (const void *)(uintptr_t)window;   // the array holds the CGWindowID itself
    CFArrayRef ids = CFArrayCreate(kCFAllocatorDefault, &wid, 1, NULL);
    CFArrayRef windows = ids ? gGLVBL.window_descriptions(ids) : NULL;
    CGRect bounds;
    CGDirectDisplayID display;
    uint32_t displays = 0;
    if (windows && CFArrayGetCount(windows) > 0 &&
        gGLVBL.rect_from_dictionary(CFDictionaryGetValue(CFArrayGetValueAtIndex(windows, 0), *gGLVBL.window_bounds_key),
                                    &bounds) &&
        gGLVBL.displays_with_rect(bounds, 1, &display, &displays) == kCGErrorSuccess && displays) {
        CGDisplayModeRef mode = gGLVBL.copy_display_mode(display);
        if (mode) {
            hz = gGLVBL.refresh_rate(mode);   // 0 for a display that does not say
            gGLVBL.release_display_mode(mode);
        }
    }
    if (windows) CFRelease(windows);
    if (ids) CFRelease(ids);
    const uint64_t period = hz > 0 ? nvglvbl_mach_from_seconds(1 / hz) : 0;

    os_unfair_lock_lock(&lock);
    int found = -1;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < NVGLVBL_WINDOW_CACHE; i++)
        if (cache[i].checked && cache[i].window == window) found = (int)i;
    const unsigned slot = found >= 0 ? (unsigned)found : next++ % NVGLVBL_WINDOW_CACHE;
    cache[slot].window = window;
    cache[slot].period = period;
    cache[slot].checked = now;
    os_unfair_lock_unlock(&lock);
    return period;
}

static void nvglvbl_synchronize(id self, SEL cmd)
{
    char *surface = (char *)(__bridge void *)self;
    NVGLVBLQueueRef queue = *(NVGLVBLQueueRef *)(surface + gGLVBL.queue_ivar);
    if (!queue || !gGLVBL.unconsumed(queue, 0, 0)) return;   // the window server has the previous frame: no wait
    struct nvglvbl_info info[NVGLVBL_ENTRIES];
    const uint32_t n = gGLVBL.vbl_info(queue, info, NVGLVBL_ENTRIES);
    const uint64_t period = nvglvbl_window_period(*(uint32_t *)(surface + gGLVBL.window_ivar));
    // the entries are the window server's vblank plus 1..n times the spacing CoreAnimation took for the period: with a
    // longer spacing than the display's period, the next vblank is that vblank plus a whole number of periods
    if (n >= 2 && n <= NVGLVBL_ENTRIES && period && info[1].host_time > info[0].host_time &&
        period < info[1].host_time - info[0].host_time) {
        const uint64_t vblank = info[0].host_time - (info[1].host_time - info[0].host_time);
        const uint64_t now = mach_absolute_time();
        mach_wait_until(vblank + (now > vblank ? (now - vblank) / period + 1 : 1) * period);
        return;
    }
    ((void (*)(id, SEL))gGLVBL.synchronize)(self, cmd);
}

static void nvglvbl_marker(id self, SEL cmd) { (void)self, (void)cmd; }

// replaces -[NSCGLSurface synchronize] once AppKit is loaded and has it, and everything it needs is found
static void nvglvbl_install(void)
{
    if (atomic_load(&gGLVBL.installed)) return;
    Class surface = objc_getClass("NSCGLSurface");
    if (!surface) return;
    Method m = class_getInstanceMethod(surface, sel_registerName("synchronize"));
    Ivar queue = class_getInstanceVariable(surface, "_imageQueue"), window = class_getInstanceVariable(surface, "_windowID");
    gGLVBL.unconsumed = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CAImageQueueGetUnconsumedImageCount");
    gGLVBL.vbl_info = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CAImageQueueGetVBLInfo");
    gGLVBL.window_descriptions = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CGWindowListCreateDescriptionFromArray");
    gGLVBL.rect_from_dictionary = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CGRectMakeWithDictionaryRepresentation");
    gGLVBL.displays_with_rect = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CGGetDisplaysWithRect");
    gGLVBL.copy_display_mode = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode");
    gGLVBL.refresh_rate = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate");
    gGLVBL.release_display_mode = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "CGDisplayModeRelease");
    gGLVBL.window_bounds_key = dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT, "kCGWindowBounds");
    if (!m || !queue || !window || !gGLVBL.unconsumed || !gGLVBL.vbl_info || !gGLVBL.window_descriptions ||
        !gGLVBL.rect_from_dictionary || !gGLVBL.displays_with_rect || !gGLVBL.copy_display_mode || !gGLVBL.refresh_rate ||
        !gGLVBL.release_display_mode || !gGLVBL.window_bounds_key) {
        nvlog("GL vblank wait: not corrected in %s (NSCGLSurface or a QuartzCore/CoreGraphics call is missing)",
              getprogname());
        atomic_store(&gGLVBL.installed, true);   // nothing to retry
        return;
    }
    if (atomic_exchange(&gGLVBL.installed, true)) return;
    if (!class_addMethod(surface, sel_registerName(NVGLVBL_MARKER), (IMP)nvglvbl_marker, "v@:")) {
        nvlog("GL vblank wait: already corrected in %s by another image", getprogname());
        return;
    }
    gGLVBL.queue_ivar = ivar_getOffset(queue);
    gGLVBL.window_ivar = ivar_getOffset(window);
    gGLVBL.synchronize = method_setImplementation(m, (IMP)nvglvbl_synchronize);
    nvlog("GL vblank wait: -[NSCGLSurface synchronize] waits by the display's refresh period in %s", getprogname());
}

// NVMTL_HITCH_MS: an OpenGL app's frame ends at -[NSOpenGLContext flushBuffer] (CGLFlushDrawable; vsync on or off)
static IMP gHitchFlush; static atomic_bool gHitchFlushInstalled;
static void nvglvbl_hitch_flush(id self, SEL cmd)
{
    nvmtl_hitch_frame("flushBuffer");
    ((void (*)(id, SEL))gHitchFlush)(self, cmd);
}
static void nvglvbl_hitch_install(void)
{
    if (atomic_load(&gHitchFlushInstalled) || (!nvmtl_hitch_ms() && NVMTL_RELEASE)) return;   // GPUTIME counts frames here too
    Class c = objc_getClass("NSOpenGLContext");
    Method m = c ? class_getInstanceMethod(c, sel_registerName("flushBuffer")) : NULL;
    if (!m || atomic_exchange(&gHitchFlushInstalled, true)) return;
    gHitchFlush = method_setImplementation(m, (IMP)nvglvbl_hitch_flush);
    nvlog("hitch log: OpenGL frames end at -[NSOpenGLContext flushBuffer] in %s", getprogname());
}

// AppKit loaded after the plugin: install once its classes are there (tried again as each image loads)
static void nvglvbl_image_added(const struct mach_header *header, intptr_t slide)
{
    (void)header, (void)slide;
    if (!getenv("NVMTL_NO_GL_VBLANK_FIX")) nvglvbl_install();
    nvglvbl_hitch_install();
}

__attribute__((constructor)) static void nvmtl_gl_vblank_fix(void)
{
    if (getenv("NVMTL_NO_GL_VBLANK_FIX")) {
        if (getenv("NVMTL_HITCH_MS") || !NVMTL_RELEASE) { nvglvbl_hitch_install(); if (!atomic_load(&gHitchFlushInstalled)) _dyld_register_func_for_add_image(nvglvbl_image_added); }
        return;
    }
    nvglvbl_install();
    nvglvbl_hitch_install();
    if (!atomic_load(&gGLVBL.installed) || ((getenv("NVMTL_HITCH_MS") || !NVMTL_RELEASE) && !atomic_load(&gHitchFlushInstalled)))
        _dyld_register_func_for_add_image(nvglvbl_image_added);
}

# metal2vulkan

[![License: LGPL-3.0-or-later](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-LGPL%203.0%20or%20later-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

> **Alpha.** The public API, CLI, reflection schema, and emitted SPIR-V may change during the `0.x`
> series. The project is suitable for experimentation and integration pilots, but consumers should
> version their cached outputs and expect upgrades to require integration work.

`metal2vulkan` translates **Metal AIR**—LLVM bitcode or sanitized LLVM IR—into Vulkan 1.2 SPIR-V
with a native Rust emitter and retained-SPIR-V passes.

## What it provides

- Vertex, post-tessellation vertex, fragment, compute-kernel, and generated passthrough interfaces
- A Rust library and an `in → out.spv` command-line interface
- Structurally selected construction with one final validation pass; unsupported inputs fail
  visibly instead of returning known-invalid SPIR-V
- Consumer reflection for descriptors, stage interfaces, function constants, argument buffers, and
  conservative buffer byte footprints
- An optional unpublished validation workspace for authored semantic cases, GPU evidence, and exact
  translator A/B

## Requirements

- Rust 1.87 or newer
- `llvm-dis` when the input is AIR bitcode
- `spirv-val` from SPIRV-Tools for product translation

Tool paths are found through the usual search path. Override an individual tool with
`METAL2VULKAN_LLVM_DIS`, `METAL2VULKAN_SPIRV_VAL`, or the corresponding
`METAL2VULKAN_<TOOL>` variable.

## Install

```sh
# CLI without reflection JSON
cargo install metal2vulkan

# CLI with --emit-meta JSON support
cargo install metal2vulkan --features serde
```

For a library dependency:

```toml
[dependencies]
metal2vulkan = { version = "0.1", features = ["serde"] } # serde is optional
```

## Quick start

The CLI auto-detects vertex, fragment, or kernel stage metadata by default:

```sh
metal2vulkan input.air output.spv
metal2vulkan input.air output.spv --emit-meta reflection.json
```

Use an explicit stage when the input does not carry stage metadata or when generating a passthrough
vertex shader:

```sh
metal2vulkan input.ll output.spv --stage kernel
metal2vulkan input.ll output.spv --stage passthrough
```

`--emit-meta` requires a build with the `serde` feature and is unavailable for passthrough output,
which has no Metal stage metadata. On success the CLI writes validated SPIR-V, prints `PASS`, and
exits `0`. On failure it prints `FALLBACK`, exits nonzero, and writes a reproducer under
`$TMPDIR/metal2vulkan-repros` by default. Set `METAL2VULKAN_REPRO_DIR` to choose another location.

Fragment AIR that calls `air.get_num_samples.i32` also needs the graphics pipeline's exact sample
count because Vulkan has no equivalent shader-side query:

```sh
metal2vulkan fragment.air fragment.spv --raster-samples 4
```

Accepted values are `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16`, `32`, and `64`. Library callers set
`TransformOptions::raster_sample_count`; translation fails visibly when the query is present and
the value is unknown.

Metal `dispatchThreads` can make boundary workgroups smaller. Exact-thread kernels therefore expose
specializable local sizes and a reflected `KernelDispatch::plan`: create a compute pipeline for
each distinct region `local_size`, specializing `KERNEL_LOCAL_SIZE_SPEC_IDS`, then dispatch every
region with its 48-byte logical-grid payload. This produces at most eight rectangular dispatches,
with no surplus invocations and uniform workgroup barriers.

For a fixed grid, the CLI can instead bake the exact bounds into a pipeline variant:

```sh
metal2vulkan kernel.air kernel.spv --local 8,8,1 --threads-per-grid 57,9,1
```

`--threads-per-grid-push-constant OFFSET` moves the default dynamic dispatch payload.
Library callers select an override with `TransformOptions::kernel_dispatch`; reflected translation
returns the effective contract in `ShaderReflection::kernel_dispatch`. Callers that can prove every
launch covers complete workgroups may explicitly select `KernelDispatch::Workgroups` or pass
`--whole-workgroups` to retain a single fixed-local-size dispatch.

## Library

Library translation takes caller-owned scratch space. Use a unique directory for concurrent calls
and remove it when the operation finishes:

```rust
use metal2vulkan::passes::Stage;
use std::path::Path;

fn translate_kernel(sanitized_ll: &str, scratch: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    metal2vulkan::translate_sanitized_native(sanitized_ll, Stage::Kernel, scratch)
}
```

For a complete executable that auto-detects the stage, writes SPIR-V and reflection JSON, and cleans
up its scratch directory on every return path:

```sh
cargo run --features serde --example translate_reflected -- \
  input.air output.spv reflection.json
```

## Documentation

| Document | Start here when… |
|---|---|
| [How to translate and integrate a shader](docs/HOWTO.md) | You want an end-to-end CLI or Rust integration recipe |
| [Shader reflection](docs/REFLECTION.md) | You need the complete reflection schema and binding contract |
| [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | You are changing the emitter, retained module, passes, or retries |
| [Validation playbook](docs/VALIDATION.md) | You are checking byte stability or authored semantic behavior |
| [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | You need the repository layout and required development gates |
| [Validation crate](validation/README.md) | You are operating the unpublished corpus tooling |
| [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | You need unreleased API and behavior changes |

The generated Rust API documentation is available from `cargo doc --all-features --open`.

## Coverage policy

Grammar and lowering behavior is locked with owned synthetic Rust tests. This repository does not
ship third-party captured shaders. Optional private system-metallib harvest, authored manifests,
and dependency-exact evidence stay in the validation workspace and are described in the
[validation playbook](docs/VALIDATION.md).

Passing `spirv-val` proves structural validity, not agreement with Metal or correct pixels. Use the
authored validation ladder for semantic claims.

(`LGPL-3.0-or-later`).

Metal is a trademark of Apple Inc. metal2vulkan is an independent project and is not affiliated
with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Apple Inc.
