//! A private table of device or threadgroup pointers into ONE buffer becomes a table of element indices.
//!
//! llama.cpp's matrix-vector kernels (and the reproducer in issue #401) keep a small private array of
//! pointers, each a row of the same input buffer:
//!
//! ```text
//!   %7  = alloca [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], align 8
//!   %30 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %29      ; %1 is a kernel argument
//!   %32 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], ptr %7, i64 0, i64 %31
//!   store ptr addrspace(1) %30, ptr %32, align 8
//!   ...
//!   %41 = load ptr addrspace(1), ptr %40, align 8
//!   %56 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %41, i64 %55
//! ```
//!
//! Under Logical addressing a StorageBuffer or Workgroup pointer cannot be stored to Function memory, so
//! the emitter had no model for the table. A device table translated anyway: the stores were dropped and
//! every load through a loaded pointer read a typed zero, so the kernel returned all zeros with no error.
//! A threadgroup table was refused ("an unmodeled pointer placeholder"). Both are measured in #401.
//!
//! Every pointer stored here is `base + index` for the same base, so the table only has to remember the
//! index: the alloca becomes `[N x i64]`, each store writes the index, and each load rebuilds
//! `getelementptr T, base, index`, which is the form the emitter already handles for direct addressing.
//!
//! DELIBERATELY NARROW. A table is rewritten only when all of this holds, and is left to the existing
//! error otherwise:
//!   * its only users are lifetime markers, no-op bitcasts used only by lifetime markers, and
//!     `getelementptr [N x ptr addrspace(K)]` slots (or the alloca itself as slot 0);
//!   * every slot is used only by a whole-pointer store or load of `ptr addrspace(K)`;
//!   * every stored pointer is the base itself or ONE `getelementptr inbounds T, base, i64 idx`, with the
//!     same `T` and the same base for every store;
//!   * that base, after no-op bitcasts, is a function argument or a global, so it dominates every load.

const LIFETIME: [&str; 2] = ["call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(", "call void @llvm.lifetime.end.p0("];

/// `%name` as an operand, so `%7` does not match `%70`.
fn uses_value(line: &str, name: &str) -> bool {
    let mut rest = line;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find(name) {
        let after = &rest[at + name.len()..];
        if after.chars().next().is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_' && c != '.') {
            return true;
        }
        rest = after;
    }
    false
}

/// `  %x = rhs` -> (`%x`, `rhs`).
fn def(line: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let t = line.trim();
    let (name, rhs) = t.split_once(" = ")?;
    (name.starts_with('%') && !name.contains(' ')).then_some((name, rhs))
}

/// The parameter names of a `define` line, read as the `%name` tokens of its parameter list.
fn params(define: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let Some(open) = define.find('(') else { return Vec::new() };
    let mut depth = 0i32;
    let mut close = None;
    for (i, c) in define[open..].char_indices() {
        match c {
            '(' => depth += 1,
            ')' => {
                depth -= 1;
                if depth == 0 {
                    close = Some(open + i);
                    break;
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let Some(close) = close else { return Vec::new() };
    define[open + 1..close]
        .split(|c: char| c == ',' || c == ' ' || c == ')')
        .filter(|t| t.starts_with('%') && t.len() > 1)
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect()
}

struct Table {
    alloca: usize,
    count: String,
    space: String,
    slots: Vec<(usize, String)>,      // slot GEP lines (and the alloca itself as slot 0)
    stores: Vec<(usize, String)>,     // (line, index operand)
    loads: Vec<(usize, String, String)>, // (line, loaded name, slot name)
    base: String,
    elem: String,
}

/// `alloca [N x ptr addrspace(K)], ...` -> (N, K).
fn table_alloca(rhs: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    let rest = rhs.strip_prefix("alloca [")?;
    let (n, rest) = rest.split_once(" x ptr addrspace(")?;
    let (k, rest) = rest.split_once(")]")?;
    (n.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) && k.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) && !k.is_empty())
        .then_some(())?;
    (rest.is_empty() || rest.starts_with(',')).then_some((n.to_string(), k.to_string()))
}

fn analyse(lines: &[&str], span: (usize, usize), alloca: usize, count: &str, space: &str) -> Option<Table> {
    let (name, _) = def(lines[alloca])?;
    let ptr_ty = format!("ptr addrspace({space})");
    let table_ty = format!("[{count} x {ptr_ty}]");
    let defs: std::collections::HashMap<&str, (usize, &str)> =
        (span.0 + 1..span.1).filter_map(|i| def(lines[i]).map(|(n, r)| (n, (i, r)))).collect();
    let roots: Vec<String> = params(lines[span.0]);
    let root_of = |v: &str| -> Option<String> {
        let mut v = v.to_string();
        for _ in 0..8 {
            if v.starts_with('@') || roots.iter().any(|r| *r == v) {
                return Some(v);
            }
            let (_, rhs) = defs.get(v.as_str())?;
            let src = rhs.strip_prefix(&format!("bitcast {ptr_ty} "))?;
            let (src, to) = src.split_once(" to ")?;
            (to.trim() == ptr_ty).then_some(())?;
            v = src.trim().to_string();
        }
        None
    };

    let mut slots = vec![(alloca, name.to_string())];
    let mut views: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    for i in span.0 + 1..span.1 {
        if i == alloca || !uses_value(lines[i], name) {
            continue;
        }
        let t = lines[i].trim();
        if LIFETIME.iter().any(|l| t.starts_with(l)) {
            continue;
        }
        let (d, rhs) = def(lines[i])?;
        if let Some(rest) = rhs.strip_prefix("bitcast ptr ") {
            // a no-op view of the table, allowed only if lifetime markers are all it feeds
            (rest.split_once(" to ")?.0.trim() == name).then_some(())?;
            let only_lifetime = (span.0 + 1..span.1).filter(|&j| j != i && uses_value(lines[j], d)).all(|j| {
                let u = lines[j].trim();
                LIFETIME.iter().any(|l| u.starts_with(l))
            });
            only_lifetime.then_some(())?;
            views.push(i);
            continue;
        }
        let gep = rhs
            .strip_prefix("getelementptr inbounds ")
            .or_else(|| rhs.strip_prefix("getelementptr "))?;
        let rest = gep.strip_prefix(&table_ty)?.strip_prefix(", ptr ")?;
        (rest.split(',').next()?.trim() == name).then_some(())?;
        slots.push((i, d.to_string()));
    }

    let mut stores = Vec::new();
    let mut loads = Vec::new();
    let mut base: Option<String> = None;
    let mut elem: Option<String> = None;
    for (si, slot) in &slots {
        for i in span.0 + 1..span.1 {
            if i == *si || !uses_value(lines[i], slot) {
                continue;
            }
            if views.contains(&i) || slots.iter().any(|(j, _)| *j == i) {
                continue; // a slot GEP naming the alloca, handled as its own slot
            }
            let t = lines[i].trim();
            if LIFETIME.iter().any(|l| t.starts_with(l)) && slot == name {
                continue;
            }
            if let Some(rest) = t.strip_prefix(&format!("store {ptr_ty} ")) {
                let (value, rest) = rest.split_once(", ptr ")?;
                (rest.split(',').next()?.trim() == slot).then_some(())?;
                (!uses_value(value, slot)).then_some(())?;
                let (b, e, idx) = if let Some(r) = root_of(value.trim()) {
                    (r, None, "0".to_string())
                } else {
                    let (_, rhs) = defs.get(value.trim())?;
                    let g = rhs.strip_prefix("getelementptr inbounds ")?;
                    let (ty, rest) = g.split_once(&format!(", {ptr_ty} "))?;
                    let (p, idx) = rest.split_once(", i64 ")?;
                    (!idx.contains(',')).then_some(())?;
                    (ty.trim() != "" && !ty.contains(&ptr_ty)).then_some(())?;
                    (root_of(p.trim())?, Some(ty.trim().to_string()), idx.trim().to_string())
                };
                if base.get_or_insert_with(|| b.clone()) != &b {
                    return None;
                }
                if let Some(e) = e {
                    if elem.get_or_insert_with(|| e.clone()) != &e {
                        return None;
                    }
                }
                stores.push((i, idx));
                continue;
            }
            let (d, rhs) = def(lines[i])?;
            let rest = rhs.strip_prefix(&format!("load {ptr_ty}, ptr "))?;
            (rest.split(',').next()?.trim() == slot).then_some(())?;
            loads.push((i, d.to_string(), slot.clone()));
        }
    }
    if stores.is_empty() || loads.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(Table {
        alloca,
        count: count.to_string(),
        space: space.to_string(),
        slots,
        stores,
        loads,
        base: base?,
        elem: elem.unwrap_or_else(|| "i8".to_string()),
    })
}

fn rewrite(ll: &str) -> Option<String> {
    if !ll.contains(" x ptr addrspace(") {
        return None;
    }
    let lines: Vec<&str> = ll.lines().collect();
    let mut spans = Vec::new();
    let mut start = None;
    for (i, l) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
        let t = l.trim();
        if t.starts_with("define ") {
            start = Some(i);
        } else if t == "}" {
            if let Some(s) = start.take() {
                spans.push((s, i));
            }
        }
    }
    let mut out: Vec<String> = lines.iter().map(|l| l.to_string()).collect();
    let mut extra: std::collections::HashMap<usize, String> = Default::default();
    let mut changed = false;
    for span in spans {
        for i in span.0 + 1..span.1 {
            let Some((_, rhs)) = def(lines[i]) else { continue };
            let Some((count, space)) = table_alloca(rhs) else { continue };
            let Some(t) = analyse(&lines, span, i, &count, &space) else { continue };
            let ptr_ty = format!("ptr addrspace({})", t.space);
            let old_ty = format!("[{} x {ptr_ty}]", t.count);
            let new_ty = format!("[{} x i64]", t.count);
            out[t.alloca] = lines[t.alloca].replacen(&old_ty, &new_ty, 1);
            for (si, _) in &t.slots {
                if *si != t.alloca {
                    out[*si] = lines[*si].replacen(&old_ty, &new_ty, 1);
                }
            }
            let indent = |l: &str| l.len() - l.trim_start().len();
            for (si, idx) in &t.stores {
                let l = lines[*si];
                let slot = l.trim().split(", ptr ").nth(1).and_then(|r| r.split(',').next()).unwrap_or("").trim();
                out[*si] = format!("{}store i64 {idx}, ptr {slot}, align 8", &l[..indent(l)]);
            }
            for (li, name, slot) in &t.loads {
                let l = lines[*li];
                let pad = &l[..indent(l)];
                let off = format!("%ptrtab.{}", name.trim_start_matches('%'));
                out[*li] = format!("{pad}{off} = load i64, ptr {slot}, align 8");
                extra.insert(
                    *li,
                    format!("{pad}{name} = getelementptr inbounds {}, {ptr_ty} {}, i64 {off}", t.elem, t.base),
                );
            }
            changed = true;
        }
    }
    if !changed {
        return None;
    }
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(ll.len() + 256);
    for (i, l) in out.iter().enumerate() {
        s.push_str(l);
        s.push('\n');
        if let Some(e) = extra.get(&i) {
            s.push_str(e);
            s.push('\n');
        }
    }
    if !ll.ends_with('\n') {
        s.pop();
    }
    Some(s)
}

pub(crate) fn offset_pointer_tables(ll: &str) -> std::borrow::Cow<'_, str> {
    match rewrite(ll) {
        Some(out) => std::borrow::Cow::Owned(out),
        None => std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(ll),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn offset_pointer_tables_owned(ll: String) -> String {
    match rewrite(&ll) {
        Some(out) => out,
        None => ll,
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// The #401 device kernel, reduced to the table: two rows of one buffer stored, one loaded back.
    const ROWS: &str = concat!(
        "define void @probe(ptr addrspace(1) noundef \"air-buffer-no-alias\" %1, i64 %r, i64 %j) {\n",
        "  %7 = alloca [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], align 8\n",
        "  %10 = bitcast ptr %7 to ptr\n",
        "  call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(ptr %7)\n",
        "  %30 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %r\n",
        "  %32 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], ptr %7, i64 0, i64 %j\n",
        "  store ptr addrspace(1) %30, ptr %32, align 8, !tbaa !41\n",
        "  %40 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], ptr %7, i64 0, i64 %j\n",
        "  %41 = load ptr addrspace(1), ptr %40, align 8, !tbaa !41\n",
        "  %56 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %41, i64 %j\n",
        "  %57 = load half, ptr addrspace(1) %56, align 2\n",
        "  call void @llvm.lifetime.end.p0(ptr %7)\n",
        "  ret void\n",
        "}\n",
    );

    #[test]
    fn a_table_of_rows_of_one_buffer_holds_indices() {
        let out = rewrite(ROWS).expect("the #401 form must rewrite");
        assert!(out.contains("%7 = alloca [2 x i64], align 8"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("store i64 %r, ptr %32, align 8\n"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("%ptrtab.41 = load i64, ptr %40, align 8\n"), "{out}");
        assert!(
            out.contains("%41 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %ptrtab.41\n"),
            "the loaded pointer must be rebuilt from the base argument:\n{out}"
        );
        assert!(!out.contains("x ptr addrspace(1)]"), "no pointer table may remain:\n{out}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_threadgroup_table_through_a_bitcast_base_holds_indices() {
        let ll = concat!(
            "define void @probe(ptr addrspace(3) noundef %4, i64 %r) {\n",
            "  %10 = alloca [2 x ptr addrspace(3)], align 8\n",
            "  %27 = bitcast ptr addrspace(3) %4 to ptr addrspace(3)\n",
            "  %53 = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr addrspace(3) %27, i64 %r\n",
            "  %55 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr addrspace(3)], ptr %10, i64 0, i64 %r\n",
            "  store ptr addrspace(3) %53, ptr %55, align 8\n",
            "  %56 = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr addrspace(3) %53, i64 %r\n",
            "  %69 = load ptr addrspace(3), ptr %55, align 8\n",
            "  store float 1.0, ptr addrspace(3) %69, align 4\n",
            "  ret void\n",
            "}\n",
        );
        let out = rewrite(ll).expect("the threadgroup form must rewrite");
        assert!(out.contains("%69 = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr addrspace(3) %4, i64 %ptrtab.69"), "{out}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_different_buffers_in_one_table_refuse() {
        let ll = concat!(
            "define void @k(ptr addrspace(1) %a, ptr addrspace(1) %b, i64 %i) {\n",
            "  %t = alloca [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], align 8\n",
            "  %pa = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr addrspace(1) %a, i64 %i\n",
            "  %pb = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr addrspace(1) %b, i64 %i\n",
            "  %s0 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], ptr %t, i64 0, i64 0\n",
            "  %s1 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr addrspace(1)], ptr %t, i64 0, i64 1\n",
            "  store ptr addrspace(1) %pa, ptr %s0, align 8\n",
            "  store ptr addrspace(1) %pb, ptr %s1, align 8\n",
            "  %l = load ptr addrspace(1), ptr %s0, align 8\n",
            "  ret void\n",
            "}\n",
        );
        assert!(rewrite(ll).is_none(), "an index cannot say which buffer it belongs to");
    }

    #[test]
    fn two_element_types_refuse() {
        let ll = ROWS.replace(
            "  %40 = getelementptr",
            "  %31 = getelementptr inbounds float, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %r\n  store ptr addrspace(1) %31, ptr %32, align 8\n  %40 = getelementptr",
        );
        assert!(rewrite(&ll).is_none(), "a half index and a float index do not share a scale");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_table_that_escapes_refuses() {
        let ll = ROWS.replace("  ret void\n", "  call void @sink(ptr %7)\n  ret void\n");
        assert!(rewrite(&ll).is_none(), "a table passed to a call may be written where this pass cannot see");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_base_computed_in_the_body_refuses() {
        let ll = ROWS
            .replace("%1, i64 %r, i64 %j)", "%1, i64 %r, i64 %j, i1 %c)")
            .replace(
                "  %30 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %1, i64 %r\n",
                "  %b = select i1 %c, ptr addrspace(1) %1, ptr addrspace(1) %1\n  %30 = getelementptr inbounds half, ptr addrspace(1) %b, i64 %r\n",
            );
        assert!(rewrite(&ll).is_none(), "only an argument or a global is known to dominate every load");
    }

    #[test]
    fn nothing_to_do_is_borrowed() {
        let ll = "define void @k() {\n  ret void\n}\n";
        assert!(matches!(offset_pointer_tables(ll), std::borrow::Cow::Borrowed(_)));
    }
}

//! An access chain whose index path lands on a member of a different scalar TYPE than its result points to.
//!
//! The ray-tracing payload is one blob of memory shared by every shader in a pipeline, and each shader was
//! compiled with its OWN view of it: measured on the game's five real pipelines, `%struct.Payload` has three
//! different layouts across the linked modules (`{i32,i32,float,float}` in 31, `{float}` in 8,
//! `{<3 x float>,float,i32}` in 7). When a helper from one module is inlined into an entry carrying another
//! view, its chain walks the caller's `{header, payload}` type and asks for a member the caller declares with
//! a different scalar type:
//!
//! ```text
//! index path = [1, 0];  base points at { header, { i32, i32, float, float } }
//! selects TypeInt 32 0, but the result pointer points to TypeFloat 32
//! ```
//!
//! A pointer of the wrong type is never legal in Logical SPIR-V and no capability admits one, so the pun has
//! to be resolved at the chain's USES, not at its construction: the chain takes the pointer type the member
//! actually has, each load of it loads that type and bitcasts the VALUE, and each store bitcasts before
//! storing. That is the same move as phi-ing loaded values rather than pointers.
//!
//! Deliberately narrow:
//! - only a scalar-for-scalar pun of IDENTICAL bit width. A different width is a different datum, not another
//!   view of one, and is left for the validator to reject.
//! - every use of the chain must be a plain load or store through it. A chain stacked on top, a pointer handed
//!   to a function, or any other mention keeps its meaning only with the original type, so the plan is dropped
//!   and the refusal reads exactly as it did before.
//!
//! THE ASSUMPTION THIS RESTS ON, SAID OUT LOUD: that member k of one shader's payload view is the same
//! datum as member k of the pipeline's. The index path is the only mapping available — byte offset is
//! provably NOT it, because the views also pad their headers differently (`[4 x i8]` against `[20 x i8]`, so
//! the payload starts at 32 bytes in one and 48 in another, and a byte-preserving map would land in padding.)
//! Translating is therefore not the same as being correct here: only a rendered frame settles whether the
//! datum is the right one.

use super::*;

fn pointee(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, pointer_ty: Word) -> Option<Word> {
    let def = defs.get(&pointer_ty)?;
    if def.class.opcode != Op::TypePointer {
        return None;
    }
    match def.operands.get(1) {
        Some(Operand::IdRef(pointee)) => Some(*pointee),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn storage_class(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, pointer_ty: Word) -> Option<Operand> {
    let def = defs.get(&pointer_ty)?;
    if def.class.opcode != Op::TypePointer {
        return None;
    }
    def.operands.first().cloned()
}

/// The bit width of a scalar type, or None for anything that is not one.
fn scalar_width(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, ty: Word) -> Option<u32> {
    let def = defs.get(&ty)?;
    match def.class.opcode {
        Op::TypeInt | Op::TypeFloat => match def.operands.first() {
            Some(Operand::LiteralBit32(width)) => Some(*width),
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn constant_u32(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, id: Word) -> Option<u32> {
    let def = defs.get(&id)?;
    if def.class.opcode != Op::Constant {
        return None;
    }
    match def.operands.first() {
        Some(Operand::LiteralBit32(value)) => Some(*value),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The type an index path selects, or None when the path cannot be walked - the validator's to report.
fn selected_type(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, mut current: Word, indices: &[Operand]) -> Option<Word> {
    for index in indices {
        let Operand::IdRef(index) = index else { return None };
        let def = defs.get(&current)?;
        current = match def.class.opcode {
            Op::TypeStruct => {
                let member = constant_u32(defs, *index)? as usize;
                match def.operands.get(member) {
                    Some(Operand::IdRef(ty)) => *ty,
                    _ => return None,
                }
            }
            Op::TypeArray | Op::TypeRuntimeArray | Op::TypeVector | Op::TypeMatrix => {
                match def.operands.first() {
                    Some(Operand::IdRef(ty)) => *ty,
                    _ => return None,
                }
            }
            _ => return None,
        };
    }
    Some(current)
}

fn find_or_create_pointer(module: &mut Module, storage: Operand, pointee_ty: Word) -> Word {
    let wanted = vec![storage, Operand::IdRef(pointee_ty)];
    if let Some(existing) = module.types_global_values.iter().find_map(|i| {
        (i.class.opcode == Op::TypePointer && i.operands == wanted)
            .then_some(i.result_id)
            .flatten()
    }) {
        return existing;
    }
    let id = module.fresh_id();
    module
        .types_global_values
        .push(Instruction::new(Op::TypePointer, None, Some(id), wanted));
    id
}

/// Retypes every access chain that is punned only by a same-width scalar; returns how many it retyped.
pub(super) fn retype_punned_access_chains(module: &mut Module) -> usize {
    let defs: HashMap<Word, Instruction> = module
        .types_global_values
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|i| i.result_id.map(|id| (id, i.clone())))
        .collect();
    let mut value_types: HashMap<Word, Word> = HashMap::default();
    for instruction in module.all_inst_iter() {
        if let (Some(id), Some(ty)) = (instruction.result_id, instruction.result_type) {
            value_types.insert(id, ty);
        }
    }

    // chain result -> (the type the result pointer claims, the type the member actually has, storage class)
    let mut candidates: HashMap<Word, (Word, Word, Operand)> = HashMap::default();
    for function in &module.functions {
        for block in &function.blocks {
            for instruction in &block.instructions {
                let first_index = match instruction.class.opcode {
                    Op::AccessChain | Op::InBoundsAccessChain => 1,
                    Op::PtrAccessChain | Op::InBoundsPtrAccessChain => 2,
                    _ => continue,
                };
                let (Some(result), Some(result_ty)) = (instruction.result_id, instruction.result_type)
                else {
                    continue;
                };
                if instruction.operands.len() <= first_index {
                    continue;
                }
                let Some(Operand::IdRef(base)) = instruction.operands.first() else { continue };
                let Some(base_ty) = value_types.get(base) else { continue };
                let (Some(base_pointee), Some(want)) =
                    (pointee(&defs, *base_ty), pointee(&defs, result_ty))
                else {
                    continue;
                };
                let Some(selected) =
                    selected_type(&defs, base_pointee, &instruction.operands[first_index..])
                else {
                    continue;
                };
                if selected == want {
                    continue;
                }
                let (Some(selected_width), Some(want_width)) =
                    (scalar_width(&defs, selected), scalar_width(&defs, want))
                else {
                    continue;
                };
                if selected_width != want_width {
                    continue;
                }
                let Some(storage) = storage_class(&defs, result_ty) else { continue };
                candidates.insert(result, (want, selected, storage));
            }
        }
    }
    if candidates.is_empty() {
        return 0;
    }

    // Drop any chain that is used as anything but the pointer of a plain load or store.
    let mut usable: std::collections::HashSet<Word> = candidates.keys().copied().collect();
    for function in &module.functions {
        for block in &function.blocks {
            for instruction in &block.instructions {
                let pointer_operand = match instruction.class.opcode {
                    Op::Load | Op::Store => match instruction.operands.first() {
                        Some(Operand::IdRef(id)) if candidates.contains_key(id) => Some(*id),
                        _ => None,
                    },
                    _ => None,
                };
                if let Some(pointer) = pointer_operand {
                    // a load must ask for exactly the punned type; otherwise this is a shape we have not seen
                    if instruction.class.opcode == Op::Load
                        && instruction.result_type != Some(candidates[&pointer].0)
                    {
                        usable.remove(&pointer);
                    }
                    // the rest of a load's/store's operands still get the general check below
                    for operand in instruction.operands.iter().skip(1) {
                        if let Operand::IdRef(id) = operand {
                            if candidates.contains_key(id) {
                                usable.remove(id);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                for operand in &instruction.operands {
                    if let Operand::IdRef(id) = operand {
                        if candidates.contains_key(id) {
                            usable.remove(id);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    candidates.retain(|id, _| usable.contains(id));
    if candidates.is_empty() {
        return 0;
    }

    // Every fresh id is taken BEFORE the rewrite: the blocks are borrowed mutably during it.
    let mut load_sites: Vec<Word> = Vec::new();
    let mut store_sites: usize = 0;
    for function in &module.functions {
        for block in &function.blocks {
            for instruction in &block.instructions {
                let Some(Operand::IdRef(pointer)) = instruction.operands.first() else { continue };
                if !candidates.contains_key(pointer) {
                    continue;
                }
                match instruction.class.opcode {
                    Op::Load => {
                        if let Some(id) = instruction.result_id {
                            load_sites.push(id);
                        }
                    }
                    Op::Store => store_sites += 1,
                    _ => {}
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let raw_load_id: HashMap<Word, Word> = load_sites
        .iter()
        .map(|&id| (id, module.fresh_id()))
        .collect();
    let mut store_cast_ids: Vec<Word> = (0..store_sites).map(|_| module.fresh_id()).collect();
    store_cast_ids.reverse(); // popped from the back, so they are handed out in order

    let mut retyped: HashMap<Word, (Word, Word, Word)> = HashMap::default(); // chain -> (ptr ty, selected, want)
    // Sorted, because `candidates` is a HashMap and find_or_create_pointer allocates ids as it
    // goes: iterating it in hash order gave the same module a different set of OpTypePointer ids on
    // every run, so the output bytes were not reproducible. That breaks a hash-keyed translation
    // cache and makes a byte-for-byte A/B of two builds meaningless.
    let mut plans: Vec<(Word, (Word, Word, Operand))> = candidates.into_iter().collect();
    plans.sort_by_key(|&(id, _)| id);
    for (id, (want, selected, storage)) in plans {
        let pointer_ty = find_or_create_pointer(module, storage, selected);
        retyped.insert(id, (pointer_ty, selected, want));
    }

    let mut repaired = 0;
    for function in &mut module.functions {
        for block in &mut function.blocks {
            let original = std::mem::take(&mut block.instructions);
            let mut rewritten: Vec<Instruction> = Vec::with_capacity(original.len() + 1);
            for instruction in original {
                // 1 · the chain itself takes the pointer type the member actually has
                if let Some((pointer_ty, _, _)) =
                    instruction.result_id.and_then(|id| retyped.get(&id))
                {
                    let mut chain = instruction;
                    chain.result_type = Some(*pointer_ty);
                    rewritten.push(chain);
                    repaired += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                let plan = match instruction.operands.first() {
                    Some(Operand::IdRef(pointer)) => retyped.get(pointer).copied(),
                    _ => None,
                };
                match (instruction.class.opcode, plan) {
                    // 2 · a load reads the declared type, then the VALUE is bitcast to what the shader wanted
                    (Op::Load, Some((_, selected, want))) => {
                        // Step 1 has already retyped the chain, so pushing the original load here
                        // emits a load of `want` through a pointer now typed `selected` - invalid
                        // SPIR-V, and silently. The id sets are built to match so neither arm should
                        // be reachable; say so loudly if one ever is, rather than shipping bad bytes.
                        let Some(load_id) = instruction.result_id else {
                            eprintln!("PUNNED-CHAIN-NO-RESULT a punned load has no result id; its pointer was already retyped");
                            rewritten.push(instruction);
                            continue;
                        };
                        let Some(&raw) = raw_load_id.get(&load_id) else {
                            eprintln!("PUNNED-CHAIN-NO-RAW no raw id for punned load %{load_id}; its pointer was already retyped");
                            rewritten.push(instruction);
                            continue;
                        };
                        let mut raw_load = instruction;
                        raw_load.result_type = Some(selected);
                        raw_load.result_id = Some(raw);
                        rewritten.push(raw_load);
                        rewritten.push(Instruction::new(
                            Op::Bitcast,
                            Some(want),
                            Some(load_id),
                            vec![Operand::IdRef(raw)],
                        ));
                    }
                    // 3 · a store bitcasts the value first, so the pointer and the value agree
                    (Op::Store, Some((_, selected, _))) => {
                        // Same hazard as the load arm above: the pointer is already retyped, so a
                        // plain push stores the wrong type through it without a word of complaint.
                        let Some(Operand::IdRef(value)) = instruction.operands.get(1).cloned() else {
                            eprintln!("PUNNED-CHAIN-NO-VALUE a punned store has no value operand; its pointer was already retyped");
                            rewritten.push(instruction);
                            continue;
                        };
                        let Some(cast) = store_cast_ids.pop() else {
                            eprintln!("PUNNED-CHAIN-NO-CAST ran out of bitcast ids for a punned store; its pointer was already retyped");
                            rewritten.push(instruction);
                            continue;
                        };
                        rewritten.push(Instruction::new(
                            Op::Bitcast,
                            Some(selected),
                            Some(cast),
                            vec![Operand::IdRef(value)],
                        ));
                        let mut store = instruction;
                        store.operands[1] = Operand::IdRef(cast);
                        rewritten.push(store);
                    }
                    _ => rewritten.push(instruction),
                }
            }
            block.instructions = rewritten;
        }
    }
    repaired
}

use crate::native::ir::{LlType, LlValue};

pub(in crate::native) fn render_type(ty: &LlType) -> Option<String> {
    Some(match ty {
        LlType::Void => "void".to_string(),
        LlType::Float => "float".to_string(),
        LlType::Half => "half".to_string(),
        LlType::BFloat => "bfloat".to_string(),
        LlType::Int(n) => format!("i{n}"),
        LlType::Ptr(0) => "ptr".to_string(),
        LlType::Ptr(n) => format!("ptr addrspace({n})"),
        LlType::Vector(elem, n) => format!("<{n} x {}>", render_type(elem)?),
        LlType::Array(elem, n) => format!("[{n} x {}]", render_type(elem)?),
        LlType::Named(name) => name.clone(),
        LlType::Struct(_) | LlType::Bool => return None,
    })
}

pub(in crate::native) fn render_value(value: &LlValue) -> Option<String> {
    Some(match value {
        LlValue::Local(name) => name.clone(),
        LlValue::Global(name) => name.clone(),
        LlValue::Bool(true) => "true".to_string(),
        LlValue::Bool(false) => "false".to_string(),
        LlValue::Int(v) => v.to_string(),
        LlValue::SignedInt(v) => v.to_string(),
        LlValue::IntToPtr {
            source,
            destination,
        } => format!(
            "inttoptr ({} {} to {})",
            render_type(&source.ty)?,
            render_value(&source.value)?,
            render_type(destination)?
        ),
        LlValue::Hex(_)
        | LlValue::Float(_)
        | LlValue::Float32Bits(_)
        | LlValue::HalfBits(_)
        | LlValue::BFloatBits(_)
        | LlValue::Vector(_)
        | LlValue::Array(_)
        | LlValue::Struct(_)
        | LlValue::Splat(_)
        | LlValue::Gep(_)
        | LlValue::Zero
        | LlValue::Undef => return None,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::native::parse::{parse_type, parse_value};

    #[test]
    fn render_type_round_trips_parse_type() {
        for text in [
            "void",
            "float",
            "half",
            "bfloat",
            "i1",
            "i8",
            "i32",
            "i64",
            "ptr",
            "ptr addrspace(1)",
            "ptr addrspace(3)",
            "<4 x i32>",
            "<2 x float>",
            "[8 x i8]",
            "[4 x <2 x half>]",
            "%struct.Foo",
            "%\"quoted.name\"",
        ] {
            let ty = parse_type(text).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("parse {text}: {e}"));
            let rendered =
                render_type(&ty).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("render {text} returned None"));
            assert_eq!(rendered, text, "round-trip mismatch for {text}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn render_type_declines_struct() {
        let ty = parse_type("{ i32, float }").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(render_type(&ty), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn render_value_round_trips_parse_value() {
        for text in ["%x", "%0", "@g", "true", "false", "-3", "7"] {
            let v = parse_value(text).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("parse {text}: {e}"));
            let rendered =
                render_value(&v).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("render {text} returned None"));
            assert_eq!(rendered, text, "round-trip mismatch for {text}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn render_value_declines_ambiguous() {
        for text in ["undef", "poison", "null", "zeroinitializer", "1.5"] {
            let v = parse_value(text).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(render_value(&v), None, "expected None for {text}");
        }
    }
}

//! A program-scope array of samplers.
//!
//! `constexpr constant sampler table[N] = {...}` becomes a module constant holding one struct per element, each naming
//! the element's `@__air_sampler_state.K` global, and the shader loads a sampler pointer out of it:
//!
//! ```llvm
//! @table = internal addrspace(2) constant [2 x %"struct.metal::sampler"] [ { ptr addrspace(2) @__air_sampler_state.1 }, ... ]
//! %g = getelementptr inbounds [2 x %"struct.metal::sampler"], ptr addrspace(2) @table, i64 0, i64 %i, i32 0
//! %s = load ptr addrspace(2), ptr addrspace(2) %g
//! ```
//!
//! The emitter has no initializer for an array of such structs and refused the module ("unsupported global initializer"),
//! which is how an application that builds its render shaders at start-up (Goodnotes) failed to open any document. Every
//! element is already a static sampler, so the load is replaced by the element's global: a constant index names it
//! directly, and a computed index becomes a chain of selects over the element globals. The table is then unused and removed.
//! A module that uses the table any other way keeps it, and keeps the refusal.

use std::borrow::Cow;

const SAMPLER_TYPE: &str = "%\"struct.metal::sampler\"";

struct Table {
    name: String,
    elements: Vec<String>,
}

pub(crate) fn lower_global_sampler_tables(san_ll: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
    if !san_ll.contains(SAMPLER_TYPE) || !san_ll.contains("x %\"struct.metal::sampler\"]") {
        return Cow::Borrowed(san_ll);
    }
    let tables: Vec<Table> = san_ll.lines().filter_map(parse_table).collect();
    if tables.is_empty() {
        return Cow::Borrowed(san_ll);
    }
    let mut text = san_ll.to_string();
    let mut changed = false;
    for table in &tables {
        if let Some(lowered) = lower_one_table(&text, table) {
            text = lowered;
            changed = true;
        }
    }
    if changed {
        Cow::Owned(text)
    } else {
        Cow::Borrowed(san_ll)
    }
}

/// `@name = ... constant [N x %"struct.metal::sampler"] [ %"struct.metal::sampler" { ptr addrspace(2) @g }, ...`
fn parse_table(line: &str) -> Option<Table> {
    let name = line.strip_prefix('@')?.split_once(" = ")?.0;
    let (head, body) = line.split_once(" constant [")?;
    if !head.contains("addrspace(2)") {
        return None;
    }
    let (count, rest) = body.split_once(" x ")?;
    let count: usize = count.parse().ok()?;
    let rest = rest.strip_prefix(SAMPLER_TYPE)?.strip_prefix("] [")?;
    let mut elements = Vec::new();
    let mut tail = rest;
    while let Some(at) = tail.find("ptr addrspace(2) @") {
        let after = &tail[at + "ptr addrspace(2) ".len()..];
        let end = after.find([' ', '}', ',']).unwrap_or(after.len());
        elements.push(after[..end].to_string());
        tail = &after[end..];
    }
    (count > 0 && elements.len() == count).then(|| Table { name: name.to_string(), elements })
}

fn is_ident_char(c: char) -> bool {
    c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '_' | '.' | '$' | '-')
}

/// `text` with every whole-token `from` replaced by `to`.
fn replace_token(text: &str, from: &str, to: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut rest = text;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find(from) {
        let before_ok = !rest[..at].chars().next_back().is_some_and(is_ident_char);
        let after = &rest[at + from.len()..];
        let after_ok = !after.chars().next().is_some_and(is_ident_char);
        out.push_str(&rest[..at]);
        out.push_str(if before_ok && after_ok { to } else { from });
        rest = after;
    }
    out.push_str(rest);
    out
}

fn count_token(text: &str, token: &str) -> usize {
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut rest = text;
    while let Some(at) = rest.find(token) {
        let before_ok = !rest[..at].chars().next_back().is_some_and(is_ident_char);
        let after = &rest[at + token.len()..];
        count += usize::from(before_ok && !after.chars().next().is_some_and(is_ident_char));
        rest = after;
    }
    count
}

fn lower_one_table(text: &str, table: &Table) -> Option<String> {
    let global = format!("@{}", table.name);
    let type_array = format!("[{} x {SAMPLER_TYPE}]", table.elements.len());
    // address of an element's pointer field: (result, index operand)
    let mut addresses: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for line in text.lines() {
        let t = line.trim();
        if t.starts_with(&format!("{global} = ")) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some((result, index)) = parse_element_address(t, &global, &type_array) {
            addresses.push((result, index));
            continue;
        }
        lines.push(line.to_string());
    }
    if addresses.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(lines.len());
    let mut renames: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    let mut dynamic: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    for line in &lines {
        let t = line.trim();
        let loaded = t.split_once(" = load ptr addrspace(2), ptr addrspace(2) ").and_then(|(result, rest)| {
            let address = rest.split([',', ' ']).next()?;
            let (_, index) = addresses.iter().find(|(a, _)| a == address)?;
            Some((result.to_string(), index.clone()))
        });
        let Some((result, index)) = loaded else {
            out.push(line.clone());
            continue;
        };
        if let Ok(constant) = index.parse::<usize>() {
            let element = table.elements.get(constant)?;
            renames.push((result, element.clone()));
            continue;
        }
        dynamic.push((result, index));
    }
    // a sampler picked at run time has no one state for a call to carry, so each sampling call that reads it is made
    // once per element and its result picked by the index; a sample has no side effect
    let mut expanded: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(out.len());
    for line in out {
        let Some((result, index)) = dynamic.iter().find(|(r, _)| replace_token(&line, r, "") != line) else {
            expanded.push(line);
            continue;
        };
        let t = line.trim();
        let call = t.split_once(" = ").filter(|(_, c)| {
            let c = c.strip_prefix("tail ").unwrap_or(c);
            c.starts_with("call ") && (c.contains(" @air.sample_") || c.contains(" @air.gather_"))
        });
        let Some((value, call)) = call.filter(|_| count_token(t, result) == 1) else {
            return None;
        };
        let ty = call.strip_prefix("tail ").unwrap_or(call).strip_prefix("call ")?.split_once(" @air.")?.0.to_string();
        let indent = &line[..line.len() - line.trim_start().len()];
        let base = value.trim_start_matches('%');
        for (k, element) in table.elements.iter().enumerate() {
            expanded.push(format!("{indent}%{base}.t{k} = {}", replace_token(call, result, element)));
        }
        let mut current = format!("%{base}.t{}", table.elements.len() - 1);
        for k in (0..table.elements.len() - 1).rev() {
            let cond = format!("%{base}.c{k}");
            let pick = if k == 0 { value.to_string() } else { format!("%{base}.m{k}") };
            expanded.push(format!("{indent}{cond} = icmp eq i64 {index}, {k}"));
            expanded.push(format!("{indent}{pick} = select i1 {cond}, {ty} %{base}.t{k}, {ty} {current}"));
            current = pick;
        }
        if table.elements.len() == 1 {
            return None;
        }
    }
    let out = expanded;
    let mut joined = out.join("\n");
    joined.push('\n');
    for (from, to) in &renames {
        joined = replace_token(&joined, from, to);
    }
    // any other use of the table, or of an address that is still read some other way, leaves the module as it was
    if joined.contains(&global) {
        return None;
    }
    for (address, _) in &addresses {
        let used = joined.lines().any(|l| {
            let t = l.trim();
            !t.starts_with(&format!("{address} = ")) && replace_token(t, address, "") != t
        });
        if used {
            return None;
        }
    }
    Some(joined)
}

/// `%r = getelementptr [inbounds] [N x sampler], ptr addrspace(2) @table, i64 0, i64 IDX, i32 0`, or the flat spelling.
fn parse_element_address(line: &str, global: &str, type_array: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    let (result, rest) = line.split_once(" = getelementptr ")?;
    let rest = rest.strip_prefix("inbounds ").unwrap_or(rest);
    let pieces: Vec<&str> = rest.split(", ").map(str::trim).collect();
    let base_ty = if pieces.first() == Some(&type_array) {
        true
    } else if pieces.first() == Some(&SAMPLER_TYPE) {
        false
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    if pieces.get(1) != Some(&format!("ptr addrspace(2) {global}").as_str()) {
        return None;
    }
    let indices = pieces.get(2..)?;
    let (index, field) = match (base_ty, indices) {
        (true, [zero, index, field]) if *zero == "i64 0" || *zero == "i32 0" => (index, field),
        (false, [index, field]) => (index, field),
        _ => return None,
    };
    if *field != "i32 0" {
        return None;
    }
    // the compares written for a computed index are 64-bit
    let index = index.strip_prefix("i64 ")?;
    if !index.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) && !index.starts_with('%') {
        return None;
    }
    Some((result.trim().to_string(), index.to_string()))
}

FILE: nullmoth/translator/translator/src/native/short_access_chain.rs

//! An access chain that stops one or more composite levels short of the type its result points to.
//!
//! LLVM's opaque pointers let a load of `i64` go straight through a pointer to `{ i64, i64 }`, because the first
//! member sits at offset 0. SPIR-V requires an access chain's index path to land exactly on its result pointer's
//! pointee, so such a chain arrives here selecting the aggregate while its result type names the first member.
//! Appending a zero index for each level down to that member addresses the same bytes with the type SPIR-V
//! requires. It is the address the raw-buffer fallback already uses for storage buffers; this lets workgroup,
//! private and function memory, which have no raw fallback, carry the same chain.
//!
//! Only the first member is ever chosen. A chain whose result type cannot be reached through member 0 is left as
//! it is for the module validator to reject: choosing any other member would read the wrong field.

use super::*;

/// Deepest descent attempted. Real chains need one or two levels; the bound keeps a malformed type graph from
/// looping.
const MAX_DESCENT: usize = 8;

fn first_child(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, ty: Word) -> Option<Word> {
    let def = defs.get(&ty)?;
    match def.class.opcode {
        Op::TypeStruct | Op::TypeArray | Op::TypeRuntimeArray | Op::TypeVector | Op::TypeMatrix => {
            match def.operands.first() {
                Some(Operand::IdRef(child)) => Some(*child),
                _ => None,
            }
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn constant_u32(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, id: Word) -> Option<u32> {
    let def = defs.get(&id)?;
    if def.class.opcode != Op::Constant {
        return None;
    }
    match def.operands.first() {
        Some(Operand::LiteralBit32(value)) => Some(*value),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn pointee(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, pointer_ty: Word) -> Option<Word> {
    let def = defs.get(&pointer_ty)?;
    if def.class.opcode != Op::TypePointer {
        return None;
    }
    match def.operands.get(1) {
        Some(Operand::IdRef(pointee)) => Some(*pointee),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The type an index path selects, or None when the path cannot be walked (a non-constant struct index, or an
/// index into a non-composite) - those are the validator's to report, not ours to guess at.
fn selected_type(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, mut current: Word, indices: &[Operand]) -> Option<Word> {
    for index in indices {
        let Operand::IdRef(index) = index else { return None };
        let def = defs.get(&current)?;
        current = match def.class.opcode {
            Op::TypeStruct => {
                let member = constant_u32(defs, *index)? as usize;
                match def.operands.get(member) {
                    Some(Operand::IdRef(ty)) => *ty,
                    _ => return None,
                }
            }
            Op::TypeArray | Op::TypeRuntimeArray | Op::TypeVector | Op::TypeMatrix => match def.operands.first() {
                Some(Operand::IdRef(ty)) => *ty,
                _ => return None,
            },
            _ => return None,
        };
    }
    Some(current)
}

/// How many zero indices take `selected` down to `want` through first members only, or None.
fn first_member_depth(defs: &HashMap<Word, Instruction>, selected: Word, want: Word) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut ty = selected;
    for depth in 0..=MAX_DESCENT {
        if ty == want {
            return (depth > 0).then_some(depth);
        }
        ty = first_child(defs, ty)?;
    }
    None
}

fn u32_zero(module: &mut Module) -> Word {
    let uint = module.types_global_values.iter().find_map(|i| {
        (i.class.opcode == Op::TypeInt
            && i.operands.first() == Some(&Operand::LiteralBit32(32))
            && i.operands.get(1) == Some(&Operand::LiteralBit32(0)))
        .then_some(i.result_id)
        .flatten()
    });
    let uint = match uint {
        Some(id) => id,
        None => {
            let id = module.fresh_id();
            module.types_global_values.push(Instruction::new(
                Op::TypeInt,
                None,
                Some(id),
                vec![Operand::LiteralBit32(32), Operand::LiteralBit32(0)],
            ));
            id
        }
    };
    if let Some(existing) = module.types_global_values.iter().find_map(|i| {
        (i.class.opcode == Op::Constant
            && i.result_type == Some(uint)
            && i.operands.first() == Some(&Operand::LiteralBit32(0)))
        .then_some(i.result_id)
        .flatten()
    }) {
        return existing;
    }
    let id = module.fresh_id();
    module
        .types_global_values
        .push(Instruction::new(Op::Constant, Some(uint), Some(id), vec![Operand::LiteralBit32(0)]));
    id
}

/// Repairs every access chain that is short only by first-member descent; returns how many it repaired.
pub(super) fn decay_short_access_chains(module: &mut Module) -> usize {
    let defs: HashMap<Word, Instruction> = module
        .types_global_values
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|i| i.result_id.map(|id| (id, i.clone())))
        .collect();
    let mut value_types: HashMap<Word, Word> = HashMap::default();
    for instruction in module.all_inst_iter() {
        if let (Some(id), Some(ty)) = (instruction.result_id, instruction.result_type) {
            value_types.insert(id, ty);
        }
    }

    let mut plans: HashMap<Word, usize> = HashMap::default();
    for function in &module.functions {
        for block in &function.blocks {
            for instruction in &block.instructions {
                // The index path starts after the base, and after the element operand of a Ptr chain, which
                // steps across the base's pointee rather than into it.
                let first_index = match instruction.class.opcode {
                    Op::AccessChain | Op::InBoundsAccessChain => 1,
                    Op::PtrAccessChain | Op::InBoundsPtrAccessChain => 2,
                    _ => continue,
                };
                let (Some(result), Some(result_ty)) = (instruction.result_id, instruction.result_type) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if instruction.operands.len() < first_index {
                    continue;
                }
                let Some(Operand::IdRef(base)) = instruction.operands.first() else { continue };
                let Some(base_ty) = value_types.get(base) else { continue };
                let (Some(base_pointee), Some(want)) = (pointee(&defs, *base_ty), pointee(&defs, result_ty)) else {
                    continue;
                };
                let Some(selected) = selected_type(&defs, base_pointee, &instruction.operands[first_index..]) else {
                    continue;
                };
                if let Some(depth) = first_member_depth(&defs, selected, want) {
                    plans.insert(result, depth);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if plans.is_empty() {
        return 0;
    }

    let zero = u32_zero(module);
    let mut repaired = 0;
    for function in &mut module.functions {
        for block in &mut function.blocks {
            for instruction in &mut block.instructions {
                if let Some(depth) = instruction.result_id.and_then(|id| plans.get(&id)) {
                    instruction.operands.extend(std::iter::repeat(Operand::IdRef(zero)).take(*depth));
                    repaired += 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    repaired
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn ty(op: Op, id: Word, operands: Vec<Operand>) -> Instruction {
        Instruction::new(op, None, Some(id), operands)
    }

    /// The type graph of the failing kernel in miniature: u64 = %1, struct { u64, u64 } = %2,
    /// struct { u32, u64 } = %6, pointers in Workgroup memory.
    fn defs() -> HashMap<Word, Instruction> {
        let wg = Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::Workgroup);
        [
            ty(Op::TypeInt, 1, vec![Operand::LiteralBit32(64), Operand::LiteralBit32(0)]),
            ty(Op::TypeStruct, 2, vec![Operand::IdRef(1), Operand::IdRef(1)]),
            ty(Op::TypePointer, 3, vec![wg.clone(), Operand::IdRef(2)]),
            ty(Op::TypePointer, 4, vec![wg.clone(), Operand::IdRef(1)]),
            ty(Op::TypeInt, 5, vec![Operand::LiteralBit32(32), Operand::LiteralBit32(0)]),
            ty(Op::TypeStruct, 6, vec![Operand::IdRef(5), Operand::IdRef(1)]),
            ty(Op::TypeArray, 7, vec![Operand::IdRef(2), Operand::IdRef(9)]),
        ]
        .into_iter()
        .map(|i| (i.result_id.unwrap(), i))
        .collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_chain_stopping_at_a_pair_of_u64_reaches_its_first_member_with_one_zero() {
        assert_eq!(first_member_depth(&defs(), 2, 1), Some(1));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_chain_two_levels_short_through_an_array_of_pairs_takes_two_zeros() {
        assert_eq!(first_member_depth(&defs(), 7, 1), Some(2));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_struct_whose_first_member_is_not_the_wanted_type_is_left_for_the_validator() {
        // struct { u32, u64 } wanting u64: member 1 has the type, member 0 does not. Choosing member 1 would
        // read a different field, so the chain must stay invalid rather than be guessed at.
        assert_eq!(first_member_depth(&defs(), 6, 1), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_chain_that_already_matches_is_not_touched() {
        assert_eq!(first_member_depth(&defs(), 1, 1), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_pointee_of_the_result_pointer_is_read_from_the_pointer_type() {
        assert_eq!(pointee(&defs(), 4), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(selected_type(&defs(), 2, &[]), Some(2));
    }
}

FILE: nullmoth/translator/translator/src/native/stencil_export.rs
================================================
//! Fragment stencil export (`[[stencil]]`) lowered for GPUs that cannot export stencil.
//!
//! Metal guarantees a fragment shader can write the stencil reference; NVIDIA hardware cannot (its own drivers expose
//! neither GL_ARB_ nor VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export), and the Vulkan driver drops the write. Blender's Metal backend
//! assumes the export and Eevee classifies its G-buffer with it, so every lit surface rendered black. This rewrite does
//! what Blender itself does where the export is missing: the shader keeps the value it would export, and at each return
//! discards unless that value has the bit the driver pushes (a push-constant block, member at offset
//! `STENCIL_EXPORT_PUSH_OFFSET`). The driver replays the draw once with bit 0 (no discard; reference 0 clears the
//! write-masked bits) and once per write-mask bit with only that bit writable, which rebuilds the exported value.

use crate::spirv_module::{Block, Instruction, Module, Operand};
use spirv::{BuiltIn, Capability, Decoration, Op, StorageClass, Word};
use std::collections::HashMap;

pub(crate) const STENCIL_EXPORT_PUSH_OFFSET: u32 = 160;

fn find_type(module: &Module, op: Op, operands: &[Operand]) -> Option<Word> {
    module
        .types_global_values
        .iter()
        .find(|i| i.class.opcode == op && i.operands == operands)
        .and_then(|i| i.result_id)
}

pub(super) fn lower_stencil_export(module: &mut Module) -> bool {
    // the stencil output variable
    let Some(var) = module.annotations.iter().find_map(|a| {
        (a.class.opcode == Op::Decorate
            && a.operands.get(1) == Some(&Operand::Decoration(Decoration::BuiltIn))
            && a.operands.get(2) == Some(&Operand::BuiltIn(BuiltIn::FragStencilRefEXT)))
        .then(|| match a.operands.first() {
            Some(Operand::IdRef(id)) => Some(*id),
            _ => None,
        })
        .flatten()
    }) else {
        return false;
    };
    // a module that already has push constants keeps the export (one push-constant block per entry point)
    if module.types_global_values.iter().any(|i| {
        i.class.opcode == Op::Variable && i.operands.first() == Some(&Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::PushConstant))
    }) {
        return false;
    }
    let defs: HashMap<Word, Instruction> =
        module.types_global_values.iter().filter_map(|i| i.result_id.map(|id| (id, i.clone()))).collect();
    let Some(var_ptr_ty) = defs.get(&var).and_then(|v| v.result_type) else { return false };
    let Some(Operand::IdRef(value_ty)) = defs.get(&var_ptr_ty).and_then(|p| p.operands.get(1)).cloned() else { return false };
    let Some(value_def) = defs.get(&value_ty).cloned() else { return false };
    if value_def.class.opcode != Op::TypeInt {
        return false;
    }
    let signed = value_def.operands.get(1) == Some(&Operand::LiteralBit32(1));
    // the fragment entry point
    let Some(entry_fn) = module.entry_points.iter().find_map(|e| match (e.operands.first(), e.operands.get(1)) {
        (Some(Operand::ExecutionModel(spirv::ExecutionModel::Fragment)), Some(Operand::IdRef(f))) => Some(*f),
        _ => None,
    }) else {
        return false;
    };

    let mut new_types: Vec<Instruction> = Vec::new();
    let fresh_type = |module: &mut Module, new_types: &mut Vec<Instruction>, op: Op, operands: Vec<Operand>| -> Word {
        if let Some(id) = find_type(module, op, &operands).or_else(|| {
            new_types.iter().find(|i| i.class.opcode == op && i.operands == operands).and_then(|i| i.result_id)
        }) {
            return id;
        }
        let id = module.fresh_id();
        new_types.push(Instruction::new(op, None, Some(id), operands));
        id
    };
    let uint_ty = fresh_type(module, &mut new_types, Op::TypeInt, vec![Operand::LiteralBit32(32), Operand::LiteralBit32(0)]);
    let bool_ty = fresh_type(module, &mut new_types, Op::TypeBool, vec![]);
    // the push-constant block gets its own struct type (Block-decorated), never shared
    let block_ty = module.fresh_id();
    new_types.push(Instruction::new(Op::TypeStruct, None, Some(block_ty), vec![Operand::IdRef(uint_ty)]));
    let block_ptr = fresh_type(module, &mut new_types, Op::TypePointer, vec![Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::PushConstant), Operand::IdRef(block_ty)]);
    let member_ptr = fresh_type(module, &mut new_types, Op::TypePointer, vec![Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::PushConstant), Operand::IdRef(uint_ty)]);
    let private_ptr = fresh_type(module, &mut new_types, Op::TypePointer, vec![Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::Private), Operand::IdRef(value_ty)]);
    let pc_var = module.fresh_id();
    let zero = module.fresh_id();
    new_types.push(Instruction::new(Op::Constant, Some(uint_ty), Some(zero), vec![Operand::LiteralBit32(0)]));
    // constants and variables after the types they use: append, then the pc variable
    module.types_global_values.extend(new_types);
    module.types_global_values.push(Instruction::new(
        Op::Variable,
        Some(block_ptr),
        Some(pc_var),
        vec![Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::PushConstant)],
    ));
    module.annotations.push(Instruction::new(Op::Decorate, None, None, vec![Operand::IdRef(block_ty), Operand::Decoration(Decoration::Block)]));
    module.annotations.push(Instruction::new(
        Op::MemberDecorate,
        None,
        None,
        vec![Operand::IdRef(block_ty), Operand::LiteralBit32(0), Operand::Decoration(Decoration::Offset), Operand::LiteralBit32(STENCIL_EXPORT_PUSH_OFFSET)],
    ));
    // the output becomes a Private variable holding the value
    module.annotations.retain(|a| {
        !(a.class.opcode == Op::Decorate
            && a.operands.first() == Some(&Operand::IdRef(var))
            && a.operands.get(1) == Some(&Operand::Decoration(Decoration::BuiltIn)))
    });
    // a Private global must follow its pointer type: move the variable to the end of the globals
    if let Some(pos) = module.types_global_values.iter().position(|i| i.result_id == Some(var)) {
        let mut v = module.types_global_values.remove(pos);
        v.result_type = Some(private_ptr);
        v.operands = vec![Operand::StorageClass(StorageClass::Private)];
        module.types_global_values.push(v);
    }
    for e in module.entry_points.iter_mut() {
        if matches!(e.operands.get(1), Some(Operand::IdRef(f)) if *f == entry_fn) {
            e.operands.push(Operand::IdRef(pc_var));
        }
    }
    module.capabilities.retain(|c| c.operands.first() != Some(&Operand::Capability(Capability::StencilExportEXT)));
    module.execution_modes.retain(|m| m.operands.get(1) != Some(&Operand::ExecutionMode(spirv::ExecutionMode::StencilRefReplacingEXT)));
    module.extensions.retain(|x| !matches!(x.operands.first(), Some(Operand::LiteralString(s)) if s == "SPV_EXT_shader_stencil_export"));

    // at each return of the entry function: discard unless (value & bit), when a bit is pushed
    let Some(fi) = module.functions.iter().position(|f| f.def.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.result_id) == Some(entry_fn)) else {
        return true;
    };
    let mut blocks: Vec<Block> = Vec::new();
    for mut block in std::mem::take(&mut module.functions[fi].blocks) {
        let ends_in_return = block.instructions.last().is_some_and(|i| i.class.opcode == Op::Return);
        if !ends_in_return {
            blocks.push(block);
            continue;
        }
        block.instructions.pop();
        let v = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::Load, Some(value_ty), Some(v), vec![Operand::IdRef(var)]));
        let vu = if signed {
            let b = module.fresh_id();
            block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::Bitcast, Some(uint_ty), Some(b), vec![Operand::IdRef(v)]));
            b
        } else {
            v
        };
        let chain = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::AccessChain, Some(member_ptr), Some(chain), vec![Operand::IdRef(pc_var), Operand::IdRef(zero)]));
        let bit = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::Load, Some(uint_ty), Some(bit), vec![Operand::IdRef(chain)]));
        let anded = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::BitwiseAnd, Some(uint_ty), Some(anded), vec![Operand::IdRef(vu), Operand::IdRef(bit)]));
        let missing = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::IEqual, Some(bool_ty), Some(missing), vec![Operand::IdRef(anded), Operand::IdRef(zero)]));
        let pushed = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::INotEqual, Some(bool_ty), Some(pushed), vec![Operand::IdRef(bit), Operand::IdRef(zero)]));
        let cond = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::LogicalAnd, Some(bool_ty), Some(cond), vec![Operand::IdRef(missing), Operand::IdRef(pushed)]));
        let kill_label = module.fresh_id();
        let ret_label = module.fresh_id();
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::SelectionMerge, None, None, vec![Operand::IdRef(ret_label), Operand::SelectionControl(spirv::SelectionControl::NONE)]));
        block.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::BranchConditional, None, None, vec![Operand::IdRef(cond), Operand::IdRef(kill_label), Operand::IdRef(ret_label)]));
        blocks.push(block);
        let mut kill = Block::new();
        kill.label = Some(Instruction::new(Op::Label, None, Some(kill_label), vec![]));
        kill.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::Kill, None, None, vec![]));
        blocks.push(kill);
        let mut ret = Block::new();
        ret.label = Some(Instruction::new(Op::Label, None, Some(ret_label), vec![]));
        ret.instructions.push(Instruction::new(Op::Return, None, None, vec![]));
        blocks.push(ret);
    }
    module.functions[fi].blocks = blocks;
    true
}
