#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# test-install-flow.sh PACKAGE_DIR: runs install.sh's whole flow against a throwaway root, without root and without kmutil:
# install, the same again, a damaged file, repair, an edited allow-list, an earlier release's allow-list, undo (with the version it puts back), uninstall;
# then NVMTLDriver.use-library with a system-volume copy of another release, with system-volume/ssv-install.sh (stubbed
# mount and bless). Each step's --status is checked.
set -uo pipefail
PKG=$(cd "$1" && pwd)
ROOT=$(mktemp -d -t ixeflow)
T=$ROOT/pkg
ditto "$PKG" "$T"
# the same script with its paths under the throwaway root, and what needs root or a real Mac stubbed
sed -E -e "s#([^H])/Library/#\1$ROOT/Library/#g" -e "s#SSV=/System/#SSV=$ROOT/System/#" "$PKG/install.sh" > "$T/install.sh"
perl -0pi -e 's/^set -euo pipefail\n/set -euo pipefail\nid() { echo 0; }\nchown() { :; }\ninstall() { local a=(); while [ \$# -gt 0 ]; do case "\$1" in -o|-g|-m) shift 2;; *) a+=("\$1"); shift;; esac; done; cp "\${a[@]}"; }\n/m; s/^check\(\) \{\n/check() { return 0; }\ncheck_real() {\n/m; s/^rebuild_auxkc\(\) \{\n/rebuild_auxkc() { echo "  ok    (kernel collection step skipped in this test)"; }\nrebuild_real() {\n/m' "$T/install.sh"
chmod +x "$T/install.sh"
mkdir -p "$ROOT/Library/Extensions" "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles" "$ROOT/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver"
fails=0
state() { "$T/install.sh" --status | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"; }
expect() { # expect WHAT KEY VALUE
    local got; got=$(state "$2")
    if [ "$got" = "$3" ]; then echo "ok    $1: $2=$got"; else echo "FAIL  $1: $2=$got, expected $3"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
}
step() { "$T/install.sh" "$1" > "$ROOT/last.log" 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL  $1 exited with an error:"; tail -5 "$ROOT/last.log"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }; }

expect "nothing installed" installed_state absent
expect "nothing installed" installed_version none
step --apply
expect "after --apply" installed_state same
expect "after --apply" installed_version "$(state package_version)"
[ -f "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl-allow.txt" ] && echo "ok    allow-list installed" || { echo "FAIL  no allow-list"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
expect "after --apply" guard_daemon yes
plutil -lint "$ROOT/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.guard.plist" >/dev/null && echo "ok    guard daemon plist is valid" || { echo "FAIL  guard daemon plist"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
sh -n "$ROOT/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver/guard-clear.sh" && echo "ok    guard script parses" || { echo "FAIL  guard script"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

K="$ROOT/Library/Extensions/IntelXeFB.kext/Contents/MacOS/IntelXeFB"
echo damaged >> "$K"
expect "a kext damaged" installed_state different
expect "a kext damaged" items_different 1
step --repair
expect "after --repair" installed_state same
grep -q "kernel collection step" "$ROOT/last.log" && echo "ok    repair of a kext rebuilds the collection" || { echo "FAIL  repair did not rebuild the collection"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

M=$(find "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl" -type f | head -1)
echo damaged >> "$M"
step --repair
expect "after a Metal file repair" installed_state same
grep -q "kernel collection step" "$ROOT/last.log" && { echo "FAIL  repair of a Metal file rebuilt the collection"; fails=$((fails + 1)); } || echo "ok    repair of a Metal file leaves the collection"

echo "+ my.app" >> "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl-allow.txt"
touch "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/ssv-component.plist"
expect "an edited allow-list and the record of a system-volume copy are not differences" installed_state same
step --repair
grep -q "my.app" "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl-allow.txt" && echo "ok    repair keeps an edited allow-list" || { echo "FAIL  repair lost the allow-list"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
rm "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/ssv-component.plist"

backup=$(state backup)
step --repair
[ "$(state backup)" = "$backup" ] && echo "ok    repair leaves the last backup" || { echo "FAIL  repair changed the backup"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

step --undo
expect "after --undo (there was nothing before)" installed_state absent
expect "after --undo" installed_version none
expect "after --undo (there was no guard daemon before)" guard_daemon no
step --apply
# undo puts back the version recorded with its backup (here an earlier version, written by hand)
echo 0.0.9-test > "$ROOT/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver/installed-version"
step --apply
expect "after --apply over 0.0.9-test" installed_version "$(state package_version)"
step --undo
expect "after --undo of that install" installed_version 0.0.9-test
expect "after --undo of that install" installed_state same
step --apply
step --uninstall
expect "after --uninstall" installed_state absent
expect "after --uninstall" guard_daemon no
expect "after --uninstall" installed_version none
[ -d "$backup" ] && echo "ok    uninstall keeps backups" || { echo "FAIL  backups are gone"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

# the allow-list an earlier release installed is replaced, one the user edited is kept
A="$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl-allow.txt"; mkdir -p "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles"
printf '%s\n' "# B580: which processes get the B580 Metal device (-Name denies, !Name = only when armed; NVMTL_ENABLE=1 bypasses)" \
    "# 4 Nov Tahoe: Safari's GPU process restarted 16 times in 2 min on the plugin (black page content): kept off until fixed" \
    -com.apple.WebKit.GPU -com.apple.dock.extra mtl_smoke '!WindowServer' '!*' > "$A"
step --apply
cmp -s "$A" "$T/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl-allow.txt" && echo "ok    apply replaces 0.1.1's allow-list" || { echo "FAIL  0.1.1's allow-list was kept"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
echo "+ my.app" >> "$A"
step --apply
grep -q "my.app" "$A" && echo "ok    apply keeps an edited allow-list" || { echo "FAIL  apply replaced an edited allow-list"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
step --uninstall
grep -q "remove IntelXe.kext" "$ROOT/last.log" && echo "ok    uninstall says to remove the kext from the EFI" || { echo "FAIL  no EFI note"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

# The system-volume copy and NVMTLDriver.use-library (0.1.6): --apply makes the file for a copy of another release and
# records that it did; system-volume/ssv-install.sh --apply removes it once it has installed this package's copy (a file
# the user made stays); a later --apply does not make it again while the new copy waits for the restart.
SV=$(sed -n 's/^SSV=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "$T/install.sh")   # the booted snapshot's copy, where the test's install.sh looks
U=$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.use-library
BKD="$ROOT/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver"
LAYOUT=$PKG/system-volume/system-layout/NVMTLDriver.bundle
old_copy() { rm -rf "$SV"; ditto "$LAYOUT" "$SV"; echo "another release" >> "$SV/Contents/Frameworks/nvmtl/libvulkan_intel.dylib"; }
check_file() { # check_file WHAT present|absent PATH
    if { [ "$2" = present ] && [ -e "$3" ]; } || { [ "$2" = absent ] && [ ! -e "$3" ]; }; then echo "ok    $1: ${3##*/} $2"
    else echo "FAIL  $1: ${3##*/} not $2"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi
}
if [ -f "$PKG/system-volume/ssv-install.sh" ] && [ -d "$LAYOUT" ]; then
    # ssv-install.sh with its paths under the throwaway root; the mount, bless, the root checks and preflight stubbed.
    # The copy goes to $ROOT/mnt (the system volume behind a new snapshot), not to the booted copy: a restart moves it.
    sed -E -e "s#^(MARK|USELIB)=/Library/#\1=$ROOT/Library/#" -e "s#^BK=\"/Library/#BK=\"$ROOT/Library/#" \
        -e "s#local L=/Library/#local L=$ROOT/Library/#" -e "s#^MNT=.*#MNT=$ROOT/mnt#" "$PKG/system-volume/ssv-install.sh" > "$T/system-volume/ssv-install.sh"
    perl -0pi -e 's/^set -uo pipefail\n/set -uo pipefail\nid() { echo 0; }\nchown() { :; }\nmount() { :; }\numount() { :; }\nbless() { :; }\n/m; s/^preflight\(\) \{\n/preflight() { return 0; }\npreflight_real() {\n/m; s/^root_device\(\) \{\n/root_device() { SYSDEV=disk9s9; }\nroot_device_real() {\n/m' "$T/system-volume/ssv-install.sh"
    mkdir -p "$ROOT/mnt/System/Library/Extensions"
    ssv() { "$T/system-volume/ssv-install.sh" --apply > "$ROOT/ssv.log" 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL  ssv-install.sh --apply exited with an error:"; tail -5 "$ROOT/ssv.log"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }; }
    restart() { rm -rf "$SV"; ditto "$ROOT/mnt/System/Library/Extensions/NVMTLDriver.bundle" "$SV"; }

    step --apply
    expect "no system-volume copy: nothing changes for it" use_library no
    expect "no system-volume copy" system_volume_state absent
    step --uninstall

    old_copy
    expect "a copy of another release" system_volume_state other
    step --apply
    expect "--apply over a copy of another release" use_library yes
    expect "--apply over a copy of another release" use_library_by install
    ssv
    check_file "ssv-install.sh --apply of this package's copy" absent "$U"
    check_file "ssv-install.sh --apply of this package's copy" absent "$BKD/use-library-by-install"
    expect "this package's copy in the new snapshot, before the restart" system_volume_state pending
    expect "before the restart" use_library_by none
    step --apply
    check_file "--apply while the new copy waits for the restart" absent "$U"
    restart
    expect "after the restart" system_volume_state same
    expect "after the restart" use_library no

    # 0.1.6 changed the plugin and not Mesa: a copy with this package's Mesa and another plugin is another release too
    sleep 1; rm -rf "$SV"; ditto "$LAYOUT" "$SV"; echo "another plugin" >> "$SV/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver"
    # its ssv-install.sh's record: the same Mesa, that release's plugin
    /usr/bin/defaults write "$ROOT/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/ssv-component" sha "$(shasum -a 256 < "$SV/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver" | cut -c1-64)"
    expect "a copy with another plugin (the same Mesa)" system_volume_state other
    step --apply
    expect "--apply over a copy with another plugin" use_library yes
    expect "--apply over a copy with another plugin" use_library_by install
    ssv
    check_file "ssv-install.sh --apply over a copy with another plugin" absent "$U"
    expect "its copy in the new snapshot, before the restart" system_volume_state pending
    restart
    expect "after that restart" system_volume_state same

    sleep 1; touch "$U"
    expect "a use-library file made by hand" use_library_by user
    step --apply
    check_file "--apply leaves the file made by hand" present "$U"
    ssv
    check_file "ssv-install.sh leaves the file made by hand" present "$U"
    grep -q "not made by install.sh" "$ROOT/ssv.log" && echo "ok    ssv-install.sh says why it kept it" || { echo "FAIL  ssv-install.sh did not say why"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
    rm -f "$U"; step --uninstall

    # 0.1.5's install.sh recorded the file only in its backup (created-use-library); this release's --apply takes it over
    old_copy; step --apply; rm -f "$BKD/use-library-by-install"
    expect "a use-library file of 0.1.5's install.sh" use_library_by install
    step --apply
    expect "--apply over 0.1.5's file" use_library_by install
    check_file "--apply over 0.1.5's file" present "$BKD/use-library-by-install"
    ssv
    check_file "ssv-install.sh after 0.1.5's install.sh" absent "$U"

    # an earlier --apply's file while the copy is this package's already (installed by an earlier ssv-install.sh):
    # --apply removes it, --undo puts it back
    sleep 1   # a new second: the backup folders are named by the second (two --apply in one second share one)
    restart; : > "$U"; : > "$BKD/use-library-by-install"
    step --apply
    check_file "--apply with this package's copy installed" absent "$U"
    step --undo
    check_file "--undo of that" present "$U"
    expect "--undo of that" use_library_by install
    step --uninstall
    check_file "--uninstall" absent "$U"
    check_file "--uninstall" absent "$BKD/use-library-by-install"

    # --undo of the --apply that made it removes it and its record
    old_copy; step --apply; step --undo
    check_file "--undo of the --apply that made it" absent "$U"
    check_file "--undo of the --apply that made it" absent "$BKD/use-library-by-install"
    rm -rf "$SV"
else
    echo "skip  the system-volume steps: the package has no system-volume/ssv-install.sh and system-layout"
fi

[ -n "$ROOT" ] && rm -rf -- "$ROOT"
echo "== $fails failure(s)"
exit $fails

FILE: release/test-package-probe.sh

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# test-package-probe.sh: package.sh with and without the Xe probe stick image (PROBE_IMG, PROBE_SKIP), on made-up inputs
# in a copy of the packager (package.sh writes its filled copies beside itself: never into this repository). It needs
# no real binaries, no Docker and no release key (a key is made for the test). Checks: no PROBE_IMG refuses before
# anything is written; PROBE_SKIP=1 packages without it; an image of another version, one whose .img.sha256 does not
# match and one without the stick's layout are refused; with PROBE_IMG, xe-probe-stick-SVER.img.zip is written, holds
# the image and its .img.sha256, is in the signed list, and the list's signature verifies; release.sh's check of the
# zip (zip-image.py verify) passes on it and fails on a damaged one.
set -uo pipefail
R=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
W=$(mktemp -d -t ixeprobepkg)
trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
fails=0
ok()  { echo "ok    $*"; }
bad() { echo "FAIL  $*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }
VER=0.0.0-test
N=intel-gpu-macos-driver-$VER
SVER=$(cat "$R/tools/probe-stick/VERSION")

# the packager and what it reads from the repository, in a throwaway tree
C=$W/repo
mkdir -p "$C/tools/probe-stick" "$C/kernel/HybridPM" "$C/windows" "$C/firmware"
cp "$R/firmware/LICENSE.xe" "$R/firmware/LICENSE.i915" "$C/firmware/"   # package.sh ships both with the kext
ditto "$R/release" "$C/release"
cp "$R/tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py" "$R/tools/probe-stick/VERSION" "$C/tools/probe-stick/"
cp "$R/kernel/HybridPM/LICENSE.Lilu" "$C/kernel/HybridPM/"
mkdir -p "$C/user/tools"; cp "$R/user/tools/ssv-install.sh" "$C/user/tools/"   # package.sh ships it in system-volume/
cp "$R/windows/IntelXe-EFI.ps1" "$R/windows/README.md" "$C/windows/"
# both apps' release key lists (package.sh's key checks read them; the test key is added to these copies below)
mkdir -p "$C/app/Sources" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release"
cp "$R/app/Sources/Signing.swift" "$C/app/Sources/"
cp "$R/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/ReleaseSigning.cs" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/"

# made-up Tahoe and Sequoia inputs: the package layout with text files (no Mach-O, so nothing to sign)
for x in tahoe sequoia; do
	i=$W/in-$x
	for f in EFI/OC/Kexts/IntelXe.kext/Contents/MacOS/IntelXe EFI/OC/Kexts/IntelXe.kext/Contents/Info.plist \
	         EFI/OC/Kexts/HybridPM.kext/Contents/MacOS/HybridPM EFI/OC/Kexts/HybridPM.kext/Contents/Info.plist \
	         EFI/OC/Kexts/HybridPM.kext/Contents/Resources/LICENSE-Lilu.txt EFI/OC/ACPI/SSDT-ARCOFF.aml EFI/OC/ACPI/SSDT-ARCOFF.dsl \
	         hpmstat sigcheck SOURCES.md LICENSES/MIT.txt Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/x.txt system-volume/x.txt; do
		mkdir -p "$i/$(dirname "$f")"; echo "$f" > "$i/$f"
	done
	(cd "$i/system-volume" && shasum -a 256 x.txt > SHA256SUMS)
done

# a made-up image with the stick's layout (2 MiB) and its .img.sha256, as build.sh writes them
img() { # img DIR NAME [label]
	mkdir -p "$1"
	python3 -I - "$1/$2" "${3:-XEPROBE}" <<'PY'
import hashlib, os, struct, sys
p, label = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
b = bytearray(2 << 20)
b[446 + 4] = 0x0C
struct.pack_into("<II", b, 446 + 8, 2048, len(b) // 512 - 2048)
b[510:512] = b"\x55\xaa"
bs = 2048 * 512
b[bs + 71:bs + 82] = label.ljust(11).encode()
b[bs + 82:bs + 90] = b"FAT32   "
b[bs + 510:bs + 512] = b"\x55\xaa"
b[bs + 4096:bs + 4096 + 32] = hashlib.sha256(p.encode()).digest()
open(p, "wb").write(b)
open(p + ".sha256", "w").write(hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() + "  " + os.path.basename(p) + "\n")
PY
	echo "$1/$2"
}
IMG=$(img "$W/img" "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img")
pkg() { # pkg OUT [VAR=value ...]: package.sh's output in $W/log
	local out=$1; shift
	# PROBE_GUC_SKIP=1: the made-up IntelXe.kext has no XeProbe GuC images (package.sh's check of them came later)
	env WINAPP_SKIP=1 PROBE_GUC_SKIP=1 "$@" bash "$C/release/package.sh" "$VER" "$W/in-tahoe" "$W/in-sequoia" "$out" > "$W/log" 2>&1
}

# no PROBE_IMG: refused before anything is written
if pkg "$W/out0"; then bad "packaged without PROBE_IMG"; else
	grep -q "no PROBE_IMG" "$W/log" && ok "no PROBE_IMG: refused" || bad "no PROBE_IMG: refused without saying why: $(tail -1 "$W/log")"
fi
[ ! -e "$W/out0" ] && ok "no PROBE_IMG: nothing written" || bad "no PROBE_IMG: $W/out0 was written"

# PROBE_SKIP=1: a release without it
if pkg "$W/out1" PROBE_SKIP=1; then
	ok "PROBE_SKIP=1 packages"
	grep -q xe-probe-stick "$W/out1/$N.sha256" && bad "PROBE_SKIP=1: the list names a probe image" || ok "PROBE_SKIP=1: no probe image in the list"
	ls "$W/out1" | grep -q xe-probe-stick && bad "PROBE_SKIP=1: a probe file was written" || ok "PROBE_SKIP=1: no probe file"
else bad "PROBE_SKIP=1 failed: $(tail -3 "$W/log")"; fi

# refused images
OTHER=$(img "$W/img2" "xe-probe-stick-9.9.9.img")
pkg "$W/out2" PROBE_IMG="$OTHER" && bad "an image of another version was packaged" || { grep -q "not $SVER" "$W/log" && ok "another version: refused" || bad "another version: $(tail -2 "$W/log")"; }
DMG=$(img "$W/img3" "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img")
printf 'x' | dd of="$DMG" bs=1 seek=1500000 conv=notrunc 2>/dev/null
pkg "$W/out3" PROBE_IMG="$DMG" && bad "a damaged image was packaged" || { grep -q "not its .img.sha256" "$W/log" && ok "a damaged image: refused" || bad "a damaged image: $(tail -2 "$W/log")"; }
LBL=$(img "$W/img4" "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img" MACOS)
pkg "$W/out4" PROBE_IMG="$LBL" && bad "an image labelled MACOS was packaged" || { grep -q "not XEPROBE" "$W/log" && ok "not the stick's layout: refused" || bad "the layout: $(tail -2 "$W/log")"; }
mv "$IMG.sha256" "$IMG.sha256.bak"
pkg "$W/out5" PROBE_IMG="$IMG" && bad "an image without its .img.sha256 was packaged" || { grep -q "no xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img.sha256" "$W/log" && ok "no .img.sha256: refused" || bad "no .img.sha256: $(tail -2 "$W/log")"; }
mv "$IMG.sha256.bak" "$IMG.sha256"
for o in out2 out3 out4 out5; do [ ! -e "$W/$o" ] || bad "$o was written for a refused image"; done

# with PROBE_IMG and a key: the zip, in the signed list
PUB=$(swift "$R/release/signing.swift" keygen "$W/test.key")
bash "$C/release/release-keys.sh" add "$PUB" >/dev/null || bad "the test key could not be added to the copies' key lists"
if pkg "$W/out" PROBE_IMG="$IMG" SIGN_KEY="$W/test.key"; then
	ok "packaged with PROBE_IMG"
	Z=xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img.zip
	[ -f "$W/out/$Z" ] && ok "$Z written" || bad "no $Z"
	grep -q "  $Z\$" "$W/out/$N.sha256" && ok "$Z is in $N.sha256" || bad "$Z is not in $N.sha256"
	(cd "$W/out" && shasum -a 256 -c "$N.sha256" >/dev/null) && ok "$N.sha256 matches the files" || bad "$N.sha256 does not match"
	swift "$R/release/signing.swift" verify "$PUB" "$W/out/$N.sha256" "$W/out/$N.sha256.sig" >/dev/null && ok "the list's signature verifies" || bad "the list's signature does not verify"
	[ "$(unzip -Z1 "$W/out/$Z" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img.sha256 " ] && ok "$Z holds the image and its .img.sha256" || bad "$Z holds $(unzip -Z1 "$W/out/$Z" | tr '\n' ' ')"
	unzip -p "$W/out/$Z" "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img" | cmp -s - "$IMG" && ok "the image in $Z is PROBE_IMG" || bad "the image in $Z differs from PROBE_IMG"
	unzip -p "$W/out/$Z" "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img.sha256" | cmp -s - "$IMG.sha256" && ok "its .img.sha256 is PROBE_IMG's" || bad "its .img.sha256 differs"
	python3 -I "$R/tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py" verify "$W/out/$Z" --version "$SVER" >/dev/null && ok "release.sh's check passes" || bad "release.sh's check (zip-image.py verify) fails on a good zip"
	ls "$W/out" | grep -q '\.sha256$' && [ "$(ls "$W/out" | grep -c '\.sha256$')" = 1 ] && ok "one .sha256 asset (the list): the macOS app finds it by its ending" || bad "more than one .sha256 asset: $(ls "$W/out" | grep '\.sha256$' | tr '\n' ' ')"
	python3 -I - "$W/out/$Z" "$W/xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img.zip" "xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img" <<'PY'
import sys, zipfile
src, dst, name = sys.argv[1:4]
with zipfile.ZipFile(src) as a, zipfile.ZipFile(dst, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as b:
    for i in a.infolist():
        data = bytearray(a.read(i.filename))
        if i.filename == name: data[1500000] ^= 1
        b.writestr(i, bytes(data))
PY
	python3 -I "$R/tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py" verify "$W/xe-probe-stick-$SVER.img.zip" >/dev/null 2>&1 && bad "release.sh's check passes a zip whose image is changed" || ok "release.sh's check refuses a zip whose image is changed"
	# package again without PROBE_IMG (PROBE_SKIP=1) into the same folder: the old zip goes
	pkg "$W/out" PROBE_SKIP=1 && [ ! -f "$W/out/$Z" ] && ok "packaging again with PROBE_SKIP=1 removes the earlier zip" || bad "an earlier $Z stayed in the folder"
else bad "packaging with PROBE_IMG failed: $(tail -5 "$W/log")"; fi

echo "== $fails failure(s)"
exit $fails



================================================
FILE: release/test-signing.sh
================================================
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# test-signing.sh: the release signing keys' change (docs/RELEASE-KEYS.md) end to end, with throwaway keys made in a
# temporary folder (never the project's key): signing.swift's keygen/sign/verify; the app's real check (app/Sources/
# Signing.swift, compiled with a small driver) as an app before the change, during it and after the old key is retired;
# release-keys.sh add/retire/check on copies of both apps' key lists; release-keys.sh release-check (release.sh's
# signature checks) on made-up releases; and package.sh's key checks, which run before it reads any input.
#
#   bash release/test-signing.sh        (macOS, swiftc; about a minute)
set -uo pipefail
R=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
T=$(mktemp -d -t ixesign)
trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
pass=0 fail=0
ok()  { pass=$((pass + 1)); printf '  ok    %s\n' "$*"; }
bad() { fail=$((fail + 1)); printf '  FAIL  %s\n' "$*"; }
expect() { # expect 0|1 "what" command...: the command's exit status is 0 (1: not 0)
    local want=$1 what=$2; shift 2
    if "$@" >"$T/last.out" 2>&1; then got=0; else got=1; fi
    [ $got = "$want" ] && ok "$what" || { bad "$what (exit $got)"; sed 's/^/        /' "$T/last.out"; }
}

echo "== building signing.swift and the app's check"
swiftc -O "$R/release/signing.swift" -o "$T/signing" 2>"$T/build.log" || { cat "$T/build.log"; exit 1; }
SIGN=$T/signing
# The driver: the app's releaseSignatureValid with the keys given (or the list built in), reading the signature the way
# an app of that generation does: "old" reads .sig only (0.1.4 and before), "new" prefers .sigs (Model.swift since the
# key change was planned; ProbeDownload.cs the same).
cat > "$T/main.swift" <<'EOF'
import Foundation
let a = CommandLine.arguments   // KEYS|default MODE LIST SIG SIGS
let keys = a[1] == "default" ? releaseSigningKeys : a[1].split(separator: ",").map(String.init)
let sigsPath = a[5]
let path = (a[2] == "new" && FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: sigsPath)) ? sigsPath : a[4]
let list = FileManager.default.contents(atPath: a[3]) ?? Data()
let text = (FileManager.default.contents(atPath: path)).map { String(decoding: $0, as: UTF8.self) } ?? ""
exit(releaseSignatureValid(list: list, signature: text, keys: keys) ? 0 : 1)
EOF
swiftc "$R/app/Sources/Signing.swift" "$T/main.swift" -o "$T/app" 2>"$T/build.log" || { cat "$T/build.log"; exit 1; }
PROJECT=$(bash "$R/release/release-keys.sh" list | head -1)
grep -a -q -F "$PROJECT" "$T/app" && ok "a key of Signing.swift is in the compiled binary as text (package.sh's check of the app finds it)" ||
    bad "the compiled app does not carry $PROJECT as text: package.sh's APP_DIR key check would refuse every app"

echo "== keys and signatures (signing.swift)"
mkdir -p "$T/keys"
OLD=$("$SIGN" keygen "$T/keys/old.key") NEW=$("$SIGN" keygen "$T/keys/new.key") EVIL=$("$SIGN" keygen "$T/keys/evil.key")
[ "$("$SIGN" public "$T/keys/old.key")" = "$OLD" ] && ok "keygen prints the key file's public key" || bad "public differs from keygen"
expect 1 "keygen does not overwrite a key file" "$SIGN" keygen "$T/keys/old.key"
[ "$(stat -f %Lp "$T/keys/old.key")" = 600 ] && ok "a new key file is mode 600" || bad "key file mode $(stat -f %Lp "$T/keys/old.key")"
# release N (the transition): package.sh with SIGN_KEY=old SIGN_KEY_NEXT=new writes .sig (old) and .sigs (old, new)
N=$T/N; mkdir -p "$N"
printf '%064d  intel-gpu-macos-driver-9.0.0-tahoe.zip\n' 1 > "$N/list"
"$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/old.key" "$N/list" && mv "$N/list.sig" "$N/sig"
for k in old new; do "$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/$k.key" "$N/list" "$N/sigs"; done
[ "$(wc -l < "$N/sigs" | tr -d ' ')" = 2 ] && ok ".sigs has one line per key" || bad ".sigs has $(wc -l < "$N/sigs") lines"
expect 0 "signing.swift verify: the old key's .sig" "$SIGN" verify "$OLD" "$N/list" "$N/sig"
expect 0 "signing.swift verify: the new key's line of .sigs" "$SIGN" verify "$NEW" "$N/list" "$N/sigs"
expect 1 "signing.swift verify: the new key is not the .sig's" "$SIGN" verify "$NEW" "$N/list" "$N/sig"
# release N+1, signed by the new key only; a release signed by someone else; a changed list
N1=$T/N1; mkdir -p "$N1"; cp "$N/list" "$N1/list"; echo "$(printf '%064d' 2)  intel-gpu-macos-driver-9.0.1-efi.zip" >> "$N1/list"
"$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/new.key" "$N1/list" && mv "$N1/list.sig" "$N1/sig"
E=$T/E; mkdir -p "$E"; cp "$N/list" "$E/list"
"$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/evil.key" "$E/list" && mv "$E/list.sig" "$E/sig"
"$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/evil.key" "$E/list" "$E/sigs"
X=$T/X; mkdir -p "$X"; sed 's/^0/f/' "$N/list" > "$X/list"; cp "$N/sig" "$N/sigs" "$X/"
B=$T/B; mkdir -p "$B"; cp "$N/list" "$B/"; sed 's/^./A/' "$N/sig" > "$B/sig"; [ "$(cat "$B/sig")" != "$(cat "$N/sig")" ] || sed 's/^./B/' "$N/sig" > "$B/sig"

echo "== the app's check (Signing.swift) across the key change"
app() { "$T/app" "$1" "$2" "$3/list" "$3/sig" "$3/sigs"; }
expect 0 "an app before the change ([old], reads .sig) accepts release N" app "$OLD" old "$N"
expect 1 "an app before the change refuses release N+1 (new key only)" app "$OLD" old "$N1"
expect 0 "an app of release N ([old,new], reads .sigs) accepts release N" app "$OLD,$NEW" new "$N"
expect 0 "an app of release N accepts release N+1 (no .sigs: reads .sig)" app "$OLD,$NEW" new "$N1"
expect 0 "an app knowing only the new key accepts release N through its .sigs" app "$NEW" new "$N"
expect 1 "an app with the old key retired ([new]) refuses a release signed by the old key only" app "$NEW" old "$N"
expect 0 "an app with the old key retired accepts release N+1" app "$NEW" new "$N1"
expect 1 "a release signed by another key is refused (.sig)" app "$OLD,$NEW" old "$E"
expect 1 "a release signed by another key is refused (.sigs)" app "$OLD,$NEW" new "$E"
expect 1 "a changed list is refused (.sig)" app "$OLD,$NEW" old "$X"
expect 1 "a changed list is refused (.sigs)" app "$OLD,$NEW" new "$X"
expect 1 "a changed signature is refused" app "$OLD,$NEW" old "$B"
expect 1 "the built-in project key refuses a throwaway-signed release" app default old "$N"

echo "== release-keys.sh on copies of both apps' lists"
C=$T/root; mkdir -p "$C/app/Sources" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release"
cp "$R/app/Sources/Signing.swift" "$C/app/Sources/"; cp "$R/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/ReleaseSigning.cs" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/"
# the copies start with the old throwaway key only, as if it were the project's
sed -i '' "s#^let releaseSigningKeys = \[.*\]\$#let releaseSigningKeys = [\"$OLD\"]#" "$C/app/Sources/Signing.swift"
sed -i '' "s#^\( *public static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> Keys = \)\[.*\];\$#\1[\"$OLD\"];#" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/ReleaseSigning.cs"
keys() { KEYS_ROOT=$C bash "$R/release/release-keys.sh" "$@"; }
expect 0 "check: one key, the same in both" keys check
expect 1 "add refuses a key that is not 32 bytes of base64" keys add "AAAA"
expect 1 "add refuses a malformed key" keys add "${NEW%?}#"
expect 1 "add refuses a key listed already" keys add "$OLD"
expect 0 "add the successor key" keys add "$NEW"
[ "$(keys list | paste -sd' ' -)" = "$OLD $NEW" ] && ok "Signing.swift lists old, new" || bad "Signing.swift lists $(keys list | paste -sd' ' -)"
grep -qF "Keys = [\"$OLD\", \"$NEW\"];" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/ReleaseSigning.cs" && ok "ReleaseSigning.cs lists old, new" || bad "ReleaseSigning.cs: $(grep 'Keys =' "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/ReleaseSigning.cs")"
# an app built from the edited list (the default keys) is the transition app
swiftc "$C/app/Sources/Signing.swift" "$T/main.swift" -o "$T/app-n" 2>"$T/build.log" || { cat "$T/build.log"; exit 1; }
expect 0 "the app built from the edited Signing.swift accepts release N" "$T/app-n" default new "$N/list" "$N/sig" "$N/sigs"
expect 0 "the app built from the edited Signing.swift accepts release N+1" "$T/app-n" default new "$N1/list" "$N1/sig" "$N1/sigs"
grep -a -q -F "$NEW" "$T/app-n" && ok "that app's binary carries the new key (package.sh's APP_DIR check)" || bad "the new key is not in the built app"
cp -R "$C" "$T/root-n"   # the transition release's tree, for release-check below
expect 1 "retire refuses a key that is not listed" keys retire "$EVIL"
expect 0 "retire the old key" keys retire "$OLD"
[ "$(keys list)" = "$NEW" ] && ok "Signing.swift lists new only" || bad "Signing.swift lists $(keys list | paste -sd' ' -)"
expect 1 "retire refuses the last key" keys retire "$NEW"
expect 0 "check after retiring" keys check
cp -R "$C" "$T/root-r"
sed -i '' "s#Keys = \[\"$NEW\"\];#Keys = [\"$OLD\"];#" "$C/windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Release/ReleaseSigning.cs"
expect 1 "check fails when the Windows app's list differs" keys check
expect 1 "add refuses to edit lists that differ" keys add "$EVIL"

echo "== release-keys.sh release-check (release.sh's signature checks)"
rc() { local root=$1; shift; KEYS_ROOT=$root SIGNING=$SIGN bash "$R/release/release-keys.sh" release-check "$@"; }
expect 0 "release N: .sig by the old key, .sigs by both, the app adds the new key" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$N/sig" "$N/sigs" "$OLD"
cp "$N1/sig" "$T/sig-new"
expect 1 "release N with its .sig by the new key: installed apps would refuse it" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$N1/sig" "$N/sigs" "$OLD"
"$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/new.key" "$N/list" && mv "$N/list.sig" "$T/sig-n-new"
expect 1 "... the same refusal for a .sig by the new key of release N's own list" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$T/sig-n-new" "$N/sigs" "$OLD"
KEY_RESET=1 expect 0 "... let through with KEY_RESET=1 (a lost or exposed key), as a warning" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$T/sig-n-new" "$N/sigs" "$OLD"
grep -q '^  warn  .*KEY_RESET=1' "$T/last.out" && ok "KEY_RESET=1 warns" || bad "no KEY_RESET warning"
: > "$T/sigs-old"; "$SIGN" sign "$T/keys/old.key" "$N/list" "$T/sigs-old"
expect 1 "release N whose .sigs lacks the new key's line" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$N/sig" "$T/sigs-old" "$OLD"
cat "$N/sigs" "$E/sigs" > "$T/sigs-evil"
expect 1 "release N whose .sigs has a line by an unknown key" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$N/sig" "$T/sigs-evil" "$OLD"
expect 0 "release N without .sigs passes (a warning: the new key is not tried)" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$N/sig" "" "$OLD"
grep -q '^  warn  .*no .sha256.sigs' "$T/last.out" && ok "... and warns" || bad "no warning for the missing .sigs"
expect 0 "release N+1: .sig by the new key, the previous app knows both" rc "$T/root-n" "$N1/list" "$N1/sig" "" "$OLD $NEW"
expect 1 "release N+1 signed by the new key while the previous app knows only the old one" rc "$T/root-n" "$N1/list" "$N1/sig" "" "$OLD"
expect 0 "the retiring release: app [new], previous app [old,new], .sig by the new key" rc "$T/root-r" "$N1/list" "$N1/sig" "" "$OLD $NEW"
expect 1 "the retiring release signed by the old key: its own app refuses it" rc "$T/root-r" "$N/list" "$N/sig" "" "$OLD $NEW"
expect 1 "a release without a .sig" rc "$T/root-n" "$N/list" "$T/none" "" "$OLD"
expect 1 "the apps' lists differ" rc "$C" "$N1/list" "$N1/sig" "" "$NEW"
expect 1 "a changed list" rc "$T/root-n" "$X/list" "$X/sig" "$X/sigs" "$OLD"

echo "== package.sh's key checks (before any input is read)"
pkg() { local root=$1; shift; env KEYS_ROOT="$root" WINAPP_SKIP=1 PROBE_SKIP=1 "$@" bash "$R/release/package.sh" 9.0.0 "$T/no-tahoe" "$T/no-sequoia" "$T/pkg-out"; }
expect 1 "SIGN_KEY not in the app's list is refused" pkg "$T/root-n" SIGN_KEY="$T/keys/evil.key"
grep -q "is not in app/Sources/Signing.swift" "$T/last.out" && ok "... with the reason" || bad "... reason: $(tail -1 "$T/last.out")"
expect 1 "SIGN_KEY_NEXT not in the app's list is refused" pkg "$T/root-n" SIGN_KEY="$T/keys/old.key" SIGN_KEY_NEXT="$T/keys/evil.key"
grep -q "is not in app/Sources/Signing.swift" "$T/last.out" && ok "... with the reason" || bad "... reason: $(tail -1 "$T/last.out")"
expect 1 "SIGN_KEY_NEXT without SIGN_KEY is refused" pkg "$T/root-n" SIGN_KEY_NEXT="$T/keys/new.key"
expect 1 "SIGN_KEY_NEXT the same key as SIGN_KEY is refused" pkg "$T/root-n" SIGN_KEY="$T/keys/old.key" SIGN_KEY_NEXT="$T/keys/old.key"
grep -q "same key" "$T/last.out" && ok "... with the reason" || bad "... reason: $(tail -1 "$T/last.out")"
expect 1 "keys that differ between the apps are refused" pkg "$C" SIGN_KEY="$T/keys/new.key"
grep -q "release keys differ" "$T/last.out" && ok "... with the reason" || bad "... reason: $(tail -1 "$T/last.out")"
[ ! -e "$T/pkg-out" ] && ok "a refused key stops package.sh before it makes OUT_DIR" || bad "package.sh made $T/pkg-out"
expect 1 "old + new keys in both lists pass the key checks (then stop at the missing inputs)" pkg "$T/root-n" SIGN_KEY="$T/keys/old.key" SIGN_KEY_NEXT="$T/keys/new.key"
grep -q "missing in the Tahoe input" "$T/last.out" && ok "... past the key checks" || bad "... stopped at: $(tail -1 "$T/last.out")"

echo "== $pass passed, $fail failed"
[ $fail = 0 ]

FILE: release/templates/hidpi.sh

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# hidpi.sh: HiDPI modes ("Larger Text ... More Space" in System Settings > Displays) for the monitor on the Arc B580.
# Needs IntelXeFB from release 0.1.3 on. Changes take effect after a restart.
#
#   ./hidpi.sh              what is set now (read-only)
#   ./hidpi.sh --status     the same as key=value lines (for IntelXe Manager)
#   sudo ./hidpi.sh --on    turns them on: NVRAM intelxefb-hidpi=1 (the framebuffer offers scaled modes, scaled on the
#                           GPU), a display override with HiDPI sizes for the connected monitor, and WindowServer's
#                           DisplayResolutionEnabled; restart afterwards
#   sudo ./hidpi.sh --off   takes back what --on wrote; restart afterwards
#
# The override goes to /Library/Displays/Contents/Resources/Overrides/DisplayVendorID-<vid>/DisplayProductID-<pid>, the
# place and format other HiDPI tools use (one-key-hidpi): scale-resolutions entries of twice each "looks like" size. An
# override this script did not write is left alone (--on stops; remove it yourself or keep using it).
set -euo pipefail
export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:$PATH   # ioreg, nvram and plutil wherever this is started from
OVR=/Library/Displays/Contents/Resources/Overrides
WS=/Library/Preferences/com.apple.windowserver
BK="/Library/Application Support/intel-gpu-macos-driver"
MARK=IntelXeHiDPI                      # a key in the override: written by this script
MAXW=4096 MAXH=2304                    # the largest scaled size IntelXeFB accepts (its IOFBScalerInfo)

display_ids() { # vid pid (decimal) of the connected monitor
    ioreg -lw0 -r -c IODisplayConnect 2>/dev/null | awk -F' = ' '/"DisplayVendorID"/{v=$2} /"DisplayProductID"/{p=$2} END{if (v != "" && p != "") print v, p}'
}
native_size() { # WxH of the panel: the first size in IntelXeFB's mode list
    ioreg -lw0 -r -c IntelXeFramebuffer 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"IntelXeFBModes" = "\([0-9]*x[0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}
fb_supports() { # the installed IntelXeFB knows intelxefb-hidpi
    grep -qa "intelxefb-hidpi" /Library/Extensions/IntelXeFB.kext/Contents/MacOS/IntelXeFB 2>/dev/null
}
ovr_path() { printf '%s/DisplayVendorID-%x/DisplayProductID-%x' "$OVR" "$1" "$2"; }

status() {
    local ids vid="" pid="" f nv ws fbp
    ids=$(display_ids)
    if [ -n "$ids" ]; then read -r vid pid <<<"$ids"; fi   # an if: a failed && list ends the script under bash 3.2's set -e
    nv=$(nvram intelxefb-hidpi 2>/dev/null | cut -f2 || true); [ "$nv" = 1 ] || nv=0   # unset: nvram fails
    ws=$(defaults read "$WS" DisplayResolutionEnabled 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    fbp=$(ioreg -lw0 -r -c IntelXeFramebuffer 2>/dev/null | grep -c '"IOFBScalerInfo"' || true)
    local ovr=none
    if [ -n "$vid" ]; then
        f=$(ovr_path "$vid" "$pid")
        if [ -f "$f" ]; then
            if /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :$MARK" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ovr=ours; else ovr=other; fi
        fi
    fi
    echo "hidpi_supported=$(fb_supports && echo 1 || echo 0)"
    echo "hidpi_nvram=$nv"
    echo "hidpi_override=$ovr"
    echo "hidpi_windowserver=$ws"
    echo "hidpi_active=$([ "$fbp" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && echo 1 || echo 0)"
    echo "display=${vid:+$(printf '%04x:%04x' "$vid" "$pid")}"
    echo "native=$(native_size)"
}

human() {
    local s; s=$(status)
    get() { sed -n "s/^$1=//p" <<<"$s"; }
    echo "== HiDPI modes for the Arc B580"
    echo "  framebuffer support (0.1.3+)   $( [ "$(get hidpi_supported)" = 1 ] && echo yes || echo 'no: install release 0.1.3 or later first')"
    echo "  monitor                        $(get display) $(get native)"
    echo "  NVRAM intelxefb-hidpi          $(get hidpi_nvram)"
    echo "  display override               $(get hidpi_override)"
    echo "  DisplayResolutionEnabled       $(get hidpi_windowserver)"
    echo "  in effect this boot            $( [ "$(get hidpi_active)" = 1 ] && echo yes || echo no)"
}

entry() { # entry W H [flags setflags]: base64 of the big-endian words
    local hex; hex=$(printf '%08x%08x' "$1" "$2"); shift 2
    for x in "$@"; do hex+=$(printf '%08x' "$x"); done
    printf '%s' "$hex" | xxd -r -p | base64
}

on() {
    [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "--on needs root: sudo $0 --on"; exit 1; }
    fb_supports || { echo "IntelXeFB does not support HiDPI modes yet: install release 0.1.3 or later first"; exit 1; }
    local ids vid pid size w h f tmp
    ids=$(display_ids); [ -n "$ids" ] || { echo "no monitor found (IODisplayConnect)"; exit 1; }
    read -r vid pid <<<"$ids"
    size=$(native_size); [ -n "$size" ] || { echo "IntelXeFB's panel size not found"; exit 1; }
    w=${size%x*} h=${size#*x}
    f=$(ovr_path "$vid" "$pid")
    if [ -f "$f" ] && ! /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :$MARK" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "$f exists and was not written by this script: left as it is (remove it first to use this one)"; exit 1
    fi
    # "looks like" sizes: the panel times 4/5, 3/4, 2/3, 5/8 and 1/2 (scale 125, 133, 150, 160, 200 %), even, whose
    # doubles IntelXeFB can take (2560x1440: 2048x1152, 1920x1080, 1706x960, 1600x900, 1280x720)
    local looks=() fx
    for fx in 4/5 3/4 2/3 5/8 1/2; do
        local lw=$(( (w * ${fx%/*} / ${fx#*/}) & ~1 )) lh=$(( (h * ${fx%/*} / ${fx#*/}) & ~1 ))
        if [ $((2 * lw)) -le $MAXW ] && [ $((2 * lh)) -le $MAXH ]; then looks+=("$lw $lh"); fi
    done
    [ ${#looks[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "no HiDPI size fits for a ${size} panel (IntelXeFB takes up to ${MAXW}x${MAXH})"; exit 1; }
    tmp=$(mktemp -t hidpi)
    plutil -create xml1 "$tmp"
    plutil -insert DisplayVendorID -integer "$vid" "$tmp"
    plutil -insert DisplayProductID -integer "$pid" "$tmp"
    plutil -insert "$MARK" -bool YES "$tmp"
    plutil -insert target-default-ppmm -float 10.0699301 "$tmp"
    plutil -insert scale-resolutions -array "$tmp"
    # each size four ways, as one-key-hidpi writes them (with fewer kinds macOS did not offer the HiDPI modes, B580 test)
    local n=0 l lw lh
    for l in "${looks[@]}"; do read -r lw lh <<<"$l"; plutil -insert "scale-resolutions.$n" -data "$(entry $((2*lw)) $((2*lh)))" "$tmp"; n=$((n+1)); done
    for l in "${looks[@]}"; do read -r lw lh <<<"$l"; plutil -insert "scale-resolutions.$n" -data "$(entry $((2*lw)) $((2*lh)) 1 $((0x00200000)))" "$tmp"; n=$((n+1)); done
    for l in "${looks[@]}"; do read -r lw lh <<<"$l"; plutil -insert "scale-resolutions.$n" -data "$(entry $((2*lw)) $((2*lh)) 1)" "$tmp"; n=$((n+1)); done
    for l in "${looks[@]}"; do read -r lw lh <<<"$l"; plutil -insert "scale-resolutions.$n" -data "$(entry $((2*lw)) $((2*lh)) 9 $((0x00A00000)))" "$tmp"; n=$((n+1)); done
    plutil -lint "$tmp" >/dev/null
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$f")" "$BK"
    install -o root -g wheel -m 644 "$tmp" "$f"; rm -f "$tmp"
    echo "  ok    $f (${#looks[@]} sizes: $(printf '%s ' "${looks[@]/ /x}"))"
    # remember whether DisplayResolutionEnabled was already on, so --off leaves it as it found it
    if [ ! -f "$BK/hidpi-ws-was-set" ]; then
        defaults read "$WS" DisplayResolutionEnabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo 1 > "$BK/hidpi-ws-was-set" || echo 0 > "$BK/hidpi-ws-was-set"
    fi
    defaults write "$WS" DisplayResolutionEnabled -bool YES
    echo "  ok    DisplayResolutionEnabled"
    nvram intelxefb-hidpi=1
    echo "  ok    NVRAM intelxefb-hidpi=1"
    echo "== restart; then choose a size in System Settings > Displays"
}

off() {
    [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "--off needs root: sudo $0 --off"; exit 1; }
    local ids vid pid f
    ids=$(display_ids)
    if [ -n "$ids" ]; then
        read -r vid pid <<<"$ids"; f=$(ovr_path "$vid" "$pid")
        if [ -f "$f" ] && /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :$MARK" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then rm -f "$f"; echo "  ok    removed $f"
        elif [ -f "$f" ]; then echo "  keep  $f (not written by this script)"; fi
    fi
    if [ -f "$BK/hidpi-ws-was-set" ]; then
        [ "$(cat "$BK/hidpi-ws-was-set")" = 1 ] || { defaults delete "$WS" DisplayResolutionEnabled 2>/dev/null || true; echo "  ok    DisplayResolutionEnabled removed"; }
        rm -f "$BK/hidpi-ws-was-set"
    fi
    nvram intelxefb-hidpi=0   # nvram -d does not delete on some macOS 26 machines; 0 reads as off
    echo "  ok    NVRAM intelxefb-hidpi=0"
    echo "== restart; a HiDPI size chosen before goes back to the panel's own"
}

case "${1:-}" in
    "") human ;;
    --status) status ;;
    --on) on ;;
    --off) off ;;
    *) sed -n '3,15p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
esac

FILE: tools/rename-intelxe.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""rename-intelxe.py: rename the driver stack from "B580" to "IntelXe" in a source tree.

  rename-intelxe.py [--dry-run] [--diff] [--review] [--no-default-excludes] [--exclude GLOB]... [--only GLOB]... TREE

The driver is for Intel Xe GPUs; "B580" stays only where it means the device (the Arc B580 card, its PCI ID 8086:e20b,
measurements, docs/devices/b580.md, the Metal device name "Intel Arc B580 Graphics"). The mapping (2026-11-05):

  B580.kext, org.hackintosh.B580            IntelXe.kext, io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXe
  B580FB.kext, org.hackintosh.B580FB        IntelXeFB.kext, io.github.yusufklncc.IntelXeFB
  class B580 / B580IntelFramebuffer         IntelXe / IntelXeFramebuffer
  B580Client, B580FB*, B580Ready, ...       IntelXeClient, IntelXeFB*, IntelXeReady, ...   (CamelCase: B580 -> IntelXe)
  B580_*, DRM_IOCTL_B580_*, NVMTL_B580_*    INTELXE_*, DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_*, NVMTL_INTELXE_*  (ALL_CAPS: B580 -> INTELXE)
  b580_*, debug.b580.*, debug.b580fb_*,     intelxe_*, debug.intelxe.*, debug.intelxefb_*,
    /dev/b580obj, libb580venc, b580-guard     /dev/intelxeobj, libintelxevenc, intelxe-guard   (lowercase: b580 -> intelxe)
  boot-args b580surfvram, -b580nofb,        intelxe_surfvram, -intelxe_nofb, -intelxefb_novrr, intelxefb_vrr, ...
    -b580fbnovrr, b580fbvrr, ...              (BOOT_ARGS below: an underscore after the prefix)
  org.b580.*, org.hackintosh.b580*          io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.*, io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe*
  file and directory names                  the same rules (kernel/B580 -> kernel/IntelXe, b580_drm.h -> intelxe_drm.h, ...)

Bare "B580" is renamed where it names the kext, the class or a file: in C/C++/Objective-C code (outside comments and
strings), the string literals "B580" and "B580: ...", and in prose when followed by .kext/.h/.cpp/:: or a path
separator, as a path component, after IOServiceOpen( / IOServiceMatching(, "class B580", "B580 service", and in
hyphenated names (Info-NMX-B580.plist). Everywhere else bare "B580" (and bare lowercase "b580" outside code and
hyphenated names) is left alone and listed by --review: there it usually means the card, and a person decides.

Never touched: "Arc B580" and the Metal device name, hex constants (0xb5800001ull, ioctl numbers stay), the fourcc
'B580' (an IOServiceOpen type, ABI), references to files outside this tree (src/b580..., ~/b580, tools/b580,
docs/reports/b580-*, patches/b580/, build-b580-* directories), historical file names (mesa/patches/*-B580-*.patch), and
any line carrying the marker "intelxe-rename: keep" (the old boot-arg names of the compatibility tables).

Default excludes (history and data that must not change; --no-default-excludes drops them): mesa/patches/,
mesa/xe2-venc/, mesa/working-tree/, data/cts/, data/video.json, data/history.json, docs/parity/HISTORY.md, and the
*.diff files that record a tree against its upstream: mesa/*.diff is regenerated from the renamed Mesa tree, and
nullmoth/b580-changes-vs-6e37546.diff is a record of that time and keeps its names; release/install.sh and
release/README-INSTALL.md name the earlier kexts and boot-args on purpose (the upgrade path), as do the EFI rules' test
vectors (release/efi-rules-vectors.json: JSON has no place for the marker). docs/devices/b580.md keeps its name. Binary files are skipped.

The script is idempotent: a second run changes nothing. --dry-run lists what would change (files, counts, renames)
and changes nothing; --diff also prints the diffs; --review lists the bare B580/b580 that remain, for a person.
"""
import argparse, difflib, fnmatch, os, re, subprocess, sys

KEEP_MARK = 'intelxe-rename: keep'
PREFIX = 'io.github.yusufklncc'

# Boot-arg names (the token without its leading '-'): old -> new.
BOOT_ARGS = {
    # IntelXe.kext
    'b580off': 'intelxe_off', 'b580nohugepages': 'intelxe_nohugepages', 'b580novideo': 'intelxe_novideo',
    'b580nousm': 'intelxe_nousm', 'b580lrcsys': 'intelxe_lrcsys', 'b580vcssingle': 'intelxe_vcssingle',
    'b580nowhitelist': 'intelxe_nowhitelist', 'b580surfvram': 'intelxe_surfvram', 'b580svwsfull': 'intelxe_svwsfull',
    'b580fds': 'intelxe_fds', 'b580lazy': 'intelxe_lazy', 'b580nometal': 'intelxe_nometal',
    # IntelXeFB.kext (and -b580noaccel, also read by NMXAccel and NMXAGDC)
    'b580nofb': 'intelxe_nofb', 'b580noaccel': 'intelxe_noaccel', 'b580fboff': 'intelxefb_off',
    'b580fbnoedidfix': 'intelxefb_noedidfix', 'b580fbnoscale': 'intelxefb_noscale', 'b580fbnorates': 'intelxefb_norates',
    'b580fbedidonly': 'intelxefb_edidonly', 'b580fbnogamma': 'intelxefb_nogamma', 'b580fbnovrr': 'intelxefb_novrr',
    'b580fbnohwcursor': 'intelxefb_nohwcursor', 'b580fbvrr': 'intelxefb_vrr', 'b580fbvrrmodes': 'intelxefb_vrrmodes',
    'b580fbnoirq': 'intelxefb_noirq',
}

# Whole phrases, applied first (their output no longer contains b580/B580).
PHRASES = [
    (re.compile(r'\borg\.hackintosh\.B580FB\b'), PREFIX + '.IntelXeFB'),
    (re.compile(r'\borg\.hackintosh\.B580\b'), PREFIX + '.IntelXe'),
    (re.compile(r'\borg\.hackintosh\.b580fb\b'), PREFIX + '.intelxefb'),
    (re.compile(r'\borg\.hackintosh\.b580\.'), PREFIX + '.intelxe.'),
    (re.compile(r'\borg\.b580\.'), PREFIX + '.intelxe.'),
    (re.compile(r'B580IntelFramebuffer'), 'IntelXeFramebuffer'),
    (re.compile(r'\bb580-prod9\.diff\b'), 'intelxe.diff'),
]

# Spans never changed (the card, ABI numbers, files outside the tree, history).
PROTECT = [re.compile(p) for p in (
    r'\b(?:Intel )?Arc[ -]B580\b', r'\bARC B580\b', r'\barc-b580\b',
    r'\b[\w./-]*devices/b580\.md\b', r'\bb580\.md\b', r'#[\w-]*b580[\w-]*', r'\bwhat-works-on-the-b580\b',
    r'\b0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+[uUlL]*\b', r'\b(?![bB]580[a-fA-F]*\b)[0-9a-fA-F]{7,}\b',   # hashes, not b580dec
    r"'B580'",
    r'(?:~|\$HOME|\$\{HOME\})/b580\b',
    r'\bsrc/b580[\w./-]*', r'\bsrc/nullmoth/build-b580[\w.-]*', r'\bbuild-b580-[\w.-]+', r'\btools/b580\b[\w./-]*',
    r'\bpatches/b580/[\w./-]*', r'\bdocs/reports/[\w./-]*', r'\bdocs/research/[\w./-]*', r'\bb5/[\w./-]*',
    r'\bb580-[\w-]*20\d{6}[\w-]*\.md\b',
    r'\bb580-(?:tile4\w*|rb\d\w*|probe|surfvram-vs-pv\.patch|webkit-[\w-]+\.patch|xeprobe-v1\.patch|driver-project|'
    r'backups|surfvram\b(?!/))',
    r'<b580-tile4\w*>',
    r'\bmesa/patches/[\w./-]*', r'\bxe2-venc/[\w./-]*', r'\b\d{4}-[\w.-]*B580[\w.-]*\.patch\b',
    r'\bb580-changes-vs-\w+\.diff\b',
)]

CLIKE = {'.c', '.h', '.cpp', '.cc', '.hpp', '.m', '.mm', '.inc', '.metal', '.comp'}
DEFAULT_EXCLUDES = ['mesa/patches/*', 'mesa/xe2-venc/*', 'mesa/working-tree/*', 'data/cts/*', 'data/video.json',
                    'data/history.json', 'docs/parity/HISTORY.md', '*-changes-vs-*.diff', 'mesa/*.diff',
                    'release/install.sh', 'release/README-INSTALL.md', 'tools/rename-intelxe.py', '.git/*',
                    'release/efi-rules-vectors.json']   # its vectors name the earlier B580.kext entry on purpose (JSON: no marker)
NO_RENAME = ['docs/devices/b580.md', 'mesa/patches/*', 'mesa/xe2-venc/*', 'mesa/working-tree/*', 'mesa/*.diff',
             '*-changes-vs-*.diff']

TOKEN = re.compile(r'\b\w*(?:B580|b580)\w*')


def case_map(tok):
    """A compound token (anything but bare B580/b580/B580FB and the boot-args)."""
    if tok.lower() in BOOT_ARGS:
        return BOOT_ARGS[tok.lower()]
    if not re.search(r'[a-z]', tok):                       # ALL_CAPS (and digits/underscores)
        return tok.replace('B580', 'INTELXE')
    return tok.replace('B580', 'IntelXe').replace('b580', 'intelxe')


def bare_upper_prose(s, a, b):
    """Bare B580 at s[a:b] outside code: renamed only where it names the kext, class, service or a file."""
    after, before = s[b:b + 40], s[max(0, a - 24):a]
    if re.match(r'\.(?:kext|h|cpp)\b|::|/[a-z]| service\b| kext\b', after):
        return 'IntelXe'
    # the kext's own threads, locks and allocators (its copy engine, mapper or VRAM are the card's)
    if re.match(r"'s (?:own )?(?:thread|threads|interrupt thread|resume|resume thread|will-suspend|work loop|"
                r"allocator|allocators|registry|records|own objects|power events)\b", after):
        return 'IntelXe'
    if re.search(r'(?:/|[A-Za-z0-9]-|IOServiceOpen\(|IOServiceMatching\(\\?"?|class )$', before):
        return 'IntelXe'
    return None


def bare_lower_prose(s, a, b):
    """Bare b580 outside code: hyphenated names (b580-guard, build-b580.sh) and debug.b580."""
    after, before = s[b:b + 2], s[max(0, a - 6):a]
    if after[:1] == '-' and re.match(r'-\w', after) or before.endswith('-') and re.search(r'\w-$', before):
        return 'intelxe'
    if before.endswith('debug.'):
        return 'intelxe'
    return None


def sub_tokens(seg, ctx, review):
    """Rename the tokens of one segment. ctx: code, string, comment, prose, path."""
    def rep(m):
        tok, a, b = m.group(0), m.start(), m.end()
        if tok == 'B580':
            if ctx in ('code', 'path'):
                return 'IntelXe'
            if ctx == 'string' and a == 1 and (seg == '"B580"' or seg.startswith('"B580: ')):
                return 'IntelXe'                            # IOServiceMatching("B580"), the log prefix "B580: "
            r = bare_upper_prose(seg, a, b)
            if r is None:
                review.append(tok)
                return tok
            return r
        if tok == 'b580':
            if ctx in ('code', 'path'):
                return 'intelxe'
            r = bare_lower_prose(seg, a, b)
            if r is None:
                review.append(tok)
                return tok
            return r
        if tok == 'B580FB':
            return 'IntelXeFB'
        return case_map(tok)
    return TOKEN.sub(rep, seg)


def protect(text):
    spans = []
    for rx in PROTECT:
        for m in rx.finditer(text):
            spans.append((m.start(), m.end()))
    spans.sort()
    merged = []
    for a, b in spans:
        if merged and a <= merged[-1][1]:
            merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], max(b, merged[-1][1]))
        else:
            merged.append((a, b))
    keep, out, pos = [], [], 0
    for a, b in merged:
        out.append(text[pos:a]); out.append('\x01%d\x02' % len(keep)); keep.append(text[a:b]); pos = b
    out.append(text[pos:])
    return ''.join(out), keep


def unprotect(text, keep):
    return re.sub(r'\x01(\d+)\x02', lambda m: keep[int(m.group(1))], text)


def lex_c(text):
    """Split C-family text into (kind, segment): code, comment, string (with its quotes), char (with its quotes)."""
    out, i, n, start, kind = [], 0, len(text), 0, 'code'
    def push(k, a, b):
        if b > a:
            out.append((k, text[a:b]))
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if c == '/' and text.startswith('//', i):
            j = text.find('\n', i); j = n if j < 0 else j
            push('code', start, i); push('comment', i, j); i = start = j; continue
        if c == '/' and text.startswith('/*', i):
            j = text.find('*/', i + 2); j = n if j < 0 else j + 2
            push('code', start, i); push('comment', i, j); i = start = j; continue
        if c == '"' or (c == "'" and not (i > 0 and (text[i - 1].isalnum()))):
            q, j = c, i + 1
            while j < n and text[j] != q and text[j] != '\n':
                j += 2 if text[j] == '\\' else 1
            j = min(j + 1, n)
            push('code', start, i); push('string' if q == '"' else 'char', i, j); i = start = j; continue
        i += 1
    push('code', start, n)
    return out


def transform_text(text, path, review):
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    lines = text.split('\n')
    # lines with the keep marker are set aside whole
    held = {}
    for k, ln in enumerate(lines):
        if KEEP_MARK in ln:
            held[k] = ln; lines[k] = '\x03%d\x04' % k
    text = '\n'.join(lines)
    for rx, new in PHRASES:
        text = rx.sub(new, text)
    text, keep = protect(text)
    if ext in CLIKE:
        parts = []
        for kind, seg in lex_c(text):
            if kind == 'char':
                parts.append(seg)
            elif kind == 'string':
                parts.append(sub_tokens(seg, 'string', review))
            else:
                parts.append(sub_tokens(seg, 'code' if kind == 'code' else 'comment', review))
        text = ''.join(parts)
    else:
        text = sub_tokens(text, 'prose', review)
    text = unprotect(text, keep)
    text = re.sub(r'\x03(\d+)\x04', lambda m: held[int(m.group(1))], text)
    return text


def new_name(name):
    """A file or directory name."""
    if name in ('B580', 'b580'):
        return 'IntelXe' if name == 'B580' else 'intelxe'
    for rx, new in PHRASES:
        name = rx.sub(new, name)
    text, keep = protect(name)
    return unprotect(sub_tokens(text, 'path', []), keep)


def matches(rel, globs):
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(rel, g) or fnmatch.fnmatch(rel + '/', g) for g in globs)


def is_text(path):
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        head = f.read(8192)
    return b'\0' not in head


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('tree')
    ap.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true', help='list the changes, change nothing')
    ap.add_argument('--diff', action='store_true', help='with --dry-run: print the content diffs')
    ap.add_argument('--review', action='store_true', help='list the bare B580/b580 left for a person to decide')
    ap.add_argument('--no-default-excludes', action='store_true')
    ap.add_argument('--exclude', action='append', default=[], help='glob relative to TREE (repeatable)')
    ap.add_argument('--only', action='append', default=[], help='touch only these paths (globs relative to TREE, '
                    'repeatable): e.g. the files a patch series changes in an upstream tree such as Mesa')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    root = os.path.abspath(a.tree)
    excl = ([] if a.no_default_excludes else DEFAULT_EXCLUDES) + a.exclude
    norename = ([] if a.no_default_excludes else NO_RENAME) + a.exclude
    files, dirs = [], []
    for d, dn, fn in os.walk(root):
        dn[:] = [x for x in dn if x != '.git']
        for x in dn:
            dirs.append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(d, x), root))
        for x in fn:
            files.append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(d, x), root))
    changed = 0
    review = []
    for rel in sorted(files):
        p = os.path.join(root, rel)
        if os.path.islink(p) or matches(rel, excl) or (a.only and not matches(rel, a.only)) or not is_text(p):
            continue
        try:
            old = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read()
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        rv = []
        new = transform_text(old, rel, rv)
        if a.review and rv:
            for k, ln in enumerate(new.split('\n'), 1):
                if re.search(r'\b[Bb]580\b', ln):
                    s, keep = protect(ln)
                    if re.search(r'\b[Bb]580\b', s):
                        review.append('%s:%d: %s' % (rel, k, ln.strip()[:200]))
        if new != old:
            changed += 1
            n = sum(1 for x, y in zip(old.split('\n'), new.split('\n')) if x != y)
            print('%s %s (%d line%s)' % ('would change' if a.dry_run else 'changed', rel, n, '' if n == 1 else 's'))
            if a.dry_run and a.diff:
                sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(old.splitlines(True), new.splitlines(True), 'a/' + rel, 'b/' + rel))
            if not a.dry_run:
                with open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    f.write(new)
    # renames, deepest first so that parents move last
    renames = []
    for rel in sorted(files + dirs, key=lambda r: -r.count('/')):
        if matches(rel, norename) or rel.startswith('.git') or (a.only and not matches(rel, a.only)):
            continue
        base = os.path.basename(rel)
        nb = new_name(base)
        if nb != base:
            renames.append((rel, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(rel), nb)))
    git = os.path.isdir(os.path.join(root, '.git'))
    for old, new in renames:
        print('%s %s -> %s' % ('would rename' if a.dry_run else 'renamed', old, new))
        if a.dry_run:
            continue
        tracked = git and subprocess.run(['git', '-C', root, 'ls-files', '--error-unmatch', old], capture_output=True).returncode == 0
        if tracked:
            subprocess.run(['git', '-C', root, 'mv', old, new], check=True)
        else:
            os.rename(os.path.join(root, old), os.path.join(root, new))
    if a.review:
        print('== bare B580/b580 left (%d lines): the card, or a name a person must rename' % len(review))
        for r in review:
            print(r)
    print('== %d file(s) %s, %d rename(s)' % (changed, 'to change' if a.dry_run else 'changed', len(renames)), file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""site-guide.py: keeps the project site's install guide (site/guide/*.html) true to the install guide of the release
packages (release/templates/README-INSTALL.md and .tr.md).

The site guide is written by hand, in English and Turkish on every page, ordered by path (getting started, installation,
troubleshooting, reference) rather than by the packages' four stages. This tool does not write it; it
checks that it has not drifted away from what the packages say:

    python3 tools/site-guide.py --check     exit 1 on drift (release/release.sh runs this before a release)
    python3 tools/site-guide.py --check --next 0.1.5
                                            the same against the working tree's templates filled for 0.1.5: a site
                                            prepared for the next release, checked before VERSION is bumped
    python3 tools/site-guide.py --tokens    print what --check looks for, per language
    python3 tools/site-guide.py --index     write site/guide/search-index.js, the guide's search index

What --check compares. From each template (English against the site's English text, Turkish against its Turkish
text; text outside any lang="..." element counts for both):
  - every line of every fenced code block (a trailing "  # comment" is dropped: comments may be worded differently);
  - every inline code span (`...`): commands, file, kext and path names, config.plist keys, boot-args, sysctls;
  - boot-args and NVRAM settings written in prose without backticks (name_with_underscore=value, -name_with_underscore);
  - version strings with three parts (26.7.1, 0.1.3, 1.7.2).
Each must appear, character for character after collapsing white space, somewhere in the site guide. It also checks
that every guide page carries the same sidebar, and that site/guide/search-index.js is what --index would write.

The templates are read as released: from the tag vVERSION (git show) when it exists, so work on the next release does
not count as drift; before the tag exists (release.sh, preparing a release) from the working tree. They are filled as
release/package.sh fills them for the Tahoe package (the site's main path). --next VERSION reads them from the
working tree and fills them for that version, as release.sh will see them once VERSION says it. No dependencies.
"""
import html
import html.parser
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
GUIDE = os.path.join(ROOT, "site", "guide")
INDEX = os.path.join(GUIDE, "search-index.js")

# release/package.sh fill() for the Tahoe package
FILL = {
    "@MACOS@": "macOS 26 Tahoe", "@MAJOR@": "26", "@CODENAME@": "tahoe",
    "@TESTED@": "Experimental. Tested on one machine only: an Arc B580 in a Z790 desktop, macOS 26.7.1, OpenCore.",
    "@TESTED_TR@": "Deneysel bir sürüm. Yalnızca tek makinede denendi: Z790 masaüstü, Arc B580, macOS 26.7.1, OpenCore.",
}
VOID = {"area", "base", "br", "col", "embed", "hr", "img", "input", "link", "meta", "source", "track", "wbr"}
BLOCK = {"p", "li", "div", "pre", "td", "th", "tr", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6", "section", "br", "dt", "dd",
         "table", "ul", "ol", "dl", "figcaption", "summary", "details", "nav", "article", "aside", "header", "footer"}


def norm(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


NEXT = None   # --next VERSION: the working tree's templates for that version


def template_text(rel, version):
    """release/templates/<rel> as released (tag vVERSION) when the tag exists, else from the working tree."""
    r = None if NEXT else subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "show", "v%s:release/templates/%s" % (version, rel)],
                                         capture_output=True)
    if r is not None and r.returncode == 0:
        return r.stdout.decode("utf-8"), "v" + version
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "release", "templates", rel), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return fh.read(), "the working tree"


def filled(rel, version):
    text, source = template_text(rel, version)
    text = text.replace("@VER@", version)
    for k, v in FILL.items():
        text = text.replace(k, v)
    left = sorted(set(re.findall(r"@[A-Z_]+@", text)))
    if left:
        sys.exit("%s: unfilled %s" % (rel, ", ".join(left)))
    return text, source


def tokens(text):
    """[(token, section heading)] of one template, in order, each token once."""
    out, seen, section, fence = [], set(), "(intro)", None

    def add(tok):
        tok = norm(tok.replace("\\|", "|"))
        if len(tok) > 1 and tok not in seen:
            seen.add(tok)
            out.append((tok, section))
    para = []

    def flush():
        prose = " ".join(para)   # a paragraph at a time: a code span may run over a line break
        del para[:]
        for m in re.finditer(r"`([^`]+)`", prose):
            add(m.group(1))
        bare = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", " ", prose)
        bare = re.sub(r"\]\([^)]*\)", "]", bare)   # link targets are not text
        for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![\w.-])(-?[a-z][a-z0-9]*_[a-z0-9_]+(?:=[0-9A-Za-z]+)?)(?![\w-])", bare):
            add(m.group(1))
        for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![\w.])(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)(?![\w.])", bare):
            add(m.group(1))
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("```"):
            flush()
            fence = None if fence is not None else s
            continue
        if fence is not None:
            if not s:
                continue
            if s.startswith("#"):
                add(s.lstrip("# "))           # an example of output, as a comment
            else:
                add(re.sub(r"\s{2,}#.*$", "", s))
            continue
        if not s or s.startswith("#") or s.startswith("|"):
            flush()
        if line.startswith("## ") or line.startswith("### "):
            section = line.lstrip("# ").strip()
            continue
        if s.startswith("<"):                  # raw HTML (the screenshots): not text
            continue
        if s:
            para.append(s)
            if s.startswith("|"):
                flush()                       # a table row is a paragraph of its own
    flush()
    return out


class Text(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    """The text of a page, per language: elements under lang="en" / lang="tr" go to that language, the rest to both."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.stack, self.buf = [], {"en": [], "tr": []}

    def lang(self):
        for _, l in reversed(self.stack):
            if l:
                return l
        return None

    def gap(self):
        for b in self.buf.values():
            b.append(" ")

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag in BLOCK:
            self.gap()
        if tag in VOID:
            return
        a = dict(attrs)
        self.stack.append((tag, a.get("lang") if tag != "html" else None))

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in VOID:
            return
        for i in range(len(self.stack) - 1, -1, -1):
            if self.stack[i][0] == tag:
                del self.stack[i:]
                break
        if tag in BLOCK:
            self.gap()

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if any(t in ("script", "style", "title") for t, _ in self.stack):
            return
        l = self.lang()
        for k in ("en", "tr"):
            if l in (None, k):
                self.buf[k].append(data)


def page_files():
    return sorted(f for f in os.listdir(GUIDE) if f.endswith(".html"))


def site_text():
    out = {"en": [], "tr": []}
    for f in page_files():
        p = Text()
        with open(os.path.join(GUIDE, f), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            p.feed(fh.read())
        for k in out:
            out[k].append(norm("".join(p.buf[k])))
    return {k: " \n ".join(v) for k, v in out.items()}


def sidebar(f):
    with open(os.path.join(GUIDE, f), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        m = re.search(r'<nav class="doc-side".*?</nav>', fh.read(), re.S)
    # what differs from page to page: the current page's link and its group, the one <details> that is open
    return m.group(0).replace(' aria-current="page"', "").replace('<details class="doc-sec" open>',
                                                                   '<details class="doc-sec">') if m else None


def guide_pages():
    """The guide's pages in sidebar order: [(file, English title, Turkish title)]."""
    nav = sidebar("index.html") or ""
    return [(m.group(1), html.unescape(m.group(2)), html.unescape(m.group(3))) for m in
            re.finditer(r'<a href="([\w-]+\.html)"><span lang="en">(.*?)</span><span lang="tr">(.*?)</span>', nav)]


class Sections(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    """For the search index: the article's sections (<section id>), each with its heading and text per language;
    the text before the first section is the page's own entry (id ""). Navigation (.doc-pn, the stage bar and anything
    else marked .noindex), the eyebrow and the h1 are left out."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.in_article, self.stack, self.secs, self.cur = False, [], [], None

    def new(self, sid):
        self.cur = {"id": sid, "h": {"en": [], "tr": []}, "t": {"en": [], "tr": []}}
        self.secs.append(self.cur)

    def gap(self):
        if self.cur:
            for k in ("en", "tr"):
                self.cur["t"][k].append(" ")

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        a = dict(attrs)
        if tag == "article":
            self.in_article = True
            self.new("")
            return
        if not self.in_article:
            return
        if tag == "section" and a.get("id"):
            self.new(a["id"])
        if tag in BLOCK:
            self.gap()
        if tag not in VOID:
            self.stack.append((tag, a.get("lang"), a.get("class", "")))

    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag == "article":
            self.in_article = False
        if not self.in_article or tag in VOID:
            return
        for i in range(len(self.stack) - 1, -1, -1):
            if self.stack[i][0] == tag:
                del self.stack[i:]
                break
        if tag in BLOCK:
            self.gap()

    def handle_data(self, data):
        if not self.in_article or self.cur is None:
            return
        tags = [t for t, _, _ in self.stack]
        classes = " ".join(c for _, _, c in self.stack).split()
        if "h1" in tags or "doc-pn" in classes or "eyebrow" in classes or "noindex" in classes:
            return
        l = next((ll for _, ll, _ in reversed(self.stack) if ll), None)
        part = "h" if ("h2" in tags and self.cur["id"]) else "t"
        for k in ("en", "tr"):
            if l in (None, k):
                self.cur[part][k].append(data)


def build_index():
    pages = []
    for f, t_en, t_tr in guide_pages():
        p = Sections()
        with open(os.path.join(GUIDE, f), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            p.feed(fh.read())
        secs = []
        for s in p.secs:
            e = {"id": s["id"], "h": [norm("".join(s["h"]["en"])), norm("".join(s["h"]["tr"]))],
                 "t": [norm("".join(s["t"]["en"])), norm("".join(s["t"]["tr"]))]}
            if e["id"] or e["t"][0] or e["t"][1]:
                secs.append(e)
        pages.append({"f": f, "t": [t_en, t_tr], "s": secs})
    body = json.dumps({"v": 1, "pages": pages}, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return ("// The install guide's search index, written by tools/site-guide.py --index from site/guide/*.html. MIT.\n"
            "window.GUIDE_INDEX = " + body + ";\n")


def check(version):
    fails = 0
    text = site_text()
    for rel, lang in (("README-INSTALL.md", "en"), ("README-INSTALL.tr.md", "tr")):
        t, source = filled(rel, version)
        toks = tokens(t)
        missing = [(tok, sec) for tok, sec in toks if tok not in text[lang]]
        if missing:
            fails += len(missing)
            print("%s (%s): %d of %d not in the site guide's %s text:" % (rel, source, len(missing), len(toks),
                                                                          "English" if lang == "en" else "Turkish"))
            for tok, sec in missing:
                print("  [%s] %s" % (sec, tok))
        else:
            print("%s (%s): all %d found in the site guide's %s text" % (rel, source, len(toks),
                                                                         "English" if lang == "en" else "Turkish"))
    ref = sidebar("index.html")
    for f, _, _ in guide_pages():
        if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(GUIDE, f)):
            fails += 1
            print("the sidebar names %s, which does not exist" % f)
        elif sidebar(f) != ref:
            fails += 1
            print("%s: its sidebar differs from index.html's" % f)
    try:
        with open(INDEX, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            stale = fh.read() != build_index()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        stale = True
    if stale:
        fails += 1
        print("site/guide/search-index.js is stale: python3 tools/site-guide.py --index")
    return fails


def main():
    global NEXT
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION")) as fh:
        version = fh.read().strip()
    if "--next" in sys.argv:
        i = sys.argv.index("--next")
        if i + 1 >= len(sys.argv) or not re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$", sys.argv[i + 1]):
            sys.exit("--next takes a version, such as 0.1.5")
        NEXT = version = sys.argv[i + 1]
    if "--tokens" in sys.argv:
        for rel in ("README-INSTALL.md", "README-INSTALL.tr.md"):
            print("== " + rel)
            for tok, sec in tokens(filled(rel, version)[0]):
                print("[%s] %s" % (sec, tok))
        return
    if "--index" in sys.argv:
        with open(INDEX, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(build_index())
        print("wrote site/guide/search-index.js (%d pages)" % len(guide_pages()))
        return
    if "--check" in sys.argv:
        n = check(version)
        print("site/guide: %s" % ("no drift" if n == 0 else "%d problem(s)" % n))
        sys.exit(1 if n else 0)
    print(__doc__.strip())
    sys.exit(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""site-links.py: checks the project site's internal links (site/*.html and site/guide/*.html).

    python3 tools/site-links.py            list every broken link; exit 1 if any
    python3 tools/site-links.py --site DIR another copy of site/

For every href and src that is not external (http:, https:, mailto:, data:, javascript:), the file it names must exist
under site/, and its #fragment, when it has one, must be an id (or <a name>) in that file. A link to "#" alone or a
fragment only a script makes would be listed too. No dependencies.
"""
import html.parser
import os
import sys
import urllib.parse

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EXTERNAL = ("http:", "https:", "mailto:", "data:", "javascript:", "tel:")


class Page(html.parser.HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.ids, self.links = set(), []

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        a = dict(attrs)
        if a.get("id"):
            self.ids.add(a["id"])
        if tag == "a" and a.get("name"):
            self.ids.add(a["name"])
        for k in ("href", "src"):
            if a.get(k) and tag != "base":
                self.links.append((self.getpos()[0], a[k]))

    handle_startendtag = handle_starttag


def pages(site):
    out = []
    for d in ("", "guide"):
        base = os.path.join(site, d)
        out += [os.path.join(base, f) for f in sorted(os.listdir(base)) if f.endswith(".html")]
    return out


def main():
    site = os.path.join(ROOT, "site")
    if "--site" in sys.argv:
        site = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--site") + 1])
    parsed = {}

    def get(path):
        if path not in parsed:
            p = Page()
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                p.feed(fh.read())
            parsed[path] = p
        return parsed[path]

    bad = checked = 0
    for path in pages(site):
        for line, link in get(path).links:
            if link.startswith(EXTERNAL) or link.startswith("//"):
                continue
            checked += 1
            u = urllib.parse.urlsplit(link)
            target = path if not u.path else os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path),
                                                                           urllib.parse.unquote(u.path)))
            if os.path.isdir(target):
                target = os.path.join(target, "index.html")
            rel = os.path.relpath(path, site)
            if not os.path.exists(target):
                bad += 1
                print("%s:%d: %s: no such file" % (rel, line, link))
                continue
            if u.fragment and target.endswith(".html") and u.fragment not in get(target).ids:
                bad += 1
                print("%s:%d: %s: no id \"%s\" in %s" % (rel, line, link, u.fragment, os.path.relpath(target, site)))
    print("site links: %d checked, %s" % (checked, "all resolve" if not bad else "%d broken" % bad))
    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
