#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""site-terms.py: the install guide's term tips (site/guide/concepts.html and the dotted term links on the other pages).

    python3 tools/site-terms.py               write site/terms.js from concepts.html, then link the first use of each
                                              term, per language, on every guide page
    python3 tools/site-terms.py --check       change nothing; list the links it would add and say whether site/terms.js
                                              is stale; exit 1 if either
    python3 tools/site-terms.py --data        write site/terms.js only
    python3 tools/site-terms.py --site DIR    work on another copy of site/ (a trial run)
    python3 tools/site-terms.py a.html ...    only these pages (names in site/guide/, or paths)

One source of truth: site/guide/concepts.html. Each <section id> there is a term; its <h2> is the term's name and the
first sentence of its first <p lang="en"> / <p lang="tr"> is the tip main.js shows when the pointer or the keyboard
focus is on a term link. site/terms.js carries those, written by this tool; main.js loads it on pages that have a term
link. A term link is <a class="term" href="concepts.html#sip">SIP</a> (guide/concepts.html#.. from the site's root).

What gets linked: on each page and in each language, the first use of each term in the article's prose (first outside
folds, else the first inside one). Never inside code, pre, kbd, headings, summary, dt, th, existing links, buttons,
<i> (interface names), svg, navigation (the stage bar, prev/next), labels (.k, .status, .card-h, ..), .noindex
(diagrams, step strips, finders), screenshot captions or anything outside the article; never on concepts.html itself.
Text marked lang="en" / lang="tr" counts for that language; text with no language (shown in both) only when the term is
still unlinked in both. A Turkish suffix after an apostrophe stays outside the link (SIP'i -> <a>SIP</a>'i); Turkish
words that take a suffix without one are linked whole (sistem diskine). Idempotent: a page that already has a term link
for a term in a language keeps it and gets no second one. No dependencies.
"""
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SITE = os.path.join(ROOT, "site")

# id: (English patterns, Turkish patterns); within one term, the first pattern that matches at a position wins, so
# longer forms come first. Each match must stand alone: no letter, digit, ".", "-" or "/" right before it, and no
# letter, digit, "-", "/" or ".letter" (a file name) right after it.
TERMS = [
    ("opencore", [r"OpenCore(?! Legacy)"], [r"OpenCore(?! Legacy)"]),
    ("efi", [r"EFI"], [r"EFI"]),
    ("config-plist", [r"config\.plist"], [r"config\.plist"]),
    ("kext", [r"[Kk]exts?"], [r"[Kk]ext"]),
    ("sip", [r"SIP"], [r"SIP"]),
    ("amfi", [r"AMFI"], [r"AMFI"]),
    ("boot-args", [r"boot-args?"], [r"boot-args?"]),
    ("quirks", [r"quirks?"], [r"quirk"]),
    ("ssdt", [r"SSDT-ARCOFF(?:\.aml)?", r"SSDTs?"], [r"SSDT-ARCOFF(?:\.aml)?", r"SSDT"]),
    ("rebar", [r"Resizable BAR", r"Above 4G [Dd]ecoding", r"BAR"], [r"Resizable BAR", r"Above 4G [Dd]ecoding", r"BAR"]),
    ("system-volume", [r"(?:sealed )?system[- ]volume"], [r"(?:mühürlü )?sistem disk\w*"]),
    ("metal-plugin", [r"Metal (?:driver|plugin)"], [r"Metal (?:sürücüs|eklentis)\w*"]),
    ("boot-guard", [r"boot guard"], [r"[Aa]çılış korumas\w*"]),
    ("stages", [r"[Ss]tages? [1-4](?:(?:, | and | or | to |-|–)[1-4])*(?![.–-]\d)", r"four stages"],
               [r"(?<!scan-out )(?<!scan-out'un )[1-4]\.(?:(?:, | ve | ya da | ile |-|–)[1-4]\.)* aşama\w*", r"dört aşama\w*"]),
    ("manager", [r"IntelXe Manager(?: for Windows)?"], [r"(?:Windows için )?IntelXe Manager"]),
]
# pages where a term's words mean something else: XeProbe's own stages; nullmoth's original Metal driver for NVIDIA
# bold app page names that contain a term but name the page, not the concept
UI_NAMES = {"EFI (OpenCore)", "EFI"}
PAGE_SKIP = {"stages": {"support.html"}, "metal-plugin": {"credits.html"}}
LEFT, RIGHT = r"(?<![\w.\-/])", r"(?![\w/\-]|\.\w)"
PATTERNS = {tid: {"en": re.compile(LEFT + "(?:" + "|".join(en) + ")" + RIGHT),
                  "tr": re.compile(LEFT + "(?:" + "|".join(tr) + ")" + RIGHT)} for tid, en, tr in TERMS}

VOID = {"area", "base", "br", "col", "embed", "hr", "img", "input", "link", "meta", "source", "track", "wbr"}
SKIP_TAGS = {"code", "pre", "kbd", "samp", "var", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6", "summary", "dt", "th", "a",
             "button", "i", "svg", "nav", "header", "footer", "aside", "script", "style", "title", "textarea", "select",
             "option", "label", "math"}
SKIP_CLASSES = {"noindex", "stagebar", "doc-pn", "eyebrow", "k", "status", "card-h", "expect-h", "checks-h", "fix-h",
                "shot-theme", "todo-h", "term", "doc-toc", "tab-list", "jm-head", "jm-chips", "jm-label", "jm-time", "badge"}
TAG = re.compile(r"<!--.*?-->|<![^>]*>|<(?:[^>\"']|\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*')*>", re.S)
ATTR = re.compile(r"([\w:.-]+)(?:\s*=\s*(\"[^\"]*\"|'[^']*'|[^\s>]+))?")
NAME = re.compile(r"</?\s*([A-Za-z][\w:-]*)")


def tokenize(s):
    """[(kind, text)]: kind is "tag" or "text"; "".join(texts) == s. script/style bodies are one "raw" token."""
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(s)
    while i < n:
        j = s.find("<", i)
        if j == -1:
            out.append(("text", s[i:]))
            break
        if j > i:
            out.append(("text", s[i:j]))
        m = TAG.match(s, j)
        if not m:
            out.append(("text", "<"))
            i = j + 1
            continue
        tag = m.group(0)
        out.append(("tag", tag))
        i = m.end()
        nm = NAME.match(tag)
        if nm and not tag.startswith("</") and nm.group(1).lower() in ("script", "style"):
            end = s.lower().find("</" + nm.group(1).lower(), i)
            end = n if end == -1 else end
            if end > i:
                out.append(("raw", s[i:end]))
            i = end
    return out


def attrs(tag):
    body = re.sub(r"^<\s*[\w:-]+", "", tag).rstrip(">").rstrip("/")
    a = {}
    for m in ATTR.finditer(body):
        v = m.group(2) or ""
        if v[:1] in "\"'":
            v = v[1:-1]
        a[m.group(1).lower()] = html.unescape(v)
    return a


def walk(tokens):
    """For each token: (index, kind, text, stack) where stack is the list of open elements [(tag, attrs)]."""
    stack = []
    for i, (kind, text) in enumerate(tokens):
        if kind != "tag" or text.startswith("<!"):
            yield i, kind, text, stack
            continue
        m = NAME.match(text)
        if not m:
            continue
        name = m.group(1).lower()
        if text.startswith("</"):
            for k in range(len(stack) - 1, -1, -1):
                if stack[k][0] == name:
                    del stack[k:]
                    break
            yield i, kind, text, stack
            continue
        a = attrs(text)
        yield i, kind, text, stack + [(name, a)]
        if name not in VOID and not text.endswith("/>"):
            stack.append((name, a))


def context(stack):
    """(eligible, language or None for both, inside a fold) for text under this stack."""
    in_article = in_fold = False
    lang = None
    figure_shot = False
    for name, a in stack:
        cls = set(a.get("class", "").split())
        if name == "article" and "doc-body" in cls:
            in_article = True
        if name in SKIP_TAGS or cls & SKIP_CLASSES:
            return False, None, False
        if name == "figure" and cls & {"shot", "gal"}:
            figure_shot = True
        if name == "figcaption" and figure_shot:
            return False, None, False
        if name == "details":
            in_fold = True
        if name != "html" and a.get("lang") in ("en", "tr"):
            lang = a["lang"]
    return in_article, lang, in_fold


def href_for(page):
    rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(SITE, "guide", "concepts.html"), os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(page)))
    return rel.replace(os.sep, "/")


def plan(page):
    """The links to add to one page: [(token index, start, end, term id, language or "both")]."""
    with open(page, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        tokens = tokenize(fh.read())
    done = {"en": set(), "tr": set()}
    texts = []
    for i, kind, text, stack in walk(tokens):
        if kind == "tag" and not text.startswith("</") and NAME.match(text) and NAME.match(text).group(1).lower() == "a":
            a = stack[-1][1]
            if "term" in a.get("class", "").split() and "#" in a.get("href", ""):
                tid = a["href"].split("#", 1)[1]
                lang = next((x.get("lang") for _, x in reversed(stack[:-1]) if x.get("lang") in ("en", "tr")
                             and _ != "html"), None)
                for l in ((lang,) if lang else ("en", "tr")):
                    done[l].add(tid)
        elif kind == "text":
            ok, lang, fold = context(stack)
            if ok and stack and stack[-1][0] == "b" and text.strip().rstrip(":") in UI_NAMES:
                ok = False   # an app page's name in bold (EFI (OpenCore)), not the concept
            if ok and text.strip():
                texts.append((i, text, lang, fold))
    chosen = []          # (token index, start, end, term id, lang)
    spans = {}           # token index -> [(start, end)]
    for want_fold in (False, True):
        for i, text, lang, fold in texts:
            if fold != want_fold:
                continue
            langs = (lang,) if lang else ("en", "tr")
            for tid, _, _ in TERMS:
                if any(tid in done[l] for l in langs) or os.path.basename(page) in PAGE_SKIP.get(tid, ()):
                    continue
                pat = PATTERNS[tid][langs[0]]
                for m in pat.finditer(text):
                    if lang is None and not PATTERNS[tid]["tr"].fullmatch(m.group(0)):
                        continue
                    s, e = m.span()
                    taken = spans.get(i, [])
                    # not inside another link, and not right beside one (two links with only a space between)
                    if any(s < te and ts < e for ts, te in taken):
                        continue
                    if any(text[te:s].strip() == "" and te <= s or text[e:ts].strip() == "" and e <= ts
                           for ts, te in taken):
                        continue
                    spans.setdefault(i, []).append((s, e))
                    chosen.append((i, s, e, tid, lang or "both"))
                    for l in langs:
                        done[l].add(tid)
                    break
    return tokens, chosen


def apply(tokens, chosen, href):
    by_tok = {}
    for i, s, e, tid, _ in chosen:
        by_tok.setdefault(i, []).append((s, e, tid))
    out = []
    for i, (kind, text) in enumerate(tokens):
        if i in by_tok:
            for s, e, tid in sorted(by_tok[i], reverse=True):
                text = text[:s] + '<a class="term" href="%s#%s">%s</a>' % (href, tid, text[s:e]) + text[e:]
        out.append(text)
    return "".join(out)


# ---- the tips' data: concepts.html -> site/terms.js ----

def strip(s):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", s))).strip()


def first_sentence(text):
    """Up to the first . ! or ? followed by white space or the end; a lone digit and its dot (a Turkish ordinal:
    "2. aşama") does not end it. (Write no abbreviation with a dot, such as "e.g.", in an entry's first sentence.)"""
    for m in re.finditer(r"[.!?](?=\s|$)", text):
        k = m.start()
        if text[k] == "." and k >= 1 and text[k - 1].isdigit() and (k < 2 or not text[k - 2].isalnum()):
            continue
        return text[:k + 1]
    return text


def concepts(site):
    with open(os.path.join(site, "guide", "concepts.html"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        s = fh.read()
    s = s[s.index('<article class="doc-body">'):]
    terms = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r'<section id="([\w-]+)">(.*?)</section>', s, re.S):
        sid, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        h = re.search(r"<h2>(.*?)</h2>", body, re.S).group(1)
        t = [strip((re.search(r'<span lang="%s">(.*?)</span>' % l, h, re.S) or re.search(r"(.*)", h, re.S)).group(1))
             for l in ("en", "tr")]
        d = []
        for l in ("en", "tr"):
            p = re.search(r'<p lang="%s">(.*?)</p>' % l, body, re.S)
            d.append(first_sentence(strip(p.group(1))) if p else "")
        terms[sid] = {"t": t, "d": d}
    return terms


def terms_js(site):
    body = json.dumps({"v": 1, "terms": concepts(site)}, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return ("// The guide's term tips, written by tools/site-terms.py from site/guide/concepts.html (the first sentence"
            " of each entry). MIT.\nwindow.SITE_TERMS = " + body + ";\n")


def main():
    global SITE
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if "--site" in args:
        k = args.index("--site")
        SITE = os.path.abspath(args[k + 1])
        del args[k:k + 2]
    check = "--check" in args
    data_only = "--data" in args
    files = [a for a in args if not a.startswith("--")]
    problems = 0

    known = concepts(SITE)
    ids = [t[0] for t in TERMS]
    for tid in ids:
        if tid not in known:
            problems += 1
            print("concepts.html has no section for the term %s" % tid)
    for tid in known:
        if tid not in ids:
            print("note: concepts.html#%s has no patterns here (no links are added for it)" % tid)
    for tid, v in known.items():
        for l, d in zip(("en", "tr"), v["d"]):
            if not d:
                problems += 1
                print("concepts.html#%s has no <p lang=\"%s\">" % (tid, l))

    out_js = os.path.join(SITE, "terms.js")
    want = terms_js(SITE)
    try:
        with open(out_js, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            stale = fh.read() != want
    except FileNotFoundError:
        stale = True
    if stale and check:
        problems += 1
        print("site/terms.js is stale: python3 tools/site-terms.py --data")
    elif stale:
        with open(out_js, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(want)
        print("wrote site/terms.js (%d terms)" % len(known))
    if data_only:
        sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)

    guide = os.path.join(SITE, "guide")
    if files:
        pages = [f if os.path.exists(f) else os.path.join(guide, f) for f in files]
    else:
        pages = [os.path.join(guide, f) for f in sorted(os.listdir(guide)) if f.endswith(".html")]
    added = 0
    for page in pages:
        if os.path.basename(page) == "concepts.html":
            continue
        tokens, chosen = plan(page)
        if not chosen:
            continue
        added += len(chosen)
        name = os.path.relpath(page, SITE)
        if check:
            for i, s, e, tid, lang in sorted(chosen, key=lambda c: (c[4], c[0], c[1])):
                text = tokens[i][1]
                ctx = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text[max(0, s - 40):s] + "[" + text[s:e] + "]" + text[e:e + 30])
                print("%s %s %-13s %s" % (name, lang, tid, ctx.strip()))
        else:
            with open(page, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write(apply(tokens, chosen, href_for(page)))
            print("%s: %d term link(s)" % (name, len(chosen)))
    if check:
        print("site-terms: %d link(s) to add%s" % (added, ", %d problem(s)" % problems if problems else ""))
        sys.exit(1 if added or problems else 0)
    sys.exit(1 if problems else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

/* igadis <zebin> <outdir>: each kernel's machine code in an Intel GPU binary (zebin, ELF64), disassembled with the
 * driver's own iga64.dll for Xe2 (Battlemage), one .asm per kernel, and a line of counts per kernel on stdout. */
#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include "iga.h"
typedef iga_status_t (*ctx_create_t)(const iga_context_options_t *, iga_context_t *);
typedef iga_status_t (*dis_t)(iga_context_t, const iga_disassemble_options_t *, const void *, uint32_t, const char *(*)(int32_t, void *), void *, char **);
static HMODULE find_iga(void) {
    HMODULE h = LoadLibraryA("iga64.dll"); if (h) return h;
    char pat[MAX_PATH]; WIN32_FIND_DATAA fd; snprintf(pat, sizeof pat, "%s\\System32\\DriverStore\\FileRepository\\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_*", getenv("SystemRoot"));
    HANDLE f = FindFirstFileA(pat, &fd); if (f == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return NULL;
    do { char p[MAX_PATH]; snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s\\System32\\DriverStore\\FileRepository\\%s\\iga64.dll", getenv("SystemRoot"), fd.cFileName);
         if ((h = LoadLibraryA(p))) { printf("iga: %s\n", p); break; } } while (FindNextFileA(f, &fd));
    FindClose(f); return h;
}
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 3) { printf("usage: igadis <zebin> <outdir>\n"); return 2; }
    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb"); if (!f) { printf("cannot open %s\n", argv[1]); return 1; }
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END); long n = ftell(f); rewind(f); unsigned char *b = malloc(n); fread(b, 1, n, f); fclose(f);
    if (n < 64 || memcmp(b, "\x7f" "ELF", 4) || b[4] != 2) { printf("not an ELF64 file\n"); return 1; }
    uint64_t shoff; uint16_t shentsize, shnum, shstrndx; memcpy(&shoff, b + 0x28, 8); memcpy(&shentsize, b + 0x3a, 2); memcpy(&shnum, b + 0x3c, 2); memcpy(&shstrndx, b + 0x3e, 2);
    const unsigned char *sh = b + shoff; uint64_t stroff; memcpy(&stroff, sh + shstrndx * shentsize + 0x18, 8);
    HMODULE h = find_iga(); if (!h) { printf("iga64.dll not found\n"); return 1; }
    ctx_create_t cc = (ctx_create_t)(void *)GetProcAddress(h, "iga_context_create"); dis_t dis = (dis_t)(void *)GetProcAddress(h, "iga_context_disassemble");
    if (!cc || !dis) { printf("iga entry points missing\n"); return 1; }
    iga_context_options_t co = IGA_CONTEXT_OPTIONS_INIT(IGA_XE2); iga_context_t ctx;
    if (cc(&co, &ctx) != IGA_SUCCESS) { printf("iga context for Xe2 failed\n"); return 1; }
    iga_disassemble_options_t dopt = IGA_DISASSEMBLE_OPTIONS_INIT_NUMERIC_LABELS();
    for (int i = 0; i < shnum; i++) {
        const unsigned char *s = sh + i * shentsize; uint32_t nm; uint64_t off, size; memcpy(&nm, s, 4); memcpy(&off, s + 0x18, 8); memcpy(&size, s + 0x20, 8);
        const char *name = (const char *)b + stroff + nm;
        if (strncmp(name, ".text.", 6) || !size) continue;
        char *txt = NULL; iga_status_t st = dis(ctx, &dopt, b + off, (uint32_t)size, NULL, NULL, &txt);
        char path[1024]; snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s\\%s.asm", argv[2], name + 6);
        FILE *o = fopen(path, "w"); if (o && txt) fputs(txt, o); if (o) fclose(o);
        int ins = 0, sends = 0, sync = 0, spill = 0; const char *p = txt;
        while (p && *p) { const char *e = strchr(p, '\n'); size_t l = e ? (size_t)(e - p) : strlen(p);
            char line[512]; size_t c = l < sizeof line - 1 ? l : sizeof line - 1; memcpy(line, p, c); line[c] = 0;
            const char *q = line; while (*q == ' ') q++;
            if (*q && *q != '/' && !(q[0] == 'L' && strchr(q, ':'))) { ins++; if (strstr(q, "send")) sends++; if (strstr(q, "sync")) sync++; if (strstr(q, "scratch")) spill++; }
            p = e ? e + 1 : NULL; }
        printf("%-16s %6llu bytes  %4d instructions  %3d sends  %2d syncs  %d scratch  (status %d)\n", name + 6, (unsigned long long)size, ins, sends, sync, spill, (int)st);
    }
    return 0;
}

FILE: tools/parity/build.sh

#!/bin/sh
# Regenerate every parity artefact in one go: data/*.json, docs/parity/index.html (embedded data), docs/parity/svg/*.svg,
# docs/parity/HISTORY.md, and one new data/history.json entry.
#
#   LINUX=/path/linux [MESA=/path/mesa MESA_BUILD=/path/mesa/build NEO=/path/compute-runtime] [MEDIA_DRIVER=/path/media-driver] \
#     [MEDIAKIT=/path/mediakit] [LABEL="kernel rb7i"] \
#     tools/parity/build.sh
#
# LINUX: sparse checkout of torvalds/linux or drm-tip with drivers/gpu/drm/xe, drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display and
# include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h (see docs/parity/README.md). MESA/MESA_BUILD: our patched Mesa tree and its meson build dir
# (optional: without them the Mesa section is left out). MEDIAKIT: the mediakit folder with out_mac/results_mac.txt
# (optional: without it data/video.json is kept as it is). NEO: sparse checkout of intel/compute-runtime with
# shared/source/os_interface/linux (with MESA it enables the need classes and docs/parity/TODO.md). MEDIA_DRIVER: a checkout
# of intel/media-driver (optional: without it data/caps.json is kept as it is); its capability tables give data/caps.json,
# from which video.py takes what Intel does not offer on the B580 and platforms.py the video rows of every platform.
# platforms.py writes docs/PLATFORMS.md, docs/parity/svg/platforms.svg and the README's platform table. CTS runs are
# imported separately with cts_import.py; the newest entry of data/cts/runs.json is drawn.
set -eu
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
root=$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)
: "${LINUX:?set LINUX to the Linux tree}"
py=python3

if [ -n "${MESA:-}" ]; then
	$py "$here/scan.py" --linux "$LINUX" --mesa "$MESA" ${MESA_BUILD:+--mesa-build "$MESA_BUILD"} --html "$root/docs/parity/index.html"
else
	$py "$here/scan.py" --linux "$LINUX" --html "$root/docs/parity/index.html"
fi
$py "$here/uapi.py" --linux "$LINUX"
if [ -n "${MESA:-}" ] && [ -n "${NEO:-}" ]; then
	$py "$here/consumers.py" --linux "$LINUX" --mesa "$MESA" --neo "$NEO"
fi
if [ -n "${MEDIA_DRIVER:-}" ]; then
	$py "$here/caps.py" --media-driver "$MEDIA_DRIVER"
fi
if [ -n "${MEDIAKIT:-}" ] && [ -f "$MEDIAKIT/out_mac/results_mac.txt" ]; then
	$py "$here/video.py" --mediakit "$MEDIAKIT"
fi
$py "$here/render.py" --history-append --label "${LABEL:-}"
$py "$here/next.py"
$py "$here/platforms.py"

FILE: tools/parity/caps.py
================================================
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""What Intel's own Linux media stack (intel/media-driver, VA-API) offers per platform: data/caps.json.

Reads a checkout of github.com/intel/media-driver and records, for each platform this driver targets, every codec x
direction it exposes with profiles, bit depths, chroma formats and the largest picture, each with the source line.

Two kinds of platform code exist upstream, and both are read as written (no estimates, nothing filled in by hand):
- "capstable" (media_softlet/linux/<ip>_r0: MTL/ARL, LNL, BMG, PTL): the ProfileMap of the platform's
  capstable_data_<ip>_specific.h lists each VA profile with its entrypoints; each entrypoint's AttribList (in the codec's
  capstable_data_<codec>_<dir>_<ip>_specific.h) gives VAConfigAttribRTFormat (-> bit depth, chroma) and
  VAConfigAttribMaxPictureWidth/Height.
- "sku" (media_driver/linux, Gen12 TGL/RKL/ADL/RPL/DG1 and DG2): the legacy caps code exposes a VA profile when its media
  feature flag is set; the flags are set by the platform's Init<...>MediaSku function (MEDIA_WR_SKU, LinuxCodecInfo
  fields for the codec switches). The functions are walked in order, including the base function they call; values
  under SET_STATUS_BY_FULL_OPEN_SOURCE(a, b) take a (the default build: ENABLE_KERNELS and ENABLE_NONFREE_KERNELS on).
  The legacy code computes the largest picture in C++ per profile; it is not extracted (max = null).
Device IDs per platform come from the RegisterDevice(0x...) calls of media-driver's media_sysinfo_*.cpp.

  tools/parity/caps.py --media-driver /path/media-driver [--out data/caps.json]

Python stdlib only.
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

# Our platform ids -> media-driver code. 'ids' = (sysinfo file, GfxDeviceInfo variable names).
PLATFORMS = [
    {'id': 'bmg', 'name': 'Battlemage (Arc B580/B570)', 'model': 'capstable', 'dir': 'media_softlet/linux/xe2_hpm_r0',
     'ip': 'xe2_hpm_r0', 'ids': ('media_softlet/linux/xe2_hpm/ddi/media_sysinfo_bmg.cpp', ['bmgInfo'])},
    {'id': 'lnl', 'name': 'Lunar Lake', 'model': 'capstable', 'dir': 'media_softlet/linux/xe2_lpm_r0', 'ip': 'xe2_lpm_r0',
     'ids': ('media_softlet/linux/xe2_lpm/ddi/media_sysinfo_lnl.cpp', ['lnlInfo'])},
    {'id': 'ptl', 'name': 'Panther Lake', 'model': 'capstable', 'dir': 'media_softlet/linux/xe3_lpm_r0', 'ip': 'xe3_lpm_r0',
     'ids': ('media_softlet/linux/xe3_lpm/ddi/media_sysinfo_ptl.cpp', ['ptlInfo'])},

def strip_comments(s):
    s = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', lambda m: '\n' * m.group(0).count('\n'), s, flags=re.S)
    return re.sub(r'//[^\n]*', '', s)


def blocks(path, kind):
    """{name: (body, line)} of every top-level `[static] [const] <kind> name [=] { ... };` in a file."""
    s = strip_comments(open(path, errors='replace').read())
    out = {}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(?:static\s+)?(?:const\s+)?%s\s+(\w+)\s*=?\s*\{' % kind, s):
        i, depth = m.end(), 1
        while depth and i < len(s):
            depth += {'{': 1, '}': -1}.get(s[i], 0)
            i += 1
        out[m.group(1)] = (s[m.end():i - 1], s.count('\n', 0, m.start()) + 1)
    return out


def constants(md):
    c = {}
    for rel in ('media_common/agnostic/common/codec/shared/codec_def_common.h',
                'media_common/agnostic/common/codec/shared/codec_def_decode_vvc.h',
                'media_common/agnostic/common/codec/shared/codec_def_encode_jpeg.h'):
        p = os.path.join(md, rel)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            for m in re.finditer(r'#define\s+(\w+)\s+(\d+)', open(p, errors='replace').read()):
                c[m.group(1)] = int(m.group(2))
    return c


def capstable(md, plat, consts):
    d = os.path.join(md, plat['dir'])
    files = [os.path.join(r, f) for r, _, fs in os.walk(d) for f in fs if f.startswith('capstable_data_') and f.endswith('.h')]
    top = [f for f in files if os.path.basename(f) == 'capstable_data_%s_specific.h' % plat['ip']][0]
    attribs, eps = {}, {}
    for f in files:
        for n, (b, l) in blocks(f, 'AttribList').items():
            attribs[n] = (b, os.path.relpath(f, md), l)
        for n, (b, l) in blocks(f, 'EntrypointData').items():
            eps[n] = (b, os.path.relpath(f, md), l)
    emaps = blocks(top, 'EntrypointMap')
    pmap = blocks(top, 'ProfileMap')
    # the base table; an "_ext" table (another media IP stepping, IP_VERSION_<..>_EXT) only adds profiles, listed apart
    base = [n for n in pmap if '_ext' not in n.lower()]
    assert len(base) == 1, 'one base ProfileMap in %s: %s' % (top, list(pmap))
    pbody, _ = pmap[base[0]]
    ext = {}
    for n, (b, _) in pmap.items():
        if n != base[0]:
            extra = sorted(set(re.findall(r'VAProfile(\w+)\s*\)?\s*,', b)) - set(re.findall(r'VAProfile(\w+)\s*\)?\s*,', pbody)))
            if extra:
                ext[n] = extra
    entries = []
    for prof, emap in re.findall(r'\{\s*(?:\(VAProfile\))?(VAProfile\w+)\s*,\s*&(\w+)\s*\}', pbody):
        codec = next((c for pre, c in CODEC_OF if prof.startswith(pre)), None)
        if not codec:
            continue
        for ep, data in re.findall(r'\{\s*(VAEntrypoint\w+)\s*,\s*&(\w+)\s*\}', emaps[emap][0]):
            if ep not in DIR_OF or data not in eps:
                continue
            al = re.search(r'&(\w+)', eps[data][0]).group(1)
            ab, af, alin = attribs[al]
            rt = re.search(r'VAConfigAttribRTFormat\s*,\s*([^}]+)\}', ab)
            fmts = [t for t in re.findall(r'VA_RT_FORMAT_(\w+)', rt.group(1))] if rt else []
            wv = re.search(r'VAConfigAttribMaxPictureWidth\s*,\s*(\w+)', ab)
            hv = re.search(r'VAConfigAttribMaxPictureHeight\s*,\s*(\w+)', ab)
            entries.append({'codec': codec, 'dir': DIR_OF[ep], 'profile': prof[len('VAProfile'):], 'entrypoint': ep[len('VAEntrypoint'):],
                            'formats': fmts, 'coded': sorted({RT[f] for f in fmts if f in RT}),
                            'max_w': consts.get(wv.group(1)) if wv else None, 'max_h': consts.get(hv.group(1)) if hv else None,
                            'src': '%s:%d' % (af, alin)})
    return entries, os.path.relpath(top, md), ext


def sku(md, plat):
    path = os.path.join(md, plat['file'])
    raw = strip_comments(open(path, errors='replace').read())
    infos = {n: {k: v.rstrip(', ') for k, v in re.findall(r'\.(\w+)\s*=\s*(.+?)\s*$', b, re.M)}
             for n, (b, _) in blocks(path, 'struct LinuxCodecInfo').items()}

    def val(v, ci):
        v = v.strip()
        m = re.match(r'SET_STATUS_BY_FULL_OPEN_SOURCE\((\w+)\s*,\s*(\w+)\)', v)
        if m:
            v = m.group(1)
        if re.match(r'^\d+$', v):
            return int(v)
        m = re.match(r'codecInfo->(\w+)$', v)
        if m and ci and m.group(1) in ci:
            return val(ci[m.group(1)], None)
        return None

    def func(name):
        m = re.search(r'static bool %s\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{' % name, raw)
        i, depth = m.end(), 1
        while depth:
            depth += {'{': 1, '}': -1}.get(raw[i], 0)
            i += 1
        return raw[m.end():i - 1], raw.count('\n', 0, m.start()) + 1

    flags = {}

    def walk(name, ci):
        body, line0 = func(name)
        local = re.search(r'LinuxCodecInfo\s*\*\s*codecInfo\s*=\s*&(\w+)', body)
        if local:
            ci = infos[local.group(1)]
        for m in re.finditer(r'(InitTglMediaSku(?:Ext)?)\s*\(([^;]*)\)|MEDIA_WR_SKU\(\s*skuTable\s*,\s*(\w+)\s*,\s*([^;]+?)\)\s*;', body):
            if m.group(1) and m.group(1) != name:
                arg = re.search(r'&(\w+CodecInfo)', m.group(2))
                walk(m.group(1), infos[arg.group(1)] if arg else ci)
            elif m.group(3):
                flags[m.group(3)] = (val(m.group(4), ci), '%s:%d' % (plat['file'], line0 + body.count('\n', 0, m.start())))

    walk(plat['init'], None)
    entries = []
    for f, (v, src) in sorted(flags.items()):
        if f in FTR and v:
            c, d, b, ch = FTR[f]
            entries.append({'codec': c, 'dir': d, 'flag': f, 'coded': [(b, ch)] if ch else [], 'max_w': None, 'max_h': None, 'src': src})
    unknown = sorted(f for f, (v, _) in flags.items() if f in FTR and v is None)
    return entries, unknown


def device_ids(md, plat):
    rel, names = plat['ids']
    s = open(os.path.join(md, rel), errors='replace').read()
    return sorted({m.group(1).lower() for m in re.finditer(r'RegisterDevice\((0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)\s*,\s*&(\w+)\)', s) if m.group(2) in names}), rel


def summarize(entries):
    out = {}
    for e in entries:
        s = out.setdefault(e['codec'], {}).setdefault(e['dir'], {'coded': set(), 'profiles': set(), 'max_w': None, 'max_h': None, 'src': []})
        s['coded'] |= {tuple(x) for x in e['coded']}
        if e.get('profile'):
            s['profiles'].add(e['profile'])
        if e['max_w']:
            s['max_w'] = max(s['max_w'] or 0, e['max_w'])
            s['max_h'] = max(s['max_h'] or 0, e['max_h'] or 0)
        if e['src'] not in s['src']:
            s['src'].append(e['src'])
    for c in out.values():
        for s in c.values():
            s['bits'] = sorted({b for b, _ in s['coded']})
            s['chroma'] = sorted({ch for _, ch in s['coded']})
            s['coded'] = ['%d-bit %s' % (b, ch) for b, ch in sorted(s['coded'])]
            s['profiles'] = sorted(s['profiles'])
    return out


def supports(caps, platform, codec, d, bits, w, h, chroma='420'):
    """(True/False/None, reason) for one combination; None when the platform is not in caps.json."""
    p = next((x for x in caps['platforms'] if x['id'] == platform), None)
    if not p:
        return None, 'platform %s not in caps.json' % platform
    s = p['summary'].get(codec, {}).get(d)
    where = p['source']
    if not s:
        return False, 'Intel media-driver offers no %s %s entrypoint on %s (%s)' % (codec, d, p['name'], where)
    if '%d-bit %s' % (bits, chroma) not in s['coded']:
        return False, 'Intel media-driver offers %s %s on %s as %s only, not %d-bit %s (%s)' % (
            codec, d, p['name'], ', '.join(s['coded']), bits, chroma, ', '.join(s['src']))
    if s['max_w'] and (w > s['max_w'] or h > (s['max_h'] or s['max_w'])):
        return False, 'beyond Intel media-driver on %s: %s %s up to %dx%d (VAConfigAttribMaxPictureWidth/Height, %s)' % (
            p['name'], codec, d, s['max_w'], s['max_h'], ', '.join(s['src']))
    return True, 'offered by Intel media-driver on %s (%s)' % (p['name'], ', '.join(s['src']))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--media-driver', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--out', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/caps.json'))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    md = a.media_driver
    git = lambda *x: subprocess.run(['git', '-C', md] + list(x), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    consts = constants(md)
    plats = []
    for p in PLATFORMS:
        if p['model'] == 'capstable':
            entries, src, ext = capstable(md, p, consts)
            unknown = []
        else:
            entries, unknown = sku(md, p)
            src, ext = '%s %s()' % (p['file'], p['init']), {}
        ids, ids_src = device_ids(md, p)
        q = {'id': p['id'], 'name': p['name'], 'model': p['model'], 'source': src, 'device_ids': ids, 'device_ids_source': ids_src,
             'entries': entries, 'summary': summarize(entries)}
        if unknown:
            q['unresolved_flags'] = unknown
        if ext:
            q['ext_tables'] = ext
        plats.append(q)
    data = {'meta': {'source': 'https://github.com/intel/media-driver', 'commit': git('rev-parse', 'HEAD'),
                     'date': git('log', '-1', '--format=%cd', '--date=short'), 'subject': git('log', '-1', '--format=%s'),
                     'build': 'default (ENABLE_KERNELS, ENABLE_NONFREE_KERNELS on): SET_STATUS_BY_FULL_OPEN_SOURCE(a, b) = a',
                     'method': __doc__.split('\n\n')[1].replace('\n', ' ')},
            'platforms': plats}
    json.dump(data, open(a.out, 'w'), indent=1)
    for p in plats:
        print('caps %-5s %-9s %3d entries: %s' % (p['id'], p['model'], len(p['entries']), ' '.join(
            '%s[%s]' % (c, '/'.join('%s %s%s' % (d[:3], ','.join(map(str, s['bits'])), ' <=%dx%d' % (s['max_w'], s['max_h']) if s['max_w'] else '')
                                    for d, s in sorted(v.items()))) for c, v in sorted(p['summary'].items()) if c in ('h264', 'hevc', 'vp9', 'av1'))))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Classify every xe uAPI item by NEED, with evidence from the user-space that consumes it.

Reads data/uapi.json (uapi.py) and searches the consumers' real sources for each token name:
  now     Mesa as we run it on macOS: src/intel/vulkan (ANV), src/intel/common, src/intel/dev (not src/intel/perf);
          our Metal plugin and VideoToolbox code in this repository. xemac (user/xemac) is NOT a consumer: it is the
          transport that forwards ioctls to IntelXe.kext (and its software "fake" device answers some itself), so a token
          in xemac says nothing about what user space needs
  future  iris (src/gallium/drivers/iris: native OpenGL), Mesa src/intel/perf (GPU profiler: OA metrics,
          VK_KHR_performance_query), Intel compute-runtime/NEO shared/source/os_interface/linux (OpenCL / oneAPI)
Overlay ("need") per item, only where our kernel does not implement it (implemented / accepted stay as they are):
  needed_now      a "now" consumer uses it                                   -> red
  needed_future   only "future" consumers use it (feature named)             -> orange
  not_needed      Linux-only concept (PXP content protection, RAS netlink), or no consumer found anywhere -> black
Every item stores consumer file:line hits (first 3 per consumer), or the list of trees searched with their commits.
Also writes docs/parity/TODO.md (red items first, then orange grouped by feature).

  python3 tools/parity/consumers.py --mesa <mesa tree> --neo <compute-runtime tree> --linux <linux tree>
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
EXT = ('.c', '.h', '.cpp', '.hpp', '.m', '.mm', '.inl')
LINUX_ONLY = [(r'PXP', 'PXP protected content (Linux/Windows DRM content protection; no macOS path)'),
              (r'_RAS_', 'RAS error reporting over Linux netlink (drm_ras), not an ioctl a macOS client calls')]
# Items Linux itself never reports on this hardware (Xe2, graphics 20), with the Linux source that decides it.
NOT_ON_XE2 = [(r'^DRM_XE_TOPO_EU_PER_DSS$', 'not reported on Xe2 by Linux either: load_eu_mask() picks XE_GT_EU_TYPE_SIMD16 '
               'for graphics >= 20 (xe_gt_topology.c) and xe_query.c then reports DRM_XE_TOPO_SIMD16_EU_PER_DSS, which we '
               'report; Mesa (intel/dev/xe/intel_device_info.c) handles both')]


def git_head(path):
    try:
        top = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', path, 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
        h = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', top, 'rev-parse', '--short=12', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
        return h
    except Exception:
        return 'no git'


def files_under(base, exclude=()):
    for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(base):
        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d not in ('build', '.git', '__pycache__'))
        for f in sorted(fs):
            p = os.path.join(root, f)
            if f.endswith(EXT) and f != 'xe_drm.h' and not any(x in p for x in exclude):
                yield p


class Consumer:
    def __init__(self, name, kind, feature, roots, exclude=()):
        """roots: [(directory, base the file:line labels are relative to)]"""
        self.name, self.kind, self.feature = name, kind, feature
        self.roots = [(r, b) for r, b in roots if os.path.isdir(r)]
        self.commit = git_head(self.roots[0][0]) if self.roots else 'missing'
        self.text = {}
        for r, b in self.roots:
            for p in files_under(r, exclude):
                try:
                    self.text[os.path.relpath(p, b)] = open(p, errors='ignore').read()
                except OSError:
                    pass

    def hits(self, tok, limit=3):
        out, rx = [], re.compile(r'\b%s\b' % re.escape(tok))
        for f, s in self.text.items():
            m = rx.search(s)
            if m:
                out.append('%s:%d' % (f, s.count('\n', 0, m.start()) + 1))
                if len(out) >= limit:
                    break
        return out


def doc_of(tok, header_text):
    """Kernel-doc text for a token in xe_drm.h ("%TOKEN - text"), else the struct its #define sits in, else ''."""
    m = re.search(r'%%%s\s+-\s+(.+)' % re.escape(tok), header_text)
    if m:
        text = [m.group(1).strip()]
        for line in header_text[m.end():].split('\n')[1:6]:
            t = line.strip()
            if not t.startswith('*') or t.startswith('*/') or re.match(r'\*\s*(-\s*%|@|$)', t):
                break
            text.append(t.lstrip('*').strip())
        return ' '.join(text).rstrip('*/ ').strip()
    d = re.search(r'#define\s+%s\b' % re.escape(tok), header_text)
    if not d:
        return ''
    before = header_text[:d.start()]
    st = list(re.finditer(r'^struct\s+(drm_xe_\w+)\s*\{', before, re.M))
    if st and before.count('{', st[-1].start()) > before.count('}', st[-1].start()):
        return 'value of a field in struct %s' % st[-1].group(1)
    return ''


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--mesa', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--neo', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--linux', required=True, help='Linux tree (for the xe_drm.h doc comments)')
    ap.add_argument('--data', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data'))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    mesa = lambda *p: (os.path.join(a.mesa, *p), a.mesa)
    repo = lambda *p: (os.path.join(ROOT, *p), ROOT)
    consumers = [
        Consumer('Mesa ANV / intel common (as run on macOS)', 'now', None,
                 [mesa('src/intel/vulkan'), mesa('src/intel/common'), mesa('src/intel/dev')], exclude=('/tests/',)),
        Consumer('Metal plugin / VideoToolbox (this repository)', 'now', None, [repo('nullmoth/plugin'), repo('videotoolbox')]),
        Consumer('iris (Mesa)', 'future', 'native OpenGL via iris', [mesa('src/gallium/drivers/iris')]),
        Consumer('Mesa intel/perf', 'future', 'GPU profiler (OA metrics, VK_KHR_performance_query)', [mesa('src/intel/perf')]),
        Consumer('Intel compute-runtime (NEO)', 'future', 'OpenCL / oneAPI (Intel compute-runtime)',
                 [(os.path.join(a.neo, 'shared/source/os_interface/linux'), a.neo)]),
    ]
    searched = ['%s @ %s (%d files)' % (c.name, c.commit, len(c.text)) for c in consumers]
    header = open(os.path.join(a.linux, 'include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h')).read()
    up = os.path.join(a.data, 'uapi.json')
    u = json.load(open(up))
    for c in u['cells']:
        tok = c['token']
        cons = []
        for k in consumers:
            h = k.hits(tok)
            if h:
                cons.append({'consumer': k.name, 'kind': k.kind, 'feature': k.feature, 'commit': k.commit, 'at': h})
        c['consumers'] = cons
        c['doc'] = doc_of(tok, header)[:200]
        now = [x for x in cons if x['kind'] == 'now']
        fut = [x for x in cons if x['kind'] == 'future']
        lo = next((r for rx, r in LINUX_ONLY if re.search(rx, tok)), None)
        hw = next((r for rx, r in NOT_ON_XE2 if re.search(rx, tok)), None)
        if c['status'] in ('implemented', 'noop'):
            c['need'], c['need_why'] = None, ''
        elif hw:
            c['need'], c['need_why'] = 'not_needed', hw
        elif lo:
            c['need'], c['need_why'] = 'not_needed', 'Linux-only concept: ' + lo
        elif now:
            c['need'] = 'needed_now'
            c['need_why'] = 'used by %s; our kernel: %s' % (', '.join(x['consumer'] for x in now), c['status'])
        elif fut:
            c['need'] = 'needed_future'
            c['need_why'] = 'only for: ' + '; '.join(sorted({x['feature'] for x in fut}))
        else:
            c['need'], c['need_why'] = 'not_needed', 'no consumer found in: ' + '; '.join(searched)
    cnt = {}
    for c in u['cells']:
        key = c['need'] or c['status']
        cnt[key] = cnt.get(key, 0) + 1
    u['need'] = {'searched': searched, 'counts': cnt,
                 'method': 'token names searched in the consumer trees (xe_drm.h copies excluded); tools/parity/consumers.py'}
    json.dump(u, open(up, 'w'), indent=1)
    print('need classes:', json.dumps(cnt))
    write_todo(u, searched)


def write_todo(u, searched):
    red = [c for c in u['cells'] if c.get('need') == 'needed_now']
    orange = [c for c in u['cells'] if c.get('need') == 'needed_future']
    black = [c for c in u['cells'] if c.get('need') == 'not_needed']
    st_tr = {'rejected': 'reddediliyor', 'absent': 'rapor edilmiyor', 'unverified': 'doğrulanmadı'}
    L = ['# Taşınacaklar / What we must port', '',
         'Üretildi / generated: `tools/parity/consumers.py` (`tools/parity/build.sh`). Kaynak: `data/uapi.json`.', '',
         '**TR:** Sıra: önce bugün çalıştırdığımız yazılımın (Mesa ANV ve ortak Intel kodu; eklenti ve VideoToolbox kodunda xe uAPI kullanımı yok) kullandığı ama '
         'çekirdeğimizin uygulamadığı xe uAPI ögeleri (kırmızı), sonra yalnızca gelecekteki bir hedefin (OpenCL/oneAPI, '
         'profiler, iris) kullandığı ögeler (turuncu), özelliğe göre gruplu. Her satır tüketicinin `dosya:satır` kanıtını '
         'taşır; "bizde" sütunu çekirdeğimizdeki durumdur (`uapi.py`). xemac tüketici sayılmaz: ioctl\'ları çekirdeğe ileten katmandır.', '',
         '**EN:** Order: first the xe uAPI items the user space we run today uses but our kernel does not implement (red), '
         'then items only a future target uses (orange), grouped by feature. Each row cites the consumer file:line.', '',
         'Aranan ağaçlar / trees searched:', ''] + ['- ' + s for s in searched] + ['',
         '## 1. Şimdi gerekli, eksik / Needed now, missing (%d)' % len(red), '',
         '| # | Öge / item | Bizde / ours | Ne işe yarar / what it is (xe_drm.h) | Tüketici / consumer (file:line) |', '|---|---|---|---|---|']
    for i, c in enumerate(red, 1):
        ev = '; '.join('%s: %s' % (x['consumer'], ', '.join(x['at'])) for x in c['consumers'] if x['kind'] == 'now')
        ours = st_tr.get(c['status'], c['status']) + (' — ' + c['uses'][0]['at'] if c.get('uses') else '')
        if c.get('comments'):
            ours += '; yalnızca yorumda anılıyor / named only in comments: ' + ', '.join(c['comments'])
        L.append('| %d | `%s` | %s | %s | %s |' % (i, c['token'], ours, c.get('doc', '').replace('|', '/'), ev))
    L += ['', '## 2. Gelecek hedefler için / Needed for a future target (%d)' % len(orange), '']
    groups = {}
    for c in orange:
        for f in sorted({x['feature'] for x in c['consumers'] if x['kind'] == 'future'}):
            groups.setdefault(f, []).append(c)
    for f, cs in sorted(groups.items(), key=lambda kv: -len(kv[1])):
        L += ['### %s (%d)' % (f, len(cs)), '', '| Öge / item | Bizde / ours | Tüketici / consumer (file:line) |', '|---|---|---|']
        for c in cs:
            ev = '; '.join('%s: %s' % (x['consumer'], ', '.join(x['at'])) for x in c['consumers'] if x['feature'] == f)
            L.append('| `%s` | %s | %s |' % (c['token'], st_tr.get(c['status'], c['status']), ev))
        L.append('')
    par_p = os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/parity.json')
    if os.path.exists(par_p):
        par = json.load(open(par_p))
        plat = {}
        for f in par['files']:
            if f.get('section') == 'kernel' and f.get('future'):
                plat.setdefault(f['future'], []).append(f)
        tot_fn = sum(f.get('total', 0) for fs in plat.values() for f in fs if f.get('kind') == 'functions')
        L += ['## 3. Diğer Intel GPU\'ları (gelecek donanım hedefleri) / Other Intel GPUs (future hardware targets)', '',
              'Linux xe / i915 display dosyaları; B580\'de olmayan ama başka bir Intel ailesinde bulunan donanım için. Platform ve '
              'gerekçe `tools/parity/map.json`\'dan (Linux kaynağındaki koşula dayanarak). / Files for hardware another Intel family '
              'has; platform and reason from map.json, based on the condition in the Linux source.', '',
              '| Platform | Dosya / files | Fonksiyon / functions | Satır / lines | Gerekçe / reason |', '|---|---|---|---|---|']
        for k, fs in sorted(plat.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(f['lines'] for f in kv[1])):
            nfn = sum(f['total'] for f in fs if f.get('kind') == 'functions')
            L.append('| %s | %d | %d | %d | %s |' % (k, len(fs), nfn, sum(f['lines'] for f in fs), fs[0]['reason']))
        L.append('')
        for k, fs in sorted(plat.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(f['lines'] for f in kv[1])):
            L += ['### %s' % k, '', ', '.join('`%s` (%d)' % (f['path'], f['lines']) for f in sorted(fs, key=lambda f: -f['lines'])), '']
        old = [f for f in par['files'] if f.get('section') == 'kernel' and f.get('na') == 'old']
        L += ['Gerekmeyen eski platformlar / pre-Gen12 platforms, not needed: %d dosya, %d satır (%s).' % (
            len(old), sum(f['lines'] for f in old), old[0]['reason'] if old else ''), '']
    L += ['## 4. macOS\'ta gerekmiyor / Not needed on macOS (%d)' % len(black), '',
          'Linux\'a özgü kavramlar (PXP, RAS) ya da hiçbir tüketicide geçmeyen ögeler. / Linux-only concepts or no consumer found.', '',
          ', '.join('`%s`' % c['token'] for c in black), '']
    open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'docs/parity/TODO.md'), 'w').write('\n'.join(L) + '\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

FILE: tools/parity/cts_import.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Import one Vulkan CTS run (deqp-vk shards written by user/tests' run.sh on the hackintosh) into the repository.

Reads <results>/<group>/*.qpa (+ events.txt CRASH/TIMEOUT lines, run.log) exactly like the run's own
parse_results.py, and writes data/cts/<run-id>.tsv.gz (case, status, shard group) plus an entry in data/cts/runs.json
with the date and driver stack you give (--date, --stack). Only cases that actually ran are recorded; shard groups the
runner stopped early are listed as partial.

  python3 tools/parity/cts_import.py --results <dir> --run-id 2026-10-29-g1-g7 --date "2026-10-29 21:03-21:15" \
      --stack "kernel sv7 c3372d3b, Mesa wsi 44c36957 (internal shaders stub)" --source "<where the files came from>"
"""
import argparse, collections, glob, gzip, json, os, re

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))


def parse_qpa(path):
    out, cur, buf = {}, None, []
    with open(path, errors='replace') as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.startswith('#beginTestCaseResult'):
                cur, buf = line.split()[1], []
            elif line.startswith('#endTestCaseResult') and cur:
                m = re.search(r'StatusCode="([A-Za-z]+)"', ''.join(buf))
                out[cur] = m.group(1) if m else 'Other'
                cur = None
            elif line.startswith('#terminateTestCaseResult') and cur:
                out[cur] = 'Timeout' if 'Timeout' in line else 'Crash'
                cur = None
            elif cur:
                buf.append(line)
    if cur:
        out[cur] = 'Crash'   # process died inside the case
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--results', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--run-id', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--date', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--stack', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--source', default='')
    ap.add_argument('--note', default='')
    ap.add_argument('--out-dir', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/cts'))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    rows, partial, per = [], [], {}
    log = open(os.path.join(a.results, 'run.log')).read() if os.path.exists(os.path.join(a.results, 'run.log')) else ''
    # <group>.runN directories hold earlier attempts of a group the runner was restarted on: they are read first and
    # the later attempt (<group>) overrides each case it ran again
    dirs = [d for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(a.results, '[gp]*')) if os.path.isdir(d)]
    dirs.sort(key=lambda d: (os.path.basename(d).split('.')[0], 0 if '.run' in os.path.basename(d) else 1, d))
    merged = {}
    for gdir in dirs:
        g = os.path.basename(gdir).split('.')[0]
        res = merged.setdefault(g, {})
        key = lambda p: (os.path.basename(p).split('.')[0], int(re.search(r'\.a(\d+)\.qpa', p).group(1)))
        for q in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(gdir, '*.qpa')), key=key):
            res.update(parse_qpa(q))
        ev = os.path.join(gdir, 'events.txt')
        if os.path.exists(ev):
            for l in open(ev):
                p = l.split()
                if len(p) > 1 and p[0] == 'TIMEOUT' and p[1] in res:
                    res[p[1]] = 'Timeout'
                if len(p) > 2 and p[0] == 'CRASH':
                    res[p[2]] = 'Crash'
        if re.search(r'GROUP %s: .*group stopped|STOP RUN after \w+ in %s/' % (g, g), log) and g not in partial:
            partial.append(g)
    for g, res in merged.items():
        per[g] = dict(collections.Counter(res.values()))
        rows += [(c, s, g) for c, s in sorted(res.items())]
    os.makedirs(a.out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    with gzip.open(os.path.join(a.out_dir, a.run_id + '.tsv.gz'), 'wt') as f:
        f.write('case\tstatus\tshard_group\n')
        for r in rows:
            f.write('\t'.join(r) + '\n')
    runs_p = os.path.join(a.out_dir, 'runs.json')
    runs = json.load(open(runs_p)) if os.path.exists(runs_p) else []
    runs = [r for r in runs if r['id'] != a.run_id]
    runs.append({'id': a.run_id, 'date': a.date, 'stack': a.stack, 'source': a.source, 'note': a.note, 'cases': len(rows),
                 'status': dict(collections.Counter(s for _, s, _ in rows)), 'shard_groups': per,
                 'partial_groups': partial})
    json.dump(runs, open(runs_p, 'w'), indent=1)
    print('%s: %d cases %s; partial groups: %s' % (a.run_id, len(rows), runs[-1]['status'], ', '.join(partial) or 'none'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""The supported-device list against every copy of it in the repository.

data/platforms.json "supported" is the one list of the PCI devices (vendor 8086) this driver attaches to. The kexts,
the install scripts, the app and the Windows EFI tool each keep their own copy, in their own language and format; this
script reads each copy and fails when one differs from that list. No copy is generated: a new card is added to
data/platforms.json, then to each copy this script names (docs/design/DESIGN-platforms.md section 4).

  copies     each must list exactly the supported ids: IntelXe.kext and NMXAccel IOPCIMatch, install.sh (template and
             the filled copy) with its "untested" mark = not "tested", release/templates/efi-rules.json (the EFI rules
             of efi.sh and the Windows tool), the app, the kernel's platform test, clbench's preferred OpenCL devices;
  kernel     the descriptor id array named by "kernel_ids" (xe_platform.cpp) holds every supported id;
  tester     the BMG-G31 personality of build.py (G31_TESTER_MATCH, started only with -intelxe_allow_g31) lists exactly
             the kernel's G31 ids, none of them supported;
  mentions   the files that describe the cards to people name every supported id and card.

One file is generated from the list instead of copied: app/Sources/SupportedDevices.swift, the GPU test's expectations
per card ("gpu_test"), which the app needs at run time. The check compares it with what --write-swift would write.

  python3 tools/parity/devices.py           check; exit 1 on a difference
  python3 tools/parity/devices.py --check   the same
  python3 tools/parity/devices.py --list    the list itself, one device per line
  python3 tools/parity/devices.py --write-swift   (re)write app/Sources/SupportedDevices.swift
Python stdlib only.
"""
import json, os, plistlib, re, sys, textwrap

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))


def read(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, rel), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return f.read()


def one(rel, pattern, flags=0):
    """The first group of the only match of pattern in rel; raises when there is not exactly one."""
    m = re.findall(pattern, read(rel), flags)
    if len(m) != 1:
        raise ValueError('%d matches of %r (the check needs exactly one; update tools/parity/devices.py with the file)' % (len(m), pattern))
    return m[0]


def pci_match_ids(value):
    """IOPCIMatch / IOPCIPrimaryMatch '0xe20b8086 0xe20c8086' -> ['e20b', 'e20c']; a mask entry is an error."""
    ids = []
    for tok in value.split():
        m = re.fullmatch(r'0x([0-9a-fA-F]{4})8086', tok)
        if not m:
            raise ValueError('unexpected match entry %r' % tok)
        ids.append(m.group(1).lower())
    return ids


def plist_match(rel, personality):
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, rel), 'rb') as f:
        p = plistlib.load(f)['IOKitPersonalities'][personality]
    return pci_match_ids(p.get('IOPCIMatch') or p['IOPCIPrimaryMatch'])


def c_ids(text):
    return [x.lower() for x in re.findall(r'0x([0-9a-fA-F]{4})', text)]


def install_cards(rel):
    """install.sh CARDS=("e20b B580" "e20c B570 untested" "e212 Pro_B50 untested") -> [(id, name, untested)]; the
    script reads each entry with `read`, so a name's spaces are written as '_' there (and shown as spaces)"""
    body = one(rel, r'^CARDS=\(([^)]*)\)$', re.M)
    out = []
    for e in re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', body):
        f = e.split()
        out.append((f[0].lower(), f[1].replace('_', ' '), f[2:] == ['untested']))
    return out


def copies(sup):
    """(where, ids found, extra problems) for each copy of the list."""
    want = [(d['id'], d['name'], not d['tested']) for d in sup['devices']]
    res = []

    def add(where, fn):
        try:
            ids, extra = fn()
        except (ValueError, KeyError, OSError) as e:
            ids, extra = None, [str(e)]
        res.append((where, ids, extra))

    # IntelXe's personality; XeProbe's matches every Intel device by mask ('0x00008086&0x0000ffff') and is not a copy
    add('kernel/IntelXe/build.py IntelXe IOPCIMatch',
        lambda: (pci_match_ids(one('kernel/IntelXe/build.py', r"IOProviderClass='IOPCIDevice',IOPCIMatch='([^'&]*)'")), []))
    add('nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/Info-NMX-IntelXe.plist IOPCIPrimaryMatch',
        lambda: (plist_match('nullmoth/kexts/NVRM/accel/Info-NMX-IntelXe.plist', 'NMXAccel-IntelXe'), []))
    add('kernel/IntelXe/tests/platform_test.cpp kMatch',
        lambda: (c_ids(one('kernel/IntelXe/tests/platform_test.cpp', r'kMatch\[\] = \{([^}]*)\}')), []))
    for rel in ('release/templates/install.sh', 'release/install.sh'):
        def f(rel=rel):
            cards = install_cards(rel)
            extra = [] if cards == want else ['CARDS %r, expected %r (id, name, untested)' % (cards, want)]
            return [c[0] for c in cards], extra
        add(rel + ' CARDS', f)
    def efi_rules():
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'release/templates/efi-rules.json'), encoding='utf-8') as f:
            cards = json.load(f)['cards']
        extra = [] if cards.get('vendor_id') == '8086' else ['vendor_id %r, expected "8086"' % cards.get('vendor_id')]
        return [x.lower() for x in cards['device_ids']], extra
    add('release/templates/efi-rules.json cards.device_ids (efi.sh and windows/IntelXe-EFI.ps1 read it)', efi_rules)

    def app():
        body = one('app/Sources/Model.swift', r'^let supportedCards: \[\(id: String, name: String\)\] = \[(.*?)\]$', re.M | re.S)
        cards = re.findall(r'\("([0-9a-fA-F]{4})", "([^"]*)"\)', body)
        extra = ['name %r for %s, expected "Intel Arc %s"' % (n, i, w[1]) for (i, n), w in zip(cards, want) if n != 'Intel Arc ' + w[1]]
        return [i.lower() for i, _ in cards], extra
    add('app/Sources/Model.swift supportedCards', app)
    add('tools/clbench/clbench.c kSupported',
        lambda: (c_ids(one('tools/clbench/clbench.c', r'kSupported\[\] = \{([^}]*)\}')), []))
    return res


SWIFT = 'app/Sources/SupportedDevices.swift'


def swift_number(v):
    return ('%d' % v) if float(v).is_integer() else repr(float(v))


def swift_source(sup):
    """app/Sources/SupportedDevices.swift: the "gpu_test" figures of each supported device, keyed by PCI device id."""
    out = ['// Generated by tools/parity/devices.py --write-swift from data/platforms.json "supported" -- do not edit.',
           '// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT',
           '// What the GPU test (GPUTest.swift) expects of each supported card, by PCI device id (vendor 8086). A card that is',
           '// not listed gets no expectation and no verdict. tools/parity/devices.py fails when this file differs from the JSON.',
           '',
           'let gpuTestExpectations: [String: GPUTestExpectation] = [']
    for d in sup['devices']:
        g = d.get('gpu_test')
        if not g:
            continue
        out += textwrap.wrap('%s (8086:%s), %s. %s' % (d['name'], d['id'], 'measured' if g['measured'] else 'not measured', g['basis']),
                             120, initial_indent='    // ', subsequent_indent='    // ')
        t, m = g['fp32_tflops'], g['memory_gbs']
        out.append('    "%s": GPUTestExpectation(name: "%s", measured: %s,' % (d['id'], d['name'], 'true' if g['measured'] else 'false'))
        out.append('                               tflops: %s, tflopsGood: %s, tflopsFair: %s,' % tuple(swift_number(t[k]) for k in ('about', 'good', 'fair')))
        out.append('                               memoryGBs: %s, memoryGood: %s, memoryFair: %s),' % tuple(swift_number(m[k]) for k in ('about', 'good', 'fair')))
    out.append(']')
    return '\n'.join(out) + '\n'


def swift_problems(sup):
    try:
        have = read(SWIFT)
    except OSError:
        have = None
    if have != swift_source(sup):
        return ['%s is %s: python3 tools/parity/devices.py --write-swift' % (SWIFT, 'missing' if have is None else 'not what data/platforms.json gives')]
    return []


def tester_problems(sup):
    """BMG-G31: kernel/IntelXe/build.py G31_TESTER_MATCH (the "<kext>-G31" personalities, which IntelXe::start refuses
    unless the entry's tester boot-arg is set) must list exactly the kernel's kIdsBMGG31, none of them supported, and
    that entry must carry the boot-arg."""
    out = []
    try:
        match = pci_match_ids(one('kernel/IntelXe/build.py', r"^G31_TESTER_MATCH='([^'&]*)'$", re.M))
    except (ValueError, OSError) as e:
        return ['kernel/IntelXe/build.py G31_TESTER_MATCH: %s' % e]
    src = read('kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp')
    m = re.search(r'const uint16_t kIdsBMGG31\[\] = \{([^}]*)\}', src)
    g31 = c_ids(m.group(1)) if m else []
    if sorted(match) != sorted(g31):
        out.append('kernel/IntelXe/build.py G31_TESTER_MATCH lists %s, xe_platform.cpp kIdsBMGG31 %s' % (' '.join(match), ' '.join(g31)))
    both = set(match) & {d['id'] for d in sup['devices']}
    if both:
        out.append('kernel/IntelXe/build.py G31_TESTER_MATCH holds supported ids %s' % ' '.join(sorted(both)))
    if 'd.testerBootArg = g21 ? nullptr : "intelxe_allow_g31";' not in src:
        out.append('kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp: the G31 entry has no tester boot-arg intelxe_allow_g31')
    return out


def kernel_problems(sup):
    src = read('kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp')
    arr = sup['kernel_ids']
    m = re.search(r'const uint16_t %s\[\] = \{([^}]*)\}' % re.escape(arr), src)
    if not m:
        return ['kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp: no id array %s' % arr]
    have = set(c_ids(m.group(1)))
    out = ['kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp %s lacks %s' % (arr, d['id']) for d in sup['devices'] if d['id'] not in have]
    if not re.search(r'entry\("[^"]*", [^,]*, XP_IDS\(%s\),' % re.escape(arr), src):
        out.append('kernel/IntelXe/xe_platform.cpp: no kXePlatforms entry uses %s' % arr)
    return out


# Files that describe the supported cards to people: each must name every id (any case) and card.
MENTIONS = [
    ('README.md', 'id name'), ('README.tr.md', 'id name'),
    ('release/templates/README-INSTALL.md', 'id name'), ('release/templates/README-INSTALL.tr.md', 'id name'),
    ('efi/README.md', 'id name'), ('tools/parity/platforms.py', 'id name'),
    ('kernel/IntelXe/IntelXe.cpp', 'model'),   # the "model" property per card
]


def mention_problems(sup):
    out = []
    for rel, what in MENTIONS:
        text = read(rel)
        for d in sup['devices']:
            for w in what.split():
                needle = d[w]
                found = needle.lower() in text.lower() if w == 'id' else needle in text
                if not found:
                    out.append('%s does not name %s (%s)' % (rel, needle, w))
    return out


def main():
    sup = json.loads(read('data/platforms.json'))['supported']
    ids = [d['id'] for d in sup['devices']]
    if '--list' in sys.argv[1:]:
        for d in sup['devices']:
            print('8086:%s  %s  %-26s %s' % (d['id'], d['name'], d['model'], 'tested' if d['tested'] else 'untested'))
        return 0
    if '--write-swift' in sys.argv[1:]:
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, SWIFT), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(swift_source(sup))
        print('wrote ' + SWIFT)
        return 0
    bad = 0
    for where, got, extra in copies(sup):
        if got is not None and sorted(got) == sorted(ids) and len(got) == len(set(got)) and not extra:
            print('ok    %s: %s' % (where, ' '.join(got)))
            continue
        bad += 1
        why = extra or ['lists %s, data/platforms.json "supported" has %s' % (' '.join(got or []), ' '.join(ids))]
        print('FAIL  %s: %s' % (where, '; '.join(why)))
    for p in kernel_problems(sup) + tester_problems(sup) + mention_problems(sup) + swift_problems(sup):
        bad += 1
        print('FAIL  ' + p)
    if not bad:
        print('ok    kernel descriptor %s holds every id; %d files name every card' % (sup['kernel_ids'], len(MENTIONS)))
        print('ok    BMG-G31 tester personality (build.py G31_TESTER_MATCH) = kIdsBMGG31, boot-arg -intelxe_allow_g31')
        print('ok    %s is what data/platforms.json gives' % SWIFT)
    print('devices: %d supported (%s), %d problem(s)' % (len(ids), ' '.join(ids), bad))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Re-measure the code numbers (Linux functions, xe uAPI) at every repository commit that changed kernel/ and write
them to data/history.json (oldest first). CTS and video columns stay empty for these rows: those results are tied to
test runs, not to commits. Run once; tools/parity/build.sh appends the current state afterwards.

  python3 tools/parity/history_backfill.py --linux <linux tree> [--scratch <dir>]
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def git(*a):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', ROOT] + list(a), check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--linux', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--scratch', default=None)
    ap.add_argument('--out', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/history.json'))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    tmp = a.scratch or tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='parity-history-')
    commits = git('log', '--reverse', '--format=%h\t%ci\t%s', '--', 'kernel').strip().splitlines()
    hist = []
    for line in commits:
        h, date, subj = line.split('\t')
        d = os.path.join(tmp, h)
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        tar = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', ROOT, 'archive', h, 'kernel'], check=True, capture_output=True).stdout
        subprocess.run(['tar', '-x', '-C', d], input=tar, check=True)
        kdir, fdir = os.path.join(d, 'kernel/IntelXe'), os.path.join(d, 'kernel/IntelXeFB')
        os.makedirs(kdir, exist_ok=True)
        os.makedirs(fdir, exist_ok=True)
        pj, uj = os.path.join(d, 'parity.json'), os.path.join(d, 'uapi.json')
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, 'scan.py'), '--linux', a.linux, '--kernel', kdir, '--fb', fdir,
                        '--out', pj], check=True, capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(HERE, 'uapi.py'), '--linux', a.linux, '--kernel', kdir, '--fb', fdir,
                        '--out', uj], check=True, capture_output=True)
        k = json.load(open(pj))['summary']['kernel']
        u = json.load(open(uj))['summary']
        m = re.match(r'kernel/IntelXe(?:FB)?: ([^,(]+)', subj)
        m2 = re.match(r'Add the (\S+)', subj)
        label = ('FB ' if 'IntelXeFB:' in subj else '') + (m.group(1).strip() if m else (m2.group(1) if m2 else subj[:24]))
        hist.append({'date': date[:16], 'commit': h, 'dirty': False, 'label': label[:28],
                     'kernel_commit': None, 'fb_commit': None, 'linux_rev': json.load(open(pj))['meta']['linux']['rev'],
                     'functions_matched': k['functions_matched'], 'functions_total': k['functions_total'],
                     'functions_pct': k['pct_functions_matched'], 'uapi_implemented': u['implemented'],
                     'uapi_total': u['cells'], 'uapi_pct': u['pct_implemented'], 'cts_run': None, 'cts_cases': None,
                     'cts_pass': None, 'cts_pass_pct': None, 'video_decode_exact': None, 'video_decode_clips': None,
                     'source': 'backfill: re-measured from commit %s' % h})
        print(h, date[:16], label, k['pct_functions_matched'], u['pct_implemented'])
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(a.out), exist_ok=True)
    json.dump(hist, open(a.out, 'w'), indent=1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One work list from every parity source, ordered by the target (docs/devices/b580.md): docs/parity/NEXT.md.

Sources, each item keeps its evidence:
  docs/devices/b580.md (Turkish tables)   rows marked 🟥 (tested, below the target); ⬜ rows are listed as "not tested yet"
  data/video.json (video.py)        cells graded 'fail' (decode slower than Windows / not bit-exact, encode BD-rate or
                                    overshoot against Intel QSV)
  data/cts/runs.json + <run>.tsv.gz the newest CTS run: Fail / Crash / Timeout cases, and NotSupported counts per group
  data/uapi.json (consumers.py)     needed_now items (red); needed_future items (orange) only as counts per feature
Nothing is estimated: an item appears only because one of these files says so.

  python3 tools/parity/next.py
"""
import collections, gzip, json, os, re

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
TARGETS = {1: 'Ekran / Display', 2: '3B / 3D', 3: 'Video', 4: 'Kararlılık / Stability'}


def parity_rows():
    """(target, section, item, status, vs_target, source) for the 🟥 and ⬜ rows of the Turkish tables of docs/devices/b580.md."""
    text = open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'docs/devices/b580.md')).read().split('\n## English')[0]
    rows, section, target = [], '', None
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        m = re.match(r'### (\d+)\. (.+)', line)
        if m:
            section = m.group(2)
            t = re.search(r'hedef (\d)', section)
            target = int(t.group(1)) if t else None
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip('|').split('|')] if line.startswith('|') else []
        # the 4-column evidence tables: item | macOS | vs target | source (the video codec matrix is read from video.json)
        if len(cells) == 4 and cells[1] in ('🟥', '⬜') and target:
            rows.append((target, section, cells[0], cells[1], cells[2], cells[3]))
    return rows


def video_fails():
    v = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/video.json')))
    return [c for c in v['cells'] if c['grade'] == 'fail']


def cts_newest():
    runs = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/cts/runs.json')))
    run = runs[-1]
    bad, ns = [], collections.Counter()
    p = os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/cts/%s.tsv.gz' % run['id'])
    if os.path.exists(p):
        for line in gzip.open(p, 'rt'):
            f = line.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
            if len(f) < 2:
                continue
            case, st = f[0], f[1]
            if st in ('Fail', 'Crash', 'Timeout', 'InternalError', 'ResourceError'):
                bad.append((case, st))
            elif st == 'NotSupported':
                ns['.'.join(case.split('.')[:2])] += 1
    return run, bad, ns


def main():
    u = json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/uapi.json')))
    red = [c for c in u['cells'] if c.get('need') == 'needed_now']
    orange = collections.Counter()
    for c in u['cells']:
        if c.get('need') == 'needed_future':
            for f in sorted({x['feature'] for x in c['consumers'] if x['kind'] == 'future'}):
                orange[f] += 1
    rows = parity_rows()
    vf = video_fails()
    run, bad, ns = cts_newest()

    L = ['# Sıradaki işler / Next work', '',
         'Üretildi / generated: `tools/parity/next.py` (`tools/parity/build.sh`). Kaynaklar / sources: `docs/devices/b580.md`, '
         '`data/video.json`, `data/cts/runs.json` (newest run), `data/uapi.json`. Her satır kanıtını taşır; tahmin yok. '
         'Sıra hedefe göre (docs/devices/b580.md): 1 ekran, 2 3B, 3 video, 4 kararlılık; sonra çekirdek arayüzü ve gelecek hedefler.', '',
         'Every line carries its evidence; nothing is estimated. Ordered by the target in docs/devices/b580.md.', '']
    n = 0
    for t in sorted(TARGETS):
        items = [r for r in rows if r[0] == t and r[3] == '🟥']
        untested = [r for r in rows if r[0] == t and r[3] == '⬜']
        vids = vf if t == 3 else []
        ctsb = bad if t == 2 else []
        if not (items or untested or vids or ctsb):
            continue
        L += ['## %d. %s' % (t, TARGETS[t]), '']
        if items or vids or ctsb:
            L += ['| # | İş / item | Durum / status | Kanıt / evidence |', '|---|---|---|---|']
            for r in items:
                n += 1
                L.append('| %d | %s | %s | %s |' % (n, r[2], r[4], r[5]))
            for c in vids:
                n += 1
                name = '%s %s %d-bit %s' % ({'h264': 'H.264', 'hevc': 'HEVC', 'av1': 'AV1', 'vp9': 'VP9'}[c['codec']],
                                           {'decode': 'çözme / decode', 'encode': 'kodlama / encode'}[c['dir']], c['bits'], c['res'])
                L.append('| %d | %s | hedefin altında / below target | %s (`data/video.json`) |' % (n, name, c['note'].replace('|', '/')))
            for case, st in ctsb:
                n += 1
                L.append('| %d | CTS `%s` | %s | koşu / run %s |' % (n, case, st, run['id']))
            L.append('')
        if untested:
            L += ['Test edilmedi / not tested yet: ' + '; '.join(r[2] for r in untested) + '.', '']
    L += ['## 5. Çekirdek arayüzü / Kernel interface (xe uAPI)', '',
          'Bugün çalışan yazılımın kullandığı, çekirdeğimizde olmayan ögeler (ayrıntı ve tüketici satırları: [TODO.md](TODO.md)):', '']
    if red:
        L += ['| # | Öge / item | Neden / why |', '|---|---|---|']
        for c in red:
            n += 1
            L.append('| %d | `%s` | %s |' % (n, c['token'], c.get('need_why', '').replace('|', '/')))
    else:
        L.append('Yok / none.')
    L += ['', '## 6. Desteklenmeyen Vulkan özellikleri / Vulkan features reported as not supported', '',
          'CTS koşusu / run %s: grup başına NotSupported sayısı (bir özelliğin eksik olduğunu gösterir, hata değildir).' % run['id'], '',
          '| Grup / group | NotSupported |', '|---|---|']
    for g, k in ns.most_common(15):
        L.append('| `%s` | %d |' % (g, k))
    L += ['', '## 7. Gelecek hedefler / Future targets (xe uAPI, turuncu / orange)', '',
          '| Özellik / feature | Öge sayısı / items |', '|---|---|']
    for f, k in orange.most_common():
        L.append('| %s | %d |' % (f, k))
    open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'docs/parity/NEXT.md'), 'w').write('\n'.join(L) + '\n')
    print('next: %d items by target, CTS run %s (%d bad), uAPI red %d' % (n, run['id'], len(bad), len(red)))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
