#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The driver's scope across Intel GPU platforms: one matrix of platform x feature, two facts per cell.

  (a) what Intel's own stack offers on that platform, from upstream sources only: data/platforms.json "intel" (Linux xe /
      i915 display descriptors, Mesa's device list, compute-runtime's product directories, each with its line), and for
      the video rows data/caps.json (tools/parity/caps.py: intel/media-driver's capability tables);
  (b) our status, one of: works (verified on the device named, with the date and where the evidence is), same (same
      code path, untested on this platform), not yet; or "-" where Intel does not offer it either. From
      data/platforms.json "ours", and for the B580's video rows from data/video.json (the mediakit runs).

Outputs: docs/parity/svg/platforms.svg, docs/PLATFORMS.md (every cell with its sources), and the table between
<!-- platforms:begin --> and <!-- platforms:end --> in README.md. No estimates. Python stdlib only.

  python3 tools/parity/platforms.py
"""
import json, os, re, sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from render import svg, text, write, FONT  # noqa: E402  (same SVG style as the other status images)
from xml.sax.saxutils import escape  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
CODECS = [('h264', 'H.264'), ('hevc', 'HEVC'), ('vp9', 'VP9'), ('av1', 'AV1')]
ICON = {'works': '🟩', 'same': '🟨', 'notyet': '⬜', 'na': '—'}
CLS = {'works': 'ok', 'same': 'warn', 'notyet': 'empty', 'na': 'ns'}
SHORT = {'works': 'works', 'same': 'same code, untested', 'notyet': 'not yet', 'na': 'not offered by Intel'}


def size_txt(w, h):
    if not w:
        return ''
    k = {4096: '4K', 8192: '8K', 16384: '16K'}
    return ' ≤%s' % k.get(w, '%dx%d' % (w, h)) if w == h or h in (12288,) else ' ≤%dx%d' % (w, h)


def intel_video(caps, plat, codec, d):
    """(short text, source) of what media-driver offers for codec/d on the platform, or (None, why) if nothing."""
    p = next(x for x in caps['platforms'] if x['id'] == plat)
    s = p['summary'].get(codec, {}).get(d)
    if not s:
        return None, 'media-driver %s: no %s %s entrypoint (%s)' % (caps['meta']['commit'][:12], codec, d, p['source'])
    bits420 = sorted({int(c.split('-')[0]) for c in s['coded'] if c.endswith(' 420')}) or s['bits']
    txt = '%s-bit%s' % ('/'.join(map(str, bits420)), size_txt(s['max_w'], s['max_h']))
    return txt, 'media-driver %s: %s' % (caps['meta']['commit'][:12], ', '.join(s['src'][:3]) + (' ...' if len(s['src']) > 3 else ''))


def intelxe_video(v, codec, d):
    """(status, evidence, date) of our B580 video row from data/video.json."""
    cells = [c for c in v['cells'] if c['codec'] == codec and c['dir'] == d]
    measured = [c for c in cells if c.get('items') or c.get('speed')]
    if all(c['grade'] == 'unsupported' for c in cells):
        return 'na', 'not offered by Intel on Xe2 (data/caps.json)', '', ''
    if not measured:
        return 'notyet', 'not measured', '', ''
    res = {'1080p': 1080, '2160p': 2160, '4320p': 4320}
    ok, bad = [], []
    for c in measured:
        tag = '%d-bit %s' % (c['bits'], c['res'])
        if d == 'decode':
            (ok if all(i['exact'] for i in c['items']) else bad).append(tag)
        else:
            (bad if c.get('failed_streams') else ok).append(tag)
    test = any('test stack' in (i.get('stack') or '') for c in measured for i in c.get('items', []))
    top = max(ok, key=lambda t: res[t.split()[1]]) if ok else None
    ev = ('%s %s up to %s' % ('bit-exact' if d == 'decode' else 'streams', 'in %d cells' % len(ok), top.split()[1])) if ok else 'no good cell'
    if bad:
        ev += '; failed: %s' % ', '.join(bad)
    if test:
        ev += '; measured with a test stack (not the installed one)'
    date = max(re.findall(r'\w{3} (\w{3}) +(\d+) [\d:]+ \+\d+ (\d{4})', ' '.join(v['meta']['runs'])) or [('', '', '')], key=lambda x: x[1])
    months = {'Oct': '10', 'Nov': '11'}
    when = '%s-%s-%02d' % (date[2], months.get(date[0], date[0]), int(date[1])) if date[2] else ''
    name = {1080: '1080p', 2160: '4K', 4320: '8K'}
    scope = ('%s-bit ≤%s' % ('/'.join(sorted({t.split('-')[0] for t in ok}, key=int)), name[res[top.split()[1]]])) if ok else ''
    return ('works' if ok else 'notyet'), ev, '%s, data/video.json (graded in docs/devices/b580.md)' % when, scope


def build(P, caps, v):
    """rows: [(feature id, english, turkish, {platform id: (status, ours text, evidence, intel text, intel source)})]"""
    rows = []
    for f in P['features']:
        if f['id'] == 'video':
            for codec, name in CODECS:
                for d in ('decode', 'encode'):
                    cells = {}
                    for p in P['platforms']:
                        it, isrc = intel_video(caps, p['caps'], codec, d)
                        scope = ''
                        if p['id'] == 'b580':
                            st, ev, when, scope = intelxe_video(v, codec, d)
                            if it is None:
                                st = 'na'
                        else:
                            st, ev, when = ('na', '', '') if it is None else ('notyet', '', '')
                        cells[p['id']] = (st, ev, when, it or '-', isrc, '', scope)
                    rows.append(('video-%s-%s' % (codec, d), '%s %s' % (name, d), '%s %s' % (name, {'decode': 'çözme', 'encode': 'kodlama'}[d]), cells))
            continue
        cells = {}
        for p in P['platforms']:
            st, ev, when = P['ours'][f['id']][p['id']][:3]
            dev = (P['ours'][f['id']][p['id']][3:] or [''])[0]
            it, isrc = P['intel'][f['id']][p['id']]
            cells[p['id']] = (st, ev, when, it, isrc, dev)
        rows.append((f['id'], f['en'], f['tr'], cells))
    return rows


SVG_TR = {
    'title': 'Intel GPU platformları: bizim durumumuz (renk ve ilk satır; videoda doğrulanmış kapsamımız) ve Intel\'in kendi Linux sürücülerinin sunduğu (ikinci satır)',
    'sources': 'Kaynaklar: Linux xe/i915 ekran kodu, Mesa cihaz listesi, compute-runtime, media-driver %s yetenek tabloları; her kutunun kanıtı docs/PLATFORMS.md\'de',
    'works': 'çalışıyor', 'same': 'aynı kod, denenmedi', 'notyet': 'henüz yok', 'na': 'Intel sunmuyor',
    'legend': [('ok', 'çalışıyor, adı geçen kartta doğrulandı'), ('warn', 'kod aynı, bu platformda denenmedi'),
               ('empty', 'henüz yok'), ('ns', 'Intel de bu platformda sunmuyor')],
    'video': 'Video: Intel satırı = 4:2:0\'da bit derinlikleri ve media-driver VA-API yeteneklerindeki en büyük görüntü; Gen12/DG2\'nin eski kodunda boyut tablosu yok',
    'one': 'Şimdiye kadar doğrulanan tek kart: Arc B580 (8086:E20B); IntelXe.kext B570\'e (E20C, 0.1.4\'ten beri), Pro B60 ve Pro B50\'ye (E211, E212) de bağlanıyor, bunlar denenmedi. Kanıt: docs/devices/b580.md',
    'svgtitle': 'Intel GPU platformları',
}


def svg_view(P, rows, caps, lang='en'):
    cols = P['platforms']
    TRL = lang == 'tr'
    tx = tr_text if TRL else (lambda s: s)
    short = (lambda st: SVG_TR[st]) if TRL else (lambda st: SHORT[st])
    ptitle = (lambda p: TR_PLATFORM.get(p['short'], p['short'])) if TRL else (lambda p: p['short'])
    cw, ch, x0, y0 = 150, 40, 300, 96
    W, H = x0 + cw * len(cols) + 12, y0 + ch * len(rows) + 84
    body = [text(12, 22, SVG_TR['title'] if TRL else 'Intel GPU platforms: our status (colour, first line; for video our verified scope) and what Intel\'s own Linux stack offers (second line)', 't'),
            text(12, 40, (SVG_TR['sources'] if TRL else 'sources: Linux xe/i915 display, Mesa device list, compute-runtime, media-driver %s caps tables; ours: evidence per cell (docs/PLATFORMS.md)') % caps['meta']['commit'][:12])]
    for i, p in enumerate(cols):
        body.append(text(x0 + i * cw + cw / 2, y0 - 22, ptitle(p), 'l', 'middle'))
        body.append(text(x0 + i * cw + cw / 2, y0 - 8, p['title'].split(':')[0], 's', 'middle'))
    for j, (fid, en, tr, cells) in enumerate(rows):
        y = y0 + j * ch
        name = tr if TRL else en
        body.append(text(12, y + ch / 2 + 4, name if len(name) < 48 else name[:46] + '…', 'l'))
        for i, p in enumerate(cols):
            st, ev, when, it, isrc, dev = cells[p['id']][:6]
            x = x0 + i * cw
            body.append('<rect x="%d" y="%d" width="%d" height="%d" rx="4" class="%s"><title>%s</title></rect>' % (
                x + 2, y + 2, cw - 4, ch - 4, CLS[st], escape('%s / %s: %s%s. Intel: %s (%s)' % (ptitle(p), name, short(st), (' - ' + ev) if ev else '', tx(it), isrc))))
            ink = {'ok': '#ffffff', 'warn': '#0b0b0b'}.get(CLS[st])
            scope = cells[p['id']][6] if len(cells[p['id']]) > 6 else ''
            # a verified video cell shows our own scope (it can be narrower than Intel's, on the second line)
            w_ = short('works')
            first = ('%s: %s' % (w_, tx(scope)) if scope else '%s (%s)' % (w_, dev or ('B580' if p['id'] == 'b580' else '?'))) if st == 'works' else short(st)
            second = '' if it in ('-', '') else 'Intel: ' + tx(it)
            for yy, s_, wgt in ((y + (17 if second else 24), first, 600), (y + 31, second, 400)):
                if not s_:
                    continue
                s_ = s_ if len(s_) <= 26 else s_[:25] + '…'
                if ink:
                    body.append('<text x="%.1f" y="%.1f" text-anchor="middle" style="fill:%s;font:%d 10.5px %s">%s</text>' % (x + cw / 2, yy, ink, wgt, FONT.replace("'", ''), escape(s_)))
                else:
                    body.append(text(x + cw / 2, yy, s_, 'l' if wgt == 600 else 's', 'middle'))
    ly = y0 + ch * len(rows) + 24
    lx = 12
    legend = SVG_TR['legend'] if TRL else [('ok', 'works, verified on the device named'), ('warn', 'same code path, untested on this platform'),
                                         ('empty', 'not yet'), ('ns', 'not offered by Intel on this platform either')]
    for cls, name in legend:
        body.append('<rect x="%d" y="%d" width="10" height="10" rx="2" class="%s"/>' % (lx, ly - 9, cls))
        body.append(text(lx + 14, ly, name))
        lx += 34 + int(len(name) * 6.2)
    body.append(text(12, ly + 20, SVG_TR['video'] if TRL else 'video: Intel = bit depths (4:2:0) and largest picture in media-driver\'s VA-API caps; Gen12/DG2 legacy code gives no size table'))
    body.append(text(12, ly + 36, SVG_TR['one'] if TRL else 'one device verified so far: the Arc B580 (8086:E20B); IntelXe.kext also attaches, untested, to the B570 (E20C, since 0.1.4), the Pro B60 and the Pro B50 (E211, E212). Evidence: docs/devices/b580.md'))
    return svg(W, H, ''.join(body), SVG_TR['svgtitle'] if TRL else 'Intel GPU platforms')


# Turkish for the compact table of README.tr.md: whole cell texts and the platform column titles that need it.
TR_CELL = {
    'ANV, Vulkan Video encode H.264/H.265': 'ANV, Vulkan Video kodlama H.264/H.265',
    'ANV, Vulkan Video encode incl. AV1': 'ANV, AV1 dahil Vulkan Video kodlama',
    'ANV; Vulkan Video encode off upstream on Xe2': "ANV; Xe2'de Vulkan Video kodlama upstream'de kapalı",
    'ANV; Vulkan Video encode off upstream on Xe3': "ANV; Xe3'te Vulkan Video kodlama upstream'de kapalı",
    'xe (default driver)': 'xe (varsayılan sürücü)',
    'xe GuC engine reset': 'xe GuC motor sıfırlama',
    'xe GuC engine reset, job timeout': 'xe GuC motor sıfırlama, iş zaman aşımı',
}
TR_PLATFORM = {'B570, other BMG': 'B570, diğer BMG'}


def tr_text(s):
    s = TR_CELL.get(s, s)
    return s.replace('-bit', '-bit')


def md_compact(P, rows, lang='en'):
    cols = P['platforms']
    tr = lang == 'tr'
    title = (lambda p: TR_PLATFORM.get(p['short'], p['short'])) if tr else (lambda p: p['short'])
    txt = tr_text if tr else (lambda s: s)
    ours, intel = ('bizim', 'Intel') if tr else ('ours', 'Intel')
    out = ['| | ' + ' | '.join(title(p) for p in cols) + ' |', '|---|' + '---|' * len(cols)]
    for fid, en, tr_name, cells in rows:
        # a verified cell names our own scope first when it is narrower than Intel's offer (e.g. VP9 8/10-bit vs 12-bit)
        cell = lambda c: ICON[c[0]] if c[0] == 'na' or c[3] in ('-', '') else (
            '%s %s %s · %s %s' % (ICON[c[0]], ours, txt(c[6]), intel, txt(c[3]).replace('|', '/')) if len(c) > 6 and c[6] and c[6] != c[3]
            else '%s %s' % (ICON[c[0]], txt(c[3]).replace('|', '/')))
        out.append('| %s | %s |' % (tr_name if tr else en, ' | '.join(cell(cells[p['id']]) for p in cols)))
    return '\n'.join(out)


def md_full(P, rows, caps, v):
    L = ['# Platformlar / Platforms', '',
         'Üretildi / generated: `tools/parity/platforms.py` (`tools/parity/build.sh`) from `data/platforms.json`, `data/caps.json`, '
         '`data/video.json`. Elle değiştirmeyin / do not edit by hand.', '',
         '**TR:** Her hücrede iki bilgi var: Intel\'in kendi yığınının o platformda sunduğu (yalnızca kaynaktan, satırıyla) ve bizim '
         'durumumuz: 🟩 çalışıyor, adı geçen cihazda doğrulandı (tarih ve kanıt) · 🟨 aynı kod yolu, bu platformda test edilmedi · '
         '⬜ henüz yok · — Intel de sunmuyor. Tahmin yok.', '',
         '**EN:** Two facts per cell: what Intel\'s own stack offers on the platform (from sources only, with the line) and our '
         'status: 🟩 works, verified on the device named (date and evidence) · 🟨 same code path, untested on this platform · '
         '⬜ not yet · — not offered by Intel either. No estimates.', '',
         'Kaynak ağaçlar / source trees: ' + '; '.join('%s: %s' % (k, s) for k, s in P['sources'].items()) +
         '; media-driver: %s %s (%s).' % (caps['meta']['commit'][:12], caps['meta']['date'], caps['meta']['build']), '',
         '![Intel GPU platforms](parity/svg/platforms.svg)', '', '## Platformlar / platforms', '']
    for p in P['platforms']:
        cp = next(x for x in caps['platforms'] if x['id'] == p['caps'])
        L.append('- **%s** — %s media-driver device IDs (%s): %s.' % (p['title'], p['detail'], cp['device_ids_source'], ', '.join(cp['device_ids'])))
    L.append('')
    for fid, en, tr, cells in rows:
        L += ['## %s / %s' % (tr, en), '', '| Platform | Bizim durum / our status | Kanıt / evidence | Intel | Intel kaynak / source |', '|---|---|---|---|---|']
        for p in P['platforms']:
            st, ev, when, it, isrc, dev = cells[p['id']][:6]
            L.append('| %s | %s %s | %s | %s | %s |' % (p['short'], ICON[st], SHORT[st], '; '.join(x for x in (ev, when) if x).replace('|', '/') or '—',
                                                     it.replace('|', '/'), (isrc or '—').replace('|', '/')))
        L.append('')
    L += ['## Video yeteneği, platform başına / video capability per platform (media-driver)', '',
          'Her codec ve yön için VA-API profilleri, `VAConfigAttribRTFormat` bit derinlikleri ve en büyük resim; satır numaralı kaynak '
          '`data/caps.json`\'da. / VA-API profiles, bit depths from `VAConfigAttribRTFormat` and the largest picture per codec and '
          'direction; every entry\'s source line is in `data/caps.json`.', '',
          '| media-driver platform | codec | decode | encode |', '|---|---|---|---|']
    for cp in caps['platforms']:
        for codec, name in CODECS + [('jpeg', 'JPEG'), ('vp8', 'VP8'), ('mpeg2', 'MPEG-2'), ('vvc', 'VVC')]:
            s = cp['summary'].get(codec)
            if not s:
                continue
            f = lambda d: '—' if d not in s else '%s%s%s' % (', '.join(s[d]['coded']) or 'yes', size_txt(s[d]['max_w'], s[d]['max_h']),
                                                              (' (' + ', '.join(s[d]['profiles']) + ')') if s[d]['profiles'] else '')
            L.append('| %s (%s) | %s | %s | %s |' % (cp['name'], cp['id'], name, f('decode'), f('encode')))
    L.append('')
    return '\n'.join(L)


def main():
    D = lambda n: json.load(open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'data', n)))
    P, caps, v = D('platforms.json'), D('caps.json'), D('video.json')
    rows = build(P, caps, v)
    write('platforms.svg', svg_view(P, rows, caps))
    write('platforms.tr.svg', svg_view(P, rows, caps, 'tr'))
    open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'docs/PLATFORMS.md'), 'w').write(md_full(P, rows, caps, v))
    m = None
    for readme in ('README.md', 'README.tr.md'):   # README.tr.md gets the table in Turkish
        rp = os.path.join(ROOT, readme)
        if not os.path.exists(rp):
            continue
        r = open(rp).read()
        mm = re.search(r'(<!-- platforms:begin -->\n)(.*?)(<!-- platforms:end -->)', r, re.S)
        if mm:
            m = mm
            r = r[:mm.start(2)] + md_compact(P, rows, 'tr' if readme.endswith('.tr.md') else 'en') + '\n' + r[mm.end(2):]
            open(rp, 'w').write(r)
    n = {}
    for _, _, _, cells in rows:
        for st, *_ in cells.values():
            n[st] = n.get(st, 0) + 1
    print('platforms: %d rows x %d platforms; %s%s' % (len(rows), len(P['platforms']), n, '' if m else ' (README has no platforms markers)'))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()



================================================
FILE: tools/parity/scan.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Code parity scan, evidence only. One record per upstream source file.

Upstream: Linux drivers/gpu/drm/xe, drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display, include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h; Mesa src/intel/{vulkan,
common,isl,blorp}, src/vulkan/wsi (+ this repository's user/xemac as "ours").

Kernel statuses are COMPUTED, never asserted:
  ported      every function the upstream file defines (headers without functions: every #define) occurs by name in
              our sources (code or a comment citing it); the matches are stored with file:line (enclosing symbol)
  partial     some of them occur (matched/total stored)
  unverified  none occurs and there is no machine-checked proof of absence
  missing     map.json gives a proof that this script checks: "refuse" regexes that must match in our sources and/or
              "absent" tokens (names, register offsets) that must not occur; a failed proof gives "unverified"
  not_applicable  from map.json with a reason category (linux = Linux-only interface, hw = hardware the B580 lacks)
Mesa statuses: upstream (unchanged from the base commit and compiled), patched (changed by our series), ours (added
by our series, or user/xemac), not_built (not in compile_commands.json; a header follows its .c of the same stem).

  python3 tools/parity/scan.py --linux <linux tree> [--mesa <tree> --mesa-build <build dir>] [--html docs/parity/index.html]
Python stdlib only. --html replaces the JSON embedded in the page (script id="parity-data").
"""
import argparse, datetime, fnmatch, json, os, re, subprocess, sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
SRC_EXT = ('.c', '.h', '.cpp', '.hpp', '.m', '.mm', '.inc')
LINUX_SETS = [('xe/', 'drivers/gpu/drm/xe'), ('display/', 'drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display')]
LINUX_FILES = [('uapi/xe_drm.h', 'include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h')]
MESA_DIRS = ['src/intel/vulkan', 'src/intel/common', 'src/intel/isl', 'src/intel/blorp', 'src/vulkan/wsi']

FDEF = re.compile(r'^(?:static\s+)?(?:inline\s+)?(?:const\s+)?(?:struct\s+|enum\s+|unsigned\s+)?[A-Za-z_0-9]+[\s\*]+\**'
                  r'([a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)\s*\(', re.M)
MDEF = re.compile(r'^#define\s+([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]+)', re.M)
CPP_HEAD = re.compile(r'^(?![\s#/{}])(?!(?:if|for|while|switch|return|else|do|case|typedef|using|namespace|extern)\b)'
                      r'[^;=]*?\b([A-Za-z_~][\w:~]*)\s*\(')
IDENT = re.compile(r'0[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]+|[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*')


def git(tree, *args):
    return subprocess.run(['git', '-C', tree] + list(args), check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def walk(base):
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(base):
        dirs.sort()
        for f in sorted(files):
            if f.endswith(SRC_EXT):
                yield os.path.join(root, f)


def count_lines(p):
    with open(p, 'rb') as f:
        return sum(1 for _ in f)


def norm(t):
    return t.lower() if t[:2] in ('0x', '0X') else t


class OurIndex:
    """token -> [(file, line, enclosing symbol, 'code'|'comment')] over our sources (uapi copies excluded)."""

    def __init__(self, dirs):
        self.occ, self.text = {}, {}
        for label, d in dirs:
            for p in walk(d):
                rel = os.path.relpath(p, d)
                if rel.split(os.sep)[0] in ('uapi', 'tests', 'build', 'scripts'):
                    continue
                name = label + '/' + rel
                s = open(p, errors='ignore').read()
                self.text[name] = s
                self._index(name, s)

    def _index(self, name, s):
        depth, cur, cand, in_block = 0, None, None, False
        for no, line in enumerate(s.split('\n'), 1):
            code, comment, i = '', '', 0
            while i < len(line):
                if in_block:
                    j = line.find('*/', i)
                    if j < 0:
                        comment += line[i:]
                        break
                    comment += line[i:j]
                    i, in_block = j + 2, False
                elif line.startswith('//', i):
                    comment += line[i:]
                    break
                elif line.startswith('/*', i):
                    in_block, i = True, i + 2
                else:
                    code += line[i]
                    i += 1
            if depth == 0:
                mm = CPP_HEAD.match(code)
                if mm and not code.rstrip().endswith(';'):
                    cand = mm.group(1)
            sym = cur or 'file scope'
            for kind, part in (('code', code), ('comment', comment)):
                for t in set(IDENT.findall(part)):
                    self.occ.setdefault(norm(t), []).append((name, no, sym, kind))
            for ch in code:
                if ch == '{':
                    if depth == 0:
                        cur = cand
                    depth += 1
                elif ch == '}':
                    depth = max(0, depth - 1)
                    if depth == 0:
                        cur, cand = None, None

    def find(self, tok):
        return self.occ.get(norm(tok), [])


def first_rule(rules, path):
    for r in rules:
        if any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path, g) for g in r['match']):
            return r
    return None


def group_of(groups, path):
    for g, name in groups:
        if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path, g):
            return name
    return 'Other'


def upstream_items(path):
    s = open(path, errors='ignore').read()
    fns = sorted(x for x in set(FDEF.findall(s)) if '_' in x and len(x) > 6)
    if fns:
        return 'functions', fns
    return 'macros', sorted(x for x in set(MDEF.findall(s)) if len(x) > 5 and not x.startswith('__'))


def check_proof(proof, idx):
    """(ok, details): every 'refuse' regex must match in our sources, no 'absent' token may occur."""
    det, ok = [], True
    for rx in proof.get('refuse', []):
        hit = None
        for f, s in idx.text.items():
            mm = re.search(rx, s)
            if mm:
                hit = '%s:%d' % (f, s.count('\n', 0, mm.start()) + 1)
                break
        det.append({'check': 'refuse', 'pattern': rx, 'found_at': hit})
        ok = ok and hit is not None
    for tok in proof.get('absent', []):
        occ = idx.find(tok)
        det.append({'check': 'absent', 'token': tok, 'found_at': ['%s:%d' % (o[0], o[1]) for o in occ[:3]]})
        ok = ok and not occ
    return ok, det


def tree_id(path):
    try:
        top = git(path, 'rev-parse', '--show-toplevel').strip()
        # a linked worktree is named after its repository (the directory of the common .git), not its own directory
        common = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(top, git(path, 'rev-parse', '--git-common-dir').strip()))
        repo = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(common)) if os.path.basename(common) == '.git' else os.path.basename(top)
        return {'path': os.path.relpath(path, top), 'repo': repo,
                'repo_head': git(top, 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD').strip(),
                'last_commit': git(path, 'log', '-1', '--format=%h %cs', '--', '.').strip(),
                'dirty': bool(git(path, 'status', '--porcelain', '--', '.').strip())}
    except Exception:
        return {'path': path, 'repo': None, 'repo_head': None, 'last_commit': None, 'dirty': None}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--linux', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--kernel', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'kernel/IntelXe'))
    ap.add_argument('--fb', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'kernel/IntelXeFB'))
    ap.add_argument('--mesa')
    ap.add_argument('--mesa-base', default='f01e9b07a91f7e7ab730edfbb383b083f146067b')
    ap.add_argument('--mesa-build')
    ap.add_argument('--map', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'tools/parity/map.json'))
    ap.add_argument('--out', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/parity.json'))
    ap.add_argument('--html')
    a = ap.parse_args()

    mp = json.load(open(a.map))
    rules, groups = mp['rules'], mp['groups']
    warnings, files = [], []
    idx = OurIndex([('kernel/IntelXe', a.kernel), ('kernel/IntelXeFB', a.fb)])
    try:
        lrev, ldate = git(a.linux, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD').strip(), git(a.linux, 'log', '-1', '--format=%cs').strip()
        lver = '.'.join(l.split('=')[1].strip() for l in git(a.linux, 'show', 'HEAD:Makefile').splitlines()[1:4])
    except Exception:
        lrev, ldate, lver = 'unknown', '', ''

    todo = []
    for prefix, sub in LINUX_SETS:
        base = os.path.join(a.linux, sub)
        todo += [(prefix + os.path.relpath(p, base), p) for p in walk(base)]
    todo += [(k, os.path.join(a.linux, s)) for k, s in LINUX_FILES if os.path.exists(os.path.join(a.linux, s))]

    for key, p in todo:
        r = first_rule(rules, key) or {}
        kind, items = upstream_items(p)
        matched = []
        for it in items:
            occ = idx.find(it)
            if occ:
                code = [o for o in occ if o[3] == 'code']
                matched.append({'name': it, 'n': len(occ), 'in_code': len(code),
                                'at': ['%s:%d (%s, %s)' % o for o in (code or occ)[:3]]})
        names = {x['name'] for x in matched}
        rec = {'path': key, 'section': 'kernel', 'group': group_of(groups, key), 'lines': count_lines(p),
               'kind': kind, 'total': len(items), 'matched': len(matched), 'evidence': matched,
               'unmatched': [x for x in items if x not in names], 'na': None, 'reason': None, 'proof': None}
        if r.get('status') == 'not_applicable':
            rec.update(status='not_applicable', na=r['na'], reason=r['reason'], future=r.get('future'))
            if kind == 'functions' and len(matched) >= 3:
                warnings.append('%s is not_applicable but %d of its functions occur in our sources' % (key, len(matched)))
        elif matched:
            rec['status'] = 'ported' if len(matched) == len(items) else 'partial'
        elif r.get('status') == 'missing':
            ok, det = check_proof(r.get('proof', {}), idx)
            rec.update(proof=det, reason=r.get('reason'), status='missing' if ok else 'unverified')
            if not ok:
                warnings.append('%s: proof of absence failed -> unverified' % key)
        else:
            rec['status'] = 'unverified'
        files.append(rec)

    mesa_meta = None
    if a.mesa:
        head = git(a.mesa, 'rev-parse', '--short=12', 'HEAD').strip()
        changed = {}
        for line in git(a.mesa, 'diff', '--name-status', a.mesa_base, '--', *MESA_DIRS).splitlines():
            parts = line.split('\t')
            changed[parts[-1]] = parts[0][0]
        built = None
        if a.mesa_build:
            built = set()
            for e in json.load(open(os.path.join(a.mesa_build, 'compile_commands.json'))):
                f = e['file'] if os.path.isabs(e['file']) else os.path.join(e['directory'], e['file'])
                built.add(os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(f), os.path.realpath(a.mesa)))
        bname = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(a.mesa_build)) if a.mesa_build else None
        mesa_meta = {'head': head, 'base': a.mesa_base[:12], 'build': bname}
        for d in MESA_DIRS:
            for p in walk(os.path.join(a.mesa, d)):
                rel = os.path.relpath(p, a.mesa)
                if '/tests/' in rel:
                    continue
                key = 'mesa/' + rel[len('src/'):]
                ch, src_built = changed.get(rel), None
                if built is not None:
                    if rel.endswith(('.c', '.cpp', '.m')):
                        src_built = rel in built
                    else:
                        stem = rel.rsplit('.', 1)[0]
                        sib = [stem + e for e in ('.c', '.cpp', '.m') if os.path.exists(os.path.join(a.mesa, stem + e))]
                        src_built = any(s in built for s in sib) if sib else None
                if ch == 'A':
                    st, why = 'ours', 'added by our patch series'
                elif src_built is False:
                    st, why = 'not_built', 'not in compile_commands.json of ' + str(bname)
                elif ch == 'M':
                    st, why = 'patched', 'changed by our patch series (git diff vs %s)' % a.mesa_base[:12]
                else:
                    st, why = 'upstream', 'identical to upstream %s' % a.mesa_base[:12]
                files.append({'path': key, 'section': 'mesa', 'group': group_of(groups, key),
                              'lines': count_lines(p), 'status': st, 'reason': why})
        for p in walk(os.path.join(ROOT, 'user/xemac')):
            rel = os.path.relpath(p, os.path.join(ROOT, 'user'))
            files.append({'path': 'ours/' + rel, 'section': 'mesa', 'group': group_of(groups, 'ours/' + rel),
                          'lines': count_lines(p), 'status': 'ours', 'reason': 'this repository, user/' + rel})

    pct = lambda x, y: round(100.0 * x / y, 1) if y else 0.0

    def summ(section):
        fs = [f for f in files if f['section'] == section]
        out = {'files': len(fs), 'lines': sum(f['lines'] for f in fs), 'by_status': {}}
        for f in fs:
            b = out['by_status'].setdefault(f['status'], {'files': 0, 'lines': 0})
            b['files'] += 1
            b['lines'] += f['lines']
        if section == 'kernel':
            app = [f for f in fs if f['status'] != 'not_applicable']
            fn = [f for f in app if f['kind'] == 'functions']
            mc = [f for f in app if f['kind'] == 'macros']
            L = sum(f['lines'] for f in app)
            out.update({
                'applicable_files': len(app), 'applicable_lines': L,
                'functions_total': sum(f['total'] for f in fn), 'functions_matched': sum(f['matched'] for f in fn),
                'pct_functions_matched': pct(sum(f['matched'] for f in fn), sum(f['total'] for f in fn)),
                'macros_total': sum(f['total'] for f in mc), 'macros_matched': sum(f['matched'] for f in mc),
                'pct_macros_matched': pct(sum(f['matched'] for f in mc), sum(f['total'] for f in mc)),
                'pct_lines_ported': pct(sum(f['lines'] for f in app if f['status'] == 'ported'), L),
                'pct_lines_with_match': pct(sum(f['lines'] for f in app if f['matched']), L),
                'pct_lines_missing': pct(sum(f['lines'] for f in app if f['status'] == 'missing'), L),
                'pct_lines_unverified': pct(sum(f['lines'] for f in app if f['status'] == 'unverified'), L),
                'pct_files_unverified': pct(len([f for f in app if f['status'] == 'unverified']), len(app)),
            })
        return out

    data = {
        'meta': {'generated': datetime.datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M'),
                 'linux': {'rev': lrev[:12], 'date': ldate, 'version': lver},
                 'ours': {'kernel': tree_id(a.kernel), 'fb': tree_id(a.fb)}, 'mesa': mesa_meta,
                 'method': 'upstream function names (headers: #define names) searched by name in our sources, '
                           'code and comments; tools/parity/scan.py'},
        'summary': {'kernel': summ('kernel'), 'mesa': summ('mesa') if a.mesa else None},
        'files': files,
    }
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(a.out), exist_ok=True)
    with open(a.out, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write('\n')
    if a.html:
        page = open(a.html).read()
        blob = json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False).replace('</', '<\\/')
        new, n = re.subn(r'(<script id="parity-data" type="application/json">).*?(</script>)',
                         lambda mm: mm.group(1) + blob + mm.group(2), page, flags=re.S)
        if n != 1:
            sys.exit('html: parity-data script tag not found')
        open(a.html, 'w').write(new)
    k = data['summary']['kernel']
    print('kernel: %d files, %d applicable (%d lines)' % (k['files'], k['applicable_files'], k['applicable_lines']))
    print('  functions matched %d/%d = %.1f%%; header #defines matched %d/%d = %.1f%%' % (
        k['functions_matched'], k['functions_total'], k['pct_functions_matched'],
        k['macros_matched'], k['macros_total'], k['pct_macros_matched']))
    print('  lines: ported %.1f%%, >=1 match %.1f%%, missing %.1f%%, unverified %.1f%% (files unverified %.1f%%)' % (
        k['pct_lines_ported'], k['pct_lines_with_match'], k['pct_lines_missing'], k['pct_lines_unverified'],
        k['pct_files_unverified']))
    for s, b in sorted(k['by_status'].items()):
        print('  %-15s %4d files %7d lines' % (s, b['files'], b['lines']))
    if a.mesa:
        for s, b in sorted(data['summary']['mesa']['by_status'].items()):
            print('  mesa %-10s %4d files %7d lines' % (s, b['files'], b['lines']))
    for w in warnings:
        print('warning:', w, file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

FILE: tools/parity/uapi.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""xe uAPI coverage: every ioctl, query, property, extension and flag of include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h is one cell.

Each token (#define or enum member named DRM_IOCTL_XE_* / DRM_XE_*; the bare ioctl numbers DRM_XE_<IOCTL> are folded
into their DRM_IOCTL_XE_* cell) gets a status from the CODE of our kernel (comments ignored, uapi copies excluded):
  implemented  used in code outside a rejection (switch case with a body, value produced, flag honoured, or a
               "!= token -> error" check that accepts it)
  noop         a case label whose body is only "return 0;" (accepted, does nothing)
  rejected     every code use is a rejection: the line returns/sets an error (EINVAL, EOPNOTSUPP, ...) and the token
               is tested with == or & (not !=, not inside ~(...))
  absent       no code use at all (an unknown value then falls into a default: error path)
Every cell keeps the file:line of the uses. Python stdlib only.
"""
import argparse, json, os, re, sys

sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import scan  # noqa: E402

ERR = re.compile(r'\b(EINVAL|EOPNOTSUPP|ENOTSUP|ENODEV|ENOTTY|EPERM|ENOSYS)\b')
DEF = re.compile(r'^[ \t]*#define\s+((?:DRM_IOCTL_XE_|DRM_XE_)[A-Z0-9_]+)', re.M)
ENUM_MEM = re.compile(r'^\s*((?:DRM_XE_)[A-Z0-9_]+)\s*(?:=[^,\n]*)?,?\s*(?:/\*.*)?$', re.M)

AREAS = [  # (prefix, area) first match wins
    ('DRM_IOCTL_XE_', 'ioctls'),
    ('DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_', 'DEVICE_QUERY types'), ('DRM_XE_QUERY_', 'DEVICE_QUERY contents'),
    ('DRM_XE_TOPO_', 'DEVICE_QUERY contents'), ('DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_', 'engine classes'),
    ('DRM_XE_MEM_REGION_CLASS_', 'DEVICE_QUERY contents'),
    ('DRM_XE_GEM_', 'GEM_CREATE / MMAP_OFFSET'), ('DRM_XE_MMAP_', 'GEM_CREATE / MMAP_OFFSET'),
    ('DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_', 'VM_CREATE'), ('DRM_XE_VM_BIND_', 'VM_BIND'), ('DRM_XE_VM_GET_PROPERTY', 'VM_GET_PROPERTY'),
    ('DRM_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_', 'EXEC_QUEUE'), ('DRM_XE_MULTI_GROUP', 'EXEC_QUEUE'),
    ('DRM_XE_SYNC_', 'syncs (EXEC / VM_BIND)'), ('DRM_XE_MAX_SYNCS', 'syncs (EXEC / VM_BIND)'),
    ('DRM_XE_UFENCE_', 'WAIT_USER_FENCE'),
    ('DRM_XE_OBSERVATION', 'OBSERVATION: OA / EU stall'), ('DRM_XE_OA', 'OBSERVATION: OA / EU stall'),
    ('DRM_XE_EU_STALL', 'OBSERVATION: OA / EU stall'),
    ('DRM_XE_PXP', 'PXP'),
    ('DRM_XE_MEM_RANGE', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'), ('DRM_XE_VMA_', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'),
    ('DRM_XE_PREFERRED_', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'), ('DRM_XE_MIGRATE_', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'),
    ('DRM_XE_ATOMIC_', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'), ('DRM_XE_CONSULT_', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'),
    ('DRM_XE_MEM_', 'MADVISE / memory ranges'),
    ('DRM_XE_RAS', 'RAS'),
    ('DRM_XE_', 'other'),
]


def area_of(tok):
    for p, a in AREAS:
        if tok.startswith(p):
            return a
    return 'other'


def tokens(header):
    s = open(header).read()
    toks = list(dict.fromkeys(DEF.findall(s)))
    for m in re.finditer(r'enum\s+\w*\s*\{(.*?)\};', s, re.S):
        toks += [t for t in ENUM_MEM.findall(m.group(1)) if t not in toks]
    ioctls = {t[len('DRM_IOCTL_'):] for t in toks if t.startswith('DRM_IOCTL_XE_')}
    # DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY (ioctl number) duplicates DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY
    return [t for t in toks if not (t.startswith('DRM_XE_') and 'XE_' + t[len('DRM_XE_'):] in ioctls)]


def code_lines(text):
    """[(lineno, code part)] with // and /* */ comments removed."""
    out, in_block = [], False
    for no, line in enumerate(text.split('\n'), 1):
        code, i = '', 0
        while i < len(line):
            if in_block:
                j = line.find('*/', i)
                if j < 0:
                    break
                i, in_block = j + 2, False
            elif line.startswith('//', i):
                break
            elif line.startswith('/*', i):
                in_block, i = True, i + 2
            else:
                code += line[i]
                i += 1
        out.append((no, code))
    return out


def classify_use(tok, lines, k):
    """'use' | 'reject' | 'noop' for the token on lines[k]."""
    code = lines[k][1]
    pos = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(r'\b%s\b' % tok, code)]
    if re.search(r'\bcase\s+%s\s*:' % tok, code):
        nxt = next((c.strip() for _, c in lines[k + 1:k + 6] if c.strip() and not c.strip().startswith('case ')), '')
        body = code.split(':', 1)[1].strip()
        first = body or nxt
        if re.match(r'^(return|err\s*=)\s*E[A-Z]+', first):
            return 'reject'
        if first == 'return 0;':
            return 'noop'
        return 'use'
    if ERR.search(code):
        if re.match(r'^\s*if\s*\(\s*[\w.>\[\]-]+\s*>\s*%s\s*\)\s*return\s+E[A-Z]+;' % tok, code):
            return 'use'                         # "if (x > TOKEN) return E..": a limit, TOKEN itself accepted
        for p in pos:
            before = code[:p]
            if re.search(r'!=\s*$', before):
                return 'use'                     # "x != TOKEN -> error" accepts TOKEN
            depth_tilde = before.rfind('~(')
            if depth_tilde >= 0 and before.count('(', depth_tilde) > before.count(')', depth_tilde):
                return 'use'                     # inside a ~(known flags) mask
        return 'reject'
    return 'use'


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ values, switches, second pass

def values(header_text, extra=()):
    """name -> int for #defines and enum members that evaluate to plain integers (ioctl macros: their nr)."""
    vals, raw = {}, {}
    for m in re.finditer(r'^[ \t]*#define\s+([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)\s+(.+?)\s*$', header_text, re.M):
        raw[m.group(1)] = re.sub(r'/\*.*?\*/', '', m.group(2)).strip()
    for m in re.finditer(r'enum\s+\w*\s*\{(.*?)\};', header_text, re.S):
        nxt = 0
        for mm in re.finditer(r'^\s*([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)\s*(?:=\s*([^,\n]+))?,?', m.group(1), re.M):
            if mm.group(2):
                raw[mm.group(1)] = mm.group(2).strip()
                v = ev(mm.group(2), vals, raw)
                nxt = v if v is not None else nxt
            else:
                raw[mm.group(1)] = str(nxt)
            vals[mm.group(1)] = ev(raw[mm.group(1)], vals, raw)
            nxt = (vals[mm.group(1)] if vals[mm.group(1)] is not None else nxt) + 1
    for k in raw:
        if k not in vals:
            vals[k] = ev(raw[k], vals, raw)
    return vals


def ev(expr, vals, raw, depth=0):
    if depth > 8:
        return None
    m = re.match(r'DRM_IO\w*\(\s*DRM_COMMAND_BASE\s*\+\s*([A-Z_0-9]+)', expr)
    if m:   # ioctl: its command number
        v = ev(raw.get(m.group(1), ''), vals, raw, depth + 1)
        return None if v is None else 0x40 + v
    e = re.sub(r'(?<=[0-9a-fA-F])[uUlL]+\b', '', expr)
    for name in set(re.findall(r'\b[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]+\b', e)):
        v = vals.get(name)
        if v is None and name in raw:
            v = ev(raw[name], vals, raw, depth + 1)
        if v is None:
            return None
        e = re.sub(r'\b%s\b' % name, str(v), e)
    if not re.fullmatch(r'[0-9xXa-fA-F\s()<>|&+\-*~]+', e):
        return None
    try:
        return int(eval(e, {'__builtins__': {}}))
    except Exception:
        return None


def switches(parsed):
    """All switch statements: {file, line, cases: [(label, line)], default: (line, first statement)}."""
    out = []
    for f, lines in parsed.items():
        depth, stack, pending = 0, [], None
        for k, (no, code) in enumerate(lines):
            st = code.strip()
            if stack and depth == stack[-1]['depth']:
                for lab in re.findall(r'\bcase\s+([^:]+?)\s*:(?!:)', code):
                    stack[-1]['cases'].append((lab.strip(), no))
                if re.match(r'default\s*:', st):
                    body = st.split(':', 1)[1].strip()
                    nxt = body or next((c.strip() for _, c in lines[k + 1:k + 6] if c.strip()), '')
                    stack[-1]['default'] = (no, nxt)
            if re.search(r'\bswitch\s*\(', code):
                pending = {'file': f, 'line': no, 'cases': [], 'default': None}
            for ch in code:
                if ch == '{':
                    depth += 1
                    if pending is not None:
                        pending['depth'] = depth
                        stack.append(pending)
                        pending = None
                elif ch == '}':
                    if stack and depth == stack[-1]['depth']:
                        out.append(stack.pop())
                    depth -= 1
    return out


VALUE_HINTS = [  # (token regex, code regex with {v} = the token's value, what a match means)
    (r'^DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_', r'(?:gEngines|gMediaEngines)\[[^\]]*\]\s*=\s*\{{\s*{v}\s*,', 'implemented'),   # engine table entry
    (r'^DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_', r'(?:drmClass|engine_class)\s*==\s*{v}\b', 'implemented'),
    (r'^DRM_XE_MAX_SYNCS$', r'\bnum\w*\s*>\s*{v}\)\s*return\s+EINVAL', 'implemented'),
]
EXT_PROPS = r'^DRM_XE_(EXEC_QUEUE_EXTENSION_SET_PROPERTY|EXEC_QUEUE_SET_PROPERTY_\w+|EXEC_QUEUE_SET_HANG_REPLAY_STATE|' \
            r'EXEC_QUEUE_SET_DISABLE_STATE_CACHE_PERF_FIX|GEM_CREATE_EXTENSION_SET_PROPERTY|GEM_CREATE_SET_PROPERTY_\w+)$'
PARENT = {'WAIT_USER_FENCE': ['DRM_IOCTL_XE_WAIT_USER_FENCE'], 'OBSERVATION: OA / EU stall': ['DRM_IOCTL_XE_OBSERVATION'],
          'MADVISE / memory ranges': ['DRM_IOCTL_XE_MADVISE', 'DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_QUERY_MEM_RANGE_ATTRS'],
          'VM_GET_PROPERTY': ['DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_GET_PROPERTY']}


def family(tok):
    """The enumeration a token belongs to: switch/default reasoning only compares tokens of the same family."""
    if tok.startswith('DRM_IOCTL_XE_'):
        return 'DRM_IOCTL_XE_'
    m = re.match(r'^(.*?_(?:OP|FLAG|TYPE|CLASS|PROPERTY|QUERY|CAPS|ATTR|STATE|LOC)_)', tok)
    return m.group(1) if m else tok


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--linux', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--kernel', default=os.path.join(scan.ROOT, 'kernel/IntelXe'))
    ap.add_argument('--fb', default=os.path.join(scan.ROOT, 'kernel/IntelXeFB'))
    ap.add_argument('--out', default=os.path.join(scan.ROOT, 'data/uapi.json'))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    header = os.path.join(a.linux, 'include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h')
    htext = open(header).read()
    vals = values(htext)
    ours_uapi = ''
    for fn in ('intelxe_drm.h', 'xe_drm.h', 'drm.h'):
        p = os.path.join(a.kernel, 'uapi', fn)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            ours_uapi += open(p).read() + '\n'
    our_vals = values(ours_uapi)
    idx = scan.OurIndex([('kernel/IntelXe', a.kernel), ('kernel/IntelXeFB', a.fb)])
    parsed = {f: code_lines(t) for f, t in idx.text.items()}
    sws = switches(parsed)
    alltext = {f: '\n'.join(c for _, c in lines) for f, lines in parsed.items()}

    def find(rx):
        for f, lines in parsed.items():
            for no, code in lines:
                if re.search(rx, code):
                    return '%s:%d' % (f, no), code.strip()[:160]
        return None, None

    cells = []
    for tok in tokens(header):
        uses = []
        for f, lines in parsed.items():
            for k, (no, code) in enumerate(lines):
                if re.search(r'\b%s\b' % tok, code):
                    uses.append({'at': '%s:%d' % (f, no), 'kind': classify_use(tok, lines, k), 'code': code.strip()[:160]})
        kinds = {u['kind'] for u in uses}
        st = None if not uses else 'implemented' if 'use' in kinds else 'noop' if 'noop' in kinds else 'rejected'
        cells.append({'token': tok, 'area': area_of(tok), 'value': vals.get(tok), 'status': st, 'by': 'name' if uses else None,
                      'uses': uses, 'why': ''})
    byname = {c['token']: c for c in cells}

    # same value under our own name (kernel/IntelXe/uapi), used in code
    for c in cells:
        if c['status'] or c['value'] is None:
            continue
        twins = [n for n, v in our_vals.items() if v == c['value'] and n != c['token'] and n.startswith(c['token'].rsplit('_', 1)[0])]
        for n in twins:
            at, code = find(r'\b%s\b' % n)
            if at:
                c.update(status='implemented', by='value (our name %s)' % n, uses=[{'at': at, 'kind': 'use', 'code': code}])
                break
    # value in a known field context
    for c in cells:
        if c['status'] or c['value'] is None:
            continue
        for trx, crx, st in VALUE_HINTS:
            if not c['status'] and re.search(trx, c['token']):
                at, code = find(crx.format(v=c['value']))
                if at:
                    c.update(status=st, by='value %d' % c['value'], uses=[{'at': at, 'kind': 'use', 'code': code}])
    # a switch that dispatches this area: covered by a case value, or falls into an error default
    for c in cells:
        if c['status']:
            continue
        fam = family(c['token'])
        sib = [x['token'] for x in cells if family(x['token']) == fam and x['token'] != c['token']]
        for sw in sws:
            labels = [l for l, _ in sw['cases']]
            if not any(l in sib for l in labels):
                continue
            lv = {vals.get(l, ev(l, vals, {})) for l in labels}
            if c['value'] is not None and c['value'] in lv:
                ln = next(n for l, n in sw['cases'] if vals.get(l, ev(l, vals, {})) == c['value'])
                c.update(status='implemented', by='value %d (case label)' % c['value'],
                         uses=[{'at': '%s:%d' % (sw['file'], ln), 'kind': 'use', 'code': 'case with the same value'}])
            elif c['value'] is not None and sw['default'] and re.match(r'(return|err\s*=)\s*E[A-Z]+', sw['default'][1]):
                c.update(status='rejected', by='switch default',
                         uses=[{'at': '%s:%d' % (sw['file'], sw['default'][0]), 'kind': 'reject', 'code': 'default: ' + sw['default'][1]}],
                         why='no case for value %d in the switch at %s:%d; its default returns an error' % (c['value'], sw['file'], sw['line']))
            break
    # parameters of an ioctl that is itself rejected
    for c in cells:
        if c['status'] or c['area'] not in PARENT:
            continue
        par = [byname.get(p) for p in PARENT[c['area']]]
        if par and all(p and p['status'] == 'rejected' for p in par):
            c.update(status='rejected', by='parent ioctl', uses=par[0]['uses'],
                     why='only reachable through %s, which our dispatch rejects' % ', '.join(PARENT[c['area']]))
    # extension properties: the extension chain is never read
    reads_ext = any(re.search(r'(->|\.)extensions\b', t) for t in alltext.values())
    for c in cells:
        if not c['status'] and re.search(EXT_PROPS, c['token']) and not reads_ext:
            c.update(status='noop', by='extension chain never read',
                     why="no code in our kernel reads an 'extensions' field: the set-property extension is accepted and ignored")
    # device-query contents our handlers do not report (their handlers write named values only)
    for c in cells:
        if c['status'] or c['area'] != 'DEVICE_QUERY contents':
            continue
        fam = c['token'].rsplit('_', 1)[0] if 'FLAG' not in c['token'] else 'DRM_XE_QUERY_CONFIG_FLAG'
        fam = 'DRM_XE_TOPO' if c['token'].startswith('DRM_XE_TOPO') else fam
        at, code = find(r'\b%s\w*' % fam)
        if at:
            c.update(status='absent', by='not reported', uses=[{'at': at, 'kind': 'use', 'code': code}],
                     why='the handler that reports %s* values does not set this one' % fam)
    for c in cells:
        c['comments'] = ['%s:%d (%s)' % (o[0], o[1], o[2]) for o in idx.find(c['token']) if o[3] == 'comment'][:3]
        if not c['status']:
            c['status'] = 'unverified'
            c['why'] = 'no use by name%s; no dispatch switch, field match or proof decides it' % (
                ' or by value %d' % c['value'] if c['value'] is not None else ' (value not resolvable)')

    tot = len(cells)
    order = ('implemented', 'noop', 'rejected', 'absent', 'unverified')
    cnt = {s: sum(1 for c in cells if c['status'] == s) for s in order}
    ioc = [c for c in cells if c['area'] == 'ioctls']
    data = {'meta': {'header': 'include/uapi/drm/xe_drm.h', 'linux': scan.git(a.linux, 'rev-parse', '--short=12', 'HEAD').strip(),
                     'ours': {'kernel': scan.tree_id(a.kernel), 'fb': scan.tree_id(a.fb)},
                     'method': 'by name, then by value (our uapi names, field contexts, switch case labels/defaults, '
                               'rejected parent ioctls, unread extension chains); see tools/parity/uapi.py'},
            'summary': {'cells': tot, **cnt, 'pct_implemented': round(100.0 * cnt['implemented'] / tot, 1),
                        'ioctls': len(ioc), 'ioctls_implemented': sum(1 for c in ioc if c['status'] == 'implemented')},
            'cells': cells}
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(a.out), exist_ok=True)
    json.dump(data, open(a.out, 'w'), indent=1)
    s = data['summary']
    print('xe uAPI: %d cells: implemented %d (%.1f%%), no-op %d, rejected %d, absent (proven) %d, unverified %d; ioctls %d/%d' % (
        tot, s['implemented'], s['pct_implemented'], s['noop'], s['rejected'], s['absent'], s['unverified'],
        s['ioctls_implemented'], s['ioctls']))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

FILE: tools/parity/video.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Video matrix from the mediakit macOS results (exact numbers only).

Reads <mediakit>/out_mac/results_mac.txt (written by mediakit's mac/run_mac.sh) and, when present,
<mediakit>/out_win/results_win.txt, and writes data/video.json: one cell per codec x direction x bit depth x resolution.

Decode cell: every clip of that combination decoded through VideoToolbox ("vt" rows) with per-frame md5 against the
software reference; fps per clip. Encode cell: VideoToolbox encode speed (encspeed rows, preset veryfast/medium/veryslow)
and the bitrate deviation of every VBR quality encode = bytes*8 / (frames/60) / target - 1, with frames as run_mac.sh
uses them (1080p60: 600, 2160p60: 300).
Grade against the B580 target (docs/devices/b580.md): decode must be bit-exact and >= Windows speed; encode BD-rate <= 0 vs QSV and
overshoot <= 5%. Without Windows numbers a cell that passes the macOS-only checks is "pending" (yellow).
Combinations Intel's own driver does not offer on Xe2 (data/caps.json from tools/parity/caps.py, with the media-driver
caps table that says so) are "unsupported" instead of "untested". Each measured item names the stack it was measured with (the run header line).
"""
import argparse, collections, json, math, os, re

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
CODECS = ['h264', 'hevc', 'av1', 'vp9']
RES = {'1080p': '1080p', '2160p': '2160p', '4320p': '4320p'}
FRAMES = {'1080p60': 600, '2160p60': 300, '4320p60': 120}

# What Intel's own driver does not offer on the B580 comes from data/caps.json (tools/parity/caps.py: media-driver's Xe2
# capability tables for Battlemage): a combination it does not offer (no entrypoint, no such bit depth, or beyond its
# largest picture) is graded "unsupported", with the table that says so.
CAPS_PLATFORM = 'bmg'
DIMS = {'1080p': (1920, 1080), '2160p': (3840, 2160), '4320p': (7680, 4320)}


def unsupported_set(caps_path):
    """{(codec, dir, bits, res): reason} for every matrix cell Intel's driver does not offer on CAPS_PLATFORM."""
    import sys
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
    sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    from caps import supports
    caps = json.load(open(caps_path))
    out = {}
    for codec in CODECS:
        for d in ('decode', 'encode'):
            for bits in (8, 10):
                for res, (w, h) in DIMS.items():
                    ok, why = supports(caps, CAPS_PLATFORM, codec, d, bits, w, h)
                    if ok is False:
                        out[(codec, d, bits, res)] = why
    return out, caps['meta']


def kv(p, k):
    return p[p.index(k) + 1] if k in p else None


def load(path, headers=None):
    """Result rows as token lists; with headers=[], also the run header line each row came after."""
    rows = []
    if os.path.exists(path):
        raw = open(path, 'rb').read()   # PowerShell writes UTF-16 with CRLF and "1,132.1" thousands separators
        txt = raw.decode('utf-16') if raw[:2] in (b'\xff\xfe', b'\xfe\xff') else raw.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
        hdr = ''
        for line in txt.replace('\r', '').split('\n'):
            if line.startswith('# mediakit'):
                hdr = line.strip()
            p = [w.replace(',', '') if w[:1].isdigit() else w for w in line.split()]
            if p and not p[0].startswith('#'):
                rows.append(p)
                if headers is not None:
                    headers.append(hdr)
    return rows


def stack_of(hdr):
    """The stack a run measured: 'installed <hashes>' plus the environment it put in front (another stack)."""
    m = re.search(r'installed: ([0-9a-f ]+?)\s*(?:env: (.*?))?\s*(?:test: (.*))?$', hdr)
    if not m:
        return 'installed stack'
    if not m.group(2):
        return 'installed stack %s' % m.group(1).strip()
    lib = re.search(r'DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=(\S+)', m.group(2))
    where = re.sub(r'^/Users/[^/]+', '~', lib.group(1)) if lib else m.group(2)
    return 'test stack %s%s over installed %s' % (where, ' (%s)' % m.group(3) if m.group(3) else '', m.group(1).strip())



def _polyfit(x, y, deg):   # least squares, as mediakit score/score.py
    n = deg + 1
    A = [[sum(xi ** (i + j) for xi in x) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
    b = [sum((xi ** i) * yi for xi, yi in zip(x, y)) for i in range(n)]
    for c in range(n):
        q = max(range(c, n), key=lambda r: abs(A[r][c])); A[c], A[q] = A[q], A[c]; b[c], b[q] = b[q], b[c]
        for r in range(n):
            if r != c and A[c][c]:
                f = A[r][c] / A[c][c]; A[r] = [x1 - f * x2 for x1, x2 in zip(A[r], A[c])]; b[r] -= f * b[c]
    return [b[i] / A[i][i] for i in range(n)]


def bd_rate(r1, q1, r2, q2):
    """Bjontegaard rate difference of (r2, q2) against (r1, q1) in %, cubic (or quadratic) fit of log rate over quality."""
    if len(r1) < 3 or len(r2) < 3:
        return None
    deg = 3 if len(r1) > 3 and len(r2) > 3 else 2
    p1 = _polyfit(q1, [math.log(r) for r in r1], deg); p2 = _polyfit(q2, [math.log(r) for r in r2], deg)
    lo, hi = max(min(q1), min(q2)), min(max(q1), max(q2))
    if hi <= lo:
        return None
    integ = lambda p: sum(c / (i + 1) * (hi ** (i + 1) - lo ** (i + 1)) for i, c in enumerate(p))
    return (math.exp((integ(p2) - integ(p1)) / (hi - lo)) - 1) * 100


def load_metrics(mediakit):
    """score/metrics_{mac,win}.txt -> {(row, content, codec, res, bits): [(kbps, psnr_y, vmaf)]}"""
    m = {}
    for f in ('score/metrics_mac.txt', 'score/metrics_win.txt'):
        path = os.path.join(mediakit, f)
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            continue
        for line in open(path):
            p = line.split()
            mm = re.match(r'(\w+)-(\w+)_(\w+)_(\d+p\d+)_(\d+)_vbr\d+$', p[0]) if len(p) >= 8 and p[4] != '-' else None
            if mm:
                m.setdefault(mm.groups(), []).append((float(p[2]), float(p[4]), float(p[7])))
    return {k: sorted(v) for k, v in m.items()}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--mediakit', required=True)
    ap.add_argument('--out', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/video.json'))
    ap.add_argument('--caps', default=os.path.join(ROOT, 'data/caps.json'))
    a = ap.parse_args()
    UNSUPPORTED, caps_meta = unsupported_set(a.caps)
    mac_p = os.path.join(a.mediakit, 'out_mac/results_mac.txt')
    mac_hdr = []
    win_hdr = []
    mac, win = load(mac_p, mac_hdr), load(os.path.join(a.mediakit, 'out_win/results_win.txt'), win_hdr)
    # The Windows GPU of each row: run_win.ps1 pins the Arc B580 since 2 Nov and names it in the run header
    # ('adapter=N 8086:e20b "..."'); rows of an older run came from whichever adapter ffmpeg/oneVPL picked (the
    # UHD 770 iGPU is an Intel adapter too), so a comparison with them is marked unpinned.
    win_pinned = [bool(re.search(r'adapter=\d+ 8086:e2[0-2][0-9a-f] ', h)) for h in win_hdr]
    met = load_metrics(a.mediakit)
    runs = [re.sub(r'/Users/[^/\s]+', '~', l.strip()) for l in open(mac_p) if l.startswith('# mediakit')]   # no home paths in the repo
    cells = {}

    def cell(codec, d, bits, res):
        return cells.setdefault((codec, d, bits, res), {'codec': codec, 'dir': d, 'bits': bits, 'res': res, 'items': []})

    for p, hdr in zip(mac, mac_hdr):   # dec <path> <clip> frames N fps F cpu% C md5frames a/b mismatches M
        if p[0] != 'dec' or p[1] != 'vt':
            continue
        m = re.match(r'dec_(h264|hevc|av1|vp9)(8|10)?_?(?:(8|10)_)?(\d+p)(\d+)', p[2])
        if not m:
            continue
        codec = m.group(1)
        bits = int(m.group(2) or m.group(3) or 8)
        c = cell(codec, 'decode', bits, m.group(4))
        ok, tot = kv(p, 'md5frames').split('/')
        c['items'] = [i for i in c['items'] if i['clip'] != p[2]]   # a rerun appends rows: the last one counts
        c['items'].append({'clip': p[2], 'fps': float(kv(p, 'fps')), 'cpu': kv(p, 'cpu%'), 'md5': '%s/%s' % (ok, tot),
                           'exact': ok == tot and int(tot) > 0 and kv(p, 'mismatches') == '0', 'stack': stack_of(hdr)})
    for p in mac:   # encspeed <codec> <res> <preset> frames N fps F
        if p[0] == 'encspeed':
            c = cell(p[1], 'encode', 8, p[2][:-2])
            c.setdefault('speed', {})[p[3]] = float(kv(p, 'fps'))
    for p, hdr in zip(mac, mac_hdr):   # enc vt-<content>_<codec>_<res>_<bits>_vbr<M>.<ext> bytes B fps F
        if p[0] != 'enc' or not p[1].startswith('vt-'):
            continue
        m = re.match(r'vt-(\w+?)_(h264|hevc|av1)_(\d+p\d+)_(8|10)_vbr(\d+)\.', p[1])
        if not m:
            continue
        content, codec, res, bits, mbit = m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), int(m.group(4)), int(m.group(5))
        kbps = int(kv(p, 'bytes')) * 8 / (FRAMES[res] / 60.0) / 1000
        c = cell(codec, 'encode', bits, res[:-2])
        c['items'] = [i for i in c['items'] if i['stream'] != p[1]]   # a rerun appends rows: the last one counts
        if int(kv(p, 'bytes')) > 0:   # a stream at this target supersedes an earlier failure at it (e.g. a renamed set)
            c['items'] = [i for i in c['items'] if not (i.get('failed') and i['target_kbps'] == mbit * 1000)]
        if int(kv(p, 'bytes')) == 0:   # the encoder produced nothing (session refused or failed)
            c['items'].append({'stream': p[1], 'content': content, 'target_kbps': mbit * 1000, 'failed': True,
                               'stack': stack_of(hdr)})
            continue
        c['items'].append({'stream': p[1], 'content': content, 'target_kbps': mbit * 1000, 'kbps': round(kbps),
                           'deviation_pct': round(100 * (kbps / (mbit * 1000) - 1), 1), 'fps': float(kv(p, 'fps')),
                           'stack': stack_of(hdr)})
    out = []
    for codec in CODECS:
        for d in ('decode', 'encode'):
            for bits in (8, 10):
                for res in ('1080p', '2160p', '4320p'):
                    c = cells.get((codec, d, bits, res))
                    if (codec, d, bits, res) in UNSUPPORTED:
                        out.append({'codec': codec, 'dir': d, 'bits': bits, 'res': res, 'grade': 'unsupported',
                                    'note': UNSUPPORTED[(codec, d, bits, res)]})
                        continue
                    if not c or (not c['items'] and not c.get('speed')):
                        out.append({'codec': codec, 'dir': d, 'bits': bits, 'res': res, 'grade': 'untested',
                                    'note': 'not in the mediakit run'})
                        continue
                    if d == 'decode':
                        exact = all(i['exact'] for i in c['items'])
                        # Windows reference: its fastest hardware path per clip (d3d11va or qsv), last row per clip
                        wfps, wpin = {}, {}
                        for q, pin in zip(win, win_pinned):
                            if q[0] == 'dec' and kv(q, 'fps'):
                                wfps[(q[1], q[2])] = float(kv(q, 'fps'))
                                wpin[(q[1], q[2])] = pin
                        ref = {i['clip']: max([v for (path, clip), v in wfps.items() if clip == i['clip']] or [0])
                               for i in c['items']}
                        measured = all(ref[i['clip']] > 0 for i in c['items'])
                        fast = measured and all(i['fps'] >= ref[i['clip']] for i in c['items'])
                        pinned = measured and all(wpin.get((path, clip)) for (path, clip), v in wfps.items()
                                                  if clip in ref and v == ref[clip])
                        if measured:
                            c['windows_gpu_pinned'] = pinned
                        c['grade'] = 'fail' if not exact else ('pass' if fast else ('fail' if measured else 'pending'))
                        stacks = sorted(set(i['stack'] for i in c['items']))
                        c['note'] = ('bit-exact, ' if exact else 'NOT bit-exact / failed, ') + \
                            ', '.join('%s %s fps (md5 %s)' % (i['clip'], i['fps'], i['md5']) +
                                      (' vs Windows %.1f fps' % ref[i['clip']] if ref[i['clip']] else '')
                                      for i in c['items']) + \
                            ('' if not exact else '; Windows speed not measured yet' if not measured else
                             '; >= Windows' if fast else '; slower than Windows') + \
                            ('' if not measured or pinned else ' (Windows run did not pin the adapter: B580 not verified)') + \
                            '; measured with the ' + ' / '.join(stacks)
                    else:
                        failed = [i['stream'] for i in c['items'] if i.get('failed')]
                        devs = [i['deviation_pct'] for i in c['items'] if not i.get('failed')]
                        over = max(devs) if devs else None
                        c['max_overshoot_pct'] = over
                        sp = c.get('speed', {})
                        bits_txt = []
                        if sp:
                            bits_txt.append('speed ' + ' / '.join('%s %s fps' % (k, v) for k, v in sorted(sp.items())))
                        if devs:
                            bits_txt.append('VBR bitrate deviation %+.1f%% .. %+.1f%% over %d streams' % (min(devs), over, len(devs)))
                        # BD-rate (PSNR-Y / VMAF) of our VideoToolbox row against Intel QSV at the same settings (qsvT4)
                        bds = []
                        for (row, content, mc, mres, mbits), pts in sorted(met.items()):
                            if row != 'vt' or mc != codec or int(mbits) != bits or mres[:-2] != res:
                                continue
                            q = met.get(('qsvT4', content, mc, mres, mbits))
                            if q:
                                bp = bd_rate([x[0] for x in q], [x[1] for x in q], [x[0] for x in pts], [x[1] for x in pts])
                                bv = bd_rate([x[0] for x in q], [x[2] for x in q], [x[0] for x in pts], [x[2] for x in pts])
                                if bp is not None:
                                    bds.append((content, bp, bv))
                        if bds:
                            c['bd_rate_vs_qsv'] = [{'content': k, 'psnr_pct': round(bp, 1), 'vmaf_pct': None if bv is None else round(bv, 1)}
                                                   for k, bp, bv in bds]
                            bits_txt.append('BD-rate vs QSV same settings (PSNR-Y/VMAF) ' + ', '.join(
                                '%s %+.1f%%/%s' % (k, bp, '-' if bv is None else '%+.1f%%' % bv) for k, bp, bv in bds))
                        worse = any(bp > 0 for k, bp, bv in bds)
                        if failed:
                            c['grade'] = 'fail'
                            c['failed_streams'] = failed
                            bits_txt.append('encode FAILED (no stream) for %s' % ', '.join(failed))
                        if over is not None and over > 5:
                            c['grade'] = 'fail'
                            bits_txt.append('overshoot > 5%')
                        if bds and worse:
                            c['grade'] = 'fail'
                            bits_txt.append('more bits than QSV for the same PSNR')
                        elif bds and c.get('grade') != 'fail':
                            c['grade'] = 'pass'
                        elif not bds and c.get('grade') != 'fail':
                            c['grade'] = 'pending'
                            bits_txt.append('BD-rate vs QSV not measured yet' + ('' if devs else '; no bitrate data'))
                        stacks = sorted(set(i['stack'] for i in c['items'] if i.get('stack')))
                        if stacks:
                            bits_txt.append('measured with the ' + ' / '.join(stacks))
                        c['note'] = '; '.join(bits_txt)
                    out.append(c)
    data = {'meta': {'source': os.path.relpath(mac_p, a.mediakit), 'mediakit': os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(a.mediakit)), 'runs': runs,
                     'windows': bool(win), 'frames': FRAMES,
                     'windows_runs': sorted({h + ('' if 'adapter=' in h else ' (adapter not pinned: GPU unverified)') for h in win_hdr if h}),
                     'unsupported_from': 'data/caps.json (%s, media-driver %s %s)' % (CAPS_PLATFORM, caps_meta['commit'][:12], caps_meta['date'])},
            'summary': {'decode_clips': sum(len(c['items']) for c in out if c['dir'] == 'decode' and c.get('items')),
                        'decode_exact': sum(1 for c in out if c['dir'] == 'decode' and c.get('items') for i in c['items'] if i['exact']),
                        'grades': dict(collections.Counter(c['grade'] for c in out))},
            'cells': out}
    json.dump(data, open(a.out, 'w'), indent=1)
    print('video: decode %d/%d clips bit-exact; grades %s' % (data['summary']['decode_exact'], data['summary']['decode_clips'],
                                                               data['summary']['grades']))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build.sh: build the Xe probe stick's USB image in Docker. The image is x86_64; on an arm64 Mac Docker emulates it
# (--platform linux/amd64). Nothing is installed on the host.
#
#   tools/probe-stick/build.sh          out/xe-probe-stick-VERSION.img, .img.sha256, .manifest.txt; out/usb/ (the files)
#   tools/probe-stick/build.sh lock     print new apk/tool lines for sources.lock, after Alpine replaced a package file
#
# Inputs are pinned in sources.lock (Docker image by digest, every downloaded file by SHA-256) and cached in out/cache.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)
IMAGE=$(awk '$1 == "image" && $2 == "alpine" { print $4 }' "$HERE/sources.lock")
[ -n "$IMAGE" ] || { echo "error: no alpine image in sources.lock" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: needs Docker" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$HERE/out/cache"
# --privileged is not needed: mknod for /dev/console in the image's root needs only Docker's default capabilities
exec docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v "$REPO":/src:ro -v "$HERE/out":/out "$IMAGE" \
	sh /src/tools/probe-stick/image/build-inside.sh "${1:-build}"

# Everything the Xe probe stick image is built from, pinned. One entry per line: KIND NAME SHA256 URL
#   image     a Docker image, by digest (SHA256 column unused)
#   epoch     the time every file in the image carries (seconds since 1970); move it when this file changes
#   kernel    the kernel package; firmware: the GPU firmware package (Arch Linux Archive: these URLs never move)
#   apk       an Alpine package that goes into the image (unpacked, never installed)
#   tool      an Alpine package the build runs whose output ships (GRUB makes BOOTX64.EFI)
#   license   a licence text that travels on the stick (SPDX license-list-data, by tag)
# The build downloads each file to out/cache/ and stops if a SHA-256 differs. Alpine removes a package file from its
# mirror when it ships a fix; then `build.sh lock` prints new apk/tool lines (out/cache keeps the old files meanwhile).

Run by tools/probe-stick/test/disk-rules-test.sh through write-stick.sh --rules, and by IntelXe.Core.Tests (StickDiskVectorTests) through StickRules. bus: usb, virtual, or another bus (nvme, sata, sas, raid, sd, spaces). system: the disk holds the running system (Windows: IsBoot/IsSystem). whole: false only where a tool can be handed a partition (write-stick.sh); the Windows app lists whole disks only (windows: false). minimum: the image's size in bytes (the probe stick); maxBytes: the size above which a disk is refused unless allowLarge.",

FILE: tools/probe-stick/write-stick.sh
