#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# write-stick.sh: write the Xe probe stick image to a USB stick, on macOS or Linux. Everything on the stick is erased.
#
#   sh write-stick.sh --list                    the external disks it would accept
#   sh write-stick.sh IMAGE DISK                write IMAGE to DISK (macOS: disk4; Linux: sdb), after checks and after you
#                                               type the disk's name to confirm; then read it back and compare
#   --allow-large                               accept a disk larger than 128 GB (refused by default: likely a backup disk)
#   --erase-efi                                 erase a stick that holds an EFI without asking for ERASE EFI (for scripts)
#   sh write-stick.sh --efi DISK                only look for an EFI on DISK (read-only) and say what it found
#
# It refuses: a disk that is not on USB (macOS: BusProtocol; Linux: the device path) or not removable media (a USB hard
# disk or SSD rather than a stick), a partition instead of a whole disk, the disk the running system boots from, a disk
# image or other virtual disk, a disk smaller than the image or larger than 128 GB, and an IMAGE whose SHA-256 does
# not match the .img.sha256 next to it. These are the rules IntelXe Manager for Windows applies (StickRules), held to
# the same answers by stick-disk-vectors.json (test/disk-rules-test.sh). It needs sudo for the write and the read-back.
# A stick that holds an EFI (an EFI system partition, by its type; or a FAT volume with EFI/OC/OpenCore.efi, or with an
# EFI/BOOT/BOOTx64.efi that is not a probe stick's own) is not refused, since it is often the stick to rewrite, but it
# may be someone's OpenCore recovery stick: the script names what it found and asks for ERASE EFI besides the disk's
# name (or takes --erase-efi). It looks read-only: mounted volumes where they are, an unmounted FAT volume through a
# temporary read-only mount (macOS: diskutil mount readOnly; Linux: mount -o ro, with sudo), unmounted again at once.
set -eu
LC_ALL=C
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:$PATH   # diskutil and plutil live in /usr/sbin and /usr/bin
export LC_ALL PATH
MAXGB=128

die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
gb() { awk -v b="$1" 'BEGIN { printf "%.1f GB", b / 1e9 }'; }
sha() { if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then shasum -a 256 | cut -d' ' -f1; else sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1; fi; }

# The shared rules: from the facts about one disk, the codes of the reasons to refuse it, one per line; nothing when it
# may be written. The same function as IntelXe Manager's StickRules (windows/app/IntelXe.Core/Stick/StickDisk.cs); the
# answers both must give are stick-disk-vectors.json.
#   rules BUS REMOVABLE WHOLE SYSTEM SIZE MINIMUM LARGE
#   BUS usb, virtual, or anything else (internal, nvme, sata, thunderbolt, sd ...); REMOVABLE, WHOLE, SYSTEM (holds the
#   running system), LARGE (--allow-large): 1 or 0; SIZE and MINIMUM in bytes
rules() {
	if [ "$3" != 1 ]; then echo partition; fi
	case "$1" in usb) ;; virtual) echo virtual ;; *) echo not-usb ;; esac
	if [ "$2" != 1 ]; then echo not-removable; fi
	if [ "$4" = 1 ]; then echo system; fi
	if [ "$5" -lt "$6" ]; then echo too-small; fi
	if [ "$7" != 1 ] && [ "$5" -gt $((MAXGB * 1000000000)) ]; then echo too-large; fi
	return 0
}
# why: the first reason as a sentence (WHY), from the codes rules printed; returns 1 when there is one
why() {
	code=$(printf '%s\n' "$2" | sed -n 1p)
	case "$code" in
	'') WHY=""; return 0 ;;
	partition) WHY="$1 is a partition: name the whole disk (see --list)" ;;
	virtual) WHY="$1 is a virtual disk (a disk image or an APFS container)" ;;
	not-usb) WHY="$1 is not a USB disk (${BUS:-internal})" ;;
	not-removable) WHY="$1 is not removable media: a USB hard disk or SSD rather than a stick" ;;
	system) WHY="$1 holds the running system" ;;
	too-small) WHY="$1 ($(gb "$SIZE")) is smaller than the image" ;;
	too-large) WHY="$1 is $(gb "$SIZE"), larger than $MAXGB GB (--allow-large if you mean it)" ;;
	*) WHY="$1: $code" ;;
	esac
	return 1
}
# The EFI rule: from the facts about one partition, the codes of the EFI on it, one per line; nothing when erasing it
# loses no EFI. The same rule as IntelXe Manager's StickRules.HoldsEfi and VolumeHoldsEfi; the answers both must give
# are stick-disk-vectors.json's "efiVectors".
#   efi_rules ESP OPENCORE BOOTX64 PROBE
#   ESP: an EFI system partition by its type (GPT C12A7328-..., MBR 0xEF); OPENCORE: EFI/OC/OpenCore.efi on it; BOOTX64:
#   EFI/BOOT/BOOTx64.efi on it; PROBE: it is a probe stick (xe-probe-stick.marker), whose BOOTx64.efi is its own GRUB.
#   Each 1 or 0.
efi_rules() {
	if [ "$1" = 1 ]; then echo esp; fi
	if [ "$2" = 1 ]; then echo opencore
	elif [ "$3" = 1 ] && [ "$4" != 1 ]; then echo boot-loader
	fi
	return 0
}
efi_text() { # the codes efi_rules printed, as words
	printf '%s\n' "$1" | awk '
		$0 == "esp" { w[n++] = "an EFI system partition" }
		$0 == "opencore" { w[n++] = "OpenCore (EFI/OC/OpenCore.efi)" }
		$0 == "boot-loader" { w[n++] = "an EFI boot loader (EFI/BOOT/BOOTx64.efi: an installer or another system'"'"'s boot stick)" }
		END { for (i = 0; i < n; i++) printf "%s%s", (i ? ", with " : ""), w[i]; print "" }'
}
if [ "${1:-}" = --rules ]; then shift; [ $# = 7 ] || die "--rules BUS REMOVABLE WHOLE SYSTEM SIZE MINIMUM LARGE"; rules "$@"; exit 0; fi
if [ "${1:-}" = --efi-rules ]; then shift; [ $# = 4 ] || die "--efi-rules ESP OPENCORE BOOTX64 PROBE"; efi_rules "$@"; exit 0; fi

LARGE=0 LIST=0 ERASE_EFI=0 EFI_ONLY=0
set -- "$@" --end
while [ "$1" != --end ]; do
	case "$1" in
	--allow-large) LARGE=1 ;;
	--erase-efi) ERASE_EFI=1 ;;
	--efi) EFI_ONLY=1 ;;
	--list) LIST=1 ;;
	-h|--help) sed -n '3,21p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
	*) set -- "$@" "$1" ;;
	esac
	shift
done
shift

OS=$(uname -s)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------- macOS
mac_pget() { plutil -extract "$2" raw -o - "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; }
# the checks set SIZE, MODEL and BUS, and WHY when they refuse the disk (return 1); MIN is the image's size (0: --list)
mac_check() {
	T=$(mktemp -d)
	diskutil info -plist "$1" > "$T/i.plist" 2>/dev/null || { WHY="diskutil does not know $1"; rm -rf "$T"; return 1; }
	whole=0 sys=0 rem=0 bus=other
	[ "$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" WholeDisk)" = true ] && whole=1
	[ "$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" RemovableMedia)" = true ] && rem=1
	BUS=$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" BusProtocol)
	if [ "$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" VirtualOrPhysical)" = Virtual ]; then bus=virtual
	elif [ "$BUS" = USB ] && [ "$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" Internal)" != true ]; then bus=usb
	fi
	# the disk the running macOS boots from: the physical stores of the / volume's APFS container
	diskutil info -plist / > "$T/root.plist" 2>/dev/null || true
	n=0
	while :; do
		s=$(mac_pget "$T/root.plist" "APFSPhysicalStores.$n.APFSPhysicalStore"); [ -n "$s" ] || break
		[ "$(printf '%s' "$s" | sed 's/s[0-9]*$//')" = "$1" ] && sys=1
		n=$((n + 1))
	done
	[ "$(mac_pget "$T/root.plist" ParentWholeDisk)" = "$1" ] && sys=1
	SIZE=$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" Size)
	MODEL=$(mac_pget "$T/i.plist" MediaName)
	rm -rf "$T"
	why "$1" "$(rules "$bus" "$rem" "$whole" "$sys" "${SIZE:-0}" "${MIN:-0}" "$LARGE")"
}
mac_list() {
	for d in $(diskutil list external physical 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's#^/dev/\(disk[0-9]*\) .*#\1#p'); do
		if mac_check "$d"; then printf '  %-8s %-10s %-10s %s\n' "$d" "$(gb "$SIZE")" "$BUS" "$MODEL"
		else printf '  %-8s refused: %s\n' "$d" "$WHY"; fi
	done
}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Linux
lin_check() {
	[ -d "/sys/block/$1" ] || { WHY="$1 is not a whole disk (see --list)"; return 1; }
	case "$(readlink -f "/sys/block/$1")" in */virtual/*) bus=virtual ;; */usb[0-9]*/*) bus=usb ;; *) bus=other ;; esac
	rem=$(cat "/sys/block/$1/removable" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
	SIZE=$(( $(cat "/sys/block/$1/size") * 512 ))
	MODEL=$(cat "/sys/block/$1/device/model" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/ *$//')
	case $bus in usb) BUS=USB ;; virtual) BUS=virtual ;; *) BUS="not USB" ;; esac
	# a mounted file system of the running system on it: /, /boot, /home, /usr, /var or swap
	sys=0
	for p in "/dev/$1" /dev/"$1"[0-9]* /dev/"$1"p[0-9]*; do
		[ -b "$p" ] || continue
		if awk -v p="$p" '$1 == p && ($2 == "/" || $2 ~ /^\/(boot|home|usr|var)(\/|$)/) { f = 1 } END { exit !f }' /proc/mounts; then sys=1; fi
		if grep -q "^$p " /proc/swaps 2>/dev/null; then sys=1; fi
	done
	why "$1" "$(rules "$bus" "$rem" 1 "$sys" "$SIZE" "${MIN:-0}" "$LARGE")"
}
lin_list() {
	for b in /sys/block/*; do
		d=${b##*/}
		case "$d" in loop*|ram*|zram*|sr*|dm-*|md*) continue ;; esac
		if lin_check "$d"; then printf '  %-8s %-10s %-10s %s\n' "$d" "$(gb "$SIZE")" "$BUS" "$MODEL"
		else printf '  %-8s refused: %s\n' "$d" "$WHY"; fi
	done
}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------- an EFI on the disk (read-only)
# efi_scan DISK sets EFI_FOUND (one line per partition that holds an EFI: "PART (LABEL): what") and EFI_NOTE (FAT
# volumes it could not look inside). Mounted volumes are looked at where they are; an unmounted FAT volume (the only
# kind a PC's firmware boots from) is mounted read-only in a temporary folder and unmounted at once. Nothing is written.
ET="" EFI_DEV="" EFI_MNT=""
as_root() { if [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]; then "$@"; else sudo "$@"; fi; }
efi_unmount() {
	[ -n "$EFI_DEV" ] || return 0
	if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then diskutil unmount "$EFI_DEV" >/dev/null 2>&1 || diskutil unmount force "$EFI_DEV" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
	else as_root umount "$EFI_MNT" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
	EFI_DEV=""
}
cleanup() {
	efi_unmount
	if [ -n "$ET" ]; then rm -f "$ET"/*.plist; rmdir "$ET/m" "$ET" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP
efi_mount() { # efi_mount DEV: DEV mounted read-only at EFI_MNT, or 1
	[ -n "$ET" ] || ET=$(mktemp -d)
	EFI_MNT=$ET/m
	mkdir -p "$EFI_MNT"
	if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then
		diskutil mount readOnly -mountPoint "$EFI_MNT" "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
	else
		echo "looking for an EFI on $1: mounting it read-only (mount -o ro, as root)" >&2
		as_root mount -o ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec -t vfat "$1" "$EFI_MNT" 2>/dev/null || return 1
	fi
	EFI_DEV=$1
}
vol_look() { # vol_look DIR: OC, BOOT and PROBE (1 or 0) for the volume at DIR; FAT ignores case, so names are compared in lower case
	OC=0 BOOT=0 PROBE=0
	files=$(cd "$1" 2>/dev/null && find . -maxdepth 3 -type f 2>/dev/null | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z') || files=""
	printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -qx './efi/oc/opencore.efi' && OC=1
	printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -qx './efi/boot/bootx64.efi' && BOOT=1
	printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -qx './xe-probe-stick.marker' && PROBE=1
	return 0
}
efi_part() { # efi_part DEV ESP FS MOUNTPOINT LABEL: one partition (FS: fat or ""), added to EFI_FOUND when it holds an EFI
	OC=0 BOOT=0 PROBE=0
	if [ -n "$4" ]; then vol_look "$4"
	elif [ "$3" = fat ]; then
		if efi_mount "$1"; then vol_look "$EFI_MNT"; efi_unmount
		elif [ "$2" != 1 ]; then EFI_NOTE="$EFI_NOTE$1 is a FAT volume the script could not mount read-only to look for an EFI
"
		fi
	fi
	codes=$(efi_rules "$2" "$OC" "$BOOT" "$PROBE")
	[ -z "$codes" ] || EFI_FOUND="$EFI_FOUND$1${5:+ ($5)}: $(efi_text "$codes")
"
}
mac_efi() {
	[ -n "$ET" ] || ET=$(mktemp -d)
	diskutil list -plist "$1" > "$ET/l.plist" 2>/dev/null || return 0
	parts="" n=0
	while :; do
		p=$(mac_pget "$ET/l.plist" "AllDisksAndPartitions.0.Partitions.$n.DeviceIdentifier"); [ -n "$p" ] || break
		parts="$parts $p"
		n=$((n + 1))
	done
	[ -n "$parts" ] || parts=$1   # a file system on the whole disk, without a partition table
	for p in $parts; do
		diskutil info -plist "$p" > "$ET/p.plist" 2>/dev/null || continue
		esp=0
		case "$(mac_pget "$ET/p.plist" Content | tr 'a-z' 'A-Z')" in EFI|C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B|0XEF) esp=1 ;; esac
		fs=""
		[ "$(mac_pget "$ET/p.plist" FilesystemType)" = msdos ] && fs=fat
		efi_part "$p" "$esp" "$fs" "$(mac_pget "$ET/p.plist" MountPoint)" "$(mac_pget "$ET/p.plist" VolumeName)"
	done
}
lin_efi() {
	parts=""
	for p in /dev/"$1"[0-9]* /dev/"$1"p[0-9]*; do [ -b "$p" ] && parts="$parts $p"; done
	[ -n "$parts" ] || parts=/dev/$1   # a file system on the whole disk, without a partition table
	for p in $parts; do
		pt=$(lsblk -dno PARTTYPE "$p" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
		[ -n "$pt" ] || pt=$(blkid -p -o value -s PART_ENTRY_TYPE "$p" 2>/dev/null || true)
		esp=0
		case "$(printf '%s' "$pt" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" in c12a7328-f81f-11d2-ba4b-00a0c93ec93b|0xef) esp=1 ;; esac
		ft=$(lsblk -dno FSTYPE "$p" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
		[ -n "$ft" ] || ft=$(blkid -p -o value -s TYPE "$p" 2>/dev/null || true)
		fs=""
		[ "$ft" = vfat ] && fs=fat
		lb=$(lsblk -dno LABEL "$p" 2>/dev/null || true)
		[ -n "$lb" ] || lb=$(blkid -p -o value -s LABEL "$p" 2>/dev/null || true)
		efi_part "$p" "$esp" "$fs" "$(lsblk -dno MOUNTPOINT "$p" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 1p || true)" "$lb"
	done
}
efi_scan() {
	EFI_FOUND="" EFI_NOTE=""
	if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then mac_efi "$1"; else lin_efi "$1"; fi
}
efi_report() { # what efi_scan found on DISK, as a warning
	if [ -n "$EFI_FOUND" ]; then
		echo "WARNING: $1 holds an EFI, and writing the stick erases it:"
		printf '%s' "$EFI_FOUND" | sed 's/^/  - /'
		echo "If a computer boots from this stick (an OpenCore recovery or boot stick, an installer), it will not boot from it any"
		echo "more: copy its EFI folder somewhere safe first."
	fi
	[ -z "$EFI_NOTE" ] || printf '%s' "$EFI_NOTE" | sed 's/^/note: /'
	return 0
}
disk_name() { # the DISK argument, checked: a whole disk's name
	D=${1#/dev/}
	if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then
		case "$D" in disk[0-9]|disk[0-9][0-9]) ;; *) die "name a whole disk such as disk4 (see --list)" ;; esac
	else
		case "$D" in */*|'') die "name a disk such as sdb (see --list)" ;; esac
	fi
}

case "$OS" in Darwin|Linux) ;; *) die "macOS or Linux only (Windows: IntelXe Manager, Report page, Probe stick)" ;; esac
if [ "$LIST" = 1 ]; then
	echo "Disks:"
	if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then mac_list; else lin_list; fi
	exit 0
fi
if [ "$EFI_ONLY" = 1 ]; then
	[ $# = 1 ] || die "usage: write-stick.sh --efi DISK"
	disk_name "$1"
	efi_scan "$D"
	if [ -n "$EFI_FOUND" ]; then efi_report "$D"; else echo "$D: no EFI found"; efi_report "$D"; fi
	exit 0
fi
[ $# = 2 ] || die "usage: write-stick.sh IMAGE DISK (or --list); see --help"
IMG=$1
disk_name "$2"
[ -f "$IMG" ] || die "no image $IMG (tools/probe-stick/build.sh makes one)"
ISZ=$(wc -c < "$IMG" | tr -d ' ')
MIN=$ISZ
if [ -f "$IMG.sha256" ]; then
	want=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$IMG.sha256")
	got=$(sha < "$IMG")
	[ "$want" = "$got" ] || die "$IMG does not match $IMG.sha256: download it again"
	echo "image: $IMG, $(gb "$ISZ"), SHA-256 matches"
else
	echo "image: $IMG, $(gb "$ISZ") (no .sha256 next to it: not checked)"
fi

check_disk() { if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then mac_check "$D" || die "$WHY"; else lin_check "$D" || die "$WHY"; fi; }
check_disk
if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then RAW=/dev/r$D; else RAW=/dev/$D; fi
echo
echo "disk:  $D  $(gb "$SIZE")  $BUS  $MODEL"
if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then diskutil list "$D" | sed '1d; s/^/       /'; else lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,LABEL,MOUNTPOINT "/dev/$D" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/       /'; fi
efi_scan "$D"
echo
efi_report "$D"
echo "Everything on $D will be erased. Type its name ($D) to go on, anything else to stop:"
printf '> '
read -r answer || answer=""
[ "$answer" = "$D" ] || die "stopped: nothing was written"
if [ -n "$EFI_FOUND" ]; then
	if [ "$ERASE_EFI" = 1 ]; then
		echo "--erase-efi: the EFI on $D is erased with the rest"
	else
		echo "$D holds an EFI (above). Type ERASE EFI to erase it too, anything else to stop:"
		printf '> '
		read -r answer || answer=""
		[ "$answer" = "ERASE EFI" ] || die "stopped: nothing was written ($D holds an EFI; --erase-efi to erase it without this question)"
	fi
fi
# still the same disk, holding the same: a stick may have been swapped while you typed
size0=$SIZE model0=$MODEL found0=$EFI_FOUND
check_disk
[ "$SIZE" = "$size0" ] && [ "$MODEL" = "$model0" ] || die "$D changed while you typed (now $(gb "$SIZE") $MODEL): nothing was written; run it again"
efi_scan "$D"
[ "$EFI_FOUND" = "$found0" ] || die "what $D holds changed while you typed: nothing was written; run it again"

if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then
	diskutil unmountDisk "/dev/$D" >/dev/null || die "could not unmount $D"
	sudo dd if="$IMG" of="$RAW" bs=4m
else
	for p in /dev/"$D"?*; do [ -b "$p" ] && grep -q "^$p " /proc/mounts && sudo umount "$p"; done
	sudo dd if="$IMG" of="$RAW" bs=4M conv=fsync
fi
sync
echo "written; reading it back..."
back=$(sudo head -c "$ISZ" "$RAW" | sha)
[ "$back" = "$(sha < "$IMG")" ] || die "the read-back differs from the image: try another stick"
echo "the stick matches the image (SHA-256 $back)"
if [ "$OS" = Darwin ]; then diskutil eject "/dev/$D" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
echo "Done. Turn Secure Boot off on the computer to scan, and boot it from this stick."

FILE: tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# zip-image.py: the Xe probe stick's image as a release ships it, xe-probe-stick-VERSION.img.zip, and its check.
#
#   python3 -I tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py check IMAGE [--version V]       the image (as build.sh wrote it) is fit to ship
#   python3 -I tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py zip IMAGE OUT_DIR [--version V]  writes OUT_DIR/xe-probe-stick-V.img.zip
#   python3 -I tools/probe-stick/zip-image.py verify ZIP [--version V]         a zip as release.sh checks it before publishing
#
# The image must be named xe-probe-stick-V.img (V: --version when given, tools/probe-stick/VERSION in release/package.sh),
# have its .img.sha256 beside it (build.sh writes both) naming it with the right SHA-256, and have the stick's layout: a
# whole number of 512-byte sectors, an MBR whose first partition is FAT32 and holds a FAT32 boot sector labelled
# XEPROBE (the same check as IntelXe Manager's ProbeImage.CheckLayout). The zip holds exactly the image and its
# .img.sha256, at its top level, with fixed dates (the same image gives the same zip). The release lists the zip in its
# signed list of hashes; the .img.sha256 rides inside it, so the release has no separate .sha256 asset for the image
# (IntelXe Manager for macOS finds a release's list of hashes by the ending .sha256). IntelXe Manager for Windows
# downloads the zip, checks it against the signed list and unpacks the two files (ProbeStick/ProbeDownload.cs).
import hashlib, os, re, struct, sys, zipfile

NAME = re.compile(r"^xe-probe-stick-(\d+(?:\.\d+){0,3})\.img$")
MAX = 4 << 30
DATE = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)


def fail(m):
    print("error: " + m, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def layout(f, length, what):
    """The stick's layout, as ProbeImage.CheckLayout reads it."""
    if length < (1 << 20) or length > MAX: fail(f"{what}: {length} bytes, not a probe stick image (about 200 MB)")
    if length % 512: fail(f"{what}: its size is not a whole number of 512-byte sectors")
    f.seek(0)
    mbr = f.read(512)
    if mbr[510:512] != b"\x55\xaa": fail(f"{what}: no MBR")
    ptype = mbr[446 + 4]
    start = struct.unpack_from("<I", mbr, 446 + 8)[0]
    if ptype not in (0x0B, 0x0C): fail(f"{what}: its first partition is not FAT32 (type 0x{ptype:02X})")
    if start == 0 or (start + 1) * 512 > length: fail(f"{what}: its first partition starts outside the image")
    f.seek(start * 512)
    boot = f.read(512)
    if boot[510:512] != b"\x55\xaa" or boot[82:90] != b"FAT32   ": fail(f"{what}: its partition holds no FAT32 file system")
    label = boot[71:82].decode("ascii", "replace").rstrip()
    if label != "XEPROBE": fail(f"{what}: its partition is labelled {label!r}, not XEPROBE")


def sha_line(text, name, what):
    """The SHA-256 a one-line sha256sum file gives for name."""
    fields = text.split()
    if len(fields) < 2 or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{64}", fields[0]) or fields[1].lstrip("*") != name:
        fail(f"{what} holds no SHA-256 line for {name} (\"HASH  {name}\", as build.sh writes it)")
    return fields[0].lower()


def check(img, version):
    name = os.path.basename(img)
    m = NAME.match(name)
    if not m: fail(f"{img}: not named xe-probe-stick-VERSION.img (as build.sh names it)")
    if version and m.group(1) != version: fail(f"{name} is version {m.group(1)}, not {version} (tools/probe-stick/VERSION)")
    if not os.path.isfile(img): fail(f"no file {img}")
    if not os.path.isfile(img + ".sha256"): fail(f"no {name}.sha256 beside {img} (build.sh writes it)")
    with open(img + ".sha256", encoding="utf-8") as s:
        text = s.read(4097)
    if len(text) > 4096: fail(f"{name}.sha256 is not a SHA-256 file")
    want = sha_line(text, name, name + ".sha256")
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(img, "rb") as f:
        length = os.fstat(f.fileno()).st_size
        layout(f, length, name)
        f.seek(0)
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(4 << 20), b""): h.update(b)
    if h.hexdigest() != want: fail(f"{name}: SHA-256 {h.hexdigest()}, not its .img.sha256's {want} (damaged, or another build)")
    return name, text, length


def info(name):
    zi = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, DATE)
    zi.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
    zi.external_attr = 0o644 << 16
    zi.create_system = 3
    return zi


def make(img, out, version):
    name, text, length = check(img, version)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    z = os.path.join(out, name + ".zip")
    tmp = z + ".part"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, allowZip64=True) as zf:
        with open(img, "rb") as f, zf.open(info(name), "w", force_zip64=length >= (1 << 31)) as w:
            for b in iter(lambda: f.read(4 << 20), b""): w.write(b)
        zf.writestr(info(name + ".sha256"), text.encode("utf-8"))
    os.replace(tmp, z)
    verify(z, version)


def verify(z, version):
    zname = os.path.basename(z)
    if not zname.endswith(".img.zip"): fail(f"{z}: not an .img.zip")
    name = zname[:-4]
    m = NAME.match(name)
    if not m: fail(f"{zname}: not named xe-probe-stick-VERSION.img.zip")
    if version and m.group(1) != version: fail(f"{zname} is version {m.group(1)}, not {version} (tools/probe-stick/VERSION)")
    try:
        zf = zipfile.ZipFile(z)
        bad = zf.testzip()
    except Exception as e:
        fail(f"{zname}: not a zip ({e})")
    if bad: fail(f"{zname}: damaged entry {bad}")
    names = sorted(i.filename for i in zf.infolist())
    if names != sorted([name, name + ".sha256"]): fail(f"{zname} holds {names}, not exactly {name} and {name}.sha256")
    want = sha_line(zf.read(name + ".sha256").decode("utf-8"), name, name + ".sha256 in " + zname)
    entry = zf.getinfo(name)
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with zf.open(name) as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(4 << 20), b""): h.update(b)
    if h.hexdigest() != want: fail(f"{name} in {zname} does not match its .img.sha256")
    with zf.open(name) as f:   # a ZipExtFile seeks (forward by reading)
        layout(f, entry.file_size, name + " in " + zname)
    print(f"  ok    {zname}: {name} ({entry.file_size / 1e6:.0f} MB, {os.path.getsize(z) / 1e6:.0f} MB zipped) and its .img.sha256, they match")


def main(a):
    version = None
    if "--version" in a:
        i = a.index("--version")
        if i + 1 >= len(a): fail("--version needs a value")
        version = a[i + 1]
        del a[i:i + 2]
    if len(a) == 2 and a[0] == "check":
        name, _, length = check(a[1], version)
        print(f"  ok    {name}: {length / 1e6:.0f} MB, the stick's layout, its .img.sha256 matches")
    elif len(a) == 3 and a[0] == "zip": make(a[1], a[2], version)
    elif len(a) == 2 and a[0] == "verify": verify(a[1], version)
    else:
        sys.stderr.write("".join(l[2:] for l in open(__file__, encoding="utf-8").readlines()[3:8]))
        sys.exit(2)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

FILE: tools/probe-stick/image/build-inside.sh

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build-inside.sh: the Xe probe stick image build. build.sh runs it in the pinned Alpine image as linux/amd64, with the
# repository read-only at /src and tools/probe-stick/out at /out.
#
#   sh build-inside.sh build   /out/xe-probe-stick-VERSION.img (raw USB image), .manifest.txt, .img.sha256, /out/usb/
#   sh build-inside.sh lock    print the apk and tool lines of sources.lock for the package files Alpine has now
#
# Nothing ships that is not pinned in sources.lock: the kernel and firmware by URL and SHA-256 (Arch Linux Archive),
# the user space by Alpine package file and SHA-256, GRUB likewise. The packages are unpacked, never installed, so no
# package script runs. The build tools themselves (kmod's depmod, cpio, zstd, mtools, ...) come from the image's
# repositories; their versions go into the manifest.
set -eu
export LC_ALL=C
SRC=/src
PS=$SRC/tools/probe-stick
LOCK=$PS/sources.lock
OUT=/out
CACHE=$OUT/cache
VERSION=$(cat "$PS/VERSION")
NAME=xe-probe-stick-$VERSION
LABEL=XEPROBE
MARKER=xe-probe-stick.marker
W=/tmp/xs            # work area (container-local)
R=$W/root            # the root file system that becomes the initramfs
K=$W/kernel
F=$W/firmware
U=$OUT/usb           # the stick's files
# the user space of the image: busybox, kmod (modprobe/modinfo/lsmod with module blacklists), lspci with names
IMAGE_APKS="busybox musl kmod kmod-libs libcrypto3 xz-libs zlib zstd-libs pciutils pciutils-libs hwdata-pci"
TOOL_APKS="grub grub-efi"
# the modules the stick loads by name; modprobe --show-depends adds what they need
ROOT_MODULES="xe i915 usb-storage uas vfat nls_iso8859_1 nls_utf8"
GRUB_MODULES="part_msdos part_gpt fat search search_fs_file search_label normal linux echo all_video efi_gop efi_uga
	configfile test sleep halt reboot"

say() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
sha() { sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }

lock() {
	apk update -q >/dev/null && apk add -q curl >/dev/null
	mkdir -p /tmp/lock
	for kind in apk tool; do
		if [ $kind = apk ]; then pk=$IMAGE_APKS; else pk=$TOOL_APKS; fi
		for p in $pk; do
			url=$(apk fetch --simulate --url --arch x86_64 "$p" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^https?://' | head -1)
			[ -n "$url" ] || die "no package $p"
			curl -fsSL -o "/tmp/lock/${url##*/}" "$url"
			printf '%-8s %-14s %s %s\n' "$kind" "$p" "$(sha "/tmp/lock/${url##*/}")" "$url"
		done
	done
}

fetch() { # every pinned file into the cache, checked
	mkdir -p "$CACHE"
	grep -E '^(kernel|firmware|apk|tool|license) ' "$LOCK" | while read -r kind name want url; do
		f=$CACHE/${url##*/}
		if [ -f "$f" ] && [ "$(sha "$f")" = "$want" ]; then continue; fi
		echo "  fetch ${url##*/}"
		curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$f.part" "$url" || die "download failed: $url (an Alpine package Alpine replaced? build.sh lock)"
		got=$(sha "$f.part")
		[ "$got" = "$want" ] || { rm -f "$f.part"; die "SHA-256 of ${url##*/} is $got, sources.lock says $want"; }
		mv "$f.part" "$f"
	done
}
cached() { f=$CACHE/$(awk -v k="$1" -v n="$2" '$1 == k && $2 == n { u = $4; sub(/.*\//, "", u); print u }' "$LOCK"); [ -f "$f" ] || die "$1 $2 is not in sources.lock"; echo "$f"; }

case "${1:-build}" in
lock) lock; exit 0 ;;
build) ;;
*) die "usage: build-inside.sh build|lock" ;;
esac

EPOCH=$(awk '$1 == "epoch" { print $4 }' "$LOCK")
export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$EPOCH
rm -rf "$W" "$U" "$OUT/$NAME".*
mkdir -p "$W" "$R" "$K" "$F" "$U"

say "build tools"
apk add -q kmod zstd cpio coreutils grep mtools dosfstools sfdisk curl tar >/dev/null
fetch
apk add -q --allow-untrusted $(for p in $TOOL_APKS; do cached tool "$p"; done) >/dev/null
TOOLS=$(apk list -I 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(kmod|zstd|cpio|coreutils|mtools|dosfstools|sfdisk|grub|grub-efi|tar)-[0-9]' | cut -d' ' -f1 | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "  $TOOLS"

say "kernel"
tar --zstd -xf "$(cached kernel linux)" -C "$K"
KVER=$(ls "$K/usr/lib/modules")
[ "$(echo "$KVER" | wc -w)" = 1 ] || die "expected one kernel version in the package, got: $KVER"
[ -f "$K/usr/lib/modules/$KVER/vmlinuz" ] || die "no vmlinuz in the kernel package"
mkdir -p "$K/lib" && mv "$K/usr/lib/modules" "$K/lib/modules"
KM=$K/lib/modules/$KVER
echo "  $KVER"
sh "$PS/image/kconfig-check.sh" "$KM/vmlinuz" "$KM/modules.builtin" "$W/config" > "$W/kconfig.txt" || { cat "$W/kconfig.txt"; die "kernel configuration check failed"; }
cat "$W/kconfig.txt"

say "modules (only what the stick loads, and what those need)"
depmod -b "$K" "$KVER"
modprobe -d "$K" -S "$KVER" --show-depends -a $ROOT_MODULES > "$W/deps.txt" || die "modprobe --show-depends failed"
M=$R/lib/modules/$KVER
mkdir -p "$M"
awk '$1 == "insmod" { print $2 }' "$W/deps.txt" | sort -u | while read -r p; do
	rel=${p#"$K"/lib/modules/"$KVER"/}
	case "$rel" in /*) die "module outside the tree: $p" ;; esac
	mkdir -p "$M/$(dirname "$rel")"
	zstd -q -d -c "$p" > "$M/${rel%.zst}"
done
cp "$KM/modules.builtin" "$KM/modules.builtin.modinfo" "$KM/modules.order" "$M/"
depmod -b "$R" "$KVER"
(cd "$M" && find kernel -name '*.ko' | sort) > "$W/modules.txt"
echo "  $(wc -l < "$W/modules.txt") modules: $(sed 's#.*/##; s#\.ko$##' "$W/modules.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
N=$(grep -cE '/(drivers/net|net/wireless|net/mac80211|net/bluetooth|drivers/bluetooth|drivers/usb/net|drivers/infiniband)/' "$W/modules.txt" || true)
[ "$N" = 0 ] || die "$N network or radio modules in the image"
echo "  network, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth modules in the image: 0"

say "GPU firmware (linux-firmware i915/ and xe/ only)"
tar --zstd -xf "$(cached firmware linux-firmware-intel)" -C "$F"
mkdir -p "$R/lib/firmware"
for d in i915 xe; do
	[ -d "$F/usr/lib/firmware/$d" ] || die "no $d/ in the firmware package"
	cp -a "$F/usr/lib/firmware/$d" "$R/lib/firmware/"
done
FWL=$F/usr/share/licenses/linux-firmware-intel
for l in LICENSE.i915 LICENSE.xe; do [ -f "$FWL/$l" ] || die "no $l in the firmware package"; cp "$FWL/$l" "$R/lib/firmware/"; done
# every firmware file xe and i915 name must be here (compressed: the kernel loads .zst)
: > "$W/fw-missing.txt"
for m in xe i915; do
	modinfo -b "$R" -k "$KVER" -F firmware "$m" | while read -r fw; do
		[ -e "$R/lib/firmware/$fw" ] || [ -e "$R/lib/firmware/$fw.zst" ] || echo "$m: $fw" >> "$W/fw-missing.txt"
	done
done
echo "  $(find "$R/lib/firmware" -type f | wc -l) files, $(du -sk "$R/lib/firmware" | cut -f1) KB"
[ -s "$W/fw-missing.txt" ] && { echo "  named by the drivers but not in linux-firmware $(basename "$(cached firmware linux-firmware-intel)"):"; sed 's/^/    /' "$W/fw-missing.txt"; }

say "user space (Alpine package files, unpacked)"
: > "$W/packages.txt"
for p in $IMAGE_APKS; do
	f=$(cached apk "$p")
	tar -xzf "$f" -C "$R" --exclude='.PKGINFO' --exclude='.SIGN.*' --exclude='.pre-*' --exclude='.post-*' --exclude='.trigger' 2>/dev/null
	tar -xzOf "$f" .PKGINFO 2>/dev/null | awk -v f="${f##*/}" '/^pkgname = /{ n = $3 } /^pkgver = /{ v = $3 } /^license = /{ sub(/^license = /, ""); l = $0 } /^origin = /{ o = $3 }
		END { printf "%s-%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", n, v, l, o, f }' >> "$W/packages.txt"
done
LD=$R/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1
[ -x "$LD" ] || die "no musl loader in the image"
IMG() { "$LD" --library-path "$R/lib:$R/usr/lib" "$@"; }
# busybox applet links, from the image's own busybox; kmod's own tools stay (they read modprobe.d and the cmdline)
IMG "$R/bin/busybox" --list-full | while read -r a; do
	[ -e "$R/$a" ] || [ -L "$R/$a" ] || { mkdir -p "$R/$(dirname "$a")"; ln -s /bin/busybox "$R/$a"; }
done
# no network client or server, nothing that formats, partitions or copies raw to a drive, nothing that turns swap on
for a in wget nc netcat telnet telnetd udhcpc udhcpc6 udhcpd dhcprelay ftpget ftpput ftpd tftp tftpd httpd ntpd ping ping6 \
	traceroute traceroute6 ssl_client arping nslookup whois sendmail popmaildir inetd dnsd nameif ifenslave tunctl vconfig \
	zcip brctl ether-wake pscan route ifconfig ifup ifdown ip ipaddr iplink ipneigh iproute iprule iptunnel nbd-client \
	rdate microcom slattach ssl_client \
	dd mkfs.vfat mkdosfs mkfs.ext2 mke2fs mkswap swapon swapoff fdisk fsck shred blkdiscard fstrim fatattr fdflush losetup \
	nandwrite nanddump partprobe raidautorun hwclock rtcwake watchdog; do
	for d in bin sbin usr/bin usr/sbin; do rm -f "$R/$d/$a"; done
done
rm -rf "$R/etc/network" "$R/etc/logrotate.d" "$R/etc/busybox-paths.d" "$R/usr/share/man" "$R/usr/share/doc"
for t in busybox lspci kmod; do
	b=$(find "$R/bin" "$R/sbin" "$R/usr/bin" "$R/usr/sbin" -name "$t" \( -type f -o -type l \) 2>/dev/null | head -1)
	[ -n "$b" ] || die "$t is not in the image"
	l=$(readlink "$b" || true); case "$l" in /*) b=$R$l ;; esac
	IMG "$b" --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || IMG "$b" --help >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "does not run: ${b#"$R"}"
	echo "  runs: $t (${b#"$R"})"
done
mkdir -p "$W/bin" && ln -sf "$R/bin/kmod" "$W/bin/modinfo"   # kmod picks its tool by the name it was started as
IMG "$W/bin/modinfo" -b "$R" -k "$KVER" -F vermagic xe >/dev/null || die "the image's modinfo cannot read xe.ko"
echo "  the image's kmod reads the image's modules"

say "the stick's programs"
mkdir -p "$R/usr/lib/xe-stick" "$R/etc/xe-stick" "$R/etc/modprobe.d"
cp -R "$PS/rootfs/." "$R/"
cp "$SRC/tools/report/collect-linux.sh" "$R/usr/lib/xe-stick/collect-linux.sh"
chmod 0755 "$R/init" "$R/usr/lib/xe-stick/"*.sh
for s in "$R/init" "$R/usr/lib/xe-stick/"*.sh; do IMG "$R/bin/busybox" sh -n "$s" || die "syntax: $s"; done
printf 'root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/sh\n' > "$R/etc/passwd"
printf 'root:x:0:\n' > "$R/etc/group"
printf 'NAME="Xe probe stick"\nID=xe-probe-stick\nVERSION_ID=%s\nPRETTY_NAME="Xe probe stick %s (Linux %s)"\n' \
	"$VERSION" "$VERSION" "$KVER" > "$R/etc/os-release"
echo "$VERSION" > "$R/etc/xe-stick/version"
{
	echo "stick:    $NAME"
	echo "kernel:   $KVER ($(basename "$(cached kernel linux)"))"
	echo "firmware: $(basename "$(cached firmware linux-firmware-intel)")"
	echo "alpine:   $(awk '$1 == "image" && $2 == "alpine" { print $4 }' "$LOCK")"
	echo "lock:     sources.lock sha256 $(sha "$LOCK")"
} > "$R/etc/xe-stick/build.txt"
mkdir -p "$R/dev" "$R/proc" "$R/sys" "$R/run" "$R/tmp" "$R/mnt/stick" "$R/root"
rm -f "$R/dev/console" "$R/dev/null"
mknod -m 600 "$R/dev/console" c 5 1
mknod -m 666 "$R/dev/null" c 1 3

say "initramfs"
find "$R" -exec touch -h -d "@$EPOCH" {} +
(cd "$R" && find . | sort | cpio -o -H newc -R 0:0 --reproducible --quiet) > "$W/initramfs.cpio"
mkdir -p "$U/EFI/BOOT" "$U/boot/grub" "$U/REPORTS" "$U/LICENSES/linux-firmware"
zstd -q -19 --single-thread -c "$W/initramfs.cpio" > "$U/boot/initramfs.img"
cp "$KM/vmlinuz" "$U/boot/vmlinuz"
echo "  initramfs $(du -k "$U/boot/initramfs.img" | cut -f1) KB (cpio $(du -k "$W/initramfs.cpio" | cut -f1) KB), vmlinuz $(du -k "$U/boot/vmlinuz" | cut -f1) KB"

cp "$FWL/LICENSE.i915" "$FWL/LICENSE.xe" "$U/LICENSES/linux-firmware/"

cp "$SRC/LICENSE" "$U/LICENSES/xe-probe-stick-MIT.txt" 2>/dev/null || cp "$(cached license MIT)" "$U/LICENSES/xe-probe-stick-MIT.txt"

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Xe probe stick boot menu. ASCII only: GRUB's EFI text console shows anything else as '?'.
set timeout=10
set default=0
insmod all_video
insmod efi_gop
# keep the firmware's frame buffer: the kernel's simpledrm shows the text until the GPU driver takes over
set gfxpayload=keep

# panic=30 softlockup_panic=1 hung_task_panic=1 nmi_watchdog=panic: a driver bind that wedges the kernel ends in a
# reboot after 30 s instead of a frozen screen; the stage file on the stick then skips that step on the next boot.
# efi_pstore.pstore_disable=1: a panic never writes the kernel log into firmware variables.
set common="rdinit=/init console=tty0 quiet loglevel=3 log_buf_len=8M panic=30 softlockup_panic=1 hung_task_panic=1 nmi_watchdog=panic efi_pstore.pstore_disable=1"

menuentry "Xe probe stick: scan this computer" {
	linux /boot/vmlinuz $common xestick.mode=full
	initrd /boot/initramfs.img
}
menuentry "Xe probe stick: safe scan (no GPU driver; use it if the scan above froze)" {
	linux /boot/vmlinuz $common nomodeset xestick.mode=safe
	initrd /boot/initramfs.img
}
menuentry "Xe probe stick: shell (for developers; every other disk read-only)" {
	linux /boot/vmlinuz $common xestick.mode=shell
	initrd /boot/initramfs.img
}
menuentry "Turn this computer off" {
	halt
}

FILE: tools/probe-stick/image/kconfig-check.sh
================================================
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# kconfig-check.sh VMLINUZ MODULES.BUILTIN CONFIG-OUT: check the configuration of the kernel the stick ships.
#
# The configuration is read from the kernel image itself (CONFIG_IKCONFIG: scripts/extract-ikconfig's method): the
# compressed vmlinux inside the bzImage is found by its zstd, xz or gzip magic, unpacked, and the gzip blob after
# "IKCFG_ST" is the .config. Then every option the stick depends on is checked, and modules.builtin is searched for a
# network, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth driver built into the kernel (the image deletes modules, it cannot delete a built-in one).
# Prints one line per check; exits 1 if any fails. Needs GNU grep (-b with -P), zstd, xz and gzip.
set -u
export LC_ALL=C
V=$1; B=$2; C=$3
T=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT

found=""
for magic in '\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd:zstd -dc' '\xfd\x37\x7a\x58\x5a\x00:xz -dc' '\x1f\x8b\x08:gzip -dc'; do
	for off in $(grep -aboP "${magic%%:*}" "$V" | cut -d: -f1 | head -8); do
		tail -c +$((off + 1)) "$V" | ${magic#*:} > "$T/vmlinux" 2>/dev/null
		o=$(grep -abo 'IKCFG_ST' "$T/vmlinux" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
		[ -n "$o" ] || continue
		tail -c +$((o + 9)) "$T/vmlinux" | gzip -dc > "$C" 2>/dev/null
		grep -q '^CONFIG_' "$C" && { found=${magic#*:}; break 2; }
	done
done
[ -n "$found" ] || { echo "FAIL could not read the configuration from $V (no CONFIG_IKCONFIG?)"; exit 1; }
echo "configuration: $(sed -n 's/^# Linux\/\(.*\) Configuration$/\1/p' "$C" | head -1), read from the kernel image (${found%% *})"

FAIL=0
val() { v=$(sed -n "s/^CONFIG_$1=//p" "$C" | head -1); [ -n "$v" ] || v=n; printf '%s' "$v"; }
need() { # SYMBOL ALLOWED(y|m|n|y/m) WHY
	v=$(val "$1")
	case "/$2/" in *"/$v/"*) r=ok ;; *) r=FAIL; FAIL=1 ;; esac
	printf '%-4s CONFIG_%s=%s (want %s): %s\n' "$r" "$1" "$v" "$2" "$3"
}
need MMIOTRACE y "the trace step records the GPU driver's register accesses"
need HOTPLUG_CPU y "mmiotrace takes all CPUs but one offline while it runs"
need TRACING y "tracefs, which mmiotrace writes to"
need DRM_XE m "xe as a module: bound per device, under the trace"
need DRM_XE_DISPLAY y "xe drives the display (VBT, DMC, connectors)"
need DRM_I915 m "i915 as a module, for the GPUs xe does not drive"
need DEBUG_FS y "debugfs: GuC/HuC state, VBT, display info (collect-linux.sh)"
need EFIVAR_FS y/m "efivarfs, mounted read-only (Secure Boot state)"
need EFI_STUB y "booted by GRUB on UEFI"
need BLK_DEV_INITRD y "the whole system is the initramfs"
need RD_ZSTD y "the initramfs is zstd-compressed"
need DEVTMPFS y "device nodes without udev"
need TMPFS y "/run and /tmp in RAM"
need FW_LOADER y "GPU firmware from /lib/firmware"
need FW_LOADER_COMPRESS_ZSTD y "the firmware files stay .zst as linux-firmware packs them"
need FW_LOADER_USER_HELPER n "the firmware loads without a user-space helper"
need MAGIC_SYSRQ y "the dead-man's fallback power-off"
need SOFTLOCKUP_DETECTOR y "softlockup_panic=1 turns a stuck CPU into a reboot"
need DETECT_HUNG_TASK y "hung_task_panic=1 turns a stuck driver bind into a reboot"
need IKCONFIG y "this check reads the configuration back from the kernel image"
need MSDOS_PARTITION y "the stick's MBR partition table"
need USB_XHCI_HCD y/m "USB 3 host (the stick)"
need USB_STORAGE y/m "the stick"
need BLK_DEV_SD y/m "the stick"
need VFAT_FS y/m "the stick's FAT32"
need MODULE_SIG_FORCE n "the image's modules are unpacked copies of the signed ones; nothing else may be required"
need LOCK_DOWN_KERNEL_FORCE_INTEGRITY n "lockdown would forbid mmiotrace"
need LOCK_DOWN_KERNEL_FORCE_CONFIDENTIALITY n "lockdown would forbid mmiotrace and debugfs"
need EFI_VARS_PSTORE_DEFAULT_DISABLE y "a panic does not write the kernel log into firmware variables"
# no network, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth stack built in (modules are deleted by the image build)
for s in CFG80211 MAC80211 BT E1000 E1000E IGB IGC IXGBE R8169 VIRTIO_NET USB_USBNET USB_RTL8152 THUNDERBOLT_NET \
	IWLWIFI ATH9K ATH10K_PCI ATH11K ATH12K RTW88 RTW89 MT76_CORE BRCMFMAC; do
	v=$(val "$s"); case "$v" in y) need "$s" n/m "no network driver built in" ;; esac
done
# modules.builtin lists every driver compiled into the kernel that could have been a module
NET=$(grep -E '^kernel/(drivers/net/(ethernet|wireless|usb|phy|wwan|ppp|can|ieee802154|hyperv|xen-netfront|vmxnet3)|drivers/bluetooth|net/(wireless|mac80211|bluetooth|nfc|can|ieee802154))/' "$B" || true)
if [ -n "$NET" ]; then
	echo "FAIL built-in network/radio drivers: $(echo "$NET" | tr '\n' ' ')"; FAIL=1
else
	echo "ok   no network, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth driver in modules.builtin (built in: $(grep -c '^kernel/drivers/net/' "$B" || true) virtual device driver(s) under drivers/net: $(grep '^kernel/drivers/net/' "$B" | sed 's#.*/##; s#\.ko$##' | tr '\n' ' '))"
fi
exit $FAIL

FILE: tools/probe-stick/rootfs/init
================================================
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Xe probe stick: PID 1. The whole system is this initramfs, in RAM: no disk is the root file system and nothing is
# installed. PID 1 must never exit (the kernel would panic), so every path ends in power-off or an endless sleep.
export PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root TERM=linux LC_ALL=C

mount -t proc -o nosuid,nodev,noexec proc /proc
mount -t sysfs -o nosuid,nodev,noexec sysfs /sys
mount -t devtmpfs -o nosuid devtmpfs /dev
mkdir -p /dev/pts /run /tmp /mnt/stick
mount -t devpts -o nosuid,noexec devpts /dev/pts
mount -t tmpfs -o mode=0755,nosuid,nodev tmpfs /run
mount -t tmpfs -o mode=1777,nosuid,nodev tmpfs /tmp
# efivarfs read-only: the stick never writes a firmware variable (a bad NVRAM write has bricked laptops)
if [ -d /sys/firmware/efi/efivars ]; then
	mount -t efivarfs -o ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec efivarfs /sys/firmware/efi/efivars
fi
mount -t debugfs -o nosuid,nodev,noexec debugfs /sys/kernel/debug
mount -t tracefs -o nosuid,nodev,noexec tracefs /sys/kernel/tracing
exec </dev/console >/dev/console 2>&1
# a name the reports need not hide (the kernel's default here is its build host's)
hostname localhost

sh /usr/lib/xe-stick/scan.sh
echo "xe-stick: scan.sh ended ($?); turning the computer off"
sync
umount /mnt/stick 2>/dev/null
sync
poweroff -f
while :; do sleep 3600; done

FILE: tools/probe-stick/rootfs/usr/lib/xe-stick/trace-filter.awk
================================================
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# trace-filter.awk: mmiotrace text in, the same text out without the accesses that fall inside the given address
# ranges: the GPU's VRAM or aperture BARs, where the console's frame-buffer writes would bury the register traffic.
#   awk -v ranges="0xSTART 0xEND [0xSTART 0xEND ...]" -v stats=FILE -f trace-filter.awk RAW > KEPT
# mmiotrace's line formats (kernel/trace/trace_mmiotrace.c): "R|W width secs.usecs map-id phys value pc pid",
# "MAP secs map-id phys virt len pc pid", "UNMAP secs map-id virt pid", "MARK secs text", "PCIDEV ...", "VERSION ...".
# MAP, UNMAP, MARK and PCIDEV lines are always kept. Addresses compare as zero-padded strings, so there is no 64-bit
# arithmetic in awk (busybox awk's numbers are doubles).
function pad(h) { h = tolower(h); sub(/^0x/, "", h); return "x" substr("0000000000000000", 1, 16 - length(h)) h }
BEGIN {
	n = split(ranges, r, " ")
	m = 0
	for (i = 1; i + 1 <= n; i += 2) { m++; lo[m] = pad(r[i]); hi[m] = pad(r[i + 1]) }
}
($1 == "R" || $1 == "W") && NF >= 5 {
	rw++
	a = pad($5)
	for (i = 1; i <= m; i++) if (a >= lo[i] && a <= hi[i]) { dropped++; next }
}
{ kept++; print }
END { if (stats != "") printf "lines %d\nkept %d\naccesses %d\ndropped %d\n", NR, kept, rw, dropped > stats }



================================================
FILE: tools/probe-stick/stick/README.txt
================================================
Xe probe stick
==============

This stick collects what the Intel GPU macOS driver project needs to bring up an Intel GPU: what Linux's own xe/i915
driver finds and programs on your hardware, and a register trace (mmiotrace) of that driver starting your GPU. It does
not install anything, has no network drivers, and sets every disk in the computer read-only before it mounts anything.

1. Turn Secure Boot off in the firmware setup (the stick's boot loader is not signed). Turn it back on afterwards.
2. Boot from this stick (the boot menu key is usually F8, F11 or F12). Choose "scan this computer".
3. Wait. It takes three to five minutes. The screen may go black or flicker while the GPU driver starts; that is
   expected. The computer turns itself off at the end.
4. Put the stick into any computer. The report is in REPORTS/: xe-stick-XR-XXXXXXXX.tar.gz, a .txt summary next to it
   and a .sha256 file. Attach the .tar.gz to a GitHub issue and write the report ID (XR-...) in the form.

If the computer freezes: hold the power button and boot the stick again. The stick remembers the step that froze this
computer and leaves it out from then on (REPORTS/xe-stick-state.txt; delete that file to try every step again).
If it freezes again, choose "safe scan": it starts no GPU driver at all.

What is collected, what never is, and why: tools/probe-stick/README.md in the project's repository.
The licences of what is on this stick: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt and LICENSES/.



================================================
FILE: tools/probe-stick/stick/REPORTS-README.txt
================================================
The Xe probe stick writes its reports here, three files per scan:
  xe-stick-XR-XXXXXXXX.tar.gz   the report: attach this file to the GitHub issue
  xe-stick-XR-XXXXXXXX.txt      a summary of it, to read first
  xe-stick-XR-XXXXXXXX.sha256   the SHA-256 of both (the .tar.gz holds SEAL.sha256 for every file inside)
xe-stick-state.txt remembers the steps that froze a computer, so that the next scan leaves them out. Delete it to try
every step again.

FILE: tools/probe-stick/test/check-report.py
================================================
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Judge the two QEMU boots of qemu-test.sh: check-report.py TESTDIR (the planted values in $SECRETS).

Boot 1 is a clean scan; boot 2 hangs in collect-after on purpose (xestick.testhang) until its dead-man powers the PC
off; boot 3 must leave that step out (and ignore a freeze planted for another computer); boot 4 is the safe scan.
Prints one line per check and exits 1 if any fails."""
import gzip
import hashlib
import os
import re
import sys
import tarfile

T = sys.argv[1]
SECRETS = os.environ["SECRETS"].split()
fails = []


def check(name, cond, detail=""):
    print(("  ok   " if cond else "  FAIL ") + name + ("   [%s]" % detail if detail != "" else ""))
    if not cond:
        fails.append(name)


def forms(v):
    """Every spelling of a planted value that would identify it."""
    out = {v, v.upper(), v.lower()}
    if re.fullmatch(r"([0-9a-f]{2}:){5}[0-9a-f]{2}", v):
        out |= {v.replace(":", ""), v.replace(":", "").upper(), v.replace(":", "-"), v.replace(":", "-").upper()}
    return out


def members(tf):
    """name -> bytes for every file in the report, trace .gz files unpacked too."""
    out = {}
    for m in tf.getmembers():
        if m.isfile():
            data = tf.extractfile(m).read()
            out[m.name] = data
            if m.name.endswith(".gz"):
                out[m.name + " (unpacked)"] = gzip.decompress(data)
    return out


def judge(n, previous=(), safe=False):
    print("\n== boot %d" % n)
    rc, secs = open(os.path.join(T, "qemu-%d.rc" % n)).read().split()
    check("QEMU powered off by itself (no time-out)", rc == "0", "exit %s after %s s" % (rc, secs))
    serial = open(os.path.join(T, "serial-%d.log" % n), "rb").read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
    check("the scan said Done on the console", "Done. On the stick: REPORTS/" in serial,
          "\n".join(serial.splitlines()[-15:]) if "Done. On the stick" not in serial else "")
    d = os.path.join(T, "reports-%d" % n)
    files = sorted(os.listdir(d)) if os.path.isdir(d) else []
    tars = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".tar.gz") and f not in previous]
    check("exactly one new report on the stick", len(tars) == 1, files)
    check("no half-written file and no privacy-check failure", not [f for f in files if f.endswith(".part") or "privacy" in f], files)
    a = open(os.path.join(T, "disk-before-%d.sha256" % n)).read().split()[0]
    b = open(os.path.join(T, "disk-after-%d.sha256" % n)).read().split()[0]
    check("the SATA disk is byte-identical after the scan", a == b, a[:12] + " -> " + b[:12])
    if len(tars) != 1:
        return None, files
    base = tars[0][:-len(".tar.gz")]
    for ext in (".txt", ".sha256"):
        check("%s%s sits next to it" % (base, ext), os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, base + ext)))
    seal = {}
    for line in open(os.path.join(d, base + ".sha256")):
        h, f = line.split()
        seal[f] = h
    ok = all(hashlib.sha256(open(os.path.join(d, f), "rb").read()).hexdigest() == h for f, h in seal.items())
    check("the .sha256 seal verifies the .tar.gz and the .txt", ok and set(seal) == {base + ".tar.gz", base + ".txt"}, seal)
    tf = tarfile.open(os.path.join(d, base + ".tar.gz"))
    m = members(tf)
    root = base
    inner = {}
    for line in m.get(root + "/SEAL.sha256", b"").decode().splitlines():
        h, f = line.split(None, 1)
        inner[f.strip()] = h
    real = {k[len(root) + 1:]: hashlib.sha256(v).hexdigest() for k, v in m.items()
            if not k.endswith(" (unpacked)") and k != root + "/SEAL.sha256"}
    check("SEAL.sha256 lists every file in the report with its SHA-256", inner == real and len(real) > 20,
          sorted(set(inner) ^ set(real))[:5] or len(real))
    size = os.path.getsize(os.path.join(d, base + ".tar.gz"))
    check("the report fits a GitHub attachment (< 25 MB)", size < 25e6, "%.2f MB" % (size / 1e6))

    blob = b"\n".join(m.values()) + open(os.path.join(d, base + ".txt"), "rb").read() + \
        open(os.path.join(d, "xe-stick-state.txt"), "rb").read()
    for s in SECRETS:
        hits = sum(blob.count(f.encode()) for f in forms(s))
        check("planted %s appears nowhere in the report, its summary or the state file" % s, hits == 0, hits)
    get = lambda p: m.get(root + "/" + p, b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    red = get("stick/redaction.txt")
    nser = int((re.search(r"serial: (\d+)", red) or [0, 0])[1])
    check("sanity: the redaction learned the planted serials (DMI, disk, USB stick)", nser >= 4, red.splitlines()[:6])
    dm = get("stick/dmesg.txt")
    check("sanity: the kernel log saw the stick's serial and it was replaced",
          "SerialNumber: <redacted>" in dm or "<serial-redacted>" in dm, [l for l in dm.splitlines() if "SerialNumber" in l][:2])
    check("sanity: the report still names the machine and board (only serials removed)",
          "QEMU-XS" in get("before/system/dmi.txt") and "XS-BOARD" in get("before/system/dmi.txt"))

    net = get("stick/net.txt")
    rows = [l.split()[1:] for l in net.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    check("no network interface but lo, at every check", len(rows) >= 2 and all(r == ["lo"] for r in rows), net.strip())
    check("sanity: the e1000e network card is on the PCI bus (no interface means no driver)",
          "8086:10d3" in get("before/gpu/pci.txt") or "8086:10d3" in dm, "")
    locks = get("stick/locks.txt")
    check("the SATA disk and its decoy were set read-only", re.search(r"\bsda\s+read-only", locks) is not None, locks.strip())
    mounts = [l.split() for l in get("stick/mounts.txt").splitlines()]
    blk = [l for l in mounts if l and l[0].startswith("/dev/")]
    check("exactly one block device was mounted: the stick, at /mnt/stick",
          len(blk) == 1 and blk[0][1] == "/mnt/stick" and not blk[0][0].startswith("/dev/sda"), blk)
    summ = get("summary.txt")
    if not safe:
        check("the trace step skipped cleanly: no Intel display device",
              "trace: skipped: no Intel display-class PCI device" in summ, [l for l in summ.splitlines() if "trace" in l][:3])
    check("   ... no trace file was written", not [k for k in m if "/trace/" in k and not k.endswith("/")])
    mods = get("stick/modules.txt")
    check("   ... and no GPU driver was loaded", not re.search(r"^(xe|i915)\s", mods, re.M))
    check("the report has the summary of the collect-linux.sh run(s)", "-------- collect-linux.sh" in summ)
    check("before/ is there (collect-linux.sh without a GPU driver)", root + "/before/summary.txt" in m)
    return (m, summ, get, files)


key = open(os.path.join(T, "key.txt")).read().strip()
r1 = judge(1)
if r1[0] is not None:
    m1, summ1, get1, files1 = r1
    check("boot 1: after/ is there (a clean run does both collections)", "Steps\n  trace: skipped" in summ1 and
          any(k.endswith("/after/summary.txt") for k in m1))
    check("boot 1: no step was left out", "left out on this computer" not in summ1, "")
    files1 = r1[3]
else:
    files1 = r1[1]

print("\n== boot 2 (xestick.testhang=collect-after)")
rc, secs = open(os.path.join(T, "qemu-2.rc")).read().split()
serial2 = open(os.path.join(T, "serial-2.log"), "rb").read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
check("the scan hung in collect-after as told", "hanging here until the dead-man" in serial2)
check("   ... and the dead-man turned the PC off (QEMU exited by itself)",
      rc == "0" and "did not finish within 15 s" in serial2, "exit %s after %s s" % (rc, secs))
files2 = sorted(os.listdir(os.path.join(T, "reports-2")))
check("   ... no report was written", [f for f in files2 if f.endswith(".tar.gz")] == [f for f in files1 if f.endswith(".tar.gz")], files2)
st2 = open(os.path.join(T, "reports-2", "xe-stick-state.txt")).read()
check("   ... the step is still marked running on the stick", "running %s collect-after" % key in st2, st2)
a = open(os.path.join(T, "disk-before-2.sha256")).read().split()[0]
b = open(os.path.join(T, "disk-after-2.sha256")).read().split()[0]
check("   ... the SATA disk is byte-identical", a == b)

prev = [f for f in files2 if f.endswith(".tar.gz")]
r3 = judge(3, prev)
if r3[0] is not None:
    m3, summ3, get3, files3 = r3
    check("boot 3: the freeze of boot 2 is reported", "the last run stopped during: collect-after" in summ3,
          [l for l in summ3.splitlines() if "last run" in l])
    check("   ... collect-after was left out and says so", "collect-after: skipped" in summ3 and
          not any(k.endswith("/after/summary.txt") for k in m3))
    check("   ... collect-before still ran (another computer's freeze changes nothing)",
          any(k.endswith("/before/summary.txt") for k in m3))
    st = open(os.path.join(T, "reports-3", "xe-stick-state.txt")).read()
    check("   ... the state file now says skip for this computer", "skip %s collect-after" % key in st, st)
    check("   ... no step of this computer is left 'running'", "running %s " % key not in st, st)
    check("   ... the other computer's line is untouched", "running 000000000000 collect-before" in st, st)
    check("   ... the machine key in the report matches", key in get3("stick/stages.txt"), get3("stick/stages.txt"))

prev = [f for f in (r3[1] if r3[0] is None else r3[3]) if f.endswith(".tar.gz")]
r4 = judge(4, prev, safe=True)
if r4[0] is not None:
    m4, summ4, get4, files4 = r4
    check("boot 4 (safe scan): mode safe, nomodeset on the command line", "mode safe" in summ4 and
          "nomodeset" in get4("stick/cmdline.txt"))
    check("   ... no GPU step ran and no after/ collection", "safe mode: no GPU driver was started" in summ4 and
          not any(k.endswith("/after/summary.txt") for k in m4) and "trace: skipped" not in summ4)

print("\n%s" % ("ALL PASSED" if not fails else "%d FAILED: %s" % (len(fails), "; ".join(fails))))
sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# disk-rules-test.sh: every vector of stick-disk-vectors.json through write-stick.sh's rules (write-stick.sh --rules for
# "vectors", --efi-rules for "efiVectors"), with each POSIX shell found here (sh, dash, bash, busybox sh). IntelXe
# Manager's StickRules runs the same vectors in windows/app/IntelXe.Core.Tests (StickDiskVectorTests). Needs python3 (to
# read the JSON); no Docker, no disk. test/efi-warning-test.sh tries the EFI warning itself on disk images.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
SHELLS=""
for s in sh dash bash "busybox sh"; do
	set -- $s
	command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 && SHELLS="$SHELLS|$s"
done
exec python3 -I -c '
import json, subprocess, sys
vectors_file, script, shells = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], [s for s in sys.argv[3].split("|") if s]
data = json.load(open(vectors_file))
assert data["maxBytes"] == 128 * 10**9, "write-stick.sh has MAXGB=128"
bad = 0
for shell in shells:
    for v in data["vectors"]:
        b = lambda k: "1" if v[k] else "0"
        args = shell.split() + [script, "--rules", v["bus"], b("removable"), b("whole"), b("system"), str(v["size"]), str(v["minimum"]), b("allowLarge")]
        got = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
        codes = sorted(got.stdout.split())
        if got.returncode != 0 or codes != sorted(v["refuse"]) or any(c not in data["codes"] for c in codes):
            bad += 1
            print("FAIL [%s] %s: got %s (exit %d, %s), expected %s" % (shell, v["name"], codes, got.returncode, got.stderr.strip(), sorted(v["refuse"])))
    for v in data["efiVectors"]:
        b = lambda k: "1" if v[k] else "0"
        args = shell.split() + [script, "--efi-rules", b("esp"), b("opencore"), b("bootx64"), b("probe")]
        got = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)
        codes = sorted(got.stdout.split())
        if got.returncode != 0 or codes != sorted(v["efi"]) or any(c not in data["efiCodes"] for c in codes):
            bad += 1
            print("FAIL [%s] EFI: %s: got %s (exit %d, %s), expected %s" % (shell, v["name"], codes, got.returncode, got.stderr.strip(), sorted(v["efi"])))
    print("%-10s %d vectors, %d EFI vectors" % (shell, len(data["vectors"]), len(data["efiVectors"])))
print("disk rules: %s" % ("FAILED (%d)" % bad if bad else "all vectors match"))
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
' "$HERE/stick-disk-vectors.json" "$HERE/write-stick.sh" "$SHELLS"

FILE: tools/probe-stick/test/efi-warning-test.sh

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# efi-warning-test.sh: write-stick.sh's EFI warning on real partition tables and file systems, without a USB stick.
#
#   sh tools/probe-stick/test/efi-warning-test.sh           on macOS: disk images (hdiutil, diskutil); then, when Docker
#                                                          runs, the same on Linux loop devices in the pinned Debian image
#   sh tools/probe-stick/test/efi-warning-test.sh --inside DIR    (in that container, as root) the Linux half
#
# The layouts (made on macOS with diskutil, as sparse files): esp-oc (GPT: an EFI system partition holding OpenCore,
# and an empty FAT32 volume), installer (FAT32 with EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI), probe (FAT32 with the probe stick's marker
# and its BOOTX64.EFI), plain (an empty FAT32 volume). Checked: --efi names what each holds (unmounted volumes looked at
# through a temporary read-only mount, and nothing left mounted); the write warns and asks for ERASE EFI only on esp-oc
# and installer, stops before dd on any other answer, writes after ERASE EFI or with --erase-efi, and writes plain and
# probe after the disk's name alone. The writes run a copy of write-stick.sh in which only the disk rules (they refuse a
# disk image as virtual) and sudo are left out; dd writes into the disk image, which is then compared with the image.
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:$PATH
fails=0
ok()  { echo "ok    $*"; }
bad() { echo "FAIL  $*"; fails=$((fails + 1)); }

# the copy of write-stick.sh for the writes: every disk passes the rules, no sudo, dd announces itself
stub() { # stub OUT
	sed -e 's/why "\$1" "\$(rules "\$bus" "\$rem" "\$whole" "\$sys" "\${SIZE:-0}" "\${MIN:-0}" "\$LARGE")"/why "$1" ""/' \
	    -e 's/why "\$1" "\$(rules "\$bus" "\$rem" 1 "\$sys" "\$SIZE" "\${MIN:-0}" "\$LARGE")"/why "$1" ""/' \
	    -e 's/sudo dd /echo DD-RAN >\&2; dd /' -e 's/sudo head /head /' -e 's/sudo umount /umount /' \
	    "$HERE/write-stick.sh" > "$1"
	[ "$(grep -c 'why "\$1" ""' "$1")" = 2 ] && grep -q DD-RAN "$1" || { echo "the stub did not take: write-stick.sh changed"; exit 1; }
}

# the image to write: 2 MiB with the stick's layout, and its .img.sha256
probe_image() { # probe_image DIR
	python3 -I - "$1/xe-probe-stick-0.0.1.img" <<'PY'
import hashlib, os, struct, sys
p = sys.argv[1]
b = bytearray(2 << 20)
b[446 + 4] = 0x0C
struct.pack_into("<II", b, 446 + 8, 2048, len(b) // 512 - 2048)
b[510:512] = b"\x55\xaa"
bs = 2048 * 512
b[bs + 71:bs + 82] = b"XEPROBE    "
b[bs + 82:bs + 90] = b"FAT32   "
b[bs + 510:bs + 512] = b"\x55\xaa"
b[bs + 8192:bs + 8224] = hashlib.sha256(b"probe").digest()
open(p, "wb").write(b)
open(p + ".sha256", "w").write(hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() + "  " + os.path.basename(p) + "\n")
PY
}

# ---- the cases, the same on both systems (attach FILE prints the disk's name; detach DISK; still_mounted DISK)
scan_case() { # scan_case LAYOUT EXPECTED-TEXT|none
	f=$W/$1-scan.img
	cp_sparse "$W/$1.img" "$f"
	d=$(attach "$f")
	out=$(sh "$HERE/write-stick.sh" --efi "$d" 2>&1) || true
	mounted=$(still_mounted "$d")
	detach "$d"
	rm -f "$f"
	if [ "$2" = none ]; then
		printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q "no EFI found" && ok "$1: --efi finds no EFI" || bad "$1: --efi says: $out"
	else
		printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qF "$2" && ok "$1: --efi names $2" || bad "$1: --efi says: $out"
	fi
	[ -z "$mounted" ] && ok "$1: nothing left mounted" || bad "$1: left mounted: $mounted"
}
write_case() { # write_case LAYOUT INPUT EXPECT(written|stopped) [OPTION]; DISK in INPUT is the attached disk's name
	f=$W/$1-write.img
	cp_sparse "$W/$1.img" "$f"
	d=$(attach "$f")
	input=$(printf "$2" | sed "s/^DISK\$/$d/")
	out=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | sh "$W/stub.sh" ${4:-} "$W/img/xe-probe-stick-0.0.1.img" "$d" 2>&1) && rc=0 || rc=$?
	detach "$d"
	what="$1, answers '$(printf '%s' "$2" | sed 's/\\n/|/g')'${4:+, $4}"
	written=no
	head -c 2097152 "$f" | cmp -s - "$W/img/xe-probe-stick-0.0.1.img" && written=yes
	rm -f "$f"
	if [ "$3" = written ]; then
		[ $rc = 0 ] && [ $written = yes ] && ok "$what: written and read back" || bad "$what: exit $rc, written $written: $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -3)"
	elif [ $rc != 0 ] && [ $written = no ] && ! printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q DD-RAN; then ok "$what: stopped before dd"
	else bad "$what: exit $rc, written $written: $(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -3)"; fi
	case "$1" in
	esp-oc|installer)
		printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "^WARNING: $d holds an EFI" && ok "$what: warned" || bad "$what: no warning"
		case "$2" in DISK*)
			if [ -n "${4:-}" ]; then
				printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q -e "--erase-efi: the EFI on $d is erased" && ok "$what: no question, --erase-efi said so" || bad "$what: --erase-efi not taken"
			else
				printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Type ERASE EFI" && ok "$what: asked for ERASE EFI" || bad "$what: did not ask for ERASE EFI"
			fi ;;
		esac ;;
	*)
		printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "WARNING\|ERASE EFI" && bad "$what: warned about an EFI it does not hold" || ok "$what: no EFI warning" ;;
	esac
}
cases() {
	stub "$W/stub.sh"
	scan_case esp-oc "an EFI system partition, with OpenCore (EFI/OC/OpenCore.efi)"
	scan_case installer "an EFI boot loader (EFI/BOOT/BOOTx64.efi"
	scan_case probe none
	scan_case plain none
	write_case esp-oc 'DISK\n' stopped
	write_case esp-oc 'DISK\nerase efi\n' stopped
	write_case esp-oc 'DISK\nERASE EFI\n' written
	write_case esp-oc 'DISK\n' written --erase-efi
	write_case esp-oc 'disk0\nERASE EFI\n' stopped
	write_case installer 'DISK\n' stopped
	write_case installer 'DISK\nERASE EFI\n' written
	write_case plain 'DISK\n' written
	write_case probe 'DISK\n' written
}

if [ "${1:-}" = --inside ]; then
	# ---- Linux, as root in the container: loop devices and their partitions (no udev here: the nodes are made)
	W=$2
	cp_sparse() { dd if="$1" of="$2" bs=4M conv=sparse status=none; }   # the shared folder takes no hole punching
	attach() {
		l=$(losetup -fP --show "$1")
		n=${l#/dev/}
		for p in /sys/block/"$n"/"$n"p*; do
			[ -e "$p/dev" ] || continue
			rm -f "/dev/${p##*/}"   # partition numbers are given out anew at each attach
			mknod "/dev/${p##*/}" b $(tr ':' ' ' < "$p/dev")
		done
		echo "$n"
	}
	detach() { sync; losetup -d "/dev/$1"; }
	still_mounted() { grep "^/dev/$1" /proc/mounts | cut -d' ' -f1-2 || true; }
	cases
	echo "== Linux: $fails failure(s)"
	exit $fails
fi

[ "$(uname -s)" = Darwin ] || { echo "run it on macOS (it makes the disk images with diskutil); the Linux half runs in Docker from there"; exit 2; }
W=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ixeefi.XXXXXX")
ATTACHED=""
trap 'for a in $ATTACHED; do hdiutil detach -force "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done; rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
cp_sparse() { cp -c "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || cp "$1" "$2"; }
attach() {
	a=$(hdiutil attach -imagekey diskimage-class=CRawDiskImage -nomount "$1" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR == 1 { sub("/dev/", "", $1); print $1 }')
	[ -n "$a" ] || { echo "hdiutil could not attach $1" >&2; exit 1; }
	ATTACHED="$ATTACHED $a"
	echo "$a"
}
detach() { hdiutil detach -force "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
still_mounted() { mount | grep "^/dev/$1" | cut -d' ' -f1-3 || true; }
mountpoint_of() { diskutil info -plist "$1" | plutil -extract MountPoint raw -o - - 2>/dev/null || true; }

layout() { # layout NAME SIZE_MB
	dd if=/dev/zero of="$W/$1.img" bs=1 count=0 seek=$(($2 * 1048576)) 2>/dev/null
	d=$(attach "$W/$1.img")
	diskutil partitionDisk "$d" GPT FAT32 STICK 100% >/dev/null
	s=$(diskutil list "$d" | awk '$0 ~ / STICK / { print $NF }')
	diskutil mount "$s" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
	vol=$(mountpoint_of "$s")
	[ -n "$vol" ] || { echo "could not mount $s"; exit 1; }
	case $1 in
	esp-oc)
		[ "$(diskutil info -plist "${d}s1" | plutil -extract Content raw -o - -)" = EFI ] || { echo "diskutil made no EFI system partition"; exit 1; }
		diskutil mount "${d}s1" >/dev/null
		e=$(mountpoint_of "${d}s1")
		mkdir -p "$e/EFI/OC" "$e/EFI/BOOT"
		echo oc > "$e/EFI/OC/OpenCore.efi"; echo oc > "$e/EFI/BOOT/BOOTx64.efi" ;;
	installer) mkdir -p "$vol/EFI/BOOT"; echo boot > "$vol/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI" ;;
	probe) mkdir -p "$vol/EFI/BOOT"; echo grub > "$vol/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI"; echo marker > "$vol/xe-probe-stick.marker" ;;
	esac
	diskutil unmountDisk "$d" >/dev/null
	detach "$d"
}
layout esp-oc 3072   # diskutil adds an EFI system partition to a GPT disk this large (a sparse file: about 12 MB)
layout installer 600
layout probe 600
layout plain 600
mkdir -p "$W/img"
probe_image "$W/img"
echo "== macOS (disk images)"
cases

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	IMAGE=$(awk '$1 == "image" && $2 == "qemu" { print $4 }' "$HERE/sources.lock")
	echo "== Linux ($IMAGE, loop devices)"
	docker run --rm --privileged -v "$W:/work" -v "$HERE:/probe-stick:ro" "$IMAGE" sh /probe-stick/test/efi-warning-test.sh --inside /work || fails=$((fails + $?))
else
	echo "note: no Docker here: the Linux half was not run"
fi
echo "== $fails failure(s)"
exit $fails

FILE: tools/probe-stick/test/qemu-inside.sh

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# qemu-inside.sh: boot the stick image on an emulated UEFI PC, four times. qemu-test.sh runs it in a Debian container
# (QEMU, OVMF, mtools) with the test directory at /t; it judges the results afterwards (check-report.py).
#
# The PC is loaded with what must not come out: SMBIOS system and board serials and a UUID, a USB serial on the stick,
# a SATA disk with a serial, and the same serial written inside the disk, which also carries a decoy FAT volume with the
# stick's own label and marker (the worst case for the stick finder). An e1000e network card sits on the PCI bus; the
# image has no driver for it. The disk's SHA-256 is taken before and after each boot.
#   boot 1: a clean scan.
#   boot 2: xestick.testhang=collect-after: the scan hangs in that step, as a frozen driver bind would; the step's
#           dead-man must turn the PC off, leaving the step marked running on the stick.
#   boot 3: a clean boot again, with a line from another computer planted in the state file: the scan must leave
#           collect-after out on this computer and say so, and the other computer's line must change nothing.
#   boot 4: the menu's second entry, the safe scan (nomodeset, no GPU driver): one collection, a report.
set -eu
T=/t
LIMIT=${LIMIT:-1500}
CODE=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_CODE_4M.fd
VARS=/usr/share/OVMF/OVMF_VARS_4M.fd
P=1M   # the stick's partition starts at 1 MiB
export MTOOLS_SKIP_CHECK=1
sha() { sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; }

cp "$T/xe-probe-stick.img" "$T/stick.img"
mcopy -n -i "$T/stick.img@@$P" ::/boot/grub/grub.cfg "$T/grub.cfg.orig"
grub() { # EXTRA [ENTRY]: the stick's own menu, entry ENTRY (default 0: the scan) as it is, with a serial console, no
	# menu delay, no wait before the power-off, and EXTRA
	sed -e 's/^set timeout=.*/set timeout=0/' -e "s/^set default=.*/set default=${2:-0}/" -e "s#^\\(\tlinux /boot/vmlinuz .*\\)\$#\\1 console=ttyS0,115200 xestick.wait=0 $1#" \
		"$T/grub.cfg.orig" > "$T/grub.cfg"
	grep -q "xestick.mode=safe console=ttyS0,115200 xestick.wait=0 $1" "$T/grub.cfg" || { echo "error: could not patch grub.cfg"; exit 1; }
	mcopy -o -i "$T/stick.img@@$P" "$T/grub.cfg" ::/boot/grub/grub.cfg
}

# the tester's disk: a decoy FAT volume labelled like the stick, with the marker and the disk's serial inside
truncate -s 64M "$T/disk.img"
mformat -i "$T/disk.img" -v XEPROBE -F ::
echo "decoy" > "$T/xe-probe-stick.marker"
printf 'serial of this disk: %s\n' "$SERIAL_DISK" > "$T/serial.txt"
mcopy -i "$T/disk.img" "$T/xe-probe-stick.marker" "$T/serial.txt" ::
printf '%s' "$SERIAL_DISK" | dd of="$T/disk.img" bs=1 seek=$((48 * 1048576)) conv=notrunc status=none
cp "$VARS" "$T/vars.fd"

boot() { # N
	echo "== boot $1 (limit ${LIMIT}s)"
	sha "$T/disk.img" > "$T/disk-before-$1.sha256"
	t0=$(date +%s)
	timeout "$LIMIT" qemu-system-x86_64 -machine q35 -cpu max -smp 2 -m 2048 \
		-drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file="$CODE" -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file="$T/vars.fd" \
		-device qemu-xhci,id=xhci \
		-drive if=none,id=stick,format=raw,file="$T/stick.img" \
		-device usb-storage,bus=xhci.0,drive=stick,serial="$SERIAL_STICK",removable=on \
		-drive if=none,id=d0,format=raw,file="$T/disk.img" -device ide-hd,drive=d0,bus=ide.0,serial="$SERIAL_DISK" \
		-netdev user,id=n0,restrict=on -device e1000e,netdev=n0,mac="$MAC" \
		-smbios type=0,vendor=XsBios,version=XS-BIOS-1 \
		-smbios type=1,manufacturer=XsTest,product=QEMU-XS,serial="$SERIAL_SYS",uuid="$UUID" \
		-smbios type=2,manufacturer=XsBoards,product=XS-BOARD,serial="$SERIAL_BOARD" \
		-display none -monitor none -serial file:"$T/serial-$1.log" -no-reboot
	rc=$?
	echo "QEMU exit $rc after $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) s"
	echo "$rc $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))" > "$T/qemu-$1.rc"
	sha "$T/disk.img" > "$T/disk-after-$1.sha256"
	mkdir -p "$T/reports-$1"
	mcopy -n -s -i "$T/stick.img@@$P" "::/REPORTS/*" "$T/reports-$1/" 2>/dev/null || true
	ls -la "$T/reports-$1"
}

set +e
grub ""
boot 1
grub "xestick.testhang=collect-after"
boot 2
# another computer froze during collect-before: that must change nothing here
mcopy -n -i "$T/stick.img@@$P" ::/REPORTS/xe-stick-state.txt "$T/state.txt"
printf 'running 000000000000 collect-before\n' >> "$T/state.txt"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# qemu-test.sh: the stick's end-to-end test. Boots out/xe-probe-stick-VERSION.img four times on an emulated UEFI PC (QEMU
# and OVMF in a Debian container, pinned in sources.lock; QEMU emulates x86_64 in software: about 30 s a boot here)
# and judges what it wrote (check-report.py). It fails if:
#   a planted serial number, the UUID or the MAC address survives anywhere in a report;
#   a network interface other than lo appears;
#   the emulated SATA disk (which carries a decoy volume with the stick's label) changes by one byte;
#   a report is missing, or its seal does not verify;
#   the trace step does not skip cleanly (QEMU has no Intel GPU);
#   boot 2's step that hangs on purpose (xestick.testhang) is not ended by its dead-man powering the PC off, or boot 3
#   does not leave that step out, or a freeze planted for another computer changes anything;
#   the safe scan (boot 4: the menu's second entry) does not write its report.
#   tools/probe-stick/test/qemu-test.sh          (after tools/probe-stick/build.sh)
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
VERSION=$(cat "$HERE/VERSION")
IMG=$HERE/out/xe-probe-stick-$VERSION.img
[ -f "$IMG" ] || { echo "error: build the image first: tools/probe-stick/build.sh" >&2; exit 1; }
BASE=$(awk '$1 == "image" && $2 == "qemu" { print $4 }' "$HERE/sources.lock")
TAG=xe-probe-stick-qemu:$(printf '%s' "$BASE" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)
if ! docker image inspect "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	printf 'FROM %s\nRUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends qemu-system-x86 ovmf mtools && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n' "$BASE" |
		docker build -q -t "$TAG" -
fi
T=$HERE/out/test
rm -rf "$T"
mkdir -p "$T"
cp "$IMG" "$T/xe-probe-stick.img"
# the planted values (none of them is a real one)
SERIAL_SYS=XSSYSSERIAL0042 SERIAL_BOARD=XSBOARDSERIAL0099 SERIAL_STICK=XSSTICKSERIAL0815 SERIAL_DISK=XSDISKSERIAL4711
UUID=5ec2e7aa-1111-2222-3333-444455556666 MAC=$(printf '%s:' 52 54 00 5e c4)e7   # spelled in parts: no address in git
docker run --rm -v "$T":/t -v "$HERE/test/qemu-inside.sh":/qemu-inside.sh:ro \
	-e SERIAL_SYS=$SERIAL_SYS -e SERIAL_BOARD=$SERIAL_BOARD -e SERIAL_STICK=$SERIAL_STICK -e SERIAL_DISK=$SERIAL_DISK \
	-e UUID=$UUID -e MAC=$MAC -e LIMIT="${LIMIT:-1500}" "$TAG" sh /qemu-inside.sh
SECRETS="$SERIAL_SYS $SERIAL_BOARD $SERIAL_STICK $SERIAL_DISK $UUID $MAC" python3 -I "$HERE/test/check-report.py" "$T"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# unit-inside.sh: unit-test.sh's checks, run inside a container with the repository at /src (read-only).
set -u
LIB=/src/tools/probe-stick/rootfs/usr/lib/xe-stick
CL=/src/tools/report/collect-linux.sh
FAILS=0
ok() { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; }
no() { printf '  FAIL %s\n' "$1"; FAILS=$((FAILS + 1)); }
t() { if eval "$2"; then ok "$1"; else no "$1"; fi; }
W=$(mktemp -d)

echo "== trace-filter.awk"
cat > "$W/raw" <<'T'
VERSION 20070824
PCIDEV 0300	8086e20b	10	fb000000	0	4000000000	0	0	0	0	1000000	0	400000000	0	0	0	0	xe
MAP 1.000000 1 0xfb000000 0xffffc90000000000 0x1000000 0x0 0
MAP 1.000100 2 0x4000000000 0xffffc90100000000 0x400000000 0x0 0
MARK 1.000200 xe-stick: bind xe 0000:03:00.0
R 4 1.000300 1 0xfb138100 0x00000001 0x0 0
W 4 1.000400 1 0xfbffffff 0x12345678 0x0 0
W 4 1.000500 2 0x4000000000 0x00000000 0x0 0
W 4 1.000600 2 0x43ffffffff 0xdeadbeef 0x0 0
R 4 1.000700 1 0xfc000000 0x0 0x0 0
UNMAP 1.000800 2 0xffffc90100000000 0
T
awk -v ranges="0x0000004000000000 0x00000043ffffffff" -v stats="$W/stats" -f "$LIB/trace-filter.awk" "$W/raw" > "$W/kept"
t "the two VRAM BAR accesses are dropped (64-bit addresses)" '[ "$(grep -c "^W 4 1.00050\|^W 4 1.00060" "$W/kept")" = 0 ]'
t "register accesses, inside and just past BAR0, are kept" '[ "$(grep -c "^[RW] " "$W/kept")" = 3 ]'
t "VERSION, PCIDEV, MAP, MARK and UNMAP lines are kept" '[ "$(grep -cE "^(VERSION|PCIDEV|MAP|MARK|UNMAP) " "$W/kept")" = 6 ]'
t "the counts: 11 lines, 9 kept, 5 accesses, 2 dropped" '[ "$(tr "\n" " " < "$W/stats")" = "lines 11 kept 9 accesses 5 dropped 2 " ]'
awk -v ranges="" -v stats="$W/stats2" -f "$LIB/trace-filter.awk" "$W/raw" > "$W/kept2"
t "no ranges (xestick.trace=full): every line kept" 'cmp -s "$W/raw" "$W/kept2"'

echo "== collect-linux.sh --redact (the stick's redaction of traces and logs)"
# test values, spelled in parts so that no address or key shape sits in the repository
MAC1=$(printf '%s:' 52 54 00 12 34)56 MAC2=$(printf '%s:' 02 11 22 33 44)55
KEY1=$(printf '%s-' ABCDE ABCDE ABCDE ABCDE)ABCDE KEY2=$(printf '%s-' GHJKL ABCDE 12345 ABCDE)ABCDE
mkdir -p "$W/r/trace" "$W/r/stick"
printf 'serial\tXSSERIAL123\nhost\tmy-box\nmac\t%s\n' "$MAC1" > "$W/lit"
cp "$W/raw" "$W/r/trace/a.mmio"
printf 'MARK 2.0 board XSSERIAL123 on my-box\n' >> "$W/r/trace/a.mmio"
printf 'usb 1-1: SerialNumber: ABCDEF12345\neth0 %s at /home/someone/x key %s\n' "$MAC2" "$KEY1" > "$W/r/stick/dmesg.txt"
sh "$CL" --redact "$W/lit" "$W/r" > "$W/out" 2>&1
t "exit 0 when everything is removed" '[ $? = 0 ]'
t "the planted values are gone from the trace" '! grep -rqE "XSSERIAL123|my-box" "$W/r"'
t "   ... replaced by their marks" 'grep -q "MARK 2.0 board <serial-redacted> on <host-redacted>" "$W/r/trace/a.mmio"'
t "the rest of the trace is byte-identical" '[ "$(head -n 11 "$W/r/trace/a.mmio" | cksum)" = "$(cksum < "$W/raw")" ]'
t "the fixed rules apply: serial line, MAC, home path, product key" 'grep -q "SerialNumber: <redacted>" "$W/r/stick/dmesg.txt" && grep -q "xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx at /home/USER/x key XXXXX-XXXXX" "$W/r/stick/dmesg.txt"'
printf 'x XSSERIAL123\n' > "$W/r/trace/vbt.bin"
sh "$CL" --redact "$W/lit" "$W/r" > "$W/out" 2>&1
t "a value inside a .bin file (left as it is) fails the privacy check: exit 3" '[ $? = 3 ] && grep -q "a serial value is still present in .*vbt.bin" "$W/out"'
rm -f "$W/r/trace/vbt.bin"
printf '%s\n' "$KEY2" > "$W/r/trace/key.bin"
sh "$CL" --redact "$W/lit" "$W/r" > "$W/out" 2>&1
t "a product key in a .bin file fails the privacy check: exit 3" '[ $? = 3 ]'
rm -f "$W/r/trace/key.bin"
sh "$CL" --redact "$W/lit" > "$W/out" 2>&1
t "--redact without a PATH is refused: exit 2" '[ $? = 2 ]'

echo "== collect-linux.sh as a standalone script"
mkdir -p "$W/o"
sh "$CL" --help > "$W/help" 2>&1
t "--help prints the usage" 'grep -q -- "--literals-out FILE" "$W/help"'
sh "$CL" --out "$W/o" --id XR-0123ABCD --time 30 --acpi --literals-out "$W/l1" > "$W/run" 2>&1
t "runs as root and writes its report" '[ -f "$W/o/xe-report-XR-0123ABCD.tar.gz" ]'
t "   ... --literals-out holds the values, mode 600" '[ -f "$W/l1" ] && [ "$(stat -c %a "$W/l1")" = 600 ]'
(cd "$W/o" && tar -xzf xe-report-XR-0123ABCD.tar.gz)
t "   ... the archive holds summary.txt and manifest.txt" '[ -f "$W/o/xe-report-XR-0123ABCD/summary.txt" ] && [ -f "$W/o/xe-report-XR-0123ABCD/manifest.txt" ]'
t "   ... no learned value is left in it" '! cut -f2 "$W/l1" | grep -qF -f - -r "$W/o/xe-report-XR-0123ABCD"'
t "   ... and the summary's own words are not redacted" '! grep -q "<redacted>" "$W/o/xe-report-XR-0123ABCD/summary.txt"'
sh "$CL" --id XR-1 > /dev/null 2>&1
t "a malformed --id is refused: exit 2" '[ $? = 2 ]'
if command -v su >/dev/null 2>&1 && id nobody >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	chmod 755 "$W" && mkdir -p "$W/u" && chmod 777 "$W/u"
	su -s /bin/sh nobody -c "cd '$W/u' && sh '$CL' --time 20" > "$W/urun" 2>&1
	t "runs as an ordinary user and writes its report" 'ls "$W/u"/xe-report-XR-*.tar.gz >/dev/null 2>&1'
fi
rm -rf "$W"
echo
if [ $FAILS = 0 ]; then echo "ALL PASSED"; else echo "$FAILS FAILED"; fi
exit $((FAILS > 0))

FILE: tools/quality/bdrate.py
