# User space

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `xemac/` | The user-space side of IntelXe.kext's xe interface: `xemac_open`/`xemac_ioctl`/`xemac_mmap` in place of a DRM render node. It also contains a libdrm stand-in (`libdrm/xf86drm.h`, `xemac_drm.c`) and an `XEMAC_FAKE=1` device. Mesa is built with `-Dxemac=<repo>/user/xemac` (see `mesa/`). It opens the xe client through NMXAccel (an IOAccelerator, so sandboxed processes may use it), falling back to IntelXe.kext directly (`XEMAC_DIRECT=1` forces that). |
| `tests/kernel/` | uAPI tests without Mesa: `kxtest` (exec on every engine, load mode), `memq`, `vfill`, `vbw`, `vlat`, `rtt`, `bomove` (BO moves in and out of the BAR window; `bomove evict`), `winfill` (`unmap`: CPU maps are unmapped and distinct; `fill`: fills the CPU-visible window and checks that allocations, binds and contents still work), `latewake`, `surffence` (IOSurface fences), `surfvram` (VRAM-shared IOSurfaces), `ulls` and `direct_lat` (job start without and with the kext's direct submission, `debug.intelxe.direct`), `ufence` (user fences: every engine, `WAIT_USER_FENCE` ops, masks and timeouts, bind fences, a destroyed queue, back-to-back compute jobs); display tools `dmode` (`dmode W H [Hz]`: switches the mode for good, at a refresh rate if given), `fbcrop`; `vmouse` (virtual HID, needs `vmouse.ent`). Build: `clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -I../../../kernel/IntelXe/uapi -o X X.c -framework IOKit -framework CoreFoundation` |
| `tests/vulkan/` | `vk_smoke` (device + fill on every queue family), `vk_videocaps` (video profiles and queue families), `vkwin` (BAR-window cost of a VkDevice and of the plugin's descriptor pools, from `debug.intelxe.stats`); `build.sh` (needs Mesa's `include/`) |
| `tests/gbcl/` | `cl_gbmicro`: a Geekbench-OpenCL-shaped microbenchmark through Apple's OpenCL (dispatch chains, buffer churn, unaligned host-pointer imports, a mixed step, 16-1024 live buffers) with per-op p50/p99 and `debug.intelxe.stats` deltas; `night-gbcl.sh` (`phase_gbclmicro`) runs every mode 3x with the plugin's import and copy alternating. See its README. |
| `tests/metal/` | `mtl_smoke`, `mtl_tests` (vadd, threadgroup/atomics, math, textures, blit, render, perf, `bw`, `mip`), `mtl_cube_read` (reads back every texel of every face, slice and level of cube, integer cube, cube-array and read-write cube textures), `mtl_props` (prints the device properties the plugin answers: registry, location and link rate, peers, feature queries, limits, sparse tiers), `mtl_f32filter` (linear filtering of R32/RG32/RGBA32 float textures gives the midpoint, as `supports32BitFloatFiltering` promises), `mtl_lat`, OpenCL `cl_img`/`cl_lat`/`cl_xfer`, `xlate_check` (offline AIR → SPIR-V), `mtl_pools` (descriptor pools: window cost per process, growth, the full-pools error, set reclaim, texel buffers), `svimg` (two-process VRAM-shared IOSurface image test), `gpt_bench` (frame loop for GPUTIME; `surf` checks IOSurface out/in), `mtl_order_stress` (command buffer ordering across queues and threads, for the plugin's commit locking), `plock_model` (a model of the lock V2 primitives, no GPU; `mtl_lat split` times the parts of one command buffer). `mtl_reflection`, `mtl4_compiler` and `mtl_sparse_buffer` (pipeline reflection, `MTL4Compiler`, placement sparse buffers; `--any` runs them on any Metal device as the reference; `night-mtl4.sh` runs them on the B580), and `tests/plugin/refl_host` (the plugin's reflection against Apple's answers, no GPU). `NVMTL_BUNDLE=<staged bundle>` tests a plugin build without installing it. `nullmoth/build/build-intelxe.sh tests` builds `mtl_smoke`, `xlate_check`, `mtl_cube_read`, `mtl_props` and `mtl_f32filter`. |
| `tests/inv/` | investigation tools and regression scripts from the bring-up of the accelerated desktop: present/IOSurface races (`burstpresent`, `surftest`), sampler/mip/pixelation (`samptest*`, `mipapp64`, `cgtest`, `citest`), OpenCL correctness/perf (`cl*`), GL (`glflat`, `glidx`), memory churn, the `final*.sh` gate scripts. Machine paths inside the scripts are those of the test machine. |
| `tests/gate/` | `gate.sh`: the post-reboot regression gate, run from the build Mac over `rsh` (time-boxed ssh; `INTELXE_HOST=user@machine`) |
| `tools/` | `sigcheck.c` (is every Mach-O code-signed? no Apple tools needed on the test machine); `install-plugin.sh`, `install-plugin-mesa.sh`, `install-plugin-lib.sh`: the guarded install scripts of a staged plugin (and Mesa) build: SHA256SUMS and signature checks, a backup in `./previous/`, `--undo` |
| `tools/ssv-install.sh`, `tools/ssv-watch/` | the optional system-volume copy of the Metal driver (Safari WebGL) and the service that offers to reinstall it after a macOS update |
| `vulkan-loader/` | notes, install script and check program for the Khronos Vulkan loader with our ICD manifest |
| `tests/cts/`, `tests/stability/`, `tests/wsi/`, `tests/wine/`, `tests/plugin/` | the Vulkan CTS runner and result parser; hang, sleep and leak loops (`vkhang`, `hangsuite.sh`, `sleeptest.sh`); presentation tests; Wine/DXVK/VKD3D runs; plugin bisect and comparison scripts |
| `tests/compute/` | `ze_hello` (Level Zero through Intel's compute runtime, `compute/`): driver/device enumeration, USM, copy-engine fill and copy, `compute` (NEO's built-in kernels from files), `kernel <bin>` (a native kernel, e.g. `kernels/fill_ids.cl` compiled by the macOS `ocloc` or `compute/ocloc-docker.sh`), `spirv <spv>` (SPIR-V compiled by IGC in the driver); `cl_hello` (Intel's OpenCL through the Khronos ICD loader: platform, buffer round trip, `kernel <bin>`, `source <cl>`: OpenCL C compiled at run time); built and staged by `compute/build-neo.sh` (`OCL=1` for `cl_hello`, `IGC_PREFIX` for the compiler) |
| `tests/igpu/` | `vttest` (VideoToolbox HW encode/decode + Metal device list), `devorder` (Metal/OpenCL device order) |

All tests are x86_64 binaries. They run on the test machine; on Apple Silicon only under Rosetta, and there without the GPU.

FILE: user/tests/compute/cl_hello.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// cl_hello: Intel's OpenCL driver (compute-runtime/NEO, libigdrcl.dylib) on macOS over IntelXe.kext, through the
// Khronos OpenCL ICD loader (libOpenCL.1.dylib, not Apple's OpenCL.framework). Steps, PASS/FAIL each:
//   1. platforms and devices: names, versions, compute units, memory
//   2. a context and an in-order queue; a buffer written and read back (blocking), compared
//   3. "kernel <file.bin> [name]": a native Battlemage binary (clCreateProgramWithBinary; fill_ids by default:
//      out[i] = i * 3 + 1 for 4096 items), run and checked
//      "source <file.cl> [name]": the same kernel from OpenCL C (clCreateProgramWithSource + clBuildProgram: IGC's
//      front end libigdfcl and back end libigc at run time), run and checked
//      "source-build <file.cl> [name]": only the build (program binary size, kernel created): no GPU work, so it also
//      runs against xemac's canned device (XEMAC_FAKE=1)
//   "lifetime": instead of 2-3, the object lifetimes only: a small buffer (from the context's small-buffers pool) and
//      a large one created and released, then the queue and the context: no GPU work, so it also runs with
//      XEMAC_FAKE=1. NEO aborts in clReleaseContext (reference_tracked_object.h:137) without patch 0012.
// Exit status 0 when every step that ran passed.
//
// Build (the build Mac; L0 = the prefix compute/build-neo.sh installs to, with the ICD loader and OpenCL headers):
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -I$L0/include -o cl_hello cl_hello.c -L$L0/lib -lOpenCL -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/../lib
// Run (the loader takes the driver from OCL_ICD_FILENAMES):
//   OCL_ICD_FILENAMES=$PWD/lib/libigdrcl.dylib DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PWD/lib ./bin/cl_hello
#define CL_TARGET_OPENCL_VERSION 300
#include <CL/cl.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static int failures;

static void step(const char *name, int ok)
{
	printf("%s %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", name);
	if (!ok)
		failures++;
}

#define CHECK(call)                                                                                                    \
	do {                                                                                                           \
		cl_int e_ = (call);                                                                                    \
		if (e_ != CL_SUCCESS) {                                                                                \
			printf("FAIL %s:%d %s = %d\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #call, e_);                             \
			return 1;                                                                                      \
		}                                                                                                      \
	} while (0)

static void *read_file(const char *path, size_t *size)
{
	FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
	if (!f)
		return NULL;
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
	long n = ftell(f);
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
	void *p = n > 0 ? malloc((size_t)n) : NULL;
	if (p && fread(p, 1, (size_t)n, f) != (size_t)n) {
		free(p);
		p = NULL;
	}
	fclose(f);
	*size = (size_t)n;
	return p;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	const int from_source = argc > 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "source") || !strcmp(argv[1], "source-build"));
	const int build_only = argc > 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "source-build");
	const char *kernel_path = argc > 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "kernel") || from_source) ? argv[2] : NULL;
	const char *kernel_name = argc > 3 ? argv[3] : "fill_ids";
	const int lifetime_only = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "lifetime");
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);

	cl_uint np = 0;
	cl_int err = clGetPlatformIDs(0, NULL, &np);
	step("clGetPlatformIDs", err == CL_SUCCESS && np > 0);
	if (err != CL_SUCCESS || !np) {
		printf("  error %d, %u platforms (OCL_ICD_FILENAMES set? OCL_ICD_ENABLE_TRACE=1 shows the loader's search)\n",
		       err, np);
		return 1;
	}
	cl_platform_id platform;
	CHECK(clGetPlatformIDs(1, &platform, NULL));
	char buf[256];
	CHECK(clGetPlatformInfo(platform, CL_PLATFORM_NAME, sizeof(buf), buf, NULL));
	printf("platform: %s", buf);
	CHECK(clGetPlatformInfo(platform, CL_PLATFORM_VERSION, sizeof(buf), buf, NULL));
	printf(", %s\n", buf);

	cl_device_id dev;
	CHECK(clGetDeviceIDs(platform, CL_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU, 1, &dev, NULL));
	cl_uint cus = 0;
	cl_ulong mem = 0, maxalloc = 0;
	CHECK(clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DEVICE_NAME, sizeof(buf), buf, NULL));
	CHECK(clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DEVICE_MAX_COMPUTE_UNITS, sizeof(cus), &cus, NULL));
	CHECK(clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DEVICE_GLOBAL_MEM_SIZE, sizeof(mem), &mem, NULL));
	CHECK(clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DEVICE_MAX_MEM_ALLOC_SIZE, sizeof(maxalloc), &maxalloc, NULL));
	printf("device: %s, %u compute units, %llu MB global, max alloc %llu MB\n", buf, cus,
	       (unsigned long long)(mem >> 20), (unsigned long long)(maxalloc >> 20));
	CHECK(clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DEVICE_VERSION, sizeof(buf), buf, NULL));
	printf("  %s", buf);
	CHECK(clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DRIVER_VERSION, sizeof(buf), buf, NULL));
	printf(", driver %s\n", buf);
	step("device info", 1);

	cl_context ctx = clCreateContext(NULL, 1, &dev, NULL, NULL, &err);
	CHECK(err);
	cl_command_queue q = clCreateCommandQueueWithProperties(ctx, dev, NULL, &err);
	CHECK(err);
	step("context and queue", 1);

	if (lifetime_only) {
		const size_t sizes[] = {4096, 16384, 4 << 20}; // within the small-buffers pool's threshold, and above it
		cl_mem m[3];
		for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
			m[i] = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, sizes[i], NULL, &err);
			CHECK(err);
		}
		for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
			CHECK(clReleaseMemObject(m[i]));
		step("buffers created and released (no GPU work)", 1);
		CHECK(clReleaseCommandQueue(q));
		CHECK(clReleaseContext(ctx));
		step("queue and context released", 1);
		printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", failures);
		return failures ? 1 : 0;
	}

	if (!kernel_path) {
		const size_t size = 4 << 20;
		uint32_t *src = malloc(size), *dst = calloc(1, size);
		for (size_t i = 0; i < size / 4; i++)
			src[i] = (uint32_t)(i * 2654435761u);
		cl_mem b = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, size, NULL, &err);
		CHECK(err);
		CHECK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, b, CL_TRUE, 0, size, src, 0, NULL, NULL));
		CHECK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, b, CL_TRUE, 0, size, dst, 0, NULL, NULL));
		step("buffer write + read back", memcmp(src, dst, size) == 0);
		clReleaseMemObject(b);
		free(dst);
		free(src);
	} else {
		size_t size = 0;
		unsigned char *bin = read_file(kernel_path, &size);
		if (!bin) {
			printf("FAIL cannot read %s\n", kernel_path);
			return 1;
		}
		cl_int status = 0;
		cl_program prog;
		if (from_source) {
			const char *text = (const char *)bin;
			prog = clCreateProgramWithSource(ctx, 1, &text, &size, &err);
		} else {
			prog = clCreateProgramWithBinary(ctx, 1, &dev, &size, (const unsigned char **)&bin, &status, &err);
		}
		CHECK(err);
		err = clBuildProgram(prog, 1, &dev, "", NULL, NULL);
		if (err != CL_SUCCESS || from_source) {
			char log[4096] = "";
			clGetProgramBuildInfo(prog, dev, CL_PROGRAM_BUILD_LOG, sizeof(log) - 1, log, NULL);
			if (log[0])
				printf("  build log: %s\n", log);
		}
		CHECK(err);
		if (from_source) {
			size_t binsize = 0;
			CHECK(clGetProgramInfo(prog, CL_PROGRAM_BINARY_SIZES, sizeof(binsize), &binsize, NULL));
			printf("  program binary: %zu bytes\n", binsize);
			step("program built from OpenCL C source", binsize > 0);
		}
		cl_kernel k = clCreateKernel(prog, kernel_name, &err);
		CHECK(err);
		if (build_only) {
			size_t wg = 0;
			CHECK(clGetKernelWorkGroupInfo(k, dev, CL_KERNEL_WORK_GROUP_SIZE, sizeof(wg), &wg, NULL));
			printf("  kernel %s: max work-group size %zu\n", kernel_name, wg);
			step("kernel created", wg > 0);
			clReleaseKernel(k);
			clReleaseProgram(prog);
			free(bin);
			clReleaseCommandQueue(q);
			clReleaseContext(ctx);
			printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", failures);
			return failures ? 1 : 0;
		}
		const size_t n = 4096;
		cl_mem out = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, n * 4, NULL, &err);
		CHECK(err);
		CHECK(clSetKernelArg(k, 0, sizeof(out), &out));
		CHECK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, k, 1, NULL, &n, NULL, 0, NULL, NULL));
		uint32_t *res = calloc(n, 4);
		CHECK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, out, CL_TRUE, 0, n * 4, res, 0, NULL, NULL));
		int ok = 1;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
			if (res[i] != i * 3 + 1) {
				printf("  out[%u] = %u, expected %u\n", i, res[i], i * 3 + 1);
				ok = 0;
				break;
			}
		step(from_source ? "kernel from OpenCL C source" : "kernel from native binary", ok);
		free(res);
		clReleaseMemObject(out);
		clReleaseKernel(k);
		clReleaseProgram(prog);
		free(bin);
	}

	clReleaseCommandQueue(q);
	clReleaseContext(ctx);
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", failures);
	return failures ? 1 : 0;
}

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# night phase Z (sourced by the night script, which defines tmo, say and $O): Level Zero sysman (zes*) over
# IntelXe.kext - compute-runtime/NEO with patches 0013 (the device's sysfs answered from the kext: sysfs_macos.cpp) and
# 0014 (frequency range control, engine activity through an emulated xe PMU) and the kext's debug.intelxe.sensors_raw
# (uapi/intelxe_sensors.h; version 2 with engine counters) and live slpc_min/slpc_max (sysman2, DESIGN-level-zero.md
# 10.6). Nothing is installed by this phase.
# Stages (the build Mac, docs/design/DESIGN-level-zero.md section 10): ~/l0sm = compute/build-neo.sh's stage with the
# patch (bin/zes_info, ze_hello, cl_hello; lib/; builtins/; SHA256SUMS), SYSMAN_L0 overrides; ~/l0smigc = the same
# with IGC (SYSMAN_L0IGC); ~/b580/sycl = build-sycl.sh's stage with the new sycl_hello (SYCL_STAGE).
# The kext: sensors_raw exists only in an IntelXe.kext built from this branch. With an older kext zesInit still works,
# the frequency domain reads -1 and there are no power or temperature handles (Z0 says which kext is loaded).
# Each run is a subshell with the variables exported (no env/perl wrapper: they would strip DYLD_*); <= 60 s each.
# Expected with the new kext: Z1 "PASS: 0 failed", frequency 0 (gpu) with a hardware range RPn-RP0 (400-2850 on the
# B580), a range of slpc_min (1200) to RP0, actual/request in MHz (actual 0 while the GT sleeps in RC6), two power
# domains (card, package) with energy counters and a few W idle, PL1/PL2/crit limits, two temperatures (gpu =
# package, memory = VRAM) in the 30-60 C range, memory 12 GB with free < size; Z2 five samples, each power > 0;
# Z3 as the user: "can control 0", "NONE zesFrequencySetRange" (not root); Z3r (only with passwordless sudo) as root:
# "can control 1", "asked 1500-2400 MHz, reads 1500-2400", the old range restored; Z3k (sudo) the kext directly:
# slpc_max 2000 then 0, sensors_raw max_freq follows at once, stats "range" line counts the writes and max sends;
# Z10 engine activity: zes_info busy idle (render/copy/compute groups near 0 %, every group "PASS ... busy"),
# then with ze_hello compute running: the compute (or all) group above 0 %; the kext log's "engine activity: buffer
# at GGTT ... given" for the primary and media GT; Z4 the same values as
# `sysctl debug.intelxe.sensors` (the text from the same sample path); Z5 ze_hello init and cl_hello lifetime still
# pass; Z6 sycl-ls lists ext_intel_power_limits; Z7 sycl_hello build: 4 PASS (device, free memory, sysman, kernels);
# Z8 sycl_hello on the B580 (all steps); Z9 zes_info over the IGC stage.
phase_sysman() {
  local L0=${SYSMAN_L0:-~/l0sm} L0IGC=${SYSMAN_L0IGC:-~/l0smigc} SY=${SYCL_STAGE:-~/b580/sycl} R="$O/sysman"; mkdir -p "$R"
  local t='tmo 60'
  say "Z: Level Zero sysman - $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -oE 'GuC context resets [0-9]+; GT resets [0-9]+')"
  ( cd "$L0" && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS 2>&1 | grep -v ': OK$' > "$R/0-sums.txt" ); say "Z0 sums: $(grep -c . "$R/0-sums.txt") not OK"
  if sysctl debug.intelxe.sensors_raw > /dev/null 2>&1; then say "Z0 kext: sensors_raw present"; else say "Z0 kext: NO sensors_raw (old kext: expect no power/temperature handles)"; fi
  sysctl -n debug.intelxe.sensors > "$R/0-sensors-before.txt" 2>&1
  # $1 result name, $2 L0 stage, $3... zes_info arguments; a failure is repeated with the sysfs trace and NEO's messages
  zrun() {
    local n=$1 l0=$2; shift 2
    ( cd "$l0" && export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$l0/lib"
      $t ./bin/zes_info "$@" > "$R/$n.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/$n.txt" )
    grep -q "exit=0" "$R/$n.txt" && return 0
    ( cd "$l0" && export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$l0/lib" NEO_MACOS_SYSFS_TRACE=1 NEOReadDebugKeys=1 PrintDebugMessages=1
      $t ./bin/zes_info "$@" > "$R/$n-debug.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/$n-debug.txt" )
  }
  zrun 1-info "$L0"
  say "Z1 zes_info: $(grep -E '^(PASS|FAIL)[:]' "$R/1-info.txt" | tail -1) $(grep -E '^FAIL ' "$R/1-info.txt" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ') $(tail -1 "$R/1-info.txt")"
  say "Z1 values: $(grep -E '^PASS (frequency 0 state|power 0:|power 1:|temperature|memory 0 state)' "$R/1-info.txt" | sed 's/^PASS //' | tr '\n' ';')"
  zrun 2-watch "$L0" watch 5
  say "Z2 watch: $(grep -E '^sample' "$R/2-watch.txt" | tail -2 | tr '\n' ' ') $(tail -1 "$R/2-watch.txt")"
  zrun 3-setfreq "$L0" set-freq 1500 2400
  say "Z3 set-freq (user): $(grep -E 'can control|SetRange|frequency set' "$R/3-setfreq.txt" | tr '\n' ' ') $(tail -1 "$R/3-setfreq.txt")"
  if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
    # as root: sudo strips DYLD_*, so the variable is exported inside the root bash, and tmo comes along as text
    sudo -n bash -c "$(declare -f tmo); cd '$L0' && export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH='$L0/lib'; tmo 60 ./bin/zes_info set-freq 1500 2400" \
      > "$R/3r-setfreq-root.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/3r-setfreq-root.txt"
    say "Z3r set-freq (root): $(grep -E 'can control|SetRange|frequency set|after set' "$R/3r-setfreq-root.txt" | tr '\n' ' ') $(tail -1 "$R/3r-setfreq-root.txt")"
    { sysctl debug.intelxe.slpc_min debug.intelxe.slpc_max; sudo -n sysctl -w debug.intelxe.slpc_max=2000
      sleep 1; sysctl -n debug.intelxe.sensors; sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -E '^slpc boost'
      sudo -n sysctl -w debug.intelxe.slpc_max=0; sleep 1; sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -E '^slpc boost'
    } > "$R/3k-kext-range.txt" 2>&1
    say "Z3k kext range: $(grep -oE 'range \(slpc_min/max\).*' "$R/3k-kext-range.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  else
    say "Z3r/Z3k skipped: no passwordless sudo (range control needs root)"
  fi
  sysctl -n debug.intelxe.sensors > "$R/4-sensors-after.txt" 2>&1
  say "Z4 sensors text: $(head -c 240 "$R/4-sensors-after.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  ( cd "$L0" && export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$L0/lib" OCL_ICD_FILENAMES="$L0/lib/libigdrcl.dylib"
    $t ./bin/ze_hello init > "$R/5-ze-init.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/5-ze-init.txt"
    $t ./bin/cl_hello lifetime > "$R/5-cl-lifetime.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/5-cl-lifetime.txt" )
  say "Z5 ze_hello init: $(tail -2 "$R/5-ze-init.txt" | tr '\n' ' '); cl_hello lifetime: $(tail -2 "$R/5-cl-lifetime.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  if [ -x "$SY/bin/sycl_hello" ]; then
    ( cd "$L0/builtins" && export ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$SY/lib:$L0/lib"
      $t "$SY/bin/sycl-ls" --verbose > "$R/6-sycl-ls.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/6-sycl-ls.txt"
      $t "$SY/bin/sycl_hello" build > "$R/7-sycl-build.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/7-sycl-build.txt"
      $t "$SY/bin/sycl_hello" > "$R/8-sycl-run.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/8-sycl-run.txt" )
    say "Z6 sycl-ls: power limits aspect $(grep -c ext_intel_power_limits "$R/6-sycl-ls.txt"), $(tail -1 "$R/6-sycl-ls.txt")"
    say "Z7 sycl_hello build: $(grep -E '^(PASS|FAIL|SKIP) ' "$R/7-sycl-build.txt" | cut -c1-40 | tr '\n' ';') $(tail -1 "$R/7-sycl-build.txt")"
    say "Z8 sycl_hello: $(grep -cE '^PASS ' "$R/8-sycl-run.txt") PASS, $(grep -m1 -E '^FAIL' "$R/8-sycl-run.txt") $(tail -2 "$R/8-sycl-run.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  else
    say "Z6-Z8 skipped: no $SY/bin/sycl_hello"
  fi
  # Z10 engine activity: idle, then with a compute workload running beside it
  zrun 10-busy-idle "$L0" busy 1000
  say "Z10 busy idle: $(grep -E '^(PASS|FAIL|NONE) engine' "$R/10-busy-idle.txt" | sed 's/^PASS engine //' | tr '\n' ';') $(tail -1 "$R/10-busy-idle.txt")"
  ( cd "$L0" && export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH="$L0/lib"
    ( for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do $t ./bin/ze_hello compute > /dev/null 2>&1; done ) &
    local bg=$!
    sleep 1; $t ./bin/zes_info busy 2000 > "$R/10-busy-load.txt" 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> "$R/10-busy-load.txt"
    kill $bg 2>/dev/null; wait $bg 2>/dev/null )
  say "Z10 busy under ze_hello compute: $(grep -E '^(PASS|FAIL) engine' "$R/10-busy-load.txt" | sed 's/^PASS engine //' | tr '\n' ';') $(tail -1 "$R/10-busy-load.txt")"
  sysctl -n debug.intelxe.state 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'engine activity' > "$R/10-kext-log.txt"
  say "Z10 kext: $(tr '\n' ';' < "$R/10-kext-log.txt" | cut -c1-300)"
  if [ -x "$L0IGC/bin/zes_info" ]; then
    zrun 9-info-igc "$L0IGC"
    say "Z9 zes_info (IGC stage): $(tail -2 "$R/9-info-igc.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  else
    say "Z9 skipped: no $L0IGC"
  fi
  say "Z: after: $(sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats | grep -oE 'GuC context resets [0-9]+; GT resets [0-9]+')"
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// ze_hello: Intel's Level Zero driver (compute-runtime/NEO, libze_intel_gpu) on macOS over IntelXe.kext, through the
// Level Zero loader. No Mesa, no Metal. Steps, each printed with PASS/FAIL; the first failure ends the run:
//   1. zeInitDrivers (GPU) -> drivers -> devices: name, PCI id, EU/thread layout, memory, command queue groups
//   2. a context; USM allocations: device (VRAM), host (system memory the GPU reaches), shared
//   3. copy engine: an immediate synchronous command list on the copy group fills a host buffer with a pattern and
//      copies host -> device -> host; the result is checked (blitter only: XY_FAST_COLOR_BLT / MEM_COPY, no kernels)
//   4. copy engine again through a regular command list, a command queue and a fence (the submission path with
//      zeCommandQueueExecuteCommandLists)
// Steps 3-4 run without arguments; with one of the arguments below, its steps run instead:
//   5. "compute": a copy (queue + fence) and a fill + copy (immediate) on the compute group. NEO does both with its
//      built-in kernels, which need IGC at run time or offline-compiled built-ins in the working directory
//      (compute/ocloc-docker.sh builtins); without either, module creation fails
//   6. "kernel <file.bin> [name]": loads a native binary (zebin, e.g. from ocloc -device bmg on Linux) and runs its
//      kernel `name` (default fill_ids: out[i] = i * 3 + 1 for a global size of 4096) on the compute group, checks
//      the output
//   7. "spirv <file.spv> [name]": the same kernel as SPIR-V (ZE_MODULE_FORMAT_IL_SPIRV), compiled by the driver with
//      IGC (libigc) at run time, then run and checked; "spirv-build <file.spv> [name]": only the module and the kernel
//      (no GPU work, so it also runs against xemac's canned device, XEMAC_FAKE=1)
//   "init": stop after step 2
// Exit status 0 when every step that ran passed.
//
// Build (the build Mac; L0 = the prefix compute/build-neo.sh installs to):
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -I$L0/include -o ze_hello ze_hello.c -L$L0/lib -lze_loader -Wl,-rpath,@executable_path/../lib
// Run (the test machine; the loader finds libze_intel_gpu.1.dylib through DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH or ZE_ENABLE_ALT_DRIVERS):
//   DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PWD/lib ./bin/ze_hello
//   XEMAC_FAKE=1 ... init: xemac's canned Battlemage, no kext (any Mac, Rosetta included). No batch runs there, so
//   only "init" ends; the other steps wait for a completion that never comes.
#include <level_zero/ze_api.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static int failures;

#define CHECK(call)                                                                                                    \
	do {                                                                                                           \
		ze_result_t r_ = (call);                                                                               \
		if (r_ != ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS) {                                                                         \
			printf("FAIL %s:%d %s = 0x%x\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #call, (unsigned)r_);                 \
			return -1;                                                                                     \
		}                                                                                                      \
	} while (0)

static void step(const char *name, int ok)
{
	printf("%s %s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", name);
	if (!ok)
		failures++;
}

static const char *group_flags(ze_command_queue_group_property_flags_t f, char *buf, size_t n)
{
	snprintf(buf, n, "%s%s%s%s", f & ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COMPUTE ? "compute " : "",
		 f & ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COPY ? "copy " : "",
		 f & ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COOPERATIVE_KERNELS ? "cooperative " : "",
		 f & ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_METRICS ? "metrics" : "");
	return buf;
}

// The first group with `want` and, for copy, without compute (the pure blitter group).
static int find_group(ze_device_handle_t dev, ze_command_queue_group_property_flags_t want, uint32_t *ordinal)
{
	uint32_t n = 0;
	zeDeviceGetCommandQueueGroupProperties(dev, &n, NULL);
	ze_command_queue_group_properties_t props[16];
	if (n > 16)
		n = 16;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
		props[i] = (ze_command_queue_group_properties_t){.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTIES};
	zeDeviceGetCommandQueueGroupProperties(dev, &n, props);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		int compute = (props[i].flags & ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COMPUTE) != 0;
		if (!(props[i].flags & want))
			continue;
		if (want == ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COPY && compute)
			continue;
		*ordinal = i;
		return 0;
	}
	return -1;
}

static int print_device(ze_device_handle_t dev)
{
	ze_device_properties_t p = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_PROPERTIES};
	CHECK(zeDeviceGetProperties(dev, &p));
	printf("device: %s, vendor 0x%04x device 0x%04x, %u slices x %u subslices x %u EUs x %u threads, SIMD %u, "
	       "core clock %u MHz, max alloc %llu MB\n",
	       p.name, p.vendorId, p.deviceId, p.numSlices, p.numSubslicesPerSlice, p.numEUsPerSubslice, p.numThreadsPerEU,
	       p.physicalEUSimdWidth, p.coreClockRate, (unsigned long long)(p.maxMemAllocSize >> 20));
	uint32_t n = 0;
	CHECK(zeDeviceGetMemoryProperties(dev, &n, NULL));
	ze_device_memory_properties_t mem[4];
	if (n > 4)
		n = 4;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
		mem[i] = (ze_device_memory_properties_t){.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_MEMORY_PROPERTIES};
	CHECK(zeDeviceGetMemoryProperties(dev, &n, mem));
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
		printf("memory %u: %s %llu MB, %u MHz, bus %u bits\n", i, mem[i].name,
		       (unsigned long long)(mem[i].totalSize >> 20), mem[i].maxClockRate, mem[i].maxBusWidth);
	n = 0;
	CHECK(zeDeviceGetCommandQueueGroupProperties(dev, &n, NULL));
	ze_command_queue_group_properties_t g[16];
	if (n > 16)
		n = 16;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
		g[i] = (ze_command_queue_group_properties_t){.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTIES};
	CHECK(zeDeviceGetCommandQueueGroupProperties(dev, &n, g));
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		char buf[64];
		printf("queue group %u: %u queues, %s\n", i, g[i].numQueues, group_flags(g[i].flags, buf, sizeof(buf)));
	}
	return 0;
}

static int check_bytes(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint8_t v, const char *what)
{
	for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
		if (p[i] != v) {
			printf("  %s: byte %zu is 0x%02x, expected 0x%02x\n", what, i, p[i], v);
			return 0;
		}
	return 1;
}

// fill(host) with a pattern, host -> device, device -> host2: immediate, synchronous.
static int copy_immediate(ze_context_handle_t ctx, ze_device_handle_t dev, uint32_t ordinal, size_t size, uint8_t pattern,
			  int *ok)
{
	ze_command_queue_desc_t qd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_QUEUE_DESC, .ordinal = ordinal,
				      .mode = ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_MODE_SYNCHRONOUS};
	ze_command_list_handle_t cl;
	CHECK(zeCommandListCreateImmediate(ctx, dev, &qd, &cl));
	ze_host_mem_alloc_desc_t hd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_HOST_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
	ze_device_mem_alloc_desc_t dd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
	void *host, *host2, *devmem;
	CHECK(zeMemAllocHost(ctx, &hd, size, 4096, &host));
	CHECK(zeMemAllocHost(ctx, &hd, size, 4096, &host2));
	CHECK(zeMemAllocDevice(ctx, &dd, size, 4096, dev, &devmem));
	memset(host, 0, size);
	memset(host2, 0, size);
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendMemoryFill(cl, host, &pattern, 1, size, NULL, 0, NULL));
	int fill_ok = check_bytes(host, size, pattern, "fill");
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy(cl, devmem, host, size, NULL, 0, NULL));
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy(cl, host2, devmem, size, NULL, 0, NULL));
	*ok = fill_ok && check_bytes(host2, size, pattern, "copy back");
	zeMemFree(ctx, devmem);
	zeMemFree(ctx, host2);
	zeMemFree(ctx, host);
	zeCommandListDestroy(cl);
	return 0;
}

// host -> device -> host through a regular command list, executed on a queue, waited on with a fence.
static int copy_queue(ze_context_handle_t ctx, ze_device_handle_t dev, uint32_t ordinal, size_t size, int *ok)
{
	ze_command_queue_desc_t qd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_QUEUE_DESC, .ordinal = ordinal,
				      .mode = ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_MODE_ASYNCHRONOUS};
	ze_command_queue_handle_t q;
	CHECK(zeCommandQueueCreate(ctx, dev, &qd, &q));
	ze_command_list_desc_t ld = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_LIST_DESC, .commandQueueGroupOrdinal = ordinal};
	ze_command_list_handle_t cl;
	CHECK(zeCommandListCreate(ctx, dev, &ld, &cl));
	ze_host_mem_alloc_desc_t hd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_HOST_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
	ze_device_mem_alloc_desc_t dd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
	uint32_t *src, *dst;
	void *devmem;
	CHECK(zeMemAllocHost(ctx, &hd, size, 4096, (void **)&src));
	CHECK(zeMemAllocHost(ctx, &hd, size, 4096, (void **)&dst));
	CHECK(zeMemAllocDevice(ctx, &dd, size, 4096, dev, &devmem));
	for (size_t i = 0; i < size / 4; i++)
		src[i] = (uint32_t)(i * 2654435761u);
	memset(dst, 0, size);
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy(cl, devmem, src, size, NULL, 0, NULL));
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendBarrier(cl, NULL, 0, NULL));
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy(cl, dst, devmem, size, NULL, 0, NULL));
	CHECK(zeCommandListClose(cl));
	ze_fence_desc_t fd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_DESC};
	ze_fence_handle_t fence;
	CHECK(zeFenceCreate(q, &fd, &fence));
	CHECK(zeCommandQueueExecuteCommandLists(q, 1, &cl, fence));
	CHECK(zeFenceHostSynchronize(fence, 5000000000ull)); // 5 s
	*ok = memcmp(src, dst, size) == 0;
	if (!*ok)
		for (size_t i = 0; i < size / 4; i++)
			if (src[i] != dst[i]) {
				printf("  word %zu is 0x%08x, expected 0x%08x\n", i, dst[i], src[i]);
				break;
			}
	zeFenceDestroy(fence);
	zeMemFree(ctx, devmem);
	zeMemFree(ctx, dst);
	zeMemFree(ctx, src);
	zeCommandListDestroy(cl);
	zeCommandQueueDestroy(q);
	return 0;
}

static void *read_file(const char *path, size_t *size)
{
	FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
	if (!f)
		return NULL;
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
	long n = ftell(f);
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
	void *p = n > 0 ? malloc((size_t)n) : NULL;
	if (p && fread(p, 1, (size_t)n, f) != (size_t)n) {
		free(p);
		p = NULL;
	}
	fclose(f);
	*size = (size_t)n;
	return p;
}

// out[i] = i * 3 + 1 from kernel(global uint *out): a native binary, or SPIR-V that the driver compiles with IGC.
// build_only: module and kernel only, no GPU work (also against xemac's canned device, XEMAC_FAKE=1).
static int run_kernel(ze_context_handle_t ctx, ze_device_handle_t dev, uint32_t ordinal, const char *path, const char *name,
		      int spirv, int build_only, int *ok)
{
	size_t size = 0;
	void *bin = read_file(path, &size);
	if (!bin) {
		printf("FAIL cannot read %s\n", path);
		return -1;
	}
	ze_module_desc_t md = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MODULE_DESC,
			       .format = spirv ? ZE_MODULE_FORMAT_IL_SPIRV : ZE_MODULE_FORMAT_NATIVE,
			       .inputSize = size, .pInputModule = bin, .pBuildFlags = ""};
	ze_module_handle_t mod;
	ze_module_build_log_handle_t log = NULL;
	ze_result_t r = zeModuleCreate(ctx, dev, &md, &mod, &log);
	if (r != ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS) {
		size_t ls = 0;
		if (log && zeModuleBuildLogGetString(log, &ls, NULL) == ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS && ls) {
			char *s = malloc(ls);
			zeModuleBuildLogGetString(log, &ls, s);
			printf("  build log: %s\n", s);
			free(s);
		}
		printf("FAIL zeModuleCreate = 0x%x\n", (unsigned)r);
		free(bin);
		return -1;
	}
	if (log)
		zeModuleBuildLogDestroy(log);
	if (spirv) {
		size_t nsize = 0;
		CHECK(zeModuleGetNativeBinary(mod, &nsize, NULL));
		printf("  native binary from SPIR-V: %zu bytes\n", nsize);
		step("module built from SPIR-V", nsize > 0);
	}
	ze_kernel_desc_t kd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_KERNEL_DESC, .pKernelName = name};
	ze_kernel_handle_t k;
	CHECK(zeKernelCreate(mod, &kd, &k));
	if (build_only) {
		ze_kernel_properties_t kp = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_KERNEL_PROPERTIES};
		CHECK(zeKernelGetProperties(k, &kp));
		printf("  kernel %s: %u argument(s), SIMD %u\n", name, kp.numKernelArgs, kp.maxSubgroupSize);
		*ok = kp.numKernelArgs == 1;
		zeKernelDestroy(k);
		zeModuleDestroy(mod);
		free(bin);
		return 0;
	}
	const uint32_t n = 4096;
	uint32_t gx = 0, gy = 0, gz = 0;
	CHECK(zeKernelSuggestGroupSize(k, n, 1, 1, &gx, &gy, &gz));
	CHECK(zeKernelSetGroupSize(k, gx, gy, gz));
	ze_device_mem_alloc_desc_t dd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
	ze_host_mem_alloc_desc_t hd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_HOST_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
	uint32_t *out;
	CHECK(zeMemAllocShared(ctx, &dd, &hd, n * 4, 4096, dev, (void **)&out));
	memset(out, 0, n * 4);
	CHECK(zeKernelSetArgumentValue(k, 0, sizeof(out), &out));
	ze_command_queue_desc_t qd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_QUEUE_DESC, .ordinal = ordinal,
				      .mode = ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_MODE_SYNCHRONOUS};
	ze_command_list_handle_t cl;
	CHECK(zeCommandListCreateImmediate(ctx, dev, &qd, &cl));
	ze_group_count_t groups = {n / gx, 1, 1};
	printf("  kernel %s: group size %u, %u groups\n", name, gx, groups.groupCountX);
	CHECK(zeCommandListAppendLaunchKernel(cl, k, &groups, NULL, 0, NULL));
	CHECK(zeCommandListHostSynchronize(cl, 5000000000ull));
	*ok = 1;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
		if (out[i] != i * 3 + 1) {
			printf("  out[%u] = %u, expected %u\n", i, out[i], i * 3 + 1);
			*ok = 0;
			break;
		}
	zeCommandListDestroy(cl);
	zeMemFree(ctx, out);
	zeKernelDestroy(k);
	zeModuleDestroy(mod);
	free(bin);
	return 0;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	int want_compute = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "compute");
	int init_only = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "init");
	const int spirv = argc > 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "spirv") || !strcmp(argv[1], "spirv-build"));
	const int build_only = argc > 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "spirv-build");
	const char *kernel_path = argc > 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "kernel") || spirv) ? argv[2] : NULL;
	const char *kernel_name = argc > 3 ? argv[3] : "fill_ids";
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0);

	ze_init_driver_type_desc_t init = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INIT_DRIVER_TYPE_DESC,
					   .flags = ZE_INIT_DRIVER_TYPE_FLAG_GPU};
	uint32_t ndrv = 0;
	ze_result_t r = zeInitDrivers(&ndrv, NULL, &init);
	step("zeInitDrivers", r == ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS && ndrv > 0);
	if (r != ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS || !ndrv) {
		printf("  result 0x%x, %u drivers (ZE_ENABLE_LOADER_DEBUG_TRACE=1 shows what the loader tried)\n", (unsigned)r,
		       ndrv);
		return 1;
	}
	ze_driver_handle_t drv;
	ndrv = 1;
	CHECK(zeInitDrivers(&ndrv, &drv, &init));
	ze_driver_properties_t dp = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DRIVER_PROPERTIES};
	CHECK(zeDriverGetProperties(drv, &dp));
	ze_api_version_t api;
	CHECK(zeDriverGetApiVersion(drv, &api));
	printf("driver version 0x%x, API %u.%u\n", dp.driverVersion, ZE_MAJOR_VERSION(api), ZE_MINOR_VERSION(api));

	uint32_t ndev = 0;
	CHECK(zeDeviceGet(drv, &ndev, NULL));
	step("zeDeviceGet", ndev > 0);
	if (!ndev)
		return 1;
	ze_device_handle_t dev;
	ndev = 1;
	CHECK(zeDeviceGet(drv, &ndev, &dev));
	if (print_device(dev))
		return 1;
	step("device properties", 1);

	ze_context_desc_t cd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_CONTEXT_DESC};
	ze_context_handle_t ctx;
	CHECK(zeContextCreate(drv, &cd, &ctx));
	step("zeContextCreate", 1);

	// USM: one of each kind, written by the CPU where it can be
	{
		ze_device_mem_alloc_desc_t dd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
		ze_host_mem_alloc_desc_t hd = {.stype = ZE_STRUCTURE_TYPE_HOST_MEM_ALLOC_DESC};
		void *d = NULL, *h = NULL, *s = NULL;
		CHECK(zeMemAllocDevice(ctx, &dd, 1 << 20, 4096, dev, &d));
		CHECK(zeMemAllocHost(ctx, &hd, 1 << 20, 4096, &h));
		CHECK(zeMemAllocShared(ctx, &dd, &hd, 1 << 20, 4096, dev, &s));
		memset(h, 0x11, 1 << 20);
		memset(s, 0x22, 1 << 20);
		printf("  device %p, host %p, shared %p\n", d, h, s);
		zeMemFree(ctx, s);
		zeMemFree(ctx, h);
		zeMemFree(ctx, d);
		step("USM device/host/shared alloc", 1);
	}
	if (init_only) {
		zeContextDestroy(ctx);
		printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", failures);
		return failures ? 1 : 0;
	}

	uint32_t copy_ord = 0, compute_ord = 0;
	if (want_compute || kernel_path) {
		// the compute-engine steps alone, so that each run tests one thing
	} else if (find_group(dev, ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COPY, &copy_ord) == 0) {
		int ok = 0;
		if (copy_immediate(ctx, dev, copy_ord, 1 << 20, 0xa5, &ok))
			return 1;
		step("copy engine: fill + copy (immediate)", ok);
		if (copy_queue(ctx, dev, copy_ord, 4 << 20, &ok))
			return 1;
		step("copy engine: copy (queue + fence)", ok);
	} else {
		printf("SKIP no copy-only queue group\n");
	}

	if (find_group(dev, ZE_COMMAND_QUEUE_GROUP_PROPERTY_FLAG_COMPUTE, &compute_ord) == 0) {
		if (want_compute) {
			int ok = 0;
			if (copy_queue(ctx, dev, compute_ord, 4 << 20, &ok))
				return 1;
			step("compute engine: copy (queue + fence)", ok);
			if (copy_immediate(ctx, dev, compute_ord, 1 << 20, 0x5a, &ok))
				return 1; // fill: built-in kernels
			step("compute engine: fill + copy (immediate, built-in kernels)", ok);
		}
		if (kernel_path) {
			int ok = 0;
			if (run_kernel(ctx, dev, compute_ord, kernel_path, kernel_name, spirv, build_only, &ok))
				return 1;
			step(build_only ? "kernel created" : spirv ? "kernel from SPIR-V" : "kernel from native binary", ok);
		}
	}

	zeContextDestroy(ctx);
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", failures ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", failures);
	return failures ? 1 : 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// ze_hello's kernel test: out[i] = i * 3 + 1. Compiled offline for Battlemage with Intel's ocloc on Linux
// (compute/ocloc-docker.sh) and loaded as a native binary (ZE_MODULE_FORMAT_NATIVE): no compiler on the Mac.
kernel void fill_ids(global uint *out)
{
	size_t i = get_global_id(0);
	out[i] = (uint)i * 3u + 1u;
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Generate deqp-vk case-list shards from the mustpass lists (deterministic stride sampling)."""
import os, re, sys, glob
MP = os.path.join(os.environ.get("VK_CTS_SRC", os.path.expanduser("~/VK-GL-CTS")),
                  "external/vulkancts/mustpass/main/vk-default")   # VK_CTS_SRC: a VK-GL-CTS checkout
OUT = sys.argv[1]
SHARD = 400
EXCL = re.compile(r"(external|win32|_fd\b|_fd_|sync_fd|opaque_fd|dma_buf|dma_heap|android|ahb|drm|ray_tracing|ray_query|video|device_group|protected|cross_instance|keyed_mutex)")

allc = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob(MP + "/**/*.txt", recursive=True)):
    allc += [l.strip() for l in open(f) if l.strip()]
allc = sorted(set(allc))

def pick(regex, maxn, excl=True):
    r = re.compile(regex)
    c = [x for x in allc if r.search(x) and not (excl and EXCL.search(x))]
    if maxn and len(c) > maxn:
        step = len(c) / maxn
        c = [c[int(i * step)] for i in range(maxn)]
    return c

P = r"^dEQP-VK\."
GROUPS = [
 ("g1_basic", [(P+r"info\.", 0), (P+r"api\.info\.", 0), (P+r"api\.smoke\.", 0),
               (P+r"api\.version_check\.", 0), (P+r"api\.device_init\.", 0)]),
 ("g2_memory", [(P+r"memory\.allocation\.basic\.", 0), (P+r"memory\.mapping\.", 1200),
                (P+r"memory\.requirements\.", 0), (P+r"memory\.binding\.", 0),
                (P+r"memory\.map_placed\.", 0), (P+r"memory\.zero_initialize_device_memory\.", 150),
                (P+r"memory\.pipeline_barrier\.", 60)]),
 ("g3_sync", [(P+r"synchronization\.(basic|smoke)\.", 0), (P+r"synchronization\.timeline_semaphore\.", 700),
              (P+r"synchronization\.op\.single_queue\.", 800), (P+r"synchronization\.op\.multi_queue\.", 300),
              (P+r"synchronization\.signal_order\.", 200), (P+r"synchronization\.implicit\.", 150),
              (P+r"synchronization\.internally_synchronized", 0),
              (P+r"synchronization2\.(basic|smoke|layout_transition)\.", 0), (P+r"synchronization2\.timeline_semaphore\.", 400),
              (P+r"synchronization2\.op\.single_queue\.", 500), (P+r"synchronization2\.none_stage\.", 100)]),
 ("g4_render", [(P+r"pipeline\.monolithic\.blend\.", 1200), (P+r"pipeline\.monolithic\.depth\.", 700),
                (P+r"pipeline\.monolithic\.stencil\.", 700), (P+r"pipeline\.monolithic\.vertex_input\.", 700),
                (P+r"draw\.renderpass\.", 1500), (P+r"draw\.dynamic_rendering\.", 600),
                (P+r"renderpasses\.renderpass1\.", 1200), (P+r"renderpasses\.renderpass2\.", 800),
                (P+r"renderpasses\.dynamic_rendering\.", 800)]),
 ("g5_image", [(P+r"image\.format_reinterpret\.", 500), (P+r"image\.mutable\.", 500),
               (P+r"image\.extended_usage_bit\.", 300), (P+r"api\.copy_and_blit\.", 2000),
               (P+r"api\.image_clearing\.", 1200)]),
 ("g7_dxvk", [(P+r"transform_feedback\.simple\.", 700), (P+r"transform_feedback\.primitives_generated_query\.", 300),
              (P+r"transform_feedback\.fuzz\.", 100),
              (P+r"robustness\.robustness2\.", 1200), (P+r"robustness\.image_robustness\.", 400),
              (P+r"robustness\.buffer_access\.", 200),
              (P+r"conditional_rendering\.", 0), (P+r"query_pool\.(occlusion_query|discard|concurrent_queries)\.", 0),
              (P+r"query_pool\.statistics_query\.", 600),
              (P+r"draw\.renderpass\.indirect_draw\.", 0),
              (P+r"pipeline\.monolithic\.extended_dynamic_state\.", 1200),
              (P+r"pipeline\.monolithic\.sampler\..*custom", 400),
              (P+r"draw\.renderpass\.vertex_attribute_divisor\.", 0),
              (P+r"rasterization\.(primitives|primitives_multisample_4_bit)\.", 0),
              (P+r"descriptor_indexing\.", 0), (P+r"multiview\.", 400),
              (P+r"(depth_clip|depth_clamp)", 500)]),
 ("g6_wsi", [(P+r"wsi\.metal\.", 300)]),
 ("g2b_memory_risky", [(P+r"memory\.allocation\.random\.", 0), (P+r"memory\.pageable_allocation\.basic\.", 0)]),
]

groups_out = []
for name, pats in GROUPS:
    cases, seen = [], set()
    for rx, n in pats:
        for c in pick(rx, n):
            if c not in seen:
                seen.add(c); cases.append(c)
    shard = 150 if name == "g2b_memory_risky" else SHARD
    if name == "g2b_memory_risky": shard = 20
    d = os.path.join(OUT, name); os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    for i in range(0, len(cases), shard):
        with open(os.path.join(d, "s%03d.txt" % (i // shard)), "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(cases[i:i+shard]) + "\n")
    print(name, len(cases), "cases", (len(cases)+shard-1)//shard, "shards")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Parse deqp-vk results copied from the host: results/<group>/*.qpa + events.txt + run.log."""
import os, re, sys, glob, json, collections

RES = sys.argv[1]
STATS = ["Pass", "Fail", "NotSupported", "QualityWarning", "CompatibilityWarning", "Crash", "Timeout", "Other"]

def parse_qpa(path):
    out = {}
    cur, buf = None, []
    with open(path, errors="replace") as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.startswith("#beginTestCaseResult"):
                cur = line.split()[1]; buf = []
            elif line.startswith("#endTestCaseResult") and cur:
                txt = "".join(buf)
                m = re.search(r'<Result StatusCode="([A-Za-z]+)">(.*?)</Result>', txt, re.S)
                st, msg = (m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()) if m else ("Other", "")
                if not m:
                    m2 = re.search(r'StatusCode="([A-Za-z]+)"', txt)
                    if m2: st = m2.group(1)
                # pull the most useful extra text for failures
                extra = ""
                if st not in ("Pass", "NotSupported"):
                    texts = re.findall(r"<Text>(.*?)</Text>", txt, re.S)
                    extra = " | ".join(t.strip() for t in texts[-3:])[:600]
                out[cur] = (st, msg[:400], extra)
                cur = None
            elif line.startswith("#terminateTestCaseResult") and cur:
                out[cur] = ("Timeout" if "Timeout" in line else "Crash", line.strip(), "")
                cur = None
            elif cur:
                buf.append(line)
    if cur:
        out[cur] = ("Crash", "process died", "")
    return out

groups = {}
times = {}
log = os.path.join(RES, "run.log")
if os.path.exists(log):
    for l in open(log):
        m = re.search(r"GROUP (\S+) end in (\d+)s", l)
        if m: times[m.group(1)] = int(m.group(2))
for gdir in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RES, "g*"))):
    g = os.path.basename(gdir)
    res = {}
    for q in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(gdir, "*.qpa")), key=lambda p: (p.split("/")[-1].split(".")[0], int(re.search(r"\.a(\d+)\.qpa", p).group(1)))):
        res.update(parse_qpa(q))
    ev = os.path.join(gdir, "events.txt")
    if os.path.exists(ev):
        for l in open(ev):
            p = l.split()
            if p and p[0] == "TIMEOUT" and len(p) > 1 and p[1] in res:
                res[p[1]] = ("Timeout", "runner: no progress 60 s, killed", "")
            if p and p[0] == "CRASH" and len(p) > 2:
                res[p[2]] = ("Crash", "runner: " + " ".join(p[:2]), "")
    groups[g] = res

summary = {}
for g, res in groups.items():
    c = collections.Counter(v[0] if v[0] in STATS else "Other" for v in res.values())
    summary[g] = {"total": len(res), **{s: c.get(s, 0) for s in STATS}, "wall_s": times.get(g)}
json.dump({"summary": summary,
           "bad": {g: {k: v for k, v in r.items() if v[0] not in ("Pass", "NotSupported")} for g, r in groups.items()}},
          open(os.path.join(RES, "parsed.json"), "w"), indent=1)
print("%-18s %6s %6s %5s %6s %4s %4s %5s %5s %5s %6s" % ("group", "total", "Pass", "Fail", "NotSup", "QW", "CW", "Crash", "Tout", "Other", "wall"))
for g, s in summary.items():
    print("%-18s %6d %6d %5d %6d %4d %4d %5d %5d %5d %6s" % (g, s["total"], s["Pass"], s["Fail"], s["NotSupported"], s["QualityWarning"], s["CompatibilityWarning"], s["Crash"], s["Timeout"], s["Other"], s["wall_s"]))

FILE: user/tests/cts/run.sh

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# deqp-vk shard runner for the hackintosh (plain sh; no dev tools).
# usage: nohup ./run.sh g1_basic g2_memory ... > results/nohup.out 2>&1 &
# Layout (BASE=$HOME/vk-cts):
#   deqp-vk, vulkan/ (archive data), caselists/<group>/sNNN.txt
#   results/<group>/sNNN.aK.qpa   one qpa per (re)start of a shard
#   results/<group>/events.txt    CRASH/TIMEOUT/HEALTH lines (case names)
#   results/run.log               everything the runner did
# Safety:
#   - watchdog (2 s): java or geekbench running -> kill -9 deqp-vk, write ABORT, stop.
#   - no qpa progress for HANG_S s -> kill -9, TIMEOUT event, stop the run.
#   - debug.intelxe.stats bans / GT resets change, new Kernel*.panic -> HEALTH event, stop the run.
#   - touch $BASE/STOP to stop after killing the current deqp-vk.
BASE=$HOME/vk-cts
DEQP=$BASE/deqp-vk
RES=$BASE/results
LOG=$RES/run.log
HANG_S=${HANG_S:-60}
LIB=/usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib
mkdir -p "$RES"
cd "$BASE" || exit 1
rm -f "$BASE/ABORT" "$BASE/STOP"

log() { echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') $*" >> "$LOG"; }
stat_bans()   { sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.* bans \([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1; }
stat_resets() { sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*GT resets \([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1; }
panics()      { ls /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ 2>/dev/null | grep -c -i 'kernel.*panic'; }
gpurestarts() { ls /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'gpuRestart'; }
# busy = any java, any geekbench_avx2 worker, or the Geekbench GUI above 20% CPU.
# An idle Geekbench GUI does not block (coordinator rule update, 2026-10-29).
games() {
  pgrep -l java
  pgrep -l geekbench_avx2
  for p in $(pgrep -i geekbench); do
    c=$(ps -o %cpu= -p $p 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' '); c=${c%%.*}; [ -z "$c" ] && c=0
    [ "$c" -gt 20 ] && echo "$p geekbench busy ${c}%"
  done
}
fsize()       { if [ -f "$1" ]; then wc -c < "$1" | tr -d ' '; else echo 0; fi; }
lastcase()    { grep '^#beginTestCaseResult' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $2}'; }

B0=$(stat_bans); R0=$(stat_resets); P0=$(panics); G0=$(gpurestarts)
log "START groups: $* ; bans=$B0 resets=$R0 panics=$P0 gpuRestart=$G0 hang=${HANG_S}s"

if [ -n "$(games)" ]; then
  log "ABORT: java/geekbench running before start: $(games | tr '\n' ' ')"
  touch "$BASE/ABORT"; exit 2
fi

# run one deqp-vk process; sets RC_KIND to ok|crash|timeout|abort|health|stop
run_deqp() {  # $1 caselist  $2 qpa  $3 events
  "$DEQP" --deqp-caselist-file="$1" --deqp-log-filename="$2" \
     --deqp-vk-library-path="$LIB" --deqp-archive-dir="$BASE" \
     --deqp-log-images=disable --deqp-log-shader-sources=disable \
     --deqp-shadercache-filename="$BASE/shadercache.bin" --deqp-shadercache-truncate=disable \
     > "$2.stdout" 2>&1 &
  PID=$!
  last_sz=0; still=0; RC_KIND=ok
  while kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; do
    sleep 2
    if [ -n "$(games)" ]; then
      kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 deqp-vk
      log "WATCHDOG: java/geekbench detected ($(games | tr '\n' ' ')) - deqp-vk killed; current case $(lastcase "$2")"
      echo "ABORT $(lastcase "$2")" >> "$3"; touch "$BASE/ABORT"; RC_KIND=abort; return
    fi
    if [ -f "$BASE/STOP" ]; then
      kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null; log "STOP file - deqp-vk killed at $(lastcase "$2")"; RC_KIND=stop; return
    fi
    b=$(stat_bans); r=$(stat_resets)
    if [ "$b" != "$B0" ] || [ "$r" != "$R0" ]; then
      log "HEALTH: bans $B0->$b GT resets $R0->$r during $(lastcase "$2")"
      echo "HEALTH bans=$B0->$b resets=$R0->$r $(lastcase "$2")" >> "$3"
      B0=$b; R0=$r
      sleep 3; kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null; RC_KIND=health; return
    fi
    sz=$(fsize "$2")
    if [ "$sz" = "$last_sz" ]; then still=$((still+2)); else still=0; last_sz=$sz; fi
    if [ $still -ge $HANG_S ]; then
      c=$(lastcase "$2")
      lm=$(grep -E '^#(begin|end|terminate)TestCaseResult' "$2" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
      kill -9 $PID 2>/dev/null
      if [ "$lm" = "#beginTestCaseResult" ]; then tag=TIMEOUT; else tag=TIMEOUT_AFTER; fi
      log "$tag: no progress for ${HANG_S}s (last case $c, last marker $lm) - kill -9"
      echo "$tag $c" >> "$3"; RC_KIND=timeout
      sleep 3; st=$(ps -o pid=,stat=,time= -p $PID 2>/dev/null)
      log "after kill -9: ${st:-gone}"
      if [ -n "$st" ]; then sleep 10; st=$(ps -o pid=,stat=,time= -p $PID 2>/dev/null); fi
      if [ -n "$st" ]; then log "UNKILLABLE deqp-vk: $st"; echo "UNKILLABLE $c" >> "$3"; RC_KIND=stuck; fi
      return
    fi
  done
  wait $PID; RC=$?
  # crashed if the last marker is a begin without end
  lm=$(grep -E '^#(begin|end|terminate)TestCaseResult' "$2" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}')
  if [ "$lm" = "#beginTestCaseResult" ]; then
    c=$(lastcase "$2"); echo "CRASH rc=$RC $c" >> "$3"; log "CRASH rc=$RC in $c"; RC_KIND=crash
  elif [ $RC -ne 0 ] && [ -z "$lm" ]; then
    log "deqp-vk rc=$RC before any case (see $2.stdout)"; RC_KIND=nostart
  fi
}

for g in "$@"; do
  [ -d "$BASE/caselists/$g" ] || { log "no caselists for $g"; continue; }
  mkdir -p "$RES/$g"; EV=$RES/$g/events.txt; touch "$EV"
  gstart=$(date +%s); log "GROUP $g begin"
  ncrash=0
  for cl in "$BASE"/caselists/$g/s*.txt; do
    s=$(basename "$cl" .txt)
    rem=$RES/$g/$s.remaining; cp "$cl" "$rem"; a=0
    while [ -s "$rem" ]; do
      qpa=$RES/$g/$s.a$a.qpa
      t0=$(date +%s)
      run_deqp "$rem" "$qpa" "$EV"
      log "$g/$s.a$a: $(grep -c '^#endTestCaseResult' "$qpa" 2>/dev/null) cases in $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s kind=$RC_KIND"
      case $RC_KIND in
        abort|stop) log "END (run stopped: $RC_KIND)"; exit 3 ;;
        health|stuck) log "STOP RUN after $RC_KIND in $g/$s (caller decides what is safe next)"; echo "$(date) $RC_KIND $g/$s" > "$BASE/STOPPED"; exit 4 ;;
        timeout) log "GROUP $g stopped after timeout in $g/$s (process killed); next group"; break 2 ;;
        nostart) log "shard $g/$s could not start; skipping it"; break ;;
      esac
      # drop the cases this attempt started (passed, failed or crashed)
      grep '^#beginTestCaseResult' "$qpa" | awk '{print $2}' > "$rem.done"
      awk 'NR==FNR{d[$1]=1;next} !($1 in d)' "$rem.done" "$rem" > "$rem.new"; mv "$rem.new" "$rem"
      if [ "$RC_KIND" = crash ]; then
        ncrash=$((ncrash+1))
        if [ $ncrash -ge 300 ]; then log "GROUP $g: 300 crashes - group stopped"; break 2; fi
      fi
      a=$((a+1))
      if [ $a -ge 300 ]; then log "$g/$s: too many restarts"; break; fi
    done
    p=$(panics); gr=$(gpurestarts)
    if [ "$p" != "$P0" ]; then log "HEALTH: new kernel panic report ($P0->$p)"; echo "HEALTH panic" >> "$EV"; exit 4; fi
    if [ "$gr" != "$G0" ]; then log "HEALTH: new gpuRestart report ($G0->$gr) after $g/$s"; echo "HEALTH gpuRestart $g/$s" >> "$EV"; G0=$gr; echo "$(date) gpuRestart $g/$s" > "$BASE/STOPPED"; exit 4; fi
  done
  log "GROUP $g end in $(( $(date +%s) - gstart ))s; status: $(cat "$RES"/$g/*.qpa 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'StatusCode="[A-Za-z]*"' | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')"
done
log "ALL DONE"
touch "$BASE/DONE"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Phase 1 gate after a reboot: gate.sh OUTPREFIX. Each remote call is time-boxed (<= 60 s). Run from the Mac.
D=$(dirname "$0"); R="$D/rsh"; O=${1:-$D/after}
ENV='cd ~/b580; export NVMTL_ENABLE=1 NVMTL_ICD_LIB=$HOME/b580/prof/mesa-rel/libvulkan_intel.dylib NVMTL_BUNDLE=$HOME/b580/fix16/NVMTLDriver.bundle;'
$R 30 'sysctl -n kern.boottime; ls -t /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/ | grep -i "^kernel.*panic" | head -3; kextstat | grep -i intelxe; sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats; sudo -n sysctl -n debug.intelxe.state | tail -25' > $O-0.txt 2>&1
$R 60 "$ENV"' echo "tests: $(./mtl_tests 2>&1 | tail -1) | mip: $(./mtl_tests mip 2>&1 | grep -v "implemented in both\|preload" | grep "FAIL\|PASSED\|failure" | tr "\n" " ") | bt: $(inv/bt | tail -1) | race: $(NVMTL_CAPTURE_WAIT=1 inv/surftest race frames 2 | tail -1)"' > $O-1.txt 2>&1

FILE: user/tests/gbcl/README.md
================================================
# gbcl: a Geekbench-OpenCL-shaped microbenchmark

`cl_gbmicro` drives Apple's `OpenCL.framework`, the layer Geekbench's OpenCL workloads use. On the B580 that is
Apple's OpenCL over our Metal plugin (`nullmoth/plugin`), over ANV's xe backend, over the kext's xe uAPI, so a kernel
change shows up in seconds instead of a 2-minute Geekbench run. `night-gbcl.sh` defines `phase_gbclmicro` for the
night scripts.

    clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -Wall -Wno-deprecated-declarations -o cl_gbmicro cl_gbmicro.c -framework OpenCL
    ./cl_gbmicro [-t secs] [-m chain,churn,import,mixed,live] [-q]     # 15 s per mode by default

`nullmoth/build/build-intelxe.sh tests` builds it too.

## What each mode does to the kernel

From the code (plugin `nvmtl_vk.c`, ANV `xe/anv_kmd_backend.c`), per op, on the B580:

| mode | op | kernel calls per op (expected) |
|---|---|---|
| `chain` | 4 tiny kernels + one 256 KB kernel, `clFinish` | 1 `XE_EXEC` per command buffer Apple's OpenCL makes (1-5), 1 syncobj wait |
| `churn` | `clCreateBuffer` (64 KB .. 24 MB, 12 sizes in turn), 4 KB blocking write, 1 kernel, 4-byte blocking read, release | buffers past the plugin's pools (4 MB shared, 1 MB private) and not reused by its buffer park: `XE_GEM_CREATE` + `XE_VM_BIND` map, later `XE_VM_BIND` unmap + `GEM_CLOSE`; 2-3 execs and waits (each blocking write/read finishes the queue) |
| `import` | `CL_MEM_USE_HOST_PTR` on 442 KB + 48 B at 16 B past a page (8 ranges in turn), 2 kernels, blocking map, unmap, release | with `NVMTL_IMPORT_UNALIGNED=1`: `XE_VM_BIND` `MAP_USERPTR` + unmap per op (no GEM object; `NVMTL_IMPORT_CACHE=1` reuses them); without: no bind, the plugin copies the range at every submission |
| `mixed` | blocking 16 KB upload, 1-4 kernels, a temporary buffer every 4th op, an import every 8th, `clWaitForEvents`, 4-byte read | a blend of the above, waits through events as Geekbench does |
| `live16`..`live1024` | with L buffers live (half 64 KB, half 4 MB + 64 KB), release one, make its replacement, 2 kernels, `clFinish` | a bind and an unbind per op against a VM holding ~L/2 BOs of their own; shows costs that grow with the VM (rebind lists, LR-mode preemption, TLB invalidation) |

Apple's OpenCL may also back an ordinary `cl_mem` with its own malloc'd memory (`newBufferWithBytesNoCopy`), which
the plugin then imports or copies like the `import` mode: compare `churn` copy against import to see which.

## Reading the output

    RESULT mode=churn ops=2098 secs=2.00 ops_s=1048.9 p50_us=831.3 p99_us=2355.3 mean_us=953.4 max_us=7861.2 check=ok
      kstat churn: user fences: execs                    +1234  (0.588/op)

- `ops_s` is the throughput; `p50_us` the typical op, `p99_us` the tail (where a slow bind, a TLB invalidation wait
  or an LR preemption cycle shows first). Compare a kernel against another with the same plugin setting, alternated,
  the median of three runs: on the B580 the spread between runs is a few percent; a difference smaller than that is
  noise.
- `kstat` lines are the counters of `debug.intelxe.stats` that changed during the timed part, with the delta and the
  delta per op. Nothing is parsed by name (the text changes with each kernel revision): every number is labelled with
  its line's head and clause. Gauges (VRAM used, live queues) appear as deltas too. Per-op rates are the useful part:
  e.g. jobs direct/via worker per op is submissions per op, TLB invalidations per op is binds and unbinds reaching the
  GPU, deferred frees per op is BO frees. If the kernel was reloaded in between, no deltas are printed.
- `CHECK` lines mean a wrong result (the GPU's answer is verified for every op); `FAIL` is an OpenCL error.
- On a machine without the IntelXe kernel (a smoke test against Apple's driver) the `kstat` line says so.

The night phase writes `$O/gbcl/table.txt` (per mode and plugin setting: the three runs' ops/s, their median, median
p50 and p99), `$O/gbcl/results.txt` and `$O/gbcl/kstat-run1.txt`, and reports GuC/GT resets per run.

FILE: user/tests/gbcl/cl_gbmicro.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// cl_gbmicro: a fast, deterministic stand-in for Geekbench's OpenCL workloads, for kernel A/B runs on the B580.
// It drives Apple's OpenCL.framework (the layer Geekbench uses; on the B580 it runs over our Metal plugin, then ANV,
// then the kext's xe uAPI) with the call shapes that reach the kernel: many small and medium kernel enqueues, cl_mem
// create/use/release churn (VM_BIND map/unmap, GEM create/close when a buffer is past the plugin's pools), unaligned
// CL_MEM_USE_HOST_PTR imports (userptr binds with NVMTL_IMPORT_UNALIGNED=1, a staged copy without), and completion
// waits (syncobj waits). Per mode: ops, ops/s, per-op latency p50/p99, and the changed counters of debug.intelxe.stats.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -Wall -Wno-deprecated-declarations -o cl_gbmicro cl_gbmicro.c -framework OpenCL
//   ./cl_gbmicro [-t secs] [-m chain,churn,import,mixed,live] [-q]
//     -t   seconds per mode (default 15; live splits it over its four levels)
//     -m   modes, in this order (default all five)
//     -q   only the RESULT lines and the counter deltas
//   GBCL_DEVICE=<n> picks GPU n of the list it prints (default: the one reporting Intel, else GPU 0).
// The op sequence is fixed (an LCG with a fixed seed): two runs of one mode do the same calls; only how many fit in
// the time differs. Counter deltas are also printed per op, so runs of different lengths compare.
#include <OpenCL/opencl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>

static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static double now_us(void) { return (double)mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e3; }
static int dcmp(const void *a, const void *b) { double x = *(const double *)a, y = *(const double *)b; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }
#define CK(x) do { cl_int e_ = (x); if (e_) { printf("FAIL %s:%d %s -> %d\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #x, e_); exit(1); } } while (0)

static int quiet;
static cl_context ctx;
static cl_device_id dev;
static cl_command_queue q;
static cl_kernel k_tiny, k_touch;
static uint32_t lcg_s;
static uint32_t lcg(void) { lcg_s = lcg_s * 1664525u + 1013904223u; return lcg_s >> 8; }

static const char *src =
	"__kernel void tiny(__global uint *o, uint v) { if (get_global_id(0) == 0) o[0] += v; }\n"
	"__kernel void touch(__global uint *b, uint n, uint v) { size_t i = get_global_id(0); if (i < n) b[i] = b[i] * 3u + v; }\n";

// ─── debug.intelxe.stats: every number of the text, with a label from the text before it ───────────────────────────
// The format changes with each kernel revision (rb8c..f added lines), so nothing is parsed by name: before and after
// are tokenized the same way, and when both have the same text around their numbers the changed ones are printed with
// "<line head>: <clause>" as the label. When the shapes differ (a kernel reload in between) nothing is printed.
#define KMAX 1024
typedef struct { int n; long long v[KMAX]; char lab[KMAX][96]; } kstats;
static int kread(char **out)
{
	size_t len = 0;
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.stats", NULL, &len, NULL, 0) || !len) return -1;
	len += 4096; char *b = calloc(1, len + 1);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.stats", b, &len, NULL, 0)) { free(b); return -1; }
	*out = b; return 0;
}
static int isal(char c) { return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_' || c == '.'; }
static void kparse(const char *t, kstats *k)
{
	k->n = 0;
	const char *line = t;
	for (const char *p = t; *p && k->n < KMAX; p++) {
		if (*p == '\n') { line = p + 1; continue; }
		if (!(*p >= '0' && *p <= '9') || (p > t && (isal(p[-1]) || p[-1] == '-'))) continue;
		if (p[0] == '0' && p[1] == 'x') { while (isal(*p)) p++; p--; continue; }   // addresses: not counters
		const char *e = p; long long v = 0; while (*e >= '0' && *e <= '9') v = v * 10 + (*e++ - '0');
		if (isal(*e)) { p = e - 1; continue; }   // part of a word ("rb8e", "4K")
		// label: the line's head up to its first ':' plus the clause the number ends (back to ; , ( or the head)
		const char *colon = memchr(line, ':', (size_t)(p - line));
		const char *cl = p; while (cl > line && cl[-1] != ';' && cl[-1] != ',' && cl[-1] != '(' && cl[-1] != ':' && cl[-1] != ')') cl--;
		while (*cl == ' ') cl++;
		const char *he = colon;   // a line without ':' ("TLB invalidations 5 (ranged 2, ...)"): its words before the first number
		if (!he) { he = line; while (he < p && !(*he >= '0' && *he <= '9')) he++; while (he > line && he[-1] == ' ') he--; }
		char head[40] = ""; if (he > line && he < cl) { size_t hl = (size_t)(he - line); if (hl > 38) hl = 38; memcpy(head, line, hl); head[hl] = 0; }
		char clause[64] = ""; size_t cn = (size_t)(p - cl); if (cn > 62) cn = 62; memcpy(clause, cl, cn); clause[cn] = 0;
		while (cn && clause[cn - 1] == ' ') clause[--cn] = 0;
		snprintf(k->lab[k->n], sizeof k->lab[0], "%s%s%s", head, *head ? ": " : "", clause);
		k->v[k->n++] = v;
		p = e - 1;
	}
}
static kstats ks0, ks1;
static int kbefore(void) { char *t; if (kread(&t)) return -1; kparse(t, &ks0); free(t); return 0; }
static void kafter(const char *mode, long ops)
{
	char *t; if (kread(&t)) { printf("  kstat %s: no debug.intelxe.stats (not the IntelXe kernel)\n", mode); return; }
	kparse(t, &ks1); free(t);
	if (ks1.n != ks0.n) { printf("  kstat %s: the stats text changed shape (%d -> %d numbers); no deltas\n", mode, ks0.n, ks1.n); return; }
	int shown = 0;
	for (int i = 0; i < ks1.n; i++) {
		if (strcmp(ks0.lab[i], ks1.lab[i])) { printf("  kstat %s: label %d moved; no deltas\n", mode, i); return; }
		const long long d = ks1.v[i] - ks0.v[i];
		if (!d) continue;
		printf("  kstat %s: %-70s %+8lld  (%.3f/op)\n", mode, ks1.lab[i], d, ops ? (double)d / ops : 0.0);
		shown++;
	}
	if (!shown) printf("  kstat %s: no counter changed\n", mode);
}

// ─── timing ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
static double *lat; static long latcap;
typedef void (*opfn)(long i, void *st);
static void run(const char *mode, opfn op, void *st, double secs, const char *check)
{
	for (long i = 0; i < 32; i++) op(-1 - i, st);   // warm-up: pipelines, pools, the first BOs (not counted)
	CK(clFinish(q));
	const int haveK = kbefore() == 0;
	long n = 0; const double t0 = now_us(), end = t0 + secs * 1e6; double t = t0;
	while (t < end && n < latcap) { op(n, st); const double t1 = now_us(); lat[n++] = t1 - t; t = t1; }
	CK(clFinish(q));
	const double wall = (now_us() - t0) / 1e6;
	qsort(lat, (size_t)n, 8, dcmp); double s = 0; for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) s += lat[i];
	printf("RESULT mode=%s ops=%ld secs=%.2f ops_s=%.1f p50_us=%.1f p99_us=%.1f mean_us=%.1f max_us=%.1f check=%s\n", mode, n, wall,
	       n / wall, lat[n / 2], lat[n * 99 / 100], s / n, lat[n - 1], check ? check : "ok");
	if (haveK) kafter(mode, n); else printf("  kstat %s: no debug.intelxe.stats (not the IntelXe kernel)\n", mode);
	fflush(stdout);
}
static void set_touch(cl_mem b, cl_uint n, cl_uint v)
{ CK(clSetKernelArg(k_touch, 0, sizeof b, &b)); CK(clSetKernelArg(k_touch, 1, 4, &n)); CK(clSetKernelArg(k_touch, 2, 4, &v)); }
static void enq_touch(cl_mem b, cl_uint n, cl_uint v, cl_event *ev)
{
	set_touch(b, n, v); size_t g = ((size_t)n + 63) & ~(size_t)63, l = 64;
	CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, k_touch, 1, NULL, &g, &l, 0, NULL, ev));
}
static void enq_tiny(cl_mem o, cl_uint v)
{
	CK(clSetKernelArg(k_tiny, 0, sizeof o, &o)); CK(clSetKernelArg(k_tiny, 1, 4, &v));
	size_t g = 64, l = 64; CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, k_tiny, 1, NULL, &g, &l, 0, NULL, NULL));
}

// ─── chain: 4 tiny kernels + one 256 KB kernel, then clFinish (one submission and one wait per op) ──────────────────
typedef struct { cl_mem o, m; unsigned long long sum; } chain_st;
static void op_chain(long i, void *p)
{
	chain_st *s = p; (void)i;
	for (cl_uint k = 1; k <= 4; k++) { enq_tiny(s->o, k); s->sum += k; }
	enq_touch(s->m, 65536, 1, NULL);
	CK(clFinish(q));
}
// ─── churn: create a buffer (sizes cycle across the plugin's pool and park limits), write 4 KB, one kernel, read
// 4 bytes back, release. Sizes past 4 MB (shared) / 1 MB (private) are their own BO: GEM_CREATE + VM_BIND + unbind +
// close each, unless the plugin's buffer park reuses one (same size class within NVMTL_BUFPARK_AGE_MS). ───────────────
static const size_t churn_sz[] = { 64 << 10, 256 << 10, (1 << 20) + 4096, (4 << 20) + (64 << 10), 6 << 20, 12 << 20,
                                   3 << 20, (24 << 20) + 4096, 512 << 10, (9 << 20) + 8192, 2 << 20, (16 << 20) + 65536 };
#define NCHURN (sizeof churn_sz / sizeof churn_sz[0])
typedef struct { uint32_t host[1024]; int bad; } churn_st;
static void op_churn(long i, void *p)
{
	churn_st *s = p; cl_int err;
	const size_t S = churn_sz[(size_t)(i < 0 ? -i : i) % NCHURN];
	cl_mem b = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, S, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	for (int k = 0; k < 1024; k++) s->host[k] = (uint32_t)i + k;
	CK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, b, CL_TRUE, 0, 4096, s->host, 0, NULL, NULL));
	enq_touch(b, 16384, 7, NULL);
	uint32_t r = 0; CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, b, CL_TRUE, 0, 4, &r, 0, NULL, NULL));
	if (r != (uint32_t)i * 3u + 7u) s->bad++;
	CK(clReleaseMemObject(b));
}
// ─── import: an unaligned malloc'd host range as CL_MEM_USE_HOST_PTR (442 KB + 48 B, like Geekbench's), 2 kernels,
// map/unmap to read it, release. Eight host ranges are reused in turn (so NVMTL_IMPORT_CACHE=1 can hit). ─────────────
#define IMP_N 8
#define IMP_SZ ((442u << 10) + 48u)
typedef struct { uint8_t *mem[IMP_N]; uint32_t *ptr[IMP_N]; int bad; } imp_st;
static void op_import_one(imp_st *s, long i)
{
	cl_int err; const int slot = (int)((i < 0 ? -i : i) % IMP_N); uint32_t *h = s->ptr[slot];
	h[0] = (uint32_t)i;
	cl_mem b = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE | CL_MEM_USE_HOST_PTR, IMP_SZ, h, &err); CK(err);
	enq_touch(b, IMP_SZ / 4, 1, NULL);
	enq_touch(b, IMP_SZ / 4, 2, NULL);
	uint32_t *m = clEnqueueMapBuffer(q, b, CL_TRUE, CL_MAP_READ, 0, IMP_SZ, 0, NULL, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	if (m[0] != ((uint32_t)i * 3u + 1u) * 3u + 2u) s->bad++;
	CK(clEnqueueUnmapMemObject(q, b, m, 0, NULL, NULL));
	CK(clReleaseMemObject(b));
}
static void op_import(long i, void *p) { op_import_one(p, i); CK(clFinish(q)); }
// ─── mixed: Geekbench-like step: blocking 16 KB upload into a long-lived input, 1-4 kernels, every 4th op a temporary
// buffer, every 8th an import, completion by clWaitForEvents on the last kernel's event, then a 4-byte read. ──────────
typedef struct { cl_mem in, acc; uint32_t up[4096]; imp_st *imp; churn_st *ch; int bad; } mixed_st;
static void op_mixed(long i, void *p)
{
	mixed_st *s = p; cl_int err;
	for (int k = 0; k < 4096; k++) s->up[k] = (uint32_t)(i + k);
	CK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, s->in, CL_TRUE, 0, sizeof s->up, s->up, 0, NULL, NULL));
	const uint32_t r = lcg(); const int nk = 1 + (int)(r & 3);
	cl_event ev = NULL;
	for (int k = 0; k < nk; k++) {
		if (ev) { CK(clReleaseEvent(ev)); ev = NULL; }
		if ((r >> (4 + k)) & 1) enq_touch(s->in, 4096, (cl_uint)k, &ev);
		else enq_touch(s->acc, 1u << (10 + ((r >> 12) & 7)), (cl_uint)k, &ev);   // 1K..128K elements
	}
	if ((i & 3) == 0) {
		cl_mem t = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, churn_sz[(r >> 16) % NCHURN], NULL, &err); CK(err);
		if (ev) { CK(clReleaseEvent(ev)); ev = NULL; }
		enq_touch(t, 16384, 3, &ev);
		CK(clReleaseMemObject(t));   // released while queued: freed when the kernel is done
	}
	CK(clWaitForEvents(1, &ev)); CK(clReleaseEvent(ev));
	if ((i & 7) == 0) op_import_one(s->imp, i);
	uint32_t v = 0; CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, s->in, CL_TRUE, 0, 4, &v, 0, NULL, NULL));
	(void)v;
}
// ─── live: L buffers live (half 64 KB, half 4 MB + 64 KB, so half are BOs of their own); each op releases one,
// makes its replacement, runs a kernel on it and on another live one, clFinish. Levels 16, 64, 256, 1024. ───────────
typedef struct { cl_mem *b; int L; } live_st;
static size_t live_sz(int k) { return (k & 1) ? (4u << 20) + (64u << 10) : 64u << 10; }
static void op_live(long i, void *p)
{
	live_st *s = p; cl_int err; (void)i;
	const int v = (int)(lcg() % (uint32_t)s->L), w = (int)(lcg() % (uint32_t)s->L);
	CK(clReleaseMemObject(s->b[v]));
	s->b[v] = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, live_sz(v), NULL, &err); CK(err);
	enq_touch(s->b[v], 16384, 1, NULL);
	enq_touch(s->b[w], 16384, 2, NULL);
	CK(clFinish(q));
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	mach_timebase_info(&tb); setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	double secs = 15; const char *modes = "chain,churn,import,mixed,live";
	for (int a = 1; a < argc; a++) {
		if (!strcmp(argv[a], "-t") && a + 1 < argc) secs = atof(argv[++a]);
		else if (!strcmp(argv[a], "-m") && a + 1 < argc) modes = argv[++a];
		else if (!strcmp(argv[a], "-q")) quiet = 1;
		else { printf("usage: %s [-t secs] [-m chain,churn,import,mixed,live] [-q]\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
	}
	cl_platform_id plat; CK(clGetPlatformIDs(1, &plat, NULL));
	cl_device_id devs[8]; cl_uint nd = 0; CK(clGetDeviceIDs(plat, CL_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU, 8, devs, &nd));
	int best = 0;
	for (cl_uint i = 0; i < nd; i++) {
		char name[256] = "", vendor[256] = ""; cl_uint vid = 0;
		clGetDeviceInfo(devs[i], CL_DEVICE_NAME, sizeof name, name, NULL);
		clGetDeviceInfo(devs[i], CL_DEVICE_VENDOR, sizeof vendor, vendor, NULL);
		clGetDeviceInfo(devs[i], CL_DEVICE_VENDOR_ID, sizeof vid, &vid, NULL);
		if (!quiet) printf("GPU %u: %s, vendor \"%s\" 0x%x\n", i, name, vendor, vid);
		const int rank = vid == 0x8086 ? 3 : (strstr(vendor, "Intel") || strstr(vendor, "intel")) ? 2 : 1;
		if (rank > best) { dev = devs[i]; best = rank; }
	}
	const char *pick = getenv("GBCL_DEVICE");
	if (pick) { cl_uint n = (cl_uint)atoi(pick); dev = n < nd ? devs[n] : NULL; }
	if (!dev) { printf("no OpenCL GPU\n"); return 2; }
	{ char name[256] = ""; clGetDeviceInfo(dev, CL_DEVICE_NAME, sizeof name, name, NULL);
	  printf("device: %s; %.0f s per mode; modes %s; NVMTL_IMPORT_UNALIGNED=%s\n", name, secs, modes,
	         getenv("NVMTL_IMPORT_UNALIGNED") ? getenv("NVMTL_IMPORT_UNALIGNED") : "unset"); }
	cl_int err;
	ctx = clCreateContext(NULL, 1, &dev, NULL, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	q = clCreateCommandQueue(ctx, dev, 0, &err); CK(err);
	cl_program pr = clCreateProgramWithSource(ctx, 1, &src, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	if (clBuildProgram(pr, 1, &dev, "", NULL, NULL)) {
		char log[8192] = ""; clGetProgramBuildInfo(pr, dev, CL_PROGRAM_BUILD_LOG, sizeof log, log, NULL); printf("build: %s\n", log); return 1; }
	k_tiny = clCreateKernel(pr, "tiny", &err); CK(err);
	k_touch = clCreateKernel(pr, "touch", &err); CK(err);
	latcap = 4 << 20; lat = malloc((size_t)latcap * 8);

	imp_st imp = { 0 };
	for (int k = 0; k < IMP_N; k++) {   // malloc-like alignment: 16 B past a page, plus 64 B per slot
		imp.mem[k] = NULL; if (posix_memalign((void **)&imp.mem[k], 4096, IMP_SZ + 8192)) return 1;
		imp.ptr[k] = (uint32_t *)(imp.mem[k] + 16 + 64 * k); memset(imp.ptr[k], 0, IMP_SZ);
	}
	char m[256]; snprintf(m, sizeof m, "%s", modes);
	for (char *tok = strtok(m, ","); tok; tok = strtok(NULL, ",")) {
		lcg_s = 12345;
		if (!strcmp(tok, "chain")) {
			chain_st s = { 0 };
			s.o = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, 4096, NULL, &err); CK(err);
			s.m = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, 65536 * 4, NULL, &err); CK(err);
			uint32_t z = 0; CK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, s.o, CL_TRUE, 0, 4, &z, 0, NULL, NULL));
			// the check needs the sum after the run, so it is printed on its own line
			run("chain", op_chain, &s, secs, NULL);
			uint32_t r = 0; CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, s.o, CL_TRUE, 0, 4, &r, 0, NULL, NULL));
			if (r != (uint32_t)s.sum) printf("CHECK chain: o[0] %u, expected %u\n", r, (uint32_t)s.sum);
			clReleaseMemObject(s.o); clReleaseMemObject(s.m);
		} else if (!strcmp(tok, "churn")) {
			churn_st s = { 0 }; run("churn", op_churn, &s, secs, NULL);
			if (s.bad) printf("CHECK churn: %d wrong read-backs\n", s.bad);
		} else if (!strcmp(tok, "import")) {
			imp.bad = 0; run("import", op_import, &imp, secs, NULL);
			if (imp.bad) printf("CHECK import: %d wrong results\n", imp.bad);
		} else if (!strcmp(tok, "mixed")) {
			churn_st ch = { 0 }; mixed_st s = { 0 }; s.imp = &imp; s.ch = &ch; imp.bad = 0;
			s.in = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, sizeof s.up, NULL, &err); CK(err);
			s.acc = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, 128 << 12, NULL, &err); CK(err);
			run("mixed", op_mixed, &s, secs, NULL);
			if (imp.bad) printf("CHECK mixed: %d wrong import results\n", imp.bad);
			clReleaseMemObject(s.in); clReleaseMemObject(s.acc);
		} else if (!strcmp(tok, "live")) {
			static const int levels[] = { 16, 64, 256, 1024 };
			for (int li = 0; li < 4; li++) {
				live_st s = { calloc((size_t)levels[li], sizeof(cl_mem)), levels[li] };
				for (int k = 0; k < s.L; k++) {
					s.b[k] = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, live_sz(k), NULL, &err); CK(err);
					enq_touch(s.b[k], 16384, 0, NULL);   // every one used once, so each is resident before timing
					if ((k & 63) == 63) CK(clFinish(q));
				}
				CK(clFinish(q));
				char nm[32]; snprintf(nm, sizeof nm, "live%d", s.L);
				run(nm, op_live, &s, secs / 4, NULL);
				for (int k = 0; k < s.L; k++) clReleaseMemObject(s.b[k]);
				CK(clFinish(q)); free(s.b);
			}
		} else { printf("unknown mode %s\n", tok); return 2; }
	}
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/gbcl/night-gbcl.sh
