FILE: user/tests/kernel/barrevoke.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// barrevoke: CPU-mapped BOs leaving the BAR window with their mappings redirected (debug.intelxe.bar_revoke;
// docs/design/DESIGN-rebar-window.md section 8), on IntelXe.kext.
//   ./barrevoke now [MB]      fills the window with CPU-mapped NEEDS_VISIBLE BOs of MB each (default 4), the CPU and the
//                             GPU write a pattern into each, then debug.intelxe.bar_revoke_now=<own pid> revokes them
//                             (needs root: run with sudo; any bar_revoke value)
//   ./barrevoke natural [MB]  the same fill, then more mapped BOs than the window has room for: GEM_CREATE's eviction
//                             must revoke the oldest (needs debug.intelxe.bar_revoke=1; SKIP otherwise)
// Then, through the pointers the maps returned before the move:
//   1. the CPU reads back what the CPU and the GPU wrote before the move (the copy, the redirect)
//   2. the CPU writes a new value, the GPU copies it to a neighbouring dword (MI_COPY_MEM_MEM through the same GPU VA:
//      the GPU reads what the CPU wrote, its PTEs rewritten), the CPU reads the GPU's copy
//   3. the GPU stores again (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM), the CPU reads it
//   4. every map is unmapped with IOConnectUnmapMemory64, which must succeed (it finds the mapping through the
//      descriptor the revocation gave the map) and the kernel's "CPU maps gone" count must follow
// and debug.intelxe.vram's bar_revoke line must show moves and no broken / latched result.
// TAKES THE WHOLE WINDOW for a few seconds: not while a game or benchmark runs.
// Test only.   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -Ikernel/IntelXe/uapi -o barrevoke user/tests/kernel/barrevoke.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags, uint16_t caching) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .flags = flags, .cpu_caching = caching};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) return 0;
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size, uint32_t *type) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) { printf("MMAP_OFFSET %d\n", errno); return NULL; }
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	*type = (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12);
	// bit 63: write-combined (what xemac_mmap asks for)
	IOOptionBits o = kIOMapAnywhere | ((m.offset >> 63) ? kIOMapWriteCombineCache : 0);
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, *type, mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, o)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) return -1;
	struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	int r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&sc.handle, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = INT64_MAX};
	if (!r) r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
	struct drm_syncobj_destroy d = {.handle = sc.handle};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_DESTROY, &d);
	return r;
}
static int sysint(const char *name, int dflt) {
	int v = 0; size_t l = sizeof(v);
	return sysctlbyname(name, &v, &l, NULL, 0) ? dflt : v;
}
static char vram[16384];
static const char *vramText(void) {
	size_t l = sizeof(vram);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.vram", vram, &l, NULL, 0)) vram[0] = 0;
	return vram;
}
static uint64_t num(const char *text, const char *key) {   // the number after `key`, 0 if absent
	const char *p = strstr(text, key);
	return p ? strtoull(p + strlen(key), NULL, 10) : 0;
}
static void revokeLine(const char *what) {
	const char *p = strstr(vramText(), "bar_revoke ");
	if (!p) { printf("%s: no bar_revoke line (kext without bar_revoke?)\n", what); return; }
	const char *e = strchr(p, '\n');
	printf("%s: %.*s\n", what, (int)(e ? e - p : (long)strlen(p)), p);
}

// Two VMs, each with its render queue: the filled BOs in 0, `natural`'s extra ones in 1, so that the extra BOs' EXECs do
// not make the filled ones recent (the policy counts a VM's last EXEC as a touch of every BO bound in it).
static uint32_t vmIds[2], qs[2], so, cur;
static volatile uint32_t *bb;
static void submit(uint32_t k) {
	bb[k++] = 0xa << 23; bb[k++] = 0;   // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END
	__sync_synchronize();
	struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = so};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = qs[cur], .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s, .address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x), "exec %d", errno);
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&so, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = INT64_MAX};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w), "wait %d", errno);
}
// MI_STORE_DATA_IMM of value ^ offset at va + offset + 8, every 64 KB
static void gpuStore(uint64_t va, uint64_t size, uint32_t value) {
	uint32_t k = 0;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size; o += 0x10000) {
		const uint64_t a = va + o + 8;
		bb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; bb[k++] = (uint32_t)a; bb[k++] = (uint32_t)(a >> 32); bb[k++] = value ^ (uint32_t)o;
	}
	submit(k);
}
// MI_COPY_MEM_MEM dword va + o + 16 -> va + o + 24, every 64 KB (destination first, as surffence.c)
static void gpuCopy(uint64_t va, uint64_t size) {
	uint32_t k = 0;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size; o += 0x10000) {
		const uint64_t s = va + o + 16, d = va + o + 24;
		bb[k++] = 0x2e << 23 | 3; bb[k++] = (uint32_t)d; bb[k++] = (uint32_t)(d >> 32); bb[k++] = (uint32_t)s; bb[k++] = (uint32_t)(s >> 32);
	}
	submit(k);
}

#define MAXB 256
static volatile uint64_t *p[MAXB];
static uint64_t each;
// barwin2: a fault on an old pointer says which BO and where (barwin's kernel answered every later fault on a revoked BO
// with SIGBUS, and the test died without a line: stdout to a file is fully buffered)
static void onFault(int sig, siginfo_t *si, void *uc) {
	(void)uc;
	char b[160];
	const uintptr_t a = (uintptr_t)si->si_addr;
	int bo = -1;
	for (int i = 0; i < MAXB; i++)
		if (p[i] && a >= (uintptr_t)p[i] && a < (uintptr_t)p[i] + each) bo = i;
	const int n = snprintf(b, sizeof(b), "FAIL: signal %d at %#lx: BO %d offset %#lx\nFAILED: fault on an old pointer\n", sig,
		(unsigned long)a, bo, bo >= 0 ? (unsigned long)(a - (uintptr_t)p[bo]) : 0ul);
	write(1, b, (size_t)n);
	_exit(3);
}
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	struct sigaction sa = {0};
	sa.sa_sigaction = onFault;
	sa.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO;
	sigaction(SIGBUS, &sa, NULL);
	sigaction(SIGSEGV, &sa, NULL);
	const int forced = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "now");
	const int natural = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "natural");
	if (!forced && !natural) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s now|natural [MB per BO]\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
	each = (uint64_t)(argc > 2 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 4) << 20;
	if (each < (64u << 10) || each > (64ull << 20)) { fprintf(stderr, "MB: 1-64\n"); return 2; }
	const int knob = sysint("debug.intelxe.bar_revoke", -1);
	if (knob < 0) { printf("SKIP: kext without debug.intelxe.bar_revoke\n"); return 0; }
	if (natural && knob != 1) { printf("SKIP: debug.intelxe.bar_revoke is %d (natural needs 1)\n", knob); return 0; }
	if (forced && geteuid()) { printf("SKIP: 'now' writes debug.intelxe.bar_revoke_now (root)\n"); return 0; }

	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	uint32_t bbType;
	const uint32_t bbh = gem(0x10000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);   // system memory: never a candidate
	bb = bbh ? map(bbh, 0x10000, &bbType) : NULL;
	if (!bb) { fprintf(stderr, "batch\n"); return 1; }
	for (int v = 0; v < 2; v++) {
		struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
		if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create\n"); return 1; }
		vmIds[v] = vc.vm_id;
		if (bind(vmIds[v], bbh, 0x100000, 0x10000)) { fprintf(stderr, "batch bind\n"); return 1; }
		struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER};
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create qc = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vmIds[v], .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
		if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &qc)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue\n"); return 1; }
		qs[v] = qc.exec_queue_id;
	}
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc);
	so = sc.handle;

	const char *t = vramText();
	const uint64_t freeMB = num(t, "free "), movedBefore = num(strstr(t, "bar_revoke ") ?: "", "moved "),
		goneBefore = num(t, "gone ");
	revokeLine("before");
	// leave ~40 MB (the page-table reserve and a margin) so the extra BOs of `natural` cannot fit
	uint32_t n = freeMB > 40 ? (uint32_t)((freeMB - 40) / (each >> 20)) : 0;
	if (n > MAXB - 16) n = MAXB - 16;
	if (n < 2) { printf("SKIP: window free %llu MB\n", (unsigned long long)freeMB); return 0; }
	printf("window free %llu MB: %u CPU-mapped BOs of %llu MB (bar_revoke %d, mode %s)\n", (unsigned long long)freeMB, n,
		(unsigned long long)(each >> 20), knob, forced ? "now" : "natural");
	static uint32_t h[MAXB], type[MAXB];
	uint32_t made = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++, made++) {
		if (!(h[i] = gem(each, 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC))) break;
		if (!(p[i] = map(h[i], each, &type[i]))) { CHECK(0, "map %u", i); break; }
		for (uint64_t o = 0; o < each; o += 0x1000) p[i][o / 8] = (uint64_t)i << 32 | o;   // the CPU's pattern
		__sync_synchronize();
		const uint64_t va = (1ull << 33) + (uint64_t)i * each;
		CHECK(!bind(vmIds[0], h[i], va, each), "bind %u", i);
		gpuStore(va, each, 0x5a000000u | i);   // the GPU's, beside it
	}
	const int hot = sysint("debug.intelxe.bar_revoke_hot_ms", 1000);
	usleep((useconds_t)(hot > 0 ? hot + 300 : 300) * 1000);   // everything filled is cold now

	uint32_t extra = 0;
	if (forced) {
		int pid = getpid();
		CHECK(!sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.bar_revoke_now", NULL, NULL, &pid, sizeof(pid)), "bar_revoke_now: %d", errno);
	} else {   // more mapped BOs than the window has room for: GEM_CREATE evicts, and only revocation can free anything
		cur = 1;
		for (uint32_t i = made; i < made + 12 && i < MAXB; i++, extra++) {
			if (!(h[i] = gem(each, 3, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC))) break;
			if (!(p[i] = map(h[i], each, &type[i]))) { CHECK(0, "map extra %u", i); break; }
			for (uint64_t o = 0; o < each; o += 0x1000) p[i][o / 8] = (uint64_t)i << 32 | o;
			__sync_synchronize();
			const uint64_t va = (1ull << 33) + (uint64_t)i * each;
			CHECK(!bind(vmIds[1], h[i], va, each), "bind extra %u", i);
			gpuStore(va, each, 0x5a000000u | i);
		}
	}
	const uint32_t total = made + extra;
	t = vramText();
	const uint64_t moved = num(strstr(t, "bar_revoke ") ?: "", "moved ") - movedBefore;
	revokeLine("after the move");
	printf("revoked: %llu BOs\n", (unsigned long long)moved);
	CHECK(moved > 0, "nothing was revoked");
	// this process's own revoked BOs (debug.intelxe.vram per process: "(N, revoked K)"): the checks below exercise old
	// pointers only for those. The natural pass takes the least recently touched BOs of every process, which may all be
	// other processes'.
	char key[32];
	snprintf(key, sizeof(key), "pid %d ", getpid());
	const char *mine = strstr(t, key);
	const uint64_t own = mine ? num(mine, "revoked ") : 0;
	printf("revoked of this process: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)own);
	if (forced) CHECK(own > 0, "bar_revoke_now took none of this process's BOs");
	else if (!own) printf("NOTE: natural revoked only other processes' BOs: the old-pointer checks are vacuous\n");
	CHECK(!strstr(t, "LATCHED OFF"), "revocation latched off");
	CHECK(num(t, "broken ") == 0 && num(t, "undecided ") == 0, "broken / undecided revocations");
	cur = 0;

	// 1. what was written before the move, through the old pointers
	uint32_t bad = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < total; i++)
		for (uint64_t o = 0; o < each; o += 0x1000) {
			if (p[i][o / 8] != ((uint64_t)i << 32 | o)) bad++;
			if (!(o & 0xffff) && ((volatile uint32_t *)p[i])[(o + 8) / 4] != ((0x5a000000u | i) ^ (uint32_t)o)) bad++;
		}
	CHECK(!bad, "%u words wrong after the move (CPU and GPU patterns)", bad);
	// 2. CPU writes, the GPU copies, the CPU reads the copy; 3. the GPU stores again
	bad = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < total; i++) {
		for (uint64_t o = 0; o < each; o += 0x10000) ((volatile uint32_t *)p[i])[(o + 16) / 4] = 0xc0000000u | i << 16 | (uint32_t)(o >> 16);
		__sync_synchronize();
		const uint64_t va = (1ull << 33) + (uint64_t)i * each;
		cur = i >= made;
		gpuCopy(va, each);
		gpuStore(va, each, 0x3c000000u | i);
		for (uint64_t o = 0; o < each; o += 0x10000) {
			if (((volatile uint32_t *)p[i])[(o + 24) / 4] != (0xc0000000u | i << 16 | (uint32_t)(o >> 16))) bad++;
			if (((volatile uint32_t *)p[i])[(o + 8) / 4] != ((0x3c000000u | i) ^ (uint32_t)o)) bad++;
		}
	}
	CHECK(!bad, "%u words wrong after CPU writes / GPU copies / GPU stores through the old pointers and VAs", bad);
	// 4. unmaps
	uint32_t unmapFails = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < total; i++)
		if (p[i] && IOConnectUnmapMemory64(conn, type[i], mach_task_self(), (mach_vm_address_t)(uintptr_t)p[i])) unmapFails++;
	CHECK(!unmapFails, "%u of %u unmaps failed", unmapFails, total);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < total; i++) {
		struct drm_gem_close c = {.handle = h[i]};
		xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &c);
	}
	usleep(200000);
	t = vramText();
	const uint64_t gone = num(t, "gone ") - goneBefore;
	CHECK(gone >= total, "CPU maps gone %llu of %u", (unsigned long long)gone, total);
	revokeLine("end");
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/bomove.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// bomove: BO moves into and out of the BAR window (p2c) on IntelXe.kext.
//   ./bomove         migrate on map: a 48 MB VRAM BO the CPU may not map lands outside the window; the GPU writes a pattern
//                    into it through its VA, then GEM_MMAP_OFFSET moves it into the window. The CPU reads the pattern
//                    through the new mapping, and the GPU writes again through the same VA (its PTEs were rewritten): the
//                    CPU must see the new values.
//   ./bomove evict   window eviction: NEEDS_VISIBLE BOs that are never mapped are filled by the GPU until the window has
//                    less room than one more; that allocation must evict some of them (debug.intelxe.stats "BO moves: ... out
//                    of it"), and mapping an evicted one brings it back with its contents.
// Test only.   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o bomove bomove.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } } while (0)
static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags, uint16_t caching) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .flags = flags, .cpu_caching = caching};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) { printf("MMAP_OFFSET %d\n", errno); return NULL; }
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
// The bind's out-fence is the BO's VRAM clear (copy engine): waited for, as Mesa makes its execs wait on it.
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) return -1;
	struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	int r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&sc.handle, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = INT64_MAX};
	if (!r) r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
	struct drm_syncobj_destroy d = {.handle = sc.handle};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_DESTROY, &d);
	return r;
}
static void stats(const char *what) {
	char buf[4096]; size_t l = sizeof(buf);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.stats", buf, &l, NULL, 0)) return;
	char *p = strstr(buf, "BO moves");
	if (p) { char *e = strchr(p, '\n'); if (e) *e = 0; printf("%s: %s\n", what, p); }
	if ((p = strstr(buf, "VRAM end"))) { char *e = strchr(p, '\n'); if (e) *e = 0; printf("%s: %s\n", what, p); }
}
static uint64_t windowFreeMB(void) {
	char buf[4096]; size_t l = sizeof(buf);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.stats", buf, &l, NULL, 0)) return 0;
	char *p = strstr(buf, "free ");
	return p ? strtoull(p + 5, NULL, 10) : 0;
}

static uint32_t vmId, q, so, bbh;
static volatile uint32_t *bb;
// One stored dword per 64 KB of [va, va + size): value ^ offset.
static void gpuPattern(uint64_t va, uint64_t size, uint32_t value) {
	uint32_t k = 0;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size; o += 0x10000) {
		bb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; bb[k++] = (uint32_t)(va + o); bb[k++] = (uint32_t)((va + o) >> 32); bb[k++] = value ^ (uint32_t)o;
	}
	bb[k++] = 0xa << 23; bb[k++] = 0;
	__sync_synchronize();
	struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = so};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s, .address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x), "exec %d", errno);
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&so, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = INT64_MAX};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w), "wait %d", errno);
}
static int checkPattern(volatile uint32_t *p, uint64_t size, uint32_t value) {
	int bad = 0;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size; o += 0x10000)
		if (p[o / 4] != (value ^ (uint32_t)o)) bad++;
	return bad;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	const int evict = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "evict");
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create\n"); return 1; }
	vmId = vc.vm_id;
	bbh = gem(0x10000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);
	bb = map(bbh, 0x10000);
	CHECK(bb && !bind(vmId, bbh, 0x100000, 0x10000), "batch");
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create qc = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vmId, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &qc)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue\n"); return 1; }
	q = qc.exec_queue_id;
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc);
	so = sc.handle;
	stats("before");
	if (!evict) {
		const uint64_t size = 48ull << 20, va = 1ull << 32;
		const uint32_t bo = gem(size, 2, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC);   // VRAM, no NEEDS_VISIBLE: outside the window
		CHECK(!bind(vmId, bo, va, size), "bind %d", errno);
		gpuPattern(va, size, 0xa5a50000);
		volatile uint32_t *p = map(bo, size);   // moves it into the window
		CHECK(p != NULL, "map of a BO outside the window failed");
		if (p) {
			const int bad = checkPattern(p, size, 0xa5a50000);
			CHECK(!bad, "%d of %llu words wrong after the move", bad, size >> 16);
			gpuPattern(va, size, 0x3c3c0000);   // the same VA: its PTEs now point into the window
			const int bad2 = checkPattern(p, size, 0x3c3c0000);
			CHECK(!bad2, "%d of %llu words wrong after a GPU write through the remapped VA", bad2, size >> 16);
		}
	} else {
		const uint64_t each = 64ull << 20;
		uint64_t freeMB = windowFreeMB();
		uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(freeMB / 64) + 1, made = 0, h[64];
		if (n > 60) n = 60;
		printf("window free %llu MB: %u never-mapped visible BOs of 64 MB, then one more\n", freeMB, n);
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
			h[i] = gem(each, 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC);
			CHECK(!bind(vmId, h[i], (2ull << 32) + i * each, each), "bind %u", i);
			gpuPattern((2ull << 32) + i * each, each, 0x77000000u | i);
			made++;
		}
		stats("filled");
		const uint32_t extra = gem(each, 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC);
		volatile uint32_t *pe = map(extra, each);
		CHECK(pe != NULL, "map of the extra BO");
		stats("after the extra BO");
		int bad = 0;
		// map them back (evicted ones return; others may go out meanwhile), leaving room: a CPU-mapped BO never moves, so
		// the window must hold all of them plus the extra one and everything other clients mapped
		const uint32_t back = made > 3 ? made - 3 : made;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < back; i++) {
			volatile uint32_t *p = map(h[i], each);
			if (!p) { bad++; continue; }
			bad += checkPattern(p, each, 0x77000000u | i) != 0;
		}
		CHECK(!bad, "%d BOs lost their contents across eviction and return", bad);
		stats("after mapping them all");
	}
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/direct_lat.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// direct_lat: what a tiny job costs through DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC on a compute queue with DRM_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_LOW_LATENCY_HINT,
// the queue kind the kext's direct submission (debug.intelxe.direct, xe_core.cpp) takes. Run it with direct=0 and 1:
// the same exec path, with the job going to the GuC (SCHED_CONTEXT) or into an armed ring slot (mailbox).
// Per CPU gap between jobs (0, 20 us, 100 us, 1 ms, 5 ms; the kext leaves direct mode after debug.intelxe.direct_idle_us,
// 2 ms by default, so 5 ms measures the way back in):
//   store:  exec ioctl -> the batch's MI_STORE_DATA_IMM visible to a spinning CPU (then the syncobj wait, untimed)
//   signal: exec ioctl -> DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT returning (the waiter sleeps at once, as Metal's does)
// Then two correctness checks: a burst of jobs submitted back to back while the first runs (each needs its own armed
// slot), and a compute job whose in-fence is a render job's, which waits in the FIFO (the kext leaves direct mode
// first). The direct-submission counters of debug.intelxe.stats are printed before and after.
// No Mesa, no Metal plugin. Measurement and checks only.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../../../kernel/IntelXe/uapi -o direct_lat direct_lat.c -framework IOKit
//   ./direct_lat [jobs]
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static int dcmp(const void *a, const void *b) { double x = *(const double *)a, y = *(const double *)b; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }
static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = 1, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static void spin_ns(uint64_t d) { uint64_t t = ns(); while (ns() - t < d) __asm__ volatile("pause"); }
static void flush(volatile void *p, size_t len) {   // the CPU's writes out to memory before the GPU reads them
	for (size_t o = 0; o < len; o += 64) _mm_clflush((const char *)p + o);
	_mm_mfence();
}
static void st(const char *nm, double *v, int n) {
	qsort(v, n, 8, dcmp); double s = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += v[i];
	printf("    %-26s p50 %7.2f  p90 %7.2f  p99 %7.2f  mean %7.2f us\n", nm, v[n / 2], v[n * 9 / 10], v[n * 99 / 100], s / n);
}
static void directStats(const char *when) {   // the "direct submission" line of debug.intelxe.stats
	static char b[8192];
	size_t len = sizeof b;
	int on = -1, idle = -1;
	size_t il = sizeof on;
	sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.direct", &on, &il, NULL, 0);
	il = sizeof idle;
	sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.direct_idle_us", &idle, &il, NULL, 0);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.stats", b, &len, NULL, 0)) { printf("%s: debug.intelxe.stats unreadable\n", when); return; }
	char *l = strstr(b, "direct submission");
	char *e = l ? strchr(l, '\n') : NULL;
	if (e) *e = 0;
	printf("%s: direct=%d idle_us=%d | %s\n", when, on, idle, l ? l : "(no direct submission line: old kext)");
}

#define MI_SDI (0x20u << 23 | 2)   // MI_STORE_DATA_IMM, PPGTT, one dword
#define MI_BBE (0x0au << 23)       // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END
enum { WORK = 0x400000, TARGET = 0x900000 };
enum { WORK_DW = 16, NBATCH = 256, BURST = 64 };

static uint32_t q, rq, so[BURST + 1];
static volatile uint32_t *work, *tg;
// batch k: store v to target dword t, end
static uint64_t batch(int k, uint32_t t, uint32_t v) {
	volatile uint32_t *b = work + (size_t)(k % NBATCH) * WORK_DW;
	b[0] = MI_SDI; b[1] = TARGET + t * 4; b[2] = 0; b[3] = v; b[4] = MI_BBE; b[5] = 0;
	flush(b, 32);
	return WORK + (uint64_t)(k % NBATCH) * WORK_DW * 4;
}
static int exec(uint32_t queue, uint64_t addr, uint32_t signal, uint32_t wait) {
	struct drm_xe_sync s[2] = {{.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = signal},
		{.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .handle = wait}};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = queue, .num_syncs = wait ? 2 : 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)s, .address = addr,
		.num_batch_buffer = 1};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x);
}
static int wait1(uint32_t h) {
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + 2000000000ull)};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
}
static uint32_t newQueue(uint32_t vm, uint16_t cls, uint32_t flags) {
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = cls};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create c = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vm, .flags = flags,
		.instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &c)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue class %u: %d\n", cls, errno); exit(1); }
	return c.exec_queue_id;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	const int N = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 1000;
	if (N < 20) { fprintf(stderr, "jobs >= 20\n"); return 1; }
	const uint64_t gaps[] = {0, 20000, 100000, 1000000, 5000000};
	const int counts[] = {N, N, N, N / 5, N / 10};

	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	const uint64_t workSize = (NBATCH * WORK_DW * 4 + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull;
	uint32_t workBo = gem(workSize), tgBo = gem(0x1000);
	work = map(workBo, workSize);
	tg = map(tgBo, 0x1000);
	if (!work || !tg) { fprintf(stderr, "map\n"); return 1; }
	if (bind(vc.vm_id, workBo, WORK, workSize) || bind(vc.vm_id, tgBo, TARGET, 0x1000)) { fprintf(stderr, "bind %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	q = newQueue(vc.vm_id, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COMPUTE, DRM_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_LOW_LATENCY_HINT);
	rq = newQueue(vc.vm_id, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER, 0);
	for (int i = 0; i <= BURST; i++) {
		struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
		if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) { fprintf(stderr, "syncobj %d\n", errno); return 1; }
		so[i] = sc.handle;
	}
	double *lat = calloc(N, 8);
	directStats("before");
	printf("direct_lat: compute queue with LOW_LATENCY_HINT, %d jobs per gap (1 ms: %d, 5 ms: %d)\n", N, N / 5, N / 10);

	uint32_t seq = 0x1000;
	int k = 0;
	for (int gi = 0; gi < 5; gi++) {
		const int n = counts[gi];
		printf("  gap %5llu us\n", gaps[gi] / 1000);
		for (int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++) {
			for (int i = 0; i < n + 5; i++, k++) {
				seq++;
				const uint64_t a = batch(k, 0, seq);
				spin_ns(gaps[gi]);
				const uint64_t t0 = ns();
				if (exec(q, a, so[0], 0)) { printf("exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
				uint64_t t1;
				if (pass == 0) {
					while (tg[0] != seq && ns() - t0 < 1000000000ull) __asm__ volatile("pause");
					t1 = ns();
					if (wait1(so[0])) { printf("wait failed %d (job %u)\n", errno, seq); return 1; }
				} else {
					if (wait1(so[0])) { printf("wait failed %d (job %u)\n", errno, seq); return 1; }
					t1 = ns();
				}
				if (tg[0] != seq) { printf("store missing: job %u, target 0x%x\n", seq, tg[0]); return 1; }
				if (i >= 5) lat[i - 5] = (t1 - t0) / 1e3;
			}
			st(pass ? "exec -> syncobj signaled" : "exec -> store visible", lat, n);
		}
	}
	directStats("after latency");

	// back to back: BURST jobs, each to its own dword and with its own syncobj, submitted without waiting; repeated
	int bad = 0;
	for (int r = 0; r < 20 && !bad; r++) {
		for (int i = 0; i < BURST; i++) tg[16 + i] = 0;
		flush(tg + 16, BURST * 4);
		for (int i = 0; i < BURST; i++, k++)
			if (exec(q, batch(k, 16 + i, 0xb0000000u | (uint32_t)(r << 8 | i)), so[1 + i], 0)) { printf("burst exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
		for (int i = 0; i < BURST; i++)
			if (wait1(so[1 + i])) { printf("burst %d: job %d wait failed %d\n", r, i, errno); return 1; }
		for (int i = 0; i < BURST; i++)
			if (tg[16 + i] != (0xb0000000u | (uint32_t)(r << 8 | i))) { printf("burst %d: job %d stored 0x%x\n", r, i, tg[16 + i]); bad = 1; }
		spin_ns(r % 2 ? 3000000 : 50000);   // every other burst starts after the idle exit
	}
	printf("  back-to-back bursts of %d: %s\n", BURST, bad ? "FAILED" : "ok");

	// a compute job behind a render job's fence (it waits in the FIFO), between direct jobs
	bad = 0;
	for (int r = 0; r < 50 && !bad; r++) {
		for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++, k++) {   // direct jobs first (arm)
			seq++;
			if (exec(q, batch(k, 0, seq), so[0], 0) || wait1(so[0])) { printf("fifo: compute exec/wait failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
		}
		tg[1] = tg[2] = 0;
		flush(tg, 64);
		const uint32_t rv = 0xc0000000u | (uint32_t)r, cv = 0xd0000000u | (uint32_t)r;
		if (exec(rq, batch(k++, 1, rv), so[1], 0)) { printf("fifo: render exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
		if (exec(q, batch(k++, 2, cv), so[2], so[1])) { printf("fifo: compute exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
		if (wait1(so[2])) { printf("fifo %d: compute wait failed %d\n", r, errno); return 1; }
		if (tg[1] != rv || tg[2] != cv) { printf("fifo %d: render 0x%x compute 0x%x\n", r, tg[1], tg[2]); bad = 1; }
	}
	printf("  compute job behind a render fence: %s\n", bad ? "FAILED" : "ok");
	directStats("after checks");

	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d = {.exec_queue_id = q};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d);
	d.exec_queue_id = rq;
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d);
	return 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// dmode: list the main display's modes, or switch to WxH (IntelXeFB scaled-mode test, run in the console session).
//   clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O1 -o dmode dmode.c -framework CoreGraphics -framework CoreFoundation
//   ./dmode            list
//   ./dmode 1920 1080  switch (first 1:1 mode of that size), permanently (CGDisplaySetDisplayMode alone reverts when
//                      the process exits, so a switch from a shell did nothing)
//   ./dmode 2560 1440 179.88  the same, at that refresh rate (HiDPI and 1:1 variants of a size share IO mode ids)
#include <CoreGraphics/CoreGraphics.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	CGDirectDisplayID d = CGMainDisplayID();
	CFStringRef k = kCGDisplayShowDuplicateLowResolutionModes;
	CFDictionaryRef opt = CFDictionaryCreate(NULL, (const void **)&k, (const void **)&kCFBooleanTrue, 1,
	                                         &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	CFArrayRef modes = CGDisplayCopyAllDisplayModes(d, opt);
	CGDisplayModeRef cur = CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode(d);
	if (!modes || !cur) { fprintf(stderr, "no display modes (not in the console session?)\n"); return 1; }
	printf("display 0x%x current %zux%zu (pixels %zux%zu) %.2f Hz\n", d, CGDisplayModeGetWidth(cur), CGDisplayModeGetHeight(cur),
	       CGDisplayModeGetPixelWidth(cur), CGDisplayModeGetPixelHeight(cur), CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate(cur));
	size_t want_w = argc > 2 ? (size_t)atoi(argv[1]) : 0, want_h = argc > 2 ? (size_t)atoi(argv[2]) : 0;
	for (CFIndex i = 0; i < CFArrayGetCount(modes); i++) {
		CGDisplayModeRef m = (CGDisplayModeRef)CFArrayGetValueAtIndex(modes, i);
		size_t w = CGDisplayModeGetWidth(m), h = CGDisplayModeGetHeight(m);
		if (!want_w)
			printf("  %zux%zu pixels %zux%zu %.2f Hz io %d%s\n", w, h, CGDisplayModeGetPixelWidth(m), CGDisplayModeGetPixelHeight(m),
			       CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate(m), CGDisplayModeGetIODisplayModeID(m), CGDisplayModeIsUsableForDesktopGUI(m) ? "" : " (not for GUI)");
		else if (w == want_w && h == want_h && CGDisplayModeGetPixelWidth(m) == w && (argc < 4 || fabs(CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate(m) - atof(argv[3])) < 0.5)) {
			CGDisplayConfigRef cfg; CGError e = CGBeginDisplayConfiguration(&cfg);
			if (!e) e = CGConfigureDisplayWithDisplayMode(cfg, d, m, NULL);
			if (!e) e = CGCompleteDisplayConfiguration(cfg, kCGConfigurePermanently);
			printf("set %zux%zu (io %d): %d\n", w, h, CGDisplayModeGetIODisplayModeID(m), e);
			return e != kCGErrorSuccess;
		}
	}
	if (want_w) { printf("no %zux%zu mode\n", want_w, want_h); return 1; }
	return 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// fbcrop: a 256x128 full-resolution window of the panel's live scan-out surface (IntelXeFB debug.intelxefb_crop) as a PPM.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -o fbcrop fbcrop.c
//   sudo ./fbcrop X Y out.ppm
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	if (argc < 4) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: fbcrop X Y out.ppm\n"); return 2; }
	uint32_t xy = (uint32_t)atoi(argv[1]) << 16 | ((uint32_t)atoi(argv[2]) & 0xFFFF);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxefb_cropxy", NULL, NULL, &xy, sizeof(xy))) { perror("cropxy"); return 1; }
	static uint32_t px[256 * 128];
	size_t len = sizeof(px);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxefb_crop", px, &len, NULL, 0) || len != sizeof(px)) { perror("crop"); return 1; }
	FILE *f = fopen(argv[3], "wb");
	if (!f) { perror("out"); return 1; }
	fprintf(f, "P6\n256 128\n255\n");
	for (int i = 0; i < 256 * 128; i++) { uint8_t rgb[3] = {(uint8_t)(px[i] >> 16), (uint8_t)(px[i] >> 8), (uint8_t)px[i]}; fwrite(rgb, 1, 3, f); }
	fclose(f);
	return 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// kxtest: drives IntelXe.kext's xe interface the way Mesa's ANV does, without Mesa. Build on the build Mac:
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -I../uapi -o kxtest kxtest.c -framework IOKit -framework CoreFoundation
// Run on the hackintosh (no developer tools needed): ./kxtest
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;

static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	kern_return_t kr = IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n);
	if (kr) {
		fprintf(stderr, "IOConnectCallScalarMethod 0x%x\n", kr);
		return -1;
	}
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}

#define CHECK(x) do { if ((x) != 0) { fprintf(stderr, "FAIL %s: errno %d\n", #x, errno); return 1; } } while (0)

static void *query(uint32_t kind, uint32_t *size) {
	struct drm_xe_device_query q = {.query = kind};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q)) return NULL;
	void *buf = calloc(1, q.size);
	q.data = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)buf;
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q)) return NULL;
	*size = q.size;
	return buf;
}

static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags, uint16_t caching) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .flags = flags, .cpu_caching = caching};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) {
		fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE failed: %d\n", errno);
		exit(1);
	}
	return g.handle;
}

static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0;
	mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}

static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range, uint16_t pat) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo;
	b.bind.range = range;
	b.bind.addr = addr;
	b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP;
	b.bind.pat_index = pat;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}

static uint64_t absNs(uint64_t fromNow) {
	mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom + fromNow;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) {
		fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n");
		return 1;
	}
	char name[16] = {0};
	struct drm_version v = {.name = name, .name_len = sizeof(name) - 1};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_VERSION, &v));
	printf("driver \"%s\" %d.%d\n", name, v.version_major, v.version_minor);

	uint32_t sz;
	struct drm_xe_query_config *cfg = query(DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_CONFIG, &sz);
	struct drm_xe_query_engines *eng = query(DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_ENGINES, &sz);
	struct drm_xe_query_mem_regions *mem = query(DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_MEM_REGIONS, &sz);
	struct drm_xe_query_gt_list *gts = query(DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_GT_LIST, &sz);
	uint32_t hwsz, topsz;
	void *hw = query(DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_HWCONFIG, &hwsz);
	uint8_t *top = query(DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_GT_TOPOLOGY, &topsz);
	if (!cfg || !eng || !mem || !gts || !hw || !top) {
		fprintf(stderr, "query failed\n");
		return 1;
	}
	printf("config: devid 0x%llx flags 0x%llx align %llu va_bits %llu\n", cfg->info[0], cfg->info[1], cfg->info[2], cfg->info[3]);
	printf("engines: %u (class %u inst %u)\n", eng->num_engines, eng->engines[0].instance.engine_class,
		eng->engines[0].instance.engine_instance);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < eng->num_engines; i++)
		printf("  engine %u: class %u inst %u gt %u\n", i, eng->engines[i].instance.engine_class,
			eng->engines[i].instance.engine_instance, eng->engines[i].instance.gt_id);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < gts->num_gt; i++)
		printf("  gt %u: type %u ip %u.%u\n", gts->gt_list[i].gt_id, gts->gt_list[i].type, gts->gt_list[i].ip_ver_major,
			gts->gt_list[i].ip_ver_minor);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < mem->num_mem_regions; i++)
		printf("mem %u: class %u inst %u total %llu MB visible %llu MB\n", i, mem->mem_regions[i].mem_class,
			mem->mem_regions[i].instance, mem->mem_regions[i].total_size >> 20, mem->mem_regions[i].cpu_visible_size >> 20);
	printf("gt0: refclk %u Hz, IP %u.%u; hwconfig %u bytes; topology %u bytes\n", gts->gt_list[0].reference_clock,
		gts->gt_list[0].ip_ver_major, gts->gt_list[0].ip_ver_minor, hwsz, topsz);

	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc));

	if (argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "load")) {
		// GPU load for frequency tests: a 4 MB batch of 65535 MI_STORE_DATA_IMM, submitted N times on the render queue.
		uint32_t lb = gem(0x400000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB), lt = gem(0x1000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);
		uint32_t *lbb = map(lb, 0x400000);
		CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, lb, 0x1000000, 0x400000, 2));
		CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, lt, 0x2000000, 0x1000, 2));
		uint32_t k = 0;
		uint32_t stores = argc > 3 ? (uint32_t)atoi(argv[3]) : 65535;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < stores; i++) {
			lbb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2;
			lbb[k++] = 0x2000000 + (i & 1023) * 4;
			lbb[k++] = 0;
			lbb[k++] = i;
		}
		lbb[k++] = 0xa << 23;
		lbb[k++] = 0;
		__sync_synchronize();
		struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER};
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create lq = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
		CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &lq));
		struct drm_syncobj_create ls = {0};
		CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &ls));
		uint32_t lh[1] = {ls.handle};
		int rounds = argc > 2 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 300;
		uint64_t t0 = absNs(0);
		for (int r = 0; r < rounds; r++) {
			struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = ls.handle};
			struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = lq.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s,
				.address = 0x1000000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
			CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x));
			struct drm_syncobj_wait lw = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)lh, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)absNs(5000000000ull)};
			CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &lw));
		}
		uint64_t t1 = absNs(0);
		printf("load: %d batches of %u stores in %llu ms (%.1f us per batch)\n", rounds, stores, (t1 - t0) / 1000000,
			(double)(t1 - t0) / 1000.0 / rounds);
		return 0;
	}
	uint32_t batch = gem(0x10000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);
	uint32_t target = gem(0x1000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);
	uint32_t vbo = gem(0x10000, 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC);
	uint32_t *bb = map(batch, 0x10000), *tg = map(target, 0x1000), *vr = map(vbo, 0x10000);
	if (!bb || !tg || !vr) {
		fprintf(stderr, "map failed\n");
		return 1;
	}
	CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, batch, 0x100000, 0x10000, 2));
	CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, target, 0x200000, 0x1000, 2));
	CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, vbo, 0x300000, 0x10000, 3));

	tg[0] = 0;
	vr[0] = 0;
	uint32_t n = 0;
	bb[n++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2;   // MI_STORE_DATA_IMM, 1 dword, PPGTT
	bb[n++] = 0x200000;
	bb[n++] = 0;
	bb[n++] = 0xa11ce001;
	bb[n++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2;
	bb[n++] = 0x300000;
	bb[n++] = 0;
	bb[n++] = 0xa11ce002;
	bb[n++] = 0xa << 23;         // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END
	bb[n++] = 0;
	__sync_synchronize();

	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance eci = {.engine_class = DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create qc = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id,
		.instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&eci};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &qc));
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0}, tl = {0};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc));
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &tl));

	struct drm_xe_sync syncs[2] = {
		{.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle},
		{.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_TIMELINE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = tl.handle, .timeline_value = 5},
	};
	struct drm_xe_exec ex = {.exec_queue_id = qc.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 2, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)syncs,
		.address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	uint64_t t0 = absNs(0);
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &ex));
	uint32_t handles[1] = {sc.handle};
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)handles, .count_handles = 1,
		.timeout_nsec = (int64_t)absNs(2000000000ull)};
	int werr = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
	uint64_t t1 = absNs(0);
	uint64_t point = 5;
	uint32_t th[1] = {tl.handle};
	struct drm_syncobj_timeline_wait tw = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)th, .points = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&point,
		.count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)absNs(2000000000ull)};
	int twerr = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE_WAIT, &tw);
	uint64_t qv = 0;
	struct drm_syncobj_timeline_array qa = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)th, .points = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&qv, .count_handles = 1};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_QUERY, &qa));
	printf("exec: binary wait %s in %llu us, timeline wait %s, timeline value %llu\n", werr ? "FAILED" : "ok",
		(t1 - t0) / 1000, twerr ? "FAILED" : "ok", qv);
	printf("system BO 0x%08x, VRAM BO 0x%08x -> %s\n", tg[0], vr[0],
		tg[0] == 0xa11ce001 && vr[0] == 0xa11ce002 ? "MESA-STYLE SUBMISSION WORKS" : "unexpected");

	// a second round on the same queue, timeline point 6
	tg[0] = 0;
	bb[3] = 0xa11ce003;
	__sync_synchronize();
	syncs[1].timeline_value = 6;
	ex.num_syncs = 2;
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &ex));
	point = 6;
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE_WAIT, &tw));
	printf("second exec: system BO 0x%08x\n", tg[0]);

	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy qd = {.exec_queue_id = qc.exec_queue_id};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &qd));

	// every engine the kext reports: its own queue, a store of a per-engine tag, a binary syncobj wait
	for (uint32_t e = 0; e < eng->num_engines; e++) {
		struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = eng->engines[e].instance;
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create c2 = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id,
			.instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
		if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &c2)) {
			printf("engine class %u inst %u: queue create failed (%d)\n", ei.engine_class, ei.engine_instance, errno);
			continue;
		}
		for (uint32_t round = 0; round < 3; round++) {   // three jobs on the same queue (later ones: SCHED_CONTEXT)
		uint32_t tag = 0xe0000000u | round << 16 | ei.engine_class << 8 | ei.engine_instance;
		tg[0] = 0;
		bb[3] = tag;
		__sync_synchronize();
		struct drm_xe_sync s1 = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
		struct drm_xe_exec x2 = {.exec_queue_id = c2.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s1,
			.address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
		uint64_t a = absNs(0);
		int xerr = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x2);
		w.timeout_nsec = (int64_t)absNs(2000000000ull);
		int werr2 = xerr ? -1 : xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
		printf("engine class %u inst %u job %u: exec %s, wait %s in %llu us, target 0x%08x %s\n", ei.engine_class,
			ei.engine_instance, round, xerr ? "FAILED" : "ok", werr2 ? "FAILED" : "ok", (absNs(0) - a) / 1000, tg[0],
			tg[0] == tag ? "OK" : "WRONG");
		}
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d2 = {.exec_queue_id = c2.exec_queue_id};
		xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d2);
	}
	// Mesa's layout: batch in CPU-visible VRAM written through the WC mapping, target in system memory bound with
	// PAT 1 (Mesa's cached-coherent index), and the same target again with PAT 0.
	{
		uint32_t vb = gem(0x10000, 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC);
		uint32_t t1 = gem(0x1000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB), t0 = gem(0x1000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);
		uint32_t *vbb = map(vb, 0x10000), *m1 = map(t1, 0x1000), *m0 = map(t0, 0x1000);
		CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, vb, 0x400000, 0x10000, 0));
		CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, t1, 0x500000, 0x1000, 1));
		CHECK(bind(vc.vm_id, t0, 0x600000, 0x1000, 0));
		uint32_t k = 0;
		vbb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; vbb[k++] = 0x500000; vbb[k++] = 0; vbb[k++] = 0xb0000001;
		vbb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; vbb[k++] = 0x600000; vbb[k++] = 0; vbb[k++] = 0xb0000000;
		vbb[k++] = 0xa << 23; vbb[k++] = 0;
		__sync_synchronize();
		for (uint32_t e = 0; e < eng->num_engines; e += 1) {
			struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = eng->engines[e].instance;
			struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create c3 = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id,
				.instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
			if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &c3)) continue;
			m1[0] = m0[0] = 0;
			struct drm_xe_sync s3 = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
			struct drm_xe_exec x3 = {.exec_queue_id = c3.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s3,
				.address = 0x400000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
			int e3 = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x3);
			w.timeout_nsec = (int64_t)absNs(2000000000ull);
			int w3 = e3 ? -1 : xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
			printf("VRAM batch on class %u inst %u: exec %s wait %s, PAT1 target 0x%08x, PAT0 target 0x%08x\n",
				ei.engine_class, ei.engine_instance, e3 ? "FAIL" : "ok", w3 ? "FAIL" : "ok", m1[0], m0[0]);
			struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d3 = {.exec_queue_id = c3.exec_queue_id};
			xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d3);
		}
	}

	struct drm_xe_vm_destroy vd = {.vm_id = vc.vm_id};
	CHECK(xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_DESTROY, &vd));
	IOServiceClose(conn);
	printf("done\n");
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/latewake.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// latewake: are completion wakeups late, per engine class, independent of when the GPU ran the job? Each job is the rtt
// batch (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM of a sequence number into system memory + MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END). A spinner thread timestamps
// the moment the store becomes visible; the main thread sleeps in SYNCOBJ_WAIT. A wait that returns more than 1 ms after
// the store was visible was not woken by the job's interrupt (the kernel's 2 ms fallback slice caught it). Also prints
// the kernel's rescue counter before and after (debug.intelxe.stats, global: other clients count too).
// Measurement only.   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o latewake latewake.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = 1, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static unsigned rescues(void) {
	char buf[2048]; size_t l = sizeof(buf);
	if (sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.stats", buf, &l, NULL, 0)) return 0;
	const char *p = strstr(buf, "(missed interrupt) ");
	return p ? (unsigned)strtoul(p + 19, NULL, 10) : 0;
}

static volatile uint32_t *tg;
static volatile uint32_t want, stop;
static volatile uint64_t seenAt, releaseAt;
// Releases the batch's MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT (dword 16 of the target) at releaseAt, then timestamps the store.
static void *spinner(void *a) {
	while (!stop) {
		const uint32_t w = want;
		if (w && releaseAt && ns() >= releaseAt && tg[16] != w) { tg[16] = w; __sync_synchronize(); }
		if (w && tg[0] == w && !seenAt) seenAt = ns();
		__asm__ volatile("pause");
	}
	return a;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	const int N = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 400;
	const uint64_t gap = (argc > 2 ? strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 0) : 200) * 1000;
	// hold: the batch first waits (MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT, polling) until the CPU releases it this many us after the exec
	const uint64_t hold = (argc > 3 ? strtoull(argv[3], NULL, 0) : 0) * 1000;
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create\n"); return 1; }
	uint32_t batch = gem(0x10000), target = gem(0x1000);
	volatile uint32_t *bb = map(batch, 0x10000);
	tg = map(target, 0x1000);
	if (!bb || !tg || bind(vc.vm_id, batch, 0x100000, 0x10000) || bind(vc.vm_id, target, 0x200000, 0x1000)) { fprintf(stderr, "setup\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc);
	uint32_t h[1] = {sc.handle};
	pthread_t th;
	pthread_create(&th, NULL, spinner, NULL);
	const char *names[] = {"render", "copy", "", "", "compute"};
	const uint16_t classes[] = {DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COMPUTE, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY};
	for (int ci = 0; ci < 3; ci++) {
		struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = classes[ci]};
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create q = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
		if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &q)) { printf("%s: no queue (%d)\n", names[classes[ci]], errno); continue; }
		const unsigned r0 = rescues();
		int late = 0, gpuLate = 0, unseen = 0;
		double worst = 0, sumLate = 0;
		for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
			const uint32_t seq = 0x20000000u | ci << 24 | (i & 0xffffff);
			uint32_t k = 0;
			if (hold) {   // MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT | POLL | SAD_EQ_SDD, PPGTT, 5 dwords
				bb[k++] = 0x1c << 23 | 1u << 15 | 4u << 12 | 3; bb[k++] = seq; bb[k++] = 0x200040; bb[k++] = 0; bb[k++] = 0;
			}
			bb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; bb[k++] = 0x200000; bb[k++] = 0; bb[k++] = seq; bb[k++] = 0xa << 23; bb[k++] = 0;
			__sync_synchronize();
			releaseAt = 0;
			const uint64_t g0 = ns();
			while (ns() - g0 < gap) __asm__ volatile("pause");
			seenAt = 0;
			want = seq;
			struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
			struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s,
				.address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
			const uint64_t t0 = ns();
			if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x)) { printf("exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
			if (hold) releaseAt = t0 + hold;
			struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + 2000000000ull)};
			if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w)) { printf("wait failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
			const uint64_t t3 = ns();
			want = 0;
			const uint64_t seen = seenAt;
			if (!seen) { unseen++; continue; }   // the spinner was descheduled: no visibility time
			const double after = seen < t3 ? (t3 - seen) / 1e3 : 0;
			if (seen - t0 > hold + 1000000) gpuLate++;
			if (after > 1000) { late++; sumLate += after; }
			if (after > worst) worst = after;
		}
		const unsigned r1 = rescues();
		printf("%-7s n %d gap %llu us hold %llu us: wait returned >1 ms after the store was visible: %d (mean %.0f us), worst %.0f us; "
			"store visible >1 ms after the release: %d; spinner missed %d; kernel rescues meanwhile %u (all clients)\n",
			names[classes[ci]], N, gap / 1000, hold / 1000, late, late ? sumLate / late : 0, worst, gpuLate, unseen, r1 - r0);
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id};
		xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d);
	}
	stop = 1;
	pthread_join(th, NULL);
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/memq.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// memq: B580 VRAM usage as the xe memory-region query reports it (total, used, CPU-visible window, its use).
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -I../uapi -o memq memq.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;

static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}

int main(void) {
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_xe_device_query q = {.query = DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_MEM_REGIONS};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q)) return 1;
	struct drm_xe_query_mem_regions *m = calloc(1, q.size);
	q.data = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)m;
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q)) return 1;
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < m->num_mem_regions; i++) {
		struct drm_xe_mem_region *r = &m->mem_regions[i];
		printf("%s: total %llu MB, used %llu MB, cpu-visible %llu MB, visible used %llu MB\n",
		       r->mem_class == DRM_XE_MEM_REGION_CLASS_VRAM ? "VRAM" : "SYSMEM",
		       r->total_size >> 20, r->used >> 20, r->cpu_visible_size >> 20, r->cpu_visible_used >> 20);
	}
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/rtt.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// rtt: job round trip through IntelXe.kext alone (no Mesa, no Metal plugin): a 2-dword batch (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM of a
// sequence number into system memory + MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END) per exec, on each engine class, timed in three pieces:
//   exec ioctl duration | exec return -> the GPU's store is visible to a spinning CPU | store visible -> SYNCOBJ_WAIT returns
// Modes: "wait" = SYNCOBJ_WAIT right after exec (interrupt path, what ANV does); "poll" = spin on the store first, then
// SYNCOBJ_WAIT (so the third piece is pure completion-notification latency). Gap = CPU spin between jobs.
// Measurement only.   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o rtt rtt.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static int dcmp(const void *a, const void *b) { double x = *(const double *)a, y = *(const double *)b; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }
static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags, uint16_t caching) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .flags = flags, .cpu_caching = caching};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range, uint16_t pat) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = pat;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static void spin_ns(uint64_t d) { uint64_t t = ns(); while (ns() - t < d) __asm__ volatile("pause"); }
static void st(const char *nm, double *v, int n) {
	qsort(v, n, 8, dcmp); double s = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += v[i];
	printf("    %-26s p50 %7.1f  p90 %7.1f  p99 %7.1f  mean %7.1f us\n", nm, v[n / 2], v[n * 9 / 10], v[n * 99 / 100], s / n);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	int N = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 500;
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create\n"); return 1; }
	uint32_t batch = gem(0x10000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB), target = gem(0x1000, 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB);
	volatile uint32_t *bb = map(batch, 0x10000), *tg = map(target, 0x1000);
	if (!bb || !tg) { fprintf(stderr, "map\n"); return 1; }
	if (bind(vc.vm_id, batch, 0x100000, 0x10000, 2) || bind(vc.vm_id, target, 0x200000, 0x1000, 2)) { fprintf(stderr, "bind\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc);
	uint32_t h[1] = {sc.handle};
	const char *cls[] = {"render", "copy", "", "", "compute"};
	uint16_t classes[] = {DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COMPUTE, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY};
	uint64_t gaps[] = {0, 20000, 100000, 1000000};
	double *ex = calloc(N, 8), *vis = calloc(N, 8), *wk = calloc(N, 8), *tot = calloc(N, 8);
	for (int ci = 0; ci < 3; ci++) {
		struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = classes[ci]};
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create q = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
		if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &q)) { printf("%s: no queue (%d)\n", cls[classes[ci]], errno); continue; }
		for (int mode = 0; mode < 2; mode++) for (int gi = 0; gi < 4; gi++) {
			int n = gi == 3 ? N / 5 : N; if (n < 20) n = 20;
			for (int i = 0; i < n + 5; i++) {
				uint32_t seq = 0x10000000u | ci << 24 | mode << 20 | gi << 16 | (i & 0xffff);
				bb[0] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; bb[1] = 0x200000; bb[2] = 0; bb[3] = seq; bb[4] = 0xa << 23; bb[5] = 0;
				__sync_synchronize();
				spin_ns(gaps[gi]);
				struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
				struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s,
					.address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
				uint64_t t0 = ns();
				if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x)) { printf("exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
				uint64_t t1 = ns(), t2 = t1;
				if (mode == 1) { while (tg[0] != seq && ns() - t1 < 1000000000ull) __asm__ volatile("pause"); t2 = ns(); }
				struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + 2000000000ull)};
				if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w)) { printf("wait failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
				uint64_t t3 = ns();
				if (tg[0] != seq) printf("store missing\n");
				if (i >= 5) { ex[i - 5] = (t1 - t0) / 1e3; vis[i - 5] = (t2 - t1) / 1e3; wk[i - 5] = (t3 - t2) / 1e3; tot[i - 5] = (t3 - t0) / 1e3; }
			}
			printf("  %-7s %s gap %5llu us (n %d)\n", cls[classes[ci]], mode ? "poll+wait" : "wait     ", gaps[gi] / 1000, n);
			st("exec ioctl", ex, n);
			if (mode) { st("exec ret -> store visible", vis, n); st("visible -> wait returns", wk, n); }
			else st("exec ret -> wait returns", wk, n);
			st("total", tot, n);
		}
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id};
		xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d);
	}
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/surffence.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// surffence: end-to-end test of the surface fence ioctls (uapi/intelxe_drm.h) and the job watchdog on IntelXe.kext.
//   ./surffence            GPU-side implicit sync: a render-queue writer (held by MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT until the CPU releases
//                          it) attaches a WRITE fence to surface 777; a copy-queue reader imports it (READER) into its own
//                          timeline and passes that point as an exec in-fence; its MI_COPY_MEM_MEM must copy the value the
//                          writer stored, and it must not complete before the writer is released. Also SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT
//                          (ETIME while held, 0 after), the dma-resv replacement rule and the error codes.
//   ./surffence watchdog   a writer that is never released: with debug.intelxe.job_timeout_ms (set it low, e.g. 2000,
//                          first) its queue is banned, its surface fence completes, the importer's exec runs, and the
//                          writer's next exec fails with ECANCELED.
// Measurement/test only.   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o surffence surffence.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"
#include "intelxe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = 1, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static uint32_t queue(uint32_t vm, uint16_t cls) {
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = cls};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create q = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vm, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &q)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue %u: %d\n", cls, errno); exit(1); }
	return q.exec_queue_id;
}
static uint32_t syncobj(void) {
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) { fprintf(stderr, "syncobj %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return sc.handle;
}
static int exec(uint32_t q, uint64_t batch, struct drm_xe_sync *s, uint32_t ns_) {
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q, .num_syncs = ns_, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)s, .address = batch, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x);
}
static int waitBin(uint32_t h, uint64_t timeoutNs) {
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + timeoutNs)};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w) ? errno : 0;
}
static int attach(uint32_t surf, uint32_t so, uint64_t point, uint32_t flags) {
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_fence_attach a = {.surface_id = surf, .syncobj = so, .point = point, .flags = flags};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_ATTACH, &a) ? errno : 0;
}
static int surfWait(uint32_t surf, uint32_t flags, uint64_t timeoutNs) {
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_fence_wait w = {.surface_id = surf, .flags = flags, .timeout_ns = (int64_t)(ns() + timeoutNs)};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT, &w) ? errno : 0;
}

// target page dwords: 0 written by the writer, 2 copied by the reader, 16 the writer's semaphore
enum { kBatchW = 0x100000, kBatchR = 0x110000, kTarget = 0x200000 };

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	const int watchdog = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "watchdog");
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_get_cap cap = {.capability = INTELXE_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap) && cap.value == 1, "INTELXE_CAP_SURFACE_FENCES = %llu", (unsigned long long)cap.value);
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create\n"); return 1; }
	uint32_t bw = gem(0x10000), br = gem(0x10000), tgh = gem(0x1000);
	volatile uint32_t *pw = map(bw, 0x10000), *pr = map(br, 0x10000), *tg = map(tgh, 0x1000);
	if (!pw || !pr || !tg || bind(vc.vm_id, bw, kBatchW, 0x10000) || bind(vc.vm_id, br, kBatchR, 0x10000) || bind(vc.vm_id, tgh, kTarget, 0x1000)) {
		fprintf(stderr, "setup\n");
		return 1;
	}
	const uint32_t qw = queue(vc.vm_id, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER), qr = queue(vc.vm_id, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY);
	const uint32_t sw = syncobj(), sr = syncobj(), tl = syncobj();
	const uint32_t X = 0x5eed0000u | (uint32_t)(ns() & 0xffff), surf = 777;
	tg[0] = 0; tg[2] = 0; tg[16] = 0;
	// writer: MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT (poll, == X) on dword 16, MI_STORE_DATA_IMM X -> dword 0
	uint32_t k = 0;
	pw[k++] = 0x1c << 23 | 1u << 15 | 4u << 12 | 3; pw[k++] = X; pw[k++] = kTarget + 64; pw[k++] = 0; pw[k++] = 0;
	pw[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2; pw[k++] = kTarget; pw[k++] = 0; pw[k++] = X;
	pw[k++] = 0xa << 23; pw[k++] = 0;
	// reader: MI_COPY_MEM_MEM dword 0 -> dword 2
	k = 0;
	pr[k++] = 0x2e << 23 | 3; pr[k++] = kTarget + 8; pr[k++] = 0; pr[k++] = kTarget; pr[k++] = 0;
	pr[k++] = 0xa << 23;
	__sync_synchronize();

	// error codes
	CHECK(attach(surf, sw, 0, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE) == EAGAIN, "attach before any submit: EAGAIN");
	CHECK(attach(0, sw, 0, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE) == EINVAL, "surface 0: EINVAL");
	CHECK(attach(surf, sw, 0, 3) == EINVAL, "flags 3: EINVAL");
	CHECK(attach(surf, 9999, 0, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE) == ENOENT, "bad syncobj: ENOENT");

	struct drm_xe_sync s1 = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sw};
	CHECK(!exec(qw, kBatchW, &s1, 1), "writer exec %d", errno);
	CHECK(!attach(surf, sw, 0, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE), "attach WRITE %d", errno);
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_fence_import im = {.surface_id = surf, .syncobj = tl, .flags = INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_READER};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_IMPORT, &im) && im.count_out == 1 && im.point_out == 1,
		"import: count %u point %llu (errno %d)", im.count_out, (unsigned long long)im.point_out, errno);
	struct drm_xe_sync s2[2] = {
		{.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_TIMELINE_SYNCOBJ, .handle = tl, .timeline_value = im.point_out},
		{.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sr}};
	const uint64_t t0 = ns();
	CHECK(!exec(qr, kBatchR, s2, 2), "reader exec %d", errno);
	CHECK(waitBin(sr, 20000000) == ETIME, "reader completed while the writer is held");
	CHECK(tg[2] == 0, "reader copied 0x%x early", tg[2]);
	CHECK(surfWait(surf, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_READER, 5000000) == ETIME, "SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT while held: ETIME");
	if (!watchdog) {
		tg[16] = X;
		__sync_synchronize();
		CHECK(!waitBin(sr, 2000000000ull), "reader wait %d", errno);
		CHECK(tg[2] == X, "reader copied 0x%x, writer stored 0x%x", tg[2], tg[0]);
		CHECK(!surfWait(surf, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITER, 1000000000ull), "SURFACE_FENCE_WAIT after release");
		printf("ordered: reader completed %.1f ms after its exec (writer released at ~20 ms)\n", (ns() - t0) / 1e6);
		// dma-resv rule: a READ from the reader's queue, then a WRITE from it supersedes the read
		CHECK(!attach(surf, sr, 0, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_READ), "attach READ (signaled: no-op) %d", errno);
		struct drm_intelxe_surface_fence_import im2 = {.surface_id = surf, .syncobj = tl, .flags = INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITER};
		CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_IMPORT, &im2) && im2.count_out == 0 && im2.point_out == 0,
			"import after everything signaled: count %u point %llu", im2.count_out, (unsigned long long)im2.point_out);
	} else {
		printf("watchdog: the writer is never released; waiting up to 30 s for its queue to be banned\n");
		const int r = waitBin(sr, 30000000000ull);
		CHECK(!r, "reader never ran (%d)", r);
		printf("reader completed %.1f s after its exec (copied 0x%x: the banned writer stored nothing)\n", (ns() - t0) / 1e9, tg[2]);
		CHECK(!surfWait(surf, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITER, 1000000000ull), "surface fence of the banned queue completes");
		struct drm_xe_exec_queue_get_property gp = {.exec_queue_id = qw, .property = DRM_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_GET_PROPERTY_BAN};
		CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_GET_PROPERTY, &gp) && gp.value == 1, "writer queue banned: %llu", (unsigned long long)gp.value);
		CHECK(exec(qw, kBatchW, NULL, 0) && errno == ECANCELED, "exec on the banned queue: %d", errno);
		tg[16] = X;   // let the context finish if the GuC ever runs it again
	}
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/surfvram.c
