// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// surfvram: end-to-end test of VRAM-shared IOSurfaces (gpuperf phase 1: IntelXe.kext SURFACE_VRAM / SURFACE_DIRTY and
// NMXAccel's family page-off). Needs debug.intelxe.surfvram >= 1 (sudo sysctl -w debug.intelxe.surfvram=1); reads
// debug.intelxe.surfvram_stats. Only when no game/benchmark runs. Each step prints PASS/FAIL:
//   1. a global 2560x1440 BGRA IOSurface; SURFACE_VRAM CREATE -> a handle to its VRAM backing; a second lookup without
//      CREATE -> the same backing (same size, same generation)
//   2. the copy engine writes pattern A into the backing (MEM_COPY from a system BO); WRITE fence attached; SURFACE_DIRTY
//   3. a CPU IOSurfaceLock (read-only) must show pattern A in the surface's pages: the family pages it off (timed)
//   4. another process (posix_spawn of this binary) looks the surface up, imports the same backing without CREATE, copies
//      it back with its own GPU job and finds pattern A; then writes pattern B into it, attaches its fence, marks it dirty
//      and exits (its handle and client go with it)
//   5. back here: a CPU lock shows pattern B (the other process's write, paged off after it exited)
//   6. errors: import of a surface without a backing ENOENT, plane 1 EINVAL, a backing over the budget ENOSPC
//   7. the surface released: its backing leaves the registry (debug.intelxe.surfvram_stats backings back to the start count)
// clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o surfvram surfvram.c -framework IOKit -framework IOSurface -framework CoreFoundation
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <IOSurface/IOSurface.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <spawn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"
#include "intelxe_drm.h"

extern char **environ;
static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) { errno = ENXIO; return -1; }
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } \
	else { printf("PASS "); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } } while (0)

enum { W = 2560, H = 1440, ROW = W * 4 };
static const uint64_t kBytes = (uint64_t)ROW * H;   // 14745600 (3600 pages)
enum { kBatch = 0x100000, kSys = 0x10000000, kSurf = 0x40000000 };

static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range, uint16_t pat) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = pat;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static uint32_t queue(uint32_t vm, uint16_t cls) {
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = cls};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create q = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vm, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &q)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue %u: %d\n", cls, errno); exit(1); }
	return q.exec_queue_id;
}
static uint32_t syncobj(void) {
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) { fprintf(stderr, "syncobj %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return sc.handle;
}
static int waitBin(uint32_t h, uint64_t timeoutNs) {
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + timeoutNs)};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w) ? errno : 0;
}
static int surfVram(uint32_t sid, uint32_t plane, uint64_t size, uint32_t flags, struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram *out) {
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v = {.surface_id = sid, .plane = plane, .size = size, .flags = flags};
	const int r = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM, &v) ? errno : 0;
	if (out) *out = v;
	return r;
}
static int surfDirty(uint32_t sid) {
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_dirty d = {.surface_id = sid};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_DIRTY, &d) ? errno : 0;
}
static int attach(uint32_t surf, uint32_t so, uint32_t flags) {
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_fence_attach a = {.surface_id = surf, .syncobj = so, .flags = flags};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_ATTACH, &a) ? errno : 0;
}
static void pattern(uint32_t *p, uint32_t seed) { for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kBytes / 4; i++) p[i] = (i * 2654435761u) ^ seed; }
static long mismatches(const uint32_t *p, uint32_t seed) {
	long bad = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < kBytes / 4; i++) if (p[i] != ((i * 2654435761u) ^ seed)) bad++;
	return bad;
}

// The GPU side of one process: a VM with a system BO (CPU-mapped) and the surface's backing, a copy queue.
static struct { uint32_t vm, q, so, batch, sys; uint32_t *bp, *sp; } g;
static void gpuSetup(uint32_t surfHandle, uint64_t surfSize) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	g.vm = vc.vm_id;
	g.batch = gem(0x10000, 1); g.sys = gem((kBytes + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull, 1);
	g.bp = map(g.batch, 0x10000); g.sp = map(g.sys, (kBytes + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull);
	if (!g.bp || !g.sp || bind(g.vm, g.batch, kBatch, 0x10000, 2) || bind(g.vm, g.sys, kSys, (kBytes + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull, 2) ||
		bind(g.vm, surfHandle, kSurf, surfSize, 0)) { fprintf(stderr, "gpu setup %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	g.q = queue(g.vm, DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY);
	g.so = syncobj();
}
// MEM_COPY (page mode, 4 MB per command) of kBytes between the system BO and the backing; waits; 0 = done
static int gpuCopy(int toSurface) {
	uint32_t k = 0;
	for (uint64_t off = 0; off < kBytes; off += 4u << 20) {
		const uint64_t chunk = kBytes - off < (4u << 20) ? kBytes - off : (4u << 20);
		const uint64_t s = (toSurface ? kSys : kSurf) + off, d = (toSurface ? kSurf : kSys) + off;
		g.bp[k++] = (2u << 29 | 0x5au << 22) | 1u << 19 | (10 - 2);
		g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(chunk / 256) - 1; g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(chunk / 0x1000) - 1; g.bp[k++] = 0xfff; g.bp[k++] = 0xfff;
		g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)s; g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(s >> 32); g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)d; g.bp[k++] = (uint32_t)(d >> 32);
		g.bp[k++] = 3u << 28 | 3u << 3;
	}
	g.bp[k++] = 0xa << 23; g.bp[k++] = 0;
	__sync_synchronize();
	struct drm_syncobj_destroy dd = {.handle = g.so};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_DESTROY, &dd);
	g.so = syncobj();
	struct drm_xe_sync sy = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = g.so};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = g.q, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&sy, .address = kBatch, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x)) return errno;
	return 0;
}
static int open_intelxe(void) {
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	struct drm_get_cap cap = {.capability = INTELXE_CAP_SURFACE_VRAM};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap) || !cap.value) {
		fprintf(stderr, "debug.intelxe.surfvram is 0 (or this IntelXe.kext has no SURFACE_VRAM): sudo sysctl -w debug.intelxe.surfvram=1\n");
		return 2;
	}
	return 0;
}
static void stats(const char *when) {
	char b[512] = ""; size_t n = sizeof b;
	if (!sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.surfvram_stats", b, &n, NULL, 0)) printf("  [%s] %s", when, b);
}
static unsigned backings(void) {
	char b[512] = ""; size_t n = sizeof b; unsigned c = 0;
	if (!sysctlbyname("debug.intelxe.surfvram_stats", b, &n, NULL, 0)) { const char *p = strstr(b, "): "); if (p) c = (unsigned)atoi(p + 3); }
	return c;
}

static int child(uint32_t sid, uint32_t seedA, uint32_t seedB) {
	if (open_intelxe()) return 3;
	IOSurfaceRef sf = IOSurfaceLookup(sid);
	CHECK(sf != NULL, "child: IOSurfaceLookup(%u)", sid);
	if (!sf) return 1;
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v;
	const int r = surfVram(sid, 0, kBytes, 0, &v);
	CHECK(r == 0, "child: import without CREATE -> handle %u, %llu bytes, gen %u (err %d)", v.handle, (unsigned long long)v.size_out, v.gen, r);
	if (r) return 1;
	gpuSetup(v.handle, v.size_out);
	memset(g.sp, 0, kBytes);
	CHECK(!gpuCopy(0) && !waitBin(g.so, 2000000000ull), "child: GPU copy backing -> system BO");
	const long bad = mismatches(g.sp, seedA);
	CHECK(bad == 0, "child: the backing holds the parent's pattern A (%ld dwords differ)", bad);
	pattern(g.sp, seedB);
	CHECK(!gpuCopy(1), "child: GPU writes pattern B into the backing");
	CHECK(!attach(sid, g.so, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE), "child: WRITE fence attached");
	CHECK(!surfDirty(sid), "child: SURFACE_DIRTY");
	CHECK(!waitBin(g.so, 2000000000ull), "child: write completed");
	CFRelease(sf);
	return fails ? 1 : 0;   // exits holding its handle: the client teardown drops it
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0);
	if (argc == 5 && !strcmp(argv[1], "child")) return child((uint32_t)strtoul(argv[2], 0, 0), (uint32_t)strtoul(argv[3], 0, 0), (uint32_t)strtoul(argv[4], 0, 0));
	int r0 = open_intelxe();
	if (r0) return r0;
	stats("start");
	const unsigned base = backings();
	int one = 1;
	CFNumberRef w = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){W}), h = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){H}),
	            bpe = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){4}), bpr = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){ROW}),
	            pf = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, (int[]){0x42475241});
	const void *k[] = {kIOSurfaceWidth, kIOSurfaceHeight, kIOSurfaceBytesPerElement, kIOSurfaceBytesPerRow, kIOSurfacePixelFormat, kIOSurfaceIsGlobal};
	const void *v[] = {w, h, bpe, bpr, pf, kCFBooleanTrue};
	(void)one;
	CFDictionaryRef props = CFDictionaryCreate(NULL, k, v, 6, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	IOSurfaceRef sf = IOSurfaceCreate(props);
	if (!sf) { fprintf(stderr, "IOSurfaceCreate\n"); return 1; }
	const uint32_t sid = IOSurfaceGetID(sf);
	printf("surface %u, %zu bytes allocated\n", sid, IOSurfaceGetAllocSize(sf));
	const uint32_t seedA = 0xa0000000u ^ (uint32_t)(ns() & 0xffffff), seedB = seedA ^ 0x0b0b0b0bu;

	// 1
	struct drm_intelxe_surface_vram v1, v2;
	int r = surfVram(sid, 0, kBytes, INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_CREATE, &v1);
	CHECK(r == 0 && v1.handle && v1.size_out >= kBytes, "CREATE -> handle %u, %llu bytes, gen %u (err %d)", v1.handle, (unsigned long long)v1.size_out, v1.gen, r);
	if (r) { stats("after create"); return 1; }
	r = surfVram(sid, 0, kBytes, 0, &v2);
	CHECK(r == 0 && v2.size_out == v1.size_out && v2.gen == v1.gen, "second lookup without CREATE -> same backing (gen %u, %llu bytes)", v2.gen, (unsigned long long)v2.size_out);
	// 2
	gpuSetup(v1.handle, v1.size_out);
	pattern(g.sp, seedA);
	CHECK(!gpuCopy(1), "GPU writes pattern A into the backing");
	CHECK(!attach(sid, g.so, INTELXE_SURFACE_FENCE_WRITE), "WRITE fence attached");
	CHECK(!surfDirty(sid), "SURFACE_DIRTY");
	// 3 (the lock may come before the copy finished: the page-off waits for the surface's writers)
	uint64_t t0 = ns();
	IOSurfaceLock(sf, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	const uint64_t lockUs = (ns() - t0) / 1000;
	long bad = mismatches(IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(sf), seedA);
	IOSurfaceUnlock(sf, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	CHECK(bad == 0, "CPU lock sees pattern A (paged off; lock took %llu us; %ld dwords differ)", (unsigned long long)lockUs, bad);
	// 4
	char a1[16], a2[16], a3[16];
	snprintf(a1, sizeof a1, "%u", sid); snprintf(a2, sizeof a2, "0x%x", seedA); snprintf(a3, sizeof a3, "0x%x", seedB);
	char *cargv[] = {argv[0], "child", a1, a2, a3, NULL};
	pid_t pid = 0; int st = 0;
	r = posix_spawn(&pid, argv[0], NULL, NULL, cargv, environ);
	CHECK(r == 0 && waitpid(pid, &st, 0) == pid && WIFEXITED(st) && WEXITSTATUS(st) == 0, "child process (import, read A, write B, exit): status %d", WIFEXITED(st) ? WEXITSTATUS(st) : -1);
	// 5
	t0 = ns();
	IOSurfaceLock(sf, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	const uint64_t lock2Us = (ns() - t0) / 1000;
	bad = mismatches(IOSurfaceGetBaseAddress(sf), seedB);
	IOSurfaceUnlock(sf, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	CHECK(bad == 0, "CPU lock sees the other process's pattern B (lock took %llu us; %ld dwords differ)", (unsigned long long)lock2Us, bad);
	// a second lock with nothing new: no copy needed
	t0 = ns();
	IOSurfaceLock(sf, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	const uint64_t lock3Us = (ns() - t0) / 1000;
	IOSurfaceUnlock(sf, kIOSurfaceLockReadOnly, NULL);
	printf("INFO third lock (nothing newer on the GPU): %llu us\n", (unsigned long long)lock3Us);
	// 6
	IOSurfaceRef s2 = IOSurfaceCreate(props);
	r = s2 ? surfVram(IOSurfaceGetID(s2), 0, kBytes, 0, NULL) : -1;
	CHECK(r == ENOENT, "import of a surface without a backing: ENOENT (%d)", r);
	r = surfVram(sid, 1, kBytes, 0, NULL);
	CHECK(r == EINVAL, "plane 1: EINVAL (%d)", r);
	r = s2 ? surfVram(IOSurfaceGetID(s2), 0, 3ull << 30, INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_CREATE, NULL) : -1;
	CHECK(r == ENOSPC, "a 3 GB backing over the budget: ENOSPC (%d)", r);
	r = surfVram(999999, 0, kBytes, INTELXE_SURFACE_VRAM_CREATE, NULL);
	CHECK(r == ENOENT, "a surface ID this task cannot see: ENOENT (%d)", r);
	stats("before release");
	// 7
	struct drm_gem_close gc1 = {.handle = v1.handle}, gc2 = {.handle = v2.handle};
	struct drm_xe_vm_destroy vd = {.vm_id = g.vm};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_DESTROY, &vd);
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &gc1); xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &gc2);
	CFRelease(sf); if (s2) CFRelease(s2);
	usleep(300000);
	const unsigned after = backings();
	CHECK(after == base, "surfaces released: %u backings in the registry (%u at the start)", after, base);
	stats("end");
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/ulls.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// ulls: what a job's round trip costs when it does not go through the kernel and the GuC at all, against the same job
// through DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC (proof of concept for direct submission, as Intel's compute driver does it: "ULLS").
// No Mesa, no Metal plugin. On the compute engine (WindowServer composites on render), one exec queue:
//   exec:   per job an exec of a 2nd-level-sized batch (MI_STORE_DATA_IMM of a sequence number + MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END),
//           the CPU spinning until the store is visible (no syncobj wait in the timed part: the GPU's own latency).
//   direct: ONE exec of a persistent batch with a slot per job: MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT (polling) until a mailbox dword in
//           system memory reaches the job's number, then MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START (second level) of that job's batch,
//           which stores the sequence number and returns. Submitting = the CPU writes the job's batch and the mailbox.
// Both timed from the CPU's "go" (exec ioctl / mailbox write) to the store being visible to a spinning CPU, with a
// CPU gap between jobs (0, 20, 100 us, 1 ms). The persistent batch ends after the last slot, well inside the job
// watchdog (debug.intelxe.job_timeout_ms). Measurement only.
// "chain" (3rd argument): each job's second-level batch is a stub that chains (MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START with the second
// level bit clear) to the batch that stores, as ANV's batches chain, and the persistent batch stores the job number to
// a second dword after the call returns: a kernel-side direct submission would call an application's chained batch at
// the second level, so its MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END has to come back to the persistent batch.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../../../kernel/IntelXe/uapi -o ulls ulls.c -framework IOKit
//   ./ulls [jobs] [compute|render] [chain]
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <immintrin.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static uint64_t ns(void) { return mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom; }
static int dcmp(const void *a, const void *b) { double x = *(const double *)a, y = *(const double *)b; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }
static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = 1, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { fprintf(stderr, "GEM_CREATE %d\n", errno); exit(1); }
	return g.handle;
}
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0; mach_vm_size_t sz = size;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12), mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz, kIOMapAnywhere)) return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = bo; b.bind.range = range; b.bind.addr = addr; b.bind.op = DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP; b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static void spin_ns(uint64_t d) { uint64_t t = ns(); while (ns() - t < d) __asm__ volatile("pause"); }
static void flush(volatile void *p, size_t len) {   // the CPU's writes out to memory before the GPU reads them
	for (size_t o = 0; o < len; o += 64) _mm_clflush((const char *)p + o);
	_mm_mfence();
}
static void st(const char *nm, double *v, int n) {
	qsort(v, n, 8, dcmp); double s = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += v[i];
	printf("    %-30s p50 %7.2f  p90 %7.2f  p99 %7.2f  mean %7.2f us\n", nm, v[n / 2], v[n * 9 / 10], v[n * 99 / 100], s / n);
}

#define MI_SDI (0x20u << 23 | 2)                    // MI_STORE_DATA_IMM, PPGTT, one dword
#define MI_BBE (0x0au << 23)                        // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_END
#define MI_BBS2 (0x31u << 23 | 1u << 22 | 1u << 8 | 1)   // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START, second level, PPGTT
#define MI_BBSC (0x31u << 23 | 1u << 8 | 1)             // MI_BATCH_BUFFER_START, chained (no level change), PPGTT
#define MI_SEMA_GTE_POLL (0x1cu << 23 | 1u << 15 | 1u << 12 | 3)   // MI_SEMAPHORE_WAIT, polling, SAD >= SDD, PPGTT
enum { RING = 0x100000, WORK = 0x400000, MBOX = 0x800000, TARGET = 0x900000 };
enum { SLOT_DW = 12, WORK_DW = 16 };

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	const int N = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 1000;
	const uint16_t cls = argc > 2 && !strcmp(argv[2], "render") ? DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER : DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COMPUTE;
	const int chain = argc > 3 && !strcmp(argv[3], "chain");
	const uint64_t gaps[] = {0, 20000, 100000, 1000000};
	const uint64_t ringBytes = (uint64_t)(4 * N + 16) * SLOT_DW * 4, workBytes = (uint64_t)4 * N * WORK_DW * 4;
	const uint64_t ringSize = (ringBytes + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull, workSize = (workBytes + 0xffff) & ~0xffffull;

	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) { fprintf(stderr, "vm create %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	uint32_t ringBo = gem(ringSize), workBo = gem(workSize), mboxBo = gem(0x1000), tgBo = gem(0x1000);
	volatile uint32_t *ring = map(ringBo, ringSize), *work = map(workBo, workSize), *mbox = map(mboxBo, 0x1000), *tg = map(tgBo, 0x1000);
	if (!ring || !work || !mbox || !tg) { fprintf(stderr, "map\n"); return 1; }
	if (bind(vc.vm_id, ringBo, RING, ringSize) || bind(vc.vm_id, workBo, WORK, workSize) || bind(vc.vm_id, mboxBo, MBOX, 0x1000) ||
		bind(vc.vm_id, tgBo, TARGET, 0x1000)) { fprintf(stderr, "bind %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = cls};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create q = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vc.vm_id, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &q)) { fprintf(stderr, "queue %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc);
	uint32_t h[1] = {sc.handle};
	double *lat = calloc(N, 8);
	printf("ulls on %s, %d jobs per gap%s\n", cls == DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COMPUTE ? "compute" : "render", N,
		chain ? ", chained second-level batches" : "");

	// 1. through the kernel: one exec per job, the CPU spinning on the store
	uint32_t seq = 0x1000;
	for (int gi = 0; gi < 4; gi++) {
		int n = gi == 3 ? N / 5 : N;
		for (int i = 0; i < n + 5; i++) {
			seq++;
			volatile uint32_t *b = work;
			b[0] = MI_SDI; b[1] = TARGET; b[2] = 0; b[3] = seq; b[4] = MI_BBE; b[5] = 0;
			flush(b, 32);
			spin_ns(gaps[gi]);
			struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
			struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s, .address = WORK,
				.num_batch_buffer = 1};
			const uint64_t t0 = ns();
			if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x)) { printf("exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
			while (tg[0] != seq && ns() - t0 < 1000000000ull) __asm__ volatile("pause");
			const uint64_t t1 = ns();
			struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + 2000000000ull)};
			if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w)) { printf("wait failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
			if (tg[0] != seq) { printf("exec: store missing\n"); return 1; }
			if (i >= 5) lat[i - 5] = (t1 - t0) / 1e3;
		}
		printf("  exec    gap %5llu us\n", gaps[gi] / 1000);
		st("exec -> store visible", lat, n);
	}

	// 2. direct: one persistent batch, a slot per job
	int total = 0;
	for (int gi = 0; gi < 4; gi++) total += (gi == 3 ? N / 5 : N) + 5;
	for (int k = 0; k < total; k++) {
		volatile uint32_t *s = ring + (size_t)k * SLOT_DW;
		const uint64_t wa = WORK + (uint64_t)k * WORK_DW * 4;
		s[0] = MI_SEMA_GTE_POLL; s[1] = (uint32_t)(k + 1); s[2] = MBOX; s[3] = 0; s[4] = 0;
		s[5] = MI_BBS2; s[6] = (uint32_t)wa; s[7] = (uint32_t)(wa >> 32);
		// after the call returns: the job number to the second dword (0 jobs' worth of extra work without chain: a no-op
		// store to an unused dword keeps the slot the same size)
		s[8] = MI_SDI; s[9] = TARGET + (chain ? 4 : 64); s[10] = 0; s[11] = (uint32_t)(k + 1);
	}
	ring[(size_t)total * SLOT_DW] = MI_BBE; ring[(size_t)total * SLOT_DW + 1] = 0;
	mbox[0] = 0; tg[0] = 0;
	flush(ring, (size_t)(total + 1) * SLOT_DW * 4); flush(mbox, 64); flush(tg, 64);
	struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = sc.handle};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s, .address = RING, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x)) { printf("persistent exec failed %d\n", errno); return 1; }
	int k = 0;
	for (int gi = 0; gi < 4; gi++) {
		int n = gi == 3 ? N / 5 : N;
		for (int i = 0; i < n + 5; i++, k++) {
			volatile uint32_t *b = work + (size_t)k * WORK_DW;
			const uint32_t v = 0x80000000u | (uint32_t)k;
			if (chain) {   // stub: chain to dword 8 of the same slot, which stores and ends
				const uint64_t to = WORK + ((uint64_t)k * WORK_DW + 8) * 4;
				b[0] = MI_BBSC; b[1] = (uint32_t)to; b[2] = (uint32_t)(to >> 32); b[3] = 0;
				b[8] = MI_SDI; b[9] = TARGET; b[10] = 0; b[11] = v; b[12] = MI_BBE; b[13] = 0;
				flush(b, 64);
			} else {
				b[0] = MI_SDI; b[1] = TARGET; b[2] = 0; b[3] = v; b[4] = MI_BBE; b[5] = 0;
				flush(b, 32);
			}
			spin_ns(gaps[gi]);
			const uint64_t t0 = ns();
			mbox[0] = (uint32_t)(k + 1);
			flush(mbox, 64);
			while (tg[0] != v && ns() - t0 < 1000000000ull) __asm__ volatile("pause");
			const uint64_t t1 = ns();
			if (chain) {   // back in the persistent batch?
				while (tg[1] != (uint32_t)(k + 1) && ns() - t0 < 1000000000ull) __asm__ volatile("pause");
				if (tg[1] != (uint32_t)(k + 1)) { printf("chain: job %d stored 0x%x but the persistent batch did not go on (0x%x)\n", k, tg[0], tg[1]);
					mbox[0] = 0xffffffffu; flush(mbox, 64); return 1; }
			}
			if (tg[0] != v) { printf("direct: store missing at job %d (mailbox %u, target 0x%x)\n", k, mbox[0], tg[0]); mbox[0] = 0xffffffffu; flush(mbox, 64); return 1; }
			if (i >= 5) lat[i - 5] = (t1 - t0) / 1e3;
		}
		printf("  direct  gap %5llu us\n", gaps[gi] / 1000);
		st("mailbox -> store visible", lat, n);
	}
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)h, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = (int64_t)(ns() + 2000000000ull)};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w)) printf("persistent batch did not end: %d\n", errno);
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_destroy d = {.exec_queue_id = q.exec_queue_id};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_DESTROY, &d);
	return 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vbw: CPU write/read speed into a mapped CPU-visible VRAM BO and a system-memory BO (cache mode check).
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o vbw vbw.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	return out ? (int)out : 0;
}
static double secs(uint64_t t) { mach_timebase_info_data_t tb; mach_timebase_info(&tb); return (double)t * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e9; }

static void run(const char *name, uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags, uint16_t caching, IOOptionBits cache) {
	const size_t sz = 16 << 20;
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = sz, .placement = placement, .cpu_caching = caching, .flags = flags};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) { printf("%s: create failed\n", name); return; }
	mach_vm_address_t va = 0; mach_vm_size_t len = 0;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, g.handle, mach_task_self(), &va, &len, kIOMapAnywhere | cache)) { printf("%s: map failed\n", name); return; }
	volatile uint32_t *p = (volatile uint32_t *)va;
	uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time();
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sz / 4; i++) p[i] = (uint32_t)i;
	double w = secs(mach_absolute_time() - t0);
	t0 = mach_absolute_time();
	uint32_t s = 0;
	for (size_t i = 0; i < (1 << 20) / 4; i++) s += p[i];   // 1 MB read
	double r = secs(mach_absolute_time() - t0);
	printf("%-16s write %8.1f MB/s, read %8.1f MB/s (%u)\n", name, sz / w / 1e6, (1 << 20) / r / 1e6, s & 1);
}

int main(void) {
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	run("VRAM default map", 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC, 0);
	run("VRAM WC map", 2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC, kIOMapWriteCombineCache);
	run("system WB", 1, 0, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB, 0);
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/vfill.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vfill: fills the CPU-visible VRAM window past its end with N MB of NEEDS_VISIBLE, VRAM-only BOs (64 MB each), maps
// every one and checks a CPU write/read pattern, so the kernel's system-memory fallback for a full window can be tested.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O1 -I../uapi -o vfill vfill.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;

static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	return out ? (int)out : 0;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	unsigned mb = argc > 1 ? (unsigned)atoi(argv[1]) : 1152, bad = 0, made = 0;
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < mb / 64; i++) {
		struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = 64ull << 20, .placement = 2, .cpu_caching = DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC,
		                              .flags = DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM};
		int e = xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g);
		if (e) { printf("BO %u: GEM_CREATE error %d\n", i, e); bad++; continue; }
		mach_vm_address_t va = 0; mach_vm_size_t len = 0;
		if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, g.handle, mach_task_self(), &va, &len, kIOMapAnywhere)) {
			printf("BO %u: map failed\n", i); bad++; continue;
		}
		volatile uint64_t *p = (volatile uint64_t *)va;
		for (uint64_t o = 0; o < len / 8; o += 4096) p[o] = (uint64_t)i << 32 | o;
		for (uint64_t o = 0; o < len / 8; o += 4096) if (p[o] != ((uint64_t)i << 32 | o)) { bad++; printf("BO %u: readback mismatch\n", i); break; }
		made++;
	}
	printf("%u x 64 MB BOs created and checked, %u failures\n", made, bad);
	struct drm_xe_device_query q = {.query = DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_MEM_REGIONS};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q);
	struct drm_xe_query_mem_regions *m = calloc(1, q.size);
	q.data = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)m;
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q);
	for (unsigned i = 0; i < m->num_mem_regions; i++)
		if (m->mem_regions[i].mem_class == DRM_XE_MEM_REGION_CLASS_VRAM)
			printf("VRAM used %llu MB, visible used %llu of %llu MB\n", m->mem_regions[i].used >> 20,
			       m->mem_regions[i].cpu_visible_used >> 20, m->mem_regions[i].cpu_visible_size >> 20);
	return bad != 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/vlat.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vlat: latency of one CPU read from a WC-mapped CPU-visible VRAM BO, as a function of how long the device was left
// alone before it (PCIe link / package power states), next to a system-memory BO. Measurement only.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o vlat vlat.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	return out ? (int)out : 0;
}
static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static double us(uint64_t t) { return (double)t * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e3; }
static int dcmp(const void *a, const void *b) { double x = *(const double *)a, y = *(const double *)b; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }

static volatile uint32_t *map(uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags, uint16_t caching) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = 1 << 20, .placement = placement, .cpu_caching = caching, .flags = flags};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t va = 0; mach_vm_size_t len = 0;
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, g.handle, mach_task_self(), &va, &len, kIOMapAnywhere | kIOMapWriteCombineCache)) return NULL;
	return (volatile uint32_t *)va;
}

static void spin_us(double d) {
	uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time();
	while (us(mach_absolute_time() - t0) < d) __asm__ volatile("pause");
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) { fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n"); return 1; }
	volatile uint32_t *v = map(2, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC);
	if (!v) { fprintf(stderr, "map failed\n"); return 1; }
	for (int i = 0; i < 4096; i++) v[i] = i;
	if (argc > 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "keep")) {   // keep <seconds> [period_us]: one VRAM read every period (default 20 us)
		double secs = atof(argv[2]), per = argc > 3 ? atof(argv[3]) : 20; uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time(); long n = 0; double worst = 0;
		while (us(mach_absolute_time() - t0) < secs * 1e6) {
			uint64_t a = mach_absolute_time(); (void)v[0]; double d = us(mach_absolute_time() - a); if (d > worst) worst = d;
			n++; spin_us(per);
		}
		printf("keep: %ld reads, worst %.1f us\n", n, worst);
		return 0;
	}
	double gaps[] = {0, 5, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 5000};
	const int N = 200;
	double s[N];
	printf("one 4-byte read from WC VRAM after the device sat idle for <gap> us (CPU spinning, so no CPU C-state)\n");
	for (int g = 0; g < 9; g++) {
		for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
			spin_us(gaps[g]);
			uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time();
			(void)v[(i * 64) & 4095];
			s[i] = us(mach_absolute_time() - t0);
		}
		qsort(s, N, sizeof *s, dcmp);
		double second;
		{ uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time(); (void)v[0]; (void)v[16]; second = us(mach_absolute_time() - t0) / 2; }
		printf("  gap %6.0f us: read p50 %6.2f us  p90 %6.2f  max %6.2f   (back-to-back reads right after: %.2f us each)\n",
		       gaps[g], s[N / 2], s[N * 9 / 10], s[N - 1], second);
	}
	// streaming: 64 consecutive 8-byte reads (one descriptor-pool free-list pop is a few of these)
	uint64_t t0 = mach_absolute_time();
	volatile uint64_t *v8 = (volatile uint64_t *)v; uint64_t acc = 0;
	for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) acc += v8[i];
	printf("  1024 back-to-back 8-byte reads: %.2f us each (%llu)\n", us(mach_absolute_time() - t0) / 1024, (unsigned long long)(acc & 1));
	t0 = mach_absolute_time();
	for (int i = 0; i < 1024; i++) v8[i] = i;
	printf("  1024 back-to-back 8-byte writes: %.3f us each\n", us(mach_absolute_time() - t0) / 1024);
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/vmouse.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Virtual USB mouse: nudges the pointer (or clicks) N times, one report every 100 ms (or every argv[3] us), so display wake on real HID input can be
// tested without anyone at the machine. Needs com.apple.developer.hid.virtual.device (ad-hoc entitlement, AMFI off).
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <IOKit/hidsystem/IOHIDUserDevice.h>
#include <IOKit/hid/IOHIDKeys.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>

static const uint8_t kDesc[] = {
	0x05, 0x01, 0x09, 0x02, 0xA1, 0x01, 0x09, 0x01, 0xA1, 0x00,
	0x05, 0x09, 0x19, 0x01, 0x29, 0x03, 0x15, 0x00, 0x25, 0x01, 0x95, 0x03, 0x75, 0x01, 0x81, 0x02,
	0x95, 0x01, 0x75, 0x05, 0x81, 0x03,
	0x05, 0x01, 0x09, 0x30, 0x09, 0x31, 0x15, 0x81, 0x25, 0x7F, 0x75, 0x08, 0x95, 0x02, 0x81, 0x06,
	0xC0, 0xC0,
};

static void num(CFMutableDictionaryRef d, CFStringRef k, int v) {
	CFNumberRef n = CFNumberCreate(NULL, kCFNumberIntType, &v);
	CFDictionarySetValue(d, k, n);
	CFRelease(n);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	int n = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 10;
	int click = argc > 2 && argv[2][0] == 'c';   // "click": press and release the left button instead of moving
	int us = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 100000;   // microseconds between reports
	CFMutableDictionaryRef p = CFDictionaryCreateMutable(NULL, 0, &kCFTypeDictionaryKeyCallBacks, &kCFTypeDictionaryValueCallBacks);
	CFDataRef desc = CFDataCreate(NULL, kDesc, sizeof(kDesc));
	CFDictionarySetValue(p, CFSTR(kIOHIDReportDescriptorKey), desc);
	num(p, CFSTR(kIOHIDVendorIDKey), 0x05ac);
	num(p, CFSTR(kIOHIDProductIDKey), 0x0b58);
	CFDictionarySetValue(p, CFSTR(kIOHIDTransportKey), CFSTR("USB"));
	CFDictionarySetValue(p, CFSTR(kIOHIDProductKey), CFSTR("B580 test mouse"));
	IOHIDUserDeviceRef dev = IOHIDUserDeviceCreateWithProperties(NULL, p, 0);
	if (!dev) { fprintf(stderr, "IOHIDUserDeviceCreate failed (entitlement?)\n"); return 1; }
	IOHIDUserDeviceSetDispatchQueue(dev, dispatch_queue_create("vmouse", NULL));
	IOHIDUserDeviceActivate(dev);
	sleep(2);   // let the HID event system attach the service
	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		int8_t dx = (i & 1) ? -20 : 20;
		uint8_t r[3] = {0, (uint8_t)dx, 0};
		if (click) { r[0] = (i & 1) ? 0 : 1; r[1] = 0; }
		IOReturn e = IOHIDUserDeviceHandleReportWithTimeStamp(dev, mach_absolute_time(), r, sizeof(r));
		if (e) fprintf(stderr, "report %d: 0x%x\n", i, e);
		usleep(us);
	}
	printf("sent %d reports\n", n);
	IOHIDUserDeviceCancel(dev);
	sleep(1);
	CFRelease(dev);
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/kernel/winfill.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// winfill: the BAR window (CPU-visible VRAM) under pressure, on IntelXe.kext.
//   ./winfill unmap  CPU maps of VRAM BOs: IOConnectUnmapMemory64 must find and remove each mapping (it failed unseen
//                    before build pv: a new memory descriptor per call), two maps of one BO must be two mappings, and
//                    the BO's VRAM must go back when it is unmapped and closed. Uses ~20 MB of the window. Safe anywhere.
//   ./winfill fill   fills the window the way Mesa does (NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM BOs allowed in system memory, mapped for
//                    good, bound), then keeps allocating: BOs that no longer fit must land in system memory, binds must
//                    still get page tables (a fresh VM, 4 KB-paged system BOs), and every BO must keep what the CPU and
//                    the GPU wrote into it. Then everything is freed and the window must come back.
//                    TAKES THE WHOLE WINDOW for a few seconds: not while a game or benchmark runs (pgrep java/geekbench).
// Test only.   clang -arch x86_64 -O2 -I../uapi -o winfill winfill.c -framework IOKit
#include <IOKit/IOKitLib.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <time.h>
#include "xe_drm.h"

static io_connect_t conn;
static int xioctl(unsigned long req, void *arg) {
	uint64_t in[2] = {req, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)arg}, out = 0;
	uint32_t n = 1;
	if (IOConnectCallScalarMethod(conn, 0, in, 2, &out, &n)) return -1;
	errno = (int)out;
	return out ? -1 : 0;
}
static int fails;
#define CHECK(c, ...) do { if (!(c)) { fails++; printf("FAIL %s:%d: ", __FILE__, __LINE__); printf(__VA_ARGS__); printf("\n"); } } while (0)

static double now(void) {
	struct timespec t;
	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &t);
	return t.tv_sec + t.tv_nsec * 1e-9;
}
static uint32_t gem(uint64_t size, uint32_t placement, uint32_t flags) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_create g = {.size = size, .placement = placement, .flags = flags,
		.cpu_caching = placement & 2 ? DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WC : DRM_XE_GEM_CPU_CACHING_WB};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_CREATE, &g) ? 0 : g.handle;
}
static void gemClose(uint32_t h) {
	struct drm_gem_close c = {.handle = h};
	xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_GEM_CLOSE, &c);
}
// As xemac_mmap: GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, then IOConnectMapMemory64 of type offset >> 12, write-combined for VRAM (bit 63).
static void *map(uint32_t handle, uint64_t size, uint32_t *type) {
	struct drm_xe_gem_mmap_offset m = {.handle = handle};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET, &m)) return NULL;
	mach_vm_address_t addr = 0;
	mach_vm_size_t sz = 0;
	*type = (uint32_t)(m.offset >> 12);
	if (IOConnectMapMemory64(conn, *type, mach_task_self(), &addr, &sz,
			kIOMapAnywhere | (m.offset >> 63 ? kIOMapWriteCombineCache : 0)) || sz < size)
		return NULL;
	return (void *)(uintptr_t)addr;
}
static kern_return_t unmap(uint32_t type, void *p) {
	return IOConnectUnmapMemory64(conn, type, mach_task_self(), (mach_vm_address_t)(uintptr_t)p);
}
static int bind(uint32_t vm, uint32_t bo, uint64_t addr, uint64_t range, uint32_t op) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_bind b = {.vm_id = vm, .num_binds = 1};
	b.bind.obj = op == DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP ? bo : 0;
	b.bind.range = range;
	b.bind.addr = addr;
	b.bind.op = op;
	b.bind.pat_index = 2;
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND, &b);
}
static void line(const char *sysctl, const char *key, const char *what) {
	char buf[16384];
	size_t l = sizeof(buf);
	if (sysctlbyname(sysctl, buf, &l, NULL, 0)) return;
	char *p = strstr(buf, key);
	if (!p) return;
	char *e = strchr(p, '\n');
	if (e) *e = 0;
	printf("  %s: %s\n", what, p);
}
static void report(const char *what) {
	line("debug.intelxe.stats", "VRAM end", what);
	line("debug.intelxe.stats", "window:", what);
}
// The kernel's view of the CPU-visible window (DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_MEM_REGIONS), and of system BOs.
static void regions(uint64_t *visUsed, uint64_t *visSize, uint64_t *sysUsed) {
	struct { struct drm_xe_query_mem_regions h; struct drm_xe_mem_region m[4]; } r;
	memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
	struct drm_xe_device_query q = {.query = DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_MEM_REGIONS};
	*visUsed = *visSize = *sysUsed = 0;
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q) || q.size > sizeof(r)) return;   // size first, as Mesa asks
	q.data = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&r;
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_DEVICE_QUERY, &q)) return;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < r.h.num_mem_regions && i < 4; i++) {
		if (r.m[i].mem_class == DRM_XE_MEM_REGION_CLASS_VRAM) {
			*visUsed = r.m[i].cpu_visible_used;
			*visSize = r.m[i].cpu_visible_size;
		} else {
			*sysUsed = r.m[i].used;
		}
	}
}

static uint32_t vmId, q, so, bbh;
static volatile uint32_t *bb;
static int gpuInit(void) {
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc)) return -1;
	vmId = vc.vm_id;
	uint32_t t;
	if (!(bbh = gem(0x10000, 1, 0)) || !(bb = map(bbh, 0x10000, &t)) || bind(vmId, bbh, 0x100000, 0x10000, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP))
		return -1;
	struct drm_xe_engine_class_instance ei = {.engine_class = DRM_XE_ENGINE_CLASS_RENDER};
	struct drm_xe_exec_queue_create qc = {.width = 1, .num_placements = 1, .vm_id = vmId, .instances = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&ei};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC_QUEUE_CREATE, &qc)) return -1;
	q = qc.exec_queue_id;
	struct drm_syncobj_create sc = {0};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &sc)) return -1;
	so = sc.handle;
	return 0;
}
// MI_STORE_DATA_IMM of value ^ offset at every 64 KB of [va, va + size), at most 2000 stores per batch.
static int gpuPattern(uint64_t va, uint64_t size, uint32_t value) {
	uint32_t k = 0;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size && k < 8000; o += 0x10000) {
		bb[k++] = 0x20 << 23 | 2;
		bb[k++] = (uint32_t)(va + o);
		bb[k++] = (uint32_t)((va + o) >> 32);
		bb[k++] = value ^ (uint32_t)o;
	}
	bb[k++] = 0xa << 23;
	bb[k++] = 0;
	__sync_synchronize();
	struct drm_xe_sync s = {.type = DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_SYNCOBJ, .flags = DRM_XE_SYNC_FLAG_SIGNAL, .handle = so};
	struct drm_xe_exec x = {.exec_queue_id = q, .num_syncs = 1, .syncs = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&s, .address = 0x100000, .num_batch_buffer = 1};
	if (xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_EXEC, &x)) return -1;
	struct drm_syncobj_wait w = {.handles = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)&so, .count_handles = 1, .timeout_nsec = INT64_MAX};
	return xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &w);
}
static int checkPattern(volatile uint32_t *p, uint64_t size, uint32_t value) {
	int bad = 0;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size && o / 0x10000 < 2000; o += 0x10000)
		if (p[o / 4] != (value ^ (uint32_t)o)) bad++;
	return bad;
}

static int testUnmap(void) {
	uint64_t used0, size, sys0, used;
	regions(&used0, &size, &sys0);
	const uint64_t bs = 8ull << 20;
	uint32_t h = gem(bs, 3, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM);
	CHECK(h, "GEM_CREATE %d", errno);
	if (!h) return 1;
	uint32_t t1, t2;
	volatile uint32_t *a = map(h, bs, &t1), *b = map(h, bs, &t2);
	CHECK(a && b, "maps %p %p", (void *)a, (void *)b);
	if (!a || !b) return 1;
	printf("two maps of one 8 MB BO: types 0x%x 0x%x at %p %p\n", t1, t2, (void *)a, (void *)b);
	CHECK(a != b, "the two maps share one mapping: the first unmap would take the second down");
	a[0] = 0x12345678;
	a[bs / 4 - 1] = 0x9abcdef0;
	__sync_synchronize();
	CHECK(b[0] == 0x12345678 && b[bs / 4 - 1] == 0x9abcdef0, "the two maps do not show the same memory");
	kern_return_t kr = unmap(t1, (void *)a);
	CHECK(kr == KERN_SUCCESS, "IOConnectUnmapMemory64 of the first map: 0x%x (the mapping was not found)", kr);
	CHECK(b[0] == 0x12345678, "the second map lost its contents after the first was unmapped");
	kr = unmap(t2, (void *)b);
	CHECK(kr == KERN_SUCCESS, "IOConnectUnmapMemory64 of the second map: 0x%x", kr);
	gemClose(h);
	// many map / unmap / close rounds: nothing may stay behind (window use back where it was)
	for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
		uint32_t hh = gem(1u << 20, 3, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM), tt;
		volatile uint32_t *p = hh ? map(hh, 1u << 20, &tt) : NULL;
		CHECK(p, "round %d: map", i);
		if (p) {
			p[0] = (uint32_t)i;
			kr = unmap(tt, (void *)p);
			CHECK(kr == KERN_SUCCESS, "round %d: unmap 0x%x", i, kr);
		}
		if (hh) gemClose(hh);
		if (fails > 4) break;
	}
	regions(&used, &size, &sys0);
	printf("window used before %llu MB, after %llu MB\n", used0 >> 20, used >> 20);
	report("after the unmap test");
	return fails;
}

#define MAXBO 4096
struct bo { uint32_t h, type; uint64_t size, va; volatile uint32_t *p; uint32_t value; };
static struct bo bos[MAXBO];
static uint32_t nbos;

// One Mesa-style BO: NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM, VRAM or system memory, mapped for good, bound, a CPU pattern written.
static int mesaBo(uint64_t size, uint64_t va) {
	struct bo *b = &bos[nbos];
	b->size = size;
	b->va = va;
	b->value = 0x51000000u | nbos;
	if (!(b->h = gem(size, 3, DRM_XE_GEM_CREATE_FLAG_NEEDS_VISIBLE_VRAM))) return -1;
	if (!(b->p = map(b->h, size, &b->type))) return -2;
	if (bind(vmId, b->h, va, size, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP)) return -3;
	for (uint64_t o = 0; o < size; o += 0x10000) b->p[o / 4] = b->value ^ (uint32_t)o;
	nbos++;
	return 0;
}

static int testFill(void) {
	const double t0 = now();
	uint64_t used, size, sys0, sys;
	regions(&used, &size, &sys0);
	printf("window %llu MB, %llu MB used; system BOs %llu MB\n", size >> 20, used >> 20, sys0 >> 20);
	report("before");
	uint64_t va = 1ull << 36;
	// 1. fill: 16 MB BOs until one lands in system memory, then 64 KB ones until those do too
	int err = 0;
	for (uint64_t each = 16ull << 20; each >= 0x10000 && nbos < MAXBO / 2; each >>= 4) {
		for (;;) {
			uint64_t s0;
			regions(&used, &size, &s0);
			if ((err = mesaBo(each, va)) != 0) break;
			va += each;
			regions(&used, &size, &sys);
			if (sys > s0 || now() - t0 > 20) break;   // spilled: the window has no room for this size any more
		}
		if (err) break;
	}
	CHECK(!err, "filling: Mesa-style BO %u failed at step %d (errno %d)", nbos, err, errno);
	regions(&used, &size, &sys);
	printf("filled: %u BOs, window %llu of %llu MB used, system BOs %llu MB (+%llu)\n", nbos, used >> 20, size >> 20,
		sys >> 20, (sys - sys0) >> 20);
	report("filled");
	// 2. keep allocating with the window full: mixed sizes, all must succeed (in system memory)
	const uint32_t before = nbos;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 300 && nbos < MAXBO - 64 && !err && now() - t0 < 35; i++) {
		const uint64_t each = 0x10000ull << (i % 8);   // 64 KB .. 8 MB
		if ((err = mesaBo(each, va)) != 0) break;
		va += each;
	}
	CHECK(!err, "with the window full: BO %u failed at step %d (errno %d) - 1 create, 2 map, 3 bind (page tables)", nbos,
		err, errno);
	// system BOs bound with 4 KB pages need page-table pages, which live in the window
	uint32_t sysOk = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 16 && !err; i++) {
		uint32_t h = gem(32ull << 20, 1, 0);
		CHECK(h, "system BO %u: %d", i, errno);
		if (!h) break;
		if (bind(vmId, h, va + 0x1000, 8ull << 20, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_MAP)) {   // 4 KB-aligned VA: 4 KB leaves
			CHECK(0, "bind of system BO %u with 4 KB pages: errno %d (no page-table pages?)", i, errno);
			break;
		}
		va += 64ull << 20;
		sysOk++;
	}
	// a new VM (its root table) and an exec queue on it
	struct drm_xe_vm_create vc = {0};
	CHECK(!xioctl(DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_CREATE, &vc), "VM_CREATE with the window full: %d", errno);
	regions(&used, &size, &sys);
	printf("under pressure: %u more BOs, %u 4K-paged system binds; window %llu MB used, system BOs %llu MB\n",
		nbos - before, sysOk, used >> 20, sys >> 20);
	report("under pressure");
	// 3. contents: the CPU patterns, then GPU writes through each BO's VA (window or system memory alike)
	int bad = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nbos; i++) bad += checkPattern(bos[i].p, bos[i].size, bos[i].value) != 0;
	CHECK(!bad, "%d BOs lost CPU-written contents", bad);
	bad = 0;
	uint32_t gpu = 0;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nbos && now() - t0 < 50; i += 1 + nbos / 200, gpu++) {
		if (gpuPattern(bos[i].va, bos[i].size, ~bos[i].value)) { bad++; continue; }
		bad += checkPattern(bos[i].p, bos[i].size, ~bos[i].value) != 0;
	}
	CHECK(!bad, "%d of %u BOs: the CPU does not see what the GPU wrote", bad, gpu);
	// 4. all gone again
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nbos; i++) {
		bind(vmId, 0, bos[i].va, bos[i].size, DRM_XE_VM_BIND_OP_UNMAP);
		kern_return_t kr = unmap(bos[i].type, (void *)bos[i].p);
		if (kr != KERN_SUCCESS && !fails) CHECK(0, "unmap of BO %u: 0x%x", i, kr);
		gemClose(bos[i].h);
	}
	regions(&used, &size, &sys);
	printf("freed: window %llu MB used, system BOs %llu MB (%.1f s)\n", used >> 20, sys >> 20, now() - t0);
	report("after");
	return fails;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	const char *mode = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "";
	if (strcmp(mode, "unmap") && strcmp(mode, "fill")) {
		fprintf(stderr, "usage: winfill unmap | fill\n");
		return 2;
	}
	io_service_t svc = IOServiceGetMatchingService(kIOMainPortDefault, IOServiceMatching("IntelXe"));
	if (!svc || IOServiceOpen(svc, mach_task_self(), 0, &conn)) {
		fprintf(stderr, "no IntelXe service\n");
		return 1;
	}
	if (gpuInit()) {
		fprintf(stderr, "VM / queue setup failed: %d\n", errno);
		return 1;
	}
	if (!strcmp(mode, "unmap")) testUnmap();
	else testFill();
	printf("%s: %d failure(s)\n", fails ? "FAILED" : "PASSED", fails);
	return fails != 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/metal/bufoff_check.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// bufoff_check: the plugin's storage-buffer offset pass (nullmoth/plugin/nvmtl_bufoff_pc.h) on real kernels, off the GPU.
// Each module goes the way nvmtl_vk_compute_pipeline_create takes it in the descriptor-buffer model: the translator's
// address lowering (with --lower: libnvmtl_translate.dylib's nvmtl_lower_buffer_addresses_ex, flags as the plugin passes
// them on ANV), cs-table-pc (nvmtl_spirv_table_pc_ex, NVMTL_PC_MERGE | NVMTL_PC_SET0 | NVMTL_PC_EXACT) and then the pass. The outputs go to
// <outdir> for spirv-val; the pass's own checks run here:
//   - every access chain into a converted binding's variable has its element index replaced by an OpIAdd of the old
//     index and (OpLoad of the new push member, converted to 64 bits when the index is) times G / S;
//   - nothing else in the module changed: with the inserted instructions taken out and the push block's new members
//     left off, the instruction stream is the input's, word for word (ids included);
//   - a module the pass refuses is returned as NULL (the plugin keeps it byte for byte).
//
//   clang -O1 -g -Wall -I nullmoth/plugin -o bufoff_check user/tests/metal/bufoff_check.c
//   ./bufoff_check [-v] [--lower <libnvmtl_translate.dylib>] <outdir> <kernel.spv>...
// -v: one line per kernel the pass left (wholly or in part) as it was, with the reasons (NVMTL_BO_R_*).
// --old-pc: cs-table-pc without NVMTL_PC_EXACT (the classic model's pass, and the buffer model's before 13 Nov night).
// Exit: 0 every check passed, 1 a check failed, 2 usage or I/O.
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "nvmtl_table_pc.h"
#include "nvmtl_bufoff_pc.h"

typedef int (*lower_ex_fn)(const uint8_t *, size_t, uint32_t, uint8_t **, size_t *, uint32_t *, char *, size_t);
typedef void (*free_fn)(uint8_t *, size_t);

static uint32_t *slurp(const char *path, size_t *nbytes)
{
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb"); if (!f) return NULL;
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END); const long n = ftell(f); fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    uint32_t *b = n > 0 ? malloc((size_t)n) : NULL;
    if (!b || fread(b, 1, (size_t)n, f) != (size_t)n) { free(b); fclose(f); return NULL; }
    fclose(f); *nbytes = (size_t)n; return b;
}
static void spit(const char *dir, const char *name, const char *ext, const void *b, size_t n)
{
    char p[1024]; const char *base = strrchr(name, '/'); base = base ? base + 1 : name;
    snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/%s.%s.spv", dir, base, ext);
    FILE *f = fopen(p, "wb"); if (f) { fwrite(b, 1, n, f); fclose(f); }
}

/* the structural check. Output instructions whose result id is new (>= the input's bound), and the push block's new
   member offsets, are the pass's own and are taken out after checking them: a rewritten chain's element index must be
   an OpIAdd of its old index and the new push member's value (loaded through an access chain into the push variable at a
   new member, converted to 64 bits when the index is, multiplied by G / S of the chain's variable). The push block's
   struct must be the input's with u32 members appended. What is left must be the input, instruction for instruction,
   except that the push block's struct, pointer type and variable may have moved within the global section. */
typedef struct { const uint32_t *i; uint32_t wc; } insn;
static size_t insns(const uint32_t *w, size_t nw, insn *out)
{
    size_t n = 0;
    for (size_t at = 5; at < nw;) { const uint32_t wc = w[at] >> 16; if (!wc || at + wc > nw) return 0; out[n++] = (insn){ w + at, wc }; at += wc; }
    return n;
}
static uint32_t result_id(const uint32_t *i)
{
    const uint32_t op = i[0] & 0xffffu, wc = i[0] >> 16;
    if (op >= 19 && op <= 39) return wc >= 2 ? i[1] : 0;
    if (op == 248) return i[1];
    if (op == 59 || op == 43 || op == 61 || op == 65 || op == 66 || op == 113 || op == 128 || op == 132) return wc >= 3 ? i[2] : 0;
    return 0;
}
static const uint32_t *find_def(const insn *v, size_t n, uint32_t id)
{
    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; k++) if (result_id(v[k].i) == id) return v[k].i;
    return NULL;
}
static int check(const uint32_t *in, size_t nin, const uint32_t *out, size_t nout, unsigned *nchains, char *why, size_t wn)
{
    insn *vi = calloc(nin, sizeof *vi), *vo = calloc(nout, sizeof *vo);
    int bad = 1; unsigned chains = 0;
    const size_t ni = vi ? insns(in, nin, vi) : 0, no = vo ? insns(out, nout, vo) : 0;
    const uint32_t bound = in[3];
    uint32_t push_var = 0, push_ptr = 0, push_block = 0, members = 0;
    if (!ni || !no) { snprintf(why, wn, "unparsable"); goto out; }
    for (size_t k = 0; k < ni; k++) if ((vi[k].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 59 && vi[k].i[3] == 9) { push_var = vi[k].i[2]; push_ptr = vi[k].i[1]; }
    { const uint32_t *pp = find_def(vi, ni, push_ptr); if (!pp) { snprintf(why, wn, "no push pointer"); goto out; } push_block = pp[3]; }
    { const uint32_t *pb = find_def(vi, ni, push_block); if (!pb) { snprintf(why, wn, "no push block"); goto out; } members = (pb[0] >> 16) - 2; }
    /* the output, the pass's instructions taken out */
    size_t a = 0;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < no; k++) {
        const uint32_t *o = vo[k].i, op = o[0] & 0xffffu, wc = vo[k].wc;
        if (op == 72 && o[1] == push_block && o[2] >= members) continue;   /* a new member's offset */
        if (op == 30 && o[1] == push_block) {   /* the block: the input's members, then u32 ones */
            const uint32_t *pb = find_def(vi, ni, push_block), *u = NULL;
            if (wc <= pb[0] >> 16 || memcmp(pb + 1, o + 1, ((pb[0] >> 16) - 1) * 4)) { snprintf(why, wn, "push block's old members changed"); goto out; }
            for (uint32_t m = (pb[0] >> 16); m < wc; m++) { u = find_def(vo, no, o[m]); if (!u || (u[0] & 0xffffu) != 21 || u[2] != 32 || u[3]) { snprintf(why, wn, "a new push member is not u32"); goto out; } }
            continue;
        }
        if ((op == 65 || op == 66) && wc >= 6 && o[5] >= bound && o[3] != push_var) {   /* a rewritten chain */
            const uint32_t *add = find_def(vo, no, o[5]);
            if (!add || (add[0] & 0xffffu) != 128) { snprintf(why, wn, "chain %%%u: index is not an OpIAdd", o[2]); goto out; }
            /* the value added: [mul] of [conv] of a load of a new push member */
            const uint32_t *v = find_def(vo, no, add[4]); uint32_t mult = 1;
            if (v && (v[0] & 0xffffu) == 132) { const uint32_t *c = find_def(vo, no, v[4]); if (!c || (c[0] & 0xffffu) != 43) { snprintf(why, wn, "multiplier not a constant"); goto out; } mult = c[3]; v = find_def(vo, no, v[3]); }
            if (v && (v[0] & 0xffffu) == 113) v = find_def(vo, no, v[3]);
            if (!v || (v[0] & 0xffffu) != 61) { snprintf(why, wn, "chain %%%u: the added value is not a load", o[2]); goto out; }
            const uint32_t *pc = find_def(vo, no, v[3]), *mc = pc ? find_def(vo, no, pc[4]) : NULL;
            if (!pc || (pc[0] & 0xffffu) != 65 || pc[3] != push_var || !mc || (mc[0] & 0xffffu) != 43 || mc[3] < members) { snprintf(why, wn, "chain %%%u: not loaded from a new push member", o[2]); goto out; }
            /* G / S: S from the chain's variable */
            const uint32_t *var = find_def(vi, ni, o[3]), *pt = var ? find_def(vi, ni, var[1]) : NULL, *st = pt ? find_def(vi, ni, pt[3]) : NULL;
            uint32_t stride = 0;
            if (st) for (size_t q = 0; q < ni; q++) { const uint32_t *d = vi[q].i; if ((d[0] & 0xffffu) == 71 && (d[0] >> 16) == 4 && d[1] == st[2] && d[2] == 6) stride = d[3]; }
            if (!stride || mult * stride != NVMTL_BUFOFF_GRAN) { snprintf(why, wn, "chain %%%u: multiplier %u for stride %u", o[2], mult, stride); goto out; }
            /* the chain without the pass: the old index */
            if (a >= ni || vi[a].wc != wc || memcmp(vi[a].i, o, 5 * 4) || vi[a].i[5] != add[3] || (wc > 6 && memcmp(vi[a].i + 6, o + 6, (wc - 6) * 4))) {
                snprintf(why, wn, "chain %%%u does not match the input's", o[2]); goto out; }
            chains++; a++; continue;
        }
        if (result_id(o) >= bound) continue;   /* new types, constants, pointer type and per-chain values (checked above) */
        if ((op == 32 && o[1] == push_ptr) || (op == 59 && o[2] == push_var)) {   /* moved: the same words as the input's */
            const uint32_t *d = find_def(vi, ni, op == 32 ? push_ptr : push_var);
            if (!d || (d[0] >> 16) != wc || memcmp(d, o, wc * 4)) { snprintf(why, wn, "push pointer or variable changed"); goto out; }
            continue;
        }
        /* skip the input's moved block, pointer and variable */
        while (a < ni && ((((vi[a].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 30) && vi[a].i[1] == push_block) || (((vi[a].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 32) && vi[a].i[1] == push_ptr) ||
                          (((vi[a].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 59) && vi[a].i[2] == push_var))) a++;
        if (a >= ni || vi[a].wc != wc || memcmp(vi[a].i, o, wc * 4)) { snprintf(why, wn, "output instruction %zu (op %u) is not the input's", k, op); goto out; }
        a++;
    }
    while (a < ni && ((((vi[a].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 30) && vi[a].i[1] == push_block) || (((vi[a].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 32) && vi[a].i[1] == push_ptr) ||
                      (((vi[a].i[0] & 0xffffu) == 59) && vi[a].i[2] == push_var))) a++;
    if (a != ni) { snprintf(why, wn, "input instruction %zu left over", a); goto out; }
    *nchains = chains; bad = 0;
out:
    free(vi); free(vo);
    return bad;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    int k = 1, verbose = 0; lower_ex_fn lower = NULL; free_fn xfree = NULL;
    static const char *const rname[] = { "module", "none", "shape", "length", "call", "chain", "other", "room" };
    unsigned rcount[8] = {0};
    uint32_t pcflags = NVMTL_PC_MERGE | NVMTL_PC_SET0 | NVMTL_PC_EXACT;
    for (; k < argc; k++) {
        if (!strcmp(argv[k], "-v")) verbose = 1;
        else if (!strcmp(argv[k], "--old-pc")) pcflags &= ~NVMTL_PC_EXACT;
        else break;
    }
    if (k + 1 < argc && !strcmp(argv[k], "--lower")) {
        void *h = dlopen(argv[k + 1], RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
        if (!h) { fprintf(stderr, "dlopen %s: %s\n", argv[k + 1], dlerror()); return 2; }
        lower = (lower_ex_fn)dlsym(h, "nvmtl_lower_buffer_addresses_ex"); xfree = (free_fn)dlsym(h, "nvmtl_translate_free");
        if (!lower || !xfree) { fprintf(stderr, "no nvmtl_lower_buffer_addresses_ex in %s\n", argv[k + 1]); return 2; }
        k += 2;
    }
    if (k + 1 >= argc) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s [--lower dylib] <outdir> <kernel.spv>...\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
    const char *dir = argv[k++];
    unsigned files = 0, converted = 0, bindings = 0, chains = 0, failed = 0, pcs = 0, kernels = 0;
    for (; k < argc; k++) {
        size_t n = 0; uint32_t *spv = slurp(argv[k], &n);
        if (!spv) { fprintf(stderr, "%s: unreadable\n", argv[k]); failed++; continue; }
        files++;
        int model = -1;   /* the entry point's execution model */
        for (size_t at = 5; at < n / 4;) { const uint32_t wc = spv[at] >> 16; if (!wc) break; if ((spv[at] & 0xffffu) == 15) { model = (int)spv[at + 1]; break; } at += wc; }
        if (model != 5) { free(spv); continue; }
        kernels++;
        if (lower) {
            uint8_t *o = NULL; size_t on = 0; uint32_t info[4] = {0}; char err[512] = {0};
            if (lower((const uint8_t *)spv, n, 2u | (2u << 8), &o, &on, info, err, sizeof err)) { free(spv); continue; }   /* refused: kept as-is by the plugin, no pass */
            free(spv); spv = malloc(on); memcpy(spv, o, on); n = on; xfree(o, on);
        }
        nvmtl_pc_table pc = {0}; size_t pn = 0;
        uint32_t *p = nvmtl_spirv_table_pc_ex(spv, n, 5, NVMTL_PC_TABLE_CS_OFFSET, NVMTL_PC_TABLE_MAX, pcflags, &pc, &pn);
        if (p) { free(spv); spv = p; n = pn; pcs++; } else pc.count = 0;
        spit(dir, argv[k], "pc", spv, n);
        nvmtl_bufoff m = {0}; size_t bn = 0;
        uint32_t *bo = nvmtl_spirv_bufoff_pc(spv, n, NVMTL_PC_TABLE_CS_OFFSET + 8 * pc.count, 256, 32, &m, &bn);
        for (unsigned r = 0; r < 8; r++) if (m.why >> r & 1u) rcount[r]++;
        if (verbose && m.why) {
            printf("keep %s: bindings %#x of %#x kept:", argv[k], m.have & ~m.mask, m.have);
            for (unsigned r = 0; r < 8; r++) if (m.why >> r & 1u) printf(" %s", rname[r]);
            if (m.op) printf(" (op %u)", m.op);
            printf("\n");
        }
        if (bo) {
            unsigned c = 0; char why[256] = {0};
            if (check(spv, n / 4, bo, bn / 4, &c, why, sizeof why)) { printf("FAIL %s: %s\n", argv[k], why); failed++; }
            else if (!c) { printf("FAIL %s: converted bindings %#x but no chain rewritten\n", argv[k], m.mask); failed++; }
            else { converted++; bindings += m.count; chains += c; printf("ok   %s: bindings %#x, %u chains, table-pc %u\n", argv[k], m.mask, c, pc.count); }
            spit(dir, argv[k], "bo", bo, bn);
            free(bo);
        }
        free(spv);
    }
    printf("bufoff_check: %u files, %u kernels, %u with table-pc, %u converted (%u bindings, %u chains): %u FAILED\n",
           files, kernels, pcs, converted, bindings, chains, failed);
    printf("bufoff_check: kernels with a binding or the module left as it was, by reason:");
    for (unsigned r = 0; r < 8; r++) printf(" %s %u", rname[r], rcount[r]);
    printf("\n");
    return failed ? 1 : 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// cl_img: OpenCL image path on the B580 (Geekbench's CL workloads are image-heavy): a 3x3 box filter image -> image,
// the same filter on float4 buffers (4x the bytes; a uchar4 buffer kernel fails AIR->SPIR-V translation), and image upload/readback. Measurement only.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -Wno-deprecated-declarations -o cl_img cl_img.c -framework OpenCL
#include <OpenCL/opencl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static double now_us(void) { return (double)mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e3; }
#define CK(x) do { cl_int e_ = (x); if (e_) { printf("%s -> %d\n", #x, e_); exit(1); } } while (0)
static const char *src =
	"__constant sampler_t s = CLK_NORMALIZED_COORDS_FALSE | CLK_ADDRESS_CLAMP_TO_EDGE | CLK_FILTER_NEAREST;\n"
	"__kernel void boxi(__read_only image2d_t in, __write_only image2d_t out) { int2 p = (int2)(get_global_id(0), get_global_id(1));\n"
	"  float4 a = 0; for (int y = -1; y <= 1; y++) for (int x = -1; x <= 1; x++) a += read_imagef(in, s, p + (int2)(x, y));\n"
	"  write_imagef(out, p, a / 9.0f); }\n"
	"__kernel void boxb(__global const float4 *in, __global float4 *out, int w, int h) { int x = get_global_id(0), y = get_global_id(1);\n"
	"  float4 a = 0; for (int dy = -1; dy <= 1; dy++) for (int dx = -1; dx <= 1; dx++) { int xx = clamp(x + dx, 0, w - 1), yy = clamp(y + dy, 0, h - 1);\n"
	"  a += in[yy * w + xx]; } out[y * w + x] = a / 9.0f; }\n";

static double prof(cl_event ev) {
	cl_ulong a = 0, b = 0; clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_START, 8, &a, NULL);
	clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_END, 8, &b, NULL); clReleaseEvent(ev); return (b - a) / 1e3;
}
int main(void) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	cl_platform_id plat; CK(clGetPlatformIDs(1, &plat, NULL));
	cl_device_id dev; CK(clGetDeviceIDs(plat, CL_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU, 1, &dev, NULL));
	cl_int err;
	cl_context ctx = clCreateContext(NULL, 1, &dev, NULL, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	cl_command_queue q = clCreateCommandQueue(ctx, dev, CL_QUEUE_PROFILING_ENABLE, &err); CK(err);
	cl_program p = clCreateProgramWithSource(ctx, 1, &src, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	if (clBuildProgram(p, 1, &dev, "", NULL, NULL)) { char log[8192] = ""; clGetProgramBuildInfo(p, dev, CL_PROGRAM_BUILD_LOG, sizeof log, log, NULL); printf("%s\n", log); return 1; }
	cl_kernel ki = clCreateKernel(p, "boxi", &err); CK(err);
	cl_kernel kb = clCreateKernel(p, "boxb", &err); CK(err);
	for (int W = 512; W <= 4096; W *= 2) {
		const int H = W; const size_t bytes = (size_t)W * H * 4;
		unsigned char *host = malloc(bytes); for (size_t i = 0; i < bytes; i++) host[i] = (unsigned char)(i * 2654435761u >> 24);
		cl_image_format f = {CL_RGBA, CL_UNORM_INT8};
		cl_image_desc d = {.image_type = CL_MEM_OBJECT_IMAGE2D, .image_width = W, .image_height = H};
		cl_mem ii = clCreateImage(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_ONLY, &f, &d, NULL, &err); CK(err);
		cl_mem io = clCreateImage(ctx, CL_MEM_WRITE_ONLY, &f, &d, NULL, &err); CK(err);
		cl_mem bi = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_ONLY, bytes * 4, NULL, &err); CK(err);
		cl_mem bo = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_WRITE_ONLY, bytes * 4, NULL, &err); CK(err);
		size_t org[3] = {0, 0, 0}, reg[3] = {W, H, 1};
		double t = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueWriteImage(q, ii, CL_TRUE, org, reg, 0, 0, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); double wi = now_us() - t;
		t = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, bi, CL_TRUE, 0, bytes, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); double wb = now_us() - t;
		CK(clSetKernelArg(ki, 0, sizeof ii, &ii)); CK(clSetKernelArg(ki, 1, sizeof io, &io));
		CK(clSetKernelArg(kb, 0, sizeof bi, &bi)); CK(clSetKernelArg(kb, 1, sizeof bo, &bo));
		CK(clSetKernelArg(kb, 2, sizeof(int), &W)); CK(clSetKernelArg(kb, 3, sizeof(int), &H));
		size_t g[2] = {W, H}, l[2] = {16, 16};
		double gi = 1e18, gb = 1e18, wwi = 1e18, wwb = 1e18;
		for (int r = 0; r < 6; r++) {
			cl_event e; t = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, ki, 2, NULL, g, l, 0, NULL, &e)); CK(clFinish(q)); double w = now_us() - t;
			double x = prof(e); if (r) { gi = fmin(gi, x); wwi = fmin(wwi, w); }
			t = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, kb, 2, NULL, g, l, 0, NULL, &e)); CK(clFinish(q)); w = now_us() - t;
			x = prof(e); if (r) { gb = fmin(gb, x); wwb = fmin(wwb, w); }
		}
		t = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueReadImage(q, io, CL_TRUE, org, reg, 0, 0, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); double ri = now_us() - t;
		t = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, bo, CL_TRUE, 0, bytes, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); double rb = now_us() - t;
		printf("%4dx%-4d: box image %7.0f us GPU (%7.0f wall) | box buffer %7.0f us GPU (%7.0f wall) | write img %6.0f buf %6.0f us | read img %6.0f buf %6.0f us\n",
		       W, H, gi, wwi, gb, wwb, wi, wb, ri, rb);
		clReleaseMemObject(ii); clReleaseMemObject(io); clReleaseMemObject(bi); clReleaseMemObject(bo); free(host);
	}
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/metal/cl_lat.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// cl_lat: OpenCL.framework round trip and small-kernel throughput on the B580 (Apple's CL over our Metal plugin),
// the OpenCL twin of mtl_lat's lat/inflight/small. Measurement only.
//   clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -Wno-deprecated-declarations -o cl_lat cl_lat.c -framework OpenCL
// Run on the hackintosh: NVMTL_ENABLE=1 ./cl_lat [n]   (CL_LAT_DEVICE=<i>: GPU i of the list it prints)
#include <OpenCL/opencl.h>
#include <mach/mach_time.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static mach_timebase_info_data_t tb;
static double now_us(void) { return (double)mach_absolute_time() * tb.numer / tb.denom / 1e3; }
static int dcmp(const void *a, const void *b) { double x = *(const double *)a, y = *(const double *)b; return x < y ? -1 : x > y; }
static void stats(const char *nm, double *v, int n) {
	qsort(v, n, 8, dcmp); double s = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += v[i];
	printf("  %-40s n %5d  p50 %8.1f  p90 %8.1f  p99 %8.1f  mean %8.1f us\n", nm, n, v[n / 2], v[n * 9 / 10], v[n * 99 / 100], s / n);
}
#define CK(x) do { cl_int e_ = (x); if (e_) { printf("%s -> %d\n", #x, e_); exit(1); } } while (0)

static const char *src =
	"__kernel void nop(__global uint *o) { if (get_global_id(0) == 0xffffffffu) o[0] = 1; }\n"
	"__kernel void saxpy(__global const float4 *x, __global float4 *y) { size_t i = get_global_id(0); y[i] = fma(x[i], (float4)(1.0001f), y[i]); }\n"
	"__kernel void sum(__global const float4 *x, __global float *o) { size_t i = get_global_id(0), n = get_global_size(0);\n"
	"  float4 a = 0; for (size_t k = i; k < n * 16; k += n) a += x[k]; o[i] = a.x + a.y + a.z + a.w; }\n";

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	mach_timebase_info(&tb);
	int N = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 1000;
	cl_platform_id plat; CK(clGetPlatformIDs(1, &plat, NULL));
	cl_device_id devs[8]; cl_uint nd = 0; CK(clGetDeviceIDs(plat, CL_DEVICE_TYPE_GPU, 8, devs, &nd));
	// Intel's GPU: CL_DEVICE_VENDOR_ID 0x8086, or else a CL_DEVICE_VENDOR naming Intel (Apple's OpenCL reports vendor ids
	// of its own, not PCI ones); without one, the first GPU (the only one on the test machine). CL_LAT_DEVICE=<n> picks GPU n.
	cl_device_id dev = NULL; int best = 0;
	for (cl_uint i = 0; i < nd; i++) {
		char name[256] = "", vendor[256] = ""; cl_uint vid = 0;
		clGetDeviceInfo(devs[i], CL_DEVICE_NAME, sizeof name, name, NULL);
		clGetDeviceInfo(devs[i], CL_DEVICE_VENDOR, sizeof vendor, vendor, NULL);
		clGetDeviceInfo(devs[i], CL_DEVICE_VENDOR_ID, sizeof vid, &vid, NULL);
		printf("GPU %u: %s, vendor \"%s\" 0x%x\n", i, name, vendor, vid);
		const int rank = vid == 0x8086 ? 3 : (strstr(vendor, "Intel") || strstr(vendor, "intel")) ? 2 : 1;
		if (rank > best) { dev = devs[i]; best = rank; }
	}
	const char *pickenv = getenv("CL_LAT_DEVICE");
	if (pickenv) { cl_uint n = (cl_uint)atoi(pickenv); dev = n < nd ? devs[n] : NULL; }
	if (!dev) { printf("no OpenCL GPU%s\n", pickenv ? " with that number" : ""); return 2; }
	if (best < 2 && !pickenv) printf("no GPU reports Intel as its vendor: measuring GPU 0\n");
	cl_int err;
	cl_context ctx = clCreateContext(NULL, 1, &dev, NULL, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	cl_command_queue q = clCreateCommandQueue(ctx, dev, CL_QUEUE_PROFILING_ENABLE, &err); CK(err);
	double t0 = now_us();
	cl_program p = clCreateProgramWithSource(ctx, 1, &src, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	err = clBuildProgram(p, 1, &dev, "", NULL, NULL);
	if (err) { char log[8192] = ""; clGetProgramBuildInfo(p, dev, CL_PROGRAM_BUILD_LOG, sizeof log, log, NULL); printf("build %d: %s\n", err, log); return 1; }
	printf("program built in %.0f ms\n", (now_us() - t0) / 1e3);
	cl_kernel kn = clCreateKernel(p, "nop", &err); CK(err);
	cl_kernel ks = clCreateKernel(p, "saxpy", &err); CK(err);
	cl_kernel ksum = clCreateKernel(p, "sum", &err); CK(err);
	cl_mem o = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, 4096, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	CK(clSetKernelArg(kn, 0, sizeof o, &o));
	size_t g = 32, l = 32;
	for (int i = 0; i < 50; i++) { CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, kn, 1, NULL, &g, &l, 0, NULL, NULL)); CK(clFinish(q)); }

	double *tot = calloc(N, 8), *enq = calloc(N, 8), *gpu = calloc(N, 8), *qs = calloc(N, 8), *se = calloc(N, 8), *ef = calloc(N, 8);
	for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
		cl_event ev;
		double a = now_us();
		CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, kn, 1, NULL, &g, &l, 0, NULL, &ev));
		double b = now_us();
		CK(clFinish(q));
		double c = now_us();
		cl_ulong tq = 0, ts = 0, tst = 0, te = 0;
		clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_QUEUED, 8, &tq, NULL);
		clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_SUBMIT, 8, &ts, NULL);
		clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_START, 8, &tst, NULL);
		clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_END, 8, &te, NULL);
		clReleaseEvent(ev);
		tot[i] = c - a; enq[i] = b - a; gpu[i] = (te - tst) / 1e3; qs[i] = (tst - tq) / 1e3; se[i] = (double)(ts - tq) / 1e3;
	}
	printf("[cl lat] 1 tiny kernel: clEnqueueNDRangeKernel + clFinish\n");
	stats("total", tot, N); stats("  clEnqueueNDRangeKernel call", enq, N);
	stats("  profiling QUEUED->SUBMIT", se, N); stats("  profiling QUEUED->START", qs, N); stats("  profiling START->END", gpu, N);

	printf("[cl inflight] M kernels enqueued, one clFinish\n");
	int ms[] = {1, 4, 16, 64, 256};
	for (int mi = 0; mi < 5; mi++) {
		int M = ms[mi], it = N / M < 10 ? 10 : N / M; double *per = calloc(it, 8);
		for (int i = 0; i < it; i++) {
			double a = now_us();
			for (int m = 0; m < M; m++) CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, kn, 1, NULL, &g, &l, 0, NULL, NULL));
			CK(clFinish(q));
			per[i] = (now_us() - a) / M;
		}
		char nm[64]; snprintf(nm, sizeof nm, "M=%d per kernel", M); stats(nm, per, it); free(per);
	}

	printf("[cl small] saxpy, device buffers: sync (enqueue+finish) and pipelined (finish every 100)\n");
	size_t sizes[] = {64 << 10, 256 << 10, 1 << 20, 4 << 20};
	for (int si = 0; si < 4; si++) {
		size_t S = sizes[si], n = S / 16, lw = 256;
		cl_mem x = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, S, NULL, &err); CK(err);
		cl_mem y = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, S, NULL, &err); CK(err);
		CK(clSetKernelArg(ks, 0, sizeof x, &x)); CK(clSetKernelArg(ks, 1, sizeof y, &y));
		for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, ks, 1, NULL, &n, &lw, 0, NULL, NULL));
		CK(clFinish(q));
		int K = 1000; double a = now_us();
		for (int i = 0; i < K; i++) { CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, ks, 1, NULL, &n, &lw, 0, NULL, NULL)); CK(clFinish(q)); }
		double s1 = (now_us() - a) / K;
		K = 4000; a = now_us();
		for (int i = 0; i < K; i++) { CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, ks, 1, NULL, &n, &lw, 0, NULL, NULL)); if (i % 100 == 99) CK(clFinish(q)); }
		CK(clFinish(q));
		double s2 = (now_us() - a) / K;
		printf("  S %5zu KB: sync %7.1f us/kernel (%6.0f /s) | pipelined %6.1f us/kernel (%7.0f /s)\n", S >> 10, s1, 1e6 / s1, s2, 1e6 / s2);
		clReleaseMemObject(x); clReleaseMemObject(y);
	}

	printf("[cl buffers] 64 MB sum kernel by allocation flag (profiling time, best of 5)\n");
	const size_t S = 64 << 20; size_t nsum = S / 16 / 16, lw = 256;
	cl_mem out = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, nsum * 4, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	struct { cl_mem_flags f; const char *nm; } fl[] = {{CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, "READ_WRITE"}, {CL_MEM_READ_ONLY, "READ_ONLY"},
		{CL_MEM_ALLOC_HOST_PTR | CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, "ALLOC_HOST_PTR"}, {CL_MEM_USE_HOST_PTR | CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, "USE_HOST_PTR"},
		{CL_MEM_COPY_HOST_PTR | CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, "COPY_HOST_PTR"}};
	void *host = NULL; posix_memalign(&host, 1 << 16, S); memset(host, 1, S);
	for (int fi = 0; fi < 5; fi++) {
		cl_mem b = clCreateBuffer(ctx, fl[fi].f, S, (fl[fi].f & (CL_MEM_USE_HOST_PTR | CL_MEM_COPY_HOST_PTR)) ? host : NULL, &err);
		if (err) { printf("  %-16s: create %d\n", fl[fi].nm, err); continue; }
		CK(clSetKernelArg(ksum, 0, sizeof b, &b)); CK(clSetKernelArg(ksum, 1, sizeof out, &out));
		double best = 1e18, bw = 1e18;
		for (int r = 0; r < 6; r++) {
			cl_event ev; double a = now_us();
			CK(clEnqueueNDRangeKernel(q, ksum, 1, NULL, &nsum, &lw, 0, NULL, &ev)); CK(clFinish(q));
			double w = now_us() - a;
			cl_ulong s0 = 0, s1 = 0; clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_START, 8, &s0, NULL);
			clGetEventProfilingInfo(ev, CL_PROFILING_COMMAND_END, 8, &s1, NULL); clReleaseEvent(ev);
			if (r) { if (s1 > s0) best = best < (s1 - s0) / 1e3 ? best : (s1 - s0) / 1e3; bw = bw < w ? bw : w; }
		}
		printf("  %-16s: %6.1f GB/s profiled (%7.0f us), %6.1f GB/s wall\n", fl[fi].nm, best < 1e17 ? S / (best * 1e3) : 0, best, S / (bw * 1e3));
		clReleaseMemObject(b);
	}
	// host <-> device transfer
	cl_mem d = clCreateBuffer(ctx, CL_MEM_READ_WRITE, S, NULL, &err); CK(err);
	double a = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, d, CL_TRUE, 0, S, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); double w1 = now_us() - a;
	a = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueWriteBuffer(q, d, CL_TRUE, 0, S, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); w1 = fmin(w1, now_us() - a);
	a = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, d, CL_TRUE, 0, S, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); double r1 = now_us() - a;
	a = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, d, CL_TRUE, 0, S, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); r1 = fmin(r1, now_us() - a);
	printf("  clEnqueueWriteBuffer 64 MB: %.1f GB/s, clEnqueueReadBuffer 64 MB: %.1f GB/s\n", S / (w1 * 1e3), S / (r1 * 1e3));
	double *sm = calloc(N, 8);
	for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { a = now_us(); CK(clEnqueueReadBuffer(q, d, CL_TRUE, 0, 64, host, 0, NULL, NULL)); sm[i] = now_us() - a; }
	stats("blocking clEnqueueReadBuffer 64 B", sm, N);
	return 0;
}

FILE: user/tests/metal/cl_xfer.c
