FILE: user/tools/ssv-watch/ssv-watch-lib.sh
================================================
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# ssv-watch-lib.sh: sourced by ssv-watch-agent.sh (the user's LaunchAgent) and ssv-watch-helper.sh (the only part that
# runs as root). Every path is fixed and absolute. The test overrides (ssvw_test_init) refuse to run as root, so nothing
# started as root can be pointed at another package, marker or system path.
# bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash): no associative arrays, no mapfile, no ${x,,}.

SSVW_LABEL=io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.ssv-watch
SSVW_ROOT="/Library/Application Support/IntelXe"
SSVW_PKG="$SSVW_ROOT/ssv"                                  # root-owned copy of the ssv-install.sh package
SSVW_DIR="$SSVW_ROOT/ssv-watch"                            # agent, helper, this file, ssv-watch.conf
SSVW_CONF="$SSVW_DIR/ssv-watch.conf"
SSVW_HELPER="$SSVW_DIR/ssv-watch-helper.sh"
SSVW_PLIST="/Library/LaunchAgents/$SSVW_LABEL.plist"
SSVW_LOGDIR=/Library/Logs/IntelXe
SSVW_LOCK="/var/run/$SSVW_LABEL.lock"                     # root's apply lock (shlock)
SSVW_SLE=/System/Library/Extensions/NVMTLDriver.bundle     # the component in the booted snapshot
SSVW_MARK=/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/ssv-component.plist    # written by ssv-install.sh --apply (data volume)
SSVW_LIBCOPY=/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriverLib.bundle     # NMXAccel's fallback when the system copy is absent
# WebKit's GPU process sandbox: the reason the component exists (it may map code from /System/Library/Extensions only)
SSVW_WKSB_LIST="/System/Cryptexes/OS/System/Library/Frameworks/WebKit.framework/Versions/A/Resources/com.apple.WebKit.GPUProcess.sb
/System/Library/Frameworks/WebKit.framework/Versions/A/Resources/com.apple.WebKit.GPUProcess.sb"
SSVW_CUR_BUILD=$(/usr/bin/sw_vers -buildVersion 2>/dev/null)
SSVW_CUR_VERS=$(/usr/bin/sw_vers -productVersion 2>/dev/null)
SSVW_STRICT=1          # ownership/permission checks and a pinned SHA256SUMS (off only in test mode)
SSVW_TEST=""; SSVW_SIM=""; SSVW_TDIR=""; SSVW_SIM_PENDING=""; SSVW_WS_OVERRIDE=""
SSVW_LOG=""; SSVW_ECHO=""; SSVW_WHO=ssv-watch

ssvw_log() {
    local line; line="$(/bin/date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') [$SSVW_WHO $$] $*"
    [ -z "$SSVW_LOG" ] || printf '%s\n' "$line" >>"$SSVW_LOG" 2>/dev/null
    [ -z "$SSVW_ECHO" ] || printf '%s\n' "$line" >&2
}
ssvw_is_sha()   { local re='^[0-9a-f]{64}$'; [[ $1 =~ $re ]]; }
ssvw_is_build() { local re='^[0-9]{2}[A-Z][0-9]{1,6}[a-z]?$'; [[ $1 =~ $re ]]; }
ssvw_major()    { printf '%s' "${1%%[A-Z]*}"; }                # 24H32 -> 24 (Darwin 24 = macOS 15)
ssvw_sha()      { /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 "$1" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/cut -c1-64; }
ssvw_boottime() { /usr/sbin/sysctl -n kern.boottime 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^\{ sec = ([0-9]+).*/\1/'; }
ssvw_mode_ok()  {   # $1: path; root-owned and not writable by group or others
    [ -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    [ "$(/usr/bin/stat -f %u "$1")" = 0 ] || return 1
    local m; m=$(/usr/bin/stat -f %Lp "$1"); m=${m: -2}
    case "${m:0:1}" in 2|3|6|7) return 1;; esac; case "${m:1:1}" in 2|3|6|7) return 1;; esac
}

# Logging. Root: /Library/Logs/IntelXe/ssv-watch.log (dir root:wheel 755, so no user can plant a link there). User: the
# per-user file install-service.sh pre-creates there, else ~/Library/Logs/IntelXe/ssv-watch-agent.log. Test: the temp dir.
ssvw_log_init() {
    SSVW_WHO=$1; SSVW_LOG=""
    if [ -n "$SSVW_TEST" ]; then SSVW_LOG="$SSVW_TDIR/$1.log"; SSVW_ECHO=1; return 0; fi
    if [ "$(/usr/bin/id -u)" = 0 ]; then
        [ -L "$SSVW_LOGDIR" ] && return 0
        /bin/mkdir -p "$SSVW_LOGDIR" && /usr/sbin/chown root:wheel "$SSVW_LOGDIR" && /bin/chmod 755 "$SSVW_LOGDIR" || return 0
        SSVW_LOG="$SSVW_LOGDIR/ssv-watch.log"
        [ ! -L "$SSVW_LOG" ] || /bin/rm -f "$SSVW_LOG"
        if [ -f "$SSVW_LOG" ] && [ "$(/usr/bin/stat -f %z "$SSVW_LOG")" -gt 1048576 ]; then /bin/mv -f "$SSVW_LOG" "$SSVW_LOG.1"; fi
        /usr/bin/touch "$SSVW_LOG" && /usr/sbin/chown root:wheel "$SSVW_LOG" && /bin/chmod 644 "$SSVW_LOG"
    else
        local f; f="$SSVW_LOGDIR/ssv-watch-agent.$(/usr/bin/id -un).log"
        if [ -f "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ] && [ -w "$f" ]; then SSVW_LOG=$f
        else /bin/mkdir -p "$HOME/Library/Logs/IntelXe" 2>/dev/null; SSVW_LOG="$HOME/Library/Logs/IntelXe/ssv-watch-agent.log"; fi
        if [ -f "$SSVW_LOG" ] && [ "$(/usr/bin/stat -f %z "$SSVW_LOG")" -gt 1048576 ]; then : >"$SSVW_LOG"; fi
    fi
}

# Test mode: simulate a situation without touching /System. $1 scenario, $2 a private temp dir, $3 package dir (optional).
# Only the agent's checks and the helper's dry-run use it; the helper's apply needs root, and root refuses this.
ssvw_test_init() {
    [ "$(/usr/bin/id -u)" != 0 ] || { echo "ssv-watch: test mode is refused as root" >&2; exit 2; }
    [ -d "$2" ] && [ ! -L "$2" ] && [ "$(/usr/bin/stat -f %u "$2")" = "$(/usr/bin/id -u)" ] || { echo "ssv-watch: bad test dir $2" >&2; exit 2; }
    SSVW_TEST=1; SSVW_SIM=$1; SSVW_TDIR=$2; SSVW_STRICT=0
    if [ -n "${3:-}" ]; then SSVW_PKG=$3; SSVW_CONF="$SSVW_TDIR/no-such.conf"; fi   # a conf pins the installed package only
    local fake="$SSVW_TDIR/sle/NVMTLDriver.bundle"
    case "$SSVW_SIM" in
        ok) ;;                                                            # the real system, read-only
        missing|major|noaccel|sandbox|pending) SSVW_SLE=$fake;;          # a path that does not exist
        hash) /bin/mkdir -p "$fake/Contents/MacOS"; printf 'not the recorded plugin\n' >"$fake/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver"; SSVW_SLE=$fake;;
        build) ;;                                                         # build changed, component still in place
        nomarker) SSVW_MARK="$SSVW_TDIR/no-such-marker.plist";;
        *) echo "ssv-watch: unknown test scenario '$SSVW_SIM' (ok missing hash build major noaccel sandbox pending nomarker)" >&2; exit 2;;
    esac
    case "$SSVW_SIM" in
        noaccel) SSVW_WS_OVERRIDE=0;;
        pending) SSVW_SIM_PENDING=1;;
        sandbox) printf '(version 1)\n(allow file-map-executable\n    (subpath "/System/Library/Frameworks")\n    (subpath "/usr/lib"))\n' >"$SSVW_TDIR/GPUProcess.sb"
                 SSVW_WKSB_LIST="$SSVW_TDIR/GPUProcess.sb";;
    esac
}

# ssv-watch.conf: written by install-service.sh, root:wheel 644. Parsed, never sourced; unknown keys and bad values ignored.
ssvw_load_conf() {
    CONF_SUMS=""; CONF_PLUGIN=""; CONF_MAJOR=""; CONF_TESTED=""
    [ -f "$SSVW_CONF" ] || return 1
    if [ "$SSVW_STRICT" = 1 ]; then ssvw_mode_ok "$SSVW_CONF" || return 2; fi
    local k v b re='^[0-9]{2}$'
    while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
        case "$k" in
            PKG_SUMS_SHA256) ssvw_is_sha "$v" && CONF_SUMS=$v;;
            PKG_PLUGIN_SHA256) ssvw_is_sha "$v" && CONF_PLUGIN=$v;;
            PKG_DARWIN_MAJOR) [[ $v =~ $re ]] && CONF_MAJOR=$v;;
            TESTED_BUILDS) for b in $v; do ssvw_is_build "$b" && CONF_TESTED="$CONF_TESTED $b"; done;;
        esac
    done <"$SSVW_CONF"
    return 0
}

ssvw_read_marker() {   # 1: no marker (component not installed), 2: marker unreadable
    MK_BUILD=""; MK_SHA=""; MK_DATE=""; MK_MTIME=0
    [ -f "$SSVW_MARK" ] || return 1
    MK_BUILD=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract build raw -o - "$SSVW_MARK" 2>/dev/null)
    MK_SHA=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract sha raw -o - "$SSVW_MARK" 2>/dev/null)
    MK_DATE=$(/usr/bin/plutil -extract date raw -o - "$SSVW_MARK" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/tr -cd '0-9T:-')
    MK_MTIME=$(/usr/bin/stat -f %m "$SSVW_MARK")
    ssvw_is_build "$MK_BUILD" && ssvw_is_sha "$MK_SHA" || return 2
}

# STATE: none | badmarker | ok | missing | hash | build | pending
ssvw_state() {
    STATE=""; SLE_SHA=""
    ssvw_read_marker; local rc=$?
    case $rc in 1) STATE=none; return 0;; 2) STATE=badmarker; return 0;; esac
    case "$SSVW_SIM" in   # simulated updates: same major with a new build, or the next major
        build) SSVW_CUR_BUILD="$(ssvw_major "$MK_BUILD")Z999";;
        major) SSVW_CUR_BUILD="$(( $(ssvw_major "$MK_BUILD") + 1 ))A100";;
    esac
    if [ ! -e "$SSVW_SLE" ]; then STATE=missing
    else
        SLE_SHA=$(ssvw_sha "$SSVW_SLE/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver")
        if [ "$SLE_SHA" != "$MK_SHA" ]; then STATE=hash
        elif [ "$SSVW_CUR_BUILD" != "$MK_BUILD" ]; then STATE=build
        else STATE=ok; fi
    fi
    # re-applied on this build after this boot: the new snapshot is blessed but not booted yet
    if { [ "$STATE" = missing ] || [ "$STATE" = hash ]; } && [ "$MK_BUILD" = "$SSVW_CUR_BUILD" ]; then
        local bt; bt=$(ssvw_boottime)
        if [ -n "$SSVW_SIM_PENDING" ] || { [ -z "$SSVW_TEST" ] && [ -n "$bt" ] && [ "$MK_MTIME" -gt "$bt" ]; }; then STATE=pending; fi
    fi
    return 0
}

# The staged package: complete, unmodified, root-owned, and the very build that the marker says was installed.
ssvw_pkg_check() {
    PKG_FAIL=""; PKG_SHA=""
    local p="$SSVW_PKG" s="$SSVW_PKG/SHA256SUMS" out bad x
    pf() { PKG_FAIL="$PKG_FAIL- $*
"; }
    if [ ! -d "$p" ] || [ -L "$p" ] || [ ! -f "$s" ]; then pf "paket yok: $p"; return 1; fi
    if [ "$SSVW_STRICT" = 1 ]; then
        for x in /Library "/Library/Application Support" "$SSVW_ROOT" "$SSVW_DIR" "$p"; do ssvw_mode_ok "$x" || pf "root'a ait değil ya da yazılabilir: $x"; done
        x=$(/usr/bin/find "$p" "$SSVW_DIR" \( ! -user 0 -o -perm -0020 -o -perm -0002 \) -print 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -3)
        [ -z "$x" ] || pf "root'a ait değil ya da yazılabilir: $(printf '%s' "$x" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' ' ')"
        if [ -z "$CONF_SUMS" ]; then pf "ssv-watch.conf'ta sabitlenmiş SHA256SUMS özeti yok"
        elif [ "$(ssvw_sha "$s")" != "$CONF_SUMS" ]; then pf "SHA256SUMS kurulumdakinden farklı (sabitlenmiş özet tutmuyor)"; fi
    elif [ -n "$CONF_SUMS" ] && [ "$(ssvw_sha "$s")" != "$CONF_SUMS" ]; then pf "SHA256SUMS sabitlenmiş özetle tutmuyor"; fi
    x=$(/usr/bin/find "$p" -type l -print 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -1); [ -z "$x" ] || pf "pakette sembolik bağ var: $x"
    bad=$(/usr/bin/grep -Ev '^[0-9a-f]{64}  \*?[A-Za-z0-9._+/-]+$' "$s" | /usr/bin/head -1)
    [ -z "$bad" ] || pf "SHA256SUMS biçimi bozuk: $bad"
    /usr/bin/grep -Eq '  \*?(/|(.*/)?\.\.(/|$))' "$s" && pf "SHA256SUMS paketin dışına işaret ediyor"
    for x in ssv-install.sh sigcheck system-layout/NVMTLDriver.bundle/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver; do
        /usr/bin/grep -Eq "^[0-9a-f]{64}  \\*?$x\$" "$s" || pf "SHA256SUMS içinde yok: $x"; done
    [ -z "$PKG_FAIL" ] || return 1
    out=$(cd "$p" && /usr/bin/shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS 2>&1); local rc=$?
    bad=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | /usr/bin/grep -v ': OK$' | /usr/bin/head -3)
    [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -z "$bad" ] || pf "dosyalar SHA256SUMS ile tutmuyor: $(printf '%s' "$bad" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' ' ')"
    bad=$(/usr/bin/comm -13 <(/usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[0-9a-f]{64}  \*?//' "$s" | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort) \
                             <(cd "$p" && /usr/bin/find . -type f ! -path ./SHA256SUMS | /usr/bin/sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C /usr/bin/sort) | /usr/bin/head -3)
    [ -z "$bad" ] || pf "SHA256SUMS'ta olmayan dosyalar: $(printf '%s' "$bad" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' ' ')"
    PKG_SHA=$(ssvw_sha "$p/system-layout/NVMTLDriver.bundle/Contents/MacOS/NVMTLDriver")
    [ -z "$CONF_PLUGIN" ] || [ "$PKG_SHA" = "$CONF_PLUGIN" ] || pf "paketteki eklenti kurulumda sabitlenenden farklı"
    [ -z "$MK_SHA" ] || [ "$PKG_SHA" = "$MK_SHA" ] || pf "hazırdaki paket (${PKG_SHA:0:12}) kurulu olan bileşen değil (${MK_SHA:0:12}): paketi install-service.sh update-package ile yenileyin"
    [ -z "$PKG_FAIL" ]
}

# Does this macOS still take the component? Hard failures (COMPAT_FAIL) mean: say so, do not offer to install.
ssvw_ws_metal() {   # Metal devices WindowServer opened on NMXAccel (= the plugin, here the /Library copy, works on this build)
    if [ -n "$SSVW_WS_OVERRIDE" ]; then printf '%s' "$SSVW_WS_OVERRIDE"; return; fi
    /usr/sbin/ioreg -r -c NMXAccel -l -w0 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/awk '
        /\+-o / { c = $0; sub(/.*\+-o /, "", c); sub(/ .*/, "", c) }
        /"IOUserClientCreator" = "pid [0-9]+, WindowServer"/ { if (c == "IOAccelDevice2" || c == "IOAccelSharedUserClient2") n++ }
        END { print n + 0 }'
}
ssvw_compat() {
    COMPAT_FAIL=""; COMPAT_WARN=""; COMPAT_OK=""; TESTED=no
    cf() { COMPAT_FAIL="$COMPAT_FAIL- $*
"; }; cw() { COMPAT_WARN="$COMPAT_WARN- $*
"; }; co() { COMPAT_OK="$COMPAT_OK- $*
"; }
    local cur pkg ior from ws sb f
    cur=$(ssvw_major "$SSVW_CUR_BUILD"); pkg=${CONF_MAJOR:-$(ssvw_major "$MK_BUILD")}
    if [ "$cur" != "$pkg" ]; then cf "macOS ana sürümü değişti (Darwin $pkg -> $cur, build $SSVW_CUR_BUILD): bu paket o macOS için yapılmadı"
    else co "aynı macOS ana sürümü (Darwin $cur)"; fi
    case " $CONF_TESTED $MK_BUILD " in *" $SSVW_CUR_BUILD "*) TESTED=yes;; esac
    ior=$(/usr/sbin/ioreg -r -c NMXAccel -d 1 -w0 2>/dev/null)
    from=$(printf '%s\n' "$ior" | /usr/bin/awk -F'= ' '/"NMXMetalPluginFrom"/{gsub(/"/, "", $2); print $2; exit}')
    if [ -z "$ior" ]; then cf "NMXAccel yüklü değil: kext bu macOS'ta yüklenmedi"
    elif [ -z "$from" ]; then cf "bu NMXAccel /System/Library/Extensions'ı yoklamıyor (NMXMetalPluginFrom yok)"
    else co "NMXAccel yüklü (eklenti şu an: $from)"; fi
    ws=$(ssvw_ws_metal)
    if [ "${ws:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then co "masaüstü Metal bu build'de çalışıyor (WindowServer'ın $ws B580 Metal istemcisi var)"
    else cf "WindowServer'ın B580 Metal aygıtı yok: eklenti bu build'de masaüstünde de çalışmıyor"; fi
    [ -d "$SSVW_LIBCOPY" ] && co "/Library yedeği NVMTLDriverLib.bundle yerinde" || cw "/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriverLib.bundle yok: sistem kopyası giderse yedek yok"
    sb=""; while IFS= read -r f; do [ -n "$f" ] && [ -f "$f" ] && { sb=$f; break; }; done <<EOF
$SSVW_WKSB_LIST
EOF
    if [ -z "$sb" ]; then cw "WebKit GPU süreci sandbox profili bulunamadı: denetlenemedi"
    elif /usr/bin/perl -0777 -ne 'my $ok = 0; while (/\(allow\s+file-map-executable\b((?:[^()]++|\((?1)\))*)\)/g) { $ok = 1 if $1 =~ m{"/System/Library/Extensions"} } exit($ok ? 0 : 1)' "$sb"
    then co "Safari'nin GPU süreci /System/Library/Extensions'tan kod yükleyebiliyor"
    else cf "Safari'nin GPU süreci sandbox'ı artık /System/Library/Extensions'tan kod yüklemeye izin vermiyor: bileşen Safari'ye yaramaz"; fi
    [ -z "$COMPAT_FAIL" ]
}

# The Khronos Vulkan loader for the B580 (notes)

So that ordinary Vulkan applications (linked against `libvulkan.1.dylib`, no driver path of their own) find the B580,
the Khronos loader is installed where the LunarG Vulkan SDK puts it on macOS, with an ICD manifest for our ANV. The
Metal plugin does not use it: it loads ANV by its own path.

- **Loader:** [Vulkan-Loader](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Loader) tag `vulkan-sdk-1.4.363.0`, **Apache-2.0**,
  built unmodified: CMake `Release`, `CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=x86_64`, `CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0`,
  `CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local`, `BUILD_TESTS=OFF`, `APPLE_STATIC_LOADER=OFF`, against Vulkan-Headers of the same tag.
- **vulkaninfo:** Vulkan-Tools, same tag (Apache-2.0), same settings.
- **ICD manifest:** `intel_icd.x86_64.json` -> `/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libvulkan_intel.dylib` (not a portability
  driver, so no `VK_KHR_portability_enumeration` is needed).

Installed by `install.sh` (`sudo ./install.sh`, `--undo` restores what was there) from a package directory with
`lib/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib`, `icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json` and `bin/vulkaninfo`:

| File | Installed as |
|---|---|
| loader | `/usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib` (+ `libvulkan.1.dylib`, `libvulkan.dylib` symlinks) |
| ICD manifest | `/usr/local/share/vulkan/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json` |
| vulkaninfo | `/usr/local/bin/vulkaninfo` |

`vk_compute.c` is the check: an app with no driver path, a compute dispatch on the first discrete GPU the loader reports.

The binaries are not in this repository. Whoever passes them on must include the Apache-2.0 licence text and the
loader's NOTICE.



================================================
FILE: user/vulkan-loader/install.sh
================================================
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# install.sh: the Khronos Vulkan loader (Vulkan-Loader vulkan-sdk-1.4.363.0, Apache-2.0) and the B580 ANV ICD manifest,
# in the same places the LunarG Vulkan SDK uses on macOS, so ordinary Vulkan apps find the B580 the standard way:
#   /usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib (+ libvulkan.1.dylib, libvulkan.dylib symlinks)   the loader
#   /usr/local/share/vulkan/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json   -> /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libvulkan_intel.dylib (unchanged)
#   /usr/local/bin/vulkaninfo                              Vulkan-Tools vulkaninfo, same tag
# The Metal plug-in (NVMTLDriver.bundle) keeps loading ANV by its own path; nothing here touches /Library/GPUBundles.
#   sudo ./install.sh          install (files that already exist are moved to *.before-vkloader first)
#   sudo ./install.sh --undo   remove what this script installed and put any *.before-vkloader back
set -euo pipefail
H=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
L=/usr/local/lib; I=/usr/local/share/vulkan/icd.d; B=/usr/local/bin
FILES="$L/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib $L/libvulkan.1.dylib $L/libvulkan.dylib $I/intel_icd.x86_64.json $B/vulkaninfo"
if [ "${1:-}" = --undo ]; then
	for f in $FILES; do
		rm -f "$f"
		if [ -e "$f.before-vkloader" ] || [ -L "$f.before-vkloader" ]; then mv -f "$f.before-vkloader" "$f"; fi
	done
	echo "removed the B580 Vulkan loader install"; exit 0
fi
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "run with sudo"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$L" "$I" "$B"
for f in $FILES; do
	if { [ -e "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; } && [ ! -e "$f.before-vkloader" ] && [ ! -L "$f.before-vkloader" ]; then mv "$f" "$f.before-vkloader"; fi
done
install -m 755 -o root -g wheel "$H/lib/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib" "$L/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib"
ln -sfh libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib "$L/libvulkan.1.dylib"
ln -sfh libvulkan.1.dylib "$L/libvulkan.dylib"
install -m 644 -o root -g wheel "$H/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json" "$I/intel_icd.x86_64.json"
install -m 755 -o root -g wheel "$H/bin/vulkaninfo" "$B/vulkaninfo"
echo "installed: $(shasum -a 256 "$L/libvulkan.1.4.363.dylib" | cut -c1-16) loader, ICD -> $(grep library_path "$I/intel_icd.x86_64.json" | cut -d'"' -f4)"
echo "check: vulkaninfo --summary"

FILE: user/vulkan-loader/vk_compute.c

// vk_compute: an ordinary Vulkan app linked against the Khronos loader (libvulkan.1.dylib), no driver path anywhere.
// Instance (no portability enumeration), every physical device the loader reports, then on the first discrete GPU
// (or argv[1] index): device + compute queue, a host-visible storage buffer, a compute dispatch writing
// data[i] = i*3 + 7 over N uints, fence wait, check on the CPU.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
//   clang -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -I<headers> vk_compute.c -L<loader lib> -lvulkan -Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/lib
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>

#define CHECK(call)                                                                          \
	do {                                                                                 \
		VkResult r_ = (call);                                                        \
		if (r_ != VK_SUCCESS) { printf("%s -> VkResult %d\nFAIL\n", #call, r_); exit(1); } \
	} while (0)

// GLSL 450: layout(local_size_x = 64) in; layout(binding = 0) buffer B { uint d[]; };
//           void main() { uint x = gl_GlobalInvocationID.x; d[x] = x * 3u + 7u; }
static const uint32_t spirv[] = {
	0x07230203, 0x00010000, 0, 23, 0,
	(2 << 16) | 17, 1,                                    // OpCapability Shader
	(3 << 16) | 14, 0, 1,                                 // OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450
	(6 << 16) | 15, 5, 1, 0x6E69616D, 0, 2,               // OpEntryPoint GLCompute %1 "main" %2
	(6 << 16) | 16, 1, 17, 64, 1, 1,                      // OpExecutionMode %1 LocalSize 64 1 1
	(4 << 16) | 71, 2, 11, 28,                            // OpDecorate %2 BuiltIn GlobalInvocationId
	(4 << 16) | 71, 8, 6, 4,                              // OpDecorate %8 ArrayStride 4
	(5 << 16) | 72, 9, 0, 35, 0,                          // OpMemberDecorate %9 0 Offset 0
	(3 << 16) | 71, 9, 3,                                 // OpDecorate %9 BufferBlock
	(4 << 16) | 71, 11, 34, 0,                            // OpDecorate %11 DescriptorSet 0
	(4 << 16) | 71, 11, 33, 0,                            // OpDecorate %11 Binding 0
	(2 << 16) | 19, 3,                                    // %3 = OpTypeVoid
	(3 << 16) | 33, 4, 3,                                 // %4 = OpTypeFunction %3
	(4 << 16) | 21, 5, 32, 0,                             // %5 = OpTypeInt 32 0
	(4 << 16) | 23, 6, 5, 3,                              // %6 = OpTypeVector %5 3
	(4 << 16) | 32, 7, 1, 6,                              // %7 = OpTypePointer Input %6
	(4 << 16) | 59, 7, 2, 1,                              // %2 = OpVariable %7 Input
	(3 << 16) | 29, 8, 5,                                 // %8 = OpTypeRuntimeArray %5
	(3 << 16) | 30, 9, 8,                                 // %9 = OpTypeStruct %8
	(4 << 16) | 32, 10, 2, 9,                             // %10 = OpTypePointer Uniform %9
	(4 << 16) | 59, 10, 11, 2,                            // %11 = OpVariable %10 Uniform
	(4 << 16) | 32, 12, 2, 5,                             // %12 = OpTypePointer Uniform %5
	(4 << 16) | 32, 13, 1, 5,                             // %13 = OpTypePointer Input %5
	(4 << 16) | 43, 5, 14, 0,                             // %14 = OpConstant %5 0
	(4 << 16) | 43, 5, 15, 3,                             // %15 = OpConstant %5 3
	(4 << 16) | 43, 5, 16, 7,                             // %16 = OpConstant %5 7
	(5 << 16) | 54, 3, 1, 0, 4,                           // %1 = OpFunction %3 None %4
	(2 << 16) | 248, 17,                                  // %17 = OpLabel
	(5 << 16) | 65, 13, 18, 2, 14,                        // %18 = OpAccessChain %13 %2 %14
	(4 << 16) | 61, 5, 19, 18,                            // %19 = OpLoad %5 %18
	(5 << 16) | 132, 5, 20, 19, 15,                       // %20 = OpIMul %5 %19 %15
	(5 << 16) | 128, 5, 21, 20, 16,                       // %21 = OpIAdd %5 %20 %16
	(6 << 16) | 65, 12, 22, 11, 14, 19,                   // %22 = OpAccessChain %12 %11 %14 %19
	(3 << 16) | 62, 22, 21,                               // OpStore %22 %21
	(1 << 16) | 253,                                      // OpReturn
	(1 << 16) | 56,                                       // OpFunctionEnd
};

static const char *type_name(VkPhysicalDeviceType t)
{
	switch (t) {
	case VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_INTEGRATED_GPU: return "integrated";
	case VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU: return "discrete";
	case VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_VIRTUAL_GPU: return "virtual";
	case VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_CPU: return "cpu";
	default: return "other";
	}
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	const uint32_t N = 1u << 20; // 1M uints, 16384 workgroups of 64
	uint32_t loader_ver = 0;
	CHECK(vkEnumerateInstanceVersion(&loader_ver));
	printf("loader instance version %u.%u.%u\n", VK_API_VERSION_MAJOR(loader_ver), VK_API_VERSION_MINOR(loader_ver),
	       VK_API_VERSION_PATCH(loader_ver));

	VkApplicationInfo app = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_APPLICATION_INFO, .pApplicationName = "vk_compute",
				 .apiVersion = VK_API_VERSION_1_3};
	VkInstanceCreateInfo ici = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INSTANCE_CREATE_INFO, .pApplicationInfo = &app};
	VkInstance instance;
	CHECK(vkCreateInstance(&ici, NULL, &instance));

	uint32_t n = 0;
	CHECK(vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices(instance, &n, NULL));
	VkPhysicalDevice pds[8];
	if (n > 8) n = 8;
	CHECK(vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices(instance, &n, pds));
	printf("%u physical device(s)\n", n);
	int pick = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : -1;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		VkPhysicalDeviceDriverProperties drv = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_DRIVER_PROPERTIES};
		VkPhysicalDeviceProperties2 p2 = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_PROPERTIES_2, .pNext = &drv};
		vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2(pds[i], &p2);
		VkPhysicalDeviceProperties *p = &p2.properties;
		printf("  [%u] %s  %04x:%04x %s  api %u.%u.%u  driver %s (%s)\n", i, p->deviceName, p->vendorID, p->deviceID,
		       type_name(p->deviceType), VK_API_VERSION_MAJOR(p->apiVersion), VK_API_VERSION_MINOR(p->apiVersion),
		       VK_API_VERSION_PATCH(p->apiVersion), drv.driverName, drv.driverInfo);
		if (pick < 0 && p->deviceType == VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU) pick = (int)i;
	}
	if (pick < 0 || (uint32_t)pick >= n) { printf("no discrete GPU\nFAIL\n"); return 1; }
	VkPhysicalDevice pd = pds[pick];

	uint32_t nq = 0;
	vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(pd, &nq, NULL);
	VkQueueFamilyProperties qf[16];
	if (nq > 16) nq = 16;
	vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties(pd, &nq, qf);
	uint32_t qfi = UINT32_MAX;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nq; i++)
		if (qf[i].queueFlags & VK_QUEUE_COMPUTE_BIT) { qfi = i; break; }
	if (qfi == UINT32_MAX) { printf("no compute queue\nFAIL\n"); return 1; }

	float prio = 1.0f;
	VkDeviceQueueCreateInfo qci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_QUEUE_CREATE_INFO, .queueFamilyIndex = qfi,
				       .queueCount = 1, .pQueuePriorities = &prio};
	VkDeviceCreateInfo dci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_CREATE_INFO, .queueCreateInfoCount = 1,
				  .pQueueCreateInfos = &qci};
	VkDevice dev;
	CHECK(vkCreateDevice(pd, &dci, NULL, &dev));
	printf("vkCreateDevice ok on [%d], queue family %u\n", pick, qfi);
	VkQueue q;
	vkGetDeviceQueue(dev, qfi, 0, &q);

	VkBufferCreateInfo bci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO, .size = (VkDeviceSize)N * 4,
				  .usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_STORAGE_BUFFER_BIT};
	VkBuffer buf;
	CHECK(vkCreateBuffer(dev, &bci, NULL, &buf));
	VkMemoryRequirements mr;
	vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements(dev, buf, &mr);
	VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties mp;
	vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties(pd, &mp);
	uint32_t mt = UINT32_MAX;
	const VkMemoryPropertyFlags want = VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < mp.memoryTypeCount; i++)
		if ((mr.memoryTypeBits & (1u << i)) && (mp.memoryTypes[i].propertyFlags & want) == want) { mt = i; break; }
	if (mt == UINT32_MAX) { printf("no host-visible coherent memory type\nFAIL\n"); return 1; }
	VkMemoryAllocateInfo mai = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MEMORY_ALLOCATE_INFO, .allocationSize = mr.size,
				    .memoryTypeIndex = mt};
	VkDeviceMemory mem;
	CHECK(vkAllocateMemory(dev, &mai, NULL, &mem));
	CHECK(vkBindBufferMemory(dev, buf, mem, 0));
	uint32_t *map;
	CHECK(vkMapMemory(dev, mem, 0, VK_WHOLE_SIZE, 0, (void **)&map));
	memset(map, 0xcd, (size_t)N * 4);

	VkShaderModuleCreateInfo smci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SHADER_MODULE_CREATE_INFO, .codeSize = sizeof spirv,
					 .pCode = spirv};
	VkShaderModule sm;
	CHECK(vkCreateShaderModule(dev, &smci, NULL, &sm));
	VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding b = {.binding = 0, .descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER,
					  .descriptorCount = 1, .stageFlags = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT};
	VkDescriptorSetLayoutCreateInfo dslci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO,
						 .bindingCount = 1, .pBindings = &b};
	VkDescriptorSetLayout dsl;
	CHECK(vkCreateDescriptorSetLayout(dev, &dslci, NULL, &dsl));
	VkPipelineLayoutCreateInfo plci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO, .setLayoutCount = 1,
					   .pSetLayouts = &dsl};
	VkPipelineLayout pl;
	CHECK(vkCreatePipelineLayout(dev, &plci, NULL, &pl));
	VkComputePipelineCreateInfo cpci = {
		.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMPUTE_PIPELINE_CREATE_INFO,
		.stage = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_INFO, .stage = VK_SHADER_STAGE_COMPUTE_BIT,
			  .module = sm, .pName = "main"},
		.layout = pl};
	VkPipeline pipe;
	CHECK(vkCreateComputePipelines(dev, VK_NULL_HANDLE, 1, &cpci, NULL, &pipe));

	VkDescriptorPoolSize ps = {.type = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER, .descriptorCount = 1};
	VkDescriptorPoolCreateInfo dpci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_INFO, .maxSets = 1,
					   .poolSizeCount = 1, .pPoolSizes = &ps};
	VkDescriptorPool dp;
	CHECK(vkCreateDescriptorPool(dev, &dpci, NULL, &dp));
	VkDescriptorSetAllocateInfo dsai = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_ALLOCATE_INFO, .descriptorPool = dp,
					    .descriptorSetCount = 1, .pSetLayouts = &dsl};
	VkDescriptorSet ds;
	CHECK(vkAllocateDescriptorSets(dev, &dsai, &ds));
	VkDescriptorBufferInfo dbi = {.buffer = buf, .offset = 0, .range = VK_WHOLE_SIZE};
	VkWriteDescriptorSet w = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_WRITE_DESCRIPTOR_SET, .dstSet = ds, .dstBinding = 0,
				  .descriptorCount = 1, .descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER, .pBufferInfo = &dbi};
	vkUpdateDescriptorSets(dev, 1, &w, 0, NULL);

	VkCommandPoolCreateInfo cpi = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_INFO, .queueFamilyIndex = qfi};
	VkCommandPool cp;
	CHECK(vkCreateCommandPool(dev, &cpi, NULL, &cp));
	VkCommandBufferAllocateInfo cbai = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_ALLOCATE_INFO, .commandPool = cp,
					    .level = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_LEVEL_PRIMARY, .commandBufferCount = 1};
	VkCommandBuffer cb;
	CHECK(vkAllocateCommandBuffers(dev, &cbai, &cb));
	VkCommandBufferBeginInfo cbbi = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_BEGIN_INFO,
					 .flags = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_USAGE_ONE_TIME_SUBMIT_BIT};
	CHECK(vkBeginCommandBuffer(cb, &cbbi));
	vkCmdBindPipeline(cb, VK_PIPELINE_BIND_POINT_COMPUTE, pipe);
	vkCmdBindDescriptorSets(cb, VK_PIPELINE_BIND_POINT_COMPUTE, pl, 0, 1, &ds, 0, NULL);
	vkCmdDispatch(cb, N / 64, 1, 1);
	VkMemoryBarrier mb = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MEMORY_BARRIER, .srcAccessMask = VK_ACCESS_SHADER_WRITE_BIT,
			      .dstAccessMask = VK_ACCESS_HOST_READ_BIT};
	vkCmdPipelineBarrier(cb, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_COMPUTE_SHADER_BIT, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_HOST_BIT, 0, 1, &mb, 0, NULL, 0,
			     NULL);
	CHECK(vkEndCommandBuffer(cb));

	VkFenceCreateInfo fci = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_CREATE_INFO};
	VkFence f;
	CHECK(vkCreateFence(dev, &fci, NULL, &f));
	VkSubmitInfo si = {.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SUBMIT_INFO, .commandBufferCount = 1, .pCommandBuffers = &cb};
	struct timespec t0, t1;
	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &t0);
	CHECK(vkQueueSubmit(q, 1, &si, f));
	CHECK(vkWaitForFences(dev, 1, &f, VK_TRUE, 5ull * 1000 * 1000 * 1000));
	clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &t1);

	uint32_t bad = 0, first_bad = UINT32_MAX;
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < N; i++)
		if (map[i] != i * 3u + 7u) { if (first_bad == UINT32_MAX) first_bad = i; bad++; }
	printf("dispatch %u x 64 invocations: %.3f ms submit->fence, %u/%u values wrong", N / 64,
	       (t1.tv_sec - t0.tv_sec) * 1e3 + (t1.tv_nsec - t0.tv_nsec) / 1e6, bad, N);
	if (bad) printf(" (first at %u: 0x%08x)", first_bad, map[first_bad]);
	printf("\n%s\n", bad ? "FAIL" : "PASS");

	vkDestroyFence(dev, f, NULL);
	vkDestroyCommandPool(dev, cp, NULL);
	vkDestroyDescriptorPool(dev, dp, NULL);
	vkDestroyPipeline(dev, pipe, NULL);
	vkDestroyPipelineLayout(dev, pl, NULL);
	vkDestroyDescriptorSetLayout(dev, dsl, NULL);
	vkDestroyShaderModule(dev, sm, NULL);
	vkUnmapMemory(dev, mem);
	vkFreeMemory(dev, mem, NULL);
	vkDestroyBuffer(dev, buf, NULL);
	vkDestroyDevice(dev, NULL);
	vkDestroyInstance(instance, NULL);
	return bad ? 1 : 0;
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// xemac: the user-space side of IntelXe.kext's xe interface. Mesa's ANV (and the tests) call these in place of
// open()/ioctl()/mmap() on a Linux DRM render node.
//
// Contract with the kext (kernel/IntelXe, class IntelXe, user client type 0):
//  - xemac_open() opens /dev/null read-only for a real file descriptor number and binds it to an IOServiceOpen()
//    connection; the other calls look the fd up in that table.
//  - xemac_ioctl(fd, request, arg) passes `request` exactly as Mesa's include/drm-uapi headers encode it on macOS
//    (<sys/ioccom.h>: IOC_IN/IOC_OUT, IOCPARM_LEN(request) bytes, group 'd', DRM_COMMAND_BASE + DRM_XE_* or a DRM core
//    number such as DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE). External method 0 takes scalars {request, arg address}; the kext copies
//    IOCPARM_LEN bytes in and out of the caller's memory itself and returns {errno} as one scalar output.
//    Pointers inside the structures (drm_xe_device_query.data, drm_xe_exec.syncs, ...) are user addresses of the
//    calling task. Returns 0, or -1 with errno set, like ioctl(2).
//  - DRM_IOCTL_XE_GEM_MMAP_OFFSET returns offset = (u64)handle << 12. xemac_mmap(addr, len, prot, flags, fd, offset)
//    maps memory type (offset >> 12) with IOConnectMapMemory64 (kIOMapAnywhere unless MAP_FIXED, write-combined for
//    VRAM and WC BOs as the kext reports through the map's cache mode). xemac_munmap() undoes it.
//  - Absolute timeouts (drm_syncobj_wait / drm_syncobj_timeline_wait timeout_nsec, xe user-fence waits with ABSTIME)
//    are compared with the kernel's mach_absolute_time() in nanoseconds, i.e. CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW. xemac_ioctl converts
//    values computed from CLOCK_MONOTONIC to that clock before passing them on (INT64_MAX stays "forever", 0 = poll).
//    Likewise DRM_XE_DEVICE_QUERY_ENGINE_CYCLES: the kext samples cpu_timestamp on CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW whatever clockid
//    asks for, and xemac_ioctl moves it to the requested clock.
//  - External method 1 returns the PCI identity as scalars {vendor, device, revision, subsystem vendor, subsystem
//    device, bus, device, function} for xemac_pci_info(), which stands in for libdrm's drmGetDevice2().
//  - Object fds (syncobj fds, sync files, PRIME): the kext cannot create a file descriptor, so for SYNCOBJ_HANDLE_TO_FD
//    and PRIME_HANDLE_TO_FD xemac_ioctl opens the clone device /dev/intelxeobj (INTELXE_OBJ_DEVICE) and passes that fd IN
//    args->fd; the kext binds the object to that open (one object per minor) and the fd is the caller's, as Linux's.
//    The imports and DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_OBJ_INFO resolve an fd in the caller's fd table. Only when the kernel reports
//    INTELXE_CAP_FD_OBJECTS (xemac_fd_sharing); otherwise the ioctls go to the kext unchanged (ENOTTY), as before.
//  - XEMAC_FAKE=1 in the environment: no kext. A canned Battlemage G21 device (the values measured on the real card:
//    graphics 20.01, 20 Xe-cores, 8 EU each, 12 GB VRAM with a 256 MB CPU-visible window) answers device queries,
//    BOs are anonymous memory, VM binds succeed, execs complete at once. For bring-up of Mesa without the hardware.
//    BOs and syncobjs are shared by all fake devices of the process; object fds are AF_UNIX socketpair ends standing in
//    for opens of /dev/intelxeobj (released on their last close; process-local). XEMAC_FAKE_FDS=0: a kernel without them.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

int xemac_open(void);
int xemac_close(int fd);
bool xemac_is_fd(int fd);
int xemac_ioctl(int fd, unsigned long request, void *arg);
void *xemac_mmap(void *addr, size_t len, int prot, int flags, int fd, uint64_t offset);
int xemac_munmap(void *addr, size_t len);
// xemac_munmap, but the range is left reserved (PROT_NONE anonymous memory) as VK_MEMORY_UNMAP_RESERVE_BIT_EXT asks,
// without a hole in between: on macOS 15 an mmap(MAP_FIXED) over a range that is partly unmapped kills the process
// with EXC_GUARD (GUARD_TYPE_VIRT_MEMORY, DEALLOC_GAP).
int xemac_munmap_reserve(void *addr, size_t len);

// fd sharing (uapi/intelxe_drm.h, INTELXE_CAP_FD_OBJECTS): which object fds the device offers, as XEMAC_FD_* bits; 0 for a
// kernel without them (and with XEMAC_FDS=0 in the environment). Asked once per device fd.
#define XEMAC_FD_SYNC 1u  // DRM syncobj fds and sync files: SYNCOBJ_HANDLE_TO_FD / SYNCOBJ_FD_TO_HANDLE
#define XEMAC_FD_PRIME 2u // BO fds: PRIME_HANDLE_TO_FD / PRIME_FD_TO_HANDLE
unsigned xemac_fd_sharing(int fd);
// The size of the BO an object fd holds (DRM_IOCTL_INTELXE_OBJ_INFO), where Linux reads lseek(dmabuf, 0, SEEK_END): an
// object fd is a character device here, whose SEEK_END is 0. -1 with errno set when obj_fd holds no BO.
int64_t xemac_obj_size(int fd, int obj_fd);

struct xemac_pci_info {
	uint16_t vendor, device, subvendor, subdevice;
	uint8_t revision, bus, dev, func;
};
int xemac_pci_info(int fd, struct xemac_pci_info *info);

// The GPU's sensors as one sample: the render GT's clocks and SLPC range, the package and VRAM temperatures, the card
// and package energy (microjoules) and average power, the power limits (struct intelxe_sensors, ../uapi/
// intelxe_sensors.h; the kext's debug.intelxe.sensors_raw sysctl, which anyone may read). Level Zero sysman over NEO
// reads its frequency, power and temperature data through this. With XEMAC_FAKE=1: canned values of the fake
// Battlemage (act 2100 MHz, request 2400, RP0 2850, RPn 400, RPe 1800, range 1200-2850; package 47 C, VRAM 52 C; the
// card's energy grows by 40 W of real time, the package's by 25 W; card PL1 190 W on, PL2 250 W off, package PL1
// 150 W on, crit 300 W), XEMAC_FAKE_SENSORS=0: a kext without the sysctl. fd -1: no device fd needed (the sysctl is
// global; XEMAC_FAKE decides fake or not). Returns 0, or -1 with errno: EBADF (not an xemac fd), ENOENT (a kext without
// debug.intelxe.sensors_raw), EPROTO (a struct version this xemac does not know). Fields the kext did not fill (an
// older, shorter struct) are 0.
struct intelxe_sensors;
int xemac_sensors(int fd, struct intelxe_sensors *out);

// Version 2 of the sample (a kext with engine activity) also carries per-engine busy and total ticks
// (INTELXE_SENSORS_ENGINES); the fake Battlemage's: RCS0 busy half the time, BCS0 a tenth, CCS0 a quarter, 19.2 MHz.

// The GPU frequency range SLPC runs with (Level Zero sysman's zesFrequencySetRange through min_freq / max_freq):
// which 0 = the floor (the kext's debug.intelxe.slpc_min), 1 = the ceiling (slpc_max); mhz 0 = the default (1200 MHz
// floor, RP0 ceiling), else clamped by the kext to RPn..RP0. The kext sends it to the GuC at once and keeps it for
// every later SLPC start. Root only. Returns 0, or -1 with errno: EPERM (not root), ENOENT (a kext without live range
// control, i.e. before sensors_raw version 2: its slpc_min/max only applied at SLPC start), EINVAL, EBADF.
// XEMAC_FAKE=1: the canned range changes instead (for any user, unless XEMAC_FAKE_ROOT=0).
int xemac_freq_set(int fd, int which, uint32_t mhz);
// Whether xemac_freq_set can work for this process: 1 when the kext has live range control and the process is root
// (fake: unless XEMAC_FAKE_ROOT=0), else 0.
int xemac_freq_can_set(int fd);

#define XEMAC_METHOD_IOCTL 0
#define XEMAC_METHOD_PCI_INFO 1

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

// xemac_drm.c: libdrm's entry points used by Mesa (libdrm/xf86drm.h), as DRM ioctls through xemac_ioctl().
// Return conventions are libdrm's: most calls return the ioctl result (0, or -1 with errno), the waits -errno.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

#include <errno.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "xemac.h"
#include "xf86drm.h"

int drmIoctl(int fd, unsigned long request, void *arg)
{
	int ret;
	do {
		ret = xemac_is_fd(fd) ? xemac_ioctl(fd, request, arg) : ioctl(fd, request, arg);
	} while (ret == -1 && (errno == EINTR || errno == EAGAIN));
	return ret;
}

int drmGetCap(int fd, uint64_t capability, uint64_t *value)
{
	struct drm_get_cap cap = {.capability = capability};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_GET_CAP, &cap);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	*value = cap.value;
	return 0;
}

drmVersionPtr drmGetVersion(int fd)
{
	struct drm_version v = {0};
	if (drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_VERSION, &v))
		return NULL;
	drmVersionPtr r = calloc(1, sizeof(*r));
	if (!r)
		return NULL;
	r->name = calloc(1, v.name_len + 1), r->date = calloc(1, v.date_len + 1), r->desc = calloc(1, v.desc_len + 1);
	v.name = r->name, v.date = r->date, v.desc = r->desc;
	if (!r->name || !r->date || !r->desc || drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_VERSION, &v)) {
		drmFreeVersion(r);
		return NULL;
	}
	r->version_major = v.version_major, r->version_minor = v.version_minor;
	r->version_patchlevel = v.version_patchlevel;
	r->name_len = strlen(r->name), r->date_len = strlen(r->date), r->desc_len = strlen(r->desc);
	return r;
}

void drmFreeVersion(drmVersionPtr version)
{
	if (!version)
		return;
	free(version->name);
	free(version->date);
	free(version->desc);
	free(version);
}

// One allocation, like libdrm: the device, its node table and strings, and the PCI info.
static drmDevicePtr device_from_fd(int fd)
{
	struct xemac_pci_info pci;
	if (xemac_pci_info(fd, &pci))
		return NULL;
	struct block {
		drmDevice dev;
		char *nodes[DRM_NODE_MAX];
		char render[sizeof(XEMAC_RENDER_NODE)];
		char empty;
		drmPciBusInfo bus;
		drmPciDeviceInfo info;
	} *b = calloc(1, sizeof(*b));
	if (!b)
		return NULL;
	for (int i = 0; i < DRM_NODE_MAX; i++)
		b->nodes[i] = &b->empty;
	memcpy(b->render, XEMAC_RENDER_NODE, sizeof(XEMAC_RENDER_NODE));
	b->nodes[DRM_NODE_RENDER] = b->render;
	b->bus = (drmPciBusInfo){.domain = 0, .bus = pci.bus, .dev = pci.dev, .func = pci.func};
	b->info = (drmPciDeviceInfo){.vendor_id = pci.vendor, .device_id = pci.device, .subvendor_id = pci.subvendor,
				     .subdevice_id = pci.subdevice, .revision_id = pci.revision};
	b->dev = (drmDevice){.nodes = b->nodes, .available_nodes = 1 << DRM_NODE_RENDER, .bustype = DRM_BUS_PCI,
			     .businfo.pci = &b->bus, .deviceinfo.pci = &b->info};
	return &b->dev;
}

int drmGetDevice2(int fd, uint32_t flags, drmDevicePtr *device)
{
	(void)flags;
	if (!xemac_is_fd(fd))
		return -ENODEV;
	*device = device_from_fd(fd);
	return *device ? 0 : -errno;
}

int drmGetDevices2(uint32_t flags, drmDevicePtr devices[], int max_devices)
{
	(void)flags;
	int fd = xemac_open();
	if (fd < 0)
		return 0; // no IntelXe service: no devices
	int count = 0;
	if (devices && max_devices > 0) {
		devices[0] = device_from_fd(fd);
		count = devices[0] ? 1 : 0;
	} else {
		count = 1;
	}
	xemac_close(fd);
	return count;
}

void drmFreeDevice(drmDevicePtr *device)
{
	if (device) {
		free(*device);
		*device = NULL;
	}
}

void drmFreeDevices(drmDevicePtr devices[], int count)
{
	for (int i = 0; devices && i < count; i++)
		drmFreeDevice(&devices[i]);
}

int drmDevicesEqual(drmDevicePtr a, drmDevicePtr b)
{
	if (!a || !b || a->bustype != b->bustype)
		return 0;
	return a->bustype == DRM_BUS_PCI && !memcmp(a->businfo.pci, b->businfo.pci, sizeof(drmPciBusInfo));
}

int drmGetNodeTypeFromFd(int fd)
{
	if (!xemac_is_fd(fd)) {
		errno = ENODEV;
		return -1;
	}
	return DRM_NODE_RENDER;
}

char *drmGetDeviceNameFromFd2(int fd)
{
	return xemac_is_fd(fd) ? strdup(XEMAC_RENDER_NODE) : NULL;
}

char *drmGetRenderDeviceNameFromFd(int fd)
{
	return drmGetDeviceNameFromFd2(fd);
}

int drmPrimeHandleToFD(int fd, uint32_t handle, uint32_t flags, int *prime_fd)
{
	struct drm_prime_handle args = {.handle = handle, .flags = flags, .fd = -1};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_PRIME_HANDLE_TO_FD, &args);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	*prime_fd = args.fd;
	return 0;
}

int drmPrimeFDToHandle(int fd, int prime_fd, uint32_t *handle)
{
	struct drm_prime_handle args = {.fd = prime_fd};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_PRIME_FD_TO_HANDLE, &args);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	*handle = args.handle;
	return 0;
}

int drmSyncobjCreate(int fd, uint32_t flags, uint32_t *handle)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_create args = {.flags = flags};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_CREATE, &args);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	*handle = args.handle;
	return 0;
}

int drmSyncobjDestroy(int fd, uint32_t handle)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_destroy args = {.handle = handle};
	return drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_DESTROY, &args);
}

static int handle_to_fd(int fd, uint32_t handle, uint32_t flags, int *out)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_handle args = {.handle = handle, .flags = flags, .fd = -1};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_HANDLE_TO_FD, &args);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	*out = args.fd;
	return 0;
}

static int fd_to_handle(int fd, int obj_fd, uint32_t flags, uint32_t *handle)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_handle args = {.handle = handle ? *handle : 0, .flags = flags, .fd = obj_fd};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_FD_TO_HANDLE, &args);
	if (ret)
		return ret;
	if (handle)
		*handle = args.handle;
	return 0;
}

int drmSyncobjHandleToFD(int fd, uint32_t handle, int *obj_fd)
{
	return handle_to_fd(fd, handle, 0, obj_fd);
}

int drmSyncobjFDToHandle(int fd, int obj_fd, uint32_t *handle)
{
	return fd_to_handle(fd, obj_fd, 0, handle);
}

int drmSyncobjImportSyncFile(int fd, uint32_t handle, int sync_file_fd)
{
	return fd_to_handle(fd, sync_file_fd, DRM_SYNCOBJ_FD_TO_HANDLE_FLAGS_IMPORT_SYNC_FILE, &handle);
}

int drmSyncobjExportSyncFile(int fd, uint32_t handle, int *sync_file_fd)
{
	return handle_to_fd(fd, handle, DRM_SYNCOBJ_HANDLE_TO_FD_FLAGS_EXPORT_SYNC_FILE, sync_file_fd);
}

int drmSyncobjWait(int fd, uint32_t *handles, unsigned num_handles, int64_t timeout_nsec, unsigned flags,
		   uint32_t *first_signaled)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_wait args = {.handles = (uintptr_t)handles, .timeout_nsec = timeout_nsec,
					.count_handles = num_handles, .flags = flags};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_WAIT, &args);
	if (ret < 0)
		return -errno;
	if (first_signaled)
		*first_signaled = args.first_signaled;
	return ret;
}

int drmSyncobjReset(int fd, const uint32_t *handles, uint32_t handle_count)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_array args = {.handles = (uintptr_t)handles, .count_handles = handle_count};
	return drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_RESET, &args);
}

int drmSyncobjSignal(int fd, const uint32_t *handles, uint32_t handle_count)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_array args = {.handles = (uintptr_t)handles, .count_handles = handle_count};
	return drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_SIGNAL, &args);
}

int drmSyncobjTimelineSignal(int fd, const uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, uint32_t handle_count)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_timeline_array args = {.handles = (uintptr_t)handles, .points = (uintptr_t)points,
						  .count_handles = handle_count};
	return drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE_SIGNAL, &args);
}

int drmSyncobjTimelineWait(int fd, uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, unsigned num_handles, int64_t timeout_nsec,
			   unsigned flags, uint32_t *first_signaled)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_timeline_wait args = {.handles = (uintptr_t)handles, .points = (uintptr_t)points,
						 .timeout_nsec = timeout_nsec, .count_handles = num_handles,
						 .flags = flags};
	int ret = drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_TIMELINE_WAIT, &args);
	if (ret < 0)
		return -errno;
	if (first_signaled)
		*first_signaled = args.first_signaled;
	return ret;
}

int drmSyncobjQuery2(int fd, uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, uint32_t handle_count, uint32_t flags)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_timeline_array args = {.handles = (uintptr_t)handles, .points = (uintptr_t)points,
						  .count_handles = handle_count, .flags = flags};
	return drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_QUERY, &args);
}

int drmSyncobjQuery(int fd, uint32_t *handles, uint64_t *points, uint32_t handle_count)
{
	return drmSyncobjQuery2(fd, handles, points, handle_count, 0);
}

int drmSyncobjTransfer(int fd, uint32_t dst_handle, uint64_t dst_point, uint32_t src_handle, uint64_t src_point,
		       uint32_t flags)
{
	struct drm_syncobj_transfer args = {.src_handle = src_handle, .dst_handle = dst_handle,
					    .src_point = src_point, .dst_point = dst_point, .flags = flags};
	return drmIoctl(fd, DRM_IOCTL_SYNCOBJ_TRANSFER, &args);
}

// xf86drm.h for macOS: the part of libdrm's API that Mesa's ANV uses, implemented by xemac_drm.c on top of xemac.
// Names, types and return conventions follow libdrm 2.4 (MIT); only the IntelXe render node exists.

#pragma once

#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus

#endif

#define DRM_NODE_PRIMARY 0
#define DRM_NODE_CONTROL 1
#define DRM_NODE_RENDER 2

#define DRM_BUS_USB 1
#define DRM_BUS_PLATFORM 2
#define DRM_BUS_HOST1X 3

FILE: videotoolbox/build.sh

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build.sh: the IntelXe AV1 VideoToolbox decoder against FFmpeg's shared libraries (FFmpeg 9.0.2 + ffmpeg/apply-patches.sh, LGPL-2.1-or-later,
# configured by ffmpeg/configure-shared.sh with install names in /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl), with the direct Vulkan Video
# path (vtdirect.c, vtdirect_h264.c, vtdirect_hevc.c, vtdirect_av1.c, vtdirect_vp9.c; INTELXEDEC_DIRECT), and vtdec (tests/vtdec.m).
#   FFMPEG_INSTALL=<ffmpeg install prefix> MESA_INCLUDE=<mesa>/include [OUT=dir] [ANV=<path of libvulkan_intel.dylib>] build.sh
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
OUT=${OUT:-$HERE/build}
: "${FFMPEG_INSTALL:?}" "${MESA_INCLUDE:?}"
SDK=${SDK:-/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX26.5.sdk}
mkdir -p "$OUT"
DEF=""; [ -n "${ANV:-}" ] && DEF="-DINTELXE_ANV=\"$ANV\""
xcrun --sdk "$SDK" clang -isysroot "$SDK" -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -g -Wall -Wno-deprecated-declarations \
  -fvisibility=hidden $DEF -I"$FFMPEG_INSTALL/include" -I"$MESA_INCLUDE" -dynamiclib \
  -install_name /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libintelxeav1dec.dylib -o "$OUT/libintelxeav1dec.dylib" "$HERE/intelxeav1.c" "$HERE/vtdirect.c" "$HERE/vtdirect_h264.c" "$HERE/vtdirect_hevc.c" "$HERE/vtdirect_av1.c" "$HERE/vtdirect_vp9.c" \
  -L"$FFMPEG_INSTALL/lib" -lavcodec -lavutil \
  -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework IOSurface
cp -p "$FFMPEG_INSTALL/lib/libavcodec.63.dylib" "$FFMPEG_INSTALL/lib/libavutil.61.dylib" "$OUT/" 2>/dev/null || {
  cp -pL "$FFMPEG_INSTALL/lib/libavcodec.63.dylib" "$OUT/libavcodec.63.dylib"; cp -pL "$FFMPEG_INSTALL/lib/libavutil.61.dylib" "$OUT/libavutil.61.dylib"; }
xcrun --sdk "$SDK" clang -isysroot "$SDK" -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -Wall -Wno-deprecated-declarations -fobjc-arc -o "$OUT/vtdec" "$HERE/tests/vtdec.m" \
  -framework Foundation -framework AVFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework Metal
# the debug map (source and object paths of this machine) stays in the .dSYM next to it, not in the shipped library
strip -S "$OUT/libintelxeav1dec.dylib"
for f in libintelxeav1dec.dylib libavcodec.63.dylib libavutil.61.dylib vtdec; do codesign -f -s - "$OUT/$f"; done

FILE: videotoolbox/vtdirect.h
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vtdirect.h: the direct Vulkan Video decode path of the IntelXe decoders (vtdirect.c): a sample goes to
// vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR with our own parsing (vtdirect_h264.c, vtdirect_hevc.c, vtdirect_av1.c, vtdirect_vp9.c) instead of libavcodec's decoder and
// Vulkan hwaccel.
// The pictures are AVFrames of a libavutil Vulkan frames context made like libavcodec's, so the decoder's copy into
// the IOSurface (gpu_copy in intelxeav1.c), its deferral and its emit queue work on them unchanged.
#ifndef VTDIRECT_H
#define VTDIRECT_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
#include <libavutil/buffer.h>
#include <libavutil/frame.h>

typedef struct {
	PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr gipa;
	VkInstance inst; VkPhysicalDevice pd; VkDevice d;
	int dec_family, dec_queues;       // the video decode queue family and its queue count
	int inline_params;                // VK_KHR_video_maintenance2 (inline session parameters) is enabled
	AVBufferRef *avdev;               // libavutil's context of the device (frames contexts, queue and frame locks)
} VtdDevice;

typedef struct Vtd Vtd;

enum { VTD_PICTURE = 0, VTD_NO_PICTURE = 1, VTD_FALLBACK = -1, VTD_ERROR = -2 };

typedef struct {
	uint64_t pictures, errors, no_ref_skips, gaps, redundant_slices;
	uint64_t skipped;                          // HEVC: RASL pictures not decoded (as libavcodec skips them)
	uint64_t parse_ns, record_ns, submit_ns;   // CPU time spent parsing, recording and submitting (wall clock)
	uint64_t bytes;                            // bitstream bytes handed to the hardware
} VtdStats;

// A direct H.264 decoder for a stream with this avcC, or NULL (why says why: a stream or device the path does not
// cover; libavcodec decodes it then)
Vtd *vtd_open_h264(const VtdDevice *dev, const uint8_t *avcc, size_t n, char *why, size_t whyn);
// the same for an HEVC stream with this hvcC (Main / Main 10 / Main Still Picture, 4:2:0, 8 or 10 bits)
Vtd *vtd_open_hevc(const VtdDevice *dev, const uint8_t *hvcc, size_t n, char *why, size_t whyn);
// the same for an AV1 stream with this av1C (Main profile, 4:2:0, 8 or 10 bits; its configOBUs must carry the sequence
// header). A sample is a temporal unit: every frame in it is decoded (hidden alt-ref frames included), the shown one
// (or a show_existing_frame's picture) is handed back; a sample that shows nothing is answered with its last decoded
// frame, as the libavcodec path answers it.
Vtd *vtd_open_av1(const VtdDevice *dev, const uint8_t *av1c, size_t n, char *why, size_t whyn);
// the same for a VP9 stream with this vpcC (Profile 0 8-bit or Profile 2 10-bit, 4:2:0). A sample is a frame or a
// superframe: every frame in it is decoded (hidden alt-refs, intra-only frames), the shown one (or a
// show_existing_frame's picture) is handed back; a sample that shows nothing is answered with its last decoded frame.
// The pictures are made at the first decoded frame's size (a larger pool when frames grow: size changes stay in the
// session); a frame of another bit depth, or larger than the device decodes: VTD_FALLBACK.
Vtd *vtd_open_vp9(const VtdDevice *dev, const uint8_t *vpcc, size_t n, char *why, size_t whyn);
// One sample (an access unit, length-prefixed NAL units). VTD_PICTURE: *pic is a new reference to the decoded picture
// (its decode submitted; the frame's timeline semaphore orders whatever reads it next). VTD_NO_PICTURE: nothing to
// show (parameter sets; an HEVC RASL picture that is not decoded). VTD_FALLBACK: from here on the stream needs libavcodec (vtd_why); nothing was submitted.
// VTD_ERROR: a damaged sample, or a picture whose references are missing (not decoded).
int vtd_decode(Vtd *v, const uint8_t *data, size_t n, AVFrame **pic);
// forget the references (a seek: FinishDelayedFrames)
void vtd_flush(Vtd *v);
// the colour range the stream's SPS states: 1 full, 0 video, -1 not stated
int vtd_full_range(const Vtd *v);
const char *vtd_why(const Vtd *v);
const VtdStats *vtd_stats(const Vtd *v);
// waits for its decodes and frees everything
void vtd_close(Vtd *v);
#endif

FILE: videotoolbox/vtdirect_av1.h
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vtdirect_av1.h: the AV1 side of the direct Vulkan Video decode path (vtdirect.c): the sequence header, every frame
// header (tiles, quantizer, segmentation, loop filter, CDEF, loop restoration, global motion, film grain), the tile
// groups, the eight reference frame slots with their order hints and saved parameters, show_existing_frame, and the
// DPB slot each picture is decoded into, for Main profile 4:2:0 streams (8 or 10 bits). No Vulkan calls and no FFmpeg:
// the Std structures only, so it is tested off the GPU (tests/av1parse_test.c, against golden files made from FFmpeg's
// trace_headers, tests/av1/mkgolden.py).
//
// Written from the AV1 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification (v1.0.0 with Errata 1) 5.3-5.12 / 6.8 / 7.20 /
// 7.21 and the Vulkan specification (VK_KHR_video_decode_av1). Where the hardware must see the same values on both
// paths it follows libavcodec 9.0.2's AV1 decoder (av1dec.c, cbs_av1*.c) and Vulkan hwaccel (vulkan_av1.c), not only
// the specification:
// - DPB slots: a picture is decoded into the lowest slot no reference frame slot holds (vulkan_av1.c frame_id);
// - the references passed are those the seven ref_frame_idx[] name, once each, in that order; for KEY and INTRA_ONLY
//   frames ref_frame_idx[] is all 0 (libavcodec's frame header is zeroed), so reference slot 0's picture is passed (if
//   there is one) and OrderHints[] / RefFrameSignBias are those of slot 0's order hint; the hardware does not read
//   references for intra frames;
// - OrderHints[0] and SavedOrderHints[0] are 0; a reference's SavedOrderHints are its own OrderHints[]; the current
//   picture's reference info has no SavedOrderHints (zeros);
// - the loop filter deltas of a frame with loop_filter_delta_enabled = 0 are the defaults (the specification keeps the
//   ones loaded from primary_ref_frame); they matter only to a later frame that loads them;
// - CDEF secondary strengths and segmentation feature values are passed as coded (3 is not turned into 4, no clip);
// - film grain: update_grain = 0 loads the referenced frame's parameters (apply_grain and film_grain_params_ref_idx
//   included, the new grain_seed kept); the Std flags carry no update_grain;
// - SkipModeFrame[] is derived even when skip_mode_present is 0 (frames with reference_select and order hints), and
//   only when every reference has a picture;
// - after a flush the reference slots keep their order hints (libavcodec's frames keep them) but no picture.
#ifndef VTDIRECT_AV1_H
#define VTDIRECT_AV1_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_av1std.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_av1std_decode.h>

#define AV1D_SLOTS 9            // DPB slots: the eight reference frames and the current picture (the B580's maxDpbSlots)
#define AV1D_MAX_TILES 256      // libavcodec's MAX_TILES (the largest any level allows)
#define AV1D_MAX_FRAMES 16      // frame headers in one temporal unit

enum {
	AV1D_PICTURE = 0,       // the sample has frames to decode or to show
	AV1D_NO_PICTURE = 1,    // a sample without frame headers (sequence header, metadata, temporal delimiter)
	AV1D_UNSUPPORTED = -1,  // a stream the direct path does not cover (av1d_why says what): libavcodec takes over
	AV1D_ERROR = -2,        // a damaged sample (the state is as before it)
};

typedef struct {
	StdVideoAV1SequenceHeader std;      // pColorConfig / pTimingInfo point at the two below (av1d_seq_fix)
	StdVideoAV1ColorConfig color;
	StdVideoAV1TimingInfo timing;
	int ops;                            // operating_points_cnt_minus_1 + 1
	uint16_t op_idc[32]; uint8_t level[32], tier[32];
	int decoder_model_info_present, buffer_removal_time_length, frame_presentation_time_length;
	uint8_t decoder_model_present_for_op[32];
	int bit_depth;
	int unsupported;                    // why the direct path cannot decode it (0: it can)
	uint8_t raw[256]; size_t rawn;      // the OBU payload, to recognise a repeated identical sequence header
} Av1dSeq;

// a reference frame slot: the saved state of 7.20 and libavcodec's AV1Frame
typedef struct {
	int valid;                          // usable for frame sizes and show_existing_frame (the parsing state)
	int pic;                            // a decoded picture is held, in DPB slot dpb (decode number gen)
	int dpb; uint64_t gen;
	int grain_dpb;                      // the picture was decoded with film grain: its reference is a separate image
	uint32_t frame_id;
	int upscaled_width, frame_width, frame_height, render_width, render_height;
	int frame_type, order_hint, showable;
	uint8_t order_hints[8];             // its OrderHints[] (the SavedOrderHints its reference info gets)
	uint8_t sign_bias;                  // its RefFrameSignBias mask
	int disable_frame_end_update_cdf, segmentation_enabled;
	int8_t lf_ref[8], lf_mode[2];
	uint8_t feature_enabled[8][8]; int16_t feature_value[8][8];
	int32_t gm[8][6];
	int grain_apply; StdVideoAV1FilmGrain grain;
	int bit_depth;
} Av1dRef;

// one frame header of a sample: a frame to decode, or a show_existing_frame
typedef struct {
	int show_existing;                  // 1: no decode, the picture of reference slot show_slot is shown
	int show_slot;
	int shown;                          // show_frame or show_existing_frame
	// what Vulkan Video gets (a decoded frame)
	Av1dSeq seq;                        // the sequence header it was parsed with (av1d_seq_fix'ed)
	StdVideoDecodeAV1PictureInfo std;   // its pointers point into this structure
	StdVideoAV1TileInfo tile; uint16_t mi_col_starts[64], mi_row_starts[64], width_sbs[64], height_sbs[64];
	StdVideoAV1Quantization quant; StdVideoAV1Segmentation seg; StdVideoAV1LoopFilter lf; StdVideoAV1CDEF cdef;
	StdVideoAV1LoopRestoration lr; StdVideoAV1GlobalMotion gm; StdVideoAV1FilmGrain grain;
	StdVideoDecodeAV1ReferenceInfo setup;     // the current picture's reference information
	int32_t name_dpb[7];                      // referenceNameSlotIndices
	int nrefs; struct { int dpb; int slot; StdVideoDecodeAV1ReferenceInfo info; } refs[7];   // slot: the AV1 slot
	int dpb; uint64_t gen;                    // the DPB slot it is decoded into, its decode number
	int apply_grain;
	int width, height, frame_width;           // UpscaledWidth (the coded extent), FrameHeight; FrameWidth (superres)
	uint32_t ntiles; uint32_t tile_src[AV1D_MAX_TILES], tile_size[AV1D_MAX_TILES];   // offsets into the sample
	size_t size;                              // the tiles' bytes
	int missing;                              // an inter frame whose references have no picture: not decoded
	// for the tests (tests/av1parse_test.c)
	int ref_frame_idx[7], refresh, hdr_bits, ntg;
} Av1dFrame;

typedef struct {
	int nframes; Av1dFrame f[AV1D_MAX_FRAMES];
	int shown;                          // the frame shown (the first one: -1 none)
	int extra_shown;                    // shown frames after it (a temporal unit has one)
} Av1dSample;

typedef struct {
	Av1dSeq seq; int have_seq;
	Av1dRef ref[8];
	uint64_t gen;
	int op_idc;                         // operating point 0's idc: OBUs of other layers are dropped
	int keyframes;                      // frames decoded since the start or a flush (for the tests)
	int check;                          // tests: keep the frame header length
	char why[160];
	uint64_t missing_refs, damaged;
} Av1dState;

void av1d_init(Av1dState *s);
// the av1C record (AV1CodecConfigurationRecord) and its configOBUs: AV1D_NO_PICTURE, or AV1D_UNSUPPORTED / AV1D_ERROR
int av1d_parse_av1c(Av1dState *s, const uint8_t *av1c, size_t n);
// one sample (a temporal unit of OBUs, low-overhead format): every frame header and tile group parsed, the reference
// slots updated, the frames described in *out (tile offsets into data). On AV1D_UNSUPPORTED / AV1D_ERROR the state is
// left as it was before the sample.
int av1d_parse_sample(Av1dState *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t n, Av1dSample *out);
// frame f was not decoded after all (no picture buffer, a failed submit): the slots holding its picture lose it
void av1d_lost(Av1dState *s, uint64_t gen);
// the DPB slots a reference frame slot holds a picture in (bit i: slot i)
unsigned av1d_dpb_busy(const Av1dState *s);
// forget every picture (a seek: libavcodec's flush; the next frames need a key frame)
void av1d_flush(Av1dState *s);
// whether the sample's first frame header is a shown key frame (a random access point: libavcodec can start there).
// Reads only the start of that frame header (show_existing_frame, frame_type, show_frame), without any state.
int av1d_is_key_sample(const uint8_t *data, size_t n);
// points the sequence header's pColorConfig / pTimingInfo at its own copies (after the structure was copied)
void av1d_seq_fix(Av1dSeq *q);
const char *av1d_why(const Av1dState *s);
#endif



================================================
FILE: videotoolbox/vtdirect_h264.h
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vtdirect_h264.h: the H.264 side of the direct Vulkan Video decode path (vtdirect.c): parameter sets, the slice header
// fields Vulkan Video needs, picture order counts and the decoded picture buffer (reference marking), for frame-coded
// 8-bit 4:2:0 streams. No Vulkan calls and no FFmpeg: the Std structures only, so it is tested off the GPU
// (tests/h264parse_test.c, against libavcodec's own POC and reference lists).
//
// The picture order counts and the marking follow libavcodec 9.0.2's H.264 decoder (h264_parse.c ff_h264_init_poc,
// h264_refs.c ff_h264_execute_ref_pic_marking, h264dec.c idr()), not only the specification, so the B580 gets the same
// values on both paths and decodes the same pictures:
// - an IDR sets the previous POC MSB to 65536 and the previous LSB to "unset" (the IDR's own LSB): POCs are offset by
//   65536 (the hardware uses their differences);
// - memory_management_control_operation 5 sets the picture's frame_num to 0 and keeps its POC (8.2.1 would subtract
//   tempPicOrderCnt);
// - the sliding window removes the oldest short-term reference once short + long >= max_num_ref_frames, before the
//   current picture is added; a short-term reference with the current frame_num is dropped when it is added; more
//   than max(max_num_ref_frames, 1) references drops the oldest short-term one (or the first long-term one);
// - a long-term reference's FrameNum is its LongTermFrameIdx (libavcodec passes pic_id, which its reference list
//   construction sets to the same value).
#ifndef VTDIRECT_H264_H
#define VTDIRECT_H264_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h264std.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h264std_decode.h>

#define H264D_SLOTS 17          // DPB slots: 16 references and the current picture
#define H264D_MAX_REFS 16

enum {
	H264D_PICTURE = 0,       // a picture: decode it, then h264d_finish_picture
	H264D_NO_PICTURE = 1,    // parameter sets, SEI, ...: nothing to decode
	H264D_UNSUPPORTED = -1,  // a stream the direct path does not cover (h264d_why says what): libavcodec takes over
	H264D_ERROR = -2,        // a damaged sample
};

typedef struct {
	int present;
	StdVideoH264SequenceParameterSet std;
	StdVideoH264ScalingLists scaling;
	int32_t offset_for_ref_frame[256];
	int profile_idc, level_idc;
	int width_mbs, height_mbs;            // the coded size in macroblocks (frames only)
	int log2_max_frame_num, log2_max_poc_lsb;
	int unsupported;                      // why the direct path cannot decode pictures that use it (0: it can)
	int full_range;                       // the VUI's video_full_range_flag, -1 if absent
} H264DSps;

typedef struct {
	int present;
	StdVideoH264PictureParameterSet std;
	StdVideoH264ScalingLists scaling;
	int sps_id;
	int num_slice_groups;
} H264DPps;

typedef struct {
	int slot;                             // DPB slot index
	int frame_num;                        // FrameNum, or LongTermFrameIdx for a long-term reference
	int32_t poc[2];
	int long_term;
} H264DRef;

// one picture: what Vulkan Video gets for it
typedef struct {
	int idr, nal_ref_idc, is_intra, frame_num, idr_pic_id;
	int slice_type;                       // the first slice's (0 P, 1 B, 2 I)
	int32_t poc[2];                       // TopFieldOrderCnt, BottomFieldOrderCnt (libavcodec's numbering, above)
	StdVideoDecodeH264PictureInfo std;
	const H264DSps *sps; const H264DPps *pps;
	uint32_t nslices; const uint32_t *slice_offsets;   // into the bitstream written by h264d_parse_sample
	size_t size;                          // bytes written (start codes and slice NAL units)
	int nrefs; H264DRef refs[H264D_MAX_REFS];         // the DPB before this picture: short-term newest first, then long-term
	int slot;                             // the slot this picture is set up in
	int max_active_l0, max_active_l1;     // the largest num_ref_idx_active of its slices (0 for intra slices)
	// reference marking, applied by h264d_finish_picture
	int long_term_reference_flag, adaptive;
	int nmmco; struct { int op, a, b; } mmco[66];
	int gap;                              // frame_num jumped (not allowed by the SPS: a lost picture)
} H264DPicture;

typedef struct {
	int frame_num;                        // libavcodec's pic->frame_num (0 after MMCO 5)
	int32_t poc[2];
	int long_idx;                         // LongTermFrameIdx, or -1 for a short-term reference
} H264DSlotInfo;

typedef struct {
	int nal_length_size;                  // the avcC's lengthSizeMinusOne + 1
	H264DSps sps[32];
	H264DPps *pps[256];
	int active_sps;                       // the SPS of the last picture (-1 before any)
	int last_sps, last_pps;               // the ids of the last parameter sets parsed (tests)
	// picture order count state (libavcodec's H264POCContext)
	int prev_poc_msb, prev_poc_lsb, prev_frame_num_offset, prev_frame_num;
	// the decoded picture buffer
	int short_ref[H264D_MAX_REFS], nshort;   // slots, newest first
	int long_ref[16];                        // slot by LongTermFrameIdx, -1 if none
	int nlong;
	H264DSlotInfo slot[H264D_SLOTS];
	int slot_busy[H264D_SLOTS];              // holds a reference
	int pictures;                            // pictures parsed since h264d_init (0: the next must be an IDR)
	int pending_poc_msb, pending_poc_lsb, pending_frame_num_offset, mmco5;   // the parsed picture's, for finish
	uint32_t *offsets; uint32_t offsets_cap; // slice offsets of the current picture
	char why[128];                           // the reason of the last H264D_UNSUPPORTED / H264D_ERROR
	uint64_t gaps, redundant_slices;
} H264DState;

// state for a stream whose samples carry NAL units with nal_length_size-byte big-endian lengths (avcC); the state must
// be zeroed before the first call (h264d_free releases what it allocates)
void h264d_init(H264DState *s, int nal_length_size);
void h264d_free(H264DState *s);
// the SPS and PPS of an avcC record; H264D_NO_PICTURE, or H264D_UNSUPPORTED / H264D_ERROR (h264d_why)
int h264d_parse_avcc(H264DState *s, const uint8_t *avcc, size_t n);
// the size h264d_parse_sample writes for this sample (start code + NAL unit for every slice); 0 for a malformed sample
size_t h264d_bitstream_size(const H264DState *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t n);
// one sample (an access unit): parameter sets are taken, the slices' NAL units copied into out (at least
// h264d_bitstream_size bytes) with start codes, and the picture described in *pic. H264D_PICTURE or another code above.
int h264d_parse_sample(H264DState *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t n, uint8_t *out, size_t cap, H264DPicture *pic);
// the picture has been submitted: reference marking (the DPB after it) and the POC state for the next one
void h264d_finish_picture(H264DState *s, const H264DPicture *pic);
// forget every reference (libavcodec's flush: the next pictures decode with what they find)
void h264d_flush(H264DState *s);
const char *h264d_why(const H264DState *s);

// helpers shared with the tests
int h264d_level_idc_to_std(int level_idc);
#endif

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vtdirect_hevc.h: the HEVC side of the direct Vulkan Video decode path (vtdirect.c): video, sequence and picture
// parameter sets, the slice segment header fields Vulkan Video needs, picture order counts and the decoded picture
// buffer driven by the reference picture sets, for Main / Main 10 / Main Still Picture 4:2:0 streams (8 or 10 bits).
// No Vulkan calls and no FFmpeg: the Std structures only, so it is tested off the GPU (tests/hevcparse_test.c, against
// golden files made from libavcodec, tests/hevc/mkgolden.py).
//
// Written from ITU-T H.265 (V10, 07/2024) 7.3 / 7.4 / 8.3.1 / 8.3.2. Where the hardware must see the same values on
// both paths it follows libavcodec 9.0.2's HEVC decoder (hevcdec.c, refs.c, ps.c) and Vulkan hwaccel (vulkan_hevc.c),
// not only the specification:
// - picture order counts: the previous TemporalId-0 picture's POC split with C's % (libavcodec's ff_hevc_compute_poc2),
//   POC MSB 0 only for BLA pictures (a CRA starting a sequence keeps the MSB derived from the previous picture);
// - an IDR picture, or a picture whose SPS is not the one active before it, drops every reference; otherwise the
//   picture's reference picture set alone marks the references (also after a CRA with NoRaslOutputFlag);
// - RASL pictures of an IRAP picture with NoRaslOutputFlag = 1 are not decoded; NoRaslOutputFlag of a CRA comes from an
//   end of sequence NAL unit (or the start of the stream, or a flush) before it;
// - a reference the RPS names that is not there: ignored in StFoll / LtFoll and for IRAP pictures; for RefPicSetStCurr*
//   / LtCurr of other pictures the picture is not decoded and the references after that entry are dropped (libavcodec
//   stops at the entry);
// - the references passed are every picture the RPS kept (StFoll / LtFoll included), RefPicSetStCurrBefore/After and
//   LtCurr their DPB slots; the SPS's Std fields read by the driver's HCP_PIC_STATE get libavcodec's values (the PCM
//   fields of an SPS without PCM wrap as libavcodec's unsigned subtraction does; the scaling lists as "present" with the
//   defaults when the SPS enables them without coding them).
#ifndef VTDIRECT_HEVC_H
#define VTDIRECT_HEVC_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h265std.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_h265std_decode.h>

#define HEVCD_SLOTS 16          // DPB slots: up to 15 references and the current picture (the B580's maxDpbSlots)
#define HEVCD_MAX_REFS 15
#define HEVCD_MAX_SUB_LAYERS 7

enum {
	HEVCD_PICTURE = 0,       // a picture: decode it, then hevcd_finish_picture
	HEVCD_NO_PICTURE = 1,    // parameter sets, SEI, a skipped RASL picture ...: nothing to decode
	HEVCD_UNSUPPORTED = -1,  // a stream the direct path does not cover (hevcd_why says what): libavcodec takes over
	HEVCD_ERROR = -2,        // a damaged sample
};

typedef struct { int num_negative, num_positive; int32_t delta[32]; uint32_t used; } HevcDRps;   // derived (7.4.8):
                                                                     // S0 closest first, then S1 closest first

typedef struct {
	StdVideoH265VideoParameterSet std;
	StdVideoH265ProfileTierLevel ptl;
	StdVideoH265DecPicBufMgr dpbm;
	int profile, level_idc;
	uint8_t *raw; size_t rawn;            // the NAL unit, to recognise a repeated identical VPS
} HevcDVps;

typedef struct {
	StdVideoH265SequenceParameterSet std;
	StdVideoH265ProfileTierLevel ptl;
	StdVideoH265DecPicBufMgr dpbm;
	StdVideoH265ScalingLists scaling;
	StdVideoH265ShortTermRefPicSet st[64];
	StdVideoH265LongTermRefPicsSps lt;
	StdVideoH265SequenceParameterSetVui vui;
	StdVideoH265HrdParameters hrd;
	StdVideoH265SubLayerHrdParameters hrd_nal[HEVCD_MAX_SUB_LAYERS], hrd_vcl[HEVCD_MAX_SUB_LAYERS];
	HevcDRps rps[65];                     // the SPS's sets, and [64] for the one in the current slice header
	int profile, level_idc;               // general_profile_idc (libavcodec's inference when 0), general_level_idc
	int width, height;                    // luma samples
	int log2_ctb, ctb_w, ctb_h, log2_max_poc_lsb;
	int bit_depth;
	int scaling_coded;                    // sps_scaling_list_data_present_flag as coded
	uint32_t conf[4];                     // conf_win_*_offset as coded
	int pcm_coded;                        // pcm_enabled_flag
	int full_range;                       // the VUI's video_full_range_flag, -1 if absent
	int unsupported;                      // why the direct path cannot decode pictures that use it (0: it can)
	uint64_t gen;                         // changes when an SPS with this id and other content replaces it
	uint8_t *raw; size_t rawn;            // the NAL unit, to recognise a repeated identical SPS
} HevcDSps;

typedef struct {
	StdVideoH265PictureParameterSet std;
	StdVideoH265ScalingLists scaling;
	int sps_id;
	int ncols, nrows; uint16_t col[20], row[22];   // tile column widths / row heights in CTBs (6.5.1)
	int unsupported;
	uint8_t *raw; size_t rawn;
} HevcDPps;

typedef struct {
	int slot;                             // DPB slot index
	int32_t poc;
	int long_term;
} HevcDRef;

// one picture: what Vulkan Video gets for it
typedef struct {
	int nal_type, tid, irap, idr;
	int32_t poc;
	StdVideoDecodeH265PictureInfo std;
	const HevcDVps *vps; const HevcDSps *sps; const HevcDPps *pps;
	uint32_t nslices; const uint32_t *slice_offsets;   // into the bitstream written by hevcd_parse_sample
	size_t size;                          // bytes written (start codes and slice segment NAL units)
	int nrefs; HevcDRef refs[HEVCD_MAX_REFS];          // the references held while it is decoded, in slot order
	int slot;                             // the slot this picture is set up in
	int missing;                          // a reference of RefPicSetStCurr* / LtCurr is not there: not decoded
	// for the tests (tests/hevcparse_test.c): what the golden files print
	int st_mode, st_idx;                  // 0: IDR, 1: short_term_ref_pic_set_idx from the SPS, 2: in the slice header
	int hdr_bits;                         // the first slice segment header's length (only with HevcDState.check)
	int nlist[3]; int32_t list[3][8]; int8_t found[3][8];   // StCurrBefore, StCurrAfter, LtCurr: POCs, found
} HevcDPicture;

typedef struct {
	int nal_length_size;                  // the hvcC's lengthSizeMinusOne + 1
	HevcDVps *vps[16];
	HevcDSps *sps[16];
	HevcDPps *pps[64];
	void *retired[128]; int nretired;      // replaced parameter sets, freed at the next sample (a picture may use them)
	uint64_t gen;
	int active_sps; uint64_t active_gen;  // the SPS of the last picture (-1 before any)
	int active_w, active_h, active_bd;    // its size and bit depth
	int last_vps, last_sps, last_pps;     // the ids of the last parameter sets parsed (tests)
	// libavcodec's decoder state
	int eos, last_eos, no_rasl_output_flag;
	int32_t poc_tid0;
	// the decoded picture buffer
	int slot_busy[HEVCD_SLOTS]; int32_t slot_poc[HEVCD_SLOTS]; int slot_long[HEVCD_SLOTS];
	int pictures;                         // pictures parsed since hevcd_init (0: the next must be an IRAP picture)
	int skipped;                          // the last sample was a RASL picture that is not decoded
	int check;                            // tests: parse every first slice segment header to its end (hdr_bits)
	uint32_t *offsets; uint32_t offsets_cap;   // slice segment offsets of the current picture
	char why[160];                        // the reason of the last HEVCD_UNSUPPORTED / HEVCD_ERROR
	uint64_t missing_refs, rasl_skipped, bad_param_sets;
} HevcDState;

// state for a stream whose samples carry NAL units with nal_length_size-byte big-endian lengths (hvcC); the state must
// be zeroed before the first call (hevcd_free releases what it allocates)
void hevcd_init(HevcDState *s, int nal_length_size);
void hevcd_free(HevcDState *s);
// the parameter sets of an hvcC record (and its lengthSizeMinusOne); HEVCD_NO_PICTURE, or HEVCD_UNSUPPORTED /
// HEVCD_ERROR (hevcd_why)
int hevcd_parse_hvcc(HevcDState *s, const uint8_t *hvcc, size_t n);
// the size hevcd_parse_sample writes for this sample (start code + NAL unit for every slice segment); 0 for a malformed
// sample or one without slices
size_t hevcd_bitstream_size(const HevcDState *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t n);
// one sample (an access unit): parameter sets are taken, the slice segments' NAL units copied into out (at least
// hevcd_bitstream_size bytes) with start codes, the references marked by the picture's RPS, and the picture described
// in *pic. HEVCD_PICTURE (pic->missing: a P/B picture whose references are not there) or another code above.
int hevcd_parse_sample(HevcDState *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t n, uint8_t *out, size_t cap, HevcDPicture *pic);
// the picture has been submitted (or could not be): a decoded picture becomes a short-term reference
void hevcd_finish_picture(HevcDState *s, const HevcDPicture *pic);
// forget every reference (libavcodec's flush: the next CRA starts a sequence, its RASL pictures are not decoded)
void hevcd_flush(HevcDState *s);
const char *hevcd_why(const HevcDState *s);

// helpers shared with the tests
const char *hevcd_nal_type_name(int t);
int hevcd_level_idc_to_std(int general_level_idc);
#endif
