// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vtdirect_vp9.h: the VP9 side of the direct Vulkan Video decode path (vtdirect.c): the superframe index, every frame's
// uncompressed header (frame size, reference names and refresh flags, loop filter, quantizer, segmentation, tile
// info), show_existing_frame, the persistent state that the uncompressed header updates (loop filter deltas,
// segmentation features, the reference frame slots' sizes), and the DPB slot each picture is decoded into, for
// Profile 0 (8-bit) and Profile 2 (10-bit) 4:2:0 streams. The compressed header and the tiles are the hardware's (the
// B580's HCP parses them; ANV keeps the four probability contexts in the session). No Vulkan calls and no FFmpeg: the
// Std structures only, so it is tested off the GPU (tests/vp9parse_test.c, against golden files made from FFmpeg's
// trace_headers, tests/vp9/mkgolden.py).
//
// Written from the VP9 Bitstream & Decoding Process Specification (v0.6, 2016) 6.1-6.2 / 7.2 / 8.4.1 / Annex B and the
// Vulkan specification (VK_KHR_video_decode_vp9). Where the hardware must see the same values on both paths it
// follows libavcodec 9.0.2's VP9 decoder (vp9.c, cbs_vp9_syntax_template.c, bsf/vp9_superframe_split.c) and Vulkan
// hwaccel (vulkan_vp9.c), not only the specification:
// - a sample is split at its superframe index as vp9_superframe_split does (an index whose first byte does not repeat
//   the marker is no index; a frame size of 0 or past the index fails the sample); each frame is then read as CBS
//   reads a packet (a frame whose last byte looks like an index marker is cut where that index says);
// - DPB slots: a picture is decoded into the lowest slot no reference frame slot holds (vulkan_vp9.c frame_id); the
//   references passed are the pictures the three ref_frame_idx[] name, once each, in that order; for KEY and
//   intra-only frames ref_frame_idx[] is 0 (libavcodec's header is zeroed), so reference slot 0's picture is passed if
//   there is one (the hardware reads no reference for intra frames);
// - UsePrevFrameMvs as vp9.c's use_last_frame_mvs: not error resilient, the previously parsed frame header was shown,
//   and for inter frames the last frame that was decoded (not a show_existing_frame) has the same size;
// - Std fields the driver reads are libavcodec's: frame_context_idx and reset_frame_context as coded (also for key
//   frames), refresh_frame_flags 0xff for key frames, ref_frame_sign_bias_mask as coded (vp9.c clears it in error
//   resilient mode, the hwaccel does not), interpolation_filter remapped to the Std enum (EIGHTTAP_SMOOTH for intra
//   frames), loop filter deltas and segmentation features as CBS keeps them across frames;
// - two segmentation values follow the specification where the hwaccel passes CBS's stale copies (the hardware decodes
//   those frames wrongly through libavcodec; vp9parse_test prints a "lavc" line for every such frame):
//   segmentation_abs_or_delta_update persists until the next segmentation_update_data (libavcodec passes the current
//   header's, 0 when the frame does not update the data), and the tree and prediction probabilities of a frame with
//   segmentation_update_map are its own (CBS copies them only when the frame also updates the data);
// - Std fields the driver does not read follow the specification: update_ref_delta / update_mode_delta as bit masks,
//   the colour configuration of the last key or intra-only frame for inter frames.
// Broken streams: a frame that does not parse is not decoded and changes nothing; an inter frame whose references
// have no picture (after a flush, a seek, or a frame that was not decoded) is not decoded, its header still updates
// the loop filter deltas, segmentation features and reference sizes (as CBS does), the pictures in the slots stay.
#ifndef VTDIRECT_VP9_H
#define VTDIRECT_VP9_H
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_vp9std.h>
#include <vk_video/vulkan_video_codec_vp9std_decode.h>

#define VP9D_SLOTS 9            // DPB slots: the eight reference frames and the current picture (the B580's maxDpbSlots is 12)
#define VP9D_MAX_FRAMES 8       // frames in one superframe

enum {
	VP9D_PICTURE = 0,       // the sample has frames to decode or to show
	VP9D_UNSUPPORTED = -1,  // a frame the direct path does not cover (vp9d_why says what): libavcodec takes over
	VP9D_ERROR = -2,        // a damaged sample (no frame in it parsed: the state is as before it)
};

// a reference frame slot
typedef struct {
	int valid;                          // a frame refreshed it (its size is known)
	int width, height, bit_depth;       // the size CBS keeps for frame_size_with_refs
	int pic;                            // a decoded picture is held, in DPB slot dpb (decode number gen)
	int dpb; uint64_t gen;
	int pic_width, pic_height;          // that picture's size
} Vp9dRef;

// a reference passed with a frame
typedef struct { int dpb, slot, width, height; } Vp9dRefPic;   // slot: the VP9 reference slot

// one frame of a sample: a frame to decode, or a show_existing_frame
typedef struct {
	int show_existing;                  // 1: no decode, the picture of reference slot show_slot is shown
	int show_slot;
	int shown;                          // show_frame or show_existing_frame
	int error;                          // the frame did not parse or its references have no picture: not decoded
	int missing;                        // (error) an inter frame whose references have no picture / an empty slot shown
	// what Vulkan Video gets (a decoded frame); the pointers of std point into this structure (vp9d_frame_fix)
	StdVideoDecodeVP9PictureInfo std;
	StdVideoVP9ColorConfig color; StdVideoVP9LoopFilter lf; StdVideoVP9Segmentation seg;
	int32_t name_dpb[3];                // referenceNameSlotIndices
	int nrefs; Vp9dRefPic refs[3];
	int dpb; uint64_t gen;              // the DPB slot it is decoded into, its decode number
	int width, height, bit_depth;
	uint32_t offset, size;              // the frame in the sample
	uint32_t uncomp_size, comp_size;    // compressedHeaderOffset; tilesOffset - compressedHeaderOffset
	// what libavcodec's Vulkan hwaccel passes where it differs (see the top): segmentation_abs_or_delta_update and
	// the tree / prediction probabilities (lavc_differs: they matter for this frame)
	int lavc_differs, lavc_abs; uint8_t lavc_tree[7], lavc_pred[3];
	// for the tests (tests/vp9parse_test.c)
	int ref_frame_idx[3], refresh, hdr_bits, intra_only;
} Vp9dFrame;

typedef struct {
	int nframes; Vp9dFrame f[VP9D_MAX_FRAMES];
	int shown;                          // the frame shown (the first one: -1 none)
	int extra_shown;                    // shown frames after it (a superframe has one)
	int superframe;                     // the sample had a superframe index
} Vp9dSample;

typedef struct {
	Vp9dRef ref[8];
	uint64_t gen;
	int profile;                        // the stream's profile (0 or 2), from the vpcC; -1 any of the two
	// the state the uncompressed header carries from frame to frame (CBS's CodedBitstreamVP9Context)
	int8_t lf_ref[4], lf_mode[2];
	uint8_t feat_en[8][4]; int16_t feat_val[8][4];
	int abs_delta;
	uint8_t tree[7], pred[3];           // the last ones a frame coded (segmentation_update_map)
	uint8_t cbs_tree[7], cbs_pred[3];   // CBS's copies (libavcodec's hwaccel passes these)
	int color_space, color_range, bit_depth;   // of the last key or intra-only frame
	// vp9.c: the last parsed header's show_frame, the last frame decoded (its size)
	int last_invisible, have_last, last_w, last_h;
	int color_known;                    // a key frame has been parsed (vp9d_full_range)
	int check;                          // tests: keep the header length
	char why[160];
} Vp9dState;

void vp9d_init(Vp9dState *s, int profile);
// one sample (a frame or a superframe): every frame's uncompressed header parsed, the reference slots updated, the
// frames described in *out (offsets into data). VP9D_PICTURE also when some frames are in error (Vp9dFrame.error); on
// VP9D_UNSUPPORTED / VP9D_ERROR the state is left as it was before the sample.
int vp9d_parse_sample(Vp9dState *s, const uint8_t *data, size_t n, Vp9dSample *out);
// frame gen was not decoded after all (no picture buffer, a failed submit): the slots holding its picture lose it
void vp9d_lost(Vp9dState *s, uint64_t gen);
// the DPB slots a reference frame slot holds a picture in (bit i: slot i)
unsigned vp9d_dpb_busy(const Vp9dState *s);
// forget every picture (a seek: libavcodec's flush; the next frames need a key frame)
void vp9d_flush(Vp9dState *s);
// whether the sample's first frame is a key frame (libavcodec can start there). Reads only the start of its header.
int vp9d_is_key_sample(const uint8_t *data, size_t n);
// points the Std picture information's pColorConfig / pLoopFilter / pSegmentation at the frame's own (after a copy)
void vp9d_frame_fix(Vp9dFrame *f);
// the colour range of the last key frame: 1 full, 0 video, -1 none yet
int vp9d_full_range(const Vp9dState *s);
const char *vp9d_why(const Vp9dState *s);
#endif

FILE: videotoolbox/vtplugin.h

// The VideoToolbox decoder plug-in ABI (not in the public SDK): CoreMedia's derived-object classes as laid out in
// macOS x86_64 builds (pack 4, a 32-bit class version), checked against Apple's and nullmoth's decoder binaries.
#pragma once
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreMedia/CoreMedia.h>
#include <CoreVideo/CoreVideo.h>
#include <VideoToolbox/VideoToolbox.h>

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build.sh: libintelxevenc.dylib, the IntelXe HEVC/H.264/AV1 VideoToolbox encoders, against FFmpeg's shared libraries
# (ffmpeg/configure-shared.sh), install name /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libintelxevenc.dylib; and vtenctest, vtencq.
#   FFMPEG_INSTALL=<ffmpeg install prefix> MESA_INCLUDE=<mesa>/include [OUT=dir] encoder/build.sh
# Every Mach-O is ad-hoc signed: x86_64 links made on arm64 are not, and dyld refuses unsigned code in platform and
# library-validated processes (WindowServer, VTDecoderXPCService).
set -eu
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
OUT=${OUT:-$HERE/build}
: "${FFMPEG_INSTALL:?}" "${MESA_INCLUDE:?}"
SDK=${SDK:-/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX26.5.sdk}
CC="xcrun --sdk $SDK clang -isysroot $SDK -arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -g -Wall -Wno-deprecated-declarations -fvisibility=hidden"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
$CC -dynamiclib -o "$OUT/libintelxevenc.dylib" "$HERE/intelxevenc.c" -I"$FFMPEG_INSTALL/include" -I"$MESA_INCLUDE" \
  -L"$FFMPEG_INSTALL/lib" -lavcodec -lavutil -install_name /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libintelxevenc.dylib \
  -framework CoreFoundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo -framework VideoToolbox -framework IOKit -framework IOSurface
$CC -fobjc-arc -o "$OUT/vtenctest" "$HERE/vtenctest.m" -framework Foundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo \
  -framework VideoToolbox -framework Metal
$CC -fobjc-arc -o "$OUT/vtencq" "$HERE/../tests/vtencq.m" -framework Foundation -framework CoreMedia -framework CoreVideo \
  -framework VideoToolbox -framework Metal
# the debug map (source and object paths of this machine) stays in the .dSYM next to it, not in the shipped library
strip -S "$OUT/libintelxevenc.dylib"
for f in libintelxevenc.dylib vtenctest vtencq; do codesign -f -s - "$OUT/$f"; done

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The VideoToolbox encoder plug-in ABI (not in the public SDK), as macOS 15 x86_64 builds lay it out: CoreMedia derived
// objects with a 32-bit class version and pack(4). Checked against Apple's x86_64 encoders on the B580 machine
// (/System/Library/Video/Plug-Ins/JPEGVideoEncoder.bundle, AppleGVAHEVCEncoder.bundle, 15.8.1): their vtables are
// { 0, &CMBaseClass, &VTVideoEncoderClass } and both use exactly the four encoder methods below (version 1 and 2).
//   startSession     (encoder, session, CMVideoDimensions in one register, encoder specification CFDictionary)
//   encodeFrame      (encoder, frame token, CVImageBuffer, CMTime pts and duration on the stack, frame properties,
//                     VTEncodeInfoFlags *): returns with kVTEncodeInfo_Asynchronous set and emits later
//   completeFrames   (encoder, CMTime complete-until, on the stack): emit everything up to it before returning
//   copySupportedPropertyDictionary (encoder, CFDictionaryRef *)
// Properties come and go through the CMBaseClass copyProperty/setProperty (one key at a time).
#pragma once
#include <CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>
#include <CoreMedia/CoreMedia.h>
#include <CoreVideo/CoreVideo.h>
#include <VideoToolbox/VideoToolbox.h>
typedef struct OpaqueCMBaseObject *CMBaseObjectRef;
typedef struct OpaqueVTVideoEncoder *VTVideoEncoderRef;
typedef struct OpaqueVTEncoderSession *VTEncoderSessionRef;
typedef struct OpaqueVTEncoderFrame *VTEncoderFrameRef;
typedef const struct OpaqueCMBaseClassID *CMBaseClassID;
#pragma pack(push, 4)
typedef struct {
	uint32_t version;
	size_t derivedStorageSize;
	Boolean (*equal)(CMBaseObjectRef, CMBaseObjectRef);
	OSStatus (*invalidate)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	void (*finalize)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	CFStringRef (*copyDebugDescription)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	OSStatus (*copyProperty)(CMBaseObjectRef, CFStringRef, CFAllocatorRef, void *);
	OSStatus (*setProperty)(CMBaseObjectRef, CFStringRef, CFTypeRef);
	OSStatus (*notificationBarrier)(CMBaseObjectRef);
	const void *protocolTable;
} CMBaseClass;
typedef struct {
	uint32_t version;
	OSStatus (*startSession)(VTVideoEncoderRef, VTEncoderSessionRef, CMVideoDimensions, CFDictionaryRef);
	OSStatus (*encodeFrame)(VTVideoEncoderRef, VTEncoderFrameRef, CVImageBufferRef, CMTime, CMTime, CFDictionaryRef, VTEncodeInfoFlags *);
	OSStatus (*completeFrames)(VTVideoEncoderRef, CMTime);
	OSStatus (*copySupportedPropertyDictionary)(VTVideoEncoderRef, CFDictionaryRef *);
	void *reserved[12];
} VTVideoEncoderClass;
#pragma pack(pop)
typedef struct { uintptr_t reserved; const CMBaseClass *baseClass; const VTVideoEncoderClass *derivedClass; } VTVideoEncoderVTable;
extern OSStatus CMDerivedObjectCreate(CFAllocatorRef, const void *vtable, CMBaseClassID, CMBaseObjectRef *);

FILE: videotoolbox/encoder/vtenctest.m
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// vtenctest [--preload binary] ...: drives a VTCompressionSession the way OBS/HandBrake/ffmpeg do and writes the result as an elementary stream.
//   vtenctest --list [--lib libintelxevenc.dylib]
//   vtenctest [--lib L] [--id EncoderID | --any] codec(hevc|h264|av1) WxH raw.nv12 frames out [--bitrate N | --cbr N | --quality Q]
//             [--realtime] [--noreorder] [--keyint N] [--10bit] [--fps F]
// raw.nv12: NV12 (or P010 with --10bit) frames, read in a loop. Output: Annex B (.hevc/.h264) or IVF (.ivf for AV1).
#import <Foundation/Foundation.h>
#import <Metal/Metal.h>
#import <VideoToolbox/VideoToolbox.h>
#import <CoreMedia/CoreMedia.h>
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <mach-o/dyld.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static FILE *out; static FourCharCode codec; static int64_t emitted, keys, bytes, errors, async_ok;
static int wrote_ivf_hdr;
static void put_le32(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v) { p[0] = v; p[1] = v >> 8; p[2] = v >> 16; p[3] = v >> 24; }

static void write_param_sets(CMFormatDescriptionRef fd) {
	size_t n = 0; int nal = 0;
	if (codec == 'hvc1') CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetHEVCParameterSetAtIndex(fd, 0, NULL, NULL, &n, &nal);
	else CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetH264ParameterSetAtIndex(fd, 0, NULL, NULL, &n, &nal);
	for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		const uint8_t *p; size_t sz;
		OSStatus r = codec == 'hvc1' ? CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetHEVCParameterSetAtIndex(fd, i, &p, &sz, NULL, NULL)
		                             : CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetH264ParameterSetAtIndex(fd, i, &p, &sz, NULL, NULL);
		if (r) continue;
		fwrite("\0\0\0\1", 1, 4, out); fwrite(p, 1, sz, out);
	}
}

static void cb(void *ref, void *src, OSStatus st, VTEncodeInfoFlags fl, CMSampleBufferRef sb) {
	if (st || !sb) { if (!(fl & kVTEncodeInfo_FrameDropped)) { errors++; fprintf(stderr, "frame error %d flags 0x%x\n", (int)st, fl); } return; }
	if (fl & kVTEncodeInfo_Asynchronous) async_ok++;
	CFArrayRef att = CMSampleBufferGetSampleAttachmentsArray(sb, false);
	CFDictionaryRef a = att && CFArrayGetCount(att) ? CFArrayGetValueAtIndex(att, 0) : NULL;
	int key = !(a && CFDictionaryGetValue(a, kCMSampleAttachmentKey_NotSync) == kCFBooleanTrue);
	CMFormatDescriptionRef fd = CMSampleBufferGetFormatDescription(sb);
	CMBlockBufferRef bb = CMSampleBufferGetDataBuffer(sb);
	size_t len = CMBlockBufferGetDataLength(bb);
	uint8_t *d = malloc(len); CMBlockBufferCopyDataBytes(bb, 0, len, d);
	if (emitted < 3 || (key && keys < 3)) {
		CMTime p = CMSampleBufferGetPresentationTimeStamp(sb), dt = CMSampleBufferGetDecodeTimeStamp(sb);
		fprintf(stderr, "out %lld: pts %lld/%d dts %lld/%d key %d %zu bytes\n", emitted, p.value, p.timescale, dt.value, dt.timescale, key, len);
	}
	if (codec == 'av01') {
		if (!wrote_ivf_hdr) {
			CMVideoDimensions dim = CMVideoFormatDescriptionGetDimensions(fd);
			uint8_t h[32] = "DKIF"; h[4] = 0; h[5] = 0; h[6] = 32; h[7] = 0; memcpy(h + 8, "AV01", 4);
			h[12] = dim.width; h[13] = dim.width >> 8; h[14] = dim.height; h[15] = dim.height >> 8;
			put_le32(h + 16, 30); put_le32(h + 20, 1); put_le32(h + 24, 0); put_le32(h + 28, 0);
			fwrite(h, 1, 32, out); wrote_ivf_hdr = 1;
		}
		// a temporal unit: temporal delimiter, then the sequence header (from av1C) on key frames, then the sample
		CFDictionaryRef atoms = CMFormatDescriptionGetExtension(fd, kCMFormatDescriptionExtension_SampleDescriptionExtensionAtoms);
		CFDataRef av1c = atoms ? CFDictionaryGetValue(atoms, CFSTR("av1C")) : NULL;
		size_t seqn = key && av1c ? CFDataGetLength(av1c) - 4 : 0;
		uint8_t fh[12]; put_le32(fh, (uint32_t)(2 + seqn + len)); put_le32(fh + 4, (uint32_t)emitted); put_le32(fh + 8, 0);
		fwrite(fh, 1, 12, out); fwrite("\x12\x00", 1, 2, out);
		if (seqn) fwrite(CFDataGetBytePtr(av1c) + 4, 1, seqn, out);
		fwrite(d, 1, len, out);
	} else {
		if (key) write_param_sets(fd);
		for (size_t o = 0; o + 4 <= len;) {
			uint32_t n = d[o] << 24 | d[o + 1] << 16 | d[o + 2] << 8 | d[o + 3];
			fwrite("\0\0\0\1", 1, 4, out); fwrite(d + o + 4, 1, n, out); o += 4 + n;
		}
	}
	free(d);
	emitted++; keys += key; bytes += len;
}

static void gpu_bundles(const char *when) {
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < _dyld_image_count(); i++) {
		const char *n = _dyld_get_image_name(i);
		if (strstr(n, "GPUBundles") || strstr(n, "intelxevenc") || strstr(n, "libavcodec")) fprintf(stderr, "[%s] image %s\n", when, n);
	}
}
// what HandBrake does to decide whether a hardware encoder exists for a codec
static void probe(FourCharCode c) {
	NSDictionary *spec = @{ (__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderSpecification_RequireHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder: @YES };
	CFStringRef eid = NULL; CFDictionaryRef sup = NULL;
	OSStatus r = VTCopySupportedPropertyDictionaryForEncoder(1920, 1080, c, (__bridge CFDictionaryRef)spec, &eid, &sup);
	NSDictionary *pl = sup ? ((__bridge NSDictionary *)sup)[(__bridge NSString *)kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ProfileLevel] : nil;
	printf("probe %c%c%c%c: %d encoder %s, %ld properties, Main10 listed: %s\n", c >> 24, c >> 16, c >> 8, c, (int)r,
	       eid ? [(__bridge NSString *)eid UTF8String] : "-", sup ? (long)CFDictionaryGetCount(sup) : 0L,
	       [pl[(__bridge NSString *)kVTPropertySupportedValueListKey] containsObject:(__bridge id)kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel] ? "yes" : "no");
}

static void list(void) {
	CFArrayRef l = NULL;
	VTCopyVideoEncoderList(NULL, &l);
	for (CFIndex i = 0; l && i < CFArrayGetCount(l); i++) {
		NSDictionary *e = (__bridge NSDictionary *)CFArrayGetValueAtIndex(l, i);
		uint32_t t = [e[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderList_CodecType] unsignedIntValue];
		printf("%c%c%c%c  %-45s  %-32s  hw=%s\n", t >> 24, t >> 16, t >> 8, t, [e[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderList_EncoderID] UTF8String],
		       [e[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderList_DisplayName] UTF8String], [[e[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderList_IsHardwareAccelerated] description] UTF8String]);
	}
	if (l) CFRelease(l);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	@autoreleasepool {
		const char *lib = NULL, *encid = NULL; int any = 0, listonly = 0, realtime = 0, noreorder = 0, keyint = 0, ten = 0;
		long bitrate = 0, cbr = 0; double quality = -1, fps = 30;
		const char *pos[8]; int np = 0;
		for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
			if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--lib")) lib = argv[++i];
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--metal")) {    // bring Metal up first, as OBS or an app with Metal views does
				uint64_t t0 = clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW);
				NSArray *d = MTLCopyAllDevices();
				fprintf(stderr, "Metal: %lu devices (%.1f ms)\n", (unsigned long)d.count, (clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW) - t0) / 1e6);
			}
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--preload")) {   // load a binary first (the GPU plug-in, as Metal would), nothing else
				const char *p = argv[++i]; uint64_t t0 = clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW);
				void *h = dlopen(p, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
				fprintf(stderr, "preload %s: %s (%.1f ms)\n", p, h ? "ok" : dlerror(), (clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW) - t0) / 1e6);
			}
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--id")) encid = argv[++i];
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--any")) any = 1;
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--list")) listonly = 1;
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--bitrate")) bitrate = atol(argv[++i]);
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--cbr")) cbr = atol(argv[++i]);
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--quality")) quality = atof(argv[++i]);
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--realtime")) realtime = 1;
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--noreorder")) noreorder = 1;
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--keyint")) keyint = atoi(argv[++i]);
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--10bit")) ten = 1;
			else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "--fps")) fps = atof(argv[++i]);
			else if (np < 8) pos[np++] = argv[i];
		}
		if (lib) {
			void *h = dlopen(lib, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
			int (*reg)(void) = h ? (int (*)(void))dlsym(h, "IntelXeVEnc_Register") : NULL;
			if (!reg) { fprintf(stderr, "dlopen %s: %s\n", lib, dlerror()); return 1; }
			fprintf(stderr, "IntelXeVEnc_Register -> %d\n", reg());
		}
		if (listonly) { gpu_bundles("start"); list(); probe('hvc1'); probe('avc1'); gpu_bundles("after list"); return 0; }
		if (np < 5) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: see source\n"); return 2; }
		codec = !strcmp(pos[0], "hevc") ? 'hvc1' : !strcmp(pos[0], "h264") ? 'avc1' : 'av01';
		int w = atoi(pos[1]), hh = atoi(strchr(pos[1], 'x') + 1), frames = atoi(pos[3]);
		FILE *in = fopen(pos[2], "rb"); out = fopen(pos[4], "wb");
		if (!in || !out) { perror("open"); return 1; }
		size_t fsz = (size_t)w * hh * 3 / 2 * (ten ? 2 : 1);
		fseek(in, 0, SEEK_END); long nraw = ftell(in) / (long)fsz; fseek(in, 0, SEEK_SET);
		uint8_t *raw = malloc(fsz * nraw); fread(raw, 1, fsz * nraw, in); fclose(in);

		NSMutableDictionary *spec = [NSMutableDictionary dictionary];
		if (encid) spec[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderSpecification_EncoderID] = @(encid);
		else if (!any) spec[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderSpecification_EncoderID] =
			codec == 'hvc1' ? @"io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.videoencoder.hevc" : codec == 'avc1' ? @"io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.videoencoder.h264" : @"io.github.yusufklncc.intelxe.videoencoder.av1";
		else spec[(__bridge NSString *)kVTVideoEncoderSpecification_RequireHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder] = @YES;
		VTCompressionSessionRef s = NULL;
		OSStatus r = VTCompressionSessionCreate(NULL, w, hh, codec, (__bridge CFDictionaryRef)spec, NULL, NULL, cb, NULL, &s);
		if (r) { fprintf(stderr, "VTCompressionSessionCreate -> %d\n", (int)r); return 1; }
		CFStringRef eid = NULL; CFBooleanRef hw = NULL;
		VTSessionCopyProperty(s, kVTCompressionPropertyKey_EncoderID, NULL, &eid);
		VTSessionCopyProperty(s, kVTCompressionPropertyKey_UsingHardwareAcceleratedVideoEncoder, NULL, &hw);
		fprintf(stderr, "session: encoder %s, hardware %s\n", eid ? [(__bridge NSString *)eid UTF8String] : "?", hw == kCFBooleanTrue ? "yes" : "no");
		CFDictionaryRef sup = NULL; VTSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionary(s, &sup);
		fprintf(stderr, "supported properties: %ld\n", sup ? (long)CFDictionaryGetCount(sup) : -1L);
#define SET(k, v) do { OSStatus e_ = VTSessionSetProperty(s, k, (__bridge CFTypeRef)(v)); if (e_) fprintf(stderr, "set %s -> %d\n", #k, (int)e_); } while (0)
		SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_RealTime, realtime ? @YES : @NO);
		SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_AllowFrameReordering, noreorder ? @NO : @YES);
		SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ExpectedFrameRate, @(fps));
		if (keyint) SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_MaxKeyFrameInterval, @(keyint));
		if (bitrate) SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_AverageBitRate, @(bitrate));
		if (cbr) SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ConstantBitRate, @(cbr));
		if (quality >= 0) SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_Quality, @(quality));
		if (codec == 'hvc1') SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ProfileLevel, ten ? (__bridge id)kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel : (__bridge id)kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main_AutoLevel);
		if (codec == 'avc1') SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ProfileLevel, (__bridge id)kVTProfileLevel_H264_High_AutoLevel);
		SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ColorPrimaries, (__bridge id)kCVImageBufferColorPrimaries_ITU_R_709_2);
		SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_TransferFunction, (__bridge id)kCVImageBufferTransferFunction_ITU_R_709_2);
		SET(kVTCompressionPropertyKey_YCbCrMatrix, (__bridge id)kCVImageBufferYCbCrMatrix_ITU_R_709_2);
		r = VTCompressionSessionPrepareToEncodeFrames(s);
		if (r) fprintf(stderr, "PrepareToEncodeFrames -> %d\n", (int)r);

		OSType pf = ten ? kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr10BiPlanarVideoRange : kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarVideoRange;
		NSDictionary *pba = @{ (id)kCVPixelBufferIOSurfacePropertiesKey: @{} };
		uint64_t t0 = clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW);
		for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
			CVPixelBufferRef pb = NULL;
			if (CVPixelBufferCreate(NULL, w, hh, pf, (__bridge CFDictionaryRef)pba, &pb)) { fprintf(stderr, "CVPixelBufferCreate failed\n"); return 1; }
			CVPixelBufferLockBaseAddress(pb, 0);
			const uint8_t *f = raw + fsz * (i % nraw);
			size_t bpp = ten ? 2 : 1;
			for (int p = 0; p < 2; p++) {
				uint8_t *dst = CVPixelBufferGetBaseAddressOfPlane(pb, p); size_t pitch = CVPixelBufferGetBytesPerRowOfPlane(pb, p);
				int rows = p ? hh / 2 : hh; const uint8_t *srcp = f + (p ? (size_t)w * hh * bpp : 0);
				for (int y = 0; y < rows; y++) memcpy(dst + y * pitch, srcp + (size_t)y * w * bpp, w * bpp);
			}
			CVPixelBufferUnlockBaseAddress(pb, 0);
			CMTime pts = CMTimeMake((int64_t)i * 1000, (int32_t)(fps * 1000)), dur = CMTimeMake(1000, (int32_t)(fps * 1000));
			VTEncodeInfoFlags fl = 0;
			r = VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame(s, pb, pts, dur, NULL, NULL, &fl);
			CVPixelBufferRelease(pb);
			if (r) { fprintf(stderr, "EncodeFrame %d -> %d\n", i, (int)r); errors++; break; }
		}
		r = VTCompressionSessionCompleteFrames(s, kCMTimeInvalid);
		uint64_t t1 = clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW);
		if (r) fprintf(stderr, "CompleteFrames -> %d\n", (int)r);
		VTCompressionSessionInvalidate(s); CFRelease(s);
		fclose(out);
		double sec = (t1 - t0) / 1e9;
		printf("%s %dx%d: %lld/%d frames out, %lld key, %lld bytes (%.0f kbit/s at %.0f fps), %lld errors, %.1f fps wall\n",
		       pos[0], w, hh, emitted, frames, keys, bytes, bytes * 8.0 / 1000 / (frames / fps), fps, errors, frames / sec);
		return errors ? 1 : 0;
	}
}



================================================
FILE: videotoolbox/ffmpeg/apply-patches.sh
================================================
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# apply-patches.sh <ffmpeg-9.0.2 source>: the FFmpeg patches of the released libavcodec/libavutil, in the order they were
# applied, to an unpacked https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz
# (sha256 8c3850283eb25fa026482078a04051e0be17347b09ef81a0849bec15a96e002e). Then configure-shared.sh.
#
# Checked 2026-11-05: these eight patches + configure-shared.sh rebuild the installed libavcodec.63.dylib (714e989a) and
# libavutil.61.dylib (1682f7ab) with identical code and data; every byte matches except LC_UUID, which ld64 derives from
# the link before `make install` strips the debug map (object file paths of the build directory). That build was

cd "${1:?usage: apply-patches.sh <ffmpeg-9.0.2 source>}"
for p in \
    ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-decode-free-a-picture-without-a-host-wait \

FFmpeg 9.0.2 vp9: release the hwaccel picture before the frame (backport of upstream FFmpeg master vp9.c)

vp9_frame_unref() dropped the frame (tf) before its hwaccel_picture_private, and vp9_frame_replace() replaced the
picture private after the frame; upstream now releases / replaces the hwaccel picture first, as av1dec.c does, so the

FILE: videotoolbox/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-decode-dpb-slots-below-maxDpbSlots.patch
================================================
FFmpeg 9.0.2 vulkan: H.264 and HEVC decode number their DPB slots below the session's maxDpbSlots

The H.264 and HEVC Vulkan hwaccels passed a picture's index in the decoder's own DPB array as its slotIndex (and as
its baseArrayLayer with a layered DPB). That array is not the Vulkan DPB: HEVC's has 32 entries, H.264's 36, and both
hold pictures that only wait for output. HEVC takes the new picture's entry in alloc_frame() before
ff_hevc_frame_rps() releases the references it no longer needs and before ff_hevc_output_frames() bumps, so with a
16-picture DPB (sps_max_dec_pic_buffering 16) the index reaches 16: on the JCT-VC streams RPS_B_qualcomm_5,
RPS_C_ericsson_5 and RPS_E_qualcomm_5 on 4 / 1 / 14 pictures (checked with libavcodec's own alloc_frame() and with
tests/hevc/dpbslots.py; at most 10 on the other 144 HEVC_v1 streams). A slotIndex at or above maxDpbSlots is invalid
usage; Mesa's ANV (16 H.265 slots) wrote it into a 16-entry stack array and the decoding process aborted in
__stack_chk_fail (Arc B580, 13 Nov 2026). H.264's long-term references were also looked up among the first 16
entries only, so a long-term reference further on was given slot 0 and the fields of entry 0.

Now, as vulkan_av1.c and vulkan_vp9.c already do: each picture keeps the slot it was decoded into in its
hwaccel_picture_private while it is a reference, and a new picture takes the lowest slot none of the current
references holds (ff_vk_decode_free_dpb_slot); a reference that was never decoded (a picture generated for a missing
reference, an H.264 frame_num gap) gets a free slot when it is first used, the second field of an H.264 pair keeps
the first one's. The references of a picture are at most maxDpbSlots - 1 for any conforming stream (HEVC: 15 + the
current picture in a 16-picture DPB; H.264: 16 + 1 in ANV's 17 slots); with none free the picture fails with
AVERROR_INVALIDDATA instead of reaching the driver. The RefPicSet* lists name the same slots.

--- a/libavcodec/vulkan_decode.h
+++ b/libavcodec/vulkan_decode.h
@@ -151,6 +151,23 @@
 /**
  * Add slice data to frame.
  */
+/**
+ * The lowest DPB slot below the session's maxDpbSlots that is not in used
+ * (a mask of the slots the current picture's references hold), or -1.
+ * Slot numbers must stay below maxDpbSlots (the slotIndex rules of
+ * VkVideoDecodeInfoKHR); a decoder's own DPB array index does not: libavcodec
+ * takes a new picture's DPB entry before the references it no longer needs
+ * are released and keeps pictures waiting for output there, so an H.265
+ * stream with a 16-picture DPB used entry 16 on a 16-slot session.
+ */
+static inline int ff_vk_decode_free_dpb_slot(uint64_t used, unsigned max_slots)
+{
+    for (unsigned i = 0; i < FFMIN(max_slots, 64); i++)
+        if (!(used & (UINT64_C(1) << i)))
+            return i;
+    return -1;
+}

FILE: videotoolbox/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-decode-free-a-picture-without-a-host-wait.patch
================================================
FFmpeg 9.0.2: vulkan_decode: free a decoded picture without a host wait

Backport of upstream FFmpeg 4e141536 ("vulkan: manage image views with AVRefStruct", Lynne, 2026-07-26:
"The biggest gain is no longer needing to spin on the CPU on a semaphore waiting for the image to become
freeable"), reduced to 9.0.2's structures: the image views ff_vk_decode_prepare_frame() makes are owned by a
refcounted holder (views_buf); ff_vk_decode_frame() makes the execution hold it for the current picture and for
every reference, so ff_vk_decode_free_frame() just drops its reference instead of vkWaitSemaphores() on the
picture's decode. The images themselves were already held by the executions (ff_vk_exec_add_dep_frame), the slice
buffer is the execution's once submitted. Pictures of the SDR (compute) path keep the old wait (views_buf NULL).

--- a/libavcodec/vulkan_decode.c
+++ b/libavcodec/vulkan_decode.c
@@ -178,6 +178,45 @@
     return avf;
 }
 
+typedef struct FFVulkanDecodeViews {
+    VkDevice                     dev;
+    const VkAllocationCallbacks *alloc;
+    PFN_vkDestroyImageView       destroy_image_view;
+    int                          nb_views;
+    VkImageView                  views[2];
+} FFVulkanDecodeViews;
+
+static void free_views(void *opaque, uint8_t *data)
+{
+    FFVulkanDecodeViews *v = (FFVulkanDecodeViews *)data;
+    for (int i = 0; i < v->nb_views; i++)
+        v->destroy_image_view(v->dev, v->views[i], v->alloc);
+    av_free(v);
+}
+
+static AVBufferRef *alloc_views(FFVulkanDecodeShared *ctx)

FILE: videotoolbox/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-exec-fence-reset-at-submit.patch
================================================
FFmpeg 9.0.2 vulkan: an execution's fence is reset at submission, so one that is never submitted is not waited on forever

ff_vk_exec_start() waited for the execution context's fence and reset it at once; the submission that signals it
again comes later, in ff_vk_exec_submit(). When anything between the two fails - vkEndCommandBuffer returning an
error, an error while recording, a failed vkQueueSubmit2 - the context is left with an unsignalled fence that nothing
will signal, and the next ff_vk_exec_start() on it (the pool hands its contexts out round robin), ff_vk_exec_wait()
or ff_vk_exec_pool_free() (after an earlier submission) waits with UINT64_MAX: the decoder hangs. Seen on an Arc
B580 (13 Nov 2026) with a Mesa build that refused out-of-range DPB slots by failing vkEndCommandBuffer
(VK_ERROR_INVALID_VIDEO_STD_PARAMETERS_KHR): the HEVC streams RPS_B/C/E_qualcomm/ericsson and the H.264 streams
HCBP2/HCMP1_HHI_A hung after the first refused picture instead of losing it.

The fence is now reset in ff_vk_exec_submit() right before vkQueueSubmit2, and replaced with a signalled one if the
submission fails (a failed vkQueueSubmit2 leaves it as it was: unsignalled). An execution that is started and
abandoned therefore keeps a signalled fence. FFmpeg master was not checked.

--- a/libavutil/vulkan.c
+++ b/libavutil/vulkan.c
@@ -598,9 +598,12 @@
         .flags = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_USAGE_ONE_TIME_SUBMIT_BIT,
     };
 
-    /* Wait for the fence to be signalled */
+    /* Wait for the fence to be signalled. It is reset in ff_vk_exec_submit(),
+     * right before the submission that signals it again: an execution that
+     * is started but never submitted (vkEndCommandBuffer failed, an error
+     * while recording) leaves it signalled, and the next ff_vk_exec_start()
+     * or ff_vk_exec_wait() on this context does not wait forever. */
     vk->WaitForFences(s->hwctx->act_dev, 1, &e->fence, VK_TRUE, UINT64_MAX);
-    vk->ResetFences(s->hwctx->act_dev, 1, &e->fence);
 
     /* Discard queue dependencies */
     ff_vk_exec_discard_deps(s, e);
@@ -973,6 +976,8 @@
         ff_vk_exec_discard_deps(s, e);
         return AVERROR_EXTERNAL;
     }
+
+    vk->ResetFences(s->hwctx->act_dev, 1, &e->fence);
 
 #if FF_API_VULKAN_SYNC_QUEUES
 FF_DISABLE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS
@@ -987,9 +992,20 @@
 #endif
 
     if (ret != VK_SUCCESS) {
+        VkFenceCreateInfo fence_create = {
+            .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_CREATE_INFO,
+            .flags = VK_FENCE_CREATE_SIGNALED_BIT,
+        };
         av_log(s, AV_LOG_ERROR, "Unable to submit command buffer: %s\n",
                ff_vk_ret2str(ret));
         ff_vk_exec_discard_deps(s, e);
+        /* A failed submission leaves the fence unsignalled (reset above):
+         * replace it with a signalled one, so nothing waits on it forever. */
+        vk->DestroyFence(s->hwctx->act_dev, e->fence, s->hwctx->alloc);
+        e->fence = VK_NULL_HANDLE;

FILE: videotoolbox/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-exec-frame-deps-keep-the-frames-context.patch
================================================
FFmpeg 9.0.2 vulkan: an execution's frame dependency keeps the frame's frames context alive

ff_vk_exec_add_dep_frame() keeps a reference to the frame's buffer (buf[0]) until the execution is reused or its pool
freed, but not to the AVHWFramesContext the buffer belongs to. When a decoder drops a frames context while an
execution still depends on one of its frames - VP9 changes resolution inside a stream and keeps predicting from the
old-size references (reference scaling), so the new size's decodes depend on frames of the old frames context, which
goes away with its last AVFrame - the buffer goes back to a freed pool: hwcontext_vulkan's vulkan_frame_free_cb then
reads the freed AVHWFramesContext (EXC_BAD_ACCESS at 0x10 in VideoToolbox clients, at the end of the session:
avcodec_free_context -> ff_vk_decode_uninit -> ff_vk_exec_pool_free -> ff_vk_exec_discard_deps -> av_buffer_unref ->
pool_release_buffer -> vulkan_frame_free_cb, on the libvpx conformance vector vp90-2-05-resize). The dependency now
also references hw_frames_ctx, after the buffer in buf_deps so that it is released after it. FFmpeg master still has
the same code (libavutil/vulkan.c ff_vk_exec_add_dep_frame).

--- a/libavutil/vulkan.c
+++ b/libavutil/vulkan.c
@@ -848,6 +848,22 @@
             return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
         }
         e->nb_buf_deps++;
+
+        /* The frame's buffer goes back to its frames context's pool when the
+         * execution drops it: keep that context alive until then (after it in
+         * buf_deps, so it is released after the buffer). A decode can depend on
+         * frames of a frames context the decoder no longer uses (VP9 reference
+         * scaling across a resolution change), which is freed with its last
+         * frame otherwise, and the pool's free callback then reads freed memory. */
+        if (f->hw_frames_ctx) {
+            ARR_REALLOC(e, buf_deps, &e->buf_deps_alloc_size, e->nb_buf_deps);
+            e->buf_deps[e->nb_buf_deps] = av_buffer_ref(f->hw_frames_ctx);
+            if (!e->buf_deps[e->nb_buf_deps]) {
+                ff_vk_exec_discard_deps(s, e);
+                return AVERROR(ENOMEM);
+            }
+            e->nb_buf_deps++;
+        }
     }
 
     e->frame_deps[e->nb_frame_deps] = f;

FILE: videotoolbox/ffmpeg/ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-one-queue-per-decode-session-fixed-exec-depth.patch
================================================
FFmpeg 9.0.2: vulkan: one queue per video decode session, a fixed exec depth of 4

Backports of upstream FFmpeg 1d14f9f8 ("vulkan: decouple execution pool depths from queue and thread counts",
Lynne, 2026-07-19: async_depth = FF_VK_DEFAULT_EXEC_CONTEXTS (4), plus the thread count for thread-safe hwaccels)
and of upstream master's queue rule in ff_vk_exec_pool_init (libavutil/vulkan.c: pin_queue for video queue families,
e->qi = phase % qf->num): all contexts of one decode pool use one queue, pools take the family's queues in turn.
9.0.2 spread a session's contexts over the queues (e->qi = i % qf->num), so consecutive pictures - which depend on
each other - alternated between two queues, and every picture waited for the previous one across queues (on the
B580: a kernel round trip per picture). Only video DECODE families are pinned here; encode is unchanged.

-     * for a majority of streams. */

-    /* We don't need more than 2 per thread context */
-    async_depth = FFMIN(async_depth, 2*avctx->thread_count);
-    /* Make sure there are enough async contexts for each thread */
-    async_depth = FFMAX(async_depth, avctx->thread_count);

+     * A small fixed depth is enough to keep the GPU fed, as submissions are
+     * serialized for hardware decoding; thread-safe hwaccels submit from
+     * every frame thread concurrently, and need a context per thread. */
+    async_depth = 4;
+    if (ffhwaccel(avctx->hwaccel)->caps_internal & HWACCEL_CAP_THREAD_SAFE)
+        async_depth = FFMAX(async_depth, avctx->thread_count);
 
     err = ff_vk_exec_pool_init(s, ctx->qf, &ctx->exec_pool,

FILE: videotoolbox/tests/av1parse_test.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// av1parse_test <stream.ivf|.obu> [golden.txt]: the direct path's AV1 parser (vtdirect_av1.c) over a recorded stream,
// without a GPU. Each IVF frame (or, for a low-overhead .obu stream, each temporal unit from one temporal delimiter
// to the next) is handed over as the sample an MP4 carries. Prints, in the format of tests/av1/mkgolden.py (made from
// FFmpeg 9.0.2's trace_headers and the same rules written again in Python; the format is described there):
//   seq ...                         a sequence header as it goes into StdVideoAV1SequenceHeader / ColorConfig
//   frame / refs / q / seg / lf / cdef / lr / tile / gm / grain / setup / tiles
//                                   a decoded frame: its Std picture information, the DPB slot, the references with
//                                   their reference information, and where its tiles are in the sample
//   show ...                        a show_existing_frame
//   tu ...                          the sample: its frames and the one shown
// With a golden file it compares line by line and exits 1 at the first difference.
//   av1parse_test --fuzz <seed> <iterations> <stream>: the samples damaged at random (bytes changed, cut, repeated),
//   parsed again and again: no crash, no read outside the sample (build with -fsanitize=address,undefined), and
//   whatever the parser hands out stays in range (tile offsets in the sample, DPB slots, reference counts).
// Build (here, no FFmpeg): cc -O1 -Wall -I<mesa>/include av1parse_test.c ../vtdirect_av1.c -o av1parse_test
#include "../vtdirect_av1.h"
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static FILE *golden; static int lineno, bad;
static void emit(const char *l) {
	lineno++;
	if (!golden) { printf("%s\n", l); return; }
	char g[65536];
	if (!fgets(g, sizeof g, golden)) { if (!bad) printf("line %d: golden ends; got: %s\n", lineno, l); bad = 1; return; }
	g[strcspn(g, "\n")] = 0;
	if (strcmp(g, l) && !bad) { printf("line %d differs\n  want: %s\n  got:  %s\n", lineno, g, l); bad = 1; }
}

typedef struct { char *b; size_t n, o; } Str;
static void add(Str *s, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
static void add(Str *s, const char *fmt, ...) {
	va_list ap; va_start(ap, fmt);
	if (s->o < s->n) s->o += (size_t)vsnprintf(s->b + s->o, s->n - s->o, fmt, ap);
	va_end(ap);
	if (s->o >= s->n) s->o = s->n - 1;
}
#define LINE(...) do { char b_[8192]; Str o_ = { b_, sizeof b_, 0 }; add(&o_, __VA_ARGS__); emit(b_); } while (0)

static void print_seq(const Av1dSeq *q) {
	char b[2048]; Str o = { b, sizeof b, 0 };
	const StdVideoAV1SequenceHeader *d = &q->std;
	const StdVideoAV1ColorConfig *c = &q->color;
	const StdVideoAV1SequenceHeaderFlags *fl = &d->flags;
	add(&o, "seq profile=%d ops=%d op0=%03x level=%d tier=%d w=%d h=%d bits=%d/%d fid=%d/%d/%d flags=", d->seq_profile, q->ops, q->op_idc[0],
	    q->level[0], q->tier[0], d->max_frame_width_minus_1 + 1, d->max_frame_height_minus_1 + 1, d->frame_width_bits_minus_1 + 1,
	    d->frame_height_bits_minus_1 + 1, fl->frame_id_numbers_present_flag, d->delta_frame_id_length_minus_2,
	    d->additional_frame_id_length_minus_1);
	const unsigned v[] = { fl->still_picture, fl->reduced_still_picture_header, fl->use_128x128_superblock, fl->enable_filter_intra,
		fl->enable_intra_edge_filter, fl->enable_interintra_compound, fl->enable_masked_compound, fl->enable_warped_motion,
		fl->enable_dual_filter, fl->enable_order_hint, fl->enable_jnt_comp, fl->enable_ref_frame_mvs, fl->frame_id_numbers_present_flag,
		fl->enable_superres, fl->enable_cdef, fl->enable_restoration, fl->film_grain_params_present, fl->timing_info_present_flag,
		fl->initial_display_delay_present_flag };
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof v / sizeof *v; i++) add(&o, "%u", v[i]);
	add(&o, " ohbits=%d sct=%d imv=%d bd=%d mono=%d ss=%d/%d range=%d cdp=%d cp=%d tc=%d mc=%d csp=%d sep=%d", d->order_hint_bits_minus_1 + 1,
	    d->seq_force_screen_content_tools, d->seq_force_integer_mv, c->BitDepth, c->flags.mono_chrome, c->subsampling_x, c->subsampling_y,
	    c->flags.color_range, c->flags.color_description_present_flag, c->color_primaries, c->transfer_characteristics,
	    c->matrix_coefficients, c->chroma_sample_position, c->flags.separate_uv_delta_q);
	if (fl->timing_info_present_flag)
		add(&o, " timing=%u/%u/%u/%u", q->timing.num_units_in_display_tick, q->timing.time_scale, q->timing.flags.equal_picture_interval,
		    q->timing.num_ticks_per_picture_minus_1);
	add(&o, " dm=%d", q->decoder_model_info_present);
	emit(b);
}

static void ref_info(Str *o, const StdVideoDecodeAV1ReferenceInfo *r, int saved) {
	add(o, "%u:%u:%02x:%u:%u", r->frame_type, r->OrderHint, r->RefFrameSignBias, r->flags.disable_frame_end_update_cdf, r->flags.segmentation_enabled);
	if (saved) { add(o, ":"); for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) add(o, "%s%u", i ? "_" : "", r->SavedOrderHints[i]); }
}

static void print_frame(int tu, const Av1dFrame *fr) {
	char b[16384]; Str o = { b, sizeof b, 0 };
	if (fr->show_existing) {
		LINE("show tu=%d slot=%d dpb=%d refresh=%02x size=%dx%d grain=%d missing=%d", tu, fr->show_slot, fr->dpb, fr->refresh, fr->width,
		     fr->height, fr->apply_grain, fr->missing);
		return;
	}
	const StdVideoDecodeAV1PictureInfo *p = &fr->std;
	const StdVideoDecodeAV1PictureInfoFlags *fl = &p->flags;
	add(&o, "frame tu=%d type=%d show=%d oh=%u prf=%u refresh=%02x fid=%u size=%dx%d fw=%d denom=%u dpb=%d hb=%d flags=", tu, p->frame_type,
	    fr->shown, p->OrderHint, p->primary_ref_frame, p->refresh_frame_flags, p->current_frame_id, fr->width, fr->height, fr->frame_width,
	    p->coded_denom, fr->dpb, fr->hdr_bits);
	const unsigned v[] = { fl->error_resilient_mode, fl->disable_cdf_update, fl->use_superres, fl->render_and_frame_size_different,
		fl->allow_screen_content_tools, fl->is_filter_switchable, fl->force_integer_mv, fl->frame_size_override_flag,
		fl->buffer_removal_time_present_flag, fl->allow_intrabc, fl->frame_refs_short_signaling, fl->allow_high_precision_mv,
		fl->is_motion_mode_switchable, fl->use_ref_frame_mvs, fl->disable_frame_end_update_cdf, fl->allow_warped_motion, fl->reduced_tx_set,
		fl->reference_select, fl->skip_mode_present, fl->delta_q_present, fl->delta_lf_present, fl->delta_lf_multi, fl->segmentation_enabled,
		fl->segmentation_update_map, fl->segmentation_temporal_update, fl->segmentation_update_data, fl->UsesLr, fl->usesChromaLr,
		fl->apply_grain };
	for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof v / sizeof *v; i++) add(&o, "%u", v[i]);
	emit(b);
	o.o = 0;
	add(&o, " refs idx=");
	for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) add(&o, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", fr->ref_frame_idx[i]);
	add(&o, " names=");
	for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) add(&o, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", fr->name_dpb[i]);
	add(&o, " ohs=");
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) add(&o, "%s%u", i ? "," : "", p->OrderHints[i]);
	add(&o, " skip=%u,%u list=", p->SkipModeFrame[0], p->SkipModeFrame[1]);
	for (int i = 0; i < fr->nrefs; i++) { add(&o, "%s%d@%d=", i ? " " : "", fr->refs[i].dpb, fr->refs[i].slot); ref_info(&o, &fr->refs[i].info, 1); }
	if (!fr->nrefs) add(&o, "-");
	add(&o, " missing=%d", fr->missing);
	emit(b);
	const StdVideoAV1Quantization *q = p->pQuantization;
	LINE(" q base=%u dq=%d,%d,%d,%d,%d diffuv=%u qm=%u:%u,%u,%u dqres=%u dlfres=%u interp=%d tx=%d", q->base_q_idx, q->DeltaQYDc, q->DeltaQUDc,
	     q->DeltaQUAc, q->DeltaQVDc, q->DeltaQVAc, q->flags.diff_uv_delta, q->flags.using_qmatrix, q->qm_y, q->qm_u, q->qm_v, p->delta_q_res,
	     p->delta_lf_res, p->interpolation_filter, p->TxMode);
	o.o = 0;
	add(&o, " seg");
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
		add(&o, " %02x:", p->pSegmentation->FeatureEnabled[i]);
		for (int j = 0; j < 8; j++) add(&o, "%s%d", j ? "," : "", p->pSegmentation->FeatureData[i][j]);
	}
	emit(b);
	const StdVideoAV1LoopFilter *lf = p->pLoopFilter;
	LINE(" lf lvl=%u,%u,%u,%u sharp=%u de=%u du=%u ref=%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d mode=%d,%d", lf->loop_filter_level[0], lf->loop_filter_level[1],
	     lf->loop_filter_level[2], lf->loop_filter_level[3], lf->loop_filter_sharpness, lf->flags.loop_filter_delta_enabled,
	     lf->flags.loop_filter_delta_update, lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[0], lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[1], lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[2],
	     lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[3], lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[4], lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[5], lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[6],
	     lf->loop_filter_ref_deltas[7], lf->loop_filter_mode_deltas[0], lf->loop_filter_mode_deltas[1]);
	const StdVideoAV1CDEF *cd = p->pCDEF;
	o.o = 0;
	add(&o, " cdef damp=%u bits=%u y=", cd->cdef_damping_minus_3, cd->cdef_bits);
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) add(&o, "%s%u/%u", i ? "," : "", cd->cdef_y_pri_strength[i], cd->cdef_y_sec_strength[i]);
	add(&o, " uv=");
	for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) add(&o, "%s%u/%u", i ? "," : "", cd->cdef_uv_pri_strength[i], cd->cdef_uv_sec_strength[i]);
	emit(b);
	const StdVideoAV1LoopRestoration *lr = p->pLoopRestoration;
	LINE(" lr type=%d,%d,%d size=%u,%u,%u", lr->FrameRestorationType[0], lr->FrameRestorationType[1], lr->FrameRestorationType[2],
	     lr->LoopRestorationSize[0], lr->LoopRestorationSize[1], lr->LoopRestorationSize[2]);
	const StdVideoAV1TileInfo *t = p->pTileInfo;
	o.o = 0;
	add(&o, " tile cols=%u rows=%u uni=%u ctx=%u tsb=%u mc=", t->TileCols, t->TileRows, t->flags.uniform_tile_spacing_flag,
	    t->context_update_tile_id, t->tile_size_bytes_minus_1);
	for (int i = 0; i < t->TileCols; i++) add(&o, "%s%u", i ? "," : "", t->pMiColStarts[i]);
	add(&o, " mr=");
	for (int i = 0; i < t->TileRows; i++) add(&o, "%s%u", i ? "," : "", t->pMiRowStarts[i]);
	add(&o, " w=");
	for (int i = 0; i < t->TileCols; i++) add(&o, "%s%u", i ? "," : "", t->pWidthInSbsMinus1[i]);
	add(&o, " h=");
	for (int i = 0; i < t->TileRows; i++) add(&o, "%s%u", i ? "," : "", t->pHeightInSbsMinus1[i]);
	emit(b);
	o.o = 0;
	add(&o, " gm");
	int any = 0;
	for (int r = 1; r < 8; r++) {
		if (!p->pGlobalMotion->GmType[r]) continue;
		any = 1;
		add(&o, " %d:%u:", r, p->pGlobalMotion->GmType[r]);
		for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++) add(&o, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", p->pGlobalMotion->gm_params[r][i]);
	}
	if (!any) add(&o, " -");
	emit(b);
	if (p->pFilmGrain) {
		const StdVideoAV1FilmGrain *g = p->pFilmGrain;
		o.o = 0;
		add(&o, " grain seed=%u ref=%u y=", g->grain_seed, g->film_grain_params_ref_idx);
		for (int i = 0; i < g->num_y_points; i++) add(&o, "%s%u:%u", i ? "," : "", g->point_y_value[i], g->point_y_scaling[i]);
		add(&o, " cfl=%u cb=", g->flags.chroma_scaling_from_luma);
		for (int i = 0; i < g->num_cb_points; i++) add(&o, "%s%u:%u", i ? "," : "", g->point_cb_value[i], g->point_cb_scaling[i]);
		add(&o, " cr=");
		for (int i = 0; i < g->num_cr_points; i++) add(&o, "%s%u:%u", i ? "," : "", g->point_cr_value[i], g->point_cr_scaling[i]);
		add(&o, " scal=%u lag=%u ary=", g->grain_scaling_minus_8, g->ar_coeff_lag);
		for (int i = 0; i < 24; i++) add(&o, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", g->ar_coeffs_y_plus_128[i]);
		add(&o, " arcb=");
		for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) add(&o, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", g->ar_coeffs_cb_plus_128[i]);
		add(&o, " arcr=");
		for (int i = 0; i < 25; i++) add(&o, "%s%d", i ? "," : "", g->ar_coeffs_cr_plus_128[i]);
		add(&o, " shift=%u gss=%u cb=%u/%u/%u cr=%u/%u/%u ov=%u clip=%u", g->ar_coeff_shift_minus_6, g->grain_scale_shift, g->cb_mult,
		    g->cb_luma_mult, g->cb_offset, g->cr_mult, g->cr_luma_mult, g->cr_offset, g->flags.overlap_flag, g->flags.clip_to_restricted_range);
		emit(b);
	}
	o.o = 0;
	add(&o, " setup ");
	ref_info(&o, &fr->setup, 0);
	add(&o, " tiles n=%u tg=%d size=%zu at=", fr->ntiles, fr->ntg, fr->size);
	for (uint32_t i = 0; i < fr->ntiles; i++) add(&o, "%s%u:%u", i ? "," : "", fr->tile_src[i], fr->tile_size[i]);
	emit(b);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

typedef struct { uint8_t *p; size_t n; } Sample;

static uint8_t *slurp(const char *path, size_t *n) {
	FILE *fp = fopen(path, "rb");
	if (!fp) return NULL;
	fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END); long l = ftell(fp); fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_SET);
	uint8_t *d = malloc(l > 0 ? (size_t)l : 1);
	*n = d ? fread(d, 1, (size_t)(l > 0 ? l : 0), fp) : 0;
	fclose(fp);
	return d;
}

// the samples of an IVF file (its frames) or of a low-overhead OBU stream (cut at temporal delimiters)
static int samples_of(const uint8_t *d, size_t n, Sample **out) {
	int cnt = 0, cap = 0;
	*out = NULL;
	if (n >= 32 && !memcmp(d, "DKIF", 4)) {
		size_t pos = d[6] | d[7] << 8;
		while (pos + 12 <= n) {
			const size_t sz = (size_t)d[pos] | (size_t)d[pos + 1] << 8 | (size_t)d[pos + 2] << 16 | (size_t)d[pos + 3] << 24;
			pos += 12;
			if (sz > n - pos) break;
			if (cnt == cap) { cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 64; *out = realloc(*out, (size_t)cap * sizeof **out); }
			(*out)[cnt].p = malloc(sz ? sz : 1); memcpy((*out)[cnt].p, d + pos, sz); (*out)[cnt].n = sz; cnt++;
			pos += sz;
		}
		return cnt;
	}
	size_t pos = 0, start = 0;
	while (pos < n) {
		const size_t at = pos;
		const int type = (d[pos] >> 3) & 15, ext = (d[pos] >> 2) & 1, has_size = (d[pos] >> 1) & 1;
		size_t h = 1 + (size_t)ext;
		uint64_t sz = 0;
		if (!has_size) break;
		for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) { if (pos + h >= n) return cnt; sz |= (uint64_t)(d[pos + h] & 0x7f) << (7 * i); if (!(d[pos + h++] & 0x80)) break; }
		if (sz > n - pos - h) break;
		pos += h + (size_t)sz;
		if (type == 2 && at > start) {   // a temporal delimiter starts the next unit
			if (cnt == cap) { cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 64; *out = realloc(*out, (size_t)cap * sizeof **out); }
			(*out)[cnt].p = malloc(at - start); memcpy((*out)[cnt].p, d + start, at - start); (*out)[cnt].n = at - start; cnt++;
			start = at;
		}
	}
	if (pos > start) {
		if (cnt == cap) { cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 64; *out = realloc(*out, (size_t)cap * sizeof **out); }
		(*out)[cnt].p = malloc(pos - start); memcpy((*out)[cnt].p, d + start, pos - start); (*out)[cnt].n = pos - start; cnt++;
	}
	return cnt;
}

static int check_invariants(const Av1dSample *out, size_t n) {
	if (out->nframes < 0 || out->nframes > AV1D_MAX_FRAMES || out->shown >= out->nframes) return 1;
	for (int k = 0; k < out->nframes; k++) {
		const Av1dFrame *fr = &out->f[k];
		if (fr->show_existing) { if (fr->dpb >= AV1D_SLOTS || fr->show_slot > 7) return 2; continue; }
		if (fr->dpb < 0 || fr->dpb >= AV1D_SLOTS || fr->nrefs > 7 || fr->ntiles > AV1D_MAX_TILES) return 3;
		size_t total = 0;
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < fr->ntiles; i++) {
			if (fr->tile_src[i] > n || fr->tile_size[i] > n - fr->tile_src[i]) return 4;
			total += fr->tile_size[i];
		}
		if (total != fr->size) return 5;
		for (int i = 0; i < fr->nrefs; i++) if (fr->refs[i].dpb < 0 || fr->refs[i].dpb >= AV1D_SLOTS || fr->refs[i].dpb == fr->dpb) return 6;
		for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) if (fr->name_dpb[i] < -1 || fr->name_dpb[i] >= AV1D_SLOTS) return 7;
		if (fr->std.pTileInfo->TileCols * fr->std.pTileInfo->TileRows > (int)AV1D_MAX_TILES) return 8;
	}
	return 0;
}

static uint64_t rng;
static uint32_t rnd(void) { rng ^= rng << 13; rng ^= rng >> 7; rng ^= rng << 17; return (uint32_t)(rng >> 11); }

static int fuzz(Sample *sm, int cnt, uint64_t seed, int iters) {
	rng = seed * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull + 1;
	static Av1dSample out;
	long pictures = 0, errors = 0, unsupported = 0;
	for (int it = 0; it < iters; it++) {
		Av1dState s; av1d_init(&s);
		for (int i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
			size_t n = sm[i].n;
			uint8_t *d = malloc(n + 64);
			memcpy(d, sm[i].p, n);
			const int what = (int)(rnd() % 8);
			if (what < 4 && n) { for (int k = 0, m = 1 + (int)(rnd() % 8); k < m; k++) d[rnd() % n] ^= (uint8_t)(1u << (rnd() % 8)); }
			else if (what == 4 && n) n = rnd() % n;   // cut
			else if (what == 5 && n > 4) { const size_t at = rnd() % n; d[at] = (uint8_t)rnd(); }
			uint8_t *e = malloc(n ? n : 1);   // exactly n bytes: ASan sees any read past the sample
			memcpy(e, d, n);
			free(d);
			const int r = av1d_parse_sample(&s, e, n, &out);
			if (r == AV1D_PICTURE) { pictures++; const int c = check_invariants(&out, n); if (c) { printf("fuzz: iteration %d sample %d: invariant %d broken\n", it, i, c); free(e); return 1; } }
			else if (r == AV1D_ERROR) errors++;
			else if (r == AV1D_UNSUPPORTED) unsupported++;
			for (int k = 0; k < out.nframes && r == AV1D_PICTURE; k++)   // as vtdirect.c: a frame it could not decode
				if (!out.f[k].show_existing && (rnd() % 16) == 0) av1d_lost(&s, out.f[k].gen);
			if ((rnd() % 64) == 0) av1d_flush(&s);
			free(e);
		}
	}
	printf("fuzz: %d iterations of %d samples: %ld with pictures, %ld damaged, %ld unsupported, no invariant broken\n", iters, cnt, pictures, errors, unsupported);
	return 0;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	if (argc >= 5 && !strcmp(argv[1], "--fuzz")) {
		size_t n; uint8_t *d = slurp(argv[4], &n);
		if (!d) { perror(argv[4]); return 2; }
		Sample *sm; const int cnt = samples_of(d, n, &sm);
		return fuzz(sm, cnt, strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 10), atoi(argv[3]));
	}
	if (argc < 2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: av1parse_test <stream.ivf|.obu> [golden.txt] | --fuzz <seed> <iterations> <stream>\n"); return 2; }
	size_t n; uint8_t *d = slurp(argv[1], &n);
	if (!d) { perror(argv[1]); return 2; }
	if (argc > 2 && !(golden = fopen(argv[2], "r"))) { perror(argv[2]); return 2; }
	Sample *sm; const int cnt = samples_of(d, n, &sm);
	static Av1dState s; av1d_init(&s);
	s.check = 1;
	static Av1dSample out;
	uint8_t seen[256]; size_t seenn = 0;
	for (int i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
		const int r = av1d_parse_sample(&s, sm[i].p, sm[i].n, &out);
		if (s.have_seq && (s.seq.rawn != seenn || memcmp(s.seq.raw, seen, seenn))) {
			print_seq(&s.seq);
			seenn = s.seq.rawn; memcpy(seen, s.seq.raw, seenn);
		}
		if (r < 0) {
			char l[256]; snprintf(l, sizeof l, "tu %d sample: %d %s", i, r, av1d_why(&s));
			if (golden) { if (!bad) printf("%s\n", l); bad = 1; } else printf("%s\n", l);
			if (r == AV1D_UNSUPPORTED) break;
			continue;
		}
		for (int k = 0; k < out.nframes; k++) print_frame(i, &out.f[k]);
		LINE("tu %d frames=%d shown=%d extra=%d", i, out.nframes, out.shown, out.extra_shown);
	}
	if (golden) {
		char g[256];
		if (!bad && fgets(g, sizeof g, golden)) { printf("line %d: output ends; golden has: %s", lineno + 1, g); bad = 1; }
		if (!bad) printf("%s: %d lines identical to %s\n", argv[1], lineno, argv[2]);
	}
	return bad;
}

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# dpbindex.sh <ffmpeg-9.0.2 source> <build dir> <stream.264|.bit ...>: libavcodec's own DPB array index of every new
# picture (H.264 find_unused_picture(), HEVC alloc_frame()), the number FFmpeg 9.0.2's Vulkan hwaccels passed as the
# DPB slotIndex before ffmpeg-9.0.2-vulkan-decode-dpb-slots-below-maxDpbSlots.patch. Builds, on this Mac (no GPU), a
# copy of the source with one fprintf at each of the two places, as a minimal software-only ffmpeg (H.264/HEVC
# decoders and raw demuxers), and decodes each stream single-threaded (as the hwaccel decodes). The source is copied,
# not changed. One line per stream: "<name> <pictures> <max index> <pictures at or above 16> <at or above 17>"
# (ANV's H.265 / H.264 decode slots).
# 13 Nov: HEVC_v1 (147 streams): only RPS_B_qualcomm_5 / RPS_C_ericsson_5 / RPS_E_qualcomm_5 reach 16 (4 / 1 / 14
# pictures; tests/hevc/dpbslots.py's replay gives the same); JVT H.264 (185): HCBP2_HHI_A and HCMP1_HHI_A reach 19 (14
# pictures at 17 or above each), MR3_TANDBERG_B 16, every other stream at most 15.
set -eu -o pipefail
SRC=$(cd "${1:?usage: dpbindex.sh <ffmpeg-9.0.2 source> <build dir> <streams...>}" && pwd)
B=${2:?build dir}; shift 2
mkdir -p "$B"; B=$(cd "$B" && pwd)
if [ ! -x "$B/ffmpeg" ]; then
  rm -rf "$B/src"; cp -R "$SRC" "$B/src"
  python3 -I - "$B/src" <<'EOF'
import sys
root = sys.argv[1]
def patch(path, anchor, line):
    p = root + '/' + path
    s = open(p).read()
    assert s.count(anchor) == 1, (path, anchor)
    open(p, 'w').write(s.replace(anchor, anchor + line))
patch('libavcodec/h264_slice.c', '    i = find_unused_picture(h);\n', '    fprintf(stderr, "DPBIDX h264 %d\\n", i);\n')
patch('libavcodec/hevc/refs.c', 'frame->pps = av_refstruct_ref_c(s->pps);\n', '        fprintf(stderr, "DPBIDX hevc %d\\n", i);\n')
EOF
  mkdir -p "$B/build"
  ( cd "$B/build" && ../src/configure --disable-everything --enable-decoder=h264,hevc --enable-parser=h264,hevc \
      --enable-demuxer=h264,hevc --enable-protocol=file --enable-muxer=null --enable-encoder=wrapped_avframe \
      --enable-filter=null,format,aformat,anull,aresample --disable-doc --disable-autodetect --disable-network \
      --disable-asm > configure.log 2>&1 && make -j8 ffmpeg > make.log 2>&1 )
  cp "$B/build/ffmpeg" "$B/ffmpeg"
fi
for f in "$@"; do
  case "$f" in *.bit|*.bin|*.265|*.hevc) fmt=hevc;; *) fmt=h264;; esac
  n=$(basename "$f"); n=${n%.*}
  "$B/ffmpeg" -nostdin -hide_banner -v quiet -threads 1 -f $fmt -i "$f" -f null - 2>&1 < /dev/null |
    awk -v s="$n" '/^DPBIDX/ { n++; if ($3 > m) m = $3; if ($3 >= 16) a++; if ($3 >= 17) b++ } END { print s, n + 0, m + 0, a + 0, b + 0 }'
done

FILE: videotoolbox/tests/h264parse_test.c

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// h264parse_test <stream.264> [golden.txt]: the direct path's H.264 parser (vtdirect_h264.c) over a recorded Annex B
// stream, without a GPU. The stream is cut into access units and handed over as the length-prefixed samples an MP4
// carries (parameter sets in-band). Prints, in the format of tests/h264/mkgolden.py (made from libavcodec 9.0.2's own
// decoder: ffmpeg -debug pict+mmco and the trace_headers bitstream filter):
//   sps ... / pps ...                    the fields that go into StdVideoH264SequenceParameterSet / PictureParameterSet,
//                                        scaling lists included
//   pic <type> [IDR] frame=.. poc=../.. slices=.. S <fn:poc>... L <idx:fn:poc>...
//                                        each picture's frame_num and POCs, and the reference pictures it is decoded
//                                        with (the DPB before it, in libavcodec's order: what the Vulkan Video decode gets)
// With a golden file it compares line by line and exits 1 at the first difference.
// Build (here, no FFmpeg): cc -O1 -Wall -I<mesa>/include h264parse_test.c ../vtdirect_h264.c -o h264parse_test
#include "../vtdirect_h264.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct { const uint8_t *p; size_t n; } Nal;

static int first_mb_is_zero(const uint8_t *nal, size_t n) {   // first_mb_in_slice == 0: ue(v) "1"
	return n > 1 && (nal[1] & 0x80);
}

static void print_list(char *b, size_t bn, const uint8_t *l, int n) {
	size_t o = strlen(b);
	for (int i = 0; i < n && o + 5 < bn; i++) o += (size_t)snprintf(b + o, bn - o, "%s%u", i ? "," : "", l[i]);
}
static void print_scaling(char *b, size_t bn, const StdVideoH264ScalingLists *sl, int present_flag) {
	if (!present_flag) { strlcat(b, " scaling=-", bn); return; }
	char t[64]; snprintf(t, sizeof t, " scaling=%x/%x", sl->scaling_list_present_mask, sl->use_default_scaling_matrix_mask); strlcat(b, t, bn);
	for (int i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
		if (!(sl->scaling_list_present_mask & (1u << i)) || (sl->use_default_scaling_matrix_mask & (1u << i))) continue;
		snprintf(t, sizeof t, " L%d=", i); strlcat(b, t, bn);
		if (i < 6) print_list(b, bn, sl->ScalingList4x4[i], 16); else print_list(b, bn, sl->ScalingList8x8[i - 6], 64);
	}
}
static void line_sps(const H264DSps *p, int id, char *b, size_t bn) {
	const StdVideoH264SequenceParameterSet *d = &p->std;
	snprintf(b, bn, "sps id=%d profile=%d level=%d chroma=%d lfn=%d poc_type=%d lpoc=%d refs=%d w=%u h=%u fmo=%d d8=%d crop=%u,%u,%u,%u",
	         id, p->profile_idc, p->level_idc, d->chroma_format_idc, d->log2_max_frame_num_minus4, d->pic_order_cnt_type,
	         d->log2_max_pic_order_cnt_lsb_minus4, d->max_num_ref_frames, d->pic_width_in_mbs_minus1, d->pic_height_in_map_units_minus1,
	         d->flags.frame_mbs_only_flag, d->flags.direct_8x8_inference_flag, d->frame_crop_left_offset, d->frame_crop_right_offset,
	         d->frame_crop_top_offset, d->frame_crop_bottom_offset);
	print_scaling(b, bn, &p->scaling, d->flags.seq_scaling_matrix_present_flag);
}
static void line_pps(const H264DPps *p, int id, char *b, size_t bn) {
	const StdVideoH264PictureParameterSet *d = &p->std;
	snprintf(b, bn, "pps id=%d sps=%d cabac=%d l0=%d l1=%d wp=%d wb=%d qp=%d qs=%d cqp=%d dbk=%d cip=%d rpc=%d t8=%d cqp2=%d",
	         id, p->sps_id, d->flags.entropy_coding_mode_flag, d->num_ref_idx_l0_default_active_minus1, d->num_ref_idx_l1_default_active_minus1,
	         d->flags.weighted_pred_flag, d->weighted_bipred_idc, d->pic_init_qp_minus26, d->pic_init_qs_minus26, d->chroma_qp_index_offset,
	         d->flags.deblocking_filter_control_present_flag, d->flags.constrained_intra_pred_flag, d->flags.redundant_pic_cnt_present_flag,
	         d->flags.transform_8x8_mode_flag, d->second_chroma_qp_index_offset);
	print_scaling(b, bn, &p->scaling, d->flags.pic_scaling_matrix_present_flag);
}
static void line_pic(const H264DPicture *pic, char *b, size_t bn) {
	static const char type[] = "PBI";
	snprintf(b, bn, "pic %c%s frame=%d poc=%d/%d slices=%u S", type[pic->slice_type], pic->idr ? " IDR" : "", pic->frame_num, pic->poc[0], pic->poc[1], pic->nslices);
	char t[64];
	for (int i = 0; i < pic->nrefs; i++) if (!pic->refs[i].long_term) {
		snprintf(t, sizeof t, " %d:%d", pic->refs[i].frame_num, pic->refs[i].poc[0] < pic->refs[i].poc[1] ? pic->refs[i].poc[0] : pic->refs[i].poc[1]);
		strlcat(b, t, bn);
	}
	strlcat(b, " L", bn);
	for (int i = 0; i < pic->nrefs; i++) if (pic->refs[i].long_term) {
		snprintf(t, sizeof t, " %d:%d", pic->refs[i].frame_num, pic->refs[i].poc[0] < pic->refs[i].poc[1] ? pic->refs[i].poc[0] : pic->refs[i].poc[1]);
		strlcat(b, t, bn);
	}
}

static FILE *golden; static int lineno, bad;
static void emit(const char *l) {
	lineno++;
	if (!golden) { printf("%s\n", l); return; }
	char g[8192];
	if (!fgets(g, sizeof g, golden)) { if (!bad) printf("line %d: golden ends; got: %s\n", lineno, l); bad = 1; return; }
	g[strcspn(g, "\n")] = 0;
	if (strcmp(g, l) && !bad) { printf("line %d differs\n  want: %s\n  got:  %s\n", lineno, g, l); bad = 1; }
}

// a sample: the NAL units with 4-byte lengths
static uint8_t *pack(const Nal *nals, int n, size_t *size) {
	size_t t = 0; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) t += 4 + nals[i].n;
	uint8_t *b = malloc(t ? t : 1), *w = b;
	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
		w[0] = (uint8_t)(nals[i].n >> 24); w[1] = (uint8_t)(nals[i].n >> 16); w[2] = (uint8_t)(nals[i].n >> 8); w[3] = (uint8_t)nals[i].n;
		memcpy(w + 4, nals[i].p, nals[i].n); w += 4 + nals[i].n;
	}
	*size = t;
	return b;
}

static int run_au(H264DState *s, const Nal *au, int n) {
	char l[16384];
	for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {   // parameter sets one by one first, to print each as it comes
		const int t = au[i].p[0] & 0x1f;
		if (t != 7 && t != 8) continue;
		size_t sz; uint8_t *b = pack(&au[i], 1, &sz);
		H264DPicture pic;
		const int r = h264d_parse_sample(s, b, sz, NULL, 0, &pic);
		free(b);
		if (r < 0) { printf("parameter set: %d %s\n", r, h264d_why(s)); return r; }
		if (t == 7) line_sps(&s->sps[s->last_sps], s->last_sps, l, sizeof l);
		else line_pps(s->pps[s->last_pps], s->last_pps, l, sizeof l);
		emit(l);
	}
	size_t sz; uint8_t *b = pack(au, n, &sz);
	const size_t need = h264d_bitstream_size(s, b, sz);
	uint8_t *out = malloc(need ? need : 1);
	H264DPicture pic;
	const int r = h264d_parse_sample(s, b, sz, out, need, &pic);
	if (r == H264D_PICTURE) {
		if (pic.size != need) { printf("bitstream size %zu, expected %zu\n", pic.size, need); bad = 1; }
		for (uint32_t i = 0; i < pic.nslices; i++)
			if (pic.slice_offsets[i] + 3 > pic.size || out[pic.slice_offsets[i]] || out[pic.slice_offsets[i] + 1] || out[pic.slice_offsets[i] + 2] != 1) {
				printf("slice %u: no start code at %u\n", i, pic.slice_offsets[i]); bad = 1;
			}
		line_pic(&pic, l, sizeof l);
		emit(l);
		h264d_finish_picture(s, &pic);
	} else if (r < 0) printf("sample: %d %s\n", r, h264d_why(s));
	free(b); free(out);
	return r < 0 ? r : 0;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
	if (argc < 2) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: h264parse_test <stream.264> [golden.txt]\n"); return 2; }
	FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
	if (!f) { perror(argv[1]); return 2; }
	fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END); const long fl = ftell(f); fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
	uint8_t *d = malloc((size_t)fl + 4);
	if (fread(d, 1, (size_t)fl, f) != (size_t)fl) { perror("read"); return 2; }
	fclose(f);
	if (argc > 2 && !(golden = fopen(argv[2], "r"))) { perror(argv[2]); return 2; }
	// NAL units of the Annex B stream
	Nal *nals = malloc(sizeof(Nal) * ((size_t)fl / 3 + 2)); int nn = 0;
	size_t i = 0, start = 0; int in = 0;
	while (i + 3 <= (size_t)fl) {
		if (d[i] == 0 && d[i + 1] == 0 && d[i + 2] == 1) {
			if (in) { size_t e = i; while (e > start && d[e - 1] == 0) e--; nals[nn++] = (Nal){ d + start, e - start }; }
			start = i + 3; in = 1; i += 3;
		} else i++;
	}
	if (in && (size_t)fl > start) nals[nn++] = (Nal){ d + start, (size_t)fl - start };
	// access units (7.4.1.2.3): a new one at an AUD / SPS / PPS / SEI after a slice, or at a slice with first_mb 0
	H264DState *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);
	h264d_init(s, 4);
	int au0 = 0, has_slice = 0, aus = 0, rc = 0;
	for (int k = 0; k <= nn && !rc; k++) {
		const int t = k < nn ? nals[k].p[0] & 0x1f : -1;
		const int vcl = t == 1 || t == 5;
		const int boundary = k == nn || (has_slice && ((t >= 6 && t <= 9) || (vcl && first_mb_is_zero(nals[k].p, nals[k].n))));
		if (boundary && k > au0) { rc = run_au(s, nals + au0, k - au0); au0 = k; has_slice = 0; aus++; }
		if (vcl) has_slice = 1;
	}
	if (golden && !bad) { char g[256]; if (fgets(g, sizeof g, golden)) { printf("line %d: golden has more: %s", lineno + 1, g); bad = 1; } }
	fprintf(stderr, "%s: %d access units, %d lines%s%s\n", argv[1], aus, lineno, golden ? (bad ? ", DIFFERS from " : ", identical to ") : "", golden ? argv[2] : "");
	h264d_free(s); free(s); free(nals); free(d);
	return rc ? 3 : bad;
}

FILE: videotoolbox/tests/hevcparse_test.c
