#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""segedit.py <in.ivf> <out.ivf>: a VP9 stream with the same pictures, whose segmented frames code the segment map
without segmentation_update_data wherever the data they code equals what the decoder already holds (the feature data
and abs_or_delta_update persist until a frame updates them, 7.2 / libvpx setup_segmentation): a valid stream, the
same decode, but one that libvpx's own encoders never produce (they send the data with every map). Made to test the
two segmentation values libavcodec 9.0.2's Vulkan hwaccel takes from CBS's stale copies (vtdirect_vp9.h): with the
data left out, CBS keeps the previous frame's tree / prediction probabilities and vulkan_vp9.c passes those.

Only the uncompressed header is rewritten (re-packed to its byte alignment); the compressed header and the tiles are
copied, the superframe indexes and the IVF frame sizes recomputed. Prints how many frames were changed."""
import struct
import sys


class Reader:
    def __init__(self, d):
        self.d, self.pos, self.out = d, 0, []

    def f(self, n, keep=True):
        v = 0
        for _ in range(n):
            b = (self.d[self.pos >> 3] >> (7 - (self.pos & 7))) & 1
            self.pos += 1
            v = v << 1 | b
            if keep:
                self.out.append(b)
        return v

    def put(self, v, n):
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            self.out.append(v >> i & 1)


refs = [(0, 0)] * 8
feat = None   # (abs, [[enabled, value, sign] x4] x8) the decoder holds
changed = 0


def frame(d):
    """the rewritten frame"""
    global refs, feat, changed
    r = Reader(d)
    if r.f(2) != 2:
        return d
    lo, hi = r.f(1), r.f(1)
    profile = hi << 1 | lo
    if profile == 3:
        r.f(1)
    if r.f(1):   # show_existing_frame
        return d
    ftype, show, er = r.f(1), r.f(1), r.f(1)

    def color():
        if profile >= 2:
            r.f(1)
        cs = r.f(3)
        if cs != 7:
            r.f(1)
            if profile in (1, 3):
                r.f(3)
        elif profile in (1, 3):
            r.f(1)

    intra_only, refresh, w, h = 0, 0xff, 0, 0
    if ftype == 0:
        r.f(24); color()
        w, h = r.f(16) + 1, r.f(16) + 1
        if r.f(1):
            r.f(32)
    else:
        intra_only = 0 if show else r.f(1)
        if not er:
            r.f(2)
        if intra_only:
            r.f(24)
            if profile > 0:
                color()
            refresh = r.f(8)
            w, h = r.f(16) + 1, r.f(16) + 1
            if r.f(1):
                r.f(32)
        else:
            refresh = r.f(8)
            idx = []
            for _ in range(3):
                idx.append(r.f(3)); r.f(1)
            found = False
            for i in range(3):
                if r.f(1):
                    w, h = refs[idx[i]]; found = True
                    break
            if not found:
                w, h = r.f(16) + 1, r.f(16) + 1
            if r.f(1):
                r.f(32)
            r.f(1)
            if not r.f(1):
                r.f(2)
    if not er:
        r.f(2)
    r.f(2)
    if ftype == 0 or intra_only or er or feat is None:
        feat = (0, [[[0, 0, 0] for _ in range(4)] for _ in range(8)])
    # loop filter
    r.f(6); r.f(3)
    if r.f(1) and r.f(1):
        for _ in range(6):
            if r.f(1):
                r.f(7)
    r.f(8)
    for _ in range(3):
        if r.f(1):
            r.f(5)
    # segmentation: the place of the edit
    if r.f(1):
        upd_map = r.f(1)
        if upd_map:
            for _ in range(7):
                if r.f(1):
                    r.f(8)
            if r.f(1):
                for _ in range(3):
                    if r.f(1):
                        r.f(8)
        at = len(r.out)
        if r.f(1):   # segmentation_update_data
            bits, signed = (8, 6, 2, 0), (1, 1, 0, 0)
            ab = r.f(1)
            new = []
            for i in range(8):
                row = []
                for j in range(4):
                    en = r.f(1)
                    val = sign = 0
                    if en and bits[j]:
                        val = r.f(bits[j])
                        if signed[j]:
                            sign = r.f(1)
                    row.append([en, val, sign])
                new.append(row)
            if upd_map and (ab, new) == feat and ftype != 0 and not intra_only:
                del r.out[at:]
                r.put(0, 1)   # segmentation_update_data = 0: the decoder keeps the same data
                changed += 1
            feat = (ab, new)
    # tile info
    sb64 = (((w + 7) >> 3) + 7) >> 3
    mn = 0
    while (64 << mn) < sb64:
        mn += 1
    mx = 0
    while (sb64 >> (mx + 1)) >= 4:
        mx += 1
    c = mn
    while c < mx and r.f(1):
        c += 1
    if r.f(1):
        r.f(1)
    r.f(16)   # header_size_in_bytes
    end = (r.pos + 7) // 8
    for i in range(8):
        if refresh >> i & 1:
            refs[i] = (w, h)
    out = r.out + [0] * (-len(r.out) % 8)
    hdr = bytes(int(''.join(str(b) for b in out[i:i + 8]), 2) for i in range(0, len(out), 8))
    return hdr + d[end:]


def sample(s):
    m = s[-1]
    if m & 0xe0 == 0xc0:
        length, count = 1 + ((m >> 3) & 3), 1 + (m & 7)
        isz = 2 + count * length
        if len(s) >= isz and s[len(s) - isz] == m:
            frames, pos = [], 0
            for i in range(count):
                at = len(s) - isz + 1 + i * length
                v = int.from_bytes(s[at:at + length], 'little')
                frames.append(frame(s[pos:pos + v])); pos += v
            length = max(1, max((len(f).bit_length() + 7) // 8 for f in frames))
            mk = 0xc0 | (length - 1) << 3 | (count - 1)
            idx = bytes([mk]) + b''.join(len(f).to_bytes(length, 'little') for f in frames) + bytes([mk])
            return b''.join(frames) + idx
    return frame(s)


src = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()
hl = struct.unpack('<H', src[6:8])[0]
out, pos = [src[:hl]], hl
while pos + 12 <= len(src):
    sz = struct.unpack('<I', src[pos:pos + 4])[0]
    s = sample(src[pos + 12:pos + 12 + sz])
    out.append(struct.pack('<I', len(s)) + src[pos + 4:pos + 12] + s)
    pos += 12 + sz
open(sys.argv[2], 'wb').write(b''.join(out))
print('segedit: %d frames code the map without the data' % changed)

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# intelxe-metal-exec <tool> [args...]: run a command-line tool with Metal brought up first, so the GPU plug-in registers
# the IntelXe VideoToolbox codecs in it (HEVC/H.264/AV1 encoders, AV1/H.264/HEVC decoders) before the tool asks
# VideoToolbox for one. Example: intelxe-metal-exec ffmpeg -i in.mov -c:v hevc_videotoolbox -b:v 8M out.mp4
exec env DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/metalpre.dylib${DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES:+:$DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES}" "$@"

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// metalpre.dylib: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES test shim - brings Metal up at load, so the GPU plug-in registers the B580
// codecs before the tool asks VideoToolbox for one (as in any app with a Metal view)
#import <Metal/Metal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
__attribute__((constructor)) static void metalpre(void) {
	NSArray *d = MTLCopyAllDevices();

FILE: vulkan/README.md
================================================
# vulkan: native Vulkan for games on the Intel Arc card (experimental)

An optional component, **not yet tested with Wine on the hardware**. Wine's DXVK (Direct3D 8-11) and vkd3d-proton
(Direct3D 12), and other programs that open a Vulkan library by name, reach the driver's ANV directly instead of
MoltenVK -> Metal -> the Metal driver -> ANV. Nothing loads it unless a program is started through `intelxe-vk run`;
Wine's own MoltenVK, the Khronos loader, ANV and the Metal driver are not touched. It needs the driver installed.
Background and the Wine source it follows: [`docs/design/DESIGN-native-vulkan.md`](../docs/design/DESIGN-native-vulkan.md).

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sudo ./install.sh` | `/Library/IntelXe/Vulkan`: the provider, the helper, `vksurf`; backs up what it replaces to `./previous/` |
| `./install.sh --test` | `vksurf` through the provider: a window, 120 cleared frames, PASS/FAIL (about 3 s) |
| `vkscene [--lib NAME]` | a renderer-path sample: MSAA, depth, bindless textures, timeline semaphores; timings, a read-back checksum, PASS/FAIL |
| `sudo ./install.sh --undo` | the state before the install |
| `intelxe-vk check [Wine.app]` | what is installed; which Vulkan library a Wine build opens and how to start it; the prefixes set up |
| `intelxe-vk fetch` | downloads DXVK 3.1.1 and vkd3d-proton 3.1 (pinned, sha256 checked) into `~/Library/Application Support/IntelXe/vulkan`; `fetch --from FILE` takes a tarball you have |
| `intelxe-vk prefix-install PREFIX` | their DLLs into a 64-bit Wine prefix, `PREFIX/dxvk.conf`, DLL overrides; the prefix's own DLLs and overrides kept |
| `intelxe-vk prefix-restore PREFIX` | Wine's own Direct3D again, as before `prefix-install` |
| `WINEPREFIX=PREFIX intelxe-vk run wine game.exe` | the game on ANV; `run --loader` uses the Khronos loader instead of the provider |
| `intelxe-vk minecraft-args` | the JVM argument for Minecraft's Vulkan renderer (official launcher, Prism); checks the Java runtimes |
| `intelxe-vk bench --wine W --exe E` | a D3D benchmark under Wine, DXVK on ANV vs on MoltenVK (same front end), runs interleaved, medians |
| `INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG=F`, `intelxe-vk frametimes F` | the provider logs present intervals (no layer); the summary: fps, p50/p95/p99, 1% low |

`intelxe-vk` is `/Library/IntelXe/Vulkan/bin/intelxe-vk` after the install. Nothing is downloaded unless you run
`fetch`; nothing in a prefix changes unless you run `prefix-install`.

## How it works

Wine's macOS Vulkan driver opens one library by the name its build was configured with (`libMoltenVK.dylib`, or
`libvulkan.1.dylib` in builds against the Khronos loader such as Gcenx's) and takes `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`,
`vkGetDeviceProcAddr` and `vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT` from it (Wine 10 also `vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK`); it uses no
MoltenVK-only function. `intelxe-vk check` reads which name a build uses. ANV exports only the driver interface
(`vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr`), so `libintelxe-vk.dylib` supplies those names and forwards to ANV; device functions go to
ANV directly, at no cost per call. `intelxe-vk run` puts `/Library/IntelXe/Vulkan/provider` (the provider under both
names) first in `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` for that one process and the Wine processes it starts, and sets `VK_DRIVER_FILES` to
ANV's manifest. Frames are presented through ANV's `VK_EXT_metal_surface` swapchain into the window Wine creates, with
IOSurfaces in video memory (no copy per frame).

## vkscene: a renderer path, not only a swapchain

`bin/vkscene` (`user/tests/vulkan/vkscene.m`, shaders in `vkscene/`) drives the driver the way an engine does: a check
pass into a 256x256 target verified pixel by pixel (64 cells, each texel (0,0) of `texture[cell]` through a bindless
array with `nonuniformEXT`, half of the descriptors written after the command buffer was recorded (update after bind);
a far layer that must lose the depth test, a near triangle that must win it, and its edge, which the 4x MSAA resolve
must blend), a GPU wait on a host-signalled timeline semaphore, then N frames of 256 instanced, textured, lit cubes
(vertex/index buffers, a dynamic storage buffer per frame in flight, dynamic rendering, synchronization2, frame pacing
by a timeline semaphore instead of fences, GPU timestamps), and a last frame read back: an FNV-1a checksum that must
be the same on every path to the same driver (`--icd` ANV directly, `--lib libvulkan.1.dylib` through the provider,
`--lib /usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib` through the loader), compared pixel for pixel with the IOSurface ANV's WSI
shows. `--immediate`/`--mailbox`, `--resize`, `--samples N`, `--grid G`, `--mtl-device` (a Wine-like layer),
`--png FILE`, `--no-wbs` (skip the opening GPU wait on a host signal, which gives Mesa's queue a submit thread; with
IntelXe before rb8g, 14 Nov, that thread made presents fail with `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`). Driver messages
(`VK_EXT_debug_utils`) are printed as `driver:`. Ends with
`RESULT vkscene fps=... p99_ms=... gpu_ms=... wbs=... memfallback=... checksum=... check=PASS`. Verified on the build
Mac against MoltenVK (arm64 build, Apple M1 Pro): all checks pass, directly and through the provider.

## Minecraft (Java 26.x, the Vulkan renderer)

One JVM argument, no mod: `intelxe-vk minecraft-args` prints it
(`-Dorg.lwjgl.vulkan.libname=/Library/IntelXe/Vulkan/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib`) and where it goes in the official
launcher and Prism. Minecraft initialises Vulkan with LWJGL's `VK.create()`, which opens the file the property names
(no MoltenVK fallback when it is set), and hands that file to its window layer: GLFW (26.2, LWJGL's
`GLFWVulkan.setPath`) or SDL3 (26.3, `SDL_Vulkan_LoadLibrary` with LWJGL's path). So instance, device and window
surface all reach ANV. Details and how this was established: the design note. `--java PATH` (or the runtimes it
finds) checks that a Java runtime is x86_64 and may load an ad-hoc signed library (Minecraft's own Java 25 carries
`disable-library-validation`). `--framelog FILE` explains how to get `INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG` into the game's
environment.

## A/B measurements

- **Frame log:** `INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG=FILE` (`%p` = process id) makes the provider wrap `vkQueuePresentKHR` and write
  one line per present: `frame t_ms interval_ms present_ms result swapchain`. Without the variable the driver's own
  function is handed out, as before. `intelxe-vk frametimes FILE [--skip S]` summarises it. `INTELXE_VK_ICD=` a
  MoltenVK (under another leaf name than `libMoltenVK.dylib`: dyld looks leaf names up in `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` first;
  the provider refuses itself with a message) puts MoltenVK behind the same front end and the same log, so A and B
  differ only in the driver. The Metal driver's plugin unsets inherited `INTELXE*`/`MESA_*` variables in every
  process it loads into unless `NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1` is set; the provider keeps a copy from its own load, which is
  enough when it loads before Metal (vkscene, Minecraft), not in Wine: `bench` and `run` set the opt-in.
- **`intelxe-vk bench`:** `--wine` (wine, its `bin/` or a Wine `.app`), `--exe` and `--prefix` (or `--prefix-mvk` for
  a DXVK build that runs on MoltenVK), `--modes anv,mvk,loader,wine`, `--runs N` (interleaved), `--seconds`,
  `--warmup`, `--score REGEX` (default `avg_fps=`, the RESULT line of `user/tests/wine`'s d3d11bench/d3d12bench),
  `--env NAME=VALUE`. Per run: the program's output, the frame log, Mesa's `MESA_VK_WSI_FPS_LOG` (shown frames per
  second, ANV modes), DXVK's log (the adapter it chose), the environment; `results.tsv`; `bench-report DIR` prints
  medians per mode and the anv/mvk ratios. `--help` lists everything. Tested offline against a stand-in Wine
  (`test/bench-test.sh`); the Wine build and the games are the maintainer's choice.

## Limits

- Not tried with Wine, DXVK or vkd3d-proton on the B580 yet; `vksurf` (V1-V6 passed on the B580, 13 Nov) and the
  offline tests are the checks so far; `vkscene` and Minecraft have not run on the B580.
- 64-bit prefixes. 32-bit games in such a prefix (WoW64) get the 32-bit DLLs too, untested.
- `dxvk.conf` turns DXVK's descriptor buffers and descriptor heap off (the file explains why); edit it to try them.
- `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` reaches games started through shell-script launchers only with the AMFI boot-arg, which the
  driver's setup already has.
- Not covered: MoltenVK's own extra functions (`vkGetMTLDeviceMVK` and the like: Wine does not use them), Vulkan
  layers in the provider mode (use `run --loader`), HDR, sharing GPU memory between processes.

## Contents and sources

| File in the package | What | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib` | the provider | `src/intelxe_vk.m` (`./build.sh OUT`) |
| `bin/vksurf` | the swapchain test | `user/tests/vulkan/vksurf.m` (same build) |
| `bin/vkscene` | the renderer-path sample | `user/tests/vulkan/vkscene.m`, shaders `user/tests/vulkan/vkscene/` (SPIR-V checked in as `spv.h`; `gen.sh` rebuilds it with glslang) |
| `icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json` | the Khronos loader's manifest for ANV | `user/vulkan-loader/` |
| `intelxe-vk`, `install.sh` | the helper and the installer | here |
| `test/` | the provider's offline test against a stand-in driver (`test/run.sh OUT`), the bench harness test (`test/bench-test.sh`), the night phase (`test/night-vkscene.sh`) | here |

Everything is x86_64 and ad-hoc signed; the build needs Vulkan-Headers 1.4 (`VK_HEADERS`). DXVK (zlib licence) and
vkd3d-proton (LGPL-2.1) are not in the package: `intelxe-vk fetch` downloads their release builds from GitHub. Our files
are MIT.

---

**Türkçe özet:** İsteğe bağlı, **deneysel ve donanımda Wine ile henüz denenmemiş** bir bileşen. Wine'daki DXVK
(Direct3D 8-11) ve vkd3d-proton (Direct3D 12) ile Vulkan kitaplığını adıyla açan diğer programlar, MoltenVK -> Metal ->
Metal sürücüsü -> ANV yerine doğrudan sürücünün ANV'sine gider. Yalnızca `intelxe-vk run` ile başlatılan program
kullanır; Wine'ın kendi MoltenVK'sı, Khronos yükleyicisi, ANV ve Metal sürücüsü değişmez. `sudo ./install.sh` kurar,
`./install.sh --test` bir pencerede 120 kare çizip PASS/FAIL yazar, `--undo` kaldırır. `intelxe-vk check` Wine
sürümünüzün hangi Vulkan kitaplığını açtığını gösterir; `intelxe-vk fetch` DXVK ve vkd3d-proton'u (sabit sürüm,
sha256 denetimli) indirir, `intelxe-vk prefix-install PREFIX` bunları 64 bit bir Wine önekine kurar (önekin kendi
DLL'leri saklanır), `prefix-restore` geri alır. Oyun: `WINEPREFIX=PREFIX intelxe-vk run wine oyun.exe`.
`vkscene` gerçek bir oyun motoru yolunu (MSAA, derinlik, bindless dokular, timeline semaforları) ölçer ve okunan son
karenin sağlama toplamını verir. Minecraft'ın Vulkan çizicisi için tek bir JVM argümanı yeterlidir (mod gerekmez):
`intelxe-vk minecraft-args`. `INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG=dosya` kare sürelerini katmansız kaydeder (`intelxe-vk frametimes`);
`intelxe-vk bench` bir D3D ölçümünü Wine altında ANV ve MoltenVK üzerinde dönüşümlü çalıştırıp karşılaştırır.

FILE: vulkan/build.sh

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# build.sh OUTDIR: the native Vulkan provider in the package layout, x86_64, ad-hoc signed. Builds on the build Mac.
#   OUTDIR/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib   the provider (src/intelxe_vk.m); install.sh links it as libMoltenVK.dylib and
#                                    libvulkan.1.dylib in /Library/IntelXe/Vulkan/provider
#   OUTDIR/bin/vksurf                the swapchain test (user/tests/vulkan/vksurf.m)
#   OUTDIR/bin/vkscene               a renderer-path sample: MSAA, depth, bindless textures, timeline semaphores,
#                                    timings and a read-back checksum (user/tests/vulkan/vkscene.m)
#   OUTDIR/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json  ANV's manifest for the Khronos loader (user/vulkan-loader)
#   OUTDIR/test/libfakeicd.dylib, OUTDIR/test/provtest   the provider's offline test (test/run.sh; runs on any Mac,
#                                    under Rosetta on Apple silicon; no GPU needed)
# Vulkan headers: VK_HEADERS (a folder with vulkan/vulkan.h, Vulkan-Headers 1.4.x), by default the Mesa tree's.
set -euo pipefail
O=${1:?usage: build.sh OUTDIR}
D=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
VKH=${VK_HEADERS:-$HOME/hackintosh/work/mesa014/include}
[ -f "$VKH/vulkan/vulkan_metal.h" ] || { echo "no Vulkan headers in $VKH (set VK_HEADERS)"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$O/lib" "$O/bin" "$O/test" "$O/icd.d"
cp "$D/../user/vulkan-loader/intel_icd.x86_64.json" "$O/icd.d/"
F=(-arch x86_64 -mmacosx-version-min=15.0 -O2 -Wall -Wno-deprecated-declarations -I"$VKH")
# -fvisibility=hidden: only the names marked EXPORT leave the library (Wine dlsym()s a few; nothing else may clash)
clang "${F[@]}" -fvisibility=hidden -fobjc-arc -dynamiclib "$D/src/intelxe_vk.m" -framework AppKit -framework QuartzCore \
    -install_name /Library/IntelXe/Vulkan/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib -current_version 1 -compatibility_version 1 \
    -o "$O/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib"
clang "${F[@]}" -fobjc-arc "$D/../user/tests/vulkan/vksurf.m" -framework AppKit -framework QuartzCore -framework Metal \
    -framework IOSurface -o "$O/bin/vksurf"
clang "${F[@]}" -fobjc-arc "$D/../user/tests/vulkan/vkscene.m" -framework AppKit -framework QuartzCore -framework Metal \
    -framework IOSurface -framework ImageIO -framework UniformTypeIdentifiers -o "$O/bin/vkscene"
clang "${F[@]}" -dynamiclib "$D/test/fakeicd.c" -o "$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib"
clang "${F[@]}" -fobjc-arc "$D/test/provtest.m" -framework AppKit -framework QuartzCore -o "$O/test/provtest"
for f in "$O/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib" "$O/bin/vksurf" "$O/bin/vkscene" "$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib" "$O/test/provtest"; do codesign -s - -f "$f" 2>/dev/null; done
lipo -archs "$O/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib"

FILE: vulkan/install.sh

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# install.sh (vulkan): native Vulkan for games, EXPERIMENTAL. Puts the Vulkan provider (libintelxe-vk: ANV for Wine's
# macOS Vulkan driver and other programs that open MoltenVK or libvulkan.1.dylib by name) into /Library/IntelXe/Vulkan.
# Nothing loads it unless started through ./intelxe-vk run (DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH for that process only); Wine's MoltenVK,
# the Khronos loader in /usr/local/lib, ANV and the Metal driver are not touched.
#
#   sudo ./install.sh          install (backs up what it replaces to ./previous/, once)
#   sudo ./install.sh --undo   put back what was there before
#   ./install.sh --status      what is installed
#   ./install.sh --test        vksurf through the provider: a window, 120 frames, PASS/FAIL (~3 s)
#
# Installs /Library/IntelXe/Vulkan/:
#   lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib              the provider
#   provider/libMoltenVK.dylib, provider/libvulkan.1.dylib   links to it: the folder "intelxe-vk run" puts first in
#                                        DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, so either name a Wine build opens gets ANV
#   loader/libMoltenVK.dylib             a link to the Khronos loader (/usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib, from zink-gl),
#                                        for "intelxe-vk run --loader" (Wine builds that open MoltenVK by name, with the
#                                        loader's layers available)
#   icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json          the loader's manifest for ANV (VK_DRIVER_FILES)
#   bin/intelxe-vk, bin/vksurf, bin/vkscene   the helper, the swapchain test and the renderer-path sample
# Not in /Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl: the driver's install.sh replaces that folder whole on every --apply and --undo.
set -euo pipefail
H=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
B=$H/previous
VK=/Library/IntelXe/Vulkan
ANV=/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/libvulkan_intel.dylib
LOADER=/usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib

root() { [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "needs root: sudo $0 $*"; exit 1; }; }
sums() { (cd "$H" && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS >/dev/null) || { echo "REFUSED: files differ from SHA256SUMS"; exit 1; }; }
sig() { "$H/sigcheck" "$1" >/dev/null || { "$H/sigcheck" "$1"; echo "REFUSED: $1 is not signed"; exit 1; }; }

status() {
    echo "native Vulkan (experimental):"
    if [ -f $VK/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib ]; then
        echo "  provider: $VK/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib ($(grep -a -o -m1 'intelxe-vk-provider [0-9]*' $VK/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib || echo '?'))"
    else echo "  provider: not installed"; fi
    [ -f $ANV ] && echo "  ANV: $ANV" || echo "  ANV: MISSING (install the driver)"
    if [ -e $LOADER ]; then echo "  Khronos loader: $LOADER (intelxe-vk run --loader works)"
    else echo "  Khronos loader: none in /usr/local/lib (only intelxe-vk run --loader needs it: install zink-gl)"; fi
    echo "  helper: $VK/bin/intelxe-vk check   (Wine builds and prefixes)"
}

# place SRC DST: replace DST with a root-owned copy of SRC
place() { rm -rf "$2.new"; ditto "$1" "$2.new"; chown -R root:wheel "$2.new"; chmod -R go-w "$2.new"; rm -rf "$2"; mv "$2.new" "$2"; }

install_all() {
    root
    sums
    [ -f $ANV ] || { echo "REFUSED: the driver is not installed (no $ANV)"; exit 1; }
    sig "$H/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib"; sig "$H/bin/vksurf"; sig "$H/bin/vkscene"
    if [ ! -d "$B" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$B"
        if [ -d $VK ]; then ditto $VK "$B/Vulkan"; else touch "$B/no-Vulkan"; fi
        echo "backup: $B"
    fi
    local S=$H/.stage/Vulkan
    rm -rf "$H/.stage"; mkdir -p "$S/lib" "$S/provider" "$S/loader" "$S/icd.d" "$S/bin"
    install -m 755 "$H/lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib" "$S/lib/"
    ln -s ../lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib "$S/provider/libMoltenVK.dylib"
    ln -s ../lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib "$S/provider/libvulkan.1.dylib"
    ln -s $LOADER "$S/loader/libMoltenVK.dylib"   # dangling until a loader is there; intelxe-vk run --loader checks
    install -m 644 "$H/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json" "$S/icd.d/"
    install -m 755 "$H/intelxe-vk" "$H/bin/vksurf" "$H/bin/vkscene" "$S/bin/"
    mkdir -p /Library/IntelXe
    place "$S" $VK; rm -rf "$H/.stage"
    status
    echo "installed. Try: $0 --test; then $VK/bin/intelxe-vk check"
}

undo() {
    root
    [ -d "$B" ] || { echo "nothing to undo (not installed from this folder)"; exit 1; }
    if [ -d "$B/Vulkan" ]; then place "$B/Vulkan" $VK; else rm -rf $VK; rmdir /Library/IntelXe 2>/dev/null || true; fi
    rm -rf "$B"
    echo "undone. Wine prefixes keep their DXVK/vkd3d-proton DLLs: intelxe-vk prefix-restore PREFIX puts theirs back."
    status
}

selftest() {
    [ -x $VK/bin/vksurf ] || { echo "install first: sudo $0"; exit 1; }
    # perl sets the variable itself: one handed to /usr/bin/perl could be dropped at its start (a protected binary)
    exec /usr/bin/perl -e '$ENV{DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH} = shift; alarm shift; exec @ARGV' $VK/provider 30 \
        $VK/bin/vksurf --lib libMoltenVK.dylib --wine10 --frames 120
}

case "${1:-}" in
    "") install_all ;;
    --undo) undo ;;
    --status) status ;;
    --test) selftest ;;
    *) sed -n '3,12p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# bench-test.sh: "intelxe-vk bench" against a stand-in Wine (a script that checks the variables each mode must set and
# writes what the provider, Mesa's WSI and DXVK would write), on any Mac, no GPU: the modes' environments, the
# interleaving, the stop after --seconds, result parsing, the report's medians and ratio.
set -euo pipefail
D=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
T=$(mktemp -d -t ixvk-bench); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$T/root/provider" "$T/root/loader" "$T/root/icd.d" "$T/wine/bin" "$T/wine/lib" "$T/prefix/drive_c/windows/system32"
: > "$T/root/provider/libMoltenVK.dylib"; : > "$T/root/provider/libvulkan.1.dylib"; : > "$T/root/loader/libMoltenVK.dylib"
: > "$T/root/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json"; : > "$T/anv.dylib"; : > "$T/wine/lib/libMoltenVK.dylib"; : > "$T/prefix/system.reg"
cat > "$T/wine/bin/wineserver" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
exit 0
EOF
cat > "$T/wine/bin/wine" <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
[ "${1:-}" = --version ] && { echo wine-fake-1.0; exit 0; }
m=${INTELXE_VK_BENCH_MODE:-?}
echo "fake wine: mode $m exe $1 args ${*:2}"
bad() { echo "BAD ENV for $m: $*"; exit 3; }
[ "${NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV:-}" = 1 ] || bad "no NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 (the Metal plugin would unset INTELXE*/MESA_*)"
case $m in
    anv) [ -n "${VK_DRIVER_FILES:-}" ] && [ -z "${INTELXE_VK_ICD:-}" ] && [ -n "${INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG:-}" ] || bad anv; iv=5 ;;
    mvk) [ -z "${VK_DRIVER_FILES:-}" ] && [ -L "${INTELXE_VK_ICD:-}" ] || bad mvk
         [ "$(basename "$INTELXE_VK_ICD")" != libMoltenVK.dylib ] || bad "INTELXE_VK_ICD has the provider's leaf name"; iv=10 ;;
    wine) [ -z "${INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG:-}${VK_DRIVER_FILES:-}${INTELXE_VK_ICD:-}" ] || bad wine; iv=20 ;;
    *) bad "no mode" ;;
esac
[ "${FAKE_HANG:-}" = 1 ] && exec sleep 30
if [ -n "${INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG:-}" ]; then
    f=${INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG//%p/$$}; : > "${INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG//%p/1}"   # a second process that never presents
    { echo "# intelxe-vk framelog 1: fake"; t=0
      for ((i = 0; i < 2000; i++)); do v=$iv; [ $i = 0 ] && v=0; [ $((i % 500)) = 499 ] && v=$((iv * 4)); echo "$i $t $v 0.1 0 1"; t=$((t + v)); done; } > "$f"
fi
if [ -n "${MESA_VK_WSI_FPS_LOG:-}" ]; then
    for t in 100 102 104 106 108 110; do s=59.5; [ $t = 100 ] && s=10.0
        echo "$t.000 pid $$ 1280x720 FIFO 3 images (shared VRAM, Tile4): 60.0 presents/s, $s shown/s, 0.5 dropped/s, acquire 0.100 ms/frame"; done > "$MESA_VK_WSI_FPS_LOG"
fi
printf 'info:  Game: game.exe\ninfo:  Fake GPU (FAKE):\ninfo:    Driver : Fake driver 1.0\n' > "$DXVK_LOG_PATH/game_d3d11.log"
echo "RESULT d3d11 iters=16 1280x720 sync=0 avg_fps=$((1000 / iv)).0 (steady 9 s) best=1.0 frames=100"
EOF
chmod +x "$T/wine/bin/wine" "$T/wine/bin/wineserver"
export INTELXE_VK_ROOT=$T/root INTELXE_VK_ANV=$T/anv.dylib
fails=0
ok() { if eval "$2"; then echo "ok    $1"; else echo "FAIL  $1"; fails=$((fails + 1)); fi; }

"$D/intelxe-vk" bench --wine "$T/wine" --exe 'C:\game.exe' --prefix "$T/prefix" --runs 2 --out "$T/out" -- -w 1280 > "$T/report.txt" 2> "$T/err.txt"
R=$T/out/results.tsv
cat "$T/report.txt" | sed 's/^/      /'
ok "4 runs, interleaved anv mvk anv mvk" '[ "$(cut -f2 "$R" | tail -n +2 | tr "\n" " ")" = "anv mvk anv mvk " ]'
ok "every run exited 0" '[ "$(cut -f3 "$R" | tail -n +2 | sort -u)" = 0 ]'
ok "anv: the presenting process's log, 5 s warmup skipped: 1002 frames, 198.2 fps, max 20 ms" '[ "$(awk -F"\t" "\$2 == \"anv\" { print \$5, \$6, \$9 }" "$R" | sort -u)" = "1002 198.2 20.000" ]'
ok "mvk: 99.4 fps, p50 10 ms, max = the 40 ms hitch, 1% low 60.9" '[ "$(awk -F"\t" "\$2 == \"mvk\" { print \$6, \$7, \$9, \$10 }" "$R" | sort -u)" = "99.4 10.000 40.000 60.9" ]'
ok "anv: Mesa WSI shown/s after the warmup 59.5" '[ "$(awk -F"\t" "\$2 == \"anv\" { print \$11 }" "$R" | sort -u)" = 59.5 ]'
ok "score from the RESULT line (avg_fps=)" '[ "$(awk -F"\t" "NR > 1 { print \$2 \"=\" \$12 }" "$R" | sort -u | tr "\n" " ")" = "anv=200.0 mvk=100.0 " ]'
ok "DXVK's adapter from its log" '[ "$(cut -f13 "$R" | tail -n +2 | sort -u)" = "Fake GPU (FAKE)" ]'
ok "report: anv/mvk fps 1.99x, score 2.00x" 'grep -q "anv/mvk: fps 1.99x, score 2.00x" "$T/report.txt"'
ok "the program got its arguments" 'grep -q "args -w 1280" "$T/out/01-anv/out.log"'
ok "MoltenVK linked under another leaf name" '[ -L "$T/out/.mvk/libMoltenVK-icd.dylib" ]'

"$D/intelxe-vk" bench --wine "$T/wine/bin/wine" --exe 'C:\game.exe' --prefix "$T/prefix" --modes wine --runs 1 --seconds 2 \
    --env FAKE_HANG=1 --out "$T/out2" > /dev/null 2>&1
ok "--seconds 2 stops a program that keeps running" '[ "$(cut -f4 "$T/out2/results.tsv" | tail -1)" = stopped ]'
ok "wine mode: no provider, no frame log" '[ ! -e "$T/out2/01-wine/frames-1.txt" ] && ! grep -q INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG "$T/out2/01-wine/env.txt"'
"$D/intelxe-vk" bench --wine "$T/wine" --exe x --prefix "$T/prefix" --modes nope --out "$T/out3" > /dev/null 2>&1 && st=0 || st=$?
ok "an unknown mode is refused" '[ $st != 0 ]'
echo "$([ $fails = 0 ] && echo PASS || echo FAIL) ($fails failure(s))"
[ $fails = 0 ]

FILE: vulkan/test/fakeicd.c
================================================
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// fakeicd: a stand-in for ANV with the same ICD exports, for the provider's offline test (test/run.sh). It offers
// VK_KHR_surface and VK_EXT_metal_surface only and, like Mesa, refuses any other extension and any create flag, so a
// provider that passed VK_MVK_macos_surface or VK_KHR_portability_enumeration through would fail here as on ANV.
// Devices: VK_KHR_swapchain only (VK_KHR_portability_subset is refused, as by ANV); vkQueuePresentKHR counts calls.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#define VK_NO_PROTOTYPES
#define VK_USE_PLATFORM_METAL_EXT
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
#define EXPORT __attribute__((visibility("default")))

struct fake_instance { int metal; };
// what the test reads back
EXPORT struct { char exts[8][64]; uint32_t n, flags; const void *layer; int negotiated; char dexts[4][64]; uint32_t dn; int presents; } fake_seen;

static VkResult VKAPI_CALL eie(const char *layer, uint32_t *count, VkExtensionProperties *p) {
    static const char *names[] = {VK_KHR_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME, VK_EXT_METAL_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME};
    if (layer) return VK_ERROR_LAYER_NOT_PRESENT;
    if (!p) { *count = 2; return VK_SUCCESS; }
    uint32_t c = *count < 2 ? *count : 2;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < c; i++) { memset(&p[i], 0, sizeof p[i]); strcpy(p[i].extensionName, names[i]); p[i].specVersion = 1; }
    *count = c;
    return c < 2 ? VK_INCOMPLETE : VK_SUCCESS;
}
static VkResult VKAPI_CALL elp(uint32_t *count, VkLayerProperties *p) { (void)p; *count = 0; return VK_SUCCESS; }
static VkResult VKAPI_CALL eiv(uint32_t *v) { *v = VK_API_VERSION_1_4; return VK_SUCCESS; }
static VkResult VKAPI_CALL create(const VkInstanceCreateInfo *ci, const VkAllocationCallbacks *a, VkInstance *out) {
    (void)a;
    struct fake_instance *fi = calloc(1, sizeof *fi);
    fake_seen.n = ci->enabledExtensionCount; fake_seen.flags = ci->flags;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < ci->enabledExtensionCount && i < 8; i++) {
        const char *e = ci->ppEnabledExtensionNames[i];
        strncpy(fake_seen.exts[i], e, 63);
        if (!strcmp(e, VK_EXT_METAL_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME)) fi->metal = 1;
        else if (strcmp(e, VK_KHR_SURFACE_EXTENSION_NAME)) { free(fi); return VK_ERROR_EXTENSION_NOT_PRESENT; }
    }
    if (ci->flags) { free(fi); return VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED; }
    *out = (VkInstance)fi;
    return VK_SUCCESS;
}
static VkResult VKAPI_CALL metal(VkInstance i, const VkMetalSurfaceCreateInfoEXT *ci, const VkAllocationCallbacks *a, VkSurfaceKHR *s) {
    (void)i; (void)a;
    fake_seen.layer = ci->pLayer;
    *s = (VkSurfaceKHR)(uintptr_t)0x5eaf;
    return VK_SUCCESS;
}
static void VKAPI_CALL destroy_surface(VkInstance i, VkSurfaceKHR s, const VkAllocationCallbacks *a) { (void)i; (void)s; (void)a; }
EXPORT void fake_marker(void) {}
EXPORT VkResult VKAPI_CALL fake_present(VkQueue q, const VkPresentInfoKHR *pi) { (void)q; (void)pi; fake_seen.presents++; return VK_SUCCESS; }
static PFN_vkVoidFunction VKAPI_CALL gdpa(VkDevice d, const char *n) {
    (void)d;
    if (!strcmp(n, "vkQueuePresentKHR")) return (PFN_vkVoidFunction)fake_present;
    return !strcmp(n, "vkMarker") ? (PFN_vkVoidFunction)fake_marker : NULL;
}
static VkResult VKAPI_CALL ede(VkPhysicalDevice pd, const char *layer, uint32_t *count, VkExtensionProperties *p) {
    (void)pd; (void)layer;
    if (!p) { *count = 1; return VK_SUCCESS; }
    if (*count < 1) return VK_INCOMPLETE;
    memset(p, 0, sizeof *p); strcpy(p->extensionName, VK_KHR_SWAPCHAIN_EXTENSION_NAME); p->specVersion = 70;
    *count = 1;
    return VK_SUCCESS;
}
static VkResult VKAPI_CALL create_device(VkPhysicalDevice pd, const VkDeviceCreateInfo *ci, const VkAllocationCallbacks *a, VkDevice *out) {
    (void)pd; (void)a;
    fake_seen.dn = ci->enabledExtensionCount;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < ci->enabledExtensionCount; i++) {
        if (i < 4) strncpy(fake_seen.dexts[i], ci->ppEnabledExtensionNames[i], 63);
        if (strcmp(ci->ppEnabledExtensionNames[i], VK_KHR_SWAPCHAIN_EXTENSION_NAME)) return VK_ERROR_EXTENSION_NOT_PRESENT;
    }
    *out = (VkDevice)(uintptr_t)0xde7;
    return VK_SUCCESS;
}

EXPORT PFN_vkVoidFunction VKAPI_CALL vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr(VkInstance inst, const char *n) {
#define R(s, f) if (!strcmp(n, s)) return (PFN_vkVoidFunction)f
    R("vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties", eie);
    R("vkEnumerateInstanceLayerProperties", elp);
    R("vkEnumerateInstanceVersion", eiv);
    R("vkCreateInstance", create);
    R("vkGetInstanceProcAddr", vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr);
    if (!inst) return NULL;
    R("vkGetDeviceProcAddr", gdpa);
    R("vkDestroySurfaceKHR", destroy_surface);
    R("vkCreateDevice", create_device);
    R("vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties", ede);
    R("vkQueuePresentKHR", fake_present);   // Mesa returns a trampoline for device functions here
    if (((struct fake_instance *)inst)->metal) R("vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT", metal);
    return NULL;
#undef R
}
EXPORT VkResult VKAPI_CALL vk_icdNegotiateLoaderICDInterfaceVersion(uint32_t *v) { fake_seen.negotiated = *v; if (*v > 7) *v = 7; return VK_SUCCESS; }

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# night-vkscene.sh: the native Vulkan renderer-path phase for the test machine's night script (sourced; defines
# phase_vkscene). Nothing is installed: the staged provider is reached through DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH (a bash subshell with
# export, never perl/env/sh, which drop DYLD_* at their start), ANV directly with --icd, the Khronos loader with
# VK_DRIVER_FILES. Every step is time-boxed with tmo (60 s at most).
#   phase_vkscene [STAGE]   STAGE: the vulkan/ folder with build.sh's output in it (lib/ bin/ icd.d/ test/),
#                           default ~/b580/vkgames
# Uses the night script's say, tmo and $O when it defines them (standalone: prints, a bash timeout, ./vkscene-out).
# Results: $O/vkscene/*.txt, PNGs of the read-back frames, frame logs; one "say" line per step.
# The "submit thread" runs (VS1w, VS2w, VS3w) need IntelXe.kext with the 14 Nov point-0 syncobj wait fix
# (xeSyncWaitEntryDone); with an older kext they fail at a present with VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN, which is expected there.
type say >/dev/null 2>&1 || say() { echo "$(date +%H:%M:%S) $*"; }
type tmo >/dev/null 2>&1 || tmo() { local s=$1; shift; "$@" & local p=$!; ( trap 'kill $sp 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM; sleep "$s" & sp=$!; wait $sp; kill -9 $p 2>/dev/null ) >/dev/null 2>&1 & local w=$!; wait $p; local r=$?; kill $w 2>/dev/null; wait $w 2>/dev/null; return $r; }

phase_vkscene() {
  local P=${1:-$HOME/b580/vkgames} R="${O:-$PWD/vkscene-out}/vkscene" ICDJ X L M f
  set -o pipefail
  mkdir -p "$R"
  X=$P/bin/vkscene; ICDJ=$P/icd.d/intel_icd.x86_64.json
  [ -x "$X" ] || { say "VS: no $X"; return 1; }
  xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "$P" 2>/dev/null
  # the staged provider under both names Wine and games open (not the installed one)
  L=$P/provider-stage; rm -rf "$L"; mkdir -p "$L"
  ln -s ../lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib "$L/libvulkan.1.dylib"; ln -s ../lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib "$L/libMoltenVK.dylib"
  stats() { sysctl -n debug.intelxe.stats 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'GuC context resets [0-9]+; GT resets [0-9]+' || echo '?'; }
  last() { grep -E '^(RESULT|PASS|FAIL)' "$1" | tail -2 | tr '\n' ' '; }
  say "VS: vkscene (MSAA, depth, bindless, timelines) - stats before: $(stats)"

  # Every path twice: --no-wbs (the queue submits directly; runs on any kernel) and the default, which first makes the
  # GPU wait on a host signal and so gives Mesa's queue a submit thread: its presents then take WAIT_PENDING +
  # SYNCOBJ_TRANSFER, which failed with IntelXe before the 14 Nov point-0 wait fix (VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN; "driver:" lines
  # carry Mesa's own text).
  # 1. ANV directly (ICD interface), FIFO, then IMMEDIATE for throughput
  tmo 60 "$X" --frames 300 --no-wbs --png "$R/1-anv.png" > "$R/1-anv.txt" 2>&1; say "VS1 ANV direct FIFO --no-wbs: $(last "$R/1-anv.txt")"
  tmo 60 "$X" --frames 300 > "$R/1w-anv-wbs.txt" 2>&1; say "VS1w ANV direct FIFO, submit thread: $(last "$R/1w-anv-wbs.txt") $(grep -m1 '^driver:' "$R/1w-anv-wbs.txt")"
  tmo 60 "$X" --frames 600 --immediate --no-wbs > "$R/1b-anv-immediate.txt" 2>&1; say "VS1b ANV direct IMMEDIATE: $(last "$R/1b-anv-immediate.txt")"
  # 2. through the provider by name, with the frame log (and its own debug log of the extensions)
  ( export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$L NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG="$R/ft-provider-%p.txt" INTELXE_VK_DEBUG=1
    tmo 60 "$X" --lib libvulkan.1.dylib --frames 300 --no-wbs --png "$R/2-provider.png" ) > "$R/2-provider.txt" 2>&1
  say "VS2 provider FIFO --no-wbs: $(last "$R/2-provider.txt")"
  ( export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$L; tmo 60 "$X" --lib libvulkan.1.dylib --frames 300 ) > "$R/2w-provider-wbs.txt" 2>&1
  say "VS2w provider FIFO, submit thread: $(last "$R/2w-provider-wbs.txt") $(grep -m1 '^driver:' "$R/2w-provider-wbs.txt")"
  ( export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$L NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG="$R/ft-provider-imm-%p.txt"
    tmo 60 "$X" --lib libMoltenVK.dylib --frames 600 --immediate --mtl-device --no-wbs ) > "$R/2b-provider-immediate.txt" 2>&1
  say "VS2b provider IMMEDIATE (as libMoltenVK.dylib, Wine-like layer with a Metal device): $(last "$R/2b-provider-immediate.txt")"
  ( export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$L; tmo 60 "$X" --lib libvulkan.1.dylib --frames 200 --resize --no-wbs ) > "$R/2c-provider-resize.txt" 2>&1
  say "VS2c provider + resize: $(last "$R/2c-provider-resize.txt")"
  # 3. the Khronos loader with ANV's manifest
  if [ -e /usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib ]; then
    ( export VK_DRIVER_FILES=$ICDJ; tmo 60 "$X" --lib /usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib --frames 300 --no-wbs ) > "$R/3-loader.txt" 2>&1
    say "VS3 loader FIFO --no-wbs: $(last "$R/3-loader.txt")"
    ( export VK_DRIVER_FILES=$ICDJ; tmo 60 "$X" --lib /usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib --frames 300 ) > "$R/3w-loader-wbs.txt" 2>&1
    say "VS3w loader FIFO, submit thread: $(last "$R/3w-loader-wbs.txt")"
  else say "VS3 loader: no /usr/local/lib/libvulkan.1.dylib, skipped"; fi
  # 4. the same frame on every path to the same driver must give the same pixels (the submit thread changes nothing)
  local sums; sums=$(grep -h -o 'scene checksum 0x[0-9a-f]*' "$R"/1-anv.txt "$R"/1w-anv-wbs.txt "$R"/2-provider.txt "$R"/2w-provider-wbs.txt \
    "$R"/3-loader.txt "$R"/3w-loader-wbs.txt 2>/dev/null | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')
  say "VS4 checksums (ANV, provider, loader, each with and without the submit thread; one value expected): $sums"
  # 5. the frame log against vkscene's own intervals
  for f in "$R"/ft-provider-[0-9]*.txt "$R"/ft-provider-imm-[0-9]*.txt; do
    [ -f "$f" ] || continue
    say "VS5 $(basename "$f"): $("$P/intelxe-vk" frametimes "$f" --skip 1 | grep '^fps')"
  done
  say "VS5 vkscene's own: FIFO $(grep -o 'fps=[0-9.]*' "$R/2-provider.txt" | head -1), IMMEDIATE $(grep -o 'fps=[0-9.]*' "$R/2b-provider-immediate.txt" | head -1)"
  # 6. A/B: the same front end over MoltenVK, if an x86_64 MoltenVK is on the machine (Wine builds, LWJGL's natives)
  M=""
  while IFS= read -r f; do case "$(file -b "$f")" in *x86_64*) M=$f; break;; esac; done < <(
    find /Applications "$HOME/Applications" "$HOME/Library/Application Support/minecraft" /usr/local/lib -name libMoltenVK.dylib 2>/dev/null | head -20)
  if [ -n "$M" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$R/mvk"; ln -sf "$M" "$R/mvk/libMoltenVK-icd.dylib"   # another leaf name: DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH holds the provider's
    ( export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$L NVMTL_PROCESS_ENV=1 INTELXE_VK_ICD="$R/mvk/libMoltenVK-icd.dylib" INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG="$R/ft-mvk-%p.txt"
      tmo 60 "$X" --lib libvulkan.1.dylib --frames 600 --immediate --no-wbs ) > "$R/6-mvk-immediate.txt" 2>&1
    say "VS6 provider -> MoltenVK ($M) IMMEDIATE: $(last "$R/6-mvk-immediate.txt") $(grep -m2 '^note:' "$R/6-mvk-immediate.txt" | tr '\n' ' ')"
  else say "VS6 MoltenVK A/B: no x86_64 libMoltenVK.dylib found, skipped"; fi
  # 7. offline checks of the stage (no GPU): the provider against a stand-in driver, the bench harness, Minecraft notes
  tmo 60 sh "$P/test/run.sh" "$P" > "$R/7-provtest.txt" 2>&1; say "VS7 provider offline test: $(grep -c '^ok' "$R/7-provtest.txt") ok, $(grep -c '^FAIL  ' "$R/7-provtest.txt") failed check(s)"
  tmo 60 "$P/test/bench-test.sh" > "$R/7-benchtest.txt" 2>&1; say "VS7 bench harness test: $(tail -1 "$R/7-benchtest.txt")"
  INTELXE_VK_ROOT=$P "$P/intelxe-vk" minecraft-args > "$R/7-minecraft.txt" 2>&1; say "VS7 minecraft-args: $(grep -c 'library validation off\|lets it load\|no hardened runtime: loads' "$R/7-minecraft.txt") Java runtime(s) able to load it; $(grep -c ': .*bin/java\|bin/java: ' "$R/7-minecraft.txt") found"
  say "VS: stats after: $(stats)"
}

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// provtest: the provider's offline test against fakeicd (test/run.sh sets it up). Opens the provider the way Wine
// does (dlopen of a bare name through DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, dlsym of the names Wine 10 and 11 resolve) and checks the
// loader-side work: extension list, VK_MVK_macos_surface -> VK_EXT_metal_surface, VK_KHR_portability_enumeration
// dropped, surfaces from a CAMetalLayer and from an NSView, vkGetDeviceProcAddr forwarding, VK_KHR_portability_subset
// dropped at vkCreateDevice, and vkQueuePresentKHR: the driver's own without INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG, the logging wrapper
// with it (test/run.sh checks the log file afterwards).
//   provtest NAME FAKEICD      e.g. provtest libMoltenVK.dylib /path/libfakeicd.dylib
#include <dlfcn.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#import <AppKit/AppKit.h>
#import <QuartzCore/CAMetalLayer.h>
#define VK_NO_PROTOTYPES
#define VK_USE_PLATFORM_METAL_EXT
#define VK_USE_PLATFORM_MACOS_MVK
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>

typedef struct { char exts[8][64]; uint32_t n, flags; const void *layer; int negotiated; char dexts[4][64]; uint32_t dn; int presents; } seen_t;
static int fails;
#define T(c, ...) do { if (c) printf("ok    " __VA_ARGS__); else { printf("FAIL  " __VA_ARGS__); fails++; } printf("\n"); } while (0)

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    @autoreleasepool {
    if (argc < 3) { printf("usage: provtest NAME FAKEICD\n"); return 2; }
    // read now: on a machine with the Metal driver, its plugin (loaded below by CAMetalLayer/NSView) unsets INTELXE*
    // variables it inherits (nvmtl_env_knobs.h); the provider keeps its own copy from load time
    const char *fl = getenv("INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG");
    fl = fl && *fl ? strdup(fl) : NULL;
    void *h = dlopen(argv[1], RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
    if (!h) { printf("FAIL  dlopen %s: %s\n", argv[1], dlerror()); return 1; }
    if (getenv("PROVTEST_STRIP")) {   // what the Metal driver's plugin does when it loads after the provider
        unsetenv("INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG");
        unsetenv("INTELXE_VK_ICD");
        printf("note  INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG and INTELXE_VK_ICD unset after the provider was loaded\n");
    }
    void *fk = dlopen(argv[2], RTLD_NOW | RTLD_NOLOAD);
    PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr gipa = (PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr)dlsym(h, "vkGetInstanceProcAddr");
    PFN_vkGetDeviceProcAddr gdpa = (PFN_vkGetDeviceProcAddr)dlsym(h, "vkGetDeviceProcAddr");
    PFN_vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT dl_metal = (PFN_vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT)dlsym(h, "vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT");
    PFN_vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK dl_mvk = (PFN_vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK)dlsym(h, "vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK");
    T(gipa && gdpa, "dlsym vkGetInstanceProcAddr, vkGetDeviceProcAddr (win32u vulkan_init_once)");
    T(dl_metal && dl_mvk, "dlsym vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT, vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK (winemac.drv VulkanInit, Wine 10 needs both)");
    T(dlsym(h, "vkGetMTLDeviceMVK") == NULL, "no MoltenVK private API exported (Wine does not use it)");
    if (!gipa) return 1;
    // after the first call the provider has loaded the fake ICD
    PFN_vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties eie = (PFN_vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties)gipa(NULL, "vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties");
    uint32_t n = 0;
    T(eie && eie(NULL, &n, NULL) == VK_SUCCESS && n == 4, "instance extensions: %u (ANV's 2 + MVK alias + portability enumeration)", n);
    VkExtensionProperties p[8] = {0};
    int metal = 0, mvk = 0, port = 0;
    eie(NULL, &n, p);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        metal |= !strcmp(p[i].extensionName, "VK_EXT_metal_surface");
        mvk |= !strcmp(p[i].extensionName, "VK_MVK_macos_surface") && p[i].specVersion == 3;
        port |= !strcmp(p[i].extensionName, "VK_KHR_portability_enumeration");
    }
    T(metal && mvk && port, "VK_EXT_metal_surface, VK_MVK_macos_surface (spec 3), VK_KHR_portability_enumeration listed");
    uint32_t two = 2;
    T(eie(NULL, &two, p) == VK_INCOMPLETE && two == 2, "a short array gets VK_INCOMPLETE");
    if (!fk) fk = dlopen(argv[2], RTLD_NOW | RTLD_NOLOAD);
    seen_t *seen = fk ? (seen_t *)dlsym(fk, "fake_seen") : NULL;
    T(seen != NULL, "the provider loaded the fake ICD (INTELXE_VK_ICD)");
    if (!seen) return 1;
    T(seen->negotiated == 7, "ICD interface negotiated at version %d", seen->negotiated);
    T((void *)gipa(NULL, "vkGetInstanceProcAddr") == (void *)gipa, "vkGetInstanceProcAddr(NULL, \"vkGetInstanceProcAddr\") is the provider's");

    const char *ex[] = {"VK_KHR_surface", "VK_MVK_macos_surface", "VK_KHR_portability_enumeration", "VK_EXT_metal_surface"};
    VkInstanceCreateInfo ci = {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INSTANCE_CREATE_INFO, NULL, VK_INSTANCE_CREATE_ENUMERATE_PORTABILITY_BIT_KHR, NULL, 0, NULL, 4, ex};
    VkInstance inst = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    PFN_vkCreateInstance create = (PFN_vkCreateInstance)gipa(NULL, "vkCreateInstance");
    VkResult r = create(&ci, NULL, &inst);
    T(r == VK_SUCCESS, "vkCreateInstance with VK_MVK_macos_surface + portability enumeration (+ flag) = %d", r);
    T(seen->n == 2 && !strcmp(seen->exts[0], "VK_KHR_surface") && !strcmp(seen->exts[1], "VK_EXT_metal_surface") && seen->flags == 0,
      "the ICD got VK_KHR_surface, VK_EXT_metal_surface once, flags 0 (got %u: %s %s, flags %u)", seen->n, seen->exts[0], seen->exts[1], seen->flags);
    if (r) return 1;

    CAMetalLayer *layer = [CAMetalLayer layer];
    VkSurfaceKHR s = 0;
    VkMetalSurfaceCreateInfoEXT mci = {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_METAL_SURFACE_CREATE_INFO_EXT, NULL, 0, layer};
    T(dl_metal(inst, &mci, NULL, &s) == VK_SUCCESS && s && seen->layer == (__bridge const void *)layer, "dlsym'd vkCreateMetalSurfaceEXT reaches the ICD with the layer");
    PFN_vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK mvkf = (PFN_vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK)gipa(inst, "vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK");
    seen->layer = NULL; s = 0;
    VkMacOSSurfaceCreateInfoMVK vci = {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MACOS_SURFACE_CREATE_INFO_MVK, NULL, 0, (__bridge const void *)layer};
    T(mvkf && mvkf(inst, &vci, NULL, &s) == VK_SUCCESS && seen->layer == (__bridge const void *)layer, "vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK with a CAMetalLayer (what Wine passes)");
    [NSApplication sharedApplication];
    NSView *v = [[NSView alloc] initWithFrame:NSMakeRect(0, 0, 64, 64)];
    seen->layer = NULL;
    vci.pView = (__bridge const void *)v;
    T(dl_mvk(inst, &vci, NULL, &s) == VK_SUCCESS && seen->layer && [(__bridge id)seen->layer isKindOfClass:[CAMetalLayer class]] &&
      (__bridge id)seen->layer == v.layer, "vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK with a plain NSView gives it a CAMetalLayer");
    vci.pView = (__bridge const void *)@"not a view";
    T(dl_mvk(inst, &vci, NULL, &s) == VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED, "vkCreateMacOSSurfaceMVK refuses an object that is neither");
    PFN_vkGetDeviceProcAddr gd2 = (PFN_vkGetDeviceProcAddr)gipa(inst, "vkGetDeviceProcAddr");
    void *marker = dlsym(fk, "fake_marker");
    T(gd2 && (void *)gdpa((VkDevice)(uintptr_t)1, "vkMarker") == marker && (void *)gd2((VkDevice)(uintptr_t)1, "vkMarker") == marker,
      "vkGetDeviceProcAddr (exported and through vkGetInstanceProcAddr) forwards to the ICD's");
    // devices
    PFN_vkCreateDevice cdev = (PFN_vkCreateDevice)gipa(inst, "vkCreateDevice");
    const char *dex[] = {"VK_KHR_swapchain", "VK_KHR_portability_subset"};
    VkDeviceCreateInfo dci = {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEVICE_CREATE_INFO, NULL, 0, 0, NULL, 0, NULL, 2, dex, NULL};
    VkDevice dev = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
    r = cdev ? cdev((VkPhysicalDevice)(uintptr_t)1, &dci, NULL, &dev) : VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED;
    T(r == VK_SUCCESS && seen->dn == 1 && !strcmp(seen->dexts[0], "VK_KHR_swapchain"),
      "vkCreateDevice with VK_KHR_portability_subset: dropped for a driver without it (= %d, driver got %u)", r, seen->dn);
    dci.enabledExtensionCount = 1;
    dci.ppEnabledExtensionNames = (const char *[]){"VK_EXT_not_there"};
    T(cdev && cdev((VkPhysicalDevice)(uintptr_t)1, &dci, NULL, &dev) == VK_ERROR_EXTENSION_NOT_PRESENT, "another unknown device extension is still refused");
    void *fpres = dlsym(fk, "fake_present");
    PFN_vkQueuePresentKHR pres = (PFN_vkQueuePresentKHR)gdpa((VkDevice)(uintptr_t)0xde7, "vkQueuePresentKHR");
    PFN_vkQueuePresentKHR pres2 = (PFN_vkQueuePresentKHR)gipa(inst, "vkQueuePresentKHR");
    if (fl)
        T(pres && pres2 && (void *)pres != fpres && (void *)pres2 != fpres, "INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG: vkQueuePresentKHR is the logging wrapper (both ways)");
    else
        T((void *)pres == fpres && (void *)pres2 == fpres, "no INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG: vkQueuePresentKHR is the driver's own (no cost per call)");
    VkSwapchainKHR swc = (VkSwapchainKHR)(uintptr_t)0x5c;
    uint32_t idx = 0;
    VkPresentInfoKHR pinfo = {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PRESENT_INFO_KHR, NULL, 0, NULL, 1, &swc, &idx, NULL};
    int before = seen->presents;
    for (int i = 0; i < 5 && pres; i++) { pres((VkQueue)(uintptr_t)1, &pinfo); usleep(2000); }
    T(seen->presents == before + 5, "5 presents reach the driver (%d)", seen->presents - before);

    VkInstanceCreateInfo bad = {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_INSTANCE_CREATE_INFO, NULL, 0, NULL, 0, NULL, 1, (const char *[]){"VK_KHR_xlib_surface"}};
    VkInstance i2;
    T(create(&bad, NULL, &i2) == VK_ERROR_EXTENSION_NOT_PRESENT, "an extension neither offers is still refused");
    const char *(*anvp)(void) = (const char *(*)(void))dlsym(h, "intelxe_vk_anv_path");
    T(anvp && anvp() && strstr(anvp(), "fakeicd"), "intelxe_vk_anv_path: %s", anvp ? anvp() : "-");
    printf("%s (%d failure(s))\n", fails ? "FAIL" : "PASS", fails);
    return fails != 0;
    }
}

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# run.sh OUTDIR: the provider's offline test (build.sh OUTDIR first). No GPU: a fake ICD stands in for ANV. The
# provider is opened by the names Wine uses, through DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, as intelxe-vk run does it.
set -eu
O=$(cd "${1:?usage: run.sh OUTDIR}" && pwd)
P=$O/test/provider; rm -rf "$P"; mkdir -p "$P"
ln -s ../../lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib "$P/libMoltenVK.dylib"
ln -s ../../lib/libintelxe-vk.dylib "$P/libvulkan.1.dylib"
for name in libMoltenVK.dylib libvulkan.1.dylib; do
    echo "== $name"
    DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$P INTELXE_VK_ICD=$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib INTELXE_VK_DEBUG=1 "$O/test/provtest" $name "$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib"
done
echo "== INTELXE_VK_ICD naming a file that DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH turns into the provider"
if DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$P INTELXE_VK_ICD=/somewhere/libMoltenVK.dylib "$O/test/provtest" libvulkan.1.dylib "$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib" 2>&1 |
        grep -q 'is the provider itself'; then echo "ok    refused with a message (no recursion)"; else echo "FAIL  no message"; exit 1; fi
echo "== libvulkan.1.dylib with INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG (unset after load, as the Metal plugin does)"
L=$O/test/frames-%p.txt; rm -f "$O"/test/frames-*.txt
# PROVTEST_STRIP: the variables are unset once the provider is loaded, as the Metal plugin does; its load-time copy counts
DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=$P INTELXE_VK_ICD=$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib INTELXE_VK_FRAMELOG=$L PROVTEST_STRIP=1 "$O/test/provtest" libvulkan.1.dylib "$O/test/libfakeicd.dylib"
F=$(ls "$O"/test/frames-*.txt 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -n "$F" ] && [ "$(grep -c '^[0-9]' "$F")" = 5 ] && grep -q '^# end: 5 presents' "$F"; then
    echo "ok    frame log $(basename "$F"): 5 lines and the end line (%p = the pid)"
else
    echo "FAIL  frame log: ${F:-none written}"; [ -n "$F" ] && cat "$F"; exit 1
fi
D=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
"$D/intelxe-vk" frametimes "$F" | sed 's/^/      /'
"$D/intelxe-vk" frametimes "$F" | grep -q '^summary frames=5 .* intervals=4 fps=[1-9]' || { echo "FAIL  intelxe-vk frametimes"; exit 1; }
echo "ok    intelxe-vk frametimes reads it"

FILE: windows/app/build.ps1
================================================
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
<#
.SYNOPSIS
build.ps1: builds IntelXe Manager for Windows. Restores, builds, runs the Core tests, and publishes the app as a
self-contained folder (no .NET or Windows App Runtime to install) plus a zip of it.

.DESCRIPTION
  .\build.ps1                    restore, build, test, publish to out\IntelXeManager-VERSION-win-x64, zip it and
                                 write the zip's SHA-256 beside it (.zip.sha256, for release/package.sh)
  .\build.ps1 -SkipTests         the same without the tests
  .\build.ps1 -SkipEngine        without the EFI builder beside the app (engine\: the Build the EFI page then says so)
  .\build.ps1 -Configuration Debug

The EFI builder (engine\ in the published folder, docs/design/DESIGN-efi-build.md section 5): python.org's embeddable
Python and the wheels pinned in engine.lock.json (SHA-256), windows/efibuild, and OpCore Simplify and Hardware Sniffer
at the commits of windows/efibuild/upstream/PINNED.json, every file checked against their manifests. The downloads are
kept in OUT\downloads\. Nothing downloaded is run here; engine\MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file for the app's own check.

Needs the .NET 10 SDK on Windows (the WinUI XAML compiler runs only there). On macOS or Linux only the Core and its
tests build: dotnet test IntelXe.Core.Tests
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [ValidateSet('Release', 'Debug')][string]$Configuration = 'Release',
    [switch]$SkipTests,
    [switch]$SkipEngine,
    [string]$OutDir
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Set-StrictMode -Version 2
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$repo = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $here '..\..')).Path
$version = (Get-Content -Raw (Join-Path $repo 'VERSION')).Trim()
if (-not $OutDir) { $OutDir = Join-Path $here 'out' }
$name = "IntelXeManager-$version-win-x64"
$publish = Join-Path $OutDir $name
$zip = Join-Path $OutDir "$name.zip"

function Invoke-Step([string]$title, [scriptblock]$block) {
    Write-Host "== $title"
    & $block
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "$title failed (exit code $LASTEXITCODE)" }
}

$app = Join-Path $here 'IntelXe.App\IntelXe.App.csproj'
$tests = Join-Path $here 'IntelXe.Core.Tests\IntelXe.Core.Tests.csproj'

Invoke-Step 'restore' { dotnet restore $app -r win-x64 -p:Platform=x64; if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { dotnet restore $tests } }
Invoke-Step 'build' { dotnet build $app -c $Configuration -r win-x64 -p:Platform=x64 --no-restore }
if (-not $SkipTests) {
    Invoke-Step 'test' { dotnet test $tests -c $Configuration --no-restore }
}
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $publish) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -LiteralPath $publish }
Invoke-Step 'publish' { dotnet publish $app -c $Configuration -r win-x64 -p:Platform=x64 --self-contained --no-restore -o $publish }

# the PDBs stay in the build folder; the folder a user unpacks holds what runs
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $publish -Recurse -Filter '*.pdb' | Remove-Item -Force

# ---- the EFI builder beside the app ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem

function Get-Sha256([string]$path) { (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath $path).Hash.ToLowerInvariant() }

# A pinned download, kept in OUT\downloads under its name; used only when its bytes have the pinned SHA-256.
function Get-Pinned([string]$url, [string]$sha256, [string]$name) {
    $dir = Join-Path $OutDir 'downloads'
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
    $file = Join-Path $dir $name
    # an upstream source archive has no pinned bytes (its contents are checked): a kept one is used as it is
    if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $file) -and (-not $sha256 -or (Get-Sha256 $file) -eq $sha256)) { return $file }
    if (-not $url.StartsWith('https://')) { throw "only https downloads: $url" }
    Write-Host "   download $url"
    $tmp = "$file.part"
    [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12 -bor [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol
    $ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
    Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -Uri $url -OutFile $tmp
    $got = Get-Sha256 $tmp
    if ($sha256 -and $got -ne $sha256) { Remove-Item -Force -LiteralPath $tmp; throw "${url}: SHA-256 $got is not the pinned $sha256" }
    Move-Item -Force -LiteralPath $tmp -Destination $file
    return $file
}

# "sha256  relative/path" per file, sorted by path (ordinal), LF: the format of windows/efibuild/upstream/*.sha256
# (upstream.py manifest_text, which skips __pycache__ folders) and of engine\MANIFEST.sha256 (EngineLayout).
function Get-ManifestText([string]$root, [string]$exclude = '') {
    $root = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $root).Path.TrimEnd('\')
    $rels = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
    $lines = New-Object 'System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary[string,string]' ([StringComparer]::Ordinal)
    foreach ($f in Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $root -Recurse -File -Force) {
        $rel = $f.FullName.Substring($root.Length + 1).Replace('\', '/')
        if ($rel -eq $exclude -or ('/' + $rel) -match '/__pycache__/') { continue }
        $rels.Add($rel)
        $lines[$rel] = '{0}  {1}' -f (Get-Sha256 $f.FullName), $rel
    }
    $sorted = $rels.ToArray()
    [Array]::Sort($sorted, [StringComparer]::Ordinal)
    return (($sorted | ForEach-Object { $lines[$_] + "`n" }) -join '')
}

function Expand-Zip([string]$zip, [string]$dest) {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dest | Out-Null
    [IO.Compression.ZipFile]::ExtractToDirectory($zip, $dest)
}

function Add-Engine([string]$engine) {
    $efibuild = Join-Path $repo 'windows\efibuild'
    $lock = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath (Join-Path $here 'engine.lock.json') | ConvertFrom-Json
    if ($lock.format -ne 'intelxe-winapp-engine' -or $lock.format_version -ne 1) { throw 'engine.lock.json: unknown format' }
    if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $engine) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -LiteralPath $engine }

    # python.org's embeddable Python; its ._pth names the search path (and turns site on for the wheels' .pth files)
    $py = Join-Path $engine 'python'
    Expand-Zip (Get-Pinned $lock.python.url $lock.python.sha256 ([IO.Path]::GetFileName($lock.python.url))) $py
    $pth = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $py -Filter 'python3*._pth')
    if ($pth.Count -ne 1) { throw 'the embeddable Python has no single python3*._pth' }
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($pth[0].FullName, (($lock.python.path -join "`r`n") + "`r`n"))

    # the wheels, unpacked as pip would into Lib\site-packages (their .data folders and pywin32's IDE and help left out)
    $site = Join-Path $py 'Lib\site-packages'
    foreach ($w in $lock.wheels) {
        Expand-Zip (Get-Pinned $w.url $w.sha256 ([IO.Path]::GetFileName($w.url))) $site
    }
    foreach ($r in $lock.remove) {
        $p = Join-Path $py $r
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $p) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -LiteralPath $p }
    }

    # windows/efibuild itself (not its tests)
    $eb = Join-Path $engine 'efibuild'
    foreach ($pattern in $lock.efibuild) {
        foreach ($f in @(Get-ChildItem -Path (Join-Path $efibuild $pattern) -File)) {
            $rel = $f.FullName.Substring($efibuild.Length + 1)
            $dst = Join-Path $eb $rel
            New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $dst) | Out-Null
            Copy-Item -LiteralPath $f.FullName -Destination $dst
        }
    }
    # the rules the engine reads (rules.py looks beside the package first): the published app has no release\ folder
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repo 'release\templates\efi-rules.json') -Destination (Join-Path $eb 'efi-rules.json')

    # OpCore Simplify and Hardware Sniffer at their pinned commits: the source archive's files must be exactly the
    # manifest's (GitHub does not promise stable archive bytes, so the contents are what is pinned)
    $pinned = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath (Join-Path $efibuild 'upstream\PINNED.json') | ConvertFrom-Json
    foreach ($prop in $pinned.projects.PSObject.Properties) {
        $name = $prop.Name; $proj = $prop.Value
        $manifest = Join-Path $efibuild ('upstream\' + $proj.manifest)
        if ((Get-Sha256 $manifest) -ne $proj.manifest_sha256) { throw "$($proj.manifest) does not match manifest_sha256 in PINNED.json" }
        $archive = Get-Pinned $proj.archive '' "$name-$($proj.commit).tar.gz"
        $tmp = Join-Path $OutDir "upstream-$name"
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $tmp) { Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -LiteralPath $tmp }
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $tmp | Out-Null
        & (Join-Path $env:SystemRoot 'System32\tar.exe') -xzf $archive -C $tmp
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "could not unpack $archive" }
        $top = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $tmp -Directory)
        if ($top.Count -ne 1) { throw "$archive does not hold one folder" }
        $want = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($manifest)
        if ((Get-ManifestText $top[0].FullName) -ne $want) {
            Remove-Item -Force -LiteralPath $archive
            throw "$name at $($proj.commit) differs from its pinned manifest (the archive was deleted; run again to download it again)"
        }
        Move-Item -LiteralPath $top[0].FullName -Destination (Join-Path $eb "upstream\$name-$($proj.commit)")
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -LiteralPath $tmp
    }

    Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $here 'engine.lock.json') -Destination (Join-Path $engine 'engine.lock.json')
    # every file, for the app's check before each scan and build (Core/EfiBuild/EngineLayout.cs)
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $engine 'MANIFEST.sha256'), (Get-ManifestText $engine 'MANIFEST.sha256'), (New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
    $engineSize = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $engine -Recurse -File | Measure-Object -Sum Length).Sum
    Write-Host ("== engine: {0} ({1:N0} MB, {2} files)" -f $engine, ($engineSize / 1MB), @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $engine -Recurse -File).Count)
}

if (-not $SkipEngine) { Invoke-Step 'engine' { Add-Engine (Join-Path $publish 'engine'); $global:LASTEXITCODE = 0 } }
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $zip) { Remove-Item -Force -LiteralPath $zip }
# the zip with '/' in its entry names, as the zip format has them (Windows PowerShell 5.1's Compress-Archive writes '\',
# which macOS and Linux unzip into file names holding backslashes); folders as their own entries, files in path order
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression, System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$base = Split-Path -Parent $publish
$zs = [IO.File]::Open($zip, [IO.FileMode]::CreateNew)
$za = New-Object IO.Compression.ZipArchive($zs, [IO.Compression.ZipArchiveMode]::Create)
try {
    $items = @(Get-Item -LiteralPath $publish) + @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $publish -Recurse) | Sort-Object FullName
    foreach ($it in $items) {
        $rel = $it.FullName.Substring($base.Length + 1).Replace('\', '/')
        if ($it.PSIsContainer) { [void]$za.CreateEntry($rel + '/'); continue }
        [void][IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($za, $it.FullName, $rel, [IO.Compression.CompressionLevel]::Optimal)
    }
} finally { $za.Dispose(); $zs.Dispose() }
# its SHA-256 beside it, as shasum writes it: release/package.sh (WINAPP_ZIP) checks the zip it is given against it
$hash = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath $zip).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
[IO.File]::WriteAllText("$zip.sha256", "$hash  $name.zip`n")

$size = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $publish -Recurse -File | Measure-Object -Sum Length).Sum
Write-Host ("== done: {0} ({1:N0} MB), {2} ({3:N0} MB), SHA-256 {4}" -f $publish, ($size / 1MB), $zip, ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $zip).Length / 1MB), $hash)

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// IntelXe Manager for Windows: check this PC, prepare the OpenCore EFI (through the shared EFI rules), collect a
// diagnostics report. The counterpart of the macOS app in app/; the same sections, wording and accent.
using Microsoft.UI.Xaml;

namespace IntelXe.App;

public partial class App : Application
{
    public static MainWindow? Window { get; private set; }
    public static Options Options { get; } = Options.Parse(Environment.GetCommandLineArgs().Skip(1).ToArray());
    public static Settings Settings => IntelXe.App.Settings.Current;

    public App()
    {
        System.Text.Encoding.RegisterProvider(System.Text.CodePagesEncodingProvider.Instance);   // the report script's console output
        InitializeComponent();
    }

    protected override void OnLaunched(LaunchActivatedEventArgs args)
    {
        L.SetLanguage(Options.Language ?? Settings.Current.Language);
        Window = new MainWindow();
        Window.Activate();
    }
}

/// The command line, as the macOS app's --section: for screenshots and support instructions.
/// --section overview|efi|report|about, --lang en-US|tr-TR, --theme light|dark, --size WIDTHxHEIGHT (in effective pixels),
/// --scroll PIXELS (the page scrolled down by that much, for a screenshot of its lower part), --report-out FOLDER (where
/// the diagnostics report goes instead of the Desktop). The EFI page: --efi-folder FOLDER (chosen as the EFI), --package
/// FOLDER|ZIP, --card-confirmed (the card's ACPI path confirmed), --plan settings|safari|settings-safari|driver|undo (that
/// plan's dialog opened), --helper-for-folders (an EFI folder through the elevated helper too, to test it without an EFI
/// partition). The BIOS page: --bios-vendor asus|msi|gigabyte|asrock|generic (that maker's menu names), --bios-html FILE
/// (its printable page written there once the facts are read). The stick page:
/// --recovery-dir FOLDER (where the recovery downloads are kept instead of %LOCALAPPDATA%), --stick-confirm (the erase
/// dialog opened, for the test disk only), and, for tests only,
/// --test-vhdx PATH (that VHD/VHDX file, attached, is offered and may be written although it is not a USB stick).
public sealed record Options(string? Section, string? Language, string? Theme, int? Width, int? Height, int? Scroll, string? ReportOut,
    string? EfiFolder = null, string? Package = null, string? Plan = null, bool CardConfirmed = false, bool HelperForFolders = false,
    string? BiosVendor = null, string? TestVhdx = null, bool StickConfirm = false, string? BiosHtml = null, string? RecoveryDir = null)
{
    public static Options Parse(string[] args)
    {
        string? Value(string name)
        {
            int i = Array.IndexOf(args, name);
            return i >= 0 && i + 1 < args.Length ? args[i + 1] : null;
        }
        int? w = null, h = null;
        var size = Value("--size")?.Split('x');
        if (size is { Length: 2 } && int.TryParse(size[0], out var sw) && int.TryParse(size[1], out var sh)) { w = sw; h = sh; }
        int? scroll = int.TryParse(Value("--scroll"), out var sc) ? sc : null;
        return new Options(Value("--section"), Value("--lang"), Value("--theme"), w, h, scroll, Value("--report-out"),
            Value("--efi-folder"), Value("--package"), Value("--plan"), args.Contains("--card-confirmed"), args.Contains("--helper-for-folders"),
            Value("--bios-vendor"), Value("--test-vhdx"), args.Contains("--stick-confirm"), Value("--bios-html"), Value("--recovery-dir"));
    }
}

FILE: windows/app/IntelXe.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
using IntelXe.App.Pages;
using Microsoft.UI;
using Microsoft.UI.Windowing;
using Microsoft.UI.Xaml;
using Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Controls;
using Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media;
using Windows.Graphics;

namespace IntelXe.App;

/// The window: Mica, the app's own title bar, and the sidebar with the macOS app's groups (Status, Install, Help) and
/// the pages this version has.
public sealed partial class MainWindow : Window
{
    public MainWindow()
    {
        InitializeComponent();
        SystemBackdrop = new MicaBackdrop();
        ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar = true;
        SetTitleBar(AppTitleBar);
        AppWindow.SetIcon(Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Assets", "AppIcon.ico"));
        AppWindow.TitleBar.ButtonBackgroundColor = Colors.Transparent;
        AppWindow.TitleBar.ButtonInactiveBackgroundColor = Colors.Transparent;

        double scale = Root.XamlRoot?.RasterizationScale ?? GetDpiScale();
        AppWindow.Resize(new SizeInt32((int)((App.Options.Width ?? 1080) * scale), (int)((App.Options.Height ?? 780) * scale)));
        if (AppWindow.Presenter is OverlappedPresenter p)
        {
            p.PreferredMinimumWidth = (int)(640 * scale);
            p.PreferredMinimumHeight = (int)(480 * scale);
        }

        ApplyTheme(App.Options.Theme ?? Settings.Current.Theme);
        ApplyLanguage();
        Root.ActualThemeChanged += (_, _) => UpdateTitleBarButtons();

        var start = Item(App.Options.Section);
        Nav.SelectedItem = start;
        _ = AppState.Current.RefreshAsync();
    }

    double GetDpiScale()
    {
        var hwnd = WinRT.Interop.WindowNative.GetWindowHandle(this);
        return Native.GetDpiForWindow(hwnd) / 96.0;
    }

    /// The sidebar's texts in the language chosen; the page shown is built again.
    public void ApplyLanguage()
    {
        Title = L.Get("App_Name");
        AppTitle.Text = L.Get("App_Name");
        HeaderStatus.Content = L.Get("Group_Status");
        HeaderInstall.Content = L.Get("Group_Install");
        HeaderHelp.Content = L.Get("Group_Help");
        ItemSetup.Content = L.Get("Nav_Setup");
        ItemOverview.Content = L.Get("Nav_Overview");
        ItemBios.Content = L.Get("Nav_Bios");
        ItemBuild.Content = L.Get("Nav_Build");
        ItemStick.Content = L.Get("Nav_Stick");
        ItemEfi.Content = L.Get("Nav_Efi");
        ItemReport.Content = L.Get("Nav_Report");
        ItemAbout.Content = L.Get("Nav_About");
        if (Nav.SelectedItem is NavigationViewItem item) Show(item);
    }

    /// "light", "dark" or anything else for the system's.
    public void ApplyTheme(string? theme)
    {
        Root.RequestedTheme = theme switch { "light" => ElementTheme.Light, "dark" => ElementTheme.Dark, _ => ElementTheme.Default };
        UpdateTitleBarButtons();
    }

    void UpdateTitleBarButtons()
    {
        bool dark = Root.ActualTheme == ElementTheme.Dark;
        AppWindow.TitleBar.ButtonForegroundColor = dark ? Colors.White : Colors.Black;
        AppWindow.TitleBar.ButtonHoverForegroundColor = dark ? Colors.White : Colors.Black;
        AppWindow.TitleBar.ButtonHoverBackgroundColor = dark ? ColorHelper.FromArgb(0x18, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF) : ColorHelper.FromArgb(0x10, 0, 0, 0);
        AppWindow.TitleBar.ButtonInactiveForegroundColor = dark ? ColorHelper.FromArgb(0x80, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF) : ColorHelper.FromArgb(0x80, 0, 0, 0);
    }

    void OnSelectionChanged(NavigationView sender, NavigationViewSelectionChangedEventArgs args)
    {
        if (args.SelectedItem is NavigationViewItem item) Show(item);
    }

    void Show(NavigationViewItem item)
    {
        var type = (item.Tag as string) switch
        {
            "setup" => typeof(SetupPage),
            "build" => typeof(BuildPage),
            "bios" => typeof(BiosPage),
            "stick" => typeof(StickPage),
            "efi" => typeof(EfiPage),
            "report" => typeof(ReportPage),
            "about" => typeof(AboutPage),
            _ => typeof(OverviewPage),
        };
        ContentFrame.Navigate(type, null, new Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Media.Animation.EntranceNavigationTransitionInfo());
        ContentFrame.BackStack.Clear();
    }

    /// Opens another page, as the macOS app's "Open the ... page" buttons do.
    public void Open(string tag)
    {
        Nav.SelectedItem = Item(tag);
    }

    /// The sidebar item of a --section / Open tag; the Set up page (the first item) for none.
    NavigationViewItem Item(string? tag) => tag switch
    {
        "overview" => ItemOverview, "build" => ItemBuild, "bios" => ItemBios, "stick" => ItemStick, "efi" => ItemEfi,
        "report" => ItemReport, "about" => ItemAbout, _ => ItemSetup,
    };
}

FILE: windows/app/IntelXe.App/Program.cs

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The entry point (instead of the one the XAML compiler generates: DISABLE_XAML_GENERATED_MAIN). "--efi-helper ..." is
// the elevated helper, the same exe started with "runas" by the EFI page for an EFI partition: it opens no window, does
// one mount + read/plan or mount + backup + change + unmount, writes its answer to the --out file and exits.
// "--efi-helper sniff ..." is the Build page's scan (Hardware Sniffer and the ACPI tables, through "runas").
// "--stick-helper ..." is the installer stick's helper (list, check, write through "runas", download); "--probe-helper
// ..." the probe stick's (check, write through "runas"). Anything else starts the app.
using Microsoft.UI.Dispatching;
using Microsoft.UI.Xaml;

namespace IntelXe.App;

public static class Program
{
    [STAThread]
    static int Main(string[] args)
    {
        if (Core.EfiBuild.SniffRequest.Is(args)) return SniffHelperMain.Run(args);
        if (args.Length > 0 && args[0] == Core.Efi.EfiHelperRequest.Switch) return HelperMain.Run(args);
        if (args.Length > 0 && args[0] == Core.Stick.StickHelperRequest.Switch) return StickHelperMain.Run(args);
        if (args.Length > 0 && args[0] == Core.ProbeStick.ProbeHelperRequest.Switch) return ProbeHelperMain.Run(args);

        WinRT.ComWrappersSupport.InitializeComWrappers();
        Application.Start(p =>
        {
            var context = new DispatcherQueueSynchronizationContext(DispatcherQueue.GetForCurrentThread());
            SynchronizationContext.SetSynchronizationContext(context);
            _ = new App();
        });
        return 0;
    }
}
